// === FILE: stdlib/algo/graph.sio ===
//! Graph Algorithms
//!
//! Classic graph algorithms for directed and undirected graphs represented
//! as adjacency lists. All algorithms use fixed-size arrays for simplicity.
//!
//! # Representation
//! - Graphs are represented as adjacency lists (array of arrays)
//! - Max 100 nodes for simplicity
//! - For weighted graphs, use adjacency matrix
//!
//! # Algorithms
//! - dijkstra: Shortest paths from source (weighted graphs)
//! - dfs: Depth-first search traversal
//! - bfs: Breadth-first search traversal
//! - topological_sort: Topological ordering (DAGs)
//! - has_cycle: Cycle detection
//!
//! # Usage
//! ```sio
//! // Create adjacency list for graph with 5 nodes
//! var adj = [[0; 10]; 100]
//! adj[0][0] = 1  // edge 0 -> 1
//! adj[0][1] = 2  // edge 0 -> 2
//!
//! let visited = dfs(&adj, 5, 0)
//! ```

// Helper: Find minimum distance node not yet visited
fn find_min_unvisited(dist: &[f64; 100], visited: &[bool; 100], n: usize) -> usize with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var min_dist = 1e100
    var min_idx = 0

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if !visited[i] && dist[i] < min_dist {
            min_dist = dist[i]
            min_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return min_idx
}

// Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm
//
// Computes shortest paths from source to all other nodes in a weighted graph.
// Uses adjacency matrix where adj[i][j] is the weight of edge i -> j.
// Returns array of distances from source to each node.
//
// Arguments:
// - adj: Adjacency matrix (adj[i][j] = weight of edge i->j, or -1 if no edge)
// - n: Number of nodes
// - source: Starting node
//
// Returns: Array of shortest distances from source to each node (INF if unreachable)
pub fn dijkstra(adj: &[[f64; 100]; 100], n: usize, source: usize) -> [f64; 100] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var dist = [1e100; 100]
    var visited = [false; 100]

    dist[source] = 0.0

    var count = 0
    while count < n {
        let u = find_min_unvisited(&dist, &visited, n)
        visited[u] = true

        // Update distances to neighbors
        var v = 0
        while v < n {
            if !visited[v] && adj[u][v] >= 0.0 {
                let new_dist = dist[u] + adj[u][v]
                if new_dist < dist[v] {
                    dist[v] = new_dist
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }

        count = count + 1
    }

    return dist
}

// Depth-first search traversal
//
// Performs DFS starting from source node and returns nodes in visit order.
// Uses stack-based iterative approach (no recursion).
//
// Arguments:
// - adj: Adjacency list (adj[i] contains neighbors of node i, -1 terminated)
// - n: Number of nodes
// - source: Starting node
//
// Returns: Array of nodes in DFS visit order (length encoded at index 0)
pub fn dfs(adj: &[[i32; 10]; 100], n: usize, source: usize) -> [i32; 100] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var visited = [false; 100]
    var result = [-1; 100]
    var result_len = 0

    // Manual stack for DFS
    var stack = [-1; 100]
    var stack_top = 0

    // Push source
    stack[stack_top] = source as i32
    stack_top = stack_top + 1

    while stack_top > 0 {
        // Pop from stack
        stack_top = stack_top - 1
        let node = stack[stack_top]
        let u = node as usize

        if !visited[u] {
            visited[u] = true
            result[result_len] = node
            result_len = result_len + 1

            // Push unvisited neighbors (in reverse order for proper DFS)
            var j = 0
            while j < 10 {
                if adj[u][j] >= 0 {
                    let neighbor = adj[u][j] as usize
                    if !visited[neighbor] {
                        stack[stack_top] = adj[u][j]
                        stack_top = stack_top + 1
                    }
                } else {
                    break
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
    }

    // Store length at index 0 (hack since we can't return dynamic size)
    var final_result = [-1; 100]
    final_result[0] = result_len as i32
    var k = 0
    while k < result_len {
        final_result[k + 1] = result[k]
        k = k + 1
    }

    return final_result
}

// Breadth-first search traversal
//
// Performs BFS starting from source node and returns nodes in visit order.
// Uses queue-based approach.
//
// Arguments:
// - adj: Adjacency list (adj[i] contains neighbors of node i, -1 terminated)
// - n: Number of nodes
// - source: Starting node
//
// Returns: Array of nodes in BFS visit order (length encoded at index 0)
pub fn bfs(adj: &[[i32; 10]; 100], n: usize, source: usize) -> [i32; 100] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var visited = [false; 100]
    var result = [-1; 100]
    var result_len = 0

    // Manual queue for BFS
    var queue = [-1; 100]
    var queue_head = 0
    var queue_tail = 0

    // Enqueue source
    queue[queue_tail] = source as i32
    queue_tail = queue_tail + 1
    visited[source] = true

    while queue_head < queue_tail {
        // Dequeue
        let node = queue[queue_head]
        queue_head = queue_head + 1
        let u = node as usize

        result[result_len] = node
        result_len = result_len + 1

        // Enqueue unvisited neighbors
        var j = 0
        while j < 10 {
            if adj[u][j] >= 0 {
                let neighbor = adj[u][j] as usize
                if !visited[neighbor] {
                    visited[neighbor] = true
                    queue[queue_tail] = adj[u][j]
                    queue_tail = queue_tail + 1
                }
            } else {
                break
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }

    // Store length at index 0
    var final_result = [-1; 100]
    final_result[0] = result_len as i32
    var k = 0
    while k < result_len {
        final_result[k + 1] = result[k]
        k = k + 1
    }

    return final_result
}

// State struct for topological sort DFS traversal
// Used to consolidate mutable state into a single parameter
struct TopoState {
    visited: [bool; 100],
    rec_stack: [bool; 100],
    result: [i32; 100],
    result_pos: usize,
    has_cycle: bool
}

// Helper for topological sort: recursive DFS
// Uses state struct to avoid 4+ mutable ref parameter limitation
fn topo_dfs_visit(
    adj: &[[i32; 10]; 100],
    node: usize,
    state: &!TopoState
) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if state.has_cycle {
        return
    }

    if state.rec_stack[node] {
        state.has_cycle = true
        return
    }

    if state.visited[node] {
        return
    }

    state.visited[node] = true
    state.rec_stack[node] = true

    // Visit all neighbors
    var j = 0
    while j < 10 {
        if adj[node][j] >= 0 {
            let neighbor = adj[node][j] as usize
            topo_dfs_visit(adj, neighbor, state)
        } else {
            break
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    state.rec_stack[node] = false

    // Add to result (reverse postorder)
    state.result_pos = state.result_pos - 1
    state.result[state.result_pos] = node as i32
}

// Topological sort
//
// Computes topological ordering of a directed acyclic graph (DAG).
// Returns array of nodes in topological order, or all -1s if cycle detected.
//
// Arguments:
// - adj: Adjacency list (adj[i] contains neighbors of node i, -1 terminated)
// - n: Number of nodes
//
// Returns: Array of nodes in topological order (length at index 0), or [-2, ...] if cycle
pub fn topological_sort(adj: &[[i32; 10]; 100], n: usize) -> [i32; 100] with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var state = TopoState {
        visited: [false; 100],
        rec_stack: [false; 100],
        result: [-1; 100],
        result_pos: n,
        has_cycle: false
    }

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if !state.visited[i] {
            topo_dfs_visit(adj, i, &!state)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if state.has_cycle {
        var cycle_result = [-2; 100]
        cycle_result[0] = -2  // Signal: cycle detected
        return cycle_result
    }

    // Shift result to start at index 1, put length at index 0
    var final_result = [-1; 100]
    final_result[0] = n as i32
    var k = 0
    while k < n {
        final_result[k + 1] = state.result[state.result_pos + k]
        k = k + 1
    }

    return final_result
}

// State struct for cycle detection DFS
struct CycleState {
    visited: [bool; 100],
    rec_stack: [bool; 100],
    has_cycle: bool
}

// Helper for cycle detection: DFS visit
fn cycle_dfs_visit(
    adj: &[[i32; 10]; 100],
    node: usize,
    state: &!CycleState
) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if state.has_cycle {
        return
    }

    if state.rec_stack[node] {
        state.has_cycle = true
        return
    }

    if state.visited[node] {
        return
    }

    state.visited[node] = true
    state.rec_stack[node] = true

    // Visit all neighbors
    var j = 0
    while j < 10 {
        if adj[node][j] >= 0 {
            let neighbor = adj[node][j] as usize
            cycle_dfs_visit(adj, neighbor, state)
        } else {
            break
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    state.rec_stack[node] = false
}

// Cycle detection
//
// Checks if the directed graph contains a cycle using DFS.
//
// Arguments:
// - adj: Adjacency list (adj[i] contains neighbors of node i, -1 terminated)
// - n: Number of nodes
//
// Returns: true if graph has a cycle, false otherwise
pub fn has_cycle(adj: &[[i32; 10]; 100], n: usize) -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var state = CycleState {
        visited: [false; 100],
        rec_stack: [false; 100],
        has_cycle: false
    }

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if !state.visited[i] {
            cycle_dfs_visit(adj, i, &!state)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return state.has_cycle
}

// Tests

fn test_bfs_simple() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // Graph: 0 -> 1 -> 2
    //        0 -> 3
    var adj = [[-1; 10]; 100]
    adj[0][0] = 1
    adj[0][1] = 3
    adj[1][0] = 2

    let result = bfs(&adj, 4, 0)
    let len = result[0]

    // Should visit: 0, 1, 3, 2 (BFS order)
    if len != 4 {
        return false
    }
    if result[1] != 0 {
        return false
    }
    if result[2] != 1 && result[2] != 3 {
        return false
    }

    return true
}

fn test_dfs_simple() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // Graph: 0 -> 1 -> 2
    //        0 -> 3
    var adj = [[-1; 10]; 100]
    adj[0][0] = 1
    adj[0][1] = 3
    adj[1][0] = 2

    let result = dfs(&adj, 4, 0)
    let len = result[0]

    // Should visit all 4 nodes
    if len != 4 {
        return false
    }
    if result[1] != 0 {
        return false
    }

    return true
}

fn test_dijkstra_simple() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // Graph: 0 --(1)-- 1 --(2)-- 2
    //        |                    |
    //       (4)                  (1)
    //        |                    |
    //        3 -------(1)--------
    var adj = [[-1.0; 100]; 100]

    // Initialize all to -1 (no edge)
    var i = 0
    while i < 100 {
        var j = 0
        while j < 100 {
            adj[i][j] = -1.0
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Add edges
    adj[0][1] = 1.0
    adj[0][3] = 4.0
    adj[1][2] = 2.0
    adj[2][3] = 1.0
    adj[3][2] = 1.0  // Also reverse

    let dist = dijkstra(&adj, 4, 0)

    // Shortest paths from 0:
    // 0 -> 0: 0
    // 0 -> 1: 1
    // 0 -> 2: 3 (via 0->1->2)
    // 0 -> 3: 4

    if dist[0] != 0.0 {
        return false
    }
    if dist[1] != 1.0 {
        return false
    }
    if dist[2] != 3.0 {
        return false
    }
    if dist[3] != 4.0 {
        return false
    }

    return true
}

fn test_topological_sort_simple() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // DAG: 0 -> 1 -> 3
    //      0 -> 2 -> 3
    var adj = [[-1; 10]; 100]
    adj[0][0] = 1
    adj[0][1] = 2
    adj[1][0] = 3
    adj[2][0] = 3

    let result = topological_sort(&adj, 4)
    let len = result[0]

    // Should not have cycle
    if len < 0 {
        return false
    }

    // Should have all 4 nodes
    if len != 4 {
        return false
    }

    // Node 0 should come before 1 and 2
    // Nodes 1 and 2 should come before 3
    var pos0 = 0
    var pos1 = 0
    var pos2 = 0
    var pos3 = 0

    let len_usize = len as usize
    var k = 1
    while k <= len_usize {
        if result[k] == 0 {
            pos0 = k
        }
        if result[k] == 1 {
            pos1 = k
        }
        if result[k] == 2 {
            pos2 = k
        }
        if result[k] == 3 {
            pos3 = k
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    if pos0 >= pos1 || pos0 >= pos2 {
        return false
    }
    if pos1 >= pos3 || pos2 >= pos3 {
        return false
    }

    return true
}

fn test_has_cycle_no_cycle() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // DAG: 0 -> 1 -> 2
    var adj = [[-1; 10]; 100]
    adj[0][0] = 1
    adj[1][0] = 2

    let result = has_cycle(&adj, 3)

    return !result  // Should NOT have cycle
}

fn test_has_cycle_with_cycle() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // Graph with cycle: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0
    var adj = [[-1; 10]; 100]
    adj[0][0] = 1
    adj[1][0] = 2
    adj[2][0] = 0  // Creates cycle

    let result = has_cycle(&adj, 3)

    return result  // Should have cycle
}

// Run all tests
pub fn graph_run_tests() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if !test_bfs_simple() {
        return false
    }
    if !test_dfs_simple() {
        return false
    }
    if !test_dijkstra_simple() {
        return false
    }
    if !test_topological_sort_simple() {
        return false
    }
    if !test_has_cycle_no_cycle() {
        return false
    }
    if !test_has_cycle_with_cycle() {
        return false
    }

    return true
}

//! stdlib/algo - Algorithms Module
//!
//! Classic algorithms for sorting, searching, and graph operations.
//!
//! # Submodules
//! - `sort` - Sorting algorithms (quicksort, mergesort, heapsort, radix)
//! - `graph` - Graph algorithms (Dijkstra, A*, DFS, topological sort)
//!
//! # Examples
//! ```sio
//! // Sorting
//! var arr = [5, 2, 8, 1, 9]
//! quicksort_i64(&!arr, 5)
//! // arr is now [1, 2, 5, 8, 9]
//!
//! // Graph shortest path
//! let result = dijkstra(&adj, 6, 0)
//! print("Distance to node 3: " ++ result.distances[3].to_string())
//! ```

pub mod sort;
pub mod graph;

// === FILE: stdlib/algo/sort.sio ===
// stdlib/algo/sort.sio — Sorting algorithms
//
// Pure Sounio implementations for fixed-size i64 and f64 arrays:
//   - Insertion sort: stable, O(n^2), good for small arrays
//   - Heapsort: in-place, O(n log n) worst-case
//   - Quicksort-style via heapsort (avoids ownership issues with recursive &! reborrow)
//
// All arrays are fixed-size [T; 1024]. Pass actual length as n parameter.

// =============================================================================
// i64 sorting
// =============================================================================

// Insertion sort for i64 arrays. Stable, O(n^2).
fn insertion_sort_i64(arr: &![i64; 1024], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let key = arr[i]
        var j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 && arr[j] > key {
            arr[j + 1] = arr[j]
            j = j - 1
        }
        arr[j + 1] = key
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Heapify subtree rooted at index root, heap size = size.
fn heapify_i64(arr: &![i64; 1024], size: i32, root: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var largest = root
    let left = 2 * root + 1
    let right = 2 * root + 2

    if left < size && arr[left] > arr[largest] {
        largest = left
    }
    if right < size && arr[right] > arr[largest] {
        largest = right
    }

    if largest != root {
        let temp = arr[root]
        arr[root] = arr[largest]
        arr[largest] = temp
        // Iterative sift-down to avoid recursive &! reborrow
        var pos = largest
        var done = false
        while !done {
            var big = pos
            let l = 2 * pos + 1
            let r = 2 * pos + 2
            if l < size && arr[l] > arr[big] { big = l }
            if r < size && arr[r] > arr[big] { big = r }
            if big != pos {
                let t = arr[pos]
                arr[pos] = arr[big]
                arr[big] = t
                pos = big
            } else {
                done = true
            }
        }
    }
}

// Heapsort for i64 arrays. In-place, O(n log n).
fn heapsort_i64(arr: &![i64; 1024], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 1 { return }

    // Build max heap
    var i = n / 2 - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        heapify_i64(arr, n, i)
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Extract elements
    var end = n - 1
    while end > 0 {
        let temp = arr[0]
        arr[0] = arr[end]
        arr[end] = temp
        heapify_i64(arr, end, 0)
        end = end - 1
    }
}

// Check if i64 array is sorted in ascending order.
fn is_sorted_i64(arr: &[i64; 1024], n: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 1 { return true }
    var i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

// =============================================================================
// f64 sorting
// =============================================================================

// Insertion sort for f64 arrays.
fn insertion_sort_f64(arr: &![f64; 1024], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let key = arr[i]
        var j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 && arr[j] > key {
            arr[j + 1] = arr[j]
            j = j - 1
        }
        arr[j + 1] = key
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Heapsort for f64 arrays.
fn heapsort_f64(arr: &![f64; 1024], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 1 { return }

    // Build max heap (iterative sift-down)
    var i = n / 2 - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        // Sift down arr[i]
        var pos = i
        var done = false
        while !done {
            var big = pos
            let l = 2 * pos + 1
            let r = 2 * pos + 2
            if l < n && arr[l] > arr[big] { big = l }
            if r < n && arr[r] > arr[big] { big = r }
            if big != pos {
                let t = arr[pos]
                arr[pos] = arr[big]
                arr[big] = t
                pos = big
            } else {
                done = true
            }
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Extract elements
    var end = n - 1
    while end > 0 {
        let temp = arr[0]
        arr[0] = arr[end]
        arr[end] = temp

        // Sift down arr[0] within heap of size end
        var pos = 0
        var done2 = false
        while !done2 {
            var big = pos
            let l = 2 * pos + 1
            let r = 2 * pos + 2
            if l < end && arr[l] > arr[big] { big = l }
            if r < end && arr[r] > arr[big] { big = r }
            if big != pos {
                let t = arr[pos]
                arr[pos] = arr[big]
                arr[big] = t
                pos = big
            } else {
                done2 = true
            }
        }
        end = end - 1
    }
}

// Check if f64 array is sorted in ascending order.
fn is_sorted_f64(arr: &[f64; 1024], n: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 1 { return true }
    var i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}


// === FILE: stdlib/analysis/complexity.sio ===
// Sprint 24 Track C: Complexity/Resource stdlib
// References: Hoffmann & Hofmann POPL 2010 (AARA)

fn bigO_flops_matmul(m: i64, k: i64, n: i64) -> i64 {
    // Matrix multiply: 2*m*k*n flops
    2 * m * k * n
}

fn amortized_stack_cost(n_ops: i64) -> i64 {
    // Total cost for n push ops on doubling stack: O(n) total (O(1) amortized each)
    // Geometric series sum: n + n/2 + n/4 + ... approx 2n
    2 * n_ops
}

fn binary_search_steps(n: i64) -> i64 {
    // Ceil(log2(n)) steps for binary search on n elements
    var steps: i64 = 0
    var size: i64 = n
    while size > 1 {
        size = size / 2
        steps = steps + 1
    }
    steps
}

fn bigO_compose_degree(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    // O(n^a) composed with O(n^b) = O(n^(a*b)), capped at 6
    if a == -1 || b == -1 { return -1 }
    let deg: i64 = a * b
    if deg > 6 { 6 } else { deg }
}

fn complexity_class_name(cls: i64) -> i64 {
    // Returns complexity class tag (0=P, 1=NC, 2=PSPACE, -1=unknown)
    cls
}


// === FILE: stdlib/async/advanced.sio ===
// async/advanced.sio — Cooperative scheduling primitives for advanced
// Sounio async model: cooperative, fixed-size, no heap

struct AsyncAdvancedState {
    ready: bool,
    value: i64,
    tag: i64,
}

fn async_advanced_state_new() -> AsyncAdvancedState {
    AsyncAdvancedState { ready: false, value: 0, tag: 0 }
}

fn async_advanced_is_ready(s: AsyncAdvancedState) -> bool {
    s.ready
}

fn async_advanced_complete(s: AsyncAdvancedState, val: i64) -> AsyncAdvancedState {
    AsyncAdvancedState { ready: true, value: val, tag: s.tag }
}

fn async_advanced_get_value(s: AsyncAdvancedState) -> i64 {
    s.value
}

struct AdvancedRingBuffer {
    data: [i64; 64],
    head: i32,
    tail: i32,
    count: i32,
}

fn advanced_ring_new() -> AdvancedRingBuffer {
    AdvancedRingBuffer { data: [0; 64], head: 0, tail: 0, count: 0 }
}

fn advanced_ring_push(rb: AdvancedRingBuffer, val: i64) -> AdvancedRingBuffer with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if rb.count >= 64 { return rb }
    var result = rb
    result.data[result.tail] = val
    result.tail = (result.tail + 1) % 64
    result.count = result.count + 1
    result
}

fn advanced_ring_pop(rb: AdvancedRingBuffer) -> AdvancedRingBuffer with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if rb.count <= 0 { return rb }
    var result = rb
    result.head = (result.head + 1) % 64
    result.count = result.count - 1
    result
}

fn advanced_ring_peek(rb: AdvancedRingBuffer) -> i64 {
    if rb.count <= 0 { return 0 }
    rb.data[rb.head]
}

fn advanced_ring_is_empty(rb: AdvancedRingBuffer) -> bool {
    rb.count <= 0
}

fn test_advanced_ring_basic() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var rb = advanced_ring_new()
    rb = advanced_ring_push(rb, 42)

// === FILE: stdlib/async/executor.sio ===
// stdlib/async/executor — Simple cooperative task executor
//
// Executor: runs tasks from a queue in round-robin order.

struct Executor {
    task_ids: [i64; 256],
    task_status: [i64; 256],
    task_result: [i64; 256],
    count: i64,
    completed: i64,
}

let EXEC_PENDING: i64 = 0
let EXEC_COMPLETED: i64 = 2

impl Executor {
    fn new() -> Executor {
        Executor {
            task_ids: [0; 256],
            task_status: [0; 256],
            task_result: [0; 256],
            count: 0,
            completed: 0,
        }
    }

    fn spawn(self: &! Executor, task_id: i64) {
        if self.count >= 256 { return }
        let i = self.count
        self.task_ids[i] = task_id
        self.task_status[i] = EXEC_PENDING
        self.task_result[i] = 0
        self.count = self.count + 1
    }

    fn complete_task(self: &! Executor, idx: i64, result: i64) {
        if idx >= 0 && idx < self.count {
            self.task_status[idx] = EXEC_COMPLETED
            self.task_result[idx] = result
            self.completed = self.completed + 1
        }
    }

    fn all_done(self: &Executor) -> bool {
        self.completed >= self.count
    }

    fn pending_count(self: &Executor) -> i64 {
        self.count - self.completed
    }

    fn task_count(self: &Executor) -> i64 {
        self.count
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/async/future.sio ===
// stdlib/async/future — Poll result and future state
//
// PollResult: represents the state of an async computation.
// tag 0 = Pending, 1 = Ready with value.

struct PollResult {
    tag: i64,
    val: i64,
}

fn poll_pending() -> PollResult {
    PollResult { tag: 0, val: 0 }
}

fn poll_ready(v: i64) -> PollResult {
    PollResult { tag: 1, val: v }
}

fn poll_is_ready(p: &PollResult) -> bool {
    p.tag == 1
}

fn poll_is_pending(p: &PollResult) -> bool {
    p.tag == 0
}

fn poll_value(p: &PollResult) -> i64 {
    p.val
}

// === FILE: stdlib/async/task.sio ===
// stdlib/async/task — Async task representation
//
// Task: a unit of async work with status tracking.
// TaskQueue: fixed-capacity queue of tasks.

let TASK_PENDING: i64 = 0
let TASK_RUNNING: i64 = 1
let TASK_COMPLETED: i64 = 2
let TASK_CANCELLED: i64 = 3

struct Task {
    id: i64,
    status: i64,
    result: i64,
    priority: i64,
}

fn task_new(id: i64) -> Task {
    Task { id: id, status: TASK_PENDING, result: 0, priority: 0 }
}

fn task_with_priority(id: i64, priority: i64) -> Task {
    Task { id: id, status: TASK_PENDING, result: 0, priority: priority }
}

impl Task {
    fn is_pending(self: &Task) -> bool { self.status == TASK_PENDING }
    fn is_running(self: &Task) -> bool { self.status == TASK_RUNNING }
    fn is_completed(self: &Task) -> bool { self.status == TASK_COMPLETED }
    fn is_cancelled(self: &Task) -> bool { self.status == TASK_CANCELLED }
}

let TASK_QUEUE_CAP: i64 = 256

struct TaskQueue {
    tasks_id: [i64; 256],
    tasks_status: [i64; 256],
    tasks_result: [i64; 256],
    tasks_priority: [i64; 256],
    count: i64,
}

impl TaskQueue {
    fn new() -> TaskQueue {
        TaskQueue {
            tasks_id: [0; 256],
            tasks_status: [0; 256],
            tasks_result: [0; 256],
            tasks_priority: [0; 256],
            count: 0,
        }
    }

    fn len(self: &TaskQueue) -> i64 { self.count }
    fn is_empty(self: &TaskQueue) -> bool { self.count == 0 }

    fn push(self: &! TaskQueue, t: Task) {
        if self.count >= TASK_QUEUE_CAP { return }
        let i = self.count
        self.tasks_id[i] = t.id
        self.tasks_status[i] = t.status
        self.tasks_result[i] = t.result
        self.tasks_priority[i] = t.priority
        self.count = self.count + 1
    }

    fn get_status(self: &TaskQueue, idx: i64) -> i64 {
        if idx < 0 || idx >= self.count { return 0 - 1 }
        self.tasks_status[idx]
    }

    fn set_status(self: &! TaskQueue, idx: i64, status: i64) {
        if idx >= 0 && idx < self.count {
            self.tasks_status[idx] = status
        }
    }

    fn set_result(self: &! TaskQueue, idx: i64, result: i64) {
        if idx >= 0 && idx < self.count {
            self.tasks_result[idx] = result
        }
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/autodiff/activity.sio ===
// stdlib/autodiff/activity.sio — Activity Analysis for Automatic Differentiation
//
// Marks variables as Active/Inactive to skip unnecessary gradient computation.
// Active variables contribute to the loss; inactive ones are constants w.r.t.
// differentiation. Skipping inactive variables yields 1.24x CPU, 1.7x GPU speedup.
//
// SOTA: Peng, Moses et al. (OOPSLA 2025):
//       "Sound and Modular Activity Analysis for AD in MLIR"
//       — Formalizes activity analysis as abstract interpretation
//       — Function summaries enable modular/separate compilation
//
// Theory:
//   A variable v is ACTIVE if it lies on a data-flow path from an
//   independent (input) to a dependent (output) variable. Otherwise inactive.
//
//   Activity propagation rules:
//     Active + Active   = Active
//     Active + Inactive = Active
//     Active * Inactive = Active   (if the active part is non-zero)
//     Inactive * Inactive = Inactive
//     f(Active) = Active            (for any differentiable f)
//     f(Inactive) = Inactive

// =============================================================================
// Activity Label
// =============================================================================

enum Activity {
    Active,      // contributes to gradient
    Inactive,    // constant w.r.t. differentiation — skip gradient
}

fn activity_is_active(a: Activity) -> bool {
    match a {
        Activity::Active => true,
        Activity::Inactive => false,
    }
}

// Activity join (lattice meet): Active wins
fn activity_join(a: Activity, b: Activity) -> Activity {
    match a {
        Activity::Active => Activity::Active,
        Activity::Inactive => b,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Activity-Aware Dual Number
// =============================================================================

// A dual number augmented with activity status.
// When activity is Inactive, gradient computation is skipped entirely.
struct ADual {
    val: f64,
    dot: f64,
    activity: Activity,
}

// Constructors
fn adual_active(val: f64, dot: f64) -> ADual {
    ADual { val: val, dot: dot, activity: Activity::Active }
}

fn adual_inactive(val: f64) -> ADual {
    ADual { val: val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive }
}

fn adual_const(val: f64) -> ADual {
    ADual { val: val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive }
}

fn adual_var(val: f64) -> ADual {
    ADual { val: val, dot: 1.0, activity: Activity::Active }
}

// =============================================================================
// Activity-Aware Arithmetic
// =============================================================================

// Addition: skip if both inactive
fn adual_add(a: ADual, b: ADual) -> ADual {
    let act = activity_join(a.activity, b.activity)
    match act {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: a.val + b.val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: a.val + b.val, dot: a.dot + b.dot, activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// Subtraction
fn adual_sub(a: ADual, b: ADual) -> ADual {
    let act = activity_join(a.activity, b.activity)
    match act {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: a.val - b.val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: a.val - b.val, dot: a.dot - b.dot, activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// Multiplication: product rule, but skip if both inactive
fn adual_mul(a: ADual, b: ADual) -> ADual {
    match (a.activity, b.activity) {
        (Activity::Inactive, Activity::Inactive) =>
            ADual { val: a.val * b.val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        _ => ADual {
            val: a.val * b.val,
            dot: a.dot * b.val + a.val * b.dot,
            activity: Activity::Active,
        },
    }
}

// Division: quotient rule, skip if both inactive
fn adual_div(a: ADual, b: ADual) -> ADual with Panic {
    match (a.activity, b.activity) {
        (Activity::Inactive, Activity::Inactive) =>
            ADual { val: a.val / b.val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        _ => {
            let b2 = b.val * b.val
            ADual {
                val: a.val / b.val,
                dot: (a.dot * b.val - a.val * b.dot) / b2,
                activity: Activity::Active,
            }
        },
    }
}

// Negation
fn adual_neg(a: ADual) -> ADual {
    match a.activity {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: 0.0 - a.val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: 0.0 - a.val, dot: 0.0 - a.dot, activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// Scale by constant
fn adual_scale(a: ADual, c: f64) -> ADual {
    match a.activity {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: c * a.val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: c * a.val, dot: c * a.dot, activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Activity-Aware Transcendentals
// =============================================================================

// exp(a): skip gradient if inactive
fn adual_exp(a: ADual) -> ADual with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.val > 500.0 { return ADual { val: 1.0e200, dot: 0.0, activity: a.activity } }
    if a.val < -500.0 { return ADual { val: 0.0, dot: 0.0, activity: a.activity } }

    // Inline exp
    let ln2_val = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = a.val / ln2_val
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = a.val - (k as f64) * ln2_val
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 { var i = 0; while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    else { var i = 0; while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 } }

    match a.activity {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: result, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: result, dot: result * a.dot, activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// ln(a)
fn adual_ln(a: ADual) -> ADual with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.val <= 0.0 { return ADual { val: 0.0 - 1.0e30, dot: 0.0, activity: a.activity } }

    var m = a.val
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sm = t
    var tm = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { tm = tm * t2; sm = sm + tm / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    let ln_val = 2.0 * sm + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453

    match a.activity {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: ln_val, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: ln_val, dot: a.dot / a.val, activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// sqrt(a)
fn adual_sqrt(a: ADual) -> ADual with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.val <= 0.0 { return ADual { val: 0.0, dot: 0.0, activity: a.activity } }
    var y = a.val
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + a.val / y); i = i + 1 }

    match a.activity {
        Activity::Inactive => ADual { val: y, dot: 0.0, activity: Activity::Inactive },
        Activity::Active => ADual { val: y, dot: a.dot / (2.0 * y), activity: Activity::Active },
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Function Summary — Modular Activity Analysis
// =============================================================================
// SOTA: Function summaries from OOPSLA 2025 paper
// A summary records: which inputs are active → which outputs are active
// This enables modular/separate compilation of differentiable modules.

struct ActivitySummary {
    n_inputs: i32,
    n_outputs: i32,
    // Flattened dependency matrix: output[i] depends on input[j]
    // If depends[i * n_inputs + j] == 1, then input j's activity
    // propagates to output i
    depends: [i32; 256],    // max 16 inputs x 16 outputs
}

fn summary_new(n_in: i32, n_out: i32) -> ActivitySummary {
    ActivitySummary {
        n_inputs: n_in,
        n_outputs: n_out,
        depends: [0; 256],
    }
}

fn summary_set_dep(s: &!ActivitySummary, output: i32, input: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    s.depends[output * s.n_inputs + input] = 1
}

// Query: is output active given input activities?
fn summary_output_activity(
    s: &ActivitySummary,
    output: i32,
    input_activities: &[i32; 16],
) -> Activity with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var j = 0
    while j < s.n_inputs {
        if s.depends[output * s.n_inputs + j] == 1 {
            if input_activities[j] == 1 {
                return Activity::Active
            }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    Activity::Inactive
}

// =============================================================================
// Utility
// =============================================================================

fn adual_value(a: &ADual) -> f64 { a.val }
fn adual_gradient(a: &ADual) -> f64 { a.dot }
fn adual_is_active(a: &ADual) -> bool { activity_is_active(a.activity) }


// === FILE: stdlib/autodiff/differentiable.sio ===
// Sprint 24 Track A: Differentiable Programming stdlib
// References: Elliott ICFP 2018, Huot et al. LICS 2020

fn smooth_composition_class(k1: i64, k2: i64) -> i64 {
    // Chain rule: C^k1 composed with C^k2 = C^min(k1, k2)
    if k1 == -1 && k2 == -1 { return -1 }
    if k1 == -1 { return k2 }
    if k2 == -1 { return k1 }
    if k1 < k2 { k1 } else { k2 }
}

fn jacobian_fwd_passes(n: i64) -> i64 {
    // Forward-mode: n JVPs for full Jacobian of f: R^n -> R^m
    n
}

fn langevin_step(x: f64, grad_f: f64, eta: f64, temp: f64, noise: f64) -> f64 {
    // Langevin MCMC step: x_{t+1} = x_t - eta*grad_f(x_t) + sqrt(2*eta*T) * noise
    let step_size: f64 = eta * grad_f
    let diffusion_coeff: f64 = 2.0 * eta * temp
    x - step_size + noise * diffusion_coeff
}

fn sgd_as_langevin_sigma(learning_rate: f64, temperature: f64) -> f64 {
    // Diffusion coefficient for Langevin: sigma^2 = 2 * lr * T
    2.0 * learning_rate * temperature
}


// === FILE: stdlib/autodiff/dual.sio ===
// dual.d - Forward-Mode Automatic Differentiation using Dual Numbers
//
// Dual numbers extend real numbers with an infinitesimal ε where ε² = 0.
// A dual number is: a + bε, where a is the value and b is the derivative.
//
// For any analytic function f:
//   f(a + bε) = f(a) + b*f'(a)*ε
//
// This enables automatic computation of derivatives by propagating through
// arithmetic operations. Perfect for functions with few inputs.
//
// Reference: "Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey"
//            Baydin et al., JMLR 2018

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// Exponential via Taylor series (15 terms)
fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Handle large values by range reduction: exp(x) = exp(x/n)^n
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }

    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 11.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 12.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 13.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 14.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 15.0
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

// Natural log via Halley's method with range reduction
fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }  // -inf approximation

    // Range reduction: ln(x) = ln(x/e^k) + k for appropriate k
    var val = x
    var k = 0.0
    let e = 2.718281828459045

    // Reduce to [1/e, e] range
    while val > e {
        val = val / e
        k = k + 1.0
    }
    while val < 1.0 / e {
        val = val * e
        k = k - 1.0
    }

    // Now use series: ln(1+u) = u - u²/2 + u³/3 - u⁴/4 + ...
    // where u = (val - 1) / (val + 1), so ln(val) = 2 * artanh(u)
    // artanh(u) = u + u³/3 + u⁵/5 + u⁷/7 + ...
    let u = (val - 1.0) / (val + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var sum = u
    var term = u
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 3.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 5.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 7.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 9.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 11.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 13.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 15.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 17.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 19.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 21.0

    return 2.0 * sum + k
}

// Power function: x^n using exp/ln
fn pow_f64(x: f64, n: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return exp_f64(n * ln_f64(x))
}

// Sine via Taylor series
fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Reduce to [-π, π]
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }

    // Taylor: sin(x) = x - x³/3! + x⁵/5! - x⁷/7! + ...
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = y
    var term = y
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (2.0 * 3.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (4.0 * 5.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (6.0 * 7.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (8.0 * 9.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (10.0 * 11.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (12.0 * 13.0)
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

// Cosine via Taylor series
fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }

    // Taylor: cos(x) = 1 - x²/2! + x⁴/4! - x⁶/6! + ...
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (1.0 * 2.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (3.0 * 4.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (5.0 * 6.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (7.0 * 8.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (9.0 * 10.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (11.0 * 12.0)
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn tanh_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2x = exp_f64(2.0 * x)
    return (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
}

fn signum_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0 }
    return 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL NUMBER TYPE
// ============================================================================
// Dual number: val + dot*ε where ε² = 0
// val is the primal (function value)
// dot is the tangent (derivative)

struct Dual {
    val: f64,  // Primal value
    dot: f64   // Tangent (derivative)
}

// Create a constant (derivative = 0)
fn dual_const(val: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: 0.0 }
}

// Create a variable (derivative = 1)
fn dual_var(val: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: 1.0 }
}

// Create with explicit derivative
fn dual_new(val: f64, dot: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: val, dot: dot }
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dual_add(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val + b.val, dot: a.dot + b.dot }
}

fn dual_sub(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val - b.val, dot: a.dot - b.dot }
}

fn dual_mul(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    // Product rule: (f*g)' = f'*g + f*g'
    return Dual {
        val: a.val * b.val,
        dot: a.dot * b.val + a.val * b.dot
    }
}

fn dual_div(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    // Quotient rule: (f/g)' = (f'*g - f*g') / g²
    let g2 = b.val * b.val
    return Dual {
        val: a.val / b.val,
        dot: (a.dot * b.val - a.val * b.dot) / g2
    }
}

fn dual_neg(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: 0.0 - a.val, dot: 0.0 - a.dot }
}

// Scale by constant
fn dual_scale(a: Dual, s: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val * s, dot: a.dot * s }
}

// Add constant
fn dual_add_const(a: Dual, c: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { val: a.val + c, dot: a.dot }
}

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dual_sqrt(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx sqrt(x) = 1/(2*sqrt(x))
    let v = sqrt_f64(a.val)
    return Dual { val: v, dot: a.dot / (2.0 * v) }
}

fn dual_exp(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx exp(x) = exp(x)
    let e = exp_f64(a.val)
    return Dual { val: e, dot: a.dot * e }
}

fn dual_ln(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx ln(x) = 1/x
    return Dual { val: ln_f64(a.val), dot: a.dot / a.val }
}

fn dual_pow(a: Dual, n: f64) -> Dual {
    // d/dx x^n = n * x^(n-1)
    let v = pow_f64(a.val, n)
    return Dual { val: v, dot: a.dot * n * pow_f64(a.val, n - 1.0) }
}

fn dual_sin(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx sin(x) = cos(x)
    return Dual { val: sin_f64(a.val), dot: a.dot * cos_f64(a.val) }
}

fn dual_cos(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx cos(x) = -sin(x)
    return Dual { val: cos_f64(a.val), dot: 0.0 - a.dot * sin_f64(a.val) }
}

fn dual_tan(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx tan(x) = sec²(x) = 1/cos²(x)
    let c = cos_f64(a.val)
    return Dual { val: sin_f64(a.val) / c, dot: a.dot / (c * c) }
}

fn dual_tanh(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx tanh(x) = 1 - tanh²(x)
    let t = tanh_f64(a.val)
    return Dual { val: t, dot: a.dot * (1.0 - t * t) }
}

fn dual_sigmoid(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // sigmoid(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
    // d/dx sigmoid(x) = sigmoid(x) * (1 - sigmoid(x))
    let s = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - a.val))
    return Dual { val: s, dot: a.dot * s * (1.0 - s) }
}

fn dual_relu(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // ReLU(x) = max(0, x)
    // d/dx ReLU(x) = 1 if x > 0, else 0
    if a.val > 0.0 {
        return Dual { val: a.val, dot: a.dot }
    }
    return Dual { val: 0.0, dot: 0.0 }
}

fn dual_abs(a: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx |x| = sign(x)
    return Dual { val: abs_f64(a.val), dot: a.dot * signum_f64(a.val) }
}

fn dual_max(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    if a.val >= b.val {
        return a
    }
    return b
}

fn dual_min(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    if a.val <= b.val {
        return a
    }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL VECTOR (for multi-variable functions)
// ============================================================================

struct DualVec3 {
    x: Dual,
    y: Dual,
    z: Dual
}

fn dualvec3_new(x: Dual, y: Dual, z: Dual) -> DualVec3 {
    return DualVec3 { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn dualvec3_const(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> DualVec3 {
    return DualVec3 {
        x: dual_const(x),
        y: dual_const(y),
        z: dual_const(z)
    }
}

// Create with i-th component as the variable (for gradient computation)
fn dualvec3_var_i(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, i: i64) -> DualVec3 {
    if i == 0 {
        return DualVec3 { x: dual_var(x), y: dual_const(y), z: dual_const(z) }
    }
    if i == 1 {
        return DualVec3 { x: dual_const(x), y: dual_var(y), z: dual_const(z) }
    }
    return DualVec3 { x: dual_const(x), y: dual_const(y), z: dual_var(z) }
}

fn dualvec3_add(a: DualVec3, b: DualVec3) -> DualVec3 {
    return DualVec3 {
        x: dual_add(a.x, b.x),
        y: dual_add(a.y, b.y),
        z: dual_add(a.z, b.z)
    }
}

fn dualvec3_scale(v: DualVec3, s: Dual) -> DualVec3 {
    return DualVec3 {
        x: dual_mul(v.x, s),
        y: dual_mul(v.y, s),
        z: dual_mul(v.z, s)
    }
}

fn dualvec3_dot(a: DualVec3, b: DualVec3) -> Dual {
    return dual_add(dual_add(dual_mul(a.x, b.x), dual_mul(a.y, b.y)), dual_mul(a.z, b.z))
}

fn dualvec3_norm(v: DualVec3) -> Dual {
    return dual_sqrt(dualvec3_dot(v, v))
}

// === FILE: stdlib/autodiff/epistemic_bridge.sio ===
// stdlib/autodiff/epistemic_bridge — Bridge between EpistemicDual and GUM uncertainty
//
// Connects forward-mode AD uncertainty tracking (EpistemicDual) with the
// GUM measurement uncertainty framework (GUMUncertainty, GUMResult).
//
// Math foundation: GUM §5.1 Law of Propagation of Uncertainty
// u(y) = |∂f/∂x| · u(x)  for y = f(x)
//
// References:
// - JCGM 100:2008 (GUM), §5.1
// - Griewank & Walther, "Evaluating Derivatives" (2008)
// - Taylor, "An Introduction to Error Analysis" (1997)

use epistemic::gum::{GUMUncertainty, GUMResult, k_normal_95}
use autodiff::epistemic_dual::EpistemicDual

// =============================================================================
// Local math helpers (no stdlib import needed)
// =============================================================================

fn bridge_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn bridge_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// =============================================================================
// Bridge Functions
// =============================================================================

/// Convert an EpistemicDual (after a forward AD pass) to a GUMUncertainty.
/// The output uncertainty is |dot| * unc via the chain rule (GUM §5.1).
///
/// Math: u(y) = |∂f/∂x| · u(x) = |dot| · unc
/// The sensitivity coefficient is set to dot (the computed derivative).
pub fn edual_to_gum_uncertainty(d: EpistemicDual) -> GUMUncertainty {
    let std_unc = bridge_abs(d.dot) * d.unc
    GUMUncertainty {
        std_uncertainty: std_unc,
        degrees_of_freedom: 1.0e9,
        sensitivity: d.dot,
    }
}

/// Convert a GUMUncertainty to an EpistemicDual for use as an AD input.
/// Value is provided externally; dot = sensitivity; unc = std_uncertainty.
///
/// This allows a GUM-characterised input to seed a forward AD computation.
pub fn gum_to_edual(val: f64, u: GUMUncertainty) -> EpistemicDual {
    EpistemicDual {
        val: val,
        dot: u.sensitivity,
        unc: u.std_uncertainty,
        unc_dot: 0.0,
    }
}

/// Convert a GUMResult to an EpistemicDual.
/// dot is set to 1.0 (neutral sensitivity); unc = std_uncertainty.
pub fn gum_result_to_edual(r: GUMResult) -> EpistemicDual {
    EpistemicDual {
        val: r.value,
        dot: 1.0,
        unc: r.std_uncertainty,
        unc_dot: 0.0,
    }
}

/// Convert an EpistemicDual (output of AD computation) to a GUMResult.
/// Applies GUM §5.1: u(y) = |dot| * unc.
/// dof: degrees of freedom (use 1e9 for Type B / infinite).
pub fn edual_to_gum_result(d: EpistemicDual, dof: f64) -> GUMResult with Div, Panic {
    let std_unc = bridge_abs(d.dot) * d.unc
    let k = k_normal_95()
    GUMResult {
        value: d.val,
        std_uncertainty: std_unc,
        degrees_of_freedom: dof,
        coverage_factor_95: k,
        expanded_uncertainty_95: k * std_unc,
    }
}

/// Compose two independent GUM propagation steps through an AD computation.
/// u_combined = sqrt(u1^2 + u2^2) when inputs are independent (GUM §5.1.2).
///
/// Each dual carries: output_unc_i = |dot_i| * unc_i
/// Combined: u_c = sqrt(sum of (|dot_i| * unc_i)^2)
pub fn edual_combine_gum(d1: EpistemicDual, d2: EpistemicDual) -> GUMUncertainty with Div, Panic {
    let u1 = bridge_abs(d1.dot) * d1.unc
    let u2 = bridge_abs(d2.dot) * d2.unc
    let combined = bridge_sqrt(u1 * u1 + u2 * u2)
    // Effective sensitivity: magnitude of combined gradient direction
    let sens = bridge_sqrt(d1.dot * d1.dot + d2.dot * d2.dot)
    GUMUncertainty {
        std_uncertainty: combined,
        degrees_of_freedom: 1.0e9,
        sensitivity: sens,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/autodiff/epistemic_dual.sio ===
// epistemic_dual.d - Uncertainty-Aware Automatic Differentiation
//
// Extends dual numbers with epistemic uncertainty tracking.
// Each value carries:
//   - val: primal value f(x)
//   - dot: tangent (derivative) f'(x)
//   - unc: epistemic uncertainty in value
//   - unc_dot: uncertainty in derivative
//
// This enables:
//   1. Automatic derivative computation (standard AD)
//   2. Uncertainty propagation through computations
//   3. Sensitivity analysis (how uncertainty affects derivatives)
//   4. Confidence tracking for scientific computing
//
// Mathematical Foundation:
//   If x = x₀ ± σₓ (value with uncertainty), then:
//   f(x) ≈ f(x₀) ± |f'(x₀)| * σₓ  (linear error propagation)
//   f'(x) ≈ f'(x₀) ± |f''(x₀)| * σₓ  (derivative uncertainty)
//
// Reference: "Error Analysis" by J.R. Taylor
//            "Automatic Differentiation of Algorithms" by Griewank & Walther

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS (from dual.d)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 11.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 12.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 13.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 14.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 15.0
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    var val = x
    var k = 0.0
    let e = 2.718281828459045
    while val > e { val = val / e; k = k + 1.0 }
    while val < 1.0 / e { val = val * e; k = k - 1.0 }
    let u = (val - 1.0) / (val + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var sum = u
    var term = u
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 3.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 5.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 7.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 9.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 11.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 13.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 15.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 17.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 19.0
    return 2.0 * sum + k
}

fn pow_f64(x: f64, n: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return exp_f64(n * ln_f64(x))
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = y
    var term = y
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (2.0 * 3.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (4.0 * 5.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (6.0 * 7.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (8.0 * 9.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (10.0 * 11.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (12.0 * 13.0); sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (1.0 * 2.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (3.0 * 4.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (5.0 * 6.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (7.0 * 8.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (9.0 * 10.0); sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (11.0 * 12.0); sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn tanh_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2x = exp_f64(2.0 * x)
    return (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC DUAL NUMBER TYPE
// ============================================================================
// Epistemic dual: (val, dot, unc, unc_dot)
// - val: primal value f(x)
// - dot: tangent f'(x)
// - unc: uncertainty in value σ_f
// - unc_dot: uncertainty in derivative σ_{f'}

struct EpistemicDual {
    val: f64,      // Primal value
    dot: f64,      // Derivative (tangent)
    unc: f64,      // Uncertainty in value (standard deviation)
    unc_dot: f64   // Uncertainty in derivative
}

// Create a constant (no uncertainty, no derivative)
fn edual_const(val: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: 0.0, unc: 0.0, unc_dot: 0.0 }
}

// Create a variable with derivative=1, no uncertainty
fn edual_var(val: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: 1.0, unc: 0.0, unc_dot: 0.0 }
}

// Create a variable with uncertainty (derivative=1)
fn edual_var_uncertain(val: f64, uncertainty: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: 1.0, unc: uncertainty, unc_dot: 0.0 }
}

// Create from measurement with relative uncertainty
fn edual_measurement(val: f64, rel_unc: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: 1.0, unc: abs_f64(val) * rel_unc, unc_dot: 0.0 }
}

// Full constructor
fn edual_new(val: f64, dot: f64, unc: f64, unc_dot: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

// ============================================================================
// UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

// Combine independent uncertainties: σ_combined = sqrt(σ₁² + σ₂²)
fn combine_unc(u1: f64, u2: f64) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(u1 * u1 + u2 * u2)
}

// Combine with correlation: σ = sqrt(σ₁² + σ₂² + 2ρσ₁σ₂)
fn combine_unc_corr(u1: f64, u2: f64, rho: f64) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(u1*u1 + u2*u2 + 2.0*rho*u1*u2)
}

// Relative uncertainty
fn relative_unc(ed: EpistemicDual) -> f64 {
    if abs_f64(ed.val) < 0.000000000000001 { return 0.0 }
    return ed.unc / abs_f64(ed.val)
}

// Confidence (inverse of relative uncertainty, capped at 1.0)
fn confidence(ed: EpistemicDual) -> f64 {
    let rel = relative_unc(ed)
    if rel < 0.000000000000001 { return 1.0 }
    let c = 1.0 / (1.0 + rel)
    if c > 1.0 { return 1.0 }
    return c
}

// ============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC OPERATIONS WITH UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

fn edual_add(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = a + b
    // f' = a' + b'
    // σ_f = sqrt(σ_a² + σ_b²)  (assuming independence)
    // σ_{f'} = sqrt(σ_{a'}² + σ_{b'}²)
    return EpistemicDual {
        val: a.val + b.val,
        dot: a.dot + b.dot,
        unc: combine_unc(a.unc, b.unc),
        unc_dot: combine_unc(a.unc_dot, b.unc_dot)
    }
}

fn edual_sub(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // Same uncertainty propagation as addition
    return EpistemicDual {
        val: a.val - b.val,
        dot: a.dot - b.dot,
        unc: combine_unc(a.unc, b.unc),
        unc_dot: combine_unc(a.unc_dot, b.unc_dot)
    }
}

fn edual_mul(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = a * b
    // f' = a'*b + a*b'  (product rule)
    // σ_f = |f| * sqrt((σ_a/a)² + (σ_b/b)²)  (relative uncertainties add)
    // σ_{f'} = sqrt((b*σ_{a'})² + (a*σ_{b'})² + (a'*σ_b)² + (b'*σ_a)²)

    let val = a.val * b.val
    let dot = a.dot * b.val + a.val * b.dot

    // Value uncertainty (linear approximation)
    let unc_a_contrib = abs_f64(b.val) * a.unc
    let unc_b_contrib = abs_f64(a.val) * b.unc
    let unc = combine_unc(unc_a_contrib, unc_b_contrib)

    // Derivative uncertainty (all four terms)
    let ud1 = abs_f64(b.val) * a.unc_dot
    let ud2 = abs_f64(a.val) * b.unc_dot
    let ud3 = abs_f64(a.dot) * b.unc
    let ud4 = abs_f64(b.dot) * a.unc
    let unc_dot = sqrt_f64(ud1*ud1 + ud2*ud2 + ud3*ud3 + ud4*ud4)

    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_div(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = a / b
    // f' = (a'*b - a*b') / b²  (quotient rule)
    // σ_f = |f| * sqrt((σ_a/a)² + (σ_b/b)²)

    let b2 = b.val * b.val
    let val = a.val / b.val
    let dot = (a.dot * b.val - a.val * b.dot) / b2

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc_a_contrib = a.unc / abs_f64(b.val)
    let unc_b_contrib = abs_f64(a.val) * b.unc / b2
    let unc = combine_unc(unc_a_contrib, unc_b_contrib)

    // Derivative uncertainty (more complex for quotient)
    let ud1 = a.unc_dot / abs_f64(b.val)
    let ud2 = abs_f64(a.val) * b.unc_dot / b2
    let ud3 = abs_f64(a.dot) * b.unc / b2
    let ud4 = abs_f64(b.dot) * a.unc / b2
    let ud5 = 2.0 * abs_f64(dot) * b.unc / abs_f64(b.val)  // Second order
    let unc_dot = sqrt_f64(ud1*ud1 + ud2*ud2 + ud3*ud3 + ud4*ud4 + ud5*ud5)

    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_neg(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    return EpistemicDual {
        val: 0.0 - a.val,
        dot: 0.0 - a.dot,
        unc: a.unc,        // Uncertainty unchanged by negation
        unc_dot: a.unc_dot
    }
}

fn edual_scale(a: EpistemicDual, s: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = s * a (s is exact constant)
    // f' = s * a'
    // σ_f = |s| * σ_a
    return EpistemicDual {
        val: a.val * s,
        dot: a.dot * s,
        unc: abs_f64(s) * a.unc,
        unc_dot: abs_f64(s) * a.unc_dot
    }
}

fn edual_add_const(a: EpistemicDual, c: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    // Adding constant doesn't change uncertainty
    return EpistemicDual {
        val: a.val + c,
        dot: a.dot,
        unc: a.unc,
        unc_dot: a.unc_dot
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL FUNCTIONS WITH UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

fn edual_sqrt(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = sqrt(a)
    // f' = a' / (2*sqrt(a))
    // f'' = -a' / (4*a^(3/2)) + a'' / (2*sqrt(a))
    // σ_f = |f'| * σ_a = σ_a / (2*sqrt(a))

    let v = sqrt_f64(a.val)
    let two_v = 2.0 * v
    let dot = a.dot / two_v

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = a.unc / two_v

    // Derivative uncertainty: includes σ_a contribution to f'
    let unc_dot_1 = a.unc_dot / two_v
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot) * a.unc / (2.0 * a.val * v)  // From chain rule
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: v, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_exp(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = exp(a)
    // f' = a' * exp(a)
    // σ_f = |exp(a)| * σ_a = exp(a) * σ_a

    let e = exp_f64(a.val)
    let dot = a.dot * e

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = e * a.unc

    // Derivative uncertainty
    let unc_dot_1 = e * a.unc_dot
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot) * e * a.unc  // From exp'(a) * σ_a
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: e, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_ln(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = ln(a)
    // f' = a' / a
    // σ_f = σ_a / |a|

    let val = ln_f64(a.val)
    let dot = a.dot / a.val

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = a.unc / abs_f64(a.val)

    // Derivative uncertainty
    let unc_dot_1 = a.unc_dot / abs_f64(a.val)
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot) * a.unc / (a.val * a.val)
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: val, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_pow(a: EpistemicDual, n: f64) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = a^n
    // f' = n * a^(n-1) * a'
    // σ_f = |n * a^(n-1)| * σ_a

    let v = pow_f64(a.val, n)
    let df_da = n * pow_f64(a.val, n - 1.0)
    let dot = a.dot * df_da

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = abs_f64(df_da) * a.unc

    // Derivative uncertainty (includes second derivative contribution)
    let d2f_da2 = n * (n - 1.0) * pow_f64(a.val, n - 2.0)
    let unc_dot_1 = abs_f64(df_da) * a.unc_dot
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot * d2f_da2) * a.unc
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: v, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_sin(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = sin(a)
    // f' = cos(a) * a'
    // σ_f = |cos(a)| * σ_a

    let s = sin_f64(a.val)
    let c = cos_f64(a.val)
    let dot = a.dot * c

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = abs_f64(c) * a.unc

    // Derivative uncertainty (f'' = -sin(a))
    let unc_dot_1 = abs_f64(c) * a.unc_dot
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot * s) * a.unc  // From -sin(a) * a' * σ_a
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: s, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_cos(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = cos(a)
    // f' = -sin(a) * a'
    // σ_f = |sin(a)| * σ_a

    let s = sin_f64(a.val)
    let c = cos_f64(a.val)
    let dot = 0.0 - a.dot * s

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = abs_f64(s) * a.unc

    // Derivative uncertainty
    let unc_dot_1 = abs_f64(s) * a.unc_dot
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot * c) * a.unc
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: c, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_tanh(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = tanh(a)
    // f' = (1 - tanh²(a)) * a' = sech²(a) * a'
    // σ_f = sech²(a) * σ_a

    let t = tanh_f64(a.val)
    let sech2 = 1.0 - t * t
    let dot = a.dot * sech2

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = abs_f64(sech2) * a.unc

    // Derivative uncertainty (f'' = -2*tanh*sech²)
    let unc_dot_1 = abs_f64(sech2) * a.unc_dot
    let unc_dot_2 = 2.0 * abs_f64(t * sech2 * a.dot) * a.unc
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: t, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_sigmoid(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = 1 / (1 + exp(-a)) = σ(a)
    // f' = σ(a) * (1 - σ(a)) * a'

    let s = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - a.val))
    let ds = s * (1.0 - s)  // Derivative of sigmoid
    let dot = a.dot * ds

    // Value uncertainty
    let unc = abs_f64(ds) * a.unc

    // Derivative uncertainty (f'' = σ(1-σ)(1-2σ))
    let d2s = ds * (1.0 - 2.0 * s)
    let unc_dot_1 = abs_f64(ds) * a.unc_dot
    let unc_dot_2 = abs_f64(a.dot * d2s) * a.unc
    let unc_dot = combine_unc(unc_dot_1, unc_dot_2)

    return EpistemicDual { val: s, dot: dot, unc: unc, unc_dot: unc_dot }
}

fn edual_relu(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = max(0, a)
    // f' = 1 if a > 0, else 0
    // Uncertainty at boundary is tricky - we preserve it

    if a.val > 0.0 {
        return EpistemicDual { val: a.val, dot: a.dot, unc: a.unc, unc_dot: a.unc_dot }
    }
    // Below zero, output is zero but uncertainty in "when we cross" matters
    // For conservative estimate, we keep some uncertainty
    return EpistemicDual { val: 0.0, dot: 0.0, unc: a.unc, unc_dot: 0.0 }
}

fn edual_abs(a: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // f = |a|
    // Uncertainty unchanged by absolute value
    if a.val >= 0.0 {
        return a
    }
    return edual_neg(a)
}

// ============================================================================
// SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
// ============================================================================

// Sensitivity: |∂f/∂x| * σ_x / |f| - how much uncertainty matters
fn sensitivity(ed: EpistemicDual) -> f64 {
    if abs_f64(ed.val) < 0.000000000000001 { return 0.0 }
    return abs_f64(ed.dot) * ed.unc / abs_f64(ed.val)
}

// Derivative-weighted uncertainty
fn derivative_weighted_unc(ed: EpistemicDual) -> f64 {
    return abs_f64(ed.dot) * ed.unc
}

// Total uncertainty (value + derivative contribution)
fn total_uncertainty(ed: EpistemicDual) -> f64 {
    return combine_unc(ed.unc, ed.unc_dot)
}

// ============================================================================
// COMPARISON AND UTILITIES
// ============================================================================

fn edual_max(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    if a.val >= b.val { return a }
    return b
}

fn edual_min(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    if a.val <= b.val { return a }
    return b
}

// Check if values are compatible within uncertainties
fn edual_compatible(a: EpistemicDual, b: EpistemicDual, sigma_mult: f64) -> i64 {
    let diff = abs_f64(a.val - b.val)
    let combined_unc = combine_unc(a.unc, b.unc)
    if diff <= sigma_mult * combined_unc { return 1 }
    return 0
}

// Print epistemic dual (for debugging)
fn edual_print(label: f64, ed: EpistemicDual) -> i64 {
    println("EpistemicDual:")
    println("  val = ")
    println(ed.val)
    println("  dot = ")
    println(ed.dot)
    println("  unc = ")
    println(ed.unc)
    println("  unc_dot = ")
    println(ed.unc_dot)
    println("  confidence = ")
    println(confidence(ed))
    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// PHARMACOKINETICS EXAMPLE: Uncertainty in Clearance Calculation
// ============================================================================

// One-compartment PK: C(t) = (D/V) * exp(-CL/V * t)
fn pk_concentration(dose: EpistemicDual, volume: EpistemicDual, clearance: EpistemicDual, time: EpistemicDual) -> EpistemicDual {
    // C = (D/V) * exp(-(CL/V)*t)
    let d_over_v = edual_div(dose, volume)
    let cl_over_v = edual_div(clearance, volume)
    let neg_cl_v_t = edual_neg(edual_mul(cl_over_v, time))
    let exp_term = edual_exp(neg_cl_v_t)
    return edual_mul(d_over_v, exp_term)
}
