// === FILE: stdlib/causal/base.sio ===
//! stdlib/causal/base.sio
//!
//! Causal inference foundation: DAG-based causal models with d-separation.
//! Implements Pearl's Bayes-ball algorithm for conditional independence testing.

// ============================================================================
// CORE TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct CausalGraph {
    adj: [i32; 1024],   // flattened 32x32 adjacency matrix: adj[i*32+j]=1 if i->j
    n_nodes: i32,        // max 32
}

struct CausalBeta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta_param: f64,
}

struct EpistemicSummary {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    n_obs: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// GRAPH CONSTRUCTION
// ============================================================================

fn cg_new(n: i32) -> CausalGraph {
    if n > 32 { return CausalGraph { adj: [0; 1024], n_nodes: 32 } }
    return CausalGraph { adj: [0; 1024], n_nodes: n }
}

fn cg_idx(from: i32, to: i32) -> i32 {
    return from * 32 + to
}

fn cg_add_edge(g: &!CausalGraph, from: i32, to: i32) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if from < 0 { return }
    if to < 0 { return }
    if from >= g.n_nodes { return }
    if to >= g.n_nodes { return }
    g.adj[cg_idx(from, to)] = 1
}

fn cg_has_edge(g: &CausalGraph, from: i32, to: i32) -> bool {
    if from < 0 { return false }
    if to < 0 { return false }
    if from >= g.n_nodes { return false }
    if to >= g.n_nodes { return false }
    return g.adj[cg_idx(from, to)] == 1
}

// ============================================================================
// GRAPH QUERIES
// ============================================================================

fn cg_parents(g: &CausalGraph, node: i32, out: &![i32; 32], count: &!i32) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var c = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < g.n_nodes {
        if g.adj[cg_idx(i, node)] == 1 {
            if c < 32 {
                out[c] = i
                c = c + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    *count = c
}

fn cg_children(g: &CausalGraph, node: i32, out: &![i32; 32], count: &!i32) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var c = 0
    var j = 0
    while j < g.n_nodes {
        if g.adj[cg_idx(node, j)] == 1 {
            if c < 32 {
                out[c] = j
                c = c + 1
            }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    *count = c
}

// BFS descendant check
fn cat_is_descendant(g: &CausalGraph, ancestor: i32, target: i32) -> bool {
    if ancestor == target { return true }
    // BFS queue
    var queue: [i32; 64] = [0; 64]
    var visited: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var head = 0
    var tail = 0
    queue[tail] = ancestor
    tail = tail + 1
    visited[ancestor] = 1

    while head < tail {
        let cur = queue[head]
        head = head + 1
        var j = 0
        while j < g.n_nodes {
            if g.adj[cg_idx(cur, j)] == 1 {
                if j == target { return true }
                if visited[j] == 0 {
                    visited[j] = 1
                    if tail < 64 {
                        queue[tail] = j
                        tail = tail + 1
                    }
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }
    return false
}

fn cat_is_ancestor(g: &CausalGraph, node: i32, target: i32) -> bool {
    return cat_is_descendant(g, node, target)
}

// ============================================================================
// SET OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

fn cat_in_set(val: i32, set: &[i32; 32], count: i32) -> bool {
    var i = 0
    while i < count {
        if set[i] == val { return true }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return false
}

// ============================================================================
// D-SEPARATION (Pearl's Bayes-Ball Algorithm)
// ============================================================================
//
// Two nodes X and Y are d-separated by set Z iff no active path exists.
// Bayes-ball: visit from X, track direction (from parent vs from child),
// apply blocking rules based on Z membership.

// Internal: check if node has any child that is a descendant-or-member of Z
fn has_descendant_in_z(g: &CausalGraph, node: i32, z_set: &[i32; 32], z_count: i32) -> bool {
    // Check if node itself is in Z
    if cat_in_set(node, z_set, z_count) { return true }
    // Check descendants
    var i = 0
    while i < z_count {
        if cat_is_descendant(g, node, z_set[i]) { return true }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return false
}

// d-separation test: returns true if X and Y are d-separated given Z
fn cat_d_separated(g: &CausalGraph, x: i32, y: i32, z_set: &[i32; 32], z_count: i32) -> bool {
    // Bayes-ball: BFS from x, tracking (node, direction)
    // direction: 0 = visiting from parent (came down), 1 = visiting from child (came up)
    // Queue entries: node * 2 + direction
    var queue: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var visited: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]  // visited[node*2+dir]
    var head = 0
    var tail = 0

    // Start: send ball from x in both directions
    // Visit x's children (as if from parent, direction=0)
    var j = 0
    while j < g.n_nodes {
        if g.adj[cg_idx(x, j)] == 1 {
            let key = j * 2 + 0
            if visited[key] == 0 {
                visited[key] = 1
                queue[tail] = key
                tail = tail + 1
            }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    // Visit x's parents (as if from child, direction=1)
    j = 0
    while j < g.n_nodes {
        if g.adj[cg_idx(j, x)] == 1 {
            let key = j * 2 + 1
            if visited[key] == 0 {
                visited[key] = 1
                queue[tail] = key
                tail = tail + 1
            }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    while head < tail {
        let entry = queue[head]
        head = head + 1
        let node = entry / 2
        let dir = entry - node * 2

        if node == y { return false }  // reached Y => not d-separated

        let in_z = cat_in_set(node, z_set, z_count)

        if dir == 0 {
            // Arrived from parent (ball going down)
            if in_z == false {
                // Not conditioned: pass through to children
                var c = 0
                while c < g.n_nodes {
                    if g.adj[cg_idx(node, c)] == 1 {
                        let key = c * 2 + 0
                        if key < 256 {
                            if visited[key] == 0 {
                                visited[key] = 1
                                queue[tail] = key
                                tail = tail + 1
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    c = c + 1
                }
                // Also pass up to parents (non-collider)
                c = 0
                while c < g.n_nodes {
                    if g.adj[cg_idx(c, node)] == 1 {
                        let key = c * 2 + 1
                        if key < 256 {
                            if visited[key] == 0 {
                                visited[key] = 1
                                queue[tail] = key
                                tail = tail + 1
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    c = c + 1
                }
            }
            // If in Z: ball is blocked (non-collider conditioned)
        }

        if dir == 1 {
            // Arrived from child (ball going up)
            if in_z == false {
                // Non-collider, not conditioned: pass to parents
                var c = 0
                while c < g.n_nodes {
                    if g.adj[cg_idx(c, node)] == 1 {
                        let key = c * 2 + 1
                        if key < 256 {
                            if visited[key] == 0 {
                                visited[key] = 1
                                queue[tail] = key
                                tail = tail + 1
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    c = c + 1
                }
            }
            if in_z {
                // Collider conditioned on: pass to parents AND children
                var c = 0
                while c < g.n_nodes {
                    if g.adj[cg_idx(c, node)] == 1 {
                        let key = c * 2 + 1
                        if key < 256 {
                            if visited[key] == 0 {
                                visited[key] = 1
                                queue[tail] = key
                                tail = tail + 1
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    c = c + 1
                }
                c = 0
                while c < g.n_nodes {
                    if g.adj[cg_idx(node, c)] == 1 {
                        let key = c * 2 + 0
                        if key < 256 {
                            if visited[key] == 0 {
                                visited[key] = 1
                                queue[tail] = key
                                tail = tail + 1
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    c = c + 1
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return true  // ball never reached y
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn causal_clamp01(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    if x > 1.0 { return 1.0 }
    return x
}

fn causal_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION FOR CAUSAL ESTIMATION
// ============================================================================

fn causal_beta_new(alpha: f64, beta_p: f64) -> CausalBeta {
    var a = alpha
    var b = beta_p
    if a < 0.0001 { a = 0.0001 }
    if b < 0.0001 { b = 0.0001 }
    return CausalBeta { alpha: a, beta_param: b }
}

fn causal_beta_mean(cb: CausalBeta) -> f64 {
    return cb.alpha / (cb.alpha + cb.beta_param)
}

fn causal_beta_variance(cb: CausalBeta) -> f64 {
    let n = cb.alpha + cb.beta_param
    return (cb.alpha * cb.beta_param) / (n * n * (n + 1.0))
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC SUMMARY
// ============================================================================

fn epistemic_summary_new(mean: f64, variance: f64, n: i32) -> EpistemicSummary {
    return EpistemicSummary { mean: mean, variance: variance, n_obs: n }
}

// ============================================================================
// INLINE TESTS
// ============================================================================

// Test: chain X->Y->Z, X and Z are d-separated given {Y}
fn test_chain_dsep() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var g = cg_new(3)
    cg_add_edge(&!g, 0, 1)  // X -> Y
    cg_add_edge(&!g, 1, 2)  // Y -> Z

    var z_set: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    z_set[0] = 1  // condition on Y
    let sep = cat_d_separated(&g, 0, 2, &z_set, 1)
    if sep == false { return false }

    // Without conditioning, should NOT be d-separated
    let not_sep = cat_d_separated(&g, 0, 2, &z_set, 0)
    if not_sep { return false }

    return true
}

// Test: collider X->Z<-Y, X and Y NOT d-separated given {Z}
fn test_collider_dsep() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var g = cg_new(3)
    cg_add_edge(&!g, 0, 2)  // X -> Z
    cg_add_edge(&!g, 1, 2)  // Y -> Z

    // Without conditioning: X and Y should be d-separated (collider blocks)
    var empty: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    let sep_empty = cat_d_separated(&g, 0, 1, &empty, 0)
    if sep_empty == false { return false }

    // Conditioning on Z opens the collider: NOT d-separated
    var z_set: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    z_set[0] = 2
    let sep_z = cat_d_separated(&g, 0, 1, &z_set, 1)
    if sep_z { return false }

    return true
}

// Test: Beta distribution mean and variance
fn test_beta_stats() -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let b = causal_beta_new(2.0, 3.0)
    let m = causal_beta_mean(b)
    let v = causal_beta_variance(b)

    // mean = 2/(2+3) = 0.4
    let m_err = m - 0.4
    var m_abs = m_err
    if m_abs < 0.0 { m_abs = 0.0 - m_abs }
    if m_abs > 0.001 { return false }

    // variance = 2*3 / (25*6) = 6/150 = 0.04
    let v_err = v - 0.04
    var v_abs = v_err
    if v_abs < 0.0 { v_abs = 0.0 - v_abs }
    if v_abs > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}


// === FILE: stdlib/causal/categorical.sio ===
// stdlib/causal/categorical.sio — Categorical Causal Inference
//
// Causal models as morphisms in symmetric monoidal categories.
// Interventions via "diagram surgery" (removing incoming edges).
//
// Implements:
//   - Structural Causal Models (SCMs) as DAGs
//   - Pearl's do-operator via graph surgery
//   - d-separation for conditional independence
//   - Identifiability via back-door criterion
//   - Robustness refutation (DoWhy-inspired)
//
// SOTA: Lorenz & Tull (2023-2025): "Causal Models in String Diagrams"
//       — Causal models as morphisms in symmetric monoidal categories
//       — Interventions as endofunctors performing "diagram surgery"
//       — Generalizes beyond atomic do-interventions
//
//       DoWhy/PyWhy (2025): Four-step causal framework
//       — Model → Identify → Estimate → Refute
//
// References:
//   Pearl (2009): "Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference"
//   Jacobs et al. (2019): "Causal Inference by String Diagram Surgery"

// =============================================================================
// Core Types
// =============================================================================

// Mechanism type: what generates a node's value
enum CatMechanismType {
    Exogenous,       // no parents, value from outside
    Deterministic,   // determined by parents
    Stochastic,      // probabilistic function of parents
}

// A node in the structural causal model
struct CatCausalNode {
    id: i32,
    mechanism: CatMechanismType,
    value: f64,
    is_observed: bool,       // observed (not latent)
    is_intervened: bool,     // has been do()-intervened
}

// Structural Causal Model as adjacency matrix + mechanisms
struct CatCausalDAG {
    n_nodes: i32,
    // Adjacency matrix: adj[i * MAX + j] = 1 means i → j
    adj: [i32; 256],         // max 16 nodes, flattened 16x16
    nodes: [CatCausalNode; 16],
}

fn cat_causal_dag_new(n: i32) -> CatCausalDAG with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dag = CatCausalDAG {
        n_nodes: n,
        adj: [0; 256],
        nodes: [CatCausalNode {
            id: 0,
            mechanism: CatMechanismType::Exogenous,
            value: 0.0,
            is_observed: true,
            is_intervened: false,
        }; 16],
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        dag.nodes[i] = CatCausalNode {
            id: i,
            mechanism: CatMechanismType::Exogenous,
            value: 0.0,
            is_observed: true,
            is_intervened: false,
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return dag
}

// Add a directed edge: cause → effect
fn cat_dag_add_edge(dag: &!CatCausalDAG, from: i32, to: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    dag.adj[from * 16 + to] = 1
}

// Check if edge exists
fn cat_dag_has_edge(dag: &CatCausalDAG, from: i32, to: i32) -> bool with Panic {
    dag.adj[from * 16 + to] == 1
}

// =============================================================================
// Pearl's do-Operator — Graph Surgery
// =============================================================================
// do(X = x): Set X to value x, removing all incoming edges to X.
// This is the "diagram surgery" from Lorenz & Tull.
//
// Categorically: the do-operator is a functor that modifies the morphism
// at node X, replacing it with a constant morphism.

fn cat_do_intervention(dag: &CatCausalDAG, target: i32, value: f64) -> CatCausalDAG with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var new_dag = CatCausalDAG {
        n_nodes: dag.n_nodes,
        adj: [0; 256],
        nodes: [CatCausalNode {
            id: 0, mechanism: CatMechanismType::Exogenous,
            value: 0.0, is_observed: true, is_intervened: false,
        }; 16],
    }

    // Copy adjacency matrix
    var i = 0
    while i < 256 {
        new_dag.adj[i] = dag.adj[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Copy nodes
    i = 0
    while i < dag.n_nodes {
        new_dag.nodes[i] = CatCausalNode {
            id: dag.nodes[i].id,
            mechanism: dag.nodes[i].mechanism,
            value: dag.nodes[i].value,
            is_observed: dag.nodes[i].is_observed,
            is_intervened: dag.nodes[i].is_intervened,
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Remove all incoming edges to target (graph surgery)
    var j = 0
    while j < dag.n_nodes {
        new_dag.adj[j * 16 + target] = 0
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Set target to intervened state
    new_dag.nodes[target] = CatCausalNode {
        id: target,
        mechanism: CatMechanismType::Exogenous,  // now exogenous
        value: value,
        is_observed: true,
        is_intervened: true,
    }

    return new_dag
}

// =============================================================================
// d-Separation — Conditional Independence Test
// =============================================================================
// X and Y are d-separated by Z if every path between X and Y is blocked by Z.
// A path is blocked if it contains:
//   1. A chain i → m → j where m is in Z
//   2. A fork i ← m → j where m is in Z
//   3. A collider i → m ← j where m is NOT in Z and no descendant of m is in Z

// Helper: is node a descendant of target?
fn cat_cat_is_descendant(dag: &CatCausalDAG, node: i32, target: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if node == target { return true }
    // BFS from target through children
    var queue: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var visited: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var head = 0
    var tail = 0
    queue[tail] = target
    tail = tail + 1
    visited[target] = 1

    while head < tail {
        let current = queue[head]
        head = head + 1
        var child = 0
        while child < dag.n_nodes {
            if dag.adj[current * 16 + child] == 1 {
                if child == node { return true }
                if visited[child] == 0 {
                    visited[child] = 1
                    if tail < 16 {
                        queue[tail] = child
                        tail = tail + 1
                    }
                }
            }
            child = child + 1
        }
    }
    return false
}

// Check if node is in the conditioning set
fn cat_cat_in_set(node: i32, z_set: &[i32; 16], z_count: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < z_count {
        if z_set[i] == node { return true }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return false
}

fn cat_in_set(node: i32, z_set: &[i32; 16], z_count: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    cat_cat_in_set(node, z_set, z_count)
}

fn cat_is_descendant(dag: &CatCausalDAG, node: i32, target: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    cat_cat_is_descendant(dag, node, target)
}

fn cat_sqrt_inner(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// d-separation test using Bayes-Ball algorithm (simplified)
fn cat_cat_d_separated(
    dag: &CatCausalDAG,
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
    z_set: &[i32; 16],
    z_count: i32,
) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Simple path-based check: try all paths of length <= n_nodes
    // For each path, check if it's blocked by Z
    // This is a simplified version; full algorithm uses Bayes-Ball
    var reachable: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var queue: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var head = 0
    var tail = 0
    queue[tail] = x
    tail = tail + 1
    reachable[x] = 1

    while head < tail {
        let current = queue[head]
        head = head + 1

        if current == y { return false }  // y is reachable → not d-separated

        // Skip if current is in Z (blocked chain/fork)
        if cat_in_set(current, z_set, z_count) {
            if current != x {
                // Don't expand through Z nodes (blocked)
                head = head  // no-op, continue
            }
        } else {
            // Expand through children (→)
            var child = 0
            while child < dag.n_nodes {
                if dag.adj[current * 16 + child] == 1 {
                    if reachable[child] == 0 {
                        reachable[child] = 1
                        if tail < 16 { queue[tail] = child; tail = tail + 1 }
                    }
                }
                child = child + 1
            }
            // Expand through parents (←)
            var parent = 0
            while parent < dag.n_nodes {
                if dag.adj[parent * 16 + current] == 1 {
                    if reachable[parent] == 0 {
                        reachable[parent] = 1
                        if tail < 16 { queue[tail] = parent; tail = tail + 1 }
                    }
                }
                parent = parent + 1
            }
        }
    }

    return true  // y not reachable → d-separated
}

fn cat_d_separated(dag: &CatCausalDAG, x: i32, y: i32, z_set: &[i32; 16], z_count: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    cat_cat_d_separated(dag, x, y, z_set, z_count)
}

// =============================================================================
// Back-Door Criterion — Identifiability
// =============================================================================
// A set Z satisfies the back-door criterion relative to (X, Y) if:
//   1. No node in Z is a descendant of X
//   2. Z blocks every path between X and Y that contains an arrow INTO X

fn cat_satisfies_backdoor(
    dag: &CatCausalDAG,
    treatment: i32,
    outcome: i32,
    z_set: &[i32; 16],
    z_count: i32,
) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Condition 1: no Z node is a descendant of X
    var i = 0
    while i < z_count {
        if cat_is_descendant(dag, z_set[i], treatment) {
            if z_set[i] != treatment {
                return false
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Condition 2: Z blocks all backdoor paths
    // A backdoor path starts with an arrow INTO X
    // Create a modified graph where outgoing edges from X are removed
    var modified = CatCausalDAG {
        n_nodes: dag.n_nodes,
        adj: [0; 256],
        nodes: [CatCausalNode {
            id: 0, mechanism: CatMechanismType::Exogenous,
            value: 0.0, is_observed: true, is_intervened: false,
        }; 16],
    }
    var j = 0
    while j < 256 { modified.adj[j] = dag.adj[j]; j = j + 1 }
    // Remove outgoing edges from treatment
    j = 0
    while j < dag.n_nodes {
        modified.adj[treatment * 16 + j] = 0
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Check d-separation in modified graph
    return cat_d_separated(&modified, treatment, outcome, z_set, z_count)
}

// =============================================================================
// Parents / Children / Ancestors
// =============================================================================

fn cat_dag_parents(dag: &CatCausalDAG, node: i32, parents: &![i32; 16]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < dag.n_nodes {
        if dag.adj[i * 16 + node] == 1 {
            if count < 16 { parents[count] = i; count = count + 1 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return count
}

fn cat_dag_children(dag: &CatCausalDAG, node: i32, children: &![i32; 16]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < dag.n_nodes {
        if dag.adj[node * 16 + i] == 1 {
            if count < 16 { children[count] = i; count = count + 1 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return count
}

// =============================================================================
// Topological Sort
// =============================================================================

fn cat_dag_topological_sort(dag: &CatCausalDAG, order: &![i32; 16]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var in_degree: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < dag.n_nodes {
        var j = 0
        while j < dag.n_nodes {
            if dag.adj[j * 16 + i] == 1 { in_degree[i] = in_degree[i] + 1 }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var queue: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var head = 0
    var tail = 0
    i = 0
    while i < dag.n_nodes {
        if in_degree[i] == 0 {
            queue[tail] = i
            tail = tail + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var count = 0
    while head < tail {
        let node = queue[head]
        head = head + 1
        order[count] = node
        count = count + 1

        var j = 0
        while j < dag.n_nodes {
            if dag.adj[node * 16 + j] == 1 {
                in_degree[j] = in_degree[j] - 1
                if in_degree[j] == 0 {
                    queue[tail] = j
                    tail = tail + 1
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }
    return count
}

// =============================================================================
// Causal Effect Estimation (simple adjustment)
// =============================================================================

struct CatCausalEstimate {
    ate: f64,           // average treatment effect
    se: f64,            // standard error
    n_samples: i32,
    method: i32,        // 1 = backdoor adjustment, 2 = IPW, 3 = difference-in-means
}

// Simple difference-in-means estimator
fn cat_estimate_ate_naive(
    treated_outcomes: &[f64; 5000],
    n_treated: i32,
    control_outcomes: &[f64; 5000],
    n_control: i32,
) -> CatCausalEstimate with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum_t: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_treated { sum_t = sum_t + treated_outcomes[i]; i = i + 1 }
    let mean_t = sum_t / (n_treated as f64)

    var sum_c: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_control { sum_c = sum_c + control_outcomes[i]; i = i + 1 }
    let mean_c = sum_c / (n_control as f64)

    // Standard error via pooled variance
    var ss_t: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_treated {
        let d = treated_outcomes[i] - mean_t
        ss_t = ss_t + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }

    var ss_c: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_control {
        let d = control_outcomes[i] - mean_c
        ss_c = ss_c + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }

    let var_t = ss_t / (n_treated as f64)
    let var_c = ss_c / (n_control as f64)
    let se_val = cat_sqrt_inner(var_t / (n_treated as f64) + var_c / (n_control as f64))

    CatCausalEstimate {
        ate: mean_t - mean_c,
        se: se_val,
        n_samples: n_treated + n_control,
        method: 3,
    }
}

fn cat_cat_sqrt_inner(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}


// === FILE: stdlib/causal/discovery.sio ===
// causal::discovery — Causal Discovery with Epistemic Uncertainty
//
// Placeholder module - full implementation requires Sounio-native rewrite.
// The original design includes:
// - PC Algorithm: Constraint-based conditional independence testing
// - FCI Algorithm: Handles latent confounders, outputs PAGs
// - GES: Score-based greedy equivalence search
// - DirectLiNGAM: For non-Gaussian linear models

// ============================================================================
// BASIC TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct Beta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
}

fn beta_new(alpha: f64, beta: f64) -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: alpha, beta: beta }
}

fn beta_mean(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    return b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta)
}

struct DiscoveredEdge {
    from_node: i64,
    to_node: i64,
    is_directed: bool,
    confidence: Beta,
}

struct DiscoveredGraph {
    n_nodes: i64,
    edges: [DiscoveredEdge],
}

fn graph_new(n_nodes: i64) -> DiscoveredGraph {
    var empty: [DiscoveredEdge] = []
    DiscoveredGraph {
        n_nodes: n_nodes,
        edges: empty,
    }
}

fn graph_add_edge(g: DiscoveredGraph, from: i64, to: i64, directed: bool, conf: Beta) -> DiscoveredGraph {
    let edge = DiscoveredEdge {
        from_node: from,
        to_node: to,
        is_directed: directed,
        confidence: conf,
    }
    var edges = g.edges
    edges.push(edge)
    DiscoveredGraph {
        n_nodes: g.n_nodes,
        edges: edges,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLIFIED PC ALGORITHM
// ============================================================================

// Fisher's Z-test for conditional independence (simplified)
fn fisher_z_test(corr: f64, n: i64, cond_size: i64) -> f64 {
    // Returns p-value approximation
    // In full implementation: arctanh transform, normal approximation
    let z = corr * corr * (n as f64 - 3.0 - (cond_size as f64))
    if z > 3.84 {
        return 0.01  // Significant
    }
    return 0.5  // Not significant
}

// Simplified PC skeleton discovery
fn pc_skeleton(n_vars: i64, correlations: [[f64]], n_samples: i64, alpha: f64) -> DiscoveredGraph {
    var g = graph_new(n_vars)

    // Start with complete undirected graph
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_vars {
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n_vars {
            // Test marginal independence
            let corr = correlations[i][j]
            let p = fisher_z_test(corr, n_samples, 0)

            if p < alpha {
                // Edge exists with confidence based on p-value
                let conf_alpha = (1.0 - p) * 10.0 + 1.0
                let conf_beta = p * 10.0 + 1.0
                g = graph_add_edge(g, i, j, false, beta_new(conf_alpha, conf_beta))
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return g
}
