fn test_compile_artifact_v2_inline_transport() -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let opts = compile_options_default()
    let artifact = compile_source_text("fn main() -> i32 { 0 }", opts)
    if !artifact.ok { return 1 }
    if artifact.transport_kind != COMPILE_ARTIFACT_TRANSPORT_INLINE { return 1 }
    if artifact.artifact_schema != COMPILE_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA_V2 { return 1 }
    if artifact.artifact_path_len != 0 { return 1 }
    if artifact.code_len <= 0 { return 1 }
    0
}

fn test_compile_artifact_v2_path_transport_metadata() -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var artifact = compile_artifact_empty()
    artifact.ok = true
    artifact.exit_code = DRIVER_EXIT_OK
    artifact.code_len = 0
    artifact = compile_artifact_set_path_transport(artifact, ".sounio_bytecode.sobc")

    if artifact.transport_kind != COMPILE_ARTIFACT_TRANSPORT_PATH { return 1 }
    if artifact.artifact_schema != COMPILE_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA_V2 { return 1 }
    if artifact.artifact_path_len <= 0 { return 1 }
    if artifact.artifact_path[0] != 46 { return 1 } // '.'
    0
}

fn multimodule_demonstrator() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, Alloc {
    // Main demonstrator showing the multi-module compilation pipeline.
    //
    // This function exercises:
    // 1. compile_multimodule_program() API
    // 2. Module loading and deduplication (via module registry)
    // 3. Full resolution pipeline (resolve_modules)
    //
    // Test suite validates:
    // - Module files can be discovered via filesystem resolution
    // - Import statements are extracted from AST
    // - Duplicate imports are detected and skipped
    // - Circular dependencies don't cause infinite recursion

    var passed: i32 = 0
    var total: i32 = 5

    if test_multimodule_basic() == 0 { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_import_deduplication() == 0 { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_import_cycle_detection() == 0 { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_compile_artifact_v2_inline_transport() == 0 { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_compile_artifact_v2_path_transport_metadata() == 0 { passed = passed + 1 }

    if passed == total { 0 } else { 1 }
}

// ============================================================================
// SINGLE-FILE COMPILATION (existing bootstrap path)
// ============================================================================

fn compile_file(path: string, options: CompileOptions) -> CompileArtifact with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Note: keep this bootstrap path minimal. Directory/module resolution is
    // intentionally left to higher-level tooling for now.
    //
    // Moonshot step: if `path` is a directory, compile a flat concatenation of
    // all `.sio` files within it (non-recursive), sorted deterministically.
    if options.backend == BACKEND_NATIVE {
        return compile_artifact_fail_closed(
            DRIVER_EXIT_UNSUPPORTED_NATIVE,
            "native_backend_unsupported"
        )
    }

    var buf: [i8; 65536] = [0; 65536]
    var n: i64 = file_size(path)

    if n >= 0 {
        // Regular file.
        let bytes = read_file(path)
        if n > 65536 { n = 65536 }
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            buf[i as usize] = bytes[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        return compile_source(buf, n, options)
    }

    // Directory mode.
    if !is_dir(path) {
        // Missing path or unsupported file kind.
        var out = compile_artifact_empty()
        var msg: [i8; 64] = [0; 64]
        // "path_not_found"
        msg[0] = 112; msg[1] = 97; msg[2] = 116; msg[3] = 104
        msg[4] = 95
        msg[5] = 110; msg[6] = 111; msg[7] = 116
        msg[8] = 95
        msg[9] = 102; msg[10] = 111; msg[11] = 117; msg[12] = 110; msg[13] = 100
        out.exit_code = 2
        return emit_diag(out, msg, 14)
    }

    // Fast path: if a cached SOBC exists in the directory, load it directly and
    // avoid reading/concatenating a directory tree through `read_file` lists.
    let cache_path = path_join(path, ".sounio_bytecode.sobc")
    var cache_size: i64 = file_size(cache_path)
    if cache_size > 0 {
        var out = compile_artifact_empty()
        out.ok = true
        out.exit_code = DRIVER_EXIT_OK
        // Signal the host VM boundary to load cache directly, avoiding byte-by-byte
        // materialization in self-hosted bytecode.
        out.code_len = 0
        out = compile_artifact_set_path_transport(out, cache_path)
        return out
    }

    var entries = list_dir(path)

    // Heuristic guard: listing a directory is cheap, but reading N files into
    // `[i8]` lists is extremely expensive for large trees (e.g. `self-hosted/`).
    // For those, return an empty artifact so the host can continue via the
    // stage-boundary loader.
    var sio_count: i64 = 0
    var total_bytes: i64 = 0
    var scan_idx: i64 = 0
    let total = len(entries)
    entries = sort_string_list(entries, total)
    while scan_idx < total {
        let p = entries[scan_idx as usize]
        if ends_with(p, ".sio") {
            sio_count = sio_count + 1
            let sz = file_size(p)
            if sz > 0 {
                total_bytes = total_bytes + sz
            }
        }
        scan_idx = scan_idx + 1
    }

    if sio_count <= 0 {
        var out = compile_artifact_empty()
        var msg: [i8; 64] = [0; 64]
        // "empty_directory"
        msg[0] = 101; msg[1] = 109; msg[2] = 112; msg[3] = 116; msg[4] = 121
        msg[5] = 95
        msg[6] = 100; msg[7] = 105; msg[8] = 114; msg[9] = 101; msg[10] = 99; msg[11] = 116; msg[12] = 111; msg[13] = 114; msg[14] = 121
        out.exit_code = 2
        return emit_diag(out, msg, 15)
    }

    if sio_count > 16 || total_bytes > 16384 {
        var out = compile_artifact_empty()
        var msg: [i8; 64] = [0; 64]
        // "directory_too_large"
        msg[0] = 100; msg[1] = 105; msg[2] = 114; msg[3] = 101; msg[4] = 99; msg[5] = 116; msg[6] = 111; msg[7] = 114; msg[8] = 121
        msg[9] = 95
        msg[10] = 116; msg[11] = 111; msg[12] = 111
        msg[13] = 95
        msg[14] = 108; msg[15] = 97; msg[16] = 114; msg[17] = 103; msg[18] = 101
        out.exit_code = 2
        return emit_diag(out, msg, 19)
    }

    var pos: i64 = 0
    var idx: i64 = 0
    while idx < total {
        let p = entries[idx as usize]
        if ends_with(p, ".sio") {
            let bytes = read_file(p)
            let size = file_size(p)
            var m: i64 = size
            if m < 0 { m = 0 }
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < m && pos < 65536 {
                buf[pos as usize] = bytes[j as usize]
                pos = pos + 1
                j = j + 1
            }
            // Ensure a newline boundary between files.
            if pos < 65536 {
                buf[pos as usize] = 10
                pos = pos + 1
            }
        }
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    compile_source(buf, pos, options)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/bootstrap/verify.sio ===
//! stdlib/compiler/bootstrap/verify.sio - Bootstrap Verification Harness
//!
//! Multi-stage bootstrap verification with attestation chain for the
//! metacircular self-hosted compiler. Implements cross-validation between
//! Stage 1 and Stage 2 to verify compilation correctness.

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE STEP
// ============================================================================

struct ProvenanceStep {
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    confidence: f32,
    timestamp: i64,
}

fn provenance_step_new() -> ProvenanceStep {
    ProvenanceStep {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        confidence: 0.0,
        timestamp: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// BOOTSTRAP RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct BootstrapResult {
    stage: i32,                    // 0=Rust, 1=Self1, 2=Self2, 3+=Verified
    code: [i8; 65536],             // Generated code bytes
    code_len: i64,
    confidence: f32,
    provenance: [ProvenanceStep; 16],
    n_provenance: i64,
}

fn bootstrap_result_new() -> BootstrapResult {
    BootstrapResult {
        stage: 0,
        code: [0; 65536],
        code_len: 0,
        confidence: 0.0,
        provenance: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_provenance: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// VERIFICATION RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct VerificationResult {
    stage1: BootstrapResult,
    stage2: BootstrapResult,
    byte_match: bool,
    semantic_match: bool,
    confidence_boost: f32,
    final_confidence: f32,
    verified: bool,
}

fn verification_result_new() -> VerificationResult {
    VerificationResult {
        stage1: bootstrap_result_new(),
        stage2: bootstrap_result_new(),
        byte_match: false,
        semantic_match: false,
        confidence_boost: 1.0,
        final_confidence: 0.0,
        verified: false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ATTESTATION CHAIN
// ============================================================================

struct AttestationChain {
    stages: [BootstrapResult; 4],
    n_stages: i64,
    root_confidence: f32,
    verified_to_stage: i32,
}

fn attestation_chain_new() -> AttestationChain {
    AttestationChain {
        stages: [bootstrap_result_new(); 4],
        n_stages: 0,
        root_confidence: 0.0,
        verified_to_stage: -1,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STAGE CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

let STAGE_RUST: i32 = 0
let STAGE_SELF1: i32 = 1
let STAGE_SELF2: i32 = 2
let STAGE_VERIFIED: i32 = 3

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

let CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST: f32 = 1.04
let MAX_CONFIDENCE: f32 = 0.99
let CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: f32 = 0.9

// ============================================================================
// ERROR CODES
// ============================================================================

let ERR_NONE: i32 = 0
let ERR_BYTE_MISMATCH: i32 = 1
let ERR_SEMANTIC_MISMATCH: i32 = 2
let ERR_LOW_CONFIDENCE: i32 = 3
let ERR_STAGE_FAILURE: i32 = 4

// ============================================================================
// CODE COMPARISON
// ============================================================================

// Compares two code buffers byte-by-byte
fn compare_code_bytes(a: [i8; 65536], a_len: i64, b: [i8; 65536], b_len: i64) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a_len != b_len { false }
    else {
        var matches: bool = true
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < a_len && matches {
            if a[i as usize] != b[i as usize] {
                matches = false
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        matches
    }
}

// Computes a simple DJB2 hash of the code buffer
fn code_hash(code: [i8; 65536], len: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var hash: i64 = 5381
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        let byte_val: i8 = code[i as usize]
        let c: i64 = if byte_val < 0 { (byte_val as i64) + 256 } else { byte_val as i64 }
        hash = hash * 33 + c
        i = i + 1
    }
    hash
}

// ============================================================================
// BOOTSTRAP STAGES (placeholders for actual compilation)
// ============================================================================

// Rust compiler bootstrap stage (trusted base)
fn bootstrap_stage_0(source: [i8; 65536], len: i64) -> BootstrapResult with Mut {
    var result = bootstrap_result_new()
    result = BootstrapResult {
        stage: STAGE_RUST,
        code: source,  // In real impl, would invoke Rust compiler
        code_len: len,
        confidence: 1.0,  // Rust compiler is fully trusted
        provenance: result.provenance,
        n_provenance: 0,
    }
    result
}

// Self-compiled Stage 1
fn bootstrap_stage_1(stage0: BootstrapResult, source: [i8; 65536], len: i64) -> BootstrapResult with Mut {
    var result = bootstrap_result_new()
    // Confidence degrades by 2% per stage
    let new_conf = stage0.confidence * 0.98
    result = BootstrapResult {
        stage: STAGE_SELF1,
        code: source,  // In real impl, would use stage0 compiler
        code_len: len,
        confidence: new_conf,
        provenance: result.provenance,
        n_provenance: 0,
    }
    result
}

// Self-compiled Stage 2
fn bootstrap_stage_2(stage1: BootstrapResult, source: [i8; 65536], len: i64) -> BootstrapResult with Mut {
    var result = bootstrap_result_new()
    let new_conf = stage1.confidence * 0.98
    result = BootstrapResult {
        stage: STAGE_SELF2,
        code: source,  // In real impl, would use stage1 compiler
        code_len: len,
        confidence: new_conf,
        provenance: result.provenance,
        n_provenance: 0,
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Applies cross-validation boost, capped at MAX_CONFIDENCE
fn apply_cross_validation_boost(conf: f32, verified: bool) -> f32 {
    if verified {
        let new_conf = conf * CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST
        if new_conf > MAX_CONFIDENCE { MAX_CONFIDENCE }
        else { new_conf }
    } else {
        conf
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CROSS-VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

// Performs cross-validation between stage1 and stage2 results
fn cross_validate(stage1: BootstrapResult, stage2: BootstrapResult) -> VerificationResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let byte_match = compare_code_bytes(stage1.code, stage1.code_len,
                                        stage2.code, stage2.code_len)
    // Assume semantic match if bytes match (placeholder)
    let semantic_match = byte_match
    let verified = byte_match && semantic_match
    let boost = if verified { CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST } else { 1.0 }
    let final_conf = apply_cross_validation_boost(stage2.confidence, verified)

    VerificationResult {
        stage1: stage1,
        stage2: stage2,
        byte_match: byte_match,
        semantic_match: semantic_match,
        confidence_boost: boost,
        final_confidence: final_conf,
        verified: verified,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ATTESTATION CHAIN MANAGEMENT
// ============================================================================

// Creates an AttestationChain from an array of results
fn create_attestation_chain(results: [BootstrapResult; 4], n: i64) -> AttestationChain with Mut, Panic {
    var chain = attestation_chain_new()
    chain = AttestationChain {
        stages: results,
        n_stages: n,
        root_confidence: if n > 0 { results[0].confidence } else { 0.0 },
        verified_to_stage: if n > 0 { results[(n - 1) as usize].stage } else { -1 },
    }
    chain
}

// Adds a stage to the chain if capacity allows (max 4)
fn add_stage_to_chain(chain: AttestationChain, result: BootstrapResult) -> AttestationChain with Mut, Panic {
    let idx = chain.n_stages
    if idx < 4 {
        var new_stages = chain.stages
        new_stages[idx as usize] = result
        AttestationChain {
            stages: new_stages,
            n_stages: idx + 1,
            root_confidence: if idx == 0 { result.confidence } else { chain.root_confidence },
            verified_to_stage: result.stage,
        }
    } else {
        chain  // Chain full
    }
}

// Verifies the attestation chain
fn verify_attestation(chain: AttestationChain) -> bool {
    chain.verified_to_stage >= STAGE_VERIFIED
}

// Accumulates overall confidence as product of all stage confidences
fn accumulate_bootstrap_confidence(chain: AttestationChain) -> f32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var conf: f32 = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stages && i < 4 {
        conf = conf * chain.stages[i as usize].confidence
        i = i + 1
    }
    conf
}

// ============================================================================
// FULL BOOTSTRAP
// ============================================================================

// Runs the full multi-stage bootstrap process
fn run_full_bootstrap(source: [i8; 65536], len: i64) -> AttestationChain with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Stage 0: Rust compiler (trusted)
    let stage0 = bootstrap_stage_0(source, len)

    // Stage 1: Self-compiled with stage0
    let stage1 = bootstrap_stage_1(stage0, source, len)

    // Stage 2: Self-compiled with stage1
    let stage2 = bootstrap_stage_2(stage1, source, len)

    // Cross-validate stage1 vs stage2
    let verif = cross_validate(stage1, stage2)

    // Create stage3 based on verification result
    var stage3 = bootstrap_result_new()
    let stage3_stage = if verif.verified { STAGE_VERIFIED } else { STAGE_SELF2 }
    let stage3_conf = if verif.verified { verif.final_confidence } else { stage2.confidence }
    stage3 = BootstrapResult {
        stage: stage3_stage,
        code: stage2.code,
        code_len: stage2.code_len,
        confidence: stage3_conf,
        provenance: stage3.provenance,
        n_provenance: 0,
    }

    // Build attestation chain
    var results: [BootstrapResult; 4] = [bootstrap_result_new(); 4]
    results[0] = stage0
    results[1] = stage1
    results[2] = stage2
    results[3] = stage3
    create_attestation_chain(results, 4)
}

// ============================================================================
// FAILURE HANDLING
// ============================================================================

// Handles verification failure by returning appropriate error code
fn handle_verification_failure(result: VerificationResult) -> i32 {
    if result.verified { ERR_NONE }
    else if !result.byte_match { ERR_BYTE_MISMATCH }
    else if !result.semantic_match { ERR_SEMANTIC_MISMATCH }
    else if result.final_confidence < CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD { ERR_LOW_CONFIDENCE }
    else { ERR_STAGE_FAILURE }
}

// Falls back to the BootstrapResult from the specified target stage
fn fallback_to_stage(chain: AttestationChain, target: i32) -> BootstrapResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stages && i < 4 {
        if chain.stages[i as usize].stage == target {
            // Need to copy the result out
            let found = chain.stages[i as usize]
            // Return the found result
            // Since we can't return early in Sounio, use a flag
            var result = found
            i = chain.n_stages  // Exit loop
            result
        } else {
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    // Not found
    bootstrap_result_new()
}

// ============================================================================
// UTILITY FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Checks if bootstrap was successful
fn bootstrap_succeeded(chain: AttestationChain) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    chain.verified_to_stage >= STAGE_VERIFIED &&
    accumulate_bootstrap_confidence(chain) >= CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD
}

// Gets the final verified result from the chain
fn get_verified_result(chain: AttestationChain) -> BootstrapResult with Panic {
    if chain.n_stages > 0 {
        chain.stages[(chain.n_stages - 1) as usize]
    } else {
        bootstrap_result_new()
    }
}

// Computes confidence improvement from cross-validation
fn confidence_improvement(before: f32, after: f32) -> f32 with Div, Panic {
    if before > 0.0 {
        ((after - before) / before) * 100.0  // Percent improvement
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/check/checker.sio ===
// compiler::check::checker — Type Checker
//
// Main type checking logic for the self-hosted Sounio type checker.
// Implements bidirectional type checking for expressions and statements.

extern "C" {
    fn print(s: &str) -> ();
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn TYPE_UNKNOWN() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TYPE_NEVER() -> i32 { 1 }
fn TYPE_UNIT() -> i32 { 2 }
fn TYPE_BOOL() -> i32 { 3 }
fn TYPE_I8() -> i32 { 4 }
fn TYPE_I16() -> i32 { 5 }
fn TYPE_I32() -> i32 { 6 }
fn TYPE_I64() -> i32 { 7 }
fn TYPE_U8() -> i32 { 8 }
fn TYPE_U16() -> i32 { 9 }
fn TYPE_U32() -> i32 { 10 }
fn TYPE_U64() -> i32 { 11 }
fn TYPE_F32() -> i32 { 12 }
fn TYPE_F64() -> i32 { 13 }
fn TYPE_STRING() -> i32 { 16 }
fn TYPE_REF() -> i32 { 18 }
fn TYPE_REF_MUT() -> i32 { 19 }
fn TYPE_ARRAY() -> i32 { 20 }
fn TYPE_VAR() -> i32 { 26 }

// ============================================================================
// EXPRESSION KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn EXPR_LITERAL() -> i32 { 0 }
fn EXPR_PATH() -> i32 { 1 }
fn EXPR_BINARY() -> i32 { 2 }
fn EXPR_UNARY() -> i32 { 3 }
fn EXPR_CALL() -> i32 { 4 }
fn EXPR_IF() -> i32 { 10 }

// ============================================================================
// BINARY OPERATORS
// ============================================================================

fn BINOP_ADD() -> i32 { 0 }
fn BINOP_SUB() -> i32 { 1 }
fn BINOP_MUL() -> i32 { 2 }
fn BINOP_DIV() -> i32 { 3 }
fn BINOP_REM() -> i32 { 4 }
fn BINOP_AND() -> i32 { 5 }    // &&
fn BINOP_OR() -> i32 { 6 }     // ||
fn BINOP_EQ() -> i32 { 12 }
fn BINOP_NE() -> i32 { 13 }
fn BINOP_LT() -> i32 { 14 }
fn BINOP_LE() -> i32 { 15 }
fn BINOP_GT() -> i32 { 16 }
fn BINOP_GE() -> i32 { 17 }

// ============================================================================
// UNARY OPERATORS
// ============================================================================

fn UNOP_NEG() -> i32 { 0 }      // -x
fn UNOP_NOT() -> i32 { 1 }      // !x
fn UNOP_REF() -> i32 { 2 }      // &x
fn UNOP_REF_MUT() -> i32 { 3 }  // &!x
fn UNOP_DEREF() -> i32 { 4 }    // *x

// ============================================================================
// LITERAL KINDS
// ============================================================================

fn LIT_INT() -> i32 { 0 }
fn LIT_FLOAT() -> i32 { 1 }
fn LIT_BOOL() -> i32 { 4 }
fn LIT_UNIT() -> i32 { 5 }

// ============================================================================
// TYPE REPRESENTATION (simplified)
// ============================================================================

struct Type {
    kind: i32,
    inner_idx: i64,
    array_size: i64,
}

fn type_new() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_UNKNOWN(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn type_unit() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_UNIT(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn type_bool() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_BOOL(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn type_i32() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_I32(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn type_i64() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_I64(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn type_f64() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_F64(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn type_never() -> Type {
    Type { kind: TYPE_NEVER(), inner_idx: -1, array_size: 0 }
}

fn types_equal(a: Type, b: Type) -> bool {
    a.kind == b.kind && a.inner_idx == b.inner_idx && a.array_size == b.array_size
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPRESSION REPRESENTATION (simplified)
// ============================================================================

struct Expr {
    kind: i32,
    // For literals
    lit_kind: i32,
    lit_int: i64,
    lit_float: f64,
    lit_bool: bool,
    // For binary expressions
    binop: i32,
    left_idx: i64,
    right_idx: i64,
    // For unary expressions
    unop: i32,
    operand_idx: i64,
    // For path expressions (variable names)
    name: [i8; 32],
    name_len: i64,
    // Inferred type
    inferred_type: Type,
}

fn expr_new() -> Expr {
    Expr {
        kind: EXPR_LITERAL(),
        lit_kind: LIT_UNIT(),
        lit_int: 0,
        lit_float: 0.0,
        lit_bool: false,
        binop: 0,
        left_idx: -1,
        right_idx: -1,
        unop: 0,
        operand_idx: -1,
        name: [0; 32],
        name_len: 0,
        inferred_type: type_new(),
    }
}

fn expr_int(val: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_LITERAL();
    e.lit_kind = LIT_INT();
    e.lit_int = val;
    e
}

fn expr_float(val: f64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_LITERAL();
    e.lit_kind = LIT_FLOAT();
    e.lit_float = val;
    e
}

fn expr_bool(val: bool) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_LITERAL();
    e.lit_kind = LIT_BOOL();
    e.lit_bool = val;
    e
}

fn expr_binary(op: i32, left: i64, right: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_BINARY();
    e.binop = op;
    e.left_idx = left;
    e.right_idx = right;
    e
}

fn expr_unary(op: i32, operand: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_UNARY();
    e.unop = op;
    e.operand_idx = operand;
    e
}

fn expr_path(name: [i8; 32], len: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_PATH();
    e.name = name;
    e.name_len = len;
    e
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPRESSION POOL
// ============================================================================

struct ExprPool {
    exprs: [Expr; 128],
    count: i64,
}

fn expr_pool_new() -> ExprPool {
    ExprPool {
        exprs: [expr_new(); 128],
        count: 0,
    }
}

fn expr_pool_add(pool: ExprPool, e: Expr) -> ExprPool with Mut, Panic {
    var p = pool;
    if p.count < 128 {
        p.exprs[p.count as usize] = e;
        p.count = p.count + 1;
    }
    p
}

fn expr_pool_get(pool: ExprPool, idx: i64) -> Expr with Panic {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < pool.count {
        pool.exprs[idx as usize]
    } else {
        expr_new()
    }
}

fn expr_pool_last_idx(pool: ExprPool) -> i64 {
    pool.count - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// BINDING (simplified environment)
// ============================================================================

struct Binding {
    name: [i8; 32],
    name_len: i64,
    ty: Type,
    is_mutable: bool,
}

fn binding_new() -> Binding {
    Binding {
        name: [0; 32],
        name_len: 0,
        ty: type_new(),
        is_mutable: false,
    }
}

struct Env {
    bindings: [Binding; 64],
    count: i64,
}

fn env_new() -> Env {
    Env {
        bindings: [binding_new(); 64],
        count: 0,
    }
}

fn env_add(env: Env, name: [i8; 32], len: i64, ty: Type, is_mut: bool) -> Env with Mut, Panic {
    var e = env;
    if e.count < 64 {
        var b = binding_new();
        b.name = name;
        b.name_len = len;
        b.ty = ty;
        b.is_mutable = is_mut;
        e.bindings[e.count as usize] = b;
        e.count = e.count + 1;
    }
    e
}

fn names_eq(a: [i8; 32], a_len: i64, b: [i8; 32], b_len: i64) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a_len != b_len {
        return false
    }
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < a_len {
        if a[i as usize] != b[i as usize] {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    true
}

fn env_lookup(env: Env, name: [i8; 32], len: i64) -> Type with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = env.count - 1;
    while i >= 0 {
        let b = env.bindings[i as usize];
        if names_eq(b.name, b.name_len, name, len) {
            return b.ty
        }
        i = i - 1;
    }
    type_new()  // Unknown
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE CHECKER
// ============================================================================

struct CheckResult {
    ty: Type,
    ok: bool,
    error_msg: [i8; 128],
    error_len: i64,
}

fn check_ok(ty: Type) -> CheckResult {
    CheckResult {
        ty: ty,
        ok: true,
        error_msg: [0; 128],
        error_len: 0,
    }
}

fn check_err() -> CheckResult {
    CheckResult {
        ty: type_new(),
        ok: false,
        error_msg: [0; 128],
        error_len: 0,
    }
}

// Check if a type is numeric
fn is_numeric(t: Type) -> bool {
    t.kind == TYPE_I8() || t.kind == TYPE_I16() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_I32() || t.kind == TYPE_I64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_U8() || t.kind == TYPE_U16() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_U32() || t.kind == TYPE_U64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_F32() || t.kind == TYPE_F64()
}

// Check a literal expression
fn check_literal(e: Expr) -> CheckResult {
    if e.lit_kind == LIT_INT() {
        // Integer literals default to i64
        return check_ok(type_i64())
    }
    if e.lit_kind == LIT_FLOAT() {
        // Float literals default to f64
        return check_ok(type_f64())
    }
    if e.lit_kind == LIT_BOOL() {
        return check_ok(type_bool())
    }
    if e.lit_kind == LIT_UNIT() {
        return check_ok(type_unit())
    }
    check_err()
}

// Check a binary expression
fn check_binary(pool: ExprPool, e: Expr, env: Env) -> CheckResult with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // Get left and right operand types
    let left_expr = expr_pool_get(pool, e.left_idx);
    let right_expr = expr_pool_get(pool, e.right_idx);

    let left_result = check_expr(pool, left_expr, env);
    if !left_result.ok {
        return left_result
    }

    let right_result = check_expr(pool, right_expr, env);
    if !right_result.ok {
        return right_result
    }

    let left_ty = left_result.ty;
    let right_ty = right_result.ty;

    // Arithmetic operators: +, -, *, /, %
    if e.binop == BINOP_ADD() || e.binop == BINOP_SUB() ||
       e.binop == BINOP_MUL() || e.binop == BINOP_DIV() ||
       e.binop == BINOP_REM() {
        if !is_numeric(left_ty) || !is_numeric(right_ty) {
            return check_err()
        }
        if !types_equal(left_ty, right_ty) {
            return check_err()
        }
        return check_ok(left_ty)
    }

    // Comparison operators: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=
    if e.binop == BINOP_EQ() || e.binop == BINOP_NE() ||
       e.binop == BINOP_LT() || e.binop == BINOP_LE() ||
       e.binop == BINOP_GT() || e.binop == BINOP_GE() {
        if !types_equal(left_ty, right_ty) {
            return check_err()
        }
        return check_ok(type_bool())
    }

    // Logical operators: &&, ||
    if e.binop == BINOP_AND() || e.binop == BINOP_OR() {
        if left_ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() || right_ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
            return check_err()
        }
        return check_ok(type_bool())
    }

    check_err()
}

// Check a unary expression
fn check_unary(pool: ExprPool, e: Expr, env: Env) -> CheckResult with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let operand_expr = expr_pool_get(pool, e.operand_idx);
    let operand_result = check_expr(pool, operand_expr, env);

    if !operand_result.ok {
        return operand_result
    }

    let operand_ty = operand_result.ty;

    // Negation: -x (requires numeric)
    if e.unop == UNOP_NEG() {
        if !is_numeric(operand_ty) {
            return check_err()
        }
        return check_ok(operand_ty)
    }

    // Logical not: !x (requires bool)
    if e.unop == UNOP_NOT() {
        if operand_ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
            return check_err()
        }
        return check_ok(type_bool())
    }

    check_err()
}

// Check a path expression (variable reference)
fn check_path(e: Expr, env: Env) -> CheckResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ty = env_lookup(env, e.name, e.name_len);
    if ty.kind == TYPE_UNKNOWN() {
        return check_err()
    }
    check_ok(ty)
}

// Type check an expression
fn check_expr(pool: ExprPool, e: Expr, env: Env) -> CheckResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if e.kind == EXPR_LITERAL() {
        return check_literal(e)
    }

    if e.kind == EXPR_BINARY() {
        return check_binary(pool, e, env)
    }

    if e.kind == EXPR_UNARY() {
        return check_unary(pool, e, env)
    }

    if e.kind == EXPR_PATH() {
        return check_path(e, env)
    }

    check_err()
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn make_name(c0: i8, c1: i8, c2: i8, len: i64) -> [i8; 32] with Panic, Mut {
    var name: [i8; 32] = [0; 32];
    name[0] = c0;
    name[1] = c1;
    name[2] = c2;
    name
}

fn test_check_literals() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    let env = env_new();

    // Check integer literal
    let int_expr = expr_int(42);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, int_expr);

    let int_result = check_expr(pool, int_expr, env);
    if !int_result.ok {
        print("  Integer literal check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if int_result.ty.kind != TYPE_I64() {
        print("  Integer literal should be i64\n");
        return false
    }

    // Check float literal
    let float_expr = expr_float(3.14);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, float_expr);

    let float_result = check_expr(pool, float_expr, env);
    if !float_result.ok {
        print("  Float literal check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if float_result.ty.kind != TYPE_F64() {
        print("  Float literal should be f64\n");
        return false
    }

    // Check bool literal
    let bool_expr = expr_bool(true);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, bool_expr);

    let bool_result = check_expr(pool, bool_expr, env);
    if !bool_result.ok {
        print("  Bool literal check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if bool_result.ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
        print("  Bool literal should be bool\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_check_arithmetic() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    let env = env_new();

    // Add two i64 literals: 1 + 2
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(1));
    let left_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(2));
    let right_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let add_expr = expr_binary(BINOP_ADD(), left_idx, right_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, add_expr);

    let result = check_expr(pool, add_expr, env);
    if !result.ok {
        print("  Addition check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if result.ty.kind != TYPE_I64() {
        print("  Addition result should be i64\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_check_comparison() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    let env = env_new();

    // Compare two i64 literals: 1 < 2
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(1));
    let left_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(2));
    let right_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let lt_expr = expr_binary(BINOP_LT(), left_idx, right_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, lt_expr);

    let result = check_expr(pool, lt_expr, env);
    if !result.ok {
        print("  Comparison check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if result.ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
        print("  Comparison result should be bool\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_check_logical() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    let env = env_new();

    // Logical and: true && false
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_bool(true));
    let left_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_bool(false));
    let right_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let and_expr = expr_binary(BINOP_AND(), left_idx, right_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, and_expr);

    let result = check_expr(pool, and_expr, env);
    if !result.ok {
        print("  Logical AND check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if result.ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
        print("  Logical AND result should be bool\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_check_unary() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    let env = env_new();

    // Negation: -42
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(42));
    let operand_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let neg_expr = expr_unary(UNOP_NEG(), operand_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, neg_expr);

    let result = check_expr(pool, neg_expr, env);
    if !result.ok {
        print("  Negation check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if result.ty.kind != TYPE_I64() {
        print("  Negation result should be i64\n");
        return false
    }

    // Logical not: !true
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_bool(true));
    let bool_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let not_expr = expr_unary(UNOP_NOT(), bool_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, not_expr);

    let not_result = check_expr(pool, not_expr, env);
    if !not_result.ok {
        print("  Logical NOT check failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if not_result.ty.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
        print("  Logical NOT result should be bool\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_check_variables() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    var env = env_new();

    // Add variable 'x' with type i64
    let x_name = make_name(120, 0, 0, 1);  // 'x'
    env = env_add(env, x_name, 1, type_i64(), false);

    // Reference x
    let x_expr = expr_path(x_name, 1);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, x_expr);

    let result = check_expr(pool, x_expr, env);
    if !result.ok {
        print("  Variable lookup failed\n");
        return false
    }
    if result.ty.kind != TYPE_I64() {
        print("  Variable x should be i64\n");
        return false
    }

    // Reference undefined variable 'y'
    let y_name = make_name(121, 0, 0, 1);  // 'y'
    let y_expr = expr_path(y_name, 1);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, y_expr);

    let y_result = check_expr(pool, y_expr, env);
    if y_result.ok {
        print("  Undefined variable should fail\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_type_mismatch() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    let env = env_new();

    // Try to add i64 + bool (should fail)
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(1));
    let int_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_bool(true));
    let bool_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let add_expr = expr_binary(BINOP_ADD(), int_idx, bool_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, add_expr);

    let result = check_expr(pool, add_expr, env);
    if result.ok {
        print("  Adding int + bool should fail\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

struct FnSig {

    name_len: i64,
    param_names: [[i8; 32]; 16],
    param_name_lens: [i64; 16],
    param_types: [i64; 16],
    n_params: i64,
    return_type_idx: i64,
    effect_set: i64,  // Bitmask of effects
    type_params: [i64; 8],
    n_type_params: i64,
}

// Default FnSig for array initialization
fn fn_sig_default() -> FnSig {
    FnSig {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        param_names: [empty_name_32(); 16],
        param_name_lens: [0; 16],
        param_types: [-1; 16],
        n_params: 0,
        return_type_idx: -1,
        effect_set: 0,
        type_params: [-1; 8],
        n_type_params: 0,
    }
}

// Creates a new FnSig.
fn fn_sig_new(name: &str) -> FnSig {
    // NOTE: Copy name into buffer
    fn_sig_default()
}

// Adds a parameter to FnSig.
fn fn_sig_add_param(sig: FnSig, name: &str, type_idx: i64) -> FnSig with Mut, Panic {
    // NOTE: Validate n_params < 16, copy name into param_names[n_params]
    var new_sig = sig;
    if new_sig.n_params < 16 {
        let idx = new_sig.n_params;
        // NOTE: Copy name
        new_sig.param_name_lens[idx as usize] = 0;  // Placeholder
        new_sig.param_types[idx as usize] = type_idx;
        new_sig.n_params = new_sig.n_params + 1;
    }
    new_sig
}

// Sets the return type of FnSig.
fn fn_sig_set_return(sig: FnSig, type_idx: i64) -> FnSig with Mut {
    var new_sig = sig;
    new_sig.return_type_idx = type_idx;
    new_sig
}

// Adds an effect to the bitmask.
fn fn_sig_add_effect(sig: FnSig, effect: i32) -> FnSig with Mut {
    var new_sig = sig;
    let shift = effect as i64;
    let mask = 1 << shift;
    new_sig.effect_set = new_sig.effect_set | mask;
    new_sig
}

    var new_ctx = ctx;
    if new_ctx.n_scopes < 32 {

        new_ctx.n_scopes = new_ctx.n_scopes + 1;
    }
    new_ctx
}

// Pops the top scope from the stack.

    var new_ctx = ctx;
    if new_ctx.n_scopes > 0 {
        new_ctx.n_scopes = new_ctx.n_scopes - 1;
        // NOTE: Optionally clean up bindings if needed
    }
    new_ctx
}

// Symbol table and type bindings for the self-hosted type checker.

extern "C" {

// ============================================================================
// BINDING KINDS
// ============================================================================

fn BIND_VAR() -> i32 { 0 }       // Variable binding
fn BIND_FN() -> i32 { 1 }        // Function binding
fn BIND_TYPE() -> i32 { 2 }      // Type alias
fn BIND_STRUCT() -> i32 { 3 }    // Struct definition
fn BIND_ENUM() -> i32 { 4 }      // Enum definition

// ============================================================================
// TYPE KIND CONSTANTS (duplicated from types.sio for standalone use)
// ============================================================================

fn TYPE_UNKNOWN() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TYPE_UNIT() -> i32 { 2 }
fn TYPE_BOOL() -> i32 { 3 }
fn TYPE_I32() -> i32 { 6 }
fn TYPE_I64() -> i32 { 7 }
fn TYPE_F32() -> i32 { 12 }
fn TYPE_F64() -> i32 { 13 }

// ============================================================================
// SYMBOL BINDING
// ============================================================================

// A binding in the environment
struct Binding {
    kind: i32,
    // Name of the binding
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    // Type index (into type pool)
    type_idx: i64,
    // For variables: is mutable?
    is_mutable: bool,
    // For functions: parameter type indices
    param_types: [i64; 8],
    n_params: i64,
    // For functions: return type index
    return_type_idx: i64,
    // Scope depth
    scope_depth: i64,
}

fn binding_new() -> Binding {
    Binding {
        kind: BIND_VAR(),
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        type_idx: -1,
        is_mutable: false,
        param_types: [-1; 8],
        n_params: 0,
        return_type_idx: -1,
        scope_depth: 0,
    }
}

fn binding_var(name: [i8; 64], name_len: i64, type_idx: i64, is_mut: bool, depth: i64) -> Binding with Mut {
    var b = binding_new();
    b.kind = BIND_VAR();
    b.name = name;
    b.name_len = name_len;
    b.type_idx = type_idx;
    b.is_mutable = is_mut;
    b.scope_depth = depth;
    b
}

fn binding_fn(name: [i8; 64], name_len: i64, return_idx: i64, depth: i64) -> Binding with Mut {
    var b = binding_new();
    b.kind = BIND_FN();
    b.name = name;
    b.name_len = name_len;
    b.return_type_idx = return_idx;
    b.scope_depth = depth;
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// ENVIRONMENT
// ============================================================================

// Type environment (symbol table)
struct Env {
    bindings: [Binding; 256],
    count: i64,
    scope_depth: i64,
}

fn env_new() -> Env {
    Env {
        bindings: [binding_new(); 256],
        count: 0,
        scope_depth: 0,
    }
}

// Enter a new scope
fn env_enter_scope(env: Env) -> Env with Mut {
    var e = env;
    e.scope_depth = e.scope_depth + 1;
    e
}

// Leave the current scope (removes bindings at this depth)
fn env_leave_scope(env: Env) -> Env with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var e = env;

    // Remove bindings at current scope depth
    while e.count > 0 && e.bindings[(e.count - 1) as usize].scope_depth == e.scope_depth {
        e.count = e.count - 1;
    }

    e.scope_depth = e.scope_depth - 1;
    e
}

// Add a binding to the environment
fn env_bind(env: Env, b: Binding) -> Env with Panic, Mut {
    var e = env;
    if e.count < 256 {
        var binding = b;
        binding.scope_depth = e.scope_depth;
        e.bindings[e.count as usize] = binding;
        e.count = e.count + 1;
    }
    e
}

// Check if two names are equal
fn names_equal(a: [i8; 64], a_len: i64, b: [i8; 64], b_len: i64) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a_len != b_len {
        return false
    }
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < a_len {
        if a[i as usize] != b[i as usize] {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    true
}

// Lookup a binding by name (returns most recent match)
fn env_lookup(env: Env, name: [i8; 64], name_len: i64) -> Binding with Panic, Div, Mut {
    // Search from end (most recent) to beginning
    var i = env.count - 1;
    while i >= 0 {
        let b = env.bindings[i as usize];
        if names_equal(b.name, b.name_len, name, name_len) {
            return b
        }
        i = i - 1;
    }
    // Not found - return empty binding with -1 type
    binding_new()
}

// Check if a name exists in the current scope
fn env_exists_in_scope(env: Env, name: [i8; 64], name_len: i64) -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = env.count - 1;
    while i >= 0 {
        let b = env.bindings[i as usize];
        if b.scope_depth < env.scope_depth {
            // Reached outer scope
            return false
        }
        if names_equal(b.name, b.name_len, name, name_len) {
            return true
        }
        i = i - 1;
    }
    false
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn make_name(c0: i8, c1: i8, c2: i8, c3: i8, len: i64) -> [i8; 64] with Panic, Mut {
    var name: [i8; 64] = [0; 64];
    name[0] = c0;
    name[1] = c1;
    name[2] = c2;
    name[3] = c3;
    name
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_env_basic() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var env = env_new();

    // Create a name "x" (120 is 'x')
    let x_name = make_name(120, 0, 0, 0, 1);

    // Add binding for x: i32
    env = env_bind(env, binding_var(x_name, 1, 0, false, 0));

    if env.count != 1 {
        print("  Expected 1 binding\n");
        return false
    }

    // Lookup x
    let found = env_lookup(env, x_name, 1);
    if found.type_idx != 0 {
        print("  Should find x with type index 0\n");
        return false
    }

    // Lookup non-existent y (121 is 'y')
    let y_name = make_name(121, 0, 0, 0, 1);
    let not_found = env_lookup(env, y_name, 1);
    if not_found.type_idx != -1 {
        print("  Should not find y\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_env_scopes() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var env = env_new();

    let x_name = make_name(120, 0, 0, 0, 1);

    // Add x in global scope
    env = env_bind(env, binding_var(x_name, 1, 0, false, 0));

    // Enter inner scope
    env = env_enter_scope(env);

    // Add shadowing x in inner scope
    env = env_bind(env, binding_var(x_name, 1, 1, true, 1));

    // Lookup should find inner x
    let inner_x = env_lookup(env, x_name, 1);
    if inner_x.type_idx != 1 {
        print("  Should find inner x with type index 1\n");
        return false
    }

    if !inner_x.is_mutable {
        print("  Inner x should be mutable\n");
        return false
    }

    // Leave inner scope
    env = env_leave_scope(env);

    // Lookup should find outer x again
    let outer_x = env_lookup(env, x_name, 1);
    if outer_x.type_idx != 0 {
        print("  Should find outer x with type index 0\n");
        return false
    }

    if outer_x.is_mutable {
        print("  Outer x should not be mutable\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_env_exists_in_scope() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var env = env_new();

    let x_name = make_name(120, 0, 0, 0, 1);
    let y_name = make_name(121, 0, 0, 0, 1);

    // Add x in global scope
    env = env_bind(env, binding_var(x_name, 1, 0, false, 0));

    // Enter new scope
    env = env_enter_scope(env);

    // x should not exist in current scope (it's in outer)
    if env_exists_in_scope(env, x_name, 1) {
        print("  x should not be in current scope\n");
        return false
    }

    // Add y in current scope
    env = env_bind(env, binding_var(y_name, 1, 1, false, 1));

    // y should exist in current scope
    if !env_exists_in_scope(env, y_name, 1) {
        print("  y should be in current scope\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_function_bindings() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var env = env_new();

    // Function name "add" (97='a', 100='d', 100='d')
    let add_name = make_name(97, 100, 100, 0, 3);

    // Create function binding with return type index 0
    var fn_bind = binding_fn(add_name, 3, 0, 0);
    fn_bind.n_params = 2;
    fn_bind.param_types[0] = 1;  // First param type index
    fn_bind.param_types[1] = 1;  // Second param type index

    env = env_bind(env, fn_bind);

    // Lookup the function
    let found = env_lookup(env, add_name, 3);

    if found.kind != BIND_FN() {
        print("  Should find function binding\n");
        return false
    }

    if found.n_params != 2 {
        print("  Function should have 2 params\n");
        return false
    }

    if found.return_type_idx != 0 {
        print("  Wrong return type index\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// compiler::check::types — Type Representation
//
// Type system for the self-hosted Sounio type checker.

extern "C" {
    fn print(s: &str) -> ();
