// ============================================================================
// TYPE KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn TYPE_UNKNOWN() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TYPE_NEVER() -> i32 { 1 }
fn TYPE_UNIT() -> i32 { 2 }
fn TYPE_BOOL() -> i32 { 3 }
fn TYPE_I8() -> i32 { 4 }
fn TYPE_I16() -> i32 { 5 }
fn TYPE_I32() -> i32 { 6 }
fn TYPE_I64() -> i32 { 7 }
fn TYPE_U8() -> i32 { 8 }
fn TYPE_U16() -> i32 { 9 }
fn TYPE_U32() -> i32 { 10 }
fn TYPE_U64() -> i32 { 11 }
fn TYPE_F32() -> i32 { 12 }
fn TYPE_F64() -> i32 { 13 }
fn TYPE_USIZE() -> i32 { 14 }
fn TYPE_ISIZE() -> i32 { 15 }
fn TYPE_STRING() -> i32 { 16 }
fn TYPE_CHAR() -> i32 { 17 }
fn TYPE_REF() -> i32 { 18 }       // &T
fn TYPE_REF_MUT() -> i32 { 19 }   // &!T
fn TYPE_ARRAY() -> i32 { 20 }     // [T; N]
fn TYPE_SLICE() -> i32 { 21 }     // [T]
fn TYPE_TUPLE() -> i32 { 22 }     // (T1, T2, ...)
fn TYPE_STRUCT() -> i32 { 23 }
fn TYPE_ENUM() -> i32 { 24 }
fn TYPE_FN() -> i32 { 25 }        // fn(T) -> R
fn TYPE_VAR() -> i32 { 26 }       // Type variable for inference

// ============================================================================
// TYPE REPRESENTATION
// ============================================================================

// Represents a type in the type system
struct Type {
    kind: i32,
    // For composite types (ref, array, etc.) - index into type pool
    inner_idx: i64,
    // For arrays - the size
    array_size: i64,
    // For named types (struct/enum) - name
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    // For tuples/function params - element type indices
    elem_types: [i64; 8],
    n_elems: i64,
    // For functions - return type index
    return_type_idx: i64,
    // For type variables - unique ID
    var_id: i64,
}

fn type_new() -> Type {
    Type {
        kind: TYPE_UNKNOWN(),
        inner_idx: -1,
        array_size: 0,
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        elem_types: [-1; 8],
        n_elems: 0,
        return_type_idx: -1,
        var_id: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

fn type_unit() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_UNIT();
    t
}

fn type_bool() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_BOOL();
    t
}

fn type_i32() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_I32();
    t
}

fn type_i64() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_I64();
    t
}

fn type_f32() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_F32();
    t
}

fn type_f64() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_F64();
    t
}

fn type_string() -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_STRING();
    t
}

fn type_ref(inner_idx: i64) -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_REF();
    t.inner_idx = inner_idx;
    t
}

fn type_ref_mut(inner_idx: i64) -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_REF_MUT();
    t.inner_idx = inner_idx;
    t
}

fn type_array(inner_idx: i64, size: i64) -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_ARRAY();
    t.inner_idx = inner_idx;
    t.array_size = size;
    t
}

fn type_var(id: i64) -> Type with Mut {
    var t = type_new();
    t.kind = TYPE_VAR();
    t.var_id = id;
    t
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE POOL
// ============================================================================

// Pool for storing types (simulating heap allocation)
struct TypePool {
    types: [Type; 256],
    count: i64,
}

fn type_pool_new() -> TypePool {
    TypePool {
        types: [type_new(); 256],
        count: 0,
    }
}

fn type_pool_add(pool: TypePool, t: Type) -> TypePool with Mut, Panic {
    var p = pool;
    if p.count < 256 {
        p.types[p.count as usize] = t;
        p.count = p.count + 1;
    }
    p
}

fn type_pool_get(pool: TypePool, idx: i64) -> Type with Panic {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < pool.count {
        pool.types[idx as usize]
    } else {
        type_new()  // Return unknown type
    }
}

fn type_pool_last_idx(pool: TypePool) -> i64 {
    pool.count - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE COMPARISON
// ============================================================================

// Check if two types are equal
fn types_equal(a: Type, b: Type) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.kind != b.kind {
        return false
    }

    // Primitive types - just compare kind
    if a.kind == TYPE_UNIT() || a.kind == TYPE_BOOL() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_I8() || a.kind == TYPE_I16() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_I32() || a.kind == TYPE_I64() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_U8() || a.kind == TYPE_U16() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_U32() || a.kind == TYPE_U64() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_F32() || a.kind == TYPE_F64() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_USIZE() || a.kind == TYPE_ISIZE() ||
       a.kind == TYPE_STRING() || a.kind == TYPE_CHAR() {
        return true
    }

    // Reference types - compare inner
    if a.kind == TYPE_REF() || a.kind == TYPE_REF_MUT() {
        return a.inner_idx == b.inner_idx
    }

    // Array types - compare inner and size
    if a.kind == TYPE_ARRAY() {
        return a.inner_idx == b.inner_idx && a.array_size == b.array_size
    }

    // Type variables - compare ID
    if a.kind == TYPE_VAR() {
        return a.var_id == b.var_id
    }

    // Named types (struct/enum) - compare names
    if a.kind == TYPE_STRUCT() || a.kind == TYPE_ENUM() {
        if a.name_len != b.name_len {
            return false
        }
        var i: i64 = 0;
        while i < a.name_len {
            if a.name[i as usize] != b.name[i as usize] {
                return false
            }
            i = i + 1;
        }
        return true
    }

    // Default: assume not equal
    false
}

// Check if type is numeric
fn is_numeric(t: Type) -> bool {
    t.kind == TYPE_I8() || t.kind == TYPE_I16() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_I32() || t.kind == TYPE_I64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_U8() || t.kind == TYPE_U16() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_U32() || t.kind == TYPE_U64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_F32() || t.kind == TYPE_F64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_USIZE() || t.kind == TYPE_ISIZE()
}

// Check if type is integer
fn is_integer(t: Type) -> bool {
    t.kind == TYPE_I8() || t.kind == TYPE_I16() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_I32() || t.kind == TYPE_I64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_U8() || t.kind == TYPE_U16() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_U32() || t.kind == TYPE_U64() ||
    t.kind == TYPE_USIZE() || t.kind == TYPE_ISIZE()
}

// Check if type is floating point
fn is_float(t: Type) -> bool {
    t.kind == TYPE_F32() || t.kind == TYPE_F64()
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE PRINTING (for debugging)
// ============================================================================

fn print_type(t: Type) -> () {
    if t.kind == TYPE_UNKNOWN() { print("unknown") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_NEVER() { print("!") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_UNIT() { print("()") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_BOOL() { print("bool") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_I8() { print("i8") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_I16() { print("i16") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_I32() { print("i32") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_I64() { print("i64") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_U8() { print("u8") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_U16() { print("u16") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_U32() { print("u32") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_U64() { print("u64") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_F32() { print("f32") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_F64() { print("f64") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_USIZE() { print("usize") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_ISIZE() { print("isize") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_STRING() { print("string") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_CHAR() { print("char") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_REF() { print("&T") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_REF_MUT() { print("&!T") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_ARRAY() { print("[T; N]") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_VAR() { print("?T") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_STRUCT() { print("struct") }
    if t.kind == TYPE_ENUM() { print("enum") }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_primitive_types() -> bool with Mut {
    let unit_t = type_unit();
    let bool_t = type_bool();
    let i32_t = type_i32();
    let i64_t = type_i64();
    let f64_t = type_f64();

    // Unit is not numeric
    if is_numeric(unit_t) {
        print("  unit should not be numeric\n");
        return false
    }

    // Bool is not numeric
    if is_numeric(bool_t) {
        print("  bool should not be numeric\n");
        return false
    }

    // i32 is numeric and integer
    if !is_numeric(i32_t) {
        print("  i32 should be numeric\n");
        return false
    }

    if !is_integer(i32_t) {
        print("  i32 should be integer\n");
        return false
    }

    // f64 is numeric but not integer
    if !is_numeric(f64_t) {
        print("  f64 should be numeric\n");
        return false
    }

    if is_integer(f64_t) {
        print("  f64 should not be integer\n");
        return false
    }

    if !is_float(f64_t) {
        print("  f64 should be float\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_type_equality() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let i32_a = type_i32();
    let i32_b = type_i32();
    let i64_t = type_i64();

    if !types_equal(i32_a, i32_b) {
        print("  i32 should equal i32\n");
        return false
    }

    if types_equal(i32_a, i64_t) {
        print("  i32 should not equal i64\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_type_pool() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = type_pool_new();

    pool = type_pool_add(pool, type_i32());
    pool = type_pool_add(pool, type_i64());
    pool = type_pool_add(pool, type_bool());

    if pool.count != 3 {
        print("  Expected 3 types in pool\n");
        return false
    }

    let t0 = type_pool_get(pool, 0);
    if t0.kind != TYPE_I32() {
        print("  First type should be i32\n");
        return false
    }

    let t1 = type_pool_get(pool, 1);
    if t1.kind != TYPE_I64() {
        print("  Second type should be i64\n");
        return false
    }

    let t2 = type_pool_get(pool, 2);
    if t2.kind != TYPE_BOOL() {
        print("  Third type should be bool\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_ref_types() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = type_pool_new();

    // Add i32 to pool
    pool = type_pool_add(pool, type_i32());
    let i32_idx = type_pool_last_idx(pool);

    // Create &i32
    let ref_i32 = type_ref(i32_idx);

    if ref_i32.kind != TYPE_REF() {
        print("  Expected TYPE_REF\n");
        return false
    }

    if ref_i32.inner_idx != i32_idx {
        print("  Wrong inner type index\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_array_types() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = type_pool_new();

    pool = type_pool_add(pool, type_i32());
    let i32_idx = type_pool_last_idx(pool);

    // Create [i32; 10]
    let arr_t = type_array(i32_idx, 10);

    if arr_t.kind != TYPE_ARRAY() {
        print("  Expected TYPE_ARRAY\n");
        return false
    }

    if arr_t.inner_idx != i32_idx {
        print("  Wrong element type index\n");
        return false
    }

    if arr_t.array_size != 10 {
        print("  Wrong array size\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/codegen/bytecode.sio ===
// compiler::codegen::bytecode — Bytecode Generation
//
// Simple stack-based bytecode generator for the self-hosted compiler.
// Generates bytecode from typed expressions that can be executed
// by the VM in vm.sio.

extern "C" {
    fn print(s: &str) -> ();
}

// ============================================================================
// BYTECODE OPCODES
// ============================================================================

// Stack operations
fn OP_NOP() -> i32 { 0 }
fn OP_PUSH_I64() -> i32 { 1 }      // Push 64-bit integer constant
fn OP_PUSH_F64() -> i32 { 2 }      // Push 64-bit float constant
fn OP_PUSH_BOOL() -> i32 { 3 }     // Push boolean constant
fn OP_PUSH_UNIT() -> i32 { 4 }     // Push unit value
fn OP_POP() -> i32 { 5 }           // Pop top of stack
fn OP_DUP() -> i32 { 6 }           // Duplicate top of stack

// Local variable operations
fn OP_LOAD_LOCAL() -> i32 { 10 }   // Push local variable onto stack
fn OP_STORE_LOCAL() -> i32 { 11 }  // Pop stack into local variable

// Arithmetic operations (i64)
fn OP_ADD_I64() -> i32 { 20 }
fn OP_SUB_I64() -> i32 { 21 }
fn OP_MUL_I64() -> i32 { 22 }
fn OP_DIV_I64() -> i32 { 23 }
fn OP_REM_I64() -> i32 { 24 }
fn OP_NEG_I64() -> i32 { 25 }

// Arithmetic operations (f64)
fn OP_ADD_F64() -> i32 { 30 }
fn OP_SUB_F64() -> i32 { 31 }
fn OP_MUL_F64() -> i32 { 32 }
fn OP_DIV_F64() -> i32 { 33 }
fn OP_NEG_F64() -> i32 { 34 }

// Comparison operations
fn OP_EQ_I64() -> i32 { 40 }
fn OP_NE_I64() -> i32 { 41 }
fn OP_LT_I64() -> i32 { 42 }
fn OP_LE_I64() -> i32 { 43 }
fn OP_GT_I64() -> i32 { 44 }
fn OP_GE_I64() -> i32 { 45 }

// Logical operations
fn OP_NOT() -> i32 { 50 }
fn OP_AND() -> i32 { 51 }
fn OP_OR() -> i32 { 52 }

// Control flow
fn OP_JUMP() -> i32 { 60 }         // Unconditional jump
fn OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE() -> i32 { 61 }// Conditional jump
fn OP_CALL() -> i32 { 62 }         // Call function
fn OP_RET() -> i32 { 63 }          // Return from function

// Misc
fn OP_HALT() -> i32 { 99 }         // Stop execution

// ============================================================================
// BYTECODE BUFFER
// ============================================================================

// Buffer for holding generated bytecode
struct ByteCode {
    code: [i32; 1024],
    len: i64,
    // Constant pool for i64 values
    const_i64: [i64; 128],
    n_const_i64: i64,
    // Constant pool for f64 values
    const_f64: [f64; 128],
    n_const_f64: i64,
}

fn bytecode_new() -> ByteCode {
    ByteCode {
        code: [0; 1024],
        len: 0,
        const_i64: [0; 128],
        n_const_i64: 0,
        const_f64: [0.0; 128],
        n_const_f64: 0,
    }
}

// Emit a single opcode
fn emit_op(bc: ByteCode, op: i32) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.len < 1024 {
        b.code[b.len as usize] = op;
        b.len = b.len + 1;
    }
    b
}

// Emit an opcode with an i32 operand
fn emit_op_i32(bc: ByteCode, op: i32, operand: i32) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.len < 1023 {
        b.code[b.len as usize] = op;
        b.code[(b.len + 1) as usize] = operand;
        b.len = b.len + 2;
    }
    b
}

// Add an i64 constant and return its index
fn add_const_i64(bc: ByteCode, val: i64) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.n_const_i64 < 128 {
        b.const_i64[b.n_const_i64 as usize] = val;
        b.n_const_i64 = b.n_const_i64 + 1;
    }
    b
}

// Get the last constant index
fn last_const_i64_idx(bc: ByteCode) -> i32 {
    (bc.n_const_i64 - 1) as i32
}

// Add an f64 constant and return its index
fn add_const_f64(bc: ByteCode, val: f64) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.n_const_f64 < 128 {
        b.const_f64[b.n_const_f64 as usize] = val;
        b.n_const_f64 = b.n_const_f64 + 1;
    }
    b
}

fn last_const_f64_idx(bc: ByteCode) -> i32 {
    (bc.n_const_f64 - 1) as i32
}

// Get current code position (for jumps)
fn current_pos(bc: ByteCode) -> i32 {
    bc.len as i32
}

// Patch a jump target
fn patch_jump(bc: ByteCode, pos: i32, target: i32) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if pos >= 0 && (pos as i64) < b.len {
        b.code[pos as usize] = target;
    }
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPRESSION KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn EXPR_LITERAL() -> i32 { 0 }
fn EXPR_BINARY() -> i32 { 2 }
fn EXPR_UNARY() -> i32 { 3 }
fn EXPR_PATH() -> i32 { 1 }

// Literal kinds
fn LIT_INT() -> i32 { 0 }
fn LIT_FLOAT() -> i32 { 1 }
fn LIT_BOOL() -> i32 { 4 }
fn LIT_UNIT() -> i32 { 5 }

// Binary operators
fn BINOP_ADD() -> i32 { 0 }
fn BINOP_SUB() -> i32 { 1 }
fn BINOP_MUL() -> i32 { 2 }
fn BINOP_DIV() -> i32 { 3 }
fn BINOP_REM() -> i32 { 4 }
fn BINOP_AND() -> i32 { 5 }
fn BINOP_OR() -> i32 { 6 }
fn BINOP_EQ() -> i32 { 12 }
fn BINOP_NE() -> i32 { 13 }
fn BINOP_LT() -> i32 { 14 }
fn BINOP_LE() -> i32 { 15 }
fn BINOP_GT() -> i32 { 16 }
fn BINOP_GE() -> i32 { 17 }

// Unary operators
fn UNOP_NEG() -> i32 { 0 }
fn UNOP_NOT() -> i32 { 1 }

// Type kinds
fn TYPE_I64() -> i32 { 7 }
fn TYPE_F64() -> i32 { 13 }
fn TYPE_BOOL() -> i32 { 3 }

// ============================================================================
// EXPRESSION REPRESENTATION (simplified)
// ============================================================================

struct Type {
    kind: i32,
}

struct Expr {
    kind: i32,
    lit_kind: i32,
    lit_int: i64,
    lit_float: f64,
    lit_bool: bool,
    binop: i32,
    left_idx: i64,
    right_idx: i64,
    unop: i32,
    operand_idx: i64,
    name: [i8; 32],
    name_len: i64,
    inferred_type: Type,
}

fn expr_new() -> Expr {
    Expr {
        kind: EXPR_LITERAL(),
        lit_kind: LIT_UNIT(),
        lit_int: 0,
        lit_float: 0.0,
        lit_bool: false,
        binop: 0,
        left_idx: -1,
        right_idx: -1,
        unop: 0,
        operand_idx: -1,
        name: [0; 32],
        name_len: 0,
        inferred_type: Type { kind: TYPE_I64() },
    }
}

fn expr_int(val: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_LITERAL();
    e.lit_kind = LIT_INT();
    e.lit_int = val;
    e.inferred_type = Type { kind: TYPE_I64() };
    e
}

fn expr_float(val: f64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_LITERAL();
    e.lit_kind = LIT_FLOAT();
    e.lit_float = val;
    e.inferred_type = Type { kind: TYPE_F64() };
    e
}

fn expr_bool(val: bool) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_LITERAL();
    e.lit_kind = LIT_BOOL();
    e.lit_bool = val;
    e.inferred_type = Type { kind: TYPE_BOOL() };
    e
}

fn expr_binary_i64(op: i32, left: i64, right: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_BINARY();
    e.binop = op;
    e.left_idx = left;
    e.right_idx = right;
    e.inferred_type = Type { kind: TYPE_I64() };
    e
}

fn expr_unary(op: i32, operand: i64) -> Expr with Mut {
    var e = expr_new();
    e.kind = EXPR_UNARY();
    e.unop = op;
    e.operand_idx = operand;
    e.inferred_type = Type { kind: TYPE_I64() };
    e
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPRESSION POOL
// ============================================================================

struct ExprPool {
    exprs: [Expr; 128],
    count: i64,
}

fn expr_pool_new() -> ExprPool {
    ExprPool {
        exprs: [expr_new(); 128],
        count: 0,
    }
}

fn expr_pool_add(pool: ExprPool, e: Expr) -> ExprPool with Mut, Panic {
    var p = pool;
    if p.count < 128 {
        p.exprs[p.count as usize] = e;
        p.count = p.count + 1;
    }
    p
}

fn expr_pool_get(pool: ExprPool, idx: i64) -> Expr with Panic {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < pool.count {
        pool.exprs[idx as usize]
    } else {
        expr_new()
    }
}

fn expr_pool_last_idx(pool: ExprPool) -> i64 {
    pool.count - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// CODE GENERATION
// ============================================================================

// Generate bytecode for a literal expression
fn gen_literal(bc: ByteCode, e: Expr) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;

    if e.lit_kind == LIT_INT() {
        // Add constant to pool and emit push
        b = add_const_i64(b, e.lit_int);
        let idx = last_const_i64_idx(b);
        b = emit_op_i32(b, OP_PUSH_I64(), idx);
        return b
    }

    if e.lit_kind == LIT_FLOAT() {
        b = add_const_f64(b, e.lit_float);
        let idx = last_const_f64_idx(b);
        b = emit_op_i32(b, OP_PUSH_F64(), idx);
        return b
    }

    if e.lit_kind == LIT_BOOL() {
        if e.lit_bool {
            b = emit_op_i32(b, OP_PUSH_BOOL(), 1);
        } else {
            b = emit_op_i32(b, OP_PUSH_BOOL(), 0);
        }
        return b
    }

    if e.lit_kind == LIT_UNIT() {
        b = emit_op(b, OP_PUSH_UNIT());
        return b
    }

    b
}

// Generate bytecode for a binary expression
fn gen_binary(bc: ByteCode, pool: ExprPool, e: Expr) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;

    // Generate left operand
    let left_expr = expr_pool_get(pool, e.left_idx);
    b = gen_expr(b, pool, left_expr);

    // Generate right operand
    let right_expr = expr_pool_get(pool, e.right_idx);
    b = gen_expr(b, pool, right_expr);

    // Emit operator
    let ty = e.inferred_type.kind;
    let is_float = ty == TYPE_F64();

    if e.binop == BINOP_ADD() {
        if is_float {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_ADD_F64());
        } else {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_ADD_I64());
        }
    }

    if e.binop == BINOP_SUB() {
        if is_float {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_SUB_F64());
        } else {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_SUB_I64());
        }
    }

    if e.binop == BINOP_MUL() {
        if is_float {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_MUL_F64());
        } else {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_MUL_I64());
        }
    }

    if e.binop == BINOP_DIV() {
        if is_float {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_DIV_F64());
        } else {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_DIV_I64());
        }
    }

    if e.binop == BINOP_REM() {
        b = emit_op(b, OP_REM_I64());
    }

    // Comparisons
    if e.binop == BINOP_EQ() { b = emit_op(b, OP_EQ_I64()); }
    if e.binop == BINOP_NE() { b = emit_op(b, OP_NE_I64()); }
    if e.binop == BINOP_LT() { b = emit_op(b, OP_LT_I64()); }
    if e.binop == BINOP_LE() { b = emit_op(b, OP_LE_I64()); }
    if e.binop == BINOP_GT() { b = emit_op(b, OP_GT_I64()); }
    if e.binop == BINOP_GE() { b = emit_op(b, OP_GE_I64()); }

    // Logical
    if e.binop == BINOP_AND() { b = emit_op(b, OP_AND()); }
    if e.binop == BINOP_OR() { b = emit_op(b, OP_OR()); }

    b
}

// Generate bytecode for a unary expression
fn gen_unary(bc: ByteCode, pool: ExprPool, e: Expr) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;

    // Generate operand
    let operand_expr = expr_pool_get(pool, e.operand_idx);
    b = gen_expr(b, pool, operand_expr);

    // Emit operator
    let ty = e.inferred_type.kind;
    let is_float = ty == TYPE_F64();

    if e.unop == UNOP_NEG() {
        if is_float {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_NEG_F64());
        } else {
            b = emit_op(b, OP_NEG_I64());
        }
    }

    if e.unop == UNOP_NOT() {
        b = emit_op(b, OP_NOT());
    }

    b
}

// Generate bytecode for an expression
fn gen_expr(bc: ByteCode, pool: ExprPool, e: Expr) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    if e.kind == EXPR_LITERAL() {
        return gen_literal(bc, e)
    }

    if e.kind == EXPR_BINARY() {
        return gen_binary(bc, pool, e)
    }

    if e.kind == EXPR_UNARY() {
        return gen_unary(bc, pool, e)
    }

    bc
}

// ============================================================================
// DISASSEMBLER (for debugging)
// ============================================================================

fn print_opcode(op: i32) -> () {
    if op == OP_NOP() { print("NOP") }
    if op == OP_PUSH_I64() { print("PUSH_I64") }
    if op == OP_PUSH_F64() { print("PUSH_F64") }
    if op == OP_PUSH_BOOL() { print("PUSH_BOOL") }
    if op == OP_PUSH_UNIT() { print("PUSH_UNIT") }
    if op == OP_POP() { print("POP") }
    if op == OP_ADD_I64() { print("ADD_I64") }
    if op == OP_SUB_I64() { print("SUB_I64") }
    if op == OP_MUL_I64() { print("MUL_I64") }
    if op == OP_DIV_I64() { print("DIV_I64") }
    if op == OP_REM_I64() { print("REM_I64") }
    if op == OP_NEG_I64() { print("NEG_I64") }
    if op == OP_ADD_F64() { print("ADD_F64") }
    if op == OP_SUB_F64() { print("SUB_F64") }
    if op == OP_MUL_F64() { print("MUL_F64") }
    if op == OP_DIV_F64() { print("DIV_F64") }
    if op == OP_NEG_F64() { print("NEG_F64") }
    if op == OP_EQ_I64() { print("EQ_I64") }
    if op == OP_NE_I64() { print("NE_I64") }
    if op == OP_LT_I64() { print("LT_I64") }
    if op == OP_LE_I64() { print("LE_I64") }
    if op == OP_GT_I64() { print("GT_I64") }
    if op == OP_GE_I64() { print("GE_I64") }
    if op == OP_NOT() { print("NOT") }
    if op == OP_AND() { print("AND") }
    if op == OP_OR() { print("OR") }
    if op == OP_HALT() { print("HALT") }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_gen_int_literal() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    let e = expr_int(42);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, e);

    bc = gen_expr(bc, pool, e);

    if bc.len != 2 {
        print("  Expected 2 bytecode instructions\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[0] != OP_PUSH_I64() {
        print("  Expected PUSH_I64 opcode\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.n_const_i64 != 1 {
        print("  Expected 1 constant\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.const_i64[0] != 42 {
        print("  Constant should be 42\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_gen_binary_add() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // 10 + 20
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(10));
    let left_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(20));
    let right_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let add = expr_binary_i64(BINOP_ADD(), left_idx, right_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, add);

    bc = gen_expr(bc, pool, add);

    // Should have: PUSH_I64 0, PUSH_I64 1, ADD_I64
    if bc.len != 5 {
        print("  Expected 5 bytecode instructions\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[0] != OP_PUSH_I64() {
        print("  First should be PUSH_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[2] != OP_PUSH_I64() {
        print("  Third should be PUSH_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[4] != OP_ADD_I64() {
        print("  Last should be ADD_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_gen_unary_neg() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // -42
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(42));
    let operand_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let neg = expr_unary(UNOP_NEG(), operand_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, neg);

    bc = gen_expr(bc, pool, neg);

    // Should have: PUSH_I64 0, NEG_I64
    if bc.len != 3 {
        print("  Expected 3 bytecode instructions\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[0] != OP_PUSH_I64() {
        print("  First should be PUSH_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[2] != OP_NEG_I64() {
        print("  Last should be NEG_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_gen_comparison() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // 5 < 10
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(5));
    let left_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(10));
    let right_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    var lt = expr_new();
    lt.kind = EXPR_BINARY();
    lt.binop = BINOP_LT();
    lt.left_idx = left_idx;
    lt.right_idx = right_idx;
    lt.inferred_type = Type { kind: TYPE_BOOL() };
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, lt);

    bc = gen_expr(bc, pool, lt);

    // Should have: PUSH_I64 0, PUSH_I64 1, LT_I64
    if bc.len != 5 {
        print("  Expected 5 bytecode instructions\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[4] != OP_LT_I64() {
        print("  Last should be LT_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_gen_complex_expr() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var pool = expr_pool_new();
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // (1 + 2) * 3
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(1));
    let one_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(2));
    let two_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let add = expr_binary_i64(BINOP_ADD(), one_idx, two_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, add);
    let add_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, expr_int(3));
    let three_idx = expr_pool_last_idx(pool);

    let mul = expr_binary_i64(BINOP_MUL(), add_idx, three_idx);
    pool = expr_pool_add(pool, mul);

    bc = gen_expr(bc, pool, mul);

    // Should have: PUSH 1, PUSH 2, ADD, PUSH 3, MUL
    // = 8 instructions (3 pushes with operands = 6, plus ADD and MUL = 2)
    if bc.len != 8 {
        print("  Expected 8 bytecode instructions\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[4] != OP_ADD_I64() {
        print("  Position 4 should be ADD_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    if bc.code[7] != OP_MUL_I64() {
        print("  Position 7 should be MUL_I64\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/codegen/vm.sio ===
// compiler::codegen::vm — Stack-Based Virtual Machine
//
// Simple stack machine for executing bytecode generated by bytecode.sio.
// Provides a complete execution environment for the self-hosted compiler.

extern "C" {
    fn print(s: &str) -> ();
}

// ============================================================================
// BYTECODE OPCODES (same as bytecode.sio)
// ============================================================================

fn OP_NOP() -> i32 { 0 }
fn OP_PUSH_I64() -> i32 { 1 }
fn OP_PUSH_F64() -> i32 { 2 }
fn OP_PUSH_BOOL() -> i32 { 3 }
fn OP_PUSH_UNIT() -> i32 { 4 }
fn OP_POP() -> i32 { 5 }
fn OP_DUP() -> i32 { 6 }
fn OP_LOAD_LOCAL() -> i32 { 10 }
fn OP_STORE_LOCAL() -> i32 { 11 }
fn OP_ADD_I64() -> i32 { 20 }
fn OP_SUB_I64() -> i32 { 21 }
fn OP_MUL_I64() -> i32 { 22 }
fn OP_DIV_I64() -> i32 { 23 }
fn OP_REM_I64() -> i32 { 24 }
fn OP_NEG_I64() -> i32 { 25 }
fn OP_ADD_F64() -> i32 { 30 }
fn OP_SUB_F64() -> i32 { 31 }
fn OP_MUL_F64() -> i32 { 32 }
fn OP_DIV_F64() -> i32 { 33 }
fn OP_NEG_F64() -> i32 { 34 }
fn OP_EQ_I64() -> i32 { 40 }
fn OP_NE_I64() -> i32 { 41 }
fn OP_LT_I64() -> i32 { 42 }
fn OP_LE_I64() -> i32 { 43 }
fn OP_GT_I64() -> i32 { 44 }
fn OP_GE_I64() -> i32 { 45 }
fn OP_NOT() -> i32 { 50 }
fn OP_AND() -> i32 { 51 }
fn OP_OR() -> i32 { 52 }
fn OP_JUMP() -> i32 { 60 }
fn OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE() -> i32 { 61 }
fn OP_CALL() -> i32 { 62 }
fn OP_RET() -> i32 { 63 }
fn OP_HALT() -> i32 { 99 }

// ============================================================================
// VALUE REPRESENTATION
// ============================================================================

fn VAL_I64() -> i32 { 0 }
fn VAL_F64() -> i32 { 1 }
fn VAL_BOOL() -> i32 { 2 }
fn VAL_UNIT() -> i32 { 3 }

struct Value {
    kind: i32,
    i64_val: i64,
    f64_val: f64,
    bool_val: bool,
}

fn value_unit() -> Value {
    Value { kind: VAL_UNIT(), i64_val: 0, f64_val: 0.0, bool_val: false }
}

fn value_i64(v: i64) -> Value {
    Value { kind: VAL_I64(), i64_val: v, f64_val: 0.0, bool_val: false }
}

fn value_f64(v: f64) -> Value {
    Value { kind: VAL_F64(), i64_val: 0, f64_val: v, bool_val: false }
}

fn value_bool(v: bool) -> Value {
    Value { kind: VAL_BOOL(), i64_val: 0, f64_val: 0.0, bool_val: v }
}

fn value_as_i64(v: Value) -> i64 {
    v.i64_val
}

fn value_as_f64(v: Value) -> f64 {
    v.f64_val
}

fn value_as_bool(v: Value) -> bool {
    v.bool_val
}

// ============================================================================
// BYTECODE (same structure as bytecode.sio)
// ============================================================================

struct ByteCode {
    code: [i32; 1024],
    len: i64,
    const_i64: [i64; 128],
    n_const_i64: i64,
    const_f64: [f64; 128],
    n_const_f64: i64,
}

fn bytecode_new() -> ByteCode {
    ByteCode {
        code: [0; 1024],
        len: 0,
        const_i64: [0; 128],
        n_const_i64: 0,
        const_f64: [0.0; 128],
        n_const_f64: 0,
    }
}

fn emit_op(bc: ByteCode, op: i32) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.len < 1024 {
        b.code[b.len as usize] = op;
        b.len = b.len + 1;
    }
    b
}

fn emit_op_i32(bc: ByteCode, op: i32, operand: i32) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.len < 1023 {
        b.code[b.len as usize] = op;
        b.code[(b.len + 1) as usize] = operand;
        b.len = b.len + 2;
    }
    b
}

fn add_const_i64(bc: ByteCode, val: i64) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.n_const_i64 < 128 {
        b.const_i64[b.n_const_i64 as usize] = val;
        b.n_const_i64 = b.n_const_i64 + 1;
    }
    b
}

fn add_const_f64(bc: ByteCode, val: f64) -> ByteCode with Mut, Panic {
    var b = bc;
    if b.n_const_f64 < 128 {
        b.const_f64[b.n_const_f64 as usize] = val;
        b.n_const_f64 = b.n_const_f64 + 1;
    }
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// VIRTUAL MACHINE
// ============================================================================

struct VM {
    // Value stack
    stack: [Value; 256],
    sp: i64,  // Stack pointer
    // Local variables
    locals: [Value; 64],
    n_locals: i64,
    // Program counter
    pc: i64,
    // Halted flag
    halted: bool,
    // Error flag
    error: bool,
}

fn vm_new() -> VM {
    VM {
        stack: [value_unit(); 256],
        sp: 0,
        locals: [value_unit(); 64],
        n_locals: 0,
        pc: 0,
        halted: false,
        error: false,
    }
}

// Push a value onto the stack
fn vm_push(vm: VM, v: Value) -> VM with Mut, Panic {
    var m = vm;
    if m.sp < 256 {
        m.stack[m.sp as usize] = v;
        m.sp = m.sp + 1;
    } else {
        m.error = true;
    }
    m
}

// Pop a value from the stack
fn vm_pop(vm: VM) -> VM with Mut {
    var m = vm;
    if m.sp > 0 {
        m.sp = m.sp - 1;
    } else {
        m.error = true;
    }
    m
}

// Get the top value without popping
fn vm_top(vm: VM) -> Value with Panic {
    if vm.sp > 0 {
        vm.stack[(vm.sp - 1) as usize]
    } else {
        value_unit()
    }
}

// Get value at offset from top (0 = top, 1 = one below top, etc.)
fn vm_peek(vm: VM, offset: i64) -> Value with Panic {
    let idx = vm.sp - 1 - offset;
    if idx >= 0 {
        vm.stack[idx as usize]
    } else {
        value_unit()
    }
}

// Execute one instruction
fn vm_step(vm: VM, bc: ByteCode) -> VM with Mut, Panic {
    var m = vm;

    if m.pc >= bc.len || m.halted || m.error {
        m.halted = true;
        return m
    }

    let op = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
    m.pc = m.pc + 1;

    // NOP
    if op == OP_NOP() {
        return m
    }

    // PUSH_I64 idx
    if op == OP_PUSH_I64() {
        let idx = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = m.pc + 1;
        let val = bc.const_i64[idx as usize];
        m = vm_push(m, value_i64(val));
        return m
    }

    // PUSH_F64 idx
    if op == OP_PUSH_F64() {
        let idx = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = m.pc + 1;
        let val = bc.const_f64[idx as usize];
        m = vm_push(m, value_f64(val));
        return m
    }

    // PUSH_BOOL val
    if op == OP_PUSH_BOOL() {
        let val = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = m.pc + 1;
        m = vm_push(m, value_bool(val != 0));
        return m
    }

    // PUSH_UNIT
    if op == OP_PUSH_UNIT() {
        m = vm_push(m, value_unit());
        return m
    }

    // POP
    if op == OP_POP() {
        m = vm_pop(m);
        return m
    }

    // DUP
    if op == OP_DUP() {
        let top = vm_top(m);
        m = vm_push(m, top);
        return m
    }

    // LOAD_LOCAL idx
    if op == OP_LOAD_LOCAL() {
        let idx = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = m.pc + 1;
        if idx >= 0 && (idx as i64) < m.n_locals {
            m = vm_push(m, m.locals[idx as usize]);
        } else {
            m.error = true;
        }
        return m
    }

    // STORE_LOCAL idx
    if op == OP_STORE_LOCAL() {
        let idx = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = m.pc + 1;
        let val = vm_top(m);
        m = vm_pop(m);
        if idx >= 0 && (idx as i64) < 64 {
            m.locals[idx as usize] = val;
            if (idx as i64) >= m.n_locals {
                m.n_locals = (idx as i64) + 1;
            }
        } else {
            m.error = true;
        }
        return m
    }

    // Binary i64 operations
    if op == OP_ADD_I64() || op == OP_SUB_I64() || op == OP_MUL_I64() ||
       op == OP_DIV_I64() || op == OP_REM_I64() {
        let b = value_as_i64(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        let a = value_as_i64(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);

        var result: i64 = 0;
        if op == OP_ADD_I64() { result = a + b; }
        if op == OP_SUB_I64() { result = a - b; }
        if op == OP_MUL_I64() { result = a * b; }
        if op == OP_DIV_I64() {
            if b != 0 { result = a / b; } else { m.error = true; }
        }
        if op == OP_REM_I64() {
            if b != 0 { result = a % b; } else { m.error = true; }
        }

        m = vm_push(m, value_i64(result));
        return m
    }

    // NEG_I64
    if op == OP_NEG_I64() {
        let a = value_as_i64(vm_top(m));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        m = vm_push(m, value_i64(-a));
        return m
    }

    // Binary f64 operations
    if op == OP_ADD_F64() || op == OP_SUB_F64() || op == OP_MUL_F64() ||
       op == OP_DIV_F64() {
        let b = value_as_f64(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        let a = value_as_f64(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);

        var result: f64 = 0.0;
        if op == OP_ADD_F64() { result = a + b; }
        if op == OP_SUB_F64() { result = a - b; }
        if op == OP_MUL_F64() { result = a * b; }
        if op == OP_DIV_F64() { result = a / b; }

        m = vm_push(m, value_f64(result));
        return m
    }

    // NEG_F64
    if op == OP_NEG_F64() {
        let a = value_as_f64(vm_top(m));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        m = vm_push(m, value_f64(-a));
        return m
    }

    // Comparison operations
    if op == OP_EQ_I64() || op == OP_NE_I64() || op == OP_LT_I64() ||
       op == OP_LE_I64() || op == OP_GT_I64() || op == OP_GE_I64() {
        let b = value_as_i64(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        let a = value_as_i64(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);

        var result = false;
        if op == OP_EQ_I64() { result = a == b; }
        if op == OP_NE_I64() { result = a != b; }
        if op == OP_LT_I64() { result = a < b; }
        if op == OP_LE_I64() { result = a <= b; }
        if op == OP_GT_I64() { result = a > b; }
        if op == OP_GE_I64() { result = a >= b; }

        m = vm_push(m, value_bool(result));
        return m
    }

    // Logical operations
    if op == OP_NOT() {
        let a = value_as_bool(vm_top(m));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        m = vm_push(m, value_bool(!a));
        return m
    }

    if op == OP_AND() {
        let b = value_as_bool(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        let a = value_as_bool(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        m = vm_push(m, value_bool(a && b));
        return m
    }

    if op == OP_OR() {
        let b = value_as_bool(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        let a = value_as_bool(vm_peek(m, 0));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        m = vm_push(m, value_bool(a || b));
        return m
    }

    // JUMP offset
    if op == OP_JUMP() {
        let target = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = target as i64;
        return m
    }

    // JUMP_IF_FALSE offset
    if op == OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE() {
        let target = bc.code[m.pc as usize];
        m.pc = m.pc + 1;
        let cond = value_as_bool(vm_top(m));
        m = vm_pop(m);
        if !cond {
            m.pc = target as i64;
        }
        return m
    }

    // HALT
    if op == OP_HALT() {
        m.halted = true;
        return m
    }

    // Unknown opcode
    m.error = true;
    m
}

// Run until halted or error
fn vm_run(vm: VM, bc: ByteCode) -> VM with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var m = vm;
    while !m.halted && !m.error {
        m = vm_step(m, bc);
    }
    m
}

// Get the result (top of stack after execution)
fn vm_result(vm: VM) -> Value with Panic {
    vm_top(vm)
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_push_pop() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // Push 42
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 42);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 0);
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.kind != VAL_I64() {
        print("  Expected i64 value\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.i64_val != 42 {
        print("  Expected 42\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_add() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // 10 + 20
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 10);
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 20);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 0);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 1);
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_ADD_I64());
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.i64_val != 30 {
        print("  10 + 20 should be 30\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_arithmetic() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // (2 + 3) * 4 = 20
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 2);
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 3);
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 4);

    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 0);  // 2
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 1);  // 3
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_ADD_I64());          // 5
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 2);  // 4
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_MUL_I64());          // 20
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.i64_val != 20 {
        print("  (2 + 3) * 4 should be 20\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_comparison() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // 5 < 10 = true
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 5);
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 10);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 0);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 1);
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_LT_I64());
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.kind != VAL_BOOL() {
        print("  Expected bool value\n");
        return false
    }

    if !result.bool_val {
        print("  5 < 10 should be true\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_negation() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // -42
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 42);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 0);
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_NEG_I64());
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.i64_val != -42 {
        print("  -42 should be -42\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_logical() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // true && false = false
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_BOOL(), 1);  // true
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_BOOL(), 0);  // false
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_AND());
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.bool_val {
        print("  true && false should be false\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_locals() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // x = 42; x + 1
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 42);
    bc = add_const_i64(bc, 1);

    // Store 42 in local 0
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 0);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_STORE_LOCAL(), 0);

    // Load local 0, push 1, add
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_LOAD_LOCAL(), 0);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_I64(), 1);
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_ADD_I64());
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.i64_val != 43 {
        print("  42 + 1 should be 43\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

fn test_float() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var bc = bytecode_new();

    // 3.14 * 2.0
    bc = add_const_f64(bc, 3.14);
    bc = add_const_f64(bc, 2.0);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_F64(), 0);
    bc = emit_op_i32(bc, OP_PUSH_F64(), 1);
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_MUL_F64());
    bc = emit_op(bc, OP_HALT());

    var vm = vm_new();
    vm = vm_run(vm, bc);

    let result = vm_result(vm);
    if result.kind != VAL_F64() {
        print("  Expected f64 value\n");
        return false
    }

    // Check approximately equal (6.28)
    let diff = result.f64_val - 6.28;
    if diff < -0.001 || diff > 0.001 {
        print("  3.14 * 2.0 should be approximately 6.28\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/effects/compile_confidence.sio ===
//! stdlib/compiler/effects/compile_confidence.sio - Epistemic Tracking Utilities
//!
//! Higher-level confidence tracking for the compilation pipeline. Provides
//! structures and functions for modeling confidence levels across phases,
//! type complexity classification, bootstrap propagation, and attestation.

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE STEP
// ============================================================================

struct ProvenanceStep {
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    confidence: f32,
    timestamp: i64,
}

fn provenance_step_new() -> ProvenanceStep {
    ProvenanceStep {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        confidence: 0.0,
        timestamp: 0,
    }
}

fn provenance_step_with_conf(conf: f32, ts: i64) -> ProvenanceStep {
    ProvenanceStep {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        confidence: conf,
        timestamp: ts,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PIPELINE CONFIDENCE
// ============================================================================

struct PipelineConfidence {
    parse_conf: f32,      // Always 1.0 (deterministic)
    check_conf: f32,      // 0.80-0.99 based on type complexity
    emit_conf: f32,       // Typically 0.98
    total_conf: f32,      // Product of all phases
    phase_count: i32,
}

fn pipeline_confidence_new() -> PipelineConfidence {
    PipelineConfidence {
        parse_conf: 1.0,
        check_conf: 0.0,
        emit_conf: 0.0,
        total_conf: 1.0,
        phase_count: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE REPORT
// ============================================================================

struct ConfidenceReport {
    pipeline: PipelineConfidence,
    bootstrap_stage: i32,
    cross_validated: bool,
    attestation_chain: [ProvenanceStep; 16],
    n_attestations: i64,
}

fn confidence_report_new() -> ConfidenceReport {
    ConfidenceReport {
        pipeline: pipeline_confidence_new(),
        bootstrap_stage: 0,
        cross_validated: false,
        attestation_chain: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_attestations: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

let CONFIDENCE_PARSE: f32 = 1.0
let CONFIDENCE_CHECK_SIMPLE: f32 = 0.99
let CONFIDENCE_CHECK_POLY: f32 = 0.95
let CONFIDENCE_CHECK_HIGHER: f32 = 0.90
let CONFIDENCE_CHECK_UNDER: f32 = 0.80
let CONFIDENCE_EMIT: f32 = 0.98
let CONFIDENCE_SPECIALIZE: f32 = 0.95
let CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST: f32 = 1.04
let MAX_CONFIDENCE: f32 = 0.99

// ============================================================================
// TYPE COMPLEXITY LEVELS
// ============================================================================

let COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE: i32 = 0    // Monomorphic types
let COMPLEXITY_POLY: i32 = 1      // Polymorphic types
let COMPLEXITY_HIGHER: i32 = 2    // Higher-rank types
let COMPLEXITY_UNDER: i32 = 3     // Underconstrained

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Clamps a value between min and max
fn clamp_f32(val: f32, min_val: f32, max_val: f32) -> f32 {
    if val < min_val { min_val }
    else if val > max_val { max_val }
    else { val }
}

// Power function for f32 (simple integer exponent)
fn pow_f32(base: f32, exp: i32) -> f32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if exp == 0 { 1.0 }
    else if exp < 0 { 1.0 / pow_f32(base, -exp) }
    else {
        var result: f32 = 1.0
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < exp {
            result = result * base
            i = i + 1
        }
        result
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PHASE AGGREGATION
// ============================================================================

// Computes product of phase confidences
fn aggregate_confidence(parse: f32, check: f32, emit: f32) -> f32 {
    var total = parse * check * emit
    clamp_f32(total, 0.0, 1.0)
}

// Updates pipeline confidence for a specific phase
// Phases: 0=parse, 1=check, 2=emit
fn update_pipeline(p: PipelineConfidence, phase: i32, conf: f32) -> PipelineConfidence with Mut {
    let clamped_conf = clamp_f32(conf, 0.0, 1.0)
    var new_p = p

    if phase == 0 {
        new_p = PipelineConfidence {
            parse_conf: clamped_conf,
            check_conf: p.check_conf,
            emit_conf: p.emit_conf,
            total_conf: p.total_conf,
            phase_count: p.phase_count + 1,
        }
    } else if phase == 1 {
        new_p = PipelineConfidence {
            parse_conf: p.parse_conf,
            check_conf: clamped_conf,
            emit_conf: p.emit_conf,
            total_conf: p.total_conf,
            phase_count: p.phase_count + 1,
        }
    } else if phase == 2 {
        new_p = PipelineConfidence {
            parse_conf: p.parse_conf,
            check_conf: p.check_conf,
            emit_conf: clamped_conf,
            total_conf: p.total_conf,
            phase_count: p.phase_count + 1,
        }
    } else {
        new_p = p
    }

    // Recompute total
    let new_total = aggregate_confidence(new_p.parse_conf, new_p.check_conf, new_p.emit_conf)
    PipelineConfidence {
        parse_conf: new_p.parse_conf,
        check_conf: new_p.check_conf,
        emit_conf: new_p.emit_conf,
        total_conf: new_total,
        phase_count: new_p.phase_count,
    }
}

// Returns the total confidence from a PipelineConfidence
fn pipeline_total(p: PipelineConfidence) -> f32 {
    p.total_conf
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE COMPLEXITY
// ============================================================================

// Maps type complexity level to the corresponding check-phase confidence
fn confidence_for_complexity(complexity: i32) -> f32 {
    if complexity == COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE { CONFIDENCE_CHECK_SIMPLE }
    else if complexity == COMPLEXITY_POLY { CONFIDENCE_CHECK_POLY }
    else if complexity == COMPLEXITY_HIGHER { CONFIDENCE_CHECK_HIGHER }
    else if complexity == COMPLEXITY_UNDER { CONFIDENCE_CHECK_UNDER }
    else { CONFIDENCE_CHECK_SIMPLE }  // Default fallback
}

// Placeholder for sedenion-based type complexity analysis
fn classify_type_complexity_placeholder(type_hint: i32) -> i32 {
    // Clamp to valid range [0,3]
    if type_hint < COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE { COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE }
    else if type_hint > COMPLEXITY_UNDER { COMPLEXITY_UNDER }
    else { type_hint }
}

// ============================================================================
// BOOTSTRAP CONFIDENCE
// ============================================================================

// Computes bootstrap confidence for a given stage, propagating from parent
// Formula: parent_conf * (0.99 ^ stage)
fn bootstrap_confidence(stage: i32, parent_conf: f32) -> f32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var effective_stage = stage
    if effective_stage < 0 { effective_stage = 0 }
    let degradation = pow_f32(0.99, effective_stage)
    let result = parent_conf * degradation
    clamp_f32(result, 0.0, 1.0)
}

// Applies cross-validation boost, capped at MAX_CONFIDENCE
fn cross_validation_boost(conf: f32) -> f32 {
    let boosted = conf * CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST
    if boosted > MAX_CONFIDENCE { MAX_CONFIDENCE }
    else if boosted < 0.0 { 0.0 }
    else { boosted }
}

// Creates an attestation ProvenanceStep for a bootstrap stage
fn create_attestation(stage: i32, conf: f32, timestamp: i64) -> ProvenanceStep with Mut {
    var effective_ts = timestamp
    if effective_ts < 0 { effective_ts = 0 }

    ProvenanceStep {
        name: [0; 64],  // Name would be set externally
        name_len: 0,
        confidence: conf,
        timestamp: effective_ts,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// REPORTING
// ============================================================================

// Creates a full ConfidenceReport from pipeline and bootstrap stage
fn create_report(pipeline: PipelineConfidence, stage: i32) -> ConfidenceReport with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var effective_stage = stage
    if effective_stage < 0 { effective_stage = 0 }

    var report_total = pipeline.total_conf
    if effective_stage > 0 {
        // Apply bootstrap degradation
        report_total = bootstrap_confidence(effective_stage, pipeline.total_conf)
    }

    let adjusted_pipeline = PipelineConfidence {
        parse_conf: pipeline.parse_conf,
        check_conf: pipeline.check_conf,
        emit_conf: pipeline.emit_conf,
        total_conf: report_total,
        phase_count: pipeline.phase_count,
    }

    ConfidenceReport {
        pipeline: adjusted_pipeline,
        bootstrap_stage: effective_stage,
        cross_validated: false,
        attestation_chain: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_attestations: 0,
    }
}

// Adds a ProvenanceStep to a ConfidenceReport's attestation chain
fn add_attestation(r: ConfidenceReport, step: ProvenanceStep) -> ConfidenceReport with Mut, Panic {
    let current_n = r.n_attestations
    if current_n < 16 {
        var new_chain = r.attestation_chain
        new_chain[current_n as usize] = step
        ConfidenceReport {
            pipeline: r.pipeline,
            bootstrap_stage: r.bootstrap_stage,
            cross_validated: r.cross_validated,
            attestation_chain: new_chain,
            n_attestations: current_n + 1,
        }
    } else {
        r  // Chain full, return unchanged
    }
}

// Applies cross-validation to an existing report
fn apply_cross_validation(r: ConfidenceReport) -> ConfidenceReport {
    if !r.cross_validated {
        let boosted = cross_validation_boost(r.pipeline.total_conf)
        let new_pipeline = PipelineConfidence {
            parse_conf: r.pipeline.parse_conf,
            check_conf: r.pipeline.check_conf,
            emit_conf: r.pipeline.emit_conf,
            total_conf: boosted,
            phase_count: r.pipeline.phase_count,
        }
        ConfidenceReport {
            pipeline: new_pipeline,
            bootstrap_stage: r.bootstrap_stage,
            cross_validated: true,
            attestation_chain: r.attestation_chain,
            n_attestations: r.n_attestations,
        }
    } else {
        r
    }
}

// Validates a ConfidenceReport for consistency
fn validate_report(report: ConfidenceReport) -> bool {
    let computed_total = aggregate_confidence(
        report.pipeline.parse_conf,
        report.pipeline.check_conf,
        report.pipeline.emit_conf
    )

    // Allow some tolerance due to bootstrap degradation
    let diff = report.pipeline.total_conf - computed_total
    let abs_diff = if diff < 0.0 { -diff } else { diff }
    let total_valid = abs_diff < 0.1  // Relaxed tolerance

    let conf_valid = report.pipeline.parse_conf >= 0.0 && report.pipeline.parse_conf <= 1.0 &&
                     report.pipeline.check_conf >= 0.0 && report.pipeline.check_conf <= 1.0 &&
                     report.pipeline.emit_conf >= 0.0 && report.pipeline.emit_conf <= 1.0 &&
                     report.pipeline.total_conf >= 0.0 && report.pipeline.total_conf <= 1.0

    let attest_valid = report.n_attestations >= 0 && report.n_attestations <= 16

    total_valid && conf_valid && attest_valid
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/effects/compile.sio ===
//! stdlib/compiler/effects/compile.sio - Compile Effect Definition
//!
//! The Compile effect models compilation as an algebraic effect.
//! This is the foundation for the metacircular self-hosted compiler.
//!
//! Novel aspects:
//! - Compilation is an effect that can be handled/intercepted
//! - Each phase returns Knowledge<T> with confidence bounds
//! - Enables partial evaluation via effect interpretation
//! - Supports cross-stage persistence of provenance

// ============================================================================
// SEDENION AST TYPE (shared with sedenion_encoding.sio)
// ============================================================================

struct Sedenion {
    e0: f32, e1: f32, e2: f32, e3: f32,
    e4: f32, e5: f32, e6: f32, e7: f32,
    e8: f32, e9: f32, e10: f32, e11: f32,
    e12: f32, e13: f32, e14: f32, e15: f32,
}

fn sed_zero() -> Sedenion {
    Sedenion {
        e0: 0.0, e1: 0.0, e2: 0.0, e3: 0.0,
        e4: 0.0, e5: 0.0, e6: 0.0, e7: 0.0,
        e8: 0.0, e9: 0.0, e10: 0.0, e11: 0.0,
        e12: 0.0, e13: 0.0, e14: 0.0, e15: 0.0
    }
}

// A provenance step in the compilation chain
struct ProvenanceStep {
    name: [i8; 64],      // Step name (e.g., "parse", "check")
    name_len: i64,
    confidence: f32,      // Confidence of this step
    timestamp: i64,       // When step occurred (optional)
}

fn provenance_step_new() -> ProvenanceStep {
    ProvenanceStep {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        confidence: 1.0,
        timestamp: 0,
    }
}

fn provenance_step_from_name(name_bytes: [i8; 64], len: i64, conf: f32) -> ProvenanceStep {
    ProvenanceStep {
        name: name_bytes,
        name_len: len,
        confidence: conf,
        timestamp: 0,
    }
}

// Knowledge type: value with epistemic metadata
// Knowledge<T, epsilon, Phi> where epsilon is confidence and Phi is provenance
struct KnowledgeAST {
    value: Sedenion,               // The AST as sedenion
    confidence: f32,               // epsilon: confidence bound [0, 1]
    provenance: [ProvenanceStep; 16], // Phi: transformation chain
    n_provenance: i64,
    is_verified: bool,             // Has been cross-validated?
}

fn knowledge_ast_new(val: Sedenion) -> KnowledgeAST {
    KnowledgeAST {
        value: val,
        confidence: 1.0,
        provenance: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_provenance: 0,
        is_verified: false,
    }
}

fn knowledge_ast_with_confidence(k: KnowledgeAST, conf: f32) -> KnowledgeAST {
    KnowledgeAST {
        value: k.value,
        confidence: conf,
        provenance: k.provenance,
        n_provenance: k.n_provenance,
        is_verified: k.is_verified,
    }
}

fn knowledge_ast_add_provenance(k: KnowledgeAST, step: ProvenanceStep) -> KnowledgeAST with Mut, Panic {
    var new_prov = k.provenance
    let idx = k.n_provenance
    if idx < 16 {
        new_prov[idx as usize] = step
    }
    KnowledgeAST {
        value: k.value,
        confidence: k.confidence * step.confidence,  // Confidence compounds
        provenance: new_prov,
        n_provenance: if idx < 16 { idx + 1 } else { idx },
        is_verified: k.is_verified,
    }
}

fn knowledge_ast_mark_verified(k: KnowledgeAST) -> KnowledgeAST {
    KnowledgeAST {
        value: k.value,
        confidence: k.confidence,
        provenance: k.provenance,
        n_provenance: k.n_provenance,
        is_verified: true,
    }
}

    n_types: i64,

fn typed_ast_new(ast: Sedenion) -> TypedAST {

    is_verified: bool,
}

fn knowledge_typed_ast_new(val: TypedAST) -> KnowledgeTypedAST {
    KnowledgeTypedAST {
        value: val,
        confidence: 1.0,
        provenance: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_provenance: 0,
        is_verified: false,
    }
}

// Effect operation kinds
fn OP_PARSE() -> i32 { 0 }      // source -> AST
fn OP_CHECK() -> i32 { 1 }      // AST -> TypedAST
fn OP_EMIT() -> i32 { 2 }       // TypedAST -> Code
fn OP_SPECIALIZE() -> i32 { 3 } // Code + static_args -> Code

// An effect operation represents a pending compilation step
struct CompileOperation {
    kind: i32,
    // Input data (varies by operation kind)
    source_ptr: i64,        // For parse: pointer to source string
    source_len: i64,
    ast_input: Sedenion,    // For check: input AST
    typed_input: TypedAST,  // For emit: input typed AST
    code_input: Code,       // For specialize: input code
    // Static arguments for specialization
    static_args: [i64; 16],
    n_static_args: i64,
}

fn compile_op_parse(src_ptr: i64, src_len: i64) -> CompileOperation {
    CompileOperation {
        kind: OP_PARSE(),
        source_ptr: src_ptr,
        source_len: src_len,
        ast_input: sed_zero(),
        typed_input: typed_ast_new(sed_zero()),
        code_input: code_new(),
        static_args: [0; 16],
        n_static_args: 0,
    }
}

fn compile_op_check(ast: Sedenion) -> CompileOperation {
    CompileOperation {
        kind: OP_CHECK(),
        source_ptr: 0,
        source_len: 0,
        ast_input: ast,
        typed_input: typed_ast_new(sed_zero()),
        code_input: code_new(),
        static_args: [0; 16],
        n_static_args: 0,
    }
}

        source_ptr: 0,

    }

// ============================================================================
// STAGE TRACKING FOR BOOTSTRAP
// ============================================================================

// Bootstrap stage constants
fn STAGE_RUST() -> i32 { 0 }    // Stage 0: Rust compiler (trusted baseline)
fn STAGE_SELF1() -> i32 { 1 }   // Stage 1: Self-compiled by Stage 0
fn STAGE_SELF2() -> i32 { 2 }   // Stage 2: Self-compiled by Stage 1
fn STAGE_VERIFIED() -> i32 { 3 } // Stage 3+: Cross-validated

struct BootstrapStage {
    stage: i32,
    parent_stage: i32,        // Which stage compiled this
    confidence: f32,          // Accumulated confidence
    cross_validated: bool,    // Stage N == Stage N-1?
}

fn bootstrap_stage_new(stage: i32, parent: i32) -> BootstrapStage {
    BootstrapStage {
        stage: stage,
        parent_stage: parent,
        confidence: 1.0,
        cross_validated: false,
    }
}

// Confidence boost when cross-validation passes
fn CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST() -> f32 { 1.04 }  // ~4% confidence boost

fn bootstrap_mark_cross_validated(bs: BootstrapStage) -> BootstrapStage {
    let boosted = if bs.confidence * CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST() > 1.0 {
        0.99  // Cap at 99%
    } else {
        bs.confidence * CROSS_VALIDATION_BOOST()
    }
    BootstrapStage {
        stage: bs.stage,
        parent_stage: bs.parent_stage,
        confidence: boosted,
        cross_validated: true,
    }
}

    CompilationRequest {

        source_len: src_len,
        target_arch: target,

// Effect type system implementation for Sounio
// Simplified stub for bootstrap

fn EFFECT_IO() -> i32 { 0 }
fn EFFECT_MUT() -> i32 { 1 }
fn EFFECT_ALLOC() -> i32 { 2 }

fn EFFECT_ASYNC() -> i32 { 4 }
fn EFFECT_GPU() -> i32 { 5 }
fn EFFECT_PROB() -> i32 { 6 }
fn EFFECT_DIV() -> i32 { 7 }

struct EffectSet {
    mask: i64,
}

struct EffectVar {
    id: i64,
    lower_bound: i64,
    upper_bound: i64,
}

fn effect_singleton(kind: i32) -> EffectSet with Panic {
    EffectSet { mask: (1 << (kind as i64)) }
}

fn effect_union(e1: EffectSet, e2: EffectSet) -> EffectSet {
    EffectSet { mask: e1.mask | e2.mask }
}

fn effect_intersect(e1: EffectSet, e2: EffectSet) -> EffectSet {
    EffectSet { mask: e1.mask & e2.mask }
}

fn effect_complement(e: EffectSet) -> EffectSet {
    EffectSet { mask: !e.mask }
}

fn effect_subset(e1: EffectSet, e2: EffectSet) -> bool {
    (e1.mask & !e2.mask) == 0
}

fn effect_disjoint(e1: EffectSet, e2: EffectSet) -> bool {
    (e1.mask & e2.mask) == 0
}

fn effect_empty() -> EffectSet {
    EffectSet { mask: 0 }
}

fn effect_full() -> EffectSet {
    EffectSet { mask: -1 }
}

fn effect_is_empty(e: EffectSet) -> bool {
    e.mask == 0
}

struct EffectConstraint {
    left_id: i64,
    right_id: i64,
    operator: i32,
}

struct EffectConstraints {
    items: [EffectConstraint; 64],
    count: i64,
}

fn effect_constraints_new() -> EffectConstraints {
    EffectConstraints { items: [EffectConstraint { left_id: 0, right_id: 0, operator: 0 }; 64], count: 0 }
}

struct EffectSubstitution {
    vars: [i64; 32],
    values: [i64; 32],
    count: i64,
}

fn effect_substitution_new() -> EffectSubstitution {
    EffectSubstitution { vars: [0; 32], values: [0; 32], count: 0 }
}

struct EffectSignature {
    effect_set: EffectSet,
    effect_vars: [EffectVar; 8],
    n_effect_vars: i64,
}

fn effect_signature_new(mask: i64) -> EffectSignature {
    EffectSignature {
        effect_set: EffectSet { mask: mask },
        effect_vars: [EffectVar { id: 0, lower_bound: 0, upper_bound: 0 }; 8],
        n_effect_vars: 0,
    }
}

struct RowVariable {
    id: i64,
    tail: i64,
}

fn row_variable_new(id: i64, tail: i64) -> RowVariable {
    RowVariable { id: id, tail: tail }
}

struct Row {
    effects: EffectSet,
    tail_var: RowVariable,
}

fn row_new() -> Row {
    Row { effects: effect_empty(), tail_var: RowVariable { id: 0, tail: 0 } }
}

fn row_union(r1: Row, r2: Row) -> Row {
    Row { effects: effect_union(r1.effects, r2.effects), tail_var: r1.tail_var }

// stdlib/compiler/effects/handler.sio
// Effect Handlers & Capabilities Implementation
// Provides interception, masking, and security for effects in computations.

// Forward declarations for types used across the module
struct Region {
    start: i64,
    end: i64,
    permissions: i32,  // Bitmask: 1=read, 2=write, 4=execute
}

fn default_region() -> Region {
    Region { start: 0, end: 0, permissions: 0 }
}

struct Operation {
    op_type: i32,      // 0=IO read, 1=IO write, etc.
    args: [i64; 8],    // Up to 8 arguments
    n_args: i64,
}

fn default_operation() -> Operation {
    Operation { op_type: 0, args: [0; 8], n_args: 0 }
}

struct Computation {
    // Placeholder for computation representation (e.g., bytecode or AST index)
    code: i64,         // Index to computation code
    effects: i64,      // Bitmask of effects used
    result_type: i64,  // Index to result type
}

struct HandlerResult {
    value: i64,        // Generic value (tagged union placeholder)
    success: bool,
    masked_effects: i64,
}

struct TypeContext {
    // Placeholder for type system context
    types_capacity: i64,   // Capacity of types array
    n_types: i64,
    handlers: [i64; 32],  // Stack of handler indices
    n_handlers: i64,
}

// Core EffectHandler struct
struct EffectHandler {
    handled_effects: i64,  // Bitmask of effects this handler intercepts (e.g., 1=IO, 2=Alloc)
    handler_fn: i64,       // Index to the handler function in the runtime
    return_type_idx: i64,  // Index to the return type after handling
}

// IO Capability struct
struct IOCapability {
    level: i32,            // 0=read-only, 1=read-write, 2=full admin
    paths: [string; 16],   // Allowed paths
    n_paths: i64,
}

// Mutable reference capability struct
struct MutCapability {
    regions: [Region; 32], // Memory regions that can be mutated
    n_regions: i64,
}

// Overall capabilities struct
struct Capabilities {
    io_cap: IOCapability,
    mut_cap: MutCapability,
    alloc_cap: bool,       // Permission to allocate memory
    gpu_cap: bool,         // Permission to use GPU resources
    // Extensible: additional bools or structs can be added
}

// Handler implementation details
struct HandlerImpl {
    effect_kind: i32,      // Specific effect ID (e.g., 1 for IO)
    handler_name: [i8; 64], // Null-terminated name for debugging

    // Function pointers as indices (resolved at runtime)
    handle_op: i64,        // Index to handle_op function: (*i64) -> i64
    resume_fn: i64,        // Index to resume function: (*i64) -> i64
}

// Continuation-based handler for resumable effects
struct ContinuationHandler {
    state: i64,            // Current state of the continuation
    operations: [Operation; 16], // Pending operations
    n_ops: i64,
}

// Example handler function for IO effects (placeholder implementation)
fn handle_io(comp: Computation) -> HandlerResult with Panic {
    // Simulate intercepting IO effects in comp
    // In real impl, this would push a handler and execute comp.code
    var result: HandlerResult = HandlerResult { value: 0, success: true, masked_effects: comp.effects & 1 }; // Mask IO bit (1)
    // Execute computation with interception (pseudocode)
    // execute_with_intercept(comp.code, current_handler_stack());
    result
}

// Mock implementation for testing (e.g., file read)
fn mock_read_file(path: string) -> string with Panic {
    // In test mode, return static mock data instead of real IO
    // This would be called by an IO handler intercepting a read op
    "mock file content\nLine 2: simulated data"
}

// Register a handler for a specific effect in the type context
fn register_handler(ctx: &!TypeContext, effect: i32, handler: HandlerImpl) -> bool with Panic, Mut {
    // Push handler index onto the stack (assume handlers stored globally or in ctx)
    if ctx.n_handlers >= 32 {
        return false;  // Stack overflow
    }
    // Store handler (pseudocode: ctx.handlers[ctx.n_handlers] = handler_index())
    ctx.n_handlers = ctx.n_handlers + 1;
    true
}

// Execute a computation under a specific effect handler
fn with_handler(handler: EffectHandler, comp: Computation) -> HandlerResult with Panic {
    // Simplified stub: in real impl, would push handler, execute computation, pop handler
    var result: HandlerResult = HandlerResult { value: 0, success: true, masked_effects: comp.effects & (-1 - handler.handled_effects) };
    result
}

// Mask a specific effect from an effect set (bitmask operation)
fn mask_effect(effect_set: i64, effect_to_mask: i32) -> i64 with Panic {
    var bit: i64 = 1 << (effect_to_mask as i64);
    effect_set & (-1 - bit)
}

// Yield control to handler for an effect operation (continuation style)
fn yield_effect(op: Operation) -> HandlerResult with Panic, Mut {
    // Pause current computation and invoke handler
    var current_handler: HandlerImpl = get_top_handler();  // Runtime stack access
    if current_handler.effect_kind != op.op_type {
        return HandlerResult { value: 0, success: false, masked_effects: 0 };
    }

    // Invoke handler's handle_op (pseudocode)
    var handler_result: i64 = invoke_fn(current_handler.handle_op, &!op);

    // Prepare continuation
    var cont_handler: ContinuationHandler = ContinuationHandler {
        state: 0,  // Suspended
        operations: [default_operation(); 16],
        n_ops: 1,
    };
    cont_handler.operations[0] = op;
    cont_handler.operations[0].n_args = op.n_args;  // Copy op

    // Return suspended result
    HandlerResult { value: handler_result, success: true, masked_effects: 1 << (op.op_type as i64) }
}

// Resume a continuation from a yielded state
fn resume_from_yield(state: i64) -> i64 with Panic, Mut {
    // Get continuation handler from state (assume state encodes handler index)
    var cont: ContinuationHandler = load_continuation(state);
    if cont.n_ops == 0 {
        return 0;  // No ops to resume
    }

    // Invoke resume function on top handler
    var top_handler: HandlerImpl = get_top_handler();
    var resume_result: i64 = invoke_fn(top_handler.resume_fn, &!cont);

    // Update state and continue execution
    cont.state = 1;  // Resumed
    store_continuation(state, cont);
    resume_result
}

// Check IO capability for a specific operation on a path
fn check_io_capability(cap: IOCapability, path: string, op: i32) -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Check level for write ops
    if op == 1 && cap.level < 1 {
        return false;  // No write permission
    }

    // Check if path is in allowed list
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < cap.n_paths {
        if paths_equal(cap.paths[i as usize], path) {
            return true;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    false
}

// Simple string equality check (placeholder; real impl would compare lengths and chars)
fn paths_equal(p1: string, p2: string) -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Assume string has len and data fields
    if p1.len != p2.len {
        return false;
    }
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < p1.len {
        if p1.data[i as usize] != p2.data[i as usize] {
            return false;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    true
}

// Restrict an IO capability to a subset of paths
fn restrict_io(cap: IOCapability, allowed_paths: [string; 16], n: i64) -> IOCapability with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var new_cap: IOCapability = cap;
    new_cap.n_paths = n;
    if n > 16 {
        new_cap.n_paths = 16;  // Cap at array size
    }
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < new_cap.n_paths {
        new_cap.paths[i as usize] = allowed_paths[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    // Optionally downgrade level if needed
    if n == 0 {
        new_cap.level = 0;
    }
    new_cap
}

// Compose two effect handlers (bitwise OR effects, combine functions)
fn compose_handlers(h1: EffectHandler, h2: EffectHandler) -> EffectHandler with Panic {
    EffectHandler {
        handled_effects: h1.handled_effects | h2.handled_effects,
        handler_fn: if h1.handler_fn != -1 { h1.handler_fn } else { h2.handler_fn },
        return_type_idx: if h1.return_type_idx != -1 { h1.return_type_idx } else { h2.return_type_idx },
    }
}

// Stack multiple handlers by composing them sequentially
fn stack_handlers(handlers: [EffectHandler; 8], n: i64) -> EffectHandler with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var result: EffectHandler = EffectHandler {
        handled_effects: 0,
        handler_fn: -1,
        return_type_idx: -1,
    };
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < n {
        result = compose_handlers(result, handlers[i as usize]);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    result
}

// Additional utility for capability management: Check mutation capability
fn check_mut_capability(cap: MutCapability, region_start: i64, op: i32) -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // op: 0=read (always allowed if region matches), 1=write
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < cap.n_regions {
        let r: Region = cap.regions[i as usize];
        if region_start >= r.start && region_start < r.end {
            if op == 1 && (r.permissions & 2) == 0 {
                return false;  // No write perm
            }
            return true;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    false
}

// Restrict mutation capability
fn restrict_mut(cap: MutCapability, allowed_regions: [Region; 32], n: i64) -> MutCapability with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var new_cap: MutCapability = cap;
    new_cap.n_regions = n;
    if n > 32 {
        new_cap.n_regions = 32;
    }
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < new_cap.n_regions {
        new_cap.regions[i as usize] = allowed_regions[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    new_cap
}

// Example: Create default capabilities
fn default_capabilities() -> Capabilities with Panic {
    Capabilities {
        io_cap: IOCapability { level: 0, paths: [""; 16], n_paths: 0 },
        mut_cap: MutCapability { regions: [default_region(); 32], n_regions: 0 },
        alloc_cap: false,
        gpu_cap: false,
    }
}

// Check overall capabilities for an effect (wrapper)
fn check_capabilities(caps: Capabilities, effect: i32, args: [i64; 4]) -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if effect == 1 {  // IO
        let path_idx: i64 = args[0];
        let path: string = resolve_string(path_idx);
        let op: i32 = args[1] as i32;
        check_io_capability(caps.io_cap, path, op)
    } else if effect == 2 {  // Mut
        let region_start: i64 = args[0];
        let op: i32 = args[1] as i32;
        check_mut_capability(caps.mut_cap, region_start, op)
    } else if effect == 3 {  // Alloc
        caps.alloc_cap
    } else if effect == 4 {  // GPU
        caps.gpu_cap
    } else {
        false
    }
}

// Compose capabilities (restrictive AND)
fn compose_capabilities(c1: Capabilities, c2: Capabilities) -> Capabilities with Panic, Mut, Div {
    Capabilities {
        io_cap: restrict_io(c1.io_cap, c2.io_cap.paths, c2.io_cap.n_paths),  // Use c2's paths as restriction
        mut_cap: restrict_mut(c1.mut_cap, c2.mut_cap.regions, c2.mut_cap.n_regions),
        alloc_cap: c1.alloc_cap && c2.alloc_cap,
        gpu_cap: c1.gpu_cap && c2.gpu_cap,
    }
}

// Mask effects in a computation's type (utility)
fn mask_computation_effects(comp: Computation, mask: i64) -> Computation with Panic, Mut {
    comp.effects = comp.effects & (-1 - mask);
    comp
}

// Example usage in a larger context: Run computation with capabilities
fn run_with_capabilities(caps: Capabilities, comp: Computation) -> HandlerResult with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Check if comp.effects are allowed by caps
    var allowed: bool = true;
    var effect_bit: i64 = 1;
    var i: i32 = 0;
    while i < 64 {  // Check each bit
        if (comp.effects & effect_bit) != 0 {
            let args: [i64; 4] = extract_effect_args(comp, i as i32);  // Placeholder
            if !check_capabilities(caps, i as i32, args) {
                allowed = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        effect_bit = effect_bit << 1;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    if !allowed {
        return HandlerResult { value: 0, success: false, masked_effects: 0 };
    }

    // Proceed with execution (using default handler if none specified)
    let default_handler: EffectHandler = EffectHandler { handled_effects: comp.effects, handler_fn: 0, return_type_idx: comp.result_type };
    with_handler(default_handler, comp)
}

    [0; 4]
}

fn resolve_string(idx: i64) -> string with Panic {
    ""  // Empty string
}

    // Simulate allocation under caps

}

struct EffectCheckResult {
    declared_effects: i64,
    inferred_effects: i64,
    is_consistent: bool,
}

        declared_effects: declared,
        inferred_effects: inferred,
        is_consistent: (inferred & !declared) == 0,

    result
