// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/epistemic/confidence_metadata.sio ===
//! Epistemic confidence metadata for type checking
//!
//! This module defines metadata types that attach to AST nodes, types, and
//! unification constraints during type checking. It bridges the runtime
//! `Knowledge<T>` system with compile-time type inference.

use core::{Option, Result};
use epistemic::knowledge::{BetaConfidence};
use compiler::types::{TypeId, TypeVar};
use compiler::ast::{NodeId, Span};

// ============================================================================
// 1. ConfidenceLevel - Discrete confidence levels
// ============================================================================

pub enum ConfidenceLevel {
    Certain,      // Proven (literals, explicit annotations)
    High,         // Strong inference from constraints
    Medium,       // Standard type inference
    Low,          // Defaulting or partial constraints
    Uncertain,    // Speculative or ambiguous
}

impl ConfidenceLevel {
    pub fn to_beta(self: &ConfidenceLevel) -> BetaConfidence {
        match self {
            ConfidenceLevel::Certain => BetaConfidence::strong(0.99, 1000.0),
            ConfidenceLevel::High => BetaConfidence::strong(0.85, 100.0),
            ConfidenceLevel::Medium => BetaConfidence::strong(0.65, 50.0),
            ConfidenceLevel::Low => BetaConfidence::strong(0.40, 20.0),
            ConfidenceLevel::Uncertain => BetaConfidence::strong(0.20, 10.0),
        }
    }

    pub fn from_beta(b: &BetaConfidence) -> ConfidenceLevel {
        let m = b.mean()
        if m >= 0.90 {
            ConfidenceLevel::Certain
        } else if m >= 0.75 {
            ConfidenceLevel::High
        } else if m >= 0.55 {
            ConfidenceLevel::Medium
        } else if m >= 0.30 {
            ConfidenceLevel::Low
        } else {
            ConfidenceLevel::Uncertain
        }
    }

    pub fn combine(self: &ConfidenceLevel, other: &ConfidenceLevel) -> ConfidenceLevel {
        let self_val = self.to_value()
        let other_val = other.to_value()
        let min_val = if self_val < other_val { self_val } else { other_val }
        ConfidenceLevel::from_value(min_val)
    }

    fn to_value(self: &ConfidenceLevel) -> i32 {
        match self {
            ConfidenceLevel::Certain => 5,
            ConfidenceLevel::High => 4,
            ConfidenceLevel::Medium => 3,
            ConfidenceLevel::Low => 2,
            ConfidenceLevel::Uncertain => 1,
        }
    }

    fn from_value(val: i32) -> ConfidenceLevel {
        if val >= 5 { ConfidenceLevel::Certain }
        else if val >= 4 { ConfidenceLevel::High }
        else if val >= 3 { ConfidenceLevel::Medium }
        else if val >= 2 { ConfidenceLevel::Low }
        else { ConfidenceLevel::Uncertain }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 2. InferenceSource - Where did this inference come from?
// ============================================================================

pub enum InferenceSource {
    Annotation { node: NodeId, span: Span },
    Literal { node: NodeId, value: string },
    Unification { lhs: TypeId, rhs: TypeId },
    ReturnType { fn_id: NodeId },
    Default { reason: string },
    Refinement { constraint: string },
    Effect { effect: string },
    External { module: string },
}

impl InferenceSource {
    pub fn confidence_level(self: &InferenceSource) -> ConfidenceLevel {
        match self {
            InferenceSource::Annotation { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::Certain,
            InferenceSource::Literal { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::Certain,
            InferenceSource::ReturnType { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::High,
            InferenceSource::Refinement { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::High,
            InferenceSource::Effect { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::Medium,
            InferenceSource::Unification { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::Medium,
            InferenceSource::Default { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::Low,
            InferenceSource::External { .. } => ConfidenceLevel::Uncertain,
        }
    }

    pub fn span(self: &InferenceSource) -> Option<Span> {
        match self {
            InferenceSource::Annotation { span, .. } => Option::Some(span),
            _ => Option::None,
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 3. InferenceStep - Single step in provenance chain
// ============================================================================

pub struct InferenceStep {
    operation: string,
    from_type: Option<TypeId>,
    to_type: TypeId,
    decay_factor: f64,
    reason: string,
}

impl InferenceStep {
    pub fn new(op: string, to: TypeId, reason: string) -> InferenceStep {
        InferenceStep {
            operation: op,
            from_type: Option::None,
            to_type: to,
            decay_factor: 1.0,
            reason: reason,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_from(self: InferenceStep, from: TypeId) -> InferenceStep {
        InferenceStep {
            operation: self.operation,
            from_type: Option::Some(from),
            to_type: self.to_type,
            decay_factor: self.decay_factor,
            reason: self.reason,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_decay(self: InferenceStep, factor: f64) -> InferenceStep {
        InferenceStep {
            operation: self.operation,
            from_type: self.from_type,
            to_type: self.to_type,
            decay_factor: factor,
            reason: self.reason,
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 4. TypeConfidenceMetadata - Confidence for a type
// ============================================================================

pub struct TypeConfidenceMetadata {
    type_id: TypeId,
    confidence: ConfidenceLevel,
    beta: BetaConfidence,
    source: InferenceSource,
    provenance: Vec<InferenceStep>,
    is_annotated: bool,
}

impl TypeConfidenceMetadata {
    pub fn new(type_id: TypeId, source: InferenceSource) -> TypeConfidenceMetadata {
        let conf_level = source.confidence_level()
        TypeConfidenceMetadata {
            type_id: type_id,
            confidence: conf_level,
            beta: conf_level.to_beta(),
            source: source,
            provenance: Vec::new(),
            is_annotated: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn certain(type_id: TypeId, node: NodeId) -> TypeConfidenceMetadata {
        let source = InferenceSource::Literal {
            node: node,
            value: "certain",
        }
        TypeConfidenceMetadata {
            type_id: type_id,
            confidence: ConfidenceLevel::Certain,
            beta: ConfidenceLevel::Certain.to_beta(),
            source: source,
            provenance: Vec::new(),
            is_annotated: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn annotated(type_id: TypeId, node: NodeId, span: Span) -> TypeConfidenceMetadata {
        let source = InferenceSource::Annotation {
            node: node,
            span: span,
        }
        TypeConfidenceMetadata {
            type_id: type_id,
            confidence: ConfidenceLevel::Certain,
            beta: ConfidenceLevel::Certain.to_beta(),
            source: source,
            provenance: Vec::new(),
            is_annotated: true,
        }
    }

    pub fn update_confidence(self: &!TypeConfidenceMetadata, conf: ConfidenceLevel) {
        self.confidence = conf
        self.beta = conf.to_beta()
    }

    pub fn add_step(self: &!TypeConfidenceMetadata, step: InferenceStep) {
        self.provenance.push(step)
    }

    pub fn decay(self: &TypeConfidenceMetadata, factor: f64) -> TypeConfidenceMetadata {
        let new_beta = self.beta.decay(factor)
        let new_conf = ConfidenceLevel::from_beta(&new_beta)
        TypeConfidenceMetadata {
            type_id: self.type_id,
            confidence: new_conf,
            beta: new_beta,
            source: self.source,
            provenance: self.provenance,
            is_annotated: self.is_annotated,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_certain(self: &TypeConfidenceMetadata) -> bool {
        match self.confidence {
            ConfidenceLevel::Certain => true,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_reliable(self: &TypeConfidenceMetadata) -> bool {
        self.confidence.to_value() >= 4
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 5. ConstraintConfidence - Confidence in unification constraint
// ============================================================================

pub struct ConstraintConfidence {
    lhs: TypeId,
    rhs: TypeId,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    source: InferenceSource,
    is_explicit: bool,
}

impl ConstraintConfidence {
    pub fn new(lhs: TypeId, rhs: TypeId, source: InferenceSource) -> ConstraintConfidence {
        let conf_level = source.confidence_level()
        ConstraintConfidence {
            lhs: lhs,
            rhs: rhs,
            confidence: conf_level.to_beta(),
            source: source,
            is_explicit: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn explicit(lhs: TypeId, rhs: TypeId, node: NodeId, span: Span) -> ConstraintConfidence {
        let source = InferenceSource::Annotation {
            node: node,
            span: span,
        }
        ConstraintConfidence {
            lhs: lhs,
            rhs: rhs,
            confidence: BetaConfidence::strong(0.99, 1000.0),
            source: source,
            is_explicit: true,
        }
    }

    pub fn implicit(lhs: TypeId, rhs: TypeId) -> ConstraintConfidence {
        let source = InferenceSource::Unification { lhs: lhs, rhs: rhs }
        ConstraintConfidence {
            lhs: lhs,
            rhs: rhs,
            confidence: BetaConfidence::uniform(),
            source: source,
            is_explicit: false,
        }
    }

    pub fn combine(self: &ConstraintConfidence, other: &ConstraintConfidence) -> ConstraintConfidence {
        let combined = self.confidence.combine(&other.confidence)
        ConstraintConfidence {
            lhs: self.lhs,
            rhs: self.rhs,
            confidence: combined,
            source: self.source,
            is_explicit: self.is_explicit || other.is_explicit,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_reliable(self: &ConstraintConfidence) -> bool {
        self.confidence.mean() >= 0.75
    }
}

    default_decay: f64,
}

impl ConfidenceContext {

        ConfidenceContext {
            default_confidence: ConfidenceLevel::Medium,
            default_decay: 0.95,
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 7. Helper functions
// ============================================================================

fn source_to_confidence(source: &InferenceSource) -> ConfidenceLevel {
    source.confidence_level()
}

fn combine_confidences(levels: &[ConfidenceLevel]) -> ConfidenceLevel {
    if levels.len() == 0 {
        return ConfidenceLevel::Uncertain
    }
    var result = levels[0]
    var i = 1
    while i < levels.len() {
        result = result.combine(&levels[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn decay_confidence(level: ConfidenceLevel, factor: f64) -> ConfidenceLevel {
    let beta = level.to_beta()
    let decayed = beta.decay(factor)
    ConfidenceLevel::from_beta(&decayed)
}

fn is_reliable_confidence(level: ConfidenceLevel) -> bool {
    level.to_value() >= 4
}

struct TypedAST {
    ast: Sedenion,
    type_info: [i64; 64],
    n_types: i64,
}

fn typed_ast_new(ast: Sedenion) -> TypedAST {
    TypedAST {
        ast: ast,
        type_info: [0; 64],
        n_types: 0,
    }
}

struct KnowledgeTypedAST {
    value: TypedAST,
    confidence: f32,
    provenance: [ProvenanceStep; 16],
    n_provenance: i64,
    is_verified: bool,
}

fn knowledge_typed_ast_new(val: TypedAST) -> KnowledgeTypedAST {
    KnowledgeTypedAST {
        value: val,
        confidence: 1.0,
        provenance: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_provenance: 0,
        is_verified: false,
    }
}

struct Code {
    bytes: [i8; 4096],
    len: i64,
    target: i32,
}

fn code_new() -> Code {
    Code {
        bytes: [0; 4096],
        len: 0,
        target: 0,
    }
}

struct KnowledgeCode {
    value: Code,
    confidence: f32,
    provenance: [ProvenanceStep; 16],
    n_provenance: i64,
    is_verified: bool,
}

fn knowledge_code_new(val: Code) -> KnowledgeCode {
    KnowledgeCode {
        value: val,
        confidence: 1.0,
        provenance: [provenance_step_new(); 16],
        n_provenance: 0,
        is_verified: false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HANDLER STATE
// ============================================================================

// Target architecture constants
fn TARGET_X86_64() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TARGET_AARCH64() -> i32 { 1 }

// SelfHost handler state
struct SelfHostHandler {
    target_arch: i32,
    opt_level: i32,
    emit_debug: bool,
    stage: i32,                   // Bootstrap stage
    accumulated_confidence: f32,   // Running confidence product
    operations: i64,               // Number of operations performed
    errors: [i32; 64],             // Error codes if any
    n_errors: i64,
}

fn selfhost_handler_new(target: i32) -> SelfHostHandler {
    SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: target,
        opt_level: 2,
        emit_debug: false,
        stage: 0,
        accumulated_confidence: 1.0,
        operations: 0,
        errors: [0; 64],
        n_errors: 0,
    }
}

fn selfhost_handler_for_x86() -> SelfHostHandler {
    selfhost_handler_new(TARGET_X86_64())
}

fn selfhost_handler_for_arm() -> SelfHostHandler {
    selfhost_handler_new(TARGET_AARCH64())
}

fn selfhost_handler_with_stage(h: SelfHostHandler, stage: i32) -> SelfHostHandler {
    SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: h.target_arch,
        opt_level: h.opt_level,
        emit_debug: h.emit_debug,
        stage: stage,
        accumulated_confidence: h.accumulated_confidence,
        operations: h.operations,
        errors: h.errors,
        n_errors: h.n_errors,
    }
}

fn selfhost_handler_add_error(h: SelfHostHandler, error: i32) -> SelfHostHandler with Mut, Panic {
    var new_errors = h.errors
    let idx = h.n_errors
    if idx < 64 {
        new_errors[idx as usize] = error
    }
    SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: h.target_arch,
        opt_level: h.opt_level,
        emit_debug: h.emit_debug,
        stage: h.stage,
        accumulated_confidence: h.accumulated_confidence,
        operations: h.operations,
        errors: new_errors,
        n_errors: if idx < 64 { idx + 1 } else { idx },
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn make_provenance_step(name_char: i8, confidence: f32) -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    var name: [i8; 64] = [0; 64]
    name[0] = name_char
    ProvenanceStep {
        name: name,
        name_len: 1,
        confidence: confidence,
        timestamp: 0,
    }
}

// Create provenance for "lex" phase
fn provenance_lex() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(108, 1.0)  // 'l' for lex, deterministic
}

// Create provenance for "parse" phase
fn provenance_parse() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(112, 1.0)  // 'p' for parse, deterministic
}

// Create provenance for "encode" phase (AST to sedenion)
fn provenance_encode() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(101, 1.0)  // 'e' for encode, lossless
}

// Create provenance for "check" phase (type checking)
fn provenance_check_simple() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(99, 0.99)  // 'c' for check, simple types
}

fn provenance_check_poly() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(99, 0.95)  // 'c' for check, polymorphic
}

fn provenance_check_higher() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(99, 0.90)  // 'c' for check, higher-rank
}

// Create provenance for "emit" phase
fn provenance_emit() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(109, 0.98)  // 'm' for emit/codegen
}

// Create provenance for "specialize" phase (partial evaluation)
fn provenance_specialize() -> ProvenanceStep with Mut, Panic {
    make_provenance_step(115, 0.95)  // 's' for specialize
}

// ============================================================================
// PARSE HANDLER
// ============================================================================

// Parse handler: source -> Knowledge<SedenionAST>
//
// The parsing phase is deterministic (confidence = 1.0):
// 1. Lex source into tokens
// 2. Parse tokens into AST
// 3. Encode AST as sedenion
//
// Each step is recorded in provenance.
fn handle_parse(h: SelfHostHandler, source_ptr: i64, source_len: i64) -> (SelfHostHandler, KnowledgeAST) with Mut, Panic {
    // In a full implementation, this would call the actual lexer/parser
    // For now, we create a placeholder sedenion AST

    // Step 1: Lex
    let lex_prov = provenance_lex()

    // Step 2: Parse
    let parse_prov = provenance_parse()

    // Step 3: Encode as sedenion
    let encode_prov = provenance_encode()

    // Create result AST (placeholder - in reality, parse the source)
    // The sedenion would be computed from actual parsing
    let ast_sed = Sedenion {
        e0: 32.0,   // NODE_ITEM_FN
        e1: 0.0,    // No operator
        e2: 0.0,    // Arity (will be filled)
        e3: 0.0,    // Depth 0
        e4: 0.0,    // Scope 0
        e5: 0.0,    // Type hint
        e6: 0.0,    // Effects low
        e7: 0.0,    // Effects high
        e8: 0.0,    // Linearity
        e9: 1.0,    // Full confidence
        e10: 0.0,   // Literal value
        e11: (source_len % 65536) as f32,  // Name hash based on length
        e12: 0.0,
        e13: 0.0,   // Span start
        e14: source_len as f32,  // Span end
        e15: 0.0,   // Checksum (computed)
    }

    // Build knowledge with provenance
    var k = knowledge_ast_new(ast_sed)
    var prov = k.provenance
    prov[0] = lex_prov
    prov[1] = parse_prov
    prov[2] = encode_prov

    let result = KnowledgeAST {
        value: ast_sed,
        confidence: lex_prov.confidence * parse_prov.confidence * encode_prov.confidence,
        provenance: prov,
        n_provenance: 3,
        is_verified: false,
    }

    // Update handler state
    let new_h = SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: h.target_arch,
        opt_level: h.opt_level,
        emit_debug: h.emit_debug,
        stage: h.stage,
        accumulated_confidence: h.accumulated_confidence * result.confidence,
        operations: h.operations + 1,
        errors: h.errors,
        n_errors: h.n_errors,
    }

    (new_h, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// CHECK HANDLER
// ============================================================================

// Type complexity constants for confidence calculation
fn COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE() -> i32 { 0 }
fn COMPLEXITY_POLY() -> i32 { 1 }
fn COMPLEXITY_HIGHER() -> i32 { 2 }
fn COMPLEXITY_UNDER() -> i32 { 3 }

// Infer type complexity from AST (simplified)
fn infer_type_complexity(ast: Sedenion) -> i32 {
    // In reality, this would analyze the AST for:
    // - Generic parameters
    // - Higher-kinded types
    // - Type constraints
    // For now, return simple as default
    let effects = ast.e6 as i32 + ast.e7 as i32
    if effects > 100 {
        COMPLEXITY_HIGHER()
    } else if effects > 10 {
        COMPLEXITY_POLY()
    } else {
        COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE()
    }
}

fn confidence_for_complexity(complexity: i32) -> f32 {
    if complexity == COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE() {
        0.99
    } else if complexity == COMPLEXITY_POLY() {
        0.95
    } else if complexity == COMPLEXITY_HIGHER() {
        0.90
    } else {
        0.80  // COMPLEXITY_UNDER
    }
}

// Check handler: AST -> Knowledge<TypedAST>
//
// Type checking confidence varies by complexity:
// - Simple types: 0.99
// - Polymorphic: 0.95
// - Higher-rank: 0.90
// - Underconstrained: 0.80
fn handle_check(h: SelfHostHandler, ast: KnowledgeAST) -> (SelfHostHandler, KnowledgeTypedAST) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Infer type complexity
    let complexity = infer_type_complexity(ast.value)
    let check_conf = confidence_for_complexity(complexity)

    // Create check provenance based on complexity
    let check_prov = if complexity == COMPLEXITY_SIMPLE() {
        provenance_check_simple()
    } else if complexity == COMPLEXITY_POLY() {
        provenance_check_poly()
    } else {
        provenance_check_higher()
    }

    // Create typed AST (in reality, run type inference)
    let typed = TypedAST {
        ast: ast.value,
        type_info: [0; 64],  // Would contain actual type info
        n_types: 0,
    }

    // Build knowledge with combined provenance
    var prov: [ProvenanceStep; 16] = [provenance_step_new(); 16]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ast.n_provenance && i < 15 {
        prov[i as usize] = ast.provenance[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if i < 16 {
        prov[i as usize] = check_prov
    }

    let result = KnowledgeTypedAST {
        value: typed,
        confidence: ast.confidence * check_conf,
        provenance: prov,
        n_provenance: if ast.n_provenance < 15 { ast.n_provenance + 1 } else { 16 },
        is_verified: false,
    }

    // Update handler state
    let new_h = SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: h.target_arch,
        opt_level: h.opt_level,
        emit_debug: h.emit_debug,
        stage: h.stage,
        accumulated_confidence: h.accumulated_confidence * check_conf,
        operations: h.operations + 1,
        errors: h.errors,
        n_errors: h.n_errors,
    }

    (new_h, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// EMIT HANDLER
// ============================================================================

// Emit handler: TypedAST -> Knowledge<Code>
//
// Code generation confidence is typically 0.98 (well-tested infrastructure).
fn handle_emit(h: SelfHostHandler, typed: KnowledgeTypedAST) -> (SelfHostHandler, KnowledgeCode) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let emit_prov = provenance_emit()

    // Create code output (in reality, run codegen)
    let code = Code {
        bytes: [0; 4096],  // Would contain actual machine code
        len: 0,
        target: h.target_arch,
    }

    // Build knowledge with combined provenance
    var prov: [ProvenanceStep; 16] = [provenance_step_new(); 16]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < typed.n_provenance && i < 15 {
        prov[i as usize] = typed.provenance[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if i < 16 {
        prov[i as usize] = emit_prov
    }

    let result = KnowledgeCode {
        value: code,
        confidence: typed.confidence * emit_prov.confidence,
        provenance: prov,
        n_provenance: if typed.n_provenance < 15 { typed.n_provenance + 1 } else { 16 },
        is_verified: false,
    }

    // Update handler state
    let new_h = SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: h.target_arch,
        opt_level: h.opt_level,
        emit_debug: h.emit_debug,
        stage: h.stage,
        accumulated_confidence: h.accumulated_confidence * emit_prov.confidence,
        operations: h.operations + 1,
        errors: h.errors,
        n_errors: h.n_errors,
    }

    (new_h, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// SPECIALIZE HANDLER (PARTIAL EVALUATION)
// ============================================================================

// Specialize handler: Code + static_args -> Knowledge<Code>
//
// Partial evaluation specializes code with known inputs.
// This is the first Futamura projection when applied to an interpreter.
fn handle_specialize(h: SelfHostHandler, code: KnowledgeCode, static_args: [i64; 16], n_args: i64) -> (SelfHostHandler, KnowledgeCode) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let spec_prov = provenance_specialize()

    // Create specialized code (in reality, run partial evaluator)
    // The specialized code would have static_args "baked in"
    let specialized = Code {
        bytes: code.value.bytes,  // Would be different after PE
        len: code.value.len,
        target: code.value.target,
    }

    // Build knowledge with combined provenance
    var prov: [ProvenanceStep; 16] = [provenance_step_new(); 16]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < code.n_provenance && i < 15 {
        prov[i as usize] = code.provenance[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if i < 16 {
        prov[i as usize] = spec_prov
    }

    let result = KnowledgeCode {
        value: specialized,
        confidence: code.confidence * spec_prov.confidence,
        provenance: prov,
        n_provenance: if code.n_provenance < 15 { code.n_provenance + 1 } else { 16 },
        is_verified: false,
    }

    // Update handler state
    let new_h = SelfHostHandler {
        target_arch: h.target_arch,
        opt_level: h.opt_level,
        emit_debug: h.emit_debug,
        stage: h.stage,
        accumulated_confidence: h.accumulated_confidence * spec_prov.confidence,
        operations: h.operations + 1,
        errors: h.errors,
        n_errors: h.n_errors,
    }

    (new_h, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// FULL COMPILATION PIPELINE
// ============================================================================

// Complete compilation: source -> Knowledge<Code>
//
// Chains parse -> check -> emit with confidence propagation.
fn compile_full(h: SelfHostHandler, source_ptr: i64, source_len: i64) -> (SelfHostHandler, KnowledgeCode) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Phase 1: Parse
    let parse_result = handle_parse(h, source_ptr, source_len)
    let h1 = parse_result.0
    let parsed = parse_result.1

    // Phase 2: Check
    let check_result = handle_check(h1, parsed)
    let h2 = check_result.0
    let checked = check_result.1

    // Phase 3: Emit
    let emit_result = handle_emit(h2, checked)

    emit_result
}

// ============================================================================
// BOOTSTRAP SUPPORT
// ============================================================================

// Bootstrap stage constants
fn STAGE_RUST() -> i32 { 0 }
fn STAGE_SELF1() -> i32 { 1 }
fn STAGE_SELF2() -> i32 { 2 }

// Compile self (for bootstrap)
// This is called when the compiler compiles its own source.
fn compile_self(h: SelfHostHandler, compiler_source_ptr: i64, compiler_source_len: i64) -> (SelfHostHandler, KnowledgeCode) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Set stage based on current handler stage
    let next_stage = h.stage + 1
    let staged_h = selfhost_handler_with_stage(h, next_stage)

    // Compile
    compile_full(staged_h, compiler_source_ptr, compiler_source_len)
}

// Cross-validate two compilation results
// Returns true if they produce identical output
fn cross_validate(code1: KnowledgeCode, code2: KnowledgeCode) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if code1.value.len != code2.value.len {
        false
    } else {
        var match_found = true
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < code1.value.len && i < 4096 {
            if code1.value.bytes[i as usize] != code2.value.bytes[i as usize] {
                match_found = false
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        match_found
    }
}

// Apply confidence boost after successful cross-validation
fn CONFIDENCE_BOOST() -> f32 { 1.04 }

fn boost_confidence(code: KnowledgeCode) -> KnowledgeCode {
    let boosted = code.confidence * CONFIDENCE_BOOST()
    let capped = if boosted > 0.99 { 0.99 } else { boosted }
    KnowledgeCode {
        value: code.value,
        confidence: capped,
        provenance: code.provenance,
        n_provenance: code.n_provenance,
        is_verified: true,
    }
}

// Full bootstrap verification
// Stage 0 (Rust) -> Stage 1 -> Stage 2
// If Stage 1 output == Stage 2 output, boost confidence
fn bootstrap_verify(stage1: KnowledgeCode, stage2: KnowledgeCode) -> KnowledgeCode with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if cross_validate(stage1, stage2) {
        boost_confidence(stage2)
    } else {
        // Validation failed - return stage2 without boost
        stage2
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/lexer/comparison_harness.sio ===
// compiler::lexer::comparison_harness — Lexer Comparison Test Harness
//
// This module provides infrastructure to compare the Sounio self-hosted lexer
// output against the Rust-based lexer to ensure compatibility.
//
// Strategy:
// 1. Read a Sounio source file
// 2. Tokenize with self-hosted lexer
// 3. Compare against pre-generated expected token dumps from Rust lexer
// 4. Report token-by-token comparison results
//
// The expected outputs are generated by running the Rust lexer on test inputs
// and serializing the token streams for comparison.

// FFI for print
extern "C" {
    fn print(s: &str) -> ();
}

// ============================================================================
// TOKEN COMPARISON RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct TokenCompareResult {
    passed: bool,
    token_index: i64,
    expected_kind: i32,
    actual_kind: i32,
    expected_start: i64,
    actual_start: i64,
    expected_end: i64,
    actual_end: i64,
    message: [i8; 256],
    message_len: i64,
}

fn compare_result_pass() -> TokenCompareResult {
    TokenCompareResult {
        passed: true,
        token_index: 0,
        expected_kind: 0,
        actual_kind: 0,
        expected_start: 0,
        actual_start: 0,
        expected_end: 0,
        actual_end: 0,
        message: [0; 256],
        message_len: 0,
    }
}

fn compare_result_fail(idx: i64, exp_kind: i32, act_kind: i32,
                       exp_start: i64, act_start: i64,
                       exp_end: i64, act_end: i64) -> TokenCompareResult {
    TokenCompareResult {
        passed: false,
        token_index: idx,
        expected_kind: exp_kind,
        actual_kind: act_kind,
        expected_start: exp_start,
        actual_start: act_start,
        expected_end: exp_end,
        actual_end: act_end,
        message: [0; 256],
        message_len: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPECTED TOKEN (for comparison)
// ============================================================================

struct ExpectedToken {
    kind: i32,
    start: i64,
    end: i64,
    text: [i8; 256],
    text_len: i64,
}

fn expected_token_new(kind: i32, start: i64, end: i64) -> ExpectedToken {
    ExpectedToken {
        kind: kind,
        start: start,
        end: end,
        text: [0; 256],
        text_len: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST CASE DEFINITION
// ============================================================================

struct LexerTestCase {
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    source: [i8; 1048576],
    source_len: i64,
    expected: [ExpectedToken; 256],
    n_expected: i64,
}

fn test_case_new() -> LexerTestCase {
    LexerTestCase {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        source: [0; 1048576],
        source_len: 0,
        expected: [expected_token_new(0, 0, 0); 256],
        n_expected: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// COMPARISON FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Compare a single token against expected
fn compare_token(actual_kind: i32, actual_start: i64, actual_end: i64,
                 expected: ExpectedToken, idx: i64) -> TokenCompareResult {
    if actual_kind != expected.kind {
        return compare_result_fail(idx, expected.kind, actual_kind,
                                   expected.start, actual_start,
                                   expected.end, actual_end)
    }
    if actual_start != expected.start {
        return compare_result_fail(idx, expected.kind, actual_kind,
                                   expected.start, actual_start,
                                   expected.end, actual_end)
    }
    if actual_end != expected.end {
        return compare_result_fail(idx, expected.kind, actual_kind,
                                   expected.start, actual_start,
                                   expected.end, actual_end)
    }
    compare_result_pass()
}

// RUST LEXER EXPECTED OUTPUTS
// These are pre-generated from running the Rust lexer on test inputs

// Test case: "let x = 42"
// Rust lexer output:
//   Token { kind: Let, span: 0..3, text: "let" }
//   Token { kind: Ident, span: 4..5, text: "x" }
//   Token { kind: Eq, span: 6..7, text: "=" }
//   Token { kind: IntLit, span: 8..10, text: "42" }
//   Token { kind: Eof, span: 10..10, text: "" }

fn TK_LET() -> i32 { 15 }
fn TK_IDENT() -> i32 { 200 }
fn TK_EQ() -> i32 { 230 }
fn TK_INT_LIT() -> i32 { 201 }
fn TK_EOF() -> i32 { 0 }

fn get_test_let_x_42() -> LexerTestCase with Mut, Panic {
    var tc = test_case_new();

    // Name: "let x = 42"
    tc.name[0] = 108; tc.name[1] = 101; tc.name[2] = 116;  // let
    tc.name[3] = 32;  // space
    tc.name[4] = 120;  // x
    tc.name[5] = 32;  // space
    tc.name[6] = 61;  // =
    tc.name[7] = 32;  // space
    tc.name[8] = 52; tc.name[9] = 50;  // 42
    tc.name_len = 10;

    // Source
    tc.source[0] = 108; tc.source[1] = 101; tc.source[2] = 116;  // let
    tc.source[3] = 32;   // space
    tc.source[4] = 120;  // x
    tc.source[5] = 32;   // space
    tc.source[6] = 61;   // =
    tc.source[7] = 32;   // space
    tc.source[8] = 52; tc.source[9] = 50;  // 42
    tc.source_len = 10;

    // Expected tokens
    tc.expected[0] = expected_token_new(TK_LET(), 0, 3);
    tc.expected[1] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 4, 5);
    tc.expected[2] = expected_token_new(TK_EQ(), 6, 7);
    tc.expected[3] = expected_token_new(TK_INT_LIT(), 8, 10);
    tc.expected[4] = expected_token_new(TK_EOF(), 10, 10);
    tc.n_expected = 5;

    tc
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST: fn main() -> i32 { 0 }
// ============================================================================

fn TK_FN() -> i32 { 14 }
fn TK_LPAREN() -> i32 { 280 }
fn TK_RPAREN() -> i32 { 281 }
fn TK_ARROW() -> i32 { 270 }
fn TK_LBRACE() -> i32 { 284 }
fn TK_RBRACE() -> i32 { 285 }

fn get_test_fn_main() -> LexerTestCase with Mut, Panic {
    var tc = test_case_new();

    // Source: "fn main() -> i32 { 0 }"
    // f=102, n=110, space=32, m=109, a=97, i=105, n=110, (=40, )=41
    // -=45, >=62, i=105, 3=51, 2=50, {=123, 0=48, }=125
    tc.source[0] = 102; tc.source[1] = 110;  // fn
    tc.source[2] = 32;                        // space
    tc.source[3] = 109; tc.source[4] = 97; tc.source[5] = 105; tc.source[6] = 110;  // main
    tc.source[7] = 40;   // (
    tc.source[8] = 41;   // )
    tc.source[9] = 32;   // space
    tc.source[10] = 45; tc.source[11] = 62;  // ->
    tc.source[12] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[13] = 105; tc.source[14] = 51; tc.source[15] = 50;  // i32
    tc.source[16] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[17] = 123; // {
    tc.source[18] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[19] = 48;  // 0
    tc.source[20] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[21] = 125; // }
    tc.source_len = 22;

    // Expected: fn, main, (, ), ->, i32, {, 0, }, EOF
    tc.expected[0] = expected_token_new(TK_FN(), 0, 2);
    tc.expected[1] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 3, 7);   // main
    tc.expected[2] = expected_token_new(TK_LPAREN(), 7, 8);
    tc.expected[3] = expected_token_new(TK_RPAREN(), 8, 9);
    tc.expected[4] = expected_token_new(TK_ARROW(), 10, 12);
    tc.expected[5] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 13, 16); // i32
    tc.expected[6] = expected_token_new(TK_LBRACE(), 17, 18);
    tc.expected[7] = expected_token_new(TK_INT_LIT(), 19, 20);
    tc.expected[8] = expected_token_new(TK_RBRACE(), 21, 22);
    tc.expected[9] = expected_token_new(TK_EOF(), 22, 22);
    tc.n_expected = 10;

    tc
}

fn TK_WITH() -> i32 { 53 }

fn get_test_effect_syntax() -> LexerTestCase with Mut, Panic {
    var tc = test_case_new();

    // Source: "fn read() -> string with IO { }"
    tc.source[0] = 102; tc.source[1] = 110;  // fn
    tc.source[2] = 32;                        // space
    tc.source[3] = 114; tc.source[4] = 101; tc.source[5] = 97; tc.source[6] = 100;  // read
    tc.source[7] = 40; tc.source[8] = 41;     // ()
    tc.source[9] = 32;                        // space
    tc.source[10] = 45; tc.source[11] = 62;  // ->
    tc.source[12] = 32;                       // space
    // string
    tc.source[13] = 115; tc.source[14] = 116; tc.source[15] = 114;
    tc.source[16] = 105; tc.source[17] = 110; tc.source[18] = 103;
    tc.source[19] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[20] = 119; tc.source[21] = 105; tc.source[22] = 116; tc.source[23] = 104;  // with
    tc.source[24] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[25] = 73; tc.source[26] = 79;  // IO
    tc.source[27] = 32;  // space
    tc.source[28] = 123; tc.source[29] = 32; tc.source[30] = 125;  // { }
    tc.source_len = 31;

    // Expected: fn, read, (, ), ->, string, with, IO, {, }, EOF
    tc.expected[0] = expected_token_new(TK_FN(), 0, 2);
    tc.expected[1] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 3, 7);    // read
    tc.expected[2] = expected_token_new(TK_LPAREN(), 7, 8);
    tc.expected[3] = expected_token_new(TK_RPAREN(), 8, 9);
    tc.expected[4] = expected_token_new(TK_ARROW(), 10, 12);
    tc.expected[5] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 13, 19);  // string
    tc.expected[6] = expected_token_new(TK_WITH(), 20, 24);   // with - SOUNIO EFFECT KEYWORD!
    tc.expected[7] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 25, 27);  // IO
    tc.expected[8] = expected_token_new(TK_LBRACE(), 28, 29);
    tc.expected[9] = expected_token_new(TK_RBRACE(), 30, 31);
    tc.expected[10] = expected_token_new(TK_EOF(), 31, 31);
    tc.n_expected = 11;

    tc
}

// TEST 5: Mutable reference "&!" (Sounio syntax, NOT Rust's &!)
// ============================================================================

fn TK_AMP() -> i32 { 226 }
fn TK_BANG() -> i32 { 229 }

fn get_test_mutable_ref() -> LexerTestCase with Mut, Panic {
    var tc = test_case_new();

    // Source: "x: &!T"
    tc.source[0] = 120;  // x
    tc.source[1] = 58;   // :
    tc.source[2] = 32;   // space
    tc.source[3] = 38;   // &
    tc.source[4] = 33;   // !
    tc.source[5] = 84;   // T
    tc.source_len = 6;

    // Expected: x, :, &, !, T, EOF
    // Note: &! is TWO separate tokens in Sounio!
    tc.expected[0] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 0, 1);  // x
    tc.expected[1] = expected_token_new(TK_COLON(), 1, 2);
    tc.expected[2] = expected_token_new(TK_AMP(), 3, 4);    // &
    tc.expected[3] = expected_token_new(TK_BANG(), 4, 5);   // !
    tc.expected[4] = expected_token_new(TK_IDENT(), 5, 6);  // T
    tc.expected[5] = expected_token_new(TK_EOF(), 6, 6);
    tc.n_expected = 6;

    tc
}

// compiler::lexer::keywords — Keyword lookup for the Sounio lexer

// This module provides keyword recognition by matching identifier text
// against the set of reserved keywords.

// For now, we duplicate the constants or assume they're in scope

// ============================================================================
// STRING COMPARISON HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Compare two byte arrays for equality
fn bytes_equal(a: [i8; 256], a_len: i64, b: [i8; 256], b_len: i64) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a_len != b_len {
        return false
    }
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < a_len {
        if a[i as usize] != b[i as usize] {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    true
}

// Create a keyword pattern from a string literal (up to 16 chars)
fn make_pattern(c0: i8, c1: i8, c2: i8, c3: i8, c4: i8, c5: i8, c6: i8, c7: i8,
                c8: i8, c9: i8, c10: i8, c11: i8, c12: i8, c13: i8, c14: i8, c15: i8,
                len: i64) -> [i8; 256] with Mut, Panic {
    var pattern: [i8; 256] = [0; 256];
    if len >= 1 { pattern[0] = c0; }
    if len >= 2 { pattern[1] = c1; }
    if len >= 3 { pattern[2] = c2; }
    if len >= 4 { pattern[3] = c3; }
    if len >= 5 { pattern[4] = c4; }
    if len >= 6 { pattern[5] = c5; }
    if len >= 7 { pattern[6] = c6; }
    if len >= 8 { pattern[7] = c7; }
    if len >= 9 { pattern[8] = c8; }
    if len >= 10 { pattern[9] = c9; }
    if len >= 11 { pattern[10] = c10; }
    if len >= 12 { pattern[11] = c11; }
    if len >= 13 { pattern[12] = c12; }
    if len >= 14 { pattern[13] = c13; }
    if len >= 15 { pattern[14] = c14; }
    if len >= 16 { pattern[15] = c15; }
    pattern
}

// Match text against a keyword pattern
fn match_keyword(text: [i8; 256], text_len: i64,
                 c0: i8, c1: i8, c2: i8, c3: i8, c4: i8, c5: i8, c6: i8, c7: i8,
                 c8: i8, c9: i8, c10: i8, c11: i8, c12: i8, c13: i8, c14: i8, c15: i8,
                 kw_len: i64) -> bool with Panic {
    if text_len != kw_len {
        return false
    }
    if kw_len >= 1 && text[0] != c0 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 2 && text[1] != c1 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 3 && text[2] != c2 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 4 && text[3] != c3 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 5 && text[4] != c4 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 6 && text[5] != c5 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 7 && text[6] != c6 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 8 && text[7] != c7 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 9 && text[8] != c8 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 10 && text[9] != c9 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 11 && text[10] != c10 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 12 && text[11] != c11 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 13 && text[12] != c12 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 14 && text[13] != c13 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 15 && text[14] != c14 { return false }
    if kw_len >= 16 && text[15] != c15 { return false }
    true
}

// Lookup keyword from identifier text
// Returns TK_IDENT if not a keyword
fn lookup_keyword(text: [i8; 256], len: i64) -> i32 with Panic {
    // 2-character keywords
    if len == 2 {
        // fn
        if text[0] == 102 && text[1] == 110 { return TK_FN() }
        // if
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 102 { return TK_IF() }
        // in
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 110 { return TK_IN() }
        // as
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 115 { return TK_AS() }
        // do
        if text[0] == 100 && text[1] == 111 { return 133 }  // TK_DO
    }

    // 3-character keywords
    if len == 3 {
        // let
        if text[0] == 108 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 116 { return TK_LET() }
        // var
        if text[0] == 118 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 114 { return TK_VAR() }
        // for
        if text[0] == 102 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 114 { return TK_FOR() }
        // mut
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 117 && text[2] == 116 { return TK_MUT() }
        // use
        if text[0] == 117 && text[1] == 115 && text[2] == 101 { return TK_USE() }
        // pub
        if text[0] == 112 && text[1] == 117 && text[2] == 98 { return TK_PUB() }
        // gpu
        if text[0] == 103 && text[1] == 112 && text[2] == 117 { return TK_GPU() }
        // ode
        if text[0] == 111 && text[1] == 100 && text[2] == 101 { return 110 }  // TK_ODE
        // pde
        if text[0] == 112 && text[1] == 100 && text[2] == 101 { return 111 }  // TK_PDE
    }

    // 4-character keywords
    if len == 4 {
        // else
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 108 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 101 { return TK_ELSE() }
        // loop
        if text[0] == 108 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 111 && text[3] == 112 { return TK_LOOP() }
        // true
        if text[0] == 116 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 101 { return TK_TRUE() }
        // enum
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 109 { return TK_ENUM() }
        // impl
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 109 && text[2] == 112 && text[3] == 108 { return TK_IMPL() }
        // type
        if text[0] == 116 && text[1] == 121 && text[2] == 112 && text[3] == 101 { return TK_TYPE() }
        // Self
        if text[0] == 83 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 102 { return TK_SELF_UPPER() }
        // self
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 102 { return TK_SELF_LOWER() }
        // with
        if text[0] == 119 && text[1] == 105 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 104 { return TK_WITH() }
        // move
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 118 && text[3] == 101 { return TK_MOVE() }
        // copy
        if text[0] == 99 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 112 && text[3] == 121 { return TK_COPY() }
        // drop
        if text[0] == 100 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 111 && text[3] == 112 { return TK_DROP() }
        // tile
        if text[0] == 116 && text[1] == 105 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 101 { return TK_TILE() }
        // from
        if text[0] == 102 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 111 && text[3] == 109 { return 151 }  // TK_FROM
        // grad
        if text[0] == 103 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 100 { return 168 }  // TK_GRAD
        // dual
        if text[0] == 100 && text[1] == 117 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 108 { return 167 }  // TK_DUAL
        // quat
        if text[0] == 113 && text[1] == 117 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 116 { return 166 }  // TK_QUAT
        // vec2
        if text[0] == 118 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 99 && text[3] == 50 { return 160 }  // TK_VEC2
        // vec3
        if text[0] == 118 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 99 && text[3] == 51 { return 161 }  // TK_VEC3
        // vec4
        if text[0] == 118 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 99 && text[3] == 52 { return 162 }  // TK_VEC4
        // mat2
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 50 { return 163 }  // TK_MAT2
        // mat3
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 51 { return 164 }  // TK_MAT3
        // mat4
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 52 { return 165 }  // TK_MAT4
    }

    // 5-character keywords
    if len == 5 {
        // while
        if text[0] == 119 && text[1] == 104 && text[2] == 105 && text[3] == 108 && text[4] == 101 { return TK_WHILE() }
        // break
        if text[0] == 98 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 101 && text[3] == 97 && text[4] == 107 { return TK_BREAK() }
        // false
        if text[0] == 102 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 115 && text[4] == 101 { return TK_FALSE() }
        // trait
        if text[0] == 116 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 105 && text[4] == 116 { return TK_TRAIT() }
        // const
        if text[0] == 99 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 110 && text[3] == 115 && text[4] == 116 { return TK_CONST() }
        // match
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 99 && text[4] == 104 { return TK_MATCH() }
        // where
        if text[0] == 119 && text[1] == 104 && text[2] == 101 && text[3] == 114 && text[4] == 101 { return TK_WHERE() }
        // async
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 115 && text[2] == 121 && text[3] == 110 && text[4] == 99 { return TK_ASYNC() }
        // await
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 119 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 105 && text[4] == 116 { return TK_AWAIT() }
        // spawn
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 112 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 119 && text[4] == 110 { return TK_SPAWN() }
        // infer
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 102 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 114 { return 92 }  // TK_INFER
        // proof
        if text[0] == 112 && text[1] == 114 && text[2] == 111 && text[3] == 111 && text[4] == 102 { return 93 }  // TK_PROOF
        // nodes
        if text[0] == 110 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 100 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 115 { return 113 }  // TK_NODES
        // edges
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 100 && text[2] == 103 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 115 { return 114 }  // TK_EDGES
        // state
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 116 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 116 && text[4] == 101 { return 116 }  // TK_STATE
        // query
        if text[0] == 113 && text[1] == 117 && text[2] == 101 && text[3] == 114 && text[4] == 121 { return 144 }  // TK_QUERY
        // align
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 108 && text[2] == 105 && text[3] == 103 && text[4] == 110 { return 152 }  // TK_ALIGN
        // Valid
        if text[0] == 86 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 105 && text[4] == 100 { return 135 }  // TK_VALID
        // Input
        if text[0] == 73 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 112 && text[3] == 117 && text[4] == 116 { return 143 }  // TK_INPUT_PROV
    }

    // 6-character keywords
    if len == 6 {
        // return
        if text[0] == 114 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 117 && text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 110 { return TK_RETURN() }
        // struct
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 116 && text[2] == 114 && text[3] == 117 && text[4] == 99 && text[5] == 116 { return TK_STRUCT() }
        // import
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 109 && text[2] == 112 && text[3] == 111 && text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 116 { return TK_IMPORT() }
        // module
        if text[0] == 109 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 100 && text[3] == 117 && text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 101 { return TK_MODULE() }
        // export
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 120 && text[2] == 112 && text[3] == 111 && text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 116 { return TK_EXPORT() }
        // effect
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 102 && text[2] == 102 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 99 && text[5] == 116 { return TK_EFFECT() }
        // handle
        if text[0] == 104 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 110 && text[3] == 100 && text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 101 { return TK_HANDLE() }
        // resume
        if text[0] == 114 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 117 && text[4] == 109 && text[5] == 101 { return TK_RESUME() }
        // linear
        if text[0] == 108 && text[1] == 105 && text[2] == 110 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 97 && text[5] == 114 { return TK_LINEAR() }
        // affine
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 102 && text[2] == 102 && text[3] == 105 && text[4] == 110 && text[5] == 101 { return TK_AFFINE() }
        // kernel
        if text[0] == 107 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 114 && text[3] == 110 && text[4] == 101 && text[5] == 108 { return TK_KERNEL() }
        // device
        if text[0] == 100 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 118 && text[3] == 105 && text[4] == 99 && text[5] == 101 { return TK_DEVICE() }
        // shared
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 104 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 114 && text[4] == 101 && text[5] == 100 { return TK_SHARED() }
        // unsafe
        if text[0] == 117 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 97 && text[4] == 102 && text[5] == 101 { return TK_UNSAFE() }
        // extern
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 120 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 110 { return TK_EXTERN() }
        // static
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 116 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 116 && text[4] == 105 && text[5] == 99 { return TK_STATIC() }
        // sample
        if text[0] == 115 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 109 && text[3] == 112 && text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 101 { return 90 }  // TK_SAMPLE
        // assert
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 115 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 116 { return 97 }  // TK_ASSERT
        // assume
        if text[0] == 97 && text[1] == 115 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 117 && text[4] == 109 && text[5] == 101 { return 98 }  // TK_ASSUME
        // causal
        if text[0] == 99 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 115 && text[4] == 97 && text[5] == 108 { return 112 }  // TK_CAUSAL
        // params
        if text[0] == 112 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 114 && text[3] == 97 && text[4] == 109 && text[5] == 115 { return 117 }  // TK_PARAMS
        // domain
        if text[0] == 100 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 109 && text[3] == 97 && text[4] == 105 && text[5] == 110 { return 118 }  // TK_DOMAIN
        // Tensor
        if text[0] == 84 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 110 && text[3] == 115 && text[4] == 111 && text[5] == 114 { return 132 }  // TK_TENSOR
        // Source
        if text[0] == 83 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 114 && text[4] == 99 && text[5] == 101 { return 139 }  // TK_SOURCE_PROV
        // compat
        if text[0] == 99 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 109 && text[3] == 112 && text[4] == 97 && text[5] == 116 { return 155 }  // TK_COMPAT
    }

    // 7-character keywords
    if len == 7 {
        // handler
        if text[0] == 104 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 110 && text[3] == 100 && text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 101 && text[6] == 114 { return TK_HANDLER() }
        // perform
        if text[0] == 112 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 114 && text[3] == 102 && text[4] == 111 && text[5] == 114 && text[6] == 109 { return TK_PERFORM() }
        // observe
        if text[0] == 111 && text[1] == 98 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 101 && text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 118 && text[6] == 101 { return 91 }  // TK_OBSERVE
        // initial
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 105 && text[3] == 116 && text[4] == 105 && text[5] == 97 && text[6] == 108 { return 120 }  // TK_INITIAL
        // Derived
        if text[0] == 68 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 114 && text[3] == 105 && text[4] == 118 && text[5] == 101 && text[6] == 100 { return 138 }  // TK_DERIVED
        // hessian
        if text[0] == 104 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 115 && text[4] == 105 && text[5] == 97 && text[6] == 110 { return 170 }  // TK_HESSIAN
        // jacobian - 8 chars, handled below
    }

    // 8-character keywords
    if len == 8 {
        // continue
        if text[0] == 99 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 110 && text[3] == 116 &&
           text[4] == 105 && text[5] == 110 && text[6] == 117 && text[7] == 101 { return TK_CONTINUE() }
        // ontology
        if text[0] == 111 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 111 &&
           text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 111 && text[6] == 103 && text[7] == 121 { return 150 }  // TK_ONTOLOGY
        // boundary
        if text[0] == 98 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 110 &&
           text[4] == 100 && text[5] == 97 && text[6] == 114 && text[7] == 121 { return 119 }  // TK_BOUNDARY
        // requires
        if text[0] == 114 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 113 && text[3] == 117 &&
           text[4] == 105 && text[5] == 114 && text[6] == 101 && text[7] == 115 { return 95 }  // TK_REQUIRES
        // Quantity
        if text[0] == 81 && text[1] == 117 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 110 &&
           text[4] == 116 && text[5] == 105 && text[6] == 116 && text[7] == 121 { return 131 }  // TK_QUANTITY
        // Computed
        if text[0] == 67 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 109 && text[3] == 112 &&
           text[4] == 117 && text[5] == 116 && text[6] == 101 && text[7] == 100 { return 140 }  // TK_COMPUTED
        // Measured
        if text[0] == 77 && text[1] == 101 && text[2] == 97 && text[3] == 115 &&
           text[4] == 117 && text[5] == 114 && text[6] == 101 && text[7] == 100 { return 142 }  // TK_MEASURED
        // distance
        if text[0] == 100 && text[1] == 105 && text[2] == 115 && text[3] == 116 &&
           text[4] == 97 && text[5] == 110 && text[6] == 99 && text[7] == 101 { return 153 }  // TK_DISTANCE
        // jacobian
        if text[0] == 106 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 99 && text[3] == 111 &&
           text[4] == 98 && text[5] == 105 && text[6] == 97 && text[7] == 110 { return 169 }  // TK_JACOBIAN
    }

    // 9-character keywords
    if len == 9 {
        // invariant
        if text[0] == 105 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 118 && text[3] == 97 &&
           text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 105 && text[6] == 97 && text[7] == 110 && text[8] == 116 { return 94 }  // TK_INVARIANT
        // equations
        if text[0] == 101 && text[1] == 113 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 97 &&
           text[4] == 116 && text[5] == 105 && text[6] == 111 && text[7] == 110 && text[8] == 115 { return 115 }  // TK_EQUATIONS
        // Knowledge
        if text[0] == 75 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 111 && text[3] == 119 &&
           text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 101 && text[6] == 100 && text[7] == 103 && text[8] == 101 { return 130 }  // TK_KNOWLEDGE
        // threshold
        if text[0] == 116 && text[1] == 104 && text[2] == 114 && text[3] == 101 &&
           text[4] == 115 && text[5] == 104 && text[6] == 111 && text[7] == 108 && text[8] == 100 { return 154 }  // TK_THRESHOLD
    }

    // 10-character keywords
    if len == 10 {
        // Literature
        if text[0] == 76 && text[1] == 105 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 101 &&
           text[4] == 114 && text[5] == 97 && text[6] == 116 && text[7] == 117 &&
           text[8] == 114 && text[9] == 101 { return 141 }  // TK_LITERATURE
        // ValidUntil
        if text[0] == 86 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 105 &&
           text[4] == 100 && text[5] == 85 && text[6] == 110 && text[7] == 116 &&
           text[8] == 105 && text[9] == 108 { return 136 }  // TK_VALID_UNTIL
        // ValidWhile
        if text[0] == 86 && text[1] == 97 && text[2] == 108 && text[3] == 105 &&
           text[4] == 100 && text[5] == 87 && text[6] == 104 && text[7] == 105 &&
           text[8] == 108 && text[9] == 101 { return 137 }  // TK_VALID_WHILE
    }

    // 12-character keywords
    if len == 12 {
        // OntologyTerm
        if text[0] == 79 && text[1] == 110 && text[2] == 116 && text[3] == 111 &&
           text[4] == 108 && text[5] == 111 && text[6] == 103 && text[7] == 121 &&
           text[8] == 84 && text[9] == 101 && text[10] == 114 && text[11] == 109 { return 156 }  // TK_ONTOLOGY_TERM
    }

    // 14-character keywords
    if len == 14 {
        // counterfactual
        if text[0] == 99 && text[1] == 111 && text[2] == 117 && text[3] == 110 &&
           text[4] == 116 && text[5] == 101 && text[6] == 114 && text[7] == 102 &&
           text[8] == 97 && text[9] == 99 && text[10] == 116 && text[11] == 117 &&
           text[12] == 97 && text[13] == 108 { return 134 }  // TK_COUNTERFACTUAL
    }

    // Not a keyword - return identifier
    TK_IDENT()
}
