            "Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood",
            "Clinical lab code for HbA1c.",
            "https://loinc.org/4548-4",
            "local:loinc"
        )
        return ontology_term_add_synonym(t0, "HbA1c")
    }
    if curie == "LOINC:1558-6" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "LOINC:1558-6",
            "Glucose [Moles/volume] in Blood",
            "Clinical lab code for blood glucose concentration.",
            "https://loinc.org/1558-6",
            "local:loinc"
        )
        return ontology_term_add_synonym(t0, "Blood glucose")
    }
    if curie == "HPO:0000118" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "HPO:0000118",
            "Phenotypic abnormality",
            "Root phenotype abnormality concept in the HPO slice.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0000118",
            "local:hpo"
        )
        return ontology_term_add_synonym(t0, "HPO root")
    }
    if curie == "HPO:0005978" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "HPO:0005978",
            "Abnormality of glucose homeostasis",
            "Bridge phenotype used between clinical and discovery contexts.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0005978",
            "local:hpo"
        )
        let t1 = ontology_term_add_parent(t0, "HPO:0000118")
        return ontology_term_add_synonym(t1, "Glucose homeostasis abnormality")
    }
    if curie == "HPO:0003074" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "HPO:0003074",
            "Hyperglycemia",
            "Phenotype for elevated glucose used in the clinical notebook demo.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0003074",
            "local:hpo"
        )
        let t1 = ontology_term_add_parent(t0, "HPO:0005978")
        return ontology_term_add_synonym(t1, "High blood glucose")
    }
    if curie == "GO:0008150" {
        return ontology_store_make(
            "GO:0008150",
            "biological_process",
            "Root biological process term in the GO slice.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0008150",
            "local:go"
        )
    }
    if curie == "GO:0042593" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "GO:0042593",
            "glucose homeostasis",
            "Biological process maintaining glucose homeostasis.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0042593",
            "local:go"
        )
        let t1 = ontology_term_add_parent(t0, "GO:0008150")
        return ontology_term_add_synonym(t1, "Glucose regulation")
    }
    if curie == "GO:0006006" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "GO:0006006",
            "glucose metabolic process",
            "Glucose metabolic process in the GO demo slice.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0006006",
            "local:go"
        )
        return ontology_term_add_parent(t0, "GO:0042593")
    }
    if curie == "CHEBI:24431" {
        return ontology_store_make(
            "CHEBI:24431",
            "chemical entity",
            "Root chemical entity term in the ChEBI slice.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_24431",
            "local:chebi"
        )
    }
    if curie == "CHEBI:17234" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "CHEBI:17234",
            "glucose",
            "ChEBI glucose concept for discovery-side mapping.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_17234",
            "local:chebi"
        )
        return ontology_term_add_parent(t0, "CHEBI:24431")
    }
    if curie == "CHEBI:6801" {
        let t0 = ontology_store_make(
            "CHEBI:6801",
            "metformin",
            "ChEBI metformin concept used for therapeutic linking.",
            "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_6801",
            "local:chebi"
        )
        return ontology_term_add_parent(t0, "CHEBI:24431")
    }
    ontology_term_empty()
}

fn ontology_store_search_local(query: string) -> ResolvedOntologyTermList {
    var out = ontology_term_list_new()
    if starts_with(query, "glucose") || starts_with(query, "Glucose") {
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("LOINC:1558-6"))
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("HPO:0005978"))
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("HPO:0003074"))
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("GO:0042593"))
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("CHEBI:17234"))
        return out
    }
    if starts_with(query, "diabetes") || starts_with(query, "Diabetes") {
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("SNOMED:73211009"))
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("SNOMED:44054006"))
        return out
    }
    if starts_with(query, "metformin") || starts_with(query, "Metformin") {
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, ontology_store_resolve_local("CHEBI:6801"))
        return out
    }
    let exact = ontology_store_resolve_local(query)
    if ontology_term_found(exact) {
        out = ontology_term_list_push(out, exact)
    }
    out
}


// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/parser/ast.sio ===
// compiler::parser::ast — Abstract Syntax Tree for Self-Hosted Sounio Compiler
//
// This module defines AST node types for the self-hosted Sounio parser.
// Following the pattern from stdlib/medlang/ast.sio using fixed-size arrays.

// ============================================================================
// COMMON TYPES
// ============================================================================

// Source span (byte offsets)
struct Span {
    start: i64,
    end: i64,
}

fn span_new(start: i64, end: i64) -> Span {
    Span { start: start, end: end }
}

fn span_dummy() -> Span {
    Span { start: 0, end: 0 }
}

// Node ID for unique identification
struct NodeId {
    value: i64,
}

fn node_id_new(v: i64) -> NodeId {
    NodeId { value: v }
}

fn node_id_dummy() -> NodeId {
    NodeId { value: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// PATH
// ============================================================================

// A path segment: identifier with optional generic args
struct PathSegment {
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    // Generic args as type indices (for later resolution)
    generic_args: [i64; 8],
    n_generics: i64,
}

fn path_segment_new() -> PathSegment {
    PathSegment {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        generic_args: [0; 8],
        n_generics: 0,
    }
}

// Path: a::b::c
struct Path {
    segments: [PathSegment; 8],
    n_segments: i64,
}

fn path_new() -> Path {
    Path {
        segments: [path_segment_new(); 8],
        n_segments: 0,
    }
}

fn path_simple_from_bytes(bytes: [i8; 64], len: i64) -> Path with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = path_new();
    var seg = path_segment_new();
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < len && i < 64 {
        seg.name[i as usize] = bytes[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    seg.name_len = len;
    p.segments[0] = seg;
    p.n_segments = 1;
    p
}

// ============================================================================
// VISIBILITY
// ============================================================================

// Visibility constants
fn VIS_PRIVATE() -> i32 { 0 }
fn VIS_PUBLIC() -> i32 { 1 }
fn VIS_CRATE() -> i32 { 2 }
fn VIS_SUPER() -> i32 { 3 }

// ============================================================================
// TYPE EXPRESSIONS
// ============================================================================

// Type expression kind constants
fn TY_PATH() -> i32 { 0 }       // i32, String, foo::Bar<T>
fn TY_REF() -> i32 { 1 }        // &T
fn TY_REF_MUT() -> i32 { 2 }    // &!T
fn TY_ARRAY() -> i32 { 3 }      // [T; N]
fn TY_SLICE() -> i32 { 4 }      // [T]
fn TY_TUPLE() -> i32 { 5 }      // (T1, T2, ...)
fn TY_FUNC() -> i32 { 6 }       // fn(T1, T2) -> R
fn TY_UNIT() -> i32 { 7 }       // ()
fn TY_NEVER() -> i32 { 8 }      // !
fn TY_INFER() -> i32 { 9 }      // _
fn TY_PTR() -> i32 { 10 }       // *T or *!T
fn TY_UNIT_TYPE() -> i32 { 11 } // Type with unit annotation (mg, mL)

// Type expression (stored inline with kind discriminator)
struct TypeExpr {
    kind: i32,
    span: Span,
    // For path types
    path: Path,
    // For ref/ptr types
    is_mut: bool,
    inner_type_idx: i64,  // Index into type pool for inner type
    // For array types
    array_size: i64,
    // For tuple/function types (indices into type pool)
    element_types: [i64; 16],
    n_elements: i64,
    return_type_idx: i64,
    // For unit types
    unit_name: [i8; 32],
    unit_name_len: i64,
}

fn type_expr_new() -> TypeExpr {
    TypeExpr {
        kind: TY_UNIT(),
        span: span_dummy(),
        path: path_new(),
        is_mut: false,
        inner_type_idx: -1,
        array_size: 0,
        element_types: [0; 16],
        n_elements: 0,
        return_type_idx: -1,
        unit_name: [0; 32],
        unit_name_len: 0,
    }
}

fn type_expr_unit() -> TypeExpr with Mut {
    var te = type_expr_new();
    te.kind = TY_UNIT();
    te
}

fn type_expr_path(p: Path) -> TypeExpr with Mut {
    var te = type_expr_new();
    te.kind = TY_PATH();
    te.path = p;
    te
}

struct FnDef {
    id: NodeId,
    visibility: i32,
    modifiers: FnModifiers,
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    generics: Generics,
    params: [Param; 32],
    n_params: i64,
    has_return_type: bool,
    return_type_idx: i64,  // Index into type pool
    effects: [EffectRef; 8],
    n_effects: i64,
    body: Block,
    span: Span,
}

fn fn_def_new() -> FnDef {
    var seg = PathSegment {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        generic_args: [0; 8],
        n_generics: 0,
    };
    var gp = GenericParam {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        bound_indices: [0; 8],
        n_bounds: 0,
        has_default: false,
        default_type_idx: -1,
    };
    var param = Param {
        id: NodeId { value: 0 },
        is_mut: false,
        pattern_idx: -1,
        type_idx: -1,
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
    };
    var effect = EffectRef {
        path: Path { segments: [seg; 8], n_segments: 0 },
        type_args: [0; 8],
        n_type_args: 0,
    };
    FnDef {
        id: NodeId { value: 0 },
        visibility: VIS_PRIVATE(),
        modifiers: FnModifiers {
            is_async: false,
            is_unsafe: false,
            is_const: false,
            is_extern: false,
            is_kernel: false,
        },
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        generics: Generics { params: [gp; 16], n_params: 0 },
        params: [param; 32],
        n_params: 0,
        has_return_type: false,
        return_type_idx: -1,
        effects: [effect; 8],
        n_effects: 0,
        body: Block {
            stmt_indices: [0; 256],
            n_stmts: 0,
            has_trailing_expr: false,
            trailing_expr_idx: -1,
        },
        span: Span { start: 0, end: 0 },
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TOKEN AND SPAN (from lexer)
// ============================================================================

struct Span {
    start: i64,
    end: i64,
}

fn span_new(s: i64, e: i64) -> Span {
    Span { start: s, end: e }
}

struct Token {
    kind: i32,
    span: Span,
    text: [i8; 256],
    text_len: i64,
}

fn token_new() -> Token {
    Token {
        kind: TK_EOF(),
        span: Span { start: 0, end: 0 },
        text: [0; 256],
        text_len: 0,
    }
}

struct TokenStream {
    tokens: [Token; 4096],
    n_tokens: i64,
    pos: i64,
}

// ============================================================================
// NODE ID GENERATOR
// ============================================================================

struct IdGenerator {
    next_val: i64,
}

fn id_generator_new() -> IdGenerator {
    IdGenerator { next_val: 1 }
}

fn id_generator_next(gen: IdGenerator) -> IdGeneratorResult {
    IdGeneratorResult {
        gen: IdGenerator { next_val: gen.next_val + 1 },
        id: NodeId { value: gen.next_val },
    }
}

struct NodeId {
    value: i64,
}

struct IdGeneratorResult {
    gen: IdGenerator,
    id: NodeId,
}

// ============================================================================
// PARSER STATE
// ============================================================================

struct Parser {
    tokens: TokenStream,
    pos: i64,
    id_gen: IdGenerator,
    allow_struct_literals: bool,
    pending_gt: bool,
}

fn parser_new(tokens: TokenStream) -> Parser {
    Parser {
        tokens: tokens,
        pos: 0,
        id_gen: id_generator_new(),
        allow_struct_literals: true,
        pending_gt: false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PARSER RESULT TYPE
// ============================================================================

struct ParseResult {
    parser: Parser,
    success: bool,
    error_msg: [i8; 256],
    error_len: i64,
}

fn parse_ok(p: Parser) -> ParseResult {
    ParseResult {
        parser: p,
        success: true,
        error_msg: [0; 256],
        error_len: 0,
    }
}

fn parse_err(p: Parser, msg: [i8; 256], len: i64) -> ParseResult {
    ParseResult {
        parser: p,
        success: false,
        error_msg: msg,
        error_len: len,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PARSER HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Get current token
fn parser_current(p: Parser) -> Token with Panic {
    if p.pos < p.tokens.n_tokens {
        p.tokens.tokens[p.pos as usize]
    } else {
        // Return EOF token (token_new already sets kind=TK_EOF)
        token_new()
    }
}

// Get current token kind
fn parser_peek(p: Parser) -> i32 with Panic {
    parser_current(p).kind
}

// Look ahead n tokens
fn parser_peek_n(p: Parser, n: i64) -> i32 with Panic {
    let idx = p.pos + n;
    if idx < p.tokens.n_tokens {
        p.tokens.tokens[idx as usize].kind
    } else {
        TK_EOF()
    }
}

// Check if at specific token kind
fn parser_at(p: Parser, kind: i32) -> bool with Panic {
    parser_peek(p) == kind
}

// Check if at any of the given kinds
fn parser_at_any(p: Parser, k1: i32, k2: i32, k3: i32) -> bool with Panic {
    let curr = parser_peek(p);
    curr == k1 || curr == k2 || curr == k3
}

// Advance parser and return the consumed token
fn parser_advance(p: Parser) -> ParserAdvanceResult with Mut, Panic {
    let tok = parser_current(p);
    var new_p = p;
    if new_p.pos < new_p.tokens.n_tokens {
        new_p.pos = new_p.pos + 1;
    }
    ParserAdvanceResult {
        parser: new_p,
        token: tok,
    }
}

struct ParserAdvanceResult {
    parser: Parser,
    token: Token,
}

// Expect a specific token kind, advance if found
fn parser_expect(p: Parser, kind: i32) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic {
    if parser_at(p, kind) {
        let result = parser_advance(p);
        parse_ok(result.parser)
    } else {
        var msg: [i8; 256] = [0; 256];
        // "Expected token kind N"
        msg[0] = 69; msg[1] = 120; msg[2] = 112; msg[3] = 101; // Expe
        msg[4] = 99; msg[5] = 116; msg[6] = 101; msg[7] = 100; // cted
        parse_err(p, msg, 8)
    }
}

// Get current span
fn parser_span(p: Parser) -> Span with Panic {
    parser_current(p).span
}

// Check if at EOF
fn parser_at_eof(p: Parser) -> bool with Panic {
    parser_at(p, TK_EOF())
}

// ============================================================================
// PATH PARSING
// ============================================================================

struct PathSegment {
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    generic_args: [i64; 8],
    n_generics: i64,
}

fn path_segment_new() -> PathSegment {
    PathSegment {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        generic_args: [0; 8],
        n_generics: 0,
    }
}

struct Path {
    segments: [PathSegment; 8],
    n_segments: i64,
}

fn path_new() -> Path {
    Path {
        segments: [path_segment_new(); 8],
        n_segments: 0,
    }
}

struct ParsePathResult {
    parser: Parser,
    path: Path,
    success: bool,
}

// Parse a path: a::b::c
fn parse_path(p: Parser) -> ParsePathResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    var path = path_new();

    // First segment must be an identifier
    if !parser_at(parser, TK_IDENT()) {
        return ParsePathResult {
            parser: parser,
            path: path,
            success: false,
        }
    }

    // Parse first segment
    let adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = adv.parser;
    var seg = path_segment_new();

    // Copy token text to segment name
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < adv.token.text_len && i < 64 {
        seg.name[i as usize] = adv.token.text[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    seg.name_len = adv.token.text_len;
    path.segments[0] = seg;
    path.n_segments = 1;

    // Parse remaining segments
    while parser_at(parser, TK_COLON_COLON()) && path.n_segments < 8 {
        // Consume ::
        let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv2.parser;

        // Expect identifier
        if !parser_at(parser, TK_IDENT()) {
            return ParsePathResult {
                parser: parser,
                path: path,
                success: false,
            }
        }

        let adv3 = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv3.parser;

        var seg2 = path_segment_new();
        var j: i64 = 0;
        while j < adv3.token.text_len && j < 64 {
            seg2.name[j as usize] = adv3.token.text[j as usize];
            j = j + 1;
        }
        seg2.name_len = adv3.token.text_len;
        path.segments[path.n_segments as usize] = seg2;
        path.n_segments = path.n_segments + 1;
    }

    ParsePathResult {
        parser: parser,
        path: path,
        success: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TYPE EXPRESSION PARSING
// ============================================================================

// Type expression kind constants
fn TY_PATH() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TY_REF() -> i32 { 1 }
fn TY_REF_MUT() -> i32 { 2 }
fn TY_ARRAY() -> i32 { 3 }
fn TY_SLICE() -> i32 { 4 }
fn TY_TUPLE() -> i32 { 5 }
fn TY_FUNC() -> i32 { 6 }
fn TY_UNIT() -> i32 { 7 }

struct TypeExpr {
    kind: i32,
    span: Span,
    path: Path,
    is_mut: bool,
    inner_type_idx: i64,
    array_size: i64,
    element_types: [i64; 16],
    n_elements: i64,
}

fn type_expr_new() -> TypeExpr {
    TypeExpr {
        kind: TY_UNIT(),
        span: Span { start: 0, end: 0 },
        path: path_new(),
        is_mut: false,
        inner_type_idx: -1,
        array_size: 0,
        element_types: [0; 16],
        n_elements: 0,
    }
}

struct ParseTypeResult {
    parser: Parser,
    ty: TypeExpr,
    success: bool,
}

// Parse a type expression
fn parse_type(p: Parser) -> ParseTypeResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    let start = parser_span(parser).start;

    // Check for reference types: & or &!
    if parser_at(parser, TK_AMP()) {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;

        // Check for &!
        let is_mut = parser_at(parser, TK_BANG());
        if is_mut {
            let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv2.parser;
        }

        // Parse inner type
        let inner = parse_type(parser);
        if !inner.success {
            return inner
        }
        parser = inner.parser;

        var ty = type_expr_new();
        if is_mut {
            ty.kind = TY_REF_MUT();
        } else {
            ty.kind = TY_REF();
        }
        ty.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

        return ParseTypeResult {
            parser: parser,
            ty: ty,
            success: true,
        }
    }

    // Check for unit type: ()
    if parser_at(parser, TK_LPAREN()) {
        let next = parser_peek_n(parser, 1);
        if next == TK_RPAREN() {
            let adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv.parser;
            let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv2.parser;

            var ty = type_expr_new();
            ty.kind = TY_UNIT();
            ty.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

            return ParseTypeResult {
                parser: parser,
                ty: ty,
                success: true,
            }
        }
    }

    // Check for array/slice: [T] or [T; N]
    if parser_at(parser, TK_LBRACKET()) {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;

        let elem = parse_type(parser);
        if !elem.success {
            return elem
        }
        parser = elem.parser;

        var ty = type_expr_new();

        if parser_at(parser, TK_SEMI()) {
            // Array: [T; N]
            let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv2.parser;

            // Parse size expression (simplified: just integer)
            if parser_at(parser, TK_INT_LIT()) {
                let adv3 = parser_advance(parser);
                parser = adv3.parser;
                // Parse integer from text (simplified)
                ty.array_size = 0;  // Would parse actual integer
            }

            ty.kind = TY_ARRAY();
        } else {
            // Slice: [T]
            ty.kind = TY_SLICE();
        }

        // Expect ]
        if !parser_at(parser, TK_RBRACKET()) {
            return ParseTypeResult {
                parser: parser,
                ty: type_expr_new(),
                success: false,
            }
        }
        let adv4 = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv4.parser;

        ty.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

        return ParseTypeResult {
            parser: parser,
            ty: ty,
            success: true,
        }
    }

    // Path type (most common): i32, String, foo::Bar<T>
    let path_result = parse_path(parser);
    if !path_result.success {
        return ParseTypeResult {
            parser: path_result.parser,
            ty: type_expr_new(),
            success: false,
        }
    }

    var ty = type_expr_new();
    ty.kind = TY_PATH();
    ty.path = path_result.path;
    ty.span = span_new(start, parser_span(path_result.parser).end);

    ParseTypeResult {
        parser: path_result.parser,
        ty: ty,
        success: true,
    }
}

// Operator tokens we need for type parsing
fn TK_AMP() -> i32 { 226 }
fn TK_BANG() -> i32 { 229 }

// ============================================================================
// ITEM PARSING
// ============================================================================

// Item kind constants
fn ITEM_FN() -> i32 { 0 }
fn ITEM_STRUCT() -> i32 { 1 }
fn ITEM_ENUM() -> i32 { 2 }
fn ITEM_TRAIT() -> i32 { 3 }
fn ITEM_IMPL() -> i32 { 4 }
fn ITEM_IMPORT() -> i32 { 8 }

struct Item {
    kind: i32,
    span: Span,
    // Function data
    fn_name: [i8; 64],
    fn_name_len: i64,
    // Struct data
    struct_name: [i8; 64],
    struct_name_len: i64,
}

fn item_new() -> Item {
    Item {
        kind: 0,
        span: Span { start: 0, end: 0 },
        fn_name: [0; 64],
        fn_name_len: 0,
        struct_name: [0; 64],
        struct_name_len: 0,
    }
}

struct ParseItemResult {
    parser: Parser,
    item: Item,
    success: bool,
}

// Parse a top-level item
fn parse_item(p: Parser) -> ParseItemResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;

    // Skip doc comments
    while parser_at(parser, TK_DOC_COMMENT_OUTER()) || parser_at(parser, TK_DOC_COMMENT_INNER()) {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;
    }

    // Check visibility
    let is_pub = parser_at(parser, TK_PUB());
    if is_pub {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;
    }

    // Check modifiers (linear, kernel, etc.)
    let is_linear = parser_at(parser, TK_LINEAR());
    if is_linear {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;
    }

    let is_kernel = parser_at(parser, TK_KERNEL());
    if is_kernel {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;
    }

    // Dispatch based on keyword
    let curr = parser_peek(parser);

    if curr == TK_FN() {
        return parse_fn(parser)
    }

    if curr == TK_STRUCT() {
        return parse_struct(parser)
    }

    if curr == TK_ENUM() {
        return parse_enum(parser)
    }

    if curr == TK_IMPORT() || curr == TK_USE() {
        return parse_import(parser)
    }

    if curr == TK_EXTERN() {
        return parse_extern(parser)
    }

    // Unknown item
    ParseItemResult {
        parser: parser,
        item: item_new(),
        success: false,
    }
}

// Doc comment token kinds
fn TK_DOC_COMMENT_OUTER() -> i32 { 310 }
fn TK_DOC_COMMENT_INNER() -> i32 { 311 }

// ============================================================================
// FUNCTION PARSING
// ============================================================================

struct FnDef {
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    n_params: i64,
    has_return_type: bool,
    return_type: TypeExpr,
    span: Span,
}

fn fn_def_new() -> FnDef {
    FnDef {
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        n_params: 0,
        has_return_type: false,
        return_type: type_expr_new(),
        span: Span { start: 0, end: 0 },
    }
}

// ParseFnResult removed - using ParseItemResult instead

// Parse function: fn name(params) -> ReturnType { body }
fn parse_fn(p: Parser) -> ParseItemResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    let start = parser_span(parser).start;

    // Consume 'fn'
    let adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = adv.parser;

    // Parse function name
    if !parser_at(parser, TK_IDENT()) {
        return ParseItemResult {
            parser: parser,
            item: item_new(),
            success: false,
        }
    }

    let name_adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = name_adv.parser;

    var item = item_new();
    item.kind = ITEM_FN();

    // Copy name
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < name_adv.token.text_len && i < 64 {
        item.fn_name[i as usize] = name_adv.token.text[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    item.fn_name_len = name_adv.token.text_len;

    // Expect (
    if !parser_at(parser, TK_LPAREN()) {
        return ParseItemResult {
            parser: parser,
            item: item_new(),
            success: false,
        }
    }
    let lparen_adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = lparen_adv.parser;

    // Parse parameters (simplified: skip to closing paren)
    var depth: i64 = 1;
    while !parser_at_eof(parser) && depth > 0 {
        let curr = parser_peek(parser);
        if curr == TK_LPAREN() {
            depth = depth + 1;
        } else if curr == TK_RPAREN() {
            depth = depth - 1;
        }
        if depth > 0 {
            let skip_adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = skip_adv.parser;
        }
    }

    // Consume )
    let rparen_adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = rparen_adv.parser;

    // Check for return type: ->
    if parser_at(parser, TK_ARROW()) {
        let arrow_adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = arrow_adv.parser;

        // Parse return type
        let ty_result = parse_type(parser);
        if ty_result.success {
            parser = ty_result.parser;
        }
    }

    // Check for effects: with Effect1, Effect2
    if parser_at(parser, TK_WITH()) {
        let with_adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = with_adv.parser;

        // Parse effect list (simplified: skip to {)
        while !parser_at_eof(parser) && !parser_at(parser, TK_LBRACE()) {
            let skip_adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = skip_adv.parser;
        }
    }

    // Parse body: { ... }
    if parser_at(parser, TK_LBRACE()) {
        // Skip body for now
        var brace_depth: i64 = 0;
        while !parser_at_eof(parser) {
            let curr = parser_peek(parser);
            if curr == TK_LBRACE() {
                brace_depth = brace_depth + 1;
            } else if curr == TK_RBRACE() {
                brace_depth = brace_depth - 1;
                if brace_depth == 0 {
                    let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
                    parser = adv2.parser;
                    break
                }
            }
            let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv2.parser;
        }
    }

    item.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

    ParseItemResult {
        parser: parser,
        item: item,
        success: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STRUCT PARSING
// ============================================================================

// Parse struct: struct Name { fields }
fn parse_struct(p: Parser) -> ParseItemResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    let start = parser_span(parser).start;

    // Consume 'struct'
    let adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = adv.parser;

    // Parse struct name
    if !parser_at(parser, TK_IDENT()) {
        return ParseItemResult {
            parser: parser,
            item: item_new(),
            success: false,
        }
    }

    let name_adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = name_adv.parser;

    var item = item_new();
    item.kind = ITEM_STRUCT();

    // Copy name
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < name_adv.token.text_len && i < 64 {
        item.struct_name[i as usize] = name_adv.token.text[i as usize];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    item.struct_name_len = name_adv.token.text_len;

    // Parse generics if present: <T, U>
    if parser_at(parser, TK_LT()) {
        // Skip generics for now
        while !parser_at_eof(parser) && !parser_at(parser, TK_GT()) {
            let skip_adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = skip_adv.parser;
        }
        if parser_at(parser, TK_GT()) {
            let gt_adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = gt_adv.parser;
        }
    }

    // Expect { or ;
    if parser_at(parser, TK_LBRACE()) {
        // Skip body
        var brace_depth: i64 = 0;
        while !parser_at_eof(parser) {
            let curr = parser_peek(parser);
            if curr == TK_LBRACE() {
                brace_depth = brace_depth + 1;
            } else if curr == TK_RBRACE() {
                brace_depth = brace_depth - 1;
                if brace_depth == 0 {
                    let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
                    parser = adv2.parser;
                    break
                }
            }
            let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv2.parser;
        }
    }

    item.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

    ParseItemResult {
        parser: parser,
        item: item,
        success: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ENUM PARSING (placeholder)
// ============================================================================

fn parse_enum(p: Parser) -> ParseItemResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Similar to struct parsing
    parse_struct(p)  // Placeholder
}

// ============================================================================
// IMPORT PARSING
// ============================================================================

fn parse_import(p: Parser) -> ParseItemResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    let start = parser_span(parser).start;

    // Consume 'import' or 'use'
    let adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = adv.parser;

    var item = item_new();
    item.kind = ITEM_IMPORT();

    // Parse path
    let path_result = parse_path(parser);
    if path_result.success {
        parser = path_result.parser;
    }

    // Consume optional ;
    if parser_at(parser, TK_SEMI()) {
        let semi_adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = semi_adv.parser;
    }

    item.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

    ParseItemResult {
        parser: parser,
        item: item,
        success: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EXTERN PARSING
// ============================================================================

fn parse_extern(p: Parser) -> ParseItemResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    let start = parser_span(parser).start;

    // Consume 'extern'
    let adv = parser_advance(parser);
    parser = adv.parser;

    var item = item_new();
    item.kind = ITEM_FN();  // extern fn

    // Skip to end of extern block
    if parser_at(parser, TK_LBRACE()) {
        var brace_depth: i64 = 0;
        while !parser_at_eof(parser) {
            let curr = parser_peek(parser);
            if curr == TK_LBRACE() {
                brace_depth = brace_depth + 1;
            } else if curr == TK_RBRACE() {
                brace_depth = brace_depth - 1;
                if brace_depth == 0 {
                    let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
                    parser = adv2.parser;
                    break
                }
            }
            let adv2 = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = adv2.parser;
        }
    }

    item.span = span_new(start, parser_span(parser).end);

    ParseItemResult {
        parser: parser,
        item: item,
        success: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// AST
// ============================================================================

struct Ast {
    module_name: Path,
    has_module_name: bool,
    items: [Item; 1024],
    n_items: i64,
}

fn ast_new() -> Ast {
    Ast {
        module_name: path_new(),
        has_module_name: false,
        items: [item_new(); 1024],
        n_items: 0,
    }
}

struct ParseAstResult {
    parser: Parser,
    ast: Ast,
    success: bool,
}

// Parse a complete Sounio program
fn parse_program(p: Parser) -> ParseAstResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var parser = p;
    var ast = ast_new();

    // Skip initial doc comments
    while parser_at(parser, TK_DOC_COMMENT_OUTER()) || parser_at(parser, TK_DOC_COMMENT_INNER()) {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;
    }

    // Optional module declaration
    if parser_at(parser, TK_MODULE()) {
        let adv = parser_advance(parser);
        parser = adv.parser;

        let path_result = parse_path(parser);
        if path_result.success {
            parser = path_result.parser;
            ast.module_name = path_result.path;
            ast.has_module_name = true;
        }

        // Consume optional ;
        if parser_at(parser, TK_SEMI()) {
            let semi_adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = semi_adv.parser;
        }
    }

    // Parse items
    while !parser_at_eof(parser) && ast.n_items < 1024 {
        let item_result = parse_item(parser);
        if item_result.success {
            parser = item_result.parser;
            ast.items[ast.n_items as usize] = item_result.item;
            ast.n_items = ast.n_items + 1;
        } else {
            // Skip unknown token
            let skip_adv = parser_advance(parser);
            parser = skip_adv.parser;
        }
    }

    ParseAstResult {
        parser: parser,
        ast: ast,
        success: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PUBLIC API
// ============================================================================

// Parse tokens into an AST
fn parse(tokens: TokenStream) -> ParseAstResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let parser = parser_new(tokens);
    parse_program(parser)
}

// This module implements statement parsing for the self-hosted Sounio parser.

// ============================================================================
// TOKEN KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn TK_EOF() -> i32 { 0 }
fn TK_IDENT() -> i32 { 200 }
fn TK_INT_LIT() -> i32 { 201 }
fn TK_FLOAT_LIT() -> i32 { 205 }
fn TK_TRUE() -> i32 { 39 }
fn TK_FALSE() -> i32 { 40 }

fn TK_LET() -> i32 { 15 }
fn TK_VAR() -> i32 { 16 }
fn TK_RETURN() -> i32 { 32 }
fn TK_BREAK() -> i32 { 30 }
fn TK_CONTINUE() -> i32 { 31 }
fn TK_IF() -> i32 { 24 }
fn TK_ELSE() -> i32 { 25 }
fn TK_WHILE() -> i32 { 28 }
fn TK_FOR() -> i32 { 27 }
fn TK_LOOP() -> i32 { 29 }
fn TK_LPAREN() -> i32 { 282 }
fn TK_RPAREN() -> i32 { 283 }

fn TK_EQ() -> i32 { 230 }
fn TK_COLON() -> i32 { 292 }
fn TK_SEMI() -> i32 { 291 }
fn TK_LBRACE() -> i32 { 284 }
fn TK_RBRACE() -> i32 { 285 }
fn TK_PLUS() -> i32 { 220 }
fn TK_MINUS() -> i32 { 221 }
fn TK_STAR() -> i32 { 222 }

// ============================================================================
// STATEMENT KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn STMT_LET() -> i32 { 0 }
fn STMT_VAR() -> i32 { 1 }
fn STMT_EXPR() -> i32 { 2 }
fn STMT_RETURN() -> i32 { 3 }
fn STMT_BREAK() -> i32 { 4 }
fn STMT_CONTINUE() -> i32 { 5 }
fn STMT_IF() -> i32 { 6 }
fn STMT_WHILE() -> i32 { 7 }
fn STMT_FOR() -> i32 { 8 }
fn STMT_LOOP() -> i32 { 9 }
fn STMT_EMPTY() -> i32 { 10 }

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLE STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct Token {
    kind: i32,
    val: i64,
    name: [i8; 32],
    name_len: i64,
}

fn token_new() -> Token {
    Token { kind: TK_EOF(), val: 0, name: [0; 32], name_len: 0 }
}

fn make_token(k: i32) -> Token {
    Token { kind: k, val: 0, name: [0; 32], name_len: 0 }
}

fn make_int_token(v: i64) -> Token {
    Token { kind: TK_INT_LIT(), val: v, name: [0; 32], name_len: 0 }
}

fn make_ident_token(c0: i8, c1: i8, c2: i8, len: i64) -> Token with Mut, Panic {
    var t = token_new();
    t.kind = TK_IDENT();
    t.name[0] = c0;
    t.name[1] = c1;
    t.name[2] = c2;
    t.name_len = len;
    t
}

struct State {
    tokens: [Token; 64],
    n: i64,
    pos: i64,
}

fn state_new() -> State {
    State {
        tokens: [token_new(); 64],
        n: 0,
        pos: 0,
    }
}

fn peek(s: State) -> i32 with Panic {
    if s.pos < s.n {
        s.tokens[s.pos as usize].kind
    } else {
        TK_EOF()
    }
}

fn at(s: State, k: i32) -> bool with Panic {
    peek(s) == k
}

fn advance(s: State) -> State with Mut {
    var new_s = s;
    if new_s.pos < new_s.n {
        new_s.pos = new_s.pos + 1;
    }
    new_s
}

fn current(s: State) -> Token with Panic {
    if s.pos < s.n {
        s.tokens[s.pos as usize]
    } else {
        token_new()
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STATEMENT STRUCTURE
// ============================================================================

struct Stmt {
    kind: i32,
    // For let/var: variable name
    var_name: [i8; 32],
    var_name_len: i64,
    is_mutable: bool,
    has_type: bool,
    has_init: bool,
    init_val: i64,  // Simplified: just store int value for now
    // For return
    has_return_val: bool,
    return_val: i64,
    // For if/while/loop - number of statements in body
    body_count: i64,
    // For if - has else branch
    has_else: bool,
    else_count: i64,
}

fn stmt_new() -> Stmt {
    Stmt {
        kind: STMT_EMPTY(),
        var_name: [0; 32],
        var_name_len: 0,
        is_mutable: false,
        has_type: false,
        has_init: false,
        init_val: 0,
        has_return_val: false,
        return_val: 0,
        body_count: 0,
        has_else: false,
        else_count: 0,
    }
}

fn stmt_let(name: [i8; 32], len: i64, init: i64) -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_LET();
    s.var_name = name;
    s.var_name_len = len;
    s.is_mutable = false;
    s.has_init = true;
    s.init_val = init;
    s
}

fn stmt_var(name: [i8; 32], len: i64, init: i64) -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_VAR();
    s.var_name = name;
    s.var_name_len = len;
    s.is_mutable = true;
    s.has_init = true;
    s.init_val = init;
    s
}

fn stmt_return(val: i64) -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_RETURN();
    s.has_return_val = true;
    s.return_val = val;
    s
}

fn stmt_return_void() -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_RETURN();
    s.has_return_val = false;
    s
}

fn stmt_break() -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_BREAK();
    s
}

fn stmt_continue() -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_CONTINUE();
    s
}

fn stmt_expr() -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_EXPR();
    s
}

fn stmt_if(body_count: i64, has_else: bool, else_count: i64) -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_IF();
    s.body_count = body_count;
    s.has_else = has_else;
    s.else_count = else_count;
    s
}

fn stmt_while(body_count: i64) -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_WHILE();
    s.body_count = body_count;
    s
}

fn stmt_loop(body_count: i64) -> Stmt with Mut {
    var s = stmt_new();
    s.kind = STMT_LOOP();
    s.body_count = body_count;
    s
}

// ============================================================================
// PARSE RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct ParseResult {
    state: State,
    stmt: Stmt,
    ok: bool,
}

fn parse_ok(s: State, st: Stmt) -> ParseResult {
    ParseResult { state: s, stmt: st, ok: true }
}

fn parse_err(s: State) -> ParseResult {
    ParseResult { state: s, stmt: stmt_new(), ok: false }
}

// ============================================================================
// STATEMENT PARSING
// ============================================================================

// Parse let statement: let x = expr;
fn parse_let(s: State) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    // Consume 'let'
    if !at(st, TK_LET()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    // Expect identifier
    if !at(st, TK_IDENT()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    let name_tok = current(st);
    st = advance(st);

    // Optional type annotation: : Type
    if at(st, TK_COLON()) {
        st = advance(st);
        // Skip type for now (just expect identifier)
        if at(st, TK_IDENT()) {
            st = advance(st);
        }
    }

    // Expect =
    if !at(st, TK_EQ()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    // Parse init expression (simplified: just int literal)
    if !at(st, TK_INT_LIT()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    let init_tok = current(st);
    st = advance(st);

    // Optional semicolon
    if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
        st = advance(st);
    }

    parse_ok(st, stmt_let(name_tok.name, name_tok.name_len, init_tok.val))
}

// Parse var statement: var x = expr;
fn parse_var(s: State) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    // Consume 'var'
    if !at(st, TK_VAR()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    // Expect identifier
    if !at(st, TK_IDENT()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    let name_tok = current(st);
    st = advance(st);

    // Optional type annotation
    if at(st, TK_COLON()) {
        st = advance(st);
        if at(st, TK_IDENT()) {
            st = advance(st);
        }
    }

    // Expect =
    if !at(st, TK_EQ()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    // Parse init expression (simplified: just int literal)
    if !at(st, TK_INT_LIT()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    let init_tok = current(st);
    st = advance(st);

    // Optional semicolon
    if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
        st = advance(st);
    }

    parse_ok(st, stmt_var(name_tok.name, name_tok.name_len, init_tok.val))
}

// Parse return statement: return expr;
fn parse_return(s: State) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    // Consume 'return'
    if !at(st, TK_RETURN()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    // Check for value or just semicolon
    if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
        st = advance(st);
        return parse_ok(st, stmt_return_void())
    }

    // Check for } (return at end of block without semicolon)
    if at(st, TK_RBRACE()) {
        return parse_ok(st, stmt_return_void())
    }

    // Parse return value (simplified: int literal or identifier)
    if at(st, TK_INT_LIT()) {
        let val_tok = current(st);
        st = advance(st);

        if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
            st = advance(st);
        }

        return parse_ok(st, stmt_return(val_tok.val))
    }

    // Handle identifier as return value (treat as returning variable)
    if at(st, TK_IDENT()) {
        // For now, skip the identifier - we'd need proper expression parsing
        // to actually capture the variable name
        st = advance(st);

        if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
            st = advance(st);
        }

        // Mark as having a return value (even though we can't store the name)
        var ret_stmt = stmt_new();
        ret_stmt.kind = STMT_RETURN();
        ret_stmt.has_return_val = true;
        ret_stmt.return_val = -1;  // Sentinel for "expression, not literal"
        return parse_ok(st, ret_stmt)
    }

    // Return without value
    parse_ok(st, stmt_return_void())
}

// Parse break statement
fn parse_break(s: State) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    if !at(st, TK_BREAK()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
        st = advance(st);
    }

    parse_ok(st, stmt_break())
}

// Parse continue statement
fn parse_continue(s: State) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    if !at(st, TK_CONTINUE()) {
        return parse_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
        st = advance(st);
    }

    parse_ok(st, stmt_continue())
}

// Skip a block and count statements (simplified - just counts braces and semicolons)
fn skip_block(s: State) -> State with Div, Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    if !at(st, TK_LBRACE()) {
        return st
    }
    st = advance(st);  // consume {

    var depth: i64 = 1;
    while depth > 0 && !at(st, TK_EOF()) {
        if at(st, TK_LBRACE()) {
            depth = depth + 1;
        }
        if at(st, TK_RBRACE()) {
            depth = depth - 1;
        }
        st = advance(st);
    }

    st
}

// Skip a condition expression (simplified - handles identifier/literal and basic ops)
fn skip_condition(s: State) -> State with Div, Mut, Panic {
    var st = s;

    // Simple condition: just identifier, literal, or small expression
    // Skip tokens until we hit {
    while !at(st, TK_LBRACE()) && !at(st, TK_EOF()) {
        st = advance(st);
    }

    st
}

// Parse any statement
fn parse_stmt(s: State) -> ParseResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var st = s;
    let curr = peek(st);

    if curr == TK_LET() {
        return parse_let(st)
    }

    if curr == TK_VAR() {
        return parse_var(st)
    }

    if curr == TK_RETURN() {
        return parse_return(st)
    }

    if curr == TK_BREAK() {
        return parse_break(st)
    }

    if curr == TK_CONTINUE() {
        return parse_continue(st)
    }

    // If statement: if condition { body } [else { body }]
    if curr == TK_IF() {
        st = advance(st);  // consume 'if'
        st = skip_condition(st);

        // Parse body block
        let body_start = st.pos;
        st = skip_block(st);
        let body_count = st.pos - body_start - 2;  // Approximate statement count

        var has_else = false;
        var else_count: i64 = 0;

        // Check for else
        if at(st, TK_ELSE()) {
            st = advance(st);
            has_else = true;

            // else if or else { }
            if at(st, TK_IF()) {
                // Treat else if as nested - for now just skip
                let else_result = parse_stmt(st);
                if else_result.ok {
                    st = else_result.state;
                    else_count = 1;
                }
            } else {
                let else_start = st.pos;
                st = skip_block(st);
                else_count = st.pos - else_start - 2;
            }
        }

        return parse_ok(st, stmt_if(body_count, has_else, else_count))
    }

    // While statement: while condition { body }
    if curr == TK_WHILE() {
        st = advance(st);  // consume 'while'
        st = skip_condition(st);

        let body_start = st.pos;
        st = skip_block(st);
        let body_count = st.pos - body_start - 2;

        return parse_ok(st, stmt_while(body_count))
    }

    // Loop statement: loop { body }
    if curr == TK_LOOP() {
        st = advance(st);  // consume 'loop'

        let body_start = st.pos;
        st = skip_block(st);
        let body_count = st.pos - body_start - 2;

        return parse_ok(st, stmt_loop(body_count))
    }

    // Empty statement
    if curr == TK_SEMI() {
        st = advance(st);
        return parse_ok(st, stmt_new())
    }

    // Default: expression statement (simplified)
    if curr == TK_IDENT() || curr == TK_INT_LIT() {
        // Skip expression
        st = advance(st);
        if at(st, TK_SEMI()) {
            st = advance(st);
        }
        return parse_ok(st, stmt_expr())
    }

    parse_err(st)
}

// ============================================================================
// BLOCK PARSING
// ============================================================================

struct Block {
    stmts: [Stmt; 64],
    n_stmts: i64,
}

fn block_new() -> Block {
    Block {
        stmts: [stmt_new(); 64],
        n_stmts: 0,
    }
}

struct ParseBlockResult {
    state: State,
    block: Block,
    ok: bool,
}

fn parse_block_ok(s: State, b: Block) -> ParseBlockResult {
    ParseBlockResult { state: s, block: b, ok: true }
}

fn parse_block_err(s: State) -> ParseBlockResult {
    ParseBlockResult { state: s, block: block_new(), ok: false }
}

// Parse a block: { stmts }
fn parse_block(s: State) -> ParseBlockResult with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var st = s;

    // Expect {
    if !at(st, TK_LBRACE()) {
        return parse_block_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    var blk = block_new();

    // Parse statements until }
    while !at(st, TK_RBRACE()) && !at(st, TK_EOF()) {
        let stmt_result = parse_stmt(st);
        if !stmt_result.ok {
            return parse_block_err(st)
        }
        st = stmt_result.state;

        if blk.n_stmts < 64 {
            blk.stmts[blk.n_stmts as usize] = stmt_result.stmt;
            blk.n_stmts = blk.n_stmts + 1;
        }
    }

    // Expect }
    if !at(st, TK_RBRACE()) {
        return parse_block_err(st)
    }
    st = advance(st);

    parse_block_ok(st, blk)
}

// Test: "let x = 42;"
fn test_parse_let() -> bool with Panic, Mut {
    var st = state_new();
    // let
    st.tokens[0] = make_token(TK_LET());
    // x (identifier)
    st.tokens[1] = make_ident_token(120, 0, 0, 1);  // 'x' = 120
    // =
    st.tokens[2] = make_token(TK_EQ());
    // 42
    st.tokens[3] = make_int_token(42);
    // ;
    st.tokens[4] = make_token(TK_SEMI());
    st.n = 5;

    let result = parse_let(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Failed to parse let\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.kind != STMT_LET() {
        print("  Expected STMT_LET\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.is_mutable {
        print("  let should not be mutable\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.init_val != 42 {
        print("  Expected init_val = 42\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// Test: "var y = 10;"
fn test_parse_var() -> bool with Panic, Mut {
    var st = state_new();
    st.tokens[0] = make_token(TK_VAR());
    st.tokens[1] = make_ident_token(121, 0, 0, 1);  // 'y' = 121
    st.tokens[2] = make_token(TK_EQ());
    st.tokens[3] = make_int_token(10);
    st.tokens[4] = make_token(TK_SEMI());
    st.n = 5;

    let result = parse_var(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Failed to parse var\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.kind != STMT_VAR() {
        print("  Expected STMT_VAR\n");
        return false
    }

    if !result.stmt.is_mutable {
        print("  var should be mutable\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.init_val != 10 {
        print("  Expected init_val = 10\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// Test: "return 0;"
fn test_parse_return() -> bool with Panic, Mut {
    var st = state_new();
    st.tokens[0] = make_token(TK_RETURN());
    st.tokens[1] = make_int_token(0);
    st.tokens[2] = make_token(TK_SEMI());
    st.n = 3;

    let result = parse_return(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Failed to parse return\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.kind != STMT_RETURN() {
        print("  Expected STMT_RETURN\n");
        return false
    }

    if !result.stmt.has_return_val {
        print("  Expected has_return_val\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.return_val != 0 {
        print("  Expected return_val = 0\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// Test: "{ let x = 1; return x; }"
fn test_parse_block() -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var st = state_new();
    // {
    st.tokens[0] = make_token(TK_LBRACE());
    // let
    st.tokens[1] = make_token(TK_LET());
    // x
    st.tokens[2] = make_ident_token(120, 0, 0, 1);
    // =
    st.tokens[3] = make_token(TK_EQ());
    // 1
    st.tokens[4] = make_int_token(1);
    // ;
    st.tokens[5] = make_token(TK_SEMI());
    // return
    st.tokens[6] = make_token(TK_RETURN());
    // (some identifier for x)
    st.tokens[7] = make_ident_token(120, 0, 0, 1);
    // ;
    st.tokens[8] = make_token(TK_SEMI());
    // }
    st.tokens[9] = make_token(TK_RBRACE());
    st.n = 10;

    let result = parse_block(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Failed to parse block\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.block.n_stmts != 2 {
        print("  Expected 2 statements in block\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.block.stmts[0].kind != STMT_LET() {
        print("  First stmt should be LET\n");
        return false
    }

    // Second is expression statement (return parsed as expr since we simplified)
    // Actually parse_stmt handles return specially
    if result.block.stmts[1].kind != STMT_RETURN() {
        print("  Second stmt should be RETURN\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// Test: "if x { return 1; }"
fn test_parse_if() -> bool with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var st = state_new();
    // if
    st.tokens[0] = make_token(TK_IF());
    // x (condition)
    st.tokens[1] = make_ident_token(120, 0, 0, 1);
    // {
    st.tokens[2] = make_token(TK_LBRACE());
    // return
    st.tokens[3] = make_token(TK_RETURN());
    // 1
    st.tokens[4] = make_int_token(1);
    // ;
    st.tokens[5] = make_token(TK_SEMI());
    // }
    st.tokens[6] = make_token(TK_RBRACE());
    st.n = 7;

    let result = parse_stmt(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Failed to parse if\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.kind != STMT_IF() {
        print("  Expected STMT_IF\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.has_else {
        print("  Should not have else\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// Test: "if x { 1 } else { 2 }"
fn test_parse_if_else() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var st = state_new();
    // if
    st.tokens[0] = make_token(TK_IF());
    // x
    st.tokens[1] = make_ident_token(120, 0, 0, 1);
    // {
    st.tokens[2] = make_token(TK_LBRACE());
    // 1
    st.tokens[3] = make_int_token(1);
    // }
    st.tokens[4] = make_token(TK_RBRACE());
    // else
    st.tokens[5] = make_token(TK_ELSE());
    // {
    st.tokens[6] = make_token(TK_LBRACE());
    // 2
    st.tokens[7] = make_int_token(2);
    // }
    st.tokens[8] = make_token(TK_RBRACE());
    st.n = 9;

    let result = parse_stmt(st);

    if !result.ok {
        print("  Failed to parse if-else\n");
        return false
    }

    if result.stmt.kind != STMT_IF() {
        print("  Expected STMT_IF\n");
        return false
    }

    if !result.stmt.has_else {
        print("  Should have else\n");
        return false
    }

    true
}

// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/parser/stmt.sio ===
// compiler::parser::stmt — Statement AST Nodes
//
// Statement types for the self-hosted Sounio parser.

// ============================================================================
// STATEMENT KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn STMT_LET() -> i32 { 0 }      // let x = ...
fn STMT_VAR() -> i32 { 1 }      // var x = ...
fn STMT_EXPR() -> i32 { 2 }     // expr;
fn STMT_ASSIGN() -> i32 { 3 }   // x = ...
fn STMT_EMPTY() -> i32 { 4 }    // ;

// ============================================================================
// ASSIGNMENT OPERATORS
// ============================================================================

fn ASSIGN_EQ() -> i32 { 0 }         // =
fn ASSIGN_ADD_EQ() -> i32 { 1 }     // +=
fn ASSIGN_SUB_EQ() -> i32 { 2 }     // -=
fn ASSIGN_MUL_EQ() -> i32 { 3 }     // *=
fn ASSIGN_DIV_EQ() -> i32 { 4 }     // /=
fn ASSIGN_REM_EQ() -> i32 { 5 }     // %=
fn ASSIGN_BIT_AND_EQ() -> i32 { 6 } // &=
fn ASSIGN_BIT_OR_EQ() -> i32 { 7 }  // |=
fn ASSIGN_BIT_XOR_EQ() -> i32 { 8 } // ^=
fn ASSIGN_SHL_EQ() -> i32 { 9 }     // <<=
fn ASSIGN_SHR_EQ() -> i32 { 10 }    // >>=

// ============================================================================
// PATTERN KIND CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn PAT_IDENT() -> i32 { 0 }      // x
fn PAT_WILDCARD() -> i32 { 1 }   // _
fn PAT_TUPLE() -> i32 { 2 }      // (a, b)
fn PAT_STRUCT() -> i32 { 3 }     // Foo { x, y }
fn PAT_ENUM() -> i32 { 4 }       // Some(x)
fn PAT_LITERAL() -> i32 { 5 }    // 42
fn PAT_RANGE() -> i32 { 6 }      // 1..10
fn PAT_OR() -> i32 { 7 }         // a | b
fn PAT_REF() -> i32 { 8 }        // &x
fn PAT_MUT() -> i32 { 9 }        // mut x

// ============================================================================
// PATTERN
// ============================================================================

struct Pattern {
    kind: i32,
    name: [i8; 64],
    name_len: i64,
    is_mut: bool,
    // For compound patterns (indices into pattern pool)
    sub_patterns: [i64; 16],
    n_sub_patterns: i64,
    // For struct patterns
    field_names: [[i8; 64]; 16],
    field_name_lens: [i64; 16],
    n_fields: i64,
    // For literal patterns
    literal_kind: i32,
    literal_int: i64,
    // Path for struct/enum patterns
    path_str: [i8; 128],
    path_len: i64,
}

fn pattern_new() -> Pattern {
    Pattern {
        kind: PAT_WILDCARD(),
        name: [0; 64],
        name_len: 0,
        is_mut: false,
        sub_patterns: [0; 16],
        n_sub_patterns: 0,
        field_names: [[0; 64]; 16],
        field_name_lens: [0; 16],
        n_fields: 0,
        literal_kind: 0,
        literal_int: 0,
        path_str: [0; 128],
        path_len: 0,
    }
}

fn pattern_ident(name: [i8; 64], len: i64, is_mut: bool) -> Pattern with Mut {
    var p = pattern_new();
    p.kind = PAT_IDENT();
    p.name = name;
    p.name_len = len;
    p.is_mut = is_mut;
    p
}

fn pattern_wildcard() -> Pattern with Mut {
    var p = pattern_new();
    p.kind = PAT_WILDCARD();
    p
}

// ============================================================================
// BLOCK
// ============================================================================

// Block of statements (indices into statement pool)
struct Block {
    stmt_indices: [i64; 256],
    n_stmts: i64,
    // Optional trailing expression (for block expressions)
    has_trailing_expr: bool,
    trailing_expr_idx: i64,
}

fn block_new() -> Block {
    Block {
        stmt_indices: [0; 256],
        n_stmts: 0,
        has_trailing_expr: false,
        trailing_expr_idx: -1,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STATEMENT
// ============================================================================

struct Stmt {
    kind: i32,
    // For let/var statements
    pattern_idx: i64,
    has_type: bool,
    type_idx: i64,
    has_value: bool,
    value_expr_idx: i64,
    // For expression statements
    expr_idx: i64,
    has_semi: bool,
    // For assignments
    target_expr_idx: i64,
    assign_op: i32,
}

fn stmt_new() -> Stmt {
    Stmt {
        kind: STMT_EMPTY(),
        pattern_idx: -1,
        has_type: false,
        type_idx: -1,
        has_value: false,
        value_expr_idx: -1,
        expr_idx: -1,
        has_semi: true,
        target_expr_idx: -1,
        assign_op: ASSIGN_EQ(),
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/transform/cfg_builder.sio ===
/// Phase 2.4: Control Flow Analysis (CFG Builder) for Self-Hosted Compiler
///
/// Builds control flow graphs (CFG) from function bodies, computes dominance,
/// detects loops, and verifies CFG properties.

/// Basic block in control flow graph
struct BasicBlock {
    id: i32,
    instructions: i32,      // Count of instructions
    terminator: Terminator,
    predecessor_count: i32,
    successor_count: i32,
    reachable: bool        // Can reach from entry
}

/// Terminator of a basic block
enum Terminator {
    ReturnTerm(i32),           // return value_id
    BranchTerm(i32, i32, i32), // if cond then block1 else block2
    UnreachableTerm,
}

/// Control flow graph
struct ControlFlowGraph {
    entry_block_id: i32,
    block_count: i32,
    edge_count: i32,
    has_cycles: bool,
    dominance_computed: bool,
    loops_found: i32
}

/// Initialize empty CFG
fn cfg_new() -> ControlFlowGraph {
    ControlFlowGraph {
        entry_block_id: 0,
        block_count: 0,
        edge_count: 0,
        has_cycles: false,
        dominance_computed: false,
        loops_found: 0
    }
}

/// Add a new basic block to CFG
fn cfg_add_block(cfg: &!ControlFlowGraph, term: Terminator) -> i32 {
    let block_id = cfg.block_count
    cfg.block_count = cfg.block_count + 1
    block_id
}

/// Add edge from block `from` to block `to`
fn cfg_add_edge(cfg: &!ControlFlowGraph, from: i32, to: i32) -> bool {
    if from < 0 || from >= cfg.block_count { return false }
    if to < 0 || to >= cfg.block_count { return false }
    cfg.edge_count = cfg.edge_count + 1
    true
}

/// Check if CFG has cycles (contains loops)
fn cfg_has_cycles(cfg: &ControlFlowGraph) -> bool {
    cfg.has_cycles
}

/// Compute dominance information
fn cfg_compute_dominance(cfg: &!ControlFlowGraph) {
    // Placeholder: real implementation would use iterative dataflow
    cfg.dominance_computed = true
}

/// Find loops in CFG (back edges in DFS)
fn cfg_find_loops(cfg: &!ControlFlowGraph) -> i32 {
    // Placeholder: real implementation would detect back edges
    cfg.loops_found = 0
    cfg.loops_found
}

/// Phase 2.3: Desugaring Pass for Self-Hosted Sedenion Compiler
///
/// Converts high-level syntax constructs (for..in, match guards, optional chaining)
/// to lower-level primitives (while loops, nested ifs).

/// Desugaring result
struct DesugarResult {
    succeeded: bool,
    original_count: i32,    // Original constructs
    desugared_count: i32,   // After desugaring
    errors: i32,
    transformations: i32    // Number of transformations applied
}

/// For loop statement
struct ForLoop {
    loop_id: i32,
    iterable_id: i32,  // ID of iterable expression
    var_name: str,
    body_id: i32
}

/// While loop statement (target)
struct WhileLoop {
    loop_id: i32,
    cond_id: i32,
    body_id: i32,
    init_stmts: i32  // Count of initialization statements
}

/// Match arm with guard
struct MatchArm {
    pattern_id: i32,
    guard_expr: i32,  // Optional guard expression
    body_id: i32
}

/// Desugared match arm (guard moved to body)
struct DesugaredArm {
    pattern_id: i32,
    body_id: i32  // Now includes guard check
}

/// Optional chaining expression
struct OptionalChain {
    expr_id: i32,
    method: str,
    args: i32  // Count of arguments
}

/// Desugared optional chaining (match-based)
struct DesugaredOptional {
    match_expr_id: i32,
    ok_body_id: i32,
    err_body_id: i32  // Return error
}

/// Desugar a for loop to while
/// for x in xs { body } →
///   {
///     var i = 0;
///     var len = xs.len();
///     while i < len {
///       let x = xs[i];
///       body;
///       i = i + 1;
///     }
///   }
fn desugar_for_loop(for_loop: &ForLoop) -> WhileLoop {
    var result: WhileLoop = {
        loop_id: for_loop.loop_id,
        cond_id: -1,        // Placeholder for i < len
        body_id: -1,        // Placeholder for expanded body
        init_stmts: 2       // i = 0; len = xs.len();
    };
    result
}

/// Desugar for loop with early break
/// for x in xs { if cond(x) break; body; } →
///   {
///     var i = 0;
///     while i < len(xs) {
///       let x = xs[i];
///       if cond(x) { i = len; break; }
///       body;
///       i = i + 1;
///     }
///   }
fn desugar_for_loop_with_break(for_loop: &ForLoop, has_break: bool) -> WhileLoop {
    var result: WhileLoop = {
        loop_id: for_loop.loop_id,
        cond_id: -1,
        body_id: -1,
        init_stmts: 2
    };
    result
}

/// Desugar match guard to nested if
/// match x {
///   Pattern if guard => body
/// } →
/// match x {
///   Pattern => if guard { body } else { ... }
/// }
fn desugar_match_guard(arm: &MatchArm) -> DesugaredArm {
    // Move guard into body as nested if
    var result: DesugaredArm = {
        pattern_id: arm.pattern_id,
        body_id: -1  // Placeholder for if-guarded body
    };
    result
}

/// Desugar multiple match guards
fn desugar_match_guards(arms: i32) -> i32 {
    // For each arm with guard, create nested if
    0  // placeholder: count of desugared arms
}

/// Desugar optional chaining
/// x?.method() →
/// match x {
///   Ok(v) => v.method(),
///   Err(e) => return Err(e)
/// }
fn desugar_optional_chaining(chain: &OptionalChain) -> DesugaredOptional {
    var result: DesugaredOptional = {
        match_expr_id: chain.expr_id,
        ok_body_id: -1,      // v.method()
        err_body_id: -1      // return Err(e)
    };
    result
}

/// Desugar optional chaining chain
/// x?.a?.b?.c() →
/// match x {
///   Ok(v1) => match v1.a {
///     Ok(v2) => match v2.b {
///       Ok(v3) => v3.c(),
///       Err(e) => return Err(e)
///     },
///     Err(e) => return Err(e)
///   },
///   Err(e) => return Err(e)
/// }
fn desugar_optional_chain(chain: &OptionalChain) -> DesugaredOptional {
    // Nested matches for each operation
    var result: DesugaredOptional = {
        match_expr_id: chain.expr_id,
        ok_body_id: -1,
        err_body_id: -1
    };
    result
}

// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/transform/hir_constructor.sio ===
/// Phase 2.5: HIR Constructor for Self-Hosted Sedenion Compiler
///
/// Constructs final High-Level IR representation from:
/// - Desugared AST
/// - Type-annotated expressions
/// - Name-resolved references
/// - Control flow graphs

/// HIR expression
enum HirExpr {
    HirLiteral(i32),              // literal value
    HirVariable(str),             // variable name
    HirCall(i32, i32),            // func_id, args_id
    HirBinary(str, i32, i32),     // op, left, right
    HirUnary(str, i32),           // op, operand
    HirBlock(i32),                // statements_id
    HirMatch(i32, i32),           // expr_id, arms_id
    HirIf(i32, i32, i32),         // cond, then_id, else_id
    HirArray(i32),                // elements_id
    HirStruct(str, i32),          // struct_name, fields_id
    HirField(i32, str),           // expr_id, field_name
}

/// HIR statement
enum HirStmt {
    HirLet(str, i32, i32),        // var_name, type_id, init_expr_id
    HirAssign(i32, i32),          // lhs_id, rhs_id
    HirExprStmt(i32),             // expr_id
    HirReturn(i32),               // value_id
    HirBreak,
    HirContinue,
}

/// HIR function
struct HirFunc {
    id: i32,
    name: str,
    params_id: i32,        // Parameter list
    return_type_id: i32,
    body_id: i32,          // Statement block
    is_exported: bool,
    doc: str
}

/// HIR struct
struct HirStruct {
    id: i32,
    name: str,
    fields_id: i32,        // Field list
    is_linear: bool,
    is_affine: bool,
    doc: str
}

/// HIR enum
struct HirEnum {
    id: i32,
    name: str,
    variants_id: i32,      // Variant list
    is_linear: bool,
    doc: str
}

/// HIR trait
struct HirTrait {
    id: i32,
    name: str,
    methods_id: i32,       // Method list
    doc: str
}

/// HIR impl block
struct HirImpl {
    id: i32,
    trait_name: str,       // Trait being implemented
    for_type: str,         // Type being implemented for
    methods_id: i32,       // Method implementations
    doc: str
}

/// HIR type alias
struct HirTypeAlias {
    id: i32,
    name: str,
    aliased_type_id: i32,
    doc: str
}

/// HIR module
struct HirModule {
    id: i32,
    name: str,
    items: i32,            // Item count
    imports: i32,          // Import count
    exports: i32           // Export count
}

/// Complete HIR tree
struct Hir {
    items_count: i32,
    functions_count: i32,
    types_count: i32,
    traits_count: i32,
    impls_count: i32,
    modules_count: i32
}

/// HIR construction context
struct HirContext {
    scope_depth: i32,
    next_id: i32,
    function_id: i32,      // Current function being lowered
    type_bindings: i32,    // Type binding count
    errors: i32
}

/// Initialize HIR context
fn hir_context_new() -> HirContext {
    var ctx: HirContext = {
        scope_depth: 0,
        next_id: 0,
        function_id: -1,
        type_bindings: 0,
        errors: 0
    };
    ctx
}

/// Generate fresh ID for HIR node
fn fresh_id(ctx: &!HirContext) -> i32 {
    var id = ctx.next_id;
    ctx.next_id = ctx.next_id + 1;
    id
}

/// Lower literal expression to HIR
fn lower_literal(value: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirLiteral(value)
}

/// Lower variable reference to HIR
fn lower_variable(name: str, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirVariable(name)
}

/// Lower function call to HIR
fn lower_call(func_id: i32, args: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirCall(func_id, args)
}

/// Lower binary operation to HIR
fn lower_binary(op: str, left: i32, right: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirBinary(op, left, right)
}

/// Lower unary operation to HIR
fn lower_unary(op: str, operand: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirUnary(op, operand)
}

/// Lower block to HIR
fn lower_block(stmts: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    var block_id = fresh_id(ctx);
    HirBlock(block_id)
}

/// Lower match expression to HIR
fn lower_match(expr: i32, arms: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    var match_id = fresh_id(ctx);
    HirMatch(expr, arms)
}

/// Lower if expression to HIR
fn lower_if(cond: i32, then_body: i32, else_body: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirIf(cond, then_body, else_body)
}

/// Lower array literal to HIR
fn lower_array(elements: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirArray(elements)
}

/// Lower struct construction to HIR
fn lower_struct(struct_name: str, fields: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirStruct(struct_name, fields)
}

/// Lower field access to HIR
fn lower_field_access(expr: i32, field_name: str, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirExpr {
    HirField(expr, field_name)
}

/// Lower let statement to HIR
fn lower_let(name: str, type_id: i32, init: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirStmt {
    HirLet(name, type_id, init)
}

/// Lower assignment to HIR
fn lower_assign(lhs: i32, rhs: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirStmt {
    HirAssign(lhs, rhs)
}

/// Lower expression statement to HIR
fn lower_expr_stmt(expr: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirStmt {
    HirExprStmt(expr)
}

/// Lower return statement to HIR
fn lower_return(value: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> HirStmt {
    HirReturn(value)
}

/// Lower function to HIR
fn lower_function(func_ast: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> Result<HirFunc, str> {
    var id = fresh_id(ctx);
    var f: HirFunc = {
        id: id,
        name: "unknown",
        params_id: 0,
        return_type_id: 0,
        body_id: 0,
        is_exported: false,
        doc: ""
    };
    Result::Ok(f)
}

fn lower_struct_decl(struct_ast: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> Result<HirStruct, str> {
    var id = fresh_id(ctx);
    var s: HirStruct = {
        id: id,
        name: "Unknown",
        fields_id: 0,
        is_linear: false,
        is_affine: false,
        doc: ""
    };

fn lower_impl(impl_ast: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> Result<HirImpl, str> {
    var id = fresh_id(ctx);
    var impl: HirImpl = {

fn lower_to_hir(ast: i32, ctx: &!HirContext) -> Result<Hir, str> {
    var hir: Hir = {
        items_count: 0,
        functions_count: 0,
        types_count: 0,
        traits_count: 0,
        impls_count: 0,
        modules_count: 0
    };
    // Walk AST:
    // 1. Lower each top-level item
    // 2. Lower expressions/statements recursively
    // 3. Attach metadata
    Result::Ok(hir)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/compiler/transform/hir_verify.sio ===
/// Phase 2.6: HIR Verification Pass for Self-Hosted Compiler
///
/// Validates HIR invariants: all names resolved, expressions typed,
/// types consistent, linear types used linearly, reachability correct.

/// Verification error
enum HirError {
    UnresolvedName(str, i32),            // name, expr_id
    UntypedExpression(i32),              // expr_id
    TypeMismatch(i32, i32, i32),         // expr_id, expected_type, actual_type
    LinearTypeViolation(str, i32),       // var_name, expr_id
    UnreachableCode(i32),                // stmt_id
    MissingReturn(i32),                  // function_id
    UnusedVariable(str, i32),            // var_name, stmt_id
}

/// Verification warning
enum HirWarning {
    ShadowedVariable(str, i32, i32),     // name, shadowed_id, shadow_id
    DeadCode(i32),                       // stmt_id
    UnusedImport(str),                   // module_name
    LargeFunction(i32, i32),             // func_id, line_count
}

/// Verification statistics
struct VerifyStats {
    items_verified: i32,
    expressions_checked: i32,
    types_consistent: i32,
    errors_found: i32,
    warnings_found: i32,
    linear_type_checks: i32,
    reachability_checks: i32
}

/// Verification report
struct VerifyReport {
    success: bool,
    errors: i32,
    warnings: i32,
    stats: VerifyStats,
    confidence: i32
}

/// Verification context
struct VerifyContext {
    current_function: i32,
    current_scope_depth: i32,
    linear_vars: i32,         // Count of linear variables
    used_vars: i32,           // Count of used variables
    errors: i32,
    warnings: i32
}

/// Initialize verification context
fn verify_context_new() -> VerifyContext {
    var ctx: VerifyContext = {
        current_function: -1,
        current_scope_depth: 0,
        linear_vars: 0,
        used_vars: 0,
        errors: 0,
        warnings: 0
    };
    ctx
}

/// Verify that a name is resolved
fn verify_name_resolved(name: str, expr_id: i32, ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // Check if name exists in symbol table
    // For now, assume all names resolved (simplified)
    Result::Ok(())
}

/// Verify that expression is typed
fn verify_expr_typed(expr_id: i32, ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // Check if expr has a type annotation
    // Simplified: assume all expressions typed
    Result::Ok(())
}

/// Verify type consistency
fn verify_type_consistent(expr_id: i32, expected_type: i32, actual_type: i32,
                          ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // Check if expected_type == actual_type
    if expected_type == actual_type {
        Result::Ok(())
    } else {
        var err: HirError = TypeMismatch(expr_id, expected_type, actual_type);
        Result::Err(err)
    }
}

/// Verify linear type is used linearly
fn verify_linear_usage(var_name: str, expr_id: i32, ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // Check if linear variable is:
    // 1. Not moved multiple times
    // 2. Not aliased
    // 3. Used exactly once before going out of scope

    // Simplified: check usage count
    Result::Ok(())
}

/// Verify unreachable code detection
fn verify_reachability(stmt_id: i32, reachable: bool, ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    if !reachable {
        var err: HirError = UnreachableCode(stmt_id);
        Result::Err(err)
    } else {
        Result::Ok(())
    }
}

/// Verify all paths in function return (non-unit return type)
fn verify_returns(func_id: i32, return_type: i32, has_return: bool,
                  ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // If return_type != unit and all paths don't return, error
    if return_type != 0 && !has_return {  // 0 = unit type
        var err: HirError = MissingReturn(func_id);
        Result::Err(err)
    } else {
        Result::Ok(())
    }
}

/// Verify single expression
fn verify_expr(expr_id: i32, ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // Check:
    // 1. All names resolved
    // 2. Expression is typed
    // 3. Types are consistent

    let _ = verify_name_resolved("unknown", expr_id, ctx);
    let _ = verify_expr_typed(expr_id, ctx);
    Result::Ok(())
}

/// Verify single statement
fn verify_stmt(stmt_id: i32, reachable: bool, ctx: &!VerifyContext) -> Result<(), HirError> {
    // Check:
    // 1. Reachable
    // 2. Bound variables are used
    // 3. Linear vars used linearly

    let _ = verify_reachability(stmt_id, reachable, ctx);
    Result::Ok(())
}
