// === FILE: stdlib/crypto/sha256.sio ===
//! stdlib/crypto/sha256.sio — SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) + HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104)
//!
//! Pure Sounio implementation. No external dependencies.
//!
//! References:
//!   FIPS 180-4 — Secure Hash Standard (SHA-256), NIST, 2015
//!   RFC 2104   — HMAC: Keyed-Hashing for Message Authentication, 1997
//!
//! NOTE: All hash state words are 32-bit unsigned values stored in i64.
//!       Every arithmetic result is masked with 0xFFFFFFFF to enforce
//!       32-bit wrap-around on Sounio's 64-bit signed i64.

// ============================================================================
// PUBLIC TYPES
// ============================================================================

pub struct SHA256State {
    h: [i64; 8],         // hash chaining values (H0..H7), 32-bit each
    buffer: [u8; 64],    // partial message block
    buf_len: i32,        // bytes currently in buffer (0..63)
    total_len: i64,      // total message bytes absorbed
}

pub struct SHA256Digest {
    bytes: [u8; 32],     // 256-bit hash output
}

// ============================================================================
// FIPS 180-4 §4.2.2 — K constants
// First 32 bits of fractional parts of cube roots of first 64 primes.
// ============================================================================

fn sha256_k() -> [i64; 64] {
    let k: [i64; 64] = [
        0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5,
        0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
        0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3,
        0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
        0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc,
        0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
        0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7,
        0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
        0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13,
        0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
        0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3,
        0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
        0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5,
        0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
        0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208,
        0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2
    ]
    return k
}

// ============================================================================
// BIT OPERATION HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Right-rotate 32-bit value stored in i64 by n positions.
fn rotr32(x: i64, n: i32) -> i64 {
    let xm = x & 0xFFFFFFFF
    let right = (xm >> n) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    let left  = (xm << (32 - n)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return (left | right) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// Logical right shift (no sign extension) of 32-bit value.
fn shr32(x: i64, n: i32) -> i64 {
    return (x & 0xFFFFFFFF) >> n
}

// ============================================================================
// FIPS 180-4 §4.1.2 — Boolean functions
// ============================================================================

fn ch(x: i64, y: i64, z: i64) -> i64 {
    return ((x & y) ^ ((x ^ 0xFFFFFFFF) & 0xFFFFFFFF & z)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

fn maj(x: i64, y: i64, z: i64) -> i64 {
    return ((x & y) ^ (x & z) ^ (y & z)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// FIPS 180-4 §4.1.2 — Big-sigma functions (compression)
fn sigma0(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 2) ^ rotr32(x, 13) ^ rotr32(x, 22)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

fn sigma1(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 6) ^ rotr32(x, 11) ^ rotr32(x, 25)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// FIPS 180-4 §4.1.2 — Small-sigma functions (message schedule)
fn gamma0(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 7) ^ rotr32(x, 18) ^ shr32(x, 3)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

fn gamma1(x: i64) -> i64 {
    return (rotr32(x, 17) ^ rotr32(x, 19) ^ shr32(x, 10)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// ============================================================================
// BLOCK COMPRESSION — FIPS 180-4 §6.2.2
// ============================================================================

// Process one 512-bit block. Returns updated H0..H7.
fn sha256_compress(h: [i64; 8], block: [u8; 64]) -> [i64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let k = sha256_k()

    // Message schedule W[0..63]
    var w: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    // W[0..15]: big-endian 32-bit words from block bytes
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < 16 {
        let b0 = block[i * 4 + 0] as i64
        let b1 = block[i * 4 + 1] as i64
        let b2 = block[i * 4 + 2] as i64
        let b3 = block[i * 4 + 3] as i64
        w[i] = ((b0 << 24) | (b1 << 16) | (b2 << 8) | b3) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        i = i + 1
    }

    // W[16..63]: σ1(W[t-2]) + W[t-7] + σ0(W[t-15]) + W[t-16]
    var t: i32 = 16
    while t < 64 {
        let g1 = gamma1(w[t - 2])
        let g0 = gamma0(w[t - 15])
        w[t] = (g1 + w[t - 7] + g0 + w[t - 16]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        t = t + 1
    }

    // Working variables a..h
    var a = h[0]
    var b = h[1]
    var c = h[2]
    var d = h[3]
    var e = h[4]
    var f = h[5]
    var g = h[6]
    var hh = h[7]

    // 64 rounds
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < 64 {
        let t1 = (hh + sigma1(e) + ch(e, f, g) + k[r] + w[r]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        let t2 = (sigma0(a) + maj(a, b, c)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        hh = g
        g = f
        f = e
        e = (d + t1) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        d = c
        c = b
        b = a
        a = (t1 + t2) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        r = r + 1
    }

    // Intermediate hash
    var out: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    out[0] = (h[0] + a) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[1] = (h[1] + b) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[2] = (h[2] + c) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[3] = (h[3] + d) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[4] = (h[4] + e) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[5] = (h[5] + f) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[6] = (h[6] + g) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    out[7] = (h[7] + hh) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return out
}

// ============================================================================
// PUBLIC API
// ============================================================================

// FIPS 180-4 §5.3.3 — Initial hash values (first 32 bits of sqrt of primes 2..19)
pub fn sha256_init() -> SHA256State {
    let h: [i64; 8] = [
        0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a,
        0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19
    ]
    let buf: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    SHA256State {
        h: h,
        buffer: buf,
        buf_len: 0,
        total_len: 0,
    }
}

// Absorb up to `len` bytes from `data` into the SHA-256 state.
// data: fixed 256-byte window; len: actual byte count to consume.
pub fn sha256_update(state: SHA256State, data: [u8; 256], len: i32) -> SHA256State with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state
    var pos: i32 = 0

    while pos < len {
        // Fill the 64-byte buffer one byte at a time.
        s.buffer[s.buf_len] = data[pos]
        s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1
        s.total_len = s.total_len + 1
        pos = pos + 1

        // Compress when buffer is full.
        if s.buf_len == 64 {
            s.h = sha256_compress(s.h, s.buffer)
            s.buf_len = 0
            // Zero buffer for cleanliness
            var bi: i32 = 0
            while bi < 64 {
                s.buffer[bi] = 0
                bi = bi + 1
            }
        }
    }

    return s
}

// Produce the final SHA-256 digest (FIPS 180-4 §5.1.1 padding + §6.2.2).
pub fn sha256_finalize(state: SHA256State) -> SHA256Digest with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state

    // Total message length in bits for the length field.
    let bit_len: i64 = s.total_len * 8

    // Append the 0x80 byte.
    s.buffer[s.buf_len] = 0x80 as u8
    s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1

    // If not enough room for the 8-byte length field, compress and start new block.
    if s.buf_len > 56 {
        // Pad with zeros to end of block.
        while s.buf_len < 64 {
            s.buffer[s.buf_len] = 0
            s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1
        }
        s.h = sha256_compress(s.h, s.buffer)
        s.buf_len = 0
        var bi: i32 = 0
        while bi < 64 {
            s.buffer[bi] = 0
            bi = bi + 1
        }
    }

    // Pad to byte 56.
    while s.buf_len < 56 {
        s.buffer[s.buf_len] = 0
        s.buf_len = s.buf_len + 1
    }

    // Append 64-bit big-endian message bit length (bytes 56..63).
    s.buffer[56] = ((bit_len >> 56) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[57] = ((bit_len >> 48) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[58] = ((bit_len >> 40) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[59] = ((bit_len >> 32) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[60] = ((bit_len >> 24) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[61] = ((bit_len >> 16) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[62] = ((bit_len >>  8) & 0xFF) as u8
    s.buffer[63] = ((bit_len      ) & 0xFF) as u8

    // Final compression.
    s.h = sha256_compress(s.h, s.buffer)

    // Serialise H0..H7 as big-endian bytes.
    var digest_bytes: [u8; 32] = [0; 32]
    var wi: i32 = 0
    while wi < 8 {
        let word = s.h[wi]
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 0] = ((word >> 24) & 0xFF) as u8
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 1] = ((word >> 16) & 0xFF) as u8
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 2] = ((word >>  8) & 0xFF) as u8
        digest_bytes[wi * 4 + 3] = ((word      ) & 0xFF) as u8
        wi = wi + 1
    }

    return SHA256Digest { bytes: digest_bytes }
}

// One-shot hash: init → update → finalize.
pub fn sha256_hash(data: [u8; 256], len: i32) -> SHA256Digest with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let s0 = sha256_init()
    let s1 = sha256_update(s0, data, len)
    return sha256_finalize(s1)
}

// ============================================================================
// HMAC-SHA256 — RFC 2104
// ============================================================================

// HMAC-SHA256(key, msg).
// key_len / msg_len: actual lengths (≤ 256 bytes each as stored in fixed arrays).
pub fn hmac_sha256(key: [u8; 256], key_len: i32, msg: [u8; 256], msg_len: i32) -> SHA256Digest with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Step 1: If key > 64 bytes, hash it to get a 32-byte derived key.
    var k: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]

    if key_len > 64 {
        // Hash key using sha256_hash (first key_len bytes of key).
        var key_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var ki: i32 = 0
        while ki < key_len {
            key_buf[ki] = key[ki]
            ki = ki + 1
        }
        let key_digest = sha256_hash(key_buf, key_len)
        // Use first 32 bytes of hash as key.
        var di: i32 = 0
        while di < 32 {
            k[di] = key_digest.bytes[di]
            di = di + 1
        }
    } else {
        // Pad key with zeros to 64 bytes.
        var ki: i32 = 0
        while ki < key_len {
            k[ki] = key[ki]
            ki = ki + 1
        }
    }

    // Step 2: Compute ipad = k XOR 0x36 and opad = k XOR 0x5c (both 64 bytes).
    var ipad: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var opad: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < 64 {
        ipad[pi] = ((k[pi] as i64) ^ 0x36) as u8
        opad[pi] = ((k[pi] as i64) ^ 0x5c) as u8
        pi = pi + 1
    }

    // Step 3: inner = SHA256(ipad || msg)
    // We need to stream ipad (64 bytes) then msg into one SHA256 state.
    var inner = sha256_init()

    // Feed ipad as first 64 bytes.
    var ipad_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var ip: i32 = 0
    while ip < 64 {
        ipad_buf[ip] = ipad[ip]
        ip = ip + 1
    }
    inner = sha256_update(inner, ipad_buf, 64)

    // Feed message.
    var msg_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var mi: i32 = 0
    while mi < msg_len {
        msg_buf[mi] = msg[mi]
        mi = mi + 1
    }
    inner = sha256_update(inner, msg_buf, msg_len)
    let inner_digest = sha256_finalize(inner)

    // Step 4: outer = SHA256(opad || inner_digest)
    var outer = sha256_init()

    var opad_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var op: i32 = 0
    while op < 64 {
        opad_buf[op] = opad[op]
        op = op + 1
    }
    outer = sha256_update(outer, opad_buf, 64)

    // Feed 32-byte inner hash result.
    var inner_buf: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
    var ii: i32 = 0
    while ii < 32 {
        inner_buf[ii] = inner_digest.bytes[ii]
        ii = ii + 1
    }
    outer = sha256_update(outer, inner_buf, 32)
    return sha256_finalize(outer)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/csv/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/csv/lib.sio - Module entry point
//!
//! This is the entry point for the csv module.
//! It re-exports the public items from mod.sio

pub use mod::*;


// === FILE: stdlib/csv/mod.sio ===
//! stdlib/csv

module csv


// === FILE: stdlib/csv/parser.sio ===
// stdlib/csv/parser.sio — CSV parser and writer for Sounio
//
// Numeric-only CSV (f64 values) backed by fixed-size arrays.
// No heap, no dynamic allocation — all capacities are compile-time constants.
//
// Capacity:
//   - max 256 rows × 16 columns  → data[4096]
//   - input / output buffer: 4096 bytes
//   - column header: up to 16 names of 32 bytes each
//
// Usage:
//   var t = csv_table_new()
//   let rc = csv_parse(&input, input_len, &!t, 44u8)   // 44 = ','
//   assert(rc == 0)
//   let m = csv_col_mean(&t, 0)

// =============================================================================
// Constants
// =============================================================================

let CSV_MAX_ROWS: i32 = 256
let CSV_MAX_COLS: i32 = 16
let CSV_DATA_CAP: i32 = 4096   // 256 * 16
let CSV_BUF_CAP:  i32 = 4096
let CSV_HDR_LEN:  i32 = 32     // bytes per column name

// =============================================================================
// CsvBuf — byte buffer for serialized CSV output
//
// Wraps [u8; 4096] in a struct so that &!CsvBuf mutations propagate
// correctly through the JIT (raw &![u8; 4096] has a known JIT limitation).
// =============================================================================

pub struct CsvBuf {
    pub bytes: [u8; 4096],
    pub len:   i32,
}

/// Return an empty CsvBuf.
pub fn csv_buf_new() -> CsvBuf {
    CsvBuf { bytes: [0u8; 4096], len: 0 }
}

// =============================================================================
// CsvTable — primary data structure
// =============================================================================

pub struct CsvTable {
    pub data:        [f64; 4096],       // row-major: data[row * n_cols + col]
    pub n_rows:      i32,
    pub n_cols:      i32,
    pub max_rows:    i32,               // fixed: CSV_MAX_ROWS
    pub max_cols:    i32,               // fixed: CSV_MAX_COLS
    pub has_header:  i32,               // 0 = no, 1 = yes
    pub header_bytes: [[u8; 32]; 16],  // column names
    pub header_lens: [i32; 16],         // byte length of each name
}

// =============================================================================
// Construction helpers
// =============================================================================

/// Return an empty CsvTable.
pub fn csv_table_new() -> CsvTable {
    CsvTable {
        data:         [0.0; 4096],
        n_rows:       0,
        n_cols:       0,
        max_rows:     256,
        max_cols:     16,
        has_header:   0,
        header_bytes: [[0u8; 32]; 16],
        header_lens:  [0; 16],
    }
}

/// Set the value at (row, col). Out-of-bounds writes are silently ignored.
pub fn csv_table_set(t: &!CsvTable, row: i32, col: i32, val: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if row < 0 || row >= t.n_rows { return }
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return }
    let idx = row * t.n_cols + col
    t.data[idx as usize] = val
}

/// Read the value at (row, col). Out-of-bounds reads return 0.0.
pub fn csv_table_get(t: &CsvTable, row: i32, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if row < 0 || row >= t.n_rows { return 0.0 }
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    let idx = row * t.n_cols + col
    t.data[idx as usize]
}

/// Append a row from values[0..n_cols-1].  n_cols must match t.n_cols (or set
/// it on the first call when the table is still empty).
pub fn csv_table_add_row(t: &!CsvTable, values: &[f64; 16], n_cols: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if t.n_rows >= 256 { return }
    if n_cols <= 0 || n_cols > 16 { return }

    // First row: establish column count
    if t.n_rows == 0 && t.n_cols == 0 {
        t.n_cols = n_cols
    }

    // Column count mismatch — silently skip
    if n_cols != t.n_cols { return }

    let base = t.n_rows * t.n_cols
    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < n_cols {
        t.data[(base + c) as usize] = values[c as usize]
        c = c + 1
    }
    t.n_rows = t.n_rows + 1
}

// =============================================================================
// Parsing helpers
// =============================================================================

// True when c is ASCII alphabetic (header-detection heuristic).
fn is_alpha(c: u8) -> bool {
    (c >= 65u8 && c <= 90u8) || (c >= 97u8 && c <= 122u8)
}

// True when c is a decimal digit.
fn is_digit(c: u8) -> bool {
    c >= 48u8 && c <= 57u8
}

// Raise 10.0 to integer power n  (n >= 0).
fn pow10(n: i32) -> f64 {
    var r: f64 = 1.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        r = r * 10.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    r
}

/// Parse an f64 from bytes[start..end) (exclusive end).
/// Handles optional leading '-', integer part, optional '.' + fraction.
/// Returns 0.0 for an empty range.
fn parse_f64(bytes: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, end: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if start >= end { return 0.0 }

    var pos: i32 = start
    var neg: i32 = 0

    // Sign
    if bytes[pos as usize] == 45u8 {   // '-'
        neg = 1
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    // Integer part
    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    while pos < end && is_digit(bytes[pos as usize]) {
        int_part = int_part * 10.0 + ((bytes[pos as usize] as i32) - 48) as f64
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    // Fractional part
    var frac: f64 = 0.0
    if pos < end && bytes[pos as usize] == 46u8 {   // '.'
        pos = pos + 1
        var denom: f64 = 10.0
        while pos < end && is_digit(bytes[pos as usize]) {
            frac = frac + ((bytes[pos as usize] as i32) - 48) as f64 / denom
            denom = denom * 10.0
            pos = pos + 1
        }
    }

    let result = int_part + frac
    if neg == 1 { return 0.0 - result }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// CSV parser
// =============================================================================

/// Parse CSV bytes into table.
///
/// - Delimiter is typically 44u8 (','). CR (\r) before \n is skipped.
/// - If the first non-whitespace character is alphabetic the entire first line
///   is treated as a header row (column names stored in table.header_bytes).
/// - Only numeric rows are stored in table.data.
///
/// Returns 0 on success, -1 on overflow / error.
pub fn csv_parse(input: &[u8; 4096], input_len: i32, table: &!CsvTable, delimiter: u8) -> i32
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    if input_len <= 0 || input_len > 4096 { return 0 - 1 }

    // Detect header: peek at first byte
    var scan_hdr: i32 = 0
    while scan_hdr < input_len && (input[scan_hdr as usize] == 32u8 || input[scan_hdr as usize] == 9u8) {
        scan_hdr = scan_hdr + 1
    }
    let first_is_alpha: i32 = if scan_hdr < input_len && is_alpha(input[scan_hdr as usize]) { 1 } else { 0 }

    var pos: i32 = 0

    // --- Header row ---
    if first_is_alpha == 1 {
        table.has_header = 1
        var col: i32 = 0
        var field_start: i32 = pos
        while pos < input_len {
            let c = input[pos as usize]
            if c == 10u8 || c == 13u8 {
                // end of header line — store last field
                if col < 16 {
                    var fs: i32 = field_start
                    var fe: i32 = pos
                    // trim trailing CR
                    if fe > fs && input[(fe - 1) as usize] == 13u8 { fe = fe - 1 }
                    let flen = fe - fs
                    let copy_len = if flen < 32 { flen } else { 31 }
                    var hc: i32 = 0
                    while hc < copy_len {
                        table.header_bytes[col as usize][hc as usize] = input[(fs + hc) as usize]
                        hc = hc + 1
                    }
                    table.header_lens[col as usize] = copy_len
                    col = col + 1
                }
                // skip \r\n
                if c == 13u8 && (pos + 1) < input_len && input[(pos + 1) as usize] == 10u8 {
                    pos = pos + 2
                } else {
                    pos = pos + 1
                }
                break
            } else if c == delimiter {
                // store field
                if col < 16 {
                    var fs: i32 = field_start
                    var fe: i32 = pos
                    let flen = fe - fs
                    let copy_len = if flen < 32 { flen } else { 31 }
                    var hc: i32 = 0
                    while hc < copy_len {
                        table.header_bytes[col as usize][hc as usize] = input[(fs + hc) as usize]
                        hc = hc + 1
                    }
                    table.header_lens[col as usize] = copy_len
                    col = col + 1
                }
                field_start = pos + 1
                pos = pos + 1
            } else {
                pos = pos + 1
            }
        }
    }

    // --- Data rows ---
    var row_count: i32 = 0
    var col_count: i32 = 0      // columns seen in current row
    var n_cols_expected: i32 = 0  // established from first data row
    var row_vals: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var field_start: i32 = pos

    while pos <= input_len {
        // Use input_len as sentinel: treat end-of-buffer like newline
        let c: u8 = if pos < input_len { input[pos as usize] } else { 10u8 }

        if c == 10u8 || c == 13u8 {
            // end of field and end of row
            var fe: i32 = pos
            if c == 13u8 && (pos + 1) < input_len && input[(pos + 1) as usize] == 10u8 {
                // \r\n  — fe points before \r
                fe = pos
            }
            // skip empty lines
            let field_len = fe - field_start
            if field_len > 0 || col_count > 0 {
                if col_count < 16 {
                    row_vals[col_count as usize] = parse_f64(input, field_start, fe)
                    col_count = col_count + 1
                }
                // store row
                if col_count > 0 {
                    if row_count >= 256 { return 0 - 1 }
                    // establish or verify column count
                    if n_cols_expected == 0 {
                        n_cols_expected = col_count
                    }
                    if col_count != n_cols_expected { return 0 - 1 }
                    // write row into table
                    if table.n_cols == 0 {
                        table.n_cols = col_count
                    }
                    let base = row_count * table.n_cols
                    var wc: i32 = 0
                    while wc < col_count {
                        table.data[(base + wc) as usize] = row_vals[wc as usize]
                        wc = wc + 1
                    }
                    row_count = row_count + 1
                }
                col_count = 0
            }
            // advance past \r\n or \n
            if pos < input_len && c == 13u8 && (pos + 1) < input_len && input[(pos + 1) as usize] == 10u8 {
                pos = pos + 2
            } else {
                pos = pos + 1
            }
            field_start = pos
        } else if c == delimiter {
            // end of field, not end of row
            if col_count < 16 {
                row_vals[col_count as usize] = parse_f64(input, field_start, pos)
                col_count = col_count + 1
            }
            pos = pos + 1
            field_start = pos
        } else {
            pos = pos + 1
        }

        // sentinel consumed
        if pos > input_len { break }
    }

    table.n_rows = row_count
    0
}

// =============================================================================
// Serialization helpers
// =============================================================================

// Write the decimal digits of a non-negative integer n into out starting at
// pos.  Returns the new pos.
fn write_i32_digits(n: i32, out: &![u8; 4096], pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 {
        out[pos as usize] = 48u8   // '0'
        return pos + 1
    }
    // Collect digits in reverse, then flip
    var tmp: [u8; 12] = [0u8; 12]
    var k: i32 = 0
    var v: i32 = n
    while v > 0 {
        tmp[k as usize] = (48 + v % 10) as u8
        v = v / 10
        k = k + 1
    }
    // Write reversed
    var i: i32 = k - 1
    var p: i32 = pos
    while i >= 0 {
        out[p as usize] = tmp[i as usize]
        p = p + 1
        i = i - 1
    }
    p
}

/// Write an f64 value as decimal text into out[pos..].
/// Format: [-]integer[.fraction] with up to 6 fractional digits (trailing
/// zeros stripped).  Returns updated pos.
fn write_f64(val: f64, out: &![u8; 4096], pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = pos
    var v: f64 = val

    // Sign
    if v < 0.0 {
        out[p as usize] = 45u8   // '-'
        p = p + 1
        v = 0.0 - v
    }

    // Integer part
    let int_part: i32 = v as i32
    p = write_i32_digits(int_part, out, p)

    // Fractional part — 6 digits max
    let frac = v - (int_part as f64)
    if frac > 0.000001 {
        out[p as usize] = 46u8   // '.'
        p = p + 1

        // Scale up to 6 decimal places
        var frac6: i32 = (frac * 1000000.0) as i32
        // Trim trailing zeros
        while frac6 > 0 && frac6 % 10 == 0 {
            frac6 = frac6 / 10
        }
        // Count digits in frac6 to determine leading zeros needed
        // We need to figure out how many digits frac6 has vs how many we need
        // to represent 6 decimal places.
        // Re-derive: original fraction scaled to 6 decimal digits
        var full6: i32 = (frac * 1000000.0) as i32
        // Count significant decimal positions
        var digits6: [u8; 6] = [0u8; 6]
        var d: i32 = 5
        var rem: i32 = full6
        while d >= 0 {
            digits6[d as usize] = (48 + rem % 10) as u8
            rem = rem / 10
            d = d - 1
        }
        // Find last non-zero digit
        var last: i32 = 5
        while last > 0 && digits6[last as usize] == 48u8 {
            last = last - 1
        }
        var di: i32 = 0
        while di <= last {
            out[p as usize] = digits6[di as usize]
            p = p + 1
            di = di + 1
        }
    }

    p
}

// =============================================================================
// CSV serializer
// =============================================================================

/// Serialize table to CSV bytes in out[0..].
///
/// - delimiter is written between fields (typically 44u8 = ',')
/// - header row is written first when table.has_header == 1
/// - Returns the total number of bytes written, or -1 on overflow.
pub fn csv_serialize(table: &CsvTable, out: &![u8; 4096], delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = 0

    // Header row
    if table.has_header == 1 {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                out[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let hlen = table.header_lens[c as usize]
            var hc: i32 = 0
            while hc < hlen {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                out[p as usize] = table.header_bytes[c as usize][hc as usize]
                p = p + 1
                hc = hc + 1
            }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        out[p as usize] = 10u8   // '\n'
        p = p + 1
    }

    // Data rows
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < table.n_rows {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                out[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let v = table.data[(r * table.n_cols + c) as usize]
            p = write_f64(v, out, p)
            if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        out[p as usize] = 10u8   // '\n'
        p = p + 1
        r = r + 1
    }

    p
}

// =============================================================================
// CsvBuf-based serialize / parse
//
// Use these variants instead of csv_serialize / csv_parse when doing
// round-trip serialize→parse in the JIT, because &!CsvBuf struct
// mutations are visible to callers (raw &![u8;4096] parameter mutations
// have a known JIT limitation).
// =============================================================================

// Write-f64 variant that targets CsvBuf.bytes
fn write_f64_buf(val: f64, b: &!CsvBuf, pos: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = pos
    var v: f64 = val

    if v < 0.0 {
        b.bytes[p as usize] = 45u8
        p = p + 1
        v = 0.0 - v
    }

    let int_part: i32 = v as i32
    // write integer digits into a temp buf then copy
    var tmp: [u8; 12] = [0u8; 12]
    var k: i32 = 0
    if int_part == 0 {
        b.bytes[p as usize] = 48u8
        p = p + 1
    } else {
        var vi: i32 = int_part
        while vi > 0 {
            tmp[k as usize] = (48 + vi % 10) as u8
            vi = vi / 10
            k = k + 1
        }
        var ii: i32 = k - 1
        while ii >= 0 {
            b.bytes[p as usize] = tmp[ii as usize]
            p = p + 1
            ii = ii - 1
        }
    }

    let frac = v - (int_part as f64)
    if frac > 0.000001 {
        b.bytes[p as usize] = 46u8
        p = p + 1
        var full6: i32 = (frac * 1000000.0) as i32
        var digits6: [u8; 6] = [0u8; 6]
        var d: i32 = 5
        var rem: i32 = full6
        while d >= 0 {
            digits6[d as usize] = (48 + rem % 10) as u8
            rem = rem / 10
            d = d - 1
        }
        var last: i32 = 5
        while last > 0 && digits6[last as usize] == 48u8 {
            last = last - 1
        }
        var di: i32 = 0
        while di <= last {
            b.bytes[p as usize] = digits6[di as usize]
            p = p + 1
            di = di + 1
        }
    }
    p
}

/// Serialize table into a CsvBuf. Sets b.len to bytes written.
/// Returns bytes written, or -1 on overflow.
pub fn csv_serialize_buf(table: &CsvTable, b: &!CsvBuf, delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = 0

    if table.has_header == 1 {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                b.bytes[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let hlen = table.header_lens[c as usize]
            var hc: i32 = 0
            while hc < hlen {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                b.bytes[p as usize] = table.header_bytes[c as usize][hc as usize]
                p = p + 1
                hc = hc + 1
            }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        b.bytes[p as usize] = 10u8
        p = p + 1
    }

    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < table.n_rows {
        var c: i32 = 0
        while c < table.n_cols {
            if c > 0 {
                if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
                b.bytes[p as usize] = delimiter
                p = p + 1
            }
            let v = table.data[(r * table.n_cols + c) as usize]
            p = write_f64_buf(v, b, p)
            if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
            c = c + 1
        }
        if p >= 4096 { return 0 - 1 }
        b.bytes[p as usize] = 10u8
        p = p + 1
        r = r + 1
    }

    b.len = p
    p
}

/// Parse CSV from a CsvBuf into table. Convenience wrapper over csv_parse.
pub fn csv_parse_buf(b: &CsvBuf, table: &!CsvTable, delimiter: u8) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    csv_parse(&b.bytes, b.len, table, delimiter)
}

// =============================================================================
// Column statistics
// =============================================================================

/// Sum of column col. Returns 0.0 for invalid col or empty table.
pub fn csv_col_sum(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < t.n_rows {
        s = s + t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize]
        r = r + 1
    }
    s
}

/// Arithmetic mean of column col. Returns 0.0 for invalid col or empty table.
pub fn csv_col_mean(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    csv_col_sum(t, col) / (t.n_rows as f64)
}

/// Population variance of column col.
pub fn csv_col_variance(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    let mean = csv_col_mean(t, col)
    var acc: f64 = 0.0
    var r: i32 = 0
    while r < t.n_rows {
        let d = t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize] - mean
        acc = acc + d * d
        r = r + 1
    }
    acc / (t.n_rows as f64)
}

/// Minimum value in column col.
pub fn csv_col_min(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var m: f64 = t.data[col as usize]
    var r: i32 = 1
    while r < t.n_rows {
        let v = t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize]
        if v < m { m = v }
        r = r + 1
    }
    m
}

/// Maximum value in column col.
pub fn csv_col_max(t: &CsvTable, col: i32) -> f64 {
    if col < 0 || col >= t.n_cols { return 0.0 }
    if t.n_rows == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var m: f64 = t.data[col as usize]
    var r: i32 = 1
    while r < t.n_rows {
        let v = t.data[(r * t.n_cols + col) as usize]
        if v > m { m = v }
        r = r + 1
    }
    m
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin/atlas.sio ===
// Darwin Atlas Kernels - Library (single-file, module-free)
// Operators, symmetry, approximate metric, and quaternion lift.

let BASE_A: u8 = 0
let BASE_C: u8 = 1
let BASE_G: u8 = 2
let BASE_T: u8 = 3

let PI: f64 = 3.14159265358979323846

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { return -x }
    return x
}

fn normalize_angle(x: f64) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var angle = x
    while angle > PI {
        angle = angle - 2.0 * PI
    }
    while angle < -PI {
        angle = angle + 2.0 * PI
    }
    return angle
}

fn sin_approx(x: f64) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let angle = normalize_angle(x)
    let x2 = angle * angle
    let x3 = angle * x2
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    let x7 = x5 * x2
    return angle - x3 / 6.0 + x5 / 120.0 - x7 / 5040.0
}

fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let angle = normalize_angle(x)
    let x2 = angle * angle
    let x4 = x2 * x2
    let x6 = x4 * x2
    return 1.0 - x2 / 2.0 + x4 / 24.0 - x6 / 720.0
}

fn atan(x: f64) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ax = abs_f64(x)
    if ax <= 1.0 {
        let x2 = x * x
        return x * (1.0 - x2 * (1.0 / 3.0 - x2 * (1.0 / 5.0 - x2 * (1.0 / 7.0))))
    }
    let sign = if x > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 }
    let inv = 1.0 / x
    let inv2 = inv * inv
    return sign * (PI / 2.0 - inv * (1.0 - inv2 * (1.0 / 3.0 - inv2 * (1.0 / 5.0))))
}

fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 0.0 {
        return atan(y / x)
    }
    if x < 0.0 && y >= 0.0 {
        return atan(y / x) + PI
    }
    if x < 0.0 && y < 0.0 {
        return atan(y / x) - PI
    }
    if x == 0.0 && y > 0.0 {
        return PI / 2.0
    }
    if x == 0.0 && y < 0.0 {
        return -PI / 2.0
    }
    return 0.0
}

fn sequence_shift(seq: [u8], k: usize) -> [u8]  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return [] }

    let k_mod = k % n
    var result: [u8] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = (i + k_mod) % n
        result.push(seq[idx])
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn sequence_reverse(seq: [u8]) -> [u8]  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return [] }

    var result: [u8] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        result.push(seq[n - 1 - i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn complement_base(b: u8) -> u8  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    return b ^ 3
}

fn sequence_complement(seq: [u8]) -> [u8]  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return [] }

    var result: [u8] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        result.push(complement_base(seq[i]))
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn sequence_reverse_complement(seq: [u8]) -> [u8]  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let rev = sequence_reverse(seq)
    return sequence_complement(rev)
}

fn sequences_equal(a: [u8], b: [u8]) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let len_a = a.len()
    let len_b = b.len()
    if len_a != len_b { return false }

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len_a {
        if a[i] != b[i] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

fn hamming_distance(a: [u8], b: [u8]) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let len_a = a.len()
    let len_b = b.len()
    if len_a != len_b { return 0 }

    var count: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len_a {
        if a[i] != b[i] {
            count = count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return count
}

fn cyclic_period(seq: [u8]) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 1 }

    var k: usize = 1
    while k <= n {
        if n % k == 0 {
            let shifted = sequence_shift(seq, k)
            if sequences_equal(seq, shifted) {
                return k
            }
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return n
}

fn rotational_symmetries(seq: [u8]) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 1 }
    return n / cyclic_period(seq)
}

fn has_reflective_symmetry(seq: [u8]) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return true }

    let rev = sequence_reverse(seq)
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < n {
        let shifted_rev = sequence_shift(rev, k)
        if sequences_equal(seq, shifted_rev) {
            return true
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return false
}

fn orbit_size(seq: [u8]) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 1 }

    let group_order = 2 * n
    let rot_sym = rotational_symmetries(seq)
    let ref_factor: usize = if has_reflective_symmetry(seq) { 2 } else { 1 }
    let stabilizer_size = rot_sym * ref_factor
    return group_order / stabilizer_size
}

fn orbit_ratio(seq: [u8]) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    return (orbit_size(seq) as f64) / ((2 * n) as f64)
}

fn is_palindrome(seq: [u8]) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let rev = sequence_reverse(seq)
    return sequences_equal(seq, rev)
}

fn is_rc_fixed(seq: [u8]) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let rc = sequence_reverse_complement(seq)
    return sequences_equal(seq, rc)
}

fn rotational_period(seq: [u8]) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 1 }

    var k: usize = 1
    while k <= n {
        if n % k == 0 {
            let shifted = sequence_shift(seq, k)
            if sequences_equal(seq, shifted) {
                return k
            }
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return n
}

struct SymmetryStats {
    length: usize,
    orbit_size: usize,
    orbit_ratio: f64,
    is_palindrome: bool,
    is_rc_fixed: bool,
    rotational_period: usize,
}

fn compute_symmetry_stats(seq: [u8]) -> SymmetryStats  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    SymmetryStats {
        length: seq.len(),
        orbit_size: orbit_size(seq),
        orbit_ratio: orbit_ratio(seq),
        is_palindrome: is_palindrome(seq),
        is_rc_fixed: is_rc_fixed(seq),
        rotational_period: rotational_period(seq),
    }
}

fn TRANSFORM_SHIFT() -> i32  with Mut, Div, Panic { 0 }
fn TRANSFORM_REVERSE_SHIFT() -> i32  with Mut, Div, Panic { 1 }
fn TRANSFORM_RC_SHIFT() -> i32  with Mut, Div, Panic { 2 }

struct NearestTransform {
    kind: i32,
    k: usize,
}

fn dmin(seq: [u8], include_rc: bool) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 0 }

    var min_dist = n

    var k: usize = 1
    while k < n {
        let shifted = sequence_shift(seq, k)
        let d = hamming_distance(seq, shifted)
        if d < min_dist { min_dist = d }
        k = k + 1
    }

    let rev = sequence_reverse(seq)
    k = 0
    while k < n {
        let shifted_rev = sequence_shift(rev, k)
        let d = hamming_distance(seq, shifted_rev)
        if d < min_dist { min_dist = d }
        k = k + 1
    }

    if include_rc {
        let rc = sequence_reverse_complement(seq)
        k = 0
        while k < n {
            let shifted_rc = sequence_shift(rc, k)
            let d = hamming_distance(seq, shifted_rc)
            if d < min_dist { min_dist = d }
            k = k + 1
        }
    }

    return min_dist
}

fn dmin_normalized(seq: [u8], include_rc: bool) -> f64  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 { return 0.0 }
    return (dmin(seq, include_rc) as f64) / (n as f64)
}

fn nearest_transform(seq: [u8], include_rc: bool) -> (usize, NearestTransform)  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = seq.len()
    if n == 0 {
        return (0, NearestTransform { kind: TRANSFORM_SHIFT(), k: 0 })
    }

    var min_dist = n
    var nearest_kind = TRANSFORM_SHIFT()
    var nearest_k: usize = 1

    var k: usize = 1
    while k < n {
        let d = hamming_distance(seq, sequence_shift(seq, k))
        if d < min_dist {
            min_dist = d
            nearest_kind = TRANSFORM_SHIFT()
            nearest_k = k
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    let rev = sequence_reverse(seq)
    k = 0
    while k < n {
        let d = hamming_distance(seq, sequence_shift(rev, k))
        if d < min_dist {
            min_dist = d
            nearest_kind = TRANSFORM_REVERSE_SHIFT()
            nearest_k = k
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    if include_rc {
        let rc = sequence_reverse_complement(seq)
        k = 0
        while k < n {
            let d = hamming_distance(seq, sequence_shift(rc, k))
            if d < min_dist {
                min_dist = d
                nearest_kind = TRANSFORM_RC_SHIFT()
                nearest_k = k
            }
            k = k + 1
        }
    }

    return (min_dist, NearestTransform { kind: nearest_kind, k: nearest_k })
}

struct Quaternion {
    w: f64,
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
}

fn quaternion_new(w: f64, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Quaternion  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    Quaternion { w: w, x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn quaternion_identity() -> Quaternion  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    quaternion_new(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
}

fn quaternion_neg_identity() -> Quaternion  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    quaternion_new(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
}

fn quaternion_mul(a: &Quaternion, b: &Quaternion) -> Quaternion  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    quaternion_new(
        a.w * b.w - a.x * b.x - a.y * b.y - a.z * b.z,
        a.w * b.x + a.x * b.w + a.y * b.z - a.z * b.y,
        a.w * b.y - a.x * b.z + a.y * b.w + a.z * b.x,
        a.w * b.z + a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x + a.z * b.w
    )
}

fn quaternion_neg(q: &Quaternion) -> Quaternion  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    quaternion_new(-q.w, -q.x, -q.y, -q.z)
}

fn quaternion_approx_eq(a: &Quaternion, b: &Quaternion, tol: f64) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    abs_f64(a.w - b.w) < tol
        && abs_f64(a.x - b.x) < tol
        && abs_f64(a.y - b.y) < tol
        && abs_f64(a.z - b.z) < tol
}

struct DicyclicGroup {
    n: usize,
}

fn dicyclic_group_new(n: usize) -> DicyclicGroup  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    DicyclicGroup { n: n }
}

fn dicyclic_order(g: &DicyclicGroup) -> usize  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    return 4 * g.n
}

struct DicyclicElement {
    q: Quaternion,
}

fn dicyclic_element(g: &DicyclicGroup, k: usize, is_reflection: bool) -> DicyclicElement  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n
    let theta = PI * (k as f64) / (n as f64)
    let a_k = quaternion_new(cos_approx(theta), sin_approx(theta), 0.0, 0.0)

    if is_reflection {
        let b = quaternion_new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0)
        return DicyclicElement { q: quaternion_mul(&a_k, &b) }
    }
    return DicyclicElement { q: a_k }
}

fn project_to_dihedral(elem: &DicyclicElement, g: &DicyclicGroup) -> (usize, bool)  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let q = &elem.q
    let n = g.n
    let is_reflection = abs_f64(q.y) > 0.0000000001 || abs_f64(q.z) > 0.0000000001

    let angle = atan2(q.x, q.w)
    let k_float = angle * (n as f64) / PI
    let k_raw: i64 = if k_float >= 0.0 { (k_float + 0.5) as i64 } else { (k_float - 0.5) as i64 }
    let n_i64 = n as i64
    let k_mod = ((k_raw % n_i64) + n_i64) % n_i64
    let k = k_mod as usize

    return (k, is_reflection)
}

fn verify_double_cover(g: &DicyclicGroup) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n

    var k: usize = 0
    while k < 2 * n {
        var is_ref_idx: usize = 0
        while is_ref_idx < 2 {
            let is_ref = is_ref_idx == 1
            let elem = dicyclic_element(g, k, is_ref)
            let neg_elem = DicyclicElement { q: quaternion_neg(&elem.q) }

            let proj1 = project_to_dihedral(&elem, g)
            let proj2 = project_to_dihedral(&neg_elem, g)

            if proj1.0 != proj2.0 || proj1.1 != proj2.1 {
                return false
            }
            is_ref_idx = is_ref_idx + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return true
}

struct AtlasMetrics {
    length: usize,
    orbit_size: usize,
    orbit_ratio: f64,
    dmin: usize,
    dmin_normalized: f64,
    is_palindrome: bool,
    is_rc_fixed: bool,
    rotational_period: usize,
    double_cover_ok: bool,
}

fn run_atlas_metrics(seq: [u8], include_rc: bool, dicyclic_n: usize) -> AtlasMetrics  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let stats = compute_symmetry_stats(seq)
    let dmin_value = dmin(seq, include_rc)
    let dmin_norm = if stats.length == 0 { 0.0 } else { (dmin_value as f64) / (stats.length as f64) }

    let g = dicyclic_group_new(dicyclic_n)
    let double_cover_ok = verify_double_cover(&g)

    AtlasMetrics {
        length: stats.length,
        orbit_size: stats.orbit_size,
        orbit_ratio: stats.orbit_ratio,
        dmin: dmin_value,
        dmin_normalized: dmin_norm,
        is_palindrome: stats.is_palindrome,
        is_rc_fixed: stats.is_rc_fixed,
        rotational_period: stats.rotational_period,
        double_cover_ok: double_cover_ok,
    }
}

fn pipeline_ok(metrics: AtlasMetrics) -> bool  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if metrics.length == 0 { return false }
    if metrics.orbit_size < 1 { return false }
    if metrics.orbit_ratio < 0.0 || metrics.orbit_ratio > 1.0 { return false }
    if metrics.dmin > metrics.length { return false }
    if metrics.dmin_normalized < 0.0 || metrics.dmin_normalized > 1.0 { return false }
    if !metrics.double_cover_ok { return false }
    return true
}

fn sample_sequence() -> [u8]  with Mut, Div, Panic {
    [BASE_A, BASE_C, BASE_G, BASE_T, BASE_A, BASE_C, BASE_G, BASE_T]
}

// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/compartments/brain.sio ===
// brain.sio — Darwin PBPK brain module
// Rewritten in Sounio syntax

fn dpbpk_brain_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_brain_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn dpbpk_brain_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn dpbpk_brain_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn dpbpk_brain_clamp(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 { if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x } }

struct Brain_State {
    concentration: f64,
    flow_in: f64,
    flow_out: f64,
    volume: f64,
    kp: f64,
}

fn brain_state_new(vol: f64, kp: f64) -> Brain_State {
    Brain_State { concentration: 0.0, flow_in: 0.0, flow_out: 0.0, volume: vol, kp: kp }
}

fn brain_compute_flux(c_arterial: f64, c_tissue: f64, kp: f64, blood_flow: f64) -> f64 {
    blood_flow * (c_arterial - c_tissue / kp)
}

fn brain_update(state: Brain_State, c_arterial: f64, blood_flow: f64, dt: f64) -> Brain_State with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let flux = brain_compute_flux(c_arterial, state.concentration, state.kp, blood_flow)
    var new_state = state
    new_state.concentration = state.concentration + dt * flux / state.volume
    if new_state.concentration < 0.0 { new_state.concentration = 0.0 }
    new_state.flow_in = dpbpk_brain_max(flux, 0.0)
    new_state.flow_out = dpbpk_brain_abs(dpbpk_brain_min(flux, 0.0))
    new_state
}

fn test_brain_flux_positive() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let flux = brain_compute_flux(10.0, 5.0, 2.0, 90.0)
    flux > 0.0
}

fn test_brain_zero_init() -> bool {
    let s = brain_state_new(1.5, 5.0)
    s.concentration == 0.0 && s.volume == 1.5
}

// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/constants.sio ===
// stdlib/darwin_pbpk/constants.sio — Shared PBPK Constants
//
// Mathematical utilities and physiological constants for PBPK modeling.
//
// References:
// - ICRP Publication 89: Basic anatomical and physiological data (2002)
// - Brown et al. (1997) Physiological parameter values for PBPK models
// - Davies & Morris (1993) Physiological parameters in laboratory animals and humans

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn dpbpk_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }
fn dpbpk_e() -> f64 { 2.71828182845904523536 }

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dpbpk_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn dpbpk_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn dpbpk_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn dpbpk_clamp(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x }
}

fn dpbpk_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Taylor series with overflow/underflow protection
    if x > 700.0 { return dpbpk_exp(350.0) * dpbpk_exp(x - 350.0) }
    if x < -700.0 { return 0.0 }
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n: i64 = 1
    while n < 30 {
        term = term * x / n as f64
        result = result + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn dpbpk_log(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Natural log via Newton's method
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000.0 }
    var y = 0.0
    var xr = x
    while xr > 2.0 {
        xr = xr / 2.71828182845904523536
        y = y + 1.0
    }
    while xr < 0.5 {
        xr = xr * 2.71828182845904523536
        y = y - 1.0
    }
    y = y + (xr - 1.0)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 15 {
        let ey = dpbpk_exp(y)
        if ey > 0.0 {
            y = y + (x - ey) / ey
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn dpbpk_log10(x: f64) -> f64 {
    dpbpk_log(x) / 2.302585092994046
}

fn dpbpk_pow(base: f64, exp_int: i64) -> f64 {
    if exp_int == 0 { return 1.0 }
    var result = 1.0
    var b = base
    var e = exp_int
    if e < 0 {
        b = 1.0 / b
        e = 0 - e
    }
    while e > 0 {
        if e % 2 == 1 {
            result = result * b
        }
        b = b * b
        e = e / 2
    }
    result
}

fn CARDIAC_OUTPUT_LPH() -> f64 { 348.0 }

// Test: dpbpk_exp(0) = 1
fn test_dpbpk_exp_zero() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_exp(0.0) - 1.0) < 0.0001
}

// Test: dpbpk_exp(1) ≈ e
fn test_dpbpk_exp_one() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_exp(1.0) - 2.71828182845904523536) < 0.001
}

// Test: dpbpk_log(e) ≈ 1
fn test_dpbpk_log_e() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_log(2.71828182845904523536) - 1.0) < 0.001
}

// Test: log(exp(x)) ≈ x round-trip
fn test_log_exp_roundtrip() -> bool {
    let x = 3.7
    let r = dpbpk_log(dpbpk_exp(x))
    dpbpk_abs(r - x) < 0.01
}

// Test: dpbpk_pow(2, 10) = 1024
fn test_dpbpk_pow_2_10() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_pow(2.0, 10) - 1024.0) < 0.001
}

// Test: dpbpk_pow(x, 0) = 1
fn test_dpbpk_pow_zero() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_pow(42.0, 0) - 1.0) < 0.0001
}

// Test: dpbpk_pow(x, -1) = 1/x
fn test_dpbpk_pow_neg() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_pow(4.0, -1) - 0.25) < 0.0001
}

// Test: dpbpk_log10(100) ≈ 2
fn test_dpbpk_log10() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_log10(100.0) - 2.0) < 0.01
}

// Test: dpbpk_sqrt(4) = 2
fn test_dpbpk_sqrt_4() -> bool {
    dpbpk_abs(dpbpk_sqrt(4.0) - 2.0) < 0.0001
}

// Test: clamp works
fn test_dpbpk_clamp() -> bool {
    let a = dpbpk_clamp(5.0, 0.0, 3.0)
    let b = dpbpk_clamp(-1.0, 0.0, 3.0)
    let c = dpbpk_clamp(1.5, 0.0, 3.0)
    let ok1 = dpbpk_abs(a - 3.0) < 0.0001
    let ok2 = dpbpk_abs(b - 0.0) < 0.0001
    let ok3 = dpbpk_abs(c - 1.5) < 0.0001
    if ok1 { if ok2 { ok3 } else { false } } else { false }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/fractal_blood.sio ===
// fractal_blood.sio — Fractal Blood Dynamics for PBPK
// Implements CTRW framework for anomalous transport in vascular networks

fn dpbpk_fb_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn dpbpk_fb_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

fn dpbpk_fb_ln(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var v = x
    var scale = 0.0
    while v > 2.0 { v = v / 2.718281828; scale = scale + 1.0 }
    while v < 0.5 { v = v * 2.718281828; scale = scale - 1.0 }
    let y = (v - 1.0) / (v + 1.0)
    let y2 = y * y
    2.0 * y * (1.0 + y2 / 3.0 + y2 * y2 / 5.0 + y2 * y2 * y2 / 7.0) + scale
}

fn dpbpk_fb_pow(base: f64, exp_v: f64) -> f64 {
    if base <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    dpbpk_fb_exp(exp_v * dpbpk_fb_ln(base))
}

fn FRACTAL_DIMENSION() -> f64 { 2.7 }
fn MURRAY_EXPONENT() -> f64 { 3.0 }
fn BLOOD_VISCOSITY() -> f64 { 0.0035 }
fn ANOMALOUS_EXPONENT_BLOOD() -> f64 { 0.85 }

struct FractalParams {
    fractal_dim: f64,
    anomalous_exponent: f64,
    spectral_dim: f64,
    hurst_exponent: f64,
}

fn fractal_params_new(d_f: f64, alpha: f64) -> FractalParams {
    FractalParams {
        fractal_dim: d_f,
        anomalous_exponent: alpha,
        spectral_dim: 2.0 * d_f / (d_f + 2.0),
        hurst_exponent: alpha / 2.0,
    }
}

fn fractal_params_default() -> FractalParams {
    fractal_params_new(FRACTAL_DIMENSION(), ANOMALOUS_EXPONENT_BLOOD())
}

struct VesselSegment {
    radius: f64,
    length: f64,
    flow_rate: f64,
    branching_level: i32,
}

// Gamma function approximation (Stirling)
fn fb_gamma(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    if x < 1.0 { return fb_gamma(x + 1.0) / x }
    // Stirling: Gamma(x) ~ sqrt(2pi/x) * (x/e)^x
    let pi = 3.14159265358979323846
    let e = 2.71828182845904523536
    dpbpk_fb_exp(0.5 * dpbpk_fb_ln(2.0 * pi / x) + x * dpbpk_fb_ln(x / e))
}

// Mittag-Leffler function E_alpha(z)
fn mittag_leffler_approx(alpha: f64, z: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if alpha == 1.0 { return dpbpk_fb_exp(z) }
    if dpbpk_fb_abs(z) < 0.0000000001 { return 1.0 }

    var sum = 0.0
    var term = 1.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 100 {
        sum = sum + term
        if dpbpk_fb_abs(term) < 0.0000000001 * dpbpk_fb_abs(sum) { return sum }
        let g = fb_gamma(alpha * ((k + 1) as f64) + 1.0)
        if g > 0.0 {
            term = term * z / g
        } else {
            return sum
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Fractional concentration decay
fn fractional_decay(c0: f64, lambda: f64, t: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    c0 * mittag_leffler_approx(alpha, 0.0 - lambda * dpbpk_fb_pow(t, alpha))
}

// Murray's law branching
fn murray_child_radius(parent_radius: f64, n_children: i64) -> f64 {
    if n_children <= 0 { return parent_radius }
    let factor = dpbpk_fb_pow(n_children as f64, 0.0 - 1.0 / MURRAY_EXPONENT())
    parent_radius * factor
}

// Anomalous dispersion coefficient
fn anomalous_dispersion(d0: f64, t: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 {
    if t <= 0.0 { return d0 }
    d0 * dpbpk_fb_pow(t, alpha - 1.0)
}

// Tests
fn test_ml_exp_recovery() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let ml_val = mittag_leffler_approx(1.0, 1.0)
    let exp_val = dpbpk_fb_exp(1.0)
    dpbpk_fb_abs(ml_val - exp_val) < 0.001
}

fn test_ml_zero() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let val = mittag_leffler_approx(0.85, 0.0)
    dpbpk_fb_abs(val - 1.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_fractional_decay_t0() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let val = fractional_decay(100.0, 0.1, 0.0, 0.85)
    dpbpk_fb_abs(val - 100.0) < 0.001
}

fn test_murray_law() -> bool {
    let child_r = murray_child_radius(1.0, 2)
    child_r > 0.0 && child_r < 1.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/darwin_pbpk/core/ode_pbpk.sio ===
// ode_pbpk.sio — ODE solver for PBPK compartmental models
// Forward Euler integration for multi-compartment pharmacokinetics

fn ode_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ode_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn ode_exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 { term = term * x / (i as f64); result = result + term; i = i + 1 }
    result
}

struct PBPKState {
    c_plasma: f64,
    c_liver: f64,
    c_brain: f64,
    c_kidney: f64,
    c_muscle: f64,
    c_fat: f64,
    c_gut: f64,
    t: f64,
}

fn pbpk_state_zero() -> PBPKState {
    PBPKState { c_plasma: 0.0, c_liver: 0.0, c_brain: 0.0, c_kidney: 0.0, c_muscle: 0.0, c_fat: 0.0, c_gut: 0.0, t: 0.0 }
}

struct PBPKParams {
    q_liver: f64,
    q_brain: f64,
    q_kidney: f64,
    q_muscle: f64,
    q_fat: f64,
    q_gut: f64,
    v_plasma: f64,
    v_liver: f64,
    v_brain: f64,
    v_kidney: f64,
    v_muscle: f64,
    v_fat: f64,
    v_gut: f64,
    kp_liver: f64,
    kp_brain: f64,
    kp_kidney: f64,
    kp_muscle: f64,
    kp_fat: f64,
    kp_gut: f64,
    cl_hepatic: f64,
    cl_renal: f64,
}

fn pbpk_params_default() -> PBPKParams {
    PBPKParams { q_liver: 90.0, q_brain: 42.0, q_kidney: 72.0, q_muscle: 42.0, q_fat: 18.0, q_gut: 60.0, v_plasma: 3.0, v_liver: 1.5, v_brain: 1.4, v_kidney: 0.31, v_muscle: 35.0, v_fat: 14.0, v_gut: 1.2, kp_liver: 5.0, kp_brain: 1.5, kp_kidney: 3.0, kp_muscle: 2.0, kp_fat: 10.0, kp_gut: 3.0, cl_hepatic: 10.0, cl_renal: 5.0 }
}

fn pbpk_rhs(state: PBPKState, params: PBPKParams) -> PBPKState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let cp = state.c_plasma
    var deriv = pbpk_state_zero()

    // Liver
    let flux_liver = params.q_liver * (cp - state.c_liver / params.kp_liver)
    deriv.c_liver = (flux_liver - params.cl_hepatic * state.c_liver / params.kp_liver) / params.v_liver

    // Brain
    let flux_brain = params.q_brain * (cp - state.c_brain / params.kp_brain)
    deriv.c_brain = flux_brain / params.v_brain

    // Kidney
    let flux_kidney = params.q_kidney * (cp - state.c_kidney / params.kp_kidney)
    deriv.c_kidney = (flux_kidney - params.cl_renal * state.c_kidney / params.kp_kidney) / params.v_kidney

    // Muscle
    let flux_muscle = params.q_muscle * (cp - state.c_muscle / params.kp_muscle)
    deriv.c_muscle = flux_muscle / params.v_muscle

    // Fat
    let flux_fat = params.q_fat * (cp - state.c_fat / params.kp_fat)
    deriv.c_fat = flux_fat / params.v_fat

    // Gut
    let flux_gut = params.q_gut * (cp - state.c_gut / params.kp_gut)
    deriv.c_gut = flux_gut / params.v_gut

    // Plasma: sum of return flows
    deriv.c_plasma = (0.0 - flux_liver - flux_brain - flux_kidney - flux_muscle - flux_fat - flux_gut) / params.v_plasma

    deriv
}

fn pbpk_euler_step(state: PBPKState, params: PBPKParams, dt: f64) -> PBPKState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let deriv = pbpk_rhs(state, params)
    PBPKState {
        c_plasma: state.c_plasma + dt * deriv.c_plasma,
        c_liver: state.c_liver + dt * deriv.c_liver,
        c_brain: state.c_brain + dt * deriv.c_brain,
        c_kidney: state.c_kidney + dt * deriv.c_kidney,
        c_muscle: state.c_muscle + dt * deriv.c_muscle,
        c_fat: state.c_fat + dt * deriv.c_fat,
        c_gut: state.c_gut + dt * deriv.c_gut,
        t: state.t + dt,
    }
}

fn pbpk_simulate(dose: f64, params: PBPKParams, t_end: f64, dt: f64) -> PBPKState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var state = pbpk_state_zero()
    state.c_plasma = dose / params.v_plasma
    while state.t < t_end {
        state = pbpk_euler_step(state, params, dt)
    }
    state
}

fn test_pbpk_iv_bolus() -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let params = pbpk_params_default()
    let result = pbpk_simulate(100.0, params, 1.0, 0.01)
    result.c_plasma >= 0.0 && result.c_liver >= 0.0
}
