// GUM Supplement 1: Propagation of distributions using a Monte Carlo method
//
// Implements multivariate uncertainty propagation with full covariance:
//   Sigma_y = J * Sigma_x * J^T
//
// where J is the Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives.
//
// This extends GUM (JCGM 100:2008) to handle:
//   - Correlated input quantities
//   - Multivariate output quantities
//   - Non-zero off-diagonal covariance terms
//
// The key equation (GUM Supplement 1, Section 7.3):
//   u^2(y) = sum_i sum_j (df/dx_i)(df/dx_j) u(x_i,x_j)
//
// When inputs are uncorrelated, u(x_i,x_j) = 0 for i != j, and this
// reduces to the standard GUM formula.
//
// Reference: JCGM 101:2008

// =============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    y
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// =============================================================================
// Upper-Triangular Index (must match covariance.sio)
// =============================================================================

fn tri_index(n: i32, i: i32, j: i32) -> i32 {
    var row = i
    var col = j
    if i > j {
        row = j
        col = i
    }
    return row * n - (row * (row - 1)) / 2 + (col - row)
}

// =============================================================================
// Covariance Matrix Type (mirrors covariance.sio)
// =============================================================================

pub struct CovarianceMatrix {
    pub n: i32,
    pub data: [f64; 300],
}

fn cov_new(n: i32) -> CovarianceMatrix {
    var dim = n
    if dim < 1 { dim = 1 }
    if dim > 24 { dim = 24 }
    return CovarianceMatrix {
        n: dim,
        data: [0.0; 300],
    }
}

fn cov_get(cov: &CovarianceMatrix, i: i32, j: i32) -> f64 {
    if i < 0 { return 0.0 }
    if j < 0 { return 0.0 }
    if i >= cov.n { return 0.0 }
    if j >= cov.n { return 0.0 }
    return cov.data[tri_index(cov.n, i, j)]
}

fn cov_set(cov: &!CovarianceMatrix, i: i32, j: i32, val: f64) {
    if i < 0 { return }
    if j < 0 { return }
    if i >= cov.n { return }
    if j >= cov.n { return }
    cov.data[tri_index(cov.n, i, j)] = val
}

// =============================================================================
// GUM Result Type (mirrors gum.sio)
// =============================================================================

pub struct GUMResult {
    pub value: f64,
    pub std_uncertainty: f64,
    pub degrees_of_freedom: f64,
    pub coverage_factor_95: f64,
    pub expanded_uncertainty_95: f64,
}

// Coverage factor for 95% at infinite DoF (normal distribution)
fn k_normal_95() -> f64 { 1.96 }

fn gum_result_from(value: f64, std_u: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let k = k_normal_95()
    return GUMResult {
        value: value,
        std_uncertainty: abs_f64(std_u),
        degrees_of_freedom: 1.0e9,
        coverage_factor_95: k,
        expanded_uncertainty_95: k * abs_f64(std_u),
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// GUM Multivariate Result
// =============================================================================

// Result of multivariate propagation: scalar output with full covariance info
pub struct GUMMultiResult {
    // Best estimate of the output
    pub value: f64,

    // Combined standard uncertainty u_c(y)
    pub std_uncertainty: f64,

    // Degrees of freedom (infinite for analytic propagation)
    pub degrees_of_freedom: f64,

    // Coverage factor k (95%)
    pub coverage_factor_95: f64,

    // Expanded uncertainty U = k * u_c
    pub expanded_uncertainty_95: f64,

    // Number of input variables
    pub n_inputs: i32,

    // Input covariance matrix (for reference)
    pub input_covariance: CovarianceMatrix,
}

fn gum_multi_result(value: f64, std_u: f64, n_in: i32, cov_x: CovarianceMatrix) -> GUMMultiResult {
    let k = k_normal_95()
    let su = abs_f64(std_u)
    return GUMMultiResult {
        value: value,
        std_uncertainty: su,
        degrees_of_freedom: 1.0e9,
        coverage_factor_95: k,
        expanded_uncertainty_95: k * su,
        n_inputs: n_in,
        input_covariance: cov_x,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Numerical Jacobian Computation
// =============================================================================

// Central difference approximation for df/dx at point x
// df/dx ~ (f(x+h) - f(x-h)) / (2h)
//
// Step size h should be ~ sqrt(epsilon_machine) * |x|
// For f64: epsilon ~ 2.2e-16, so h ~ 1.5e-8 * |x|
pub fn numerical_jacobian_1d(f: fn(f64) -> f64, x: f64, h: f64) -> f64 {
    let step = if abs_f64(h) > 0.0 { abs_f64(h) } else { 1.0e-8 * max_f64(abs_f64(x), 1.0) }
    let f_plus = f(x + step)
    let f_minus = f(x - step)
    return (f_plus - f_minus) / (2.0 * step)
}

// Numerical gradient of f(x1, x2) -> [df/dx1, df/dx2]
pub fn numerical_jacobian_2d(f: fn(f64, f64) -> f64, x1: f64, x2: f64, h: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
    let step = if abs_f64(h) > 0.0 { abs_f64(h) } else { 1.0e-8 }

    // df/dx1 via central difference (hold x2 fixed)
    let h1 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x1), 1.0)
    let df_dx1 = (f(x1 + h1, x2) - f(x1 - h1, x2)) / (2.0 * h1)

    // df/dx2 via central difference (hold x1 fixed)
    let h2 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x2), 1.0)
    let df_dx2 = (f(x1, x2 + h2) - f(x1, x2 - h2)) / (2.0 * h2)

    return [df_dx1, df_dx2]
}

// Numerical gradient of f(x1, x2, x3) -> [df/dx1, df/dx2, df/dx3]
pub fn numerical_jacobian_3d(f: fn(f64, f64, f64) -> f64, x1: f64, x2: f64, x3: f64, h: f64) -> [f64; 3] {
    let step = if abs_f64(h) > 0.0 { abs_f64(h) } else { 1.0e-8 }

    let h1 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x1), 1.0)
    let df_dx1 = (f(x1 + h1, x2, x3) - f(x1 - h1, x2, x3)) / (2.0 * h1)

    let h2 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x2), 1.0)
    let df_dx2 = (f(x1, x2 + h2, x3) - f(x1, x2 - h2, x3)) / (2.0 * h2)

    let h3 = step * max_f64(abs_f64(x3), 1.0)
    let df_dx3 = (f(x1, x2, x3 + h3) - f(x1, x2, x3 - h3)) / (2.0 * h3)

    return [df_dx1, df_dx2, df_dx3]
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Covariance Propagation
// =============================================================================

// Propagate covariance for y = f(x1, x2) with correlated inputs
//
// Var(y) = J * Sigma_x * J^T
//        = (df/dx1)^2 * Var(x1) + (df/dx2)^2 * Var(x2)
//          + 2 * (df/dx1) * (df/dx2) * Cov(x1, x2)
//
// The cross-term 2*(df/dx1)*(df/dx2)*Cov(x1,x2) is what distinguishes
// GUM Supplement 1 from basic GUM propagation.
pub fn propagate_covariance_2d(
    f: fn(f64, f64) -> f64,
    x: [f64; 2],
    cov_x: CovarianceMatrix
) -> GUMMultiResult {
    // Compute function value
    let y_val = f(x[0], x[1])

    // Compute numerical Jacobian
    let jac = numerical_jacobian_2d(f, x[0], x[1], 1.0e-8)

    // Propagate: Var(y) = J * Sigma_x * J^T
    let j0 = jac[0]
    let j1 = jac[1]

    let s00 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 0)
    let s01 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 1)
    let s11 = cov_get(&cov_x, 1, 1)

    let var_y = j0 * j0 * s00 + 2.0 * j0 * j1 * s01 + j1 * j1 * s11

    let std_y = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_multi_result(y_val, std_y, 2, cov_x)
}

// =============================================================================
// 3D Covariance Propagation
// =============================================================================

// Propagate covariance for y = f(x1, x2, x3) with correlated inputs
pub fn propagate_covariance_3d(
    f: fn(f64, f64, f64) -> f64,
    x: [f64; 3],
    cov_x: CovarianceMatrix
) -> GUMMultiResult {
    let y_val = f(x[0], x[1], x[2])

    let jac = numerical_jacobian_3d(f, x[0], x[1], x[2], 1.0e-8)

    let j0 = jac[0]
    let j1 = jac[1]
    let j2 = jac[2]

    let s00 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 0)
    let s01 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 1)
    let s02 = cov_get(&cov_x, 0, 2)
    let s11 = cov_get(&cov_x, 1, 1)
    let s12 = cov_get(&cov_x, 1, 2)
    let s22 = cov_get(&cov_x, 2, 2)

    let var_y = j0*j0*s00 + j1*j1*s11 + j2*j2*s22
              + 2.0*j0*j1*s01 + 2.0*j0*j2*s02 + 2.0*j1*j2*s12

    let std_y = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_multi_result(y_val, std_y, 3, cov_x)
}

// =============================================================================
// Correlated Operations on GUMResult
// =============================================================================

// Add two correlated measurements: y = x1 + x2
//
// Var(y) = Var(x1) + Var(x2) + 2*rho*sigma_1*sigma_2
//
// When rho = 0: reduces to standard GUM RSS
// When rho = 1: uncertainties add linearly (worst case)
// When rho = -1: uncertainties cancel (best case)
pub fn gum_s1_add_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let value = x1.value + x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty

    // Clamp correlation to [-1, 1]
    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 + 2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = u1*u1 + u2*u2 + 2.0 * rho * u1 * u2

    // Protect against numerical noise giving negative variance
    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))

    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// Subtract two correlated measurements: y = x1 - x2
//
// Var(y) = Var(x1) + Var(x2) - 2*rho*sigma_1*sigma_2
//
// Note the sign flip vs. addition: positive correlation REDUCES
// uncertainty in subtraction (common-mode rejection).
pub fn gum_s1_sub_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let value = x1.value - x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Var(y) = u1^2 + u2^2 - 2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = u1*u1 + u2*u2 - 2.0 * rho * u1 * u2

    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// Multiply two correlated measurements: y = x1 * x2
//
// Using first-order Taylor expansion:
//   dy/dx1 = x2,  dy/dx2 = x1
//   Var(y) = x2^2*Var(x1) + x1^2*Var(x2) + 2*x1*x2*rho*u1*u2
pub fn gum_s1_product_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    let value = x1.value * x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty
    let v1 = x1.value
    let v2 = x2.value

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Var(y) = x2^2*u1^2 + x1^2*u2^2 + 2*x1*x2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = v2*v2*u1*u1 + v1*v1*u2*u2 + 2.0*v1*v2*rho*u1*u2

    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// Divide two correlated measurements: y = x1 / x2
//
// Using first-order Taylor expansion:
//   dy/dx1 = 1/x2,  dy/dx2 = -x1/x2^2
//   Var(y) = (1/x2)^2*Var(x1) + (x1/x2^2)^2*Var(x2)
//            + 2*(1/x2)*(-x1/x2^2)*rho*u1*u2
pub fn gum_s1_div_correlated(x1: GUMResult, x2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> GUMResult {
    if abs_f64(x2.value) < 1.0e-15 {
        return gum_result_from(0.0, 1.0e308)
    }

    let value = x1.value / x2.value

    let u1 = x1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = x2.std_uncertainty
    let v1 = x1.value
    let v2 = x2.value

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Sensitivity coefficients
    let c1 = 1.0 / v2                   // dy/dx1
    let c2 = 0.0 - v1 / (v2 * v2)       // dy/dx2

    // Var(y) = c1^2*u1^2 + c2^2*u2^2 + 2*c1*c2*rho*u1*u2
    let var_y = c1*c1*u1*u1 + c2*c2*u2*u2 + 2.0*c1*c2*rho*u1*u2

    let std_u = sqrt_f64(abs_f64(var_y))
    return gum_result_from(value, std_u)
}

// =============================================================================
// Convenience: Build covariance from two GUMResults + correlation
// =============================================================================

// Create a 2x2 covariance matrix from two GUMResults and their correlation
pub fn cov_from_gum_results_2(r1: GUMResult, r2: GUMResult, correlation: f64) -> CovarianceMatrix {
    var cov = cov_new(2)

    let u1 = r1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = r2.std_uncertainty

    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Diagonal: variances
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 0, u1 * u1)
    cov_set(&!cov, 1, 1, u2 * u2)

    // Off-diagonal: covariance = rho * u1 * u2
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 1, rho * u1 * u2)

    return cov
}

// Create a 3x3 covariance matrix from three GUMResults and pairwise correlations
pub fn cov_from_gum_results_3(
    r1: GUMResult, r2: GUMResult, r3: GUMResult,
    rho_12: f64, rho_13: f64, rho_23: f64
) -> CovarianceMatrix {
    var cov = cov_new(3)

    let u1 = r1.std_uncertainty
    let u2 = r2.std_uncertainty
    let u3 = r3.std_uncertainty

    // Diagonal: variances
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 0, u1 * u1)
    cov_set(&!cov, 1, 1, u2 * u2)
    cov_set(&!cov, 2, 2, u3 * u3)

    // Off-diagonal: covariances
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 1, rho_12 * u1 * u2)
    cov_set(&!cov, 0, 2, rho_13 * u1 * u3)
    cov_set(&!cov, 1, 2, rho_23 * u2 * u3)

    return cov
}

// =============================================================================
// Validation: Compare Supplement 1 with basic GUM for uncorrelated case
// =============================================================================

// For uncorrelated inputs, GUM Supplement 1 should reduce to basic GUM.
// This function computes the relative difference between the two approaches.
// A small value (< 1e-6) confirms consistency.
pub fn validate_s1_vs_gum(s1_uncertainty: f64, gum_uncertainty: f64) -> f64 {
    let avg = 0.5 * (abs_f64(s1_uncertainty) + abs_f64(gum_uncertainty))
    if avg < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    return abs_f64(s1_uncertainty - gum_uncertainty) / avg
}

// =============================================================================
// Effective degrees of freedom for correlated case
// =============================================================================

// Welch-Satterthwaite with correlation (extended form)
// For two correlated inputs:
//   v_eff = u_c^4 / (c1^4*u1^4/v1 + c2^4*u2^4/v2)
//
// Note: The correlation affects u_c but not the W-S denominator
// (which depends on individual contributions, not their correlation).
pub fn welch_satterthwaite_correlated_2(
    u1: f64, dof1: f64, c1: f64,
    u2: f64, dof2: f64, c2: f64,
    correlation: f64
) -> f64 {
    var rho = correlation
    if rho > 1.0 { rho = 1.0 }
    if rho < 0.0 - 1.0 { rho = 0.0 - 1.0 }

    // Combined variance including correlation
    let var_y = c1*c1*u1*u1 + c2*c2*u2*u2 + 2.0*c1*c2*rho*u1*u2
    let u_c_sq = abs_f64(var_y)
    let u_c_4 = u_c_sq * u_c_sq

    // Denominator: sum of (c_i * u_i)^4 / v_i
    let term1 = c1*c1*u1*u1 * c1*c1*u1*u1 / max_f64(dof1, 1.0)
    let term2 = c2*c2*u2*u2 * c2*c2*u2*u2 / max_f64(dof2, 1.0)
    let denom = term1 + term2

    if denom < 1.0e-30 {
        return 1.0e9
    }

    return min_f64(u_c_4 / denom, 1.0e9)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/interval_ieee.sio ===
//! IEEE 1788-2015 Interval Arithmetic Semantics
//!
//! This module aligns Sounio interval arithmetic with IEEE 1788 standard,
//! ensuring reproducibility and well-defined behavior for edge cases.
//!
//! Key IEEE 1788 concepts:
//!   - Empty interval: {} (result of impossible constraints)
//!   - Entire interval: [-∞, +∞] (maximum ignorance)
//!   - Exception handling for division by interval spanning zero
//!   - Decorations for tracking validity
//!
//! References:
//!   - IEEE 1788-2015: "Standard for Interval Arithmetic"
//!   - IEEE 1788.1-2017: "Simplified subset (Level 1)"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 INTERVAL REPRESENTATION
// ============================================================================

// IEEE 1788 bare interval [a, b]
// Special cases:
//   - Empty: is_empty = true
//   - Entire: lo = -inf, hi = +inf
//   - Point: lo == hi
struct Interval {
    lo: f64,
    hi: f64,
    is_empty: bool,
}

fn interval_empty() -> Interval {
    return Interval {
        lo: 0.0,
        hi: 0.0,
        is_empty: true,
    }
}

fn interval_entire() -> Interval {
    return Interval {
        lo: 0.0 - 1.0e308,
        hi: 1.0e308,
        is_empty: false,
    }
}

fn interval_new(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> Interval {
    if lo > hi {
        // Invalid bounds -> empty
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return Interval {
        lo: lo,
        hi: hi,
        is_empty: false,
    }
}

fn interval_point(x: f64) -> Interval {
    return Interval {
        lo: x,
        hi: x,
        is_empty: false,
    }
}

fn interval_symmetric(center: f64, half_width: f64) -> Interval {
    return interval_new(center - half_width, center + half_width)
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 DECORATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Decorations track interval validity through computations
// Per IEEE 1788 Section 9
// 0 = ill (undefined/invalid)
// 1 = trv (trivial - could be any value)
// 2 = def (defined but possibly unbounded)
// 3 = dac (defined and continuous)
// 4 = com (common - bounded and continuous)
struct Decoration {
    value: i32,
}

fn dec_ill() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 0 } }  // Invalid
fn dec_trv() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 1 } }  // Trivial
fn dec_def() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 2 } }  // Defined
fn dec_dac() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 3 } }  // DAC
fn dec_com() -> Decoration { return Decoration { value: 4 } }  // Common

// Decorated interval: interval + decoration
struct DecoratedInterval {
    interval: Interval,
    decoration: Decoration,
}

fn decorated_new(interval: Interval, dec: Decoration) -> DecoratedInterval {
    return DecoratedInterval {
        interval: interval,
        decoration: dec,
    }
}

fn decorated_common(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> DecoratedInterval {
    let interval = interval_new(lo, hi)
    if interval.is_empty {
        return DecoratedInterval { interval: interval, decoration: dec_ill() }
    }
    return DecoratedInterval { interval: interval, decoration: dec_com() }
}

// Combine decorations (take minimum)
fn dec_combine(a: Decoration, b: Decoration) -> Decoration {
    if a.value < b.value {
        return a
    }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 BASIC OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Addition: [a, b] + [c, d] = [a+c, b+d]
fn interval_add(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return interval_new(x.lo + y.lo, x.hi + y.hi)
}

// Subtraction: [a, b] - [c, d] = [a-d, b-c]
fn interval_sub(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return interval_new(x.lo - y.hi, x.hi - y.lo)
}

// Multiplication: [a, b] × [c, d]
fn interval_mul(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }

    // All four products
    let p1 = x.lo * y.lo
    let p2 = x.lo * y.hi
    let p3 = x.hi * y.lo
    let p4 = x.hi * y.hi

    let lo = min_f64(min_f64(p1, p2), min_f64(p3, p4))
    let hi = max_f64(max_f64(p1, p2), max_f64(p3, p4))

    return interval_new(lo, hi)
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 DIVISION: THE CRITICAL OPERATION
// ============================================================================

// Division result with exception handling
struct DivisionResult {
    result: Interval,
    exception: i32,    // 0=none, 1=div_by_zero, 2=entire_result
    decoration: Decoration,
}

// Division: [a, b] / [c, d]
// Per IEEE 1788, division by interval containing zero is well-defined
// but requires careful handling:
//   - If 0 ∈ [c, d]: result may be unbounded or split
//   - If [c, d] = [0, 0]: result is empty (not infinity!)
fn interval_div(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> DivisionResult {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return DivisionResult {
            result: interval_empty(),
            exception: 0,
            decoration: dec_ill(),
        }
    }

    // Check if y contains zero
    let y_contains_zero = y.lo <= 0.0 && y.hi >= 0.0

    if y_contains_zero {
        // Special cases per IEEE 1788
        if y.lo == 0.0 && y.hi == 0.0 {
            // [c, d] = [0, 0]: division by zero interval -> empty
            return DivisionResult {
                result: interval_empty(),
                exception: 1,  // Division by zero
                decoration: dec_ill(),
            }
        }

        if y.lo == 0.0 {
            // [0, d] with d > 0: result is [a/d, +∞] or similar
            if x.lo >= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(x.lo / y.hi, 1.0e308),
                    exception: 2,  // Entire result
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            } else if x.hi <= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(0.0 - 1.0e308, x.hi / y.hi),
                    exception: 2,
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            }
        }

        if y.hi == 0.0 {
            // [c, 0] with c < 0: result is [-∞, a/c] or similar
            if x.lo >= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(0.0 - 1.0e308, x.lo / y.lo),
                    exception: 2,
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            } else if x.hi <= 0.0 {
                return DivisionResult {
                    result: interval_new(x.hi / y.lo, 1.0e308),
                    exception: 2,
                    decoration: dec_def(),
                }
            }
        }

        // General case: 0 strictly inside [c, d]
        // Result is entire (two disconnected pieces reunited)
        return DivisionResult {
            result: interval_entire(),
            exception: 2,
            decoration: dec_trv(),
        }
    }

    // Normal division: 0 ∉ [c, d]
    // [a, b] / [c, d] = [a, b] × [1/d, 1/c]
    let inv_lo = 1.0 / y.hi
    let inv_hi = 1.0 / y.lo

    let p1 = x.lo * inv_lo
    let p2 = x.lo * inv_hi
    let p3 = x.hi * inv_lo
    let p4 = x.hi * inv_hi

    let lo = min_f64(min_f64(p1, p2), min_f64(p3, p4))
    let hi = max_f64(max_f64(p1, p2), max_f64(p3, p4))

    return DivisionResult {
        result: interval_new(lo, hi),
        exception: 0,
        decoration: dec_com(),
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 ELEMENTARY FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Square root: sqrt([a, b])
fn interval_sqrt(x: Interval) -> DecoratedInterval {
    if x.is_empty {
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    if x.hi < 0.0 {
        // Entirely negative -> empty (no real square root)
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    let lo = max_f64(0.0, x.lo)
    return decorated_new(
        interval_new(sqrt_f64(lo), sqrt_f64(x.hi)),
        if x.lo >= 0.0 { dec_com() } else { dec_def() }
    )
}

// Exponential: exp([a, b])
fn interval_exp(x: Interval) -> DecoratedInterval {
    if x.is_empty {
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    // exp is monotonically increasing
    return decorated_new(
        interval_new(exp(x.lo), exp(x.hi)),
        dec_com()
    )
}

// Natural logarithm: log([a, b])
fn interval_log(x: Interval) -> DecoratedInterval {
    if x.is_empty {
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    if x.hi <= 0.0 {
        // Entirely non-positive -> undefined
        return decorated_new(interval_empty(), dec_ill())
    }

    var dec = dec_com()
    var lo_val: f64 = 0.0

    if x.lo <= 0.0 {
        // Interval includes non-positive -> clamp, degrade decoration
        lo_val = 0.0 - 1.0e308  // -infinity for log(0+)
        dec = dec_def()
    } else {
        lo_val = log(x.lo)
    }

    return decorated_new(
        interval_new(lo_val, log(x.hi)),
        dec
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 SET OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Intersection: [a, b] ∩ [c, d]
fn interval_intersect(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty {
        return interval_empty()
    }

    let lo = max_f64(x.lo, y.lo)
    let hi = min_f64(x.hi, y.hi)

    if lo > hi {
        return interval_empty()
    }
    return interval_new(lo, hi)
}

// Hull (convex union): hull([a, b], [c, d])
fn interval_hull(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> Interval {
    if x.is_empty { return y }
    if y.is_empty { return x }

    return interval_new(
        min_f64(x.lo, y.lo),
        max_f64(x.hi, y.hi)
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 COMPARISONS
// ============================================================================

// Check if interval is subset of another
fn interval_subset(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> bool {
    if x.is_empty { return true }  // Empty is subset of everything
    if y.is_empty { return false } // Non-empty not subset of empty

    return x.lo >= y.lo && x.hi <= y.hi
}

// Check if intervals overlap
fn interval_overlaps(x: Interval, y: Interval) -> bool {
    if x.is_empty || y.is_empty { return false }

    return x.lo <= y.hi && y.lo <= x.hi
}

// Width of interval
fn interval_width(x: Interval) -> f64 {
    if x.is_empty { return 0.0 }
    return x.hi - x.lo
}

// Midpoint of interval
fn interval_mid(x: Interval) -> f64 {
    if x.is_empty { return 0.0 }
    return (x.lo + x.hi) / 2.0
}

// Radius of interval
fn interval_rad(x: Interval) -> f64 {
    if x.is_empty { return 0.0 }
    return (x.hi - x.lo) / 2.0
}

// ============================================================================
// IEEE 1788 EXCEPTION HANDLING
// ============================================================================

// Exception flags per IEEE 1788
struct IntervalException {
    undefined_operation: bool,   // e.g., sqrt of negative
    possibly_undefined: bool,    // e.g., sqrt of interval spanning 0
    division_by_zero: bool,
    overflow: bool,
}

fn exception_none() -> IntervalException {
    return IntervalException {
        undefined_operation: false,
        possibly_undefined: false,
        division_by_zero: false,
        overflow: false,
    }
}

fn exception_from_div(result: DivisionResult) -> IntervalException {
    return IntervalException {
        undefined_operation: result.exception == 1,
        possibly_undefined: result.exception == 2,
        division_by_zero: result.exception == 1,
        overflow: false,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_interval_add() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval_new(3.0, 4.0)
    let c = interval_add(a, b)

    if abs_f64(c.lo - 4.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(c.hi - 6.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_mul() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(-2.0, 3.0)
    let b = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let c = interval_mul(a, b)

    // Products: -2*1=-2, -2*2=-4, 3*1=3, 3*2=6
    // Min = -4, Max = 6
    if abs_f64(c.lo - (0.0 - 4.0)) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(c.hi - 6.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_div_normal() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(2.0, 4.0)
    let b = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let result = interval_div(a, b)

    // [2,4] / [1,2] = [2/2, 4/1] = [1, 4]
    if result.exception != 0 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.result.lo - 1.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.result.hi - 4.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_div_by_zero() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval_new(0.0, 0.0)
    let result = interval_div(a, b)

    // Division by [0,0] -> empty with exception
    if !result.result.is_empty { return false }
    if result.exception != 1 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_div_spanning_zero() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = interval_new(-1.0, 1.0)  // Spans zero
    let result = interval_div(a, b)

    // Should be entire or have exception
    if result.exception != 2 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_interval_sqrt() -> bool {
    let a = interval_new(4.0, 9.0)
    let result = interval_sqrt(a)

    if result.interval.is_empty { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.interval.lo - 2.0) > 0.001 { return false }
    if abs_f64(result.interval.hi - 3.0) > 0.001 { return false }

    // Negative interval -> empty
    let b = interval_new(-4.0, -1.0)
    let result2 = interval_sqrt(b)
    if !result2.interval.is_empty { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_decorated_operations() -> bool {
    let a = decorated_common(1.0, 2.0)
    let b = decorated_common(3.0, 4.0)

    if a.decoration.value != 4 { return false }  // com
    if b.decoration.value != 4 { return false }

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/invariants.sio ===
//! Property-Based Tests for Epistemic Laws
//!
//! These invariants must ALWAYS hold. Violation indicates a bug.
//!
//! Categories:
//!   1. Beta Posterior Laws (Bayesian consistency)
//!   2. GUM Propagation Laws (uncertainty conservation)
//!   3. Entropy Conservation (information theory)
//!   4. Combination Calculus Laws (algebraic identities)
//!   5. Ledger Invariants (entropic accounting)

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// Tolerance for floating point comparisons
fn EPS() -> f64 { return 1.0e-10 }

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION PROPERTIES
// ============================================================================

struct Beta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
}

fn beta_mean(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    let ba = b.alpha
    let bb = b.beta
    return ba / (ba + bb)
}

fn beta_variance(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    let ba = b.alpha
    let bb = b.beta
    let n = ba + bb
    return (ba * bb) / (n * n * (n + 1.0))
}

// Law 1: Mean must be in [0, 1] for valid Beta
fn law_beta_mean_bounded(b: Beta) -> bool {
    let m = beta_mean(b)
    return m >= 0.0 && m <= 1.0
}

// Law 2: Variance must be positive and bounded
fn law_beta_variance_positive(b: Beta) -> bool {
    let v = beta_variance(b)
    return v > 0.0 && v <= 0.25  // Max variance at Beta(1,1)
}

// Law 3: More observations -> lower variance
fn law_beta_observations_reduce_variance(alpha1: f64, beta1: f64, k: f64) -> bool {
    let a1 = alpha1
    let b1 = beta1
    let k_val = k

    let prior = Beta { alpha: a1, beta: b1 }
    let posterior = Beta { alpha: a1 + k_val, beta: b1 + k_val }

    let v_prior = beta_variance(prior)
    let v_post = beta_variance(posterior)

    return v_post < v_prior  // Variance must decrease
}

// Law 4: Uniform prior is symmetric (Beta(1,1))
fn law_uniform_prior_symmetric() -> bool {
    let uniform = Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
    let m = beta_mean(uniform)
    return abs_f64(m - 0.5) < EPS()
}

// Law 5: After k successes, n-k failures, mean = (1+k)/(2+n)
fn law_beta_posterior_formula(k: i32, n: i32) -> bool {
    let k_f = 0.0 + k
    let n_f = 0.0 + n
    if n < k { return true }  // Invalid input
    if k < 0 { return true }

    let posterior = Beta { alpha: 1.0 + k_f, beta: 1.0 + (n_f - k_f) }
    let expected = (1.0 + k_f) / (2.0 + n_f)
    let actual = beta_mean(posterior)

    return abs_f64(actual - expected) < EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// GUM PROPAGATION LAWS
// ============================================================================

// GUM uncertainty for y = f(x1, x2) with sensitivities c1, c2
fn gum_combined_uncertainty(u1: f64, u2: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64) -> f64 {
    return sqrt(c1*c1*u1*u1 + c2*c2*u2*u2)
}

// Law 6: Combined uncertainty >= max individual contribution
fn law_gum_uncertainty_additive(u1: f64, u2: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let u2_val = u2
    let c1_val = c1
    let c2_val = c2

    let u_combined = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, u2_val, c1_val, c2_val)
    let contrib1 = abs_f64(c1_val) * u1_val
    let contrib2 = abs_f64(c2_val) * u2_val
    let max_contrib = max_f64(contrib1, contrib2)

    return u_combined >= max_contrib - EPS()
}

// Law 7: Zero input uncertainty -> zero contribution
fn law_gum_zero_uncertainty_zero_contribution(u1: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let c1_val = c1
    let c2_val = c2

    // u2 = 0, so contribution from x2 should be 0
    let u_combined = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, 0.0, c1_val, c2_val)
    let u_from_x1_only = abs_f64(c1_val) * u1_val

    return abs_f64(u_combined - u_from_x1_only) < EPS()
}

// Law 8: Zero sensitivity -> zero contribution
fn law_gum_zero_sensitivity_zero_contribution(u1: f64, u2: f64, c1: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let u2_val = u2
    let c1_val = c1

    // c2 = 0, so x2 doesn't contribute
    let u_combined = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, u2_val, c1_val, 0.0)
    let u_from_x1_only = abs_f64(c1_val) * u1_val

    return abs_f64(u_combined - u_from_x1_only) < EPS()
}

// Law 9: Scaling uncertainty scales output
fn law_gum_scaling(u1: f64, c1: f64, k: f64) -> bool {
    let u1_val = u1
    let c1_val = c1
    let k_val = k

    let u_orig = gum_combined_uncertainty(u1_val, 0.0, c1_val, 0.0)
    let u_scaled = gum_combined_uncertainty(k_val * u1_val, 0.0, c1_val, 0.0)

    return abs_f64(u_scaled - abs_f64(k_val) * u_orig) < EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// ENTROPY CONSERVATION LAWS
// ============================================================================

// Shannon entropy H(p) = -p log(p) - (1-p) log(1-p)
fn shannon_entropy(p: f64) -> f64 {
    let p_val = p
    if p_val <= 0.0 || p_val >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    let ln2 = 0.693147180559945
    let h = 0.0 - (p_val * log(p_val) + (1.0 - p_val) * log(1.0 - p_val)) / ln2
    return h
}

// Law 10: Entropy is maximized at p = 0.5
fn law_entropy_max_at_half() -> bool {
    let h_half = shannon_entropy(0.5)
    let h_quarter = shannon_entropy(0.25)
    let h_threequarter = shannon_entropy(0.75)

    return h_half > h_quarter && h_half > h_threequarter
}

// Law 11: Entropy is symmetric around 0.5
fn law_entropy_symmetric(p: f64) -> bool {
    let p_val = p
    if p_val < 0.0 || p_val > 1.0 { return true }

    let h_p = shannon_entropy(p_val)
    let h_1mp = shannon_entropy(1.0 - p_val)

    return abs_f64(h_p - h_1mp) < EPS()
}

// Law 12: Entropy is non-negative
fn law_entropy_non_negative(p: f64) -> bool {
    let h = shannon_entropy(p)
    return h >= 0.0 - EPS()
}

// Law 13: Entropy at certainty (p=0 or p=1) is zero
fn law_entropy_zero_at_certainty() -> bool {
    let h0 = shannon_entropy(0.0)
    let h1 = shannon_entropy(1.0)
    return abs_f64(h0) < EPS() && abs_f64(h1) < EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// COMBINATION CALCULUS LAWS
// ============================================================================

// Law 14: Dempster-Shafer plausibility >= belief
fn law_ds_plausibility_ge_belief(bel_true: f64, pl_true: f64) -> bool {
    return pl_true >= bel_true - EPS()
}

// Law 15: Frechet bounds are valid (P(A AND B) >= max(0, P(A)+P(B)-1))
fn law_frechet_lower_bound(p_a: f64, p_b: f64, p_and: f64) -> bool {
    let pa = p_a
    let pb = p_b
    let pab = p_and

    let lower = max_f64(0.0, pa + pb - 1.0)
    return pab >= lower - EPS()
}

// Law 16: Frechet bounds upper (P(A AND B) <= min(P(A), P(B)))
fn law_frechet_upper_bound(p_a: f64, p_b: f64, p_and: f64) -> bool {
    let pa = p_a
    let pb = p_b
    let pab = p_and

    let upper = min_f64(pa, pb)
    return pab <= upper + EPS()
}

// Law 17: Bayesian update preserves total probability
fn law_bayes_preserves_probability(prior: f64, likelihood_t: f64, likelihood_f: f64) -> bool {
    let pr = prior
    let lt = likelihood_t
    let lf = likelihood_f

    if pr <= 0.0 || pr >= 1.0 { return true }
    if lt < 0.0 || lf < 0.0 { return true }

    // Posterior = P(H|E) = P(E|H)P(H) / P(E)
    // P(E) = P(E|H)P(H) + P(E|not H)P(not H)
    let p_evidence = lt * pr + lf * (1.0 - pr)
    if p_evidence < EPS() { return true }

    let posterior = (lt * pr) / p_evidence

    return posterior >= 0.0 && posterior <= 1.0
}

// ============================================================================
// LEDGER INVARIANTS
// ============================================================================

struct MockLedger {
    total_debt: f64,
    total_credit: f64,
    net_balance: f64,
}

// Law 18: Net balance = debt - credit
fn law_ledger_balance_correct(ledger: MockLedger) -> bool {
    let l = ledger
    let expected = l.total_debt - l.total_credit
    return abs_f64(l.net_balance - expected) < EPS()
}

// Law 19: Debt is non-negative
fn law_ledger_debt_non_negative(ledger: MockLedger) -> bool {
    return ledger.total_debt >= 0.0 - EPS()
}

// Law 20: Credit is non-negative
fn law_ledger_credit_non_negative(ledger: MockLedger) -> bool {
    return ledger.total_credit >= 0.0 - EPS()
}

// Law 21: Debt monotonically increases (or stays same)
fn law_ledger_debt_monotonic(old_debt: f64, new_debt: f64) -> bool {
    return new_debt >= old_debt - EPS()
}

// Law 22: Credit monotonically increases (or stays same)
fn law_ledger_credit_monotonic(old_credit: f64, new_credit: f64) -> bool {
    return new_credit >= old_credit - EPS()
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST HARNESS
// ============================================================================

fn test_beta_laws() -> bool {
    // Test Beta laws with various parameters
    let b1 = Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
    let b2 = Beta { alpha: 10.0, beta: 5.0 }
    let b3 = Beta { alpha: 2.0, beta: 8.0 }

    if !law_beta_mean_bounded(b1) { return false }
    if !law_beta_mean_bounded(b2) { return false }
    if !law_beta_mean_bounded(b3) { return false }

    if !law_beta_variance_positive(b1) { return false }
    if !law_beta_variance_positive(b2) { return false }
    if !law_beta_variance_positive(b3) { return false }

    if !law_beta_observations_reduce_variance(1.0, 1.0, 5.0) { return false }
    if !law_beta_observations_reduce_variance(10.0, 5.0, 10.0) { return false }

    if !law_uniform_prior_symmetric() { return false }

    if !law_beta_posterior_formula(5, 10) { return false }
    if !law_beta_posterior_formula(0, 10) { return false }
    if !law_beta_posterior_formula(10, 10) { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_gum_laws() -> bool {
    // Test GUM propagation laws
    if !law_gum_uncertainty_additive(0.1, 0.2, 1.0, 1.0) { return false }
    if !law_gum_uncertainty_additive(1.0, 0.5, 2.0, 3.0) { return false }

    if !law_gum_zero_uncertainty_zero_contribution(0.1, 1.0, 2.0) { return false }
    if !law_gum_zero_sensitivity_zero_contribution(0.1, 0.2, 1.0) { return false }

    if !law_gum_scaling(0.1, 2.0, 3.0) { return false }
    if !law_gum_scaling(0.5, 1.0, 0.5) { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_entropy_laws() -> bool {
    if !law_entropy_max_at_half() { return false }
    if !law_entropy_zero_at_certainty() { return false }

    if !law_entropy_symmetric(0.3) { return false }
    if !law_entropy_symmetric(0.1) { return false }
    if !law_entropy_symmetric(0.9) { return false }

    if !law_entropy_non_negative(0.0) { return false }
    if !law_entropy_non_negative(0.5) { return false }
    if !law_entropy_non_negative(1.0) { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_combination_laws() -> bool {
    // DS: Plausibility >= Belief
    if !law_ds_plausibility_ge_belief(0.6, 0.8) { return false }
    if !law_ds_plausibility_ge_belief(0.3, 0.5) { return false }

    // Frechet bounds
    if !law_frechet_lower_bound(0.6, 0.7, 0.3) { return false }
    if !law_frechet_upper_bound(0.6, 0.7, 0.5) { return false }

    // Bayes preserves probability
    if !law_bayes_preserves_probability(0.5, 0.9, 0.1) { return false }
    if !law_bayes_preserves_probability(0.3, 0.8, 0.2) { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_ledger_laws() -> bool {
    let l1 = MockLedger { total_debt: 5.0, total_credit: 3.0, net_balance: 2.0 }
    let l2 = MockLedger { total_debt: 10.0, total_credit: 10.0, net_balance: 0.0 }

    if !law_ledger_balance_correct(l1) { return false }
    if !law_ledger_balance_correct(l2) { return false }

    if !law_ledger_debt_non_negative(l1) { return false }
    if !law_ledger_credit_non_negative(l1) { return false }

    if !law_ledger_debt_monotonic(5.0, 6.0) { return false }
    if !law_ledger_credit_monotonic(3.0, 4.0) { return false }

    // These should fail (and we verify they correctly detect violations)
    if law_ledger_debt_monotonic(6.0, 5.0) { return false }  // Should be false

    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/knowledge.sio ===
//! stdlib/epistemic/knowledge.d
//!
//! Knowledge<T> - The core epistemic type for Sounio
//!
//! Every value knows its uncertainty. Every computation propagates variance.
//! Every result carries its provenance.
//!
//! This is not a wrapper around T with metadata. This is a fundamental
//! epistemic primitive that changes how we compute.
//!
//! # Philosophy
//!
//! Traditional: `let mass = 3.14`
//! Epistemic:   `let mass: Knowledge<f64> = 3.14 ± 0.01 from "scale_A"`
//!
//! The ± is not syntax sugar. It's an assertion about reality.
//! The variance tells us HOW CERTAIN we are about the value.
//! The provenance tells us WHERE the certainty came from.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```sounio
//! use epistemic::{Knowledge, BetaConfidence}
//! use units::{mg, mL}
//!
//! let dose: Knowledge<mg> = measure(500.0_mg, variance: 25.0)
//! let volume: Knowledge<mL> = measure(10.0_mL, variance: 0.1)
//! let concentration = dose / volume  // Variance auto-propagates
//!
//! // P(concentration > 45 mg/mL) computed from posterior
//! if concentration.prob_gt(45.0) > 0.95 {
//!     println("Therapeutic range achieved with 95% confidence")
//! }
//! ```

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION (inlined — prob::beta module currently disabled)
// ============================================================================

pub struct Beta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
}

fn beta_new(alpha: f64, b: f64) -> Beta {
    var sa = alpha
    var sb = b
    if sa < 0.0001 { sa = 0.0001 }
    if sb < 0.0001 { sb = 0.0001 }
    Beta { alpha: sa, beta: sb }
}

fn beta_mean(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta)
}

fn beta_variance(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    let n = b.alpha + b.beta
    (b.alpha * b.beta) / (n * n * (n + 1.0))
}

fn beta_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn beta_std(b: Beta) -> f64 {
    beta_sqrt_f64(beta_variance(b))
}

fn beta_posterior(prior: Beta, successes: i64, failures: i64) -> Beta {
    var sf = 0.0
    var count = 0
    while count < successes {
        sf = sf + 1.0
        count = count + 1
    }
    var ff = 0.0
    count = 0
    while count < failures {
        ff = ff + 1.0
        count = count + 1
    }
    Beta { alpha: prior.alpha + sf, beta: prior.beta + ff }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE TYPES
// ============================================================================

// Source of knowledge - where did this value come from?
pub enum Source {
    /// Direct measurement from instrument
    Measurement { instrument: string, timestamp: i64 },

    /// Computed from other values
    Computed { operation: string },

    /// User assertion (not independently verified)
    Assertion { author: string },

    /// External data source
    External { source: string, url: string },

    /// Unknown origin
    Unknown,
}

// Single step in the provenance chain
pub struct ProvenanceStep {
    /// What operation was performed
    operation: string,

    /// When (unix timestamp)
    timestamp: i64,

    /// Confidence decay from this operation
    decay_factor: f64,
}

// Complete provenance chain
pub struct Provenance {
    /// Original source (display string: instrument name, operation, author, etc.)
    source: string,

    /// Chain of transformations
    steps: Vec<ProvenanceStep>,
}

// ============================================================================
// BETA CONFIDENCE
// ============================================================================

// BetaConfidence wraps Beta distribution for epistemic use
//
// Provides the semantic layer on top of raw Beta parameters:
// - `concentration()` = how much evidence we have
// - `uncertainty()` = how much we don't know
// - `needs_exploration()` = should we acquire more data?
pub struct BetaConfidence {
    /// Underlying Beta distribution
    dist: Beta,
}

impl BetaConfidence {
    /// Create from raw alpha, beta parameters
    pub fn new(alpha: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
        BetaConfidence { dist: beta_new(alpha, b) }
    }

    /// Uniform prior (maximum ignorance)
    pub fn uniform() -> BetaConfidence {
        BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 } }
    }

    /// Jeffreys prior (uninformative)
    pub fn jeffreys() -> BetaConfidence {
        BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 0.5, beta: 0.5 } }
    }

    /// From success rate and sample size
    /// e.g., observed 8 successes in 10 trials → from_rate(0.8, 10)
    pub fn from_rate(rate: f64, n: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
        let alpha = rate * n + 1.0
        let b = (1.0 - rate) * n + 1.0
        BetaConfidence { dist: beta_new(alpha, b) }
    }

    /// From observations
    pub fn from_observations(successes: i64, failures: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
        let prior = Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
        BetaConfidence { dist: beta_posterior(prior, successes, failures) }
    }

    /// Strong confidence centered at value
    pub fn strong(center: f64, strength: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
        let alpha = center * strength + 1.0
        let b = (1.0 - center) * strength + 1.0
        BetaConfidence { dist: beta_new(alpha, b) }
    }

    // Accessors

    /// Mean confidence (point estimate)
    pub fn mean(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        beta_mean(self.dist)
    }

    /// Variance (measure of uncertainty about the confidence)
    pub fn variance(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        beta_variance(self.dist)
    }

    /// Standard deviation
    pub fn std(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        beta_std(self.dist)
    }

    /// Concentration (effective sample size)
    /// Higher = more evidence backing this confidence
    pub fn concentration(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        self.dist.alpha + self.dist.beta
    }

    /// Uncertainty score: inverse of concentration
    /// Higher = we should explore more
    pub fn uncertainty(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        1.0 / self.concentration()
    }

    /// Should we acquire more data?
    /// Returns true if variance is high (we don't know much)
    pub fn needs_exploration(self: &BetaConfidence, threshold: f64) -> bool {
        self.variance() > threshold
    }

    /// Update with new evidence
    pub fn update(self: &BetaConfidence, successes: i64, failures: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
        BetaConfidence { dist: beta_posterior(self.dist, successes, failures) }
    }

    /// Combine two confidences (independent evidence)
    /// Result has combined evidence: α_new = α1 + α2 - 1, β_new = β1 + β2 - 1
    pub fn combine(self: &BetaConfidence, other: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
        let alpha = self.dist.alpha + other.dist.alpha - 1.0
        let b = self.dist.beta + other.dist.beta - 1.0
        BetaConfidence { dist: beta_new(alpha, b) }
    }

    /// Decay confidence (for propagation through transformations)
    pub fn decay(self: &BetaConfidence, factor: f64) -> BetaConfidence {
        // Reduce effective sample size while preserving mean
        let m = self.mean()
        let n = self.concentration() * factor
        BetaConfidence::from_rate(m, n)
    }

    /// Raw access to alpha
    pub fn alpha(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        self.dist.alpha
    }

    /// Raw access to beta
    pub fn beta_param(self: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 {
        self.dist.beta
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC - THE CORE EPISTEMIC TYPE
// ============================================================================

// Epistemic wraps a value with epistemic metadata
//
// This is THE fundamental type for scientific computing in Sounio.
// Every Epistemic value knows:
// - Its point estimate (value)
// - Its uncertainty (variance)
// - Its credibility (confidence as Beta posterior)
// - Its history (provenance chain)
//
// Arithmetic operations propagate variance using the delta method.
// Confidence decays through transformations.
// Provenance accumulates through the computation graph.
//
// Note: named Epistemic (not Knowledge) to avoid checker conflict with the
// built-in Knowledge<T> type in souc v1.0.0-beta.4 and earlier.
pub struct Epistemic {
    /// The point estimate
    value: f64,

    /// Variance (uncertainty in the value)
    variance: f64,

    /// Confidence as Beta posterior
    confidence: BetaConfidence,

    /// Where this knowledge came from
    provenance: Provenance,
}

/// Type alias: Knowledge<f64> = Epistemic (for documentation purposes)
// type Knowledge = Epistemic

impl Epistemic {
    /// Create new epistemic value with full specification
    pub fn new(
        value: f64,
        variance: f64,
        confidence: BetaConfidence,
        source: string,
    ) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: value,
            variance: variance,
            confidence: confidence,
            provenance: Provenance { source: source, steps: Vec::new() },
        }
    }

    /// Create from measurement (typical lab scenario)
    pub fn measured(value: f64, variance: f64, instrument: string) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: value,
            variance: variance,
            confidence: BetaConfidence::uniform(),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: instrument,
                steps: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }

    /// Create constant (zero variance, maximum confidence)
    pub fn constant(value: f64) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: value,
            variance: 0.0,
            confidence: BetaConfidence::strong(0.99, 1000.0),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: "constant",
                steps: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }

    /// Create from assertion (user says this is true)
    pub fn asserted(value: f64, variance: f64, author: string) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: value,
            variance: variance,
            confidence: BetaConfidence::uniform(),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: author,
                steps: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }

    // Accessors

    /// Get the point estimate
    pub fn get(self: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
        self.value
    }

    /// Get variance
    pub fn var(self: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
        self.variance
    }

    /// Get standard deviation
    pub fn std(self: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
        sqrt_f64(self.variance)
    }

    /// Get confidence
    pub fn conf(self: &Epistemic) -> &BetaConfidence {
        &self.confidence
    }

    /// Get provenance
    pub fn prov(self: &Epistemic) -> &Provenance {
        &self.provenance
    }

    /// Map the inner value while preserving epistemic metadata
    pub fn map(self: Epistemic, f: fn(f64) -> f64, operation: string) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = f(self.value)
        let step = ProvenanceStep {
            operation: operation,
            timestamp: 0,
            decay_factor: 0.95,
        }
        var new_steps = self.provenance.steps.clone()
        new_steps.push(step)

        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: self.variance,  // Note: may need adjustment based on f
            confidence: self.confidence.decay(0.95),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: self.provenance.source,
                steps: new_steps,
            },
        }
    }

    /// Add provenance step without changing value
    pub fn with_provenance(self: Epistemic, operation: string) -> Epistemic {
        let step = ProvenanceStep {
            operation: operation,
            timestamp: 0,
            decay_factor: 1.0,
        }
        var new_steps = self.provenance.steps.clone()
        new_steps.push(step)

        Epistemic {
            value: self.value,
            variance: self.variance,
            confidence: self.confidence,
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: self.provenance.source,
                steps: new_steps,
            },
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC - ARITHMETIC WITH VARIANCE PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

impl Epistemic {
    /// Standard deviation
    pub fn std_dev(self: &Epistemic) -> f64 {
        sqrt_f64(self.variance)
    }

    /// 95% confidence interval (normal approximation)
    pub fn ci95(self: &Epistemic) -> (f64, f64) {
        let z = 1.96
        let lo = self.value - z * self.std_dev()
        let hi = self.value + z * self.std_dev()
        (lo, hi)
    }

    /// P(X > threshold) using normal approximation
    pub fn prob_gt(self: &Epistemic, threshold: f64) -> f64 {
        if self.variance <= 0.0000001 {
            if self.value > threshold { return 1.0 }
            return 0.0
        }
        let z = (self.value - threshold) / self.std_dev()
        // Approximation of Φ(z) using erf
        0.5 * (1.0 + erf_approx(z / 1.4142135623730951))
    }

    /// P(X < threshold)
    pub fn prob_lt(self: &Epistemic, threshold: f64) -> f64 {
        1.0 - self.prob_gt(threshold)
    }

    /// P(lo < X < hi)
    pub fn prob_between(self: &Epistemic, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 {
        self.prob_lt(hi) - self.prob_lt(lo)
    }
}

// Arithmetic operators with variance propagation

impl Add for Epistemic {
    /// X + Y: Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) for independent X, Y
    fn add(self: Epistemic, other: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = self.value + other.value
        let new_variance = self.variance + other.variance
        let new_confidence = self.confidence.combine(&other.confidence)

        let step = ProvenanceStep {
            operation: "add",
            timestamp: 0,
            decay_factor: 0.99,
        }
        var new_steps = self.provenance.steps.clone()
        new_steps.extend(other.provenance.steps.clone())
        new_steps.push(step)

        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: new_confidence.decay(0.99),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: "add",
                steps: new_steps,
            },
        }
    }
}

impl Sub for Epistemic {
    /// X - Y: Var(X - Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) for independent X, Y
    fn sub(self: Epistemic, other: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = self.value - other.value
        let new_variance = self.variance + other.variance
        let new_confidence = self.confidence.combine(&other.confidence)

        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: new_confidence.decay(0.99),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: "sub",
                steps: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl Mul for Epistemic {
    /// X * Y: Var(XY) ≈ Y²Var(X) + X²Var(Y) (delta method)
    fn mul(self: Epistemic, other: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = self.value * other.value
        // Delta method for product
        let new_variance = other.value * other.value * self.variance
                         + self.value * self.value * other.variance
        let new_confidence = self.confidence.combine(&other.confidence)

        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: new_confidence.decay(0.98),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: "mul",
                steps: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }
}

impl Div for Epistemic {
    /// X / Y: Var(X/Y) ≈ (1/Y²)Var(X) + (X²/Y⁴)Var(Y) (delta method)
    fn div(self: Epistemic, other: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = self.value / other.value
        // Delta method for quotient
        let y2 = other.value * other.value
        let y4 = y2 * y2
        let new_variance = self.variance / y2
                         + self.value * self.value * other.variance / y4
        let new_confidence = self.confidence.combine(&other.confidence)

        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: new_confidence.decay(0.97),
            provenance: Provenance {
                source: "div",
                steps: Vec::new(),
            },
        }
    }
}

// Scalar operations

impl Epistemic {
    /// Multiply by scalar constant
    pub fn scale(self: Epistemic, c: f64) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: self.value * c,
            variance: self.variance * c * c,  // Var(cX) = c²Var(X)
            confidence: self.confidence,
            provenance: self.provenance.with_step("scale"),
        }
    }

    /// Add scalar constant
    pub fn shift(self: Epistemic, c: f64) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: self.value + c,
            variance: self.variance,  // Var(X + c) = Var(X)
            confidence: self.confidence,
            provenance: self.provenance.with_step("shift"),
        }
    }

    /// Square: Var(X²) ≈ 4X²Var(X)
    pub fn square(self: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        Epistemic {
            value: self.value * self.value,
            variance: 4.0 * self.value * self.value * self.variance,
            confidence: self.confidence.decay(0.98),
            provenance: self.provenance.with_step("square"),
        }
    }

    /// Square root: Var(√X) ≈ Var(X)/(4X)
    pub fn sqrt(self: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = sqrt_f64(self.value)
        let new_variance = self.variance / (4.0 * self.value)
        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: self.confidence.decay(0.98),
            provenance: self.provenance.with_step("sqrt"),
        }
    }

    /// Exponential: Var(e^X) ≈ e^(2X) Var(X)
    pub fn exp(self: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = exp_f64(self.value)
        let new_variance = exp_f64(2.0 * self.value) * self.variance
        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: self.confidence.decay(0.95),
            provenance: self.provenance.with_step("exp"),
        }
    }

    /// Natural log: Var(ln X) ≈ Var(X)/X²
    pub fn ln(self: Epistemic) -> Epistemic {
        let new_value = ln_f64(self.value)
        let new_variance = self.variance / (self.value * self.value)
        Epistemic {
            value: new_value,
            variance: new_variance,
            confidence: self.confidence.decay(0.95),
            provenance: self.provenance.with_step("ln"),
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE HELPERS
// ============================================================================

impl Provenance {
    /// Add a step to provenance
    pub fn with_step(self: Provenance, operation: string) -> Provenance {
        let step = ProvenanceStep {
            operation: operation,
            timestamp: 0,
            decay_factor: 1.0,
        }
        var new_steps = self.steps.clone()
        new_steps.push(step)
        Provenance {
            source: self.source,
            steps: new_steps,
        }
    }

    /// Format provenance as string (simplified: returns source + step count)
    pub fn to_string(self: &Provenance) -> string {
        self.source.clone()
    }

    /// Count transformation depth
    pub fn depth(self: &Provenance) -> i64 {
        self.steps.len() as i64
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// NUMERIC HELPERS (copied from beta.d for standalone compilation)
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Taylor series approximation for small x
    if x > 10.0 { return 22026.465794806718 * exp_f64(x - 10.0) }
    if x < -10.0 { return 0.00004539992976248485 * exp_f64(x + 10.0) }

    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        result = result + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }  // -inf approximation
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    // ln(x) = 2 * arctanh((x-1)/(x+1)) for x > 0
    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result = 0.0
    var term = y
    var i = 1
    while i < 30 {
        result = result + term / (i as f64)
        term = term * y * y
        i = i + 2
    }
    return 2.0 * result
}

fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Abramowitz and Stegun approximation
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = 0.0 - 0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = 0.0 - 1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911

    let sign = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x_abs = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }

    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * x_abs)
    let y = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t + a4) * t) + a3) * t + a2) * t + a1) * t * exp_f64(0.0 - x_abs * x_abs)

    return sign * y
}
