// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/linalg.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/linalg.sio
//
// Epistemic Linear Algebra — Sounio
//
// Matrix and vector operations with uncertainty propagation.
// Fixed arrays: max 16x16 matrices, max 64-element vectors.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn la_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn la_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn la_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// ============================================================================
// Epistemic Vector: value + variance per element
// ============================================================================

struct EVector {
    values: [f64; 64],
    variances: [f64; 64],
    n: i64,
}

fn evec_new(n: i64) -> EVector {
    EVector {
        values: [0.0; 64],
        variances: [0.0; 64],
        n: n,
    }
}

fn evec_set(v: &!EVector, idx: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 {
        v.values[idx] = val
        v.variances[idx] = var_
    }
}

fn evec_get_value(v: &EVector, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 { v.values[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

fn evec_get_variance(v: &EVector, idx: i64) -> f64 {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 64 { v.variances[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

fn evec_std(v: &EVector, idx: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    la_sqrt(evec_get_variance(v, idx))
}

// Dot product with uncertainty propagation
fn evec_dot(a: &EVector, b: &EVector) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    let n = if a.n < b.n { a.n } else { b.n }
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            sum = sum + a.values[i] * b.values[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Dot product variance: Var(a.b) = sum(b_i^2 * Var(a_i) + a_i^2 * Var(b_i))
fn evec_dot_variance(a: &EVector, b: &EVector) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var vsum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    let n = if a.n < b.n { a.n } else { b.n }
    while i < n {
        if i < 64 {
            vsum = vsum + b.values[i] * b.values[i] * a.variances[i]
                       + a.values[i] * a.values[i] * b.variances[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    vsum
}

// Vector norm with uncertainty
fn evec_norm(v: &EVector) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < v.n {
        if i < 64 {
            sum = sum + v.values[i] * v.values[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    la_sqrt(sum)
}

// Vector addition with uncertainty propagation
fn evec_add(a: &EVector, b: &EVector) -> EVector with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = evec_new(a.n)
    var i = 0
    while i < a.n {
        if i < 64 {
            result.values[i] = a.values[i] + b.values[i]
            result.variances[i] = a.variances[i] + b.variances[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Vector subtraction with uncertainty propagation
fn evec_sub(a: &EVector, b: &EVector) -> EVector with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = evec_new(a.n)
    var i = 0
    while i < a.n {
        if i < 64 {
            result.values[i] = a.values[i] - b.values[i]
            result.variances[i] = a.variances[i] + b.variances[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Scalar multiply with uncertainty propagation
fn evec_scale(v: &EVector, s: f64) -> EVector with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = evec_new(v.n)
    var i = 0
    while i < v.n {
        if i < 64 {
            result.values[i] = s * v.values[i]
            result.variances[i] = s * s * v.variances[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Epistemic Matrix: value + variance per element
// Max 16x16
// ============================================================================

struct EMatrix {
    values: [f64; 256],
    variances: [f64; 256],
    rows: i64,
    cols: i64,
}

fn emat_new(rows: i64, cols: i64) -> EMatrix {
    EMatrix {
        values: [0.0; 256],
        variances: [0.0; 256],
        rows: rows,
        cols: cols,
    }
}

fn emat_set(m: &!EMatrix, r: i64, c: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    let idx = r * m.cols + c
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 256 {
        m.values[idx] = val
        m.variances[idx] = var_
    }
}

fn emat_get_value(m: &EMatrix, r: i64, c: i64) -> f64 {
    let idx = r * m.cols + c
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 256 { m.values[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

fn emat_get_variance(m: &EMatrix, r: i64, c: i64) -> f64 {
    let idx = r * m.cols + c
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 256 { m.variances[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

// Identity matrix
fn emat_identity(n: i64) -> EMatrix with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m = emat_new(n, n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 16 {
            m.values[i * n + i] = 1.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    m
}

// Matrix-vector multiply with uncertainty propagation
// result[i] = sum_j(A[i,j] * x[j])
// Var(result[i]) = sum_j(A[i,j]^2 * Var(x[j]) + x[j]^2 * Var(A[i,j]))
fn emat_vec_mul(a: &EMatrix, x: &EVector) -> EVector with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = evec_new(a.rows)
    var i = 0
    while i < a.rows {
        var sum = 0.0
        var vsum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < a.cols {
            let aij = emat_get_value(a, i, j)
            let xj = evec_get_value(x, j)
            sum = sum + aij * xj
            vsum = vsum + aij * aij * evec_get_variance(x, j)
                       + xj * xj * emat_get_variance(a, i, j)
            j = j + 1
        }
        if i < 64 {
            result.values[i] = sum
            result.variances[i] = vsum
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Matrix multiply C = A * B with uncertainty propagation
fn emat_mul(a: &EMatrix, b: &EMatrix) -> EMatrix with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var c = emat_new(a.rows, b.cols)
    var i = 0
    while i < a.rows {
        var j = 0
        while j < b.cols {
            var sum = 0.0
            var vsum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < a.cols {
                let aik = emat_get_value(a, i, k)
                let bkj = emat_get_value(b, k, j)
                sum = sum + aik * bkj
                vsum = vsum + aik * aik * emat_get_variance(b, k, j)
                           + bkj * bkj * emat_get_variance(a, i, k)
                k = k + 1
            }
            let idx = i * c.cols + j
            if idx < 256 {
                c.values[idx] = sum
                c.variances[idx] = vsum
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    c
}

// Matrix transpose
fn emat_transpose(a: &EMatrix) -> EMatrix with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var t = emat_new(a.cols, a.rows)
    var i = 0
    while i < a.rows {
        var j = 0
        while j < a.cols {
            let idx_src = i * a.cols + j
            let idx_dst = j * a.rows + i
            if idx_src < 256 && idx_dst < 256 {
                t.values[idx_dst] = a.values[idx_src]
                t.variances[idx_dst] = a.variances[idx_src]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    t
}

// ============================================================================
// Stability risk classification
// ============================================================================

fn STABILITY_LOW() -> i64 { 0 }
fn STABILITY_MEDIUM() -> i64 { 1 }
fn STABILITY_HIGH() -> i64 { 2 }
fn STABILITY_CRITICAL() -> i64 { 3 }

// Estimate condition number (ratio of max/min diagonal for simple estimate)
fn emat_condition_estimate(a: &EMatrix) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var max_diag = 0.0
    var min_diag = 1.0e30
    var i = 0
    while i < a.rows {
        let d = la_abs(emat_get_value(a, i, i))
        if d > max_diag { max_diag = d }
        if d < min_diag && d > 1.0e-15 { min_diag = d }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if min_diag < 1.0e-15 { return 1.0e15 }
    max_diag / min_diag
}

fn classify_stability(condition_number: f64) -> i64 {
    if condition_number < 1000.0 { return STABILITY_LOW() }
    if condition_number < 1000000.0 { return STABILITY_MEDIUM() }
    if condition_number < 1000000000.0 { return STABILITY_HIGH() }
    STABILITY_CRITICAL()
}

// ============================================================================
// LU Decomposition (simple, no pivoting, with uncertainty)
// ============================================================================

struct LUDecomp {
    lu: EMatrix,
    n: i64,
    valid: bool,
}

fn lu_decompose(a: &EMatrix) -> LUDecomp with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = a.rows
    var lu = emat_new(n, n)
    // Copy A into LU
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let idx = i * n + j
            if idx < 256 {
                lu.values[idx] = a.values[idx]
                lu.variances[idx] = a.variances[idx]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Gaussian elimination
    var k = 0
    while k < n {
        let pivot = emat_get_value(&lu, k, k)
        if la_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-15 {
            return LUDecomp { lu: lu, n: n, valid: false }
        }

        i = k + 1
        while i < n {
            let factor = emat_get_value(&lu, i, k) / pivot
            let idx_ik = i * n + k
            if idx_ik < 256 {
                lu.values[idx_ik] = factor
            }

            var j = k + 1
            while j < n {
                let idx_ij = i * n + j
                let idx_kj = k * n + j
                if idx_ij < 256 && idx_kj < 256 {
                    lu.values[idx_ij] = lu.values[idx_ij] - factor * lu.values[idx_kj]
                    // Variance propagation through subtraction and multiplication
                    lu.variances[idx_ij] = lu.variances[idx_ij]
                        + factor * factor * lu.variances[idx_kj]
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    LUDecomp { lu: lu, n: n, valid: true }
}

// Solve Ax = b using LU decomposition
fn lu_solve(decomp: &LUDecomp, b: &EVector) -> EVector with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = decomp.n
    var x = evec_new(n)

    // Forward substitution: Ly = b
    var y = evec_new(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = evec_get_value(b, i)
        var vsum = evec_get_variance(b, i)
        var j = 0
        while j < i {
            let lij = emat_get_value(&decomp.lu, i, j)
            sum = sum - lij * y.values[j]
            vsum = vsum + lij * lij * y.variances[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        if i < 64 {
            y.values[i] = sum
            y.variances[i] = vsum
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution: Ux = y
    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = y.values[i]
        var vsum = y.variances[i]
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            let uij = emat_get_value(&decomp.lu, i, j)
            sum = sum - uij * x.values[j]
            vsum = vsum + uij * uij * x.variances[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let uii = emat_get_value(&decomp.lu, i, i)
        if la_abs(uii) > 1.0e-15 {
            if i < 64 {
                x.values[i] = sum / uii
                x.variances[i] = vsum / (uii * uii)
            }
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    x
}

// Convenience: solve Ax = b directly
fn emat_solve(a: &EMatrix, b: &EVector) -> EVector with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let decomp = lu_decompose(a)
    lu_solve(&decomp, b)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/mcmc_core.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/mcmc_core.sio
// Metropolis-Hastings MCMC Sampler with Diagnostics
//
// Implements:
// - LCG pseudo-random number generator (f64-based, via RngState struct)
// - Box-Muller normal proposal
// - Metropolis-Hastings acceptance
// - Chain statistics: mean, variance, std
// - Effective sample size (autocorrelation-based)
// - Gelman-Rubin R-hat (multi-chain via split-chain)
// - Full diagnostics struct
//
// References:
// - Metropolis et al. (1953): "Equation of State Calculations"
// - Gelman & Rubin (1992): "Inference from Iterative Simulation"
// - Geyer (1992): "Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo"

// =============================================================================
// Helper Functions (must precede callers)
// =============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x;
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn pi_val() -> f64 {
    3.14159265358979323846
}

// Natural logarithm via range reduction + Taylor series
// ln(x) = ln(m * 2^e) = ln(m) + e*ln(2)
// where m is in [0.5, 2). Series: ln(m) = 2*(t + t^3/3 + t^5/5 + ...)
// with t = (m-1)/(m+1)
fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 {
        m = m / 2.0
        e = e + 1
    }
    while m < 0.5 {
        m = m * 2.0
        e = e - 1
    }

    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        let denom = (2 * k + 1) as f64
        sum = sum + term / denom
        k = k + 1
    }
    let ln_m = 2.0 * sum

    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    return ln_m + (e as f64) * ln2
}

// Exponential function via Taylor series with range reduction
// exp(x) = 2^k * exp(r) where r = x - k*ln2
fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }

    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 {
        k = k_f as i32
    } else {
        k = (k_f as i32) - 1
    }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2

    // Taylor series for exp(r) where |r| < ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }

    // Multiply by 2^k
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k {
            result = result * 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) {
            result = result / 2.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    return result
}

// Cosine approximation via Taylor series (must precede mcmc_normal_proposal)
fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var a = x
    let twopi = 2.0 * pi_val()
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }

    // Shift to [-pi, pi] for better convergence
    if a > pi_val() { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// Sine approximation via Taylor series
fn sin_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    return cos_approx(x - pi_val() / 2.0)
}

// =============================================================================
// LCG Pseudo-Random Number Generator
// =============================================================================
// Uses an f64-based multiplicative LCG with fractional part extraction.
// The RngState struct wraps the seed to avoid VM limitations with &!f64
// primitive references (the VM dereferences &!f64 as Pointer, not Float,
// which breaks arithmetic operations).
//
// LCG recurrence: seed <- frac(a * seed + c)
// where a = 16807.1234, c = 0.4231567890
// Output is in [0, 1).

struct RngState {
    seed: f64
}

fn frac(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var v = x
    while v >= 1.0 { v = v - 1.0 }
    while v < 0.0 { v = v + 1.0 }
    return v
}

fn lcg_next(rng: &!RngState) -> f64 {
    let a = 16807.1234
    let c = 0.4231567890
    let s = rng.seed
    rng.seed = frac(a * s + c)
    return rng.seed
}

// =============================================================================
// Box-Muller Transform for Normal Proposals
// =============================================================================
// Generates a sample from N(current, step_size^2) using two uniform samples.
// Uses the polar form: z = sqrt(-2*ln(u1)) * cos(2*pi*u2)

fn mcmc_normal_proposal(current: f64, step_size: f64, rng: &!RngState) -> f64 {
    var u1 = lcg_next(rng)
    if u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let u2 = lcg_next(rng)
    let z = sqrt_f64(0.0 - 2.0 * ln_f64(u1)) * cos_approx(2.0 * pi_val() * u2)
    return current + step_size * z
}

// =============================================================================
// MCMC Configuration
// =============================================================================

struct MCMCConfig {
    n_samples: i32,
    n_warmup: i32,
    step_size: f64,
    target_accept: f64,
    initial_seed: f64
}

fn mcmc_config_default() -> MCMCConfig {
    return MCMCConfig {
        n_samples: 5000,
        n_warmup: 1000,
        step_size: 0.5,
        target_accept: 0.44,
        initial_seed: 0.7123456789
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// MCMC Chain Storage
// =============================================================================

struct MCMCChain {
    samples: [f64; 10000],
    n_stored: i32,
    n_accepted: i32,
    n_total: i32
}

fn mcmc_chain_new() -> MCMCChain {
    return MCMCChain {
        samples: [0.0; 10000],
        n_stored: 0,
        n_accepted: 0,
        n_total: 0
    }
}

fn mcmc_store_sample(chain: &!MCMCChain, value: f64) {
    if chain.n_stored < 10000 {
        chain.samples[chain.n_stored] = value
        chain.n_stored = chain.n_stored + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Chain Statistics
// =============================================================================

fn mcmc_chain_mean(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stored {
        sum = sum + chain.samples[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum / (chain.n_stored as f64)
}

fn mcmc_chain_variance(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < 2 { return 0.0 }
    let mean = mcmc_chain_mean(chain)
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < chain.n_stored {
        let diff = chain.samples[i] - mean
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum_sq / ((chain.n_stored - 1) as f64)
}

fn mcmc_chain_std(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(mcmc_chain_variance(chain))
}

// =============================================================================
// Effective Sample Size (autocorrelation-based)
// =============================================================================
// ESS = n / (1 + 2 * sum_{k=1}^{K} rho_k)
// where rho_k is the lag-k autocorrelation.
// We truncate the sum when rho_k drops below 0.05 (Geyer initial positive
// sequence estimator, simplified).

fn mcmc_autocorrelation(chain: &MCMCChain, lag: i32) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < lag + 2 { return 0.0 }
    let mean = mcmc_chain_mean(chain)
    var cov: f64 = 0.0
    var var_sum: f64 = 0.0
    let n = chain.n_stored - lag
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let d1 = chain.samples[i] - mean
        let d2 = chain.samples[i + lag] - mean
        cov = cov + d1 * d2
        var_sum = var_sum + d1 * d1
        i = i + 1
    }
    if var_sum < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
    return cov / var_sum
}

fn mcmc_effective_sample_size(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < 10 { return chain.n_stored as f64 }
    let n = chain.n_stored as f64

    var sum_rho: f64 = 0.0
    let max_lag = chain.n_stored / 2
    var max_check = max_lag
    if max_check > 500 { max_check = 500 }

    var lag: i32 = 1
    while lag < max_check {
        let rho = mcmc_autocorrelation(chain, lag)
        if rho < 0.05 {
            lag = max_check
        } else {
            sum_rho = sum_rho + rho
            lag = lag + 1
        }
    }

    let tau = 1.0 + 2.0 * sum_rho
    if tau < 1.0 { return n }
    return n / tau
}

// =============================================================================
// Gelman-Rubin R-hat (split-chain version)
// =============================================================================
// For a single chain, we split it in half to compute split R-hat.
// R-hat = sqrt(var_plus / W) where:
//   W = average within-half variance
//   B = n * variance of half-means
//   var_plus = (n-1)/n * W + B/n

fn mcmc_split_rhat(chain: &MCMCChain) -> f64 {
    if chain.n_stored < 10 { return 2.0 }

    let half = chain.n_stored / 2
    let n = half as f64

    // Compute mean for each half
    var sum1: f64 = 0.0
    var sum2: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < half {
        sum1 = sum1 + chain.samples[i]
        sum2 = sum2 + chain.samples[i + half]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean1 = sum1 / n
    let mean2 = sum2 / n

    // Compute variance for each half
    var var1: f64 = 0.0
    var var2: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < half {
        let d1 = chain.samples[i] - mean1
        let d2 = chain.samples[i + half] - mean2
        var1 = var1 + d1 * d1
        var2 = var2 + d2 * d2
        i = i + 1
    }
    var1 = var1 / (n - 1.0)
    var2 = var2 / (n - 1.0)

    // Within-chain variance
    let W = (var1 + var2) / 2.0

    // Between-chain variance
    let grand_mean = (mean1 + mean2) / 2.0
    let d1 = mean1 - grand_mean
    let d2 = mean2 - grand_mean
    let B = n * (d1 * d1 + d2 * d2)

    if W < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0 }

    // Pooled variance
    let var_plus = (n - 1.0) / n * W + B / n

    return sqrt_f64(var_plus / W)
}

// =============================================================================
// Full Diagnostics
// =============================================================================

struct MCMCDiagnostics {
    mean: f64,
    std_dev: f64,
    acceptance_rate: f64,
    ess: f64,
    r_hat: f64
}

fn mcmc_diagnostics(chain: &MCMCChain) -> MCMCDiagnostics {
    let mean = mcmc_chain_mean(chain)
    let std_dev = mcmc_chain_std(chain)
    var accept_rate: f64 = 0.0
    if chain.n_total > 0 {
        accept_rate = (chain.n_accepted as f64) / (chain.n_total as f64)
    }
    let ess = mcmc_effective_sample_size(chain)
    let r_hat = mcmc_split_rhat(chain)

    return MCMCDiagnostics {
        mean: mean,
        std_dev: std_dev,
        acceptance_rate: accept_rate,
        ess: ess,
        r_hat: r_hat
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Metropolis-Hastings Sampler
// =============================================================================
// Runs MH sampling given a log-density function evaluated inline.
// Because Sounio does not support function pointers in self-hosted codegen,
// the actual sampling loop that calls a target log-density must be written
// at the call site. This module provides all the building blocks.
//
// Usage pattern:
//   var chain = mcmc_chain_new()
//   var config = mcmc_config_default()
//   var rng = RngState { seed: config.initial_seed }
//   var current = 0.0
//   var current_lp = <log_density(current)>
//   var i = 0
//   while i < config.n_samples + config.n_warmup {
//       let proposal = mcmc_normal_proposal(current, config.step_size, &!rng)
//       let proposal_lp = <log_density(proposal)>
//       let log_alpha = proposal_lp - current_lp
//       let u = lcg_next(&!rng)
//       let accept = ln_f64(u) < log_alpha
//       if accept {
//           current = proposal
//           current_lp = proposal_lp
//           chain.n_accepted = chain.n_accepted + 1
//       }
//       chain.n_total = chain.n_total + 1
//       if i >= config.n_warmup {
//           mcmc_store_sample(&!chain, current)
//       }
//       i = i + 1
//   }
//   let diag = mcmc_diagnostics(&chain)


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/mcmc.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/mcmc.sio
//
// Epistemic MCMC Samplers with Uncertainty Quantification
//
// Metropolis-Hastings and diagnostics (R-hat, ESS).
// Fixed arrays: max 16 parameters, max 4 chains, max 2048 samples per chain.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn mcmc_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn mcmc_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// MCMC Configuration
// ============================================================================

struct MHOptions {
    proposal_scale: f64,
    n_warmup: i64,
    n_samples: i64,
    n_chains: i64,
    seed: i64,
}

fn mh_options_default() -> MHOptions {
    MHOptions {
        proposal_scale: 0.1,
        n_warmup: 500,
        n_samples: 1000,
        n_chains: 4,
        seed: 42,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MCMC Chain: samples for a single chain
// Max 2048 samples, max 16 parameters
// ============================================================================

struct MCMCChain {
    // samples[i * 16 + j] = value of parameter j at sample i
    samples: [f64; 4096],
    // log_prob[i] = log probability at sample i
    log_probs: [f64; 2048],
    n_samples: i64,
    n_params: i64,
    n_accepted: i64,
}

fn mcmc_chain_new(n_params: i64) -> MCMCChain {
    MCMCChain {
        samples: [0.0; 4096],
        log_probs: [0.0; 2048],
        n_samples: 0,
        n_params: n_params,
        n_accepted: 0,
    }
}

fn chain_add_sample(c: &!MCMCChain, theta: [f64; 16], lp: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if c.n_samples >= 2048 { return }
    let s = c.n_samples
    var j = 0
    while j < c.n_params {
        if j < 16 {
            c.samples[s * 16 + j] = theta[j]
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    c.log_probs[s] = lp
    c.n_samples = c.n_samples + 1
}

fn chain_get_sample(c: &MCMCChain, i: i64, j: i64) -> f64 {
    let idx = i * 16 + j
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 4096 { c.samples[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

// Acceptance rate
fn chain_acceptance_rate(c: &MCMCChain) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if c.n_samples == 0 { return 0.0 }
    (c.n_accepted as f64) / (c.n_samples as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// Simple pseudo-random number generator (LCG)
// ============================================================================

struct RNG {
    state: i64,
}

fn rng_new(seed: i64) -> RNG {
    RNG { state: seed }
}

fn rng_next_i64(rng: &!RNG) -> i64 {
    // Linear congruential generator
    rng.state = rng.state * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
    rng.state
}

fn rng_next_f64(rng: &!RNG) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let v = rng_next_i64(rng)
    let pos = if v < 0 { 0 - v } else { v }
    (pos as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
}

// Approximate normal sample via Box-Muller-like transform
fn rng_normal(rng: &!RNG) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Simple approximation: sum of 12 uniform - 6
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 12 {
        sum = sum + rng_next_f64(rng)
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum - 6.0
}

// ============================================================================
// Metropolis-Hastings Sampler
// ============================================================================

// Demo log-posterior: bivariate normal
// log p(theta) = -0.5 * (theta[0]^2 + theta[1]^2)
fn demo_log_posterior(theta: [f64; 16], n_params: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var lp = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_params {
        if i < 16 {
            lp = lp - 0.5 * theta[i] * theta[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    lp
}

// Run one MH chain
fn mh_sample_chain(
    n_params: i64,
    opts: &MHOptions,
    chain_seed: i64
) -> MCMCChain with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var chain = mcmc_chain_new(n_params)
    var rng = rng_new(chain_seed)
    var theta = [0.0; 16]
    var lp = demo_log_posterior(theta, n_params)

    let total = opts.n_warmup + opts.n_samples
    var step = 0
    while step < total {
        // Propose: theta_new = theta + scale * N(0,1)
        var theta_new = [0.0; 16]
        var j = 0
        while j < n_params {
            if j < 16 {
                theta_new[j] = theta[j] + opts.proposal_scale * rng_normal(&!rng)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }

        let lp_new = demo_log_posterior(theta_new, n_params)
        let log_alpha = lp_new - lp
        let u = rng_next_f64(&!rng)

        // Accept/reject (compare log_alpha with log(u))
        // Approximate: accept if log_alpha > log(u) ~ u < exp(log_alpha)
        // Simple: if log_alpha >= 0, always accept; else accept with prob ~ 1 + log_alpha (rough)
        var accept = false
        if log_alpha >= 0.0 {
            accept = true
        } else {
            // Rough exp approximation for small negative values
            let p_accept = 1.0 + log_alpha
            if p_accept > 0.0 && u < p_accept {
                accept = true
            }
        }

        if accept {
            j = 0
            while j < n_params {
                if j < 16 { theta[j] = theta_new[j] }
                j = j + 1
            }
            lp = lp_new
            if step >= opts.n_warmup {
                chain.n_accepted = chain.n_accepted + 1
            }
        }

        // Record post-warmup
        if step >= opts.n_warmup {
            chain_add_sample(&!chain, theta, lp)
        }

        step = step + 1
    }

    chain
}

// ============================================================================
// Chain Diagnostics
// ============================================================================

struct ChainDiagnostics {
    r_hat: f64,
    ess: f64,
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
}

// Compute mean of parameter j in a chain
fn chain_mean(c: &MCMCChain, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < c.n_samples {
        sum = sum + chain_get_sample(c, i, j)
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (c.n_samples as f64)
}

// Compute variance of parameter j in a chain
fn chain_variance(c: &MCMCChain, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = chain_mean(c, j)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < c.n_samples {
        let d = chain_get_sample(c, i, j) - m
        sum = sum + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / ((c.n_samples - 1) as f64)
}

// R-hat diagnostic for two chains
fn compute_r_hat(c1: &MCMCChain, c2: &MCMCChain, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m1 = chain_mean(c1, j)
    let m2 = chain_mean(c2, j)
    let v1 = chain_variance(c1, j)
    let v2 = chain_variance(c2, j)

    let grand_mean = (m1 + m2) / 2.0
    let n_f = (c1.n_samples as f64)

    // Between-chain variance B
    let b = n_f * ((m1 - grand_mean) * (m1 - grand_mean) + (m2 - grand_mean) * (m2 - grand_mean))

    // Within-chain variance W
    let w = (v1 + v2) / 2.0

    // Variance estimate
    let var_hat = (1.0 - 1.0 / n_f) * w + b / n_f
    if w < 1.0e-15 { return 1.0 }
    mcmc_sqrt(var_hat / w)
}

// Effective sample size (simple autocorrelation-based estimate)
fn compute_ess(c: &MCMCChain, j: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = c.n_samples
    let v = chain_variance(c, j)
    if v < 1.0e-15 { return (n as f64) }

    let m = chain_mean(c, j)

    // Compute lag-1 autocorrelation
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        let d1 = chain_get_sample(c, i, j) - m
        let d2 = chain_get_sample(c, i + 1, j) - m
        sum = sum + d1 * d2
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rho1 = sum / ((n - 1) as f64) / v
    let rho_abs = mcmc_abs(rho1)

    // ESS ~ n / (1 + 2 * rho1)
    let denom = 1.0 + 2.0 * rho_abs
    if denom < 0.01 { return (n as f64) }
    (n as f64) / denom
}

// ============================================================================
// Posterior Summary
// ============================================================================

struct PosteriorSummary {
    mean: f64,
    std_dev: f64,
    ci_lower: f64,
    ci_upper: f64,
    r_hat: f64,
    ess: f64,
}

fn summarize_param(c: &MCMCChain, j: i64) -> PosteriorSummary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = chain_mean(c, j)
    let v = chain_variance(c, j)
    let sd = mcmc_sqrt(v)

    // 95% CI approximation: mean +/- 1.96 * sd
    let ci_lo = m - 1.96 * sd
    let ci_hi = m + 1.96 * sd

    let ess = compute_ess(c, j)

    PosteriorSummary {
        mean: m,
        std_dev: sd,
        ci_lower: ci_lo,
        ci_upper: ci_hi,
        r_hat: 1.0,
        ess: ess,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/merkle.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/merkle.sio
//
// Merkle Provenance: Cryptographic Audit Trails for Epistemic Computing
//
// Every computation leaves a hash. Every result can be verified.
// The provenance DAG is tamper-evident.
//
// Uses fixed-size arrays (no heap). Max 256 nodes, max 8 parents per node.

// ============================================================================
// HASH TYPE
// ============================================================================

// 256-bit hash (represented as 4 i64s for simplicity)
struct Hash256 {
    h0: i64,
    h1: i64,
    h2: i64,
    h3: i64,
}

fn hash256_zero() -> Hash256 {
    Hash256 { h0: 0, h1: 0, h2: 0, h3: 0 }
}

fn hash256_is_zero(h: Hash256) -> bool {
    h.h0 == 0 && h.h1 == 0 && h.h2 == 0 && h.h3 == 0
}

fn hash256_eq(a: Hash256, b: Hash256) -> bool {
    a.h0 == b.h0 && a.h1 == b.h1 && a.h2 == b.h2 && a.h3 == b.h3
}

// Simple hash combine via XOR with shifts
fn hash256_combine(a: Hash256, b: Hash256) -> Hash256 {
    Hash256 {
        h0: a.h0 ^ ((b.h1 * 31) + 17),
        h1: a.h1 ^ ((b.h2 * 37) + 19),
        h2: a.h2 ^ ((b.h3 * 41) + 23),
        h3: a.h3 ^ ((b.h0 * 43) + 29),
    }
}

// Hash from an f64 value (approximate bit-level hash)
fn hash256_from_f64(v: f64) -> Hash256 {
    // Use multiplication to spread bits
    let iv = (v * 1000000.0) as i64
    Hash256 {
        h0: iv ^ 6364136223846793005,
        h1: (iv * 31) ^ 1442695040888963407,
        h2: (iv * 37) ^ 3141592653589793238,
        h3: (iv * 41) ^ 2718281828459045235,
    }
}

// Hash from an integer tag (used for operation type hashing)
fn hash256_from_tag(tag: i64) -> Hash256 {
    Hash256 {
        h0: tag ^ 6364136223846793005,
        h1: (tag * 2654435761) ^ 1442695040888963407,
        h2: (tag * 40503) ^ 3141592653589793238,
        h3: (tag * 12345) ^ 2718281828459045235,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// OPERATION TYPES (as i64 constants)
// ============================================================================

fn OP_LEAF() -> i64 { 0 }
fn OP_TRANSFORM() -> i64 { 1 }
fn OP_AGGREGATE() -> i64 { 2 }
fn OP_IMPORT() -> i64 { 3 }

// ============================================================================
// MERKLE NODE (fixed-size, no heap)
// ============================================================================

// A node in the Merkle provenance DAG
// Max 8 parents per node
struct MerkleNode {
    hash: Hash256,
    content_hash: Hash256,
    operation: i64,
    op_tag: i64,
    parent_hashes: [Hash256; 8],
    parent_count: i64,
    valid: bool,
}

fn merkle_node_empty() -> MerkleNode {
    MerkleNode {
        hash: hash256_zero(),
        content_hash: hash256_zero(),
        operation: OP_LEAF(),
        op_tag: 0,
        parent_hashes: [hash256_zero(); 8],
        parent_count: 0,
        valid: false,
    }
}

// Create a leaf node from a data hash
fn merkle_leaf(content_hash: Hash256) -> MerkleNode {
    let leaf_tag = hash256_from_tag(OP_LEAF())
    let h = hash256_combine(content_hash, leaf_tag)
    MerkleNode {
        hash: h,
        content_hash: content_hash,
        operation: OP_LEAF(),
        op_tag: 0,
        parent_hashes: [hash256_zero(); 8],
        parent_count: 0,
        valid: true,
    }
}

// Create a transform node from parent hashes and result hash
// parents_arr: array of parent hashes, n_parents: how many are valid
fn merkle_transform(
    op_tag: i64,
    parents_arr: [Hash256; 8],
    n_parents: i64,
    content_hash: Hash256
) -> MerkleNode {
    var combined = hash256_from_tag(op_tag)
    var i = 0
    while i < n_parents {
        if i < 8 {
            combined = hash256_combine(combined, parents_arr[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    combined = hash256_combine(combined, content_hash)

    MerkleNode {
        hash: combined,
        content_hash: content_hash,
        operation: OP_TRANSFORM(),
        op_tag: op_tag,
        parent_hashes: parents_arr,
        parent_count: n_parents,
        valid: true,
    }
}

// Verify a node by recomputing its hash
fn merkle_node_verify(node: MerkleNode) -> bool {
    if !node.valid { return false }

    if node.operation == OP_LEAF() {
        let expected = hash256_combine(node.content_hash, hash256_from_tag(OP_LEAF()))
        return hash256_eq(node.hash, expected)
    }

    // Transform/Aggregate/Import: recompute from op_tag + parents + content
    var combined = hash256_from_tag(node.op_tag)
    var i = 0
    while i < node.parent_count {
        if i < 8 {
            combined = hash256_combine(combined, node.parent_hashes[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    combined = hash256_combine(combined, node.content_hash)
    hash256_eq(node.hash, combined)
}

// ============================================================================
// MERKLE DAG (fixed-size, max 256 nodes)
// ============================================================================

struct MerkleDAG {
    nodes: [MerkleNode; 256],
    count: i64,
}

fn merkle_dag_new() -> MerkleDAG {
    MerkleDAG {
        nodes: [merkle_node_empty(); 256],
        count: 0,
    }
}

// Add a leaf node for a single f64 value, return its hash
fn merkle_dag_add_leaf(dag: &!MerkleDAG, value: f64) -> Hash256 {
    if dag.count >= 256 { return hash256_zero() }
    let content_hash = hash256_from_f64(value)
    let node = merkle_leaf(content_hash)
    let h = node.hash
    dag.nodes[dag.count] = node
    dag.count = dag.count + 1
    h
}

// Add a transform node with one parent
fn merkle_dag_add_transform_1(
    dag: &!MerkleDAG,
    op_tag: i64,
    parent: Hash256,
    result_value: f64
) -> Hash256 {
    if dag.count >= 256 { return hash256_zero() }
    var parents = [hash256_zero(); 8]
    parents[0] = parent
    let content_hash = hash256_from_f64(result_value)
    let node = merkle_transform(op_tag, parents, 1, content_hash)
    let h = node.hash
    dag.nodes[dag.count] = node
    dag.count = dag.count + 1
    h
}

// Add a transform node with two parents
fn merkle_dag_add_transform_2(
    dag: &!MerkleDAG,
    op_tag: i64,
    parent1: Hash256,
    parent2: Hash256,
    result_value: f64
) -> Hash256 {
    if dag.count >= 256 { return hash256_zero() }
    var parents = [hash256_zero(); 8]
    parents[0] = parent1
    parents[1] = parent2
    let content_hash = hash256_from_f64(result_value)
    let node = merkle_transform(op_tag, parents, 2, content_hash)
    let h = node.hash
    dag.nodes[dag.count] = node
    dag.count = dag.count + 1
    h
}

// Find node index by hash, returns -1 if not found
fn merkle_dag_find(dag: &MerkleDAG, hash: Hash256) -> i64 {
    var i = 0
    while i < dag.count {
        if dag.nodes[i].valid && hash256_eq(dag.nodes[i].hash, hash) {
            return i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0 - 1
}

// Verify a single node by hash
fn merkle_dag_verify_node(dag: &MerkleDAG, hash: Hash256) -> bool {
    let idx = merkle_dag_find(dag, hash)
    if idx < 0 { return false }
    merkle_node_verify(dag.nodes[idx])
}

// Verify entire chain from a node back to leaves (iterative with stack)
fn merkle_dag_verify_chain(dag: &MerkleDAG, hash: Hash256) -> bool {
    // Use a fixed stack for traversal
    var stack: [Hash256; 64] = [hash256_zero(); 64]
    stack[0] = hash
    var sp = 1

    while sp > 0 {
        sp = sp - 1
        let current = stack[sp]

        let idx = merkle_dag_find(dag, current)
        if idx < 0 { return false }

        let node = dag.nodes[idx]
        if !merkle_node_verify(node) { return false }

        // Push parents onto stack
        var j = 0
        while j < node.parent_count {
            if j < 8 && sp < 64 {
                stack[sp] = node.parent_hashes[j]
                sp = sp + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }
    true
}

// Get the count of nodes in the DAG
fn merkle_dag_len(dag: &MerkleDAG) -> i64 {
    dag.count
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/meta.sio ===
//! stdlib/epistemic/meta.d
//!
//! Meta-Analysis: Combining Knowledge Across Studies
//!
//! When you have multiple Knowledge values from different sources
//! (experiments, measurements, studies), this module combines them
//! using principled statistical methods.
//!
//! # Methods Implemented
//!
//! - Fixed-effects pooling (inverse-variance weighted)
//! - Random-effects pooling (DerSimonian-Laird)
//! - Heterogeneity statistics (Q, I², τ²)
//! - Bayesian hierarchical combination
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! ```sounio
//! use epistemic::{Knowledge, meta}
//!
//! // Results from 3 clinical trials
//! let trial1 = Knowledge::measured(0.35, 0.04, "RCT_2021")
//! let trial2 = Knowledge::measured(0.42, 0.06, "RCT_2022")
//! let trial3 = Knowledge::measured(0.38, 0.03, "RCT_2023")
//!
//! let pooled = meta::random_effects([trial1, trial2, trial3])
//! println("Pooled effect: {} ± {}", pooled.value, pooled.std())
//! println("Heterogeneity I²: {}%", pooled.heterogeneity.i_squared * 100)
//! ```

use epistemic::knowledge::{Epistemic, Beta, BetaConfidence, Provenance};

// ============================================================================
// HETEROGENEITY STATISTICS
// ============================================================================

// Heterogeneity metrics from meta-analysis
pub struct Heterogeneity {
    /// Cochran's Q statistic (chi-squared test for heterogeneity)
    q: f64,

    /// Degrees of freedom (k - 1 where k = number of studies)
    df: i64,

    /// I² statistic: percentage of variability due to heterogeneity
    /// 0% = no heterogeneity, 25% = low, 50% = moderate, 75% = high
    i_squared: f64,

    /// τ² (tau-squared): between-study variance
    tau_squared: f64,

    /// p-value for Q statistic
    p_value: f64,
}

impl Heterogeneity {
    /// Create from Q statistic and degrees of freedom
    pub fn from_q(q: f64, df: i64) -> Heterogeneity {
        let tau_sq = if q > df as f64 {
            (q - df as f64) / compute_c(df)  // Simplified
        } else {
            0.0
        }

        let i_sq = if q > 0.0 {
            max_f64((q - df as f64) / q, 0.0)
        } else {
            0.0
        }

        Heterogeneity {
            q: q,
            df: df,
            i_squared: i_sq,
            tau_squared: tau_sq,
            p_value: chi_squared_pvalue(q, df),
        }
    }

    /// Is there significant heterogeneity?
    pub fn is_significant(self: &Heterogeneity, alpha: f64) -> bool {
        self.p_value < alpha
    }

    /// Qualitative interpretation of I²
    pub fn interpretation(self: &Heterogeneity) -> string {
        if self.i_squared < 0.25 {
            "low heterogeneity"
        } else if self.i_squared < 0.50 {
            "moderate heterogeneity"
        } else if self.i_squared < 0.75 {
            "substantial heterogeneity"
        } else {
            "considerable heterogeneity"
        }
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// META-ANALYSIS RESULT
// ============================================================================

// Result of meta-analysis combining multiple Knowledge values
pub struct MetaResult {
    /// Pooled effect estimate
    pooled: Epistemic,

    /// Heterogeneity statistics
    heterogeneity: Heterogeneity,

    /// Number of studies combined
    k: i64,

    /// Method used
    method: string,

    /// Individual study weights
    weights: Vec<f64>,
}

impl MetaResult {
    /// Get the pooled Knowledge value
    pub fn get(self: &MetaResult) -> &Epistemic {
        &self.pooled
    }

    /// Get heterogeneity
    pub fn het(self: &MetaResult) -> &Heterogeneity {
        &self.heterogeneity
    }

    /// Should we use random effects instead of fixed?
    /// Returns true if significant heterogeneity detected
    pub fn needs_random_effects(self: &MetaResult) -> bool {
        self.heterogeneity.is_significant(0.10) || self.heterogeneity.i_squared > 0.50
    }

    /// Forest plot data (study index, effect, weight)
    pub fn forest_data(self: &MetaResult) -> Vec<(i64, f64, f64)> {
        // Would need original values stored
        vec![]
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FIXED-EFFECTS META-ANALYSIS
// ============================================================================

// Fixed-effects meta-analysis using inverse-variance weighting
//
// Assumes all studies estimate the same underlying effect.
// Appropriate when heterogeneity is low (I² < 25%).
//
// Formula:
// θ̂ = Σ(wᵢθᵢ) / Σwᵢ  where wᵢ = 1/Var(θᵢ)
// Var(θ̂) = 1/Σwᵢ
pub fn fixed_effects(studies: &[Epistemic]) -> MetaResult {
    let k = studies.len() as i64

    if k == 0 {
        return MetaResult {
            pooled: Epistemic { value: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 1000.0, beta: 1.0 } }, provenance: Provenance { source: "constant", steps: Vec::new() } },
            heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(0.0, 0),
            k: 0,
            method: "fixed_effects",
            weights: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    if k == 1 {
        return MetaResult {
            pooled: studies[0].clone(),
            heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(0.0, 0),
            k: 1,
            method: "fixed_effects",
            weights: vec![1.0],
        }
    }

    // Compute weights (inverse variance)
    var weights = vec![]
    var sum_weights = 0.0
    for study in studies {
        let w = 1.0 / max_f64(study.variance, 0.0000001)
        weights.push(w)
        sum_weights = sum_weights + w
    }

    // Compute weighted mean
    var weighted_sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < k {
        weighted_sum = weighted_sum + weights[i] * studies[i].value
        i = i + 1
    }
    let pooled_mean = weighted_sum / sum_weights

    // Pooled variance
    let pooled_variance = 1.0 / sum_weights

    // Cochran's Q statistic
    var q = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < k {
        let diff = studies[i].value - pooled_mean
        q = q + weights[i] * diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Combine confidence from all studies
    var combined_conf = BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 } }
    for study in studies {
        combined_conf = combined_conf.combine(&study.confidence)
    }

    let pooled = Epistemic {
        value: pooled_mean,
        variance: pooled_variance,
        confidence: combined_conf,
        provenance: Provenance {
            source: "fixed_effects_meta",
            steps: Vec::new(),
        },
    }

    MetaResult {
        pooled: pooled,
        heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(q, k - 1),
        k: k,
        method: "fixed_effects",
        weights: weights,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// RANDOM-EFFECTS META-ANALYSIS
// ============================================================================

// Random-effects meta-analysis using DerSimonian-Laird method
//
// Assumes studies estimate different but related effects.
// Appropriate when heterogeneity exists (I² > 25%).
//
// Adds between-study variance τ² to weights:
// w*ᵢ = 1/(Var(θᵢ) + τ²)
pub fn random_effects(studies: &[Epistemic]) -> MetaResult {
    let k = studies.len() as i64

    if k == 0 {
        return MetaResult {
            pooled: Epistemic { value: 0.0, variance: 0.0, confidence: BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 1000.0, beta: 1.0 } }, provenance: Provenance { source: "constant", steps: Vec::new() } },
            heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(0.0, 0),
            k: 0,
            method: "random_effects",
            weights: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    if k == 1 {
        return MetaResult {
            pooled: studies[0].clone(),
            heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(0.0, 0),
            k: 1,
            method: "random_effects",
            weights: vec![1.0],
        }
    }

    // First, compute fixed-effects to get Q
    let fe = fixed_effects(studies)
    let q = fe.heterogeneity.q
    let df = fe.heterogeneity.df

    // Estimate τ² (DerSimonian-Laird)
    let c = compute_c_from_weights(&fe.weights)
    let tau_sq = if q > df as f64 {
        (q - df as f64) / c
    } else {
        0.0
    }

    // Compute random-effects weights
    var weights = vec![]
    var sum_weights = 0.0
    for study in studies {
        let w = 1.0 / max_f64(study.variance + tau_sq, 0.0000001)
        weights.push(w)
        sum_weights = sum_weights + w
    }

    // Compute weighted mean with new weights
    var weighted_sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < k {
        weighted_sum = weighted_sum + weights[i] * studies[i].value
        i = i + 1
    }
    let pooled_mean = weighted_sum / sum_weights

    // Pooled variance includes between-study variance
    let pooled_variance = 1.0 / sum_weights

    // Recalculate Q with random-effects estimate (for diagnostics)
    var q_re = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < k {
        let diff = studies[i].value - pooled_mean
        q_re = q_re + weights[i] * diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Combine confidence
    var combined_conf = BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 } }
    for study in studies {
        combined_conf = combined_conf.combine(&study.confidence)
    }

    let pooled = Epistemic {
        value: pooled_mean,
        variance: pooled_variance,
        confidence: combined_conf,
        provenance: Provenance {
            source: "random_effects_meta",
            steps: Vec::new(),
        },
    }

    var het = Heterogeneity::from_q(q, df)
    het.tau_squared = tau_sq

    MetaResult {
        pooled: pooled,
        heterogeneity: het,
        k: k,
        method: "random_effects",
        weights: weights,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// BAYESIAN HIERARCHICAL META-ANALYSIS
// ============================================================================

// Bayesian hierarchical pooling with informative prior
//
// Uses precision-weighted combination with prior beliefs:
// - Prior on pooled effect (can be informative or non-informative)
// - Partial pooling: studies contribute based on their precision
//
// This is especially useful when:
// - You have domain knowledge about plausible effect sizes
// - Small studies shouldn't dominate
// - You want to properly quantify uncertainty
pub fn bayesian_pool(
    studies: &[Epistemic],
    prior_mean: f64,
    prior_variance: f64,
) -> MetaResult {
    let k = studies.len() as i64

    if k == 0 {
        // Return prior as posterior
        return MetaResult {
            pooled: Epistemic {
                value: prior_mean,
                variance: prior_variance,
                confidence: BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 } },
                provenance: Provenance {
                    source: "prior",
                    steps: Vec::new(),
                },
            },
            heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(0.0, 0),
            k: 0,
            method: "bayesian_hierarchical",
            weights: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    // Prior precision
    let prior_precision = 1.0 / max_f64(prior_variance, 0.0000001)

    // Likelihood precisions
    var total_precision = prior_precision
    var weighted_sum = prior_precision * prior_mean
    var weights = vec![]

    for study in studies {
        let precision = 1.0 / max_f64(study.variance, 0.0000001)
        weights.push(precision)
        total_precision = total_precision + precision
        weighted_sum = weighted_sum + precision * study.value
    }

    // Posterior mean and variance
    let posterior_mean = weighted_sum / total_precision
    let posterior_variance = 1.0 / total_precision

    // Compute Q for heterogeneity assessment
    var q = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < k {
        let diff = studies[i].value - posterior_mean
        q = q + weights[i] * diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Build posterior confidence from evidence
    // More evidence (higher total precision) → higher confidence
    let evidence_strength = total_precision / prior_precision
    let conf_n = min_f64(evidence_strength, 100.0)
    let conf = BetaConfidence { dist: Beta { alpha: 0.8 * conf_n + 1.0, beta: 0.2 * conf_n + 1.0 } }

    let pooled = Epistemic {
        value: posterior_mean,
        variance: posterior_variance,
        confidence: conf,
        provenance: Provenance {
            source: "bayesian_meta",
            steps: Vec::new(),
        },
    }

    MetaResult {
        pooled: pooled,
        heterogeneity: Heterogeneity::from_q(q, k - 1),
        k: k,
        method: "bayesian_hierarchical",
        weights: weights,
    }
}

// Bayesian pooling with non-informative prior
pub fn bayesian_pool_flat(studies: &[Epistemic]) -> MetaResult {
    // Use very wide prior (non-informative)
    bayesian_pool(studies, 0.0, 1000000.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// CONVENIENCE FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Automatically choose fixed or random effects based on heterogeneity
pub fn auto_pool(studies: &[Epistemic]) -> MetaResult {
    let fe = fixed_effects(studies)

    if fe.needs_random_effects() {
        random_effects(studies)
    } else {
        fe
    }
}

// Pool with sensitivity analysis (returns both FE and RE)
pub struct SensitivityResult {
    fixed: MetaResult,
    random: MetaResult,
    recommendation: string,
}

pub fn sensitivity_analysis(studies: &[Epistemic]) -> SensitivityResult {
    let fe = fixed_effects(studies)
    let re = random_effects(studies)

    let recommendation = if fe.needs_random_effects() {
        "Use random-effects due to significant heterogeneity"
    } else {
        "Fixed-effects appropriate, low heterogeneity"
    }

    SensitivityResult {
        fixed: fe,
        random: re,
        recommendation: recommendation,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Compute C for DerSimonian-Laird estimator
fn compute_c(df: i64) -> f64 {
    // Simplified: C ≈ df for equal-variance case
    df as f64
}

fn compute_c_from_weights(weights: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    var sum_w = 0.0
    var sum_w2 = 0.0
    for w in weights {
        sum_w = sum_w + w
        sum_w2 = sum_w2 + w * w
    }
    sum_w - sum_w2 / sum_w
}

// Chi-squared p-value approximation
fn chi_squared_pvalue(x: f64, df: i64) -> f64 {
    if df <= 0 { return 1.0 }
    if x <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }

    // Wilson-Hilferty approximation
    let k = df as f64
    let cube_root = pow_f64(x / k, 1.0 / 3.0)
    let z = (cube_root - (1.0 - 2.0 / (9.0 * k)))
          / sqrt_f64(2.0 / (9.0 * k))

    // Standard normal CDF approximation
    0.5 * (1.0 - erf_approx(z / 1.4142135623730951))
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y
}

fn pow_f64(base: f64, exp: f64) -> f64 {
    exp_f64(exp * ln_f64(base))
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 10.0 { return 22026.0 * exp_f64(x - 10.0) }
    if x < -10.0 { return 0.000045 * exp_f64(x + 10.0) }

    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 15 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        result = result + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result = 0.0
    var term = y
    var i = 1
    while i < 30 {
        result = result + term / (i as f64)
        term = term * y * y
        i = i + 2
    }
    2.0 * result
}

fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = 0.0 - 0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = 0.0 - 1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911

    let sign = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x_abs = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }

    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * x_abs)
    let y = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t + a4) * t) + a3) * t + a2) * t + a1) * t * exp_f64(0.0 - x_abs * x_abs)

    sign * y
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}
