    return var_xy / pce.variance
}

// =============================================================================
// ADDITIONAL UTILITIES
// =============================================================================

// Compute coefficient of variation (CV = std / mean)
pub fn coefficient_of_variation(pce: PCE) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if abs_f64(pce.mean) < 1e-14 { return 0.0 }
    return std(pce) / abs_f64(pce.mean)
}

// Get percentile bounds (approximate via normal assumption)
pub fn percentile_bounds(pce: PCE, coverage: f64) -> (f64, f64) with Panic {
    // coverage = 0.95 -> 95% interval -> z ≈ 1.96
    // coverage = 0.99 -> 99% interval -> z ≈ 2.576
    let z = if coverage > 0.98 {
        2.576  // 99%
    } else if coverage > 0.94 {
        1.960  // 95%
    } else {
        1.645  // 90%
    }

    let pce_std = std(pce)
    let lower = pce.mean - z * pce_std
    let upper = pce.mean + z * pce_std
    return (lower, upper)
}

// Check if PCE is effectively linear (higher-order terms negligible)
pub fn is_linear(pce: PCE) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    if pce.variance < 1e-14 { return true }

    // Fraction of variance in first-order term
    let first_order_frac = (pce.c1 * pce.c1) / pce.variance

    // If > 95% variance is first-order, consider it linear
    return first_order_frac > 0.95
}

// =============================================================================
// ADDITIONAL TESTS
// =============================================================================

// Test 6: Bivariate sum
pub fn test_bivariate_sum() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let input1 = input_normal(3.0, 1.0)
    let input2 = input_normal(5.0, 2.0)
    let pce = build_bivariate_sum(input1, input2, 2)

    // E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] = 3 + 5 = 8
    let mean_ok = abs_f64(pce.mean - 8.0) < 0.01

    // Var[X + Y] = Var[X] + Var[Y] = 1 + 4 = 5 (independent)
    let var_ok = abs_f64(pce.variance - 5.0) < 0.01

    return mean_ok && var_ok
}

// Test 7: Bivariate product
pub fn test_bivariate_product() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let input1 = input_normal(2.0, 0.5)
    let input2 = input_normal(3.0, 0.5)
    let pce = build_bivariate_product(input1, input2, 2)

    // E[XY] = E[X]E[Y] = 2 * 3 = 6 (independent)
    let mean_ok = abs_f64(pce.mean - 6.0) < 0.1

    return mean_ok
}

// Test 8: Method comparison
pub fn test_comparison() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let input = input_normal(1.0, 0.3)
    let result = compare_exp(input, 4, 50)

    // PCE should be more accurate than GUM for nonlinear functions
    let pce_better = result.pce_vs_mc_error < result.gum_vs_mc_error

    return pce_better
}

// Test 9: Linearity detection
pub fn test_linearity() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let input = input_normal(5.0, 1.0)
    let pce_linear = build_identity(input, 2)
    let pce_nonlinear = build_square(input, 4)

    let linear_ok = is_linear(pce_linear)
    let nonlinear_ok = is_linear(pce_nonlinear) == false

    return linear_ok && nonlinear_ok
}

// Run extended test suite
pub fn run_all_tests() -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var passed = 0

    // Original tests
    if test_orthogonality() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_identity() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_square() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_exp_comparison() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_sobol() { passed = passed + 1 }

    // Extended tests
    if test_bivariate_sum() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_bivariate_product() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_comparison() { passed = passed + 1 }
    if test_linearity() { passed = passed + 1 }

    return passed  // Returns number of tests passed (out of 9)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/pde.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/pde.sio
//
// Epistemic PDE Solvers — Sounio
//
// Finite difference methods with uncertainty propagation.
// 1D heat equation and wave equation solvers.
// Max grid: 256 points, max time steps: 1024.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn pde_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn pde_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// 1D Grid
// ============================================================================

struct Grid1D {
    x: [f64; 256],
    n: i64,
    dx: f64,
    x_min: f64,
    x_max: f64,
}

fn grid_1d(x_min: f64, x_max: f64, n: i64) -> Grid1D with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g = Grid1D {
        x: [0.0; 256],
        n: n,
        dx: (x_max - x_min) / ((n - 1) as f64),
        x_min: x_min,
        x_max: x_max,
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 256 {
            g.x[i] = x_min + (i as f64) * g.dx
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    g
}

// ============================================================================
// PDE State: value + variance at each grid point
// ============================================================================

struct PDEState {
    values: [f64; 256],
    variances: [f64; 256],
    n: i64,
}

fn pde_state_new(n: i64) -> PDEState {
    PDEState {
        values: [0.0; 256],
        variances: [0.0; 256],
        n: n,
    }
}

fn pde_state_set(s: &!PDEState, idx: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 256 {
        s.values[idx] = val
        s.variances[idx] = var_
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PDE Solution: solution at multiple time steps
// ============================================================================

struct PDESolution {
    // states[step * 256 + i] = value at grid point i at time step
    values: [f64; 4096],
    variances: [f64; 4096],
    times: [f64; 256],
    n_spatial: i64,
    n_time: i64,
    total_error: f64,
}

fn pde_solution_new(n_spatial: i64) -> PDESolution {
    PDESolution {
        values: [0.0; 4096],
        variances: [0.0; 4096],
        times: [0.0; 256],
        n_spatial: n_spatial,
        n_time: 0,
        total_error: 0.0,
    }
}

fn pde_solution_record(sol: &!PDESolution, t: f64, state: &PDEState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sol.n_time >= 256 { return }
    let step = sol.n_time
    sol.times[step] = t
    var i = 0
    while i < sol.n_spatial {
        if i < 256 {
            let idx = step * 256 + i
            if idx < 4096 {
                sol.values[idx] = state.values[i]
                sol.variances[idx] = state.variances[i]
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sol.n_time = sol.n_time + 1
}

fn pde_solution_get_value(sol: &PDESolution, step: i64, i: i64) -> f64 {
    let idx = step * 256 + i
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 4096 { sol.values[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

fn pde_solution_get_variance(sol: &PDESolution, step: i64, i: i64) -> f64 {
    let idx = step * 256 + i
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 4096 { sol.variances[idx] } else { 0.0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// 1D Heat Equation: u_t = alpha * u_xx
// Forward Euler finite difference with uncertainty propagation
// ============================================================================

fn solve_heat_1d_euler(
    grid: &Grid1D,
    alpha_val: f64,
    alpha_var: f64,
    initial: &PDEState,
    t_end: f64,
    dt: f64
) -> PDESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = grid.n
    let dx = grid.dx
    let r = alpha_val * dt / (dx * dx)

    var state = pde_state_new(n)
    // Copy initial condition
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i < 256 {
            state.values[i] = initial.values[i]
            state.variances[i] = initial.variances[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var sol = pde_solution_new(n)
    pde_solution_record(&!sol, 0.0, &state)

    var t = 0.0
    while t < t_end {
        var new_state = pde_state_new(n)

        // Boundary conditions (Dirichlet: keep endpoints fixed)
        if n > 0 {
            new_state.values[0] = state.values[0]
            new_state.variances[0] = state.variances[0]
        }
        if n > 1 {
            new_state.values[n - 1] = state.values[n - 1]
            new_state.variances[n - 1] = state.variances[n - 1]
        }

        // Interior points: u_new[i] = u[i] + r * (u[i+1] - 2*u[i] + u[i-1])
        i = 1
        while i < n - 1 {
            if i < 255 {
                let u_left = state.values[i - 1]
                let u_mid = state.values[i]
                let u_right = state.values[i + 1]
                let laplacian = u_right - 2.0 * u_mid + u_left

                new_state.values[i] = u_mid + r * laplacian

                // Variance propagation
                // Var(u_new) = Var(u_mid) * (1-2r)^2 + Var(u_left) * r^2 + Var(u_right) * r^2
                //            + laplacian^2 * (dt/(dx*dx))^2 * alpha_var
                let coeff_mid = 1.0 - 2.0 * r
                new_state.variances[i] = coeff_mid * coeff_mid * state.variances[i]
                    + r * r * state.variances[i - 1]
                    + r * r * state.variances[i + 1]
                    + laplacian * laplacian * dt * dt / (dx * dx * dx * dx) * alpha_var
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Update state
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            if i < 256 {
                state.values[i] = new_state.values[i]
                state.variances[i] = new_state.variances[i]
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        t = t + dt
        pde_solution_record(&!sol, t, &state)
    }

    sol
}

// ============================================================================
// Crank-Nicolson scheme for 1D heat equation (implicit, more stable)
// Simplified: uses explicit for now with smaller effective dt
// ============================================================================

fn solve_heat_1d_cn(
    grid: &Grid1D,
    alpha_val: f64,
    alpha_var: f64,
    initial: &PDEState,
    t_end: f64,
    dt: f64
) -> PDESolution with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Crank-Nicolson: average of forward and backward Euler
    // For simplicity, use forward Euler with dt/2 safety factor
    solve_heat_1d_euler(grid, alpha_val, alpha_var, initial, t_end, dt * 0.5)
}

// ============================================================================
// Error estimation for PDE solutions
// ============================================================================

struct PDEError {
    max_variance: f64,
    mean_variance: f64,
    stability_ratio: f64,
}

fn pde_error_estimate(sol: &PDESolution) -> PDEError with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sol.n_time < 1 { return PDEError { max_variance: 0.0, mean_variance: 0.0, stability_ratio: 0.0 } }

    let last_step = sol.n_time - 1
    var max_var = 0.0
    var sum_var = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < sol.n_spatial {
        let v = pde_solution_get_variance(sol, last_step, i)
        if v > max_var { max_var = v }
        sum_var = sum_var + v
        i = i + 1
    }

    let mean_var = if sol.n_spatial > 0 { sum_var / (sol.n_spatial as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    // Stability ratio: compare final variance to initial variance
    var init_var = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < sol.n_spatial {
        init_var = init_var + pde_solution_get_variance(sol, 0, i)
        i = i + 1
    }
    let init_mean = if sol.n_spatial > 0 { init_var / (sol.n_spatial as f64) } else { 1.0 }
    let ratio = if init_mean > 1.0e-15 { mean_var / init_mean } else { 0.0 }

    PDEError {
        max_variance: max_var,
        mean_variance: mean_var,
        stability_ratio: ratio,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/pk_plugin.sio ===
//! PK Domain Uncertainty Plugin — Pharmacokinetic-Specific Sensitivity Analysis
//!
//! Detects clearance dominance (sensitivity index S_Ti > 0.7) and provides
//! PK-specific uncertainty recommendations for clinical pharmacology.
//!
//! PK Parameter codes:
//!   0 = CL  (clearance)
//!   1 = V   (volume of distribution)
//!   2 = ka  (absorption rate constant)
//!   3 = ke  (elimination rate constant)
//!   4 = F   (bioavailability)
//!   5 = Dose
//!   6 = Weight
//!   7 = SCr (serum creatinine)
//!
//! PK Recommendation codes:
//!   10 = Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)
//!   11 = Body composition assessment
//!   12 = Bioequivalence study
//!   13 = Cystatin C measurement (alternative to SCr)
//!   14 = Population PK analysis
//!   15 = Dose individualization
//!    0 = No recommendation
//!
//! Source type codes:
//!   0 = measured, 1 = population, 2 = estimated, 3 = fixed
//!
//! References:
//!   - GUM (JCGM 100:2008) Section 5: Combined Uncertainty
//!   - Saltelli et al. (2008): Global Sensitivity Analysis
//!   - Ette & Williams (2004): Pharmacometrics — Science of Quantitative Pharmacology
//!   - FDA Guidance: Population PK (2022)

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS (must precede all callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x / 2.0
    if guess < 0.001 { guess = 0.001 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return guess
}

fn max_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// PK PARAMETER STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct PKParameter {
    code: i32,           // parameter code (0=CL, 1=V, 2=ka, etc.)
    value: f64,
    std_uncert: f64,
    sensitivity: f64,    // sensitivity coefficient |dy/dxi|
    contribution: f64,   // contribution to variance (%)
    source_type: i32     // 0=measured, 1=population, 2=estimated, 3=fixed
}

fn empty_pk_param() -> PKParameter {
    return PKParameter {
        code: 0,
        value: 0.0,
        std_uncert: 0.0,
        sensitivity: 0.0,
        contribution: 0.0,
        source_type: 0
    }
}

fn make_pk_param(code: i32, value: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64, source_type: i32) -> PKParameter {
    // contribution = (c_i * u_i)^2 as raw variance contribution
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    return PKParameter {
        code: code,
        value: value,
        std_uncert: std_uncert,
        sensitivity: sensitivity,
        contribution: contrib,
        source_type: source_type
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK UNCERTAINTY PROFILE
// ============================================================================

struct PKUncertaintyProfile {
    n_params: i32,
    p0: PKParameter,
    p1: PKParameter,
    p2: PKParameter,
    p3: PKParameter,
    p4: PKParameter,
    p5: PKParameter,
    p6: PKParameter,
    p7: PKParameter,
    combined_variance: f64,
    combined_std_uncert: f64,
    clearance_contribution: f64,    // % contribution from CL-related params
    volume_contribution: f64,       // % contribution from V-related params
    absorption_contribution: f64,   // % contribution from absorption params
    is_clearance_dominant: bool,    // true if CL-related > 70%
    dominant_param_idx: i32,
    dominant_param_contribution: f64,
    r0: i32,
    r1: i32,
    r2: i32,
    r3: i32,
    n_recommendations: i32
}

fn empty_pk_profile() -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    return PKUncertaintyProfile {
        n_params: 0,
        p0: empty_pk_param(),
        p1: empty_pk_param(),
        p2: empty_pk_param(),
        p3: empty_pk_param(),
        p4: empty_pk_param(),
        p5: empty_pk_param(),
        p6: empty_pk_param(),
        p7: empty_pk_param(),
        combined_variance: 0.0,
        combined_std_uncert: 0.0,
        clearance_contribution: 0.0,
        volume_contribution: 0.0,
        absorption_contribution: 0.0,
        is_clearance_dominant: false,
        dominant_param_idx: 0,
        dominant_param_contribution: 0.0,
        r0: 0,
        r1: 0,
        r2: 0,
        r3: 0,
        n_recommendations: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK SENSITIVITY RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct PKSensitivityResult {
    s_ti_0: f64,
    s_ti_1: f64,
    s_ti_2: f64,
    s_ti_3: f64,
    s_ti_4: f64,
    s_ti_5: f64,
    s_ti_6: f64,
    s_ti_7: f64,
    s_i_0: f64,
    s_i_1: f64,
    s_i_2: f64,
    s_i_3: f64,
    s_i_4: f64,
    s_i_5: f64,
    s_i_6: f64,
    s_i_7: f64,
    n_params: i32,
    dominant_idx: i32,       // index with highest S_Ti
    dominant_s_ti: f64,      // S_Ti of dominant parameter
    clearance_dominant: bool // S_Ti(CL-related) > 0.7
}

fn empty_pk_sensitivity() -> PKSensitivityResult {
    return PKSensitivityResult {
        s_ti_0: 0.0, s_ti_1: 0.0, s_ti_2: 0.0, s_ti_3: 0.0,
        s_ti_4: 0.0, s_ti_5: 0.0, s_ti_6: 0.0, s_ti_7: 0.0,
        s_i_0: 0.0, s_i_1: 0.0, s_i_2: 0.0, s_i_3: 0.0,
        s_i_4: 0.0, s_i_5: 0.0, s_i_6: 0.0, s_i_7: 0.0,
        n_params: 0,
        dominant_idx: 0,
        dominant_s_ti: 0.0,
        clearance_dominant: false
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK PARAMETER CLASSIFICATION FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Returns a name code for display (identity mapping for now)
fn pk_param_name(code: i32) -> i32 {
    // 0=CL, 1=V, 2=ka, 3=ke, 4=F, 5=Dose, 6=Weight, 7=SCr
    return code
}

// Clearance-related: CL(0), ke(3), SCr(7), Weight(6)
// Rationale: CrCl = (140-Age)*Weight/(72*SCr), CL ~ CrCl for renally cleared drugs
// ke = CL/V, so ke is clearance-related
fn pk_param_is_clearance_related(code: i32) -> bool {
    if code == 0 { return true }
    if code == 3 { return true }
    if code == 7 { return true }
    if code == 6 { return true }
    return false
}

// Volume-related: V(1), Weight(6)
// Rationale: Vd scales with body weight
fn pk_param_is_volume_related(code: i32) -> bool {
    if code == 1 { return true }
    if code == 6 { return true }
    return false
}

// Absorption-related: ka(2), F(4)
// Rationale: absorption rate and bioavailability govern drug input
fn pk_param_is_absorption_related(code: i32) -> bool {
    if code == 2 { return true }
    if code == 4 { return true }
    return false
}

// ============================================================================
// PARAMETER ACCESS HELPER
// ============================================================================

fn get_pk_param(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, idx: i32) -> PKParameter {
    if idx == 0 { return profile.p0 }
    if idx == 1 { return profile.p1 }
    if idx == 2 { return profile.p2 }
    if idx == 3 { return profile.p3 }
    if idx == 4 { return profile.p4 }
    if idx == 5 { return profile.p5 }
    if idx == 6 { return profile.p6 }
    if idx == 7 { return profile.p7 }
    return empty_pk_param()
}

fn set_pk_param(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, idx: i32, param: PKParameter) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = profile
    if idx == 0 { result.p0 = param }
    else if idx == 1 { result.p1 = param }
    else if idx == 2 { result.p2 = param }
    else if idx == 3 { result.p3 = param }
    else if idx == 4 { result.p4 = param }
    else if idx == 5 { result.p5 = param }
    else if idx == 6 { result.p6 = param }
    else if idx == 7 { result.p7 = param }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// CONTRIBUTION COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================

// Compute variance contributions and classify dominance.
// Each parameter's contribution is (c_i * u_i)^2 / total_variance * 100%.
// CL-related params are summed; if that sum > 70%, clearance is dominant.
fn compute_pk_contributions(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, n: i32) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = profile
    result.n_params = n

    // Step 1: Compute total variance
    var total_var: f64 = 0.0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        total_var = total_var + p.contribution
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    result.combined_variance = total_var
    result.combined_std_uncert = sqrt_val(total_var)

    // Step 2: If total variance is zero, nothing to classify
    if total_var < 1.0e-15 {
        return result
    }

    // Step 3: Compute percentage contributions and classify by PK domain
    var cl_contrib: f64 = 0.0
    var v_contrib: f64 = 0.0
    var abs_contrib: f64 = 0.0
    var best_idx = 0
    var best_pct: f64 = 0.0

    idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        let pct = 100.0 * p.contribution / total_var

        // Update parameter with its percentage contribution
        var updated_p = p
        updated_p.contribution = p.contribution
        result = set_pk_param(result, idx, updated_p)

        // Track dominant parameter
        if pct > best_pct {
            best_pct = pct
            best_idx = idx
        }

        // Accumulate by PK domain
        if pk_param_is_clearance_related(p.code) {
            cl_contrib = cl_contrib + pct
        }
        if pk_param_is_volume_related(p.code) {
            v_contrib = v_contrib + pct
        }
        if pk_param_is_absorption_related(p.code) {
            abs_contrib = abs_contrib + pct
        }

        idx = idx + 1
    }

    result.clearance_contribution = cl_contrib
    result.volume_contribution = v_contrib
    result.absorption_contribution = abs_contrib
    result.dominant_param_idx = best_idx
    result.dominant_param_contribution = best_pct

    // Clearance dominance flag: CL-related > 70%
    if cl_contrib > 70.0 {
        result.is_clearance_dominant = true
    } else {
        result.is_clearance_dominant = false
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// CLEARANCE DOMINANCE DETECTION
// ============================================================================

// Returns true if CL-related parameters contribute > 70% of total variance.
fn detect_clearance_dominance(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile) -> bool {
    return profile.is_clearance_dominant
}

// ============================================================================
// SOBOL-LIKE SENSITIVITY INDICES
// ============================================================================

// Compute Sobol-like total sensitivity indices from variance contributions.
// S_Ti = V_i / V_total (total-order index, approximation from linear model).
// For linear models, S_Ti = S_i (no interactions), so interaction = 0.
// This is a first approximation; true Sobol requires Monte Carlo sampling.
fn compute_pk_sensitivity(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, n: i32) -> PKSensitivityResult {
    var result = empty_pk_sensitivity()
    result.n_params = n

    // Total variance
    var total_var: f64 = 0.0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        total_var = total_var + p.contribution
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    if total_var < 1.0e-15 {
        return result
    }

    // Compute S_Ti for each parameter
    var best_idx = 0
    var best_s_ti: f64 = 0.0

    idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        let s_ti = p.contribution / total_var
        // First-order index equals total-order for linear models
        let s_i = s_ti

        // Store indices (unrolled for each slot)
        if idx == 0 { result.s_ti_0 = s_ti; result.s_i_0 = s_i }
        else if idx == 1 { result.s_ti_1 = s_ti; result.s_i_1 = s_i }
        else if idx == 2 { result.s_ti_2 = s_ti; result.s_i_2 = s_i }
        else if idx == 3 { result.s_ti_3 = s_ti; result.s_i_3 = s_i }
        else if idx == 4 { result.s_ti_4 = s_ti; result.s_i_4 = s_i }
        else if idx == 5 { result.s_ti_5 = s_ti; result.s_i_5 = s_i }
        else if idx == 6 { result.s_ti_6 = s_ti; result.s_i_6 = s_i }
        else if idx == 7 { result.s_ti_7 = s_ti; result.s_i_7 = s_i }

        if s_ti > best_s_ti {
            best_s_ti = s_ti
            best_idx = idx
        }

        idx = idx + 1
    }

    result.dominant_idx = best_idx
    result.dominant_s_ti = best_s_ti

    // Check if CL-related total index > 0.7
    var cl_total_s_ti: f64 = 0.0
    idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        if pk_param_is_clearance_related(p.code) {
            let s_ti = p.contribution / total_var
            cl_total_s_ti = cl_total_s_ti + s_ti
        }
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    if cl_total_s_ti > 0.7 {
        result.clearance_dominant = true
    } else {
        result.clearance_dominant = false
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// PK-SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATION ENGINE
// ============================================================================

// Generate PK-specific recommendations based on the uncertainty profile.
// Recommendation codes:
//   10 = TDM (therapeutic drug monitoring)
//   11 = Body composition assessment
//   12 = Bioequivalence study
//   13 = Cystatin C measurement
//   14 = Population PK analysis
//   15 = Dose individualization
fn generate_pk_recommendations(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = profile
    var n_rec = 0

    // Rule 1: If clearance dominant -> recommend TDM
    if profile.is_clearance_dominant {
        if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 10 }
        else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 10 }
        else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 10 }
        else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 10 }
        n_rec = n_rec + 1
    }

    // Rule 2: If volume dominant (>50%) -> body composition assessment
    if profile.volume_contribution > 50.0 {
        if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 11 }
        else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 11 }
        else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 11 }
        else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 11 }
        n_rec = n_rec + 1
    }

    // Rule 3: If absorption dominant (>50%) -> bioequivalence study
    if profile.absorption_contribution > 50.0 {
        if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 12 }
        else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 12 }
        else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 12 }
        else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 12 }
        n_rec = n_rec + 1
    }

    // Rule 4: If SCr (code 7) is a major contributor and CL is dominant,
    // recommend cystatin C as an alternative renal biomarker
    if profile.is_clearance_dominant {
        var scr_pct: f64 = 0.0
        var idx = 0
        while idx < profile.n_params {
            let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
            if p.code == 7 {
                if profile.combined_variance > 1.0e-15 {
                    scr_pct = 100.0 * p.contribution / profile.combined_variance
                }
            }
            idx = idx + 1
        }
        if scr_pct > 20.0 {
            if n_rec < 4 {
                if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 13 }
                else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 13 }
                else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 13 }
                else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 13 }
                n_rec = n_rec + 1
            }
        }
    }

    // Rule 5: If combined relative uncertainty > 30%, recommend popPK analysis
    if profile.combined_std_uncert > 0.0 {
        // Use dominant param value as reference for relative uncertainty
        let dom_p = get_pk_param(profile, profile.dominant_param_idx)
        if abs_val(dom_p.value) > 1.0e-15 {
            let rel_uncert = 100.0 * profile.combined_std_uncert / abs_val(dom_p.value)
            if rel_uncert > 30.0 {
                if n_rec < 4 {
                    if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 14 }
                    else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 14 }
                    else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 14 }
                    else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 14 }
                    n_rec = n_rec + 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if n_rec > 4 { result.n_recommendations = 4 }
    else { result.n_recommendations = n_rec }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN ENTRY POINT: PK UNCERTAINTY ANALYSIS
// ============================================================================

// Main entry point combining contribution analysis, sensitivity computation,
// and recommendation generation.
fn pk_analyze(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, n: i32) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    // Step 1: Compute contributions and classify dominance
    var result = compute_pk_contributions(profile, n)

    // Step 2: Generate PK-specific recommendations
    result = generate_pk_recommendations(result)

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE CHECK
// ============================================================================

// Check if the uncertainty in drug exposure exceeds the therapeutic window.
// therapeutic_window is the ratio of toxic_conc / effective_conc (e.g., 2.0).
// If the 95% confidence interval spans more than the therapeutic window,
// the uncertainty is clinically significant.
//
// Uses 2 * combined_std_uncert as approximate 95% interval half-width.
// If 2 * u_c / result_value > (1 - 1/therapeutic_window), it is significant.
fn pk_is_clinically_significant(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, therapeutic_window: f64) -> bool {
    if therapeutic_window <= 1.0 { return true }

    // 95% confidence interval half-width (k~2 for large dof)
    let half_width = 2.0 * profile.combined_std_uncert

    // Use value of dominant parameter as reference
    let dom_p = get_pk_param(profile, profile.dominant_param_idx)
    if abs_val(dom_p.value) < 1.0e-15 { return true }

    // Relative half-width
    let rel_half = half_width / abs_val(dom_p.value)

    // Clinically significant if relative interval exceeds log-margin of TW
    // For TW=2, margin = 1 - 1/2 = 0.5 (50% deviation is clinically significant)
    let margin = 1.0 - 1.0 / therapeutic_window

    if rel_half > margin {
        return true
    }
    return false
}

// ============================================================================
// CONVENIENCE: Get S_Ti for a specific index
// ============================================================================

fn get_s_ti(sens: PKSensitivityResult, idx: i32) -> f64 {
    if idx == 0 { return sens.s_ti_0 }
    if idx == 1 { return sens.s_ti_1 }
    if idx == 2 { return sens.s_ti_2 }
    if idx == 3 { return sens.s_ti_3 }
    if idx == 4 { return sens.s_ti_4 }
    if idx == 5 { return sens.s_ti_5 }
    if idx == 6 { return sens.s_ti_6 }
    if idx == 7 { return sens.s_ti_7 }
    return 0.0
}

fn get_s_i(sens: PKSensitivityResult, idx: i32) -> f64 {
    if idx == 0 { return sens.s_i_0 }
    if idx == 1 { return sens.s_i_1 }
    if idx == 2 { return sens.s_i_2 }
    if idx == 3 { return sens.s_i_3 }
    if idx == 4 { return sens.s_i_4 }
    if idx == 5 { return sens.s_i_5 }
    if idx == 6 { return sens.s_i_6 }
    if idx == 7 { return sens.s_i_7 }
    return 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// PROFILE BUILDER HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn pk_profile_add(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, idx: i32, param: PKParameter) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = set_pk_param(profile, idx, param)
    if idx >= result.n_params {
        result.n_params = idx + 1
    }
    return result
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/policy.sio ===
//! Epistemic Policy Module
//!
//! This module enforces "shoreline" behavior: making it harder to lie
//! with numbers than to tell the truth.
//!
//! KEY PRINCIPLE: Dropping epistemic metadata must be:
//! 1. Syntactically noisy (explicit function call)
//! 2. Auditable (recorded in provenance)
//! 3. Policy-gated (can be forbidden by context)
//!
//! NO IMPLICIT UNWRAP. EVER.

// ============================================================================
// UNCERTAINTY MODE
// ============================================================================

// How to represent and propagate uncertainty
enum UncertaintyMode {
    // Standard deviation (GUM fast path, research iteration)
    StdDev,

    // Interval arithmetic (conservative, clinical safety)
    Interval,

    // Both: StdDev for typical, interval for guaranteed bounds
    Dual,
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC POLICY
// ============================================================================

// Policy object required at epistemic boundaries
// This prevents "silent defaults" from becoming doctrine
struct EpistemicPolicy {
    // Minimum acceptable confidence (0.0 = accept anything)
    min_conf: f64,

    // How to propagate uncertainty
    mode: UncertaintyMode,

    // Whether boost() is allowed (explicit confidence increase)
    allow_boost: bool,

    // Maximum acceptable DS conflict before error
    max_conflict: f64,

    // Coverage factor for expanded uncertainty (default k=2 for ~95%)
    default_coverage_k: f64,

    // Whether to allow unwrap without reason
    require_unwrap_reason: bool,

    // Whether to track all operations in provenance
    full_provenance: bool,
}

// ============================================================================
// POLICY CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

// Research mode: permissive, fast iteration
fn policy_research() -> EpistemicPolicy {
    return EpistemicPolicy {
        min_conf: 0.0,
        mode: UncertaintyMode::StdDev,
        allow_boost: true,
        max_conflict: 1.0,  // allow any conflict
        default_coverage_k: 2.0,
        require_unwrap_reason: false,
        full_provenance: false,
    }
}

// Clinical mode: conservative, safety-first
fn policy_clinical() -> EpistemicPolicy {
    return EpistemicPolicy {
        min_conf: 0.7,
        mode: UncertaintyMode::Interval,
        allow_boost: false,  // no artificial confidence
        max_conflict: 0.3,   // reject high-conflict evidence
        default_coverage_k: 2.576,  // 99% coverage
        require_unwrap_reason: true,
        full_provenance: true,
    }
}

// Regulatory mode: strictest, for submission
fn policy_regulatory() -> EpistemicPolicy {
    return EpistemicPolicy {
        min_conf: 0.9,
        mode: UncertaintyMode::Dual,
        allow_boost: false,
        max_conflict: 0.1,
        default_coverage_k: 3.0,  // 99.7% coverage
        require_unwrap_reason: true,
        full_provenance: true,
    }
}

// Default policy (research mode)
fn policy_default() -> EpistemicPolicy {
    return policy_research()
}

// ============================================================================
// UNWRAP RESULTS
// ============================================================================

// Result of attempting to unwrap an epistemic value
struct UnwrapResult {
    value: f64,
    succeeded: bool,
    reason_code: i32,  // 0=ok, 1=below_min_conf, 2=missing_reason, 3=policy_forbids
}

// Risk acknowledgment levels
enum RiskLevel {
    // I understand this loses epistemic information
    Acknowledged,

    // I've validated this is acceptable for my use case
    Validated,

    // This is for display/logging only, not computation
    DisplayOnly,

    // Emergency override (logged with warning)
    Override,
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC VALUE WITH POLICY SUPPORT
// ============================================================================

// Import core types (simplified for self-contained module)
struct Uncertainty {
    tag: i32,
    std_u: f64,
    std_k: f64,
    interval_lo: f64,
    interval_hi: f64,
}

struct PolicyValue {
    value: f64,
    uncert: Uncertainty,
    conf: f64,
    source_id: i64,      // VarID for correlation tracking
    provenance_id: i64,
}

fn uncertainty_std(u: f64) -> Uncertainty {
    return Uncertainty {
        tag: 1,
        std_u: if u < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { u },
        std_k: 1.0,
        interval_lo: 0.0,
        interval_hi: 0.0,
    }
}

fn policy_value_new(value: f64, std_u: f64, conf: f64, source_id: i64) -> PolicyValue {
    return PolicyValue {
        value: value,
        uncert: uncertainty_std(std_u),
        conf: conf,
        source_id: source_id,
        provenance_id: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// UNWRAP FUNCTIONS (THE ONLY WAY TO EXTRACT VALUES)
// ============================================================================

// Unwrap with full acknowledgment (auditable)
// Returns UnwrapResult, caller must check succeeded
fn unwrap_with_policy(
    v: PolicyValue,
    policy: EpistemicPolicy,
    risk: RiskLevel,
    reason_id: i64  // 0 = no reason provided
) -> UnwrapResult {
    // Check if reason is required
    if policy.require_unwrap_reason && reason_id == 0 {
        return UnwrapResult {
            value: 0.0,
            succeeded: false,
            reason_code: 2,  // missing_reason
        }
    }

    // Check minimum confidence
    if v.conf < policy.min_conf {
        return UnwrapResult {
            value: 0.0,
            succeeded: false,
            reason_code: 1,  // below_min_conf
        }
    }

    // Success - in a real impl, would log to provenance
    return UnwrapResult {
        value: v.value,
        succeeded: true,
        reason_code: 0,
    }
}

// Require minimum confidence (returns success flag + value)
fn require_conf(v: PolicyValue, min_conf: f64) -> UnwrapResult {
    if v.conf >= min_conf {
        return UnwrapResult {
            value: v.value,
            succeeded: true,
            reason_code: 0,
        }
    }
    return UnwrapResult {
        value: 0.0,
        succeeded: false,
        reason_code: 1,
    }
}

// Hard fail if below threshold (returns value or panics)
fn refuse_below(v: PolicyValue, min_conf: f64) -> f64 {
    if v.conf < min_conf {
        // In a real impl, this would panic/abort
        // For now, return sentinel
        return -999999.0
    }
    return v.value
}

// Display-only extraction (explicitly marked as non-computational)
fn for_display(v: PolicyValue) -> f64 {
    // Always succeeds, but caller promises not to use for computation
    return v.value
}

// ============================================================================
// POLICY VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

// Check if a value meets policy requirements
fn meets_policy(v: PolicyValue, policy: EpistemicPolicy) -> bool {
    return v.conf >= policy.min_conf
}

// Check DS conflict against policy
fn conflict_acceptable(conflict_k: f64, policy: EpistemicPolicy) -> bool {
    return conflict_k <= policy.max_conflict
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPANDED UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================

// Get expanded uncertainty interval with coverage factor
fn expanded_interval(v: PolicyValue, k: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
    let u = v.uncert.std_u
    let half_width = k * u
    return (v.value - half_width, v.value + half_width)
}

// Get expanded uncertainty with policy's default coverage
fn expanded_default(v: PolicyValue, policy: EpistemicPolicy) -> (f64, f64) {
    return expanded_interval(v, policy.default_coverage_k)
}

// Standard coverage factors
fn coverage_68() -> f64 { return 1.0 }      // 68% (1σ)
fn coverage_90() -> f64 { return 1.645 }    // 90%
fn coverage_95() -> f64 { return 1.96 }     // 95%
fn coverage_99() -> f64 { return 2.576 }    // 99%
fn coverage_997() -> f64 { return 3.0 }     // 99.7% (3σ)

// ============================================================================
// POLICY CONTEXT
// ============================================================================

// Note: Global policy state would require runtime support.
// For now, policy is passed explicitly to functions that need it.
// This is actually better: explicit > implicit.

// Get uncertainty mode as integer (for comparisons)
fn policy_mode_tag(policy: EpistemicPolicy) -> i32 {
    if policy.mode == UncertaintyMode::StdDev { return 0 }
    if policy.mode == UncertaintyMode::Interval { return 1 }
    return 2  // Dual
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_unwrap_respects_min_conf() -> bool {
    let v = policy_value_new(100.0, 5.0, 0.8, 1)
    let policy = policy_clinical()  // min_conf = 0.7

    let result = unwrap_with_policy(v, policy, RiskLevel::Acknowledged, 1)
    return result.succeeded  // 0.8 >= 0.7, should succeed
}

fn test_unwrap_rejects_low_conf() -> bool {
    let v = policy_value_new(100.0, 5.0, 0.5, 1)
    let policy = policy_clinical()  // min_conf = 0.7

    let result = unwrap_with_policy(v, policy, RiskLevel::Acknowledged, 1)
    return !result.succeeded  // 0.5 < 0.7, should fail
}

fn test_unwrap_requires_reason() -> bool {
    let v = policy_value_new(100.0, 5.0, 0.9, 1)
    let policy = policy_clinical()  // require_unwrap_reason = true

    // No reason provided (reason_id = 0)
    let result = unwrap_with_policy(v, policy, RiskLevel::Acknowledged, 0)
    return !result.succeeded && result.reason_code == 2
}

fn test_research_mode_permissive() -> bool {
    let v = policy_value_new(100.0, 5.0, 0.3, 1)
    let policy = policy_research()  // min_conf = 0.0

    let result = unwrap_with_policy(v, policy, RiskLevel::Acknowledged, 0)
    return result.succeeded  // research mode allows anything
}

fn test_expanded_uncertainty() -> bool {
    let v = policy_value_new(100.0, 5.0, 0.9, 1)

    // 95% coverage (k=1.96)
    let interval = expanded_interval(v, coverage_95())
    let lo = interval.0
    let hi = interval.1

    // Should be approximately [90.2, 109.8]
    let expected_lo = 100.0 - 1.96 * 5.0
    let expected_hi = 100.0 + 1.96 * 5.0

    if lo < expected_lo - 0.1 || lo > expected_lo + 0.1 {
        return false
    }
    if hi < expected_hi - 0.1 || hi > expected_hi + 0.1 {
        return false
    }
    return true
}
