// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/timeseries.sio ===
// stdlib/epistemic/timeseries.sio
//
// Time Series Analysis with Epistemic Uncertainty
//
// Kalman filter, exponential smoothing, and ARIMA core with uncertainty.
// Fixed arrays: max 1024 observations, max 16 state dimensions.

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn ts_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn ts_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// Time Series Data: value + variance per observation
// ============================================================================

struct TimeSeries {
    values: [f64; 1024],
    variances: [f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
}

fn ts_new(n: i64) -> TimeSeries {
    TimeSeries {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        variances: [0.0; 1024],
        n: n,
    }
}

fn ts_set(ts: &!TimeSeries, idx: i64, val: f64, var_: f64) {
    if idx >= 0 && idx < 1024 {
        ts.values[idx] = val
        ts.variances[idx] = var_
    }
}

fn ts_mean(ts: &TimeSeries) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 { sum = sum + ts.values[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (ts.n as f64)
}

fn ts_variance(ts: &TimeSeries) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = ts_mean(ts)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 {
            let d = ts.values[i] - m
            sum = sum + d * d
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / ((ts.n - 1) as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// Forecast result
// ============================================================================

struct Forecast {
    values: [f64; 64],
    variances: [f64; 64],
    n: i64,
}

fn forecast_new(n: i64) -> Forecast {
    Forecast {
        values: [0.0; 64],
        variances: [0.0; 64],
        n: n,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Exponential Smoothing (Simple)
// ============================================================================

struct ExpSmoothResult {
    smoothed: TimeSeries,
    alpha_used: f64,
    residual_variance: f64,
}

fn exp_smooth(ts: &TimeSeries, alpha: f64) -> ExpSmoothResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = ts_new(ts.n)
    if ts.n == 0 {
        return ExpSmoothResult { smoothed: result, alpha_used: alpha, residual_variance: 0.0 }
    }

    // Initialize with first value
    result.values[0] = ts.values[0]
    result.variances[0] = ts.variances[0]

    var i = 1
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 {
            // s[i] = alpha * y[i] + (1-alpha) * s[i-1]
            result.values[i] = alpha * ts.values[i] + (1.0 - alpha) * result.values[i - 1]
            // Variance: alpha^2 * Var(y[i]) + (1-alpha)^2 * Var(s[i-1])
            result.variances[i] = alpha * alpha * ts.variances[i]
                + (1.0 - alpha) * (1.0 - alpha) * result.variances[i - 1]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute residual variance
    var res_sum = 0.0
    i = 1
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 {
            let r = ts.values[i] - result.values[i]
            res_sum = res_sum + r * r
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let res_var = if ts.n > 1 { res_sum / ((ts.n - 1) as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    ExpSmoothResult { smoothed: result, alpha_used: alpha, residual_variance: res_var }
}

// Forecast from exponential smoothing
fn exp_smooth_forecast(
    result: &ExpSmoothResult,
    n_ahead: i64
) -> Forecast with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fc = forecast_new(n_ahead)
    let last_val = if result.smoothed.n > 0 {
        result.smoothed.values[result.smoothed.n - 1]
    } else { 0.0 }
    let last_var = if result.smoothed.n > 0 {
        result.smoothed.variances[result.smoothed.n - 1]
    } else { 0.0 }

    var i = 0
    while i < n_ahead {
        if i < 64 {
            // Forecast is constant (simple ES)
            fc.values[i] = last_val
            // Variance grows with horizon
            fc.variances[i] = last_var + result.residual_variance * ((i + 1) as f64)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    fc
}

// ============================================================================
// Kalman Filter (scalar observation model)
// State: x_t = F * x_{t-1} + w_t, w ~ N(0, Q)
// Obs:   y_t = H * x_t + v_t,     v ~ N(0, R)
// ============================================================================

struct KalmanConfig {
    f_coeff: f64,
    h_coeff: f64,
    q_var: f64,
    r_var: f64,
}

fn kalman_config_default() -> KalmanConfig {
    KalmanConfig {
        f_coeff: 1.0,
        h_coeff: 1.0,
        q_var: 0.01,
        r_var: 0.1,
    }
}

struct KalmanState {
    x: f64,
    p: f64,
}

struct KalmanResult {
    filtered: TimeSeries,
    innovations: TimeSeries,
    log_likelihood: f64,
}

fn kalman_filter(
    ts: &TimeSeries,
    cfg: &KalmanConfig
) -> KalmanResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var filtered = ts_new(ts.n)
    var innovations = ts_new(ts.n)
    var log_lik = 0.0

    // Initialize state
    var x = if ts.n > 0 { ts.values[0] } else { 0.0 }
    var p = 1.0

    var i = 0
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 {
            // Predict
            let x_pred = cfg.f_coeff * x
            let p_pred = cfg.f_coeff * cfg.f_coeff * p + cfg.q_var

            // Innovation
            let y = ts.values[i]
            let innov = y - cfg.h_coeff * x_pred
            let s = cfg.h_coeff * cfg.h_coeff * p_pred + cfg.r_var

            // Kalman gain
            let k = if s > 1.0e-15 { p_pred * cfg.h_coeff / s } else { 0.0 }

            // Update
            x = x_pred + k * innov
            p = (1.0 - k * cfg.h_coeff) * p_pred

            filtered.values[i] = x
            filtered.variances[i] = p
            innovations.values[i] = innov
            innovations.variances[i] = s

            // Log-likelihood contribution (approximate)
            if s > 1.0e-15 {
                log_lik = log_lik - 0.5 * (innov * innov / s)
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    filtered.n = ts.n
    innovations.n = ts.n

    KalmanResult {
        filtered: filtered,
        innovations: innovations,
        log_likelihood: log_lik,
    }
}

// Kalman forecast
fn kalman_forecast(
    kr: &KalmanResult,
    cfg: &KalmanConfig,
    n_ahead: i64
) -> Forecast with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fc = forecast_new(n_ahead)

    var x = if kr.filtered.n > 0 { kr.filtered.values[kr.filtered.n - 1] } else { 0.0 }
    var p = if kr.filtered.n > 0 { kr.filtered.variances[kr.filtered.n - 1] } else { 1.0 }

    var i = 0
    while i < n_ahead {
        x = cfg.f_coeff * x
        p = cfg.f_coeff * cfg.f_coeff * p + cfg.q_var
        if i < 64 {
            fc.values[i] = x
            fc.variances[i] = p + cfg.r_var
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    fc
}

// ============================================================================
// AR(1) model fitting (method of moments)
// ============================================================================

struct AR1Result {
    phi: f64,
    phi_variance: f64,
    sigma2: f64,
    intercept: f64,
}

fn fit_ar1(ts: &TimeSeries) -> AR1Result with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = ts_mean(ts)
    let v = ts_variance(ts)

    // Lag-1 autocovariance
    var cov1 = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 {
            cov1 = cov1 + (ts.values[i] - m) * (ts.values[i - 1] - m)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    cov1 = if ts.n > 1 { cov1 / ((ts.n - 1) as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    let phi = if v > 1.0e-15 { cov1 / v } else { 0.0 }
    let sigma2 = v * (1.0 - phi * phi)
    let intercept = m * (1.0 - phi)

    // Variance of phi estimate ~ (1 - phi^2) / n
    let phi_var = if ts.n > 2 { (1.0 - phi * phi) / (ts.n as f64) } else { 1.0 }

    AR1Result {
        phi: phi,
        phi_variance: phi_var,
        sigma2: if sigma2 > 0.0 { sigma2 } else { 0.001 },
        intercept: intercept,
    }
}

// Forecast from AR(1)
fn ar1_forecast(ar: &AR1Result, last_val: f64, n_ahead: i64) -> Forecast with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fc = forecast_new(n_ahead)
    var x = last_val

    var i = 0
    while i < n_ahead {
        x = ar.intercept + ar.phi * x
        if i < 64 {
            fc.values[i] = x
            // Variance grows with horizon for AR(1)
            var total_var = 0.0
            var k = 0
            var phi_pow = 1.0
            while k <= i {
                total_var = total_var + phi_pow * phi_pow * ar.sigma2
                phi_pow = phi_pow * ar.phi
                k = k + 1
            }
            // Add parameter uncertainty contribution
            total_var = total_var + (i + 1) as f64 * ar.phi_variance * x * x
            fc.variances[i] = total_var
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    fc
}

// ============================================================================
// Change Point Detection (CUSUM)
// ============================================================================

struct ChangePoint {
    location: i64,
    statistic: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn cusum_detect(ts: &TimeSeries, threshold: f64) -> ChangePoint with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let m = ts_mean(ts)
    let sd = ts_sqrt(ts_variance(ts))
    if sd < 1.0e-15 {
        return ChangePoint { location: 0 - 1, statistic: 0.0, confidence: 0.0 }
    }

    var s_pos = 0.0
    var s_neg = 0.0
    var max_stat = 0.0
    var max_loc: i64 = 0 - 1

    var i = 0
    while i < ts.n {
        if i < 1024 {
            let z = (ts.values[i] - m) / sd
            s_pos = s_pos + z
            if s_pos < 0.0 { s_pos = 0.0 }
            s_neg = s_neg - z
            if s_neg < 0.0 { s_neg = 0.0 }

            let stat = if s_pos > s_neg { s_pos } else { s_neg }
            if stat > max_stat {
                max_stat = stat
                max_loc = i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let detected = max_stat > threshold
    let conf = if detected { 0.95 } else { 0.1 }

    ChangePoint {
        location: if detected { max_loc } else { 0 - 1 },
        statistic: max_stat,
        confidence: conf,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/traceability.sio ===
//! Metrological Traceability: Provable Claims, Not Labels
//!
//! Per VIM (International Vocabulary of Metrology):
//!   "Metrological traceability is a property of a measurement result
//!    whereby the result can be related to a reference through a
//!    documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing
//!    to the measurement uncertainty."
//!
//! NIST emphasizes: traceability is a property of the RESULT, not the instrument.
//!
//! This module enforces:
//!   - traceability_claim_without_chain is a HARD ERROR
//!   - Every link in the chain must contribute documented uncertainty
//!   - The chain must terminate at a recognized reference
//!
//! References:
//!   - VIM3 (JCGM 200:2012): Section 2.41 "metrological traceability"
//!   - NIST Policy on Traceability: https://www.nist.gov/traceability

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// REFERENCE STANDARDS
// ============================================================================

// Recognized reference standard types
// Higher level = more authoritative
struct ReferenceStandard {
    standard_type: i32,     // 0=SI, 1=national, 2=accredited_lab, 3=working_standard
    level: i32,             // 0=primary, 1=secondary, 2=tertiary, 3=working
    identifier_hash: i64,   // Hash of standard identifier (e.g., NIST SRM number)
    is_recognized: bool,    // True if from a recognized body
}

fn si_primary() -> ReferenceStandard {
    return ReferenceStandard {
        standard_type: 0,
        level: 0,
        identifier_hash: 0,
        is_recognized: true,
    }
}

fn national_standard(id_hash: i64) -> ReferenceStandard {
    return ReferenceStandard {
        standard_type: 1,
        level: 1,
        identifier_hash: id_hash,
        is_recognized: true,
    }
}

fn accredited_lab_standard(id_hash: i64) -> ReferenceStandard {
    return ReferenceStandard {
        standard_type: 2,
        level: 2,
        identifier_hash: id_hash,
        is_recognized: true,
    }
}

fn working_standard(id_hash: i64) -> ReferenceStandard {
    return ReferenceStandard {
        standard_type: 3,
        level: 3,
        identifier_hash: id_hash,
        is_recognized: false,  // Must be validated
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CALIBRATION LINK WITH VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

// A single link in the traceability chain
struct TraceabilityLink {
    // Reference this link points to
    reference_id: i64,
    reference_type: ReferenceStandard,

    // Calibration documentation
    certificate_hash: i64,
    calibration_date: i64,
    expiry_date: i64,
    lab_id_hash: i64,
    procedure_hash: i64,

    // Uncertainty contribution
    contributed_uncertainty: f64,
    coverage_factor: f64,
    dof: f64,              // Degrees of freedom

    // Validation status
    is_documented: bool,
    is_expired: bool,
    is_valid: bool,
}

fn empty_link() -> TraceabilityLink {
    return TraceabilityLink {
        reference_id: 0,
        reference_type: working_standard(0),
        certificate_hash: 0,
        calibration_date: 0,
        expiry_date: 0,
        lab_id_hash: 0,
        procedure_hash: 0,
        contributed_uncertainty: 0.0,
        coverage_factor: 1.0,
        dof: 1.0e30,
        is_documented: false,
        is_expired: false,
        is_valid: false,
    }
}

// Create a documented calibration link
fn calibration_link(
    ref_id: i64,
    ref_type: ReferenceStandard,
    cert_hash: i64,
    cal_date: i64,
    expiry: i64,
    lab_hash: i64,
    proc_hash: i64,
    uncert: f64,
    k: f64,
    dof: f64,
    current_time: i64
) -> TraceabilityLink {
    let is_expired = current_time > expiry
    let is_documented = cert_hash != 0 && lab_hash != 0 && proc_hash != 0
    let is_valid = is_documented && !is_expired && ref_type.is_recognized

    return TraceabilityLink {
        reference_id: ref_id,
        reference_type: ref_type,
        certificate_hash: cert_hash,
        calibration_date: cal_date,
        expiry_date: expiry,
        lab_id_hash: lab_hash,
        procedure_hash: proc_hash,
        contributed_uncertainty: uncert,
        coverage_factor: k,
        dof: dof,
        is_documented: is_documented,
        is_expired: is_expired,
        is_valid: is_valid,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TRACEABILITY CHAIN
// ============================================================================

// Complete traceability chain with validation
struct TraceabilityChain {
    // Links in the chain (up to 4)
    link_count: i32,
    link0: TraceabilityLink,
    link1: TraceabilityLink,
    link2: TraceabilityLink,
    link3: TraceabilityLink,

    // Chain properties
    terminates_at_si: bool,
    terminates_at_national: bool,
    is_unbroken: bool,
    all_links_valid: bool,
    total_uncertainty: f64,
    effective_dof: f64,

    // Validation result
    is_complete: bool,
    error_code: i32,    // 0=ok, 1=broken, 2=expired, 3=undocumented, 4=no_recognized_ref
}

fn chain_new() -> TraceabilityChain {
    return TraceabilityChain {
        link_count: 0,
        link0: empty_link(),
        link1: empty_link(),
        link2: empty_link(),
        link3: empty_link(),
        terminates_at_si: false,
        terminates_at_national: false,
        is_unbroken: true,
        all_links_valid: true,
        total_uncertainty: 0.0,
        effective_dof: 1.0e30,
        is_complete: false,
        error_code: 0,
    }
}

fn get_link(chain: TraceabilityChain, idx: i32) -> TraceabilityLink {
    if idx == 0 { return chain.link0 }
    if idx == 1 { return chain.link1 }
    if idx == 2 { return chain.link2 }
    if idx == 3 { return chain.link3 }
    return empty_link()
}

// Add a link to the chain
fn chain_add_link(chain: TraceabilityChain, link: TraceabilityLink) -> TraceabilityChain {
    var result = chain
    let idx = chain.link_count

    if idx == 0 { result.link0 = link }
    else if idx == 1 { result.link1 = link }
    else if idx == 2 { result.link2 = link }
    else if idx == 3 { result.link3 = link }

    if idx < 4 {
        result.link_count = idx + 1

        // Update total uncertainty (quadrature)
        let u = link.contributed_uncertainty
        let prev_u2 = chain.total_uncertainty * chain.total_uncertainty
        result.total_uncertainty = sqrt_f64(prev_u2 + u * u)

        // Update validity
        if !link.is_valid {
            result.all_links_valid = false
        }

        // Check if terminates at recognized reference
        if link.reference_type.standard_type == 0 {
            result.terminates_at_si = true
        }
        if link.reference_type.standard_type == 1 {
            result.terminates_at_national = true
        }
    }

    return result
}

// Finalize and validate the chain
fn chain_finalize(chain: TraceabilityChain) -> TraceabilityChain {
    var result = chain

    if chain.link_count == 0 {
        result.is_complete = false
        result.error_code = 1  // Broken (no links)
        return result
    }

    // Check all links valid
    if !chain.all_links_valid {
        result.is_complete = false

        // Find first invalid link for error code
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < chain.link_count {
            let link = get_link(chain, i)
            if link.is_expired {
                result.error_code = 2  // Expired
                return result
            }
            if !link.is_documented {
                result.error_code = 3  // Undocumented
                return result
            }
            if !link.reference_type.is_recognized {
                result.error_code = 4  // No recognized reference
                return result
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        result.error_code = 1  // Generic broken
        return result
    }

    // Check terminates at recognized reference
    if !chain.terminates_at_si && !chain.terminates_at_national {
        result.is_complete = false
        result.error_code = 4  // No recognized reference
        return result
    }

    result.is_complete = true
    result.error_code = 0
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// TRACEABILITY CLAIM VALIDATION (THE LINT)
// ============================================================================

// Result of traceability claim validation
struct TraceabilityValidation {
    is_valid: bool,
    error_code: i32,
    error_level: i32,       // 0=none, 1=warning, 2=hard_error
    message_hash: i64,
}

// CRITICAL LINT: traceability_claim_without_chain
// This is a HARD ERROR - no exceptions
fn validate_traceability_claim(chain: TraceabilityChain, claimed: bool) -> TraceabilityValidation {
    if !claimed {
        // No claim made - OK
        return TraceabilityValidation {
            is_valid: true,
            error_code: 0,
            error_level: 0,
            message_hash: 0,
        }
    }

    // Claim made - chain must be complete and valid
    let finalized = chain_finalize(chain)

    if !finalized.is_complete {
        // HARD ERROR: traceability claimed but chain is incomplete
        return TraceabilityValidation {
            is_valid: false,
            error_code: finalized.error_code,
            error_level: 2,  // Hard error
            message_hash: 100 + finalized.error_code,  // Error message lookup
        }
    }

    // Chain is complete - claim is justified
    return TraceabilityValidation {
        is_valid: true,
        error_code: 0,
        error_level: 0,
        message_hash: 0,
    }
}

// Get error message for validation failure
fn get_error_message(validation: TraceabilityValidation) -> i32 {
    // Return message code (would be string in real impl)
    if validation.error_code == 1 {
        return 1  // "Traceability claim without documented chain"
    }
    if validation.error_code == 2 {
        return 2  // "Traceability chain contains expired calibration"
    }
    if validation.error_code == 3 {
        return 3  // "Traceability chain contains undocumented link"
    }
    if validation.error_code == 4 {
        return 4  // "Traceability chain does not terminate at recognized reference"
    }
    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// TRACEABLE VALUE TYPE
// ============================================================================

// A value that carries its traceability chain hash
// (Simplified to avoid nested struct issues)
struct TracedResult {
    value: f64,
    uncertainty: f64,
    chain_hash: i64,           // Hash of the traceability chain
    chain_link_count: i32,     // Number of links in chain
    terminates_at_si: bool,    // True if chain reaches SI
    is_traceable: bool,        // True if chain is complete and valid
}

fn traced_result(val: f64, uncert: f64, chain: TraceabilityChain) -> TracedResult {
    let finalized = chain_finalize(chain)
    // Compute a simple chain hash for verification
    let hash = finalized.total_uncertainty as i64
             + (finalized.link_count as i64) * 1000
             + (finalized.effective_dof as i64)
    return TracedResult {
        value: val,
        uncertainty: uncert,
        chain_hash: hash,
        chain_link_count: finalized.link_count,
        terminates_at_si: finalized.terminates_at_si,
        is_traceable: finalized.is_complete,
    }
}

// Assert traceability on a chain - returns error if not provable
fn assert_chain_traceable(chain: TraceabilityChain) -> TraceabilityValidation {
    return validate_traceability_claim(chain, true)
}

// ============================================================================
// CHAIN CONTINUITY VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

// Check that chain is unbroken (each link references the next)
struct ContinuityCheck {
    is_continuous: bool,
    break_at: i32,          // Index of first break (-1 if none)
    gap_description: i32,   // 0=none, 1=date_gap, 2=reference_mismatch
}

fn check_continuity(chain: TraceabilityChain) -> ContinuityCheck {
    if chain.link_count < 2 {
        return ContinuityCheck {
            is_continuous: true,
            break_at: -1,
            gap_description: 0,
        }
    }

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < chain.link_count - 1 {
        let curr = get_link(chain, i)
        let next = get_link(chain, i + 1)

        // Check date ordering: current calibration should be after next
        // (we're going from measurement to primary standard)
        if curr.calibration_date < next.expiry_date {
            // Current was calibrated before next expired - OK
        } else {
            return ContinuityCheck {
                is_continuous: false,
                break_at: i,
                gap_description: 1,  // Date gap
            }
        }

        // Check reference continuity: curr.reference should match next.level
        // (simplified check)

        i = i + 1
    }

    return ContinuityCheck {
        is_continuous: true,
        break_at: -1,
        gap_description: 0,
    }
}

}

// === FILE: stdlib/epistemic/uplift.sio ===
// epistemic/uplift.sio — Uplift Modeling with Epistemic Uncertainty
// CATE estimation with credible intervals

fn uplift_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn uplift_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}
fn uplift_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn uplift_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

// Treatment effect estimate with uncertainty
struct CATEEstimate {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64,
    ci_lo: f64,
    ci_hi: f64,
    n_treated: i64,
    n_control: i64,
}

fn cate_estimate_new() -> CATEEstimate {
    CATEEstimate { value: 0.0, variance: 0.0, ci_lo: 0.0, ci_hi: 0.0, n_treated: 0, n_control: 0 }
}

// Simple difference-in-means estimator
fn estimate_ate(
    treated_outcomes: &[f64; 256], n_treated: i64,
    control_outcomes: &[f64; 256], n_control: i64
) -> CATEEstimate with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = cate_estimate_new()
    if n_treated <= 0 || n_control <= 0 { return result }

    var sum_t = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_treated { sum_t = sum_t + treated_outcomes[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    let mean_t = sum_t / (n_treated as f64)

    var sum_c = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_control { sum_c = sum_c + control_outcomes[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    let mean_c = sum_c / (n_control as f64)

    result.value = mean_t - mean_c
    result.n_treated = n_treated
    result.n_control = n_control

    // Variance of difference in means
    var ss_t = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_treated { let d = treated_outcomes[i as usize] - mean_t; ss_t = ss_t + d * d; i = i + 1 }
    var ss_c = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_control { let d = control_outcomes[i as usize] - mean_c; ss_c = ss_c + d * d; i = i + 1 }

    let var_t = ss_t / (n_treated as f64)
    let var_c = ss_c / (n_control as f64)
    result.variance = var_t / (n_treated as f64) + var_c / (n_control as f64)

    let se = uplift_sqrt(result.variance)
    result.ci_lo = result.value - 1.96 * se
    result.ci_hi = result.value + 1.96 * se

    result
}

// Uplift tree node (simplified)
struct UpliftNode {
    split_feature: i32,
    split_value: f64,
    left_cate: f64,
    right_cate: f64,
    is_leaf: bool,
}

fn uplift_leaf(cate: f64) -> UpliftNode {
    UpliftNode { split_feature: 0, split_value: 0.0, left_cate: cate, right_cate: cate, is_leaf: true }
}

// Qini coefficient (area between uplift and random curves)
fn qini_coefficient(
    predicted_uplift: &[f64; 256],
    actual_outcome: &[f64; 256],
    treatment: &[i32; 256],
    n: i64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    // Simplified: compute average uplift for treated vs control
    var sum_treated = 0.0
    var sum_control = 0.0
    var n_t: i64 = 0
    var n_c: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if treatment[i as usize] == 1 {
            sum_treated = sum_treated + actual_outcome[i as usize]
            n_t = n_t + 1
        } else {
            sum_control = sum_control + actual_outcome[i as usize]
            n_c = n_c + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if n_t == 0 || n_c == 0 { return 0.0 }
    (sum_treated / (n_t as f64)) - (sum_control / (n_c as f64))
}

fn test_ate_estimate() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var treated: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var control: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    treated[0] = 5.0
    treated[1] = 6.0
    treated[2] = 7.0
    control[0] = 3.0
    control[1] = 4.0
    control[2] = 5.0
    let ate = estimate_ate(&treated, 3, &control, 3)
    uplift_abs(ate.value - 2.0) < 0.01
}

fn test_zero_uplift() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var outcomes: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    outcomes[0] = 5.0
    outcomes[1] = 5.0
    let ate = estimate_ate(&outcomes, 2, &outcomes, 2)
    uplift_abs(ate.value) < 0.01
}


// === FILE: stdlib/fairness/metrics.sio ===
// stdlib/fairness/metrics.sio — ML Fairness Metrics and Impossibility Theorem
//
// Canonical implementations of the four most widely used group fairness criteria,
// plus the Chouldechova (2017) impossibility theorem and Lipschitz individual fairness.
//
// REFERENCES:
//   Dwork et al. (2012) "Fairness Through Awareness" — demographic parity, individual fairness
//   Hardt et al. (2016) "Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning" — equalized odds
//   Chouldechova (2017) "Fair Prediction with Disparate Impact" — impossibility theorem
//   Kusner et al. (2017) "Counterfactual Fairness" — causal counterfactual criterion
//   Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan (2023) "Fairness and Machine Learning" — textbook survey
//   Menon & Williamson (2018) "The cost of fairness in binary classification"
//
// Sounio Sprint 22 Track F — first type system with fairness as a type-level constraint.
// Paper: FAccT 2027 + POPL 2027 short paper "From Privacy to Fairness: Unified Responsible AI Types"

// ============================================================
// Fairness criterion codes (matches TyFairPrediction.array_size)
// ============================================================

let FAIRNESS_DP: i64 = 0   // demographic parity
let FAIRNESS_EO: i64 = 1   // equalized odds
let FAIRNESS_IF: i64 = 2   // individual fairness (Lipschitz)
let FAIRNESS_CWG: i64 = 3  // calibration within group
let FAIRNESS_CF: i64 = 4   // counterfactual fairness

// ============================================================
// Group fairness metrics
// ============================================================

// --- Demographic Parity ---

// dp_gap: |P(Ŷ=1|A=0) - P(Ŷ=1|A=1)|
// Perfect demographic parity: dp_gap = 0.
// EU AI Act threshold (high-risk systems): dp_gap ≤ 0.05 recommended.
fn dp_gap(rate_a0: f64, rate_a1: f64) -> f64 with IO {
    let d = rate_a1 + (0.0 - rate_a0)
    if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
}

// dp_ratio: min(rate)/max(rate) — the "80% rule" (EEOC 1978, EU AI Act 2024)
// Violation when dp_ratio < 0.8 (minority gets < 80% of majority's approval rate).
fn dp_ratio(rate_a0: f64, rate_a1: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    let lo = if rate_a0 < rate_a1 { rate_a0 } else { rate_a1 }
    let hi = if rate_a0 > rate_a1 { rate_a0 } else { rate_a1 }
    lo / hi
}

// dp_satisfied: true if gap ≤ epsilon
fn dp_satisfied(rate_a0: f64, rate_a1: f64, epsilon: f64) -> bool with IO {
    dp_gap(rate_a0, rate_a1) <= epsilon
}

// --- Equalized Odds ---

// eo_gap: max(|ΔTPR|, |ΔFPR|)
// Both true and false positive rates must be equal across groups.
fn eo_gap(tpr0: f64, tpr1: f64, fpr0: f64, fpr1: f64) -> f64 with IO {
    let dt = tpr1 + (0.0 - tpr0)
    let df = fpr1 + (0.0 - fpr0)
    let at = if dt < 0.0 { 0.0 - dt } else { dt }
    let af = if df < 0.0 { 0.0 - df } else { df }
    if at > af { at } else { af }
}

// eop_gap: |ΔTPR| — equal opportunity (Hardt et al. 2016)
// Weaker than equalized odds: only TPR must be equal.
fn eop_gap(tpr0: f64, tpr1: f64) -> f64 with IO {
    let d = tpr1 + (0.0 - tpr0)
    if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
}

// eo_satisfied: true if max(|ΔTPR|, |ΔFPR|) ≤ epsilon
fn eo_satisfied(tpr0: f64, tpr1: f64, fpr0: f64, fpr1: f64, epsilon: f64) -> bool with IO {
    eo_gap(tpr0, tpr1, fpr0, fpr1) <= epsilon
}

// --- Calibration within group ---

// cwg_gap: |P(Y=1|Ŷ≈p, A=0) - P(Y=1|Ŷ≈p, A=1)|
// At each predicted probability p, actual outcomes should not differ by group.
fn cwg_gap(actual0: f64, actual1: f64) -> f64 with IO {
    let d = actual1 + (0.0 - actual0)
    if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
}

// positive_predictive_value: P(Y=1|Ŷ=1) = TP / (TP + FP)
// Required for Chouldechova impossibility calculation.
fn ppv(true_positive_rate: f64, prevalence: f64, false_positive_rate: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    // Bayes theorem: PPV = TPR * P / (TPR * P + FPR * (1-P))
    let num = true_positive_rate * prevalence
    let denom = num + false_positive_rate * (1.0 + (0.0 - prevalence))
    num / denom
}

// ============================================================
// Chouldechova impossibility theorem (2017)
// ============================================================

// chouldechova_check: computes the necessary gap between PPV values when base rates differ.
// When P(Y=1|A=0) ≠ P(Y=1|A=1), the following cannot all hold simultaneously:
//   (a) Equal PPV across groups (calibration within group)
//   (b) Equal FPR across groups (equalized odds component)
//   (c) Equal TPR across groups (equalized odds component)
// Returns the minimum inevitable PPV gap given different prevalences and equal TPR/FPR.
fn chouldechova_ppv_gap(
    prevalence_a0: f64,     // P(Y=1|A=0)
    prevalence_a1: f64,     // P(Y=1|A=1)
    shared_tpr: f64,        // common TPR (assuming equal TPR for equalized opportunity)
    shared_fpr: f64         // common FPR (assuming equal FPR for equalized odds)
) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    // PPV for each group given shared TPR/FPR but different prevalences
    let ppv0 = ppv(shared_tpr, prevalence_a0, shared_fpr)
    let ppv1 = ppv(shared_tpr, prevalence_a1, shared_fpr)
    let d = ppv1 + (0.0 - ppv0)
    if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
}

// fairness_criteria_incompatible: Chouldechova 2017 — returns true if
// demographic parity and calibration within group are contradictory given unequal base rates.
fn fairness_criteria_incompatible(criterion_a: i64, criterion_b: i64, base_rates_equal: bool) -> bool with IO {
    // When base rates are equal, all criteria can be jointly satisfied.
    if base_rates_equal {
        return false
    }
    // Chouldechova: DP ∧ CWG is impossible when base rates differ
    let dp_and_cwg = (criterion_a == FAIRNESS_DP && criterion_b == FAIRNESS_CWG)
        || (criterion_a == FAIRNESS_CWG && criterion_b == FAIRNESS_DP)
    // EO ∧ CWG is also impossible when base rates differ
    let eo_and_cwg = (criterion_a == FAIRNESS_EO && criterion_b == FAIRNESS_CWG)
        || (criterion_a == FAIRNESS_CWG && criterion_b == FAIRNESS_EO)
    dp_and_cwg || eo_and_cwg
}

// ============================================================
// Individual fairness (Lipschitz)
// ============================================================

// if_violation: |f(x) - f(x')| - L * d(x, x')
// Negative means individual fairness holds (Lipschitz satisfied).
// d(x, x') should be a task-specific metric capturing "similarity".
fn if_violation(score_x: f64, score_x_prime: f64, lipschitz: f64, distance: f64) -> f64 with IO {
    let sd = score_x + (0.0 - score_x_prime)
    let abs_sd = if sd < 0.0 { 0.0 - sd } else { sd }
    abs_sd + (0.0 - (lipschitz * distance))
}

// if_satisfied: true if Lipschitz condition holds (no individual fairness violation)
fn if_satisfied(score_x: f64, score_x_prime: f64, lipschitz: f64, distance: f64) -> bool with IO {
    if_violation(score_x, score_x_prime, lipschitz, distance) <= 0.0
}

// ============================================================
// Counterfactual fairness
// ============================================================

// cf_gap: |Ŷ(A←a) - Ŷ(A←a')| — counterfactual gap
// Counterfactually fair if cf_gap = 0 for all pairs (a, a').
fn cf_gap(score_a0: f64, score_a1: f64) -> f64 with IO {
    let d = score_a1 + (0.0 - score_a0)
    if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
}

// cf_satisfied: true if counterfactual gap ≤ epsilon
fn cf_satisfied(score_a0: f64, score_a1: f64, epsilon: f64) -> bool with IO {
    cf_gap(score_a0, score_a1) <= epsilon
}

// ============================================================
// Aggregate fairness report from raw prediction arrays
// ============================================================

// FairnessReport — comprehensive fairness metrics computed from prediction arrays
struct FairnessReport {
    demographic_parity_diff: f64,       // |P(Ŷ=1|A=0) - P(Ŷ=1|A=1)|
    equalized_odds_diff: f64,           // max(|ΔTPR|, |ΔFPR|)
    predictive_parity_diff: f64,        // |PPV(A=0) - PPV(A=1)|
    calibration_diff: f64,              // |P(Y=1|Ŷ=1,A=0) - P(Y=1|Ŷ=1,A=1)|
    disparate_impact_ratio: f64,        // min(P₀/P₁, P₁/P₀)
    individual_fairness_lipschitz: f64, // placeholder (requires distance metric)
    chouldechova_impossible: i32,       // 1 if impossibility theorem triggered
}

// Helper: integer absolute value
fn abs_i32(x: i32) -> i32 {
    if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
}

// Helper: f64 absolute value
fn abs_f64_local(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// Helper: safe f64 division (returns 0 if denominator is 0)
fn safe_div(num: f64, denom: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if denom == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    num / denom
}

// demographic_parity: |P(Ŷ=1|A=0) - P(Ŷ=1|A=1)|
// Ref: Dwork et al. 2012 "Fairness Through Awareness"
fn demographic_parity(predictions: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos0: f64 = 0.0
    var count1: f64 = 0.0
    var pos1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let p = predictions[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            count0 = count0 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos0 = pos0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            count1 = count1 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos1 = pos1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rate0 = safe_div(pos0, count0)
    let rate1 = safe_div(pos1, count1)
    abs_f64_local(rate0 - rate1)
}

// equalized_odds: max(|ΔTPR|, |ΔFPR|)
// Ref: Hardt et al. 2016 "Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning"
fn equalized_odds(predictions: [i32; 256], true_labels: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Group 0
    var tp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fn0: f64 = 0.0
    var tn0: f64 = 0.0
    // Group 1
    var tp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fn1: f64 = 0.0
    var tn1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let y_hat = predictions[idx]
        let y = true_labels[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp0 = tp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp0 = fp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 0 { fn0 = fn0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 0 { tn0 = tn0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp1 = tp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp1 = fp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 0 { fn1 = fn1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 0 { tn1 = tn1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let tpr0 = safe_div(tp0, tp0 + fn0)
    let tpr1 = safe_div(tp1, tp1 + fn1)
    let fpr0 = safe_div(fp0, fp0 + tn0)
    let fpr1 = safe_div(fp1, fp1 + tn1)
    let d_tpr = abs_f64_local(tpr0 - tpr1)
    let d_fpr = abs_f64_local(fpr0 - fpr1)
    if d_tpr > d_fpr { d_tpr } else { d_fpr }
}

// disparate_impact: min(P₀/P₁, P₁/P₀)
// 4/5 rule (EEOC 1978): value < 0.8 signals adverse impact.
fn disparate_impact(predictions: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos0: f64 = 0.0
    var count1: f64 = 0.0
    var pos1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let p = predictions[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            count0 = count0 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos0 = pos0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            count1 = count1 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos1 = pos1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rate0 = safe_div(pos0, count0)
    let rate1 = safe_div(pos1, count1)
    if rate0 == 0.0 && rate1 == 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    if rate0 == 0.0 || rate1 == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let r01 = safe_div(rate0, rate1)
    let r10 = safe_div(rate1, rate0)
    if r01 < r10 { r01 } else { r10 }
}

// chouldechova_check: returns 1 if the impossibility theorem applies.
// Chouldechova 2017: when base rates differ (base0 ≠ base1), you cannot
// simultaneously equalize FPR, FNR, and PPV.
// Inputs: tp0, fp0, tp1, fp1 are rates; base0, base1 are prevalences P(Y=1|A=g).
fn chouldechova_check(tp0: f64, fp0: f64, tp1: f64, fp1: f64, base0: f64, base1: f64) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    // Impossibility requires: base rates differ
    let rate_diff = abs_f64_local(base0 - base1)
    if rate_diff < 0.001 {
        return 0  // base rates equal → all criteria can hold simultaneously
    }
    // PPV = TPR * P / (TPR * P + FPR * (1 - P))
    let ppv0 = safe_div(tp0 * base0, tp0 * base0 + fp0 * (1.0 - base0))
    let ppv1 = safe_div(tp1 * base1, tp1 * base1 + fp1 * (1.0 - base1))
    // Equalized FPR and FNR (TPR) imply unequal PPV when base rates differ
    let fpr_diff = abs_f64_local(fp0 - fp1)
    let tpr_diff = abs_f64_local(tp0 - tp1)
    let ppv_diff = abs_f64_local(ppv0 - ppv1)
    // If FPR and TPR are roughly equal but PPV is not (base rate effect):
    // impossibility is demonstrated
    if fpr_diff < 0.05 && tpr_diff < 0.05 && ppv_diff > 0.05 {
        return 1
    }
    // Also flag if base rates differ significantly: Chouldechova's theorem
    // guarantees impossibility in principle even if not yet realized
    if rate_diff > 0.1 {
        return 1
    }
    0
}

// predictive_parity: |PPV(A=0) - PPV(A=1)|
// PPV = P(Y=1 | Ŷ=1); equal across groups means equal precision.
fn predictive_parity_diff_from_arrays(predictions: [i32; 256], true_labels: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var tp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fp0: f64 = 0.0
    var tp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fp1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let y_hat = predictions[idx]
        let y = true_labels[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp0 = tp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp0 = fp0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp1 = tp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp1 = fp1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let ppv0 = safe_div(tp0, tp0 + fp0)
    let ppv1 = safe_div(tp1, tp1 + fp1)
    abs_f64_local(ppv0 - ppv1)
}

// fairness_report: compute all metrics from raw arrays in one pass
fn fairness_report(predictions: [i32; 256], true_labels: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> FairnessReport with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Group 0 and 1 counts
    var count0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos0: f64 = 0.0
    var count1: f64 = 0.0
    var pos1: f64 = 0.0
    var tp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fn0: f64 = 0.0
    var tn0: f64 = 0.0
    var tp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fn1: f64 = 0.0
    var tn1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let y_hat = predictions[idx]
        let y = true_labels[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            count0 = count0 + 1.0
            if y_hat == 1 { pos0 = pos0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp0 = tp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp0 = fp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 0 { fn0 = fn0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 0 { tn0 = tn0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            count1 = count1 + 1.0
            if y_hat == 1 { pos1 = pos1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp1 = tp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp1 = fp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 0 { fn1 = fn1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 0 { tn1 = tn1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rate0 = safe_div(pos0, count0)
    let rate1 = safe_div(pos1, count1)
    let dp_diff = abs_f64_local(rate0 - rate1)
    let tpr0 = safe_div(tp0, tp0 + fn0)
    let tpr1 = safe_div(tp1, tp1 + fn1)
    let fpr0 = safe_div(fp0, fp0 + tn0)
    let fpr1 = safe_div(fp1, fp1 + tn1)
    let d_tpr = abs_f64_local(tpr0 - tpr1)
    let d_fpr = abs_f64_local(fpr0 - fpr1)
    let eo_diff = if d_tpr > d_fpr { d_tpr } else { d_fpr }
    let ppv0 = safe_div(tp0, tp0 + fp0)
    let ppv1 = safe_div(tp1, tp1 + fp1)
    let pp_diff = abs_f64_local(ppv0 - ppv1)
    // Calibration diff: same as predictive parity here (PPV-based)
    let cal_diff = pp_diff
    // Disparate impact ratio
    let di = if rate0 == 0.0 && rate1 == 0.0 {
        1.0
    } else if rate0 == 0.0 || rate1 == 0.0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        let r01 = safe_div(rate0, rate1)
        let r10 = safe_div(rate1, rate0)
        if r01 < r10 { r01 } else { r10 }
    }
    // Chouldechova impossibility (with base rates estimated from true_labels)
    var pos_true0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos_true1: f64 = 0.0
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < n {
        let jdx = j as usize
        let y = true_labels[jdx]
        let g = protected[jdx]
        if g == 0 && y == 1 { pos_true0 = pos_true0 + 1.0 }
        if g == 1 && y == 1 { pos_true1 = pos_true1 + 1.0 }
        j = j + 1
    }
    let base0 = safe_div(pos_true0, count0)
    let base1 = safe_div(pos_true1, count1)
    let chould = chouldechova_check(tpr0, fpr0, tpr1, fpr1, base0, base1)
    FairnessReport {
        demographic_parity_diff: dp_diff,
        equalized_odds_diff: eo_diff,
        predictive_parity_diff: pp_diff,
        calibration_diff: cal_diff,
        disparate_impact_ratio: di,
        individual_fairness_lipschitz: 0.0,  // requires distance metric
        chouldechova_impossible: chould,
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Epistemic confidence tracking for fairness metrics
// ============================================================

// EpistemicFairnessValue — a fairness metric with uncertainty from finite sample size.
// Uses Wilson score interval (Brown, Cai, DasGupta 2001) for binomial proportions.
struct EpistemicFairnessValue {
    point_estimate: f64,    // the raw metric
    lower_95: f64,          // 95% CI lower bound
    upper_95: f64,          // 95% CI upper bound
    n_samples: i32,         // effective sample size
}

// sqrt helper for epistemic CI (Newton, 5 iterations)
fn ep_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x / 2.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 8 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    y
}

// Wilson interval half-width for a proportion p over n trials at z=1.96 (95%)
// half = z * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n + z²/(4n²)) / (1 + z²/n)
fn wilson_half(p: f64, n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let z = 1.96
    let nf: f64 = n as f64
    let z2 = z * z
    let inner = p * (1.0 - p) / nf + z2 / (4.0 * nf * nf)
    z * ep_sqrt(inner) / (1.0 + z2 / nf)
}

// epistemic_dp_metric — wrap demographic parity with Wilson-style CI
// Uses normal approximation for the difference of two proportions.
fn epistemic_demographic_parity(predictions: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> EpistemicFairnessValue with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos0: f64 = 0.0
    var count1: f64 = 0.0
    var pos1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let p = predictions[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            count0 = count0 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos0 = pos0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            count1 = count1 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos1 = pos1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rate0 = safe_div(pos0, count0)
    let rate1 = safe_div(pos1, count1)
    let diff = abs_f64_local(rate0 - rate1)
    // SE of difference of proportions: sqrt(p0(1-p0)/n0 + p1(1-p1)/n1)
    let se = ep_sqrt(safe_div(rate0 * (1.0 - rate0), count0) + safe_div(rate1 * (1.0 - rate1), count1))
    let half = 1.96 * se
    EpistemicFairnessValue {
        point_estimate: diff,
        lower_95: if diff - half < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { diff - half },
        upper_95: diff + half,
        n_samples: n,
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Fairness audit summary
// ============================================================

struct FairnessAuditResult {
    dp_gap_val: f64,
    eo_gap_val: f64,
    cwg_gap_val: f64,
    cf_gap_val: f64,
    impossibility_triggered: bool,
    overall_fair: bool,
}

fn fairness_audit(
    rate_a0: f64, rate_a1: f64,       // approval rates for DP
    tpr_a0: f64, tpr_a1: f64,         // true positive rates for EO
    fpr_a0: f64, fpr_a1: f64,         // false positive rates for EO
    cal_a0: f64, cal_a1: f64,         // calibration rates for CWG
    score_cf_a0: f64, score_cf_a1: f64, // counterfactual scores
    base_rates_equal: bool,           // are base rates equal? (for impossibility)
    epsilon: f64                      // shared tolerance for all criteria
) -> FairnessAuditResult with IO, Div, Panic {
    let dp = dp_gap(rate_a0, rate_a1)
    let eo = eo_gap(tpr_a0, tpr_a1, fpr_a0, fpr_a1)
    let cwg = cwg_gap(cal_a0, cal_a1)
    let cf = cf_gap(score_cf_a0, score_cf_a1)
    let impossible = fairness_criteria_incompatible(FAIRNESS_DP, FAIRNESS_CWG, base_rates_equal)
    let all_ok = dp <= epsilon && eo <= epsilon && cwg <= epsilon && cf <= epsilon
    FairnessAuditResult {
        dp_gap_val: dp,
        eo_gap_val: eo,
        cwg_gap_val: cwg,
        cf_gap_val: cf,
        impossibility_triggered: impossible,
        overall_fair: all_ok,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ffi/callback.sio ===
// stdlib/ffi/callback.sio — Callback registry for FFI boundaries
//
// Arena-style registry for storing and invoking callbacks across the FFI
// boundary. Uses a fixed-capacity table to avoid heap allocation.

// Maximum number of registered callbacks
let CALLBACK_CAPACITY: usize = 64

// Slot states
let SLOT_EMPTY: i32 = 0
let SLOT_OCCUPIED: i32 = 1

// A callback entry: an opaque function pointer and user data
struct CallbackEntry {
    func: *mut u8,
    data: *mut u8,
    state: i32
}

// Registry holding up to CALLBACK_CAPACITY callbacks
struct CallbackRegistry {
    entries: [CallbackEntry; 64],
    count: usize
}

fn callback_entry_empty() -> CallbackEntry {
    CallbackEntry {
        func: 0 as *mut u8,
        data: 0 as *mut u8,
        state: SLOT_EMPTY
    }
}

fn callback_registry_new() -> CallbackRegistry {
    CallbackRegistry {
        entries: [callback_entry_empty(); 64],
        count: 0
    }
}

fn callback_registry_len(reg: &CallbackRegistry) -> usize {
    reg.count
}

fn callback_registry_is_full(reg: &CallbackRegistry) -> bool {
    reg.count >= CALLBACK_CAPACITY
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ffi/cstring.sio ===
// stdlib/ffi/cstring.sio
// Minimal C string utilities for FFI
//
// Provides functions for working with null-terminated byte arrays.

// Copy a Sounio string into a fixed buffer with null terminator
// Returns the length written (including null byte)
fn cstring_write(src: [u8; 256], src_len: i64, dst: &![u8; 257]) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < src_len {
        if i >= 256 { break }
        dst[i] = src[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    dst[i] = 0
    return i + 1
}

// Measure length of a null-terminated buffer (up to max)
fn cstring_len(buf: [u8; 257], max: i64) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < max {
        if buf[i] == 0 { return i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return max
}

// Compare two null-terminated buffers
// Returns 0 if equal, non-zero otherwise
fn cstring_eq(a: [u8; 257], b: [u8; 257], max: i64) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < max {
        if a[i] != b[i] { return 1 }
        if a[i] == 0 { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 0
}

let NULL_PTR: usize = 0


// === FILE: stdlib/ffi/library.sio ===
// stdlib/ffi/library.sio — Dynamic library loading via dlopen/dlsym
//
// Provides a minimal wrapper around the POSIX dynamic linking interface
// for loading shared libraries at runtime.

extern "C" {
    fn dlopen(filename: *const u8, flags: i32) -> *mut u8;
    fn dlsym(handle: *mut u8, symbol: *const u8) -> *mut u8;
    fn dlclose(handle: *mut u8) -> i32;
    fn dlerror() -> *const u8;
}

// dlopen flags
let RTLD_LAZY: i32 = 1
let RTLD_NOW: i32 = 2
let RTLD_GLOBAL: i32 = 256
let RTLD_LOCAL: i32 = 0

// Handle to an open dynamic library
struct Library {
    handle: *mut u8,
    valid: bool
}

fn library_open(path: *const u8) -> Library {
    let h = dlopen(path, RTLD_LAZY)
    let ok = h as usize != 0
    Library { handle: h, valid: ok }
}

fn library_is_valid(lib: &Library) -> bool {
    lib.valid
}

fn library_symbol(lib: &Library, name: *const u8) -> *mut u8 {
    dlsym(lib.handle, name)
}

fn library_close(lib: Library) -> i32 {
    dlclose(lib.handle)
}

// ============================================================================
// STRING HELPER
// ============================================================================

fn copy_str_to_arr(src: &[u8], dst: &![i8; 64]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 64 && i < src.len() as i64 && src[i as usize] != 0 {
        dst[i as usize] = src[i as usize] as i8
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn copy_str_to_arr_16(src: &[u8], dst: &![i8; 16]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 && i < src.len() as i64 && src[i as usize] != 0 {
        dst[i as usize] = src[i as usize] as i8
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn atlas_str_byte_u8(src: string, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= src.len() as i64 {
        return 0
    }
    let raw = src[idx as usize] as i64
    if raw < 0 { raw + 256 } else { raw }
}

fn copy_str_to_arr_str(src: string, dst: &![i8; 64]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 64 && i < src.len() as i64 && atlas_str_byte_u8(src, i) != 0 {
        dst[i as usize] = atlas_str_byte_u8(src, i) as i8
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn copy_str_to_arr_16_str(src: string, dst: &![i8; 16]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 && i < src.len() as i64 && atlas_str_byte_u8(src, i) != 0 {
        dst[i as usize] = atlas_str_byte_u8(src, i) as i8
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn copy_str_to_arr_32_str(src: string, dst: &![i8; 32]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 32 && i < src.len() as i64 && atlas_str_byte_u8(src, i) != 0 {
        dst[i as usize] = atlas_str_byte_u8(src, i) as i8
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ATLAS OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Get region by index (1-based)
fn atlas_get_region(atlas: &Atlas, index: i32) -> &AtlasRegion {
    if index > 0 && index <= atlas.n_regions as i32 {
        &atlas.regions[(index - 1) as usize]
    } else {
        &atlas.regions[0]
    }
}

// Find region by label (returns 0 if not found)
fn atlas_find_region(atlas: &Atlas, label: &[i8; 64]) -> i32 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < atlas.n_regions {
        var match_found = true
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < 64 {
            if atlas.regions[i as usize].label[j as usize] != label[j as usize] {
                if atlas.regions[i as usize].label[j as usize] == 0 && label[j as usize] == 0 {
                    break
                }
                match_found = false
                break
            }
            if label[j as usize] == 0 {
                break
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if match_found {
            return atlas.regions[i as usize].index
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0
}

// Get regions by network
fn atlas_get_network_regions(
    atlas: &Atlas,
    network: Network7,
    indices: &![i32; 200],
    n_indices: &!i64
) {
    *n_indices = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < atlas.n_regions {
        if atlas.regions[i as usize].network_7 == network {
            if *n_indices < 200 {
                indices[(*n_indices) as usize] = atlas.regions[i as usize].index
                *n_indices = *n_indices + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Get regions by lobe
fn atlas_get_lobe_regions(
    atlas: &Atlas,
    lobe: Lobe,
    indices: &![i32; 200],
    n_indices: &!i64
) {
    *n_indices = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < atlas.n_regions {
        if atlas.regions[i as usize].lobe == lobe {
            if *n_indices < 200 {
                indices[(*n_indices) as usize] = atlas.regions[i as usize].index
                *n_indices = *n_indices + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Get regions by hemisphere
fn atlas_get_hemisphere_regions(
    atlas: &Atlas,
    hemi: Hemisphere,
    indices: &![i32; 500],
    n_indices: &!i64
) {
    *n_indices = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < atlas.n_regions {
        if atlas.regions[i as usize].hemisphere == hemi {
            if *n_indices < 500 {
                indices[(*n_indices) as usize] = atlas.regions[i as usize].index
                *n_indices = *n_indices + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Euclidean distance between two regions
fn atlas_region_distance(atlas: &Atlas, idx1: i32, idx2: i32) -> f64 {
    let r1 = atlas_get_region(atlas, idx1)
    let r2 = atlas_get_region(atlas, idx2)

    let dx = r1.mni_x - r2.mni_x
    let dy = r1.mni_y - r2.mni_y
    let dz = r1.mni_z - r2.mni_z

    sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
}

// Find nearest region to MNI coordinate
fn atlas_nearest_region(atlas: &Atlas, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> i32 {
    var min_dist = 1e10
    var nearest_idx: i32 = 0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < atlas.n_regions {
        let r = &atlas.regions[i as usize]
        let dx = r.mni_x - x
        let dy = r.mni_y - y
        let dz = r.mni_z - z
        let dist = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)

        if dist < min_dist {
            min_dist = dist
            nearest_idx = r.index
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    nearest_idx
}

// ============================================================================
// NETWORK EXTRACTION
// ============================================================================

// Network connectivity submatrix
struct NetworkSubmatrix {
    network: Network7,
    indices: [i32; 200],
    n_regions: i64,
    matrix: [[f64; 200]; 200],
    mean_within: f64,
    mean_between: f64,
}

fn network_submatrix_new() -> NetworkSubmatrix {
    NetworkSubmatrix {
        network: Network7::Unknown,
        indices: [0; 200],
        n_regions: 0,
        matrix: [[0.0; 200]; 200],
        mean_within: 0.0,
        mean_between: 0.0,
    }
}

// Extract network submatrix from full connectivity
fn extract_network_connectivity(
    atlas: &Atlas,
    full_matrix: &[[f64; 500]; 500],
    network: Network7
) -> NetworkSubmatrix {
    var sub = network_submatrix_new()
    sub.network = network

    // Get network indices
    atlas_get_network_regions(atlas, network, &!sub.indices, &!sub.n_regions)

    // Extract submatrix
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < sub.n_regions {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < sub.n_regions {
            let idx_i = (sub.indices[i as usize] - 1) as usize
            let idx_j = (sub.indices[j as usize] - 1) as usize
            sub.matrix[i as usize][j as usize] = full_matrix[idx_i][idx_j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Calculate mean within-network connectivity
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < sub.n_regions {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < sub.n_regions {
            sum = sum + sub.matrix[i as usize][j as usize]
            count = count + 1
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if count > 0 {
        sub.mean_within = sum / count as f64
    }

    sub
}

// Calculate between-network connectivity
fn between_network_connectivity(
    atlas: &Atlas,
    full_matrix: &[[f64; 500]; 500],
    network1: Network7,
    network2: Network7
) -> f64 {
    var indices1 = [0i32; 200]
    var n1: i64 = 0
    atlas_get_network_regions(atlas, network1, &!indices1, &!n1)

    var indices2 = [0i32; 200]
    var n2: i64 = 0
    atlas_get_network_regions(atlas, network2, &!indices2, &!n2)

    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n1 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n2 {
            let idx_i = (indices1[i as usize] - 1) as usize
            let idx_j = (indices2[j as usize] - 1) as usize
            sum = sum + full_matrix[idx_i][idx_j]
            count = count + 1
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if count > 0 {
        sum / count as f64
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ATLAS FACTORY
// ============================================================================

// Create atlas by type
fn create_atlas(atlas_type: AtlasType) -> Atlas {
    match atlas_type {
        AtlasType::AAL => atlas_aal(),
        AtlasType::Schaefer100 => atlas_schaefer100(),
        AtlasType::Schaefer400 => atlas_schaefer400(),
        AtlasType::HarvardOxford => atlas_harvard_oxford(),
        _ => atlas_new()
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/fmri/connectivity_epistemic.sio ===
// fmri::connectivity_epistemic — Epistemic-Aware Functional Connectivity
//
// Connectivity matrices with uncertainty propagation:
// - Pearson correlation with Fisher-z CI
// - Phase-locking value (PLV)
// - Graph-theoretic metrics with uncertainty
//
// All outputs integrate with epistemic principles.

// Math helpers inlined

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r = 0.5 * (r + x / r)
    r
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i = 1
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        result = result + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

fn log_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var v = x
    var scale = 0.0
    while v > 2.0 { v = v / 2.718281828; scale = scale + 1.0 }
    while v < 0.5 { v = v * 2.718281828; scale = scale - 1.0 }
    let y = (v - 1.0) / (v + 1.0)
    let y2 = y * y
    let result = 2.0 * y * (1.0 + y2 / 3.0 + y2 * y2 / 5.0 + y2 * y2 * y2 / 7.0 + y2 * y2 * y2 * y2 / 9.0)
    result + scale
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let x2 = x * x
    let x4 = x2 * x2
    let x6 = x4 * x2
    let x8 = x6 * x2
    1.0 - x2 / 2.0 + x4 / 24.0 - x6 / 720.0 + x8 / 40320.0
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let x2 = x * x
    let x3 = x2 * x
    let x5 = x3 * x2
    let x7 = x5 * x2
    let x9 = x7 * x2
    x - x3 / 6.0 + x5 / 120.0 - x7 / 5040.0 + x9 / 362880.0
}

fn fisher_z(r: f64) -> f64 {
    var rc = r
    if rc > 0.999 { rc = 0.999 }
    if rc < 0.0 - 0.999 { rc = 0.0 - 0.999 }
    0.5 * log_f64((1.0 + rc) / (1.0 - rc))
}

fn fisher_z_inv(z: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2z = exp_f64(2.0 * z)
    (e2z - 1.0) / (e2z + 1.0)
}

fn fisher_z_se(n: i64) -> f64 {
    if n < 4 { return 1.0 }
    1.0 / sqrt_f64((n - 3) as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC STATUS
// ============================================================================

// Epistemic status for connectivity values
enum EpistemicStatus {
    Verified,           // High confidence, validated
    Provisional,        // Reasonable confidence
    Uncertain,          // Low confidence, needs validation
}

// ============================================================================
// CONNECTIVITY RESULT WITH UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================

// Single connectivity edge with uncertainty
struct ConnectivityEdge {
    r: f64,             // Correlation value
    uncertainty: f64,   // Uncertainty (SE)
    ci_lower: f64,      // 95% CI lower bound
    ci_upper: f64,      // 95% CI upper bound
    p_value: f64,       // P-value
}

fn edge_new() -> ConnectivityEdge {
    ConnectivityEdge {
        r: 0.0,
        uncertainty: 0.0,
        ci_lower: 0.0,
        ci_upper: 0.0,
        p_value: 1.0,
    }
}

// Connectivity matrix with uncertainty (small for demo)
struct ConnectivityMatrix {
    matrix: [[f64; 50]; 50],
    uncertainty: [[f64; 50]; 50],
    ci_lower: [[f64; 50]; 50],
    ci_upper: [[f64; 50]; 50],
    n_rois: i64,
    n_volumes_used: i64,
    mean_fd: f64,
}

fn connectivity_matrix_new() -> ConnectivityMatrix {
    ConnectivityMatrix {
        matrix: [[0.0; 50]; 50],
        uncertainty: [[0.0; 50]; 50],
        ci_lower: [[0.0; 50]; 50],
        ci_upper: [[0.0; 50]; 50],
        n_rois: 0,
        n_volumes_used: 0,
        mean_fd: 0.0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PEARSON CORRELATION WITH FISHER-Z CI
// ============================================================================

// Pearson correlation between two timeseries
fn pearson_correlation(x: [f64; 200], y: [f64; 200], n: i64) -> f64 {
    // Compute means
    var mean_x: f64 = 0.0
    var mean_y: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        mean_x = mean_x + x[i as usize]
        mean_y = mean_y + y[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    mean_x = mean_x / n as f64
    mean_y = mean_y / n as f64

    // Compute correlation
    var cov: f64 = 0.0
    var var_x: f64 = 0.0
    var var_y: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let dx = x[i as usize] - mean_x
        let dy = y[i as usize] - mean_y
        cov = cov + dx * dy
        var_x = var_x + dx * dx
        var_y = var_y + dy * dy
        i = i + 1
    }

    let denom = sqrt_f64(var_x * var_y)
    if denom > 1e-10 {
        cov / denom
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// fisher_z, fisher_z_inv, fisher_z_se defined in preprocess.sio

// Compute correlation with confidence interval
fn compute_fc_with_ci(x: [f64; 200], y: [f64; 200], n: i64) -> ConnectivityEdge {
    var edge = edge_new()

    edge.r = pearson_correlation(x, y, n)

    // Fisher z confidence interval
    let z = fisher_z(edge.r)
    let z_se = fisher_z_se(n)
    let z_lower = z - 1.96 * z_se
    let z_upper = z + 1.96 * z_se

    edge.ci_lower = fisher_z_inv(z_lower)
    edge.ci_upper = fisher_z_inv(z_upper)
    edge.uncertainty = (edge.ci_upper - edge.ci_lower) / 2.0

    // P-value approximation
    let z_stat = abs_f64(z) / z_se
    edge.p_value = 2.0 * (1.0 - normal_cdf(z_stat))

    edge
}

// Standard normal CDF approximation
fn normal_cdf(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.2316419 * abs_f64(x))
    let d = 0.3989422804014327  // 1/sqrt_f64(2*pi)
    let p = d * exp_f64(-x * x / 2.0) *
            (0.319381530 * t - 0.356563782 * t * t + 1.781477937 * t * t * t -
             1.821255978 * t * t * t * t + 1.330274429 * t * t * t * t * t)

    if x > 0.0 {
        1.0 - p
    } else {
        p
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PHASE-LOCKING VALUE (PLV)
// ============================================================================

// Phase-locking value between two phase series
fn compute_plv(phase_x: [f64; 200], phase_y: [f64; 200], n: i64) -> f64 {
    // PLV = |mean(exp_f64(i * (phase_x - phase_y)))|
    var sum_cos: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_sin: f64 = 0.0

    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < n {
        let diff = phase_x[t as usize] - phase_y[t as usize]
        sum_cos = sum_cos + cos_f64(diff)
        sum_sin = sum_sin + sin_f64(diff)
        t = t + 1
    }

    sqrt_f64(sum_cos * sum_cos + sum_sin * sum_sin) / n as f64
}

// PLV with significance test (Rayleigh test)
fn compute_plv_with_pvalue(phase_x: [f64; 200], phase_y: [f64; 200], n: i64) -> ConnectivityEdge {
    var edge = edge_new()

    edge.r = compute_plv(phase_x, phase_y, n)

    // Rayleigh test for circular uniformity
    let rayleigh_z = n as f64 * edge.r * edge.r
    edge.p_value = exp_f64(-rayleigh_z)

    // Uncertainty from sample size
    edge.uncertainty = 1.0 / sqrt_f64(n as f64)
    edge.ci_lower = edge.r - 1.96 * edge.uncertainty
    edge.ci_upper = edge.r + 1.96 * edge.uncertainty

    // Clamp to valid range
    if edge.ci_lower < 0.0 { edge.ci_lower = 0.0 }
    if edge.ci_upper > 1.0 { edge.ci_upper = 1.0 }

    edge
}

// ============================================================================
// GRAPH METRICS WITH UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================

// Graph metric with uncertainty
struct GraphMetric {
    value: f64,
    uncertainty: f64,
    ci_lower: f64,
    ci_upper: f64,
    status: EpistemicStatus,
}

fn graph_metric_new() -> GraphMetric {
    GraphMetric {
        value: 0.0,
        uncertainty: 0.0,
        ci_lower: 0.0,
        ci_upper: 0.0,
        status: EpistemicStatus::Provisional,
    }
}

// Node degree (weighted sum of connections)
fn node_degree_weighted(
    conn_row: [f64; 50],
    unc_row: [f64; 50],
    n_nodes: i64,
    threshold: f64
) -> GraphMetric {
    var metric = graph_metric_new()
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var sum_unc_sq: f64 = 0.0

    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < n_nodes {
        if conn_row[j as usize] > threshold {
            sum = sum + conn_row[j as usize]
            sum_unc_sq = sum_unc_sq + unc_row[j as usize] * unc_row[j as usize]
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    metric.value = sum
    metric.uncertainty = sqrt_f64(sum_unc_sq)
    metric.ci_lower = sum - 1.96 * metric.uncertainty
    metric.ci_upper = sum + 1.96 * metric.uncertainty

    if metric.uncertainty < metric.value * 0.1 {
        metric.status = EpistemicStatus::Verified
    } else if metric.uncertainty < metric.value * 0.3 {
        metric.status = EpistemicStatus::Provisional
    } else {
        metric.status = EpistemicStatus::Uncertain
    }

    metric
}

// Mean connectivity strength
fn mean_connectivity(matrix: [[f64; 50]; 50], n_rois: i64) -> GraphMetric {
    var metric = graph_metric_new()
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_rois {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n_rois {
            sum = sum + matrix[i as usize][j as usize]
            count = count + 1
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if count > 0 {
        metric.value = sum / count as f64
    }

    // Approximate SE for mean correlation
    metric.uncertainty = 0.1  // Placeholder
    metric.ci_lower = metric.value - 1.96 * metric.uncertainty
    metric.ci_upper = metric.value + 1.96 * metric.uncertainty
    metric.status = EpistemicStatus::Provisional

    metric
}

// ============================================================================
// MOTION-AWARE UNCERTAINTY
// ============================================================================

// Inflate uncertainty based on motion quality
fn inflate_uncertainty_for_motion(
    base_uncertainty: f64,
    mean_fd: f64,
    scrub_fraction: f64
) -> f64 {
    // 2x per mm mean FD + 50% max from scrubbing
    let fd_factor = 1.0 + mean_fd * 2.0
    let scrub_factor = 1.0 + scrub_fraction * 0.5
    base_uncertainty * fd_factor * scrub_factor
}

// Determine epistemic status from uncertainty
fn status_from_uncertainty(r: f64, uncertainty: f64) -> EpistemicStatus {
    let rel_unc = if abs_f64(r) > 0.01 { uncertainty / abs_f64(r) } else { uncertainty }

    if rel_unc < 0.1 {
        EpistemicStatus::Verified
    } else if rel_unc < 0.3 {
        EpistemicStatus::Provisional
    } else {
        EpistemicStatus::Uncertain
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// BRIDGE: FC → EPISTEMIC ORC PIPELINE
// ============================================================================
//
// Connects functional connectivity computation to graph::epistemic_curvature.
// Takes an FC matrix with Fisher-z CIs, thresholds to binary graph, and
// propagates uncertainty into the cost matrix for epistemic ORC.

// Result of FC-to-graph conversion with uncertainty propagation
struct FCtoGraphResult {
    // Adjacency list (undirected)
    adj: [[usize; 50]; 50],
    adj_len: [usize; 50],
    n_rois: usize,

    // Cost uncertainty matrix for ORC
    // sigma_d(i,j) = uncertainty on BFS distance due to edge-existence uncertainty
    cost_uncertainty: [[f64; 50]; 50],

    // Edge classification
    n_certain_edges: usize,    // |r| - threshold > sigma_r
    n_uncertain_edges: usize,  // |r| - threshold < sigma_r (near threshold)
    n_total_edges: usize,

    // Per-edge correlations and CIs (for provenance)
    edge_rs: [f64; 1250],        // max 50*50/2 edges
    edge_sigmas: [f64; 1250],
    edge_u: [usize; 1250],
    edge_v: [usize; 1250],
    n_stored_edges: usize,
}

fn fc_to_graph_new() -> FCtoGraphResult {
    FCtoGraphResult {
        adj: [[0; 50]; 50],
        adj_len: [0; 50],
        n_rois: 0,
        cost_uncertainty: [[0.0; 50]; 50],
        n_certain_edges: 0,
        n_uncertain_edges: 0,
        n_total_edges: 0,
        edge_rs: [0.0; 1250],
        edge_sigmas: [0.0; 1250],
        edge_u: [0; 1250],
        edge_v: [0; 1250],
        n_stored_edges: 0,
    }
}

// Convert FC matrix to binary graph with epistemic edge uncertainty
//
// For each pair (i,j):
//   if |r_ij| > threshold: add edge
//   Classify edge as "certain" (|r|-threshold > sigma_r) or "uncertain"
//
// Cost uncertainty for BFS distance d(i,j):
//   sigma_d ≈ sqrt(d * frac_uncertain)
//   where frac_uncertain = n_uncertain / n_total
//   (each hop has probability frac_uncertain of being wrong)
fn build_epistemic_graph(
    fc_matrix: &ConnectivityMatrix,
    threshold: f64,
    motion_mean_fd: f64,
    scrub_fraction: f64
) -> FCtoGraphResult {
    var result = fc_to_graph_new()
    let n = fc_matrix.n_rois
    result.n_rois = n as usize

    // Phase 1: Build adjacency and classify edges
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            let r = fc_matrix.matrix[i as usize][j as usize]
            let abs_r = abs_f64(r)

            if abs_r > threshold {
                // Add edge
                let ui = i as usize
                let uj = j as usize
                let li = result.adj_len[ui]
                let lj = result.adj_len[uj]
                result.adj[ui][li] = uj
                result.adj[uj][lj] = ui
                result.adj_len[ui] = li + 1
                result.adj_len[uj] = lj + 1

                // Get base uncertainty and inflate for motion
                let base_sigma = fc_matrix.uncertainty[ui][uj]
                let sigma_r = inflate_uncertainty_for_motion(
                    base_sigma, motion_mean_fd, scrub_fraction
                )

                // Classify: certain if well above threshold
                if abs_r - threshold > sigma_r {
                    result.n_certain_edges = result.n_certain_edges + 1
                } else {
                    result.n_uncertain_edges = result.n_uncertain_edges + 1
                }
                result.n_total_edges = result.n_total_edges + 1

                // Store edge provenance
                if result.n_stored_edges < 1250 {
                    let idx = result.n_stored_edges
                    result.edge_rs[idx] = r
                    result.edge_sigmas[idx] = sigma_r
                    result.edge_u[idx] = ui
                    result.edge_v[idx] = uj
                    result.n_stored_edges = result.n_stored_edges + 1
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Phase 2: BFS distance matrix (for cost uncertainty computation)
    let frac_uncertain = if result.n_total_edges > 0 {
        (result.n_uncertain_edges as f64) / (result.n_total_edges as f64)
    } else { 0.0 }

    // BFS from each source node
    var source: usize = 0
    while source < (n as usize) {
        var dist: [i64; 50] = [-1; 50]
        dist[source] = 0
        var queue: [usize; 50] = [0; 50]
        queue[0] = source
        var head: usize = 0
        var tail: usize = 1

        while head < tail {
            let u = queue[head]
            head = head + 1
            var k: usize = 0
            while k < result.adj_len[u] {
                let v = result.adj[u][k]
                if dist[v] == -1 {
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + 1
                    queue[tail] = v
                    tail = tail + 1
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
        }

        // Set cost uncertainty: sigma_d(source, target) = sqrt(d * frac_uncertain)
        var target: usize = 0
        while target < (n as usize) {
            if dist[target] > 0 {
                result.cost_uncertainty[source][target] =
                    sqrt_f64((dist[target] as f64) * frac_uncertain)
            }
            target = target + 1
        }

        source = source + 1
    }

    result
}

// Compute mean ORC with uncertainty from an FC matrix
// This is the main entry point for fMRI → curvature analysis
//
// Returns: (mean_kappa, sigma_kappa, gci, eta, clustering)
struct FCCurvatureSummary {
    mean_kappa: f64,
    sigma_mean_kappa: f64,
    gci: f64,
    eta: f64,
    clustering: f64,
    n_nodes: usize,
    n_edges: usize,
    n_uncertain_edges: usize,
    frac_uncertain: f64,
}

fn compute_fc_curvature_summary(
    fc_matrix: &ConnectivityMatrix,
    threshold: f64,
    motion_mean_fd: f64,
    scrub_fraction: f64
) -> FCCurvatureSummary {
    let graph = build_epistemic_graph(fc_matrix, threshold, motion_mean_fd, scrub_fraction)

    // Compute eta = mean_k^2 / N
    var total_deg: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < graph.n_rois {
        total_deg = total_deg + graph.adj_len[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_k = if graph.n_rois > 0 {
        (total_deg as f64) / (graph.n_rois as f64)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let eta = if graph.n_rois > 0 {
        mean_k * mean_k / (graph.n_rois as f64)
    } else { 0.0 }

    let frac_unc = if graph.n_total_edges > 0 {
        (graph.n_uncertain_edges as f64) / (graph.n_total_edges as f64)
    } else { 0.0 }

    FCCurvatureSummary {
        mean_kappa: 0.0,          // Filled by epistemic_curvature pipeline
        sigma_mean_kappa: 0.0,
        gci: 1.0 - frac_unc,     // Approximate GCI from edge certainty fraction
        eta: eta,
        clustering: 0.0,         // Filled by graph metrics computation
        n_nodes: graph.n_rois,
        n_edges: graph.n_total_edges,
        n_uncertain_edges: graph.n_uncertain_edges,
        frac_uncertain: frac_unc,
    }
}
