// === FILE: stdlib/genomics/embedding.sio ===
// stdlib/genomics/embedding.sio — Sequence Embedding & Motif Discovery
//
// k-mer frequency profiles, position weight matrices (PWMs), and motif
// scanning for DNA/RNA sequences. All operations use the GF(4) base
// encoding (A=0, C=1, G=2, T=3) from genomics/types.sio.
//
// Epistemic uncertainty on motif scores is derived from PWM entropy:
// high-entropy columns contribute less information, increasing score
// uncertainty.
//
// SOTA: Nucleotide Transformer v3 (2026): single-base tokenization, 1Mb context
//       BMFM-DNA (2025): SNP-aware DNA foundation model
//       METAGENE-1 (2025): 7B params, 1.5T bp metagenomic pretraining
//
// References:
//   - Stormo (2000): "DNA binding sites: representation and discovery"
//   - Altschul+ (2009): "PSI-BLAST position-specific scoring matrices"
//   - Lin (1991): "Divergence measures based on Shannon entropy"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn emb_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn emb_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn emb_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn emb_log2(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    emb_ln(x) / 0.6931471805599453
}

// =============================================================================
// k-mer Profile
// =============================================================================
// A k-mer profile counts all subsequences of length k in a DNA sequence.
// For k=1: 4 bins (A,C,G,T). For k=2: 16 bins. k=3: 64. k=4: 256.

struct KmerProfile {
    counts: [f64; 256],     // max 4^4 = 256 k-mers
    n_kmers: i32,           // 4^k
    k: i32,
    total: f64,
}

// Compute k-mer index from a subsequence of bases (each 0-3)
fn kmer_index(seq: &[i32; 4096], start: i32, k: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var idx: i64 = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < k {
        idx = idx * 4 + (seq[start + i]) as i64
        i = i + 1
    }
    idx as i32
}

fn kmer_count(seq: &[i32; 4096], seq_len: i32, k: i32) -> KmerProfile with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var n_kmers: i64 = 1
    var i = 0
    while i < k { n_kmers = n_kmers * 4; i = i + 1 }

    var profile = KmerProfile {
        counts: [0.0; 256],
        n_kmers: n_kmers as i32,
        k: k,
        total: 0.0,
    }

    var pos = 0
    while pos <= seq_len - k {
        let idx = kmer_index(seq, pos, k)
        if idx >= 0 {
            if idx < 256 {
                profile.counts[idx] = profile.counts[idx] + 1.0
                profile.total = profile.total + 1.0
            }
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    profile
}

fn kmer_normalize(profile: &!KmerProfile) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if profile.total <= 0.0 { return }
    var i = 0
    while i < profile.n_kmers {
        profile.counts[i] = profile.counts[i] / profile.total
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// k-mer Distance (Jensen-Shannon Divergence)
// =============================================================================
// JSD(P||Q) = 0.5 * KLD(P||M) + 0.5 * KLD(Q||M), where M = 0.5*(P+Q)
// Returns sqrt(JSD) which is a proper metric.

fn kmer_distance(a: &KmerProfile, b: &KmerProfile) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a.k != b.k { return 0.0 - 1.0 }  // incompatible

    var jsd = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.n_kmers {
        let p = a.counts[i]
        let q = b.counts[i]
        let m = 0.5 * (p + q)

        if m > 1.0e-15 {
            if p > 1.0e-15 {
                jsd = jsd + 0.5 * p * emb_log2(p / m)
            }
            if q > 1.0e-15 {
                jsd = jsd + 0.5 * q * emb_log2(q / m)
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    emb_sqrt(if jsd > 0.0 { jsd } else { 0.0 })
}

// =============================================================================
// Position Weight Matrix (PWM)
// =============================================================================
// A PWM represents a DNA binding motif as a matrix of log-odds scores.
// Rows = positions (up to 256), Columns = 4 bases (A, C, G, T)
// Weight[pos][base] = log2(freq[pos][base] / background)

struct PWM {
    weights: [f64; 1024],   // n_positions * 4, row-major
    n_positions: i32,
    info_content: [f64; 256],  // information content per position (bits)
}

struct MotifHit {
    position: i32,
    score: f64,
    u_score: f64,           // uncertainty from low-info columns
    strand: i32,            // 1 = forward, -1 = reverse complement
}

struct MotifResult {
    hits: [MotifHit; 512],
    n_hits: i32,
    threshold: f64,
}

// Build PWM from aligned sequences
fn pwm_from_alignment(
    seqs: &[[i32; 256]; 128],
    n_seqs: i32,
    seq_len: i32,
) -> PWM with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pwm = PWM {
        weights: [0.0; 1024],
        n_positions: seq_len,
        info_content: [0.0; 256],
    }

    // Count frequencies at each position
    var pos = 0
    while pos < seq_len {
        var base_counts: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
        var s = 0
        while s < n_seqs {
            let b = seqs[s][pos]
            if b >= 0 {
                if b < 4 {
                    base_counts[b] = base_counts[b] + 1.0
                }
            }
            s = s + 1
        }

        // Add pseudocount (Laplace smoothing)
        var total = 0.0
        var b2 = 0
        while b2 < 4 {
            base_counts[b2] = base_counts[b2] + 0.5
            total = total + base_counts[b2]
            b2 = b2 + 1
        }

        // Compute log-odds and information content
        let bg = 0.25  // uniform background
        var entropy = 0.0
        var b3 = 0
        while b3 < 4 {
            let freq = base_counts[b3] / total
            pwm.weights[pos * 4 + b3] = emb_log2(freq / bg)
            if freq > 1.0e-15 {
                entropy = entropy - freq * emb_log2(freq)
            }
            b3 = b3 + 1
        }

        // Info content = 2 - H(position) bits
        pwm.info_content[pos] = 2.0 - entropy
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    pwm
}

// Add pseudocount to existing PWM (re-normalizes)
fn pwm_add_pseudocount(pwm: &!PWM, pseudo: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pos = 0
    while pos < pwm.n_positions {
        var b = 0
        while b < 4 {
            // Convert back from log-odds, add pseudo, re-log
            let w = pwm.weights[pos * 4 + b]
            // Approximate: just shift weights slightly toward 0
            pwm.weights[pos * 4 + b] = w * (1.0 - pseudo) + 0.0 * pseudo
            b = b + 1
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }
}

// Score a single position in a sequence against the PWM
fn pwm_score_position(
    pwm: &PWM,
    seq: &[i32; 4096],
    pos: i32,
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var score = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < pwm.n_positions {
        let base = seq[pos + i]
        if base >= 0 {
            if base < 4 {
                score = score + pwm.weights[i * 4 + base]
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    score
}

// Uncertainty of a score based on PWM information content
fn pwm_score_uncertainty(pwm: &PWM) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Low-info positions contribute more uncertainty
    var total_info = 0.0
    var max_info = 2.0 * (pwm.n_positions as f64)  // max 2 bits per position
    var i = 0
    while i < pwm.n_positions {
        total_info = total_info + pwm.info_content[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if max_info > 0.0 {
        1.0 - total_info / max_info  // 0 = certain, 1 = random
    } else {
        1.0
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Motif Scanning
// =============================================================================

fn pwm_scan(
    pwm: &PWM,
    seq: &[i32; 4096],
    seq_len: i32,
    threshold: f64,
) -> MotifResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = MotifResult {
        hits: [MotifHit { position: 0, score: 0.0, u_score: 0.0, strand: 0 }; 512],
        n_hits: 0,
        threshold: threshold,
    }

    let u = pwm_score_uncertainty(pwm)

    var pos = 0
    while pos <= seq_len - pwm.n_positions {
        let score = pwm_score_position(pwm, seq, pos)
        if score >= threshold {
            if result.n_hits < 512 {
                result.hits[result.n_hits] = MotifHit {
                    position: pos,
                    score: score,
                    u_score: u * emb_abs(score),
                    strand: 1,
                }
                result.n_hits = result.n_hits + 1
            }
        }
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Sequence Embedding via k-mer feature hashing
// =============================================================================
// Project k-mer frequencies into a lower-dimensional space using
// deterministic hash-based projection (no randomness needed).

struct SeqEmbedding {
    vector: [f64; 64],
    u_vector: [f64; 64],    // uncertainty per dimension
    dim: i32,
}

fn seq_embed_kmer(
    seq: &[i32; 4096],
    seq_len: i32,
    dim: i32,
) -> SeqEmbedding with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var emb = SeqEmbedding {
        vector: [0.0; 64],
        u_vector: [0.0; 64],
        dim: dim,
    }

    // Use k=3 (64 trimers) projected into dim dimensions
    let profile = kmer_count(seq, seq_len, 3)

    // Hash-based projection: kmer_idx mod dim determines target dimension
    // Sign: kmer_idx / dim determines +/-
    var i = 0
    while i < profile.n_kmers {
        let target = i % dim
        let sign = if (i / dim) % 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
        emb.vector[target] = emb.vector[target] + sign * profile.counts[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Normalize to unit vector and compute uncertainty
    var norm = 0.0
    var j = 0
    while j < dim {
        norm = norm + emb.vector[j] * emb.vector[j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    norm = emb_sqrt(norm)

    if norm > 1.0e-15 {
        var k = 0
        while k < dim {
            emb.vector[k] = emb.vector[k] / norm
            // Uncertainty from counting: sqrt(count) / total
            emb.u_vector[k] = 1.0 / emb_sqrt(profile.total + 1.0)
            k = k + 1
        }
    }

    emb
}

// Cosine similarity between two embeddings
fn seq_cosine_similarity(a: &SeqEmbedding, b: &SeqEmbedding) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dot = 0.0
    var na = 0.0
    var nb = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.dim {
        dot = dot + a.vector[i] * b.vector[i]
        na = na + a.vector[i] * a.vector[i]
        nb = nb + b.vector[i] * b.vector[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let denom = emb_sqrt(na) * emb_sqrt(nb)
    if denom > 1.0e-15 { dot / denom } else { 0.0 }
}

// Euclidean distance between embeddings
fn seq_embedding_distance(a: &SeqEmbedding, b: &SeqEmbedding) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.dim {
        let d = a.vector[i] - b.vector[i]
        sum_sq = sum_sq + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    emb_sqrt(sum_sq)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/information.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry/information.sio — Information Geometry on Statistical Manifolds
//
// Fisher-Rao metric, natural gradient, geodesics on manifolds of probability
// distributions. The correct geometry for optimization on parameter spaces.
//
// SOTA: GSI 2025 (Saint-Malo): "From Classical to Quantum Information Geometry"
//       Geomstats (2023-2025): Computations on manifolds
//       Amari (2016): "Information Geometry and Its Applications"
//
// Theory:
//   A statistical model {p(x|theta)} is a manifold M with coordinates theta.
//   The Fisher information matrix g_ij(theta) = E[d_i log p * d_j log p]
//   defines a Riemannian metric. The natural gradient is:
//     grad_nat = g^{-1} * grad_euclidean
//   which gives the steepest descent direction ON THE MANIFOLD.
//
// Why it matters:
//   Euclidean gradient descent on probability distributions is WRONG.
//   It treats the parameter space as flat, but probability distributions
//   live on curved manifolds. Natural gradient respects the geometry.

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn sqrt_val(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn ln_val(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn exp_val(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2_c = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2_c
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2_c
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 { var i = 0; while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    else { var i = 0; while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Statistical Manifold
// =============================================================================

// A point on a statistical manifold with its Fisher information matrix
struct StatisticalManifold {
    params: [f64; 16],              // manifold coordinates (max 16 parameters)
    n_params: i32,
    fisher: [f64; 256],             // Fisher information matrix (16x16 max)
}

fn manifold_new(n: i32) -> StatisticalManifold {
    StatisticalManifold {
        params: [0.0; 16],
        n_params: n,
        fisher: [0.0; 256],
    }
}

// Access Fisher matrix element
fn fisher_get(m: &StatisticalManifold, i: i32, j: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    m.fisher[i * m.n_params + j]
}

fn fisher_set(m: &!StatisticalManifold, i: i32, j: i32, val: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    m.fisher[i * m.n_params + j] = val
}

// =============================================================================
// Fisher Information for Common Distributions
// =============================================================================

// Normal distribution: theta = (mu, sigma)
// Fisher matrix: [[1/sigma^2, 0], [0, 2/sigma^2]]
fn fisher_normal(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(2)
    m.params[0] = mu
    m.params[1] = sigma
    let s2 = sigma * sigma
    // F[0,0] = 1/sigma^2, F[0,1] = 0, F[1,0] = 0, F[1,1] = 2/sigma^2
    m.fisher[0] = 1.0 / s2
    m.fisher[1] = 0.0
    m.fisher[2] = 0.0
    m.fisher[3] = 2.0 / s2
    return m
}

// Exponential distribution: theta = lambda
// Fisher matrix: [[1/lambda^2]]
fn fisher_exponential(lambda: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(1)
    m.params[0] = lambda
    m.fisher[0] = 1.0 / (lambda * lambda)
    return m
}

// Bernoulli distribution: theta = p
// Fisher matrix: [[1/(p*(1-p))]]
fn fisher_bernoulli(p: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(1)
    m.params[0] = p
    m.fisher[0] = 1.0 / (p * (1.0 - p))
    return m
}

// Gamma distribution: theta = (alpha, beta)
// Fisher[0,0] = trigamma(alpha), Fisher[1,1] = alpha/beta^2
// Fisher[0,1] = Fisher[1,0] = -1/beta
fn fisher_gamma(alpha: f64, beta_param: f64) -> StatisticalManifold with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m = manifold_new(2)
    m.params[0] = alpha
    m.params[1] = beta_param

    // Trigamma approximation: psi_1(x) ~ 1/x + 1/(2x^2) + 1/(6x^3) - ...
    var tx = alpha
    var shift: f64 = 0.0
    while tx < 8.0 { shift = shift + 1.0 / (tx * tx); tx = tx + 1.0 }
    let inv_t = 1.0 / tx
    let trigamma = inv_t + 0.5 * inv_t * inv_t + inv_t * inv_t * inv_t / 6.0 + shift

    m.fisher[0] = trigamma
    m.fisher[1] = 0.0 - 1.0 / beta_param
    m.fisher[2] = 0.0 - 1.0 / beta_param
    m.fisher[3] = alpha / (beta_param * beta_param)
    return m
}

// =============================================================================
// Natural Gradient
// =============================================================================
// g_nat = F^{-1} * g_euclidean
// For optimization on manifolds, this is the correct gradient direction.

// 2x2 matrix inverse (covers Normal, Gamma, etc.)
fn fisher_inverse_2x2(m: &StatisticalManifold) -> [f64; 4] with Mut, Panic {
    let a = m.fisher[0]
    let b = m.fisher[1]
    let c = m.fisher[2]
    let d = m.fisher[3]
    let det = a * d - b * c
    var inv: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    inv[0] = d / det
    inv[1] = (0.0 - b) / det
    inv[2] = (0.0 - c) / det
    inv[3] = a / det
    return inv
}

// Natural gradient for 2-parameter manifold
fn natural_gradient_2d(
    m: &StatisticalManifold,
    euclidean_grad: &[f64; 2],
) -> [f64; 2] with Panic, Mut {
    let inv = fisher_inverse_2x2(m)
    var nat_grad: [f64; 2] = [0.0; 2]
    nat_grad[0] = inv[0] * euclidean_grad[0] + inv[1] * euclidean_grad[1]
    nat_grad[1] = inv[2] * euclidean_grad[0] + inv[3] * euclidean_grad[1]
    return nat_grad
}

// General natural gradient via Cholesky solve (for n_params <= 16)
fn natural_gradient(
    m: &StatisticalManifold,
    euclidean_grad: &[f64; 16],
    result: &![f64; 16],
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = m.n_params

    // Cholesky decomposition: F = L * L^T
    var lower: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j <= i {
            var sum: f64 = 0.0
            if i == j {
                var k = 0
                while k < j {
                    let l_jk = lower[j * n + k]
                    sum = sum + l_jk * l_jk
                    k = k + 1
                }
                lower[j * n + j] = sqrt_val(m.fisher[j * n + j] - sum)
            } else {
                var k = 0
                while k < j {
                    sum = sum + lower[i * n + k] * lower[j * n + k]
                    k = k + 1
                }
                lower[i * n + j] = (m.fisher[i * n + j] - sum) / lower[j * n + j]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Forward substitution: L * y = g
    var y: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k < i { s = s + lower[i * n + k] * y[k]; k = k + 1 }
        y[i] = (euclidean_grad[i] - s) / lower[i * n + i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution: L^T * x = y
    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var k = i + 1
        while k < n { s = s + lower[k * n + i] * result[k]; k = k + 1 }
        result[i] = (y[i] - s) / lower[i * n + i]
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// KL Divergence via Fisher Metric (local approximation)
// =============================================================================
// KL(p_theta || p_{theta+d}) ~ 0.5 * d^T * F * d
// Valid for small perturbations d

fn fisher_kl_local(
    m: &StatisticalManifold,
    delta: &[f64; 16],
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = m.n_params
    var kl: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            kl = kl + delta[i] * m.fisher[i * n + j] * delta[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0.5 * kl
}

// =============================================================================
// Geodesic Distance (approximate via shooting)
// =============================================================================
// Geodesic equation: d^2 theta^k / dt^2 + Gamma^k_{ij} dtheta^i/dt dtheta^j/dt = 0
// We approximate via the local Fisher metric: d ~ sqrt(delta^T F delta)

fn fisher_distance(
    m1: &StatisticalManifold,
    m2: &StatisticalManifold,
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var delta: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var i = 0
    while i < m1.n_params {
        delta[i] = m2.params[i] - m1.params[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Use m1's Fisher metric as the local metric
    let kl_sq = fisher_kl_local(m1, &delta)
    sqrt_val(2.0 * kl_sq)
}

// =============================================================================
// Natural Gradient Descent Step
// =============================================================================

fn natural_gradient_step(
    m: &!StatisticalManifold,
    euclidean_grad: &[f64; 16],
    learning_rate: f64,
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nat_grad: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    natural_gradient(m, euclidean_grad, &!nat_grad)
    var i = 0
    while i < m.n_params {
        m.params[i] = m.params[i] - learning_rate * nat_grad[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/geometry/types.sio ===
// stdlib/geometry/types.sio
//
// Basic geometry types with f64 coordinates.

struct Point2D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

fn point2d_new(x: f64, y: f64) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: x, y: y }
}

fn point2d_add(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: a.x + b.x, y: a.y + b.y }
}

fn point2d_sub(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> Point2D {
    Point2D { x: a.x - b.x, y: a.y - b.y }
}

fn point2d_dot(a: Point2D, b: Point2D) -> f64 {
    a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y
}

struct Point3D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64,
}

fn point3d_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn point3d_add(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: a.x + b.x, y: a.y + b.y, z: a.z + b.z }
}

fn point3d_sub(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D { x: a.x - b.x, y: a.y - b.y, z: a.z - b.z }
}

fn point3d_dot(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> f64 {
    a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z
}

fn point3d_cross(a: Point3D, b: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D {
        x: a.y * b.z - a.z * b.y,
        y: a.z * b.x - a.x * b.z,
        z: a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x,
    }
}

// 3x3 matrix stored as 9 f64 fields
struct Matrix3 {
    m00: f64, m01: f64, m02: f64,
    m10: f64, m11: f64, m12: f64,
    m20: f64, m21: f64, m22: f64,
}

fn matrix3_identity() -> Matrix3 {
    Matrix3 {
        m00: 1.0, m01: 0.0, m02: 0.0,
        m10: 0.0, m11: 1.0, m12: 0.0,
        m20: 0.0, m21: 0.0, m22: 1.0,
    }
}

fn matrix3_mul_vec(m: Matrix3, v: Point3D) -> Point3D {
    Point3D {
        x: m.m00 * v.x + m.m01 * v.y + m.m02 * v.z,
        y: m.m10 * v.x + m.m11 * v.y + m.m12 * v.z,
        z: m.m20 * v.x + m.m21 * v.y + m.m22 * v.z,
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/gpu/tilelang.sio ===
// stdlib/gpu/tilelang.sio — Dataflow/Scheduling Separation for GPU Kernels
//
// Separates WHAT to compute (dataflow specification) from HOW to compute it
// (scheduling policy). This enables:
//   1. Writing kernels in terms of tiles and data movement
//   2. Independently tuning scheduling parameters
//   3. Auto-tuning by searching the scheduling space
//
// SOTA: TileLang (Jan 2025): 98% of FlashMLA performance in ~70 lines
//       — Separation of dataflow and scheduling
//       — Multi-backend: NVIDIA, AMD, Apple Metal
//
//       ParallelKittens (Stanford, Nov 2025):
//       — Generalizes tile-based programming to multi-GPU
//
//       ML-Triton (Mar 2025):
//       — Multi-level compilation: workgroup → warp → intrinsic
//
// References:
//   Zheng et al. (2020): "Ansor: Generating High-Performance Tensor Programs"
//   Ragan-Kelley et al. (2013): "Halide: Decoupling Algorithms from Schedules"

// =============================================================================
// Tile Specification — WHAT to compute
// =============================================================================

// A tile is a rectangular block of data processed as a unit
struct BlockSpec {
    blk_m: i32,    // tile height
    blk_n: i32,    // tile width
    blk_k: i32,    // reduction dimension tile size
}

fn block_spec_new(m: i32, n: i32, k: i32) -> BlockSpec {
    BlockSpec { blk_m: m, blk_n: n, blk_k: k }
}

// Common tile sizes for different operations
fn block_spec_matmul() -> BlockSpec { BlockSpec { blk_m: 128, blk_n: 128, blk_k: 32 } }
fn block_spec_attention() -> BlockSpec { BlockSpec { blk_m: 64, blk_n: 64, blk_k: 64 } }
fn block_spec_elementwise() -> BlockSpec { BlockSpec { blk_m: 256, blk_n: 1, blk_k: 1 } }
fn block_spec_reduction() -> BlockSpec { BlockSpec { blk_m: 1024, blk_n: 1, blk_k: 1 } }

// =============================================================================
// Schedule — HOW to compute it
// =============================================================================

// Thread block configuration
struct BlockConfig {
    dim_x: i32,     // threads per block (x dimension)
    dim_y: i32,     // threads per block (y dimension)
    dim_z: i32,     // threads per block (z dimension)
}

// Memory configuration
enum MemoryLevel {
    Global,          // HBM/DRAM (slow, large)
    Shared,          // shared memory (fast, limited)
    Register,        // registers (fastest, most limited)
}

struct MemoryConfig {
    shared_mem_bytes: i32,
    use_async_copy: bool,
    prefetch_depth: i32,      // how many tiles ahead to prefetch
}

// Loop optimization
struct LoopConfig {
    unroll_factor: i32,       // loop unrolling factor
    vectorize_width: i32,     // SIMD vectorization width
    pipeline_depth: i32,      // software pipelining depth
}

// Complete schedule
struct Schedule {
    block: BlockConfig,
    memory: MemoryConfig,
    loops: LoopConfig,
    n_warps: i32,             // warps per block (for warp-level primitives)
    use_tensor_cores: bool,
}

// =============================================================================
// Schedule Constructors
// =============================================================================

fn schedule_default() -> Schedule {
    Schedule {
        block: BlockConfig { dim_x: 128, dim_y: 1, dim_z: 1 },
        memory: MemoryConfig { shared_mem_bytes: 49152, use_async_copy: false, prefetch_depth: 1 },
        loops: LoopConfig { unroll_factor: 4, vectorize_width: 4, pipeline_depth: 1 },
        n_warps: 4,
        use_tensor_cores: false,
    }
}

fn schedule_matmul(m: i32, n: i32, k: i32) -> Schedule {
    Schedule {
        block: BlockConfig { dim_x: 16, dim_y: 16, dim_z: 1 },
        memory: MemoryConfig {
            shared_mem_bytes: 16 * 16 * 8 * 2,  // two tiles of f64
            use_async_copy: true,
            prefetch_depth: 2,
        },
        loops: LoopConfig { unroll_factor: 4, vectorize_width: 4, pipeline_depth: 2 },
        n_warps: 8,
        use_tensor_cores: false,
    }
}

fn schedule_attention(seq_len: i32, head_dim: i32) -> Schedule {
    // FlashAttention-style schedule: tile over sequence length
    let block_m = if seq_len > 128 { 128 } else { seq_len }
    Schedule {
        block: BlockConfig { dim_x: block_m, dim_y: 1, dim_z: 1 },
        memory: MemoryConfig {
            shared_mem_bytes: 98304,  // 96KB for Q, K, V tiles
            use_async_copy: true,
            prefetch_depth: 2,
        },
        loops: LoopConfig { unroll_factor: 8, vectorize_width: 4, pipeline_depth: 3 },
        n_warps: 4,
        use_tensor_cores: true,
    }
}

fn schedule_elementwise(n_elements: i32) -> Schedule {
    Schedule {
        block: BlockConfig { dim_x: 256, dim_y: 1, dim_z: 1 },
        memory: MemoryConfig { shared_mem_bytes: 0, use_async_copy: false, prefetch_depth: 0 },
        loops: LoopConfig { unroll_factor: 4, vectorize_width: 8, pipeline_depth: 1 },
        n_warps: 8,
        use_tensor_cores: false,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Kernel Descriptor — Combines dataflow + schedule
// =============================================================================

enum KernelOp {
    MatMul,          // C = A @ B
    Attention,       // softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V
    Elementwise,     // C = f(A)
    Reduction,       // y = reduce(A)
    Conv2D,          // convolution
    Scatter,         // scatter/gather
}

struct KernelDescriptor {
    op: KernelOp,
    block: BlockSpec,
    schedule: Schedule,
    // Problem dimensions
    m: i32, n: i32, k: i32,
    // Data type (0=f32, 1=f64, 2=f16, 3=bf16, 4=i32)
    dtype: i32,
}

fn kernel_matmul(m: i32, n: i32, k: i32) -> KernelDescriptor {
    KernelDescriptor {
        op: KernelOp::MatMul,
        block: block_spec_matmul(),
        schedule: schedule_matmul(m, n, k),
        m: m, n: n, k: k,
        dtype: 1,  // f64
    }
}

fn kernel_attention(seq_len: i32, head_dim: i32) -> KernelDescriptor {
    KernelDescriptor {
        op: KernelOp::Attention,
        block: block_spec_attention(),
        schedule: schedule_attention(seq_len, head_dim),
        m: seq_len, n: seq_len, k: head_dim,
        dtype: 1,
    }
}

fn kernel_elementwise(n: i32) -> KernelDescriptor {
    KernelDescriptor {
        op: KernelOp::Elementwise,
        block: block_spec_elementwise(),
        schedule: schedule_elementwise(n),
        m: n, n: 1, k: 1,
        dtype: 1,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Grid Configuration — Compute launch parameters
// =============================================================================

struct GridConfig {
    grid_x: i32,
    grid_y: i32,
    grid_z: i32,
    block_x: i32,
    block_y: i32,
    block_z: i32,
    shared_mem: i32,
}

fn compute_grid(desc: &KernelDescriptor) -> GridConfig with Panic {
    let grid_x = (desc.m + desc.block.blk_m - 1) / desc.block.blk_m
    let grid_y = (desc.n + desc.block.blk_n - 1) / desc.block.blk_n

    GridConfig {
        grid_x: grid_x,
        grid_y: grid_y,
        grid_z: 1,
        block_x: desc.schedule.block.dim_x,
        block_y: desc.schedule.block.dim_y,
        block_z: desc.schedule.block.dim_z,
        shared_mem: desc.schedule.memory.shared_mem_bytes,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Performance Model — Estimate kernel performance
// =============================================================================

struct PerfEstimate {
    flops: f64,              // total floating-point operations
    bytes_loaded: f64,       // total bytes loaded from global memory
    arithmetic_intensity: f64, // flops / bytes
    estimated_occupancy: f64,  // fraction of GPU utilized (0-1)
    is_compute_bound: bool,
    is_memory_bound: bool,
}

fn estimate_matmul_perf(m: i32, n: i32, k: i32, desc: &KernelDescriptor) -> PerfEstimate with Panic {
    let flops = 2.0 * (m as f64) * (n as f64) * (k as f64)
    let bytes_per_elem = if desc.dtype == 1 { 8.0 } else { 4.0 }
    let bytes = bytes_per_elem * ((m as f64) * (k as f64) + (k as f64) * (n as f64) + (m as f64) * (n as f64))
    let ai = flops / bytes

    // Rough occupancy estimate based on shared memory usage
    let max_shared = 163840.0  // 160KB on A100
    let shmem_fraction = (desc.schedule.memory.shared_mem_bytes as f64) / max_shared
    let occupancy = if shmem_fraction > 0.5 { 0.5 } else { 1.0 - shmem_fraction }

    PerfEstimate {
        flops: flops,
        bytes_loaded: bytes,
        arithmetic_intensity: ai,
        estimated_occupancy: occupancy,
        is_compute_bound: ai > 100.0,
        is_memory_bound: ai < 10.0,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/graph/algorithms.sio ===
// Graph Algorithms Module - BFS, shortest paths, connected components,
// weighted shortest paths (Dijkstra), PageRank, MST (Kruskal), topo sort.
//
// Epistemic edge weights: uncertainty propagated via GUM (quadrature) along paths.
// WeightedGraph uses a 32x32 adjacency matrix (max 32 nodes, 1024 entries).
//
// Ref: GUM (JCGM 100:2008) §5.1 — combined standard uncertainty by quadrature.

module graph::algorithms

// =============================================================================
// Constants
// =============================================================================

let INF_DIST: i64 = -1  // -1 = unreachable in unweighted results
let WGRAPH_MAX: i32 = 32
let WGRAPH_MAT: i32 = 1024  // 32*32

let F64_INF: f64 = 1.0e300  // sentinel "infinite" distance

// =============================================================================
// Unweighted BFS result (kept for backward compat with test_algorithms_e2e.sio)
// =============================================================================

pub struct BfsResult {
    pub distances: [i64],   // -1 means unreachable
    pub parents: [i64],     // -1 means no parent
    pub source: usize,
}

impl BfsResult {
    pub fn distance_to(&self, target: usize) -> i64 {
        if target < self.distances.len() {
            self.distances[target]
        } else {
            INF_DIST
        }
    }

    pub fn is_reachable(&self, target: usize) -> bool {
        target < self.distances.len() && self.distances[target] >= 0
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Breadth-First Search (unweighted, adjacency-list)
// =============================================================================

pub fn bfs(adj: &[[usize]], source: usize) -> BfsResult {
    let n = adj.len()
    var distances: [i64] = []
    var parents: [i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        distances.push(-1)
        parents.push(-1)
        i = i + 1
    }

    if source >= n {
        return BfsResult { distances, parents, source }
    }

    var queue: [usize] = []
    queue.push(source)
    distances[source] = 0

    var head: usize = 0
    while head < queue.len() {
        let u = queue[head]
        head = head + 1
        let neighbors = &adj[u]
        var j: usize = 0
        while j < neighbors.len() {
            let v = neighbors[j]
            if distances[v] == -1 {
                distances[v] = distances[u] + 1
                parents[v] = u as i64
                queue.push(v)
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }

    BfsResult { distances, parents, source }
}

pub fn shortest_path_distance(adj: &[[usize]], u: usize, v: usize) -> i64 {
    let result = bfs(adj, u)
    result.distance_to(v)
}

pub fn num_components(adj: &[[usize]]) -> usize {
    let n = adj.len()
    let unvisited: usize = n

    var labels: [usize] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        labels.push(unvisited)
        i = i + 1
    }

    var current_label: usize = 0
    var node: usize = 0

    while node < n {
        if labels[node] == unvisited {
            var queue: [usize] = []
            queue.push(node)
            labels[node] = current_label

            var head: usize = 0
            while head < queue.len() {
                let u = queue[head]
                head = head + 1
                let neighbors = &adj[u]
                var j: usize = 0
                while j < neighbors.len() {
                    let v = neighbors[j]
                    if labels[v] == unvisited {
                        labels[v] = current_label
                        queue.push(v)
                    }
                    j = j + 1
                }
            }
            current_label = current_label + 1
        }
        node = node + 1
    }

    var max_label: usize = 0
    i = 0
    while i < labels.len() {
        if labels[i] < labels.len() && labels[i] > max_label {
            max_label = labels[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if labels.len() == 0 { 0 } else { max_label + 1 }
}

pub fn is_connected(adj: &[[usize]]) -> bool {
    let n = adj.len()
    if n <= 1 { return true }
    let result = bfs(adj, 0)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        if result.distances[i] < 0 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

// =============================================================================
// WeightedGraph — 32×32 adjacency matrix with GUM uncertainty
// =============================================================================

pub struct WeightedGraph {
    pub weights: [f64; 1024],     // weights[i*32+j] = edge weight (0.0 = no edge)
    pub weight_unc: [f64; 1024],  // uncertainty on each edge weight
    pub n_nodes: i32,
    pub directed: i32,            // 0=undirected, 1=directed
}

// =============================================================================
// ShortestPathResult — Dijkstra output with GUM uncertainty on distances
// =============================================================================

pub struct ShortestPathResult {
    pub distances: [f64; 32],
    pub dist_unc: [f64; 32],      // GUM-propagated path uncertainty
    pub predecessors: [i32; 32],
    pub reachable: [i32; 32],     // 1=reachable, 0=not
}

// =============================================================================
// PageRankResult
// =============================================================================

pub struct PageRankResult {
    pub scores: [f64; 32],
    pub scores_unc: [f64; 32],
    pub n_iterations: i32,
    pub converged: i32,
}

// =============================================================================
// TopoSortResult
// =============================================================================

pub struct TopoSortResult {
    pub order: [i32; 32],     // topological order
    pub count: i32,           // nodes sorted (-1 = cycle detected)
}

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (must precede callers)
// =============================================================================

// Newton-Raphson sqrt (20 iterations)
fn w_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn w_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// Union-Find for Kruskal — flat arrays, max 32 nodes
fn uf_find(parent: &[i32; 32], x: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = x
    var steps = 0
    while steps < 32 {
        let p = parent[cur as usize]
        if p == cur { return cur }
        cur = p
        steps = steps + 1
    }
    cur
}

fn uf_union(parent: &![i32; 32], rank: &![i32; 32], a: i32, b: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ra = uf_find(parent, a)
    let rb = uf_find(parent, b)
    if ra == rb { return }
    if rank[ra as usize] < rank[rb as usize] {
        parent[ra as usize] = rb
    } else if rank[ra as usize] > rank[rb as usize] {
        parent[rb as usize] = ra
    } else {
        parent[rb as usize] = ra
        rank[ra as usize] = rank[ra as usize] + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Graph Construction
// =============================================================================

pub fn wgraph_new(n: i32, directed: i32) -> WeightedGraph with Mut {
    WeightedGraph {
        weights:    [0.0; 1024],
        weight_unc: [0.0; 1024],
        n_nodes:    n,
        directed:   directed,
    }
}

pub fn wgraph_add_edge(g: WeightedGraph, from: i32, to: i32, weight: f64, unc: f64) -> WeightedGraph with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g2 = g
    let idx = (from * WGRAPH_MAX + to) as usize
    g2.weights[idx]    = weight
    g2.weight_unc[idx] = unc
    if g2.directed == 0 {
        let idx2 = (to * WGRAPH_MAX + from) as usize
        g2.weights[idx2]    = weight
        g2.weight_unc[idx2] = unc
    }
    g2
}

// =============================================================================
// BFS on WeightedGraph — hop-count distances, no uncertainty on hops
// =============================================================================

pub fn graph_bfs(g: &WeightedGraph, source: i32) -> ShortestPathResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var dist:  [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var dunc:  [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var pred:  [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var reach: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]

    let n = g.n_nodes
    // initialise to "unreachable"
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        dist[i as usize]  = F64_INF
        dunc[i as usize]  = 0.0
        pred[i as usize]  = -1
        reach[i as usize] = 0
        i = i + 1
    }

    if source < 0 || source >= n {
        return ShortestPathResult {
            distances: dist, dist_unc: dunc,
            predecessors: pred, reachable: reach,
        }
    }

    // BFS queue — fixed array, max 32 entries
    var queue: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var qhead: i32 = 0
    var qtail: i32 = 0

    dist[source as usize]  = 0.0
    reach[source as usize] = 1
    queue[qtail as usize] = source
    qtail = qtail + 1

    while qhead < qtail {
        let u = queue[qhead as usize]
        qhead = qhead + 1
        var v: i32 = 0
        while v < n {
            let idx = (u * WGRAPH_MAX + v) as usize
            if g.weights[idx] > 0.0 && reach[v as usize] == 0 {
                dist[v as usize]  = dist[u as usize] + 1.0
                reach[v as usize] = 1
                pred[v as usize]  = u
                if qtail < WGRAPH_MAX {
                    queue[qtail as usize] = v
                    qtail = qtail + 1
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
    }

    ShortestPathResult {
        distances: dist, dist_unc: dunc,
        predecessors: pred, reachable: reach,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Connected components on WeightedGraph (undirected)
// =============================================================================

pub fn graph_dfs_connected(g: &WeightedGraph) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n_nodes
    var visited: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var components: i32 = 0

    var start: i32 = 0
    while start < n {
        if visited[start as usize] == 0 {
            components = components + 1
            // iterative DFS via stack (fixed array)
            var stack: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
            var stop: i32 = 0
            stack[stop as usize] = start
            stop = stop + 1
            while stop > 0 {
                stop = stop - 1
                let u = stack[stop as usize]
                if visited[u as usize] == 0 {
                    visited[u as usize] = 1
                    var v: i32 = 0
                    while v < n {
                        let idx = (u * WGRAPH_MAX + v) as usize
                        if g.weights[idx] > 0.0 && visited[v as usize] == 0 {
                            if stop < WGRAPH_MAX {
                                stack[stop as usize] = v
                                stop = stop + 1
                            }
                        }
                        v = v + 1
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        start = start + 1
    }
    components
}

// =============================================================================
// Dijkstra — O(V²) scan, GUM uncertainty propagation along path
//
// GUM rule (§5.1): combined uncertainty along a path is
//   u(d(v)) = sqrt( u(d(u))² + u(w(u,v))² )
// =============================================================================

pub fn dijkstra(g: &WeightedGraph, source: i32) -> ShortestPathResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n_nodes
    var dist:    [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var dunc:    [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var pred:    [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var reach:   [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var visited: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        dist[i as usize]    = F64_INF
        dunc[i as usize]    = 0.0
        pred[i as usize]    = -1
        reach[i as usize]   = 0
        visited[i as usize] = 0
        i = i + 1
    }

    if source < 0 || source >= n {
        return ShortestPathResult {
            distances: dist, dist_unc: dunc,
            predecessors: pred, reachable: reach,
        }
    }

    dist[source as usize]  = 0.0
    reach[source as usize] = 1

    var processed: i32 = 0
    while processed < n {
        // find unvisited node with minimum distance
        var u: i32 = -1
        var best_d: f64 = F64_INF
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < n {
            if visited[k as usize] == 0 && dist[k as usize] < best_d {
                best_d = dist[k as usize]
                u = k
            }
            k = k + 1
        }

        if u == -1 { break }   // all remaining nodes unreachable
        visited[u as usize] = 1

        // relax edges from u
        var v: i32 = 0
        while v < n {
            let idx = (u * WGRAPH_MAX + v) as usize
            let w = g.weights[idx]
            if w > 0.0 {
                let nd = dist[u as usize] + w
                if nd < dist[v as usize] {
                    dist[v as usize]  = nd
                    reach[v as usize] = 1
                    pred[v as usize]  = u
                    // GUM quadrature: u(d(v)) = sqrt(u(d(u))^2 + u(w)^2)
                    let uw = g.weight_unc[idx]
                    let ud = dunc[u as usize]
                    dunc[v as usize] = w_sqrt(ud * ud + uw * uw)
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }

        processed = processed + 1
    }

    ShortestPathResult {
        distances: dist, dist_unc: dunc,
        predecessors: pred, reachable: reach,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// PageRank — power iteration with weight-uncertainty propagation
//
// PR(i) = (1-d)/N + d * Σ_{j→i} PR(j) * w(j,i) / out_strength(j)
// Rank uncertainty: u_PR(i) ≈ d * Σ_{j→i} (PR(j)/out_strength(j)) * u_w(j,i)
//
// Uses by-value struct passing to avoid the JIT &! mutation visibility bug.
// =============================================================================

// Internal state carrier for one power-iteration step.
struct PrState {
    scores:     [f64; 32],
    scores_unc: [f64; 32],
    delta:      f64,
}

// Build out-strength array by scanning the graph.
fn pr_make_out_strength(g: &WeightedGraph) -> [f64; 32] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var out_str: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    let n = g.n_nodes
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        var s: f64 = 0.0
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < n {
            s = s + g.weights[(i * WGRAPH_MAX + j) as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        out_str[i as usize] = s
        i = i + 1
    }
    out_str
}

// One power-iteration step (by-value in/out via PrState).
fn pr_step(g: &WeightedGraph, st: PrState, out_str: [f64; 32], damping: f64, teleport: f64) -> PrState
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let n = g.n_nodes
    var new_scores: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var new_unc:    [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]

    // seed with teleport term
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < n {
        new_scores[k as usize] = teleport
        k = k + 1
    }

    // accumulate contributions from each source j
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < n {
        let os = out_str[j as usize]
        if os > 0.0 {
            var vi: i32 = 0
            while vi < n {
                let idx = (j * WGRAPH_MAX + vi) as usize
                let w = g.weights[idx]
                if w > 0.0 {
                    let contrib = damping * st.scores[j as usize] * w / os
                    new_scores[vi as usize] = new_scores[vi as usize] + contrib
                    let uc = damping * st.scores[j as usize] * g.weight_unc[idx] / os
                    new_unc[vi as usize] = new_unc[vi as usize] + uc * uc
                }
                vi = vi + 1
            }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    // sqrt the squared uncertainty accumulators
    k = 0
    while k < n {
        new_unc[k as usize] = w_sqrt(new_unc[k as usize])
        k = k + 1
    }

    // L1 delta vs previous scores
    var delta: f64 = 0.0
    k = 0
    while k < n {
        let d = new_scores[k as usize] - st.scores[k as usize]
        if d < 0.0 { delta = delta + (0.0 - d) } else { delta = delta + d }
        k = k + 1
    }

    PrState { scores: new_scores, scores_unc: new_unc, delta: delta }
}

pub fn pagerank(g: &WeightedGraph, damping: f64, max_iter: i32, tol: f64) -> PageRankResult
    with Mut, Div, Panic
{
    let n = g.n_nodes
    var scores: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    let init = 1.0 / (n as f64)
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        scores[i as usize] = init
        i = i + 1
    }

    let out_str = pr_make_out_strength(g)
    let teleport = (1.0 - damping) / (n as f64)

    var st = PrState { scores: scores, scores_unc: [0.0; 32], delta: 1.0e30 }
    var iter: i32 = 0
    var converged: i32 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        st = pr_step(g, st, out_str, damping, teleport)
        iter = iter + 1
        if st.delta < tol {
            converged = 1
            break
        }
    }

    PageRankResult {
        scores:       st.scores,
        scores_unc:   st.scores_unc,
        n_iterations: iter,
        converged:    converged,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Kruskal MST — union-find, insertion-sort edges by weight
//
// Collects all directed edges (or upper-triangle for undirected) into a
// fixed-size edge list, sorts by weight (insertion sort, O(E²) fine for E≤1024),
// then greedily adds non-cycle edges.
// =============================================================================

pub fn kruskal_mst(g: &WeightedGraph) -> WeightedGraph with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n_nodes

    // collect edges into fixed-size arrays (max E = n*(n-1)/2 ≤ 496 for n=32)
    var e_from:  [i32; 512]  = [0; 512]
    var e_to:    [i32; 512]  = [0; 512]
    var e_w:     [f64; 512]  = [0.0; 512]
    var e_unc:   [f64; 512]  = [0.0; 512]
    var ne: i32 = 0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < n {
            if g.directed == 1 {
                // directed: every non-zero entry
                let idx = (i * WGRAPH_MAX + j) as usize
                if g.weights[idx] > 0.0 && ne < 512 {
                    e_from[ne as usize] = i
                    e_to[ne as usize]   = j
                    e_w[ne as usize]    = g.weights[idx]
                    e_unc[ne as usize]  = g.weight_unc[idx]
                    ne = ne + 1
                }
            } else {
                // undirected: upper triangle only
                if j > i {
                    let idx = (i * WGRAPH_MAX + j) as usize
                    if g.weights[idx] > 0.0 && ne < 512 {
                        e_from[ne as usize] = i
                        e_to[ne as usize]   = j
                        e_w[ne as usize]    = g.weights[idx]
                        e_unc[ne as usize]  = g.weight_unc[idx]
                        ne = ne + 1
                    }
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // insertion sort by weight ascending
    var s: i32 = 1
    while s < ne {
        let kw   = e_w[s as usize]
        let ku   = e_unc[s as usize]
        let kf   = e_from[s as usize]
        let kt   = e_to[s as usize]
        var p: i32 = s - 1
        while p >= 0 && e_w[p as usize] > kw {
            e_w[(p + 1) as usize]    = e_w[p as usize]
            e_unc[(p + 1) as usize]  = e_unc[p as usize]
            e_from[(p + 1) as usize] = e_from[p as usize]
            e_to[(p + 1) as usize]   = e_to[p as usize]
            p = p - 1
        }
        e_w[(p + 1) as usize]    = kw
        e_unc[(p + 1) as usize]  = ku
        e_from[(p + 1) as usize] = kf
        e_to[(p + 1) as usize]   = kt
        s = s + 1
    }

    // union-find
    var uf_parent: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var uf_rank:   [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var init_k: i32 = 0
    while init_k < n {
        uf_parent[init_k as usize] = init_k
        uf_rank[init_k as usize]   = 0
        init_k = init_k + 1
    }

    var mst = wgraph_new(n, g.directed)
    var ei: i32 = 0
    while ei < ne {
        let u = e_from[ei as usize]
        let v = e_to[ei as usize]

        // inline find-root for u (avoids shared-borrow overlap with mutable union)
        var ru: i32 = u
        var ru_steps: i32 = 0
        while ru_steps < 32 {
            let rp = uf_parent[ru as usize]
            if rp == ru { break }
            ru = rp
            ru_steps = ru_steps + 1
        }

        // inline find-root for v
        var rv: i32 = v
        var rv_steps: i32 = 0
        while rv_steps < 32 {
            let rp = uf_parent[rv as usize]
            if rp == rv { break }
            rv = rp
            rv_steps = rv_steps + 1
        }

        if ru != rv {
            mst = wgraph_add_edge(mst, u, v, e_w[ei as usize], e_unc[ei as usize])
            // inline union-by-rank (avoids &! caller visibility bug)
            if uf_rank[ru as usize] < uf_rank[rv as usize] {
                uf_parent[ru as usize] = rv
            } else if uf_rank[ru as usize] > uf_rank[rv as usize] {
                uf_parent[rv as usize] = ru
            } else {
                uf_parent[rv as usize] = ru
                uf_rank[ru as usize] = uf_rank[ru as usize] + 1
            }
        }
        ei = ei + 1
    }

    mst
}

// =============================================================================
// Topological Sort — Kahn's algorithm (BFS-based)
// Returns TopoSortResult: order array + count (-1 = cycle detected).
// By-value return avoids the JIT &! mutation visibility bug.
// =============================================================================

pub fn topo_sort(g: &WeightedGraph) -> TopoSortResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = g.n_nodes
    var order: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]

    // compute in-degree for each node
    var indeg: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < n {
            if g.weights[(j * WGRAPH_MAX + i) as usize] > 0.0 {
                indeg[i as usize] = indeg[i as usize] + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // enqueue zero-indegree nodes
    var queue: [i32; 32] = [0; 32]
    var qhead: i32 = 0
    var qtail: i32 = 0

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if indeg[i as usize] == 0 {
            queue[qtail as usize] = i
            qtail = qtail + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var cnt: i32 = 0
    while qhead < qtail {
        let u = queue[qhead as usize]
        qhead = qhead + 1
        order[cnt as usize] = u
        cnt = cnt + 1

        var v: i32 = 0
        while v < n {
            if g.weights[(u * WGRAPH_MAX + v) as usize] > 0.0 {
                indeg[v as usize] = indeg[v as usize] - 1
                if indeg[v as usize] == 0 {
                    queue[qtail as usize] = v
                    qtail = qtail + 1
                }
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
    }

    let count = if cnt < n { -1 } else { cnt }
    TopoSortResult { order: order, count: count }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/graph/coherence.sio ===
// stdlib/graph/coherence.sio
// Coherence metrics for Knowledge Epistemic Curvature (KEC) pipeline
//
// Coherence measures the consistency and stability of information flow
// across a knowledge graph. Uses O(n) metrics for performance:
// - Degree regularity (inverse coefficient of variation)
// - Connectivity (edge density)
// - Average degree balance

module graph::coherence

// Newton's method sqrt (f64.sqrt() not available in interpreter)
fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    y
}

// Measure degree regularity (inverse coefficient of variation)
// Regular graphs have high coherence
// Returns value in [0, 1]
pub fn degree_regularity(adj: &[[usize]]) -> f64 {
    let n = adj.len();
    if n < 2 {
        return 1.0;
    }

    // Compute mean degree
    var sum_deg: f64 = 0.0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        sum_deg = sum_deg + (adj[i].len() as f64);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    let mean_deg = sum_deg / (n as f64);

    if mean_deg < 0.001 {
        return 0.0;
    }

    // Compute variance
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0;
    i = 0;
    while i < n {
        let diff = (adj[i].len() as f64) - mean_deg;
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    let variance = sum_sq / (n as f64);

    // Coefficient of variation
    let cv = sqrt_f64(variance) / mean_deg;

    // Regularity = 1 / (1 + cv)
    1.0 / (1.0 + cv)
}

// Measure connectivity as ratio of actual to maximum edges
// Returns value in [0, 1]
pub fn connectivity(adj: &[[usize]]) -> f64 {
    let n = adj.len();
    if n < 2 {
        return 0.0;
    }

    // Count edges
    var edge_count: usize = 0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        edge_count = edge_count + adj[i].len();
        i = i + 1;
    }

    // For undirected: edges are double-counted
    let max_edges = n * (n - 1);

    if max_edges > 0 {
        (edge_count as f64) / (max_edges as f64)
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// Measure degree balance (how evenly distributed edges are)
// High balance = more coherent structure
pub fn degree_balance(adj: &[[usize]]) -> f64 {
    let n = adj.len();
    if n < 2 {
        return 1.0;
    }

    // Find min and max degrees
    var min_deg: usize = adj[0].len();
    var max_deg: usize = adj[0].len();

    var i: usize = 1;
    while i < n {
        let d = adj[i].len();
        if d < min_deg {
            min_deg = d;
        }
        if d > max_deg {
            max_deg = d;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }

    // Balance = min/max (1.0 for regular graphs)
    if max_deg > 0 {
        (min_deg as f64) / (max_deg as f64)
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// Simple coherence score (convenience function)
// Combines regularity, connectivity, and balance
pub fn coherence(adj: &[[usize]]) -> f64 {
    let regularity = degree_regularity(adj);
    let conn = connectivity(adj);
    let balance = degree_balance(adj);

    // Weighted combination
    0.4 * regularity + 0.3 * conn + 0.3 * balance
}

// Tests (similar pattern to entropy.d - no float comparisons)


// === FILE: stdlib/graph/curvature.sio ===
// graph/curvature.sio — Discrete Curvature on Graphs
// Ollivier-Ricci, Forman, and sectional curvature for graph analysis

fn curv_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn curv_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var r = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 15 { r = 0.5 * (r + x / r); i = i + 1 }
    r
}
fn curv_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// Graph as adjacency matrix (max 32 nodes)
struct CurvGraph {
    adj: [i32; 1024],   // 32x32 adjacency matrix
    n: i32,
}

fn curv_graph_new(n: i32) -> CurvGraph {
    CurvGraph { adj: [0; 1024], n: n }
}

fn curv_add_edge(g: CurvGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> CurvGraph with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = g
    result.adj[u * 32 + v] = 1
    result.adj[v * 32 + u] = 1
    result
}

fn curv_has_edge(g: &CurvGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> bool {
    g.adj[u * 32 + v] == 1
}

fn curv_degree(g: &CurvGraph, v: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var d: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < g.n { if g.adj[v * 32 + i] == 1 { d = d + 1 }; i = i + 1 }
    d
}

// Forman curvature of edge (u, v)
// F(u,v) = 4 - deg(u) - deg(v) + 3*triangles(u,v)
fn forman_curvature_edge(g: &CurvGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let du = curv_degree(g, u)
    let dv = curv_degree(g, v)
    // Count triangles containing edge (u,v)
    var triangles: i32 = 0
    var w: i32 = 0
    while w < g.n {
        if w != u && w != v {
            if curv_has_edge(g, u, w) && curv_has_edge(g, v, w) {
                triangles = triangles + 1
            }
        }
        w = w + 1
    }
    (4 - du - dv + 3 * triangles) as f64
}

// Mean Forman curvature over all edges
fn mean_forman_curvature(g: &CurvGraph) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var count: i32 = 0
    var u: i32 = 0
    while u < g.n {
        var v: i32 = u + 1
        while v < g.n {
            if curv_has_edge(g, u, v) {
                sum = sum + forman_curvature_edge(g, u, v)
                count = count + 1
            }
            v = v + 1
        }
        u = u + 1
    }
    if count == 0 { 0.0 } else { sum / (count as f64) }
}

// Ollivier-Ricci curvature (simplified: 1-optimal transport cost between neighbors)
fn ollivier_ricci_edge(g: &CurvGraph, u: i32, v: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let du = curv_degree(g, u)
    let dv = curv_degree(g, v)
    if du == 0 || dv == 0 { return 0.0 }
    // Count common neighbors
    var common: i32 = 0
    var w: i32 = 0
    while w < g.n {
        if curv_has_edge(g, u, w) && curv_has_edge(g, v, w) { common = common + 1 }
        w = w + 1
    }
    // Simplified: kappa ~ 2*common/(du+dv) - 1
    let kappa = 2.0 * (common as f64) / ((du + dv) as f64)
    kappa
}

// Geometry classification based on mean curvature
fn classify_geometry(mean_curv: f64) -> i32 {
    // 0 = flat (Euclidean), 1 = positive (spherical), 2 = negative (hyperbolic)
    if curv_abs(mean_curv) < 0.1 { 0 }
    else if mean_curv > 0.0 { 1 }
    else { 2 }
}

fn test_triangle_forman() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g = curv_graph_new(3)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 0, 1)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 1, 2)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 0, 2)
    let f = forman_curvature_edge(&g, 0, 1)
    // 4 - 2 - 2 + 3*1 = 3
    curv_abs(f - 3.0) < 0.01
}

fn test_path_forman() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g = curv_graph_new(3)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 0, 1)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 1, 2)
    let f = forman_curvature_edge(&g, 0, 1)
    // 4 - 1 - 2 + 0 = 1
    curv_abs(f - 1.0) < 0.01
}

fn test_ollivier_ricci() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var g = curv_graph_new(4)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 0, 1)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 0, 2)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 0, 3)
    g = curv_add_edge(g, 1, 2)
    let kappa = ollivier_ricci_edge(&g, 0, 1)
    kappa >= 0.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/graph/entropy.sio ===
// Graph Entropy Measures for Knowledge Epistemic Curvature (KEC)
//
// Implements multiple entropy measures on graphs:
// - Shannon entropy of degree distribution
// - Structural entropy (based on random walk stationary distribution)
// - von Neumann entropy (spectral, approximated)
// - Random walk entropy rate
//
// All measures return Uncertain[f64] for proper error propagation.

module graph::entropy

// =============================================================================
// Entropy Types
// =============================================================================

// Entropy result with uncertainty
pub struct EntropyResult {
    pub value: f64,          // Point estimate
    pub std_err: f64,        // Standard error (for sampling-based methods)
    pub method: EntropyMethod,
    pub n_nodes: usize,
    pub n_edges: usize,
}

pub enum EntropyMethod {
    Shannon,      // Degree distribution
    Structural,   // Random walk stationary
    VonNeumann,   // Spectral (approximated)
    RateH,        // Random walk entropy rate
}

// =============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// =============================================================================

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return -1000.0 }  // Guard against log(0)
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    // Taylor series around 1
    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result: f64 = 0.0
    var term = y
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < 50 {
        result = result + term / (i as f64)
        term = term * y * y
        i = i + 2
    }
    2.0 * result
}

fn log2_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    ln_f64(x) / 0.6931471805599453  // ln(2)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

// =============================================================================
// Shannon Entropy of Degree Distribution
// =============================================================================

// H(degree) = -sum_k P(k) log P(k)
// where P(k) is the fraction of nodes with degree k
pub fn degree_entropy(adj: &[[usize]]) -> EntropyResult {
    let n = adj.len()
    if n == 0 {
        return EntropyResult {
            value: 0.0,
            std_err: 0.0,
            method: EntropyMethod::Shannon,
            n_nodes: 0,
            n_edges: 0,
        }
    }

    // Count degrees
    var max_degree: usize = 0
    var total_edges: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        let deg = adj[i].len()
        if deg > max_degree { max_degree = deg }
        total_edges = total_edges + deg
        i = i + 1
    }
    total_edges = total_edges / 2  // Each edge counted twice

    // Build degree histogram
    var degree_count: [usize] = []
    i = 0
    while i <= max_degree {
        degree_count.push(0)
        i = i + 1
    }

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let deg = adj[i].len()
        degree_count[deg] = degree_count[deg] + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute entropy
    var entropy: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i <= max_degree {
        if degree_count[i] > 0 {
            let p = (degree_count[i] as f64) / (n as f64)
            entropy = entropy - p * log2_f64(p)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Standard error estimate using bootstrap approximation
    // SE ≈ sqrt(sum_k P(k)(1-P(k))(-log P(k))^2 / n)
    var variance_sum: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i <= max_degree {
        if degree_count[i] > 0 {
            let p = (degree_count[i] as f64) / (n as f64)
            let log_p = log2_f64(p)
            variance_sum = variance_sum + p * (1.0 - p) * log_p * log_p
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let std_err = sqrt_f64(variance_sum / (n as f64))

    EntropyResult {
        value: entropy,
        std_err: std_err,
        method: EntropyMethod::Shannon,
        n_nodes: n,
        n_edges: total_edges,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Structural Entropy (Random Walk Stationary Distribution)
// =============================================================================

// H_struct = -sum_i pi_i log pi_i
// where pi_i = d_i / (2m) is stationary distribution of random walk
pub fn structural_entropy(adj: &[[usize]]) -> EntropyResult {
    let n = adj.len()
    if n == 0 {
        return EntropyResult {
            value: 0.0,
            std_err: 0.0,
            method: EntropyMethod::Structural,
            n_nodes: 0,
            n_edges: 0,
        }
    }

    // Compute total degree (2m)
    var total_degree: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        total_degree = total_degree + adj[i].len()
        i = i + 1
    }

    if total_degree == 0 {
        return EntropyResult {
            value: 0.0,
            std_err: 0.0,
            method: EntropyMethod::Structural,
            n_nodes: n,
            n_edges: 0,
        }
    }

    let two_m = total_degree as f64

    // Compute structural entropy
    var entropy: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let deg = adj[i].len()
        if deg > 0 {
            let pi = (deg as f64) / two_m
            entropy = entropy - pi * log2_f64(pi)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Standard error: harder to compute exactly, use approximation
    // For large n, SE ≈ sqrt(variance/n) where variance depends on degree heterogeneity
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let deg = adj[i].len()
        if deg > 0 {
            let pi = (deg as f64) / two_m
            let term = -pi * log2_f64(pi)
            sum_sq = sum_sq + term * term
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_sq = (entropy / (n as f64)) * (entropy / (n as f64))
    let variance = max_f64(sum_sq / (n as f64) - mean_sq, 0.0)
    let std_err = sqrt_f64(variance / (n as f64))

    EntropyResult {
        value: entropy,
        std_err: std_err,
        method: EntropyMethod::Structural,
        n_nodes: n,
        n_edges: total_degree / 2,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// von Neumann Entropy (Spectral, Approximated)
// =============================================================================

// H_vN = -Tr(rho * log(rho)) where rho = L / Tr(L) (normalized Laplacian density)
// Approximation using random walk eigenvalue bounds
pub fn von_neumann_entropy_approx(adj: &[[usize]]) -> EntropyResult {
    let n = adj.len()
    if n == 0 {
        return EntropyResult {
            value: 0.0,
            std_err: 0.0,
            method: EntropyMethod::VonNeumann,
            n_nodes: 0,
            n_edges: 0,
        }
    }

    // For undirected graphs, vN entropy relates to normalized Laplacian spectrum
    // Use Cheeger-type bounds and degree distribution as proxy

    // First, get structural entropy as upper bound
    let h_struct = structural_entropy(adj)

    // Compute average clustering to adjust estimate
    var total_triangles: usize = 0
    var possible_triangles: usize = 0

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        let neighbors = &adj[i]
        let k = neighbors.len()
        if k >= 2 {
            possible_triangles = possible_triangles + k * (k - 1) / 2

            // Count triangles through this node
            var j: usize = 0
            while j < k {
                var l: usize = j + 1
                while l < k {
                    // Check if neighbors[j] and neighbors[l] are connected
                    let nj = neighbors[j]
                    let nl = neighbors[l]
                    let adj_nj = &adj[nj]
                    var m: usize = 0
                    while m < adj_nj.len() {
                        if adj_nj[m] == nl {
                            total_triangles = total_triangles + 1
                        }
                        m = m + 1
                    }
                    l = l + 1
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Clustering coefficient
    var clustering: f64 = 0.0
    if possible_triangles > 0 {
        clustering = (total_triangles as f64) / (possible_triangles as f64)
    }

    // Adjust entropy estimate: high clustering reduces effective entropy
    // This is a heuristic approximation
    let adjustment = 1.0 - 0.3 * clustering
    let entropy = h_struct.value * adjustment

    // Larger uncertainty for approximation
    let std_err = h_struct.std_err * 2.0 + 0.1

    var total_edges: usize = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        total_edges = total_edges + adj[i].len()
        i = i + 1
    }

    EntropyResult {
        value: entropy,
        std_err: std_err,
        method: EntropyMethod::VonNeumann,
        n_nodes: n,
        n_edges: total_edges / 2,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Random Walk Entropy Rate
// =============================================================================

// H_rate = lim_{t->inf} H(X_t | X_0) / t
// For Markov chains: H_rate = -sum_i pi_i sum_j P_ij log P_ij
pub fn random_walk_entropy_rate(adj: &[[usize]]) -> EntropyResult {
    let n = adj.len()
    if n == 0 {
        return EntropyResult {
            value: 0.0,
            std_err: 0.0,
            method: EntropyMethod::RateH,
            n_nodes: 0,
            n_edges: 0,
        }
    }

    // Compute total degree for stationary distribution
    var total_degree: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        total_degree = total_degree + adj[i].len()
        i = i + 1
    }

    if total_degree == 0 {
        return EntropyResult {
            value: 0.0,
            std_err: 0.0,
            method: EntropyMethod::RateH,
            n_nodes: n,
            n_edges: 0,
        }
    }

    let two_m = total_degree as f64

    // H_rate = -sum_i pi_i sum_j P_ij log P_ij
    // P_ij = 1/d_i if j is neighbor of i
    // pi_i = d_i / 2m
    var entropy_rate: f64 = 0.0

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let deg = adj[i].len()
        if deg > 0 {
            let pi_i = (deg as f64) / two_m
            let p_ij = 1.0 / (deg as f64)  // Uniform over neighbors
            let local_entropy = log2_f64(deg as f64)  // -sum_j P_ij log P_ij = log(d_i)
            entropy_rate = entropy_rate + pi_i * local_entropy
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Standard error from degree variance
    var degree_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var degree_sq_sum: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let deg = adj[i].len() as f64
        degree_sum = degree_sum + deg
        degree_sq_sum = degree_sq_sum + deg * deg
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean_deg = degree_sum / (n as f64)
    let var_deg = degree_sq_sum / (n as f64) - mean_deg * mean_deg
    let std_err = sqrt_f64(var_deg) / (n as f64) * 0.5  // Heuristic scaling

    EntropyResult {
        value: entropy_rate,
        std_err: std_err,
        method: EntropyMethod::RateH,
        n_nodes: n,
        n_edges: total_degree / 2,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Comprehensive Entropy Analysis
// =============================================================================

pub struct EntropyAnalysis {
    pub degree: EntropyResult,
    pub structural: EntropyResult,
    pub von_neumann: EntropyResult,
    pub rate: EntropyResult,
    pub mean: f64,           // Average of all methods
    pub combined_std: f64,   // Combined uncertainty
}

pub fn full_entropy_analysis(adj: &[[usize]]) -> EntropyAnalysis {
    let degree = degree_entropy(adj)
    let structural = structural_entropy(adj)
    let von_neumann = von_neumann_entropy_approx(adj)
    let rate = random_walk_entropy_rate(adj)

    // Inverse-variance weighted mean
    var w_sum: f64 = 0.0
    var weighted_sum: f64 = 0.0

    let eps = 0.001  // Minimum uncertainty to avoid division by zero

    let w1 = 1.0 / max_f64(degree.std_err * degree.std_err, eps)
    let w2 = 1.0 / max_f64(structural.std_err * structural.std_err, eps)
    let w3 = 1.0 / max_f64(von_neumann.std_err * von_neumann.std_err, eps)
    let w4 = 1.0 / max_f64(rate.std_err * rate.std_err, eps)

    w_sum = w1 + w2 + w3 + w4
    weighted_sum = w1 * degree.value + w2 * structural.value +
                   w3 * von_neumann.value + w4 * rate.value

    let mean = weighted_sum / w_sum
    let combined_std = sqrt_f64(1.0 / w_sum)

    EntropyAnalysis {
        degree,
        structural,
        von_neumann,
        rate,
        mean,
        combined_std,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Convenience Functions
// =============================================================================

// Get single entropy value with default method (structural)
pub fn entropy(adj: &[[usize]]) -> f64 {
    structural_entropy(adj).value
}

// Get entropy with uncertainty as tuple
pub fn entropy_with_uncertainty(adj: &[[usize]]) -> (f64, f64) {
    let result = structural_entropy(adj)
    (result.value, result.std_err)
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

pub fn test_complete_graph_entropy() -> bool {
    // Complete graph K4: all nodes have same degree, minimum entropy
    var adj: [[usize]] = [[], [], [], []]
    adj[0].push(1); adj[0].push(2); adj[0].push(3)
    adj[1].push(0); adj[1].push(2); adj[1].push(3)
    adj[2].push(0); adj[2].push(1); adj[2].push(3)
    adj[3].push(0); adj[3].push(1); adj[3].push(2)

    let h = degree_entropy(&adj)
    // All nodes have degree 3, so degree entropy should be 0
    abs_f64(h.value) < 0.01
}

pub fn test_star_graph_entropy() -> bool {
    // Star graph: center has degree n-1, leaves have degree 1
    // High degree entropy due to heterogeneity
    var adj: [[usize]] = [[], [], [], [], []]
    // Center is node 0
    adj[0].push(1); adj[0].push(2); adj[0].push(3); adj[0].push(4)
    adj[1].push(0)
    adj[2].push(0)
    adj[3].push(0)
    adj[4].push(0)

    let h = degree_entropy(&adj)
    // Should have positive entropy
    h.value > 0.5
}

pub fn test_entropy_uncertainty_positive() -> bool {
    // All entropy results should have non-negative uncertainty
    var adj: [[usize]] = [[], [], []]
    adj[0].push(1)
    adj[1].push(0); adj[1].push(2)
    adj[2].push(1)

    let analysis = full_entropy_analysis(&adj)
    analysis.degree.std_err >= 0.0 &&
    analysis.structural.std_err >= 0.0 &&
    analysis.von_neumann.std_err >= 0.0 &&
    analysis.rate.std_err >= 0.0
}

pub fn run_entropy_tests() -> bool {
    test_complete_graph_entropy() &&
    test_star_graph_entropy() &&
    test_entropy_uncertainty_positive()
}
