// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/shaped.sio ===
// stdlib/linalg/shaped.sio — Shape-Typed Linear Algebra Utilities
// Sprint 23 Track V: Vec<T,n>, Matrix<T,m,n> shape-safe operations
//
// References:
//   Golub & Van Loan (2013) "Matrix Computations" 4th ed.
//   Henriksen et al. (2017) PLDI "Futhark"
//   Trefethen & Bau (1997) "Numerical Linear Algebra"

// ============================================================
// Shape validation helpers
// ============================================================

fn matmul_shapes_valid(left_rows: i64, left_cols: i64, right_rows: i64, right_cols: i64) -> bool with IO {
    // Matrix multiply valid iff left_cols == right_rows
    if left_cols == -1 { return true }
    if right_rows == -1 { return true }
    left_cols == right_rows
}

fn cholesky_shape_valid(m: i64, n: i64) -> bool with IO {
    // Cholesky requires square matrix
    m == n || m == -1 || n == -1
}

fn qr_shape_valid(m: i64, n: i64) -> bool with IO {
    // QR requires m >= n (overdetermined)
    if m == -1 || n == -1 { return true }
    m >= n
}

fn broadcast_shape_compatible(a_m: i64, a_n: i64, b_m: i64, b_n: i64) -> bool with IO {
    // NumPy broadcast: dim of 1 broadcasts to any
    let m_ok = (a_m == 1) || (b_m == 1) || (a_m == b_m) || (a_m == -1) || (b_m == -1)
    let n_ok = (a_n == 1) || (b_n == 1) || (a_n == b_n) || (a_n == -1) || (b_n == -1)
    m_ok && n_ok
}

// ============================================================
// Dot product (Vec<f64, n>)
// ============================================================

fn dot_8(v1: [f64; 8], v2: [f64; 8], n: i64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n && i < 8 {
        s = s + v1[i as usize] * v2[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

fn vec_norm_8(v: [f64; 8], n: i64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    let sq = dot_8(v, v, n)
    if sq <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = sq / 2.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = (y + sq / y) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// ============================================================
// Frobenius norm (Matrix<f64, m, n>)
// ============================================================

fn frobenius_norm(vals: [f64; 16], m: i64, n: i64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    let total = m * n
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < total && i < 16 {
        s = s + vals[i as usize] * vals[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if s <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = s / 2.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < 20 {
        y = (y + s / y) / 2.0
        j = j + 1
    }
    y
}

// ============================================================
// Kronecker product shape: (m1 x n1) otimes (m2 x n2) = (m1*m2 x n1*n2)
// ============================================================

fn kronecker_product_rows(m1: i64, m2: i64) -> i64 with IO { m1 * m2 }
fn kronecker_product_cols(n1: i64, n2: i64) -> i64 with IO { n1 * n2 }

// ============================================================
// Hadamard product shape check: requires same shape
// ============================================================

fn hadamard_shape_valid(m1: i64, n1: i64, m2: i64, n2: i64) -> bool with IO {
    (m1 == m2 || m1 == -1 || m2 == -1) && (n1 == n2 || n1 == -1 || n2 == -1)
}

// ============================================================
// Cholesky forward substitution (for Lx = b where L is lower-triangular 2x2)
// ============================================================

fn cholesky_forward_sub_2x2(l11: f64, l21: f64, l22: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64) -> [f64; 2] with IO, Div, Panic {
    let x1 = b1 / l11
    let x2 = (b2 + (0.0 - l21 * x1)) / l22
    [x1, x2]
}

// ============================================================
// QR via Gram-Schmidt (3x2 = 3 rows, 2 cols, m >= n check)
// ============================================================

fn gram_schmidt_3x2_col0(col0: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    // Normalize first column
    let n = col0[0]*col0[0] + col0[1]*col0[1] + col0[2]*col0[2]
    var y = n / 2.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 20 { if y > 0.0 { y = (y + n / y) / 2.0 } i = i + 1 }
    [col0[0]/y, col0[1]/y, col0[2]/y]
}


// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/sparse.sio ===
// sparse.sio - Sparse Matrix Library (CSR Format) for Sounio Linear Algebra
//
// Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) format for efficient sparse matrix operations.
// Designed for scientific computing: FDM/FEM stiffness matrices, Jacobians,
// Laplacians, and iterative solvers (Conjugate Gradient).
//
// Fixed-size arrays with limits:
//   - Up to 1024 non-zero entries
//   - Up to 128 rows/columns
//   - Dense vectors up to 128 elements
//
// Key operations:
//   - SpMV (sparse matrix-vector multiply) — the critical kernel
//   - Sparse-sparse addition and transpose
//   - Triangular solves (forward/backward substitution)
//   - Conjugate Gradient iterative solver for SPD systems

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn spr_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 {
        return 0.0 - x
    }
    return x
}

fn spr_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Range reduction: scale x into [1, 4) by multiplying by powers of 4
    // then scale the result back by dividing by the power of 2
    var scaled = x
    var scale_back = 1.0
    // Scale up small numbers
    while scaled < 1.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 4.0
        scale_back = scale_back * 2.0
    }
    // Scale down large numbers
    while scaled > 4.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 0.25
        scale_back = scale_back * 0.5
    }
    // Newton-Raphson on scaled value (now in [1, 4))
    var y = 1.5
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    return y / scale_back
}

fn spr_max_i32(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn spr_min_i32(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// DENSE VECTOR HELPERS (operate on [f64; 128])
// ============================================================================

fn vec_dot(a: [f64; 128], b: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn vec_axpy(alpha: f64, x: [f64; 128], y: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // result = alpha*x + y
    var result: [f64; 128] = y
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result[i] = alpha * x[i] + y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn vec_copy(src: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dst: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        dst[i] = src[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return dst
}

fn vec_norm(x: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + x[i] * x[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return spr_sqrt_f64(sum)
}

fn vec_scale(alpha: f64, x: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result[i] = alpha * x[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn vec_sub(a: [f64; 128], b: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result[i] = a[i] - b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn vec_add(a: [f64; 128], b: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result[i] = a[i] + b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

fn vec_zeros(n: i32) -> [f64; 128] {
    let result: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

// Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) matrix format.
// For an m x n matrix with nnz non-zeros:
//   values[0..nnz]:    non-zero values in row-major order
//   col_idx[0..nnz]:   column index of each non-zero value
//   row_ptr[0..m+1]:   row_ptr[i] is the start index in values/col_idx for row i
//                      row_ptr[m] = nnz
struct SparseCSR {
    values: [f64; 1024],
    col_idx: [i32; 1024],
    row_ptr: [i32; 129],
    nrows: i32,
    ncols: i32,
    nnz: i32
}

// Result of the Conjugate Gradient solver
struct CGResult {
    x: [f64; 128],
    iterations: i32,
    residual: f64,
    converged: bool
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTION
// ============================================================================

// Create an empty sparse matrix with given dimensions
fn sparse_new(nrows: i32, ncols: i32) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: nrows,
        ncols: ncols,
        nnz: 0
    }
    // All row pointers start at 0
    var i = 0
    while i <= nrows {
        result.row_ptr[i] = 0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// Build a CSR matrix from COO (coordinate) format triplets.
// Sorts by row then column. Sums duplicate entries.
// rows[0..count], cols[0..count], vals[0..count] are the triplets.
fn sparse_from_triplets(
    rows: [i32; 1024],
    cols: [i32; 1024],
    vals: [f64; 1024],
    count: i32,
    nrows: i32,
    ncols: i32
) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Sort triplets by (row, col) using insertion sort (stable, good for small count)
    var s_rows: [i32; 1024] = rows
    var s_cols: [i32; 1024] = cols
    var s_vals: [f64; 1024] = vals

    var i = 1
    while i < count {
        let r = s_rows[i]
        let c = s_cols[i]
        let v = s_vals[i]
        var j = i - 1
        var done = false
        while j >= 0 && !done {
            // Compare (row, col) lexicographically
            let should_shift = s_rows[j] > r || (s_rows[j] == r && s_cols[j] > c)
            if should_shift {
                s_rows[j + 1] = s_rows[j]
                s_cols[j + 1] = s_cols[j]
                s_vals[j + 1] = s_vals[j]
                j = j - 1
            } else {
                done = true
            }
        }
        s_rows[j + 1] = r
        s_cols[j + 1] = c
        s_vals[j + 1] = v
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Merge duplicates: if consecutive entries have same (row, col), sum values
    var m_rows: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    var m_cols: [i32; 1024] = [0; 1024]
    var m_vals: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
    var m_count = 0

    if count > 0 {
        m_rows[0] = s_rows[0]
        m_cols[0] = s_cols[0]
        m_vals[0] = s_vals[0]
        m_count = 1

        i = 1
        while i < count {
            if s_rows[i] == m_rows[m_count - 1] && s_cols[i] == m_cols[m_count - 1] {
                // Duplicate: sum values
                m_vals[m_count - 1] = m_vals[m_count - 1] + s_vals[i]
            } else {
                m_rows[m_count] = s_rows[i]
                m_cols[m_count] = s_cols[i]
                m_vals[m_count] = s_vals[i]
                m_count = m_count + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    // Build CSR from sorted, merged triplets
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: nrows,
        ncols: ncols,
        nnz: m_count
    }

    // Count entries per row
    var row_count: [i32; 129] = [0; 129]
    i = 0
    while i < m_count {
        row_count[m_rows[i]] = row_count[m_rows[i]] + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute row_ptr as cumulative sum
    result.row_ptr[0] = 0
    i = 0
    while i < nrows {
        result.row_ptr[i + 1] = result.row_ptr[i] + row_count[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Fill values and col_idx (already sorted)
    i = 0
    while i < m_count {
        result.values[i] = m_vals[i]
        result.col_idx[i] = m_cols[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    return result
}

// Create an n x n identity matrix in CSR format
fn sparse_identity(n: i32) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: n,
        ncols: n,
        nnz: n
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result.values[i] = 1.0
        result.col_idx[i] = i
        result.row_ptr[i] = i
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.row_ptr[n] = n
    return result
}

// Create a diagonal matrix from an array of diagonal values
fn sparse_diagonal(diag: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: n,
        ncols: n,
        nnz: n
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result.values[i] = diag[i]
        result.col_idx[i] = i
        result.row_ptr[i] = i
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.row_ptr[n] = n
    return result
}

// Create a tridiagonal matrix (common in FDM discretizations).
// lower[0..n-1]: sub-diagonal values (lower[0] is at position (1,0))
// main[0..n]:    main diagonal values
// upper[0..n-1]: super-diagonal values (upper[0] is at position (0,1))
fn sparse_tridiagonal(
    lower: [f64; 128],
    main: [f64; 128],
    upper: [f64; 128],
    n: i32
) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: n,
        ncols: n,
        nnz: 0
    }

    var pos = 0

    // Row 0: main[0], upper[0]
    result.row_ptr[0] = 0
    if n >= 1 {
        result.values[pos] = main[0]
        result.col_idx[pos] = 0
        pos = pos + 1
        if n > 1 {
            result.values[pos] = upper[0]
            result.col_idx[pos] = 1
            pos = pos + 1
        }
    }

    // Middle rows i (1..n-2): lower[i-1], main[i], upper[i]
    var i = 1
    while i < n - 1 {
        result.row_ptr[i] = pos
        result.values[pos] = lower[i - 1]
        result.col_idx[pos] = i - 1
        pos = pos + 1
        result.values[pos] = main[i]
        result.col_idx[pos] = i
        pos = pos + 1
        result.values[pos] = upper[i]
        result.col_idx[pos] = i + 1
        pos = pos + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Last row (n-1): lower[n-2], main[n-1]
    if n > 1 {
        result.row_ptr[n - 1] = pos
        result.values[pos] = lower[n - 2]
        result.col_idx[pos] = n - 2
        pos = pos + 1
        result.values[pos] = main[n - 1]
        result.col_idx[pos] = n - 1
        pos = pos + 1
    }

    result.row_ptr[n] = pos
    result.nnz = pos

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// ELEMENT ACCESS
// ============================================================================

// Get element (i, j) from a CSR matrix.
// Uses linear search within the row (rows are typically short).
fn sparse_get(a: SparseCSR, i: i32, j: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let row_start = a.row_ptr[i]
    let row_end = a.row_ptr[i + 1]
    var k = row_start
    while k < row_end {
        if a.col_idx[k] == j {
            return a.values[k]
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return 0.0
}

// Return the number of non-zero entries
fn sparse_nnz(a: SparseCSR) -> i32 {
    return a.nnz
}

// Return the number of non-zeros in a specific row
fn sparse_row_nnz(a: SparseCSR, row: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    return a.row_ptr[row + 1] - a.row_ptr[row]
}

// ============================================================================
// SPARSE-DENSE OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Sparse matrix-vector multiply: y = A*x  (SpMV)
// This is the critical kernel for iterative solvers.
fn sparse_matvec(a: SparseCSR, x: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nrows {
        var sum = 0.0
        var k = a.row_ptr[i]
        let row_end = a.row_ptr[i + 1]
        while k < row_end {
            let col = a.col_idx[k]
            sum = sum + a.values[k] * x[col]
            k = k + 1
        }
        y[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

// Sparse matrix-vector multiply with scaling: y = alpha*A*x + beta*y
fn sparse_matvec_add(
    a: SparseCSR,
    x: [f64; 128],
    y: [f64; 128],
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
    n: i32
) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nrows {
        var sum = 0.0
        var k = a.row_ptr[i]
        let row_end = a.row_ptr[i + 1]
        while k < row_end {
            let col = a.col_idx[k]
            sum = sum + a.values[k] * x[col]
            k = k + 1
        }
        result[i] = alpha * sum + beta * y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// SPARSE-SPARSE OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

// Sparse addition: C = A + B (merge sorted rows)
// Both A and B must have the same dimensions.
fn sparse_add(a: SparseCSR, b: SparseCSR) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: a.nrows,
        ncols: a.ncols,
        nnz: 0
    }

    var pos = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nrows {
        result.row_ptr[i] = pos

        // Merge sorted entries from row i of A and B
        var ka = a.row_ptr[i]
        let ka_end = a.row_ptr[i + 1]
        var kb = b.row_ptr[i]
        let kb_end = b.row_ptr[i + 1]

        while ka < ka_end && kb < kb_end {
            if a.col_idx[ka] < b.col_idx[kb] {
                result.values[pos] = a.values[ka]
                result.col_idx[pos] = a.col_idx[ka]
                pos = pos + 1
                ka = ka + 1
            } else if a.col_idx[ka] > b.col_idx[kb] {
                result.values[pos] = b.values[kb]
                result.col_idx[pos] = b.col_idx[kb]
                pos = pos + 1
                kb = kb + 1
            } else {
                // Same column: sum values
                let sum = a.values[ka] + b.values[kb]
                if spr_abs_f64(sum) > 1e-30 {
                    result.values[pos] = sum
                    result.col_idx[pos] = a.col_idx[ka]
                    pos = pos + 1
                }
                ka = ka + 1
                kb = kb + 1
            }
        }
        // Remaining entries from A
        while ka < ka_end {
            result.values[pos] = a.values[ka]
            result.col_idx[pos] = a.col_idx[ka]
            pos = pos + 1
            ka = ka + 1
        }
        // Remaining entries from B
        while kb < kb_end {
            result.values[pos] = b.values[kb]
            result.col_idx[pos] = b.col_idx[kb]
            pos = pos + 1
            kb = kb + 1
        }

        i = i + 1
    }
    result.row_ptr[a.nrows] = pos
    result.nnz = pos
    return result
}

// Scale all values in a sparse matrix: B = alpha * A
fn sparse_scale(a: SparseCSR, alpha: f64) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = a
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nnz {
        result.values[i] = alpha * a.values[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// Compute the transpose of a CSR matrix: B = A^T
// Uses a two-pass algorithm: first count, then fill.
fn sparse_transpose(a: SparseCSR) -> SparseCSR with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = SparseCSR {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        col_idx: [0; 1024],
        row_ptr: [0; 129],
        nrows: a.ncols,
        ncols: a.nrows,
        nnz: a.nnz
    }

    // Pass 1: count entries per column of A (= per row of A^T)
    var col_count: [i32; 129] = [0; 129]
    var k = 0
    while k < a.nnz {
        col_count[a.col_idx[k]] = col_count[a.col_idx[k]] + 1
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Build row_ptr for transposed matrix
    result.row_ptr[0] = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.ncols {
        result.row_ptr[i + 1] = result.row_ptr[i] + col_count[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Pass 2: fill values and col_idx
    // Use a position tracker for each row of the result
    var pos: [i32; 129] = [0; 129]
    i = 0
    while i < a.ncols {
        pos[i] = result.row_ptr[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    i = 0
    while i < a.nrows {
        k = a.row_ptr[i]
        let row_end = a.row_ptr[i + 1]
        while k < row_end {
            let col = a.col_idx[k]
            let dest = pos[col]
            result.values[dest] = a.values[k]
            result.col_idx[dest] = i
            pos[col] = pos[col] + 1
            k = k + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// SPARSE TRIANGULAR SOLVE
// ============================================================================

// Forward substitution: solve Lx = b where L is lower triangular.
// Assumes the diagonal is the last entry in each row of L.
fn sparse_lower_solve(l: SparseCSR, b: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var x: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        x[i] = b[i]
        var k = l.row_ptr[i]
        let row_end = l.row_ptr[i + 1]
        var diag_val = 1.0

        // Process all entries in row i
        while k < row_end {
            let col = l.col_idx[k]
            if col < i {
                // Off-diagonal: subtract L[i,col] * x[col]
                x[i] = x[i] - l.values[k] * x[col]
            } else if col == i {
                // Diagonal entry
                diag_val = l.values[k]
            }
            k = k + 1
        }
        // Divide by diagonal
        x[i] = x[i] / diag_val
        i = i + 1
    }
    return x
}

// Back substitution: solve Ux = b where U is upper triangular.
// Assumes the diagonal is the first entry in each row of U.
fn sparse_upper_solve(u: SparseCSR, b: [f64; 128], n: i32) -> [f64; 128] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var x: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    // Copy b into x
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        x[i] = b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Backward sweep
    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var k = u.row_ptr[i]
        let row_end = u.row_ptr[i + 1]
        var diag_val = 1.0

        while k < row_end {
            let col = u.col_idx[k]
            if col > i {
                // Off-diagonal: subtract U[i,col] * x[col]
                x[i] = x[i] - u.values[k] * x[col]
            } else if col == i {
                diag_val = u.values[k]
            }
            k = k + 1
        }
        x[i] = x[i] / diag_val
        i = i - 1
    }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// SPARSE MATRIX PROPERTIES
// ============================================================================

// Frobenius norm: sqrt(sum of values[i]^2)
fn sparse_frobenius_norm(a: SparseCSR) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nnz {
        sum = sum + a.values[i] * a.values[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return spr_sqrt_f64(sum)
}

// Maximum absolute value of any entry
fn sparse_max_abs(a: SparseCSR) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var mx = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nnz {
        let av = spr_abs_f64(a.values[i])
        if av > mx {
            mx = av
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return mx
}

// Check if a sparse matrix is symmetric within tolerance.
// Tests whether A[i,j] == A[j,i] for all stored entries.
fn sparse_is_symmetric(a: SparseCSR, tol: f64) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if a.nrows != a.ncols {
        return false
    }
    var i = 0
    while i < a.nrows {
        var k = a.row_ptr[i]
        let row_end = a.row_ptr[i + 1]
        while k < row_end {
            let j = a.col_idx[k]
            let aij = a.values[k]
            // Look up A[j,i]
            let aji = sparse_get(a, j, i)
            if spr_abs_f64(aij - aji) > tol {
                return false
            }
            k = k + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// CONJUGATE GRADIENT SOLVER
// ============================================================================

// Conjugate Gradient method for symmetric positive definite systems Ax = b.
//
// Parameters:
//   a:        SPD sparse matrix
//   b:        right-hand side vector
//   x0:       initial guess
//   n:        dimension
//   tol:      convergence tolerance (on ||r||)
//   max_iter: maximum number of iterations
//
// Returns a CGResult with the solution, iteration count, residual, and convergence flag.
fn cg_solve(
    a: SparseCSR,
    b: [f64; 128],
    x0: [f64; 128],
    n: i32,
    tol: f64,
    max_iter: i32
) -> CGResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // x = x0
    var x: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        x[i] = x0[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // r = b - A*x
    let ax = sparse_matvec(a, x, n)
    var r = vec_sub(b, ax, n)

    // p = r
    var p = vec_copy(r, n)

    // rsold = r . r
    var rsold = vec_dot(r, r, n)

    // Check initial residual
    if spr_sqrt_f64(rsold) < tol {
        return CGResult {
            x: x,
            iterations: 0,
            residual: spr_sqrt_f64(rsold),
            converged: true
        }
    }

    var iter = 0
    var converged = false
    var done = false
    while iter < max_iter && !done {
        // Ap = A * p
        let ap = sparse_matvec(a, p, n)

        // alpha = rsold / (p . Ap)
        let pap = vec_dot(p, ap, n)
        if spr_abs_f64(pap) < 1e-30 {
            // Breakdown: p is orthogonal to Ap
            converged = false
            done = true
        } else {
            let alpha = rsold / pap

            // x = x + alpha * p
            i = 0
            while i < n {
                x[i] = x[i] + alpha * p[i]
                i = i + 1
            }

            // r = r - alpha * Ap
            i = 0
            while i < n {
                r[i] = r[i] - alpha * ap[i]
                i = i + 1
            }

            // rsnew = r . r
            let rsnew = vec_dot(r, r, n)

            // Check convergence
            if spr_sqrt_f64(rsnew) < tol {
                converged = true
                done = true
            } else {
                // p = r + (rsnew/rsold) * p
                let beta = rsnew / rsold
                i = 0
                while i < n {
                    p[i] = r[i] + beta * p[i]
                    i = i + 1
                }

                rsold = rsnew
            }
        }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_res = spr_sqrt_f64(vec_dot(r, r, n))

    return CGResult {
        x: x,
        iterations: iter,
        residual: final_res,
        converged: converged
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/tensor16.sio ===
//! stdlib/linalg/tensor16.sio - Rank-3 Tensor (16x16x16, f64)
//!
//! Dense storage for the FSNN Hessian H_n in R^{16x16x16}.
//! The Hessian is symmetric in the last two indices: H[i,j,k] = H[i,k,j].
//! Stored as flat [f64; 4096]: element (i,j,k) at index i*256 + j*16 + k.
//! Total size: 4096 * 8 = 32 KiB (fits in L1 cache).
//!
//! Key operations for the orbit engine:
//! - tensor16_jordan_transport: apply J_{z_n} to each fibre H[:,j,k]
//! - tensor16_frobenius_norm: ||H_n||_F for feature extraction

use linalg::mat16::{Mat16, mat16_vec_mul}

// ============================================================================
// TENSOR16 TYPE
// ============================================================================

pub struct Tensor16 {
    data: [f64; 4096],
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

pub fn tensor16_zeros() -> Tensor16 {
    Tensor16 { data: [0.0; 4096] }
}

// ============================================================================
// ELEMENT ACCESS
// ============================================================================
// Index: i*256 + j*16 + k

pub fn tensor16_get(t: Tensor16, i: i32, j: i32, k: i32) -> f64 {
    t.data[i * 256 + j * 16 + k]
}

pub fn tensor16_set(t: Tensor16, i: i32, j: i32, k: i32, val: f64) -> Tensor16 {
    var result = t
    result.data[i * 256 + j * 16 + k] = val
    return result
}

// Set symmetrically: H[i,j,k] = H[i,k,j] = val
pub fn tensor16_set_sym(t: Tensor16, i: i32, j: i32, k: i32, val: f64) -> Tensor16 {
    var result = t
    result.data[i * 256 + j * 16 + k] = val
    result.data[i * 256 + k * 16 + j] = val
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMS
// ============================================================================

fn t16_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// Frobenius norm: ||H||_F = sqrt(sum of squares of all elements)
pub fn tensor16_frobenius_norm(t: Tensor16) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 {
        sum = sum + t.data[i] * t.data[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    t16_sqrt(sum)
}

// ============================================================================
// JORDAN TRANSPORT
// ============================================================================
// Apply the 16x16 Jordan matrix Jz to each fibre H[:,j,k].
// For each (j,k) pair, compute: result[i,j,k] = sum_m Jz[i,m] * H[m,j,k]
// This is 16*16 = 256 matrix-vector products of size 16.
// Total: 256 * 256 = 65536 FMA.

pub fn tensor16_jordan_transport(jz: Mat16, h: Tensor16) -> Tensor16 {
    var result = Tensor16 { data: [0.0; 4096] }
    var j = 0
    while j < 16 {
        var k = 0
        while k < 16 {
            // Extract fibre h[:,j,k] as a 16-vector
            var fibre = [0.0; 16]
            var m = 0
            while m < 16 {
                fibre[m] = h.data[m * 256 + j * 16 + k]
                m = m + 1
            }
            // Apply Jz: new_fibre = Jz * fibre
            let new_fibre = mat16_vec_mul(jz, fibre)
            // Store back
            var i = 0
            while i < 16 {
                result.data[i * 256 + j * 16 + k] = new_fibre[i]
                i = i + 1
            }
            k = k + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// ADDITION
// ============================================================================

pub fn tensor16_add(a: Tensor16, b: Tensor16) -> Tensor16 {
    var d = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 {
        d[i] = a.data[i] + b.data[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    Tensor16 { data: d }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/linalg/vector.sio ===
// vector.d - Fixed-size vector types for Sounio linear algebra
//
// Provides small vector types (Vec2, Vec3, Vec4) and operations commonly
// needed in scientific computing: addition, scaling, dot product, norms.
//
// These are stack-allocated, Copy types optimized for SIMD operations.

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 {
        return 0.0 - x
    }
    return x
}

fn max_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// Square root via Newton-Raphson (10 iterations)
fn sqrt_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// VEC2 - 2-ELEMENT VECTOR
// ============================================================================

struct Vec2 {
    x: f64,
    y: f64
}

fn vec2_new(x: f64, y: f64) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: x, y: y }
}

fn vec2_zero() -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }
}

fn vec2_ones() -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: 1.0, y: 1.0 }
}

fn vec2_add(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: a.x + b.x, y: a.y + b.y }
}

fn vec2_sub(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: a.x - b.x, y: a.y - b.y }
}

fn vec2_scale(v: Vec2, s: f64) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: v.x * s, y: v.y * s }
}

fn vec2_neg(v: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: 0.0 - v.x, y: 0.0 - v.y }
}

fn vec2_dot(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> f64 {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y
}

fn vec2_norm_sq(v: Vec2) -> f64 {
    return v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y
}

fn vec2_norm(v: Vec2) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_val(vec2_norm_sq(v))
}

fn vec2_normalize(v: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    let n = vec2_norm(v)
    if n < 0.0000000001 {
        return vec2_zero()
    }
    return vec2_scale(v, 1.0 / n)
}

fn vec2_hadamard(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: a.x * b.x, y: a.y * b.y }
}

fn vec2_max(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: max_val(a.x, b.x), y: max_val(a.y, b.y) }
}

fn vec2_min(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: min_val(a.x, b.x), y: min_val(a.y, b.y) }
}

fn vec2_abs(v: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    return Vec2 { x: abs_val(v.x), y: abs_val(v.y) }
}

fn vec2_max_component(v: Vec2) -> f64 {
    return max_val(v.x, v.y)
}

fn vec2_sum(v: Vec2) -> f64 {
    return v.x + v.y
}

// ============================================================================
// VEC3 - 3-ELEMENT VECTOR
// ============================================================================

struct Vec3 {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    z: f64
}

fn vec3_new(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn vec3_zero() -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0 }
}

fn vec3_ones() -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: 1.0, y: 1.0, z: 1.0 }
}

fn vec3_add(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: a.x + b.x, y: a.y + b.y, z: a.z + b.z }
}

fn vec3_sub(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: a.x - b.x, y: a.y - b.y, z: a.z - b.z }
}

fn vec3_scale(v: Vec3, s: f64) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: v.x * s, y: v.y * s, z: v.z * s }
}

fn vec3_neg(v: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: 0.0 - v.x, y: 0.0 - v.y, z: 0.0 - v.z }
}

fn vec3_dot(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> f64 {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + a.z * b.z
}

fn vec3_cross(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 {
        x: a.y * b.z - a.z * b.y,
        y: a.z * b.x - a.x * b.z,
        z: a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x
    }
}

fn vec3_norm_sq(v: Vec3) -> f64 {
    return v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y + v.z * v.z
}

fn vec3_norm(v: Vec3) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_val(vec3_norm_sq(v))
}

fn vec3_normalize(v: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    let n = vec3_norm(v)
    if n < 0.0000000001 {
        return vec3_zero()
    }
    return vec3_scale(v, 1.0 / n)
}

fn vec3_hadamard(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: a.x * b.x, y: a.y * b.y, z: a.z * b.z }
}

fn vec3_max(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: max_val(a.x, b.x), y: max_val(a.y, b.y), z: max_val(a.z, b.z) }
}

fn vec3_min(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: min_val(a.x, b.x), y: min_val(a.y, b.y), z: min_val(a.z, b.z) }
}

fn vec3_abs(v: Vec3) -> Vec3 {
    return Vec3 { x: abs_val(v.x), y: abs_val(v.y), z: abs_val(v.z) }
}

fn vec3_max_component(v: Vec3) -> f64 {
    return max_val(max_val(v.x, v.y), v.z)
}

fn vec3_sum(v: Vec3) -> f64 {
    return v.x + v.y + v.z
}

struct Vec4 {

fn vec4_hadamard(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4 {

fn vec4_max(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4 {

struct Vec14 {
    c0: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64, c3: f64, c4: f64,
    c5: f64, c6: f64, c7: f64, c8: f64, c9: f64,
    c10: f64, c11: f64, c12: f64, c13: f64
}

fn vec14_new(
    v0: f64, v1: f64, v2: f64, v3: f64, v4: f64,
    v5: f64, v6: f64, v7: f64, v8: f64, v9: f64,
    v10: f64, v11: f64, v12: f64, v13: f64
) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: v0, c1: v1, c2: v2, c3: v3, c4: v4,
        c5: v5, c6: v6, c7: v7, c8: v8, c9: v9,
        c10: v10, c11: v11, c12: v12, c13: v13
    }
}

fn vec14_zero() -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: 0.0, c1: 0.0, c2: 0.0, c3: 0.0, c4: 0.0,
        c5: 0.0, c6: 0.0, c7: 0.0, c8: 0.0, c9: 0.0,
        c10: 0.0, c11: 0.0, c12: 0.0, c13: 0.0
    }
}

fn vec14_ones() -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: 1.0, c1: 1.0, c2: 1.0, c3: 1.0, c4: 1.0,
        c5: 1.0, c6: 1.0, c7: 1.0, c8: 1.0, c9: 1.0,
        c10: 1.0, c11: 1.0, c12: 1.0, c13: 1.0
    }
}

fn vec14_add(a: Vec14, b: Vec14) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: a.c0 + b.c0, c1: a.c1 + b.c1, c2: a.c2 + b.c2, c3: a.c3 + b.c3, c4: a.c4 + b.c4,
        c5: a.c5 + b.c5, c6: a.c6 + b.c6, c7: a.c7 + b.c7, c8: a.c8 + b.c8, c9: a.c9 + b.c9,
        c10: a.c10 + b.c10, c11: a.c11 + b.c11, c12: a.c12 + b.c12, c13: a.c13 + b.c13
    }
}

fn vec14_sub(a: Vec14, b: Vec14) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: a.c0 - b.c0, c1: a.c1 - b.c1, c2: a.c2 - b.c2, c3: a.c3 - b.c3, c4: a.c4 - b.c4,
        c5: a.c5 - b.c5, c6: a.c6 - b.c6, c7: a.c7 - b.c7, c8: a.c8 - b.c8, c9: a.c9 - b.c9,
        c10: a.c10 - b.c10, c11: a.c11 - b.c11, c12: a.c12 - b.c12, c13: a.c13 - b.c13
    }
}

fn vec14_scale(v: Vec14, s: f64) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: v.c0 * s, c1: v.c1 * s, c2: v.c2 * s, c3: v.c3 * s, c4: v.c4 * s,
        c5: v.c5 * s, c6: v.c6 * s, c7: v.c7 * s, c8: v.c8 * s, c9: v.c9 * s,
        c10: v.c10 * s, c11: v.c11 * s, c12: v.c12 * s, c13: v.c13 * s
    }
}

fn vec14_neg(v: Vec14) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: 0.0 - v.c0, c1: 0.0 - v.c1, c2: 0.0 - v.c2, c3: 0.0 - v.c3, c4: 0.0 - v.c4,
        c5: 0.0 - v.c5, c6: 0.0 - v.c6, c7: 0.0 - v.c7, c8: 0.0 - v.c8, c9: 0.0 - v.c9,
        c10: 0.0 - v.c10, c11: 0.0 - v.c11, c12: 0.0 - v.c12, c13: 0.0 - v.c13
    }
}

fn vec14_dot(a: Vec14, b: Vec14) -> f64 {
    return a.c0 * b.c0 + a.c1 * b.c1 + a.c2 * b.c2 + a.c3 * b.c3 + a.c4 * b.c4
         + a.c5 * b.c5 + a.c6 * b.c6 + a.c7 * b.c7 + a.c8 * b.c8 + a.c9 * b.c9
         + a.c10 * b.c10 + a.c11 * b.c11 + a.c12 * b.c12 + a.c13 * b.c13
}

fn vec14_norm_sq(v: Vec14) -> f64 {
    return vec14_dot(v, v)
}

fn vec14_norm(v: Vec14) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_val(vec14_norm_sq(v))
}

fn vec14_sum(v: Vec14) -> f64 {
    return v.c0 + v.c1 + v.c2 + v.c3 + v.c4 + v.c5 + v.c6
         + v.c7 + v.c8 + v.c9 + v.c10 + v.c11 + v.c12 + v.c13
}

fn vec14_hadamard(a: Vec14, b: Vec14) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: a.c0 * b.c0, c1: a.c1 * b.c1, c2: a.c2 * b.c2, c3: a.c3 * b.c3, c4: a.c4 * b.c4,
        c5: a.c5 * b.c5, c6: a.c6 * b.c6, c7: a.c7 * b.c7, c8: a.c8 * b.c8, c9: a.c9 * b.c9,
        c10: a.c10 * b.c10, c11: a.c11 * b.c11, c12: a.c12 * b.c12, c13: a.c13 * b.c13
    }
}

fn vec14_abs(v: Vec14) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: abs_val(v.c0), c1: abs_val(v.c1), c2: abs_val(v.c2), c3: abs_val(v.c3), c4: abs_val(v.c4),
        c5: abs_val(v.c5), c6: abs_val(v.c6), c7: abs_val(v.c7), c8: abs_val(v.c8), c9: abs_val(v.c9),
        c10: abs_val(v.c10), c11: abs_val(v.c11), c12: abs_val(v.c12), c13: abs_val(v.c13)
    }
}

fn vec14_max(a: Vec14, b: Vec14) -> Vec14 {
    return Vec14 {
        c0: max_val(a.c0, b.c0), c1: max_val(a.c1, b.c1), c2: max_val(a.c2, b.c2),
        c3: max_val(a.c3, b.c3), c4: max_val(a.c4, b.c4), c5: max_val(a.c5, b.c5),
        c6: max_val(a.c6, b.c6), c7: max_val(a.c7, b.c7), c8: max_val(a.c8, b.c8),
        c9: max_val(a.c9, b.c9), c10: max_val(a.c10, b.c10), c11: max_val(a.c11, b.c11),
        c12: max_val(a.c12, b.c12), c13: max_val(a.c13, b.c13)
    }
}

// RMS norm for ODE error estimation (weighted)
fn vec14_rms_weighted(err: Vec14, scale: Vec14) -> f64 {
    let e0 = err.c0 / scale.c0
    let e1 = err.c1 / scale.c1
    let e2 = err.c2 / scale.c2
    let e3 = err.c3 / scale.c3
    let e4 = err.c4 / scale.c4
    let e5 = err.c5 / scale.c5
    let e6 = err.c6 / scale.c6
    let e7 = err.c7 / scale.c7
    let e8 = err.c8 / scale.c8
    let e9 = err.c9 / scale.c9
    let e10 = err.c10 / scale.c10
    let e11 = err.c11 / scale.c11
    let e12 = err.c12 / scale.c12
    let e13 = err.c13 / scale.c13
    let sum_sq = e0*e0 + e1*e1 + e2*e2 + e3*e3 + e4*e4 + e5*e5 + e6*e6
               + e7*e7 + e8*e8 + e9*e9 + e10*e10 + e11*e11 + e12*e12 + e13*e13
    return sqrt_val(sum_sq / 14.0)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/logic/proof_certificates.sio ===
// Sprint 24 Track D: Proof Certificate stdlib
// References: Wadler (2015), Martin-Lof (1984), Chlipala CPDT

fn constructive_add_comm(a: i64, b: i64) -> bool {
    // Constructive proof of commutativity (trivially true for integers)
    a + b == b + a
}

fn lemma_transitivity(ab: bool, bc: bool) -> bool {
    // Transitivity: (A->B) ^ (B->C) -> (A->C)
    ab && bc
}

fn axiom_minimum(arr: [i64; 8], n: i64) -> i64 {
    // Axiom of choice: select minimum from first n elements
    var m: i64 = arr[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let v: i64 = arr[i as usize]
        if v < m { m = v }
        i = i + 1
    }
    m
}

fn proof_confidence_combine(c1: f64, c2: f64) -> f64 {
    // Conservative combination: minimum of two independent confidences
    if c1 < c2 { c1 } else { c2 }
}

fn is_constructive_proof(proof_kind: i64) -> bool {
    proof_kind == 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/log/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/log/lib.sio — Structured logging with level filtering
//
// LogEntry:  single log record (level, code, value, timestamp)
// LogBuffer: ring of up to 256 entries with min_level filter
//
// Level constants: LOG_TRACE=0 LOG_DEBUG=1 LOG_INFO=2
//                  LOG_WARN=3  LOG_ERROR=4 LOG_FATAL=5

struct LogEntry {
    level: i32,
    code: i32,
    value: f64,
    timestamp: i64,
}

struct LogBuffer {
    entries: [LogEntry; 256],
    count: i32,
    min_level: i32,
}

fn LOG_TRACE() -> i32 { 0 }
fn LOG_DEBUG() -> i32 { 1 }
fn LOG_INFO()  -> i32 { 2 }
fn LOG_WARN()  -> i32 { 3 }
fn LOG_ERROR() -> i32 { 4 }
fn LOG_FATAL() -> i32 { 5 }

fn log_buffer_new(min_level: i32) -> LogBuffer {
    let e0 = LogEntry { level: 0, code: 0, value: 0.0, timestamp: 0 }
    LogBuffer { entries: [e0; 256], count: 0, min_level: min_level }
}

fn log_append(buf: LogBuffer, level: i32, code: i32, value: f64, timestamp: i64) -> LogBuffer {
    var nb = buf
    if level >= nb.min_level && nb.count < 256 {
        let e = LogEntry { level: level, code: code, value: value, timestamp: timestamp }
        nb.entries[nb.count] = e
        nb.count = nb.count + 1
    }
    nb
}

fn log_count(buf: &LogBuffer) -> i32 {
    buf.count
}

fn log_count_level(buf: &LogBuffer, level: i32) -> i32 {
    var n: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < buf.count {
        if buf.entries[i].level == level {
            n = n + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    n
}

fn log_last_value(buf: &LogBuffer) -> f64 {
    if buf.count <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    buf.entries[buf.count - 1].value
}

fn log_clear(buf: LogBuffer) -> LogBuffer {
    var nb = buf
    nb.count = 0
    nb
}

fn log_filter_level(buf: &LogBuffer, level: i32, out: &! LogBuffer) {
    out.count = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < buf.count {
        if buf.entries[i].level == level && out.count < 256 {
            out.entries[out.count] = buf.entries[i]
            out.count = out.count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/log/mod.sio ===
//! stdlib/log

module log


// === FILE: stdlib/math/approx.sio ===
// stdlib/math/approx.sio — Approximation theory
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Chebyshev approximation: coefficients, Clenshaw evaluation, derivative, integral
//   Pade approximation: compute [p/q] approximant from Taylor coefficients
//   Minimax polynomial: Remez exchange algorithm
//
// References:
//   Mason & Handscomb (2003): "Chebyshev Polynomials"
//   Trefethen (2019): "Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice"
//   Press et al. (2007): "Numerical Recipes" Ch. 5.8, 5.12
//   Powell (1981): "Approximation Theory and Methods"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn ap_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ap_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

fn ap_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn ap_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

// =============================================================================
// Chebyshev approximation
// =============================================================================

// Compute Chebyshev coefficients c[0..n-1] for f on [a, b].
// Uses the DCT at Chebyshev nodes: x_k = cos(pi*(k+0.5)/n), k=0..n-1.
// c_j = (2/n) * sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(x_k) * cos(pi*j*(k+0.5)/n)
fn cheb_coeffs(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
               a: f64, b: f64, n: i32,
               out: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let bma = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let bpa = 0.5 * (b + a)

    // Evaluate f at Chebyshev nodes
    var fvals: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var k = 0
    while k < n {
        let theta = ap_pi() * ((k as f64) + 0.5) / (n as f64)
        let x = ap_cos(theta) * bma + bpa
        fvals[k] = f(x)
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Compute coefficients via DCT
    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        k = 0
        while k < n {
            let theta = ap_pi() * (j as f64) * ((k as f64) + 0.5) / (n as f64)
            sum = sum + fvals[k] * ap_cos(theta)
            k = k + 1
        }
        out[j] = 2.0 * sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Evaluate Chebyshev approximation at x in [a, b] using Clenshaw recurrence.
// coeffs[0..n-1] are the Chebyshev coefficients.
fn cheb_eval(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Map x from [a, b] to [-1, 1]
    let y = (2.0 * x - a - b) / (b - a)

    // Clenshaw recurrence: evaluate sum c_k * T_k(y)
    var d1 = 0.0
    var d2 = 0.0
    var j = n - 1
    while j >= 1 {
        let temp = d1
        d1 = 2.0 * y * d1 - d2 + coeffs[j]
        d2 = temp
        j = j - 1
    }
    y * d1 - d2 + 0.5 * coeffs[0]
}

// Derivative of Chebyshev series.
// If c[0..n-1] are coefficients of f, compute c'[0..n-2] of f'.
// Scaled to [a, b]: multiply by 2/(b-a).
fn cheb_derivative(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                   out: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let scale = 2.0 / (b - a)
    out[n - 1] = 0.0
    if n >= 2 { out[n - 2] = 2.0 * ((n - 1) as f64) * coeffs[n - 1] }

    var j = n - 3
    while j >= 0 {
        out[j] = out[j + 2] + 2.0 * ((j + 1) as f64) * coeffs[j + 1]
        j = j - 1
    }
    // Scale all coefficients
    var i = 0
    while i < n { out[i] = out[i] * scale; i = i + 1 }
    // First coefficient halved (standard convention)
    out[0] = out[0] * 0.5
}

// Integral of Chebyshev series.
// Computes antiderivative coefficients c_int[0..n] from c[0..n-1].
// c_int[0] is set to 0 (arbitrary constant).
fn cheb_integral(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, a: f64, b: f64,
                 out: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let scale = 0.5 * (b - a)
    out[0] = 0.0

    var j = 1
    while j < n {
        if j == 1 {
            out[1] = scale * (coeffs[0] - 0.5 * coeffs[2])
        } else if j < n - 1 {
            out[j] = scale * (coeffs[j - 1] - coeffs[j + 1]) / (2.0 * (j as f64))
        } else {
            out[j] = scale * coeffs[j - 1] / (2.0 * (j as f64))
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Truncation: number of significant Chebyshev coefficients.
// Returns the smallest m such that |c[m]|, |c[m+1]|, ... are all < tol.
fn cheb_truncate(coeffs: &[f64; 128], n: i32, tol: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var m = n
    while m > 1 {
        if ap_abs(coeffs[m - 1]) > tol { return m }
        m = m - 1
    }
    1
}

// =============================================================================
// Pade approximation
// =============================================================================

// Compute [p/q] Pade approximant from Taylor coefficients.
// Given f(x) = sum_{k=0}^{p+q} taylor[k] * x^k, find
// num[0..p] and den[0..q] such that num(x)/den(x) agrees with f(x)
// to order p+q.
//
// Method: solve the linear system for denominator coefficients,
// then compute numerator coefficients.
// Returns true if successful, false if singular.
fn pade_coeffs(taylor: &[f64; 64], n_taylor: i32,
               p: i32, q: i32,
               num: &![f64; 32], den: &![f64; 32]) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if p + q >= n_taylor { return false }

    // den[0] = 1 (normalization)
    den[0] = 1.0

    if q == 0 {
        // Polynomial approximation (no denominator)
        var i = 0
        while i <= p { num[i] = taylor[i]; i = i + 1 }
        return true
    }

    // Solve for den[1..q] from the equations:
    // sum_{j=0}^{q} den[j] * taylor[p+1-j+i] = 0, i = 0..q-1
    // (where taylor[k] = 0 for k < 0)
    // This is a q x q system: A * d = -b

    // Build the system (row-major in a flat array)
    var mat: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]  // q x q matrix
    var rhs: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]

    var i = 0
    while i < q {
        var j = 0
        while j < q {
            let idx = p + 1 + i - j - 1
            if idx >= 0 && idx < n_taylor {
                mat[i * q + j] = taylor[idx]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        let rhs_idx = p + 1 + i
        if rhs_idx >= 0 && rhs_idx < n_taylor {
            rhs[i] = 0.0 - taylor[rhs_idx]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting
    var col = 0
    while col < q {
        // Find pivot
        var max_val = ap_abs(mat[col * q + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < q {
            if ap_abs(mat[row * q + col]) > max_val {
                max_val = ap_abs(mat[row * q + col])
                max_row = row
            }
            row = row + 1
        }
        if max_val < 1.0e-14 { return false }

        // Swap rows
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < q {
                let temp = mat[col * q + j]
                mat[col * q + j] = mat[max_row * q + j]
                mat[max_row * q + j] = temp
                j = j + 1
            }
            let temp_r = rhs[col]
            rhs[col] = rhs[max_row]
            rhs[max_row] = temp_r
        }

        // Eliminate
        row = col + 1
        while row < q {
            let factor = mat[row * q + col] / mat[col * q + col]
            var j = col
            while j < q { mat[row * q + j] = mat[row * q + j] - factor * mat[col * q + j]; j = j + 1 }
            rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
            row = row + 1
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    var k = q - 1
    while k >= 0 {
        var s = rhs[k]
        var j = k + 1
        while j < q { s = s - mat[k * q + j] * den[j + 1]; j = j + 1 }
        den[k + 1] = s / mat[k * q + k]
        k = k - 1
    }

    // Compute numerator: num[k] = sum_{j=0}^{min(k,q)} den[j] * taylor[k-j]
    i = 0
    while i <= p {
        var s = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j <= q && j <= i {
            s = s + den[j] * taylor[i - j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        num[i] = s
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// Evaluate Pade rational function num(x)/den(x).
fn pade_eval(num: &[f64; 32], p: i32,
             den: &[f64; 32], q: i32,
             x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Horner evaluation for numerator
    var numer = num[p]
    var i = p - 1
    while i >= 0 { numer = numer * x + num[i]; i = i - 1 }

    // Horner evaluation for denominator
    var denom = den[q]
    i = q - 1
    while i >= 0 { denom = denom * x + den[i]; i = i - 1 }

    numer / denom
}

// =============================================================================
// Minimax polynomial (Remez exchange algorithm)
// =============================================================================

// Remez exchange algorithm to find the minimax polynomial of degree d
// approximating f on [a, b].
// Stores polynomial coefficients (monomial basis) in coeffs[0..d].
// Returns the maximum approximation error (equioscillation error).
fn remez(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
         a: f64, b: f64, degree: i32,
         coeffs: &![f64; 32]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = degree + 2  // n = d+2 reference points

    // Initialize reference points as Chebyshev nodes on [a, b]
    var refs: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let theta = ap_pi() * (i as f64) / ((n - 1) as f64)
        refs[i] = 0.5 * (a + b) - 0.5 * (b - a) * ap_cos(theta)
        i = i + 1
    }

    var max_err = 0.0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < 50 {
        // Solve the interpolation system:
        // p(x_i) + (-1)^i * E = f(x_i), i = 0..n-1
        // This is a (d+2) x (d+2) system for coeffs[0..d] and E.

        // Build matrix (row-major)
        var mat: [f64; 1024] = [0.0; 1024]
        var rhs: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            // Monomial basis: x^0, x^1, ..., x^d
            var x_pow = 1.0
            var j = 0
            while j <= degree {
                mat[i * n + j] = x_pow
                x_pow = x_pow * refs[i]
                j = j + 1
            }
            // Error column
            let sign = if i - (i / 2) * 2 == 0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
            mat[i * n + (degree + 1)] = sign
            rhs[i] = f(refs[i])
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Gaussian elimination
        var col = 0
        while col < n {
            var max_val = ap_abs(mat[col * n + col])
            var max_row = col
            var row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                if ap_abs(mat[row * n + col]) > max_val { max_val = ap_abs(mat[row * n + col]); max_row = row }
                row = row + 1
            }
            if max_row != col {
                var j = 0
                while j < n {
                    let temp = mat[col * n + j]; mat[col * n + j] = mat[max_row * n + j]; mat[max_row * n + j] = temp
                    j = j + 1
                }
                let tr = rhs[col]; rhs[col] = rhs[max_row]; rhs[max_row] = tr
            }
            row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                if ap_abs(mat[col * n + col]) > 1.0e-30 {
                    let factor = mat[row * n + col] / mat[col * n + col]
                    var j = col
                    while j < n { mat[row * n + j] = mat[row * n + j] - factor * mat[col * n + j]; j = j + 1 }
                    rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
                }
                row = row + 1
            }
            col = col + 1
        }

        // Back substitution
        var sol: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]
        var k = n - 1
        while k >= 0 {
            var s = rhs[k]
            var j = k + 1
            while j < n { s = s - mat[k * n + j] * sol[j]; j = j + 1 }
            if ap_abs(mat[k * n + k]) > 1.0e-30 { sol[k] = s / mat[k * n + k] }
            k = k - 1
        }

        // Extract coefficients and error
        i = 0
        while i <= degree { coeffs[i] = sol[i]; i = i + 1 }
        let levelled_err = ap_abs(sol[degree + 1])

        // Check convergence
        if ap_abs(levelled_err - max_err) < 1.0e-14 * ap_max(levelled_err, 1.0) {
            return levelled_err
        }
        max_err = levelled_err

        // Exchange step: find new reference points where error is maximal
        // Sample error at many points
        let n_sample = 200
        var new_refs: [f64; 34] = [0.0; 34]
        var ref_count = 0

        // Find extrema of error function by sampling
        var prev_err = 0.0
        var prev_x = a
        var si = 0
        while si <= n_sample && ref_count < n {
            let x = a + (b - a) * (si as f64) / (n_sample as f64)
            // Evaluate polynomial
            var px = 0.0
            var x_pow = 1.0
            var j = 0
            while j <= degree { px = px + coeffs[j] * x_pow; x_pow = x_pow * x; j = j + 1 }
            let err = f(x) - px

            if si > 0 {
                // Check for sign change (local extremum between prev and current)
                if (err > 0.0 && prev_err < 0.0) || (err < 0.0 && prev_err > 0.0) {
                    // Extremum near midpoint
                    if ref_count < n {
                        new_refs[ref_count] = 0.5 * (prev_x + x)
                        ref_count = ref_count + 1
                    }
                }
            }
            prev_err = err
            prev_x = x
            si = si + 1
        }

        // If we found enough reference points, update
        if ref_count >= n {
            i = 0
            while i < n { refs[i] = new_refs[i]; i = i + 1 }
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }
    max_err
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/cayley_dickson.sio ===
//! stdlib/math/cayley_dickson.sio - Cayley-Dickson Construction Helpers (f64)
//!
//! Concrete helper functions for the Cayley-Dickson doubling construction:
//!   R -> C -> H -> O -> S
//! Provides f64-precision octonionic multiplication and conjugation components
//! used by sedenion64.sio for the FSNN pipeline.
//!
//! The Cayley-Dickson product rule for (a,b)*(c,d):
//!   real part = a*c - conj(d)*b
//!   imag part = d*a + b*conj(c)
//! where a,b,c,d are elements of the algebra at the previous level.
//!
//! References:
//! - Baez, "The Octonions", Bull. AMS 2002
//! - Cayley-Dickson construction: each level doubles dimension, loses one property
//!   C: loses ordering | H: loses commutativity | O: loses associativity | S: loses alternativity

// ============================================================================
// OCTONIONIC MULTIPLICATION (f64)
// ============================================================================
// Standard Cayley-Dickson multiplication table for octonions.
// Same formula as oct_mul in octonion.sio but with f64 precision.
// Verified for norm multiplicativity |ab| = |a||b| and Moufang identities.
// Complexity: 64 multiplications + 56 additions = 120 FLOPs

fn oct64_mul_components(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64,
    b0: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64, b3: f64, b4: f64, b5: f64, b6: f64, b7: f64
) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64) {
    let c0 = a0*b0 - a1*b1 - a2*b2 - a3*b3 - a4*b4 - a5*b5 - a6*b6 - a7*b7
    let c1 = a0*b1 + a1*b0 + a2*b3 - a3*b2 + a4*b5 - a5*b4 - a6*b7 + a7*b6
    let c2 = a0*b2 - a1*b3 + a2*b0 + a3*b1 + a4*b6 + a5*b7 - a6*b4 - a7*b5
    let c3 = a0*b3 + a1*b2 - a2*b1 + a3*b0 + a4*b7 - a5*b6 + a6*b5 - a7*b4
    let c4 = a0*b4 - a1*b5 - a2*b6 - a3*b7 + a4*b0 + a5*b1 + a6*b2 + a7*b3
    let c5 = a0*b5 + a1*b4 - a2*b7 + a3*b6 - a4*b1 + a5*b0 - a6*b3 + a7*b2
    let c6 = a0*b6 + a1*b7 + a2*b4 - a3*b5 - a4*b2 + a5*b3 + a6*b0 - a7*b1
    let c7 = a0*b7 - a1*b6 + a2*b5 + a3*b4 - a4*b3 - a5*b2 + a6*b1 + a7*b0
    (c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7)
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONIONIC CONJUGATION (f64)
// ============================================================================
// conj(a0 + a1*e1 + ... + a7*e7) = a0 - a1*e1 - ... - a7*e7
// Property: conj(ab) = conj(b)*conj(a) (anti-automorphism)

fn oct64_conj_components(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64
) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64) {
    (a0, 0.0 - a1, 0.0 - a2, 0.0 - a3, 0.0 - a4, 0.0 - a5, 0.0 - a6, 0.0 - a7)
}

// ============================================================================
// CAYLEY-DICKSON SEDENION PRODUCT (f64)
// ============================================================================
// Given sedenion s1 = (a, b) and s2 = (c, d) where a,b,c,d are octonions:
//   (a,b) * (c,d) = (a*c - conj(d)*b, d*a + b*conj(c))
//
// This requires 4 octonionic multiplications + 2 conjugations:
//   p1 = a * c
//   p2 = conj(d) * b
//   p3 = d * a
//   p4 = b * conj(c)
//   result_lo = p1 - p2
//   result_hi = p3 + p4
//
// Complexity: 4 * 120 + 16 + 16 = 512 FLOPs

fn cd_product_16(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64,
    b0: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64, b3: f64, b4: f64, b5: f64, b6: f64, b7: f64,
    c0: f64, c1: f64, c2: f64, c3: f64, c4: f64, c5: f64, c6: f64, c7: f64,
    d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64, d3: f64, d4: f64, d5: f64, d6: f64, d7: f64
) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64,
      f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64) {

    // p1 = a * c
    let p1 = oct64_mul_components(a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7,
                                   c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7)

    // p2 = conj(d) * b
    let cd = oct64_conj_components(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7)
    let p2 = oct64_mul_components(cd.0, cd.1, cd.2, cd.3, cd.4, cd.5, cd.6, cd.7,
                                   b0, b1, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, b7)

    // p3 = d * a
    let p3 = oct64_mul_components(d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7,
                                   a0, a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7)

    // p4 = b * conj(c)
    let cc = oct64_conj_components(c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c7)
    let p4 = oct64_mul_components(b0, b1, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, b7,
                                   cc.0, cc.1, cc.2, cc.3, cc.4, cc.5, cc.6, cc.7)

    // result_lo = p1 - p2 (real octonion half)
    let r0 = p1.0 - p2.0
    let r1 = p1.1 - p2.1
    let r2 = p1.2 - p2.2
    let r3 = p1.3 - p2.3
    let r4 = p1.4 - p2.4
    let r5 = p1.5 - p2.5
    let r6 = p1.6 - p2.6
    let r7 = p1.7 - p2.7

    // result_hi = p3 + p4 (imaginary octonion half)
    let r8  = p3.0 + p4.0
    let r9  = p3.1 + p4.1
    let r10 = p3.2 + p4.2
    let r11 = p3.3 + p4.3
    let r12 = p3.4 + p4.4
    let r13 = p3.5 + p4.5
    let r14 = p3.6 + p4.6
    let r15 = p3.7 + p4.7

    (r0, r1, r2, r3, r4, r5, r6, r7,
     r8, r9, r10, r11, r12, r13, r14, r15)
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONIONIC NORM SQUARED (f64)
// ============================================================================

fn oct64_norm_sq_components(
    a0: f64, a1: f64, a2: f64, a3: f64, a4: f64, a5: f64, a6: f64, a7: f64
) -> f64 {
    a0*a0 + a1*a1 + a2*a2 + a3*a3 + a4*a4 + a5*a5 + a6*a6 + a7*a7
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/combinatorics.sio ===
// stdlib/math/combinatorics.sio — Combinatorial functions
//
// Pure Sounio implementations of classical combinatorial quantities:
//   Binomial coefficients, Stirling numbers (1st & 2nd kind), Catalan numbers,
//   Bell numbers, integer partitions, derangements, multinomial coefficients,
//   falling/rising factorials, harmonic numbers, Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers.
//
// All functions are pure Sounio — zero FFI.
//
// References:
//   Graham, Knuth, Patashnik (1994): "Concrete Mathematics" (2nd ed.)
//   Stanley (2011): "Enumerative Combinatorics" Vol. 1 (2nd ed.)
//   Comtet (1974): "Advanced Combinatorics"
//   DLMF Ch. 24, 26

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (must precede callers)
// =============================================================================

fn comb_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn comb_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn comb_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    var k_f = x / 0.6931471805599453
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn comb_lgamma(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 1.0e30 }
    var val = x
    var shift = 0.0
    while val < 8.0 {
        shift = shift + comb_ln(val)
        val = val + 1.0
    }
    var result = (val - 0.5) * comb_ln(val) - val + 0.5 * 1.8378770664093453
    let inv_v = 1.0 / val
    let iv2 = inv_v * inv_v
    result = result + inv_v / 12.0
    result = result - inv_v * iv2 / 360.0
    result = result + inv_v * iv2 * iv2 / 1260.0
    result - shift
}

// =============================================================================
// Binomial coefficients
// =============================================================================

// Exact integer binomial coefficient C(n, k) = n! / (k! * (n-k)!).
// Uses the multiplicative formula to avoid overflow as long as possible.
// For n, k >= 0.
fn binomial(n: i64, k: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k < 0 || k > n { return 0 }
    if k == 0 || k == n { return 1 }
    // Use symmetry: C(n, k) = C(n, n-k)
    var kk = k
    if kk > n - kk { kk = n - kk }

    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < kk {
        result = result * (n - i)
        result = result / (i + 1)
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Generalized binomial coefficient for real arguments via lgamma.
// C(n, k) = Gamma(n+1) / (Gamma(k+1) * Gamma(n-k+1))
fn binomial_f64(n: f64, k: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k < 0.0 || k > n { return 0.0 }
    comb_exp(comb_lgamma(n + 1.0) - comb_lgamma(k + 1.0) - comb_lgamma(n - k + 1.0))
}

// =============================================================================
// Falling / Rising factorials
// =============================================================================

// Falling factorial: (n)_k = n * (n-1) * ... * (n-k+1)
// Also known as Pochhammer symbol (in some conventions).
fn falling_factorial(n: i64, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k <= 0 { return 1 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < k {
        result = result * (n - (i as i64))
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol): n^{(k)} = n * (n+1) * ... * (n+k-1)
fn rising_factorial(n: i64, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if k <= 0 { return 1 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < k {
        result = result * (n + (i as i64))
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Stirling numbers
// =============================================================================

// Unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind |s(n, k)|.
// Number of permutations of n elements with exactly k disjoint cycles.
// Recurrence: |s(n, k)| = (n-1)*|s(n-1, k)| + |s(n-1, k-1)|
// Uses a DP table. Max n, k = 20.
fn stirling_first(n: i32, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 || k < 0 || k > n { return 0 }
    if n == 0 && k == 0 { return 1 }
    if n == 0 || k == 0 { return 0 }
    if k == n { return 1 }

    // DP: use two rows
    var prev: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    var curr: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    prev[0] = 1   // s(0, 0) = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        var j = 0
        while j <= 20 { curr[j] = 0; j = j + 1 }

        j = 1
        while j <= i {
            curr[j] = ((i - 1) as i64) * prev[j] + prev[j - 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Copy curr to prev
        j = 0
        while j <= 20 { prev[j] = curr[j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    prev[k]
}

// Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n, k).
// Number of ways to partition n elements into k non-empty subsets.
// Recurrence: S(n, k) = k*S(n-1, k) + S(n-1, k-1)
// Max n, k = 20.
fn stirling_second(n: i32, k: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 || k < 0 || k > n { return 0 }
    if n == 0 && k == 0 { return 1 }
    if n == 0 || k == 0 { return 0 }
    if k == 1 || k == n { return 1 }

    var prev: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    var curr: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    prev[0] = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        var j = 0
        while j <= 20 { curr[j] = 0; j = j + 1 }

        j = 1
        while j <= i {
            curr[j] = (j as i64) * prev[j] + prev[j - 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        j = 0
        while j <= 20 { prev[j] = curr[j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    prev[k]
}

// =============================================================================
// Named sequences
// =============================================================================

// Catalan number C_n = C(2n, n) / (n+1).
// Counts Dyck paths, valid parenthesizations, binary trees with n+1 leaves, etc.
fn catalan_number(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return 1 }
    let b = binomial((2 * n) as i64, n as i64)
    b / ((n + 1) as i64)
}

// Bell number B_n = total partitions of an n-element set.
// Uses the Bell triangle. Max n = 25.
fn bell(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return 1 }

    var row: [i64; 26] = [0; 26]
    row[0] = 1  // B_0

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        // Bell triangle: row starts with last element of previous row
        var new_row: [i64; 26] = [0; 26]
        new_row[0] = row[i - 1]
        var j = 1
        while j <= i {
            new_row[j] = new_row[j - 1] + row[j - 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        // Copy
        j = 0
        while j <= i { row[j] = new_row[j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    row[0]
}

// Partition function p(n) = number of integer partitions of n.
// Uses Euler's pentagonal number theorem recurrence:
//   p(n) = sum_{k!=0} (-1)^{k+1} * p(n - k*(3k-1)/2)
// Max n = 500.
fn partition_count(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return 1 }

    var table: [i64; 501] = [0; 501]
    table[0] = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        var sum: i64 = 0
        var k = 1
        var done = false
        while !done {
            // Generalized pentagonal numbers: k*(3k-1)/2 and k*(3k+1)/2
            let pent1 = k * (3 * k - 1) / 2
            let pent2 = k * (3 * k + 1) / 2

            if pent1 > i { done = true }
            else {
                let sign: i64 = if k - (k / 2) * 2 == 1 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
                sum = sum + sign * table[i - pent1]
                if pent2 <= i {
                    sum = sum + sign * table[i - pent2]
                }
                k = k + 1
            }
        }
        table[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
    table[n]
}

// Derangement (subfactorial) !n = number of permutations with no fixed points.
// D(n) = (n-1) * (D(n-1) + D(n-2)), D(0) = 1, D(1) = 0.
fn derangements(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 { return 1 }
    if n == 1 { return 0 }
    if n == 2 { return 1 }

    var prev2: i64 = 1   // D(0)
    var prev1: i64 = 0   // D(1)
    var i = 2
    while i <= n {
        let current = ((i - 1) as i64) * (prev1 + prev2)
        prev2 = prev1
        prev1 = current
        i = i + 1
    }
    prev1
}

// Multinomial coefficient: (n1 + n2 + ... + nc)! / (n1! * n2! * ... * nc!)
// Input: array ks of length count.
fn multinomial(ks: &[i32; 16], count: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if count <= 0 { return 1 }

    var total: i64 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < count { total = total + (ks[i] as i64); i = i + 1 }

    var result: i64 = 1
    var running: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < count {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < ks[i] {
            running = running + 1
            result = result * running
            result = result / ((j + 1) as i64)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Harmonic numbers
// =============================================================================

// Harmonic number H_n = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n.
fn harmonic(n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 1 { return 1.0 }

    // For large n, use asymptotic: H_n ~ ln(n) + gamma + 1/(2n) - 1/(12n^2) + ...
    if n > 1000 {
        let nf = n as f64
        let gamma = 0.57721566490153286061
        return comb_ln(nf) + gamma + 1.0 / (2.0 * nf) - 1.0 / (12.0 * nf * nf) + 1.0 / (120.0 * nf * nf * nf * nf)
    }

    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i <= n {
        sum = sum + 1.0 / (i as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Generalized harmonic number H_{n, s} = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k^s.
fn generalized_harmonic(n: i32, s: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    var sum = 0.0
    var k = 1
    while k <= n {
        let kf = k as f64
        // k^s = exp(s * ln(k))
        let term = if s == 1.0 { 1.0 / kf }
                   else if s == 2.0 { 1.0 / (kf * kf) }
                   else { 1.0 / comb_exp(s * comb_ln(kf)) }
        sum = sum + term
        k = k + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Bernoulli numbers
// =============================================================================

// Bernoulli number B_n via the Akiyama-Tanigawa algorithm.
// B_0=1, B_1=-1/2, B_2=1/6, B_3=0, B_4=-1/30, B_5=0, ...
// Odd B_n = 0 for n >= 3.
// Max n = 30.
fn bernoulli(n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 0 { return 1.0 }
    if n == 1 { return 0.0 - 0.5 }
    // Odd Bernoulli numbers (n >= 3) are 0
    if n >= 3 && n - (n / 2) * 2 == 1 { return 0.0 }

    // Akiyama-Tanigawa algorithm
    var a: [f64; 31] = [0.0; 31]
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        a[i] = 1.0 / ((i + 1) as f64)
        var j = i
        while j >= 1 {
            a[j - 1] = (j as f64) * (a[j - 1] - a[j])
            j = j - 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    a[0]
}

// =============================================================================
// Euler (zigzag) numbers
// =============================================================================

// Euler number E_n (also called secant/tangent numbers).
// E_0=1, E_1=0, E_2=-1, E_3=0, E_4=5, ...
// Related to sec(x) = sum E_{2n} * x^{2n} / (2n)!
// Uses the triangle method. Max n = 20.
fn euler_number(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 0 { return 0 }
    if n == 0 { return 1 }
    if n - (n / 2) * 2 == 1 { return 0 }

    // Compute via tangent/secant number triangle
    let m = n / 2

    var t: [i64; 21] = [0; 21]
    t[0] = 1  // E_0 = 1

    var i = 1
    while i <= m {
        // Build up using recurrence for secant numbers
        t[i] = 0
        var j = i
        while j >= 1 {
            t[j] = t[j - 1] * ((2 * (i - j) + 1) as i64) + t[j]
            j = j - 1
        }
        t[0] = 0
        j = 0
        while j < i {
            t[j] = t[j + 1]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Sign: (-1)^m
    let val = t[0]
    if m - (m / 2) * 2 == 0 { val } else { 0 - val }
}

// =============================================================================
// Double factorial
// =============================================================================

// Double factorial n!! = n * (n-2) * (n-4) * ... * (1 or 2).
fn double_factorial(n: i32) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n <= 0 { return 1 }
    if n <= 2 { return n as i64 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var k = n
    while k > 1 {
        result = result * (k as i64)
        k = k - 2
    }
    result
}

// === FILE: stdlib/math/constrained.sio ===
// stdlib/math/constrained.sio — Constrained nonlinear optimization
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   L-BFGS (limited-memory quasi-Newton)
//   Projected gradient descent (box constraints)
//   Augmented Lagrangian method
//   Quadratic penalty method
//   Log-barrier interior point method
//   KKT violation checking
//
// References:
//   Nocedal & Wright (2006): "Numerical Optimization" Ch. 17-18
//   Bertsekas (1999): "Nonlinear Programming"
//   Boyd & Vandenberghe (2004): "Convex Optimization" Ch. 11

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (co_ prefix, self-contained)
// =============================================================================

fn co_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn co_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn co_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn co_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// exp(x) via Taylor series with Div, Mut, Panic, range reduction
fn co_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 700.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -700.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f - 1.0) as i32 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 30 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    var j = 0
    if k >= 0 {
        while j < k { result = result * 2.0; j = j + 1 }
    } else {
        var neg_k = 0 - k
        while j < neg_k { result = result * 0.5; j = j + 1 }
    }
    result
}

// ln(x) via series with Div, Mut, Panic, range reduction
fn co_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e308 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var m = x
    var k: i32 = 0
    while m > 2.0 { m = m * 0.5; k = k + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; k = k - 1 }
    let u = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var sum = u
    var term = u
    var n = 1
    while n < 40 {
        term = term * u2
        sum = sum + term / (2.0 * (n as f64) + 1.0)
        n = n + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (k as f64) * ln2
}
