// ============================================================
// Value of information (Cramer-Rao lower bound proxy)
// ============================================================

fn cramer_rao_lower_bound(fisher_info: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    // Var(theta_hat) >= 1 / I(theta)
    1.0 / fisher_info
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/integral_eq.sio ===
// stdlib/math/integral_eq.sio — Integral equations
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Fredholm equations of the 1st and 2nd kind
//   Volterra equations of the 2nd kind
//   Nystrom method with Gauss-Legendre quadrature
//   Tikhonov regularization for ill-posed problems
//   Green's function methods for BVPs
//   Eigenvalue problems for integral operators
//
// References:
//   Atkinson (1997): "The Numerical Solution of Integral Equations of the Second Kind"
//   Kress (2014): "Linear Integral Equations"
//   Press et al. (2007): "Numerical Recipes" Ch. 19

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn ie_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ie_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn ie_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn ie_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn ie_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    var kf = x / 0.6931471805599453
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 { var i = 0; while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    else { var i = 0; while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    result
}

fn ie_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn ie_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    ie_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn ie_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64); k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn ie_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn ie_pow(base: f64, exp_val: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // base^exp_val = exp(exp_val * ln(base))
    if base <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    ie_exp(exp_val * ie_ln(base))
}

// =============================================================================
// Linear algebra helpers
// =============================================================================

// Dot product of a[0..n-1] and b[0..n-1].
fn ie_dot(a: &[f64; 128], b: &[f64; 128], n: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]; i = i + 1 }
    sum
}

// Matrix-vector product y = A*x, A is m x n stored row-major in flat array.
fn ie_mat_vec(A: &[f64; 16384], x: &[f64; 128], y: &![f64; 128], m: i32, n: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n { sum = sum + A[i * n + j] * x[j]; j = j + 1 }
        y[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.
// Solves Ax = b where A is n x n stored row-major in flat array.
// A and b are modified in-place; solution stored in x.
fn ie_gauss_solve(A: &![f64; 16384], b: &![f64; 128], x: &![f64; 128], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Forward elimination with partial pivoting
    var col = 0
    while col < n {
        // Find pivot
        var max_val = ie_abs(A[col * n + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let v = ie_abs(A[row * n + col])
            if v > max_val { max_val = v; max_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }

        // Swap rows in A and b
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                let tmp = A[col * n + j]
                A[col * n + j] = A[max_row * n + j]
                A[max_row * n + j] = tmp
                j = j + 1
            }
            let tmp_b = b[col]
            b[col] = b[max_row]
            b[max_row] = tmp_b
        }

        // Eliminate below pivot
        let pivot = A[col * n + col]
        if ie_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            // Singular or near-singular — skip
            col = col + 1
            // continue equivalent: just proceed
        } else {
            row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                let factor = A[row * n + col] / pivot
                var j = col + 1
                while j < n {
                    A[row * n + j] = A[row * n + j] - factor * A[col * n + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
                A[row * n + col] = 0.0
                b[row] = b[row] - factor * b[col]
                row = row + 1
            }
            col = col + 1
        }
    }

    // Back substitution
    var k = n - 1
    while k >= 0 {
        var s = b[k]
        var j = k + 1
        while j < n { s = s - A[k * n + j] * x[j]; j = j + 1 }
        if ie_abs(A[k * n + k]) > 1.0e-30 {
            x[k] = s / A[k * n + k]
        } else {
            x[k] = 0.0
        }
        k = k - 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Result structs
// =============================================================================

struct IEResult {
    u: [f64; 128],
    nodes: [f64; 128],
    weights: [f64; 128],
    n: i32,
    residual: f64,
    converged: bool
}

struct IEEigenResult {
    eigenvalues: [f64; 64],
    eigenvectors: [f64; 8192],
    n_found: i32,
    n_quad: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Gauss-Legendre quadrature
// =============================================================================

// Compute n-point Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights on [-1, 1].
// Uses Newton's method on the Legendre polynomial P_n(x).
// Recurrence: (k+1) P_{k+1}(x) = (2k+1) x P_k(x) - k P_{k-1}(x)
// Derivative: P'_n(x) = n (x P_n(x) - P_{n-1}(x)) / (x^2 - 1)
// Initial guess: x_i = cos(pi * (i - 0.25) / (n + 0.5))
// Weights: w_i = 2 / ((1 - x_i^2) * [P'_n(x_i)]^2)
fn ie_gauss_legendre(n: i32, nodes: &![f64; 128], weights: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n_half = (n + 1) / 2
    var i = 0
    while i < n_half {
        // Initial guess: cos(pi * (i + 0.75) / (n + 0.5))
        var x = ie_cos(ie_pi() * ((i as f64) + 0.75) / ((n as f64) + 0.5))

        // Newton iterations to refine root of P_n(x)
        var iter = 0
        while iter < 50 {
            // Evaluate P_n(x) and P_{n-1}(x) via recurrence
            var p0 = 1.0   // P_0(x)
            var p1 = x     // P_1(x)
            var k = 1
            while k < n {
                let p2 = ((2 * k + 1) as f64 * x * p1 - (k as f64) * p0) / ((k + 1) as f64)
                p0 = p1
                p1 = p2
                k = k + 1
            }
            // p1 = P_n(x), p0 = P_{n-1}(x)

            // Derivative: P'_n(x) = n * (x * P_n - P_{n-1}) / (x^2 - 1)
            let dp = (n as f64) * (x * p1 - p0) / (x * x - 1.0)

            let dx = p1 / dp
            x = x - dx
            if ie_abs(dx) < 1.0e-15 { iter = 50 }
            iter = iter + 1
        }

        // Store symmetric pair
        nodes[i] = 0.0 - x
        nodes[n - 1 - i] = x

        // Re-evaluate derivative at converged x for weight computation
        var p0w = 1.0
        var p1w = x
        var k = 1
        while k < n {
            let p2 = ((2 * k + 1) as f64 * x * p1w - (k as f64) * p0w) / ((k + 1) as f64)
            p0w = p1w
            p1w = p2
            k = k + 1
        }
        let dpw = (n as f64) * (x * p1w - p0w) / (x * x - 1.0)
        let w = 2.0 / ((1.0 - x * x) * dpw * dpw)

        weights[i] = w
        weights[n - 1 - i] = w

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Map GL nodes/weights from [-1, 1] to [a, b].
// x_mapped = (b - a) / 2 * t + (a + b) / 2
// w_mapped = w * (b - a) / 2
fn ie_gauss_legendre_ab(a: f64, b: f64, n: i32,
                        nodes: &![f64; 128], weights: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    ie_gauss_legendre(n, nodes, weights)
    let half_len = 0.5 * (b - a)
    let midpoint = 0.5 * (a + b)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        nodes[i] = half_len * nodes[i] + midpoint
        weights[i] = weights[i] * half_len
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Residual computation
// =============================================================================

// Internal helper for Fredholm 2nd kind residual.
// Compute ||u - f - lambda K u||_inf at quadrature nodes.
fn ie_residual_fredholm2_internal(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                                  f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                                  lambda: f64, result: &IEResult) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var max_res = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < result.n {
        var ku_i = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < result.n {
            ku_i = ku_i + result.weights[j] * K(result.nodes[i], result.nodes[j]) * result.u[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let expected = f(result.nodes[i]) + lambda * ku_i
        let res_i = ie_abs(result.u[i] - expected)
        if res_i > max_res { max_res = res_i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    max_res
}

// Public residual computation for Fredholm 2nd kind.
// Compute ||u - f - lambda K u||_inf at quadrature nodes.
fn ie_residual_fredholm2(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                         f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                         lambda: f64, result: &IEResult) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    ie_residual_fredholm2_internal(K, f, lambda, result)
}

// =============================================================================
// Fredholm equations of the 2nd kind — Nystrom method
// =============================================================================

// Solve u(x) = f(x) + lambda * integral_a^b K(x,t) u(t) dt
// via the Nystrom method with Gauss-Legendre quadrature.
//
// Discretization: at quadrature nodes {t_j}, the equation becomes
//   u(t_i) = f(t_i) + lambda * sum_j w_j K(t_i, t_j) u(t_j)
// which is the linear system (I - lambda W K) u = f where
//   W K is the matrix with entries w_j K(t_i, t_j).
fn fredholm2_nystrom(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                     f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                     a: f64, b: f64, lambda: f64, n: i32,
                     result: &!IEResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute GL quadrature on [a, b]
    ie_gauss_legendre_ab(a, b, n, &!result.nodes, &!result.weights)
    result.n = n

    // Build system matrix A = I - lambda * W * K
    // A[i * n + j] = delta_{ij} - lambda * w_j * K(t_i, t_j)
    var mat: [f64; 16384] = [0.0; 16384]
    var rhs: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        rhs[i] = f(result.nodes[i])
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let kval = K(result.nodes[i], result.nodes[j])
            mat[i * n + j] = 0.0 - lambda * result.weights[j] * kval
            if i == j {
                mat[i * n + j] = mat[i * n + j] + 1.0
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Solve the system
    var sol: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    ie_gauss_solve(&!mat, &!rhs, &!sol, n)

    // Store solution
    i = 0
    while i < n { result.u[i] = sol[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Compute residual
    result.residual = ie_residual_fredholm2_internal(K, f, lambda, result)
    result.converged = result.residual < 1.0e-10
}

// Nystrom interpolation formula: evaluate solution at arbitrary x.
// u(x) = f(x) + lambda * sum_j w_j K(x, t_j) u(t_j)
fn fredholm2_eval(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  lambda: f64, result: &IEResult, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var j = 0
    while j < result.n {
        sum = sum + result.weights[j] * K(x, result.nodes[j]) * result.u[j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    f(x) + lambda * sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Fredholm equations of the 1st kind — Tikhonov regularization
// =============================================================================

// Solve the ill-posed equation integral_a^b K(x,t) u(t) dt = f(x)
// with Tikhonov regularization: minimize ||Ku - f||^2 + alpha ||u||^2.
//
// Discretization via GL quadrature:
//   K_ij = sqrt(w_i) * K(t_i, t_j) * sqrt(w_j)   (symmetrized)
//   f_i  = sqrt(w_i) * f(t_i)
// Normal equations: (K^T K + alpha I) u = K^T f
// where alpha is the regularization parameter.
fn fredholm1_tikhonov(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                      a: f64, b: f64, alpha: f64, n: i32,
                      result: &!IEResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute GL quadrature on [a, b]
    ie_gauss_legendre_ab(a, b, n, &!result.nodes, &!result.weights)
    result.n = n

    // Build the discrete kernel matrix K_ij = w_j * K(t_i, t_j)
    // and the RHS vector f_i = f(t_i)
    var kmat: [f64; 16384] = [0.0; 16384]
    var fvec: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        fvec[i] = f(result.nodes[i])
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            kmat[i * n + j] = result.weights[j] * K(result.nodes[i], result.nodes[j])
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Build normal equations: (K^T W_diag K + alpha I) u = K^T W_diag f
    // where W_diag accounts for quadrature in the outer integral.
    // Here we use: A = K^T diag(w) K + alpha I, rhs = K^T diag(w) f
    // Note: kmat already contains w_j factors, so K^T * diag(w_i) * K
    // has entry (j, k) = sum_i w_i * kmat[i,j] * kmat[i,k] / w_j / w_k * w_j * w_k
    // Simpler: just form A[j,k] = sum_i w_i * K(t_i,t_j)*w_j * K(t_i,t_k)*w_k
    // But let's directly compute K^T W K where K has entries w_j K(t_i,t_j).

    var ata: [f64; 16384] = [0.0; 16384]
    var atf: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]

    // A^T A: ata[j, k] = sum_i kmat[i,j] * kmat[i,k] * w_i
    // A^T f: atf[j] = sum_i kmat[i,j] * fvec[i] * w_i
    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        var k = 0
        while k < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            i = 0
            while i < n {
                sum = sum + kmat[i * n + j] * kmat[i * n + k] * result.weights[i]
                i = i + 1
            }
            ata[j * n + k] = sum
            k = k + 1
        }
        var sumf = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            sumf = sumf + kmat[i * n + j] * fvec[i] * result.weights[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        atf[j] = sumf
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Add regularization: ata += alpha * I
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        ata[i * n + i] = ata[i * n + i] + alpha
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Solve the regularized system
    var sol: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    ie_gauss_solve(&!ata, &!atf, &!sol, n)

    // Store solution
    i = 0
    while i < n { result.u[i] = sol[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Compute residual: ||Ku - f||_inf at quadrature nodes
    var max_res = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var ku_i = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j < n {
            ku_i = ku_i + kmat[i * n + j] * sol[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let res_i = ie_abs(ku_i - fvec[i])
        if res_i > max_res { max_res = res_i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.residual = max_res
    result.converged = max_res < 1.0e-6
}

// =============================================================================
// Volterra equations of the 2nd kind
// =============================================================================

// Solve u(x) = f(x) + integral_a^x K(x,t) u(t) dt (Volterra 2nd kind)
// using the product trapezoidal method with forward marching.
//
// At uniform nodes x_i = a + i*h, the discretization gives:
//   u_0 = f(a)
//   u_i = f(x_i) + h * [K(x_i,x_0)*u_0/2 + sum_{j=1}^{i-1} K(x_i,x_j)*u_j
//                        + K(x_i,x_i)*u_i/2]
// Rearranging for u_i:
//   u_i * (1 - h/2 * K(x_i,x_i)) = f(x_i) + h * [K(x_i,x_0)*u_0/2
//                                    + sum_{j=1}^{i-1} K(x_i,x_j)*u_j]
fn volterra2_solve(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                   a: f64, b: f64, n: i32,
                   result: &!IEResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    result.n = n
    let h = (b - a) / ((n - 1) as f64)

    // Set up uniform nodes
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result.nodes[i] = a + (i as f64) * h
        result.weights[i] = h  // trapezoidal weights (uniform)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Initial value
    result.u[0] = f(a)

    // Forward march
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        let xi = result.nodes[i]

        // Sum of interior quadrature contributions
        var sum = 0.5 * K(xi, result.nodes[0]) * result.u[0]
        var j = 1
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + K(xi, result.nodes[j]) * result.u[j]
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Solve for u_i: u_i * (1 - h/2 * K(xi,xi)) = f(xi) + h * sum
        let kii = K(xi, xi)
        let denom = 1.0 - 0.5 * h * kii
        let numer = f(xi) + h * sum

        if ie_abs(denom) < 1.0e-30 {
            // Degenerate case: approximate without implicit term
            result.u[i] = numer
        } else {
            result.u[i] = numer / denom
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute residual at quadrature nodes
    var max_res = 0.0
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        let xi = result.nodes[i]
        // Compute integral_a^{x_i} K(x_i, t) u(t) dt via trapezoidal rule
        var integral = 0.5 * K(xi, result.nodes[0]) * result.u[0]
        var j = 1
        while j < i {
            integral = integral + K(xi, result.nodes[j]) * result.u[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        integral = integral + 0.5 * K(xi, result.nodes[i]) * result.u[i]
        integral = integral * h

        let res_i = ie_abs(result.u[i] - f(xi) - integral)
        if res_i > max_res { max_res = res_i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.residual = max_res
    result.converged = max_res < 1.0e-8
}

// =============================================================================
// Abel integral equation (weakly singular Volterra)
// =============================================================================

// Solve the Abel integral equation:
//   integral_a^x u(t) / (x - t)^alpha dt = f(x),  0 < alpha < 1
//
// Uses product integration to handle the weakly singular kernel (x-t)^{-alpha}.
// At uniform nodes x_i = a + i*h, the weights for the singular kernel are
// computed analytically:
//   w_{i,j} = integral_{x_j}^{x_{j+1}} (x_i - t)^{-alpha} dt
//           = [(x_i - x_j)^{1-alpha} - (x_i - x_{j+1})^{1-alpha}] / (1 - alpha)
//
// This gives the system: sum_j w_{ij} * u_j = f(x_i), solved forward.
fn volterra2_abel(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  alpha: f64, a: f64, b: f64, n: i32,
                  result: &!IEResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    result.n = n
    let h = (b - a) / ((n - 1) as f64)
    let one_m_a = 1.0 - alpha

    // Set up uniform nodes
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        result.nodes[i] = a + (i as f64) * h
        result.weights[i] = h
        i = i + 1
    }

    // First node: u(a) = f(a) / integral_a^{a+epsilon} (a+epsilon - t)^{-alpha} dt
    // For the first point, use the analytical value if available.
    // The integral from a to a is zero, so we need special treatment.
    // Use: integral_a^{x_1} (x_1 - t)^{-alpha} u(t) dt = f(x_1)
    // With piecewise constant assumption: u_0 * h^{1-alpha} / (1-alpha) = f(x_1)
    // So u_0 = f(x_1) * (1-alpha) / h^{1-alpha}

    // Forward marching with product integration
    // For each x_i, the Abel equation discretizes as:
    //   sum_{j=0}^{i-1} integral_{x_j}^{x_{j+1}} (x_i - t)^{-alpha} u(t) dt = f(x_i)
    //
    // With piecewise linear u(t) on each subinterval, approximate u(t) = u_j
    // (piecewise constant) and pull out of integral:
    //   sum_{j=0}^{i-1} u_j * mu_{i,j} = f(x_i)
    // where mu_{i,j} = integral_{x_j}^{x_{j+1}} (x_i - t)^{-alpha} dt
    //                 = [(x_i - x_j)^{1-alpha} - (x_i - x_{j+1})^{1-alpha}] / (1-alpha)

    // For i=1 (first nontrivial equation): u_0 * mu_{1,0} = f(x_1)
    let mu_10 = ie_pow(h, one_m_a) / one_m_a
    if ie_abs(mu_10) > 1.0e-30 {
        result.u[0] = f(result.nodes[1]) / mu_10
    } else {
        result.u[0] = 0.0
    }

    // Forward march for i = 2, 3, ..., n-1
    i = 2
    while i < n {
        let xi = result.nodes[i]
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < i - 1 {
            // mu_{i,j} = [(x_i - x_j)^{1-alpha} - (x_i - x_{j+1})^{1-alpha}] / (1-alpha)
            let dist_j = xi - result.nodes[j]
            let dist_jp1 = xi - result.nodes[j + 1]
            let mu_ij = (ie_pow(dist_j, one_m_a) - ie_pow(dist_jp1, one_m_a)) / one_m_a
            sum = sum + result.u[j] * mu_ij
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Last interval: j = i-1, integration from x_{i-1} to x_i
        // mu_{i,i-1} = [(x_i - x_{i-1})^{1-alpha} - 0^{1-alpha}] / (1-alpha)
        //            = h^{1-alpha} / (1-alpha)
        let mu_last = ie_pow(h, one_m_a) / one_m_a

        // sum + u_{i-1} * mu_last = f(x_i)
        // But we want u_{i-1} — however we already computed it in previous step.
        // The unknown here is u_{i-1} that was already solved.
        // Actually, we need to solve for u[i-1]:
        // sum_{j=0}^{i-2} u_j * mu_{i,j} + u_{i-1} * mu_{i,i-1} = f(x_i)
        // u_{i-1} is already known. So this determines consistency.
        // For the Abel equation, we solve a sequential system.
        // Let's use the equation for step i to determine u[i-1]:
        // Actually, the standard approach is:
        //   equation at x_i gives us u[i-1] from the last sub-interval contribution.
        // Re-derive: with n subintervals and n+1 nodes,
        // the equation at x_i uses subintervals [x_0,x_1], ..., [x_{i-1},x_i].
        // u_j is constant on [x_j, x_{j+1}], so u_j corresponds to the j-th subinterval.
        // Then: sum_{j=0}^{i-1} u_j * mu_{i,j} = f(x_i)
        // and u_{i-1} is the unknown.

        if ie_abs(mu_last) > 1.0e-30 {
            result.u[i - 1] = (f(xi) - sum) / mu_last
        } else {
            result.u[i - 1] = 0.0
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    // The last unknown u[n-2] is already set by the loop.
    // Set u[n-1] by extrapolation or by using a supplementary equation.
    // Use simple extrapolation from last two values.
    if n >= 3 {
        result.u[n - 1] = 2.0 * result.u[n - 2] - result.u[n - 3]
    } else {
        result.u[n - 1] = result.u[n - 2]
    }

    // Compute residual
    var max_res = 0.0
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        let xi = result.nodes[i]
        // Compute integral_a^{x_i} u(t) / (x_i - t)^alpha dt
        var integral_val = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < i {
            let dist_j = xi - result.nodes[j]
            let dist_jp1 = if j + 1 < i { xi - result.nodes[j + 1] } else { 0.0 }
            let mu_ij = if j + 1 < i {
                (ie_pow(dist_j, one_m_a) - ie_pow(dist_jp1, one_m_a)) / one_m_a
            } else {
                ie_pow(dist_j, one_m_a) / one_m_a
            }
            integral_val = integral_val + result.u[j] * mu_ij
            j = j + 1
        }
        let res_i = ie_abs(integral_val - f(xi))
        if res_i > max_res { max_res = res_i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.residual = max_res
    result.converged = max_res < 1.0e-4
}

// =============================================================================
// Green's function methods
// =============================================================================

// Green's function for -u'' = f on [a, b] with u(a) = u(b) = 0.
// G(x, t) = (b - t)(x - a) / (b - a)   for a <= x <= t
//          = (b - x)(t - a) / (b - a)   for t <= x <= b
fn greens_poisson_1d(x: f64, t: f64, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let l = b - a
    if x <= t {
        (b - t) * (x - a) / l
    } else {
        (b - x) * (t - a) / l
    }
}

// Solve a BVP via Green's function:
//   u(x_i) = integral_a^b G(x_i, t) f(t) dt
// where G is the Green's function and f is the source term.
// Uses Gauss-Legendre quadrature for the integral.
fn bvp_via_greens(G: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  a: f64, b: f64, n: i32,
                  result: &!IEResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute GL quadrature on [a, b]
    ie_gauss_legendre_ab(a, b, n, &!result.nodes, &!result.weights)
    result.n = n

    // Evaluate u at each quadrature node
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = result.nodes[i]
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + result.weights[j] * G(xi, result.nodes[j]) * f(result.nodes[j])
            j = j + 1
        }
        result.u[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }

    result.residual = 0.0
    result.converged = true
}

// =============================================================================
// Eigenvalue problems for integral operators
// =============================================================================

// Find eigenvalues of the integral operator T with kernel K:
//   integral_a^b K(x, t) phi(t) dt = lambda * phi(x)
//
// Discretize via Nystrom: w_j^{1/2} K(t_i, t_j) w_j^{1/2} is symmetric.
// Let B_{ij} = sqrt(w_i) * K(t_i, t_j) * sqrt(w_j).
// Then eigenvalues of B approximate eigenvalues of T.
//
// Uses power iteration with deflation to find the top n_eig eigenvalues.
fn ie_eigenvalues(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  a: f64, b: f64, n_quad: i32, n_eig: i32,
                  result: &!IEEigenResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    result.n_quad = n_quad
    result.n_found = 0

    // Compute GL quadrature on [a, b]
    var nodes: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var weights: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    ie_gauss_legendre_ab(a, b, n_quad, &!nodes, &!weights)

    // Build symmetrized kernel matrix B_{ij} = sqrt(w_i) * K(t_i, t_j) * sqrt(w_j)
    var bmat: [f64; 16384] = [0.0; 16384]
    var sqrt_w: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]

    var i = 0
    while i < n_quad {
        sqrt_w[i] = ie_sqrt(weights[i])
        i = i + 1
    }

    i = 0
    while i < n_quad {
        var j = 0
        while j < n_quad {
            bmat[i * n_quad + j] = sqrt_w[i] * K(nodes[i], nodes[j]) * sqrt_w[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Power iteration with deflation for each eigenvalue
    var eig_idx = 0
    while eig_idx < n_eig && eig_idx < n_quad {
        // Initialize random-ish vector
        var v: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
        i = 0
        while i < n_quad {
            // Deterministic pseudo-random initialization
            let seed_val = (i as f64) * 0.618033988749895 + (eig_idx as f64) * 1.324717957244746
            v[i] = ie_sin(seed_val * 17.0 + 3.7)
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Normalize
        var norm = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n_quad { norm = norm + v[i] * v[i]; i = i + 1 }
        norm = ie_sqrt(norm)
        if norm > 1.0e-30 {
            i = 0
            while i < n_quad { v[i] = v[i] / norm; i = i + 1 }
        }

        // Power iteration
        var lambda_est = 0.0
        var iter = 0
        while iter < 500 {
            // w = B * v
            var w: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
            i = 0
            while i < n_quad {
                var s = 0.0
                var j = 0
                while j < n_quad { s = s + bmat[i * n_quad + j] * v[j]; j = j + 1 }
                w[i] = s
                i = i + 1
            }

            // Deflate: remove components along previously found eigenvectors
            var d = 0
            while d < eig_idx {
                var proj = 0.0
                i = 0
                while i < n_quad {
                    proj = proj + w[i] * result.eigenvectors[d * n_quad + i]
                    i = i + 1
                }
                i = 0
                while i < n_quad {
                    w[i] = w[i] - proj * result.eigenvectors[d * n_quad + i]
                    i = i + 1
                }
                d = d + 1
            }

            // Compute eigenvalue estimate: Rayleigh quotient v^T w
            var lambda_new = 0.0
            i = 0
            while i < n_quad { lambda_new = lambda_new + v[i] * w[i]; i = i + 1 }

            // Normalize w
            norm = 0.0
            i = 0
            while i < n_quad { norm = norm + w[i] * w[i]; i = i + 1 }
            norm = ie_sqrt(norm)
            if norm < 1.0e-30 {
                // Zero vector — no more eigenvalues
                iter = 500
            } else {
                i = 0
                while i < n_quad { v[i] = w[i] / norm; i = i + 1 }
            }

            // Check convergence
            if ie_abs(lambda_new - lambda_est) < 1.0e-12 * ie_max(ie_abs(lambda_new), 1.0) {
                lambda_est = lambda_new
                iter = 500
            }
            lambda_est = lambda_new
            iter = iter + 1
        }

        // Store eigenvalue and eigenvector
        result.eigenvalues[eig_idx] = lambda_est

        // Convert back to eigenfunction: phi_i = v_i / sqrt(w_i)
        i = 0
        while i < n_quad {
            if ie_abs(sqrt_w[i]) > 1.0e-30 {
                result.eigenvectors[eig_idx * n_quad + i] = v[i] / sqrt_w[i]
            } else {
                result.eigenvectors[eig_idx * n_quad + i] = 0.0
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // For deflation: store the normalized eigenvector v (in B-space)
        // We already have v normalized from the iteration.
        // Overwrite eigenvectors with the B-space vector for deflation.
        // Actually, keep the eigenfunction but re-use v for deflation.
        // Store v in eigenvectors for deflation purposes.
        i = 0
        while i < n_quad {
            result.eigenvectors[eig_idx * n_quad + i] = v[i]
            i = i + 1
        }

        result.n_found = eig_idx + 1
        eig_idx = eig_idx + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Iterative solvers — Neumann series
// =============================================================================

// Solve Fredholm 2nd kind by Neumann series:
//   u = f + lambda K f + lambda^2 K^2 f + ...
// Converges when |lambda| * ||K|| < 1 (spectral radius condition).
//
// Each iterate: u_{k+1} = f + lambda K u_k
// The integral K u is evaluated via GL quadrature at the quadrature nodes.
fn fredholm2_neumann(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                     f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                     a: f64, b: f64, lambda: f64, n: i32,
                     max_iter: i32, tol: f64,
                     result: &!IEResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute GL quadrature on [a, b]
    ie_gauss_legendre_ab(a, b, n, &!result.nodes, &!result.weights)
    result.n = n

    // Initialize: u_0 = f
    var i = 0
    while i < n { result.u[i] = f(result.nodes[i]); i = i + 1 }

    var prev: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    i = 0
    while i < n { prev[i] = result.u[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Iterate: u_{k+1}(t_i) = f(t_i) + lambda * sum_j w_j K(t_i, t_j) u_k(t_j)
    var iter = 0
    result.converged = false
    while iter < max_iter {
        // Compute new iterate
        var max_diff = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var j = 0
            while j < n {
                sum = sum + result.weights[j] * K(result.nodes[i], result.nodes[j]) * prev[j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            result.u[i] = f(result.nodes[i]) + lambda * sum

            let diff = ie_abs(result.u[i] - prev[i])
            if diff > max_diff { max_diff = diff }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Copy current to prev
        i = 0
        while i < n { prev[i] = result.u[i]; i = i + 1 }

        if max_diff < tol {
            result.converged = true
            result.residual = max_diff
            return
        }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Did not converge — compute residual
    result.residual = ie_residual_fredholm2_internal(K, f, lambda, result)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/interpolation.sio ===
// stdlib/math/interpolation.sio — Interpolation methods
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Barycentric Lagrange interpolation (O(n) evaluation after O(n) setup)
//   Newton divided differences
//   Hermite interpolation (values + derivatives)
//   PCHIP (Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial) — shape preserving
//   Rational interpolation (Stoer-Bulirsch)
//   Linear interpolation (1D)
//
// References:
//   Berrut & Trefethen (2004): "Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation" SIAM Review
//   Fritsch & Carlson (1980): "Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolation"
//   Stoer & Bulirsch (2002): "Introduction to Numerical Analysis"
//   de Boor (2001): "A Practical Guide to Splines"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn ip_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn ip_sign(x: f64) -> f64 { if x > 0.0 { 1.0 } else if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 0.0 } }
fn ip_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn ip_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// =============================================================================
// Linear interpolation
// =============================================================================

// 1D linear interpolation: given sorted x[0..n-1] and y[0..n-1], evaluate at t.
// Uses binary search to find the enclosing interval.
fn interp_linear(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Clamp to domain
    if t <= x[0] { return y[0] }
    if t >= x[n - 1] { return y[n - 1] }

    // Binary search
    var lo = 0
    var hi = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if x[mid] > t { hi = mid } else { lo = mid }
    }

    let h = x[hi] - x[lo]
    if ip_abs(h) < 1.0e-30 { return y[lo] }
    let alpha = (t - x[lo]) / h
    y[lo] + alpha * (y[hi] - y[lo])
}

// =============================================================================
// Barycentric Lagrange interpolation
// =============================================================================

// Compute barycentric weights for nodes x[0..n-1].
// w[i] = 1 / prod_{j != i} (x[i] - x[j])
fn bary_weights(x: &[f64; 256], n: i32, w: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        w[i] = 1.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            if j != i {
                w[i] = w[i] / (x[i] - x[j])
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Evaluate barycentric interpolant at t.
// x, y: data points; w: barycentric weights; n: count.
// Uses the second (stable) form of the barycentric formula:
//   p(t) = (sum w[i]*y[i]/(t-x[i])) / (sum w[i]/(t-x[i]))
fn bary_eval(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], w: &[f64; 256],
             n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Check if t coincides with a node
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if ip_abs(t - x[i]) < 1.0e-15 { return y[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var numer = 0.0
    var denom = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let term = w[i] / (t - x[i])
        numer = numer + term * y[i]
        denom = denom + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    numer / denom
}

// =============================================================================
// Newton divided differences
// =============================================================================

// Compute Newton divided difference coefficients c[0..n-1].
// After this, p(t) = c[0] + c[1]*(t-x[0]) + c[2]*(t-x[0])*(t-x[1]) + ...
fn newton_coeffs(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], n: i32,
                 c: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize c = y
    var i = 0
    while i < n { c[i] = y[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Build divided difference table in-place
    var j = 1
    while j < n {
        i = n - 1
        while i >= j {
            c[i] = (c[i] - c[i - 1]) / (x[i] - x[i - j])
            i = i - 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
}

// Evaluate Newton interpolant via Horner-like nesting.
fn newton_eval(x: &[f64; 256], c: &[f64; 256], n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = c[n - 1]
    var i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        result = result * (t - x[i]) + c[i]
        i = i - 1
    }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Hermite interpolation
// =============================================================================

// Hermite interpolation using values y[i] and derivatives dy[i] at nodes x[i].
// Returns the value of the 2n-1 degree polynomial at t.
fn hermite_interp(x: &[f64; 128], y: &[f64; 128], dy: &[f64; 128],
                  n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Build divided difference table for doubled nodes
    var z: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var q: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        z[2 * i] = x[i]
        z[2 * i + 1] = x[i]
        q[2 * i] = y[i]
        q[2 * i + 1] = y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // First divided differences
    let nn = 2 * n
    // For coincident nodes, use derivative
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        q[2 * i + 1] = dy[i]  // f[x_i, x_i] = f'(x_i)
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Non-coincident first divided differences
    i = nn - 1
    while i >= 2 {
        if ip_abs(z[i] - z[i - 1]) > 1.0e-30 {
            // Already have q[i] = f[x_i], now compute f[x_{i-1}, x_i]
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Actually, let's use the standard Hermite approach via
    // Newton's form on doubled nodes.
    // Re-initialize properly
    var dd: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    i = 0
    while i < nn { dd[i] = q[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // First divided differences
    i = 1
    while i < nn {
        if ip_abs(z[i] - z[i - 1]) < 1.0e-30 {
            // Coincident: use derivative
            dd[i] = dy[i / 2]
        } else {
            dd[i] = (dd[i] - dd[i - 1]) / (z[i] - z[i - 1])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Higher order divided differences
    var j = 2
    while j < nn {
        i = nn - 1
        while i >= j {
            dd[i] = (dd[i] - dd[i - 1]) / (z[i] - z[i - j])
            i = i - 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Evaluate via nested form
    var result = dd[nn - 1]
    i = nn - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        result = result * (t - z[i]) + dd[i]
        i = i - 1
    }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// PCHIP — Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial
// =============================================================================

// Compute PCHIP slopes d[0..n-1] from data (x, y).
// Ensures monotonicity preservation: if data is locally monotone, so is the interpolant.
// Uses Fritsch-Carlson (1980) algorithm.
fn pchip_slopes(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], n: i32,
                d: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 2 { d[0] = 0.0; return }
    if n == 2 {
        let s = (y[1] - y[0]) / (x[1] - x[0])
        d[0] = s
        d[1] = s
        return
    }

    // Compute secant slopes
    var delta: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        delta[i] = (y[i + 1] - y[i]) / (x[i + 1] - x[i])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Interior slopes via Fritsch-Carlson
    i = 1
    while i < n - 1 {
        if delta[i - 1] * delta[i] <= 0.0 {
            // Local extremum: zero slope
            d[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            // Weighted harmonic mean
            let h1 = x[i] - x[i - 1]
            let h2 = x[i + 1] - x[i]
            let w1 = 2.0 * h2 + h1
            let w2 = h2 + 2.0 * h1
            d[i] = (w1 + w2) / (w1 / delta[i - 1] + w2 / delta[i])
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Endpoint slopes: one-sided shape-preserving
    // Left endpoint
    d[0] = ((2.0 * (x[1] - x[0]) + (x[2] - x[1])) * delta[0] - (x[1] - x[0]) * delta[1]) / (x[2] - x[0])
    if ip_sign(d[0]) != ip_sign(delta[0]) {
        d[0] = 0.0
    } else if ip_sign(delta[0]) != ip_sign(delta[1]) && ip_abs(d[0]) > ip_abs(3.0 * delta[0]) {
        d[0] = 3.0 * delta[0]
    }

    // Right endpoint
    let nm1 = n - 1
    let nm2 = n - 2
    let nm3 = n - 3
    d[nm1] = ((2.0 * (x[nm1] - x[nm2]) + (x[nm2] - x[nm3])) * delta[nm2] - (x[nm1] - x[nm2]) * delta[nm3]) / (x[nm1] - x[nm3])
    if ip_sign(d[nm1]) != ip_sign(delta[nm2]) {
        d[nm1] = 0.0
    } else if ip_sign(delta[nm2]) != ip_sign(delta[nm3]) && ip_abs(d[nm1]) > ip_abs(3.0 * delta[nm2]) {
        d[nm1] = 3.0 * delta[nm2]
    }
}

// Evaluate PCHIP interpolant at t.
fn pchip_eval(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], d: &[f64; 256],
              n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Clamp
    if t <= x[0] { return y[0] }
    if t >= x[n - 1] { return y[n - 1] }

    // Binary search
    var lo = 0
    var hi = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if x[mid] > t { hi = mid } else { lo = mid }
    }

    let h = x[hi] - x[lo]
    let s = (t - x[lo]) / h
    let s2 = s * s
    let s3 = s2 * s

    // Hermite basis functions
    let h00 = 2.0 * s3 - 3.0 * s2 + 1.0
    let h10 = s3 - 2.0 * s2 + s
    let h01 = 0.0 - 2.0 * s3 + 3.0 * s2
    let h11 = s3 - s2

    h00 * y[lo] + h10 * h * d[lo] + h01 * y[hi] + h11 * h * d[hi]
}

// =============================================================================
// Rational interpolation (Stoer-Bulirsch)
// =============================================================================

// Rational interpolation through (x[i], y[i]) evaluated at t.
// Returns value in out[0], error estimate in out[1].
// Based on the diagonal rational interpolation algorithm of
// Stoer & Bulirsch via the Neville-like scheme.
fn rational_interp(x: &[f64; 64], y: &[f64; 64], n: i32, t: f64,
                   out: &![f64; 2]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let tiny = 1.0e-25

    var c: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var d: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Find closest point to t
    var ns = 0
    var min_dist = ip_abs(t - x[0])
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let dist = ip_abs(t - x[i])
        if dist == 0.0 {
            out[0] = y[i]
            out[1] = 0.0
            return
        }
        if dist < min_dist { min_dist = dist; ns = i }
        c[i] = y[i]
        d[i] = y[i] + tiny  // small perturbation to avoid 0/0
        i = i + 1
    }

    out[0] = y[ns]
    ns = ns - 1

    var m = 1
    while m < n {
        i = 0
        while i < n - m {
            let w = c[i + 1] - d[i]
            let h_val = t - x[i + m]
            let t_val = (t - x[i]) * d[i] / h_val
            let dd = t_val - c[i + 1]
            if ip_abs(dd) < 1.0e-30 {
                // Pole: return current estimate
                out[1] = 1.0e30
                return
            }
            let dd2 = w / dd
            d[i] = c[i + 1] * dd2
            c[i] = t_val * dd2
            i = i + 1
        }

        if 2 * (ns + 1) < n - m {
            out[1] = c[ns + 1]
        } else {
            out[1] = d[ns]
            ns = ns - 1
        }
        out[0] = out[0] + out[1]
        m = m + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Cubic spline interpolation (natural boundary conditions)
// =============================================================================

// Compute natural cubic spline second derivatives s[0..n-1].
// Natural BC: s[0] = s[n-1] = 0.
fn spline_natural(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], n: i32,
                  s: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 3 { s[0] = 0.0; if n > 1 { s[1] = 0.0 } return }

    // Tridiagonal system
    var a: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]  // sub-diagonal
    var b: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]  // diagonal
    var c: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]  // super-diagonal
    var r: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]  // RHS

    s[0] = 0.0
    s[n - 1] = 0.0

    var i = 1
    while i < n - 1 {
        let h0 = x[i] - x[i - 1]
        let h1 = x[i + 1] - x[i]
        a[i] = h0
        b[i] = 2.0 * (h0 + h1)
        c[i] = h1
        r[i] = 6.0 * ((y[i + 1] - y[i]) / h1 - (y[i] - y[i - 1]) / h0)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Thomas algorithm (tridiagonal solver)
    i = 2
    while i < n - 1 {
        let m = a[i] / b[i - 1]
        b[i] = b[i] - m * c[i - 1]
        r[i] = r[i] - m * r[i - 1]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    s[n - 2] = r[n - 2] / b[n - 2]
    i = n - 3
    while i >= 1 {
        s[i] = (r[i] - c[i] * s[i + 1]) / b[i]
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// Evaluate cubic spline at t.
fn spline_eval(x: &[f64; 256], y: &[f64; 256], s: &[f64; 256],
               n: i32, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if t <= x[0] { return y[0] }
    if t >= x[n - 1] { return y[n - 1] }

    // Binary search
    var lo = 0
    var hi = n - 1
    while hi - lo > 1 {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if x[mid] > t { hi = mid } else { lo = mid }
    }

    let h = x[hi] - x[lo]
    let a_val = (x[hi] - t) / h
    let b_val = (t - x[lo]) / h

    a_val * y[lo] + b_val * y[hi]
    + ((a_val * a_val * a_val - a_val) * s[lo] + (b_val * b_val * b_val - b_val) * s[hi]) * h * h / 6.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/math/lib.sio - Mathematical operations
//!
//! This module is the entry point for math functionality.
//! Import submodules directly: use math::core, use math::sedenion, etc.

// Note: pub use not supported - import submodules directly


// === FILE: stdlib/math/lie.sio ===
// stdlib/math/lie.sio — Lie algebras and Lie groups
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Classical Lie algebras (su(2), su(3), so(3))
//   Structure constants, Lie bracket, adjoint representation
//   Killing form, Cartan subalgebra
//   Exponential and logarithm maps
//   SO(3) Rodrigues formula
//   Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula (truncated)
//   Wigner D-matrices for SU(2)
//   Lie group integrators (Crouch-Grossman)
//
// References:
//   Hall (2015): "Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations"
//   Iserles et al. (2000): "Lie-group methods" Acta Numerica
//   Hairer, Lubich & Wanner (2006): "Geometric Numerical Integration"

// =============================================================================
// Scalar helpers
// =============================================================================

fn lie_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn lie_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

fn lie_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 24 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn lie_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 20 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn lie_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    lie_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn lie_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    var kf = x / 0.6931471805599453
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 { var i = 0; while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    else { var i = 0; while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    result
}

fn lie_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64); k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

// Arctangent for non-negative argument via Taylor + range reduction
fn lie_atan_core(z: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let pi2 = 1.57079632679489661923
    if z > 1.0 { return pi2 - lie_atan_core(1.0 / z) }
    let z2 = z * z
    var sum = z
    var term = z
    var k = 1
    while k < 40 { term = 0.0 - term * z2; sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64); k = k + 1 }
    sum
}

fn lie_atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let pi = 3.14159265358979323846
    let pi2 = 1.57079632679489661923
    if lie_abs(x) < 1.0e-30 {
        if y > 0.0 { return pi2 }
        if y < 0.0 { return 0.0 - pi2 }
        return 0.0
    }
    var at = lie_atan_core(lie_abs(y / x))
    if x < 0.0 { at = pi - at }
    if y < 0.0 { at = 0.0 - at }
    at
}

fn lie_acos(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let pi2 = 1.57079632679489661923
    var cx = x
    if cx > 1.0 { cx = 1.0 }
    if cx < -1.0 { cx = -1.0 }
    if lie_abs(cx) < 1.0e-15 { return pi2 }
    let s = lie_sqrt(1.0 - cx * cx)
    pi2 - lie_atan2(cx, s)
}

fn lie_factorial(n: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var result = 1.0
    var i = 2
    while i <= n { result = result * (i as f64); i = i + 1 }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Matrix helpers (flat row-major, max 8x8 = 64 elements)
// =============================================================================

fn lie_mat_zero(m: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { m[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
}

fn lie_mat_eye(m: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { m[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < dim { m[i * dim + i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
}

fn lie_mat_copy(dst: &![f64; 64], src: &[f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { dst[i] = src[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

fn lie_mat_add(a: &[f64; 64], b: &[f64; 64], c: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { c[i] = a[i] + b[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

fn lie_mat_sub(a: &[f64; 64], b: &[f64; 64], c: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { c[i] = a[i] - b[i]; i = i + 1 }
}

fn lie_mat_mul(a: &[f64; 64], b: &[f64; 64], c: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { c[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < dim {
        var j = 0
        while j < dim {
            var s = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < dim { s = s + a[i * dim + k] * b[k * dim + j]; k = k + 1 }
            c[i * dim + j] = s
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn lie_mat_scale(m: &![f64; 64], s: f64, dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { m[i] = m[i] * s; i = i + 1 }
}

fn lie_mat_trace(m: &[f64; 64], dim: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < dim { s = s + m[i * dim + i]; i = i + 1 }
    s
}

fn lie_mat_transpose(src: &[f64; 64], dst: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < dim {
        var j = 0
        while j < dim { dst[j * dim + i] = src[i * dim + j]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn lie_mat_norm(m: &[f64; 64], dim: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var s = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { s = s + m[i] * m[i]; i = i + 1 }
    lie_sqrt(s)
}

fn lie_mat_norm_inf(m: &[f64; 64], dim: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var mx = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < dim {
        var rs = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < dim { rs = rs + lie_abs(m[i * dim + j]); j = j + 1 }
        if rs > mx { mx = rs }
        i = i + 1
    }
    mx
}

// Gauss-Jordan inversion: solve D * X = N via D^{-1} * N
fn lie_mat_solve(D: [f64; 64], N: [f64; 64], X: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var A: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var inv: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { A[i] = D[i]; i = i + 1 }
    lie_mat_eye(&!inv, dim)

    var col = 0
    while col < dim {
        // Partial pivoting
        var max_val = lie_abs(A[col * dim + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < dim {
            let v = lie_abs(A[row * dim + col])
            if v > max_val { max_val = v; max_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < dim {
                let tmp = A[col * dim + j]
                A[col * dim + j] = A[max_row * dim + j]
                A[max_row * dim + j] = tmp
                let tmp2 = inv[col * dim + j]
                inv[col * dim + j] = inv[max_row * dim + j]
                inv[max_row * dim + j] = tmp2
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        let pivot = A[col * dim + col]
        if lie_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-30 { lie_mat_eye(X, dim); return }
        let inv_pivot = 1.0 / pivot
        var j = 0
        while j < dim {
            A[col * dim + j] = A[col * dim + j] * inv_pivot
            inv[col * dim + j] = inv[col * dim + j] * inv_pivot
            j = j + 1
        }
        row = 0
        while row < dim {
            if row != col {
                let factor = A[row * dim + col]
                j = 0
                while j < dim {
                    A[row * dim + j] = A[row * dim + j] - factor * A[col * dim + j]
                    inv[row * dim + j] = inv[row * dim + j] - factor * inv[col * dim + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
            }
            row = row + 1
        }
        col = col + 1
    }
    lie_mat_mul(&inv, &N, X, dim)
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs
// =============================================================================

struct LieElement {
    coeffs: [f64; 16],
    dim: i32
}

struct LieAlgebra {
    structure_constants: [f64; 4096],
    dim: i32,
    matrix_dim: i32
}

struct LieGroupElement {
    matrix: [f64; 64],
    dim: i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Element initialization
// =============================================================================

fn lie_elem_zero(e: &!LieElement, dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { e.coeffs[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    e.dim = dim
}

fn lie_elem_basis(e: &!LieElement, dim: i32, idx: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { e.coeffs[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    e.coeffs[idx] = 1.0
    e.dim = dim
}

fn lie_elem_copy(dst: &!LieElement, src: &LieElement) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 16 { dst.coeffs[i] = src.coeffs[i]; i = i + 1 }
    dst.dim = src.dim
}

fn lie_group_eye(g: &!LieGroupElement, dim: i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < 64 { g.matrix[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    i = 0
    while i < dim { g.matrix[i * dim + i] = 1.0; i = i + 1 }
    g.dim = dim
}

// =============================================================================
// Predefined algebras: su(2)
// =============================================================================

// su(2): dim=3, matrix_dim=2. Structure constants = Levi-Civita epsilon_{ijk}.
fn lie_su2(alg: &!LieAlgebra) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    alg.dim = 3
    alg.matrix_dim = 2
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 { alg.structure_constants[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    // c^k_{ij} at index i*9 + j*3 + k
    alg.structure_constants[0 * 9 + 1 * 3 + 2] = 1.0
    alg.structure_constants[1 * 9 + 0 * 3 + 2] = -1.0
    alg.structure_constants[1 * 9 + 2 * 3 + 0] = 1.0
    alg.structure_constants[2 * 9 + 1 * 3 + 0] = -1.0
    alg.structure_constants[2 * 9 + 0 * 3 + 1] = 1.0
    alg.structure_constants[0 * 9 + 2 * 3 + 1] = -1.0
}

// =============================================================================
// Predefined algebras: so(3)
// =============================================================================

// so(3): dim=3, matrix_dim=3. Isomorphic to su(2), same structure constants.
fn lie_so3(alg: &!LieAlgebra) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    alg.dim = 3
    alg.matrix_dim = 3
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 { alg.structure_constants[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    alg.structure_constants[0 * 9 + 1 * 3 + 2] = 1.0
    alg.structure_constants[1 * 9 + 0 * 3 + 2] = -1.0
    alg.structure_constants[1 * 9 + 2 * 3 + 0] = 1.0
    alg.structure_constants[2 * 9 + 1 * 3 + 0] = -1.0
    alg.structure_constants[2 * 9 + 0 * 3 + 1] = 1.0
    alg.structure_constants[0 * 9 + 2 * 3 + 1] = -1.0
}

// =============================================================================
// Predefined algebras: su(3)
// =============================================================================

// Set totally antisymmetric structure constant f_{abc} = val into c^k_{ij}.
fn lie_su3_set_f(alg: &!LieAlgebra, a: i32, b: i32, c: i32, val: f64) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let d = alg.dim
    alg.structure_constants[a * d * d + b * d + c] = val
    alg.structure_constants[b * d * d + a * d + c] = 0.0 - val
    alg.structure_constants[b * d * d + c * d + a] = val
    alg.structure_constants[c * d * d + b * d + a] = 0.0 - val
    alg.structure_constants[c * d * d + a * d + b] = val
    alg.structure_constants[a * d * d + c * d + b] = 0.0 - val
}

// su(3): dim=8, matrix_dim=3. Gell-Mann matrices / 2i.
// Nonzero f_{ijk} (0-based): f_012=1, f_036=1/2, f_045=-1/2,
//   f_135=1/2, f_146=1/2, f_234=1/2, f_256=-1/2,
//   f_347=sqrt(3)/2, f_567=sqrt(3)/2
fn lie_su3(alg: &!LieAlgebra) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    alg.dim = 8
    alg.matrix_dim = 3
    var i = 0
    while i < 4096 { alg.structure_constants[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    let s32 = lie_sqrt(3.0) / 2.0
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 0, 1, 2, 1.0)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 0, 3, 6, 0.5)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 0, 4, 5, -0.5)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 1, 3, 5, 0.5)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 1, 4, 6, 0.5)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 2, 3, 4, 0.5)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 2, 5, 6, -0.5)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 3, 4, 7, s32)
    lie_su3_set_f(alg, 5, 6, 7, s32)
}

// =============================================================================
// Lie bracket
// =============================================================================

// [X, Y]_k = sum_{i,j} c^k_{ij} * X_i * Y_j
fn lie_bracket(alg: &LieAlgebra, X: &LieElement, Y: &LieElement, result: &!LieElement) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = alg.dim
    result.dim = d
    var k = 0
    while k < d {
        var s = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < d {
            var j = 0
            while j < d {
                s = s + alg.structure_constants[i * d * d + j * d + k] * X.coeffs[i] * Y.coeffs[j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        result.coeffs[k] = s
        k = k + 1
    }
    while k < 16 { result.coeffs[k] = 0.0; k = k + 1 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Adjoint representation
// =============================================================================

// (ad_X)_{ki} = sum_j c^k_{ji} * X_j. Result: dim x dim matrix (row-major).
fn lie_adjoint(alg: &LieAlgebra, X: &LieElement, ad_X: &![f64; 256]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = alg.dim
    var k = 0
    while k < d {
        var i = 0
        while i < d {
            var s = 0.0
            var j = 0
            while j < d {
                s = s + alg.structure_constants[j * d * d + i * d + k] * X.coeffs[j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            ad_X[k * d + i] = s
            i = i + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Killing form
// =============================================================================

// B(X,Y) = tr(ad_X * ad_Y)
fn lie_killing(alg: &LieAlgebra, X: &LieElement, Y: &LieElement) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = alg.dim
    var adx: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var ady: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    lie_adjoint(alg, X, &!adx)
    lie_adjoint(alg, Y, &!ady)
    var trace = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < d {
        var j = 0
        while j < d { trace = trace + adx[i * d + j] * ady[j * d + i]; j = j + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    trace
}

// Full Killing form matrix K_{ij} = B(e_i, e_j)
fn lie_killing_matrix(alg: &LieAlgebra, K: &![f64; 256]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = alg.dim
    var ei: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: d }
    var ej: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: d }
    var i = 0
    while i < d {
        var ii = 0
        while ii < 16 { ei.coeffs[ii] = 0.0; ii = ii + 1 }
        ei.coeffs[i] = 1.0
        var j = 0
        while j < d {
            ii = 0
            while ii < 16 { ej.coeffs[ii] = 0.0; ii = ii + 1 }
            ej.coeffs[j] = 1.0
            K[i * d + j] = lie_killing(alg, &ei, &ej)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Matrix representation
// =============================================================================

// Gell-Mann matrices lambda_k / 2, stored as real 3x3
fn lie_su3_basis_matrix(idx: i32, mat: &![f64; 64]) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if idx == 0 { mat[0 * 3 + 1] = 0.5; mat[1 * 3 + 0] = 0.5 }
    if idx == 1 { mat[0 * 3 + 1] = -0.5; mat[1 * 3 + 0] = 0.5 }
    if idx == 2 { mat[0 * 3 + 0] = 0.5; mat[1 * 3 + 1] = -0.5 }
    if idx == 3 { mat[0 * 3 + 2] = 0.5; mat[2 * 3 + 0] = 0.5 }
    if idx == 4 { mat[0 * 3 + 2] = -0.5; mat[2 * 3 + 0] = 0.5 }
    if idx == 5 { mat[1 * 3 + 2] = 0.5; mat[2 * 3 + 1] = 0.5 }
    if idx == 6 { mat[1 * 3 + 2] = -0.5; mat[2 * 3 + 1] = 0.5 }
    if idx == 7 {
        let s = 1.0 / (2.0 * 1.7320508075688772)
        mat[0 * 3 + 0] = s
        mat[1 * 3 + 1] = s
        mat[2 * 3 + 2] = -2.0 * s
    }
}

// Return the idx-th basis matrix of the algebra representation.
fn lie_basis_matrix(alg: &LieAlgebra, idx: i32, mat: &![f64; 64]) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let md = alg.matrix_dim
    lie_mat_zero(mat, md)
    if alg.dim == 3 && md == 3 {
        // so(3): L_x, L_y, L_z
        if idx == 0 { mat[1 * 3 + 2] = -1.0; mat[2 * 3 + 1] = 1.0 }
        if idx == 1 { mat[0 * 3 + 2] = 1.0; mat[2 * 3 + 0] = -1.0 }
        if idx == 2 { mat[0 * 3 + 1] = -1.0; mat[1 * 3 + 0] = 1.0 }
    }
    if alg.dim == 3 && md == 2 {
        // su(2): sigma_k / 2
        if idx == 0 { mat[0 * 2 + 1] = 0.5; mat[1 * 2 + 0] = 0.5 }
        if idx == 1 { mat[0 * 2 + 1] = -0.5; mat[1 * 2 + 0] = 0.5 }
        if idx == 2 { mat[0 * 2 + 0] = 0.5; mat[1 * 2 + 1] = -0.5 }
    }
    if alg.dim == 8 && md == 3 {
        lie_su3_basis_matrix(idx, mat)
    }
}

// mat = sum_i X.coeffs[i] * basis_matrix(i)
fn lie_to_matrix(alg: &LieAlgebra, X: &LieElement, mat: &![f64; 64]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let md = alg.matrix_dim
    lie_mat_zero(mat, md)
    var basis: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < alg.dim {
        lie_mat_zero(&!basis, md)
        lie_basis_matrix(alg, i, &!basis)
        var r = 0
        while r < md {
            var c = 0
            while c < md {
                mat[r * md + c] = mat[r * md + c] + X.coeffs[i] * basis[r * md + c]
                c = c + 1
            }
            r = r + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Matrix exponential: Pade [6/6] with Div, Mut, Panic, scaling and squaring
// =============================================================================

// exp(A) via [6/6] Pade approximation with Div, Mut, Panic, scaling and squaring.
// Pade coefficients b_k = (12-k)! 6! / (12! k! (6-k)!)
fn lie_exp_pade(mat: &[f64; 64], dim: i32, result: &![f64; 64]) with Panic, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var b: [f64; 7] = [0.0; 7]
    b[0] = 1.0
    b[1] = 0.5
    b[2] = 0.11363636363636363636
    b[3] = 0.01515151515151515152
    b[4] = 0.00126262626262626263
    b[5] = 0.00006313131313131313
    b[6] = 0.00000150300150300150

    // Scaling: find s such that ||A||_inf / 2^s < 0.5
    let norm_a = lie_mat_norm_inf(mat, dim)
    var s = 0
    var scale = norm_a
    while scale > 0.5 { scale = scale / 2.0; s = s + 1 }

    var As: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { As[i] = mat[i]; i = i + 1 }
    var si = 0
    while si < s { i = 0; while i < dim * dim { As[i] = As[i] / 2.0; i = i + 1 }; si = si + 1 }

    var A2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var A4: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var A6: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_mul(&As, &As, &!A2, dim)
    lie_mat_mul(&A2, &A2, &!A4, dim)
    lie_mat_mul(&A4, &A2, &!A6, dim)

    // Even part: U = b_0*I + b_2*A^2 + b_4*A^4 + b_6*A^6
    var U: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_eye(&!U, dim)
    i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { U[i] = b[0] * U[i] + b[2] * A2[i] + b[4] * A4[i] + b[6] * A6[i]; i = i + 1 }

    // Odd part inner: Vi = b_1*I + b_3*A^2 + b_5*A^4
    var Vi: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_eye(&!Vi, dim)
    i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { Vi[i] = b[1] * Vi[i] + b[3] * A2[i] + b[5] * A4[i]; i = i + 1 }
    var V: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_mul(&As, &Vi, &!V, dim)

    // N = U + V, D = U - V
    var N: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var D: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_add(&U, &V, &!N, dim)
    lie_mat_sub(&U, &V, &!D, dim)

    // result = D^{-1} * N
    lie_mat_solve(D, N, result, dim)

    // Squaring s times
    var temp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    si = 0
    while si < s {
        lie_mat_mul(result, result, &!temp, dim)
        lie_mat_copy(result, &temp, dim)
        si = si + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Matrix logarithm
// =============================================================================

// Matrix square root via Denman-Beavers iteration (in-place).
// Y_{k+1} = (Y_k + Z_k^{-1})/2, Z_{k+1} = (Z_k + Y_k^{-1})/2
fn lie_mat_sqrt_db(A: &![f64; 64], dim: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var Y: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var Z: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var Yinv: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var Zinv: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var t1: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var t2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var eye: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_copy(&!Y, A, dim)
    lie_mat_eye(&!Z, dim)
    lie_mat_eye(&!eye, dim)
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 30 {
        lie_mat_solve(Y, eye, &!Yinv, dim)
        lie_mat_solve(Z, eye, &!Zinv, dim)
        lie_mat_add(&Y, &Zinv, &!t1, dim)
        lie_mat_scale(&!t1, 0.5, dim)
        lie_mat_add(&Z, &Yinv, &!t2, dim)
        lie_mat_scale(&!t2, 0.5, dim)
        lie_mat_copy(&!Y, &t1, dim)
        lie_mat_copy(&!Z, &t2, dim)
        var diff: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        lie_mat_sub(&Z, &eye, &!diff, dim)
        if lie_mat_norm(&diff, dim) < 1.0e-14 { iter = 30 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    lie_mat_copy(A, &Y, dim)
}

// log(A) via inverse scaling/squaring + Taylor series.
// Repeatedly square-roots until ||A - I|| < 0.4, then uses
// log(I+X) = X - X^2/2 + X^3/3 - ..., then scales back by 2^s.
fn lie_log_series(mat: &[f64; 64], dim: i32, result: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var A: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < dim * dim { A[i] = mat[i]; i = i + 1 }
    var eye: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_eye(&!eye, dim)

    var s = 0
    var diff: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var diff_copy: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_sub(&A, &eye, &!diff, dim)
    // Copy diff for shared borrow in norm check (avoids shared+mutable conflict)
    var di = 0
    while di < dim * dim { diff_copy[di] = diff[di]; di = di + 1 }
    while lie_mat_norm(&diff_copy, dim) > 0.4 && s < 20 {
        lie_mat_sqrt_db(&!A, dim)
        lie_mat_sub(&A, &eye, &!diff, dim)
        di = 0
        while di < dim * dim { diff_copy[di] = diff[di]; di = di + 1 }
        s = s + 1
    }

    var X: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_sub(&A, &eye, &!X, dim)
    lie_mat_zero(result, dim)
    var Xk: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_copy(&!Xk, &X, dim)
    var temp: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var k = 1
    while k <= 20 {
        let sign = if k - 2 * (k / 2) == 1 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 }
        let coeff = sign / (k as f64)
        i = 0
        while i < dim * dim { result[i] = result[i] + coeff * Xk[i]; i = i + 1 }
        lie_mat_mul(&Xk, &X, &!temp, dim)
        lie_mat_copy(&!Xk, &temp, dim)
        k = k + 1
    }
    var sf = 1.0
    i = 0
    while i < s { sf = sf * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    lie_mat_scale(result, sf, dim)
}

// =============================================================================
// SO(3) specific: hat, vee, exponential, logarithm
// =============================================================================

// Hat: vector -> skew-symmetric 3x3
fn so3_hat(omega: &[f64; 3], mat: &![f64; 9]) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    mat[0] = 0.0;              mat[1] = 0.0 - omega[2]; mat[2] = omega[1]
    mat[3] = omega[2];         mat[4] = 0.0;             mat[5] = 0.0 - omega[0]
    mat[6] = 0.0 - omega[1];  mat[7] = omega[0];        mat[8] = 0.0
}

// Vee: skew-symmetric 3x3 -> vector
fn so3_vee(mat: &[f64; 9], omega: &![f64; 3]) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    omega[0] = mat[7]
    omega[1] = mat[2]
    omega[2] = mat[3]
}

// Rodrigues: R = I + sin(t)/t * [w]_x + (1-cos(t))/t^2 * [w]_x^2, t = ||w||
fn so3_exp(omega: &[f64; 3], R: &![f64; 9]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let wx = omega[0]
    let wy = omega[1]
    let wz = omega[2]
    let t2 = wx * wx + wy * wy + wz * wz
    let t = lie_sqrt(t2)
    if t < 1.0e-10 {
        R[0] = 1.0;  R[1] = 0.0 - wz; R[2] = wy
        R[3] = wz;   R[4] = 1.0;       R[5] = 0.0 - wx
        R[6] = 0.0 - wy; R[7] = wx;    R[8] = 1.0
        return
    }
    let sc = lie_sin(t) / t
    let cc = (1.0 - lie_cos(t)) / t2
    var K: [f64; 9] = [0.0; 9]
    so3_hat(omega, &!K)
    // K^2 via direct 3x3 multiply
    var K2: [f64; 9] = [0.0; 9]
    var ri = 0
    while ri < 3 {
        var ci = 0
        while ci < 3 {
            var s = 0.0
            var p = 0
            while p < 3 { s = s + K[ri * 3 + p] * K[p * 3 + ci]; p = p + 1 }
            K2[ri * 3 + ci] = s
            ci = ci + 1
        }
        ri = ri + 1
    }
    // R = I + sc*K + cc*K^2
    R[0] = 1.0 + sc * K[0] + cc * K2[0]
    R[1] = sc * K[1] + cc * K2[1]
    R[2] = sc * K[2] + cc * K2[2]
    R[3] = sc * K[3] + cc * K2[3]
    R[4] = 1.0 + sc * K[4] + cc * K2[4]
    R[5] = sc * K[5] + cc * K2[5]
    R[6] = sc * K[6] + cc * K2[6]
    R[7] = sc * K[7] + cc * K2[7]
    R[8] = 1.0 + sc * K[8] + cc * K2[8]
}

// Inverse Rodrigues: omega = theta/(2*sin(theta)) * vee(R - R^T)
fn so3_log(R: &[f64; 9], omega: &![f64; 3]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let tr = R[0] + R[4] + R[8]
    var ct = (tr - 1.0) / 2.0
    if ct > 1.0 { ct = 1.0 }
    if ct < -1.0 { ct = -1.0 }
    let theta = lie_acos(ct)
    if theta < 1.0e-10 {
        omega[0] = (R[7] - R[5]) / 2.0
        omega[1] = (R[2] - R[6]) / 2.0
        omega[2] = (R[3] - R[1]) / 2.0
        return
    }
    let st = lie_sin(theta)
    if lie_abs(st) < 1.0e-10 {
        // theta ~ pi: extract axis from diagonal of R + I
        omega[0] = lie_sqrt(lie_max((R[0] + 1.0) / 2.0, 0.0)) * theta
        omega[1] = lie_sqrt(lie_max((R[4] + 1.0) / 2.0, 0.0)) * theta
        omega[2] = lie_sqrt(lie_max((R[8] + 1.0) / 2.0, 0.0)) * theta
        if R[1] + R[3] < 0.0 { omega[1] = 0.0 - omega[1] }
        if R[2] + R[6] < 0.0 { omega[2] = 0.0 - omega[2] }
        return
    }
    let f = theta / (2.0 * st)
    omega[0] = f * (R[7] - R[5])
    omega[1] = f * (R[2] - R[6])
    omega[2] = f * (R[3] - R[1])
}

// =============================================================================
// Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula
// =============================================================================

// BCH: Z = log(exp(X)*exp(Y)), truncated to given order (max 4).
//   1: X+Y, 2: +1/2[X,Y], 3: +1/12([X,[X,Y]]-[Y,[X,Y]]), 4: -1/24[Y,[X,[X,Y]]]
fn lie_bch(alg: &LieAlgebra, X: &LieElement, Y: &LieElement, order: i32, result: &!LieElement) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let d = alg.dim
    result.dim = d
    var i = 0
    while i < d { result.coeffs[i] = X.coeffs[i] + Y.coeffs[i]; i = i + 1 }
    while i < 16 { result.coeffs[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
    if order < 2 { return }

    var xy: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: d }
    lie_bracket(alg, X, Y, &!xy)
    i = 0
    while i < d { result.coeffs[i] = result.coeffs[i] + 0.5 * xy.coeffs[i]; i = i + 1 }
    if order < 3 { return }

    var xxy: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: d }
    lie_bracket(alg, X, &xy, &!xxy)
    var yxy: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: d }
    lie_bracket(alg, Y, &xy, &!yxy)
    i = 0
    while i < d { result.coeffs[i] = result.coeffs[i] + (xxy.coeffs[i] - yxy.coeffs[i]) / 12.0; i = i + 1 }
    if order < 4 { return }

    var yxxy: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: d }
    lie_bracket(alg, Y, &xxy, &!yxxy)
    i = 0
    while i < d { result.coeffs[i] = result.coeffs[i] - yxxy.coeffs[i] / 24.0; i = i + 1 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Wigner D-matrices for SU(2)
// =============================================================================

// Small Wigner d-matrix d^j_{m',m}(beta).
// All quantum numbers DOUBLED for half-integer support: j2=2j, m1_2=2m', m2_2=2m.
// Uses the Wigner sum formula over s.
fn su2_wigner_d(j2: i32, m1_2: i32, m2_2: i32, beta: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let cb = lie_cos(beta / 2.0)
    let sb = lie_sin(beta / 2.0)
    // Integer quantities (all guaranteed integer since j2, m1_2, m2_2 have same parity)
    let jpm = (j2 + m2_2) / 2      // j + m
    let jmm = (j2 - m2_2) / 2      // j - m
    let jpmp = (j2 + m1_2) / 2     // j + m'
    let jmmp = (j2 - m1_2) / 2     // j - m'
    let mpm = (m1_2 - m2_2) / 2    // m' - m

    var s_min = 0
    if mpm < 0 { s_min = 0 - mpm }
    var s_max = jpm
    if jmmp < s_max { s_max = jmmp }

    let pf = lie_sqrt(lie_factorial(jpmp) * lie_factorial(jmmp) *
                      lie_factorial(jpm) * lie_factorial(jmm))
    var result = 0.0
    var s = s_min
    while s <= s_max {
        let denom = lie_factorial(jpm - s) * lie_factorial(s) *
                    lie_factorial(mpm + s) * lie_factorial(jmmp - s)
        // cos exponent = (j+m-s) + (j-m'-s), sin exponent = (m'-m) + 2s
        let ce = jpm - s + jmmp - s
        let se = mpm + 2 * s
        var ct = 1.0
        var ci = 0
        while ci < ce { ct = ct * cb; ci = ci + 1 }
        var st = 1.0
        var si_c = 0
        while si_c < se { st = st * sb; si_c = si_c + 1 }
        // (-1)^{m'-m+s}
        let sign_exp = mpm + s
        var sign_abs = sign_exp
        if sign_abs < 0 { sign_abs = 0 - sign_abs }
        var sign = 1.0
        if sign_abs - 2 * (sign_abs / 2) != 0 { sign = -1.0 }
        result = result + sign * ct * st / denom
        s = s + 1
    }
    pf * result
}

// Full D-matrix: D^j_{m'm}(a,b,g) = e^{-im'a} d^j_{m'm}(b) e^{-img}
// Stored as Re/Im pairs: D[2*(row*ncols+col)] = Re, D[2*(...)+1] = Im.
// Matrix size (2j+1) x (2j+1), j2 = 2j.
fn su2_rotation_matrix(alpha: f64, beta: f64, gamma: f64, j2: i32,
                       D: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nj = j2 + 1
    var mp_idx = 0
    while mp_idx < nj {
        let mp2 = 0 - j2 + 2 * mp_idx
        var m_idx = 0
        while m_idx < nj {
            let m2 = 0 - j2 + 2 * m_idx
            let d_val = su2_wigner_d(j2, mp2, m2, beta)
            let phase = (mp2 as f64) * alpha / 2.0 + (m2 as f64) * gamma / 2.0
            let idx = 2 * (mp_idx * nj + m_idx)
            D[idx] = lie_cos(phase) * d_val
            D[idx + 1] = (0.0 - lie_sin(phase)) * d_val
            m_idx = m_idx + 1
        }
        mp_idx = mp_idx + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Lie group integrator: Crouch-Grossman RK2
// =============================================================================

// Crouch-Grossman RK2 on Lie groups:
//   k1 = dt * V(t, g);  g1 = exp(k1/2) * g
//   k2 = dt * V(t+dt/2, g1);  g_{n+1} = exp(k2) * g_n
fn lie_group_step(alg: &LieAlgebra, velocity: fn(f64, &[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 16]) with Mut, Div, Panic,
                  g: &![f64; 64], dim: i32, t: f64, dt: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var k1: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    velocity(t, g, dim, &!k1)
    var i = 0
    while i < alg.dim { k1[i] = dt * k1[i]; i = i + 1 }

    var k1_elem: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: alg.dim }
    i = 0
    while i < alg.dim { k1_elem.coeffs[i] = k1[i] / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    var k1_mat: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_to_matrix(alg, &k1_elem, &!k1_mat)
    var exp_k1: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_exp_pade(&k1_mat, dim, &!exp_k1)

    var g1: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_mul(&exp_k1, g, &!g1, dim)

    var k2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    velocity(t + dt / 2.0, &g1, dim, &!k2)
    i = 0
    while i < alg.dim { k2[i] = dt * k2[i]; i = i + 1 }

    var k2_elem: LieElement = LieElement { coeffs: [0.0; 16], dim: alg.dim }
    i = 0
    while i < alg.dim { k2_elem.coeffs[i] = k2[i]; i = i + 1 }
    var k2_mat: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_to_matrix(alg, &k2_elem, &!k2_mat)
    var exp_k2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_exp_pade(&k2_mat, dim, &!exp_k2)

    var g_new: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    lie_mat_mul(&exp_k2, g, &!g_new, dim)
    lie_mat_copy(g, &g_new, dim)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/mor.sio ===
// stdlib/math/mor.sio — Model order reduction
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) via SVD
//   POD energy-based rank selection
//   Galerkin projection of matrices and vectors
//   Reduced basis reconstruction
//   Greedy basis construction with error estimation
//   Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (DEIM)
//   A posteriori error bounds
//   One-sided Jacobi SVD
//
// References:
//   Quarteroni, Manzoni & Negri (2016): "Reduced Basis Methods for PDEs"
//   Hesthaven, Rozza & Stamm (2016): "Certified Reduced Basis Methods"
//   Chaturantabut & Sorensen (2010): "Nonlinear Model Reduction via DEIM"
//   Golub & Van Loan (2013): "Matrix Computations" (SVD)

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (prefix mr_)
