// =============================================================================

fn mr_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn mr_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn mr_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn mr_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// Dot product of two vectors of length n.
fn mr_dot(a: &[f64; 4096], a_off: i32, b: &[f64; 4096], b_off: i32, n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[a_off + i] * b[b_off + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Dot product for 256-element vectors.
fn mr_dot256(a: &[f64; 256], b: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Dot product for 64-element vectors.
fn mr_dot64(a: &[f64; 64], b: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

// Euclidean norm of a contiguous slice within a 4096-array.
fn mr_norm2(a: &[f64; 4096], off: i32, n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[off + i] * a[off + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    mr_sqrt(sum)
}

// Euclidean norm for a 256-element vector.
fn mr_norm2_256(a: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * a[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    mr_sqrt(sum)
}

// Euclidean norm for a 64-element vector.
fn mr_norm2_64(a: &[f64; 64], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * a[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    mr_sqrt(sum)
}

// Copy n elements: dst[d_off..] = src[s_off..].
fn mr_copy(src: &[f64; 4096], s_off: i32, dst: &![f64; 4096], d_off: i32, n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        dst[d_off + i] = src[s_off + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// AXPY: y[off..] += alpha * x[off..], n elements.
fn mr_axpy(alpha: f64, x: &[f64; 4096], x_off: i32, y: &![f64; 4096], y_off: i32, n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        y[y_off + i] = y[y_off + i] + alpha * x[x_off + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Scale: a[off..off+n] *= alpha.
fn mr_scale(a: &![f64; 4096], off: i32, n: i32, alpha: f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        a[off + i] = a[off + i] * alpha
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Zero out n elements starting at off.
fn mr_zero(a: &![f64; 4096], off: i32, n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        a[off + i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Zero a 256-element array.
fn mr_zero_256(a: &![f64; 256], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Zero a 64-element array.
fn mr_zero_64(a: &![f64; 64], n: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Matrix-vector product: y = A*x, A is m x n row-major in flat array.
// y has m elements, x has n elements. Both stored in 4096-arrays.
fn mr_matvec(A: &[f64; 4096], x: &[f64; 4096], x_off: i32,
             m: i32, n: i32,
             y: &![f64; 4096], y_off: i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + A[i * n + j] * x[x_off + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        y[y_off + i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Matrix-vector: y[256] = A[4096]*x[64], A is m x n.
fn mr_matvec_mixed(A: &[f64; 4096], x: &[f64; 64],
                   m: i32, n: i32,
                   y: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + A[i * n + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        y[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Matrix multiply: C = A * B.
// A is m x k, B is k x n, C is m x n. All row-major in 4096-arrays.
fn mr_mat_mul(A: &[f64; 4096], B: &[f64; 4096],
              m: i32, k: i32, n: i32,
              C: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var p = 0
            while p < k {
                sum = sum + A[i * k + p] * B[p * n + j]
                p = p + 1
            }
            C[i * n + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Transpose of A (m x n) into At (n x m). Both in 4096-arrays.
fn mr_transpose(A: &[f64; 4096], m: i32, n: i32, At: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            At[j * m + i] = A[i * n + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Index of element with maximum absolute value in a column of a 4096-array.
// Column col of an m x n matrix, searching rows start_row..m-1.
fn mr_argmax_abs_col(A: &[f64; 4096], m: i32, n: i32, col: i32, start_row: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var best_idx = start_row
    var best_val = mr_abs(A[start_row * n + col])
    var i = start_row + 1
    while i < m {
        let v = mr_abs(A[i * n + col])
        if v > best_val {
            best_val = v
            best_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    best_idx
}

// Index of maximum absolute value in a 256-element vector (first n elements).
fn mr_argmax_abs_256(v: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var best_idx = 0
    var best_val = mr_abs(v[0])
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let a = mr_abs(v[i])
        if a > best_val {
            best_val = a
            best_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    best_idx
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs
// =============================================================================

struct SnapshotMatrix {
    data: [f64; 4096],
    n_dof: i32,
    n_snap: i32
}

struct ReducedBasis {
    V: [f64; 4096],
    n_dof: i32,
    n_basis: i32,
    singular_values: [f64; 64]
}

struct DEIMBasis {
    U: [f64; 4096],
    P: [i32; 64],
    n_dof: i32,
    n_deim: i32
}

struct MORResult {
    u_reduced: [f64; 64],
    u_full: [f64; 256],
    n_basis: i32,
    error_est: f64,
    converged: bool
}

// =============================================================================
// One-Sided Jacobi SVD
// =============================================================================

// One-sided Jacobi SVD: compute thin SVD of an m x n matrix A (m >= n).
//
// Algorithm (Golub & Van Loan, 2013, Section 8.6.3):
//   1. Compute B = A^T A  (n x n symmetric positive semi-definite)
//   2. Eigendecompose B via cyclic Jacobi rotations: B = V * diag(lambda) * V^T
//   3. Singular values: sigma_i = sqrt(lambda_i)
//   4. Left singular vectors: U = A * V * diag(1/sigma_i) for nonzero sigma_i
//
// Output:
//   U  — m x n matrix (thin), row-major in 4096-array
//   S  — n singular values in descending order
//   Vt — n x n matrix (V^T), row-major in 4096-array
fn mr_svd(A: &[f64; 4096], m: i32, n: i32,
          U: &![f64; 4096], S: &![f64; 64], Vt: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {

    // Step 1: Compute B = A^T A (n x n)
    var B: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < m {
                sum = sum + A[k * n + i] * A[k * n + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            B[i * n + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 2: Eigendecompose B via cyclic Jacobi rotations.
    // Initialize V = I_n.
    var V: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        V[i * n + i] = 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Jacobi iterations: sweep through all off-diagonal pairs (p, q) with p < q.
    let max_sweeps = 100
    let tol = 1.0e-12
    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < max_sweeps {
        // Compute off-diagonal Frobenius norm to check convergence
        var off_norm = 0.0
        var p = 0
        while p < n {
            var q = p + 1
            while q < n {
                off_norm = off_norm + B[p * n + q] * B[p * n + q]
                q = q + 1
            }
            p = p + 1
        }
        if off_norm < tol * tol {
            sweep = max_sweeps  // converged, exit
        } else {
            // One full sweep of Jacobi rotations
            p = 0
            while p < n {
                var q = p + 1
                while q < n {
                    let bpq = B[p * n + q]
                    if mr_abs(bpq) > 1.0e-15 {
                        let bpp = B[p * n + p]
                        let bqq = B[q * n + q]

                        // Compute rotation angle: tan(2*theta) = 2*bpq / (bpp - bqq)
                        let tau = (bqq - bpp) / (2.0 * bpq)
                        var t = 0.0
                        if mr_abs(tau) > 1.0e30 {
                            t = 1.0 / (2.0 * tau)
                        } else {
                            let sign_tau = if tau >= 0.0 { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 }
                            t = sign_tau / (mr_abs(tau) + mr_sqrt(1.0 + tau * tau))
                        }
                        let c = 1.0 / mr_sqrt(1.0 + t * t)
                        let s = t * c

                        // Update B: Apply rotation on both sides
                        // B <- G^T B G where G is Givens rotation in (p, q) plane
                        // Rows/cols p and q of B are affected

                        // Update columns of B: B[:, p] and B[:, q]
                        var k = 0
                        while k < n {
                            let bp = B[k * n + p]
                            let bq = B[k * n + q]
                            B[k * n + p] = c * bp - s * bq
                            B[k * n + q] = s * bp + c * bq
                            k = k + 1
                        }
                        // Update rows of B: B[p, :] and B[q, :]
                        k = 0
                        while k < n {
                            let bp = B[p * n + k]
                            let bq = B[q * n + k]
                            B[p * n + k] = c * bp - s * bq
                            B[q * n + k] = s * bp + c * bq
                            k = k + 1
                        }

                        // Restore exact symmetry on diagonal block
                        B[p * n + q] = 0.0
                        B[q * n + p] = 0.0

                        // Accumulate eigenvectors: V <- V * G
                        k = 0
                        while k < n {
                            let vp = V[k * n + p]
                            let vq = V[k * n + q]
                            V[k * n + p] = c * vp - s * vq
                            V[k * n + q] = s * vp + c * vq
                            k = k + 1
                        }
                    }
                    q = q + 1
                }
                p = p + 1
            }
            sweep = sweep + 1
        }
    }

    // Step 3: Extract eigenvalues (diagonal of B) and compute singular values.
    // Also sort in descending order by insertion sort.
    var eig: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var order: [i32; 64] = [0; 64]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        eig[i] = B[i * n + i]
        if eig[i] < 0.0 { eig[i] = 0.0 }  // clamp numerical negatives
        order[i] = i
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Insertion sort descending by eigenvalue
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        let key_val = eig[i]
        let key_idx = order[i]
        var j = i - 1
        var done = false
        while j >= 0 && done == false {
            if eig[j] < key_val {
                eig[j + 1] = eig[j]
                order[j + 1] = order[j]
                j = j - 1
            } else {
                done = true
            }
        }
        eig[j + 1] = key_val
        order[j + 1] = key_idx
        i = i + 1
    }

    // S[i] = sqrt(eig[i])
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        S[i] = mr_sqrt(eig[i])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 4: Build Vt from reordered eigenvectors.
    // V_sorted[:, i] = V[:, order[i]], then Vt = V_sorted^T
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            // Vt[i, j] = V[j, order[i]]
            Vt[i * n + j] = V[j * n + order[i]]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 5: Compute U = A * V_sorted * diag(1/sigma).
    // First build V_sorted in a temporary (it is Vt^T, so V_sorted[j, i] = Vt[i, j]).
    var Vs: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            Vs[j * n + i] = Vt[i * n + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // U[:, i] = A * Vs[:, i] / S[i]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if S[i] > 1.0e-14 {
            let inv_s = 1.0 / S[i]
            var r = 0
            while r < m {
                var sum = 0.0
                var c = 0
                while c < n {
                    sum = sum + A[r * n + c] * Vs[c * n + i]
                    c = c + 1
                }
                U[r * n + i] = sum * inv_s
                r = r + 1
            }
        } else {
            // Zero singular value: set column to zero
            var r = 0
            while r < m {
                U[r * n + i] = 0.0
                r = r + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// POD: Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
// =============================================================================

// Determine smallest rank r such that cumulative energy >= energy_frac.
// Energy fraction = sum_{i<=r} sigma_i^2 / sum_all sigma_i^2.
fn pod_rank_for_energy(sv: &[f64; 64], n: i32, energy_frac: f64) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var total = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        total = total + sv[i] * sv[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    if total < 1.0e-30 { return 1 }

    var cumul = 0.0
    var r = 0
    while r < n {
        cumul = cumul + sv[r] * sv[r]
        if cumul / total >= energy_frac { return r + 1 }
        r = r + 1
    }
    n
}

// Compute POD basis from snapshot matrix.
//
// 1. Compute SVD of snapshot matrix (n_dof x n_snap)
// 2. Select r basis vectors capturing >= energy_thresh fraction of total energy
// 3. Store first r left singular vectors as reduced basis V (n_dof x r)
fn pod_compute(snapshots: &SnapshotMatrix, energy_thresh: f64,
               basis: &!ReducedBasis) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nd = snapshots.n_dof
    let ns = snapshots.n_snap

    // SVD of the snapshot matrix (nd x ns)
    var U_svd: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var S_svd: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var Vt_svd: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]

    mr_svd(&snapshots.data, nd, ns, &!U_svd, &!S_svd, &!Vt_svd)

    // Determine rank from energy threshold
    let r = pod_rank_for_energy(&S_svd, ns, energy_thresh)

    // Store first r left singular vectors as basis: V (nd x r)
    // V[:, j] = U_svd[:, j] for j = 0..r-1
    var i = 0
    while i < nd {
        var j = 0
        while j < r {
            basis.V[i * r + j] = U_svd[i * ns + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    basis.n_dof = nd
    basis.n_basis = r

    // Copy singular values
    i = 0
    while i < ns {
        basis.singular_values[i] = S_svd[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Galerkin Projection
// =============================================================================

// Project matrix: A_r = V^T * A * V  (n_basis x n_basis reduced matrix).
// V is n_dof x n_basis, A is n_dof x n_dof. All row-major.
// Compute AV = A * V (n_dof x n_basis), then A_r = V^T * AV.
fn mor_project_matrix(V: &[f64; 4096], A: &[f64; 4096],
                      n_dof: i32, n_basis: i32,
                      A_r: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: AV = A * V (n_dof x n_basis)
    var AV: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        var j = 0
        while j < n_basis {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < n_dof {
                sum = sum + A[i * n_dof + k] * V[k * n_basis + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            AV[i * n_basis + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 2: A_r = V^T * AV (n_basis x n_basis)
    i = 0
    while i < n_basis {
        var j = 0
        while j < n_basis {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < n_dof {
                // V^T[i, k] = V[k, i] = V[k * n_basis + i]
                sum = sum + V[k * n_basis + i] * AV[k * n_basis + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            A_r[i * n_basis + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Project vector: b_r = V^T * b  (n_basis x 1 reduced vector).
// V is n_dof x n_basis, b has n_dof elements.
fn mor_project_vector(V: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 256],
                      n_dof: i32, n_basis: i32,
                      b_r: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n_basis {
        var sum = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k < n_dof {
            // V^T[i, k] = V[k * n_basis + i]
            sum = sum + V[k * n_basis + i] * b[k]
            k = k + 1
        }
        b_r[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Project right-hand side: f_r = V^T * f.
// Alias for mor_project_vector for notational clarity in RB methods.
fn mor_project_rhs(V: &[f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 256],
                   n_dof: i32, n_basis: i32,
                   f_r: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    mor_project_vector(V, f, n_dof, n_basis, f_r)
}

// =============================================================================
// Reconstruction
// =============================================================================

// Reconstruct full solution: u_full = V * u_red  (n_dof x 1).
// V is n_dof x n_basis, u_red has n_basis elements.
fn mor_reconstruct(V: &[f64; 4096], u_red: &[f64; 64],
                   n_dof: i32, n_basis: i32,
                   u_full: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n_basis {
            sum = sum + V[i * n_basis + j] * u_red[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        u_full[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Reduced System Solve (Gaussian Elimination)
// =============================================================================

// Solve A_r * u_r = b_r via Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.
// A_r is n_basis x n_basis, b_r and u_r have n_basis elements.
// A_r is copied internally (not destroyed).
fn mor_solve_reduced(A_r: &[f64; 4096], b_r: &[f64; 64], n_basis: i32,
                     u_r: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nb = n_basis

    // Copy A_r and b_r into working arrays
    var M: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var rhs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < nb {
        var j = 0
        while j < nb {
            M[i * nb + j] = A_r[i * nb + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        rhs[i] = b_r[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Forward elimination with partial pivoting
    var col = 0
    while col < nb {
        // Find pivot: row with max absolute value in column col, rows col..nb-1
        var pivot_row = col
        var pivot_val = mr_abs(M[col * nb + col])
        var row = col + 1
        while row < nb {
            let v = mr_abs(M[row * nb + col])
            if v > pivot_val {
                pivot_val = v
                pivot_row = row
            }
            row = row + 1
        }

        // Swap rows col and pivot_row
        if pivot_row != col {
            var k = 0
            while k < nb {
                let tmp = M[col * nb + k]
                M[col * nb + k] = M[pivot_row * nb + k]
                M[pivot_row * nb + k] = tmp
                k = k + 1
            }
            let tmp_r = rhs[col]
            rhs[col] = rhs[pivot_row]
            rhs[pivot_row] = tmp_r
        }

        // Eliminate below
        let diag = M[col * nb + col]
        if mr_abs(diag) < 1.0e-30 {
            // Singular or nearly singular — set solution to zero for this component
            col = col + 1
        } else {
            row = col + 1
            while row < nb {
                let factor = M[row * nb + col] / diag
                var k = col + 1
                while k < nb {
                    M[row * nb + k] = M[row * nb + k] - factor * M[col * nb + k]
                    k = k + 1
                }
                M[row * nb + col] = 0.0
                rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
                row = row + 1
            }
            col = col + 1
        }
    }

    // Back substitution
    i = nb - 1
    var done_back = false
    while i >= 0 && done_back == false {
        var sum = rhs[i]
        var j = i + 1
        while j < nb {
            sum = sum - M[i * nb + j] * u_r[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = M[i * nb + i]
        if mr_abs(diag) < 1.0e-30 {
            u_r[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            u_r[i] = sum / diag
        }
        if i == 0 { done_back = true } else { i = i - 1 }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Error Estimation
// =============================================================================

// Residual-based a posteriori error estimate:
//   ||b - A * V * u_red|| / ||b||
//
// This is the relative residual norm, which provides a computable
// upper bound when combined with the inf-sup constant (Hesthaven et al., 2016).
fn mor_error_estimate(A: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 256], V: &[f64; 4096],
                      u_red: &[f64; 64],
                      n_dof: i32, n_basis: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute u_full = V * u_red
    var u_full: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    mor_reconstruct(V, u_red, n_dof, n_basis, &!u_full)

    // Compute residual r = b - A * u_full
    var res: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n_dof {
            sum = sum + A[i * n_dof + j] * u_full[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        res[i] = b[i] - sum
        i = i + 1
    }

    let res_norm = mr_norm2_256(&res, n_dof)
    let b_norm = mr_norm2_256(b, n_dof)

    if b_norm < 1.0e-30 { return res_norm }
    res_norm / b_norm
}

// True relative error: ||u_exact - u_approx|| / ||u_exact||.
fn mor_true_error(u_full_exact: &[f64; 256], u_full_approx: &[f64; 256],
                  n_dof: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var diff_sq = 0.0
    var exact_sq = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        let d = u_full_exact[i] - u_full_approx[i]
        diff_sq = diff_sq + d * d
        exact_sq = exact_sq + u_full_exact[i] * u_full_exact[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    if exact_sq < 1.0e-30 { return mr_sqrt(diff_sq) }
    mr_sqrt(diff_sq) / mr_sqrt(exact_sq)
}

// =============================================================================
// Full MOR Pipeline
// =============================================================================

// Solve a reduced-order model: project, solve reduced system, reconstruct,
// compute error estimate.
//
// Given full system A*u = b and a precomputed ReducedBasis:
//   1. A_r = V^T A V
//   2. b_r = V^T b
//   3. Solve A_r u_r = b_r
//   4. u_full = V u_r
//   5. error_est = ||b - A u_full|| / ||b||
fn mor_solve(A: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 256], n_dof: i32,
             basis: &ReducedBasis,
             result: &!MORResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nb = basis.n_basis

    // Project matrix
    var A_r: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mor_project_matrix(&basis.V, A, n_dof, nb, &!A_r)

    // Project RHS
    var b_r: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    mor_project_rhs(&basis.V, b, n_dof, nb, &!b_r)

    // Solve reduced system
    var u_r: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    mor_solve_reduced(&A_r, &b_r, nb, &!u_r)

    // Store reduced solution
    var i = 0
    while i < nb {
        result.u_reduced[i] = u_r[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Reconstruct full solution
    mor_reconstruct(&basis.V, &u_r, n_dof, nb, &!result.u_full)

    // Compute error estimate
    let err = mor_error_estimate(A, b, &basis.V, &u_r, n_dof, nb)

    result.n_basis = nb
    result.error_est = err
    result.converged = err < 1.0e-6
}

// =============================================================================
// Modified Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization
// =============================================================================

// Orthogonalize v_new against the existing columns of V and append it.
// V is n_dof x n_basis (the existing basis). After this call, column n_basis
// of V contains the orthonormalized new vector.
//
// Uses modified Gram-Schmidt (MGS) for numerical stability:
//   for each existing column q_j:
//     v_new = v_new - <v_new, q_j> * q_j
//   v_new = v_new / ||v_new||
fn mr_gram_schmidt(V: &![f64; 4096], n_dof: i32, n_basis: i32,
                   v_new: &[f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Copy v_new into a working array within V's column space
    var w: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        w[i] = v_new[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Two passes of MGS for improved orthogonality (reorthogonalization).
    // This is standard practice in reduced basis methods
    // (Daniel, Gragg, Kaufman & Stewart, 1976).
    var pass = 0
    while pass < 2 {
        var j = 0
        while j < n_basis {
            // Compute projection coefficient: <w, V[:, j]>
            var proj = 0.0
            i = 0
            while i < n_dof {
                proj = proj + w[i] * V[i * n_basis + j]
                i = i + 1
            }
            // Subtract projection: w = w - proj * V[:, j]
            i = 0
            while i < n_dof {
                w[i] = w[i] - proj * V[i * n_basis + j]
                i = i + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        pass = pass + 1
    }

    // Normalize
    let nrm = mr_norm2_256(&w, n_dof)
    if nrm < 1.0e-14 {
        // Linearly dependent: store zero vector (caller should check)
        i = 0
        while i < n_dof {
            V[i * (n_basis + 1) + n_basis] = 0.0
            i = i + 1
        }
        return
    }

    let inv_nrm = 1.0 / nrm

    // We need to write into a reshaped V: the new column width is n_basis + 1.
    // However, since V is a flat 4096-array and the caller will update n_basis,
    // we write into column n_basis of the (n_dof x (n_basis+1)) layout.
    // IMPORTANT: The caller must have allocated V with enough logical columns.
    // We write at offset positions: V[i * new_width + n_basis] where
    // new_width is what the caller will use after incrementing n_basis.
    // Since the caller controls the stride, and the greedy algorithm rebuilds
    // V from scratch, here we write using stride (n_basis + 1).
    //
    // Actually, to keep consistent with the greedy_basis function that
    // rebuilds V with the new stride, we simply return the normalized vector
    // in V's column n_basis using stride = n_basis + 1.
    i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        V[i * (n_basis + 1) + n_basis] = w[i] * inv_nrm
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Greedy Basis Construction
// =============================================================================

// Greedy reduced basis construction with error-driven parameter selection.
//
// Algorithm (Hesthaven, Rozza & Stamm, 2016, Ch. 3):
//   1. Start with first parameter: solve full system, set as initial basis
//   2. For each candidate parameter in the training set:
//      a. Compute full solution u(mu)
//      b. Project onto current basis: u_proj = V * V^T * u(mu)
//      c. Measure error = ||u(mu) - u_proj||
//   3. Add parameter with largest projection error to the basis
//      (Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization)
//   4. Repeat until error < tol or max_basis reached
//
// solve_full(param_vec, n_dof, u_out): solves the full-order model for the
// parameter values encoded in param_vec (first entry used as scalar param).
fn greedy_basis(params: &[f64; 64], n_params: i32, n_dof: i32,
                max_basis: i32, tol: f64,
                basis: &!ReducedBasis,
                solve_full: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Clamp max_basis to avoid exceeding array bounds
    var max_b = max_basis
    if max_b > 64 { max_b = 64 }
    if max_b > n_params { max_b = n_params }

    // Storage for all full solutions (precompute for efficiency)
    // We store them in a flat array: solutions[j * n_dof + i] = u_j[i]
    // Limited by 4096: n_params * n_dof must fit.
    var solutions: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var param_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var u_tmp: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]

    // Track which parameters have been selected
    var selected: [i32; 64] = [0; 64]  // 1 if selected, 0 otherwise

    // Solve for the first parameter and initialize basis
    param_vec[0] = params[0]
    solve_full(&param_vec, n_dof, &!u_tmp)

    // Store solution
    var i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        solutions[0 * n_dof + i] = u_tmp[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute remaining solutions
    var j = 1
    while j < n_params {
        param_vec[0] = params[j]
        solve_full(&param_vec, n_dof, &!u_tmp)
        i = 0
        while i < n_dof {
            solutions[j * n_dof + i] = u_tmp[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Initialize basis with first solution (normalized)
    let nrm0 = mr_norm2_256(&u_tmp, n_dof)

    // Reload first solution into u_tmp
    i = 0
    while i < n_dof {
        u_tmp[i] = solutions[0 * n_dof + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let norm_first = mr_norm2_256(&u_tmp, n_dof)

    // V starts as n_dof x 1
    if norm_first > 1.0e-14 {
        let inv_n = 1.0 / norm_first
        i = 0
        while i < n_dof {
            basis.V[i * 1 + 0] = u_tmp[i] * inv_n
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        i = 0
        while i < n_dof {
            basis.V[i * 1 + 0] = 0.0
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    basis.n_dof = n_dof
    basis.n_basis = 1
    selected[0] = 1

    // Greedy loop
    var nb = 1
    var max_err = 1.0e30
    while nb < max_b && max_err > tol {
        // Find parameter with largest projection error
        var worst_idx = -1
        var worst_err = 0.0

        j = 0
        while j < n_params {
            if selected[j] == 0 {
                // Compute projection of solution j onto current basis
                // u_proj = V * V^T * u_j
                // Error = ||u_j - u_proj||

                // Load u_j
                var u_j: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
                i = 0
                while i < n_dof {
                    u_j[i] = solutions[j * n_dof + i]
                    i = i + 1
                }

                // Compute V^T * u_j (nb coefficients)
                var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
                var c = 0
                while c < nb {
                    var dot = 0.0
                    i = 0
                    while i < n_dof {
                        dot = dot + basis.V[i * nb + c] * u_j[i]
                        i = i + 1
                    }
                    coeffs[c] = dot
                    c = c + 1
                }

                // Compute u_proj = V * coeffs and error = u_j - u_proj
                var err_sq = 0.0
                i = 0
                while i < n_dof {
                    var proj_i = 0.0
                    c = 0
                    while c < nb {
                        proj_i = proj_i + basis.V[i * nb + c] * coeffs[c]
                        c = c + 1
                    }
                    let diff = u_j[i] - proj_i
                    err_sq = err_sq + diff * diff
                    i = i + 1
                }

                let err = mr_sqrt(err_sq)
                if err > worst_err {
                    worst_err = err
                    worst_idx = j
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }

        max_err = worst_err

        if worst_idx < 0 || max_err <= tol {
            // No more candidates or tolerance met
            max_err = 0.0  // exit loop
        } else {
            // Add the worst-error solution to the basis via Gram-Schmidt
            selected[worst_idx] = 1

            // Load the solution
            i = 0
            while i < n_dof {
                u_tmp[i] = solutions[worst_idx * n_dof + i]
                i = i + 1
            }

            // Rebuild V with new column width (nb + 1).
            // Copy existing V (n_dof x nb) into new layout (n_dof x (nb+1))
            var V_new: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
            i = 0
            while i < n_dof {
                var c = 0
                while c < nb {
                    V_new[i * (nb + 1) + c] = basis.V[i * nb + c]
                    c = c + 1
                }
                i = i + 1
            }

            // Copy V_new back to basis.V
            i = 0
            while i < 4096 {
                basis.V[i] = V_new[i]
                i = i + 1
            }

            // Orthogonalize u_tmp against existing columns and append
            mr_gram_schmidt(&!basis.V, n_dof, nb, &u_tmp)

            nb = nb + 1
            basis.n_basis = nb
        }
    }

    // Store singular values as zeros (not computed in greedy — would need SVD
    // of the snapshot matrix for true singular values; the greedy basis is
    // not guaranteed to produce them in order)
    i = 0
    while i < 64 {
        basis.singular_values[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// DEIM: Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method
// =============================================================================

// Compute DEIM interpolation indices from a basis.
//
// Algorithm (Chaturantabut & Sorensen, 2010):
//   Input: U = [u_1, ..., u_m] orthonormal DEIM basis (n_dof x m)
//   Output: P = interpolation indices (m integers)
//
//   1. p_1 = argmax |u_1|
//      P = {p_1}
//   2. For l = 2, ..., m:
//      a. Solve (P^T U_{1:l-1}) c = P^T u_l  (small (l-1) x (l-1) system)
//      b. r = u_l - U_{1:l-1} * c             (residual)
//      c. p_l = argmax |r|
//      P = P union {p_l}
//
// Uses the first n_deim columns of basis.V as the DEIM basis U.
fn deim_compute(basis: &ReducedBasis, deim: &!DEIMBasis) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nd = basis.n_dof
    var m = basis.n_basis
    if m > 64 { m = 64 }

    // Copy first m columns of basis.V into deim.U (nd x m)
    var i = 0
    while i < nd {
        var j = 0
        while j < m {
            deim.U[i * m + j] = basis.V[i * basis.n_basis + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    deim.n_dof = nd
    deim.n_deim = m

    // Step 1: p_1 = argmax |u_1|
    var u_col: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    i = 0
    while i < nd {
        u_col[i] = deim.U[i * m + 0]
        i = i + 1
    }
    deim.P[0] = mr_argmax_abs_256(&u_col, nd)

    // Step 2: For l = 1, 2, ..., m-1 (0-indexed: adding column l)
    var l = 1
    while l < m {
        // Extract u_l (column l of U)
        i = 0
        while i < nd {
            u_col[i] = deim.U[i * m + l]
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Build the small system (P^T U_{1:l}) c = P^T u_l
        // (P^T U_{1:l}) is l x l: row i selects row P[i] from U_{1:l}
        var PtU: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        var Ptu: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        i = 0
        while i < l {
            let pi = deim.P[i]
            var j = 0
            while j < l {
                PtU[i * l + j] = deim.U[pi * m + j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            Ptu[i] = u_col[pi]
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Solve PtU * c = Ptu via Gaussian elimination (small l x l system)
        var c_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

        // Forward elimination with partial pivoting
        var M: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        var rhs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        i = 0
        while i < l {
            var j = 0
            while j < l {
                M[i * l + j] = PtU[i * l + j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            rhs[i] = Ptu[i]
            i = i + 1
        }

        var col = 0
        while col < l {
            // Partial pivoting
            var pivot_row = col
            var pivot_val = mr_abs(M[col * l + col])
            var row = col + 1
            while row < l {
                let v = mr_abs(M[row * l + col])
                if v > pivot_val { pivot_val = v; pivot_row = row }
                row = row + 1
            }
            if pivot_row != col {
                var k = 0
                while k < l {
                    let tmp = M[col * l + k]
                    M[col * l + k] = M[pivot_row * l + k]
                    M[pivot_row * l + k] = tmp
                    k = k + 1
                }
                let tmp_r = rhs[col]
                rhs[col] = rhs[pivot_row]
                rhs[pivot_row] = tmp_r
            }

            let diag = M[col * l + col]
            if mr_abs(diag) > 1.0e-30 {
                row = col + 1
                while row < l {
                    let factor = M[row * l + col] / diag
                    var k = col + 1
                    while k < l {
                        M[row * l + k] = M[row * l + k] - factor * M[col * l + k]
                        k = k + 1
                    }
                    rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
                    row = row + 1
                }
            }
            col = col + 1
        }

        // Back substitution
        i = l - 1
        var done_bs = false
        while i >= 0 && done_bs == false {
            var sum = rhs[i]
            var j = i + 1
            while j < l {
                sum = sum - M[i * l + j] * c_vec[j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            let diag = M[i * l + i]
            if mr_abs(diag) > 1.0e-30 {
                c_vec[i] = sum / diag
            } else {
                c_vec[i] = 0.0
            }
            if i == 0 { done_bs = true } else { i = i - 1 }
        }

        // Compute residual: r = u_l - U_{1:l} * c
        var res: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
        i = 0
        while i < nd {
            var val = u_col[i]
            var j = 0
            while j < l {
                val = val - deim.U[i * m + j] * c_vec[j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            res[i] = val
            i = i + 1
        }

        // p_l = argmax |r|
        deim.P[l] = mr_argmax_abs_256(&res, nd)

        l = l + 1
    }
}

// Approximate a nonlinear function using DEIM.
//
// f_approx = U * (P^T U)^{-1} * P^T * f_full
//
// This requires evaluating f only at the m DEIM interpolation indices
// (stored in deim.P), not at all n_dof DOFs. The complexity reduction
// from O(n_dof) to O(m) per nonlinear evaluation is the key benefit.
fn deim_approximate(deim: &DEIMBasis, f_full: &[f64; 256],
                    f_approx: &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nd = deim.n_dof
    let m = deim.n_deim

    // Step 1: Extract f at DEIM indices: f_P = P^T * f_full (m elements)
    var f_P: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < m {
        f_P[i] = f_full[deim.P[i]]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 2: Build (P^T U) — m x m matrix
    var PtU: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < m {
        let pi = deim.P[i]
        var j = 0
        while j < m {
            PtU[i * m + j] = deim.U[pi * m + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 3: Solve (P^T U) * c = f_P via Gaussian elimination
    var c_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Copy PtU and f_P into working arrays
    var M: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var rhs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    i = 0
    while i < m {
        var j = 0
        while j < m {
            M[i * m + j] = PtU[i * m + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        rhs[i] = f_P[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Forward elimination with partial pivoting
    var col = 0
    while col < m {
        var pivot_row = col
        var pivot_val = mr_abs(M[col * m + col])
        var row = col + 1
        while row < m {
            let v = mr_abs(M[row * m + col])
            if v > pivot_val { pivot_val = v; pivot_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }
        if pivot_row != col {
            var k = 0
            while k < m {
                let tmp = M[col * m + k]
                M[col * m + k] = M[pivot_row * m + k]
                M[pivot_row * m + k] = tmp
                k = k + 1
            }
            let tmp_r = rhs[col]
            rhs[col] = rhs[pivot_row]
            rhs[pivot_row] = tmp_r
        }

        let diag = M[col * m + col]
        if mr_abs(diag) > 1.0e-30 {
            row = col + 1
            while row < m {
                let factor = M[row * m + col] / diag
                var k = col + 1
                while k < m {
                    M[row * m + k] = M[row * m + k] - factor * M[col * m + k]
                    k = k + 1
                }
                rhs[row] = rhs[row] - factor * rhs[col]
                row = row + 1
            }
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    i = m - 1
    var done_bs = false
    while i >= 0 && done_bs == false {
        var sum = rhs[i]
        var j = i + 1
        while j < m {
            sum = sum - M[i * m + j] * c_vec[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = M[i * m + i]
        if mr_abs(diag) > 1.0e-30 {
            c_vec[i] = sum / diag
        } else {
            c_vec[i] = 0.0
        }
        if i == 0 { done_bs = true } else { i = i - 1 }
    }

    // Step 4: f_approx = U * c_vec (nd x 1)
    i = 0
    while i < nd {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < m {
            sum = sum + deim.U[i * m + j] * c_vec[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        f_approx[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Snapshot Collection
// =============================================================================

// Collect snapshots by solving the full-order model for each parameter.
//
// For each parameter mu_j in params[0..n_params-1]:
//   solve_full(param_vec, n_dof, u_out) computes u(mu_j)
//   Store as column j of snapshot matrix: data[i * n_snap + j] = u_j[i]
//
// The snapshot matrix has dimensions n_dof x n_params (row-major).
fn mor_collect_snapshots(params: &[f64; 64], n_params: i32, n_dof: i32,
                         snapshots: &!SnapshotMatrix,
                         solve: fn(&[f64; 64], i32, &![f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    snapshots.n_dof = n_dof
    snapshots.n_snap = n_params

    var param_vec: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var u_out: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]

    var j = 0
    while j < n_params {
        param_vec[0] = params[j]
        solve(&param_vec, n_dof, &!u_out)

        // Store as column j: data[i * n_params + j] = u_out[i]
        var i = 0
        while i < n_dof {
            snapshots.data[i * n_params + j] = u_out[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/multigrid.sio ===
// stdlib/math/multigrid.sio — Geometric multigrid solvers
//
// Pure Sounio implementations:
//   Full-weighting restriction (1D and 2D)
//   Linear interpolation prolongation (1D and 2D)
//   Weighted Jacobi smoother
//   Red-black Gauss-Seidel smoother (1D and 2D)
//   V-cycle and W-cycle
//   Full multigrid solver for Poisson's equation
//   2D Poisson multigrid
//
// References:
//   Briggs, Henson & McCormick (2000): "A Multigrid Tutorial"
//   Trottenberg, Oosterlee & Schuller (2001): "Multigrid"
//   Hackbusch (1985): "Multi-Grid Methods and Applications"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers (prefixed mg_ to avoid collisions)
// =============================================================================

fn mg_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn mg_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

fn mg_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// =============================================================================
// Structs
// =============================================================================

// Configuration for multigrid solver.
//   n_levels:   number of grid levels (coarsest = level n_levels-1)
//   nu1:        pre-smoothing steps
//   nu2:        post-smoothing steps
//   max_cycles: maximum outer iterations
//   tol:        convergence tolerance (L2 residual norm)
//   omega:      relaxation weight for Jacobi (typically 2/3)
struct MGConfig { n_levels: i32, nu1: i32, nu2: i32, max_cycles: i32, tol: f64, omega: f64 }

// Result of a multigrid solve.
//   u:             solution values on the finest grid
//   iterations:    number of cycles performed
//   residual_norm: final L2 residual norm
//   converged:     whether tol was reached
struct MGResult { u: [f64; 4096], iterations: i32, residual_norm: f64, converged: bool }

// A single multigrid grid level (used internally for scratch storage).
struct MGGrid { u: [f64; 4096], f: [f64; 4096], r: [f64; 4096], n: i32 }

// =============================================================================
// Utility: default configuration
// =============================================================================

// Populate config with sensible defaults for a given number of levels.
// nu1=2 pre-smooth, nu2=2 post-smooth, max_cycles=100, tol=1e-10, omega=2/3.
fn mg_default_config(n_levels: i32, config: &!MGConfig) with Panic, Mut {
    config.n_levels = n_levels
    config.nu1 = 2
    config.nu2 = 2
    config.max_cycles = 100
    config.tol = 1.0e-10
    config.omega = 2.0 / 3.0
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D Transfer Operators
// =============================================================================

// Full-weighting restriction from fine grid to coarse grid (1D).
// n_fine is the number of intervals (grid has n_fine+1 points indexed 0..n_fine).
// Coarse grid has n_coarse = n_fine/2 intervals (n_coarse+1 points).
// Interior: coarse[i] = 0.25*fine[2i-1] + 0.5*fine[2i] + 0.25*fine[2i+1]
// Boundary: coarse[0] = fine[0], coarse[n_c] = fine[n_f]
fn mg_restrict_1d(fine: &[f64; 4096], n_fine: i32, coarse: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let n_coarse = n_fine / 2

    // Boundary points
    coarse[0] = fine[0]
    coarse[n_coarse] = fine[n_fine]

    // Interior points: full-weighting stencil [1/4, 1/2, 1/4]
    var i = 1
    while i < n_coarse {
        let fi = 2 * i
        coarse[i] = 0.25 * fine[fi - 1] + 0.5 * fine[fi] + 0.25 * fine[fi + 1]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Linear interpolation prolongation from coarse to fine grid (1D).
// n_coarse is the number of intervals on the coarse grid.
// Fine grid has n_fine = 2*n_coarse intervals.
// Coincident points: fine[2i] = coarse[i]
// Midpoints:         fine[2i+1] = 0.5*(coarse[i] + coarse[i+1])
fn mg_prolongate_1d(coarse: &[f64; 4096], n_coarse: i32, fine: &![f64; 4096]) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Coincident points
    var i = 0
    while i <= n_coarse {
        fine[2 * i] = coarse[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Midpoints by linear interpolation
    i = 0
    while i < n_coarse {
        fine[2 * i + 1] = 0.5 * (coarse[i] + coarse[i + 1])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D Smoothers
// =============================================================================

// Weighted Jacobi smoother for 1D Poisson: -u'' = f on [0,1].
// Performs nu sweeps. h = 1/n is the mesh spacing. omega is the damping
// parameter (2/3 for optimal high-frequency damping).
// Update: u_new[i] = omega * (u[i-1] + u[i+1] + h^2*f[i]) / 2  +  (1-omega)*u[i]
fn mg_smooth_jacobi_1d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096], n: i32,
                       h: f64, omega: f64, nu: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h2 = h * h
    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < nu {
        // We need the old values; copy u into a temporary array.
        var u_old: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        var k = 0
        while k <= n {
            u_old[k] = u[k]
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Jacobi update for interior points (boundary stays fixed)
        var i = 1
        while i < n {
            let avg = (u_old[i - 1] + u_old[i + 1] + h2 * f[i]) / 2.0
            u[i] = omega * avg + (1.0 - omega) * u_old[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        sweep = sweep + 1
    }
}

// Red-black Gauss-Seidel smoother for 1D Poisson.
// Red = odd indices, black = even indices.
// Update: u[i] = (u[i-1] + u[i+1] + h^2*f[i]) / 2
// Performs nu full red-black sweeps.
fn mg_smooth_gs_rb_1d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096], n: i32,
                      h: f64, nu: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h2 = h * h
    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < nu {
        // Red sweep: odd indices
        var i = 1
        while i < n {
            // Check if i is odd: i - (i/2)*2 == 1
            let rem = i - (i / 2) * 2
            if rem == 1 {
                u[i] = (u[i - 1] + u[i + 1] + h2 * f[i]) / 2.0
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Black sweep: even indices (skip boundary 0 and n)
        i = 2
        while i < n {
            let rem = i - (i / 2) * 2
            if rem == 0 {
                u[i] = (u[i - 1] + u[i + 1] + h2 * f[i]) / 2.0
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        sweep = sweep + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D Residual
// =============================================================================

// Compute residual for 1D Poisson: r[i] = f[i] - (-u[i-1] + 2*u[i] - u[i+1])/h^2
// for interior points. r[0] = r[n] = 0 (boundary residual is zero for
// homogeneous Dirichlet BCs).
fn mg_residual_1d(u: &[f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096], n: i32,
                  h: f64, r: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h2 = h * h
    r[0] = 0.0
    r[n] = 0.0

    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let lap = (0.0 - u[i - 1] + 2.0 * u[i] - u[i + 1]) / h2
        r[i] = f[i] - lap
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// L2 norm of the residual on a 1D grid with n intervals:
// ||r||_2 = sqrt(h * sum_{i=1}^{n-1} r[i]^2)
fn mg_residual_norm_1d(r: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h = 1.0 / (n as f64)
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + r[i] * r[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    mg_sqrt(h * sum)
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D Coarse Solve (Thomas algorithm)
// =============================================================================

// Direct solve of the 1D Poisson equation on a small grid using the Thomas
// algorithm (tridiagonal solver). The system is:
//   -u[i-1] + 2*u[i] - u[i+1] = h^2 * f[i],  i = 1..n-1
// with u[0] = u[n] = 0 (homogeneous Dirichlet).
// Tridiagonal: a[i] = -1, b[i] = 2, c[i] = -1, d[i] = h^2*f[i].
fn mg_coarse_solve_1d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096], n: i32,
                      h: f64) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let h2 = h * h
    let m = n - 1  // number of interior unknowns

    if m <= 0 { return }

    // Diagonal and RHS arrays for the tridiagonal system
    // We solve in-place: b_mod[i] for modified diagonal, d_mod[i] for modified RHS.
    var b_mod: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var d_mod: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]

    // Sub-diagonal a = -1.0, main diagonal b = 2.0, super-diagonal c = -1.0
    // Forward sweep: eliminate sub-diagonal
    // b_mod[0] = 2.0, d_mod[0] = h^2 * f[1]
    b_mod[0] = 2.0
    d_mod[0] = h2 * f[1]

    var i = 1
    while i < m {
        // w = a / b_mod[i-1] = -1 / b_mod[i-1]
        let w = 0.0 - 1.0 / b_mod[i - 1]
        b_mod[i] = 2.0 - (0.0 - 1.0) * w   // 2.0 - c * w where c = -1
        d_mod[i] = h2 * f[i + 1] - d_mod[i - 1] * w
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    u[m] = d_mod[m - 1] / b_mod[m - 1]   // interior index m maps to u[n-1]

    // Careful: the interior points are u[1]..u[n-1].
    // We stored them as index 0..m-1 in b_mod/d_mod.
    // u[interior_k+1] where interior_k = m-1 is u[n-1], already done.
    // Now go backwards.
    i = m - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        // u[interior index i+1] = (d_mod[i] - c * u[interior index i+2]) / b_mod[i]
        // c = -1, interior index i+1 = i+1, i+2 = i+2
        u[i + 1] = (d_mod[i] + u[i + 2]) / b_mod[i]
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Boundary
    u[0] = 0.0
    u[n] = 0.0
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D V-Cycle
// =============================================================================

// Recursive V-cycle for 1D Poisson.
//   1. Pre-smooth nu1 sweeps of red-black GS
//   2. Compute residual
//   3. Restrict residual to coarse grid
//   4. If at coarsest level, direct solve; otherwise recurse
//   5. Prolongate coarse correction and add to u
//   6. Post-smooth nu2 sweeps of red-black GS
fn mg_vcycle_1d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096], n: i32,
                h: f64, config: &MGConfig, level: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Base case: coarsest level or grid too small — direct solve
    if level >= config.n_levels - 1 {
        mg_coarse_solve_1d(u, f, n, h)
        return
    }
    if n <= 2 {
        mg_coarse_solve_1d(u, f, n, h)
        return
    }

    // 1. Pre-smoothing
    mg_smooth_gs_rb_1d(u, f, n, h, config.nu1)

    // 2. Compute residual
    var r_fine: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_residual_1d(u, f, n, h, &!r_fine)

    // 3. Restrict residual to coarse grid
    let n_coarse = n / 2
    var r_coarse: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_restrict_1d(&r_fine, n, &!r_coarse)

    // 4. Solve on coarse grid for the correction e: A_c * e = r_coarse
    var e_coarse: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let h_coarse = 2.0 * h
    mg_vcycle_1d(&!e_coarse, &r_coarse, n_coarse, h_coarse, config, level + 1)

    // 5. Prolongate correction and add to u
    var e_fine: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_prolongate_1d(&e_coarse, n_coarse, &!e_fine)

    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        u[i] = u[i] + e_fine[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // 6. Post-smoothing
    mg_smooth_gs_rb_1d(u, f, n, h, config.nu2)
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D W-Cycle
// =============================================================================

// Recursive W-cycle for 1D Poisson. Same as V-cycle but the coarse grid
// correction is applied TWICE (two recursive calls instead of one).
fn mg_wcycle_1d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096], n: i32,
                h: f64, config: &MGConfig, level: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Base case: coarsest level or grid too small
    if level >= config.n_levels - 1 {
        mg_coarse_solve_1d(u, f, n, h)
        return
    }
    if n <= 2 {
        mg_coarse_solve_1d(u, f, n, h)
        return
    }

    // 1. Pre-smoothing
    mg_smooth_gs_rb_1d(u, f, n, h, config.nu1)

    // 2. Compute residual
    var r_fine: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_residual_1d(u, f, n, h, &!r_fine)

    // 3. Restrict residual to coarse grid
    let n_coarse = n / 2
    var r_coarse: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_restrict_1d(&r_fine, n, &!r_coarse)

    // 4. Recurse TWICE on coarse grid (W-cycle pattern)
    var e_coarse: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let h_coarse = 2.0 * h

    // First coarse-grid correction
    mg_wcycle_1d(&!e_coarse, &r_coarse, n_coarse, h_coarse, config, level + 1)

    // Second coarse-grid correction
    mg_wcycle_1d(&!e_coarse, &r_coarse, n_coarse, h_coarse, config, level + 1)

    // 5. Prolongate correction and add to u
    var e_fine: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_prolongate_1d(&e_coarse, n_coarse, &!e_fine)

    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        u[i] = u[i] + e_fine[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // 6. Post-smoothing
    mg_smooth_gs_rb_1d(u, f, n, h, config.nu2)
}

// =============================================================================
// 1D Full Multigrid Solver
// =============================================================================

// Solve -u'' = f_rhs(x) on [0,1] with u(0) = u(1) = 0.
// n is the number of intervals (must be a power of 2).
// Iterates V-cycles until the residual norm drops below config.tol
// or max_cycles is reached.
fn mg_solve_poisson_1d(f_rhs: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       n: i32, config: &MGConfig,
                       result: &!MGResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h = 1.0 / (n as f64)

    // Initialize solution to zero
    var i = 0
    while i <= n {
        result.u[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Set up RHS: evaluate f_rhs at grid points
    var f_vals: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i <= n {
        let x = (i as f64) * h
        f_vals[i] = f_rhs(x)
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Enforce boundary in RHS
    f_vals[0] = 0.0
    f_vals[n] = 0.0

    // Iterate V-cycles
    result.converged = false
    result.iterations = 0

    var cycle = 0
    while cycle < config.max_cycles {
        mg_vcycle_1d(&!result.u, &f_vals, n, h, config, 0)

        // Compute residual and its norm
        var r: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        mg_residual_1d(&result.u, &f_vals, n, h, &!r)
        let rnorm = mg_residual_norm_1d(&r, n)

        result.residual_norm = rnorm
        result.iterations = cycle + 1

        if rnorm < config.tol {
            result.converged = true
            return
        }
        cycle = cycle + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Index Helpers
// =============================================================================

// Convert 2D grid index (i, j) to flat array index.
// Grid has (nx+1) columns, so point (i, j) is at i*(nx+1) + j.
fn mg_idx2d(i: i32, j: i32, nx: i32) -> i32 {
    i * (nx + 1) + j
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Transfer Operators
// =============================================================================

// Full-weighting restriction from fine to coarse grid (2D).
// Fine grid has (nx_f+1) x (ny_f+1) points.
// Coarse grid has (nx_c+1) x (ny_c+1) where nx_c = nx_f/2, ny_c = ny_f/2.
// Stencil weights:
//   corners (1/16): fine[2i-1,2j-1], fine[2i-1,2j+1], fine[2i+1,2j-1], fine[2i+1,2j+1]
//   edges   (1/8):  fine[2i,2j-1], fine[2i,2j+1], fine[2i-1,2j], fine[2i+1,2j]
//   center  (1/4):  fine[2i,2j]
fn mg_restrict_2d(fine: &[f64; 4096], nx_f: i32, ny_f: i32,
                  coarse: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let nx_c = nx_f / 2
    let ny_c = ny_f / 2

    // Boundary: copy directly from fine grid boundaries
    // Top and bottom rows
    var j = 0
    while j <= nx_c {
        coarse[mg_idx2d(0, j, nx_c)] = fine[mg_idx2d(0, 2 * j, nx_f)]
        coarse[mg_idx2d(ny_c, j, nx_c)] = fine[mg_idx2d(ny_f, 2 * j, nx_f)]
        j = j + 1
    }
    // Left and right columns
    var i = 0
    while i <= ny_c {
        coarse[mg_idx2d(i, 0, nx_c)] = fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i, 0, nx_f)]
        coarse[mg_idx2d(i, nx_c, nx_c)] = fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i, nx_f, nx_f)]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Interior points: full-weighting stencil
    i = 1
    while i < ny_c {
        j = 1
        while j < nx_c {
            let fi = 2 * i
            let fj = 2 * j

            // Corners: weight 1/16 each
            let corners = fine[mg_idx2d(fi - 1, fj - 1, nx_f)]
                        + fine[mg_idx2d(fi - 1, fj + 1, nx_f)]
                        + fine[mg_idx2d(fi + 1, fj - 1, nx_f)]
                        + fine[mg_idx2d(fi + 1, fj + 1, nx_f)]

            // Edges: weight 1/8 each
            let edges = fine[mg_idx2d(fi, fj - 1, nx_f)]
                      + fine[mg_idx2d(fi, fj + 1, nx_f)]
                      + fine[mg_idx2d(fi - 1, fj, nx_f)]
                      + fine[mg_idx2d(fi + 1, fj, nx_f)]

            // Center: weight 1/4
            let center = fine[mg_idx2d(fi, fj, nx_f)]

            coarse[mg_idx2d(i, j, nx_c)] = corners / 16.0 + edges / 8.0 + center / 4.0

            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Bilinear interpolation prolongation from coarse to fine grid (2D).
// Coarse grid: (nx_c+1) x (ny_c+1). Fine grid: (nx_f+1) x (ny_f+1)
// where nx_f = 2*nx_c, ny_f = 2*ny_c.
fn mg_prolongate_2d(coarse: &[f64; 4096], nx_c: i32, ny_c: i32,
                    fine: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let nx_f = 2 * nx_c
    let ny_f = 2 * ny_c

    // Step 1: Inject coarse points onto coincident fine points
    var i = 0
    while i <= ny_c {
        var j = 0
        while j <= nx_c {
            fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i, 2 * j, nx_f)] = coarse[mg_idx2d(i, j, nx_c)]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 2: Interpolate along rows (horizontal midpoints)
    i = 0
    while i <= ny_c {
        var j = 0
        while j < nx_c {
            fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i, 2 * j + 1, nx_f)] = 0.5 * (
                coarse[mg_idx2d(i, j, nx_c)] + coarse[mg_idx2d(i, j + 1, nx_c)]
            )
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 3: Interpolate along columns (vertical midpoints) — these rows
    // now have all horizontal values filled from steps 1 and 2.
    i = 0
    while i < ny_c {
        var j = 0
        while j <= nx_f {
            fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i + 1, j, nx_f)] = 0.5 * (
                fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i, j, nx_f)] + fine[mg_idx2d(2 * i + 2, j, nx_f)]
            )
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Smoothers
// =============================================================================

// Weighted Jacobi smoother for 2D Poisson: -(u_xx + u_yy) = f on [0,1]^2.
// Grid: (nx+1) x (ny+1) points, hx = 1/nx, hy = 1/ny.
// Stencil:  (u[i-1,j] + u[i+1,j])/hx^2 + (u[i,j-1] + u[i,j+1])/hy^2
//           = (2/hx^2 + 2/hy^2)*u[i,j] - f[i,j]
// Jacobi update:
//   u_new = omega * [(u_L+u_R)/hx^2 + (u_D+u_U)/hy^2 + f] / (2/hx^2 + 2/hy^2)
//         + (1 - omega) * u_old
fn mg_smooth_jacobi_2d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096],
                       nx: i32, ny: i32, hx: f64, hy: f64,
                       omega: f64, nu: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let hx2 = hx * hx
    let hy2 = hy * hy
    let diag = 2.0 / hx2 + 2.0 / hy2

    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < nu {
        // Copy current solution
        var u_old: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        var k = 0
        let total = (nx + 1) * (ny + 1)
        while k < total {
            u_old[k] = u[k]
            k = k + 1
        }

        // Update interior points
        var i = 1
        while i < ny {
            var j = 1
            while j < nx {
                let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)
                let u_left  = u_old[mg_idx2d(i, j - 1, nx)]
                let u_right = u_old[mg_idx2d(i, j + 1, nx)]
                let u_down  = u_old[mg_idx2d(i - 1, j, nx)]
                let u_up    = u_old[mg_idx2d(i + 1, j, nx)]

                let stencil = (u_left + u_right) / hx2 + (u_down + u_up) / hy2
                let avg = (stencil + f[idx]) / diag
                u[idx] = omega * avg + (1.0 - omega) * u_old[idx]

                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        sweep = sweep + 1
    }
}

// Red-black Gauss-Seidel smoother for 2D Poisson.
// Red = (i+j) even, black = (i+j) odd.
// In-place update: u[i,j] = [(u_L+u_R)/hx^2 + (u_D+u_U)/hy^2 + f] / (2/hx^2 + 2/hy^2)
fn mg_smooth_gs_rb_2d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096],
                      nx: i32, ny: i32, hx: f64, hy: f64,
                      nu: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let hx2 = hx * hx
    let hy2 = hy * hy
    let diag = 2.0 / hx2 + 2.0 / hy2

    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < nu {
        // Red sweep: (i+j) even
        var i = 1
        while i < ny {
            var j = 1
            while j < nx {
                let sum_ij = i + j
                let rem = sum_ij - (sum_ij / 2) * 2
                if rem == 0 {
                    let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)
                    let u_left  = u[mg_idx2d(i, j - 1, nx)]
                    let u_right = u[mg_idx2d(i, j + 1, nx)]
                    let u_down  = u[mg_idx2d(i - 1, j, nx)]
                    let u_up    = u[mg_idx2d(i + 1, j, nx)]

                    let stencil = (u_left + u_right) / hx2 + (u_down + u_up) / hy2
                    u[idx] = (stencil + f[idx]) / diag
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Black sweep: (i+j) odd
        i = 1
        while i < ny {
            var j = 1
            while j < nx {
                let sum_ij = i + j
                let rem = sum_ij - (sum_ij / 2) * 2
                if rem == 1 {
                    let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)
                    let u_left  = u[mg_idx2d(i, j - 1, nx)]
                    let u_right = u[mg_idx2d(i, j + 1, nx)]
                    let u_down  = u[mg_idx2d(i - 1, j, nx)]
                    let u_up    = u[mg_idx2d(i + 1, j, nx)]

                    let stencil = (u_left + u_right) / hx2 + (u_down + u_up) / hy2
                    u[idx] = (stencil + f[idx]) / diag
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        sweep = sweep + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Residual
// =============================================================================

// Compute residual for 2D Poisson: -(u_xx + u_yy) = f.
// r[i,j] = f[i,j] + (u[i-1,j] - 2*u[i,j] + u[i+1,j])/hx^2
//                   + (u[i,j-1] - 2*u[i,j] + u[i,j+1])/hy^2
// Boundary residual is zero.
fn mg_residual_2d(u: &[f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096],
                  nx: i32, ny: i32, hx: f64, hy: f64,
                  r: &![f64; 4096]) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let hx2 = hx * hx
    let hy2 = hy * hy

    // Zero out boundary residual
    var j = 0
    while j <= nx {
        r[mg_idx2d(0, j, nx)] = 0.0
        r[mg_idx2d(ny, j, nx)] = 0.0
        j = j + 1
    }
    var i = 0
    while i <= ny {
        r[mg_idx2d(i, 0, nx)] = 0.0
        r[mg_idx2d(i, nx, nx)] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Interior residual
    i = 1
    while i < ny {
        j = 1
        while j < nx {
            let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)
            let u_ij = u[idx]
            let lap_x = (u[mg_idx2d(i, j - 1, nx)] - 2.0 * u_ij + u[mg_idx2d(i, j + 1, nx)]) / hx2
            let lap_y = (u[mg_idx2d(i - 1, j, nx)] - 2.0 * u_ij + u[mg_idx2d(i + 1, j, nx)]) / hy2

            r[idx] = f[idx] + lap_x + lap_y
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// L2 norm of the 2D residual:
// ||r||_2 = sqrt(hx*hy * sum_{interior} r[i,j]^2)
fn mg_residual_norm_2d(r: &[f64; 4096], nx: i32, ny: i32,
                       hx: f64, hy: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i < ny {
        var j = 1
        while j < nx {
            let val = r[mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)]
            sum = sum + val * val
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    mg_sqrt(hx * hy * sum)
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Coarse Solve
// =============================================================================

// Direct solve on the coarsest 2D grid via damped Jacobi iteration.
// For small grids (e.g. 2x2 or 4x4), convergence is rapid.
// Iterates until residual < 1e-12 or max 500 iterations.
fn mg_coarse_solve_2d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096],
                      nx: i32, ny: i32,
                      hx: f64, hy: f64) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let hx2 = hx * hx
    let hy2 = hy * hy
    let diag = 2.0 / hx2 + 2.0 / hy2
    let tol_coarse = 1.0e-12

    var iter = 0
    while iter < 500 {
        // Jacobi sweep with omega = 1.0 (no damping on tiny grid)
        var u_old: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        let total = (nx + 1) * (ny + 1)
        var k = 0
        while k < total {
            u_old[k] = u[k]
            k = k + 1
        }

        var i = 1
        while i < ny {
            var j = 1
            while j < nx {
                let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)
                let u_left  = u_old[mg_idx2d(i, j - 1, nx)]
                let u_right = u_old[mg_idx2d(i, j + 1, nx)]
                let u_down  = u_old[mg_idx2d(i - 1, j, nx)]
                let u_up    = u_old[mg_idx2d(i + 1, j, nx)]

                let stencil = (u_left + u_right) / hx2 + (u_down + u_up) / hy2
                u[idx] = (stencil + f[idx]) / diag
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Check convergence
        var r: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        mg_residual_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy, &!r)
        let rnorm = mg_residual_norm_2d(&r, nx, ny, hx, hy)
        if rnorm < tol_coarse { return }

        iter = iter + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D V-Cycle
// =============================================================================

// Recursive V-cycle for 2D Poisson on an (nx+1) x (ny+1) grid.
// Uses red-black Gauss-Seidel for smoothing.
//   1. Pre-smooth nu1 sweeps
//   2. Compute residual
//   3. Restrict residual to coarse grid
//   4. If coarsest level, direct solve; else recurse
//   5. Prolongate correction, add to u
//   6. Post-smooth nu2 sweeps
fn mg_vcycle_2d(u: &![f64; 4096], f: &[f64; 4096],
                nx: i32, ny: i32, hx: f64, hy: f64,
                config: &MGConfig, level: i32) with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Base case: coarsest level or grid too small
    if level >= config.n_levels - 1 {
        mg_coarse_solve_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy)
        return
    }
    if nx <= 2 {
        mg_coarse_solve_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy)
        return
    }
    if ny <= 2 {
        mg_coarse_solve_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy)
        return
    }

    // 1. Pre-smoothing
    mg_smooth_gs_rb_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy, config.nu1)

    // 2. Compute residual on fine grid
    var r_fine: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_residual_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy, &!r_fine)

    // 3. Restrict residual to coarse grid
    let nx_c = nx / 2
    let ny_c = ny / 2
    var r_coarse: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_restrict_2d(&r_fine, nx, ny, &!r_coarse)

    // 4. Solve for correction on coarse grid: A_c * e = r_coarse
    var e_coarse: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let hx_c = 2.0 * hx
    let hy_c = 2.0 * hy
    mg_vcycle_2d(&!e_coarse, &r_coarse, nx_c, ny_c, hx_c, hy_c, config, level + 1)

    // 5. Prolongate correction to fine grid and add
    var e_fine: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    mg_prolongate_2d(&e_coarse, nx_c, ny_c, &!e_fine)

    var i = 1
    while i < ny {
        var j = 1
        while j < nx {
            let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)
            u[idx] = u[idx] + e_fine[idx]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // 6. Post-smoothing
    mg_smooth_gs_rb_2d(u, f, nx, ny, hx, hy, config.nu2)
}

// =============================================================================
// 2D Full Multigrid Solver
// =============================================================================

// Solve -(u_xx + u_yy) = f_rhs(x, y) on [0,1]x[0,1] with u = 0 on boundary.
// nx, ny are the number of intervals in each direction (must be powers of 2).
// Iterates V-cycles until the residual norm drops below config.tol or
// max_cycles is reached.
fn mg_solve_poisson_2d(f_rhs: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       nx: i32, ny: i32, config: &MGConfig,
                       result: &!MGResult) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let hx = 1.0 / (nx as f64)
    let hy = 1.0 / (ny as f64)

    // Initialize solution to zero
    let total = (nx + 1) * (ny + 1)
    var k = 0
    while k < total {
        result.u[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Set up RHS on interior grid points
    var f_vals: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i <= ny {
        var j = 0
        while j <= nx {
            let x = (j as f64) * hx
            let y = (i as f64) * hy
            let idx = mg_idx2d(i, j, nx)

            // Interior only; boundary RHS is zero
            if i > 0 {
                if i < ny {
                    if j > 0 {
                        if j < nx {
                            f_vals[idx] = f_rhs(x, y)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Iterate V-cycles
    result.converged = false
    result.iterations = 0

    var cycle = 0
    while cycle < config.max_cycles {
        mg_vcycle_2d(&!result.u, &f_vals, nx, ny, hx, hy, config, 0)

        // Compute residual norm
        var r: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        mg_residual_2d(&result.u, &f_vals, nx, ny, hx, hy, &!r)
        let rnorm = mg_residual_norm_2d(&r, nx, ny, hx, hy)

        result.residual_norm = rnorm
        result.iterations = cycle + 1

        if rnorm < config.tol {
            result.converged = true
            return
        }
        cycle = cycle + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Convergence Analysis
// =============================================================================

// Compute the average convergence factor from a sequence of residual norms.
// Given residuals[0..n-1], returns the geometric mean of
//   residuals[k+1] / residuals[k] for k = 0..n-2.
// A value near 0.1 indicates rapid convergence; near 1.0 indicates stalling.
fn mg_convergence_factor(residuals: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if n < 2 { return 0.0 }

    // Compute product of ratios, then take (n-1)-th root.
    // To avoid overflow/underflow, compute via log of the ratio sum.
    // log(geometric mean) = (1/(n-1)) * sum log(r[k+1]/r[k])
    //                     = (1/(n-1)) * (log(r[n-1]) - log(r[0]))
    // But we don't have log. Instead compute the product directly
    // and iteratively take roots.

    // Simple approach: average of individual ratios (arithmetic mean of ratios).
    // This is a practical approximation for the convergence factor.
    var sum_ratio = 0.0
    var count = 0
    var k = 0
    while k < n - 1 {
        if mg_abs(residuals[k]) > 1.0e-30 {
            let ratio = residuals[k + 1] / residuals[k]
            sum_ratio = sum_ratio + ratio
            count = count + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }

    if count == 0 { return 0.0 }
    sum_ratio / (count as f64)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/math/number_theory.sio ===
// stdlib/math/number_theory.sio — Number theory functions
//
// Pure Sounio implementations of fundamental number-theoretic algorithms:
//   GCD/LCM (Euclidean), extended GCD, modular arithmetic, primality
//   testing (trial division + Miller-Rabin), factorization (trial + Pollard rho),
//   Euler totient, Möbius function, Jacobi symbol, Chinese Remainder Theorem,
//   Fibonacci/Lucas via matrix doubling.
//
// All functions are pure Sounio — zero FFI.
//
// References:
//   Hardy & Wright (2008): "An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers" (6th ed.)
//   Crandall & Pomerance (2005): "Prime Numbers: A Computational Perspective"
//   Knuth (1997): "The Art of Computer Programming" Vol. 2
//   Cohen (1993): "A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory"

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn nt_abs(x: i64) -> i64 {
    if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
}

// =============================================================================
// GCD / LCM
// =============================================================================

// Greatest common divisor via Euclidean algorithm.
// gcd(a, b) >= 0 always. gcd(0, 0) = 0.
fn gcd(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = nt_abs(a)
    var y = nt_abs(b)
    while y > 0 {
        let t = y
        y = x - (x / y) * y
        x = t
    }
    x
}

// Least common multiple. lcm(a, 0) = 0.
fn lcm(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if a == 0 || b == 0 { return 0 }
    let g = gcd(a, b)
    nt_abs(a) / g * nt_abs(b)
}

// Extended Euclidean algorithm.
// Returns (g, x, y) such that a*x + b*y = g = gcd(a, b).
// Result stored in output array: [gcd, x, y].
fn gcd_extended(a: i64, b: i64, result: &![i64; 3]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if b == 0 {
        result[0] = nt_abs(a)
        result[1] = if a >= 0 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
        result[2] = 0
        return
    }
    var old_r = nt_abs(a)
    var r = nt_abs(b)
    var old_s: i64 = 1
    var s: i64 = 0
    var old_t: i64 = 0
    var t: i64 = 1

    while r > 0 {
        let q = old_r / r
        let temp_r = r
        r = old_r - q * r
        old_r = temp_r
        let temp_s = s
        s = old_s - q * s
        old_s = temp_s
        let temp_t = t
        t = old_t - q * t
        old_t = temp_t
    }

    result[0] = old_r
    // Adjust signs for original a, b
    if a < 0 { old_s = 0 - old_s }
    if b < 0 { old_t = 0 - old_t }
    result[1] = old_s
    result[2] = old_t
}

// =============================================================================
// Modular arithmetic
// =============================================================================

// Modular exponentiation: base^exp mod modulus.
// Uses binary (right-to-left) exponentiation. O(log exp).
// Requires modulus > 0, exp >= 0.
fn mod_pow(base: i64, exp: i64, modulus: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if modulus == 1 { return 0 }
    var result: i64 = 1
    var b = base - (base / modulus) * modulus
    if b < 0 { b = b + modulus }
    var e = exp

    while e > 0 {
        // If e is odd
        if e - (e / 2) * 2 == 1 {
            result = result * b
            result = result - (result / modulus) * modulus
        }
        e = e / 2
        b = b * b
        b = b - (b / modulus) * modulus
    }
    result
}

// Modular inverse: a^{-1} mod m.
// Returns x such that a*x ≡ 1 (mod m), or 0 if gcd(a, m) != 1.
fn mod_inv(a: i64, m: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result: [i64; 3] = [0; 3]
    gcd_extended(a, m, &!result)
    if result[0] != 1 { return 0 }
    var x = result[1]
    // Ensure positive
    x = x - (x / m) * m
    if x < 0 { x = x + m }
    x
}

// =============================================================================
// Primality testing
// =============================================================================

// Trial division up to sqrt(n). Sufficient for n < ~10^14 in practice.
fn is_prime_trial(n: i64) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 2 { return false }
    if n < 4 { return true }
    if n - (n / 2) * 2 == 0 { return false }
