// === FILE: stdlib/mem/arc.sio ===
// stdlib/mem/arc.sio
// Atomic reference counting simulation using fixed arrays
//
// Since Sounio has no heap allocation or generics,
// this provides a slot-based ARC pool for i64 values.

// ARC pool: fixed slots for reference-counted values
// Each slot has: value, strong_count, weak_count
struct ArcPool {
    values: [i64; 64],
    strong: [i64; 64],
    weak: [i64; 64],
    next_free: i64,
}

fn arc_pool_new() -> ArcPool {
    ArcPool {
        values: [0; 64],
        strong: [0; 64],
        weak: [0; 64],
        next_free: 0,
    }
}

// Allocate a new arc slot, returns slot index (-1 if full)
fn arc_new(pool: &!ArcPool, value: i64) -> i64 {
    let idx = pool.next_free
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 - 1 }
    pool.values[idx] = value
    pool.strong[idx] = 1
    pool.weak[idx] = 0
    pool.next_free = idx + 1
    return idx
}

// Clone (increment strong count)
fn arc_clone(pool: &!ArcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return idx }
    if idx >= 64 { return idx }
    pool.strong[idx] = pool.strong[idx] + 1
    return idx
}

// Drop (decrement strong count), returns 1 if value was freed
fn arc_drop(pool: &!ArcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    pool.strong[idx] = pool.strong[idx] - 1
    if pool.strong[idx] == 0 {
        pool.values[idx] = 0
        return 1
    }
    return 0
}

// Get value
fn arc_get(pool: ArcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    return pool.values[idx]
}

// Get strong count
fn arc_strong_count(pool: ArcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    return pool.strong[idx]
}


// === FILE: stdlib/mem/arena.sio ===
//! Arena allocator (bump allocator)
//!
//! Arena provides fast O(1) allocation with no individual deallocation.
//! All memory is freed at once when the arena is dropped or reset.
//!
//! Functions:
//! - arena_new() -> Arena
//! - arena_with_chunk_size(size) -> Arena
//! - arena_alloc_raw(&!arena, size, align) -> *mut u8
//! - arena_alloc_bytes(&!arena, count) -> *mut u8
//! - arena_reset(&!arena)
//! - arena_drop(&!arena)
//! - arena_allocated_bytes(&arena) -> usize
//! - arena_chunk_size(&arena) -> usize
//! - arena_available(&arena) -> usize
//! - arena_is_empty(&arena) -> bool

extern "C" {
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

// Default chunk size (64 KB)
const DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE: usize = 65536

// A bump allocator that allocates memory in contiguous chunks.
pub struct Arena {
    base: *mut u8,
    chunk_size: usize,
    offset: usize,
    total_allocated: usize,
}

// Creates a new arena with default chunk size (64 KB).
pub fn arena_new() -> Arena with Alloc {
    let result = arena_with_chunk_size(DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE)
    return result
}

// Creates a new arena with the specified chunk size.
pub fn arena_with_chunk_size(chunk_size: usize) -> Arena with Alloc {
    let base = malloc(chunk_size)
    let result = Arena {
        base: base,
        chunk_size: chunk_size,
        offset: 0,
        total_allocated: 0,
    }
    return result
}

// Allocates raw bytes with the specified size and alignment.
// Returns a pointer to the allocated memory, or null if allocation fails.
pub fn arena_alloc_raw(arena: &!Arena, size: usize, align: usize) -> *mut u8 with Alloc, Mut {
    let aligned_offset = (arena.offset + align - 1) & !(align - 1)

    if aligned_offset + size <= arena.chunk_size {
        // Compute pointer using integer arithmetic
        let base_addr = arena.base as usize
        let ptr_addr = base_addr + aligned_offset
        let ptr = ptr_addr as *mut u8
        arena.offset = aligned_offset + size
        arena.total_allocated = arena.total_allocated + size
        return ptr
    }

    let null = null_mut()
    return null
}

// Allocates an array of bytes in the arena.
pub fn arena_alloc_bytes(arena: &!Arena, count: usize) -> *mut u8 with Alloc, Mut {
    let ptr = arena_alloc_raw(arena, count, 1)
    return ptr
}

// Resets the arena, making all memory available for reuse.
pub fn arena_reset(arena: &!Arena) with Mut {
    arena.offset = 0
    arena.total_allocated = 0
}

// Returns the total number of bytes allocated from this arena.
pub fn arena_allocated_bytes(arena: &Arena) -> usize {
    return arena.total_allocated
}

// Returns the chunk size used by this arena.
pub fn arena_chunk_size(arena: &Arena) -> usize {
    return arena.chunk_size
}

// Returns the remaining bytes available in the current chunk.
pub fn arena_available(arena: &Arena) -> usize {
    return arena.chunk_size - arena.offset
}

// Returns true if the arena is empty (no allocations since last reset).
pub fn arena_is_empty(arena: &Arena) -> bool {
    return arena.total_allocated == 0
}

// Frees all memory associated with the arena.
pub fn arena_drop(arena: &!Arena) with Alloc, Mut {
    if arena.base != null_mut() {
        free(arena.base)
        arena.base = null_mut()
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/mem/box.sio ===
// stdlib/mem/box — Heap allocation wrappers via C FFI
//
// Provides alloc/dealloc functions for heap memory management.
// Uses libc malloc/free underneath.

extern "C" {
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn calloc(nmemb: usize, size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn realloc(ptr: *mut u8, size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

// Allocate n bytes of heap memory, zero-initialized.
fn heap_alloc(n: i64) -> *mut u8 with Alloc {
    let size = n as usize
    let ptr = calloc(1 as usize, size)
    ptr
}

// Reallocate a heap block to a new size.
fn heap_realloc(ptr: *mut u8, new_size: i64) -> *mut u8 with Alloc {
    let size = new_size as usize
    let new_ptr = realloc(ptr, size)
    new_ptr
}

// Free a heap-allocated block.
fn heap_free(ptr: *mut u8) with Alloc {
    free(ptr)
}

// Interior mutability primitives
//
// Cell: get/set through shared reference (simulated with &! pass pattern)
// Since Sounio has no interior mutability at the language level,
// we model Cell as a struct with explicit get/set functions.

struct CellI64 {

}

fn cell_new(value: i64) -> CellI64 {
    CellI64 { value: value }
}

fn cell_get(c: CellI64) -> i64 {
    return c.value
}

fn cell_set(c: &!CellI64, value: i64) {
    c.value = value
}

fn cell_replace(c: &!CellI64, value: i64) -> i64 {
    let old = c.value
    c.value = value
    return old
}

fn cell_swap(a: &!CellI64, b: &!CellI64) {
    let tmp = a.value
    a.value = b.value
    b.value = tmp
}

fn cell_f64_get(c: CellF64) -> f64 {

}

    c.value = value
    return old
}

// === FILE: stdlib/mem/pool.sio ===
//! Object pool allocator
//!
//! Pool provides efficient allocation and deallocation of fixed-size objects.
//! All objects in a pool have the same size, enabling O(1) allocation and
//! deallocation with minimal fragmentation.
//!
//! Ideal for:
//! - Frequently allocated/deallocated objects of the same type
//! - Game entities, network connections, database records
//! - Any scenario with high allocation churn
//!
//! Functions:
//! - pool_new(slot_size, capacity) -> Pool
//! - pool_with_default_capacity(slot_size) -> Pool
//! - pool_alloc(&!pool) -> *mut u8
//! - pool_free(&!pool, ptr)
//! - pool_reset(&!pool)
//! - pool_drop(&!pool)
//! - pool_allocated(&pool) -> usize
//! - pool_capacity(&pool) -> usize
//! - pool_available(&pool) -> usize
//! - pool_slot_size(&pool) -> usize
//! - pool_is_empty(&pool) -> bool
//! - pool_is_full(&pool) -> bool

extern "C" {
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

// Default pool capacity (256 objects)
const DEFAULT_POOL_CAPACITY: usize = 256

// Minimum slot size (must hold a pointer for the free list)
const MIN_SLOT_SIZE: usize = 8

// A fixed-size object pool allocator with free list.
pub struct Pool {
    base: *mut u8,
    slot_size: usize,
    capacity: usize,
    free_head: *mut u8,
    allocated: usize,
}

// Creates a new pool with the specified slot size and capacity.
// The slot_size is automatically bumped to at least 8 bytes.
pub fn pool_new(slot_size: usize, capacity: usize) -> Pool with Mut, Alloc, Div, Panic {
    // Ensure slot size can hold a pointer
    let actual_slot_size = if slot_size < MIN_SLOT_SIZE { MIN_SLOT_SIZE } else { slot_size }

    let total_size = actual_slot_size * capacity
    let base = malloc(total_size)

    // Initialize free list: each slot stores address of next free slot
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < capacity - 1 {
        let current_addr = (base as usize) + (i * actual_slot_size)
        let next_addr = (base as usize) + ((i + 1) * actual_slot_size)
        // Store next slot address at current slot
        let current_ptr = current_addr as *mut i64
        current_ptr[0] = next_addr as i64
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Last slot has null (0) as next pointer
    let last_addr = (base as usize) + ((capacity - 1) * actual_slot_size)
    let last_ptr = last_addr as *mut i64
    last_ptr[0] = 0

    let result = Pool {
        base: base,
        slot_size: actual_slot_size,
        capacity: capacity,
        free_head: base,
        allocated: 0,
    }
    return result
}

// Creates a new pool with default capacity (256 slots).
pub fn pool_with_default_capacity(slot_size: usize) -> Pool with Mut, Alloc, Div, Panic {
    let result = pool_new(slot_size, DEFAULT_POOL_CAPACITY)
    return result
}

// Allocates a slot from the pool.
// Returns a pointer to the allocated slot, or null if the pool is exhausted.
pub fn pool_alloc(pool: &!Pool) -> *mut u8 with Mut, Panic {
    if pool.free_head == null_mut() {
        let null = null_mut()
        return null
    }

    let result = pool.free_head
    // Read next free slot address from current slot
    let slot_ptr = result as *mut i64
    let next_addr = slot_ptr[0] as usize
    pool.free_head = next_addr as *mut u8
    pool.allocated = pool.allocated + 1
    return result
}

// Frees a slot back to the pool.
pub fn pool_free(pool: &!Pool, ptr: *mut u8) with Mut, Panic {
    // Store current free_head at the slot being freed
    let slot_ptr = ptr as *mut i64
    slot_ptr[0] = pool.free_head as i64
    pool.free_head = ptr
    pool.allocated = pool.allocated - 1
}

// Returns the number of objects currently allocated.
pub fn pool_allocated(pool: &Pool) -> usize {
    return pool.allocated
}

// Returns the total capacity of the pool.
pub fn pool_capacity(pool: &Pool) -> usize {
    return pool.capacity
}

// Returns the number of free slots available.
pub fn pool_available(pool: &Pool) -> usize {
    return pool.capacity - pool.allocated
}

// Returns the size of each slot.
pub fn pool_slot_size(pool: &Pool) -> usize {
    return pool.slot_size
}

// Returns true if the pool has no allocated objects.
pub fn pool_is_empty(pool: &Pool) -> bool {
    return pool.allocated == 0
}

// Returns true if all slots are allocated.
pub fn pool_is_full(pool: &Pool) -> bool {
    return pool.free_head == null_mut()
}

// Resets the pool, returning all slots to the free list.
pub fn pool_reset(pool: &!Pool) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Rebuild the free list
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < pool.capacity - 1 {
        let current_addr = (pool.base as usize) + (i * pool.slot_size)
        let next_addr = (pool.base as usize) + ((i + 1) * pool.slot_size)
        let current_ptr = current_addr as *mut i64
        current_ptr[0] = next_addr as i64
        i = i + 1
    }

    let last_addr = (pool.base as usize) + ((pool.capacity - 1) * pool.slot_size)
    let last_ptr = last_addr as *mut i64
    last_ptr[0] = 0

    pool.free_head = pool.base
    pool.allocated = 0
}

// Frees all memory associated with the pool.
pub fn pool_drop(pool: &!Pool) with Mut, Alloc {
    if pool.base != null_mut() {
        free(pool.base)
        pool.base = null_mut()
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/mem/rc.sio ===
// stdlib/mem/rc.sio
// Single-threaded reference counting using fixed slot pool
//
// Rc pool for i64 values with strong/weak counts.

struct RcPool {
    values: [i64; 64],
    strong: [i64; 64],
    weak: [i64; 64],
    next_free: i64,
}

fn rc_pool_new() -> RcPool {
    RcPool {
        values: [0; 64],
        strong: [0; 64],
        weak: [0; 64],
        next_free: 0,
    }
}

fn rc_new(pool: &!RcPool, value: i64) -> i64 {
    let idx = pool.next_free
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 - 1 }
    pool.values[idx] = value
    pool.strong[idx] = 1
    pool.weak[idx] = 0
    pool.next_free = idx + 1
    return idx
}

fn rc_clone(pool: &!RcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return idx }
    if idx >= 64 { return idx }
    pool.strong[idx] = pool.strong[idx] + 1
    return idx
}

fn rc_drop(pool: &!RcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    pool.strong[idx] = pool.strong[idx] - 1
    if pool.strong[idx] == 0 {
        pool.values[idx] = 0
        return 1
    }
    return 0
}

fn rc_get(pool: RcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    return pool.values[idx]
}

fn rc_strong_count(pool: RcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    return pool.strong[idx]
}

fn rc_downgrade(pool: &!RcPool, idx: i64) {
    if idx < 0 { return }
    if idx >= 64 { return }
    pool.weak[idx] = pool.weak[idx] + 1
}

fn rc_weak_count(pool: RcPool, idx: i64) -> i64 {
    if idx < 0 { return 0 }
    if idx >= 64 { return 0 }
    return pool.weak[idx]
}


// === FILE: stdlib/mem/stack.sio ===
//! Stack allocator (LIFO allocator)
//!
//! Stack provides fast LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) allocation where
//! deallocations must occur in reverse order of allocations.
//!
//! Ideal for:
//! - Function-scoped temporary allocations
//! - Recursive algorithms with bounded memory
//! - Any scenario with strictly nested lifetimes
//!
//! Functions:
//! - stack_new() -> Stack
//! - stack_with_size(size) -> Stack
//! - stack_marker(&stack) -> StackMarker
//! - stack_alloc_raw(&!stack, size, align) -> *mut u8
//! - stack_alloc_bytes(&!stack, count) -> *mut u8
//! - stack_reset_to(&!stack, marker)
//! - stack_reset(&!stack)
//! - stack_drop(&!stack)
//! - stack_used(&stack) -> usize
//! - stack_size(&stack) -> usize
//! - stack_available(&stack) -> usize
//! - stack_high_water_mark(&stack) -> usize
//! - stack_is_empty(&stack) -> bool
//! - stack_is_full(&stack) -> bool

extern "C" {
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

// Default stack size (1 MB)
const DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE: usize = 1048576

// Marker for stack allocation positions.
// Used to reset the stack to a previous state.
pub struct StackMarker {
    offset: usize,
}

// Returns the byte offset this marker represents.
pub fn marker_offset(marker: &StackMarker) -> usize {
    return marker.offset
}

// A LIFO stack allocator.
pub struct Stack {
    base: *mut u8,
    size: usize,
    offset: usize,
    high_water: usize,
}

// Creates a new stack allocator with default size (1 MB).
pub fn stack_new() -> Stack with Alloc {
    let result = stack_with_size(DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE)
    return result
}

// Creates a new stack allocator with the specified size.
pub fn stack_with_size(size: usize) -> Stack with Alloc {
    let base = malloc(size)
    let result = Stack {
        base: base,
        size: size,
        offset: 0,
        high_water: 0,
    }
    return result
}

// Returns a marker for the current stack position.
pub fn stack_marker(stack: &Stack) -> StackMarker {
    let result = StackMarker { offset: stack.offset }
    return result
}

// Allocates raw bytes with the specified size and alignment.
// Returns a pointer to the allocated memory, or null if out of space.
pub fn stack_alloc_raw(stack: &!Stack, size: usize, align: usize) -> *mut u8 with Mut {
    // Calculate aligned offset
    let aligned = (stack.offset + align - 1) & !(align - 1)
    let new_offset = aligned + size

    if new_offset > stack.size {
        let null = null_mut()
        return null
    }

    stack.offset = new_offset

    // Update high water mark
    if new_offset > stack.high_water {
        stack.high_water = new_offset
    }

    // Compute pointer using integer arithmetic
    let base_addr = stack.base as usize
    let ptr_addr = base_addr + aligned
    let ptr = ptr_addr as *mut u8
    return ptr
}

// Allocates an array of bytes on the stack.
pub fn stack_alloc_bytes(stack: &!Stack, count: usize) -> *mut u8 with Mut {
    let ptr = stack_alloc_raw(stack, count, 1)
    return ptr
}

// Resets the stack to a previous marker position.
pub fn stack_reset_to(stack: &!Stack, marker: StackMarker) with Mut {
    stack.offset = marker.offset
}

// Resets the stack to empty, freeing all allocations.
pub fn stack_reset(stack: &!Stack) with Mut {
    stack.offset = 0
}

// Returns the current amount of memory used (in bytes).
pub fn stack_used(stack: &Stack) -> usize {
    return stack.offset
}

// Returns the total size of the stack (in bytes).
pub fn stack_size(stack: &Stack) -> usize {
    return stack.size
}

// Returns the remaining available space (in bytes).
pub fn stack_available(stack: &Stack) -> usize {
    return stack.size - stack.offset
}

// Returns the high water mark (maximum bytes ever used).
pub fn stack_high_water_mark(stack: &Stack) -> usize {
    return stack.high_water
}

// Returns true if the stack is empty.
pub fn stack_is_empty(stack: &Stack) -> bool {
    return stack.offset == 0
}

// Returns true if the stack is full.
pub fn stack_is_full(stack: &Stack) -> bool {
    return stack.offset == stack.size
}

// Frees all memory associated with the stack.
pub fn stack_drop(stack: &!Stack) with Alloc, Mut {
    if stack.base != null_mut() {
        free(stack.base)
        stack.base = null_mut()
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/autodiff.sio ===
// autodiff.d - Automatic Differentiation for Machine Learning in Sounio
//
// Comprehensive automatic differentiation (AD) system designed specifically for
// neural network training and optimization. Combines forward-mode AD (dual numbers)
// with reverse-mode AD (tape-based backpropagation) for efficient gradient computation.
//
// Key Features:
//   1. Dual Numbers: Forward-mode AD for functions with few inputs
//   2. Tape-based Reverse AD: Efficient backpropagation for ML (R^n -> R)
//   3. Epistemic Derivative Tracking: Uncertainty quantification in gradients
//   4. Vector Jacobian Products (VJP): Essential for backprop through layers
//   5. Numerical Derivative Verification: Testing and debugging
//
// Mathematical Foundation:
//   Forward Mode:  Computes J·v (Jacobian-vector product) efficiently
//   Reverse Mode:  Computes v^T·J (vector-Jacobian product) - ideal for ML
//
//   For loss L(θ) where θ ∈ R^n, reverse mode computes ∇L in O(1) backward pass
//   versus O(n) forward passes, making it essential for high-dimensional optimization.
//
// References:
//   - Baydin et al., "Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning", JMLR 2018
//   - Griewank & Walther, "Evaluating Derivatives", SIAM 2008
//   - Goodfellow et al., "Deep Learning", MIT Press 2016 (Chapter 6)

// ============================================================================
// MATHEMATICAL HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 11.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 12.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 13.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 14.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 15.0
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn log_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    var val = x
    var k = 0.0
    let e = 2.718281828459045
    while val > e {
        val = val / e
        k = k + 1.0
    }
    while val < 1.0 / e {
        val = val * e
        k = k - 1.0
    }
    let u = (val - 1.0) / (val + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var sum = u
    var term = u
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 3.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 5.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 7.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 9.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 11.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 13.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 15.0
    term = term * u2
    sum = sum + term / 17.0
    return 2.0 * sum + k
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = y
    var term = y
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (2.0 * 3.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (4.0 * 5.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (6.0 * 7.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (8.0 * 9.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (10.0 * 11.0)
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var y = x
    while y > pi { y = y - 2.0 * pi }
    while y < 0.0 - pi { y = y + 2.0 * pi }
    let x2 = y * y
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (1.0 * 2.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (3.0 * 4.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (5.0 * 6.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (7.0 * 8.0)
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * (0.0 - x2) / (9.0 * 10.0)
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn tanh_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2x = exp_f64(2.0 * x)
    return (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// PART 1: DUAL NUMBERS (FORWARD MODE AD)
// ============================================================================
// Dual numbers: a + b·ε where ε² = 0
// Enables automatic derivative computation via chain rule

struct Dual {
    value: f64,
    derivative: f64
}

// Create dual number with explicit value and derivative
fn dual_new(value: f64, derivative: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { value: value, derivative: derivative }
}

// Create constant (derivative = 0)
fn dual_constant(value: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { value: value, derivative: 0.0 }
}

// Create variable (derivative = 1)
fn dual_variable(value: f64) -> Dual {
    return Dual { value: value, derivative: 1.0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL ARITHMETIC OPERATIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dual_add(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        value: a.value + b.value,
        derivative: a.derivative + b.derivative
    }
}

fn dual_sub(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        value: a.value - b.value,
        derivative: a.derivative - b.derivative
    }
}

fn dual_mul(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    // Product rule: (f·g)' = f'·g + f·g'
    return Dual {
        value: a.value * b.value,
        derivative: a.derivative * b.value + a.value * b.derivative
    }
}

fn dual_div(a: Dual, b: Dual) -> Dual {
    // Quotient rule: (f/g)' = (f'·g - f·g') / g²
    let g2 = b.value * b.value
    return Dual {
        value: a.value / b.value,
        derivative: (a.derivative * b.value - a.value * b.derivative) / g2
    }
}

fn dual_neg(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    return Dual {
        value: 0.0 - d.value,
        derivative: 0.0 - d.derivative
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL MATHEMATICAL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dual_exp(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx exp(x) = exp(x)
    let e = exp_f64(d.value)
    return Dual { value: e, derivative: d.derivative * e }
}

fn dual_log(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx log(x) = 1/x
    return Dual {
        value: log_f64(d.value),
        derivative: d.derivative / d.value
    }
}

fn dual_sin(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx sin(x) = cos(x)
    return Dual {
        value: sin_f64(d.value),
        derivative: d.derivative * cos_f64(d.value)
    }
}

fn dual_cos(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx cos(x) = -sin(x)
    return Dual {
        value: cos_f64(d.value),
        derivative: 0.0 - d.derivative * sin_f64(d.value)
    }
}

fn dual_tanh(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx tanh(x) = 1 - tanh²(x)
    let t = tanh_f64(d.value)
    return Dual {
        value: t,
        derivative: d.derivative * (1.0 - t * t)
    }
}

fn dual_pow(d: Dual, p: f64) -> Dual {
    // d/dx x^p = p·x^(p-1)
    let v = exp_f64(p * log_f64(d.value))
    let dv = p * exp_f64((p - 1.0) * log_f64(d.value))
    return Dual { value: v, derivative: d.derivative * dv }
}

fn dual_sqrt(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // d/dx sqrt(x) = 1/(2·sqrt(x))
    let v = sqrt_f64(d.value)
    return Dual {
        value: v,
        derivative: d.derivative / (2.0 * v)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// DUAL NEURAL NETWORK ACTIVATIONS
// ============================================================================

fn dual_relu(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // ReLU(x) = max(0, x)
    // d/dx ReLU(x) = 1 if x > 0, else 0
    if d.value > 0.0 {
        return Dual { value: d.value, derivative: d.derivative }
    }
    return Dual { value: 0.0, derivative: 0.0 }
}

fn dual_sigmoid(d: Dual) -> Dual {
    // sigmoid(x) = 1/(1 + exp(-x))
    // d/dx sigmoid(x) = sigmoid(x)·(1 - sigmoid(x))
    let s = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - d.value))
    return Dual {
        value: s,
        derivative: d.derivative * s * (1.0 - s)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PART 2: TAPE-BASED REVERSE MODE AD
// ============================================================================
// Efficient for R^n -> R (many inputs, one output) - ideal for ML loss functions

// Maximum tape size for computational graph
fn max_tape_entries() -> i64 { return 50 }

// Operation type codes
fn op_const() -> i64 { return 0 }
fn op_var() -> i64 { return 1 }
fn op_add() -> i64 { return 2 }
fn op_mul() -> i64 { return 3 }
fn op_exp() -> i64 { return 4 }
fn op_log() -> i64 { return 5 }
fn op_sin() -> i64 { return 6 }
fn op_tanh() -> i64 { return 7 }
fn op_relu() -> i64 { return 8 }
fn op_sigmoid() -> i64 { return 9 }

// Tape entry: records one operation in computational graph
struct TapeEntry {
    op_type: i64,       // Operation type
    input1_idx: i64,    // Index of first input (-1 if none)
    input2_idx: i64,    // Index of second input (-1 if unary)
    output_idx: i64     // Index where output is stored in values array
}

// Fixed-size gradient tape
struct ADTape {
    // Values array (forward pass results)
    v0: f64, v1: f64, v2: f64, v3: f64, v4: f64, v5: f64, v6: f64, v7: f64, v8: f64, v9: f64,
    v10: f64, v11: f64, v12: f64, v13: f64, v14: f64, v15: f64, v16: f64, v17: f64, v18: f64, v19: f64,

    v30: f64, v31: f64, v32: f64, v33: f64, v34: f64, v35: f64, v36: f64, v37: f64, v38: f64, v39: f64,
    v40: f64, v41: f64, v42: f64, v43: f64, v44: f64, v45: f64, v46: f64, v47: f64, v48: f64, v49: f64,

    // Derivative array (backward pass results)
    g0: f64, g1: f64, g2: f64, g3: f64, g4: f64, g5: f64, g6: f64, g7: f64, g8: f64, g9: f64,
    g10: f64, g11: f64, g12: f64, g13: f64, g14: f64, g15: f64, g16: f64, g17: f64, g18: f64, g19: f64,
    g20: f64, g21: f64, g22: f64, g23: f64, g24: f64, g25: f64, g26: f64, g27: f64, g28: f64, g29: f64,
    g30: f64, g31: f64, g32: f64, g33: f64, g34: f64, g35: f64, g36: f64, g37: f64, g38: f64, g39: f64,
    g40: f64, g41: f64, g42: f64, g43: f64, g44: f64, g45: f64, g46: f64, g47: f64, g48: f64, g49: f64,

    // Entries array (operation log)
    e0: TapeEntry, e1: TapeEntry, e2: TapeEntry, e3: TapeEntry, e4: TapeEntry,
    e5: TapeEntry, e6: TapeEntry, e7: TapeEntry, e8: TapeEntry, e9: TapeEntry,
    e10: TapeEntry, e11: TapeEntry, e12: TapeEntry, e13: TapeEntry, e14: TapeEntry,
    e15: TapeEntry, e16: TapeEntry, e17: TapeEntry, e18: TapeEntry, e19: TapeEntry,
    e20: TapeEntry, e21: TapeEntry, e22: TapeEntry, e23: TapeEntry, e24: TapeEntry,
    e25: TapeEntry, e26: TapeEntry, e27: TapeEntry, e28: TapeEntry, e29: TapeEntry,
    e30: TapeEntry, e31: TapeEntry, e32: TapeEntry, e33: TapeEntry, e34: TapeEntry,
    e35: TapeEntry, e36: TapeEntry, e37: TapeEntry, e38: TapeEntry, e39: TapeEntry,
    e40: TapeEntry, e41: TapeEntry, e42: TapeEntry, e43: TapeEntry, e44: TapeEntry,
    e45: TapeEntry, e46: TapeEntry, e47: TapeEntry, e48: TapeEntry, e49: TapeEntry,

    n_entries: i64,
    n_values: i64
}

// Value tracked on tape
struct TrackedValue {
    value: f64,
    tape_idx: i64
}

fn empty_entry() -> TapeEntry {
    return TapeEntry { op_type: 0, input1_idx: 0 - 1, input2_idx: 0 - 1, output_idx: 0 - 1 }
}

// Helper: Create tracked value from tape's last value
fn tape_last_tracked(tape: ADTape) -> TrackedValue {
    let idx = tape.n_values - 1
    return TrackedValue { value: tape_get_value(tape, idx), tape_idx: idx }
}

// Add variable to tape (participates in gradient computation)
fn tape_variable(tape: ADTape, value: f64) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let idx = tape.n_values
    let new_tape = tape_set_value(tape, idx, value)
    let tape2 = tape_with_n_values(new_tape, idx + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: value, tape_idx: idx }
    return (tape2, tv)
}

// Add constant to tape (does not participate in gradient computation)
fn tape_constant(tape: ADTape, value: f64) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let idx = tape.n_values
    let new_tape = tape_set_value(tape, idx, value)
    let tape2 = tape_with_n_values(new_tape, idx + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: value, tape_idx: idx }
    return (tape2, tv)
}

// ============================================================================
// TAPE OPERATIONS (FORWARD PASS)
// ============================================================================

fn tape_add(tape: ADTape, a: TrackedValue, b: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = a.value + b.value
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_add(),
        input1_idx: a.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: b.tape_idx,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_mul(tape: ADTape, a: TrackedValue, b: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = a.value * b.value
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_mul(),
        input1_idx: a.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: b.tape_idx,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_exp(tape: ADTape, x: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = exp_f64(x.value)
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_exp(),
        input1_idx: x.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: 0 - 1,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_log(tape: ADTape, x: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = log_f64(x.value)
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_log(),
        input1_idx: x.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: 0 - 1,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_sin(tape: ADTape, x: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = sin_f64(x.value)
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_sin(),
        input1_idx: x.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: 0 - 1,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_tanh(tape: ADTape, x: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = tanh_f64(x.value)
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_tanh(),
        input1_idx: x.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: 0 - 1,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_relu(tape: ADTape, x: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = max_f64(0.0, x.value)
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_relu(),
        input1_idx: x.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: 0 - 1,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

fn tape_sigmoid(tape: ADTape, x: TrackedValue) -> (ADTape, TrackedValue) {
    let result = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp_f64(0.0 - x.value))
    let out_idx = tape.n_values
    let entry = TapeEntry {
        op_type: op_sigmoid(),
        input1_idx: x.tape_idx,
        input2_idx: 0 - 1,
        output_idx: out_idx
    }
    let tape2 = tape_set_value(tape, out_idx, result)
    let tape3 = tape_set_entry(tape2, tape.n_entries, entry)
    let tape4 = tape_with_n_values(tape3, out_idx + 1)
    let tape5 = tape_with_n_entries(tape4, tape.n_entries + 1)
    let tv = TrackedValue { value: result, tape_idx: out_idx }
    return (tape5, tv)
}

// ============================================================================
// TAPE BACKWARD PASS (COMPUTE GRADIENTS)
// ============================================================================

fn tape_backward(tape: ADTape, output_idx: i64) -> ADTape {
    // Initialize output gradient to 1.0 (dL/dL = 1)
    var working_tape = tape_set_grad(tape, output_idx, 1.0)

    // Traverse entries in reverse order
    var i = tape.n_entries - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        let entry = tape_get_entry(working_tape, i)
        working_tape = tape_backward_entry(working_tape, entry)
        i = i - 1
    }

    return working_tape
}

fn tape_backward_entry(tape: ADTape, entry: TapeEntry) -> ADTape {
    let out_grad = tape_get_grad(tape, entry.output_idx)

    if entry.op_type == op_add() {
        // d/da (a + b) = 1, d/db (a + b) = 1
        let tape2 = tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad)
        return tape_add_grad(tape2, entry.input2_idx, out_grad)
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_mul() {
        // d/da (a * b) = b, d/db (a * b) = a
        let a_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.input1_idx)
        let b_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.input2_idx)
        let tape2 = tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad * b_val)
        return tape_add_grad(tape2, entry.input2_idx, out_grad * a_val)
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_exp() {
        // d/dx exp(x) = exp(x)
        let exp_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.output_idx)
        return tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad * exp_val)
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_log() {
        // d/dx log(x) = 1/x
        let x_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.input1_idx)
        return tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad / x_val)
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_sin() {
        // d/dx sin(x) = cos(x)
        let x_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.input1_idx)
        return tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad * cos_f64(x_val))
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_tanh() {
        // d/dx tanh(x) = 1 - tanh²(x)
        let tanh_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.output_idx)
        return tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad * (1.0 - tanh_val * tanh_val))
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_relu() {
        // d/dx ReLU(x) = 1 if x > 0, else 0
        let x_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.input1_idx)
        let deriv = if x_val > 0.0 { out_grad } else { 0.0 }
        return tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, deriv)
    }

    if entry.op_type == op_sigmoid() {
        // d/dx sigmoid(x) = sigmoid(x) * (1 - sigmoid(x))
        let sig_val = tape_get_value(tape, entry.output_idx)
        return tape_add_grad(tape, entry.input1_idx, out_grad * sig_val * (1.0 - sig_val))
    }

    return tape
}

// ============================================================================
// GRADIENT COMPUTATION HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn compute_gradient(tape: ADTape, loss_idx: i64, param_idx: i64) -> f64 {
    let tape_with_grads = tape_backward(tape, loss_idx)
    return tape_get_grad(tape_with_grads, param_idx)
}

// Note: numerical_gradient with function pointer removed - not yet supported in D
// Use the tape-based gradient computation instead

// ============================================================================
// PART 3: EPISTEMIC GRADIENT TRACKING
// ============================================================================

struct DerivativeWithVariance {
    gradient: f64,
    variance: f64,
    n_samples: i64
}

fn grad_var_new(gradient: f64) -> DerivativeWithVariance {
    return DerivativeWithVariance {
        gradient: gradient,
        variance: 0.0,
        n_samples: 1
    }
}

// Welford's online algorithm for variance
fn grad_var_update(gv: DerivativeWithVariance, new_gradient: f64) -> DerivativeWithVariance {
    let n = gv.n_samples + 1
    let delta = new_gradient - gv.gradient
    let new_mean = gv.gradient + delta / (n as f64)
    let delta2 = new_gradient - new_mean
    let new_variance = (gv.variance * (gv.n_samples as f64) + delta * delta2) / (n as f64)

    return DerivativeWithVariance {
        gradient: new_mean,
        variance: new_variance,
        n_samples: n
    }
}

fn grad_var_std_dev(gv: DerivativeWithVariance) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(gv.variance)
}

fn grad_var_confidence_interval(gv: DerivativeWithVariance, z_score: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
    // Returns (lower, upper) bounds for confidence interval
    let std_err = sqrt_f64(gv.variance / (gv.n_samples as f64))
    let margin = z_score * std_err
    return (gv.gradient - margin, gv.gradient + margin)
}

// ============================================================================
// PART 4: VECTOR JACOBIAN PRODUCTS (VJP)
// ============================================================================

// VJP for linear layer: grad_out → grad_in
fn vjp_linear(grad_output: f64, weight: f64) -> f64 {
    return grad_output * weight
}

// VJP for ReLU activation
fn vjp_relu(grad_output: f64, input: f64) -> f64 {
    if input > 0.0 {
        return grad_output
    }
    return 0.0
}

// VJP for sigmoid activation
fn vjp_sigmoid_scalar(grad_output: f64, output: f64) -> f64 {
    // d/dx sigmoid(x) = sigmoid(x) * (1 - sigmoid(x))
    return grad_output * output * (1.0 - output)
}

// VJP for tanh activation
fn vjp_tanh_scalar(grad_output: f64, output: f64) -> f64 {
    // d/dx tanh(x) = 1 - tanh²(x)
    return grad_output * (1.0 - output * output)
}

fn tape_add_grad(tape: ADTape, idx: i64, delta: f64) -> ADTape {
    let current = tape_get_grad(tape, idx)
    return tape_set_grad(tape, idx, current + delta)
}

fn tape_get_entry(tape: ADTape, idx: i64) -> TapeEntry {
    if idx == 0 { return tape.e0 }
    if idx == 1 { return tape.e1 }
    if idx == 2 { return tape.e2 }
    return empty_entry()
}
