// ============================================================================
// TESTS AND EXAMPLES


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/classifier.sio ===
// stdlib/ml/classifier.sio
// k-Nearest Neighbors and Gaussian Naive Bayes classifiers
// with epistemic confidence for multi-class classification.
//
// Dataset: up to 256 samples, 8 features, 4 classes.
// All arrays are fixed-size; shapes tracked via i32 fields.
//
// Compiler workaround: functions that accept &![i32; 256] mutable refs
// must not declare local [f64; N] arrays in the same scope — a type-unifier
// quirk causes Knowledge[f64] confusion. Use helpers that build float arrays
// and return them by value instead.
//
// References:
// - Cover & Hart (1967). Nearest Neighbor Pattern Classification. IEEE Trans IT.
// - John & Langley (1995). Estimating Continuous Distributions in Bayesian
//   Classifiers. UAI 1995.
// - Duda, Hart & Stork (2001). Pattern Classification. Wiley.

// ============================================================================
// Math helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn clf_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn clf_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    return y
}

fn clf_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x > 20.0 {
        let h = clf_exp(x / 2.0)
        return h * h
    }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / clf_exp(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i: i32 = 1
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn clf_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    var val = x
    var k = 0.0
    let e = 2.718281828459045
    while val > e { val = val / e; k = k + 1.0 }
    while val < 1.0 / e { val = val * e; k = k - 1.0 }
    let u = (val - 1.0) / (val + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var s = u
    var t = u
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 3.0
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 5.0
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 7.0
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 9.0
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 11.0
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 13.0
    t = t * u2; s = s + t / 15.0
    return 2.0 * s + k
}

fn clf_max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn clf_min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

// ============================================================================
// Core data types
// ============================================================================

// Dataset: up to 256 samples, 8 features, 4 classes.
// features is row-major: features[i * n_features + j] = sample i, feature j.
pub struct Dataset {
    pub features: [f64; 2048],
    pub labels: [i32; 256],
    pub n_samples: i32,
    pub n_features: i32,
    pub n_classes: i32,
}

// Classification output: predicted class + epistemic confidence.
pub struct Prediction {
    pub class: i32,
    pub confidence: f64,
    pub probabilities: [f64; 4],
}

// Prediction buffer: wraps [i32; 256] so mutable-ref mutations propagate
// correctly through the JIT interpreter (bare &![i32;256] mutations are
// invisible to callers — see KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md §JIT mutable ref bug).
pub struct PredBuf {
    pub data: [i32; 256],
}

// Per-class and aggregate evaluation metrics.
pub struct ClassifierMetrics {
    pub accuracy: f64,
    pub precision: [f64; 4],
    pub recall: [f64; 4],
    pub f1: [f64; 4],
    pub confusion: [i32; 16],
    pub n_correct: i32,
    pub n_total: i32,
}

// Gaussian Naive Bayes model parameters.
pub struct GaussianNB {
    pub means: [f64; 32],
    pub variances: [f64; 32],
    pub class_priors: [f64; 4],
    pub n_classes: i32,
    pub n_features: i32,
    pub fitted: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Array helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

// Extract row t from a flat [f64; 2048] feature matrix into a [f64; 8] query.
// Kept as a separate function so that callers with &![i32; 256] mutable refs
// can call this rather than declaring a local float array in the same scope.
fn clf_build_query(feat: &[f64; 2048], t: i32, nf: i32) -> [f64; 8] with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var q: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < nf {
        q[j] = feat[t * nf + j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    return q
}

// Extract row i from Dataset.features into a [f64; 8].
fn clf_dataset_row(data: &Dataset, i: i32) -> [f64; 8] with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var row: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    let nf = data.n_features
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < nf {
        row[j] = data.features[i * nf + j]
        j = j + 1
    }
    return row
}

// ============================================================================
// Distance helper
// ============================================================================

// Euclidean distance between two feature vectors (up to 8 dimensions).
fn euclidean_dist(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], n_features: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_features {
        let d = a[i] - b[i]
        sum = sum + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    return clf_sqrt(sum)
}

// ============================================================================
// k-Nearest Neighbors
// ============================================================================

// knn_predict: find the k nearest training samples and vote by majority.
// Confidence = fraction of votes cast for the winning class.
// k is clamped to [1, n_samples]. Ties broken by smallest class index.
pub fn knn_predict(train: &Dataset, feat_vec: &[f64; 8], k: i32) -> Prediction with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let n = train.n_samples
    let nf = train.n_features

    // Clamp k
    var kk = k
    if kk < 1 { kk = 1 }
    if kk > n { kk = n }

    // Compute distances to all training samples
    var dists: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let row = clf_dataset_row(train, i)
        dists[i] = euclidean_dist(&row, feat_vec, nf)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Partial sort: bubble the k smallest distances to the front (selection sort).
    var nn_idx: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        nn_idx[i] = i
        i = i + 1
    }

    var outer: i32 = 0
    while outer < kk {
        var inner = outer + 1
        while inner < n {
            if dists[nn_idx[inner]] < dists[nn_idx[outer]] {
                let tmp = nn_idx[outer]
                nn_idx[outer] = nn_idx[inner]
                nn_idx[inner] = tmp
            }
            inner = inner + 1
        }
        outer = outer + 1
    }

    // Count votes per class among the k nearest
    var votes: [i32; 4] = [0; 4]
    var vi: i32 = 0
    while vi < kk {
        let label = train.labels[nn_idx[vi]]
        if label >= 0 {
            if label < 4 {
                votes[label] = votes[label] + 1
            }
        }
        vi = vi + 1
    }

    // Find winning class (ties broken by smallest index)
    var best_class: i32 = 0
    var best_votes: i32 = votes[0]
    var ci: i32 = 1
    while ci < 4 {
        if votes[ci] > best_votes {
            best_votes = votes[ci]
            best_class = ci
        }
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    // Confidence = fraction of k votes for winner; probabilities per class
    let kk_f64 = kk as f64
    var probs: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    var pi: i32 = 0
    while pi < 4 {
        probs[pi] = (votes[pi] as f64) / kk_f64
        pi = pi + 1
    }
    let conf = probs[best_class]

    return Prediction {
        class: best_class,
        confidence: conf,
        probabilities: probs,
    }
}

// knn_predict_all: predict all n_test samples stored in test_features (row-major,
// n_features columns). Writes predicted labels to predictions.
// Returns mean confidence across all predictions as an epistemic quality signal.
// Note: uses clf_build_query helper to avoid local float array + &![i32;256] clash.
pub fn knn_predict_all(
    train: &Dataset,
    test_features: &[f64; 2048],
    n_test: i32,
    n_features: i32,
    k: i32,
    buf: &!PredBuf,
) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var sum_conf = 0.0
    var t: i32 = 0
    while t < n_test {
        // Build feature vector via helper (avoids local float array in this scope)
        let fv = clf_build_query(test_features, t, n_features)
        let pred = knn_predict(train, &fv, k)
        buf.data[t] = pred.class
        sum_conf = sum_conf + pred.confidence
        t = t + 1
    }
    if n_test == 0 { return 0.0 }
    return sum_conf / (n_test as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// Gaussian Naive Bayes
// ============================================================================

// gnb_new: create an unfitted GaussianNB.
pub fn gnb_new(n_classes: i32, n_features: i32) -> GaussianNB {
    return GaussianNB {
        means: [0.0; 32],
        variances: [0.0; 32],
        class_priors: [0.0; 4],
        n_classes: n_classes,
        n_features: n_features,
        fitted: 0,
    }
}

// gnb_fit: compute per-class, per-feature means and variances, plus log priors.
// Returns a new fitted GaussianNB.
pub fn gnb_fit(nb: GaussianNB, data: &Dataset) -> GaussianNB with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let nc = nb.n_classes
    let nf = nb.n_features
    let n = data.n_samples

    var means: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var variances: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var class_priors: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    var counts: [i32; 4] = [0; 4]

    // Pass 1: accumulate sums per class per feature
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let c = data.labels[i]
        if c >= 0 {
            if c < nc {
                counts[c] = counts[c] + 1
                var j: i32 = 0
                while j < nf {
                    means[c * nf + j] = means[c * nf + j] + data.features[i * nf + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute means and log priors
    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < nc {
        let cnt = counts[c]
        if cnt > 0 {
            class_priors[c] = clf_ln((cnt as f64) / (n as f64))
            var j: i32 = 0
            while j < nf {
                means[c * nf + j] = means[c * nf + j] / (cnt as f64)
                j = j + 1
            }
        } else {
            class_priors[c] = clf_ln(1.0 / (nc as f64))
        }
        c = c + 1
    }

    // Pass 2: accumulate squared deviations for variance
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let c2 = data.labels[i]
        if c2 >= 0 {
            if c2 < nc {
                var j: i32 = 0
                while j < nf {
                    let diff = data.features[i * nf + j] - means[c2 * nf + j]
                    variances[c2 * nf + j] = variances[c2 * nf + j] + diff * diff
                    j = j + 1
                }
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Finalise variance; clamp minimum to 1e-9 for numerical stability
    c = 0
    while c < nc {
        let cnt = counts[c]
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < nf {
            if cnt > 1 {
                variances[c * nf + j] = variances[c * nf + j] / (cnt as f64)
            } else {
                variances[c * nf + j] = 1.0
            }
            if variances[c * nf + j] < 0.000000001 {
                variances[c * nf + j] = 0.000000001
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        c = c + 1
    }

    return GaussianNB {
        means: means,
        variances: variances,
        class_priors: class_priors,
        n_classes: nc,
        n_features: nf,
        fitted: 1,
    }
}

// gnb_log_likelihood: log P(x | class c) under Gaussian assumption.
// Computes sum over features of log N(x_j; mu_cj, sigma^2_cj).
fn gnb_log_likelihood(nb: &GaussianNB, feat_vec: &[f64; 8], c: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let nf = nb.n_features
    var ll = 0.0
    let pi_const = 3.141592653589793
    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < nf {
        let mu = nb.means[c * nf + j]
        let sig2 = nb.variances[c * nf + j]
        let diff = feat_vec[j] - mu
        // log N(x; mu, sig2) = -0.5*log(2*pi*sig2) - 0.5*(x-mu)^2/sig2
        let log_norm = 0.0 - 0.5 * clf_ln(2.0 * pi_const * sig2)
        let log_exp = 0.0 - 0.5 * (diff * diff) / sig2
        ll = ll + log_norm + log_exp
        j = j + 1
    }
    return ll
}

// gnb_predict: compute posterior log-probability for each class, convert to
// softmax probabilities, return the argmax class and its probability.
pub fn gnb_predict(nb: &GaussianNB, feat_vec: &[f64; 8]) -> Prediction with Panic, Mut, Div {
    let nc = nb.n_classes

    // Log posteriors: log P(c) + log P(x|c)
    var log_post: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < nc {
        log_post[c] = nb.class_priors[c] + gnb_log_likelihood(nb, feat_vec, c)
        c = c + 1
    }

    // Subtract max for numerical stability before softmax
    var max_lp = log_post[0]
    c = 1
    while c < nc {
        if log_post[c] > max_lp { max_lp = log_post[c] }
        c = c + 1
    }

    // Softmax: exp(log_post - max) / sum
    var probs: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    var sum_exp = 0.0
    c = 0
    while c < nc {
        probs[c] = clf_exp(log_post[c] - max_lp)
        sum_exp = sum_exp + probs[c]
        c = c + 1
    }
    if sum_exp > 0.0 {
        c = 0
        while c < nc {
            probs[c] = probs[c] / sum_exp
            c = c + 1
        }
    }

    // Argmax class
    var best_class: i32 = 0
    var best_prob = probs[0]
    c = 1
    while c < nc {
        if probs[c] > best_prob {
            best_prob = probs[c]
            best_class = c
        }
        c = c + 1
    }

    return Prediction {
        class: best_class,
        confidence: best_prob,
        probabilities: probs,
    }
}

// gnb_predict_all: predict all n_test samples from a flat feature matrix.
// Writes predicted labels to predictions. Returns mean confidence.
// Note: uses clf_build_query helper to avoid float-array + mutable-ref bug.
pub fn gnb_predict_all(
    nb: &GaussianNB,
    test_features: &[f64; 2048],
    n_test: i32,
    buf: &!PredBuf,
) -> f64 with Panic, Mut, Div {
    var sum_conf = 0.0
    var t: i32 = 0
    while t < n_test {
        let fv = clf_build_query(test_features, t, nb.n_features)
        let pred = gnb_predict(nb, &fv)
        buf.data[t] = pred.class
        sum_conf = sum_conf + pred.confidence
        t = t + 1
    }
    if n_test == 0 { return 0.0 }
    return sum_conf / (n_test as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// Evaluation
// ============================================================================

// classifier_evaluate: compute accuracy, confusion matrix, and per-class
// precision / recall / F1 from two parallel label arrays of length n.
pub fn classifier_evaluate(
    true_labels: &[i32; 256],
    pred_labels: &[i32; 256],
    n: i32,
    n_classes: i32,
) -> ClassifierMetrics with Panic, Mut, Div {
    // Build 4x4 confusion matrix (row = true class, col = predicted class)
    var confusion: [i32; 16] = [0; 16]
    var n_correct: i32 = 0

    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let t = true_labels[i]
        let p = pred_labels[i]
        if t >= 0 {
            if t < n_classes {
                if p >= 0 {
                    if p < n_classes {
                        confusion[t * n_classes + p] = confusion[t * n_classes + p] + 1
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if t == p { n_correct = n_correct + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let accuracy = if n > 0 { (n_correct as f64) / (n as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    // Per-class precision, recall, F1
    var precision: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    var recall: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]
    var f1: [f64; 4] = [0.0; 4]

    var c: i32 = 0
    while c < n_classes {
        // TP = confusion[c][c]
        let tp = confusion[c * n_classes + c] as f64

        // Column sum: all predicted as c (true positives + false positives)
        var col_sum = 0.0
        var r: i32 = 0
        while r < n_classes {
            col_sum = col_sum + (confusion[r * n_classes + c] as f64)
            r = r + 1
        }

        // Row sum: all actually c (true positives + false negatives)
        var row_sum = 0.0
        var k: i32 = 0
        while k < n_classes {
            row_sum = row_sum + (confusion[c * n_classes + k] as f64)
            k = k + 1
        }

        if col_sum > 0.0 { precision[c] = tp / col_sum } else { precision[c] = 0.0 }
        if row_sum > 0.0 { recall[c] = tp / row_sum } else { recall[c] = 0.0 }

        let pr = precision[c] + recall[c]
        if pr > 0.0 {
            f1[c] = 2.0 * precision[c] * recall[c] / pr
        } else {
            f1[c] = 0.0
        }

        c = c + 1
    }

    return ClassifierMetrics {
        accuracy: accuracy,
        precision: precision,
        recall: recall,
        f1: f1,
        confusion: confusion,
        n_correct: n_correct,
        n_total: n,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/gp.sio ===
// stdlib/ml/gp.sio
// Gaussian Processes for Sounio ML
//
// GPs are naturally epistemic: every prediction has a posterior variance.
// Uses fixed arrays. Max training size: 16 points, max dim: 4.

fn gp_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn gp_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    return y
}

fn gp_exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 { return gp_exp_f64(x / 2.0) * gp_exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / gp_exp_f64(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn gp_log_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1000000.0 }
    var val = x
    var k = 0.0
    let e = 2.718281828459045
    while val > e { val = val / e; k = k + 1.0 }
    while val < 1.0 / e { val = val * e; k = k - 1.0 }
    let u = (val - 1.0) / (val + 1.0)
    let u2 = u * u
    var sum = u
    var term = u
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 3.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 5.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 7.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 9.0
    term = term * u2; sum = sum + term / 11.0
    return 2.0 * sum + k
}

// RBF kernel: k(x1, x2) = variance * exp(-0.5 * ||x1-x2||^2 / length_scale^2)
fn kernel_rbf(x1: [f64; 4], x2: [f64; 4], d: i64, length_scale: f64, variance: f64) -> f64 {
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < d {
        let diff = x1[i] - x2[i]
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    return variance * gp_exp_f64(0.0 - 0.5 * sum_sq / (length_scale * length_scale))
}

struct KernelParams {
    length_scale: f64,
    variance: f64,
}

// GP prediction result
struct GPPrediction {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    conf_lo: f64,
    conf_hi: f64,
}

// Compute kernel matrix K[n x n] for training data X[n x d]
// X is flattened row-major, K output is flattened row-major
fn gp_kernel_matrix(X: [f64; 64], n: i64, d: i64, params: KernelParams, K: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            var x1 = [0.0; 4]
            var x2 = [0.0; 4]
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < d {
                x1[k] = X[i * d + k]
                x2[k] = X[j * d + k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            K[i * n + j] = kernel_rbf(x1, x2, d, params.length_scale, params.variance)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Cholesky decomposition: A = L * L^T (in-place, lower triangle)
fn gp_cholesky(A: [f64; 256], n: i64, L: &![f64; 256]) {
    // Zero out L
    var idx: i64 = 0
    while idx < n * n {
        L[idx] = 0.0
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j <= i {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < j {
                sum = sum + L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            if i == j {
                L[i * n + j] = gp_sqrt_f64(A[i * n + i] - sum)
            } else {
                let diag = L[j * n + j]
                if diag > 0.0 {
                    L[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / diag
                }
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Solve L * x = b where L is lower triangular
fn gp_solve_lower(L: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 16], n: i64, x: &![f64; 16]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + L[i * n + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = L[i * n + i]
        if diag > 0.0 {
            x[i] = (b[i] - sum) / diag
        } else {
            x[i] = 0.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Solve L^T * x = b where L is lower triangular
fn gp_solve_upper(L: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 16], n: i64, x: &![f64; 16]) {
    var i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + L[j * n + i] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = L[i * n + i]
        if diag > 0.0 {
            x[i] = (b[i] - sum) / diag
        } else {
            x[i] = 0.0
        }
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// Dot product of two vectors
fn gp_dot(a: [f64; 16], b: [f64; 16], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// Fit GP: compute alpha = (K + noise*I)^{-1} * y via Cholesky
// Returns alpha in out_alpha, L in out_L
fn gp_fit(X: [f64; 64], y: [f64; 16], n: i64, d: i64, params: KernelParams, noise: f64,
          out_alpha: &![f64; 16], out_L: &![f64; 256]) {
    // Compute K
    var K = [0.0; 256]
    gp_kernel_matrix(X, n, d, params, &!K)

    // K_noisy = K + noise * I
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        K[i * n + i] = K[i * n + i] + noise
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Cholesky
    gp_cholesky(K, n, out_L)

    // Solve L * tmp = y
    var tmp = [0.0; 16]
    var L_copy = [0.0; 256]
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci < n * n {
        L_copy[ci] = out_L[ci]
        ci = ci + 1
    }
    gp_solve_lower(L_copy, y, n, &!tmp)

    // Solve L^T * alpha = tmp
    gp_solve_upper(L_copy, tmp, n, out_alpha)
}

// Predict at a single test point
fn gp_predict(X_train: [f64; 64], n: i64, d: i64, params: KernelParams,
              alpha: [f64; 16], L: [f64; 256], x_test: [f64; 4]) -> GPPrediction {
    // k_star[i] = kernel(x_test, X_train[i])
    var k_star = [0.0; 16]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var x_i = [0.0; 4]
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < d {
            x_i[j] = X_train[i * d + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        k_star[i] = kernel_rbf(x_test, x_i, d, params.length_scale, params.variance)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // mean = k_star^T * alpha
    let mean = gp_dot(k_star, alpha, n)

    // variance = k(x*,x*) - v^T v where L*v = k_star
    let k_ss = kernel_rbf(x_test, x_test, d, params.length_scale, params.variance)
    var v = [0.0; 16]
    gp_solve_lower(L, k_star, n, &!v)
    let vtv = gp_dot(v, v, n)
    var variance = k_ss - vtv
    if variance < 0.0 { variance = 0.0 }

    let std_dev = gp_sqrt_f64(variance)

    GPPrediction {
        mean: mean,
        variance: variance,
        conf_lo: mean - 1.96 * std_dev,
        conf_hi: mean + 1.96 * std_dev,
    }
}

// Log marginal likelihood
fn gp_log_marginal_likelihood(y: [f64; 16], alpha: [f64; 16], L: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793

    // -0.5 * y^T * alpha
    let term1 = 0.0 - 0.5 * gp_dot(y, alpha, n)

    // -sum(log(diag(L)))
    var log_det = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        log_det = log_det + gp_log_f64(L[i * n + i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    let term2 = 0.0 - log_det

    // -n/2 * log(2*pi)
    let term3 = 0.0 - 0.5 * (n as f64) * gp_log_f64(2.0 * pi)

    return term1 + term2 + term3
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/ml/lib.sio - Module entry point
//!
//! This module contains ml functionality.


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/loss.sio ===
// stdlib/ml/loss.sio
// Loss functions for neural network training
//
// MSE, MAE, Huber, cross-entropy, and epistemic losses.
// All operate on fixed-size f64 arrays.

struct LossResult {
    loss: f64,
    grad_0: f64,
    grad_1: f64,
    grad_2: f64,
    grad_3: f64,
    n_grads: i64,
}

fn loss_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn loss_sign(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 { 1.0 } else if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 0.0 }
}

fn loss_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

fn loss_clip(x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x }
}

// Mean Squared Error for up to 4 elements
// L = (1/n) * sum((pred - target)^2)
fn mse_loss(pred: [f64; 4], target: [f64; 4], n: i64) -> LossResult {
    var sum = 0.0
    var g0 = 0.0
    var g1 = 0.0
    var g2 = 0.0
    var g3 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = pred[i] - target[i]
        sum = sum + diff * diff
        let g = 2.0 * diff / (n as f64)
        if i == 0 { g0 = g }
        if i == 1 { g1 = g }
        if i == 2 { g2 = g }
        if i == 3 { g3 = g }
        i = i + 1
    }
    LossResult {
        loss: sum / (n as f64),
        grad_0: g0, grad_1: g1, grad_2: g2, grad_3: g3,
        n_grads: n,
    }
}

// Mean Absolute Error
fn mae_loss(pred: [f64; 4], target: [f64; 4], n: i64) -> LossResult {
    var sum = 0.0
    var g0 = 0.0
    var g1 = 0.0
    var g2 = 0.0
    var g3 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = pred[i] - target[i]
        sum = sum + loss_abs(diff)
        let g = loss_sign(diff) / (n as f64)
        if i == 0 { g0 = g }
        if i == 1 { g1 = g }
        if i == 2 { g2 = g }
        if i == 3 { g3 = g }
        i = i + 1
    }
    LossResult {
        loss: sum / (n as f64),
        grad_0: g0, grad_1: g1, grad_2: g2, grad_3: g3,
        n_grads: n,
    }
}

// Huber Loss
fn huber_loss(pred: [f64; 4], target: [f64; 4], n: i64, delta: f64) -> LossResult {
    var sum = 0.0
    var g0 = 0.0
    var g1 = 0.0
    var g2 = 0.0
    var g3 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = pred[i] - target[i]
        let abs_diff = loss_abs(diff)
        var g = 0.0
        if abs_diff <= delta {
            sum = sum + 0.5 * diff * diff
            g = diff / (n as f64)
        } else {
            sum = sum + delta * (abs_diff - 0.5 * delta)
            g = delta * loss_sign(diff) / (n as f64)
        }
        if i == 0 { g0 = g }
        if i == 1 { g1 = g }
        if i == 2 { g2 = g }
        if i == 3 { g3 = g }
        i = i + 1
    }
    LossResult {
        loss: sum / (n as f64),
        grad_0: g0, grad_1: g1, grad_2: g2, grad_3: g3,
        n_grads: n,
    }
}

// L1 regularization on fixed array
fn l1_regularization(weights: [f64; 64], n: i64, lambda: f64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + loss_abs(weights[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    return lambda * sum
}

// L2 regularization
fn l2_regularization(weights: [f64; 64], n: i64, lambda: f64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + weights[i] * weights[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 0.5 * lambda * sum
}

// Elastic Net
fn elastic_net(weights: [f64; 64], n: i64, l1_lambda: f64, l2_lambda: f64) -> f64 {
    l1_regularization(weights, n, l1_lambda) + l2_regularization(weights, n, l2_lambda)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/neural.sio ===
// neural.d - Neural Network Layers and Activation Functions
//
// This module provides core neural network building blocks for Sounio ML:
// - Dense (fully connected) layers with optional Bayesian uncertainty
// - Convolutional layers (Conv2D)
// - Batch normalization
// - Dropout with MC dropout for uncertainty quantification
// - LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) recurrent layers
// - Activation functions (ReLU, GELU, Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax)
// - Weight initialization strategies (Xavier, Kaiming)
//
// All layers use flattened arrays for weight storage and operate on batched inputs.
// Shapes are tracked explicitly through dimension parameters.

// Dense Layer (Fully Connected)
struct DenseLayer {
    weights: [f64],      // Flattened [out_features, in_features]
    bias: [f64],         // [out_features]
    in_features: i64,
    out_features: i64,
}

// Dense Layer with Bayesian uncertainty (weight distributions)
struct DenseLayerWithUncertainty {
    weights_mean: [f64],
    weights_var: [f64],   // Weight uncertainty (Bayesian)
    bias_mean: [f64],
    bias_var: [f64],
    in_features: i64,
    out_features: i64,
}

// 2D Convolutional Layer
struct Conv2DLayer {
    weights: [f64],       // [out_channels, in_channels, kH, kW]
    bias: [f64],          // [out_channels]
    in_channels: i64,
    out_channels: i64,
    kernel_h: i64,
    kernel_w: i64,
    stride: i64,
    padding: i64,
}

// Batch Normalization Layer
struct BatchNormLayer {
    gamma: [f64],         // Scale
    beta: [f64],          // Shift
    running_mean: [f64],
    running_var: [f64],
    num_features: i64,
    momentum: f64,
    eps: f64,
}

// Dropout Layer
struct DropoutLayer {
    p: f64,               // Dropout probability
    training: i64,        // 1 = training mode, 0 = eval
}

// LSTM Layer
struct LSTMLayer {
    W_ii: [f64], W_if: [f64], W_ig: [f64], W_io: [f64],  // Input weights
    W_hi: [f64], W_hf: [f64], W_hg: [f64], W_ho: [f64],  // Hidden weights
    b_i: [f64], b_f: [f64], b_g: [f64], b_o: [f64],      // Biases
    hidden_size: i64,
    input_size: i64,
}

// ============================================================================
// Weight Initialization
// ============================================================================

// Xavier/Glorot initialization - good for sigmoid/tanh activations
fn xavier_init(in_features: i64, out_features: i64, seed: i64) -> [f64] {
    let size = in_features * out_features
    var weights = array_zeros(size)
    let scale = sqrt(2.0 / (in_features as f64 + out_features as f64))

    var i = 0
    while i < size {
        weights[i] = randn_seeded(seed + i) * scale
        i = i + 1
    }
    weights
}

// Kaiming/He initialization - good for ReLU activations
fn kaiming_init(in_features: i64, out_features: i64, seed: i64) -> [f64] {
    let size = in_features * out_features
    var weights = array_zeros(size)
    let scale = sqrt(2.0 / (in_features as f64))

    var i = 0
    while i < size {
        weights[i] = randn_seeded(seed + i) * scale
        i = i + 1
    }
    weights
}

// ============================================================================
// Dense Layer Operations
// ============================================================================

fn dense_new(in_features: i64, out_features: i64, seed: i64) -> DenseLayer {
    DenseLayer {
        weights: kaiming_init(in_features, out_features, seed),
        bias: array_zeros(out_features),
        in_features: in_features,
        out_features: out_features,
    }
}

// Forward pass for single sample: output[j] = sum_i(W[j,i] * input[i]) + b[j]
fn dense_forward(layer: DenseLayer, input: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    var output = array_zeros(layer.out_features)

    var j = 0
    while j < layer.out_features {
        var sum = layer.bias[j]
        var i = 0
        while i < layer.in_features {
            sum = sum + layer.weights[j * layer.in_features + i] * input[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        output[j] = sum
        j = j + 1
    }
    output
}

// Forward pass for batch: input shape [batch_size, in_features]
fn dense_forward_batch(layer: DenseLayer, input: [f64], batch_size: i64) -> [f64] {
    var output = array_zeros(batch_size * layer.out_features)

    var b = 0
    while b < batch_size {
        var j = 0
        while j < layer.out_features {
            var sum = layer.bias[j]
            var i = 0
            while i < layer.in_features {
                sum = sum + layer.weights[j * layer.in_features + i] * input[b * layer.in_features + i]
                i = i + 1
            }
            output[b * layer.out_features + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        b = b + 1
    }
    output
}

// ============================================================================
// Dense Layer with Uncertainty (Bayesian)
// ============================================================================

fn dense_uncertain_new(in_features: i64, out_features: i64, seed: i64) -> DenseLayerWithUncertainty {
    DenseLayerWithUncertainty {
        weights_mean: kaiming_init(in_features, out_features, seed),
        weights_var: array_fill(in_features * out_features, 0.01),
        bias_mean: array_zeros(out_features),
        bias_var: array_fill(out_features, 0.01),
        in_features: in_features,
        out_features: out_features,
    }
}

// Forward with uncertainty propagation (returns mean and variance)
fn dense_uncertain_forward(layer: DenseLayerWithUncertainty, input: [f64]) -> ([f64], [f64]) {
    var mean = array_zeros(layer.out_features)
    var variance = array_zeros(layer.out_features)

    var j = 0
    while j < layer.out_features {
        var mu = layer.bias_mean[j]
        var var_sum = layer.bias_var[j]

        var i = 0
        while i < layer.in_features {
            let idx = j * layer.in_features + i
            mu = mu + layer.weights_mean[idx] * input[i]
            var_sum = var_sum + layer.weights_var[idx] * input[i] * input[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        mean[j] = mu
        variance[j] = var_sum
        j = j + 1
    }
    (mean, variance)
}

// ============================================================================
// Convolutional Layer (Conv2D)
// ============================================================================

fn conv2d_new(in_channels: i64, out_channels: i64, kernel_h: i64, kernel_w: i64,
              stride: i64, padding: i64, seed: i64) -> Conv2DLayer {
    let weight_size = out_channels * in_channels * kernel_h * kernel_w
    Conv2DLayer {
        weights: kaiming_init(in_channels * kernel_h * kernel_w, out_channels, seed),
        bias: array_zeros(out_channels),
        in_channels: in_channels,
        out_channels: out_channels,
        kernel_h: kernel_h,
        kernel_w: kernel_w,
        stride: stride,
        padding: padding,
    }
}

// Convolutional forward pass for single sample
// Input: [in_channels, H, W], Output: [out_channels, H_out, W_out]
fn conv2d_forward(layer: Conv2DLayer, input: [f64], H: i64, W: i64) -> [f64] {
    let H_out = (H + 2 * layer.padding - layer.kernel_h) / layer.stride + 1
    let W_out = (W + 2 * layer.padding - layer.kernel_w) / layer.stride + 1
    var output = array_zeros(layer.out_channels * H_out * W_out)

    var oc = 0
    while oc < layer.out_channels {
        var oh = 0
        while oh < H_out {
            var ow = 0
            while ow < W_out {
                var sum = layer.bias[oc]

                var ic = 0
                while ic < layer.in_channels {
                    var kh = 0
                    while kh < layer.kernel_h {
                        var kw = 0
                        while kw < layer.kernel_w {
                            let ih = oh * layer.stride + kh - layer.padding
                            let iw = ow * layer.stride + kw - layer.padding

                            if ih >= 0 && ih < H && iw >= 0 && iw < W {
                                let input_idx = ic * H * W + ih * W + iw
                                let weight_idx = ((oc * layer.in_channels + ic) * layer.kernel_h + kh) * layer.kernel_w + kw
                                sum = sum + input[input_idx] * layer.weights[weight_idx]
                            }
                            kw = kw + 1
                        }
                        kh = kh + 1
                    }
                    ic = ic + 1
                }

                output[oc * H_out * W_out + oh * W_out + ow] = sum
                ow = ow + 1
            }
            oh = oh + 1
        }
        oc = oc + 1
    }
    output
}

// ============================================================================
// Batch Normalization
// ============================================================================

fn batchnorm_new(num_features: i64) -> BatchNormLayer {
    BatchNormLayer {
        gamma: array_fill(num_features, 1.0),
        beta: array_zeros(num_features),
        running_mean: array_zeros(num_features),
        running_var: array_fill(num_features, 1.0),
        num_features: num_features,
        momentum: 0.1,
        eps: 1e-5,
    }
}

// Batch normalization forward pass
// Input: [batch_size, num_features]
fn batchnorm_forward(layer: BatchNormLayer, input: [f64], batch_size: i64) -> [f64] {
    var output = array_zeros(batch_size * layer.num_features)

    // Compute batch mean and variance
    var batch_mean = array_zeros(layer.num_features)
    var batch_var = array_zeros(layer.num_features)

    var f = 0
    while f < layer.num_features {
        var sum = 0.0
        var b = 0
        while b < batch_size {
            sum = sum + input[b * layer.num_features + f]
            b = b + 1
        }
        batch_mean[f] = sum / (batch_size as f64)
        f = f + 1
    }

    f = 0
    while f < layer.num_features {
        var sum_sq = 0.0
        var b = 0
        while b < batch_size {
            let diff = input[b * layer.num_features + f] - batch_mean[f]
            sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
            b = b + 1
        }
        batch_var[f] = sum_sq / (batch_size as f64)
        f = f + 1
    }

    // Normalize and transform
    var b = 0
    while b < batch_size {
        var f = 0
        while f < layer.num_features {
            let normalized = (input[b * layer.num_features + f] - batch_mean[f]) / sqrt(batch_var[f] + layer.eps)
            output[b * layer.num_features + f] = layer.gamma[f] * normalized + layer.beta[f]
            f = f + 1
        }
        b = b + 1
    }

    output
}

// ============================================================================
// Dropout
// ============================================================================

fn dropout_new(p: f64) -> DropoutLayer {
    DropoutLayer {
        p: p,
        training: 1,
    }
}

// Dropout forward pass
fn dropout_forward(layer: DropoutLayer, input: [f64], seed: i64) -> [f64] {
    if layer.training == 0 {
        return input
    }

    let n = array_length(input)
    var output = array_zeros(n)
    let scale = 1.0 / (1.0 - layer.p)

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if rand_seeded(seed + i) > layer.p {
            output[i] = input[i] * scale
        } else {
            output[i] = 0.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

// MC Dropout for uncertainty estimation
// Returns (mean, variance) from multiple stochastic forward passes
fn dropout_as_uncertainty(layer: DropoutLayer, input: [f64], n_samples: i64, seed: i64) -> ([f64], [f64]) {
    let n = array_length(input)
    var sum = array_zeros(n)
    var sum_sq = array_zeros(n)

    var s = 0
    while s < n_samples {
        let sample = dropout_forward(layer, input, seed + s * 1000)
        var i = 0
        while i < n {
            sum[i] = sum[i] + sample[i]
            sum_sq[i] = sum_sq[i] + sample[i] * sample[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        s = s + 1
    }

    var mean = array_zeros(n)
    var variance = array_zeros(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        mean[i] = sum[i] / (n_samples as f64)
        variance[i] = sum_sq[i] / (n_samples as f64) - mean[i] * mean[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    (mean, variance)
}

// ============================================================================
// LSTM Layer
// ============================================================================

fn lstm_new(input_size: i64, hidden_size: i64, seed: i64) -> LSTMLayer {
    LSTMLayer {
        W_ii: xavier_init(input_size, hidden_size, seed),
        W_if: xavier_init(input_size, hidden_size, seed + 1),
        W_ig: xavier_init(input_size, hidden_size, seed + 2),
        W_io: xavier_init(input_size, hidden_size, seed + 3),
        W_hi: xavier_init(hidden_size, hidden_size, seed + 4),
        W_hf: xavier_init(hidden_size, hidden_size, seed + 5),
        W_hg: xavier_init(hidden_size, hidden_size, seed + 6),
        W_ho: xavier_init(hidden_size, hidden_size, seed + 7),
        b_i: array_zeros(hidden_size),
        b_f: array_fill(hidden_size, 1.0),  // Forget gate bias init to 1
        b_g: array_zeros(hidden_size),
        b_o: array_zeros(hidden_size),
        hidden_size: hidden_size,
        input_size: input_size,
    }
}

// LSTM forward pass for single timestep
// Returns (new_h, new_c)
fn lstm_forward(layer: LSTMLayer, input: [f64], h: [f64], c: [f64]) -> ([f64], [f64]) {
    var i_gate = array_zeros(layer.hidden_size)
    var f_gate = array_zeros(layer.hidden_size)
    var g_gate = array_zeros(layer.hidden_size)
    var o_gate = array_zeros(layer.hidden_size)

    // Compute gates
    var i = 0
    while i < layer.hidden_size {
        var i_sum = layer.b_i[i]
        var f_sum = layer.b_f[i]
        var g_sum = layer.b_g[i]
        var o_sum = layer.b_o[i]

        var j = 0
        while j < layer.input_size {
            i_sum = i_sum + layer.W_ii[i * layer.input_size + j] * input[j]
            f_sum = f_sum + layer.W_if[i * layer.input_size + j] * input[j]
            g_sum = g_sum + layer.W_ig[i * layer.input_size + j] * input[j]
            o_sum = o_sum + layer.W_io[i * layer.input_size + j] * input[j]
            j = j + 1
        }

        j = 0
        while j < layer.hidden_size {
            i_sum = i_sum + layer.W_hi[i * layer.hidden_size + j] * h[j]
            f_sum = f_sum + layer.W_hf[i * layer.hidden_size + j] * h[j]
            g_sum = g_sum + layer.W_hg[i * layer.hidden_size + j] * h[j]
            o_sum = o_sum + layer.W_ho[i * layer.hidden_size + j] * h[j]
            j = j + 1
        }

        i_gate[i] = sigmoid_scalar(i_sum)
        f_gate[i] = sigmoid_scalar(f_sum)
        g_gate[i] = tanh_scalar(g_sum)
        o_gate[i] = sigmoid_scalar(o_sum)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Update cell state and hidden state
    var new_c = array_zeros(layer.hidden_size)
    var new_h = array_zeros(layer.hidden_size)

    i = 0
    while i < layer.hidden_size {
        new_c[i] = f_gate[i] * c[i] + i_gate[i] * g_gate[i]
        new_h[i] = o_gate[i] * tanh_scalar(new_c[i])
        i = i + 1
    }

    (new_h, new_c)
}

// ============================================================================
// Activation Functions
// ============================================================================

fn relu(x: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = if x[i] > 0.0 { x[i] } else { 0.0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

fn leaky_relu(x: [f64], alpha: f64) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = if x[i] > 0.0 { x[i] } else { alpha * x[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

fn gelu(x: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        // GELU approximation: 0.5 * x * (1 + tanh(sqrt(2/pi) * (x + 0.044715 * x^3)))
        let x_cubed = x[i] * x[i] * x[i]
        let inner = 0.7978845608 * (x[i] + 0.044715 * x_cubed)
        output[i] = 0.5 * x[i] * (1.0 + tanh_scalar(inner))
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

fn sigmoid(x: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = sigmoid_scalar(x[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

fn tanh_activation(x: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = tanh_scalar(x[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

fn softmax(x: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)

    // Find max for numerical stability
    var max_val = x[0]
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        if x[i] > max_val {
            max_val = x[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute exp and sum
    var sum = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = exp(x[i] - max_val)
        sum = sum + output[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Normalize
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = output[i] / sum
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

fn log_softmax(x: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = array_length(x)
    var output = array_zeros(n)

    // Find max for numerical stability
    var max_val = x[0]
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        if x[i] > max_val {
            max_val = x[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute log-sum-exp
    var sum_exp = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum_exp = sum_exp + exp(x[i] - max_val)
        i = i + 1
    }
    let log_sum_exp = max_val + log(sum_exp)

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        output[i] = x[i] - log_sum_exp
        i = i + 1
    }
    output
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// ============================================================================

fn sigmoid_scalar(x: f64) -> f64 {
    1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-x))
}

fn tanh_scalar(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let e2x = exp(2.0 * x)
    (e2x - 1.0) / (e2x + 1.0)
}

fn array_zeros(n: i64) -> [f64] {
    var arr = []
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        arr = array_push(arr, 0.0)
        i = i + 1
    }
    arr
}

fn array_fill(n: i64, value: f64) -> [f64] {
    var arr = []
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        arr = array_push(arr, value)
        i = i + 1
    }
    arr
}

fn array_length(arr: [f64]) -> i64 {
    var count = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < 1000000 {  // Arbitrary large number
        if i >= 1000000 {
            return count
        }
        count = count + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

fn array_push(arr: [f64], value: f64) -> [f64] {
    arr
}

// Simple PRNG for initialization
fn randn_seeded(seed: i64) -> f64 {
    // Box-Muller transform
    let u1 = rand_seeded(seed)
    let u2 = rand_seeded(seed + 1000)
    sqrt(-2.0 * log(u1)) * cos(2.0 * 3.14159265359 * u2)
}

fn rand_seeded(seed: i64) -> f64 {
    // Linear congruential generator
    let a = 1103515245
    let c = 12345
    let m = 2147483648
    let x = (a * seed + c) % m
    (x as f64) / (m as f64)
}

fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    x
}

fn exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    x
}

fn log(x: f64) -> f64 {
    x
}

fn cos(x: f64) -> f64 {
    x
}

fn sin(x: f64) -> f64 {
    x
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/pac.sio ===
// Sounio Standard Library: PAC Learning Types
//
// This module provides compile-time verified machine learning with PAC
// (Probably Approximately Correct) learning theory guarantees.
//
// Key concepts:
// - VC Dimension: Measures hypothesis class complexity
// - Sample Complexity: Minimum samples for (ε, δ)-learning
// - Generalization Bounds: test_error ≤ train_error + ε with prob ≥ 1-δ
//
// References:
// - Valiant, L. (1984). A theory of the learnable. CACM.
// - Blumer et al. (1989). Learnability and the VC dimension. JACM.
// - Hanneke, S. (2016). The optimal sample complexity of PAC learning. JMLR.
// - McAllester, D. (1999). PAC-Bayesian model averaging. COLT.

// Note: epistemic/knowledge import removed to reduce type inference overhead
// Knowledge<> integration can be done by callers if needed
// Note: math::core import removed — math/core.sio does not exist and caused
// the compiler to load the full math directory, duplicating pi/constants and
// pulling in math/ga/simd.sio (which references undefined ga_and).

// ============================================================================
// Utility Functions (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return -1e30 }
    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result = 0.0
    var term = y
    for i in 0..30 {
        let n = 2 * i + 1
        result = result + term / (n as f64)
        term = term * y * y
    }
    2.0 * result
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x / 2.0
    for i in 0..20 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    }
    guess
}

fn ceil_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let i = x as i64
    if (i as f64) < x { (i + 1) as f64 } else { i as f64 }
}

fn log2_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    // log2(x) = ln(x) / ln(2)
    ln_f64(x) / 0.6931471805599453
}

// ============================================================================
// Core Types
// ============================================================================

// VC Dimension - measures hypothesis class complexity
// A class can shatter d points but not d+1 points
pub type VCDim = i64;

// Sample complexity parameters
pub struct SampleComplexityParams {
    vc_dim: VCDim,       // VC dimension of hypothesis class
    epsilon: f64,        // Accuracy parameter (0 < ε < 1)
    delta: f64,          // Confidence parameter (0 < δ < 1)
}

// Generalization bound result
pub struct GeneralizationBound {
    train_error: f64,    // Training error achieved
    gap: f64,            // Generalization gap bound
    confidence: f64,     // Probability bound holds (1 - δ)
}

// ============================================================================
// Hypothesis Classes
// ============================================================================

// Trait for hypothesis classes with known VC dimension
pub trait Learnable {
    // The VC dimension of this hypothesis class
    fn vc_dim() -> VCDim;

    // The associated model type
    type Model;
}

// Decision stump (single threshold on one feature)
// VC dimension = 1
pub struct DecisionStump {
    feature_idx: i32,
    threshold: f64,
    direction: bool,
}

impl Learnable for DecisionStump {
    fn vc_dim() -> VCDim {
        1i64
    }

    type Model = DecisionStump;
}

// NOTE: Const generic types (LinearClassifier<const D>, AxisAlignedRectangle<const D>,
// NeuralNetwork<const L, const W>, DecisionTree<const D, const F>) are deferred
// until const generics and fixed-size arrays [T; N] are implemented in the parser.
// VC dimension formulas:
//   LinearClassifier<D>:          D + 1 (Radon's theorem)
//   AxisAlignedRectangle<D>:      2 * D
//   NeuralNetwork<L, W>:          W * L (Bartlett et al.)
//   DecisionTree<D, F>:           2^D * log2(F)

// ============================================================================
// Sample Complexity Functions
// ============================================================================

// Compute minimum samples required for (ε, δ)-PAC learning
//
// Formula: m ≥ (1/ε²) * (d + ln(1/δ))
//
// Returns the minimum number of samples needed to achieve:
// - accuracy: at least 1 - ε (e.g., ε=0.01 means 99% accuracy)
// - confidence: at least 1 - δ (e.g., δ=0.05 means 95% confidence)
pub fn sample_complexity(vc_dim: VCDim, epsilon: f64, delta: f64) -> i64 with Panic, Mut
{
    let eps_sq = epsilon * epsilon
    let d = vc_dim as f64
    let bound = (1.0 / eps_sq) * (d + ln_f64(1.0 / delta))
    ceil_f64(bound) as i64
}

// Compute tighter sample complexity (Hanneke 2016)
//
// Formula: m ≥ d/ε + ln(1/δ)/ε²
//
// This is asymptotically optimal and tighter when ε is small.
pub fn sample_complexity_tight(vc_dim: VCDim, epsilon: f64, delta: f64) -> i64 with Panic, Mut
{
    let d = vc_dim as f64
    let eps = epsilon
    let eps_sq = epsilon * epsilon
    let bound = d / eps + ln_f64(1.0 / delta) / eps_sq
    ceil_f64(bound) as i64
}

// ============================================================================
// Generalization Bounds
// ============================================================================

// Compute generalization gap from VC theory
//
// Gap ≤ √((d·ln(2m/d) + ln(4/δ)) / m)
//
// With probability ≥ 1-δ: |test_error - train_error| ≤ gap
pub fn generalization_gap(vc_dim: VCDim, samples: i64, delta: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut
{
    let d = vc_dim as f64
    let m = samples as f64

    let term1 = d * ln_f64(2.0 * m / d)
    let term2 = ln_f64(4.0 / delta)

    sqrt_f64((term1 + term2) / m)
}

// Create a generalization bound from PAC parameters
pub fn make_bound(
    vc_dim: VCDim,
    samples: i64,
    delta: f64,
    train_error: f64
) -> GeneralizationBound with Panic, Mut
{
    let gap = generalization_gap(vc_dim, samples, delta)
    GeneralizationBound {
        train_error: train_error,
        gap: gap,
        confidence: 1.0 - delta,
    }
}

// Get upper bound on test error
pub fn test_error_bound(bound: GeneralizationBound) -> f64
{
    bound.train_error + bound.gap
}

// ============================================================================
// Training with PAC Guarantees
// ============================================================================

// Compute PAC-validated generalization bound
//
// After training on a hypothesis class H, use this to compute the bound on test error.
// With probability ≥ 1-δ: test_error ≤ train_error + gap
//
// The returned GeneralizationBound can be wrapped in Knowledge<> by the caller
// if needed for epistemic tracking.
pub fn pac_bound(
    vc_dim: VCDim,
    samples: i64,
    train_error: f64,
    delta: f64
) -> GeneralizationBound with Panic, Mut
{
    make_bound(vc_dim, samples, delta, train_error)
}

// Check if dataset is sufficient for learning
pub fn is_sufficient(
    vc_dim: VCDim,
    samples: i64,
    epsilon: f64,
    delta: f64
) -> bool with Panic, Mut
{
    samples >= sample_complexity(vc_dim, epsilon, delta)
}

// ============================================================================
// PAC-Bayes Bounds (Tighter for Bayesian learning)
// ============================================================================

// PAC-Bayes bound parameters
pub struct PACBayesParams {
    kl_divergence: f64,  // KL(posterior || prior)
    samples: i64,
    delta: f64,
}

// Compute PAC-Bayes generalization gap
//
// Gap ≤ √((KL + ln(2√m/δ)) / (2m))
//
// Tighter than VC bounds when we have a good prior.
pub fn pac_bayes_gap(params: PACBayesParams) -> f64 with Panic, Mut
{
    let m = params.samples as f64
    let kl = params.kl_divergence

    let numerator = kl + ln_f64(2.0 * sqrt_f64(m) / params.delta)
    sqrt_f64(numerator / (2.0 * m))
}

// ============================================================================
// Rademacher Complexity Bounds
// ============================================================================

// Rademacher complexity based generalization bound
//
// Gap ≤ 2R(H, m) + √(ln(1/δ)/(2m))
//
// where R(H, m) is the empirical Rademacher complexity.
pub fn rademacher_gap(rademacher: f64, samples: i64, delta: f64) -> f64 with Panic, Mut
{
    let m = samples as f64
    2.0 * rademacher + sqrt_f64(ln_f64(1.0 / delta) / (2.0 * m))
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ml/tensor.sio ===
// stdlib/ml/tensor.sio
// Fixed-size tensor operations for machine learning
//
// Uses [f64; 256] as flat storage with shape metadata.
// Supports up to 4D tensors with max 256 total elements.

struct TensorShape {
    dims: [i64; 4],
    ndim: i64,
    size: i64,
}

fn tshape_compute_size(dims: [i64; 4], ndim: i64) -> i64 {
    var size: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < ndim {
        size = size * dims[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return size
}

fn tshape_new1(d0: i64) -> TensorShape {
    var dims = [0; 4]
    dims[0] = d0
    TensorShape { dims: dims, ndim: 1, size: d0 }
}

fn tshape_new2(d0: i64, d1: i64) -> TensorShape {
    var dims = [0; 4]
    dims[0] = d0
    dims[1] = d1
    TensorShape { dims: dims, ndim: 2, size: d0 * d1 }
}

// Element-wise add
fn tensor_add(a: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = a[i] + b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Element-wise sub
fn tensor_sub(a: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = a[i] - b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Element-wise mul
fn tensor_mul(a: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = a[i] * b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Element-wise negate
fn tensor_neg(a: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = 0.0 - a[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Scalar multiply
fn tensor_scale(a: [f64; 256], n: i64, s: f64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = a[i] * s
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Scalar add
fn tensor_shift(a: [f64; 256], n: i64, s: f64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = a[i] + s
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Sum all elements
fn tensor_sum(a: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// Mean
fn tensor_mean(a: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    if n == 0 { return 0.0 }
    return tensor_sum(a, n) / (n as f64)
}

// Max
fn tensor_max(a: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    if n == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = a[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if a[i] > m { m = a[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return m
}

// Min
fn tensor_min(a: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    if n == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = a[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if a[i] < m { m = a[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return m
}

// Matrix multiply: C[m x n] = A[m x k] * B[k x n]  (row-major)
fn tensor_matmul(a: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 256], m: i64, k: i64, n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < m {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var p: i64 = 0
            while p < k {
                sum = sum + a[i * k + p] * b[p * n + j]
                p = p + 1
            }
            out[i * n + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Dot product
fn tensor_dot(a: [f64; 256], b: [f64; 256], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// Transpose 2D: out[j*rows + i] = a[i*cols + j]
fn tensor_transpose(a: [f64; 256], rows: i64, cols: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < rows {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < cols {
            out[j * rows + i] = a[i * cols + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Fill with zeros
fn tensor_zeros(out: &![f64; 256], n: i64) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Fill with ones
fn tensor_ones(out: &![f64; 256], n: i64) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Fill with constant
fn tensor_fill(out: &![f64; 256], n: i64, value: f64) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = value
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Identity matrix (row-major, n x n)
fn tensor_eye(out: &![f64; 256], n: i64) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n * n {
        out[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i * n + i] = 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Simple exp approximation
fn tensor_exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 10.0 { return 22026.465794806718 * tensor_exp_f64(x - 10.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 10.0 { return 0.00004539992976248485 * tensor_exp_f64(x + 10.0) }
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * x / (i as f64)
        result = result + term
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// Element-wise exp
fn tensor_exp(a: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = tensor_exp_f64(a[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Simple sqrt (Newton)
fn tensor_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// Element-wise sqrt
fn tensor_sqrt(a: [f64; 256], n: i64, out: &![f64; 256]) {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        out[i] = tensor_sqrt_f64(a[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/net/addr.sio ===
// stdlib/net/addr — Network address types

struct IPv4Addr {
    a: i64,
    b: i64,
    c: i64,
    d: i64,
}

fn ipv4_new(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64, d: i64) -> IPv4Addr {
    IPv4Addr { a: a, b: b, c: c, d: d }
}

fn ipv4_loopback() -> IPv4Addr {
    IPv4Addr { a: 127, b: 0, c: 0, d: 1 }
}

fn ipv4_any() -> IPv4Addr {
    IPv4Addr { a: 0, b: 0, c: 0, d: 0 }
}

impl IPv4Addr {
    fn is_loopback(self: &IPv4Addr) -> bool { self.a == 127 }

    fn is_private(self: &IPv4Addr) -> bool {
        if self.a == 10 { return true }
        if self.a == 172 && self.b >= 16 && self.b <= 31 { return true }
        if self.a == 192 && self.b == 168 { return true }
        return false
    }

    fn is_any(self: &IPv4Addr) -> bool {
        self.a == 0 && self.b == 0 && self.c == 0 && self.d == 0
    }

    fn to_u32(self: &IPv4Addr) -> i64 {
        self.a * 16777216 + self.b * 65536 + self.c * 256 + self.d
    }

    fn equals(self: &IPv4Addr, other: &IPv4Addr) -> bool {
        self.a == other.a && self.b == other.b && self.c == other.c && self.d == other.d
    }
}

struct SocketAddr {
    ip: IPv4Addr,
    port: i64,
}

fn socket_addr_new(ip: IPv4Addr, port: i64) -> SocketAddr {
    SocketAddr { ip: ip, port: port }
}

impl SocketAddr {
    fn port(self: &SocketAddr) -> i64 { self.port }
    fn is_loopback(self: &SocketAddr) -> bool { self.ip.is_loopback() }
}
