fn tensor32_ones() -> Tensor32 {
    return Tensor32 {
        e0: 1.0, e1: 1.0, e2: 1.0, e3: 1.0, e4: 1.0, e5: 1.0, e6: 1.0, e7: 1.0,
        e8: 1.0, e9: 1.0, e10: 1.0, e11: 1.0, e12: 1.0, e13: 1.0, e14: 1.0, e15: 1.0,
        e16: 1.0, e17: 1.0, e18: 1.0, e19: 1.0, e20: 1.0, e21: 1.0, e22: 1.0, e23: 1.0,
        e24: 1.0, e25: 1.0, e26: 1.0, e27: 1.0, e28: 1.0, e29: 1.0, e30: 1.0, e31: 1.0
    }
}

fn tensor32_add(a: Tensor32, b: Tensor32) -> Tensor32 {
    return Tensor32 {
        e0: a.e0 + b.e0, e1: a.e1 + b.e1, e2: a.e2 + b.e2, e3: a.e3 + b.e3,
        e4: a.e4 + b.e4, e5: a.e5 + b.e5, e6: a.e6 + b.e6, e7: a.e7 + b.e7,
        e8: a.e8 + b.e8, e9: a.e9 + b.e9, e10: a.e10 + b.e10, e11: a.e11 + b.e11,
        e12: a.e12 + b.e12, e13: a.e13 + b.e13, e14: a.e14 + b.e14, e15: a.e15 + b.e15,
        e16: a.e16 + b.e16, e17: a.e17 + b.e17, e18: a.e18 + b.e18, e19: a.e19 + b.e19,
        e20: a.e20 + b.e20, e21: a.e21 + b.e21, e22: a.e22 + b.e22, e23: a.e23 + b.e23,
        e24: a.e24 + b.e24, e25: a.e25 + b.e25, e26: a.e26 + b.e26, e27: a.e27 + b.e27,
        e28: a.e28 + b.e28, e29: a.e29 + b.e29, e30: a.e30 + b.e30, e31: a.e31 + b.e31
    }
}

fn tensor32_scale(vec: Tensor32, scalar: f64) -> Tensor32 {
    return Tensor32 {
        e0: vec.e0 * scalar, e1: vec.e1 * scalar, e2: vec.e2 * scalar, e3: vec.e3 * scalar,
        e4: vec.e4 * scalar, e5: vec.e5 * scalar, e6: vec.e6 * scalar, e7: vec.e7 * scalar,
        e8: vec.e8 * scalar, e9: vec.e9 * scalar, e10: vec.e10 * scalar, e11: vec.e11 * scalar,
        e12: vec.e12 * scalar, e13: vec.e13 * scalar, e14: vec.e14 * scalar, e15: vec.e15 * scalar,
        e16: vec.e16 * scalar, e17: vec.e17 * scalar, e18: vec.e18 * scalar, e19: vec.e19 * scalar,
        e20: vec.e20 * scalar, e21: vec.e21 * scalar, e22: vec.e22 * scalar, e23: vec.e23 * scalar,
        e24: vec.e24 * scalar, e25: vec.e25 * scalar, e26: vec.e26 * scalar, e27: vec.e27 * scalar,
        e28: vec.e28 * scalar, e29: vec.e29 * scalar, e30: vec.e30 * scalar, e31: vec.e31 * scalar
    }
}

fn tensor32_dot(a: Tensor32, b: Tensor32) -> f64 {
    let sum0 = a.e0 * b.e0 + a.e1 * b.e1 + a.e2 * b.e2 + a.e3 * b.e3
    let sum1 = a.e4 * b.e4 + a.e5 * b.e5 + a.e6 * b.e6 + a.e7 * b.e7
    let sum2 = a.e8 * b.e8 + a.e9 * b.e9 + a.e10 * b.e10 + a.e11 * b.e11
    let sum3 = a.e12 * b.e12 + a.e13 * b.e13 + a.e14 * b.e14 + a.e15 * b.e15
    let sum4 = a.e16 * b.e16 + a.e17 * b.e17 + a.e18 * b.e18 + a.e19 * b.e19
    let sum5 = a.e20 * b.e20 + a.e21 * b.e21 + a.e22 * b.e22 + a.e23 * b.e23
    let sum6 = a.e24 * b.e24 + a.e25 * b.e25 + a.e26 * b.e26 + a.e27 * b.e27
    let sum7 = a.e28 * b.e28 + a.e29 * b.e29 + a.e30 * b.e30 + a.e31 * b.e31
    return sum0 + sum1 + sum2 + sum3 + sum4 + sum5 + sum6 + sum7
}

fn tensor32_norm(vec: Tensor32) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_val(tensor32_dot(vec, vec))
}

fn tensor32_sum(vec: Tensor32) -> f64 {
    let s0 = vec.e0 + vec.e1 + vec.e2 + vec.e3 + vec.e4 + vec.e5 + vec.e6 + vec.e7
    let s1 = vec.e8 + vec.e9 + vec.e10 + vec.e11 + vec.e12 + vec.e13 + vec.e14 + vec.e15
    let s2 = vec.e16 + vec.e17 + vec.e18 + vec.e19 + vec.e20 + vec.e21 + vec.e22 + vec.e23
    let s3 = vec.e24 + vec.e25 + vec.e26 + vec.e27 + vec.e28 + vec.e29 + vec.e30 + vec.e31
    return s0 + s1 + s2 + s3
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS


// === FILE: stdlib/ode/bdf.sio ===
// bdf.sio - Backward Differentiation Formula (BDF) Implicit Stiff ODE Solver
//
// BDF methods for stiff systems of ODEs, orders 1-4.
// Implicit equations solved via simplified Newton iteration with
// finite-difference Jacobian approximation and Gaussian elimination.
//
// BDF-k uses k previous solution values to compute next step implicitly:
//   BDF-1 (Backward Euler): y_{n+1} = y_n + h*f(t_{n+1}, y_{n+1})
//   BDF-2: y_{n+1} = (4/3)*y_n - (1/3)*y_{n-1} + (2/3)*h*f(t_{n+1}, y_{n+1})
//   BDF-3: y_{n+1} = (18/11)*y_n - (9/11)*y_{n-1} + (2/11)*y_{n-2} + (6/11)*h*f(...)
//   BDF-4: y_{n+1} = (48/25)*y_n - (36/25)*y_{n-1} + (16/25)*y_{n-2}
//          - (3/25)*y_{n-3} + (12/25)*h*f(...)
//
// Supports systems up to 8 equations.
//
// Error estimation uses the BDF error constant (Gear's formula) applied to
// the predictor-corrector difference. Step size control follows standard
// LSODE/CVODE conventions.
//
// References:
//   Hairer, Wanner (1996) "Solving Ordinary Differential Equations II: Stiff
//     and Differential-Algebraic Problems"
//   Shampine, Reichelt (1997) "The MATLAB ODE Suite"
//   Gear (1971) "Numerical Initial Value Problems in ODEs"
//   Brenan, Campbell, Petzold (1996) "Numerical Solution of Initial-Value
//     Problems in Differential-Algebraic Equations"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS (must precede all callers)
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn bdf_max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn bdf_min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

fn bdf_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return sqrt(x)
}

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct BDFState {
    // Current solution
    y: [f64; 8],
    t: f64,
    dt: f64,
    dt_max: f64,
    n_eqs: i32,

    // History for multi-step (previous solutions)
    y_prev1: [f64; 8],
    y_prev2: [f64; 8],
    y_prev3: [f64; 8],
    n_history: i32,

    // Step control
    order: i32,
    max_order: i32,
    n_steps: i32,
    n_function_evals: i32,
    n_jac_evals: i32,

    // Tolerances
    atol: f64,
    rtol: f64,
    newton_tol: f64,
    max_newton_iter: i32
}

struct BDFResult {
    t_final: f64,
    y_final: [f64; 8],
    n_steps: i32,
    n_accepted: i32,
    n_rejected: i32,
    n_function_evals: i32,
    n_jac_evals: i32,
    success: bool
}

struct BDFTrajectory {
    times: [f64; 256],
    states: [f64; 2048],
    n_points: i32,
    n_eqs: i32
}

struct NewtonResult {
    y: [f64; 8],
    converged: bool,
    iters: i32,
    fevals: i32,
    jevals: i32
}

struct BDFStepResult {
    new_state: BDFState,
    accepted: bool
}

// ============================================================================
// RHS FUNCTIONS (test problems for stiff ODEs)
// ============================================================================

// Problem 0: Exponential decay  dy/dt = -1000*y  (single stiff equation)
fn rhs_exponential_decay(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i32, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    out[0] = 0.0 - 1000.0 * y[0]
    var k: i32 = 1
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

// Problem 1: Robertson chemical kinetics (classic stiff benchmark)
//   dy1/dt = -0.04*y1 + 1e4*y2*y3
//   dy2/dt = 0.04*y1 - 1e4*y2*y3 - 3e7*y2^2
//   dy3/dt = 3e7*y2^2
fn rhs_robertson(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i32, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    out[0] = 0.0 - 0.04 * y[0] + 10000.0 * y[1] * y[2]
    out[1] = 0.04 * y[0] - 10000.0 * y[1] * y[2] - 30000000.0 * y[1] * y[1]
    out[2] = 30000000.0 * y[1] * y[1]
    var k: i32 = 3
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

// Problem 2: Van der Pol oscillator (stiff for large mu)
//   dy1/dt = y2
//   dy2/dt = mu*(1 - y1^2)*y2 - y1,  mu = 1000
fn rhs_van_der_pol(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i32, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    let mu = 1000.0
    out[0] = y[1]
    out[1] = mu * (1.0 - y[0] * y[0]) * y[1] - y[0]
    var k: i32 = 2
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

// Problem 3: Linear stiff 2x2 system
//   dy/dt = [-1000, 0; 0, -1] * y
//   Exact: y1 = exp(-1000t), y2 = exp(-t)
fn rhs_linear_stiff(t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i32, dydt: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [f64; 8] = dydt
    out[0] = 0.0 - 1000.0 * y[0]
    out[1] = 0.0 - 1.0 * y[1]
    var k: i32 = 2
    while k < 8 {
        out[k] = 0.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    return out
}

// ============================================================================
// RHS DISPATCHER
// ============================================================================

fn eval_rhs(fn_id: i32, t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i32) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dydt: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    if fn_id == 0 {
        return rhs_exponential_decay(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    if fn_id == 1 {
        return rhs_robertson(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    if fn_id == 2 {
        return rhs_van_der_pol(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    if fn_id == 3 {
        return rhs_linear_stiff(t, y, n, dydt)
    }
    return dydt
}

// ============================================================================
// GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION (partial pivoting, up to 8x8)
// ============================================================================

fn gauss_solve_8(a: [f64; 64], b: [f64; 8], n: i32) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var aa: [f64; 64] = a
    var bb: [f64; 8] = b
    var x: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]

    // Forward elimination with partial pivoting
    var col: i32 = 0
    while col < n {
        var max_val: f64 = bdf_abs_f64(aa[col * 8 + col])
        var max_row: i32 = col
        var row: i32 = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let val = bdf_abs_f64(aa[row * 8 + col])
            if val > max_val {
                max_val = val
                max_row = row
            }
            row = row + 1
        }

        if max_row != col {
            var k: i32 = 0
            while k < n {
                let tmp_a = aa[col * 8 + k]
                aa[col * 8 + k] = aa[max_row * 8 + k]
                aa[max_row * 8 + k] = tmp_a
                k = k + 1
            }
            let tmp_b = bb[col]
            bb[col] = bb[max_row]
            bb[max_row] = tmp_b
        }

        let pivot = aa[col * 8 + col]
        if bdf_abs_f64(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            return x
        }

        row = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let factor = aa[row * 8 + col] / pivot
            var k: i32 = col + 1
            while k < n {
                aa[row * 8 + k] = aa[row * 8 + k] - factor * aa[col * 8 + k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            aa[row * 8 + col] = 0.0
            bb[row] = bb[row] - factor * bb[col]
            row = row + 1
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    // Back substitution
    var i: i32 = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum: f64 = bb[i]
        var j: i32 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum - aa[i * 8 + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = aa[i * 8 + i]
        if bdf_abs_f64(diag) < 1.0e-30 {
            x[i] = 0.0
        } else {
            x[i] = sum / diag
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// BDF PREDICTORS
// ============================================================================

fn bdf1_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = state.y[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

fn bdf2_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = 2.0 * state.y[i] - state.y_prev1[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

fn bdf3_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = 3.0 * state.y[i] - 3.0 * state.y_prev1[i] + state.y_prev2[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

fn bdf4_predict(state: BDFState) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < state.n_eqs {
        y_pred[i] = 4.0 * state.y[i] - 6.0 * state.y_prev1[i]
                     + 4.0 * state.y_prev2[i] - state.y_prev3[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y_pred
}

// ============================================================================
// BDF COEFFICIENT ACCESS
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_beta(order: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    if order == 1 { return 1.0 }
    if order == 2 { return 2.0 / 3.0 }
    if order == 3 { return 6.0 / 11.0 }
    if order == 4 { return 12.0 / 25.0 }
    return 1.0
}

// Error constant for BDF-k (Gear's formula)
fn bdf_error_constant(order: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    if order == 1 { return 0.5 }
    if order == 2 { return 2.0 / 9.0 }
    if order == 3 { return 3.0 / 22.0 }
    if order == 4 { return 12.0 / 125.0 }
    return 0.5
}

fn bdf_history_sum(state: BDFState, order: i32) -> [f64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i32 = 0

    if order == 1 {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = state.y[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else if order == 2 {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = (4.0 / 3.0) * state.y[i] - (1.0 / 3.0) * state.y_prev1[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else if order == 3 {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = (18.0 / 11.0) * state.y[i]
                 - (9.0 / 11.0) * state.y_prev1[i]
                 + (2.0 / 11.0) * state.y_prev2[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        while i < state.n_eqs {
            s[i] = (48.0 / 25.0) * state.y[i]
                 - (36.0 / 25.0) * state.y_prev1[i]
                 + (16.0 / 25.0) * state.y_prev2[i]
                 - (3.0 / 25.0) * state.y_prev3[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }
    return s
}

// ============================================================================
// FINITE-DIFFERENCE JACOBIAN APPROXIMATION
// ============================================================================

fn compute_jacobian(fn_id: i32, t: f64, y: [f64; 8], n: i32, f0: [f64; 8]) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var jac: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    let eps = 1.0e-8

    var j: i32 = 0
    while j < n {
        var y_pert: [f64; 8] = y
        let delta = eps * bdf_max_f64(bdf_abs_f64(y[j]), 1.0)
        y_pert[j] = y[j] + delta

        let f_pert = eval_rhs(fn_id, t, y_pert, n)

        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < n {
            jac[i * 8 + j] = (f_pert[i] - f0[i]) / delta
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    return jac
}

// ============================================================================
// NEWTON SOLVE FOR BDF CORRECTOR
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_newton_solve(
    fn_id: i32,
    t_new: f64,
    y_pred: [f64; 8],
    hist_sum: [f64; 8],
    beta_h: f64,
    n_eqs: i32,
    newton_tol: f64,
    max_iter: i32
) -> NewtonResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var y_k: [f64; 8] = y_pred
    var converged: bool = false
    var iters: i32 = 0
    var fevals: i32 = 0
    var jevals: i32 = 0

    let f_pred = eval_rhs(fn_id, t_new, y_pred, n_eqs)
    fevals = fevals + 1

    let jac = compute_jacobian(fn_id, t_new, y_pred, n_eqs, f_pred)
    fevals = fevals + n_eqs
    jevals = jevals + 1

    // Build iteration matrix M = I - beta*h*J
    var M: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n_eqs {
        var j: i32 = 0
        while j < n_eqs {
            let jac_val = jac[i * 8 + j]
            if i == j {
                M[i * 8 + j] = 1.0 - beta_h * jac_val
            } else {
                M[i * 8 + j] = 0.0 - beta_h * jac_val
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var iter: i32 = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        let f_k = eval_rhs(fn_id, t_new, y_k, n_eqs)
        fevals = fevals + 1

        var neg_G: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
        i = 0
        while i < n_eqs {
            neg_G[i] = 0.0 - (y_k[i] - hist_sum[i] - beta_h * f_k[i])
            i = i + 1
        }

        var g_norm: f64 = 0.0
        i = 0
        while i < n_eqs {
            g_norm = g_norm + neg_G[i] * neg_G[i]
            i = i + 1
        }
        g_norm = bdf_sqrt_f64(g_norm)

        if g_norm < newton_tol {
            converged = true
            iters = iter + 1
            return NewtonResult {
                y: y_k,
                converged: converged,
                iters: iters,
                fevals: fevals,
                jevals: jevals
            }
        }

        let delta = gauss_solve_8(M, neg_G, n_eqs)

        i = 0
        while i < n_eqs {
            y_k[i] = y_k[i] + delta[i]
            i = i + 1
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Check if final residual is small enough
    let f_final = eval_rhs(fn_id, t_new, y_k, n_eqs)
    fevals = fevals + 1
    var final_norm: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n_eqs {
        let g_i = y_k[i] - hist_sum[i] - beta_h * f_final[i]
        final_norm = final_norm + g_i * g_i
        i = i + 1
    }
    final_norm = bdf_sqrt_f64(final_norm)
    if final_norm < newton_tol * 100.0 {
        converged = true
    }

    iters = max_iter
    return NewtonResult {
        y: y_k,
        converged: converged,
        iters: iters,
        fevals: fevals,
        jevals: jevals
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ERROR ESTIMATION
// ============================================================================

fn error_norm_weighted(err: [f64; 8], y_old: [f64; 8], y_new: [f64; 8],
                       n: i32, atol: f64, rtol: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        var scale = atol + rtol * bdf_max_f64(bdf_abs_f64(y_old[i]), bdf_abs_f64(y_new[i]))
        if scale < 1.0e-30 { scale = 1.0e-30 }
        let e = err[i] / scale
        sum = sum + e * e
        i = i + 1
    }
    if n > 0 {
        return bdf_sqrt_f64(sum / (n as f64))
    }
    return 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// BDF STEP
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_step(state: BDFState, rhs_fn_id: i32) -> BDFStepResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state
    let n = s.n_eqs
    let h = s.dt
    let t_new = s.t + h

    // Determine effective order
    // Stay at BDF-1 during rapid step growth (variable step BDF-k>1
    // requires constant step size for accurate predictors)
    var eff_order: i32 = 1
    if s.order > 1 && s.n_history >= s.order - 1 {
        eff_order = s.order
    }
    if eff_order > s.n_history + 1 {
        eff_order = s.n_history + 1
    }
    if eff_order < 1 {
        eff_order = 1
    }
    if eff_order > s.max_order {
        eff_order = s.max_order
    }

    var y_pred: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    if eff_order == 1 {
        y_pred = bdf1_predict(s)
    } else if eff_order == 2 {
        y_pred = bdf2_predict(s)
    } else if eff_order == 3 {
        y_pred = bdf3_predict(s)
    } else {
        y_pred = bdf4_predict(s)
    }

    let beta = bdf_beta(eff_order)
    let beta_h = beta * h
    let hist_sum = bdf_history_sum(s, eff_order)

    let newton = bdf_newton_solve(
        rhs_fn_id, t_new, y_pred, hist_sum,
        beta_h, n, s.newton_tol, s.max_newton_iter
    )

    s.n_function_evals = s.n_function_evals + newton.fevals
    s.n_jac_evals = s.n_jac_evals + newton.jevals

    if !newton.converged {
        s.dt = s.dt * 0.25
        s.dt = bdf_max_f64(1.0e-14, s.dt)
        // Also reduce order on Newton failure
        if s.order > 1 {
            s.order = s.order - 1
        }
        return BDFStepResult { new_state: s, accepted: false }
    }

    // Error estimation using predictor-corrector difference with error constant
    // This is the standard LSODE/CVODE approach for all orders
    let err_const = bdf_error_constant(eff_order)

    var lte: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        lte[i] = err_const * (newton.y[i] - y_pred[i])
        i = i + 1
    }

    let err_n = error_norm_weighted(lte, s.y, newton.y, n, s.atol, s.rtol)

    let accepted = err_n <= 1.0

    if accepted {
        s.y_prev3 = s.y_prev2
        s.y_prev2 = s.y_prev1
        s.y_prev1 = s.y
        s.y = newton.y
        s.t = t_new
        s.n_steps = s.n_steps + 1

        if s.n_history < 3 {
            s.n_history = s.n_history + 1
        }

        // Conservative order control: only promote if error is comfortably small
        if s.n_history >= s.order && s.order < s.max_order && err_n < 0.1 {
            s.order = s.order + 1
        }

        if err_n > 1.0e-10 {
            let order_p1 = (eff_order + 1) as f64
            let factor = 0.9 * exp(log(1.0 / err_n) / order_p1)
            let factor_lim = bdf_min_f64(1.5, bdf_max_f64(0.8, factor))
            s.dt = s.dt * factor_lim
        } else {
            s.dt = s.dt * 1.5
        }
    } else {
        // Rejected: shrink step and reduce order
        if s.order > 1 {
            s.order = s.order - 1
        }
        if err_n > 1.0e-10 {
            let order_p1 = (eff_order + 1) as f64
            let factor = 0.9 * exp(log(1.0 / err_n) / order_p1)
            let factor_lim = bdf_max_f64(0.1, bdf_min_f64(0.5, factor))
            s.dt = s.dt * factor_lim
        } else {
            s.dt = s.dt * 0.5
        }
    }

    s.dt = bdf_max_f64(1.0e-14, s.dt)
    s.dt = bdf_min_f64(s.dt, s.dt_max)

    return BDFStepResult { new_state: s, accepted: accepted }
}

// ============================================================================
// INITIALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_init(n_eqs: i32, y0: [f64; 8], t0: f64, dt: f64,
            dt_max: f64, atol: f64, rtol: f64) -> BDFState {
    return BDFState {
        y: y0,
        t: t0,
        dt: dt,
        dt_max: dt_max,
        n_eqs: n_eqs,
        y_prev1: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev2: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev3: [0.0; 8],
        n_history: 0,
        order: 1,
        max_order: 4,
        n_steps: 0,
        n_function_evals: 0,
        n_jac_evals: 0,
        atol: atol,
        rtol: rtol,
        newton_tol: 1.0e-10,
        max_newton_iter: 20
    }
}

fn bdf_init_order(n_eqs: i32, y0: [f64; 8], t0: f64, dt: f64,
                  dt_max: f64, atol: f64, rtol: f64, max_order: i32) -> BDFState {
    return BDFState {
        y: y0,
        t: t0,
        dt: dt,
        dt_max: dt_max,
        n_eqs: n_eqs,
        y_prev1: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev2: [0.0; 8],
        y_prev3: [0.0; 8],
        n_history: 0,
        order: 1,
        max_order: max_order,
        n_steps: 0,
        n_function_evals: 0,
        n_jac_evals: 0,
        atol: atol,
        rtol: rtol,
        newton_tol: 1.0e-10,
        max_newton_iter: 20
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// INTEGRATION DRIVERS
// ============================================================================

fn bdf_integrate(state: BDFState, t_end: f64, rhs_fn_id: i32) -> BDFResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = state
    var n_accepted: i32 = 0
    var n_rejected: i32 = 0
    let max_total_steps: i32 = 50000

    var total_attempts: i32 = 0
    while s.t < t_end && total_attempts < max_total_steps {
        if s.t + s.dt > t_end {
            s.dt = t_end - s.t
        }
        if s.dt < 1.0e-15 {
            s.dt = 1.0e-15
        }

        let step_result = bdf_step(s, rhs_fn_id)
        s = step_result.new_state

        if step_result.accepted {
            n_accepted = n_accepted + 1
        } else {
            n_rejected = n_rejected + 1
        }

        total_attempts = total_attempts + 1
    }

    let success = s.t >= t_end - 1.0e-12

    return BDFResult {
        t_final: s.t,
        y_final: s.y,
        n_steps: s.n_steps,
        n_accepted: n_accepted,
        n_rejected: n_rejected,
        n_function_evals: s.n_function_evals,
        n_jac_evals: s.n_jac_evals,
        success: success
    }
}

fn bdf_integrate_trajectory(state: BDFState, t_end: f64, rhs_fn_id: i32) -> BDFTrajectory with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var traj = BDFTrajectory {
        times: [0.0; 256],
        states: [0.0; 2048],
        n_points: 0,
        n_eqs: state.n_eqs
    }

    var s = state

    traj.times[0] = s.t
    var k: i32 = 0
    while k < s.n_eqs {
        traj.states[0 * 8 + k] = s.y[k]
        k = k + 1
    }
    traj.n_points = 1

    let max_total_steps: i32 = 50000
    var total_attempts: i32 = 0

    while s.t < t_end && total_attempts < max_total_steps && traj.n_points < 256 {
        if s.t + s.dt > t_end {
            s.dt = t_end - s.t
        }
        if s.dt < 1.0e-15 {
            s.dt = 1.0e-15
        }

        let step_result = bdf_step(s, rhs_fn_id)
        s = step_result.new_state

        if step_result.accepted {
            let idx = traj.n_points
            traj.times[idx] = s.t
            k = 0
            while k < s.n_eqs {
                traj.states[idx * 8 + k] = s.y[k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            traj.n_points = traj.n_points + 1
        }

        total_attempts = total_attempts + 1
    }

    return traj
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ode/epistemic_pk_fit.sio ===
// stdlib/ode/epistemic_pk_fit.sio — Closed-Form PK Parameter Inference with GUM Uncertainty
//
// 1-compartment pharmacokinetic model with first-order absorption (closed form):
//   C(t) = (dose * ka) / (Vd * (ka - ke)) * (exp(-ke*t) - exp(-ka*t))
//
// Fitting uses Gauss-Newton nonlinear least squares with forward-mode AD
// (EpistemicDual) for exact Jacobians. Parameter uncertainties come from
// the Fisher information matrix (Type A GUM §5.1).
//
// References:
//   JCGM 100:2008: "Evaluation of measurement data" (GUM)
//   Rowland & Tozer (2011) "Clinical Pharmacokinetics" 5th ed. §2
//   Nocedal & Wright (2006) "Numerical Optimization" §10.3

use autodiff::epistemic_dual::{
    EpistemicDual,
    edual_new, edual_const,
    edual_add, edual_sub, edual_mul, edual_div,
    edual_scale, edual_exp,
}

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn pk_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn pk_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// =============================================================================
// Data types
// =============================================================================

pub struct PKFitResult {
    ka: f64,
    u_ka: f64,
    ka_lo95: f64,
    ka_hi95: f64,
    ke: f64,
    u_ke: f64,
    ke_lo95: f64,
    ke_hi95: f64,
    rms_residual: f64,
    sens_ka_pct: f64,
    sens_ke_pct: f64,
    converged: i32,
    iterations: i32,
}

// =============================================================================
// 1-compartment PK model with EpistemicDual parameters
// =============================================================================
//
// C(t) = (dose * ka) / (Vd * (ka - ke)) * (exp(-ke*t) - exp(-ka*t))
//
// To get dC/dka: seed ka.dot=1.0, ke.dot=0.0
// To get dC/dke: seed ka.dot=0.0, ke.dot=1.0
// Output .dot is the requested partial derivative

fn pk_conc_dual(t: f64, ka: EpistemicDual, ke: EpistemicDual,
                dose: f64, vd: f64) -> EpistemicDual with Div, Panic {
    // num = dose * ka
    let num = edual_scale(ka, dose)
    // denom = Vd * (ka - ke)
    let denom = edual_scale(edual_sub(ka, ke), vd)
    // factor = dose*ka / (Vd*(ka-ke))
    let factor = edual_div(num, denom)
    // Compute exp(-ke*t) = 1/exp(ke*t) to avoid Taylor series for negative args
    let one = edual_const(1.0)
    let exp_ke_pos = edual_exp(edual_scale(ke, t))
    let exp_ka_pos = edual_exp(edual_scale(ka, t))
    let exp_ke = edual_div(one, exp_ke_pos)
    let exp_ka = edual_div(one, exp_ka_pos)
    // C = factor * (exp(-ke*t) - exp(-ka*t))
    edual_mul(factor, edual_sub(exp_ke, exp_ka))
}

// =============================================================================
// Gauss-Newton fitting (6 observations, 2 parameters: ka, ke)
// =============================================================================
//
// Normal equations (2x2):
//   [A  B] [Δka]   [g1]
//   [B  D] [Δke] = [g2]
//
// where A = Σ Jka²/σ², B = Σ Jka*Jke/σ², D = Σ Jke²/σ²
//       g1 = Σ Jka*r/σ²,  g2 = Σ Jke*r/σ²,  r = C_pred - C_obs
//
// Analytical 2x2 inversion: det = A*D - B*B

pub fn epistemic_pk_gauss_newton(
    obs_t: [f64; 6],
    obs_c: [f64; 6],
    obs_u: [f64; 6],
    dose: f64,
    vd: f64,
    ka_init: f64,
    ke_init: f64,
) -> PKFitResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let k95 = 1.96
    let max_iter = 50
    let tol = 1.0e-7

    var ka = ka_init
    var ke = ke_init
    var iter = 0
    var converged = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // --- build normal matrix ---
        var big_a: f64 = 0.0
        var big_b: f64 = 0.0
        var big_d: f64 = 0.0
        var g1: f64 = 0.0
        var g2: f64 = 0.0

        var i = 0
        while i < 6 {
            let t = obs_t[i]
            let c_obs = obs_c[i]
            let sigma = obs_u[i]
            let w = 1.0 / (sigma * sigma)

            // J_ka = dC/dka  (seed ka.dot=1, ke.dot=0)
            let ka_d_ka = edual_new(ka, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            let ke_d_ka = edual_new(ke, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            let c_for_ka = pk_conc_dual(t, ka_d_ka, ke_d_ka, dose, vd)
            let j_ka = c_for_ka.dot
            let c_pred = c_for_ka.val

            // J_ke = dC/dke  (seed ka.dot=0, ke.dot=1)
            let ka_d_ke = edual_new(ka, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            let ke_d_ke = edual_new(ke, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            let c_for_ke = pk_conc_dual(t, ka_d_ke, ke_d_ke, dose, vd)
            let j_ke = c_for_ke.dot

            let r = c_pred - c_obs

            big_a = big_a + j_ka * j_ka * w
            big_b = big_b + j_ka * j_ke * w
            big_d = big_d + j_ke * j_ke * w
            g1 = g1 + j_ka * r * w
            g2 = g2 + j_ke * r * w

            i = i + 1
        }

        // --- invert 2x2 and compute step ---
        let det = big_a * big_d - big_b * big_b
        if pk_abs(det) < 1.0e-15 {
            // singular — stop
            iter = max_iter
        } else {
            var d_ka = (0.0 - (big_d * g1 - big_b * g2)) / det
            var d_ke = (0.0 - (0.0 - big_b * g1 + big_a * g2)) / det

            // Trust region: cap step size to prevent divergence when far from solution
            let step_raw = pk_abs(d_ka) + pk_abs(d_ke)
            let max_step = 0.5
            if step_raw > max_step {
                let scale = max_step / step_raw
                d_ka = d_ka * scale
                d_ke = d_ke * scale
            }

            ka = ka + d_ka
            ke = ke + d_ke

            // guard: rates must be positive
            if ka < 1.0e-4 { ka = 1.0e-4 }
            if ke < 1.0e-4 { ke = 1.0e-4 }
            // prevent ka == ke (formula singular); nudge ke slightly
            if pk_abs(ka - ke) < 1.0e-4 { ke = ke + 0.01 }

            let step_norm = pk_abs(d_ka) + pk_abs(d_ke)
            if step_norm < tol {
                converged = 1
                iter = max_iter
            }
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // --- compute residual RMS and final Jacobian at converged params ---
    var sum_r2: f64 = 0.0
    var fin_a: f64 = 0.0
    var fin_b: f64 = 0.0
    var fin_d: f64 = 0.0
    var last_j_ka: f64 = 0.0
    var last_j_ke: f64 = 0.0
    var last_c_pred: f64 = 0.0

    var j = 0
    while j < 6 {
        let t = obs_t[j]
        let c_obs = obs_c[j]
        let sigma = obs_u[j]
        let w = 1.0 / (sigma * sigma)

        let ka_d = edual_new(ka, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        let ke_d = edual_new(ke, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        let out_ka = pk_conc_dual(t, ka_d, ke_d, dose, vd)
        let jka = out_ka.dot
        let cpred = out_ka.val

        let ka_d2 = edual_new(ka, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        let ke_d2 = edual_new(ke, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        let out_ke = pk_conc_dual(t, ka_d2, ke_d2, dose, vd)
        let jke = out_ke.dot

        let r = cpred - c_obs
        sum_r2 = sum_r2 + r * r
        fin_a = fin_a + jka * jka * w
        fin_b = fin_b + jka * jke * w
        fin_d = fin_d + jke * jke * w

        last_j_ka = jka
        last_j_ke = jke
        last_c_pred = cpred

        j = j + 1
    }

    let rms = pk_sqrt(sum_r2 / 6.0)

    // --- parameter uncertainties from Fisher information (GUM Type A) ---
    // σ²_fit = rms² (already per observation)
    let sigma2_fit = rms * rms
    let det_fin = fin_a * fin_d - fin_b * fin_b
    var u_ka: f64 = 0.0
    var u_ke: f64 = 0.0
    if pk_abs(det_fin) > 1.0e-15 {
        let cov_ka = fin_d / det_fin * sigma2_fit
        let cov_ke = fin_a / det_fin * sigma2_fit
        u_ka = pk_sqrt(pk_abs(cov_ka))
        u_ke = pk_sqrt(pk_abs(cov_ke))
    }

    // --- sensitivity at last time point (t=12h, index 5) ---
    // u²(C_pred) = Jka² * u²(ka) + Jke² * u²(ke)
    let u2_c = last_j_ka * last_j_ka * u_ka * u_ka + last_j_ke * last_j_ke * u_ke * u_ke
    var sens_ka: f64 = 50.0
    var sens_ke: f64 = 50.0
    if u2_c > 1.0e-30 {
        sens_ka = last_j_ka * last_j_ka * u_ka * u_ka / u2_c * 100.0
        sens_ke = last_j_ke * last_j_ke * u_ke * u_ke / u2_c * 100.0
    }

    PKFitResult {
        ka: ka,
        u_ka: u_ka,
        ka_lo95: ka - k95 * u_ka,
        ka_hi95: ka + k95 * u_ka,
        ke: ke,
        u_ke: u_ke,
        ke_lo95: ke - k95 * u_ke,
        ke_hi95: ke + k95 * u_ke,
        rms_residual: rms,
        sens_ka_pct: sens_ka,
        sens_ke_pct: sens_ke,
        converged: converged,
        iterations: max_iter,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_pk_conc_dual() with Div, Panic {
    // At t=2h, ka=0.5, ke=0.2, dose=100, Vd=10:
    // C = (100*0.5)/(10*(0.5-0.2)) * (exp(-0.4) - exp(-1.0))
    //   = 50/3 * (0.6703 - 0.3679) = 16.667 * 0.3024 ≈ 5.04 mg/L
    let ka = edual_new(0.5, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let ke = edual_new(0.2, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    let c = pk_conc_dual(2.0, ka, ke, 100.0, 10.0)
    assert(c.val > 4.5 && c.val < 5.5)
    // Jacobian dC/dka should be nonzero
    assert(pk_abs(c.dot) > 0.1)
}

fn test_pk_gauss_newton_converges() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // True params: ka=0.5, ke=0.2, Vd=10, dose=100
    // Exact formula values with alternating ±5% noise:
    // C(0.5)=2.101 +5%→2.206  C(1.0)=3.537 -5%→3.360
    // C(2.0)=5.041 +5%→5.293  C(4.0)=5.233 -5%→4.971
    // C(8.0)=3.060 +5%→3.213  C(12.0)=1.465 -5%→1.392
    let obs_t: [f64; 6] = [0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0, 12.0]
    let obs_c: [f64; 6] = [2.206, 3.360, 5.293, 4.971, 3.213, 1.392]
    let obs_u: [f64; 6] = [0.110, 0.177, 0.252, 0.261, 0.153, 0.073]

    let result = epistemic_pk_gauss_newton(
        obs_t, obs_c, obs_u,
        100.0, 10.0,
        0.6, 0.25,   // initial guesses (1.2x true values)
    )

    // Convergence
    assert(result.converged == 1)

    // Parameter recovery within 20% relative error
    let ka_err = pk_abs(result.ka - 0.5) / 0.5
    let ke_err = pk_abs(result.ke - 0.2) / 0.2
    assert(ka_err < 0.20)
    assert(ke_err < 0.20)

    // Fitted params within 3σ of true values
    assert(pk_abs(result.ka - 0.5) < 3.0 * result.u_ka + 0.01)
    assert(pk_abs(result.ke - 0.2) < 3.0 * result.u_ke + 0.01)

    // Sensitivities sum to ~100%
    let sens_sum = result.sens_ka_pct + result.sens_ke_pct
    assert(sens_sum > 95.0 && sens_sum < 105.0)
}

pub fn epistemic_pk_fit_main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    test_pk_conc_dual()
    test_pk_gauss_newton_converges()
    println("PASS: epistemic PK fitting")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ode/epistemic_pkpd_fit.sio ===
// stdlib/ode/epistemic_pkpd_fit.sio — Epistemic PK/PD Link Model Inference
//
// Sequential fitting of a full pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model
// with GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation from dose to clinical effect:
//
//   PK: C(t) = (dose*ka) / (Vd*(ka-ke)) * (exp(-ke*t) - exp(-ka*t))
//   PD: E(t) = Emax * C(t) / (EC50 + C(t))           [Emax/Hill model]
//
// Fitting algorithm:
//   Step 1 — Fit {ka, ke} from plasma concentration data (Gauss-Newton)
//   Step 2 — Propagate PK uncertainty into predicted C(t) via EpistemicDual
//   Step 3 — Fit {Emax, EC50} from observed effect data (Gauss-Newton on Emax model)
//   Step 4 — Propagate ALL uncertainties into predicted E(t) via sensitivity coefficients
//
// Output: parameter estimates with GUM 95% CI + sensitivity analysis showing
// which parameter drives therapeutic uncertainty at peak effect time.
//
// Scientific significance: first closed-form PK/PD inference with full
// GUM §5.1 uncertainty chain from measurement to therapeutic decision.
//
// References:
//   Holford & Sheiner (1981) "Understanding the dose-effect relationship" ClinPharmacokinet
//   JCGM 100:2008 §5.1: Law of propagation of uncertainty
//   Rowland & Tozer (2011) "Clinical Pharmacokinetics" Ch.8

use ode::epistemic_pk_fit::{PKFitResult, epistemic_pk_gauss_newton}
use autodiff::epistemic_dual::{
    EpistemicDual,
    edual_new, edual_const,
    edual_add, edual_sub, edual_mul, edual_div, edual_scale, edual_exp,
}

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn pd_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn pd_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// Numerically stable exp(-t) via 1/exp(t)
fn pd_exp_neg(t: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let one = edual_const(1.0)
    let epos = edual_exp(edual_new(t, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
    edual_div(one, epos).val
}

// =============================================================================
// PK concentration (scalar, using fitted params)
// =============================================================================

fn pk_conc(t: f64, ka: f64, ke: f64, dose: f64, vd: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if pd_abs(ka - ke) < 1.0e-6 { return 0.0 }
    let f = dose * ka / (vd * (ka - ke))
    f * (pd_exp_neg(ke * t) - pd_exp_neg(ka * t))
}

// PK concentration with EpistemicDual propagation of ka and ke uncertainty
fn pk_conc_epis(t: f64, ka: EpistemicDual, ke: EpistemicDual,
                dose: f64, vd: f64) -> EpistemicDual with Div, Panic {
    let num = edual_scale(ka, dose)
    let denom = edual_scale(edual_sub(ka, ke), vd)
    let factor = edual_div(num, denom)
    let one = edual_const(1.0)
    let exp_ke_pos = edual_exp(edual_scale(ke, t))
    let exp_ka_pos = edual_exp(edual_scale(ka, t))
    let exp_ke = edual_div(one, exp_ke_pos)
    let exp_ka = edual_div(one, exp_ka_pos)
    edual_mul(factor, edual_sub(exp_ke, exp_ka))
}

// =============================================================================
// Emax/Hill pharmacodynamic model
// =============================================================================
//
// E(C) = Emax * C / (EC50 + C)
//
// Jacobians (analytic):
//   dE/dEmax = C / (EC50 + C)
//   dE/dEC50 = -Emax * C / (EC50 + C)^2
//   dE/dC    = Emax * EC50 / (EC50 + C)^2

fn emax_pred(c: f64, emax: f64, ec50: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    emax * c / (ec50 + c)
}

fn emax_j_emax(c: f64, ec50: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    c / (ec50 + c)
}

fn emax_j_ec50(c: f64, emax: f64, ec50: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let denom = ec50 + c
    0.0 - emax * c / (denom * denom)
}

fn emax_j_c(c: f64, emax: f64, ec50: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let denom = ec50 + c
    emax * ec50 / (denom * denom)
}

// =============================================================================
// Emax Gauss-Newton fitter (6 observations, params: Emax, EC50)
//
// We fit E_obs[i] ~ Emax * C_pred[i] / (EC50 + C_pred[i])
// where C_pred[i] are the PK-model predictions at obs times.
// =============================================================================

fn epistemic_emax_gauss_newton(
    obs_c: [f64; 6],    // predicted concentrations at 6 time points
    obs_e: [f64; 6],    // observed effects
    obs_eu: [f64; 6],   // uncertainty in effect observations
    emax_init: f64,
    ec50_init: f64,
) -> [f64; 6] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Returns [emax, u_emax, ec50, u_ec50, rms, converged_flag]
    let k95 = 1.96
    let max_iter = 60
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    var emax = emax_init
    var ec50 = ec50_init
    var converged = 0.0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        var big_a: f64 = 0.0
        var big_b: f64 = 0.0
        var big_d: f64 = 0.0
        var g1: f64 = 0.0
        var g2: f64 = 0.0

        var i = 0
        while i < 6 {
            let c = obs_c[i]
            let e_obs = obs_e[i]
            let sigma = obs_eu[i]
            let w = 1.0 / (sigma * sigma)

            let je = emax_j_emax(c, ec50)
            let jc = emax_j_ec50(c, emax, ec50)
            let e_pred = emax_pred(c, emax, ec50)
            let r = e_pred - e_obs

            big_a = big_a + je * je * w
            big_b = big_b + je * jc * w
            big_d = big_d + jc * jc * w
            g1 = g1 + je * r * w
            g2 = g2 + jc * r * w

            i = i + 1
        }

        let det = big_a * big_d - big_b * big_b
        if pd_abs(det) < 1.0e-20 {
            iter = max_iter
        } else {
            var d_emax = (0.0 - (big_d * g1 - big_b * g2)) / det
            var d_ec50 = (0.0 - (0.0 - big_b * g1 + big_a * g2)) / det

            let step = pd_abs(d_emax) + pd_abs(d_ec50)
            if step > 0.5 {
                let scale = 0.5 / step
                d_emax = d_emax * scale
                d_ec50 = d_ec50 * scale
            }

            emax = emax + d_emax
            ec50 = ec50 + d_ec50

            if emax < 1.0e-4 { emax = 1.0e-4 }
            if ec50 < 1.0e-4 { ec50 = 1.0e-4 }

            let norm = pd_abs(d_emax) + pd_abs(d_ec50)
            if norm < tol {
                converged = 1.0
                iter = max_iter
            }
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Compute residual and Fisher information at convergence
    var sum_r2: f64 = 0.0
    var fin_a: f64 = 0.0
    var fin_b: f64 = 0.0
    var fin_d: f64 = 0.0

    var j = 0
    while j < 6 {
        let c = obs_c[j]
        let e_obs = obs_e[j]
        let sigma = obs_eu[j]
        let w = 1.0 / (sigma * sigma)
        let je = emax_j_emax(c, ec50)
        let jc = emax_j_ec50(c, emax, ec50)
        let r = emax_pred(c, emax, ec50) - e_obs
        sum_r2 = sum_r2 + r * r
        fin_a = fin_a + je * je * w
        fin_b = fin_b + je * jc * w
        fin_d = fin_d + jc * jc * w
        j = j + 1
    }

    let rms = pd_sqrt(sum_r2 / 6.0)
    let sigma2_fit = rms * rms
    let det_fin = fin_a * fin_d - fin_b * fin_b
    var u_emax = 0.0
    var u_ec50 = 0.0
    if pd_abs(det_fin) > 1.0e-20 {
        u_emax = pd_sqrt(pd_abs(fin_d / det_fin * sigma2_fit))
        u_ec50 = pd_sqrt(pd_abs(fin_a / det_fin * sigma2_fit))
    }

    // Return as flat array: [emax, u_emax, ec50, u_ec50, rms, converged]
    [emax, u_emax, ec50, u_ec50, rms, converged]
}

// =============================================================================
// Result type
// =============================================================================

pub struct PKPDFitResult {
    // PK parameters
    ka: f64,
    u_ka: f64,
    ka_lo95: f64,
    ka_hi95: f64,
    ke: f64,
    u_ke: f64,
    ke_lo95: f64,
    ke_hi95: f64,
    rms_pk: f64,
    // PD parameters
    emax: f64,
    u_emax: f64,
    emax_lo95: f64,
    emax_hi95: f64,
    ec50: f64,
    u_ec50: f64,
    ec50_lo95: f64,
    ec50_hi95: f64,
    rms_pd: f64,
    // Effect prediction at peak (t=4h for this model)
    e_peak: f64,
    u_e_peak: f64,
    // Sensitivity: which param drives most of u(E_peak)?
    sens_ka_pct: f64,
    sens_ke_pct: f64,
    sens_emax_pct: f64,
    sens_ec50_pct: f64,
    // Convergence
    converged_pk: i32,
    converged_pd: i32,
}

// =============================================================================
// Main entry: sequential PK/PD fitting
// =============================================================================

pub fn epistemic_pkpd_fit(
    obs_t: [f64; 6],
    obs_c: [f64; 6],
    obs_cu: [f64; 6],
    obs_e: [f64; 6],
    obs_eu: [f64; 6],
    dose: f64,
    vd: f64,
    ka_init: f64,
    ke_init: f64,
    emax_init: f64,
    ec50_init: f64,
) -> PKPDFitResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let k95 = 1.96

    // --- Step 1: Fit PK ---
    let pk = epistemic_pk_gauss_newton(
        obs_t, obs_c, obs_cu, dose, vd, ka_init, ke_init
    )

    // --- Step 2: Compute C_pred(t) with uncertainty from (ka, ke) ---
    var c_pred: [f64; 6] = [0.0; 6]
    var i = 0
    while i < 6 {
        c_pred[i] = pk_conc(obs_t[i], pk.ka, pk.ke, dose, vd)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // --- Step 3: Fit PD (Emax model) ---
    let pd_out = epistemic_emax_gauss_newton(
        c_pred, obs_e, obs_eu, emax_init, ec50_init
    )
    let emax = pd_out[0]
    let u_emax = pd_out[1]
    let ec50 = pd_out[2]
    let u_ec50 = pd_out[3]
    let rms_pd = pd_out[4]
    let conv_pd = pd_out[5]

    // --- Step 4: Sensitivity analysis at peak (t=4h, index 3) ---
    // u²(E_peak) = (dE/dka)²u²(ka) + (dE/dke)²u²(ke) + (dE/dEmax)²u²(Emax) + (dE/dEC50)²u²(EC50)
    //
    // dE/dka  = (dE/dC) * (dC/dka)   — chain rule via EpistemicDual
    // dE/dke  = (dE/dC) * (dC/dke)
    // dE/dEmax = C / (EC50 + C)
    // dE/dEC50 = -Emax * C / (EC50 + C)^2

    let t_peak = obs_t[3]   // t=4h

    // Get dC/dka and dC/dke at t_peak via forward-mode AD
    let c_dka = pk_conc_epis(t_peak,
        edual_new(pk.ka, 1.0, pk.u_ka, 0.0),
        edual_new(pk.ke, 0.0, pk.u_ke, 0.0),
        dose, vd)
    let c_dke = pk_conc_epis(t_peak,
        edual_new(pk.ka, 0.0, pk.u_ka, 0.0),
        edual_new(pk.ke, 1.0, pk.u_ke, 0.0),
        dose, vd)

    let c_pk = c_dka.val
    let dc_dka = c_dka.dot
    let dc_dke = c_dke.dot

    // dE/dC at fitted params
    let de_dc = emax_j_c(c_pk, emax, ec50)

    // Sensitivity coefficients
    let de_dka = de_dc * dc_dka
    let de_dke = de_dc * dc_dke
    let de_demax = emax_j_emax(c_pk, ec50)
    let de_dec50 = emax_j_ec50(c_pk, emax, ec50)

    // Variance contributions
    let v_ka = de_dka * de_dka * pk.u_ka * pk.u_ka
    let v_ke = de_dke * de_dke * pk.u_ke * pk.u_ke
    let v_emax = de_demax * de_demax * u_emax * u_emax
    let v_ec50 = de_dec50 * de_dec50 * u_ec50 * u_ec50
    let v_total = v_ka + v_ke + v_emax + v_ec50

    let e_peak = emax_pred(c_pk, emax, ec50)
    let u_e_peak = pd_sqrt(v_total)

    var s_ka = 25.0; var s_ke = 25.0; var s_emax = 25.0; var s_ec50 = 25.0
    if v_total > 1.0e-30 {
        s_ka   = v_ka   / v_total * 100.0
        s_ke   = v_ke   / v_total * 100.0
        s_emax = v_emax / v_total * 100.0
        s_ec50 = v_ec50 / v_total * 100.0
    }

    let conv_pd_i32 = if conv_pd > 0.5 { 1 } else { 0 }

    PKPDFitResult {
        ka: pk.ka, u_ka: pk.u_ka,
        ka_lo95: pk.ka - k95 * pk.u_ka, ka_hi95: pk.ka + k95 * pk.u_ka,
        ke: pk.ke, u_ke: pk.u_ke,
        ke_lo95: pk.ke - k95 * pk.u_ke, ke_hi95: pk.ke + k95 * pk.u_ke,
        rms_pk: pk.rms_residual,
        emax: emax, u_emax: u_emax,
        emax_lo95: emax - k95 * u_emax, emax_hi95: emax + k95 * u_emax,
        ec50: ec50, u_ec50: u_ec50,
        ec50_lo95: ec50 - k95 * u_ec50, ec50_hi95: ec50 + k95 * u_ec50,
        rms_pd: rms_pd,
        e_peak: e_peak, u_e_peak: u_e_peak,
        sens_ka_pct: s_ka, sens_ke_pct: s_ke,
        sens_emax_pct: s_emax, sens_ec50_pct: s_ec50,
        converged_pk: pk.converged,
        converged_pd: conv_pd_i32,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_emax_model_basics() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // E(C=3, Emax=1, EC50=3) = 0.5 (by definition of EC50)
    let e = emax_pred(3.0, 1.0, 3.0)
    assert(pd_abs(e - 0.5) < 0.001)
    // Jacobian dE/dC at C=3, EC50=3, Emax=1: = Emax*EC50/(EC50+C)^2 = 3/36 = 1/12
    let j = emax_j_c(3.0, 1.0, 3.0)
    assert(pd_abs(j - 1.0/12.0) < 0.001)
}

fn test_pkpd_fit_converges() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // True: ka=0.5, ke=0.2, Vd=10, dose=100, Emax=1.0, EC50=3.0
    // Concentration data (5% alternating noise):
    let obs_t: [f64; 6] = [0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0, 12.0]
    let obs_c: [f64; 6] = [2.206, 3.360, 5.293, 4.971, 3.213, 1.392]
    let obs_cu: [f64; 6] = [0.110, 0.177, 0.252, 0.261, 0.153, 0.073]
    // Effect data (3% alternating noise on true E values):
    // E_true ≈ [0.412, 0.541, 0.627, 0.636, 0.505, 0.329]
    let obs_e: [f64; 6] = [0.424, 0.514, 0.646, 0.604, 0.520, 0.319]
    let obs_eu: [f64; 6] = [0.012, 0.016, 0.019, 0.019, 0.015, 0.010]

    let result = epistemic_pkpd_fit(
        obs_t, obs_c, obs_cu, obs_e, obs_eu,
        100.0, 10.0,
        0.6, 0.25,   // PK init (1.2x true)
        1.2, 3.6,    // PD init (1.2x true)
    )

    // PK convergence
    assert(result.converged_pk == 1)
    // PD convergence
    assert(result.converged_pd == 1)
    // PK recovery within 15%
    assert(pd_abs(result.ka - 0.5) / 0.5 < 0.15)
    assert(pd_abs(result.ke - 0.2) / 0.2 < 0.15)
    // PD recovery within 15%
    assert(pd_abs(result.emax - 1.0) / 1.0 < 0.15)
    assert(pd_abs(result.ec50 - 3.0) / 3.0 < 0.15)
    // Sensitivities sum to ~100%
    let sens_sum = result.sens_ka_pct + result.sens_ke_pct +
                   result.sens_emax_pct + result.sens_ec50_pct
    assert(sens_sum > 95.0 && sens_sum < 105.0)
}

pub fn epistemic_pkpd_fit_main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    test_emax_model_basics()
    test_pkpd_fit_converges()
    println("PASS: epistemic PK/PD fitting")
}


// === FILE: stdlib/ode/epistemic.sio ===
// stdlib/ode/epistemic.sio — Epistemic ODE Solver
//
// ODE integration that propagates uncertainty through time steps.
// Every state variable carries its standard uncertainty and confidence.
// Uncertainty grows with each step; confidence never increases.
//
// This is the ODE solver that scientific computing SHOULD have:
// after integrating, you know not just the solution but HOW UNCERTAIN
// each state is and HOW CONFIDENT you can be in the result.
//
// Implements:
//   - Epistemic RK4 (4th-order Runge-Kutta with uncertainty propagation)
//   - GUM-compliant linearized uncertainty propagation
//   - Step-size-dependent confidence degradation
//   - Adaptive uncertainty monitoring
//
// References:
//   Butcher (2008): "Numerical Methods for ODEs"
//   GUM JCGM 100:2008: "Evaluation of measurement data"
//   Hairer et al. (1993): "Solving ODEs I: Nonstiff Problems"

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_ode(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn abs_ode(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn min_ode(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

fn max_ode(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { a } else { b }
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic State Vector
// =============================================================================

struct EpistemicState {
    values: [f64; 16],          // state variables (max 16 dimensions)
    uncertainties: [f64; 16],   // standard uncertainty per component
    confidences: [f64; 16],     // confidence per component [0, 1]
    n_dims: i32,
    time: f64,
}

fn estate_new(n: i32) -> EpistemicState {
    EpistemicState {
        values: [0.0; 16],
        uncertainties: [0.0; 16],
        confidences: [1.0; 16],
        n_dims: n,
        time: 0.0,
    }
}

fn estate_set(s: &!EpistemicState, idx: i32, val: f64, unc: f64, conf: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    s.values[idx] = val
    s.uncertainties[idx] = unc
    s.confidences[idx] = conf
}

// =============================================================================
// Derivative with Uncertainty
// =============================================================================
// The derivative function returns both the derivative value AND
// the sensitivity (Jacobian diagonal) for uncertainty propagation.

struct DerivResult {
    deriv: [f64; 16],           // dy/dt for each component
    sensitivity: [f64; 16],     // |df_i/dy_i| for uncertainty propagation
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic RK4 Step
// =============================================================================
// Standard RK4 for the values, with linearized GUM propagation for uncertainty.
//
// Uncertainty propagation rule:
//   u(y_{n+1})^2 = u(y_n)^2 + dt^2 * |df/dy|^2 * u(y_n)^2 + u_trunc^2
//   where u_trunc = O(dt^5) is the local truncation error estimate
//
// Confidence degradation:
//   conf(y_{n+1}) = conf(y_n) * (1 - epsilon)
//   where epsilon depends on the relative uncertainty growth

// For a simple single-step demonstration with inline derivative:
// This computes RK4 for a general system where derivative values are
// provided externally (since Sounio doesn't support function pointers).

struct RK4EpistemicConfig {
    dt: f64,
    n_steps: i32,
    confidence_decay_rate: f64,  // per-step confidence decay (e.g., 0.001)
    max_relative_uncertainty: f64, // stop if u/|y| exceeds this
}

fn rk4_epistemic_config_default() -> RK4EpistemicConfig {
    RK4EpistemicConfig {
        dt: 0.01,
        n_steps: 1000,
        confidence_decay_rate: 0.001,
        max_relative_uncertainty: 0.5,  // 50% relative uncertainty = stop
    }
}

// Single RK4 step with uncertainty propagation
// k1..k4 are the RK4 derivative evaluations at the 4 stages
// sens is the sensitivity (|df/dy|) at the current state
fn epistemic_rk4_step(
    state: &!EpistemicState,
    k1: &[f64; 16],
    k2: &[f64; 16],
    k3: &[f64; 16],
    k4: &[f64; 16],
    sens: &[f64; 16],
    dt: f64,
    conf_decay: f64,
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < state.n_dims {
        // Standard RK4 update
        let dy = dt / 6.0 * (k1[i] + 2.0 * k2[i] + 2.0 * k3[i] + k4[i])
        state.values[i] = state.values[i] + dy

        // Uncertainty propagation (GUM linearization)
        // u_{n+1}^2 = u_n^2 * (1 + dt * |df/dy|)^2 + truncation_error^2
        let growth_factor = 1.0 + dt * abs_ode(sens[i])
        let u_propagated = state.uncertainties[i] * growth_factor

        // Truncation error estimate: O(dt^5) ~ |k4 - k3| * dt / 6
        let u_trunc = abs_ode(k4[i] - k3[i]) * dt / 6.0

        state.uncertainties[i] = sqrt_ode(u_propagated * u_propagated + u_trunc * u_trunc)

        // Confidence degrades monotonically
        let rel_growth = if abs_ode(state.values[i]) > 1.0e-30 {
            state.uncertainties[i] / abs_ode(state.values[i])
        } else {
            0.0
        }
        // Faster decay for larger relative uncertainty
        let effective_decay = conf_decay * (1.0 + 10.0 * rel_growth)
        state.confidences[i] = state.confidences[i] * (1.0 - effective_decay)

        i = i + 1
    }
    state.time = state.time + dt
}

// =============================================================================
// Simple Exponential Decay: dy/dt = -lambda * y
// =============================================================================
// Exact solution: y(t) = y0 * exp(-lambda * t)
// This serves as a test case and demonstration.

// Compute one RK4 step of exponential decay and update state.
// Returns (updated_value, relative_uncertainty) so caller doesn't
// need to re-read from state (avoids ownership conflicts in loops).
fn exp_decay_step(
    state: &!EpistemicState,
    lambda: f64,
    y: f64,
    dt: f64,
    conf_decay: f64,
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var k1: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    k1[0] = 0.0 - lambda * y

    var k2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    k2[0] = 0.0 - lambda * (y + dt / 2.0 * k1[0])

    var k3: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    k3[0] = 0.0 - lambda * (y + dt / 2.0 * k2[0])

    var k4: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    k4[0] = 0.0 - lambda * (y + dt * k3[0])

    var sens: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    sens[0] = lambda

    epistemic_rk4_step(state, &k1, &k2, &k3, &k4, &sens, dt, conf_decay)

    // Return updated value so caller can track it without re-reading state
    state.values[0]
}

// Create an initialized epistemic state for 1D exponential decay
fn estate_init_1d(y0: f64, u0: f64) -> EpistemicState with Mut, Panic {
    var s = estate_new(1)
    s.values[0] = y0
    s.uncertainties[0] = u0
    s.confidences[0] = 1.0
    s
}

fn exp_decay_epistemic(
    y0: f64,
    u0: f64,           // initial uncertainty
    lambda: f64,
    config: &RK4EpistemicConfig,
) -> EpistemicState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize using combined constructor to avoid double &! borrow
    var state = estate_init_1d(y0, u0)

    // Track value externally to avoid shared/exclusive borrow conflicts in loop
    var y = y0
    var step = 0
    while step < config.n_steps {
        let dt = config.dt
        // Perform RK4 step (only exclusive borrow of state in this loop body)
        y = exp_decay_step(&!state, lambda, y, dt, config.confidence_decay_rate)
        step = step + 1
    }
    state
}

// =============================================================================
// Integration Summary
// =============================================================================

struct IntegrationSummary {
    final_time: f64,
    n_steps_taken: i32,
    min_confidence: f64,
    max_relative_uncertainty: f64,
    converged: bool,
}

fn integration_summary(state: &EpistemicState, n_steps: i32) -> IntegrationSummary with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var min_conf: f64 = 1.0
    var max_rel: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < state.n_dims {
        min_conf = min_ode(min_conf, state.confidences[i])
        let val = abs_ode(state.values[i])
        if val > 1.0e-30 {
            let rel = state.uncertainties[i] / val
            max_rel = max_ode(max_rel, rel)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    IntegrationSummary {
        final_time: state.time,
        n_steps_taken: n_steps,
        min_confidence: min_conf,
        max_relative_uncertainty: max_rel,
        converged: max_rel < 0.1,  // less than 10% relative uncertainty
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/ode/rk4.sio ===
// rk4.d - Classic 4th-order Runge-Kutta ODE Solver for Sounio
//
// Fixed-step RK4 method. Simple, robust, but requires user to specify step size.
// Use when you need predictable timing or when Tsit5's adaptivity isn't needed.
//
// Note: Due to compiler limitations with nested function calls, state is wrapped
// in structs for proper loop iteration behavior.
//
// Reference: Standard RK4 method (Kutta 1901)

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// SCALAR ODE STATE
// ============================================================================

struct ScalarState {
    u: f64,
    t: f64
}

struct ScalarStepResult {
    state_new: ScalarState
}

struct RK4Solution {
    t_final: f64,
    u_final: f64,
    nsteps: i64,
    nfeval: i64
}

// Example ODE: exponential decay du/dt = -k*u
fn exp_decay_f(u: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let k = 0.1
    return 0.0 - k * u
}

// Single RK4 step for scalar ODE du/dt = f(u, t)
fn rk4_step_scalar(s: ScalarState, dt: f64) -> ScalarStepResult {
    let u = s.u
    let t = s.t
    let k1 = exp_decay_f(u, t)
    let k2 = exp_decay_f(u + 0.5 * dt * k1, t + 0.5 * dt)
    let k3 = exp_decay_f(u + 0.5 * dt * k2, t + 0.5 * dt)
    let k4 = exp_decay_f(u + dt * k3, t + dt)
    let u_new = u + (dt / 6.0) * (k1 + 2.0 * k2 + 2.0 * k3 + k4)
    return ScalarStepResult {
        state_new: ScalarState { u: u_new, t: t + dt }
    }
}

fn solve_rk4_scalar(u0: f64, t0: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i64) -> RK4Solution {
    let dt = (t_end - t0) / (n_steps as f64)
    var s = ScalarState { u: u0, t: t0 }
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n_steps {
        let result = rk4_step_scalar(s, dt)
        s = result.state_new
        i = i + 1
    }

    return RK4Solution {
        t_final: s.t,
        u_final: s.u,
        nsteps: n_steps,
        nfeval: n_steps * 4
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 3-COMPARTMENT PK MODEL (matching tsit5_multicomp.d)
// ============================================================================

struct PKState3 {
    gut: f64,
    central: f64,
    periph: f64,
    t: f64
}

struct PKDeriv3 {
    d_gut: f64,
    d_central: f64,
    d_periph: f64
}

struct PKParams3 {
    ka: f64,
    ke: f64,
    k12: f64,
    k21: f64
}

struct PKStepResult3 {
    state_new: PKState3
}

fn default_pk3_params() -> PKParams3 {
    return PKParams3 {
        ka: 1.5,
        ke: 0.1,
        k12: 0.3,
        k21: 0.15
    }
}

fn pk3_ode(gut: f64, central: f64, periph: f64, t: f64, p: PKParams3) -> PKDeriv3 {
    return PKDeriv3 {
        d_gut: 0.0 - p.ka * gut,
        d_central: p.ka * gut - p.ke * central - p.k12 * central + p.k21 * periph,
        d_periph: p.k12 * central - p.k21 * periph
    }
}

fn rk4_step_pk3(s: PKState3, dt: f64, p: PKParams3) -> PKStepResult3 {
    let t = s.t

    // Stage 1
    let k1 = pk3_ode(s.gut, s.central, s.periph, t, p)

    // Stage 2
    let gut2 = s.gut + 0.5 * dt * k1.d_gut
    let central2 = s.central + 0.5 * dt * k1.d_central
    let periph2 = s.periph + 0.5 * dt * k1.d_periph
    let k2 = pk3_ode(gut2, central2, periph2, t + 0.5 * dt, p)

    // Stage 3
    let gut3 = s.gut + 0.5 * dt * k2.d_gut
    let central3 = s.central + 0.5 * dt * k2.d_central
    let periph3 = s.periph + 0.5 * dt * k2.d_periph
    let k3 = pk3_ode(gut3, central3, periph3, t + 0.5 * dt, p)

    // Stage 4
    let gut4 = s.gut + dt * k3.d_gut
    let central4 = s.central + dt * k3.d_central
    let periph4 = s.periph + dt * k3.d_periph
    let k4 = pk3_ode(gut4, central4, periph4, t + dt, p)

    // Combine
    let gut_new = s.gut + (dt / 6.0) * (k1.d_gut + 2.0*k2.d_gut + 2.0*k3.d_gut + k4.d_gut)
    let central_new = s.central + (dt / 6.0) * (k1.d_central + 2.0*k2.d_central + 2.0*k3.d_central + k4.d_central)
    let periph_new = s.periph + (dt / 6.0) * (k1.d_periph + 2.0*k2.d_periph + 2.0*k3.d_periph + k4.d_periph)

    return PKStepResult3 {
        state_new: PKState3 {
            gut: gut_new,
            central: central_new,
            periph: periph_new,
            t: t + dt
        }
    }
}

struct RK4SolutionPK3 {
    t_final: f64,
    gut: f64,
    central: f64,
    periph: f64,
    nsteps: i64,
    nfeval: i64
}

fn solve_rk4_pk3(s0: PKState3, p: PKParams3, t_end: f64, n_steps: i64) -> RK4SolutionPK3 {
    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    var s = s0
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n_steps {
        let result = rk4_step_pk3(s, dt, p)
        s = result.state_new
        i = i + 1
    }

    return RK4SolutionPK3 {
        t_final: s.t,
        gut: s.gut,
        central: s.central,
        periph: s.periph,
        nsteps: n_steps,
        nfeval: n_steps * 4
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ANALYTICAL SOLUTION FOR VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

fn exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let x2 = x * x
    let x3 = x2 * x
    let x4 = x3 * x
    let x5 = x4 * x
    let x6 = x5 * x
    let x7 = x6 * x
    let x8 = x7 * x
    return 1.0 + x + x2/2.0 + x3/6.0 + x4/24.0 + x5/120.0 + x6/720.0 + x7/5040.0 + x8/40320.0
}

fn exp_decay_analytical(u0: f64, k: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    return u0 * exp_approx(0.0 - k * t)
}

// solver.sio - Generic ODE Solver API for Sounio
//
// Provides a unified solve() interface for ordinary differential equations:
//   dy/dt = f(t, y),  y(t0) = y0
//
// Supports multiple methods:
// - RK4: Fixed-step 4th-order Runge-Kutta
// - RK45: Adaptive Dormand-Prince 5(4) method
// - Tsit5: Tsitouras 5(4) adaptive method
//
// Reference: Hairer, Norsett, Wanner - "Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I"

// ============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// Fifth root for step size control (order p=5)
fn pow_1_5(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = 1.0
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    y = y - (y * y * y * y * y - x) / (5.0 * y * y * y * y)
    return y
}

    /// Relative tolerance (default: 1e-4)
    rtol: f64,
    /// Absolute tolerance (default: 1e-7)
    atol: f64,
    /// Initial step size (0 = auto)
    dt_init: f64,
    /// Minimum step size
    dt_min: f64,
    /// Maximum step size
    dt_max: f64,
    /// Maximum number of steps
    max_steps: i64,
    /// Safety factor for step control (default: 0.9)
    safety: f64,
    /// Maximum step growth factor (default: 10.0)
    max_growth: f64,
    /// Minimum step shrink factor (default: 0.2)
    min_shrink: f64
}

    return ODEOptions {
        rtol: 0.0001,
        atol: 0.0000001,
        dt_init: 0.0,
        dt_min: 0.000000000001,
        dt_max: 1000000.0,
        max_steps: 1000000,
        safety: 0.9,
        max_growth: 10.0,
        min_shrink: 0.2
    }
}

        max_steps: 10000000,
        safety: 0.9,
        max_growth: 5.0,

// ============================================================================
// STEP RESULT TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct RK45StepResult {
    u_new: f64,
    err: f64
}

struct RK45StepResultVec3 {
    u1_new: f64,
    u2_new: f64,
    u3_new: f64,
    err: f64
}

// ============================================================================
// GENERIC SOLVE API FOR SCALAR ODE
// ============================================================================

// Solve scalar ODE using RK45 (Dormand-Prince 5(4)) with adaptive stepping
//
// Parameters:
// - f_eval: User provides ODE function value at (t, u)
// - u0: Initial condition
// - t_span_start: Start time
// - t_span_end: End time
// - opts: Solver options
//
// The user must provide the ODE system via a specific function pattern.
// For custom ODEs, create wrapper functions that match the interface.

// Example ODE: Exponential decay du/dt = -k*u
fn ode_exp_decay(u: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    let k = 0.1
    return 0.0 - k * u
}

// Single RK45 step for exponential decay
fn rk45_step_exp_decay(u: f64, t: f64, dt: f64) -> RK45StepResult {
    // Stage 1
    let k1 = ode_exp_decay(u, t)

    // Stage 2
    let u2 = u + dt * dp_a21() * k1
    let k2 = ode_exp_decay(u2, t + dp_c2() * dt)

    // Stage 3
    let u3 = u + dt * (dp_a31() * k1 + dp_a32() * k2)
    let k3 = ode_exp_decay(u3, t + dp_c3() * dt)

    // Stage 4
    let u4 = u + dt * (dp_a41() * k1 + dp_a42() * k2 + dp_a43() * k3)
    let k4 = ode_exp_decay(u4, t + dp_c4() * dt)

    // Stage 5
    let u5 = u + dt * (dp_a51() * k1 + dp_a52() * k2 + dp_a53() * k3 + dp_a54() * k4)
    let k5 = ode_exp_decay(u5, t + dp_c5() * dt)

    // Stage 6
    let u6 = u + dt * (dp_a61() * k1 + dp_a62() * k2 + dp_a63() * k3 + dp_a64() * k4 + dp_a65() * k5)
    let k6 = ode_exp_decay(u6, t + dp_c6() * dt)

    // 5th order solution
    let u_new = u + dt * (dp_b1() * k1 + dp_b3() * k3 + dp_b4() * k4 + dp_b5() * k5 + dp_b6() * k6)

    // Stage 7 for error estimate (FSAL property)
    let k7 = ode_exp_decay(u_new, t + dt)

    // Error estimate
    let err_raw = dt * (dp_e1() * k1 + dp_e3() * k3 + dp_e4() * k4 + dp_e5() * k5 + dp_e6() * k6 + dp_e7() * k7)

    return RK45StepResult { u_new: u_new, err: abs_f64(err_raw) }
}

// Compute optimal step size based on error
fn compute_optimal_step(dt: f64, err_norm: f64, opts: ODEOptions) -> f64 {
    if err_norm <= 0.0 {
        return dt * opts.max_growth
    }
    let factor = opts.safety * pow_1_5(1.0 / err_norm)
    let factor_limited = max_f64(opts.min_shrink, min_f64(opts.max_growth, factor))
    return dt * factor_limited
}

// Solve exponential decay ODE using RK45
fn solve_rk45_exp_decay(u0: f64, t_start: f64, t_end: f64, opts: ODEOptions) -> SolverODESolution {
    var u = u0
    var t = t_start

    // Initialize step size
    var dt = opts.dt_init
    if dt <= 0.0 {
        let f0 = abs_f64(ode_exp_decay(u0, t_start))
        let scale = opts.atol + opts.rtol * abs_f64(u0)
        let dt_est = scale / max_f64(f0, 0.0000000001)
        dt = min_f64(0.01 * (t_end - t_start), dt_est)
    }
    dt = max_f64(opts.dt_min, min_f64(opts.dt_max, dt))

    var nsteps: i64 = 0
    var nfeval: i64 = 1
    var nreject: i64 = 0
    var status: i64 = 0

    while t < t_end && nsteps < opts.max_steps {
        // Don't overshoot
        let dt_use = if t + dt > t_end { t_end - t } else { dt }

        // Take step
        let result = rk45_step_exp_decay(u, t, dt_use)
        nfeval = nfeval + 7

        // Error norm
        let scale = opts.atol + opts.rtol * max_f64(abs_f64(u), abs_f64(result.u_new))
        let err_norm = result.err / scale

        if err_norm <= 1.0 {
            // Accept step
            t = t + dt_use
            u = result.u_new
            nsteps = nsteps + 1
            dt = compute_optimal_step(dt_use, err_norm, opts)
        } else {
            // Reject step
            nreject = nreject + 1
            dt = compute_optimal_step(dt_use, err_norm, opts)
        }

        // Enforce limits
        dt = max_f64(opts.dt_min, min_f64(opts.dt_max, dt))

        // Check for step size too small
        if dt < opts.dt_min * 2.0 {
            status = 2
        }
    }

    if nsteps >= opts.max_steps {
        status = 1
    }

    return SolverODESolution {
        success: t >= t_end - opts.dt_min,
        nsteps: nsteps,
        nfeval: nfeval,
        nreject: nreject,
        t_final: t,
        u_final: u,
        status: status
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FIXED-STEP RK4 SOLVER
// ============================================================================

// Single RK4 step for exponential decay
fn rk4_step_exp_decay(u: f64, t: f64, dt: f64) -> f64 {
    let k1 = ode_exp_decay(u, t)
    let k2 = ode_exp_decay(u + 0.5 * dt * k1, t + 0.5 * dt)
    let k3 = ode_exp_decay(u + 0.5 * dt * k2, t + 0.5 * dt)
    let k4 = ode_exp_decay(u + dt * k3, t + dt)
    return u + (dt / 6.0) * (k1 + 2.0 * k2 + 2.0 * k3 + k4)
}

// Solve exponential decay using fixed-step RK4
fn solve_rk4_exp_decay(u0: f64, t_start: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i64) -> SolverODESolution {
    let dt = (t_end - t_start) / (n_steps as f64)
    var u = u0
    var t = t_start
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n_steps {
        u = rk4_step_exp_decay(u, t, dt)
        t = t + dt
        i = i + 1
    }

    return SolverODESolution {
        success: true,
        nsteps: n_steps,
        nfeval: n_steps * 4,
        nreject: 0,
        t_final: t,
        u_final: u,
        status: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 3-COMPONENT VECTOR ODE SOLVER (for systems like 3-compartment PK)
// ============================================================================

// State for 3-component ODE system
struct State3 {
    u1: f64,
    u2: f64,
    u3: f64,
    t: f64
}

// Derivative for 3-component system
struct Deriv3 {
    du1: f64,
    du2: f64,
    du3: f64
}

// Parameters for 3-compartment PK model
struct SolverPKParams3 {
    ka: f64,   // Absorption rate (gut -> central)
    ke: f64,   // Elimination rate (central -> eliminated)
    k12: f64,  // Transfer rate (central -> peripheral)
    k21: f64   // Transfer rate (peripheral -> central)
}

fn solver_default_pk3_params() -> SolverPKParams3 {
    return SolverPKParams3 {
        ka: 1.5,
        ke: 0.1,
        k12: 0.3,
        k21: 0.15
    }
}

// 3-compartment PK ODE system
fn ode_pk3(s: State3, p: SolverPKParams3) -> Deriv3 {
    return Deriv3 {
        du1: 0.0 - p.ka * s.u1,  // Gut: absorption only
        du2: p.ka * s.u1 - p.ke * s.u2 - p.k12 * s.u2 + p.k21 * s.u3,  // Central
        du3: p.k12 * s.u2 - p.k21 * s.u3  // Peripheral
    }
}

// RK4 step for 3-component PK system
fn solver_rk4_step_pk3(s: State3, dt: f64, p: SolverPKParams3) -> State3 {
    // Stage 1
    let k1 = ode_pk3(s, p)

    // Stage 2
    let s2 = State3 {
        u1: s.u1 + 0.5 * dt * k1.du1,
        u2: s.u2 + 0.5 * dt * k1.du2,
        u3: s.u3 + 0.5 * dt * k1.du3,
        t: s.t + 0.5 * dt
    }
    let k2 = ode_pk3(s2, p)

    // Stage 3
    let s3 = State3 {
        u1: s.u1 + 0.5 * dt * k2.du1,
        u2: s.u2 + 0.5 * dt * k2.du2,
        u3: s.u3 + 0.5 * dt * k2.du3,
        t: s.t + 0.5 * dt
    }
    let k3 = ode_pk3(s3, p)

    // Stage 4
    let s4 = State3 {
        u1: s.u1 + dt * k3.du1,
        u2: s.u2 + dt * k3.du2,
        u3: s.u3 + dt * k3.du3,
        t: s.t + dt
    }
    let k4 = ode_pk3(s4, p)

    // Combine
    return State3 {
        u1: s.u1 + (dt / 6.0) * (k1.du1 + 2.0*k2.du1 + 2.0*k3.du1 + k4.du1),
        u2: s.u2 + (dt / 6.0) * (k1.du2 + 2.0*k2.du2 + 2.0*k3.du2 + k4.du2),
        u3: s.u3 + (dt / 6.0) * (k1.du3 + 2.0*k3.du3 + 2.0*k3.du3 + k4.du3),
        t: s.t + dt
    }
}

// Solve 3-compartment PK model with RK4
fn solve_pk3_rk4(s0: State3, p: SolverPKParams3, t_end: f64, n_steps: i64) -> ODESolutionVec3 {
    let dt = (t_end - s0.t) / (n_steps as f64)
    var s = s0
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n_steps {
        s = solver_rk4_step_pk3(s, dt, p)
        i = i + 1
    }

    return ODESolutionVec3 {
        success: true,
        nsteps: n_steps,
        nfeval: n_steps * 4,
        nreject: 0,
        t_final: s.t,
        u1_final: s.u1,
        u2_final: s.u2,
        u3_final: s.u3,
        status: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STIFF SOLVER: BACKWARD EULER (BDF1)
// ============================================================================

// Backward Euler step for exponential decay (analytically solved)
// For du/dt = -k*u, implicit: u_{n+1} = u_n / (1 + k*dt)
fn backward_euler_step_exp_decay(u: f64, dt: f64, k: f64) -> f64 {
    return u / (1.0 + k * dt)
}

// Solve exponential decay using Backward Euler (L-stable for stiff)
fn solve_bdf1_exp_decay(u0: f64, t_start: f64, t_end: f64, n_steps: i64) -> SolverODESolution {
    let k = 0.1  // Decay constant
    let dt = (t_end - t_start) / (n_steps as f64)
    var u = u0
    var t = t_start
    var i: i64 = 0

    while i < n_steps {
        u = backward_euler_step_exp_decay(u, dt, k)
        t = t + dt
        i = i + 1
    }

    return SolverODESolution {
        success: true,
        nsteps: n_steps,
        nfeval: n_steps,
        nreject: 0,
        t_final: t,
        u_final: u,
        status: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ANALYTICAL SOLUTIONS FOR VALIDATION
// ============================================================================

fn solver_exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 20.0 { return solver_exp_approx(x / 2.0) * solver_exp_approx(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / solver_exp_approx(0.0 - x) }

    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    term = term * x / 1.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 2.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 3.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 4.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 5.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 6.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 7.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 8.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 9.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 10.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 11.0
    sum = sum + term
    term = term * x / 12.0
    sum = sum + term
    return sum
}

fn solver_exp_decay_analytical(u0: f64, k: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    return u0 * solver_exp_approx(0.0 - k * t)
}
