fn bg_yellow() with IO { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_blue() with IO { print("\x1b[44m") }
fn bg_magenta() with IO { print("\x1b[45m") }
fn bg_cyan() with IO { print("\x1b[46m") }
fn bg_white() with IO { print("\x1b[47m") }

// ============================================================================
// COLOR MAPPING: Value → Color
// ============================================================================

// Map a normalized value [0.0, 1.0] to a traffic-light color
// 0.0 = green (good), 0.5 = yellow (caution), 1.0 = red (danger)
fn traffic_color(normalized: f64) with IO {
    if normalized < 0.3 {
        green()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.3 && normalized < 0.6 {
        yellow()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.6 {
        red()
    }
}

// Map a normalized value [0.0, 1.0] to a blue-red gradient
// 0.0 = blue (cold), 0.5 = white, 1.0 = red (hot)
fn heatmap_color(normalized: f64) with IO {
    if normalized < 0.25 {
        blue()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.25 && normalized < 0.5 {
        cyan()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.5 && normalized < 0.75 {
        yellow()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.75 {
        red()
    }
}

// Map a normalized value [0.0, 1.0] to a background heatmap color
fn heatmap_bg(normalized: f64) with IO {
    if normalized < 0.25 {
        bg_blue()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.25 && normalized < 0.5 {
        bg_cyan()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.5 && normalized < 0.75 {
        bg_yellow()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.75 {
        bg_red()
    }
}

// Map confidence level to color (epistemic)
// High confidence = green, low = red
fn confidence_color(confidence: f64) with IO {
    if confidence >= 0.95 {
        bright_green()
    }
    if confidence >= 0.8 && confidence < 0.95 {
        green()
    }
    if confidence >= 0.5 && confidence < 0.8 {
        yellow()
    }
    if confidence < 0.5 {
        red()
    }
}

// Map uncertainty to background intensity
fn uncertainty_bg(uncertainty: f64, max_uncertainty: f64) with IO, Panic {
    let normalized = uncertainty / max_uncertainty
    if normalized < 0.3 {
        bg_green()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.3 && normalized < 0.6 {
        bg_yellow()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.6 {
        bg_red()
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/plot/epistemic.sio ===
// Epistemic Visualization: Uncertainty and Confidence Display
//
// Specialized plot functions for Knowledge<T> types:
// - Error bars showing uncertainty ranges
// - Confidence color-coded bars
// - Provenance chain display
// - Uncertainty comparison tables
// - Temporal decay visualization

// ============================================================================
// ERROR BAR TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct ErrorBarEntry {
    label: string,
    value: f64,
    uncertainty: f64,   // +/- range (1 sigma)
    confidence: f64,    // [0.0, 1.0]
}

fn error_bar_entry(label: string, value: f64, uncertainty: f64, confidence: f64) -> ErrorBarEntry {
    ErrorBarEntry {
        label: label,
        value: value,
        uncertainty: uncertainty,
        confidence: confidence,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ERROR BAR CHART
// ============================================================================

// Horizontal bar chart with error bars showing uncertainty
fn error_bar_chart(entries: &[ErrorBarEntry], n: i64, title: string) with Mut, Panic, Div, IO {
    if n <= 0 { return }

    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    // Find max value + uncertainty for scaling
    var max_val = 0.0
    var max_label_len: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let upper = entries[i as usize].value + entries[i as usize].uncertainty
        if upper > max_val { max_val = upper }
        let label_len = entries[i as usize].label.len() as i64
        if label_len > max_label_len { max_label_len = label_len }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if max_val <= 0.0 { max_val = 1.0 }

    let width: i64 = 40

    // Title
    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
        println("")
    }

    // Render entries
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let entry = entries[i as usize]
        let bar_len = (entry.value / max_val * width as f64) as i64
        let err_lower = ((entry.value - entry.uncertainty) / max_val * width as f64) as i64
        let err_upper = ((entry.value + entry.uncertainty) / max_val * width as f64) as i64

        // Label
        let padding = max_label_len - entry.label.len() as i64
        var p: i64 = 0
        while p < padding {
            print(" ")
            p = p + 1
        }
        print(entry.label)
        print(" │ ")

        // Confidence-colored bar
        if entry.confidence >= 0.95 {
            print("\x1b[92m")  // bright green
        }
        if entry.confidence >= 0.8 && entry.confidence < 0.95 {
            print("\x1b[32m")  // green
        }
        if entry.confidence >= 0.5 && entry.confidence < 0.8 {
            print("\x1b[33m")  // yellow
        }
        if entry.confidence < 0.5 {
            print("\x1b[31m")  // red
        }

        // Draw bar with error range
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < width {
            if col < err_lower {
                print(" ")
            }
            if col >= err_lower && col < bar_len {
                if col >= err_lower && col < bar_len {
                    print("▓")
                }
            }
            if col == bar_len {
                print("│")  // center mark
            }
            if col > bar_len && col <= err_upper {
                print("░")
            }
            if col > err_upper {
                print(" ")
            }
            col = col + 1
        }

        print(reset)

        // Value +/- uncertainty
        print(" ")
        print_f64_ep(entry.value, 2)
        print(" ± ")
        print_f64_ep(entry.uncertainty, 2)

        // Confidence badge
        print(" [")
        if entry.confidence >= 0.95 {
            print("\x1b[92m")
        }
        if entry.confidence >= 0.8 && entry.confidence < 0.95 {
            print("\x1b[32m")
        }
        if entry.confidence >= 0.5 && entry.confidence < 0.8 {
            print("\x1b[33m")
        }
        if entry.confidence < 0.5 {
            print("\x1b[31m")
        }
        print_f64_ep(entry.confidence * 100.0, 0)
        print("%")
        print(reset)
        print("]")

        println("")
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CONFIDENCE GAUGE
// ============================================================================

// Visual confidence gauge: ████████░░ 80%
fn confidence_gauge(label: string, confidence: f64, width: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    print("  ")
    print(label)
    print(": ")

    let filled = (confidence * width as f64) as i64
    let empty = width - filled

    // Color based on confidence
    if confidence >= 0.95 { print("\x1b[92m") }
    if confidence >= 0.8 && confidence < 0.95 { print("\x1b[32m") }
    if confidence >= 0.5 && confidence < 0.8 { print("\x1b[33m") }
    if confidence < 0.5 { print("\x1b[31m") }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < filled {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)
    print("\x1b[2m")
    i = 0
    while i < empty {
        print("░")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)

    print(" ")
    print_f64_ep(confidence * 100.0, 1)
    print("%")
    println("")
}

// Multiple confidence gauges stacked
fn confidence_dashboard(
    labels: &[string],
    confidences: &[f64],
    n: i64,
    title: string,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
        println("")
    }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        confidence_gauge(labels[i as usize], confidences[i as usize], 30)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// UNCERTAINTY DECOMPOSITION CHART
// ============================================================================

// Visualize uncertainty breakdown: statistical + identification + structural
fn uncertainty_decomposition(
    stat: f64,
    identification: f64,
    structural: f64,
    total: f64,
    title: string,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"
    let width: i64 = 40

    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
    }

    println("")
    println("  Uncertainty Decomposition (GUM)")
    println("  ─────────────────────────────────────")

    // Normalize to total for proportional bars
    let max_comp = if stat > identification {
        if stat > structural { stat } else { structural }
    } else {
        if identification > structural { identification } else { structural }
    }
    let scale = if max_comp > 0.0 { max_comp } else { 1.0 }

    // Statistical
    print("  Statistical:     ")
    print("\x1b[36m")  // cyan
    let stat_len = (stat / scale * width as f64) as i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < stat_len {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)
    print(" ")
    print_f64_ep(stat, 4)
    println("")

    // Identification
    print("  Identification:  ")
    print("\x1b[33m")  // yellow
    let id_len = (identification / scale * width as f64) as i64
    i = 0
    while i < id_len {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)
    print(" ")
    print_f64_ep(identification, 4)
    println("")

    // Structural
    print("  Structural:      ")
    print("\x1b[35m")  // magenta
    let struct_len = (structural / scale * width as f64) as i64
    i = 0
    while i < struct_len {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)
    print(" ")
    print_f64_ep(structural, 4)
    println("")

    println("  ─────────────────────────────────────")

    // Total
    print("  Total (GUM):     ")
    print("\x1b[1m\x1b[37m")
    let total_len = (total / scale * width as f64) as i64
    i = 0
    while i < total_len {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)
    print(" ")
    print_f64_ep(total, 4)
    println("")
}

// ============================================================================
// PROVENANCE CHAIN DISPLAY
// ============================================================================

// Display a provenance chain as a vertical timeline
struct ProvenanceStep {
    operation: string,
    source: string,
    uncertainty_before: f64,
    uncertainty_after: f64,
}

fn provenance_step(op: string, src: string, unc_before: f64, unc_after: f64) -> ProvenanceStep {
    ProvenanceStep {
        operation: op,
        source: src,
        uncertainty_before: unc_before,
        uncertainty_after: unc_after,
    }
}

fn provenance_chain(steps: &[ProvenanceStep], n: i64, title: string) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
    }

    println("")
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let step = steps[i as usize]

        // Step indicator
        if i == 0 {
            print("  ◉ ")  // origin
        } else {
            print("  ├─")
        }

        // Operation
        print("\x1b[1m")
        print(step.operation)
        print(reset)

        // Source
        print(" (")
        print("\x1b[2m")
        print(step.source)
        print(reset)
        print(")")

        println("")

        // Uncertainty change
        if i > 0 {
            print("  │  ε: ")
            print_f64_ep(step.uncertainty_before, 4)
            print(" → ")

            // Color based on direction
            if step.uncertainty_after > step.uncertainty_before {
                print("\x1b[31m")  // red = increased
            } else {
                print("\x1b[32m")  // green = decreased
            }
            print_f64_ep(step.uncertainty_after, 4)
            print(reset)
            println("")
        } else {
            print("  │  ε: ")
            print_f64_ep(step.uncertainty_after, 4)
            println("")
        }

        // Connector
        if i < n - 1 {
            println("  │")
        } else {
            println("  ╰─ [current]")
        }

        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TEMPORAL DECAY VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

// Show how confidence decays over time
fn temporal_decay(
    timestamps: &[f64],
    confidences: &[f64],
    n: i64,
    title: string,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
    }

    println("")
    let width: i64 = 40

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let t = timestamps[i as usize]
        let c = confidences[i as usize]

        // Timestamp
        print("  t=")
        print_f64_ep(t, 1)
        print("  ")

        // Confidence bar
        let filled = (c * width as f64) as i64

        if c >= 0.8 { print("\x1b[32m") }
        if c >= 0.5 && c < 0.8 { print("\x1b[33m") }
        if c < 0.5 { print("\x1b[31m") }

        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < filled {
            print("█")
            j = j + 1
        }
        print(reset)

        j = filled
        while j < width {
            print("░")
            j = j + 1
        }

        print(" ")
        print_f64_ep(c * 100.0, 1)
        print("%")

        // Decay warning
        if c < 0.5 {
            print(" ⚠")
        }
        if c < 0.2 {
            print(" STALE")
        }

        println("")
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn print_f64_ep(value: f64, decimals: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let int_part = value as i64
    let frac = value - int_part as f64
    let frac_abs = if frac < 0.0 { -frac } else { frac }
    if value < 0.0 && int_part == 0 { print("-") }
    print(int_part)

    if decimals > 0 {
        print(".")
        var d: i64 = 0
        var remaining = frac_abs
        while d < decimals {
            remaining = remaining * 10.0
            let digit = remaining as i64
            print(digit)
            remaining = remaining - digit as f64
            d = d + 1
        }
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/plot/heatmap.sio ===
// 2D Heatmap Rendering
//
// Grid-based heatmaps using Unicode block characters and ANSI colors.
// Supports:
// - Float matrices
// - Custom color scales
// - Row/column labels
// - Color legend

// ============================================================================
// HEATMAP TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct HeatmapConfig {
    title: string,
    cell_width: i64,      // characters per cell (1=compact, 2=normal, 3=wide)
    show_values: bool,    // show numeric values in cells
    show_legend: bool,    // show color scale legend
    color_scale: i64,     // 0=blue-red, 1=grayscale, 2=green-red
}

fn heatmap_config_default() -> HeatmapConfig {
    HeatmapConfig {
        title: "",
        cell_width: 2,
        show_values: false,
        show_legend: true,
        color_scale: 0,
    }
}

fn heatmap_config_new(title: string) -> HeatmapConfig {
    HeatmapConfig {
        title: title,
        cell_width: 2,
        show_values: false,
        show_legend: true,
        color_scale: 0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HEATMAP RENDERING
// ============================================================================

// Render a 2D matrix as a heatmap
// data: row-major array
// rows: number of rows
// cols: number of columns
fn heatmap(data: &[f64], rows: i64, cols: i64, title: string) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let config = heatmap_config_new(title)
    heatmap_matrix(data, rows, cols, &config)
}

fn heatmap_matrix(
    data: &[f64],
    rows: i64,
    cols: i64,
    config: &HeatmapConfig,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    if rows <= 0 || cols <= 0 { return }

    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    // Find range
    var min_val = data[0]
    var max_val = data[0]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < rows * cols {
        if data[i as usize] < min_val { min_val = data[i as usize] }
        if data[i as usize] > max_val { max_val = data[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let range = max_val - min_val
    if range <= 0.0 { return }

    // Title
    if config.title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(config.title)
        print(reset)
        println("")
    }

    // Top border
    print("    ┌")
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < cols * config.cell_width {
        print("─")
        c = c + 1
    }
    println("┐")

    // Render rows
    var r: i64 = 0
    while r < rows {
        // Row label
        print_row_label(r, 4)
        print("│")

        c = 0
        while c < cols {
            let idx = r * cols + c
            let normalized = (data[idx as usize] - min_val) / range

            // Apply color
            heatmap_cell_color(normalized, config.color_scale)

            // Cell content
            if config.cell_width == 1 {
                print(shade_char_hm(normalized))
            }
            if config.cell_width >= 2 {
                print(shade_char_hm(normalized))
                print(shade_char_hm(normalized))
            }
            if config.cell_width >= 3 {
                print(shade_char_hm(normalized))
            }

            print(reset)
            c = c + 1
        }

        println("│")
        r = r + 1
    }

    // Bottom border
    print("    └")
    c = 0
    while c < cols * config.cell_width {
        print("─")
        c = c + 1
    }
    println("┘")

    // Legend
    if config.show_legend {
        println("")
        print("    ")
        print_heatmap_legend(min_val, max_val, config.color_scale)
        println("")
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// LABELED HEATMAP
// ============================================================================

// Heatmap with row and column labels
fn heatmap_labeled(
    data: &[f64],
    rows: i64,
    cols: i64,
    row_labels: &[string],
    col_labels: &[string],
    title: string,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    if rows <= 0 || cols <= 0 { return }

    // Find max label width
    var max_label: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < rows {
        let l = row_labels[i as usize].len() as i64
        if l > max_label { max_label = l }
        i = i + 1
    }
    max_label = max_label + 1

    // Find range
    var min_val = data[0]
    var max_val = data[0]
    i = 0
    while i < rows * cols {
        if data[i as usize] < min_val { min_val = data[i as usize] }
        if data[i as usize] > max_val { max_val = data[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let range = if max_val > min_val { max_val - min_val } else { 1.0 }

    // Title
    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
    }

    // Column headers
    var pad: i64 = 0
    while pad < max_label + 1 {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad + 1
    }
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < cols {
        print(" ")
        print(col_labels[c as usize])
        c = c + 1
    }
    println("")

    // Rows
    var r: i64 = 0
    while r < rows {
        // Label with padding
        let label = row_labels[r as usize]
        let lpad = max_label - label.len() as i64
        var p: i64 = 0
        while p < lpad {
            print(" ")
            p = p + 1
        }
        print(label)
        print(" ")

        c = 0
        while c < cols {
            let idx = r * cols + c
            let normalized = (data[idx as usize] - min_val) / range

            heatmap_cell_color(normalized, 0)
            print(shade_char_hm(normalized))
            print(shade_char_hm(normalized))
            print(reset)
            c = c + 1
        }
        println("")
        r = r + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CORRELATION MATRIX
// ============================================================================

// Specialized heatmap for correlation matrices [-1, 1]
fn correlation_matrix(
    data: &[f64],
    n: i64,
    labels: &[string],
    title: string,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    if title.len() > 0 {
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(title)
        print(reset)
    }

    // Find max label width
    var max_label: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let l = labels[i as usize].len() as i64
        if l > max_label { max_label = l }
        i = i + 1
    }
    max_label = max_label + 1

    // Column headers
    var pad: i64 = 0
    while pad < max_label + 1 {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad + 1
    }
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < n {
        print("  ")
        // Truncate label to 2 chars
        if labels[c as usize].len() >= 2 {
            print(labels[c as usize][0])
            print(labels[c as usize][1])
        } else {
            print(labels[c as usize])
            print(" ")
        }
        c = c + 1
    }
    println("")

    // Rows
    var r: i64 = 0
    while r < n {
        let label = labels[r as usize]
        let lpad = max_label - label.len() as i64
        var p: i64 = 0
        while p < lpad {
            print(" ")
            p = p + 1
        }
        print(label)
        print(" ")

        c = 0
        while c < n {
            let val = data[(r * n + c) as usize]
            // Map [-1, 1] to [0, 1] for coloring
            let normalized = (val + 1.0) / 2.0

            // Blue for negative, red for positive
            if val < -0.3 {
                print("\x1b[34m")  // blue
            }
            if val >= -0.3 && val < 0.3 {
                print("\x1b[37m")  // white/neutral
            }
            if val >= 0.3 {
                print("\x1b[31m")  // red
            }

            // Print value as 2-char
            if val >= 0.0 { print(" ") } else { print("-") }
            let abs_val = if val < 0.0 { -val } else { val }
            let d1 = (abs_val * 10.0) as i64
            print(".")
            print(d1)

            print(reset)
            c = c + 1
        }
        println("")
        r = r + 1
    }

    // Legend
    println("")
    print("  ")
    print("\x1b[34m")
    print("████")
    print(reset)
    print(" -1.0  ")
    print("\x1b[37m")
    print("████")
    print(reset)
    print("  0.0  ")
    print("\x1b[31m")
    print("████")
    print(reset)
    print(" +1.0")
    println("")
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn shade_char_hm(normalized: f64) -> string {
    if normalized <= 0.0 { return " " }
    if normalized < 0.25 { return "░" }
    if normalized < 0.5 { return "▒" }
    if normalized < 0.75 { return "▓" }
    "█"
}

fn heatmap_cell_color(normalized: f64, scale: i64) with IO {
    if scale == 0 {
        // Blue-red scale
        if normalized < 0.25 { print("\x1b[34m") }
        if normalized >= 0.25 && normalized < 0.5 { print("\x1b[36m") }
        if normalized >= 0.5 && normalized < 0.75 { print("\x1b[33m") }
        if normalized >= 0.75 { print("\x1b[31m") }
    }
    if scale == 1 {
        // Grayscale
        if normalized < 0.5 { print("\x1b[90m") }
        if normalized >= 0.5 { print("\x1b[37m") }
    }
    if scale == 2 {
        // Green-red
        if normalized < 0.5 { print("\x1b[32m") }
        if normalized >= 0.5 { print("\x1b[31m") }
    }
}

fn print_row_label(row: i64, width: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let pad = width - 2
    var p: i64 = 0
    while p < pad {
        print(" ")
        p = p + 1
    }
    print(row)
    print(" ")
}

fn print_heatmap_legend(min_val: f64, max_val: f64, scale: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    // Print gradient bar
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 20 {
        let normalized = i as f64 / 19.0
        heatmap_cell_color(normalized, scale)
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    print(reset)

    // Range labels
    print("  ")
    print_f64_hm(min_val)
    print(" → ")
    print_f64_hm(max_val)
}

fn print_f64_hm(value: f64) with IO {
    let int_part = value as i64
    let frac = value - int_part as f64
    let frac_abs = if frac < 0.0 { -frac } else { frac }
    if value < 0.0 && int_part == 0 { print("-") }
    print(int_part)
    print(".")
    let d1 = (frac_abs * 10.0) as i64
    let d2 = (frac_abs * 100.0) as i64 - d1 * 10
    print(d1)
    print(d2)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/plot/line.sio ===
// Line Plot Rendering
//
// ASCII line plots with:
// - Multiple series support
// - Automatic axis scaling
// - Grid lines
// - Series markers and colors
// - Y-axis labels

// ============================================================================
// LINE PLOT TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct LineSeries {
    values: [f64; 1024],
    n: i64,
    label: string,
    marker: string,
    color_code: string,
}

struct LinePlotConfig {
    title: string,
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    x_label: string,
    y_label: string,
    show_grid: bool,
    show_legend: bool,
}

fn line_series_new(label: string, marker: string, color: string) -> LineSeries {
    LineSeries {
        values: [0.0; 1024],
        n: 0,
        label: label,
        marker: marker,
        color_code: color,
    }
}

fn line_series_add(s: &!LineSeries, value: f64) {
    if s.n < 1024 {
        s.values[s.n as usize] = value
        s.n = s.n + 1
    }
}

fn line_config_default() -> LinePlotConfig {
    LinePlotConfig {
        title: "",
        width: 60,
        height: 20,
        x_label: "",
        y_label: "",
        show_grid: false,
        show_legend: true,
    }
}

fn line_config_new(title: string, width: i64, height: i64) -> LinePlotConfig {
    LinePlotConfig {
        title: title,
        width: width,
        height: height,
        x_label: "",
        y_label: "",
        show_grid: false,
        show_legend: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SINGLE SERIES LINE PLOT
// ============================================================================

// Plot a single array of values
fn line_plot(values: &[f64], n: i64, title: string) with Div, Mut, Panic, IO {
    let config = line_config_new(title, 60, 20)
    line_plot_single(values, n, &config)
}

fn line_plot_single(values: &[f64], n: i64, config: &LinePlotConfig) with Div, Div, Mut, Mut, Panic, Panic, IO {
    if n <= 0 { return }

    let reset = "\x1b[0m"
    let margin_left: i64 = 10  // space for y-axis labels

    // Find data range
    var min_val = values[0]
    var max_val = values[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if values[i as usize] < min_val { min_val = values[i as usize] }
        if values[i as usize] > max_val { max_val = values[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Add 5% padding
    let range = max_val - min_val
    let padding = if range > 0.0 { range * 0.05 } else { 1.0 }
    min_val = min_val - padding
    max_val = max_val + padding

    // Title
    if config.title.len() > 0 {
        var pad: i64 = 0
        while pad < margin_left + config.width / 2 - config.title.len() as i64 / 2 {
            print(" ")
            pad = pad + 1
        }
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(config.title)
        print(reset)
    }

    // Render rows from top (max_val) to bottom (min_val)
    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < config.height {
        let y_val = max_val - (row as f64 / (config.height - 1) as f64) * (max_val - min_val)

        // Y-axis label
        print_y_label(y_val, margin_left)

        // Vertical axis
        if row == config.height - 1 {
            print("└")
        } else {
            print("│")
        }

        // Plot area
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < config.width {
            // Map column to data index
            let data_idx = (col as f64 / (config.width - 1) as f64 * (n - 1) as f64) as i64
            let data_val = values[data_idx as usize]

            // Map data value to row
            let data_row = ((max_val - data_val) / (max_val - min_val) * (config.height - 1) as f64) as i64

            if data_row == row {
                print("\x1b[36m")  // cyan
                print("●")
                print(reset)
            } else {
                if config.show_grid && col > 0 && col % 10 == 0 {
                    print("\x1b[2m")  // dim
                    print("·")
                    print(reset)
                } else {
                    print(" ")
                }
            }
            col = col + 1
        }

        println("")
        row = row + 1
    }

    // X-axis
    var pad: i64 = 0
    while pad < margin_left {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad + 1
    }
    print("└")
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < config.width {
        print("─")
        j = j + 1
    }
    println("→")

    // X-axis label
    if config.x_label.len() > 0 {
        var pad2: i64 = 0
        while pad2 < margin_left + config.width / 2 - config.x_label.len() as i64 / 2 {
            print(" ")
            pad2 = pad2 + 1
        }
        println(config.x_label)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MULTI-SERIES LINE PLOT
// ============================================================================

// Plot multiple series with different colors and markers
fn line_plot_multi(
    series: &[LineSeries],
    n_series: i64,
    config: &LinePlotConfig,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    if n_series <= 0 { return }

    let reset = "\x1b[0m"
    let margin_left: i64 = 10

    // Find global data range across all series
    var min_val = series[0].values[0]
    var max_val = series[0].values[0]
    var max_n: i64 = 0

    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < n_series {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < series[s as usize].n {
            let v = series[s as usize].values[i as usize]
            if v < min_val { min_val = v }
            if v > max_val { max_val = v }
            i = i + 1
        }
        if series[s as usize].n > max_n { max_n = series[s as usize].n }
        s = s + 1
    }

    let range = max_val - min_val
    let padding = if range > 0.0 { range * 0.05 } else { 1.0 }
    min_val = min_val - padding
    max_val = max_val + padding

    // Title
    if config.title.len() > 0 {
        var pad: i64 = 0
        while pad < margin_left + config.width / 2 - config.title.len() as i64 / 2 {
            print(" ")
            pad = pad + 1
        }
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(config.title)
        print(reset)
    }

    // Render rows
    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < config.height {
        let y_val = max_val - (row as f64 / (config.height - 1) as f64) * (max_val - min_val)
        print_y_label(y_val, margin_left)

        if row == config.height - 1 {
            print("└")
        } else {
            print("│")
        }

        // For each column, check each series
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < config.width {
            var drawn = false
            var si: i64 = 0
            while si < n_series && !drawn {
                let ser = series[si as usize]
                if ser.n > 0 {
                    let data_idx = (col as f64 / (config.width - 1) as f64 * (ser.n - 1) as f64) as i64
                    let data_val = ser.values[data_idx as usize]
                    let data_row = ((max_val - data_val) / (max_val - min_val) * (config.height - 1) as f64) as i64

                    if data_row == row {
                        if ser.color_code.len() > 0 {
                            print(ser.color_code)
                        }
                        if ser.marker.len() > 0 {
                            print(ser.marker)
                        } else {
                            print("●")
                        }
                        if ser.color_code.len() > 0 {
                            print(reset)
                        }
                        drawn = true
                    }
                }
                si = si + 1
            }
            if !drawn {
                print(" ")
            }
            col = col + 1
        }
        println("")
        row = row + 1
    }

    // X-axis
    var pad: i64 = 0
    while pad < margin_left {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad + 1
    }
    print("└")
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < config.width {
        print("─")
        j = j + 1
    }
    println("→")

    // Legend
    if config.show_legend {
        println("")
        print("  Legend: ")
        var si: i64 = 0
        while si < n_series {
            let ser = series[si as usize]
            if ser.color_code.len() > 0 { print(ser.color_code) }
            if ser.marker.len() > 0 { print(ser.marker) } else { print("●") }
            if ser.color_code.len() > 0 { print(reset) }
            print(" ")
            print(ser.label)
            if si < n_series - 1 { print("  ") }
            si = si + 1
        }
        println("")
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SPARKLINE (inline mini-chart)
// ============================================================================

// Render a sparkline: compact single-line chart using block characters
// ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█ (8 levels)
fn sparkline(values: &[f64], n: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    if n <= 0 { return }

    let blocks = "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"

    var min_val = values[0]
    var max_val = values[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if values[i as usize] < min_val { min_val = values[i as usize] }
        if values[i as usize] > max_val { max_val = values[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let range = max_val - min_val
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let normalized = if range > 0.0 {
            (values[i as usize] - min_val) / range
        } else {
            0.5
        }
        let level = (normalized * 7.0) as i64
        let idx = if level > 7 { 7 } else { if level < 0 { 0 } else { level } }
        // Print block character at level
        if idx == 0 { print("▁") }
        if idx == 1 { print("▂") }
        if idx == 2 { print("▃") }
        if idx == 3 { print("▄") }
        if idx == 4 { print("▅") }
        if idx == 5 { print("▆") }
        if idx == 6 { print("▇") }
        if idx == 7 { print("█") }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Sparkline with color gradient
fn sparkline_colored(values: &[f64], n: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    if n <= 0 { return }

    let reset = "\x1b[0m"

    var min_val = values[0]
    var max_val = values[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if values[i as usize] < min_val { min_val = values[i as usize] }
        if values[i as usize] > max_val { max_val = values[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let range = max_val - min_val
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let normalized = if range > 0.0 {
            (values[i as usize] - min_val) / range
        } else {
            0.5
        }

        // Color based on value
        if normalized < 0.33 { print("\x1b[34m") }       // blue (low)
        if normalized >= 0.33 && normalized < 0.66 { print("\x1b[33m") }  // yellow (mid)
        if normalized >= 0.66 { print("\x1b[31m") }       // red (high)

        let level = (normalized * 7.0) as i64
        if level <= 0 { print("▁") }
        if level == 1 { print("▂") }
        if level == 2 { print("▃") }
        if level == 3 { print("▄") }
        if level == 4 { print("▅") }
        if level == 5 { print("▆") }
        if level == 6 { print("▇") }
        if level >= 7 { print("█") }

        print(reset)
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn print_y_label(value: f64, width: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    // Format value and right-align to width
    let int_part = value as i64
    let frac = value - int_part as f64
    let frac_abs = if frac < 0.0 { -frac } else { frac }

    // Simple formatting: right-align a number in `width` chars
    // We approximate label length as 8 chars
    var pad = width - 8
    while pad > 0 {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad - 1
    }

    if value < 0.0 && int_part == 0 {
        print("-0")
    } else {
        print(int_part)
    }
    print(".")
    let d1 = (frac_abs * 10.0) as i64
    let d2 = (frac_abs * 100.0) as i64 - d1 * 10
    print(d1)
    print(d2)
    print(" ")
}

module plot


// === FILE: stdlib/plot/scatter.sio ===
// Scatter Plot Rendering
//
// 2D scatter plots with:
// - Multiple series with distinct markers
// - Automatic axis scaling
// - Quadrant labels
// - Correlation display

// ============================================================================
// SCATTER PLOT TYPES
// ============================================================================

struct ScatterPoint {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

struct ScatterSeries {
    points: [ScatterPoint; 512],
    n: i64,
    label: string,
    marker: string,
    color_code: string,
}

struct ScatterConfig {
    title: string,
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    x_label: string,
    y_label: string,
    show_axes: bool,
    show_correlation: bool,
}

fn scatter_point(x: f64, y: f64) -> ScatterPoint {
    ScatterPoint { x: x, y: y }
}

fn scatter_series_new(label: string, marker: string, color: string) -> ScatterSeries {
    ScatterSeries {
        points: [scatter_point(0.0, 0.0); 512],
        n: 0,
        label: label,
        marker: marker,
        color_code: color,
    }
}

fn scatter_series_add(s: &!ScatterSeries, x: f64, y: f64) {
    if s.n < 512 {
        s.points[s.n as usize] = scatter_point(x, y)
        s.n = s.n + 1
    }
}

fn scatter_config_default() -> ScatterConfig {
    ScatterConfig {
        title: "",
        width: 60,
        height: 20,
        x_label: "x",
        y_label: "y",
        show_axes: true,
        show_correlation: true,
    }
}

fn scatter_config_new(title: string, width: i64, height: i64) -> ScatterConfig {
    ScatterConfig {
        title: title,
        width: width,
        height: height,
        x_label: "x",
        y_label: "y",
        show_axes: true,
        show_correlation: true,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SCATTER PLOT RENDERING
// ============================================================================

// Plot x,y arrays as a scatter plot
fn scatter_plot(
    xs: &[f64],
    ys: &[f64],
    n: i64,
    title: string,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let config = scatter_config_new(title, 60, 20)
    scatter_plot_arrays(xs, ys, n, &config)
}

fn scatter_plot_arrays(
    xs: &[f64],
    ys: &[f64],
    n: i64,
    config: &ScatterConfig,
) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    if n <= 0 { return }

    let reset = "\x1b[0m"
    let margin_left: i64 = 10

    // Data range
    var x_min = xs[0]
    var x_max = xs[0]
    var y_min = ys[0]
    var y_max = ys[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        if xs[i as usize] < x_min { x_min = xs[i as usize] }
        if xs[i as usize] > x_max { x_max = xs[i as usize] }
        if ys[i as usize] < y_min { y_min = ys[i as usize] }
        if ys[i as usize] > y_max { y_max = ys[i as usize] }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Padding
    let x_range = x_max - x_min
    let y_range = y_max - y_min
    let x_pad = if x_range > 0.0 { x_range * 0.05 } else { 1.0 }
    let y_pad = if y_range > 0.0 { y_range * 0.05 } else { 1.0 }
    x_min = x_min - x_pad
    x_max = x_max + x_pad
    y_min = y_min - y_pad
    y_max = y_max + y_pad

    // Title
    if config.title.len() > 0 {
        var pad: i64 = 0
        while pad < margin_left + config.width / 2 - config.title.len() as i64 / 2 {
            print(" ")
            pad = pad + 1
        }
        print("\x1b[1m")
        println(config.title)
        print(reset)
    }

    // Build occupancy grid
    var grid: [bool; 4096] = [false; 4096]  // max 64x64
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let col = ((xs[i as usize] - x_min) / (x_max - x_min) * (config.width - 1) as f64) as i64
        let row = config.height - 1 - ((ys[i as usize] - y_min) / (y_max - y_min) * (config.height - 1) as f64) as i64
        if row >= 0 && row < config.height && col >= 0 && col < config.width {
            grid[(row * config.width + col) as usize] = true
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Render
    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < config.height {
        let y_val = y_max - (row as f64 / (config.height - 1) as f64) * (y_max - y_min)

        // Y-axis label
        print_y_label_scatter(y_val, margin_left)

        if row == config.height - 1 {
            print("└")
        } else {
            print("│")
        }

        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < config.width {
            if grid[(row * config.width + col) as usize] {
                print("\x1b[35m")  // magenta
                print("●")
                print(reset)
            } else {
                print(" ")
            }
            col = col + 1
        }
        println("")
        row = row + 1
    }

    // X-axis
    var pad: i64 = 0
    while pad < margin_left {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad + 1
    }
    print("└")
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < config.width {
        print("─")
        j = j + 1
    }
    println("→")

    // Correlation
    if config.show_correlation {
        let r = pearson_corr(xs, ys, n)
        print("  r = ")
        print_f64_scatter(r, 4)
        println("")
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STATISTICS
// ============================================================================

fn pearson_corr(xs: &[f64], ys: &[f64], n: i64) -> f64 {
    if n <= 1 { return 0.0 }

    var sum_x = 0.0
    var sum_y = 0.0
    var sum_xy = 0.0
    var sum_x2 = 0.0
    var sum_y2 = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum_x = sum_x + xs[i as usize]
        sum_y = sum_y + ys[i as usize]
        sum_xy = sum_xy + xs[i as usize] * ys[i as usize]
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + xs[i as usize] * xs[i as usize]
        sum_y2 = sum_y2 + ys[i as usize] * ys[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let nf = n as f64
    let num = nf * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y
    let den_x = nf * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x
    let den_y = nf * sum_y2 - sum_y * sum_y

    if den_x <= 0.0 || den_y <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }

    let den = sqrt_approx(den_x * den_y)
    if den <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    num / den
}

fn sqrt_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn print_y_label_scatter(value: f64, width: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    var pad = width - 8
    while pad > 0 {
        print(" ")
        pad = pad - 1
    }
    let int_part = value as i64
    let frac = value - int_part as f64
    let frac_abs = if frac < 0.0 { -frac } else { frac }
    if value < 0.0 && int_part == 0 { print("-0") } else { print(int_part) }
    print(".")
    let d1 = (frac_abs * 10.0) as i64
    let d2 = (frac_abs * 100.0) as i64 - d1 * 10
    print(d1)
    print(d2)
    print(" ")
}

fn print_f64_scatter(value: f64, decimals: i64) with Panic, Div, Mut, IO {
    let int_part = value as i64
    let frac = value - int_part as f64
    let frac_abs = if frac < 0.0 { -frac } else { frac }
    if value < 0.0 && int_part == 0 { print("-") }
    print(int_part)
    print(".")
    var d: i64 = 0
    var remaining = frac_abs
    while d < decimals {
        remaining = remaining * 10.0
        let digit = remaining as i64
        print(digit)
        remaining = remaining - digit as f64
        d = d + 1
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/polynomial/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/polynomial/lib.sio - Polynomial operations
//!
//! Provides polynomial arithmetic and evaluation for scientific computing:
//! - Polynomial representation with coefficients
//! - Evaluation using Horner's method
//! - Arithmetic operations (add, sub, mul)
//! - Calculus (derivative, integral)
//! - Root finding for quadratic polynomials
//!
//! Polynomials are represented as p(x) = c[0] + c[1]*x + c[2]*x² + ... + c[n]*x^n

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// A polynomial with coefficients stored in ascending order of degree.
// p(x) = coeffs[0] + coeffs[1]*x + coeffs[2]*x² + ... + coeffs[degree]*x^degree
pub struct Polynomial {
    coeffs: [f64; 64],
    degree: i32,
}

// Create the zero polynomial (degree -1 by convention)
pub fn poly_zero() -> Polynomial {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: -1 }
}

// Create a constant polynomial: p(x) = c
pub fn poly_constant(c: f64) -> Polynomial with Panic, Mut {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c
    let deg = if c == 0.0 { -1 } else { 0 }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Create a linear polynomial: p(x) = a*x + b
pub fn poly_linear(a: f64, b: f64) -> Polynomial with Panic, Mut {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = b
    coeffs[1] = a
    let deg = if a != 0.0 { 1 } else { if b != 0.0 { 0 } else { -1 } }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Create a quadratic polynomial: p(x) = a*x² + b*x + c
pub fn poly_quadratic(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Panic, Mut {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c
    coeffs[1] = b
    coeffs[2] = a
    let deg = if a != 0.0 { 2 } else { if b != 0.0 { 1 } else { if c != 0.0 { 0 } else { -1 } } }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Create a monomial: p(x) = c * x^n
pub fn poly_monomial(c: f64, n: i32) -> Polynomial with Panic, Mut {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    if n >= 0 && n < 64 {
        coeffs[n] = c
    }
    let deg = if c == 0.0 { -1 } else { n }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// =============================================================================
// EVALUATION
// =============================================================================

// Evaluate polynomial at x using Horner's method.
// Horner's method: p(x) = c[n] + x*(c[n-1] + x*(c[n-2] + ... + x*c[0]))
// This is numerically stable and efficient (n multiplications, n additions).
pub fn poly_eval(p: Polynomial, x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree < 0 {
        return 0.0
    }
    var result = p.coeffs[p.degree]
    var i = p.degree - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        result = result * x + p.coeffs[i]
        i = i - 1
    }
    result
}

// Get coefficient at index i (returns 0.0 if out of range)
pub fn poly_coeff(p: Polynomial, i: i32) -> f64 with Panic, Mut {
    if i < 0 || i > p.degree {
        return 0.0
    }
    p.coeffs[i]
}

// Get the degree of the polynomial (-1 for zero polynomial)
pub fn poly_degree(p: Polynomial) -> i32 {
    p.degree
}

// Check if polynomial is zero
pub fn poly_is_zero(p: Polynomial) -> bool {
    p.degree < 0
}

// =============================================================================
// ARITHMETIC OPERATIONS
// =============================================================================

// Add two polynomials
pub fn poly_add(a: Polynomial, b: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let max_deg = if a.degree > b.degree { a.degree } else { b.degree }
    if max_deg < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= max_deg {
        let ca = if i <= a.degree { a.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        let cb = if i <= b.degree { b.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        coeffs[i] = ca + cb
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = max_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Subtract two polynomials: a - b
pub fn poly_sub(a: Polynomial, b: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let max_deg = if a.degree > b.degree { a.degree } else { b.degree }
    if max_deg < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= max_deg {
        let ca = if i <= a.degree { a.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        let cb = if i <= b.degree { b.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        coeffs[i] = ca - cb
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = max_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Multiply two polynomials (convolution of coefficients)
pub fn poly_mul(a: Polynomial, b: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if a.degree < 0 || b.degree < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    let result_deg = a.degree + b.degree
    let max_deg = if result_deg > 63 { 63 } else { result_deg }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= a.degree {
        var j = 0
        while j <= b.degree {
            let k = i + j
            if k <= max_deg {
                coeffs[k] = coeffs[k] + a.coeffs[i] * b.coeffs[j]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = max_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Scale polynomial by a constant: c * p(x)
pub fn poly_scale(p: Polynomial, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if c == 0.0 || p.degree < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= p.degree {
        coeffs[i] = p.coeffs[i] * c
        i = i + 1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: p.degree }
}

// Negate polynomial: -p(x)
pub fn poly_neg(p: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    poly_scale(p, -1.0)
}

// =============================================================================
// CALCULUS
// =============================================================================

// Compute the derivative: d/dx[c[i]*x^i] = i*c[i]*x^(i-1)
pub fn poly_derivative(p: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree <= 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    let new_deg = p.degree - 1
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= new_deg {
        coeffs[i] = (i + 1) as f64 * p.coeffs[i + 1]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = new_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Compute the indefinite integral with constant c: ∫p(x)dx + c
// ∫c[i]*x^i dx = c[i]*x^(i+1)/(i+1)
pub fn poly_integral(p: Polynomial, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree < 0 {
        return poly_constant(c)
    }

    let new_deg = if p.degree < 63 { p.degree + 1 } else { 63 }
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c

    var i = 0
    while i <= p.degree && i < 63 {
        coeffs[i + 1] = p.coeffs[i] / ((i + 1) as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: new_deg }
}

// =============================================================================
// ROOT FINDING
// =============================================================================

// Quadratic roots result
pub struct QuadraticRoots {
    r1: f64,
    r2: f64,
    discriminant: f64,
    has_real_roots: bool,
}

// Solve quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0
// Returns real roots if discriminant >= 0
pub fn poly_roots_quadratic(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64) -> QuadraticRoots with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if a == 0.0 {
        // Linear case: bx + c = 0
        if b == 0.0 {
            return QuadraticRoots { r1: 0.0, r2: 0.0, discriminant: 0.0, has_real_roots: false }
        }
        let r = -c / b
        return QuadraticRoots { r1: r, r2: r, discriminant: 0.0, has_real_roots: true }
    }

    let disc = b * b - 4.0 * a * c
    if disc < 0.0 {
        return QuadraticRoots { r1: 0.0, r2: 0.0, discriminant: disc, has_real_roots: false }
    }

    let sqrt_disc = sqrt(disc)
    let r1 = (-b + sqrt_disc) / (2.0 * a)
    let r2 = (-b - sqrt_disc) / (2.0 * a)
    QuadraticRoots { r1: r1, r2: r2, discriminant: disc, has_real_roots: true }
}

// Evaluate polynomial using numerically stable Horner with error bound
// Returns (value, error_estimate)
pub fn poly_eval_with_error(p: Polynomial, x: f64) -> (f64, f64) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree < 0 {
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    }

    let abs_x = if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
    var result = p.coeffs[p.degree]
    var error = fabs(result)

    var i = p.degree - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        result = result * x + p.coeffs[i]
        error = error * abs_x + fabs(result)
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Machine epsilon estimate
    let eps = 2.220446049250313e-16
    (result, error * eps)
}

// =============================================================================
// EXTENDED API — poly_new, poly_deriv, poly_integrate, poly_from_roots,
//               poly_deflate, poly_find_real_roots
// =============================================================================

// Create a zero polynomial of a given degree (all coefficients zero).
// Caller sets coefficients after creation.
pub fn poly_new(degree: i32) -> Polynomial with Panic, Mut {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    let d = if degree < 0 { -1 } else { if degree > 63 { 63 } else { degree } }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: d }
}

// Alias: poly_deriv = poly_derivative (formal derivative)
pub fn poly_deriv(p: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree <= 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }
    let new_deg = p.degree - 1
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= new_deg {
        coeffs[i] = (i + 1) as f64 * p.coeffs[i + 1]
        i = i + 1
    }
    var deg = new_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 { deg = deg - 1 }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 { deg = -1 }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Alias: poly_integrate = poly_integral (antiderivative with constant c)
pub fn poly_integrate(p: Polynomial, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree < 0 {
        return poly_constant(c)
    }
    let new_deg = if p.degree < 63 { p.degree + 1 } else { 63 }
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c
    var i = 0
    while i <= p.degree && i < 63 {
        coeffs[i + 1] = p.coeffs[i] / ((i + 1) as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: new_deg }
}

// Build polynomial from n roots: (x - r[0])*(x - r[1])*...*(x - r[n-1])
// Uses repeated multiplication by the linear factor (x - r[i]).
// NOTE: roots passed by value (fixed array). Uses by-value poly_mul.
pub fn poly_from_roots(roots: [f64; 32], n: i32) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Start with p(x) = 1
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = 1.0
    var p = Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: 0 }

    var k = 0
    while k < n {
        // Multiply p by (x - roots[k]): linear factor coeffs[0]=-r, coeffs[1]=1
        var lcoeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
        lcoeffs[0] = 0.0 - roots[k]
        lcoeffs[1] = 1.0
        let factor = Polynomial { coeffs: lcoeffs, degree: 1 }
        p = poly_mul(p, factor)
        k = k + 1
    }
    p
}

// Synthetic division: divide p(x) by (x - root), return quotient.
// If root is truly a root of p, the remainder is zero (or near-zero).
pub fn poly_deflate(p: Polynomial, root: f64) -> Polynomial with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree <= 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }
    let n = p.degree
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    // Synthetic division: b[n-1] = a[n], b[k] = a[k+1] + root*b[k+1]
    coeffs[n - 1] = p.coeffs[n]
    var i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        coeffs[i] = p.coeffs[i + 1] + root * coeffs[i + 1]
        i = i - 1
    }
    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = n - 1
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 { deg = deg - 1 }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 { deg = -1 }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Result of poly_find_real_roots — returned by value to avoid JIT &! mutation bug.
pub struct PolyRoots {
    roots: [f64; 32],
    count: i32,
}

// Inline Newton iterate: one step of Newton's method on polynomial p at x.
fn pf_newton_iter(p: Polynomial, x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var result = p.coeffs[p.degree]
    var i = p.degree - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        result = result * x + p.coeffs[i]
        i = i - 1
    }
    let fx = result
    // Derivative via Horner
    var dresult = (p.degree as f64) * p.coeffs[p.degree]
    var j = p.degree - 1
    while j >= 1 {
        dresult = dresult * x + (j as f64) * p.coeffs[j]
        j = j - 1
    }
    let dfx = dresult
    if fabs(dfx) < 1.0e-30 { return x }
    x - fx / dfx
}

// Evaluate polynomial at x (inline, by value).
fn pf_eval(p: Polynomial, x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if p.degree < 0 { return 0.0 }
    var result = p.coeffs[p.degree]
    var i = p.degree - 1
    while i >= 0 { result = result * x + p.coeffs[i]; i = i - 1 }
    result
}

// Find all real roots of polynomial p by repeated Newton + deflation.
// Returns PolyRoots (by value) to avoid the JIT &! mutation limitation.
// Works for polynomials up to degree 31.
pub fn poly_find_real_roots(p: Polynomial) -> PolyRoots with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var out_roots: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    var count = 0

    // Work on a local copy so we can deflate
    var work_coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= p.degree {
        work_coeffs[i] = p.coeffs[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    var work = Polynomial { coeffs: work_coeffs, degree: p.degree }

    // Starting guesses spread across [-10, 10]
    var starts: [f64; 32] = [0.0; 32]
    starts[0] = -9.0; starts[1] = -7.0; starts[2] = -5.0; starts[3] = -3.0
    starts[4] = -1.5; starts[5] = 0.0;  starts[6] = 0.5;  starts[7] = 1.5
    starts[8] = 3.0;  starts[9] = 5.0;  starts[10] = 7.0; starts[11] = 9.0

    var attempts = 0
    while work.degree >= 1 && count < 32 {
        let x0 = starts[attempts % 12]
        var x = x0
        var iter = 0
        while iter < 80 {
            let xn = pf_newton_iter(work, x)
            if fabs(xn - x) < 1.0e-12 {
                x = xn
                iter = 80
            } else {
                x = xn
                iter = iter + 1
            }
        }

        // Accept root if residual is small
        let res = pf_eval(work, x)

        if fabs(res) < 1.0e-8 {
            out_roots[count] = x
            count = count + 1
            // Deflate work by (x - root)
            work = poly_deflate(work, x)
        }

        attempts = attempts + 1
        if attempts > 200 { work = poly_zero() }
    }

    PolyRoots { roots: out_roots, count: count }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/privacy/differential.sio ===
// stdlib/privacy/differential.sio — Differential Privacy mechanisms and budget accounting
//
// Implements canonical DP mechanisms from Dwork et al. 2006 and Dwork, Rothblum, Vadhan 2010.
// All mechanisms are calibrated to their stated ε (and δ for approximate DP).
//
// CODATA 2022 / NIST SP 800-188 alignment:
//   ε-DP (pure DP): Laplace mechanism, Randomized Response
//   (ε, δ)-DP (approximate DP): Gaussian mechanism
//   Advanced composition: sqrt(2k * ln(1/δ)) * ε bound
//
// Sounio Sprint 21 DP track — first PL with ε as a type-level graded quantity.
// Paper target: POPL 2026 / CCS 2027
//   "Graded Differential Privacy: ε-Budget as a Compile-Time Algebraic Effect in Sounio"

// ============================================================
// Sensitivity computation helpers
// ============================================================

// l1-sensitivity of a counting query: Δf = 1 (adding/removing one record changes count by 1)
fn counting_query_sensitivity() -> f64 with IO {
    1.0
}

// l1-sensitivity of a sum query on bounded domain [lo, hi]: Δf = hi - lo
fn sum_query_sensitivity(lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    hi + (0.0 - lo)
}

// l1-sensitivity of a mean query on bounded domain, n records: Δf = (hi - lo) / n
fn mean_query_sensitivity(lo: f64, hi: f64, n: i64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    let range = hi + (0.0 - lo)
    let n_f: f64 = n as f64
    range / n_f
}

// ============================================================
// Laplace mechanism (pure ε-DP)
// ============================================================
// Theorem (Dwork 2006, Proposition 3.5): Adding Lap(Δf/ε) noise achieves ε-DP.
// Scale parameter b = Δf / ε.

fn laplace_scale(sensitivity: f64, epsilon: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    sensitivity / epsilon
}

// Variance of Laplace mechanism output: Var[Lap(b)] = 2b²
fn laplace_variance(sensitivity: f64, epsilon: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    let b = laplace_scale(sensitivity, epsilon)
    2.0 * b * b
}

// Mean squared error of Laplace mechanism: E[(M(D) - f(D))²] = 2(Δf/ε)²
fn laplace_mse(sensitivity: f64, epsilon: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    laplace_variance(sensitivity, epsilon)
}

// ============================================================
// Gaussian mechanism (approximate (ε, δ)-DP)
// ============================================================
// Theorem (Dwork 2006, Proposition 3.6):
//   σ ≥ sqrt(2 * ln(1.25/δ)) * Δf / ε achieves (ε, δ)-DP.
// For δ = 0.01: sqrt(2 * ln(1.25/0.01)) = sqrt(2 * 4.828) ≈ 3.105

fn gaussian_sigma(sensitivity: f64, epsilon: f64, delta: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    // Compute ln(1.25/δ) via identity: ln(1.25/δ) = ln(1.25) - ln(δ)
    // Approximate: for δ = 0.01, ln(1.25/δ) ≈ 4.828; for δ = 0.001, ≈ 7.13
    // We use a linear approximation around common δ values (for bootstrap purposes)
    // Full implementation would use stdlib/math/log.sio when available
    let log_inv_delta_approx: f64 = if delta > 0.05 {
        3.0  // δ ≈ 0.1: ln(12.5) ≈ 2.53, rounded up
    } else if delta > 0.005 {
        4.828  // δ ≈ 0.01 (common choice)
    } else if delta > 0.0005 {
        7.13   // δ ≈ 0.001
    } else {
        9.43   // δ ≈ 0.0001
    }
    let factor_sq = 2.0 * log_inv_delta_approx
    // Approximate sqrt via Newton (2 iterations from factor_sq/2)
    let x0 = factor_sq / 2.0
    let x1 = (x0 + factor_sq / x0) / 2.0
    let sqrt_factor = (x1 + factor_sq / x1) / 2.0
    sqrt_factor * sensitivity / epsilon
}

// Variance of Gaussian mechanism output: Var = σ²
fn gaussian_variance(sensitivity: f64, epsilon: f64, delta: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    let sigma = gaussian_sigma(sensitivity, epsilon, delta)
    sigma * sigma
}

// ============================================================
// Composition theorems
// ============================================================

// Sequential composition: k mechanisms each εᵢ-DP → Σεᵢ-DP overall
// (Theorem 3.14, Dwork 2006)
fn dp_sequential_epsilon(eps_list: [f64; 8], count: i64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    var total: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < count && i < 8 {
        total = total + eps_list[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    total
}

// Parallel composition: disjoint datasets → max(εᵢ)-DP overall
// (Theorem 3.20, Dwork 2006)
fn dp_parallel_epsilon(eps_list: [f64; 8], count: i64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    var max_eps: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < count && i < 8 {
        let ei = eps_list[i as usize]
        max_eps = if ei > max_eps { ei } else { max_eps }
        i = i + 1
    }
    max_eps
}

// Advanced composition (Dwork, Rothblum, Vadhan 2010):
// k mechanisms each ε-DP → (ε', δ')-DP where
//   ε' = sqrt(2k * ln(1/δ')) * ε + k * ε * (exp(ε) - 1)
// Simple approximation for small ε (ε ≤ 1): ε' ≈ ε * sqrt(2k * ln(1/δ'))
fn dp_advanced_composition(epsilon: f64, k_queries: i64, delta: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    let k_f: f64 = k_queries as f64
    // ln(1/δ) approximation (same as gaussian_sigma above)
    let log_inv_delta: f64 = if delta > 0.05 {
        3.0
    } else if delta > 0.005 {
        4.605  // ln(100) ≈ 4.605 for δ=0.01
    } else if delta > 0.0005 {
        6.908  // ln(1000) ≈ 6.908 for δ=0.001
    } else {
        9.21   // ln(10000) ≈ 9.21 for δ=0.0001
    }
    let under_sqrt = 2.0 * k_f * log_inv_delta
    // Newton sqrt (2 iterations)
    let x0 = under_sqrt / 2.0
    let x1 = (x0 + under_sqrt / x0) / 2.0
    let sqrt_factor = (x1 + under_sqrt / x1) / 2.0
    epsilon * sqrt_factor
}

// ============================================================
// Randomized response (local DP)
// ============================================================
// Warner 1965 / Dwork 2006: For binary response, answer truthfully with prob p = exp(ε)/(1+exp(ε))
// Achieves ε-LDP (local differential privacy).
// Privacy parameter: p (probability of truthful response)
fn randomized_response_p(epsilon: f64) -> f64 with IO, Div, Panic {
    // p = exp(ε) / (1 + exp(ε)) = 1 / (1 + exp(-ε))
    // Approximate exp(ε) for ε ∈ [0,1]: exp(ε) ≈ 1 + ε + ε²/2 + ε³/6
    let e2 = epsilon * epsilon
    let e3 = e2 * epsilon
    let exp_eps = 1.0 + epsilon + e2 / 2.0 + e3 / 6.0
    exp_eps / (1.0 + exp_eps)
}

// ============================================================
// Budget tracking
// ============================================================

// DPBudgetTracker: accumulates ε spent across multiple queries
struct DPBudgetTracker {
    epsilon_total: f64,
    epsilon_spent: f64,
    query_count: i64,
}

fn dp_budget_new(epsilon_total: f64) -> DPBudgetTracker {
    DPBudgetTracker {
        epsilon_total: epsilon_total,
        epsilon_spent: 0.0,
        query_count: 0,
    }
}

fn dp_budget_remaining_f64(tracker: DPBudgetTracker) -> f64 with IO {
    tracker.epsilon_total + (0.0 - tracker.epsilon_spent)
}

fn dp_budget_is_exhausted(tracker: DPBudgetTracker) -> bool with IO {
    tracker.epsilon_spent > tracker.epsilon_total
}

// ============================================================
// Public structs for complete DP API
// ============================================================

// DPConfig — configuration for a DP mechanism
struct DPConfig {
    epsilon: f64,        // privacy budget ε
    delta: f64,          // approximate DP parameter δ (0 for pure DP)
    sensitivity: f64,    // query sensitivity Δf
    mechanism: i32,      // 0=Laplace, 1=Gaussian, 2=Exponential
}

// DPResult — result of a differentially private query
struct DPResult {
    noisy_value: f64,
    true_value: f64,
    noise_added: f64,
    epsilon_spent: f64,
    remaining_budget: f64,
}

// PrivacyAccountant — tracks cumulative ε-spending across queries
struct PrivacyAccountant {
    total_epsilon: f64,
    spent_epsilon: f64,
    n_queries: i32,
    max_queries: i32,
}

// ============================================================
// DPConfig constructors
// ============================================================

fn dp_config_laplace(epsilon: f64, sensitivity: f64) -> DPConfig {
    DPConfig {
        epsilon: epsilon,
        delta: 0.0,
        sensitivity: sensitivity,
        mechanism: 0,
    }
}

fn dp_config_gaussian(epsilon: f64, delta: f64, sensitivity: f64) -> DPConfig {
    DPConfig {
        epsilon: epsilon,
        delta: delta,
        sensitivity: sensitivity,
        mechanism: 1,
    }
}

// ============================================================
// Noise generation via inverse CDF (deterministic for given seed)
// ============================================================

// Laplace inverse CDF: F⁻¹(u) = -b * sign(u - 0.5) * ln(1 - 2|u - 0.5|)
// where b = sensitivity / ε and u = pseudo-random from seed.
// Uses a simple multiplicative LCG to derive u ∈ (0,1) from seed.
fn dp_laplace_noise_helper_u(seed: i64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    // LCG: x_{n+1} = (a*x + c) mod m
    let a: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    let c: i64 = 1442695040888963407
    let mixed = a * seed + c
    // Map to (0,1) — avoid exact 0 or 1 for log stability
    let raw: f64 = mixed as f64
    let scaled = raw / 9223372036854775807.0
    let u = if scaled < 0.0 { 0.0 - scaled } else { scaled }
    // Clamp to (0.001, 0.999) to avoid log(0)
    if u < 0.001 { return 0.001 }
    if u > 0.999 { return 0.999 }
    u
}

// Natural log approximation (sufficient for Laplace noise)
fn dp_ln_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    // Use identity: ln(x) = 2 * arctanh((x-1)/(x+1))
    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result = 0.0
    var term = y
    var i = 1
    while i < 30 {
        let i_f: f64 = i as f64
        result = result + term / i_f
        term = term * y * y
        i = i + 2
    }
    2.0 * result
}

// dp_laplace_noise: samples from Laplace(0, sensitivity/ε) via inverse CDF
// Ref: Dwork 2006, Proposition 3.5
fn dp_laplace_noise(config: DPConfig, seed: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let b = config.sensitivity / config.epsilon
    let u = dp_laplace_noise_helper_u(seed)
    let centered = u - 0.5
    let sign = if centered < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let abs_centered = if centered < 0.0 { 0.0 - centered } else { centered }
    let arg = 1.0 - 2.0 * abs_centered
    // Clamp arg to avoid log(0)
    let arg_safe = if arg < 0.0001 { 0.0001 } else { arg }
    0.0 - sign * b * dp_ln_approx(arg_safe)
}

// Sqrt via Newton's method (3 iterations)
fn dp_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x / 2.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// dp_gaussian_noise: samples from N(0, σ²) via polar Box-Muller (no trig needed).
// σ = sensitivity * sqrt(2 * ln(1.25/δ)) / ε
// Ref: Dwork 2006, Proposition 3.6; Marsaglia & Bray 1964 (polar method)
//
// Polar method:
//   u1, u2 ~ Uniform(0,1); v1 = 2u1-1, v2 = 2u2-1
//   s = v1² + v2²; if s < 1 then Z = v1 * sqrt(-2*ln(s)/s) ~ N(0,1)
//   The polar form avoids cos/sin entirely.
fn dp_gaussian_noise(config: DPConfig, seed: i64) -> f64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let sigma = gaussian_sigma(config.sensitivity, config.epsilon, config.delta)
    let u1 = dp_laplace_noise_helper_u(seed)
    let u2 = dp_laplace_noise_helper_u(seed + 1)
    // Map to [-1, 1]
    let v1 = 2.0 * u1 - 1.0
    let v2 = 2.0 * u2 - 1.0
    let s = v1 * v1 + v2 * v2
    // If s >= 1, it falls outside the unit circle; clamp to 0.99 to avoid rejection
    let s_safe = if s >= 1.0 { 0.99 } else if s < 0.000001 { 0.000001 } else { s }
    // Z = v1 * sqrt(-2 * ln(s) / s)
    let log_s = dp_ln_approx(s_safe)
    let factor = dp_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * log_s / s_safe)
    v1 * factor * sigma
}

// ============================================================
// dp_query — apply noise to a true value
// ============================================================

fn dp_query(config: DPConfig, true_value: f64, seed: i64) -> DPResult with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let noise = if config.mechanism == 0 {
        dp_laplace_noise(config, seed)
    } else {
        dp_gaussian_noise(config, seed)
    }
    DPResult {
        noisy_value: true_value + noise,
        true_value: true_value,
        noise_added: noise,
        epsilon_spent: config.epsilon,
        remaining_budget: 0.0,  // updated by accountant
    }
}

// ============================================================
// PrivacyAccountant
// ============================================================

fn accountant_new(total_epsilon: f64, max_queries: i32) -> PrivacyAccountant {
    PrivacyAccountant {
        total_epsilon: total_epsilon,
        spent_epsilon: 0.0,
        n_queries: 0,
        max_queries: max_queries,
    }
}

fn accountant_spend(acc: PrivacyAccountant, epsilon: f64) -> PrivacyAccountant {
    PrivacyAccountant {
        total_epsilon: acc.total_epsilon,
        spent_epsilon: acc.spent_epsilon + epsilon,
        n_queries: acc.n_queries + 1,
        max_queries: acc.max_queries,
    }
}

fn accountant_can_query(acc: PrivacyAccountant, epsilon: f64) -> bool {
    let remaining = acc.total_epsilon - acc.spent_epsilon
    remaining >= epsilon && acc.n_queries < acc.max_queries
}

fn accountant_remaining(acc: PrivacyAccountant) -> f64 {
    acc.total_epsilon - acc.spent_epsilon
}

// ============================================================
// Simple 2-mechanism composition (public interface)
// ============================================================

// Sequential composition: running ε₁ + ε₂ on same dataset → (ε₁ + ε₂)-DP
fn dp_compose_sequential(epsilon1: f64, epsilon2: f64) -> f64 {
    epsilon1 + epsilon2
}

// Parallel composition: running ε₁, ε₂ on disjoint partitions → max(ε₁, ε₂)-DP
fn dp_compose_parallel(epsilon1: f64, epsilon2: f64) -> f64 {
    if epsilon1 > epsilon2 { epsilon1 } else { epsilon2 }
}

// ============================================================
// Epistemic confidence tracking for DP queries
// ============================================================

// EpistemicDPValue — a DP result annotated with epistemic uncertainty.
// The variance tracks how much uncertainty is introduced by the DP noise,
// on top of any pre-existing measurement uncertainty.
struct EpistemicDPValue {
    noisy_value: f64,
    true_value: f64,
    noise_variance: f64,   // Var[noise] (known from mechanism)
    conf_lower: f64,       // 95% CI lower bound on true value
    conf_upper: f64,       // 95% CI upper bound on true value
    epsilon_spent: f64,
}

// epistemic_dp_query: wraps dp_query with GUM-style uncertainty propagation.
// For Laplace(b): Var = 2b², so 95% CI half-width ≈ 1.96 * sqrt(2) * b.
// For Gaussian(σ): Var = σ², 95% CI half-width = 1.96 * σ.
fn epistemic_dp_query(config: DPConfig, true_value: f64, seed: i64) -> EpistemicDPValue with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = dp_query(config, true_value, seed)
    let noise_var = if config.mechanism == 0 {
        // Laplace: Var = 2 * b²
        let b = config.sensitivity / config.epsilon
        2.0 * b * b
    } else {
        // Gaussian: Var = σ²
        let sigma = gaussian_sigma(config.sensitivity, config.epsilon, config.delta)
        sigma * sigma
    }
    let half_width = 1.96 * dp_sqrt(noise_var)
    EpistemicDPValue {
        noisy_value: result.noisy_value,
        true_value: true_value,
        noise_variance: noise_var,
        conf_lower: result.noisy_value - half_width,
        conf_upper: result.noisy_value + half_width,
        epsilon_spent: config.epsilon,
    }
}

// epistemic_dp_ci_contains: checks if the CI contains the true value
fn epistemic_dp_ci_contains(e: EpistemicDPValue) -> bool {
    e.true_value >= e.conf_lower && e.true_value <= e.conf_upper
}


// === FILE: stdlib/prob/beta.sio ===
// beta.sio - Beta distribution with variance-first API for epistemic computing
//
// Core epistemic primitive: represents probability as a full posterior
// distribution, not just a point estimate. Variance measures "ignorance."
//
// Now uses proper struct-based API with field access (compiler bug fixed).
//
// Future upgrades intentionally deferred:
// - Exact Beta quantiles (require incomplete beta function)
// - Special functions (gamma, beta, ln, exp)
// - Normal distribution conjugacy
// - MCMC sampling

// ============================================================================
// TYPE DEFINITIONS
// ============================================================================

// Beta distribution parameters
pub struct BetaDist {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

// Confidence interval bounds
pub struct CI {
    lo: f64,
    hi: f64
}

// ============================================================================
// NUMERIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Absolute value for f64
fn beta_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// Clamp value to [0, 1] range
fn clamp01(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    if x > 1.0 { return 1.0 }
    return x
}

// Square root via Newton-Raphson (10 unrolled iterations)
fn beta_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION API
// ============================================================================

// Minimum epsilon to prevent invalid states (alpha, beta must be > 0)
fn beta_epsilon() -> f64 {
    return 0.0001
}

// Create a new Beta distribution with clamped parameters
pub fn beta_dist_new(alpha: f64, b: f64) -> BetaDist {
    let eps = beta_epsilon()
    let safe_alpha = alpha
    let safe_beta = b
    if safe_alpha < eps {
        if safe_beta < eps {
            return BetaDist { alpha: eps, beta: eps }
        }
        return BetaDist { alpha: eps, beta: safe_beta }
    }
    if safe_beta < eps {
        return BetaDist { alpha: safe_alpha, beta: eps }
    }
    return BetaDist { alpha: safe_alpha, beta: safe_beta }
}

// Common priors
pub fn beta_uniform() -> BetaDist {
    return BetaDist { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
}

pub fn beta_jeffreys() -> BetaDist {
    return BetaDist { alpha: 0.5, beta: 0.5 }
}

pub fn beta_weak() -> BetaDist {
    return BetaDist { alpha: 2.0, beta: 2.0 }
}

// Conjugate posterior update: Beta(a, b) + (successes, failures) -> Beta(a+s, b+f)
pub fn beta_posterior(prior: BetaDist, successes: i64, failures: i64) -> BetaDist {
    // Convert i64 to f64
    var sf = 0.0
    var count = 0
    if successes > 0 {
        while count < successes {
            sf = sf + 1.0
            count = count + 1
        }
    }

    var ff = 0.0
    count = 0
    if failures > 0 {
        while count < failures {
            ff = ff + 1.0
            count = count + 1
        }
    }

    return BetaDist { alpha: prior.alpha + sf, beta: prior.beta + ff }
}

// Mean of Beta distribution: E[X] = alpha / (alpha + beta)
pub fn beta_dist_mean(b: BetaDist) -> f64 {
    return b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta)
}

// Variance: Var[X] = (alpha * beta) / ((alpha + beta)^2 * (alpha + beta + 1))
// This is the KEY epistemic quantity - measures "how much we don't know"
pub fn beta_dist_variance(b: BetaDist) -> f64 {
    let n = b.alpha + b.beta
    return (b.alpha * b.beta) / (n * n * (n + 1.0))
}

// Standard deviation
pub fn beta_std(b: BetaDist) -> f64 {
    return beta_sqrt_f64(beta_dist_variance(b))
}

// Effective sample size: n = alpha + beta
pub fn beta_sample_size(b: BetaDist) -> f64 {
    return b.alpha + b.beta
}
