// === FILE: stdlib/quantum/linear.sio ===
// stdlib/quantum/linear.sio — Quantum Computing via Linear Types
//
// The no-cloning theorem of quantum mechanics states that an unknown
// quantum state cannot be copied. Sounio enforces this at COMPILE TIME
// via linear types: a Qubit is a linear resource that must be consumed
// exactly once. Attempting to copy produces a compile error.
//
// SOTA: Guppy (Quantinuum, Oct 2025): "Imperative Quantum Programming
//       with Ownership and Borrowing"
//       — Linear types enforce no-cloning at the type level
//       — Statically compiled, strongly typed quantum programs
//
//       Beryllium (Horizon Quantum, Dec 2025):
//       — "Manage information, not qubits" philosophy
//       — Quantum computation as effectful computation
//
// This module provides:
//   - Linear Qubit type (cannot be cloned)
//   - Standard quantum gates (H, X, Y, Z, CNOT, T, S)
//   - Measurement (consumes qubit, returns classical bit)
//   - Quantum state simulation (for testing)
//   - Bell pair creation and teleportation primitives

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers for state simulation
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_sim(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

// =============================================================================
// Qubit — A Linear Resource
// =============================================================================

// A qubit is a linear type: it MUST be consumed exactly once.
// The compiler will reject programs that:
//   1. Use a qubit twice (violates no-cloning)
//   2. Forget to use a qubit (violates no-deleting — optional)
//
// Internally, state_id indexes into the quantum simulator.
linear struct Qubit {
    state_id: i64,
}

// =============================================================================
// Quantum State Simulator
// =============================================================================
// For simulation/testing. A real quantum backend would replace this.
// State vector: 2^n complex amplitudes (max 8 qubits = 256 amplitudes)
// We store real and imaginary parts separately.

struct QuantumState {
    real: [f64; 256],
    imag: [f64; 256],
    n_qubits: i32,
    n_amplitudes: i32,      // 2^n_qubits
    next_id: i64,
}

fn quantum_state_new() -> QuantumState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var qs = QuantumState {
        real: [0.0; 256],
        imag: [0.0; 256],
        n_qubits: 0,
        n_amplitudes: 1,
        next_id: 0,
    }
    // |0...0⟩ state
    qs.real[0] = 1.0
    return qs
}

// =============================================================================
// Qubit Allocation
// =============================================================================

// Allocate a new qubit in the |0⟩ state
fn qubit_alloc(qs: &!QuantumState) -> Qubit with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = qs.next_id
    qs.next_id = qs.next_id + 1
    qs.n_qubits = qs.n_qubits + 1

    // Double the state space
    let old_n = qs.n_amplitudes
    qs.n_amplitudes = old_n * 2
    // New qubit in |0⟩: amplitudes for |...0⟩ stay, |...1⟩ = 0
    // Already correct since we initialized to zeros

    Qubit { state_id: qid }
}

// =============================================================================
// Single-Qubit Gates
// =============================================================================
// Each gate CONSUMES the input qubit and RETURNS a new one.
// This is the linear type pattern: the old state is gone, replaced by new state.

// Hadamard gate: |0⟩ → (|0⟩ + |1⟩)/sqrt(2), |1⟩ → (|0⟩ - |1⟩)/sqrt(2)
fn hadamard(q: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> Qubit with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = q.state_id     // consumes q (linear move)
    let target = qid as i32
    let inv_sqrt2 = 0.7071067811865476

    let n = qs.n_amplitudes
    let stride = 1 << target  // 2^target
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        if bit == 0 {
            let j = i | stride  // partner with bit=1
            let r0 = qs.real[i]
            let i0 = qs.imag[i]
            let r1 = qs.real[j]
            let i1 = qs.imag[j]
            qs.real[i] = inv_sqrt2 * (r0 + r1)
            qs.imag[i] = inv_sqrt2 * (i0 + i1)
            qs.real[j] = inv_sqrt2 * (r0 - r1)
            qs.imag[j] = inv_sqrt2 * (i0 - i1)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    Qubit { state_id: qid }
}

// Pauli-X (NOT gate): |0⟩ → |1⟩, |1⟩ → |0⟩
fn pauli_x(q: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> Qubit with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = q.state_id
    let target = qid as i32
    let stride = 1 << target
    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        if bit == 0 {
            let j = i | stride
            let tmp_r = qs.real[i]
            let tmp_i = qs.imag[i]
            qs.real[i] = qs.real[j]
            qs.imag[i] = qs.imag[j]
            qs.real[j] = tmp_r
            qs.imag[j] = tmp_i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    Qubit { state_id: qid }
}

// Pauli-Z: |0⟩ → |0⟩, |1⟩ → -|1⟩
fn pauli_z(q: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> Qubit with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = q.state_id
    let target = qid as i32
    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        if bit == 1 {
            qs.real[i] = 0.0 - qs.real[i]
            qs.imag[i] = 0.0 - qs.imag[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    Qubit { state_id: qid }
}

// S gate (phase gate): |0⟩ → |0⟩, |1⟩ → i|1⟩
fn s_gate(q: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> Qubit with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = q.state_id
    let target = qid as i32
    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        if bit == 1 {
            // Multiply by i: (a + bi) * i = -b + ai
            let r = qs.real[i]
            let im = qs.imag[i]
            qs.real[i] = 0.0 - im
            qs.imag[i] = r
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    Qubit { state_id: qid }
}

// T gate: |0⟩ → |0⟩, |1⟩ → e^{i*pi/4}|1⟩
fn t_gate(q: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> Qubit with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = q.state_id
    let target = qid as i32
    let cos_pi4 = 0.7071067811865476
    let sin_pi4 = 0.7071067811865476
    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        if bit == 1 {
            let r = qs.real[i]
            let im = qs.imag[i]
            qs.real[i] = r * cos_pi4 - im * sin_pi4
            qs.imag[i] = r * sin_pi4 + im * cos_pi4
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    Qubit { state_id: qid }
}

// =============================================================================
// Two-Qubit Gates
// =============================================================================

// CNOT: Controlled-NOT
// |control, target⟩: flips target if control is |1⟩
// Consumes BOTH qubits linearly, returns BOTH
struct QubitPair {
    first: Qubit,
    second: Qubit,
}

fn cnot(control: Qubit, target: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> QubitPair with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let cid = control.state_id   // consumes control
    let tid = target.state_id    // consumes target
    let c = cid as i32
    let t = tid as i32
    let t_stride = 1 << t

    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let c_bit = (i >> c) & 1
        let t_bit = (i >> t) & 1
        // Only swap when control=1, target=0
        if c_bit == 1 {
            if t_bit == 0 {
                let j = i | t_stride  // same but target=1
                let tmp_r = qs.real[i]
                let tmp_i = qs.imag[i]
                qs.real[i] = qs.real[j]
                qs.imag[i] = qs.imag[j]
                qs.real[j] = tmp_r
                qs.imag[j] = tmp_i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    QubitPair {
        first: Qubit { state_id: cid },
        second: Qubit { state_id: tid },
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Measurement — Collapses the Qubit (consumes it forever!)
// =============================================================================
// Measurement is the ultimate linear consumption: the qubit ceases to exist
// as a quantum resource and becomes a classical bit.
//
// Returns: true for |1⟩, false for |0⟩

struct MeasurementResult {
    outcome: bool,          // true = |1⟩, false = |0⟩
    probability: f64,       // probability of the observed outcome
}

fn measure(q: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState, rng_seed: f64) -> MeasurementResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let qid = q.state_id        // consumes q — qubit ceases to exist
    let target = qid as i32
    let stride = 1 << target

    // Compute probability of measuring |1⟩
    var prob_one: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        if bit == 1 {
            prob_one = prob_one + qs.real[i] * qs.real[i] + qs.imag[i] * qs.imag[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Pseudo-random "coin flip" using seed (deterministic for reproducibility)
    let coin = rng_seed  // should be uniform [0,1)
    let outcome = coin < prob_one

    // Collapse: zero out the non-observed branch and renormalize
    let prob_observed = if outcome { prob_one } else { 1.0 - prob_one }
    let norm = if prob_observed > 1.0e-30 { 1.0 / sqrt_sim(prob_observed) } else { 0.0 }

    i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        let bit = (i >> target) & 1
        let keep = if outcome { bit == 1 } else { bit == 0 }
        if keep {
            qs.real[i] = qs.real[i] * norm
            qs.imag[i] = qs.imag[i] * norm
        } else {
            qs.real[i] = 0.0
            qs.imag[i] = 0.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Qubit q is consumed here — linear type system ensures it cannot be used again
    MeasurementResult {
        outcome: outcome,
        probability: prob_observed,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Bell Pair — Entanglement via H + CNOT
// =============================================================================
// Creates the Bell state |Φ+⟩ = (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/sqrt(2)

fn bell_pair(q1: Qubit, q2: Qubit, qs: &!QuantumState) -> QubitPair with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h_q1 = hadamard(q1, qs)
    cnot(h_q1, q2, qs)
}

// =============================================================================
// State Inspection (for simulation/testing only)
// =============================================================================

struct StateInfo {
    n_qubits: i32,
    prob_zero: f64,     // probability of all-zeros state
    total_prob: f64,    // should be 1.0 (normalization check)
}

fn quantum_state_info(qs: &QuantumState) -> StateInfo with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var total: f64 = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < qs.n_amplitudes {
        total = total + qs.real[i] * qs.real[i] + qs.imag[i] * qs.imag[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let p0 = qs.real[0] * qs.real[0] + qs.imag[0] * qs.imag[0]

    StateInfo {
        n_qubits: qs.n_qubits,
        prob_zero: p0,
        total_prob: total,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/quantum/mod.sio ===
//! stdlib/quantum

module quantum


// === FILE: stdlib/quantum/vqe.sio ===
//! vqe (disabled)


// === FILE: stdlib/random/distributions.sio ===
// random::distributions — Probability Distributions
//
// Sample from common distributions with epistemic awareness.
// Every sample carries its distributional provenance.
//
// Distributions:
// - Uniform: U(low, high)
// - Normal: N(mean, std)
// - LogNormal: ln(X) ~ N(mu, sigma)
// - Exponential: Exp(rate)
// - Gamma: Gamma(shape, rate)
// - Beta: Beta(alpha, beta)
// - Poisson: Pois(rate)
//
// References:
// - Devroye (1986): "Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation"
// - Marsaglia & Tsang (2000): "A Simple Method for Generating Gamma Variables"

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sin(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn floor(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
}

// ============================================================================
// RNG (inline from rng.d for self-contained module)
// ============================================================================

struct DstPcg64 {
    state_hi: i64,
    state_lo: i64,
    inc_hi: i64,
    inc_lo: i64,
}

fn dst_pcg64_new(seed: i64) -> DstPcg64 {
    // Simplified initialization
    DstPcg64 {
        state_hi: seed ^ 0x853c49e6748fea9b,
        state_lo: seed * 6364136223846793005,
        inc_hi: 1,
        inc_lo: 1,
    }
}

fn dst_pcg64_next_i64(rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, i64) {
    let old_state = rng.state_lo
    let new_lo = rng.state_lo * 6364136223846793005 + rng.inc_lo
    let new_hi = rng.state_hi + rng.inc_hi

    let xorshifted = (old_state >> 18) ^ old_state
    let rot = (old_state >> 59) & 63
    let result = xorshifted >> rot

    return (DstPcg64 {
        state_hi: new_hi,
        state_lo: new_lo,
        inc_hi: rng.inc_hi,
        inc_lo: rng.inc_lo,
    }, result)
}

fn dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_i64(rng)
    let bits = result.1
    let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
    let fraction = (positive as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
    return (result.0, fraction)
}

fn dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    var current = rng
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64(current)
        current = result.0
        if result.1 > 0.0 {
            return (current, result.1)
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    (current, 0.0000001)
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSTANTS
// ============================================================================

fn dst_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }
fn e() -> f64 { 2.71828182845904523536 }

// ============================================================================
// UNIFORM DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Uniform {
    low: f64,
    high: f64,
}

fn uniform_new(low: f64, high: f64) -> Uniform {
    Uniform { low: low, high: high }
}

fn uniform_standard() -> Uniform {
    Uniform { low: 0.0, high: 1.0 }
}

fn uniform_sample(dist: Uniform, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    let v = dist.low + result.1 * (dist.high - dist.low)
    return (result.0, v)
}

fn uniform_mean(dist: Uniform) -> f64 {
    (dist.low + dist.high) / 2.0
}

fn uniform_variance(dist: Uniform) -> f64 {
    let range = dist.high - dist.low
    range * range / 12.0
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMAL (GAUSSIAN) DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Normal {
    mean: f64,
    std: f64,
}

fn normal_new(mean: f64, std: f64) -> Normal {
    Normal { mean: mean, std: std }
}

fn normal_standard() -> Normal {
    Normal { mean: 0.0, std: 1.0 }
}

// Sample using Box-Muller transform
fn normal_sample(dist: Normal, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let r1 = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let rng2 = r1.0
    let u1 = r1.1

    let r2 = dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng2)
    let rng3 = r2.0
    let u2 = r2.1

    // Box-Muller transform
    let mag = sqrt(-2.0 * log(u1))
    let z = mag * cos(2.0 * dst_pi() * u2)

    let v = dist.mean + dist.std * z
    return (rng3, v)
}

// Sample using Box-Muller (returns both values)
fn normal_sample_pair(dist: Normal, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64, f64) {
    let r1 = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let r2 = dst_pcg64_next_f64(r1.0)

    let mag = sqrt(-2.0 * log(r1.1))
    let z1 = mag * cos(2.0 * dst_pi() * r2.1)
    let z2 = mag * sin(2.0 * dst_pi() * r2.1)

    let v1 = dist.mean + dist.std * z1
    let v2 = dist.mean + dist.std * z2
    return (r2.0, v1, v2)
}

fn normal_mean(dist: Normal) -> f64 { dist.mean }
fn normal_variance(dist: Normal) -> f64 { dist.std * dist.std }

fn normal_pdf(dist: Normal, x: f64) -> f64 {
    let z = (x - dist.mean) / dist.std
    exp(-0.5 * z * z) / (dist.std * sqrt(2.0 * dst_pi()))
}

// ============================================================================
// LOG-NORMAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct LogNormal {
    mu: f64,     // Mean of ln(X)
    sigma: f64,  // Std of ln(X)
}

fn lognormal_new(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> LogNormal {
    LogNormal { mu: mu, sigma: sigma }
}

// Create from desired mean and std of the distribution (not log-space)
fn lognormal_from_mean_std(mean: f64, std: f64) -> LogNormal {
    let variance = std * std
    let mu = log(mean * mean / sqrt(variance + mean * mean))
    let sigma = sqrt(log(1.0 + variance / (mean * mean)))
    LogNormal { mu: mu, sigma: sigma }
}

fn lognormal_sample(dist: LogNormal, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let n = normal_new(dist.mu, dist.sigma)
    let result = normal_sample(n, rng)
    return (result.0, exp(result.1))
}

fn lognormal_mean(dist: LogNormal) -> f64 {
    exp(dist.mu + dist.sigma * dist.sigma / 2.0)
}

fn lognormal_variance(dist: LogNormal) -> f64 {
    let s2 = dist.sigma * dist.sigma
    return (exp(s2) - 1.0) * exp(2.0 * dist.mu + s2)
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPONENTIAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Exponential {
    rate: f64,  // lambda
}

fn exponential_new(rate: f64) -> Exponential {
    Exponential { rate: rate }
}

fn exponential_from_mean(mean: f64) -> Exponential {
    Exponential { rate: 1.0 / mean }
}

fn exponential_sample(dist: Exponential, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let v = -log(result.1) / dist.rate
    return (result.0, v)
}

fn exponential_mean(dist: Exponential) -> f64 { 1.0 / dist.rate }
fn exponential_variance(dist: Exponential) -> f64 { 1.0 / (dist.rate * dist.rate) }

// ============================================================================
// GAMMA DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Gamma {
    shape: f64,  // alpha > 0
    rate: f64,   // beta > 0
}

fn gamma_new(shape: f64, rate: f64) -> Gamma {
    Gamma { shape: shape, rate: rate }
}

fn gamma_with_scale(shape: f64, scale: f64) -> Gamma {
    Gamma { shape: shape, rate: 1.0 / scale }
}

// Marsaglia & Tsang method for shape >= 1
fn gamma_sample_shape_ge1(shape: f64, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let d = shape - 1.0 / 3.0
    let c = 1.0 / sqrt(9.0 * d)
    let n = normal_standard()

    var current_rng = rng

    // Rejection sampling
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 1000 {
        let nr = normal_sample(n, current_rng)
        current_rng = nr.0
        let x = nr.1
        let v = 1.0 + c * x

        if v > 0.0 {
            let v3 = v * v * v
            let ur = dst_pcg64_next_f64(current_rng)
            current_rng = ur.0
            let u = ur.1

            let x2 = x * x
            let x4 = x2 * x2

            if u < 1.0 - 0.0331 * x4 {
                return (current_rng, d * v3)
            }
            if log(u) < 0.5 * x2 + d * (1.0 - v3 + log(v3)) {
                return (current_rng, d * v3)
            }
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }

    // Fallback (shouldn't reach here normally)
    return (current_rng, shape)
}

fn gamma_sample(dist: Gamma, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    if dist.shape >= 1.0 {
        let result = gamma_sample_shape_ge1(dist.shape, rng)
        return (result.0, result.1 / dist.rate)
    } else {
        // For shape < 1: use Gamma(1+shape) * U^(1/shape)
        let g_result = gamma_sample_shape_ge1(1.0 + dist.shape, rng)
        let u_result = dst_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(g_result.0)
        let scale_factor = pow(u_result.1, 1.0 / dist.shape)
        return (u_result.0, g_result.1 * scale_factor / dist.rate)
    }
}

fn gamma_mean(dist: Gamma) -> f64 { dist.shape / dist.rate }
fn gamma_variance(dist: Gamma) -> f64 { dist.shape / (dist.rate * dist.rate) }

// ============================================================================
// BETA DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Beta {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64,
}

fn beta_new(alpha: f64, beta_val: f64) -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: alpha, beta: beta_val }
}

fn beta_uniform() -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
}

fn beta_jeffreys() -> Beta {
    Beta { alpha: 0.5, beta: 0.5 }
}

// Sample using ratio of gammas: X/(X+Y) where X~Gamma(alpha,1), Y~Gamma(beta,1)
fn beta_sample(dist: Beta, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, f64) {
    let g_a = gamma_new(dist.alpha, 1.0)
    let g_b = gamma_new(dist.beta, 1.0)

    let r1 = gamma_sample(g_a, rng)
    let r2 = gamma_sample(g_b, r1.0)

    let x = r1.1
    let y = r2.1
    let v = x / (x + y)

    return (r2.0, v)
}

fn beta_mean(dist: Beta) -> f64 {
    dist.alpha / (dist.alpha + dist.beta)
}

fn beta_variance(dist: Beta) -> f64 {
    let ab = dist.alpha + dist.beta
    return (dist.alpha * dist.beta) / (ab * ab * (ab + 1.0))
}

// ============================================================================
// POISSON DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Poisson {
    rate: f64,  // lambda > 0
}

fn poisson_new(rate: f64) -> Poisson {
    Poisson { rate: rate }
}

// Knuth's algorithm for small lambda
fn poisson_sample(dist: Poisson, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, i64) {
    if dist.rate < 30.0 {
        // Knuth's algorithm
        let l = exp(0.0 - dist.rate)
        var k: i64 = 0
        var p = 1.0
        var current_rng = rng

        var done = false
        while !done {
            k = k + 1
            let ur = dst_pcg64_next_f64(current_rng)
            current_rng = ur.0
            p = p * ur.1
            if p <= l {
                done = true
            }
        }

        return (current_rng, k - 1)
    } else {
        // Normal approximation for large lambda
        let n = normal_new(dist.rate, sqrt(dist.rate))
        let result = normal_sample(n, rng)
        let val = if result.1 < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { result.1 }
        let rounded = floor(val + 0.5) as i64
        return (result.0, rounded)
    }
}

fn poisson_mean(dist: Poisson) -> f64 { dist.rate }
fn poisson_variance(dist: Poisson) -> f64 { dist.rate }

// ============================================================================
// BERNOULLI DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Bernoulli {
    p: f64,
}

fn bernoulli_new(p: f64) -> Bernoulli {
    Bernoulli { p: p }
}

fn bernoulli_sample(dist: Bernoulli, rng: DstPcg64) -> (DstPcg64, bool) {
    let result = dst_pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    return (result.0, result.1 < dist.p)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/random/rng.sio ===
// random::rng — Random Number Generators
//
// Fast, high-quality PRNGs for scientific computing.
// PCG64: Default, excellent statistical quality
// RngXoshiro256++: Fast for simulations
// SplitMix64: For seeding other generators
//
// References:
// - O'Neill (2014): "PCG: A Family of Simple Fast Space-Efficient PRNGs"
// - Blackman & Vigna (2018): "Scrambled Linear Pseudorandom Number Generators"

// ============================================================================
// SPLITMIX64 — FOR SEEDING
// ============================================================================

struct SplitMix64 {
    state: i64,
}

fn splitmix64_new(seed: i64) -> SplitMix64 {
    SplitMix64 { state: seed }
}

fn splitmix64_next(rng: SplitMix64) -> (SplitMix64, i64) {
    // state += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    let new_state = rng.state + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 as i64
    var z = new_state

    // z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = z ^ (z >> 30)
    // Simplified multiplication for interpreter
    z = z * 0xbf58476d as i64

    // z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    z = z ^ (z >> 27)
    z = z * 0x94d049bb as i64

    z = z ^ (z >> 31)

    (SplitMix64 { state: new_state }, z)
}

// ============================================================================
// PCG64 — DEFAULT GENERATOR
// ============================================================================

// PCG64 state (simplified for interpreter)
struct Pcg64 {
    state_hi: i64,
    state_lo: i64,
    inc_hi: i64,
    inc_lo: i64,
}

fn pcg64_new(seed: i64) -> Pcg64 {
    // Initialize using SplitMix64
    var sm = splitmix64_new(seed)
    let r1 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r1.0
    let s1 = r1.1

    let r2 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r2.0
    let s2 = r2.1

    let r3 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r3.0
    let s3 = r3.1

    let r4 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    let s4 = r4.1

    Pcg64 {
        state_hi: s1,
        state_lo: s2,
        inc_hi: s3 | 1,  // Ensure odd
        inc_lo: s4 | 1,
    }
}

fn pcg64_next_i64(rng: Pcg64) -> (Pcg64, i64) {
    let old_state = rng.state_lo

    // Linear congruential update (simplified)
    // state = state * MULTIPLIER + inc
    let new_lo = rng.state_lo * 6364136223846793005 as i64 + rng.inc_lo
    let new_hi = rng.state_hi + rng.inc_hi

    // XSL-RR output function (simplified)
    let xorshifted = (old_state >> 18) ^ old_state
    let rot = (old_state >> 59) as i64
    let result = xorshifted >> (rot & 63)

    (Pcg64 {
        state_hi: new_hi,
        state_lo: new_lo,
        inc_hi: rng.inc_hi,
        inc_lo: rng.inc_lo,
    }, result)
}

// Generate f64 in [0, 1)
fn pcg64_next_f64(rng: Pcg64) -> (Pcg64, f64) {
    let result = pcg64_next_i64(rng)
    let new_rng = result.0
    let bits = result.1

    // Use upper bits for better distribution
    let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
    let fraction = (positive as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0

    (new_rng, fraction)
}

// Generate f64 in (0, 1) — excludes 0
fn pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng: Pcg64) -> (Pcg64, f64) {
    var current = rng
    var value = 0.0

    // Keep generating until we get non-zero
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let result = pcg64_next_f64(current)
        current = result.0
        value = result.1
        if value > 0.0 {
            return (current, value)
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }

    // Fallback to small positive value
    (current, 0.0000001)
}

// Generate bool with probability p
fn pcg64_next_bool(rng: Pcg64, p: f64) -> (Pcg64, bool) {
    let result = pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    (result.0, result.1 < p)
}

// Generate integer in [0, n)
fn pcg64_bounded(rng: Pcg64, n: i64) -> (Pcg64, i64) {
    let result = pcg64_next_i64(rng)
    let new_rng = result.0
    let x = result.1

    // Simple modulo (with bias for simplicity)
    let positive = if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
    let bounded = positive % n

    (new_rng, bounded)
}

// ============================================================================
// XOSHIRO256++ — FAST SIMULATION RNG
// ============================================================================

struct RngXoshiro256 {
    s0: i64,
    s1: i64,
    s2: i64,
    s3: i64,
}

fn xoshiro256_new(seed: i64) -> RngXoshiro256 {
    var sm = splitmix64_new(seed)

    let r1 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r1.0
    let r2 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r2.0
    let r3 = splitmix64_next(sm)
    sm = r3.0
    let r4 = splitmix64_next(sm)

    RngXoshiro256 {
        s0: r1.1,
        s1: r2.1,
        s2: r3.1,
        s3: r4.1,
    }
}

fn rng_rotl(x: i64, k: i64) -> i64 {
    (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k))
}

fn xoshiro256_next_i64(rng: RngXoshiro256) -> (RngXoshiro256, i64) {
    // result = rng_rotl(s0 + s3, 23) + s0
    let result = rng_rotl(rng.s0 + rng.s3, 23) + rng.s0

    let t = rng.s1 << 17

    var s2 = rng.s2 ^ rng.s0
    var s3 = rng.s3 ^ rng.s1
    var s1 = rng.s1 ^ s2
    var s0 = rng.s0 ^ s3

    s2 = s2 ^ t
    s3 = rng_rotl(s3, 45)

    (RngXoshiro256 { s0: s0, s1: s1, s2: s2, s3: s3 }, result)
}

fn xoshiro256_next_f64(rng: RngXoshiro256) -> (RngXoshiro256, f64) {
    let result = xoshiro256_next_i64(rng)
    let new_rng = result.0
    let bits = result.1

    let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
    let fraction = (positive as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0

    (new_rng, fraction)
}

// ============================================================================
// RNG WRAPPER (functional approach)
// ============================================================================

// Since global mutable state isn't supported, we use a functional approach
// where the RNG state is passed through and returned

struct RngPcgWrapper {
    rng: Pcg64,
}

fn rng_pcg_new(seed: i64) -> RngPcgWrapper {
    RngPcgWrapper { rng: pcg64_new(seed) }
}

fn rng_pcg_next_f64(state: RngPcgWrapper) -> (RngPcgWrapper, f64) {
    let result = pcg64_next_f64(state.rng)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

fn rng_pcg_next_i64(state: RngPcgWrapper) -> (RngPcgWrapper, i64) {
    let result = pcg64_next_i64(state.rng)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

fn rng_pcg_next_bool(state: RngPcgWrapper, p: f64) -> (RngPcgWrapper, bool) {
    let result = pcg64_next_bool(state.rng, p)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

fn rng_pcg_bounded(state: RngPcgWrapper, n: i64) -> (RngPcgWrapper, i64) {
    let result = pcg64_bounded(state.rng, n)
    (RngPcgWrapper { rng: result.0 }, result.1)
}

// ============================================================================
// XORSHIFT128+ RNG WITH FUNCTIONAL (VALUE-PASSING) API
// ============================================================================
//
// Design: Explicit state threading — no global mutable state.
// Algorithm: xorshift128+ (Vigna 2014) with splitmix64 seeding.
// Each function returns (value, new_state) so callers chain state.

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Inline math helpers — no imports required
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn rng_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn rng_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64
        k = k + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn rng_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn rng_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// RngState — xorshift128+ state (two 64-bit words)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct RngState {
    s0: i64,
    s1: i64,
}

// splitmix64 step: expand a single seed word into well-mixed output
fn rng_splitmix_step(s: i64) -> (i64, i64) with Mut {
    let next = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    var z = next
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let out = z ^ (z >> 31)
    (next, out)
}

// Initialize RngState from a seed using splitmix64
fn rng_new(seed: i64) -> RngState with Mut {
    let step1 = rng_splitmix_step(seed)
    let s = step1.0
    let s0 = step1.1
    let step2 = rng_splitmix_step(s)
    let s1 = step2.1
    RngState { s0: s0, s1: s1 }
}

// xorshift128+: returns (random i64, new state)
fn rng_next(state: RngState) -> (i64, RngState) with Mut {
    var x = state.s0
    let y = state.s1
    x = x ^ (x << 23)
    x = x ^ (x >> 17)
    x = x ^ y
    x = x ^ (y >> 26)
    let out = state.s0 + y
    (out, RngState { s0: y, s1: x })
}

// Uniform [0, 1) — clears sign bit via AND, maps to [0, 1) by dividing by 2^63-1
fn rng_uniform(state: RngState) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = rng_next(state)
    let bits = r.0
    // Clear sign bit: AND with 0x7fffffffffffffff gives value in [0, 2^63-1]
    let pos = bits & 0x7fffffffffffffff
    let f = (pos as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
    (f, r.1)
}

// Uniform [lo, hi)
fn rng_uniform_range(state: RngState, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = rng_uniform(state)
    (lo + r.0 * (hi - lo), r.1)
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Distributions
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Normal N(mu, sigma) — Box-Muller transform
fn rng_normal(state: RngState, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Need u1 > 0 for log; retry up to 10 times
    var cur = state
    var u1 = 0.0
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        if r.0 > 0.0 {
            u1 = r.0
            attempts = 100  // break
        } else {
            attempts = attempts + 1
        }
    }
    if u1 <= 0.0 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let r2 = rng_uniform(cur)
    let u2 = r2.0
    let new_state = r2.1
    let mag = rng_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * rng_ln(u1))
    let z = mag * rng_cos(2.0 * 3.14159265358979323846 * u2)
    (mu + sigma * z, new_state)
}

// Exponential Exp(lambda) — inverse CDF: -ln(u)/lambda
fn rng_exponential(state: RngState, lambda: f64) -> (f64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var u = 0.0
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        if r.0 > 0.0 {
            u = r.0
            attempts = 100
        } else {
            attempts = attempts + 1
        }
    }
    if u <= 0.0 { u = 1.0e-10 }
    ((0.0 - rng_ln(u)) / lambda, cur)
}

// Poisson Pois(lambda) — Knuth's algorithm (good for lambda < 30)
fn rng_poisson(state: RngState, lambda: f64) -> (i64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let l = rng_ln(1.0)  // just 0 — used as a warmup call
    // e^-lambda as a product threshold
    // We compute exp(-lambda) via repeated multiply on ln comparison
    // Using Knuth: generate uniform products until < e^-lambda
    // e^-lambda: approximate via rng_ln(p) < -lambda
    var cur = state
    var k: i64 = 0
    var log_p = 0.0
    var done = false
    while !done {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        var u = r.0
        if u <= 0.0 { u = 1.0e-10 }
        log_p = log_p + rng_ln(u)
        if log_p < (0.0 - lambda) {
            done = true
        } else {
            k = k + 1
        }
    }
    (k, cur)
}

// Bernoulli(p) — 1 with probability p, 0 otherwise
fn rng_bernoulli(state: RngState, p: f64) -> (i32, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = rng_uniform(state)
    let v: i32 = if r.0 < p { 1 } else { 0 }
    (v, r.1)
}

// Geometric(p) — number of trials until first success (1-indexed)
fn rng_geometric(state: RngState, p: f64) -> (i64, RngState) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var u = 0.0
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        cur = r.1
        if r.0 > 0.0 {
            u = r.0
            attempts = 100
        } else {
            attempts = attempts + 1
        }
    }
    if u <= 0.0 { u = 1.0e-10 }
    // ceiling(ln(u) / ln(1-p))
    let log_u = rng_ln(u)
    let log_1mp = rng_ln(1.0 - p)
    var k = log_u / log_1mp
    // ceiling: if k is not already integer
    let ki = k as i64
    let result: i64 = if (ki as f64) < k { ki + 1 } else { ki }
    let final_k: i64 = if result < 1 { 1 } else { result }
    (final_k, cur)
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sampling utilities — fixed-size array operations
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Fisher-Yates shuffle of first n elements in arr (max 256)
// Returns (new_state, shuffled_array) — by-value for JIT compatibility
fn rng_shuffle(state: RngState, arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> (RngState, [f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var out = arr
    var i = n - 1
    while i > 0 {
        // Get random j in [0, i]
        let r = rng_next(cur)
        cur = r.1
        let bits = r.0
        let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
        let j = (positive % ((i + 1) as i64)) as i32
        let tmp = out[i]
        out[i] = out[j]
        out[j] = tmp
        i = i - 1
    }
    (cur, out)
}

// Fill first n elements with uniform [0, 1) samples
// Returns (new_state, filled_array) — by-value for JIT compatibility
fn rng_fill_uniform(state: RngState, n: i32) -> (RngState, [f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var arr: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let r = rng_uniform(cur)
        arr[i] = r.0
        cur = r.1
        i = i + 1
    }
    (cur, arr)
}

// Fill first n elements with normal samples N(mu, sigma)
// Returns (new_state, filled_array) — by-value for JIT compatibility
fn rng_fill_normal(state: RngState, n: i32, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> (RngState, [f64; 256]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cur = state
    var arr: [f64; 256] = [0.0; 256]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let r = rng_normal(cur, mu, sigma)
        arr[i] = r.0
        cur = r.1
        i = i + 1
    }
    (cur, arr)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/random/sampling.sio ===
// random::sampling — Random Sampling Utilities
//
// Functions for sampling from collections, shuffling, and PK/PD variability.
//
// Features:
// - sample: Random selection from arrays
// - sample_weighted: Weighted random selection
// - shuffle: Random permutation
// - resample: Bootstrap resampling
// - pk_variability: PK parameter variability (IIV, IOV)
//
// References:
// - Knuth (1997): "The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 2"
// - Lavielle (2014): "Mixed Effects Models for the Population Approach"

// ============================================================================
// RNG (inline from rng.d for self-contained module)
// ============================================================================

struct SmpPcg64 {
    state_hi: i64,
    state_lo: i64,
    inc_hi: i64,
    inc_lo: i64,
}

fn smp_pcg64_new(seed: i64) -> SmpPcg64 {
    SmpPcg64 {
        state_hi: seed ^ 0x853c49e6748fea9b,
        state_lo: seed * 6364136223846793005,
        inc_hi: 1,
        inc_lo: 1,
    }
}

fn smp_pcg64_next_i64(rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    let old_state = rng.state_lo
    let new_lo = rng.state_lo * 6364136223846793005 + rng.inc_lo
    let new_hi = rng.state_hi + rng.inc_hi

    let xorshifted = (old_state >> 18) ^ old_state
    let rot = (old_state >> 59) & 63
    let result = xorshifted >> rot

    return (SmpPcg64 {
        state_hi: new_hi,
        state_lo: new_lo,
        inc_hi: rng.inc_hi,
        inc_lo: rng.inc_lo,
    }, result)
}

fn smp_pcg64_next_f64(rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let result = smp_pcg64_next_i64(rng)
    let bits = result.1
    let positive = if bits < 0 { 0 - bits } else { bits }
    let fraction = (positive as f64) / 9223372036854775807.0
    return (result.0, fraction)
}

// Generate integer in [0, n)
fn smp_pcg64_bounded(rng: SmpPcg64, n: i64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    let result = smp_pcg64_next_i64(rng)
    let x = result.1
    let positive = if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
    let bounded = positive % n
    return (result.0, bounded)
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMAL DISTRIBUTION (for variability)
// ============================================================================

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn cos(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn smp_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn smp_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    var current = rng
    var attempts = 0
    while attempts < 10 {
        let result = smp_pcg64_next_f64(current)
        current = result.0
        if result.1 > 0.0 {
            return (current, result.1)
        }
        attempts = attempts + 1
    }
    return (current, 0.0000001)
}

fn sample_normal(mean: f64, std: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let r1 = smp_pcg64_next_f64_nonzero(rng)
    let r2 = smp_pcg64_next_f64(r1.0)

    let mag = sqrt(-2.0 * log(r1.1))
    let z = mag * cos(2.0 * smp_pi() * r2.1)

    return (r2.0, mean + std * z)
}

// ============================================================================
// BASIC SAMPLING
// ============================================================================

// Sample a single random index from [0, n)
fn sample_index(n: i64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    return smp_pcg64_bounded(rng, n)
}

// Sample a single element from an f64 array
fn sample_one_f64(arr: [f64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let n = arr.len() as i64
    let idx_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(rng, n)
    return (idx_result.0, arr[idx_result.1 as usize])
}

// Sample a single element from an i64 array
fn sample_one_i64(arr: [i64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    let n = arr.len() as i64
    let idx_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(rng, n)
    return (idx_result.0, arr[idx_result.1 as usize])
}

// ============================================================================
// WEIGHTED SAMPLING
// ============================================================================

// Sample index with weights (weights don't need to sum to 1)
fn sample_weighted_index(weights: [f64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, i64) {
    // Compute total weight
    var total = 0.0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < weights.len() {
        total = total + weights[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Sample uniform [0, total)
    let u_result = smp_pcg64_next_f64(rng)
    let threshold = u_result.1 * total

    // Find which bucket
    var cumsum = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < weights.len() {
        cumsum = cumsum + weights[i]
        if cumsum > threshold {
            return (u_result.0, i as i64)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Fallback to last index
    return (u_result.0, (weights.len() - 1) as i64)
}

// ============================================================================
// SHUFFLING (Fisher-Yates)
// ============================================================================

// Shuffle an array in place using Fisher-Yates
fn smp_shuffle_f64(arr: [f64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, [f64]) {
    var result = arr
    var current_rng = rng
    var i = result.len()

    while i > 1 {
        i = i - 1
        let j_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(current_rng, (i + 1) as i64)
        current_rng = j_result.0
        let j = j_result.1 as usize

        // Swap result[i] and result[j]
        let temp = result[i]
        result[i] = result[j]
        result[j] = temp
    }

    return (current_rng, result)
}

// Shuffle an i64 array
fn shuffle_i64(arr: [i64], rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, [i64]) {
    var result = arr
    var current_rng = rng
    var i = result.len()

    while i > 1 {
        i = i - 1
        let j_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(current_rng, (i + 1) as i64)
        current_rng = j_result.0
        let j = j_result.1 as usize

        let temp = result[i]
        result[i] = result[j]
        result[j] = temp
    }

    return (current_rng, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// RESAMPLING (BOOTSTRAP)
// ============================================================================

// Bootstrap resample: sample n items with replacement
fn resample_f64(arr: [f64], n: i64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, [f64]) {
    var result: [f64] = []
    var current_rng = rng
    let arr_len = arr.len() as i64

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx_result = smp_pcg64_bounded(current_rng, arr_len)
        current_rng = idx_result.0
        result.push(arr[idx_result.1 as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }

    return (current_rng, result)
}

// ============================================================================
// PK/PD VARIABILITY
// ============================================================================

// Inter-Individual Variability (IIV) parameters
struct IIV {
    omega_cl: f64,   // CV for clearance
    omega_vc: f64,   // CV for central volume
    omega_ka: f64,   // CV for absorption rate
}

fn iiv_new(omega_cl: f64, omega_vc: f64, omega_ka: f64) -> IIV {
    IIV {
        omega_cl: omega_cl,
        omega_vc: omega_vc,
        omega_ka: omega_ka,
    }
}

fn iiv_typical() -> IIV {
    // Typical PK variability (30% CV)
    IIV {
        omega_cl: 0.3,
        omega_vc: 0.3,
        omega_ka: 0.5,
    }
}

// Generate individual PK parameters with IIV
struct IndividualPK {
    cl: f64,   // Individual clearance
    vc: f64,   // Individual central volume
    ka: f64,   // Individual absorption rate constant
}

fn generate_individual_pk(
    pop_cl: f64, pop_vc: f64, pop_ka: f64,
    iiv: IIV, rng: SmpPcg64
) -> (SmpPcg64, IndividualPK) {
    // Sample eta values (random effects)
    let eta_cl_result = sample_normal(0.0, iiv.omega_cl, rng)
    let eta_vc_result = sample_normal(0.0, iiv.omega_vc, eta_cl_result.0)
    let eta_ka_result = sample_normal(0.0, iiv.omega_ka, eta_vc_result.0)

    // Apply exponential transformation
    let ind = IndividualPK {
        cl: pop_cl * exp(eta_cl_result.1),
        vc: pop_vc * exp(eta_vc_result.1),
        ka: pop_ka * exp(eta_ka_result.1),
    }

    return (eta_ka_result.0, ind)
}

// Generate a virtual population
fn generate_population(
    pop_cl: f64, pop_vc: f64, pop_ka: f64,
    iiv: IIV, n_subjects: i64, rng: SmpPcg64
) -> (SmpPcg64, [IndividualPK]) {
    var population: [IndividualPK] = []
    var current_rng = rng

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n_subjects {
        let result = generate_individual_pk(pop_cl, pop_vc, pop_ka, iiv, current_rng)
        current_rng = result.0
        population.push(result.1)
        i = i + 1
    }

    return (current_rng, population)
}

// ============================================================================
// RESIDUAL ERROR MODELS
// ============================================================================

// Add proportional residual error
fn add_proportional_error(value: f64, sigma: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let eps_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma, rng)
    return (eps_result.0, value * (1.0 + eps_result.1))
}

// Add additive residual error
fn add_additive_error(value: f64, sigma: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let eps_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma, rng)
    return (eps_result.0, value + eps_result.1)
}

// Add combined (additive + proportional) residual error
fn add_combined_error(value: f64, sigma_add: f64, sigma_prop: f64, rng: SmpPcg64) -> (SmpPcg64, f64) {
    let eps1_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma_add, rng)
    let eps2_result = sample_normal(0.0, sigma_prop, eps1_result.0)
    return (eps2_result.0, value * (1.0 + eps2_result.1) + eps1_result.1)
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS


// === FILE: stdlib/random/xoshiro.sio ===
// stdlib/random/xoshiro.sio — Xoshiro256** PRNG with Prob Effect
//
// A proper pseudo-random number generator for Sounio.
// Every probabilistic function declares `with Prob` — effects are the API contract.
//
// Xoshiro256** is the current state-of-the-art PRNG:
//   - Period: 2^256 - 1
//   - Passes BigCrush, PractRand
//   - Very fast: ~1ns per generation
//   - No heap allocation, fixed 256-bit state
//
// SOTA: Blackman & Vigna (2021): "Scrambled Linear Pseudorandom Number Generators"
//
// Note on Prob effect: In Sounio, any function that involves randomness
// MUST declare `with Prob`. This makes non-determinism visible at the type
// level. Pure functions cannot call probabilistic functions.

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_rng(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn ln_rng(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e_val = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e_val = e_val + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e_val = e_val - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e_val as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn cos_rng(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// Xoshiro256** State
// =============================================================================

struct Xoshiro256 {
    s0: i64,
    s1: i64,
    s2: i64,
    s3: i64,
}

// =============================================================================
// Seed from a single i64
// =============================================================================
// Uses SplitMix64 to expand a single seed into the 256-bit state.

fn xoshiro_seed(seed: i64) -> Xoshiro256 with Mut {
    // SplitMix64 expansion
    var s = seed
    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    var z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s0 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s1 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s2 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    s = s + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15
    z = s
    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb
    let s3 = z ^ (z >> 31)

    Xoshiro256 { s0: s0, s1: s1, s2: s2, s3: s3 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Core: next_i64
// =============================================================================

fn rotl(x: i64, k: i32) -> i64 {
    (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k))
}

fn xoshiro_next_i64(rng: &!Xoshiro256) -> i64 with Mut {
    let result = rotl(rng.s1 * 5, 7) * 9

    let t = rng.s1 << 17
    rng.s2 = rng.s2 ^ rng.s0
    rng.s3 = rng.s3 ^ rng.s1
    rng.s1 = rng.s1 ^ rng.s2
    rng.s0 = rng.s0 ^ rng.s3
    rng.s2 = rng.s2 ^ t
    rng.s3 = rotl(rng.s3, 45)

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Uniform [0, 1) — The fundamental distribution
// =============================================================================

fn uniform(rng: &!Xoshiro256) -> f64 with Prob, Mut {
    let bits = xoshiro_next_i64(rng)
    // Use upper 53 bits for double precision
    let shifted = bits >> 11
    // Convert to f64 in [0, 1)
    // Note: i64 to f64 conversion, then divide by 2^53
    let val = (shifted as f64) * 1.1102230246251565e-16
    if val < 0.0 { 0.0 - val } else { val }
}

// Uniform in [lo, hi)
fn uniform_range(rng: &!Xoshiro256, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64 with Prob, Mut {
    lo + uniform(rng) * (hi - lo)
}

// =============================================================================
// Normal (Gaussian) — Box-Muller transform
// =============================================================================

fn normal(rng: &!Xoshiro256, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> f64 with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var u1 = uniform(rng)
    if u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let u2 = uniform(rng)
    let z = sqrt_rng(0.0 - 2.0 * ln_rng(u1)) * cos_rng(2.0 * 3.14159265358979323846 * u2)
    mu + sigma * z
}

// Standard normal N(0, 1)
fn standard_normal(rng: &!Xoshiro256) -> f64 with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    normal(rng, 0.0, 1.0)
}

// =============================================================================
// Exponential distribution
// =============================================================================

fn exponential(rng: &!Xoshiro256, lambda: f64) -> f64 with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var u = uniform(rng)
    if u < 1.0e-10 { u = 1.0e-10 }
    (0.0 - ln_rng(u)) / lambda
}

// =============================================================================
// Bernoulli distribution
// =============================================================================

fn bernoulli(rng: &!Xoshiro256, p: f64) -> bool with Prob, Mut {
    uniform(rng) < p
}

// =============================================================================
// Discrete uniform [lo, hi] (inclusive)
// =============================================================================

fn discrete_uniform(rng: &!Xoshiro256, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32 with Prob, Mut, Panic {
    let range = (hi - lo + 1) as f64
    let u = uniform(rng)
    lo + (u * range) as i32
}

// =============================================================================
// Shuffle (Fisher-Yates)
// =============================================================================

fn shuffle_f64(rng: &!Xoshiro256, arr: &![f64; 1024], n: i32) with Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = n - 1
    while i > 0 {
        let j = discrete_uniform(rng, 0, i)
        // Swap arr[i] and arr[j]
        let tmp = arr[i]
        arr[i] = arr[j]
        arr[j] = tmp
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Summary Statistics (for testing/validation)
// =============================================================================

struct SampleStats {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    min_val: f64,
    max_val: f64,
    n: i32,
}

fn sample_stats(samples: &[f64; 10000], n: i32) -> SampleStats with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n == 0 {
        return SampleStats { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, min_val: 0.0, max_val: 0.0, n: 0 }
    }

    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var min_v = samples[0]
    var max_v = samples[0]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + samples[i]
        if samples[i] < min_v { min_v = samples[i] }
        if samples[i] > max_v { max_v = samples[i] }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let mean = sum / (n as f64)

    var ss: f64 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = samples[i] - mean
        ss = ss + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    let variance = ss / ((n - 1) as f64)

    SampleStats {
        mean: mean,
        variance: variance,
        min_val: min_v,
        max_val: max_v,
        n: n,
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/regex/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/regex/lib.sio — Minimal pattern matching
//
// Supported pattern syntax:
//   .    matches any single byte
//   *    matches zero-or-more of the immediately preceding char/dot
//   ?    matches zero-or-one of the immediately preceding char/dot
//   ^    anchor to start of text (must be first character in pattern)
//   $    anchor to end of text   (must be last  character in pattern)
//   otherwise: literal byte match
//
// Fixed-size buffer API (no dynamic allocation):
//   pattern: &[u8; 64]   max pattern length 64 bytes
//   text:    &[u8; 256]  max text length 256 bytes

// =============================================================================
// Result type
// =============================================================================

struct MatchResult {
    matched: i32,   // 1 = match found, 0 = no match
    start:   i32,   // inclusive start position in text
    end:     i32,   // exclusive end position in text
}

// =============================================================================
// Internal helpers — must precede callers
// =============================================================================

// Returns 1 if pattern byte at pi matches text byte at ti
fn byte_matches(pat: &[u8; 64], pi: i32, txt: &[u8; 256], ti: i32) -> i32 {
    let p: u8 = pat[pi as usize]
    if p == 46 { return 1 }    // '.' matches anything
    let t: u8 = txt[ti as usize]
    if p == t { return 1 }
    0
}

// Try to match pattern[pi..pat_len) against text[ti..text_len).
// Returns end position (exclusive) on success, -1 on failure.
// Handles . * ? ^ $ anchoring.
fn match_here(pat: &[u8; 64], pi: i32, pat_len: i32,
              txt: &[u8; 256], ti: i32, text_len: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Base case: pattern exhausted → match succeeds at current ti
    if pi >= pat_len { return ti }

    // $ anchor: pattern ends here, text must also end here
    let pc: u8 = pat[pi as usize]
    if pc == 36 {       // '$'
        if pi + 1 == pat_len {
            if ti == text_len { return ti }
            return -1
        }
    }

    // Look-ahead for * or ?
    let next_pi = pi + 1
    let has_next: i32 = if next_pi < pat_len { 1 } else { 0 }
    let next_pc: u8 = if has_next == 1 { pat[next_pi as usize] } else { 0 }

    // '*' quantifier: zero or more
    if has_next == 1 && next_pc == 42 {     // '*'
        // Try zero repetitions first (skip both pattern char and '*')
        let zero_result = match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, ti, text_len)
        if zero_result >= 0 { return zero_result }
        // Try one-or-more repetitions
        var cur = ti
        while cur < text_len && byte_matches(pat, pi, txt, cur) == 1 {
            cur = cur + 1
            let r = match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, cur, text_len)
            if r >= 0 { return r }
        }
        return -1
    }

    // '?' quantifier: zero or one
    if has_next == 1 && next_pc == 63 {     // '?'
        // Try one match
        if ti < text_len && byte_matches(pat, pi, txt, ti) == 1 {
            let r = match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, ti + 1, text_len)
            if r >= 0 { return r }
        }
        // Try zero match
        return match_here(pat, pi + 2, pat_len, txt, ti, text_len)
    }

    // Literal or dot (no quantifier)
    if ti < text_len && byte_matches(pat, pi, txt, ti) == 1 {
        return match_here(pat, pi + 1, pat_len, txt, ti + 1, text_len)
    }
    -1
}

// =============================================================================
// Public API
// =============================================================================

// regex_match — find first (leftmost) match of pattern in text.
fn regex_match(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
               text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> MatchResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var pi_start = 0
    var anchored = 0

    // Check for ^ anchor
    if pat_len > 0 {
        let first: u8 = pattern[0]
        if first == 94 {    // '^'
            anchored = 1
            pi_start = 1
        }
    }

    if anchored == 1 {
        let end = match_here(pattern, pi_start, pat_len, text, 0, text_len)
        if end >= 0 {
            return MatchResult { matched: 1, start: 0, end: end }
        }
        return MatchResult { matched: 0, start: 0, end: 0 }
    }

    // Unanchored: try each start position
    var start = 0
    while start <= text_len {
        let end = match_here(pattern, 0, pat_len, text, start, text_len)
        if end >= 0 {
            return MatchResult { matched: 1, start: start, end: end }
        }
        start = start + 1
    }
    MatchResult { matched: 0, start: 0, end: 0 }
}

// regex_match_full — entire text must match pattern (implicitly anchored ^ and $).
fn regex_match_full(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
                    text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // Build anchored pattern: ^ + original + $
    var anchpat: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    anchpat[0] = 94    // '^'
    var i = 0
    while i < pat_len && i < 62 {
        anchpat[i + 1] = pattern[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let dol_pos = i + 1
    anchpat[dol_pos] = 36    // '$'
    let anchlen = dol_pos + 1

    let r = regex_match(&anchpat, anchlen, text, text_len)
    r.matched == 1
}

// regex_count — count non-overlapping matches.
fn regex_count(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
               text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var count = 0
    var pos = 0
    while pos <= text_len {
        // Try matching at pos by building a sub-view via offset
        // We use a scratch buffer for the remaining text slice
        var sub: [u8; 256] = [0; 256]
        var j = 0
        let sublen = text_len - pos
        while j < sublen {
            sub[j] = text[(pos + j) as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let r = regex_match(pattern, pat_len, &sub, sublen)
        if r.matched == 1 {
            count = count + 1
            // Advance past this match (avoid infinite loop on zero-length match)
            let advance = if r.end > r.start { r.end } else { 1 }
            pos = pos + advance
        } else {
            pos = pos + 1
        }
    }
    count
}

// glob_match — shell-style glob: '*' matches any sequence, '?' matches any single char.
// Returns true if the entire text is covered by the pattern.
fn glob_match(pattern: &[u8; 64], pat_len: i32,
              text: &[u8; 256], text_len: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    // dp table: dp[ti] = 1 if text[0..ti] can be matched by pattern[0..current_pi]
    var dp: [i32; 257] = [0; 257]
    dp[0] = 1

    // Handle leading '*' patterns that can match empty text prefix
    var pi = 0
    while pi < pat_len {
        let pc: u8 = pattern[pi]
        if pc != 42 { break }    // '*'
        dp[0] = 1
        pi = pi + 1
    }

    // Reset pi to 0 and do full DP
    // Standard DP for glob matching
    var dp2: [i32; 257] = [0; 257]
    dp2[0] = 1

    var p = 0
    while p < pat_len {
        var next_dp: [i32; 257] = [0; 257]
        let pc: u8 = pattern[p]

        if pc == 42 {    // '*' matches any sequence (including empty)
            // next_dp[t] = dp2[t] (match empty) OR next_dp[t-1] (extend match)
            var t = 0
            while t <= text_len {
                if dp2[t] == 1 { next_dp[t] = 1 }
                t = t + 1
            }
            // propagate forward: if next_dp[t] then next_dp[t+1]
            t = 0
            while t < text_len {
                if next_dp[t] == 1 { next_dp[t + 1] = 1 }
                t = t + 1
            }
        } else {
            // '?' or literal
            var t = 1
            while t <= text_len {
                if dp2[t - 1] == 1 {
                    let matches: i32 = if pc == 63 {
                        1    // '?' matches anything
                    } else {
                        let tc: u8 = text[(t - 1) as usize]
                        if pc == tc { 1 } else { 0 }
                    }
                    if matches == 1 { next_dp[t] = 1 }
                }
                t = t + 1
            }
        }

        // Copy next_dp → dp2
        var t = 0
        while t <= text_len {
            dp2[t] = next_dp[t]
            t = t + 1
        }

        p = p + 1
    }

    dp2[text_len] == 1
}

// === FILE: stdlib/render/framebuffer.sio ===
// Software framebuffer for PPM rendering
//
// Uses flat [i64; 196608] arrays for R, G, B channels (256x256 max).
// Each pixel stores 0-255 integer color value.
// Output via PPM P3 text format to stdout.

// Max framebuffer size: 256x256 = 65536 pixels
// Each channel is a separate array to avoid struct-of-arrays complexity

struct Framebuffer {
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    r: [i64; 65536],
    g: [i64; 65536],
    b: [i64; 65536],
    depth: [f64; 65536],
}

fn fb_new(w: i64, h: i64) -> Framebuffer {
    Framebuffer {
        width: w,
        height: h,
        r: [0; 65536],
        g: [0; 65536],
        b: [0; 65536],
        depth: [1000000.0; 65536],
    }
}

fn fb_set_pixel(fb: &!Framebuffer, x: i64, y: i64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < (*fb).width && y >= 0 && y < (*fb).height {
        let idx = y * (*fb).width + x
        (*fb).r[idx] = r
        (*fb).g[idx] = g
        (*fb).b[idx] = b
    }
}

fn fb_set_pixel_depth(fb: &!Framebuffer, x: i64, y: i64, z: f64, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < (*fb).width && y >= 0 && y < (*fb).height {
        let idx = y * (*fb).width + x
        if z < (*fb).depth[idx] {
            (*fb).r[idx] = r
            (*fb).g[idx] = g
            (*fb).b[idx] = b
            (*fb).depth[idx] = z
        }
    }
}

fn fb_clear(fb: &!Framebuffer, r: i64, g: i64, b: i64) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    let total = (*fb).width * (*fb).height
    while i < total {
        (*fb).r[i] = r
        (*fb).g[i] = g
        (*fb).b[i] = b
        (*fb).depth[i] = 1000000.0
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn clamp_byte(v: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0 { return 0 }
    if v > 255 { return 255 }
    v
}

fn float_to_byte(f: f64) -> i64 {
    let v = (f * 255.0) as i64
    clamp_byte(v)
}

// Emit PPM P3 header + pixels to stdout
fn fb_emit_ppm(fb: &Framebuffer) with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("P3\n")
    print_int((*fb).width)
    print(" ")
    print_int((*fb).height)
    print("\n255\n")

    var y: i64 = 0
    while y < (*fb).height {
        var x: i64 = 0
        while x < (*fb).width {
            let idx = y * (*fb).width + x
            print_int(clamp_byte((*fb).r[idx]))
            print(" ")
            print_int(clamp_byte((*fb).g[idx]))
            print(" ")
            print_int(clamp_byte((*fb).b[idx]))
            print("\n")
            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    0
}

// === FILE: stdlib/render/rasterizer.sio ===
// Software triangle rasterizer using barycentric coordinates
//
// Implements scanline triangle fill with per-pixel color interpolation.
// Supports z-buffer depth testing for correct occlusion.

struct Vec3 { x: f64, y: f64, z: f64 }
struct Color { r: f64, g: f64, b: f64, a: f64 }
struct Vertex2D { x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, r: f64, g: f64, b: f64 }

fn min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn max_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// Edge function for barycentric coordinates
// Positive = left side, negative = right side
fn edge_fn(ax: f64, ay: f64, bx: f64, by: f64, cx: f64, cy: f64) -> f64 {
    (cx - ax) * (by - ay) - (cy - ay) * (bx - ax)
}

// Rasterize a single triangle into a framebuffer (flat arrays)
// Returns number of pixels written
fn rasterize_triangle(
    v0: Vertex2D, v1: Vertex2D, v2: Vertex2D,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_depth: &![f64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Bounding box
    let min_x = max_i64(0, (min_f64(min_f64(v0.x, v1.x), v2.x)) as i64)
    let max_x = min_i64(fb_w - 1, (max_f64(max_f64(v0.x, v1.x), v2.x)) as i64 + 1)
    let min_y = max_i64(0, (min_f64(min_f64(v0.y, v1.y), v2.y)) as i64)
    let max_y = min_i64(fb_h - 1, (max_f64(max_f64(v0.y, v1.y), v2.y)) as i64 + 1)

    let area = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y)
    if area == 0.0 { return 0 }  // degenerate triangle

    var pixels_written: i64 = 0
    var py: i64 = min_y
    while py <= max_y {
        var px: i64 = min_x
        while px <= max_x {
            let cx = (px as f64) + 0.5
            let cy = (py as f64) + 0.5

            let w0 = edge_fn(v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y, cx, cy)
            let w1 = edge_fn(v2.x, v2.y, v0.x, v0.y, cx, cy)
            let w2 = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, cx, cy)

            // Inside triangle if all same sign as area
            let inside = if area > 0.0 {
                w0 >= 0.0 && w1 >= 0.0 && w2 >= 0.0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0.0 && w1 <= 0.0 && w2 <= 0.0
            }

            if inside {
                // Barycentric interpolation
                let b0 = w0 / area
                let b1 = w1 / area
                let b2 = w2 / area

                // Interpolate depth
                let z = b0 * v0.z + b1 * v1.z + b2 * v2.z

                let idx = py * fb_w + px
                if z < (*fb_depth)[idx] {
                    // Interpolate color
                    let r = b0 * v0.r + b1 * v1.r + b2 * v2.r
                    let g = b0 * v0.g + b1 * v1.g + b2 * v2.g
                    let b_col = b0 * v0.b + b1 * v1.b + b2 * v2.b

                    (*fb_r)[idx] = (r * 255.0) as i64
                    (*fb_g)[idx] = (g * 255.0) as i64
                    (*fb_b)[idx] = (b_col * 255.0) as i64
                    (*fb_depth)[idx] = z
                    pixels_written = pixels_written + 1
                }
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
    pixels_written
}

// Draw a line (Bresenham) into flat framebuffer arrays
fn rasterize_line(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, x1: i64, y1: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var cx: i64 = x0
    var cy: i64 = y0
    var dx: i64 = x1 - x0
    var dy: i64 = y1 - y0
    if dx < 0 { dx = 0 - dx }
    if dy < 0 { dy = 0 - dy }
    let sx: i64 = if x0 < x1 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
    let sy: i64 = if y0 < y1 { 1 } else { 0 - 1 }
    var err: i64 = dx - dy

    var steps: i64 = 0
    let max_steps = dx + dy + 1
    while steps < max_steps {
        if cx >= 0 && cx < fb_w && cy >= 0 && cy < fb_h {
            let idx = cy * fb_w + cx
            (*fb_r)[idx] = r
            (*fb_g)[idx] = g
            (*fb_b)[idx] = b
        }
        if cx == x1 && cy == y1 { steps = max_steps }
        let e2 = err * 2
        if e2 > (0 - dy) {
            err = err - dy
            cx = cx + sx
        }
        if e2 < dx {
            err = err + dx
            cy = cy + sy
        }
        steps = steps + 1
    }
}

fn rasterize_rect(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, rw: i64, rh: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dy: i64 = 0
    while dy < rh {
        var dx: i64 = 0
        while dx < rw {
            let px = x0 + dx
            let py = y0 + dy
            if px >= 0 && px < fb_w && py >= 0 && py < fb_h {
                let idx = py * fb_w + px
                (*fb_r)[idx] = r
                (*fb_g)[idx] = g
                (*fb_b)[idx] = b
            }
            dx = dx + 1
        }
        dy = dy + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    0
}

struct ScreenPt { sx: i64, sy: i64, depth: f64 }

fn project_point3d(
    wx: f64, wy: f64, wz: f64,
    focal: f64, z_offset: f64,
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) -> ScreenPt with Div, Panic {
    let z_cam = wz + z_offset
    let scale = focal / z_cam
    ScreenPt {
        sx: (wx * scale + ((fb_w as f64) * 0.5)) as i64,
        sy: ((0.0 - wy) * scale + ((fb_h as f64) * 0.5)) as i64,
        depth: z_cam,
    }
}
