// === FILE: stdlib/roots/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/roots/lib.sio - Root finding algorithms
//!
//! Provides numerical methods for finding roots of equations:
//! - Bisection method (bracketing, guaranteed convergence)
//! - Newton-Raphson method (fast convergence with derivative)
//! - Secant method (fast, no derivative needed)
//! - Fixed-point iteration
//! - Brent's method (robust hybrid)
//!
//! Each method returns a RootResult with the root, iteration count, and convergence status.
//!
//! Function-index dispatch variants (bisection_id, newton_id, secant_id, brent_id)
//! use integer f_id to select from built-in test functions without function pointers.
//! These return RootResult2 which carries epistemic uncertainty from convergence tolerance.

extern "C" {
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

// Result of a root-finding algorithm
pub struct RootResult {
    root: f64,
    iterations: i32,
    converged: bool,
    function_value: f64,
}

// Create a successful root result
fn root_success(root: f64, iterations: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult {
    RootResult { root: root, iterations: iterations, converged: true, function_value: fval }
}

// Create a failed root result
fn root_failure(root: f64, iterations: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult {
    RootResult { root: root, iterations: iterations, converged: false, function_value: fval }
}

// =============================================================================
// BISECTION METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Bisection method for root finding.
//
// Finds a root of f(x) = 0 in the interval [a, b].
// Requires f(a) and f(b) to have opposite signs (bracket the root).
//
// Parameters:
// - a, b: Interval endpoints (must bracket the root)
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence (stops when |b-a| < tol)
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
//
// Convergence: Guaranteed if f is continuous and brackets are valid.
// Convergence rate: Linear (one bit of precision per iteration).
pub fn bisection(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = f(lo)
    var f_hi = f(hi)

    // Check if endpoints bracket a root
    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        return root_failure((lo + hi) / 2.0, 0, f_lo)
    }

    // Handle case where endpoint is already a root
    if f_lo == 0.0 {
        return root_success(lo, 0, 0.0)
    }
    if f_hi == 0.0 {
        return root_success(hi, 0, 0.0)
    }

    var iter = 0
    var mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
    var f_mid = f(mid)

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return root_success(mid, iter, f_mid)
        }

        mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        f_mid = f(mid)

        if fabs(f_mid) < tol {
            return root_success(mid, iter + 1, f_mid)
        }

        if f_lo * f_mid < 0.0 {
            hi = mid
            f_hi = f_mid
        } else {
            lo = mid
            f_lo = f_mid
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(mid, iter, f_mid)
}

// =============================================================================
// NEWTON-RAPHSON METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Newton-Raphson method for root finding.
//
// Uses the iteration x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) / f'(x_n)
//
// Parameters:
// - x0: Initial guess
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence (stops when |f(x)| < tol)
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
// - df: Derivative of f
//
// Convergence: Quadratic near simple roots (doubles precision each step).
// Warning: May diverge if starting point is far from root or derivative is small.
pub fn newton_raphson(x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64, df: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let fx = f(x)

        if fabs(fx) < tol {
            return root_success(x, iter, fx)
        }

        let dfx = df(x)

        // Check for zero derivative
        if dfx == 0.0 {
            return root_failure(x, iter, fx)
        }

        x = x - fx / dfx
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_fx = f(x)
    root_failure(x, iter, final_fx)
}

// =============================================================================
// SECANT METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Secant method for root finding.
//
// Similar to Newton's method but approximates the derivative using finite differences:
// x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) * (x_n - x_{n-1}) / (f(x_n) - f(x_{n-1}))
//
// Parameters:
// - x0, x1: Two initial guesses
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
//
// Convergence: Superlinear (~1.618, the golden ratio).
// Advantage: Does not require derivative computation.
pub fn secant(x0: f64, x1: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x_prev = x0
    var x_curr = x1
    var f_prev = f(x_prev)
    var f_curr = f(x_curr)
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_curr) < tol {
            return root_success(x_curr, iter, f_curr)
        }

        let denom = f_curr - f_prev
        if denom == 0.0 {
            return root_failure(x_curr, iter, f_curr)
        }

        let x_next = x_curr - f_curr * (x_curr - x_prev) / denom

        x_prev = x_curr
        f_prev = f_curr
        x_curr = x_next
        f_curr = f(x_curr)

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(x_curr, iter, f_curr)
}

// =============================================================================
// FIXED-POINT ITERATION
// =============================================================================

// Fixed-point iteration for solving x = g(x).
//
// Uses the iteration x_{n+1} = g(x_n)
// Converges to a fixed point x* where x* = g(x*).
//
// Parameters:
// - x0: Initial guess
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence (stops when |x_{n+1} - x_n| < tol)
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - g: Iteration function (seeking fixed point of g)
//
// Convergence: Linear, requires |g'(x*)| < 1 near the fixed point.
// Note: To solve f(x) = 0, rewrite as x = x - c*f(x) for some constant c.
pub fn fixed_point(x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, g: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let x_new = g(x)

        if fabs(x_new - x) < tol {
            return root_success(x_new, iter + 1, x_new - g(x_new))
        }

        x = x_new
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(x, iter, x - g(x))
}

// =============================================================================
// BRENT'S METHOD
// =============================================================================

// Brent's method for root finding.
//
// A robust hybrid method combining bisection, secant, and inverse quadratic interpolation.
// Guaranteed to converge like bisection but often achieves superlinear convergence.
//
// Parameters:
// - a, b: Interval endpoints (must bracket the root)
// - tol: Tolerance for convergence
// - max_iter: Maximum number of iterations
// - f: Function to find root of
//
// This is generally the best choice for bracketed root finding.
pub fn brent(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = f(lo)
    var f_hi = f(hi)

    // Check bracket
    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        return root_failure((lo + hi) / 2.0, 0, f_lo)
    }

    // Ensure |f(lo)| >= |f(hi)|
    if fabs(f_lo) < fabs(f_hi) {
        // Swap
        let tmp = lo
        lo = hi
        hi = tmp
        let tmp_f = f_lo
        f_lo = f_hi
        f_hi = tmp_f
    }

    var c = lo
    var f_c = f_lo
    var d = hi - lo
    var e = d

    var iter = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_hi) < tol {
            return root_success(hi, iter, f_hi)
        }

        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return root_success(hi, iter, f_hi)
        }

        var use_bisection = true
        var s = 0.0

        // Try inverse quadratic interpolation if we have 3 distinct points
        if f_lo != f_c && f_hi != f_c {
            // Inverse quadratic interpolation
            let r = f_hi / f_c
            let q = f_lo / f_c
            let p = f_hi / f_lo
            s = p * (q * (r - q) * (c - hi) - (1.0 - r) * (hi - lo)) / ((q - 1.0) * (r - 1.0) * (p - 1.0))
            s = hi + s
            use_bisection = false
        } else if f_lo != f_hi {
            // Secant method
            s = hi - f_hi * (hi - lo) / (f_hi - f_lo)
            use_bisection = false
        }

        // Check if interpolation is acceptable
        if !use_bisection {
            let cond1 = if lo < hi { s < lo || s > hi } else { s < hi || s > lo }
            let cond2 = fabs(s - hi) >= fabs(e) / 2.0
            if cond1 || cond2 {
                use_bisection = true
            }
        }

        if use_bisection {
            s = (lo + hi) / 2.0
            e = hi - lo
            d = e
        } else {
            e = d
            d = s - hi
        }

        // Update points
        c = hi
        f_c = f_hi

        let f_s = f(s)

        if f_lo * f_s < 0.0 {
            hi = s
            f_hi = f_s
        } else {
            lo = s
            f_lo = f_s
        }

        // Ensure |f(lo)| >= |f(hi)|
        if fabs(f_lo) < fabs(f_hi) {
            let tmp = lo
            lo = hi
            hi = tmp
            let tmp_f = f_lo
            f_lo = f_hi
            f_hi = tmp_f
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    root_failure(hi, iter, f_hi)
}

// =============================================================================
// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// =============================================================================

// Halley's method - cubic convergence when second derivative is available
// x_{n+1} = x_n - 2*f*f' / (2*f'^2 - f*f'')
pub fn halley(x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, f: fn(f64) -> f64, df: fn(f64) -> f64, d2f: fn(f64) -> f64) -> RootResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let fx = f(x)

        if fabs(fx) < tol {
            return root_success(x, iter, fx)
        }

        let dfx = df(x)
        let d2fx = d2f(x)

        let denom = 2.0 * dfx * dfx - fx * d2fx
        if denom == 0.0 {
            return root_failure(x, iter, fx)
        }

        x = x - 2.0 * fx * dfx / denom
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_fx = f(x)
    root_failure(x, iter, final_fx)
}

// =============================================================================
// FUNCTION-INDEX DISPATCH VARIANTS
// =============================================================================
//
// These variants take an f_id: i32 selecting from built-in test functions.
// They return RootResult2 which adds epistemic uncertainty (root_unc) from
// the convergence tolerance and the residual f_at_root.
//
// f_id table:
//   0 — f(x) = x²-2           f'(x) = 2x           (root = √2 ≈ 1.41421)
//   1 — f(x) = x³-x-1         f'(x) = 3x²-1        (root ≈ 1.32472)
//   2 — f(x) = cos(x)-x       f'(x) = -sin(x)-1    (root ≈ 0.73909)
//   3 — f(x) = exp(x)-3       f'(x) = exp(x)       (root = ln(3) ≈ 1.09861)

// Root result with epistemic uncertainty field
pub struct RootResult2 {
    pub root: f64,
    pub root_unc: f64,
    pub iterations: i32,
    pub converged: i32,
    pub f_at_root: f64,
}

// ---- inline pure-Sounio math helpers (no FFI) used by dispatch variants ----
// Newton-Raphson sqrt (20 iters)
fn rt_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

// |x|
fn rt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// exp via range-reduction + Taylor (25 terms)
fn rt_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2v = 0.6931471805599453
    var kf = x / ln2v
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2v
    var s = 1.0
    var t = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 {
        t = t * r / (n as f64)
        s = s + t
        n = n + 1
    }
    var result = s
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

// cos via Taylor (15 terms, range-reduced)
fn rt_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi_v = 3.14159265358979323846
    let twopi = 6.28318530717958647692
    var a = x
    while a >= twopi { a = a - twopi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + twopi }
    if a > pi_v { a = a - twopi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

// sin(x) = cos(x - pi/2)
fn rt_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let half_pi = 1.5707963267948966
    rt_cos(x - half_pi)
}

// ---- function dispatch ----

// Evaluate f(x) for the function selected by f_id
fn eval_f(f_id: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if f_id == 0 { return x * x - 2.0 }
    if f_id == 1 { return x * x * x - x - 1.0 }
    if f_id == 2 { return rt_cos(x) - x }
    if f_id == 3 { return rt_exp(x) - 3.0 }
    // default: same as f_id=0
    x * x - 2.0
}

// Evaluate f'(x) for the function selected by f_id
fn eval_df(f_id: i32, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if f_id == 0 { return 2.0 * x }
    if f_id == 1 { return 3.0 * x * x - 1.0 }
    if f_id == 2 { return 0.0 - rt_sin(x) - 1.0 }
    if f_id == 3 { return rt_exp(x) }
    2.0 * x
}

// Build a successful RootResult2
fn rr2_ok(root: f64, unc: f64, iter: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult2 {
    RootResult2 { root: root, root_unc: unc, iterations: iter, converged: 1, f_at_root: fval }
}

// Build a failed RootResult2
fn rr2_fail(root: f64, unc: f64, iter: i32, fval: f64) -> RootResult2 {
    RootResult2 { root: root, root_unc: unc, iterations: iter, converged: 0, f_at_root: fval }
}

// Bisection using function-index dispatch.
// Interval [a,b] must bracket the root: eval_f(f_id,a)*eval_f(f_id,b) < 0.
// root_unc is set to half the final bracket width (convergence uncertainty).
pub fn bisection_id(f_id: i32, a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = eval_f(f_id, lo)
    var f_hi = eval_f(f_id, hi)

    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        return rr2_fail(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, 0, eval_f(f_id, mid))
    }
    if f_lo == 0.0 { return rr2_ok(lo, 0.0, 0, 0.0) }
    if f_hi == 0.0 { return rr2_ok(hi, 0.0, 0, 0.0) }

    var iter = 0
    var mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
    var f_mid = eval_f(f_id, mid)

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_mid)
        }
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        f_mid = eval_f(f_id, mid)
        if fabs(f_mid) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(mid, tol / 2.0, iter + 1, f_mid)
        }
        if f_lo * f_mid < 0.0 {
            hi = mid
            f_hi = f_mid
        } else {
            lo = mid
            f_lo = f_mid
        }
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    rr2_fail(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_mid)
}

// Newton-Raphson using function-index dispatch.
// Uses both eval_f and eval_df. root_unc is derived from |f(root)| / |f'(root)|.
pub fn newton_id(f_id: i32, x0: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x = x0
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        let fx = eval_f(f_id, x)
        if fabs(fx) < tol {
            let dfx = eval_df(f_id, x)
            let unc = if fabs(dfx) > 1.0e-30 { fabs(fx) / fabs(dfx) } else { tol }
            return rr2_ok(x, unc, iter, fx)
        }
        let dfx = eval_df(f_id, x)
        if dfx == 0.0 { return rr2_fail(x, tol, iter, fx) }
        x = x - fx / dfx
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let final_fx = eval_f(f_id, x)
    rr2_fail(x, tol, iter, final_fx)
}

// Secant method using function-index dispatch.
// root_unc is |x_curr - x_prev| at convergence.
pub fn secant_id(f_id: i32, x0: f64, x1: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x_prev = x0
    var x_curr = x1
    var f_prev = eval_f(f_id, x_prev)
    var f_curr = eval_f(f_id, x_curr)
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_curr) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(x_curr, fabs(x_curr - x_prev), iter, f_curr)
        }
        let denom = f_curr - f_prev
        if denom == 0.0 { return rr2_fail(x_curr, tol, iter, f_curr) }
        let x_next = x_curr - f_curr * (x_curr - x_prev) / denom
        x_prev = x_curr
        f_prev = f_curr
        x_curr = x_next
        f_curr = eval_f(f_id, x_curr)
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    rr2_fail(x_curr, fabs(x_curr - x_prev), iter, f_curr)
}

// Brent's method using function-index dispatch (gold-standard bracketed solver).
// root_unc is half the final bracket width.
pub fn brent_id(f_id: i32, a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32) -> RootResult2 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var lo = a
    var hi = b
    var f_lo = eval_f(f_id, lo)
    var f_hi = eval_f(f_id, hi)

    if f_lo * f_hi > 0.0 {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0
        return rr2_fail(mid, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, 0, eval_f(f_id, mid))
    }

    // Ensure |f(lo)| >= |f(hi)|
    if fabs(f_lo) < fabs(f_hi) {
        var tmp = lo; lo = hi; hi = tmp
        var tf = f_lo; f_lo = f_hi; f_hi = tf
    }

    var c = lo
    var f_c = f_lo
    var d = hi - lo
    var e = d
    var iter = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        if fabs(f_hi) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(hi, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_hi)
        }
        if fabs(hi - lo) < tol {
            return rr2_ok(hi, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_hi)
        }

        var use_bisect = true
        var s = 0.0

        if f_lo != f_c && f_hi != f_c {
            let r = f_hi / f_c
            let q = f_lo / f_c
            let p = f_hi / f_lo
            s = p * (q * (r - q) * (c - hi) - (1.0 - r) * (hi - lo)) / ((q - 1.0) * (r - 1.0) * (p - 1.0))
            s = hi + s
            use_bisect = false
        } else if f_lo != f_hi {
            s = hi - f_hi * (hi - lo) / (f_hi - f_lo)
            use_bisect = false
        }

        if !use_bisect {
            let cond1 = if lo < hi { s < lo || s > hi } else { s < hi || s > lo }
            let cond2 = fabs(s - hi) >= fabs(e) / 2.0
            if cond1 || cond2 { use_bisect = true }
        }

        if use_bisect {
            s = (lo + hi) / 2.0
            e = hi - lo
            d = e
        } else {
            e = d
            d = s - hi
        }

        c = hi
        f_c = f_hi
        let f_s = eval_f(f_id, s)

        if f_lo * f_s < 0.0 {
            hi = s; f_hi = f_s
        } else {
            lo = s; f_lo = f_s
        }

        if fabs(f_lo) < fabs(f_hi) {
            var tmp = lo; lo = hi; hi = tmp
            var tf = f_lo; f_lo = f_hi; f_hi = tf
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }
    rr2_fail(hi, fabs(hi - lo) / 2.0, iter, f_hi)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/science/clintrials.sio ===
/// ClinicalTrials.gov typed data protocol
/// Typed session for clinical trial data with epistemic quality tracking

struct TrialQuery {
    nct_id: [i8; 16],       // NCT ID e.g. "NCT01234567"
    nct_id_len: i64,
    phase: i64,             // 1=Phase I, 2=Phase II, 3=Phase III, 4=Phase IV
}

struct TrialOutcome {
    nct_id: [i8; 16],
    nct_id_len: i64,
    primary_outcome_met: bool,
    p_value: f64,
    effect_size: f64,
    confidence_lower: f64,
    confidence_upper: f64,
    sample_size: i64,
    phase: i64,
}

/// Evidence quality score for a trial outcome [0.0, 1.0]
/// Phase III + large sample + p<0.05 -> high quality
fn trial_evidence_quality(outcome: TrialOutcome) -> f64 {
    var score = 0.0
    if outcome.phase >= 3 { score = score + 0.4 }
    if outcome.p_value < 0.05 { score = score + 0.3 }
    if outcome.sample_size >= 100 { score = score + 0.2 }
    if outcome.effect_size > 0.3 { score = score + 0.1 }
    score
}

/// Uncertainty of the trial evidence
fn trial_uncertainty(outcome: TrialOutcome) -> f64 {
    1.0 - trial_evidence_quality(outcome)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/science/ncbi.sio ===
/// NCBI genomics typed data protocol
/// Typed session for gene expression queries against NCBI databases

struct GeneQuery {
    gene_id: [i8; 32],
    gene_id_len: i64,
    organism_id: i64,   // 0=human, 1=mouse, 2=rat
    database: i64,      // 0=gene, 1=nucleotide, 2=protein
}

struct GeneExpression {
    gene_id: [i8; 32],
    gene_id_len: i64,
    expression_level: f64,
    std_dev: f64,        // standard deviation = epistemic uncertainty
    sample_count: i64,
    tissue_id: i64,
}

/// Build a human gene query
fn query_human_gene(gene_id: [i8; 32], len: i64) -> GeneQuery {
    GeneQuery {
        gene_id: gene_id,
        gene_id_len: len,
        organism_id: 0,
        database: 0,
    }
}

/// Uncertainty of a gene expression measurement
/// Based on sample count and std_dev: higher samples -> lower uncertainty
fn expression_uncertainty(expr: GeneExpression) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if expr.sample_count <= 0 {
        1.0
    } else {
        let base = expr.std_dev / (expr.expression_level + 0.001)
        let n_factor = 1.0 / (expr.sample_count as f64)
        if base * n_factor > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { base * n_factor }
    }
}

/// Check if expression is reliably measured (uncertainty < threshold)
fn expression_reliable(expr: GeneExpression, threshold: f64) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    expression_uncertainty(expr) < threshold
}


// === FILE: stdlib/search/algorithms.sio ===
// stdlib/search/algorithms.sio — Search and Sorting Algorithms
//
// Self-contained (no imports). Fixed [f64; 256] arrays throughout.
// Sorting functions return by value to avoid the &![T;N] JIT mutation bug.
//
// Structures
//   SearchResult — result of a search operation
//   SortStats    — swap/comparison counts
//   SortResult   — sorted array + SortStats bundled for by-value return
//
// Search:
//   linear_search, binary_search, interpolation_search
//
// Sorting (return by value):
//   insertion_sort, selection_sort, quicksort, merge_sort, heapsort
//
// Utilities:
//   is_sorted, nth_smallest, median, unique_count

// =============================================================================
// Structures
// =============================================================================

pub struct SearchResult {
    pub found: i32,
    pub index: i32,
    pub comparisons: i32,
}

pub struct SortStats {
    pub swaps: i32,
    pub comparisons: i32,
}

// Carrier struct for sorting functions: sorted array + stats.
// Using a struct avoids the JIT tuple-return and &! mutation issues.
pub struct SortResult {
    pub data: [f64; 256],
    pub stats: SortStats,
}

// =============================================================================
// Helper: absolute value for f64
// =============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// =============================================================================
// Search: Linear Search
// =============================================================================

// linear_search — O(n) search in unsorted data.
//
// Returns SearchResult with found=1 and the first matching index,
// or found=0 and index=-1 if not found.
pub fn linear_search(arr: &[f64; 256], n: i32, target: f64) -> SearchResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var comps = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        comps = comps + 1
        if arr[i] == target {
            return SearchResult { found: 1, index: i, comparisons: comps }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: comps }
}

// =============================================================================
// Search: Binary Search
// =============================================================================

// binary_search — O(log n) search in a sorted array.
//
// The array must be sorted in ascending order.
// Returns SearchResult with found=1 and the matching index, or found=0/-1.
pub fn binary_search(arr: &[f64; 256], n: i32, target: f64) -> SearchResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if n <= 0 {
        return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: 0 }
    }
    var lo = 0
    var hi = n - 1
    var comps = 0
    while lo <= hi {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
        comps = comps + 1
        if arr[mid] == target {
            return SearchResult { found: 1, index: mid, comparisons: comps }
        } else if arr[mid] < target {
            lo = mid + 1
        } else {
            hi = mid - 1
        }
    }
    return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: comps }
}

// =============================================================================
// Search: Interpolation Search
// =============================================================================

// interpolation_search — O(log log n) average for uniformly distributed data.
//
// The array must be sorted in ascending order.
// Degrades to O(n) for non-uniform data.
pub fn interpolation_search(arr: &[f64; 256], n: i32, target: f64) -> SearchResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if n <= 0 {
        return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: 0 }
    }
    var lo = 0
    var hi = n - 1
    var comps = 0
    while lo <= hi && target >= arr[lo] && target <= arr[hi] {
        if lo == hi {
            comps = comps + 1
            if arr[lo] == target {
                return SearchResult { found: 1, index: lo, comparisons: comps }
            }
            return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: comps }
        }
        let range = arr[hi] - arr[lo]
        if range == 0.0 {
            comps = comps + 1
            if arr[lo] == target {
                return SearchResult { found: 1, index: lo, comparisons: comps }
            }
            return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: comps }
        }
        // Interpolation probe
        let frac = (target - arr[lo]) / range
        let span = hi - lo
        let probe_f = frac * (span as f64)
        var probe = lo + (probe_f as i32)
        if probe < lo { probe = lo }
        if probe > hi { probe = hi }
        comps = comps + 1
        if arr[probe] == target {
            return SearchResult { found: 1, index: probe, comparisons: comps }
        } else if arr[probe] < target {
            lo = probe + 1
        } else {
            hi = probe - 1
        }
    }
    return SearchResult { found: 0, index: -1, comparisons: comps }
}

// =============================================================================
// Utility: is_sorted
// =============================================================================

// is_sorted — returns true when arr[0..n-1] is non-decreasing.
pub fn is_sorted(arr: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if n <= 1 { return true }
    var i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// =============================================================================
// Sort: Insertion Sort
// =============================================================================

// insertion_sort — stable O(n²) sort. Returns SortResult by value.
pub fn insertion_sort(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> SortResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var data = arr
    var swaps = 0
    var comps = 0
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let key = data[i]
        // Find how far left to shift by scanning rightward from the left.
        // insert_at: the index where key will be placed.
        // We scan j from i-1 down to 0; every element > key shifts right by 1.
        // We stop when data[j] <= key (insert at j+1) or j < 0 (insert at 0).
        var insert_at = i   // default: no shift needed
        var j = i - 1
        var scanning = true
        while j >= 0 && scanning {
            comps = comps + 1
            if data[j] > key {
                data[j + 1] = data[j]
                swaps = swaps + 1
                insert_at = j
                j = j - 1
            } else {
                // data[j] <= key: key belongs at j+1
                insert_at = j + 1
                scanning = false
            }
        }
        data[insert_at] = key
        i = i + 1
    }
    return SortResult {
        data: data,
        stats: SortStats { swaps: swaps, comparisons: comps }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Sort: Selection Sort
// =============================================================================

// selection_sort — O(n²), not stable. Returns SortResult by value.
pub fn selection_sort(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> SortResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var data = arr
    var swaps = 0
    var comps = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var min_idx = i
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            comps = comps + 1
            if data[j] < data[min_idx] {
                min_idx = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if min_idx != i {
            let tmp = data[i]
            data[i] = data[min_idx]
            data[min_idx] = tmp
            swaps = swaps + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return SortResult {
        data: data,
        stats: SortStats { swaps: swaps, comparisons: comps }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Sort: Quicksort (Lomuto partition, median-of-3 pivot)
// =============================================================================

// qs_median3 — returns index of median of three elements for pivot selection.
fn qs_median3(data: &[f64; 256], lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    // Sort lo, mid, hi by value and return median index
    let a = data[lo]
    let b = data[mid]
    let c = data[hi]
    if a <= b && b <= c { return mid }
    if a <= c && c <= b { return hi }
    if b <= a && a <= c { return lo }
    if b <= c && c <= a { return hi }
    if c <= a && a <= b { return lo }
    return mid
}

// qs_partition — Lomuto partition with median-of-3 pivot.
// Returns the final pivot position and updates swaps/comps via out-params
// encoded in a small carrier struct.
struct QsState {
    data: [f64; 256],
    swaps: i32,
    comparisons: i32,
}

fn qs_partition(state: QsState, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> (QsState, i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = state
    // Choose pivot: median of three
    let pivot_idx = qs_median3(&s.data, lo, hi)
    // Move pivot to hi
    let pivot_val = s.data[pivot_idx]
    s.data[pivot_idx] = s.data[hi]
    s.data[hi] = pivot_val
    s.swaps = s.swaps + 1

    var store = lo
    var j = lo
    while j < hi {
        s.comparisons = s.comparisons + 1
        if s.data[j] <= s.data[hi] {
            let tmp = s.data[store]
            s.data[store] = s.data[j]
            s.data[j] = tmp
            if store != j { s.swaps = s.swaps + 1 }
            store = store + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    let tmp2 = s.data[store]
    s.data[store] = s.data[hi]
    s.data[hi] = tmp2
    if store != hi { s.swaps = s.swaps + 1 }
    return (s, store)
}

// qs_run — iterative quicksort using an explicit stack (avoids recursive &! issues).
fn qs_run(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> QsState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = QsState { data: arr, swaps: 0, comparisons: 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return s }

    // Explicit stack for [lo, hi] pairs; max depth = 256 levels
    var stack_lo = [0; 256]
    var stack_hi = [0; 256]
    var top = 0

    stack_lo[0] = 0
    stack_hi[0] = n - 1
    top = 1

    while top > 0 {
        top = top - 1
        let lo = stack_lo[top]
        let hi = stack_hi[top]
        if lo < hi {
            let pair = qs_partition(s, lo, hi)
            s = pair.0
            let p = pair.1
            // Push larger partition first for stack efficiency
            if p - 1 - lo > hi - (p + 1) {
                if lo < p - 1 {
                    stack_lo[top] = lo
                    stack_hi[top] = p - 1
                    top = top + 1
                }
                if p + 1 < hi {
                    stack_lo[top] = p + 1
                    stack_hi[top] = hi
                    top = top + 1
                }
            } else {
                if p + 1 < hi {
                    stack_lo[top] = p + 1
                    stack_hi[top] = hi
                    top = top + 1
                }
                if lo < p - 1 {
                    stack_lo[top] = lo
                    stack_hi[top] = p - 1
                    top = top + 1
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return s
}

// quicksort — Lomuto partition with median-of-3 pivot, iterative. Returns SortResult.
pub fn quicksort(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> SortResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let s = qs_run(arr, n)
    return SortResult {
        data: s.data,
        stats: SortStats { swaps: s.swaps, comparisons: s.comparisons }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Sort: Merge Sort (bottom-up iterative, no recursion)
// =============================================================================

// merge_sort — bottom-up iterative merge sort. O(n log n) stable.
// Uses a scratch buffer to avoid recursive stack issues.
pub fn merge_sort(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> SortResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var data = arr
    var tmp = [0.0; 256]
    var swaps = 0
    var comps = 0

    var width = 1
    while width < n {
        var lo = 0
        while lo < n {
            let mid_raw = lo + width - 1
            let mid = if mid_raw < n - 1 { mid_raw } else { n - 1 }
            let hi_raw = lo + 2 * width - 1
            let hi = if hi_raw < n - 1 { hi_raw } else { n - 1 }

            if mid < hi {
                // Merge data[lo..mid] and data[mid+1..hi] into tmp[lo..hi]
                var a = lo
                var b = mid + 1
                var k = lo
                while a <= mid && b <= hi {
                    comps = comps + 1
                    if data[a] <= data[b] {
                        tmp[k] = data[a]
                        a = a + 1
                    } else {
                        tmp[k] = data[b]
                        b = b + 1
                        swaps = swaps + 1
                    }
                    k = k + 1
                }
                while a <= mid {
                    tmp[k] = data[a]
                    a = a + 1
                    k = k + 1
                }
                while b <= hi {
                    tmp[k] = data[b]
                    b = b + 1
                    k = k + 1
                }
                // Copy merged segment back
                var idx = lo
                while idx <= hi {
                    data[idx] = tmp[idx]
                    idx = idx + 1
                }
            }
            lo = lo + 2 * width
        }
        width = width * 2
    }

    return SortResult {
        data: data,
        stats: SortStats { swaps: swaps, comparisons: comps }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Sort: Heapsort (in-place, iterative sift-down)
// =============================================================================

// hs_sift_down — sift element at pos down within heap of given size.
fn hs_sift_down(data: &[f64; 256], size: i32, pos: i32, swaps_ref: &[i32; 1], comps_ref: &[i32; 1]) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var p = pos
    var sw = swaps_ref[0]
    var cp = comps_ref[0]
    var done = false
    while !done {
        var largest = p
        let l = 2 * p + 1
        let r = 2 * p + 2
        if l < size {
            cp = cp + 1
            if data[l] > data[largest] { largest = l }
        }
        if r < size {
            cp = cp + 1
            if data[r] > data[largest] { largest = r }
        }
        if largest != p {
            let tmp = data[p]
            data[p] = data[largest]
            data[largest] = tmp
            sw = sw + 1
            p = largest
        } else {
            done = true
        }
    }
    // Note: can't write back via &[i32;1] refs in JIT — use QsState pattern instead
    // This function is only valid when called from hs_run which owns swaps/comps
}

// hs_run — full heapsort implementation using QsState carrier.
fn hs_run(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> QsState with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = QsState { data: arr, swaps: 0, comparisons: 0 }
    if n <= 1 { return s }

    // Build max heap (bottom-up)
    var i = n / 2 - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        // Sift down s.data[i] in heap of size n
        var p = i
        var done = false
        while !done {
            var largest = p
            let l = 2 * p + 1
            let r = 2 * p + 2
            if l < n {
                s.comparisons = s.comparisons + 1
                if s.data[l] > s.data[largest] { largest = l }
            }
            if r < n {
                s.comparisons = s.comparisons + 1
                if s.data[r] > s.data[largest] { largest = r }
            }
            if largest != p {
                let tmp = s.data[p]
                s.data[p] = s.data[largest]
                s.data[largest] = tmp
                s.swaps = s.swaps + 1
                p = largest
            } else {
                done = true
            }
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Extract phase: swap root with end, sift down
    var end = n - 1
    while end > 0 {
        let tmp = s.data[0]
        s.data[0] = s.data[end]
        s.data[end] = tmp
        s.swaps = s.swaps + 1

        // Sift down s.data[0] in heap of size end
        var p = 0
        var done2 = false
        while !done2 {
            var largest = p
            let l = 2 * p + 1
            let r = 2 * p + 2
            if l < end {
                s.comparisons = s.comparisons + 1
                if s.data[l] > s.data[largest] { largest = l }
            }
            if r < end {
                s.comparisons = s.comparisons + 1
                if s.data[r] > s.data[largest] { largest = r }
            }
            if largest != p {
                let tmp2 = s.data[p]
                s.data[p] = s.data[largest]
                s.data[largest] = tmp2
                s.swaps = s.swaps + 1
                p = largest
            } else {
                done2 = true
            }
        }
        end = end - 1
    }

    return s
}

// heapsort — in-place O(n log n). Returns SortResult by value.
pub fn heapsort(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> SortResult with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let s = hs_run(arr, n)
    return SortResult {
        data: s.data,
        stats: SortStats { swaps: s.swaps, comparisons: s.comparisons }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Utility: nth_smallest via Quickselect
// =============================================================================

// qs_select_partition — Lomuto partition on a subrange; returns pivot position.
// Operates on the QsState carrier (reused from quicksort infrastructure).
fn qs_select_partition(state: QsState, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> (QsState, i32) with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = state
    let pivot = s.data[hi]
    var store = lo
    var j = lo
    while j < hi {
        s.comparisons = s.comparisons + 1
        if s.data[j] <= pivot {
            let tmp = s.data[store]
            s.data[store] = s.data[j]
            s.data[j] = tmp
            if store != j { s.swaps = s.swaps + 1 }
            store = store + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    let tmp2 = s.data[store]
    s.data[store] = s.data[hi]
    s.data[hi] = tmp2
    if store != hi { s.swaps = s.swaps + 1 }
    return (s, store)
}

// nth_smallest — O(n) average quickselect.
// k is 0-indexed: k=0 → minimum, k=n-1 → maximum.
// Behaviour is undefined for k < 0 or k >= n.
pub fn nth_smallest(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32, k: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = QsState { data: arr, swaps: 0, comparisons: 0 }
    var lo = 0
    var hi = n - 1
    while lo < hi {
        let pair = qs_select_partition(s, lo, hi)
        s = pair.0
        let p = pair.1
        if p == k {
            return s.data[p]
        } else if p < k {
            lo = p + 1
        } else {
            hi = p - 1
        }
    }
    return s.data[lo]
}

// =============================================================================
// Utility: Median
// =============================================================================

// median — returns the median value via quickselect.
// For even n, returns the lower median (element at index n/2 - 1 after sort).
pub fn median(arr: [f64; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if n <= 0 { return 0.0 }
    if n == 1 { return arr[0] }
    let k = (n - 1) / 2
    return nth_smallest(arr, n, k)
}

// =============================================================================
// Utility: unique_count
// =============================================================================

// unique_count — count distinct values in arr[0..n-1].
// Sorts a copy, then scans for runs.
pub fn unique_count(arr: &[f64; 256], n: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    if n <= 0 { return 0 }

    // Copy into a local array for sorting
    var copy = [0.0; 256]
    var ci = 0
    while ci < n {
        copy[ci] = arr[ci]
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    // Sort the copy with insertion sort (small n expected)
    var i = 1
    while i < n {
        let key = copy[i]
        var insert_at = i
        var j = i - 1
        var scanning2 = true
        while j >= 0 && scanning2 {
            if copy[j] > key {
                copy[j + 1] = copy[j]
                insert_at = j
                j = j - 1
            } else {
                insert_at = j + 1
                scanning2 = false
            }
        }
        copy[insert_at] = key
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Count distinct values
    var count = 1
    var k = 1
    while k < n {
        if copy[k] != copy[k - 1] {
            count = count + 1
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    return count
}


// === FILE: stdlib/search/basic.sio ===
//! Basic Search Algorithms
//!
//! Fundamental search algorithms for sorted and unsorted sequences.
//!
//! # Algorithms
//! - `linear_search` - O(n) search in unsorted data
//! - `binary_search` - O(log n) search in sorted data
//! - `lower_bound` - First element >= target
//! - `upper_bound` - First element > target
//! - `equal_range` - Range of elements equal to target
//!
//! # Examples
//! ```sio
//! let arr = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9]
//! match binary_search_i64(&arr, 5, 5) {
//!     Some(idx) => print("Found at index " ++ idx.to_string()),
//!     None => print("Not found"),
//! }
//! ```

// =============================================================================
// Linear Search
// =============================================================================

// Searches for target in an unsorted slice, returning the first matching index.
//
// Time complexity: O(n)
// Space complexity: O(1)
pub fn linear_search_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        if arr[i] == target {
            return Some(i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return None
}

// Searches for target in an unsorted slice of f64.
pub fn linear_search_f64(arr: &[f64], len: usize, target: f64, epsilon: f64) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        let diff = arr[i] - target
        if diff < epsilon && diff > -epsilon {
            return Some(i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return None
}

// Searches for target using a comparison function.
//
// Returns the index of the first element where cmp(element) returns true.
pub fn linear_search_by<T>(
    arr: &[T],
    len: usize,
    predicate: fn(&T) -> bool
) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        if predicate(&arr[i]) {
            return Some(i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return None
}

// =============================================================================
// Binary Search
// =============================================================================

// Binary search for target in a sorted slice.
//
// Returns the index if found, None otherwise.
// Time complexity: O(log n)
// Space complexity: O(1)
//
// # Precondition
// The slice must be sorted in ascending order.
pub fn binary_search_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

        if arr[mid] == target {
            return Some(mid)
        } else if arr[mid] < target {
            left = mid + 1
        } else {
            right = mid
        }
    }

    return None
}

// Binary search for target in a sorted slice of f64.
//
// Uses epsilon for floating-point comparison.
pub fn binary_search_f64(arr: &[f64], len: usize, target: f64, epsilon: f64) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2
        let diff = arr[mid] - target

        if diff < epsilon && diff > -epsilon {
            return Some(mid)
        } else if arr[mid] < target {
            left = mid + 1
        } else {
            right = mid
        }
    }

    return None
}

// Binary search using a comparison function.
//
// The comparison function should return:
// - Ordering::Less if element < target
// - Ordering::Equal if element == target
// - Ordering::Greater if element > target
pub fn binary_search_by<T>(
    arr: &[T],
    len: usize,
    cmp: fn(&T) -> Ordering
) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

        match cmp(&arr[mid]) {
            Ordering::Equal => { return Some(mid) },
            Ordering::Less => { left = mid + 1 },
            Ordering::Greater => { right = mid },
        }
    }

    return None
}

// =============================================================================
// Lower Bound / Upper Bound
// =============================================================================

// Returns the index of the first element >= target.
//
// If all elements are less than target, returns len.
// Time complexity: O(log n)
pub fn lower_bound_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> usize with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

        if arr[mid] < target {
            left = mid + 1
        } else {
            right = mid
        }
    }

    return left
}

// Returns the index of the first element > target.
//
// If all elements are <= target, returns len.
// Time complexity: O(log n)
pub fn upper_bound_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> usize with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

        if arr[mid] <= target {
            left = mid + 1
        } else {
            right = mid
        }
    }

    return left
}

// Returns the index of the first element >= target for f64.
pub fn lower_bound_f64(arr: &[f64], len: usize, target: f64) -> usize with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

        if arr[mid] < target {
            left = mid + 1
        } else {
            right = mid
        }
    }

    return left
}

// Returns the index of the first element > target for f64.
pub fn upper_bound_f64(arr: &[f64], len: usize, target: f64) -> usize with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var left: usize = 0
    var right: usize = len

    while left < right {
        let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

        if arr[mid] <= target {
            left = mid + 1
        } else {
            right = mid
        }
    }

    return left
}

// =============================================================================
// Equal Range
// =============================================================================

// Range of indices for elements equal to target.
pub struct EqualRange {
    start: usize,
    end: usize,
}

impl EqualRange {
    // Returns the number of elements in the range.
    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {
        self.end - self.start
    }
    // Returns true if the range is empty.
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.start >= self.end
    }
}

// Returns the range [lower_bound, upper_bound) of elements equal to target.
//
// Time complexity: O(log n)
pub fn equal_range_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> EqualRange with Panic, Div, Mut {
    EqualRange {
        start: lower_bound_i64(arr, len, target),
        end: upper_bound_i64(arr, len, target),
    }
}

// Returns the count of elements equal to target.
pub fn count_equal_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> usize with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let range = equal_range_i64(arr, len, target)
    range.count()
}

// =============================================================================
// Contains
// =============================================================================

// Returns true if the sorted slice contains the target.
pub fn contains_sorted_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    match binary_search_i64(arr, len, target) {
        Some(_) => true,
        None => false,
    }
}

// Returns true if the unsorted slice contains the target.
pub fn contains_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    match linear_search_i64(arr, len, target) {
        Some(_) => true,
        None => false,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Ordering enum (if not already defined elsewhere)
// =============================================================================

// Result of comparing two values.
pub enum Ordering {
    Less,
    Equal,
    Greater,
}

// =============================================================================
// Exponential Search
// =============================================================================

// Exponential search for unbounded or very large sorted arrays.
//
// Useful when the target is expected to be near the beginning.
// Time complexity: O(log n) where n is the position of the target.
pub fn exponential_search_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    // Check first element
    if arr[0] == target {
        return Some(0)
    }

    // Find range for binary search by repeated doubling
    var bound: usize = 1
    while bound < len && arr[bound] < target {
        bound = bound * 2
    }

    // Binary search in the found range
    let left = bound / 2
    let right = if bound < len { bound + 1 } else { len }

    // Perform binary search in [left, right)
    var lo = left
    var hi = right

    while lo < hi {
        let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2

        if arr[mid] == target {
            return Some(mid)
        } else if arr[mid] < target {
            lo = mid + 1
        } else {
            hi = mid
        }
    }

    return None
}

// =============================================================================
// Interpolation Search
// =============================================================================

// Interpolation search for uniformly distributed sorted data.
//
// Time complexity: O(log log n) for uniform data, O(n) worst case.
//
// Best suited for large arrays with uniformly distributed numeric values.
pub fn interpolation_search_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize, target: i64) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi: usize = len - 1

    while lo <= hi && target >= arr[lo] && target <= arr[hi] {
        if lo == hi {
            if arr[lo] == target {
                return Some(lo)
            }
            return None
        }

        // Interpolation formula
        let range = arr[hi] - arr[lo]
        if range == 0 {
            // All elements are equal
            if arr[lo] == target {
                return Some(lo)
            }
            return None
        }

        let pos_f64 = (lo as f64) + (((target - arr[lo]) as f64) * ((hi - lo) as f64) / (range as f64))
        var pos = pos_f64 as usize

        // Clamp to valid range
        if pos < lo {
            pos = lo
        } else if pos > hi {
            pos = hi
        }

        if arr[pos] == target {
            return Some(pos)
        } else if arr[pos] < target {
            lo = pos + 1
        } else {
            if pos == 0 {
                return None
            }
            hi = pos - 1
        }
    }

    return None
}

// =============================================================================
// Index of Minimum/Maximum
// =============================================================================

// Returns the index of the minimum element.
//
// Returns None if the slice is empty.
pub fn index_of_min_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var min_idx: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < len {
        if arr[i] < arr[min_idx] {
            min_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return Some(min_idx)
}

// Returns the index of the maximum element.
//
// Returns None if the slice is empty.
pub fn index_of_max_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize) -> Option<usize> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var max_idx: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < len {
        if arr[i] > arr[max_idx] {
            max_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return Some(max_idx)
}

// Returns indices of both minimum and maximum in a single pass.
pub fn index_of_minmax_i64(arr: &[i64], len: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)> with Panic, Div, Mut {
    if len == 0 {
        return None
    }

    var min_idx: usize = 0
    var max_idx: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < len {
        if arr[i] < arr[min_idx] {
            min_idx = i
        }
        if arr[i] > arr[max_idx] {
            max_idx = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return Some((min_idx, max_idx))
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests

fn test_linear_search() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let arr: [i64; 5] = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]

    match linear_search_i64(&arr, 5, 4) {
        Some(2) => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    match linear_search_i64(&arr, 5, 1) {
        Some(1) => {},  // First occurrence
        _ => return false,
    }

    match linear_search_i64(&arr, 5, 9) {
        None => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    return true
}

fn test_binary_search() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let arr: [i64; 5] = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9]

    match binary_search_i64(&arr, 5, 5) {
        Some(2) => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    match binary_search_i64(&arr, 5, 1) {
        Some(0) => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    match binary_search_i64(&arr, 5, 9) {
        Some(4) => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    match binary_search_i64(&arr, 5, 4) {
        None => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    return true
}

fn test_bounds() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let arr: [i64; 7] = [1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5]

    // lower_bound: first element >= 2
    if lower_bound_i64(&arr, 7, 2) != 1 { return false }

    // upper_bound: first element > 2
    if upper_bound_i64(&arr, 7, 2) != 4 { return false }

    // equal_range for 2
    let range = equal_range_i64(&arr, 7, 2)
    if range.start != 1 { return false }
    if range.end != 4 { return false }
    if range.count() != 3 { return false }

    return true
}

fn test_minmax() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    let arr: [i64; 5] = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]

    match index_of_min_i64(&arr, 5) {
        Some(1) => {},  // First occurrence of min
        _ => return false,
    }

    match index_of_max_i64(&arr, 5) {
        Some(4) => {},
        _ => return false,
    }

    return true
}

pub fn run_tests() -> bool with Panic, Div, Mut {
    test_linear_search() &&
    test_binary_search() &&
    test_bounds() &&
    test_minmax()
}

// === FILE: stdlib/search/mcts/examples/tictactoe.sio ===
// stdlib/search/mcts/examples/tictactoe.d
// Tic-Tac-Toe MCTS Example
//
// Demonstrates MCTS with UCB1/PUCT for game tree search.

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0; }
    var y = x;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    y
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e308; }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0; }

    var normalized = x;
    var exponent: f64 = 0.0;

    while normalized > 2.0 {
        normalized = normalized / 2.0;
        exponent = exponent + 1.0;
    }
    while normalized < 1.0 {
        normalized = normalized * 2.0;
        exponent = exponent - 1.0;
    }

    let y = (normalized - 1.0) / (normalized + 1.0);
    let y2 = y * y;

    var result = y;
    var term = y;
    var n: f64 = 1.0;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * y2;
        n = n + 2.0;
        result = result + term / n;
        i = i + 1;
    }

    let ln2 = 0.693147180559945;
    2.0 * result + exponent * ln2
}

// =============================================================================
// Tic-Tac-Toe Game State
// =============================================================================

// Board positions: 0-8 (3x3 grid)
// Player encoding: 0=empty, 1=X, 2=O

// Encode board state as i64 (9 positions, 2 bits each)
fn encode_board(board: &[i32]) -> i64 {
    var state: i64 = 0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 9 {
        let shift = (i as i64) * 2;
        state = state + ((board[i] as i64) << (shift as u8));
        i = i + 1;
    }
    state
}

// Decode board state from i64
fn get_cell(state: i64, pos: usize) -> i32 {
    let shift = (pos as i64) * 2;
    ((state >> (shift as u8)) & 3) as i32
}

// Get current player from move count
fn get_player(move_count: i32) -> i32 {
    let two: i32 = 2;
    if move_count % two == 0 { 1 } else { 2 }  // 1=X starts
}

// =============================================================================
// Game Logic
// =============================================================================

// Check for winner: returns 1=X wins, 2=O wins, 0=no winner
fn check_winner(state: i64) -> i32 {
    // Win patterns (bit positions for each line)
    // Rows: 0,1,2  3,4,5  6,7,8
    // Cols: 0,3,6  1,4,7  2,5,8
    // Diags: 0,4,8  2,4,6

    var player: i32 = 1;
    let two: i32 = 2;
    while player <= two {
        // Check rows
        if get_cell(state, 0) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 1) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 2) == player { return player; }
            }
        }
        if get_cell(state, 3) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 4) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 5) == player { return player; }
            }
        }
        if get_cell(state, 6) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 7) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 8) == player { return player; }
            }
        }

        // Check columns
        if get_cell(state, 0) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 3) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 6) == player { return player; }
            }
        }
        if get_cell(state, 1) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 4) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 7) == player { return player; }
            }
        }
        if get_cell(state, 2) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 5) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 8) == player { return player; }
            }
        }

        // Check diagonals
        if get_cell(state, 0) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 4) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 8) == player { return player; }
            }
        }
        if get_cell(state, 2) == player {
            if get_cell(state, 4) == player {
                if get_cell(state, 6) == player { return player; }
            }
        }

        player = player + 1;
    }

    0  // No winner
}

// Count empty cells (for move count / draw detection)
fn count_empty(state: i64) -> i32 {
    var count: i32 = 0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    let zero: i32 = 0;
    while i < 9 {
        if get_cell(state, i) == zero {
            count = count + 1;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    count
}

// Make a move
fn make_move(state: i64, pos: i32, player: i32) -> i64 {
    let shift = (pos as i64) * 2;
    state + ((player as i64) << (shift as u8))
}

// Get legal moves as array of positions
fn get_legal_moves(state: i64) -> [i32] {
    var moves: [i32] = [];
    var i: usize = 0;
    let zero: i32 = 0;
    while i < 9 {
        if get_cell(state, i) == zero {
            moves.push(i as i32);
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    moves
}

// =============================================================================
// MCTS Node (simplified for TTT)
// =============================================================================

pub struct TTTNode {
    pub state: i64,
    pub action: i32,
    pub total_value: f64,
    pub visits: u32,
    pub parent_idx: i32,
    pub first_child_idx: i32,
    pub num_children: u32,
    pub is_terminal: bool,
    pub move_count: i32,
}

pub struct TTTTree {
    pub nodes: [TTTNode],
    pub root_idx: i32,
    pub exploration_c: f64,
}

// Create new tree from initial state
pub fn new_ttt_tree(root_state: i64) -> TTTTree {
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;

    var tree = TTTTree {
        nodes: [],
        root_idx: zero_i32,
        exploration_c: 1.414,
    };

    let root = TTTNode {
        state: root_state,
        action: neg_one,
        total_value: 0.0,
        visits: zero_u32,
        parent_idx: neg_one,
        first_child_idx: neg_one,
        num_children: zero_u32,
        is_terminal: false,
        move_count: zero_i32,
    };
    tree.nodes.push(root);
    tree
}

// UCB1 selection
fn ucb1(q: f64, child_visits: u32, parent_visits: u32, c: f64) -> f64 {
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    if child_visits == zero_u32 { return 1.0e308; }
    q + c * sqrt_f64(ln_f64(parent_visits as f64) / (child_visits as f64))
}

// Add child node
pub fn add_ttt_child(tree: &TTTTree, parent_idx: i32, state: i64, action: i32, move_count: i32) -> i32 {
    let child_idx = tree.nodes.len() as i32;
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    let one_u32: u32 = 1;

    let child = TTTNode {
        state: state,
        action: action,
        total_value: 0.0,
        visits: zero_u32,
        parent_idx: parent_idx,
        first_child_idx: neg_one,
        num_children: zero_u32,
        is_terminal: false,
        move_count: move_count,
    };
    tree.nodes.push(child);

    let p = parent_idx as usize;
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    if tree.nodes[p].first_child_idx < zero_i32 {
        tree.nodes[p].first_child_idx = child_idx;
    }
    tree.nodes[p].num_children = tree.nodes[p].num_children + one_u32;

    child_idx
}

// Select best child using UCB1
fn select_child_ucb1(tree: &TTTTree, node_idx: i32) -> i32 {
    let node = tree.nodes[node_idx as usize];
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    if node.num_children == zero_u32 { return neg_one; }

    let parent_visits = node.visits;
    let first = node.first_child_idx as usize;
    let n = node.num_children as usize;

    var best_idx = first as i32;
    var best_score = 0.0 - 1.0e308;
    let one_usize: usize = 1;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let child_idx = (first + i) as i32;
        let child = tree.nodes[child_idx as usize];

        let zero_u32_check: u32 = 0;
        let q = if child.visits == zero_u32_check { 0.0 } else { child.total_value / (child.visits as f64) };
        let score = ucb1(q, child.visits, parent_visits, tree.exploration_c);

        if score > best_score {
            best_score = score;
            best_idx = child_idx;
        }
        i = i + one_usize;
    }

    best_idx
}

// Select to leaf
pub fn select_to_leaf_ttt(tree: &TTTTree) -> i32 {
    var current = tree.root_idx;
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;

    while tree.nodes[current as usize].num_children > zero_u32 {
        let next = select_child_ucb1(tree, current);
        if next < zero_i32 { break; }
        current = next;
    }

    current
}

// Expand node with all legal moves
pub fn expand_ttt(tree: &TTTTree, node_idx: i32) {
    let node = tree.nodes[node_idx as usize];
    let moves = get_legal_moves(node.state);
    let n = moves.len();
    let one_i32: i32 = 1;

    let next_move_count = node.move_count + one_i32;
    let player = get_player(node.move_count);

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let action = moves[i];
        let new_state = make_move(node.state, action, player);
        add_ttt_child(tree, node_idx, new_state, action, next_move_count);
        i = i + 1;
    }
}

// Simulate random playout and return value (1=X wins, -1=O wins, 0=draw)
fn simulate_ttt(state: i64, move_count: i32) -> f64 {
    var current_state = state;
    var current_moves = move_count;
    let nine: i32 = 9;

    while current_moves < nine {
        let winner = check_winner(current_state);
        let zero: i32 = 0;
        let one: i32 = 1;
        if winner == one { return 1.0; }  // X wins
        let two: i32 = 2;
        if winner == two { return 0.0 - 1.0; }  // O wins

        let moves = get_legal_moves(current_state);
        if moves.len() == 0 { return 0.0; }  // Draw

        // Pick first legal move (simple simulation)
        let player = get_player(current_moves);
        current_state = make_move(current_state, moves[0], player);
        current_moves = current_moves + one;
    }

    0.0  // Draw
}

// Backpropagate value (negate for adversarial)
pub fn backprop_ttt(tree: &TTTTree, leaf_idx: i32, value: f64) {
    var current = leaf_idx;
    var v = value;
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    let one_u32: u32 = 1;

    while current >= zero_i32 {
        let idx = current as usize;
        tree.nodes[idx].visits = tree.nodes[idx].visits + one_u32;
        tree.nodes[idx].total_value = tree.nodes[idx].total_value + v;

        current = tree.nodes[idx].parent_idx;
        v = 0.0 - v;
    }
}

// Run MCTS for n iterations
pub fn run_mcts_ttt(tree: &TTTTree, iterations: i32) {
    var iter: i32 = 0;
    let one_i32: i32 = 1;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;

    while iter < iterations {
        // Selection
        let leaf_idx = select_to_leaf_ttt(tree);
        let leaf = tree.nodes[leaf_idx as usize];

        // Check terminal
        let winner = check_winner(leaf.state);
        let zero: i32 = 0;
        if winner != zero {
            let one: i32 = 1;
            let value = if winner == one { 1.0 } else { 0.0 - 1.0 };
            backprop_ttt(tree, leaf_idx, value);
        } else {
            let nine: i32 = 9;
            if leaf.move_count >= nine {
                // Draw
                backprop_ttt(tree, leaf_idx, 0.0);
            } else {
                // Expansion
                if leaf.num_children == zero_u32 {
                    expand_ttt(tree, leaf_idx);
                }

                // Simulate from first new child
                if tree.nodes[leaf_idx as usize].num_children > zero_u32 {
                    let first_child = tree.nodes[leaf_idx as usize].first_child_idx;
                    let child = tree.nodes[first_child as usize];
                    let value = simulate_ttt(child.state, child.move_count);
                    backprop_ttt(tree, first_child, value);
                }
            }
        }

        iter = iter + one_i32;
    }
}

// Get best move from root
pub fn best_move_ttt(tree: &TTTTree) -> i32 {
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let root = tree.nodes[tree.root_idx as usize];
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    if root.num_children == zero_u32 { return neg_one; }

    let first = root.first_child_idx as usize;
    let n = root.num_children as usize;

    var best_action: i32 = neg_one;
    var best_visits: u32 = 0;
    let one_usize: usize = 1;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let child = tree.nodes[first + i];
        if child.visits > best_visits {
            best_visits = child.visits;
            best_action = child.action;
        }
        i = i + one_usize;
    }

    best_action
}

// === FILE: stdlib/search/mcts/examples/uncertainty_demo.sio ===
// stdlib/search/mcts/examples/uncertainty_demo.d
// MCTS with GUM-style Uncertainty Integration
//
// Demonstrates how to propagate measurement variance through MCTS.
// Values are represented as (mean, variance) pairs.

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0; }
    var y = x;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    y
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e308; }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0; }

    var normalized = x;
    var exponent: f64 = 0.0;

    while normalized > 2.0 {
        normalized = normalized / 2.0;
        exponent = exponent + 1.0;
    }
    while normalized < 1.0 {
        normalized = normalized * 2.0;
        exponent = exponent - 1.0;
    }

    let y = (normalized - 1.0) / (normalized + 1.0);
    let y2 = y * y;

    var result = y;
    var term = y;
    var n: f64 = 1.0;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 20 {
        term = term * y2;
        n = n + 2.0;
        result = result + term / n;
        i = i + 1;
    }

    let ln2 = 0.693147180559945;
    2.0 * result + exponent * ln2
}

// =============================================================================
// Measured Value Type
// =============================================================================

// Value with variance (GUM-style uncertainty squared)
pub struct MeasuredValue {
    pub mean: f64,       // Best estimate
    pub var: f64,        // Variance (u^2)
}

// Create measured value
pub fn measured(mean: f64, std_dev: f64) -> MeasuredValue {
    MeasuredValue { mean: mean, var: std_dev * std_dev }
}

// Combine two measured values (weighted average by inverse variance)
pub fn combine_values(a: &MeasuredValue, b: &MeasuredValue) -> MeasuredValue {
    if a.var < 1.0e-15 { return MeasuredValue { mean: a.mean, var: 0.0 }; }
    if b.var < 1.0e-15 { return MeasuredValue { mean: b.mean, var: 0.0 }; }

    let w_a = 1.0 / a.var;
    let w_b = 1.0 / b.var;
    let total_w = w_a + w_b;

    let mean = (w_a * a.mean + w_b * b.mean) / total_w;
    let var_combined = 1.0 / total_w;

    MeasuredValue { mean: mean, var: var_combined }
}

// Add measured values (sum of random variables)
pub fn add_values(a: &MeasuredValue, b: &MeasuredValue) -> MeasuredValue {
    MeasuredValue { mean: a.mean + b.mean, var: a.var + b.var }
}

// Get standard deviation from measured value
pub fn get_std(v: &MeasuredValue) -> f64 {
    sqrt_f64(v.var)
}

// =============================================================================
// MCTS Node with Variance Tracking
// =============================================================================

pub struct VarNode {
    pub state: i64,
    pub action: i32,
    pub value_mean: f64,
    pub value_var: f64,
    pub visits: u32,
    pub parent_idx: i32,
    pub first_child_idx: i32,
    pub num_children: u32,
}

pub struct VarTree {
    pub nodes: [VarNode],
    pub root_idx: i32,
    pub exploration_c: f64,
}

// Create new tree
pub fn new_var_tree(root_state: i64) -> VarTree {
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;

    var tree = VarTree {
        nodes: [],
        root_idx: zero_i32,
        exploration_c: 1.414,
    };

    let root = VarNode {
        state: root_state,
        action: neg_one,
        value_mean: 0.0,
        value_var: 1.0,
        visits: zero_u32,
        parent_idx: neg_one,
        first_child_idx: neg_one,
        num_children: zero_u32,
    };
    tree.nodes.push(root);
    tree
}

// Add child node
pub fn add_var_child(tree: &VarTree, parent_idx: i32, state: i64, action: i32) -> i32 {
    let child_idx = tree.nodes.len() as i32;
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    let one_u32: u32 = 1;

    let child = VarNode {
        state: state,
        action: action,
        value_mean: 0.0,
        value_var: 1.0,
        visits: zero_u32,
        parent_idx: parent_idx,
        first_child_idx: neg_one,
        num_children: zero_u32,
    };
    tree.nodes.push(child);

    let p = parent_idx as usize;
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    if tree.nodes[p].first_child_idx < zero_i32 {
        tree.nodes[p].first_child_idx = child_idx;
    }
    tree.nodes[p].num_children = tree.nodes[p].num_children + one_u32;

    child_idx
}

// UCB1 with variance bonus (encourages exploration of high-variance nodes)
fn ucb1_var(mean: f64, var: f64, child_visits: u32, parent_visits: u32, c: f64) -> f64 {
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    if child_visits == zero_u32 { return 1.0e308; }

    let ucb_term = c * sqrt_f64(ln_f64(parent_visits as f64) / (child_visits as f64));
    let var_bonus = 0.5 * sqrt_f64(var);

    mean + ucb_term + var_bonus
}

// Select best child
fn select_child_var(tree: &VarTree, node_idx: i32) -> i32 {
    let node = tree.nodes[node_idx as usize];
    let neg_one: i32 = (0 - 1) as i32;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;
    if node.num_children == zero_u32 { return neg_one; }

    let parent_visits = node.visits;
    let first = node.first_child_idx as usize;
    let n = node.num_children as usize;

    var best_idx = first as i32;
    var best_score = 0.0 - 1.0e308;
    let one_usize: usize = 1;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let child_idx = (first + i) as i32;
        let child = tree.nodes[child_idx as usize];
        let score = ucb1_var(child.value_mean, child.value_var, child.visits, parent_visits, tree.exploration_c);
        if score > best_score {
            best_score = score;
            best_idx = child_idx;
        }
        i = i + one_usize;
    }

    best_idx
}

// Select to leaf
pub fn select_leaf_var(tree: &VarTree) -> i32 {
    var current = tree.root_idx;
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    let zero_u32: u32 = 0;

    while tree.nodes[current as usize].num_children > zero_u32 {
        let next = select_child_var(tree, current);
        if next < zero_i32 { break; }
        current = next;
    }

    current
}

// Backpropagate with Welford's algorithm for online variance
pub fn backprop_var(tree: &VarTree, leaf_idx: i32, value: &MeasuredValue) {
    var current = leaf_idx;
    var v = value.mean;
    var u2 = value.var;
    let zero_i32: i32 = 0;
    let one_u32: u32 = 1;

    while current >= zero_i32 {
        let idx = current as usize;
        let old_visits = tree.nodes[idx].visits;
        let old_mean = tree.nodes[idx].value_mean;
        let old_var = tree.nodes[idx].value_var;

        let new_visits = old_visits + one_u32;
        tree.nodes[idx].visits = new_visits;

        // Welford's algorithm
        let delta = v - old_mean;
        let new_mean = old_mean + delta / (new_visits as f64);
        tree.nodes[idx].value_mean = new_mean;

        let delta2 = v - new_mean;
        let n = new_visits as f64;
        let new_var = if n > 1.0 {
            (old_var * (n - 1.0) + delta * delta2 + u2) / n
        } else {
            u2
        };
        tree.nodes[idx].value_var = new_var;

        current = tree.nodes[idx].parent_idx;
        v = 0.0 - v;
    }
}

// Get value at node
pub fn get_node_val(tree: &VarTree, node_idx: i32) -> MeasuredValue {
    let node = tree.nodes[node_idx as usize];
    MeasuredValue { mean: node.value_mean, var: node.value_var }
}

// MCTS Tree Node Structure
//
// Generic tree node for Monte Carlo Tree Search.
// Tracks visit counts, values, and child relationships.

// =============================================================================
// Node Structure
// =============================================================================

// MCTS tree node
pub struct MCTSNode {
    pub state: i64,          // State hash/encoding
    pub action: i32,         // Action that led here (-1 for root)
    pub total_value: f64,    // Sum of backpropagated values
    pub visits: u32,         // Visit count
    pub prior: f64,          // Prior probability (for PUCT)
    pub parent_idx: i32,     // Parent index (-1 if root)
    pub children: [i32],     // Child indices
    pub is_expanded: bool,
    pub is_terminal: bool,
}

// Create a new root node
pub fn new_root(state: i64) -> MCTSNode {
    MCTSNode {
        state: state,
        action: 0 - 1,
        total_value: 0.0,
        visits: 0,
        prior: 1.0,
        parent_idx: 0 - 1,
        children: [],
        is_expanded: false,
        is_terminal: false,
    }
}

// Create a child node
pub fn new_child(state: i64, action: i32, parent_idx: i32, prior: f64) -> MCTSNode {
    MCTSNode {
        state: state,
        action: action,
        total_value: 0.0,
        visits: 0,
        prior: prior,
        parent_idx: parent_idx,
        children: [],
        is_expanded: false,
        is_terminal: false,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Node Statistics (pure functions)
// =============================================================================

// Get Q-value (mean value)
pub fn q_value(total: f64, visits: u32) -> f64 {
    if visits == 0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        total / (visits as f64)
    }
}

// Check if node is leaf
pub fn is_leaf(num_children: usize) -> bool {
    num_children == 0
}
