// HELPER FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn mean(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

fn variance(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    let m = mean(data, n)
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = data[i as usize] - m
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum_sq / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

fn std_dev(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    sqrt(variance(data, n))
}

// Approximate p-value from t-distribution using normal approximation
// Valid for df > 30; conservative for smaller df
fn t_to_p_approx(t: f64, df: f64) -> f64 {
    let abs_t = if t < 0.0 { -t } else { t }

    // Normal approximation for large df
    // For df < 30, this underestimates p (conservative)
    // Using logistic approximation to normal CDF
    let z = abs_t

    // Approximate 2-tailed p-value using error function approximation
    // P(|T| > t) ≈ 2 * Φ(-|t|) for large df
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = -0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = -1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911

    let sign = if z < 0.0 { -1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x = if z < 0.0 { -z } else { z }

    let t_erf = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * x)
    let erf = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t_erf + a4) * t_erf) + a3) * t_erf + a2) * t_erf + a1) * t_erf * exp(-x * x)

    // Two-tailed p-value
    1.0 - erf
}

// Approximate p-value from F-distribution
fn f_to_p_approx(f: f64, df1: i64, df2: i64) -> f64 {
    // Very rough approximation using chi-square relationship
    // For production: use proper incomplete beta function
    if f <= 0.0 {
        return 1.0
    }

    // Fisher's approximation for large df
    let x = ((df1 as f64) * f) / ((df1 as f64) * f + (df2 as f64))

    // Approximate p-value (underestimates for small df)
    let p = 1.0 - x

    if p < 0.0 { 0.0 } else if p > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { p }
}

// Approximate p-value from z-score (normal distribution)
fn z_to_p(z: f64) -> f64 {
    let abs_z = if z < 0.0 { -z } else { z }

    // Error function approximation
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = -0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = -1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911

    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * abs_z)
    let erf = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t + a4) * t) + a3) * t + a2) * t + a1) * t * exp(-abs_z * abs_z)

    // Two-tailed p-value
    1.0 - erf
}

// ============================================================================
// T-TESTS
// ============================================================================

// One-sample t-test: test if mean differs from mu0
fn t_test_one_sample(data: [f64; 100], n: i64, mu0: f64) -> TTestResult {
    var result = ttest_result_new()

    let m = mean(data, n)
    let s = std_dev(data, n)
    let se = s / sqrt(n as f64)

    result.mean_diff = m - mu0
    result.se_diff = se
    result.df = (n - 1) as f64

    if se > 1e-10 {
        result.t_stat = result.mean_diff / se
    }

    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)

    // 95% CI (using t-critical ≈ 2.0 for large n)
    let t_crit = 2.0
    result.ci_lower = result.mean_diff - t_crit * se
    result.ci_upper = result.mean_diff + t_crit * se

    // Cohen's d = (mean - mu0) / s
    if s > 1e-10 {
        result.cohens_d = result.mean_diff / s
    }

    result
}

// Independent samples t-test (equal variance assumed)
fn t_test_independent(x: [f64; 100], nx: i64, y: [f64; 100], ny: i64) -> TTestResult {
    var result = ttest_result_new()

    let mx = mean(x, nx)
    let my = mean(y, ny)
    let sx = std_dev(x, nx)
    let sy = std_dev(y, ny)

    result.mean_diff = mx - my
    result.df = (nx + ny - 2) as f64

    // Pooled standard deviation
    let var_x = sx * sx
    let var_y = sy * sy
    let sp_sq = (((nx - 1) as f64) * var_x + ((ny - 1) as f64) * var_y) / result.df
    let sp = sqrt(sp_sq)

    // Standard error of difference
    result.se_diff = sp * sqrt(1.0 / (nx as f64) + 1.0 / (ny as f64))

    if result.se_diff > 1e-10 {
        result.t_stat = result.mean_diff / result.se_diff
    }

    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)

    // 95% CI
    let t_crit = 2.0
    result.ci_lower = result.mean_diff - t_crit * result.se_diff
    result.ci_upper = result.mean_diff + t_crit * result.se_diff

    // Cohen's d
    if sp > 1e-10 {
        result.cohens_d = result.mean_diff / sp
    }

    result
}

// Welch's t-test (unequal variance)
fn t_test_welch(x: [f64; 100], nx: i64, y: [f64; 100], ny: i64) -> TTestResult {
    var result = ttest_result_new()

    let mx = mean(x, nx)
    let my = mean(y, ny)
    let var_x = variance(x, nx)
    let var_y = variance(y, ny)

    result.mean_diff = mx - my

    // Welch's SE
    let se_x_sq = var_x / (nx as f64)
    let se_y_sq = var_y / (ny as f64)
    result.se_diff = sqrt(se_x_sq + se_y_sq)

    // Welch-Satterthwaite df
    let num = (se_x_sq + se_y_sq) * (se_x_sq + se_y_sq)
    let denom = se_x_sq * se_x_sq / ((nx - 1) as f64) + se_y_sq * se_y_sq / ((ny - 1) as f64)
    result.df = if denom > 1e-10 { num / denom } else { ((nx + ny - 2) as f64) }

    if result.se_diff > 1e-10 {
        result.t_stat = result.mean_diff / result.se_diff
    }

    result.p_value = t_to_p_approx(result.t_stat, result.df)

    // 95% CI
    let t_crit = 2.0
    result.ci_lower = result.mean_diff - t_crit * result.se_diff
    result.ci_upper = result.mean_diff + t_crit * result.se_diff

    // Cohen's d using pooled SD approximation
    let avg_var = (var_x + var_y) / 2.0
    let sp = sqrt(avg_var)
    if sp > 1e-10 {
        result.cohens_d = result.mean_diff / sp
    }

    result
}

// Paired t-test
fn t_test_paired(x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> TTestResult {
    // Compute differences
    var diff: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        diff[i as usize] = x[i as usize] - y[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // One-sample t-test on differences
    t_test_one_sample(diff, n, 0.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// ANOVA
// ============================================================================

// One-way ANOVA for 3 groups
fn anova_oneway_3(g1: [f64; 100], n1: i64,
                  g2: [f64; 100], n2: i64,
                  g3: [f64; 100], n3: i64) -> AnovaResult {
    var result = anova_result_new()

    let n_total = n1 + n2 + n3
    let k = 3  // number of groups

    // Group means
    let m1 = mean(g1, n1)
    let m2 = mean(g2, n2)
    let m3 = mean(g3, n3)

    // Grand mean
    var sum_total = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n1 {
        sum_total = sum_total + g1[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n2 {
        sum_total = sum_total + g2[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n3 {
        sum_total = sum_total + g3[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let grand_mean = sum_total / (n_total as f64)

    // SS between
    result.ss_between = (n1 as f64) * (m1 - grand_mean) * (m1 - grand_mean)
                      + (n2 as f64) * (m2 - grand_mean) * (m2 - grand_mean)
                      + (n3 as f64) * (m3 - grand_mean) * (m3 - grand_mean)

    // SS within
    result.ss_within = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n1 {
        let diff = g1[i as usize] - m1
        result.ss_within = result.ss_within + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n2 {
        let diff = g2[i as usize] - m2
        result.ss_within = result.ss_within + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n3 {
        let diff = g3[i as usize] - m3
        result.ss_within = result.ss_within + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    result.df_between = k - 1
    result.df_within = n_total - k

    // Mean squares
    let ms_between = result.ss_between / (result.df_between as f64)
    let ms_within = result.ss_within / (result.df_within as f64)

    if ms_within > 1e-10 {
        result.f_stat = ms_between / ms_within
    }

    result.p_value = f_to_p_approx(result.f_stat, result.df_between, result.df_within)

    // Eta squared
    let ss_total = result.ss_between + result.ss_within
    if ss_total > 1e-10 {
        result.eta_squared = result.ss_between / ss_total
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// NON-PARAMETRIC TESTS
// ============================================================================

// Mann-Whitney U test (Wilcoxon rank-sum)
fn mann_whitney_u(x: [f64; 100], nx: i64, y: [f64; 100], ny: i64) -> MannWhitneyResult {
    var result = mannwhitney_result_new()

    // Combine and rank
    // For simplicity, count pairwise comparisons
    var u_x = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < nx {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < ny {
            if x[i as usize] > y[j as usize] {
                u_x = u_x + 1.0
            } else if x[i as usize] == y[j as usize] {
                u_x = u_x + 0.5
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let u_y = (nx as f64) * (ny as f64) - u_x
    result.u_stat = if u_x < u_y { u_x } else { u_y }

    // Normal approximation for z-score
    let n_xy = (nx as f64) * (ny as f64)
    let mu_u = n_xy / 2.0
    let sigma_u = sqrt(n_xy * ((nx + ny + 1) as f64) / 12.0)

    if sigma_u > 1e-10 {
        result.z_stat = (u_x - mu_u) / sigma_u
    }

    result.p_value = z_to_p(result.z_stat)

    // Rank-biserial correlation (effect size)
    if n_xy > 0.0 {
        result.rank_biserial = (2.0 * u_x - n_xy) / n_xy
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// EFFECT SIZE INTERPRETATION
// ============================================================================

// Cohen's d interpretation
fn cohens_d_interpret(d: f64) -> i64 {
    let abs_d = if d < 0.0 { -d } else { d }
    if abs_d < 0.2 {
        return 0  // negligible
    }
    if abs_d < 0.5 {
        return 1  // small
    }
    if abs_d < 0.8 {
        return 2  // medium
    }
    3  // large
}

// Eta-squared interpretation
fn eta_squared_interpret(eta2: f64) -> i64 {
    if eta2 < 0.01 {
        return 0  // negligible
    }
    if eta2 < 0.06 {
        return 1  // small
    }
    if eta2 < 0.14 {
        return 2  // medium
    }
    3  // large
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn inf_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
}

fn test_one_sample_t() -> bool {
    var data: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    data[0] = 5.0
    data[1] = 6.0
    data[2] = 7.0
    data[3] = 8.0
    data[4] = 9.0

    // Mean = 7, test against mu0 = 7 -> t should be ~0
    let result = t_test_one_sample(data, 5, 7.0)

    inf_abs_f64(result.t_stat) < 0.01
}

fn test_independent_t() -> bool {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Group 1: mean = 10
    x[0] = 9.0
    x[1] = 10.0
    x[2] = 11.0
    x[3] = 10.0
    x[4] = 10.0

    // Group 2: mean = 15
    y[0] = 14.0
    y[1] = 15.0
    y[2] = 16.0
    y[3] = 15.0
    y[4] = 15.0

    let result = t_test_independent(x, 5, y, 5)

    // mean_diff should be -5
    inf_abs_f64(result.mean_diff - (-5.0)) < 0.1
}

fn test_paired_t() -> bool {
    var pre: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var post: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Pre-treatment: 100, 102, 104, 101, 103
    pre[0] = 100.0
    pre[1] = 102.0
    pre[2] = 104.0
    pre[3] = 101.0
    pre[4] = 103.0

    // Post-treatment: 95, 97, 99, 96, 98 (decrease of 5)
    post[0] = 95.0
    post[1] = 97.0
    post[2] = 99.0
    post[3] = 96.0
    post[4] = 98.0

    let result = t_test_paired(pre, post, 5)

    // mean difference should be 5
    inf_abs_f64(result.mean_diff - 5.0) < 0.1
}

fn test_mann_whitney() -> bool {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Group with lower values
    x[0] = 1.0
    x[1] = 2.0
    x[2] = 3.0

    // Group with higher values
    y[0] = 4.0
    y[1] = 5.0
    y[2] = 6.0

    let result = mann_whitney_u(x, 3, y, 3)

    // U should reflect clear separation
    result > 0.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/stats - Statistical Analysis

module stats


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/multiple_testing.sio ===
// stats::multiple_testing — P-value correction for multiple comparisons
//
// Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) corrections.
// Fixed-array implementations, max 100 tests.
//
// References:
// - Bonferroni (1936): correction for familywise error rate
// - Benjamini & Hochberg (1995): "Controlling the false discovery rate"

// =============================================================================
// Bonferroni correction
// =============================================================================

// Multiply each p-value by the number of tests, cap at 1.0
fn bonferroni(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    adjusted: &![f64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let adj = p_values[i as usize] * (n as f64)
        adjusted[i as usize] = if adj > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { adj }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction
// =============================================================================

// Sort indices by p-value (selection sort, small n)
fn sort_indices_by_pval(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    indices: &![i64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize indices
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        indices[i as usize] = i
        i = i + 1
    }
    // Selection sort
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var min_idx = i
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < n {
            if p_values[indices[j as usize] as usize] < p_values[indices[min_idx as usize] as usize] {
                min_idx = j
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if min_idx != i {
            let tmp = indices[i as usize]
            indices[i as usize] = indices[min_idx as usize]
            indices[min_idx as usize] = tmp
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn benjamini_hochberg(
    p_values: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    adjusted: &![f64; 100]
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: Sort p-values
    var indices: [i64; 100] = [0; 100]
    sort_indices_by_pval(p_values, n, &indices)

    // Step 2: Compute adjusted p-values
    // adjusted[rank] = p * n / rank, then enforce monotonicity from bottom up
    var temp: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let rank = i + 1
        let adj = p_values[indices[i as usize] as usize] * (n as f64) / (rank as f64)
        temp[i as usize] = if adj > 1.0 { 1.0 } else { adj }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 3: Enforce monotonicity (cumulative min from end)
    i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 {
        if temp[(i + 1) as usize] < temp[i as usize] {
            temp[i as usize] = temp[(i + 1) as usize]
        }
        i = i - 1
    }

    // Step 4: Map back to original order
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        adjusted[indices[i as usize] as usize] = temp[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Significance counting
// =============================================================================

fn count_significant(adjusted: [f64; 100], n: i64, alpha: f64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if adjusted[i as usize] < alpha {
            count = count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    count
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn mt_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn test_bonferroni() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pvals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    pvals[0] = 0.01
    pvals[1] = 0.04
    pvals[2] = 0.03
    pvals[3] = 0.20

    var adj: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    bonferroni(pvals, 4, &adj)

    // 0.01 * 4 = 0.04, 0.04 * 4 = 0.16, 0.03 * 4 = 0.12, 0.20 * 4 = 0.80
    let ok1 = mt_abs(adj[0] - 0.04) < 0.001
    let ok2 = mt_abs(adj[1] - 0.16) < 0.001
    ok1 && ok2
}

fn test_bh() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var pvals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    pvals[0] = 0.01
    pvals[1] = 0.04
    pvals[2] = 0.03
    pvals[3] = 0.20

    var adj: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    benjamini_hochberg(pvals, 4, &adj)

    // Smallest p (0.01) adjusted = 0.01*4/1 = 0.04
    let ok1 = mt_abs(adj[0] - 0.04) < 0.001
    // All adjusted p-values should be <= 1.0
    let ok2 = adj[3] <= 1.0
    ok1 && ok2
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/multivariate/cluster.sio ===
// stats::multivariate::cluster — Epistemic Clustering
//
// Unsupervised clustering with epistemic quality metrics:
// - K-means (Lloyd's algorithm)
// - Hierarchical agglomerative (single/complete/average linkage)
// - Silhouette scores for cluster quality
// - Elbow method for optimal K
// - Knowledge<ClusterResult> with confidence
//
// References:
// - Lloyd (1982): "Least squares quantization in PCM"
// - Ward (1963): "Hierarchical grouping to optimize an objective function"
// - Rousseeuw (1987): "Silhouettes: a graphical aid" (silhouette scores)
// - Tibshirani et al. (2001): "Estimating the number of clusters" (gap statistic)

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn cl_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn cl_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn cl_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn cl_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// =============================================================================
// Types
// =============================================================================

let MAX_K: i64 = 10
let MAX_N: i64 = 100
let MAX_P: i64 = 10

struct KMeansResult {
    centroids: [[f64; 10]; 10],   // k × p centroid positions
    assignments: [i64; 100],       // Cluster label for each observation
    k: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
    within_ss: f64,                // Total within-cluster sum of squares
    between_ss: f64,               // Between-cluster sum of squares
    total_ss: f64,
    n_iterations: i64,
    converged: bool
}

struct SilhouetteResult {
    scores: [f64; 100],            // Per-observation silhouette score [-1, 1]
    avg_score: f64,                 // Average silhouette width
    cluster_avg: [f64; 10]         // Per-cluster average
}



struct ClusterDiagnostics {
    silhouette: SilhouetteResult,
    calinski_harabasz: f64,   // CH index (higher = better)
    cluster_quality: BetaConfidence
}

struct ClusterProvenance {
    method: String,
    k: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
    diagnostics: ClusterDiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgeCluster {
    value: KMeansResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: ClusterProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Distance Functions
// =============================================================================

fn euclidean_dist(
    a: [f64; 10],
    b: [f64; 10],
    p: i64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        let d = a[j as usize] - b[j as usize]
        sum = sum + d * d
        j = j + 1
    }
    cl_sqrt(sum)
}

fn euclidean_dist_sq(a: [f64; 10], b: [f64; 10], p: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        let d = a[j as usize] - b[j as usize]
        sum = sum + d * d
        j = j + 1
    }
    sum
}

// =============================================================================
// K-MEANS (Lloyd's Algorithm)
// =============================================================================

fn kmeans(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    k: i64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> KMeansResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initialize centroids (first k observations)
    var centroids: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < k {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            centroids[c as usize][j as usize] = data[c as usize][j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        c = c + 1
    }

    var assignments: [i64; 100] = [0; 100]
    var converged = false
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        var changed = false

        // Assignment step: assign each point to nearest centroid
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            var best_c: i64 = 0
            var best_dist = euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], centroids[0], p)

            c = 1
            while c < k {
                let d = euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], centroids[c as usize], p)
                if d < best_dist {
                    best_dist = d
                    best_c = c
                }
                c = c + 1
            }

            if assignments[i as usize] != best_c {
                assignments[i as usize] = best_c
                changed = true
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        if !changed {
            converged = true
            break
        }

        // Update step: recompute centroids
        var counts: [i64; 10] = [0; 10]
        var sums: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let cl = assignments[i as usize]
            counts[cl as usize] = counts[cl as usize] + 1
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < p {
                sums[cl as usize][j as usize] = sums[cl as usize][j as usize] + data[i as usize][j as usize]
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        c = 0
        while c < k {
            if counts[c as usize] > 0 {
                var j: i64 = 0
                while j < p {
                    centroids[c as usize][j as usize] = sums[c as usize][j as usize] / (counts[c as usize] as f64)
                    j = j + 1
                }
            }
            c = c + 1
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Compute within-cluster SS and between-cluster SS
    // Grand mean
    var grand: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        var sum = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n { sum = sum + data[i as usize][j as usize]; i = i + 1 }
        grand[j as usize] = sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }

    var wss = 0.0
    var bss = 0.0
    var tss = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let cl = assignments[i as usize]
        wss = wss + euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], centroids[cl as usize], p)
        tss = tss + euclidean_dist_sq(data[i as usize], grand, p)
        i = i + 1
    }
    bss = tss - wss

    KMeansResult {
        centroids: centroids,
        assignments: assignments,
        k: k,
        n_obs: n,
        n_vars: p,
        within_ss: wss,
        between_ss: bss,
        total_ss: tss,
        n_iterations: iter,
        converged: converged
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// SILHOUETTE SCORES
// =============================================================================

fn silhouette_scores(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    assignments: [i64; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    k: i64
) -> SilhouetteResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var scores: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var cluster_sums: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var cluster_counts: [i64; 10] = [0; 10]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let ci = assignments[i as usize]

        // a(i) = average distance to points in same cluster
        var a_sum = 0.0
        var a_count: i64 = 0

        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            if j != i && assignments[j as usize] == ci {
                a_sum = a_sum + euclidean_dist(data[i as usize], data[j as usize], p)
                a_count = a_count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        let a_i = if a_count > 0 { a_sum / (a_count as f64) } else { 0.0 }

        // b(i) = min over other clusters of avg distance
        var b_i = 1.0e30
        var c: i64 = 0
        while c < k {
            if c == ci { c = c + 1; continue }

            var b_sum = 0.0
            var b_count: i64 = 0
            j = 0
            while j < n {
                if assignments[j as usize] == c {
                    b_sum = b_sum + euclidean_dist(data[i as usize], data[j as usize], p)
                    b_count = b_count + 1
                }
                j = j + 1
            }
            let b_c = if b_count > 0 { b_sum / (b_count as f64) } else { 1.0e30 }
            b_i = cl_min(b_i, b_c)

            c = c + 1
        }

        // s(i) = (b(i) - a(i)) / max(a(i), b(i))
        let max_ab = cl_max(a_i, b_i)
        let s = if max_ab > 1.0e-10 { (b_i - a_i) / max_ab } else { 0.0 }
        scores[i as usize] = s

        cluster_sums[ci as usize] = cluster_sums[ci as usize] + s
        cluster_counts[ci as usize] = cluster_counts[ci as usize] + 1

        i = i + 1
    }

    // Average silhouette
    var total = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n { total = total + scores[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    let avg = total / (n as f64)

    // Per-cluster averages
    var cluster_avg: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var c: i64 = 0
    while c < k {
        cluster_avg[c as usize] = if cluster_counts[c as usize] > 0 {
            cluster_sums[c as usize] / (cluster_counts[c as usize] as f64)
        } else { 0.0 }
        c = c + 1
    }

    SilhouetteResult {
        scores: scores,
        avg_score: avg,
        cluster_avg: cluster_avg
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC CLUSTERING
// =============================================================================

fn kmeans_epistemic(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    k: i64
) -> KnowledgeCluster with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = kmeans(data, n, p, k, 100)
    let sil = silhouette_scores(data, result.assignments, n, p, k)

    // Calinski-Harabasz index: (BSS/(k-1)) / (WSS/(n-k))
    let ch = if k > 1 && result.within_ss > 1.0e-10 {
        (result.between_ss / ((k - 1) as f64)) / (result.within_ss / ((n - k) as f64))
    } else { 0.0 }

    // Cluster quality confidence
    let sil_conf = if sil.avg_score > 0.70 { 0.95 }      // Strong
                   else if sil.avg_score > 0.50 { 0.80 }   // Reasonable
                   else if sil.avg_score > 0.25 { 0.60 }   // Weak
                   else { 0.40 }                             // No structure
    let quality_beta = beta_new(sil_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - sil_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let diag = ClusterDiagnostics {
        silhouette: sil,
        calinski_harabasz: ch,
        cluster_quality: quality_beta
    }

    let prov = ClusterProvenance {
        method: "KMeans_Lloyd",
        k: k,
        n_obs: n,
        n_vars: p,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeCluster {
        value: result,
        variance: 0.0,
        confidence: quality_beta,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_kmeans_two_clusters() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: [[f64; 10]; 100] = [[0.0; 10]; 100]

    // Cluster 1: near (0, 0)
    data[0][0] = 0.1; data[0][1] = 0.2
    data[1][0] = 0.3; data[1][1] = 0.1
    data[2][0] = 0.0; data[2][1] = 0.3
    data[3][0] = 0.2; data[3][1] = 0.0
    data[4][0] = 0.1; data[4][1] = 0.1

    // Cluster 2: near (5, 5)
    data[5][0] = 4.9; data[5][1] = 5.1
    data[6][0] = 5.1; data[6][1] = 4.9
    data[7][0] = 5.0; data[7][1] = 5.0
    data[8][0] = 4.8; data[8][1] = 5.2
    data[9][0] = 5.2; data[9][1] = 4.8

    let result = kmeans_epistemic(data, 10, 2, 2)

    // Should separate into two clusters
    let converged = result.value.converged

    // High silhouette (well-separated)
    let sil_ok = result.provenance.diagnostics.silhouette.avg_score > 0.5

    converged && sil_ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/multivariate/pca.sio ===
// stats::multivariate::pca — Epistemic Principal Component Analysis
//
// Dimensionality reduction with full uncertainty tracking:
// - SVD-based PCA (power iteration method)
// - Scree analysis with broken-stick model
// - Component loadings and scores
// - Variance explained with bootstrap CIs
// - Knowledge<PCAResult> with epistemic metadata
//
// References:
// - Pearson (1901): "On lines and planes of closest fit"
// - Hotelling (1933): "Analysis of complex statistical variables"
// - Jackson (1993): "Stopping rules in PCA" (broken-stick)
// - Cattell (1966): "The scree test for the number of factors"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn pca_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn pca_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn pca_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

struct EigenResult {
    eigenvalue: f64,
    eigenvector: [f64; 10]
}

// =============================================================================
// Types
// =============================================================================

// Max dimensions: 10 variables, 100 observations
let MAX_VARS: i64 = 10

struct PCAResult {
    eigenvalues: [f64; 10],            // Sorted descending
    variance_explained: [f64; 10],     // Proportion of variance
    cumulative_variance: [f64; 10],    // Cumulative proportion
    loadings: [[f64; 10]; 10],         // Component loadings (p × k)
    scores: [[f64; 10]; 100],          // Observation scores (n × k)
    n_components_optimal: i64,         // Recommended components
    n_vars: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    total_variance: f64
}

struct PCADiagnostics {
    kaiser_criterion: i64,        // Components with eigenvalue > 1
    broken_stick_criterion: i64,  // Broken-stick model
    variance_80_pct: i64,         // Components for 80% variance
    sample_adequate: BetaConfidence  // KMO-like adequacy
}

struct PCAProvenance {
    method_id: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_vars: i64,
    standardized: i64,
    diagnostics: PCADiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgePCA {
    value: PCAResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: PCAProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Matrix Operations
// =============================================================================

// Compute column means
fn col_means(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) -> [f64; 10] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var means: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        var sum = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            sum = sum + data[i as usize][j as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        means[j as usize] = sum / (n as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
    means
}

// Center data (subtract column means)
fn center_data(
    data: &![[f64; 10]; 100],
    means: [f64; 10],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            data[i as usize][j as usize] = data[i as usize][j as usize] - means[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Standardize data (center + divide by SD)
fn standardize_data(
    data: &![[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let means = col_means(*data, n, p)

    // Compute SDs
    var sds: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        var ss = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            let d = data[i as usize][j as usize] - means[j as usize]
            ss = ss + d * d
            i = i + 1
        }
        sds[j as usize] = pca_sqrt(ss / ((n - 1) as f64))
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Center and scale
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            let sd = pca_max(sds[j as usize], 1.0e-10)
            data[i as usize][j as usize] = (data[i as usize][j as usize] - means[j as usize]) / sd
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Compute covariance matrix (p × p) from centered data
fn covariance_matrix(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) -> [[f64; 10]; 10] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var cov: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]

    var j1: i64 = 0
    while j1 < p {
        var j2: i64 = j1
        while j2 < p {
            var sum = 0.0
            var i: i64 = 0
            while i < n {
                sum = sum + data[i as usize][j1 as usize] * data[i as usize][j2 as usize]
                i = i + 1
            }
            let c = sum / ((n - 1) as f64)
            cov[j1 as usize][j2 as usize] = c
            cov[j2 as usize][j1 as usize] = c  // Symmetric
            j2 = j2 + 1
        }
        j1 = j1 + 1
    }

    cov
}

// =============================================================================
// Power Iteration for Eigenvalues/Eigenvectors
// =============================================================================

// Extract dominant eigenvalue/eigenvector via power iteration
fn power_iteration(
    mat: [[f64; 10]; 10],
    p: i64,
    max_iter: i64
) -> EigenResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Initial vector
    var v: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        v[j as usize] = 1.0 / pca_sqrt(p as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }

    var eigenvalue = 0.0
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // w = A * v
        var w: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < p {
                sum = sum + mat[j as usize][k as usize] * v[k as usize]
                k = k + 1
            }
            w[j as usize] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Eigenvalue = ||w||
        var norm = 0.0
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            norm = norm + w[j as usize] * w[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        eigenvalue = pca_sqrt(norm)

        if eigenvalue < 1.0e-10 { break }

        // Normalize: v = w / ||w||
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            v[j as usize] = w[j as usize] / eigenvalue
            j = j + 1
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    EigenResult { eigenvalue: eigenvalue, eigenvector: v }
}

// Deflate matrix: A' = A - λ·v·v'
fn deflate_matrix(
    mat: &![[f64; 10]; 10],
    eigenvalue: f64,
    eigenvector: [f64; 10],
    p: i64
) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < p {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            mat[i as usize][j as usize] = mat[i as usize][j as usize] -
                eigenvalue * eigenvector[i as usize] * eigenvector[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Broken-Stick Model (for optimal component selection)
// =============================================================================

fn broken_stick_expected(k: i64, p: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Expected proportion for k-th component under broken-stick:
    // b_k = (1/p) * Σ_{j=k}^{p} 1/j
    var sum = 0.0
    var j: i64 = k
    while j <= p {
        sum = sum + 1.0 / (j as f64)
        j = j + 1
    }
    sum / (p as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// PCA IMPLEMENTATION
// =============================================================================

fn fit_pca(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    standardize: i64
) -> PCAResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: Center (and optionally standardize)
    var work_data: [[f64; 10]; 100] = data

    if standardize != 0 {
        standardize_data(&work_data, n, p)
    } else {
        let means = col_means(work_data, n, p)
        center_data(&work_data, means, n, p)
    }

    // Step 2: Covariance matrix
    var cov = covariance_matrix(work_data, n, p)

    // Step 3: Total variance
    var total_var = 0.0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        total_var = total_var + cov[j as usize][j as usize]
        j = j + 1
    }

    // Step 4: Extract eigenvalues/vectors via repeated power iteration + deflation
    var eigenvalues: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var loadings: [[f64; 10]; 10] = [[0.0; 10]; 10]
    var var_explained: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    var cum_var: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]

    var cum = 0.0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < p {
        let eig = power_iteration(cov, p, 100)
        let ev = eig.eigenvalue
        let evec = eig.eigenvector
        eigenvalues[k as usize] = ev

        // Store loadings
        j = 0
        while j < p {
            loadings[j as usize][k as usize] = evec[j as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Variance explained
        let prop = if total_var > 1.0e-10 { ev / total_var } else { 0.0 }
        var_explained[k as usize] = prop
        cum = cum + prop
        cum_var[k as usize] = cum

        // Deflate
        deflate_matrix(&cov, ev, evec, p)

        k = k + 1
    }

    // Step 5: Compute scores (n × k): S = X_centered · V
    var scores: [[f64; 10]; 100] = [[0.0; 10]; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        k = 0
        while k < p {
            var sum = 0.0
            j = 0
            while j < p {
                sum = sum + work_data[i as usize][j as usize] * loadings[j as usize][k as usize]
                j = j + 1
            }
            scores[i as usize][k as usize] = sum
            k = k + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Step 6: Optimal components
    // Kaiser criterion: eigenvalue > 1 (for correlation PCA)
    var kaiser = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        if eigenvalues[k as usize] > 1.0 { kaiser = kaiser + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Broken-stick criterion
    var broken_stick = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        let expected = broken_stick_expected(k + 1, p)
        if var_explained[k as usize] > expected { broken_stick = broken_stick + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // 80% variance
    var var80 = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        var80 = var80 + 1
        if cum_var[k as usize] >= 0.80 { break }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Use most conservative criterion
    let optimal = if kaiser < broken_stick { kaiser } else { broken_stick }
    let optimal_final = if optimal < var80 { var80 } else { optimal }

    PCAResult {
        eigenvalues: eigenvalues,
        variance_explained: var_explained,
        cumulative_variance: cum_var,
        loadings: loadings,
        scores: scores,
        n_components_optimal: optimal_final,
        n_vars: p,
        n_obs: n,
        total_variance: total_var
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC PCA
// =============================================================================

fn fit_pca_epistemic(
    data: [[f64; 10]; 100],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    standardize: i64
) -> KnowledgePCA with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let result = fit_pca(data, n, p, standardize)

    // Diagnostics
    var kaiser = 0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < p {
        if result.eigenvalues[k as usize] > 1.0 { kaiser = kaiser + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    var broken = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        let exp = broken_stick_expected(k + 1, p)
        if result.variance_explained[k as usize] > exp { broken = broken + 1 }
        k = k + 1
    }

    var var80 = 0
    k = 0
    while k < p {
        var80 = var80 + 1
        if result.cumulative_variance[k as usize] >= 0.80 { break }
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Sample adequacy: n/p ratio (rule of thumb: 5-10 per variable)
    let np_ratio = (n as f64) / (p as f64)
    let sample_conf = if np_ratio >= 10.0 { 0.95 }
                      else if np_ratio >= 5.0 { 0.80 }
                      else if np_ratio >= 3.0 { 0.60 }
                      else { 0.40 }
    let sample_beta = beta_new(sample_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - sample_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let diag = PCADiagnostics {
        kaiser_criterion: kaiser as i64,
        broken_stick_criterion: broken as i64,
        variance_80_pct: var80 as i64,
        sample_adequate: sample_beta
    }

    let prov = PCAProvenance {
        method_id: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        n_vars: p,
        standardized: standardize,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    // Asymptotic variance of first eigenvalue (Girshick 1939):
    // Var(λ̂₁) ≈ 2λ₁² / n  — exact under multivariate normality
    // Reference: Anderson (2003) "An Introduction to Multivariate Statistical Analysis", p.477
    let lambda1 = result.eigenvalues[0]
    let eigenvalue_variance = if n > 0 { 2.0 * lambda1 * lambda1 / (n as f64) } else { 0.0 }

    KnowledgePCA {
        value: result,
        variance: eigenvalue_variance,
        confidence: sample_beta,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_pca_basic() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // 2 variables, 5 observations (correlated)
    var data: [[f64; 10]; 100] = [[0.0; 10]; 100]
    data[0][0] = 1.0; data[0][1] = 2.0
    data[1][0] = 2.0; data[1][1] = 4.0
    data[2][0] = 3.0; data[2][1] = 5.0
    data[3][0] = 4.0; data[3][1] = 7.0
    data[4][0] = 5.0; data[4][1] = 8.0

    let result = fit_pca_epistemic(data, 5, 2, 1)

    // First component should explain most variance (highly correlated)
    let pc1_ok = result.value.variance_explained[0] > 0.80

    // Two eigenvalues (2 variables)
    let ev_ok = result.value.eigenvalues[0] > result.value.eigenvalues[1]

    pc1_ok && ev_ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/regression/linear.sio ===
// stats::regression::linear — Epistemic Linear Regression
//
// Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression with:
// - Knowledge<LinearModel> return type
// - Full diagnostics (VIF, Cook's D, leverage, residual plots)
// - Assumption checks as BetaConfidence
// - GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation
//
// References:
// - Gauss (1809): Method of least squares
// - Cook (1977): Detection of influential observations
// - Belsley et al. (1980): Regression Diagnostics (VIF)
// - Durbin & Watson (1950): Testing for serial correlation

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn fabs(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn log(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn exp(x: f64) -> f64;
}

pub use stats::shared::*
use special::beta::{ibeta}

// ============================================================================
// CORE TYPES
// ============================================================================

/// Linear model coefficients and statistics.
///
/// # Builder Pattern
///
/// ```sio
/// let model = LinearRegression::new()
///     .with_data(&x, &y, n)
///     .fit();
///
/// // Or with method chaining:
/// let prediction = LinearRegression::new()
///     .with_data(&x, &y, n)
///     .fit()
///     .predict(5.0);
/// ```
pub struct LinearModel {
    pub coefficients: [f64; 10],      // β₀, β₁, ..., β_p
    pub std_errors: [f64; 10],         // SE(βⱼ)
    pub t_statistics: [f64; 10],       // t = βⱼ / SE(βⱼ)
    pub p_values: [f64; 10],           // Two-tailed p-values
    pub n_predictors: i64,             // Number of predictors (excluding intercept)
    pub n_obs: i64,                    // Sample size
    pub r_squared: f64,                // R²
    pub adj_r_squared: f64,            // Adjusted R²
    pub f_statistic: f64,              // Overall model F-test
    pub residual_se: f64,              // Residual standard error
    pub residuals: [f64; 100]          // Residuals eᵢ = yᵢ - ŷᵢ
}

// ============================================================================
// LinearRegression Builder
// ============================================================================

/// Builder for linear regression with method chaining.
///
/// # Example
///
/// ```sio
/// let model = LinearRegression::builder()
///     .with_x(&x)
///     .with_y(&y)
///     .with_n(10)
///     .fit_simple();
///
/// // Predict new value
/// let y_pred = model.predict(5.0);
/// ```
pub struct LinearRegression {
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    fitted: bool,
    model: LinearModel,
}

impl LinearRegression {
    /// Create a new empty regression builder.
    pub fn builder() -> LinearRegression {
        LinearRegression {
            x: [0.0; 100],
            y: [0.0; 100],
            n: 0,
            fitted: false,
            model: LinearModel {
                coefficients: [0.0; 10],
                std_errors: [0.0; 10],
                t_statistics: [0.0; 10],
                p_values: [0.0; 10],
                n_predictors: 0,
                n_obs: 0,
                r_squared: 0.0,
                adj_r_squared: 0.0,
                f_statistic: 0.0,
                residual_se: 0.0,
                residuals: [0.0; 100],
            },
        }
    }

    /// Alias for builder() for convenience.
    pub fn new() -> LinearRegression {
        LinearRegression::builder()
    }

    /// Set predictor variable X.
    pub fn with_x(self, x: [f64; 100]) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.x = x
        result
    }

    /// Set response variable Y.
    pub fn with_y(self, y: [f64; 100]) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.y = y
        result
    }

    /// Set number of observations.
    pub fn with_n(self, n: i64) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.n = n
        result
    }

    /// Set all data at once.
    pub fn with_data(self, x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> LinearRegression {
        var result = self
        result.x = x
        result.y = y
        result.n = n
        result
    }

    /// Fit simple linear regression (y = β₀ + β₁x).
    pub fn fit_simple(self) -> LinearModel {
        fit_simple_linear_regression(self.x, self.y, self.n)
    }

    /// Fit epistemic linear regression with full diagnostics.
    pub fn fit_epistemic(self) -> KnowledgeLinearModel {
        fit_linear_regression_epistemic(self.x, self.y, self.n)
    }
}

impl LinearModel {
    /// Predict y for a given x value.
    ///
    /// # Parameters
    /// - `x_val`: Predictor value
    ///
    /// # Return
    /// Predicted y value (ŷ = β₀ + β₁x)
    pub fn predict(&self, x_val: f64) -> f64 {
        self.coefficients[0] + self.coefficients[1] * x_val
    }

    /// Get intercept (β₀).
    pub fn intercept(&self) -> f64 {
        self.coefficients[0]
    }

    /// Get slope (β₁).
    pub fn slope(&self) -> f64 {
        self.coefficients[1]
    }

    /// Get standard error of slope.
    pub fn slope_se(&self) -> f64 {
        self.std_errors[1]
    }

    /// Get R² (coefficient of determination).
    pub fn r2(&self) -> f64 {
        self.r_squared
    }

    /// Get adjusted R².
    pub fn adj_r2(&self) -> f64 {
        self.adj_r_squared
    }

    /// Check if slope is significant at p < 0.05.
    pub fn is_slope_significant(&self) -> bool {
        self.p_values[1] < 0.05
    }

    /// Get confidence interval for slope.
    pub fn slope_ci(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
        // 95% CI: β₁ ± 1.96 * SE(β₁)
        let margin = 1.96 * self.std_errors[1]
        (self.coefficients[1] - margin, self.coefficients[1] + margin)
    }
}

// Regression diagnostics
pub struct ModelDiagnostics {
    pub vif: [f64; 10],
    pub cooks_distance: [f64; 100],
    pub leverage: [f64; 100],
    pub dffits: [f64; 100],
    pub normality_resid: BetaConfidence,
    pub homoscedasticity: BetaConfidence,
    pub no_autocorrelation: BetaConfidence,
    pub no_multicollinearity: BetaConfidence,
    pub influential_points: i64
}

pub struct RegressionAssumptions {
    pub linearity: BetaConfidence,
    pub normality_residuals: BetaConfidence,
    pub homoscedasticity: BetaConfidence,
    pub independence: BetaConfidence,
    pub no_multicollinearity: BetaConfidence
}

pub struct RegressionProvenance {
    pub method_code: i32,  // 0=OLS, 1=WeightedLS, 2=RobustLS
    pub n_obs: i64,
    pub n_predictors: i64,
    pub timestamp: i64,
    pub assumptions: RegressionAssumptions,
    pub diagnostics: ModelDiagnostics
}

pub struct KnowledgeLinearModel {
    pub value: LinearModel,
    pub variance: f64,
    pub confidence: BetaConfidence,
    pub provenance: RegressionProvenance
}

// ============================================================================
// MATRIX OPERATIONS (Simplified)
// ============================================================================

// Compute X'X (2x2 for simple regression: intercept + 1 predictor)
fn xtx_simple(x: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> (f64, f64, f64, f64) {
    var sum_1 = 0.0
    var sum_x = 0.0
    var sum_x2 = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        sum_1 = sum_1 + 1.0
        sum_x = sum_x + xi
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + xi * xi
        i = i + 1
    }

    // X'X = [[n, Σx], [Σx, Σx²]]
    (sum_1, sum_x, sum_x, sum_x2)
}

// Compute X'y (2x1 for simple regression)
fn xty_simple(x: [f64; 100], y: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> (f64, f64) {
    var sum_y = 0.0
    var sum_xy = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        sum_y = sum_y + yi
        sum_xy = sum_xy + xi * yi
        i = i + 1
    }

    (sum_y, sum_xy)
}

// Solve 2x2 system: (X'X)β = X'y
fn solve_2x2(a11: f64, a12: f64, a21: f64, a22: f64, b1: f64, b2: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
    let det = a11 * a22 - a12 * a21

    if abs_f64(det) < 1e-10 {
        // Singular matrix
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    }

    let beta0 = (a22 * b1 - a12 * b2) / det
    let beta1 = (a11 * b2 - a21 * b1) / det

    (beta0, beta1)
}

// Compute mean
fn mean(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

// Compute variance
fn variance(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 {
    let m = mean(data, n)
    var sum_sq = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = data[i as usize] - m
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum_sq / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMPLE LINEAR REGRESSION (y = β₀ + β₁x)
// ============================================================================

pub fn fit_simple_linear_regression(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> LinearModel {
    // Compute X'X and X'y
    let (xx_11, xx_12, xx_21, xx_22) = xtx_simple(x, n)
    let (xy_1, xy_2) = xty_simple(x, y, n)

    // Solve for coefficients: β = (X'X)⁻¹ X'y
    let (beta0, beta1) = solve_2x2(xx_11, xx_12, xx_21, xx_22, xy_1, xy_2)

    // Compute fitted values and residuals
    var y_hat: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var residuals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var rss = 0.0  // Residual sum of squares

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        let pred = beta0 + beta1 * xi
        y_hat[i as usize] = pred
        residuals[i as usize] = yi - pred
        rss = rss + (yi - pred) * (yi - pred)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Degrees of freedom
    let df_resid = (n - 2) as f64  // n - p - 1 where p=1
    let residual_se = sqrt(rss / df_resid)

    // Total sum of squares
    let y_mean = mean(y, n)
    var tss = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = y[i as usize] - y_mean
        tss = tss + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    // R² = 1 - RSS/TSS
    let r_squared = if tss > 1e-10 { 1.0 - rss / tss } else { 0.0 }

    // Adjusted R²
    let n_f = n as f64
    let p = 1.0  // Number of predictors
    let adj_r_squared = 1.0 - (1.0 - r_squared) * (n_f - 1.0) / (n_f - p - 1.0)

    // F-statistic: F = (TSS - RSS) / p / (RSS / df_resid)
    let f_stat = if rss > 1e-10 {
        ((tss - rss) / p) / (rss / df_resid)
    } else {
        0.0
    }

    // Standard errors of coefficients
    // Var(β) = σ² (X'X)⁻¹
    let det = xx_11 * xx_22 - xx_12 * xx_21
    let var_beta0 = if abs_f64(det) > 1e-10 {
        (residual_se * residual_se) * xx_22 / det
    } else {
        0.0
    }
    let var_beta1 = if abs_f64(det) > 1e-10 {
        (residual_se * residual_se) * xx_11 / det
    } else {
        0.0
    }

    let se_beta0 = sqrt(var_beta0)
    let se_beta1 = sqrt(var_beta1)

    // t-statistics
    let t0 = if se_beta0 > 1e-10 { beta0 / se_beta0 } else { 0.0 }
    let t1 = if se_beta1 > 1e-10 { beta1 / se_beta1 } else { 0.0 }

    // p-values (approximation)
    let p0 = t_to_p_approx(t0, df_resid)
    let p1 = t_to_p_approx(t1, df_resid)

    // Construct result
    var coefficients: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    coefficients[0] = beta0
    coefficients[1] = beta1

    var std_errors: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    std_errors[0] = se_beta0
    std_errors[1] = se_beta1

    var t_stats: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    t_stats[0] = t0
    t_stats[1] = t1

    var p_vals: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    p_vals[0] = p0
    p_vals[1] = p1

    LinearModel {
        coefficients: coefficients,
        std_errors: std_errors,
        t_statistics: t_stats,
        p_values: p_vals,
        n_predictors: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        r_squared: r_squared,
        adj_r_squared: adj_r_squared,
        f_statistic: f_stat,
        residual_se: residual_se,
        residuals: residuals
    }
}

// p-value from t-distribution using regularized incomplete beta
// Two-tailed: p = 2 * I_{df/(df+t²)}(df/2, 1/2)
// References: Abramowitz & Stegun §26.7.1; Press et al. §6.4
fn t_to_p_approx(t: f64, df: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if df <= 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    let t2 = t * t
    let x = df / (df + t2)
    let p_one_tail = ibeta(df / 2.0, 0.5, x)
    // two-tailed: 2 * (1 - p_one_tail) but ibeta gives lower tail
    // For t-dist: p_two_tail = ibeta(df/2, 0.5, df/(df+t^2))
    // since p_one_tail here is already P(T >= |t|) = I_x(df/2, 0.5)
    let p = p_one_tail
    if p > 1.0 { return 1.0 }
    if p < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    p
}

// ============================================================================
// DIAGNOSTICS
// ============================================================================

// Compute leverage (hat matrix diagonals)
fn compute_leverage(x: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> [f64; 100] {
    let x_mean = mean(x, n)
    var sxx = 0.0

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = x[i as usize] - x_mean
        sxx = sxx + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }

    var leverage: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let diff = x[i as usize] - x_mean
        // hᵢᵢ = 1/n + (xᵢ - x̄)² / Σ(xⱼ - x̄)²
        let h = 1.0 / (n as f64) + (diff * diff) / sxx
        leverage[i as usize] = h
        i = i + 1
    }

    leverage
}

// Compute Cook's distance
fn compute_cooks_distance(
    model: &LinearModel,
    leverage: [f64; 100]
) -> [f64; 100] {
    var cooks_d: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    let p = (model.n_predictors + 1) as f64  // Including intercept
    let mse = model.residual_se * model.residual_se

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < model.n_obs {
        let e = model.residuals[i as usize]
        let h = leverage[i as usize]

        // D = (eᵢ² / (p * MSE)) * (hᵢᵢ / (1 - hᵢᵢ)²)
        if abs_f64(1.0 - h) > 1e-10 && mse > 1e-10 {
            let d = (e * e / (p * mse)) * (h / ((1.0 - h) * (1.0 - h)))
            cooks_d[i as usize] = d
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    cooks_d
}

// Compute VIF (for simple regression: VIF = 1 always)
fn compute_vif_simple() -> [f64; 10] {
    var vif: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    vif[0] = 1.0  // Intercept: not applicable
    vif[1] = 1.0  // Single predictor: VIF = 1
    vif
}

// Check normality of residuals
fn check_residual_normality(residuals: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> BetaConfidence {
    // Use Shapiro-Wilk approximation from assumption checks
    // Simplified: check standardized range
    let resid_mean = mean(residuals, n)
    let resid_var = variance(residuals, n)
    let resid_sd = sqrt(resid_var)

    if resid_sd < 1e-10 {
        return beta_new(100.0, 1.0)
    }

    var min_r = residuals[0]
    var max_r = residuals[0]
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let r = residuals[i as usize]
        if r < min_r { min_r = r }
        if r > max_r { max_r = r }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let range = max_r - min_r
    let expected_range = resid_sd * (2.5 + 0.5 * sqrt(n as f64))
    let ratio = range / expected_range
    let deviation = abs_f64(ratio - 1.0)

    let p_conf = if deviation < 0.15 { 0.90 }
                 else if deviation < 0.30 { 0.70 }
                 else { 0.50 }

    let nf = n as f64
    let n_factor = if nf >= 30.0 { 1.0 } else { sqrt(nf / 30.0) }
    let concentration = nf * 0.5

    beta_new(p_conf * n_factor * concentration, (1.0 - p_conf * n_factor) * concentration)
}

// Check homoscedasticity (Breusch-Pagan approximation)
fn check_homoscedasticity(
    residuals: [f64; 100],
    x: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> BetaConfidence {
    // Simplified: check if |residuals| correlate with x
    // Full BP: regress e² on x

    var abs_resid: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        abs_resid[i as usize] = abs_f64(residuals[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Compute correlation between |e| and x
    let mean_abs_r = mean(abs_resid, n)
    let mean_x = mean(x, n)

    var cov = 0.0
    var var_abs_r = 0.0
    var var_x = 0.0

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d_abs_r = abs_resid[i as usize] - mean_abs_r
        let d_x = x[i as usize] - mean_x
        cov = cov + d_abs_r * d_x
        var_abs_r = var_abs_r + d_abs_r * d_abs_r
        var_x = var_x + d_x * d_x
        i = i + 1
    }

    let denom = sqrt(var_abs_r * var_x)
    let corr = if denom > 1e-10 { cov / denom } else { 0.0 }

    // High |corr| → heteroscedasticity
    let abs_corr = abs_f64(corr)
    let p_conf = if abs_corr < 0.3 { 0.90 }
                 else if abs_corr < 0.5 { 0.70 }
                 else { 0.50 }

    let nf = n as f64
    beta_new(p_conf * nf * 0.3, (1.0 - p_conf) * nf * 0.3)
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC LINEAR REGRESSION
// ============================================================================

pub fn fit_linear_regression_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeLinearModel {
    // Fit classical OLS
    let model = fit_simple_linear_regression(x, y, n)

    // Compute diagnostics
    let leverage = compute_leverage(x, n)
    let cooks_d = compute_cooks_distance(&model, leverage)
    let vif = compute_vif_simple()

    // Assumption checks
    let norm_resid = check_residual_normality(model.residuals, n)
    let homosked = check_homoscedasticity(model.residuals, x, n)

    // Independence: Durbin-Watson approximation
    // DW ≈ 2 → no autocorrelation
    var dw_num = 0.0
    var dw_denom = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < n {
        let diff = model.residuals[i as usize] - model.residuals[(i - 1) as usize]
        dw_num = dw_num + diff * diff
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let e = model.residuals[i as usize]
        dw_denom = dw_denom + e * e
        i = i + 1
    }
    let dw = if dw_denom > 1e-10 { dw_num / dw_denom } else { 2.0 }
    let dw_deviation = abs_f64(dw - 2.0)
    let indep_conf = if dw_deviation < 0.5 { 0.90 }
                     else if dw_deviation < 1.0 { 0.70 }
                     else { 0.50 }
    let independence = beta_new(indep_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - indep_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    // Multicollinearity: VIF check (for simple regression: always ok)
    let multicol = beta_new(100.0, 1.0)

    // Count influential points (Cook's D > 1)
    var influential = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if cooks_d[i as usize] > 1.0 {
            influential = influential + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let diagnostics = ModelDiagnostics {
        vif: vif,
        cooks_distance: cooks_d,
        leverage: leverage,
        dffits: [0.0; 100],  // Placeholder
        normality_resid: norm_resid,
        homoscedasticity: homosked,
        no_autocorrelation: independence,
        no_multicollinearity: multicol,
        influential_points: influential
    }

    let assumptions = RegressionAssumptions {
        linearity: beta_new(50.0, 10.0),  // Placeholder: would check residual patterns
        normality_residuals: norm_resid,
        homoscedasticity: homosked,
        independence: independence,
        no_multicollinearity: multicol
    }

    // Combine confidences
    let conf1 = beta_combine(&norm_resid, &homosked)
    let conf2 = beta_combine(&conf1, &independence)
    let overall_conf = conf2

    // Variance on coefficient estimates (already in model.std_errors)
    let coef_variance = model.std_errors[1] * model.std_errors[1]

    let prov = RegressionProvenance {
        method_code: 0,
        n_obs: n,
        n_predictors: 1,
        timestamp: 0,
        assumptions: assumptions,
        diagnostics: diagnostics
    }

    KnowledgeLinearModel {
        value: model,
        variance: coef_variance,
        confidence: overall_conf,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_simple_regression() -> bool {
    // y = 2 + 3x with small noise
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 10 {
        x[i as usize] = i as f64
        y[i as usize] = 2.0 + 3.0 * (i as f64) + 0.1  // Small noise
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fit_linear_regression_epistemic(x, y, 10)

    // Check β₀ ≈ 2.0, β₁ ≈ 3.0
    let beta0 = result.value.coefficients[0]
    let beta1 = result.value.coefficients[1]

    let beta0_ok = abs_f64(beta0 - 2.0) < 0.5
    let beta1_ok = abs_f64(beta1 - 3.0) < 0.5

    // Check R² is high
    let r2_ok = result.value.r_squared > 0.95

    beta0_ok && beta1_ok && r2_ok
}

// =============================================================================
// Top-level constructor (avoids cross-module static resolution issue)
// =============================================================================

/// Create a new empty LinearRegression builder.
/// Use instead of LinearRegression::new() when calling from other modules.
pub fn linear_regression_new() -> LinearRegression {
    LinearRegression {
        x: [0.0; 100],
        y: [0.0; 100],
        n: 0,
        fitted: false,
        model: LinearModel {
            coefficients: [0.0; 10],
            std_errors: [0.0; 10],
            t_statistics: [0.0; 10],
            p_values: [0.0; 10],
            n_predictors: 0,
            n_obs: 0,
            r_squared: 0.0,
            adj_r_squared: 0.0,
            f_statistic: 0.0,
            residual_se: 0.0,
            residuals: [0.0; 100],
        },
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/regression/logistic.sio ===
// stats::regression::logistic — Epistemic Logistic Regression
//
// Generalized linear model for binary outcomes with:
// - Maximum likelihood estimation via IRLS
// - Odds ratios as Knowledge<f64> with confidence
// - Dose-response modeling (ED50, ED90)
// - ROC/AUC curve analysis
// - Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit
//
// Returns Knowledge<LogisticModel> with full diagnostics
//
// References:
// - Cox (1958): "The regression analysis of binary sequences"
// - Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000): "Applied Logistic Regression"
// - McCullagh & Nelder (1989): "Generalized Linear Models"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers (self-contained, following medical/ pattern)
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn logit_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn logit_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn logit_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64
        k = k + 1
    }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn logit_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k_f = x / ln2
    var k: i32 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = k_f as i32 } else { k = (k_f as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 {
        var i = 0
        while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    } else {
        var i = 0
        while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    }
    result
}

fn logit_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn logit_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

// =============================================================================
// Link Functions
// =============================================================================

// Logistic (sigmoid) function: p = 1 / (1 + exp(-z))
fn sigmoid(z: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if z > 20.0 { return 1.0 - 1.0e-10 }
    if z < -20.0 { return 1.0e-10 }
    1.0 / (1.0 + logit_exp(0.0 - z))
}

// Logit (inverse sigmoid): z = ln(p / (1 - p))
fn logit(p: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let clipped = logit_max(1.0e-10, logit_min(1.0 - 1.0e-10, p))
    logit_ln(clipped / (1.0 - clipped))
}

// =============================================================================
// Core Types
// =============================================================================

struct LogisticModel {
    beta: [f64; 10],          // Coefficients (β₀ = intercept)
    se: [f64; 10],            // Standard errors
    z_scores: [f64; 10],       // Wald z-scores (β/SE)
    p_values: [f64; 10],       // Two-tailed p-values
    odds_ratios: [f64; 10],    // exp(β) for each predictor
    or_ci_lower: [f64; 10],    // 95% CI lower for OR
    or_ci_upper: [f64; 10],    // 95% CI upper for OR
    n_predictors: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_events: i64,             // Number of y=1
    log_likelihood: f64,
    aic: f64,
    bic: f64,
    deviance: f64,
    null_deviance: f64,
    pseudo_r_squared: f64,     // McFadden's R²
    converged: bool,
    iterations: i64
}



// Diagnostics
struct LogisticDiagnostics {
    hosmer_lemeshow_stat: f64,  // Goodness-of-fit
    hosmer_lemeshow_p: f64,
    auc: f64,                    // Area under ROC curve
    concordance: f64,            // C-statistic
    separation_adequate: BetaConfidence,
    sample_events_adequate: BetaConfidence
}

// Provenance
struct LogisticProvenance {
    method_id: i64,  // 1 = IRLS_MLE
    n_obs: i64,
    n_events: i64,
    n_predictors: i64,
    iterations: i64,
    converged: bool,
    diagnostics: LogisticDiagnostics
}

// Knowledge wrapper
struct KnowledgeLogistic {
    value: LogisticModel,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: LogisticProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Dose-Response Types
// =============================================================================

struct DoseResponseResult {
    ed50: f64,        // Dose producing 50% effect
    ed90: f64,        // Dose producing 90% effect
    ed50_ci_lower: f64,
    ed50_ci_upper: f64,
    slope: f64,        // Hill slope at ED50
    max_effect: f64
}

struct KnowledgeDoseResponse {
    value: DoseResponseResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence
}

// =============================================================================
// Simple Linear Regression (used internally)
// =============================================================================

fn mean_arr(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + data[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// IRLS (Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares)
// =============================================================================

// Simple logistic regression: logit(p) = β₀ + β₁x
fn fit_logistic_simple(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],   // Binary: 0 or 1
    n: i64
) -> LogisticModel with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let max_iter = 25
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    // Count events
    var n_events: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        if y[i as usize] > 0.5 { n_events = n_events + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Initialize β₀ = logit(p_bar), β₁ = 0
    let p_bar = (n_events as f64) / (n as f64)
    var beta0 = logit(p_bar)
    var beta1 = 0.0

    // Null log-likelihood (for pseudo-R²)
    var null_ll = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        if yi > 0.5 {
            null_ll = null_ll + logit_ln(p_bar)
        } else {
            null_ll = null_ll + logit_ln(1.0 - p_bar)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // IRLS iterations
    var converged = false
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // E-step: compute predicted probabilities
        var sum_w = 0.0
        var sum_wx = 0.0
        var sum_wxx = 0.0
        var sum_wz = 0.0
        var sum_wxz = 0.0

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let xi = x[i as usize]
            let yi = y[i as usize]

            // Linear predictor
            let eta = beta0 + beta1 * xi

            // Predicted probability
            let pi = sigmoid(eta)

            // Weight: w = p(1-p)
            let w = pi * (1.0 - pi)
            if w < 1.0e-10 { i = i + 1; continue }

            // Working response: z = eta + (y - p) / w_raw
            let z = eta + (yi - pi) / w

            // Accumulate weighted normal equations
            sum_w = sum_w + w
            sum_wx = sum_wx + w * xi
            sum_wxx = sum_wxx + w * xi * xi
            sum_wz = sum_wz + w * z
            sum_wxz = sum_wxz + w * xi * z

            i = i + 1
        }

        // Solve 2x2 weighted normal equations
        let det = sum_w * sum_wxx - sum_wx * sum_wx
        if logit_abs(det) < 1.0e-10 { break }

        let new_beta0 = (sum_wxx * sum_wz - sum_wx * sum_wxz) / det
        let new_beta1 = (sum_w * sum_wxz - sum_wx * sum_wz) / det

        // Check convergence
        let delta0 = logit_abs(new_beta0 - beta0)
        let delta1 = logit_abs(new_beta1 - beta1)

        beta0 = new_beta0
        beta1 = new_beta1

        if delta0 < tol && delta1 < tol {
            converged = true
            break
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Compute final statistics
    var log_lik = 0.0
    var deviance = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let yi = y[i as usize]
        let eta = beta0 + beta1 * xi
        let pi = sigmoid(eta)

        // Log-likelihood: Σ[y·ln(p) + (1-y)·ln(1-p)]
        if yi > 0.5 {
            log_lik = log_lik + logit_ln(logit_max(pi, 1.0e-10))
        } else {
            log_lik = log_lik + logit_ln(logit_max(1.0 - pi, 1.0e-10))
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    deviance = -2.0 * log_lik
    let null_deviance = -2.0 * null_ll

    // AIC = -2LL + 2k, BIC = -2LL + k·ln(n)
    let k = 2.0  // Number of parameters
    let aic = deviance + 2.0 * k
    let bic = deviance + k * logit_ln(n as f64)

    // McFadden's pseudo-R²
    let pseudo_r2 = 1.0 - log_lik / null_ll

    // Standard errors from Fisher Information (last IRLS weights)
    var sum_w = 0.0
    var sum_wx = 0.0
    var sum_wxx = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let xi = x[i as usize]
        let eta = beta0 + beta1 * xi
        let pi = sigmoid(eta)
        let w = pi * (1.0 - pi)
        sum_w = sum_w + w
        sum_wx = sum_wx + w * xi
        sum_wxx = sum_wxx + w * xi * xi
        i = i + 1
    }

    let det = sum_w * sum_wxx - sum_wx * sum_wx
    let se_beta0 = if logit_abs(det) > 1.0e-10 {
        logit_sqrt(sum_wxx / det)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let se_beta1 = if logit_abs(det) > 1.0e-10 {
        logit_sqrt(sum_w / det)
    } else { 0.0 }

    // Wald z-scores
    let z0 = if se_beta0 > 1.0e-10 { beta0 / se_beta0 } else { 0.0 }
    let z1 = if se_beta1 > 1.0e-10 { beta1 / se_beta1 } else { 0.0 }

    // Approximate p-values (normal)
    let p0 = 2.0 * (1.0 - sigmoid(logit_abs(z0)))
    let p1 = 2.0 * (1.0 - sigmoid(logit_abs(z1)))

    // Odds ratios: exp(β)
    let or0 = logit_exp(beta0)
    let or1 = logit_exp(beta1)

    // 95% CI for OR: exp(β ± 1.96·SE)
    let or1_lower = logit_exp(beta1 - 1.96 * se_beta1)
    let or1_upper = logit_exp(beta1 + 1.96 * se_beta1)

    // Construct result
    var betas: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    betas[0] = beta0
    betas[1] = beta1

    var ses: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    ses[0] = se_beta0
    ses[1] = se_beta1

    var zs: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    zs[0] = z0
    zs[1] = z1

    var ps: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    ps[0] = p0
    ps[1] = p1

    var ors: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    ors[0] = or0
    ors[1] = or1

    var or_lo: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    or_lo[1] = or1_lower

    var or_hi: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    or_hi[1] = or1_upper

    LogisticModel {
        beta: betas,
        se: ses,
        z_scores: zs,
        p_values: ps,
        odds_ratios: ors,
        or_ci_lower: or_lo,
        or_ci_upper: or_hi,
        n_predictors: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        n_events: n_events,
        log_likelihood: log_lik,
        aic: aic,
        bic: bic,
        deviance: deviance,
        null_deviance: null_deviance,
        pseudo_r_squared: pseudo_r2,
        converged: converged,
        iterations: iter
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// ROC / AUC
// =============================================================================

fn compute_auc(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    beta0: f64,
    beta1: f64
) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Compute AUC via Mann-Whitney U statistic
    // AUC = P(score(positive) > score(negative))

    // Compute predicted probabilities
    var probs: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        probs[i as usize] = sigmoid(beta0 + beta1 * x[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Count concordant pairs
    var concordant: i64 = 0
    var discordant: i64 = 0
    var tied: i64 = 0

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if y[i as usize] < 0.5 { i = i + 1; continue }  // Only positive cases

        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            if y[j as usize] > 0.5 { j = j + 1; continue }  // Only negative cases

            let pi = probs[i as usize]
            let pj = probs[j as usize]

            if pi > pj { concordant = concordant + 1 }
            else if pi < pj { discordant = discordant + 1 }
            else { tied = tied + 1 }

            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let total = concordant + discordant + tied
    if total == 0 { return 0.5 }

    (concordant as f64 + 0.5 * (tied as f64)) / (total as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic Logistic Regression
// =============================================================================

fn fit_logistic_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeLogistic with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let model = fit_logistic_simple(x, y, n)

    // AUC
    let auc = compute_auc(x, y, n, model.beta[0], model.beta[1])

    // Assumption checks
    // 1. Sufficient events (rule of thumb: 10 events per predictor)
    let events_per_pred = model.n_events / (model.n_predictors + 1)
    let event_conf = if events_per_pred >= 10 { 0.95 }
                     else if events_per_pred >= 5 { 0.75 }
                     else { 0.50 }
    let event_beta = beta_new(
        event_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3,
        (1.0 - event_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3
    )

    // 2. Separation (complete separation → infinite β)
    let sep_conf = if model.converged { 0.90 } else { 0.40 }
    let sep_beta = beta_new(
        sep_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3,
        (1.0 - sep_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3
    )

    // Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test
    // Bins observations into 10 equal-width probability groups [0,0.1), [0.1,0.2), ..., [0.9,1.0]
    // HL = Σ_g [(O1g - E1g)² / E1g + (O0g - E0g)² / E0g]
    // Under H₀ (good fit): HL ~ χ²(8)
    // Reference: Hosmer & Lemeshow (2000), "Applied Logistic Regression", Ch. 5
    var hl_stat = 0.0
    var g: i64 = 0
    while g < 10 {
        let lo = (g as f64) * 0.1
        let hi = if g == 9 { 1.0001 } else { lo + 0.1 }
        var obs1 = 0.0   // observed events in bin
        var exp1 = 0.0   // expected events in bin
        var ng = 0.0     // total observations in bin
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n {
            let p_j = 1.0 / (1.0 + logit_exp(0.0 - model.beta[0] - model.beta[1] * x[j as usize]))
            if p_j >= lo && p_j < hi {
                obs1 = obs1 + y[j as usize]
                exp1 = exp1 + p_j
                ng = ng + 1.0
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        if ng > 0.0 && exp1 > 1.0e-8 && (ng - exp1) > 1.0e-8 {
            let obs0 = ng - obs1
