            let exp0 = ng - exp1
            hl_stat = hl_stat + (obs1 - exp1) * (obs1 - exp1) / exp1
                    + (obs0 - exp0) * (obs0 - exp0) / exp0
        }
        g = g + 1
    }
    // p-value approximation for χ²(8): critical values 15.51 (p=0.05), 20.09 (p=0.01)
    let hl_p = if hl_stat > 20.09 { 0.01 }
               else if hl_stat > 15.51 { 0.05 }
               else if hl_stat > 13.36 { 0.10 }
               else { 0.50 }

    let diag = LogisticDiagnostics {
        hosmer_lemeshow_stat: hl_stat,
        hosmer_lemeshow_p: hl_p,
        auc: auc,
        concordance: auc,  // C-statistic = AUC for binary
        separation_adequate: sep_beta,
        sample_events_adequate: event_beta
    }

    let overall_conf = beta_combine(&event_beta, &sep_beta)

    let prov = LogisticProvenance {
        method_id: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        n_events: model.n_events,
        n_predictors: model.n_predictors,
        iterations: model.iterations,
        converged: model.converged,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeLogistic {
        value: model,
        variance: model.se[1] * model.se[1],  // Variance of slope
        confidence: overall_conf,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Dose-Response Modeling
// =============================================================================

fn fit_dose_response(
    doses: [f64; 100],
    responses: [f64; 100],  // Binary: 0 or 1
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeDoseResponse with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Fit logistic model: logit(P(response=1)) = β₀ + β₁·dose
    let model = fit_logistic_simple(doses, responses, n)

    let beta0 = model.beta[0]
    let beta1 = model.beta[1]

    // ED50: dose where P(response) = 0.5
    // logit(0.5) = 0 = β₀ + β₁·ED50
    // ED50 = -β₀/β₁
    let ed50 = if logit_abs(beta1) > 1.0e-10 {
        0.0 - beta0 / beta1
    } else { 0.0 }

    // ED90: dose where P(response) = 0.9
    // logit(0.9) = 2.197 = β₀ + β₁·ED90
    let logit_90 = logit_ln(0.9 / 0.1)
    let ed90 = if logit_abs(beta1) > 1.0e-10 {
        (logit_90 - beta0) / beta1
    } else { 0.0 }

    // CI for ED50 using delta method
    // Var(ED50) ≈ (1/β₁²)[Var(β₀) + ED50²·Var(β₁) + 2·ED50·Cov(β₀,β₁)]
    // Simplified (ignoring covariance):
    let se_beta0 = model.se[0]
    let se_beta1 = model.se[1]
    let var_ed50 = if logit_abs(beta1) > 1.0e-10 {
        (1.0 / (beta1 * beta1)) * (se_beta0 * se_beta0 + ed50 * ed50 * se_beta1 * se_beta1)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let se_ed50 = logit_sqrt(var_ed50)

    let ed50_lower = ed50 - 1.96 * se_ed50
    let ed50_upper = ed50 + 1.96 * se_ed50

    // Hill slope at ED50
    let slope = beta1 * 0.25  // p(1-p) = 0.25 at ED50

    let result = DoseResponseResult {
        ed50: ed50,
        ed90: ed90,
        ed50_ci_lower: ed50_lower,
        ed50_ci_upper: ed50_upper,
        slope: slope,
        max_effect: 1.0
    }

    // Confidence from model fit
    let auc = compute_auc(doses, responses, n, beta0, beta1)
    let conf_level = if auc > 0.80 { 0.90 }
                     else if auc > 0.70 { 0.70 }
                     else { 0.50 }

    KnowledgeDoseResponse {
        value: result,
        variance: var_ed50,
        confidence: beta_new(
            conf_level * (n as f64) * 0.3,
            (1.0 - conf_level) * (n as f64) * 0.3
        )
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_logistic_regression() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Dose-response data: higher dose → more response
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Low doses: mostly 0
    x[0] = 1.0;  y[0] = 0.0
    x[1] = 2.0;  y[1] = 0.0
    x[2] = 3.0;  y[2] = 0.0
    x[3] = 4.0;  y[3] = 0.0
    // Medium doses: mixed
    x[4] = 5.0;  y[4] = 1.0
    x[5] = 6.0;  y[5] = 0.0
    x[6] = 7.0;  y[6] = 1.0
    // High doses: mostly 1
    x[7] = 8.0;  y[7] = 1.0
    x[8] = 9.0;  y[8] = 1.0
    x[9] = 10.0; y[9] = 1.0

    let result = fit_logistic_epistemic(x, y, 10)

    // β₁ should be positive (higher dose → more response)
    let slope_positive = result.value.beta[1] > 0.0

    // OR > 1 (each unit increase in dose increases odds)
    let or_positive = result.value.odds_ratios[1] > 1.0

    // Model should converge
    let did_converge = result.value.converged

    slope_positive && or_positive && did_converge
}

fn test_dose_response() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var doses: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var responses: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    doses[0] = 1.0;  responses[0] = 0.0
    doses[1] = 2.0;  responses[1] = 0.0
    doses[2] = 3.0;  responses[2] = 0.0
    doses[3] = 4.0;  responses[3] = 0.0
    doses[4] = 5.0;  responses[4] = 1.0
    doses[5] = 6.0;  responses[5] = 0.0
    doses[6] = 7.0;  responses[6] = 1.0
    doses[7] = 8.0;  responses[7] = 1.0
    doses[8] = 9.0;  responses[8] = 1.0
    doses[9] = 10.0; responses[9] = 1.0

    let dr = fit_dose_response(doses, responses, 10)

    // ED50 should be around 5-6 (transition zone)
    let ed50_reasonable = dr.value.ed50 > 3.0 && dr.value.ed50 < 8.0

    // ED90 > ED50
    let ed90_greater = dr.value.ed90 > dr.value.ed50

    ed50_reasonable && ed90_greater
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/regression/robust.sio ===
// stats::regression::robust — Robust Regression with M-Estimators
//
// Outlier-resistant regression using:
// - Huber M-estimator (ψ = min(|r|, k))
// - Tukey bisquare M-estimator (fully redescending)
// - Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS)
// - Breakdown point analysis
//
// Returns Knowledge<RobustModel> with confidence and diagnostics
//
// References:
// - Huber (1964): "Robust estimation of a location parameter"
// - Tukey (1977): "Exploratory Data Analysis" (bisquare)
// - Maronna et al. (2019): "Robust Statistics: Theory and Methods"
// - Rousseeuw & Leroy (1987): "Robust Regression and Outlier Detection"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn rob_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn rob_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn rob_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn rob_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn rob_sign(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 { 1.0 }
    else if x < 0.0 { -1.0 }
    else { 0.0 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Types
// =============================================================================

struct RobustModel {
    coefficients: [f64; 10],
    std_errors: [f64; 10],
    n_predictors: i64,
    n_obs: i64,
    residual_scale: f64,       // Robust scale (MAD-based)
    weights: [f64; 100],       // IRLS weights (low for outliers)
    n_outliers: i64,           // Observations with weight < 0.01
    n_iterations: i64,
    converged: bool,
    breakdown_point: f64       // Fraction of contamination tolerable
}



struct RobustDiagnostics {
    outlier_fraction: f64,
    scale_estimate: f64,    // MAD
    efficiency: f64,         // Asymptotic efficiency relative to OLS
    convergence_conf: BetaConfidence,
    outlier_impact_conf: BetaConfidence
}

// Method IDs: 1 = Huber, 2 = TukeyBisquare
struct RobustProvenance {
    method_id: i64,
    tuning_constant: f64,
    n_obs: i64,
    n_outliers: i64,
    n_iterations: i64,
    diagnostics: RobustDiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgeRobust {
    value: RobustModel,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: RobustProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Robust Scale Estimation: MAD (Median Absolute Deviation)
// =============================================================================

fn median(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Copy and sort
    var sorted: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sorted[i as usize] = data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Bubble sort (small n)
    i = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n - i - 1 {
            if sorted[j as usize] > sorted[(j + 1) as usize] {
                let temp = sorted[j as usize]
                sorted[j as usize] = sorted[(j + 1) as usize]
                sorted[(j + 1) as usize] = temp
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if n % 2 == 1 {
        sorted[(n / 2) as usize]
    } else {
        (sorted[(n / 2 - 1) as usize] + sorted[(n / 2) as usize]) / 2.0
    }
}

fn mad(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // MAD = median(|xᵢ - median(x)|) * 1.4826
    // Factor 1.4826 makes MAD consistent estimator for σ at normal

    let med = median(data, n)

    var abs_dev: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        abs_dev[i as usize] = rob_abs(data[i as usize] - med)
        i = i + 1
    }

    let mad_raw = median(abs_dev, n)
    mad_raw * 1.4826
}

// =============================================================================
// Influence Functions (ψ)
// =============================================================================

// Huber ψ: ψ(r) = max(-k, min(k, r))
fn huber_psi(r: f64, k: f64) -> f64 {
    rob_max(-k, rob_min(k, r))
}

// Huber weight: w(r) = min(1, k/|r|)
fn huber_weight(r: f64, k: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let abs_r = rob_abs(r)
    if abs_r < 1.0e-10 { return 1.0 }
    rob_min(1.0, k / abs_r)
}

// Tukey bisquare ψ: ψ(r) = r(1 - (r/c)²)² if |r| ≤ c, else 0
fn tukey_psi(r: f64, c: f64) -> f64 {
    if rob_abs(r) > c { return 0.0 }
    let u = r / c
    r * (1.0 - u * u) * (1.0 - u * u)
}

// Tukey bisquare weight: w(r) = (1 - (r/c)²)² if |r| ≤ c, else 0
fn tukey_weight(r: f64, c: f64) -> f64 {
    if rob_abs(r) > c { return 0.0 }
    let u = r / c
    (1.0 - u * u) * (1.0 - u * u)
}

// =============================================================================
// IRLS for Robust Regression
// =============================================================================

fn mean_arr(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + data[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

fn fit_robust_simple(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    method: i64,       // 1 = huber, 2 = tukey
    tuning: f64        // k=1.345 for Huber, c=4.685 for Tukey
) -> RobustModel with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let max_iter = 50
    let tol = 1.0e-6

    // Initial OLS fit
    let x_mean = mean_arr(x, n)
    let y_mean = mean_arr(y, n)

    var cov = 0.0
    var var_x = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let dx = x[i as usize] - x_mean
        let dy = y[i as usize] - y_mean
        cov = cov + dx * dy
        var_x = var_x + dx * dx
        i = i + 1
    }

    var beta1 = if var_x > 1.0e-10 { cov / var_x } else { 0.0 }
    var beta0 = y_mean - beta1 * x_mean

    var weights: [f64; 100] = [1.0; 100]
    var residuals: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // IRLS iterations
    var converged = false
    var iter: i64 = 0

    while iter < max_iter {
        // Compute residuals
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            residuals[i as usize] = y[i as usize] - beta0 - beta1 * x[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Robust scale estimate (MAD of residuals)
        let scale = rob_max(mad(residuals, n), 1.0e-10)

        // Compute weights based on standardized residuals
        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let r_std = residuals[i as usize] / scale
            if method == 1 {
                weights[i as usize] = huber_weight(r_std, tuning)
            } else {
                weights[i as usize] = tukey_weight(r_std, tuning)
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        // Weighted least squares
        var sum_w = 0.0
        var sum_wx = 0.0
        var sum_wy = 0.0
        var sum_wxx = 0.0
        var sum_wxy = 0.0

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            let w = weights[i as usize]
            let xi = x[i as usize]
            let yi = y[i as usize]
            sum_w = sum_w + w
            sum_wx = sum_wx + w * xi
            sum_wy = sum_wy + w * yi
            sum_wxx = sum_wxx + w * xi * xi
            sum_wxy = sum_wxy + w * xi * yi
            i = i + 1
        }

        let det = sum_w * sum_wxx - sum_wx * sum_wx
        if rob_abs(det) < 1.0e-10 { break }

        let new_beta0 = (sum_wxx * sum_wy - sum_wx * sum_wxy) / det
        let new_beta1 = (sum_w * sum_wxy - sum_wx * sum_wy) / det

        // Convergence check
        let delta0 = rob_abs(new_beta0 - beta0)
        let delta1 = rob_abs(new_beta1 - beta1)

        beta0 = new_beta0
        beta1 = new_beta1

        if delta0 < tol && delta1 < tol {
            converged = true
            break
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Final residuals and scale
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        residuals[i as usize] = y[i as usize] - beta0 - beta1 * x[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let final_scale = mad(residuals, n)

    // Count outliers (weight < 0.01)
    var n_outliers: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if weights[i as usize] < 0.01 { n_outliers = n_outliers + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // SE from weighted regression
    var sum_w = 0.0
    var sum_wxx = 0.0
    var sum_wx = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let w = weights[i as usize]
        sum_w = sum_w + w
        sum_wx = sum_wx + w * x[i as usize]
        sum_wxx = sum_wxx + w * x[i as usize] * x[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let det = sum_w * sum_wxx - sum_wx * sum_wx
    let se_beta0 = if rob_abs(det) > 1.0e-10 {
        rob_sqrt(final_scale * final_scale * sum_wxx / det)
    } else { 0.0 }
    let se_beta1 = if rob_abs(det) > 1.0e-10 {
        rob_sqrt(final_scale * final_scale * sum_w / det)
    } else { 0.0 }

    // Breakdown point
    let breakdown = if method == 2 { 0.50 } else { 0.0 }  // Huber: 0, Tukey: up to 50%

    var coefficients: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    coefficients[0] = beta0
    coefficients[1] = beta1

    var std_errors: [f64; 10] = [0.0; 10]
    std_errors[0] = se_beta0
    std_errors[1] = se_beta1

    RobustModel {
        coefficients: coefficients,
        std_errors: std_errors,
        n_predictors: 1,
        n_obs: n,
        residual_scale: final_scale,
        weights: weights,
        n_outliers: n_outliers,
        n_iterations: iter,
        converged: converged,
        breakdown_point: breakdown
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic Robust Regression
// =============================================================================

fn fit_huber_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeRobust with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Huber with k = 1.345 (95% efficiency at normal)
    fit_robust_epistemic(x, y, n, 1, 1.345)
}

fn fit_tukey_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64
) -> KnowledgeRobust with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Tukey bisquare with c = 4.685 (95% efficiency at normal)
    fit_robust_epistemic(x, y, n, 2, 4.685)
}

fn fit_robust_epistemic(
    x: [f64; 100],
    y: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    method: i64,
    tuning: f64
) -> KnowledgeRobust with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let model = fit_robust_simple(x, y, n, method, tuning)

    // Compute diagnostics
    let outlier_frac = (model.n_outliers as f64) / (n as f64)
    let efficiency = if method == 1 { 0.95 } else { 0.95 }

    // Confidence: higher if few outliers, converged, enough data
    let conv_conf = if model.converged { 0.90 } else { 0.50 }
    let conv_beta = beta_new(conv_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - conv_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let outlier_conf = if outlier_frac < 0.10 { 0.90 }
                       else if outlier_frac < 0.20 { 0.75 }
                       else if outlier_frac < 0.30 { 0.60 }
                       else { 0.40 }
    let outlier_beta = beta_new(outlier_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - outlier_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let overall_conf = beta_combine(&conv_beta, &outlier_beta)

    let diag = RobustDiagnostics {
        outlier_fraction: outlier_frac,
        scale_estimate: model.residual_scale,
        efficiency: efficiency,
        convergence_conf: conv_beta,
        outlier_impact_conf: outlier_beta
    }

    let prov = RobustProvenance {
        method_id: method,
        tuning_constant: tuning,
        n_obs: n,
        n_outliers: model.n_outliers,
        n_iterations: model.n_iterations,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeRobust {
        value: model,
        variance: model.std_errors[1] * model.std_errors[1],
        confidence: overall_conf,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_huber_with_outliers() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // y = 2 + 3x with outliers
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    // Clean data: y = 2 + 3x
    x[0] = 0.0;  y[0] = 2.0
    x[1] = 1.0;  y[1] = 5.0
    x[2] = 2.0;  y[2] = 8.0
    x[3] = 3.0;  y[3] = 11.0
    x[4] = 4.0;  y[4] = 14.0
    x[5] = 5.0;  y[5] = 17.0
    x[6] = 6.0;  y[6] = 20.0
    x[7] = 7.0;  y[7] = 23.0

    // Outliers
    x[8] = 3.0;  y[8] = 50.0   // Outlier!
    x[9] = 5.0;  y[9] = -10.0  // Outlier!

    let result = fit_huber_epistemic(x, y, 10)

    // Slope should be close to 3.0 despite outliers
    let slope = result.value.coefficients[1]
    let slope_ok = rob_abs(slope - 3.0) < 1.5  // Within 1.5 of true slope

    // Should detect outliers
    let outliers_detected = result.value.n_outliers > 0

    slope_ok && outliers_detected
}

fn test_tukey_with_outliers() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]

    x[0] = 0.0;  y[0] = 2.0
    x[1] = 1.0;  y[1] = 5.0
    x[2] = 2.0;  y[2] = 8.0
    x[3] = 3.0;  y[3] = 11.0
    x[4] = 4.0;  y[4] = 14.0
    x[5] = 5.0;  y[5] = 17.0
    x[6] = 6.0;  y[6] = 20.0
    x[7] = 7.0;  y[7] = 23.0
    x[8] = 3.0;  y[8] = 50.0
    x[9] = 5.0;  y[9] = -10.0

    let result = fit_tukey_epistemic(x, y, 10)

    // Tukey bisquare should be even more resistant
    let slope = result.value.coefficients[1]
    let slope_ok = rob_abs(slope - 3.0) < 1.5

    // Tukey gives zero weight to extreme outliers
    let outliers_zero_weight = result.value.n_outliers >= 2

    slope_ok && outliers_zero_weight
}

fn test_mad() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    data[0] = 1.0
    data[1] = 2.0
    data[2] = 3.0
    data[3] = 4.0
    data[4] = 5.0

    let m = mad(data, 5)

    // MAD of {1,2,3,4,5}: deviations from median (3) = {2,1,0,1,2}
    // Median of deviations = 1
    // MAD = 1.4826 * 1 ≈ 1.4826
    rob_abs(m - 1.4826) < 0.01
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/resampling.sio ===
// stats::resampling — Bootstrap and permutation resampling
//
// Fixed-array bootstrap for confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.
// Uses a simple LCG PRNG (no heap allocation).
//
// References:
// - Efron (1979): "Bootstrap methods: another look at the jackknife"
// - Efron & Tibshirani (1993): "An Introduction to the Bootstrap"

// =============================================================================
// LCG Pseudo-Random Number Generator
// =============================================================================

struct LCGState {
    seed: i64
}

fn lcg_new(seed: i64) -> LCGState {
    LCGState { seed: seed }
}

fn lcg_next(state: &!LCGState) -> i64 with Mut {
    // LCG: x_{n+1} = (a*x_n + c) mod m
    // Using Numerical Recipes constants
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    // Mask to 31 bits (positive)
    state.seed = (a * state.seed + c) & 2147483647
    state.seed
}

// Random index in [0, n)
fn lcg_rand_index(state: &!LCGState, n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = lcg_next(state)
    // Use modulo (biased but sufficient for bootstrap)
    let idx = r - (r / n) * n
    if idx < 0 { idx + n } else { idx }
}

// =============================================================================
// Bootstrap Mean
// =============================================================================

fn resample_mean(data: [f64; 100], n: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

struct BootstrapResult {
    estimate: f64,
    se: f64,
    ci_lower: f64,
    ci_upper: f64,
    n_resamples: i64
}

fn bootstrap_mean(
    data: [f64; 100],
    n: i64,
    n_boot: i64,
    seed: i64
) -> BootstrapResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Cap bootstrap resamples
    let max_boot: i64 = 500
    let actual_boot = if n_boot > max_boot { max_boot } else { n_boot }

    var rng = lcg_new(seed)
    var boot_means: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]

    // Generate bootstrap samples and compute means
    var b: i64 = 0
    while b < actual_boot {
        var sum = 0.0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            let idx = lcg_rand_index(&rng, n)
            sum = sum + data[idx as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        boot_means[b as usize] = sum / (n as f64)
        b = b + 1
    }

    // Compute mean of bootstrap means
    let point_est = resample_mean(data, n)

    // Compute SE (standard deviation of bootstrap means)
    var ss = 0.0
    b = 0
    while b < actual_boot {
        let d = boot_means[b as usize] - point_est
        ss = ss + d * d
        b = b + 1
    }
    let se = boot_se_sqrt(ss / ((actual_boot - 1) as f64))

    // Sort bootstrap means for percentile CI
    sort_f64(boot_means, actual_boot)

    // 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles
    let lo_idx = (actual_boot as f64 * 0.025) as i64
    let hi_idx = (actual_boot as f64 * 0.975) as i64
    let ci_lo = boot_means[lo_idx as usize]
    let ci_hi = boot_means[hi_idx as usize]

    BootstrapResult {
        estimate: point_est,
        se: se,
        ci_lower: ci_lo,
        ci_upper: ci_hi,
        n_resamples: actual_boot
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Helpers
// =============================================================================

fn boot_se_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn sort_f64(data: [f64; 500], n: i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Bubble sort (sufficient for n <= 500)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n - 1 {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < n - i - 1 {
            if data[j as usize] > data[(j + 1) as usize] {
                let tmp = data[j as usize]
                data[j as usize] = data[(j + 1) as usize]
                data[(j + 1) as usize] = tmp
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn boot_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_bootstrap_mean() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100]
    data[0] = 10.0
    data[1] = 12.0
    data[2] = 11.0
    data[3] = 13.0
    data[4] = 11.0

    let result = bootstrap_mean(data, 5, 200, 42)

    // Mean should be close to 11.4
    let mean_ok = boot_abs(result.estimate - 11.4) < 0.001
    // SE should be positive
    let se_ok = result.se > 0.0
    // CI should bracket the mean
    let ci_ok = result.ci_lower <= result.estimate && result.estimate <= result.ci_upper

    mean_ok && se_ok && ci_ok
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/shared.sio ===
// stats::shared — Canonical types shared across stats submodules
//
// Centralizes BetaConfidence and its core operations to avoid
// duplicate definitions across the stats module cluster.

pub struct BetaConfidence {
    pub alpha: f64,
    pub beta: f64
}

pub fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
pub fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
pub fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

pub fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
pub fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
pub fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

let MAX_OBS: i64 = 100


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/timeseries/arima.sio ===
// stats::timeseries::arima — Epistemic ARIMA Models
//
// Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with:
// - AR(p), MA(q), ARMA(p,q), ARIMA(p,d,q)
// - Auto-ARIMA model selection (AIC/BIC)
// - Forecasting with uncertainty bounds
// - Diagnostic checks (Ljung-Box, ACF/PACF)
// - Knowledge<ARIMAResult> with epistemic metadata
//
// References:
// - Box & Jenkins (1970): "Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control"
// - Akaike (1974): "A new look at the statistical model identification" (AIC)
// - Ljung & Box (1978): "On a measure of lack of fit in time series models"
// - Hyndman & Khandakar (2008): "Automatic time series forecasting" (auto.arima)

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn ar_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn ar_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn ar_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn ar_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

// =============================================================================
// Types
// =============================================================================

let MAX_T: i64 = 500
let MAX_ORDER: i64 = 5

struct ARIMAResult {
    ar_coeffs: [f64; 5],   // φ₁, φ₂, ..., φ_p
    ma_coeffs: [f64; 5],   // θ₁, θ₂, ..., θ_q
    intercept: f64,
    p: i64,                  // AR order
    d: i64,                  // Differencing order
    q: i64,                  // MA order
    sigma_squared: f64,      // Residual variance
    aic: f64,
    bic: f64,
    log_likelihood: f64,
    residuals: [f64; 500],
    n_obs: i64
}

struct ForecastResult {
    point: [f64; 50],       // Point forecasts
    lower_95: [f64; 50],    // 95% CI lower
    upper_95: [f64; 50],    // 95% CI upper
    n_ahead: i64
}



struct ARIMADiagnostics {
    ljung_box_stat: f64,
    ljung_box_p: f64,
    residual_normality: BetaConfidence,
    stationarity: BetaConfidence
}

struct ARIMAProvenance {
    method: String,
    order: String,  // "(p,d,q)"
    n_obs: i64,
    diagnostics: ARIMADiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgeARIMA {
    value: ARIMAResult,
    variance: f64,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: ARIMAProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// Differencing
// =============================================================================

fn difference(
    series: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    d: i64
) -> ([f64; 500], i64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result: [f64; 500] = series
    var current_n = n

    var diff_order: i64 = 0
    while diff_order < d {
        var new_series: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
        var i: i64 = 1
        while i < current_n {
            new_series[(i - 1) as usize] = result[i as usize] - result[(i - 1) as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        result = new_series
        current_n = current_n - 1
        diff_order = diff_order + 1
    }

    (result, current_n)
}

// =============================================================================
// Autocorrelation Function
// =============================================================================

fn acf(series: [f64; 500], n: i64, max_lag: i64) -> [f64; 20] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result: [f64; 20] = [0.0; 20]

    // Mean
    var mean = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { mean = mean + series[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    mean = mean / (n as f64)

    // Variance (lag 0)
    var c0 = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let d = series[i as usize] - mean
        c0 = c0 + d * d
        i = i + 1
    }
    c0 = c0 / (n as f64)

    if c0 < 1.0e-10 { return result }

    var lag: i64 = 1
    while lag <= max_lag && lag < 20 {
        var ck = 0.0
        i = lag
        while i < n {
            ck = ck + (series[i as usize] - mean) * (series[(i - lag) as usize] - mean)
            i = i + 1
        }
        ck = ck / (n as f64)
        result[lag as usize] = ck / c0
        lag = lag + 1
    }

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Levinson-Durbin Recursion
// =============================================================================
//
// Solves the Yule-Walker system for AR(p) coefficients given the normalised
// autocorrelation sequence r[0..p] (r[0] == 1.0 after normalisation).
//
// Reference: Durbin (1960), Levinson (1947).
//
// Arguments:
//   acf_vals  — autocorrelation array of length >= p+1 (index 0 == lag-0 ACF,
//               which must be 1.0 for the normalised form expected here)
//   order     — AR order p (1 <= p <= 5)
//
// Returns: AR coefficient array of length 5 (coefficients at indices 0..p-1).

fn levinson_durbin(acf_vals: [f64; 20], order: i64) -> [f64; 5] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var phi: [f64; 5] = [0.0; 5]

    if order <= 0 { return phi }

    // phi_prev holds the coefficients from the previous order.
    // We use two explicit arrays and swap conceptually.
    var phi_prev: [f64; 5] = [0.0; 5]

    // Initialise for k = 1
    // Reflection coefficient: phi_11 = r(1) / r(0) = r(1)  (r(0) == 1.0)
    phi_prev[0] = acf_vals[1]
    // Prediction-error variance (unnormalised): P_1 = 1 - phi_11^2
    var P = 1.0 - phi_prev[0] * phi_prev[0]

    // Copy into phi (will be returned if order == 1)
    var idx: i64 = 0
    while idx < 5 { phi[idx as usize] = phi_prev[idx as usize]; idx = idx + 1 }

    var k: i64 = 2
    while k <= order {
        // --- Compute reflection coefficient for order k ---
        // lambda = r(k) - sum_{j=1}^{k-1} phi_{k-1,j} * r(k-j)
        var lambda = acf_vals[k as usize]
        var j: i64 = 1
        while j <= k - 1 {
            lambda = lambda - phi_prev[(j - 1) as usize] * acf_vals[(k - j) as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }

        // Guard against near-zero prediction-error variance
        var phi_kk = 0.0
        if ar_abs(P) > 1.0e-12 { phi_kk = lambda / P }

        // --- Update AR coefficients ---
        // phi_{k,j} = phi_{k-1,j} - phi_kk * phi_{k-1,k-j}   for j = 1..k-1
        // phi_{k,k} = phi_kk
        var phi_new: [f64; 5] = [0.0; 5]
        j = 1
        while j <= k - 1 {
            phi_new[(j - 1) as usize] =
                phi_prev[(j - 1) as usize]
                - phi_kk * phi_prev[(k - j - 1) as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        phi_new[(k - 1) as usize] = phi_kk

        // --- Update prediction-error variance ---
        P = P * (1.0 - phi_kk * phi_kk)

        // Copy phi_new → phi_prev for next iteration and into phi for return
        idx = 0
        while idx < 5 {
            phi_prev[idx as usize] = phi_new[idx as usize]
            phi[idx as usize]      = phi_new[idx as usize]
            idx = idx + 1
        }

        k = k + 1
    }

    phi
}

// =============================================================================
// MA(q) Estimation via OLS on Innovations
// =============================================================================
//
// After fitting the AR part the residuals approximate the innovation process.
// For MA(q) we regress each residual e[t] on the q most-recent lagged residuals
// e[t-1], ..., e[t-q] by solving the normal equations directly.
//
// For q = 1 this is just the sample correlation between e[t] and e[t-1].
// For q = 2 we solve a 2x2 system.  For q > 2 we iteratively refine using a
// single Gauss-Seidel sweep (sufficient for initial estimates).
//
// Arguments:
//   residuals — residual array (length n, stored in a [f64; 500] buffer)
//   n         — number of valid residuals
//   q         — MA order (1 <= q <= 5)
//
// Returns: MA coefficient array of length 5 (indices 0..q-1).

fn estimate_ma_coefficients(residuals: [f64; 500], n: i64, q: i64) -> [f64; 5] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var theta: [f64; 5] = [0.0; 5]

    if q <= 0 || n <= q { return theta }

    // Build the sample autocovariance of the residuals up to lag q.
    // c[k] = (1/n) * sum_{t=k}^{n-1} e[t] * e[t-k]
    var c: [f64; 6] = [0.0; 6]  // index 0..q, q <= 5
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k <= q && k < 6 {
        var sum = 0.0
        var t: i64 = k
        while t < n {
            sum = sum + residuals[t as usize] * residuals[(t - k) as usize]
            t = t + 1
        }
        c[k as usize] = sum / (n as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Guard: if residual variance is negligible MA coefficients stay zero
    if ar_abs(c[0]) < 1.0e-12 { return theta }

    if q == 1 {
        // theta_1 = c(1) / c(0)   (OLS slope, also moment estimator)
        theta[0] = c[1] / c[0]
    } else if q == 2 {
        // Solve 2x2 Yule-Walker–like system for the MA side:
        //   [c(0)  c(1)] [theta_1]   [c(1)]
        //   [c(1)  c(0)] [theta_2] = [c(2)]
        let det = c[0] * c[0] - c[1] * c[1]
        if ar_abs(det) > 1.0e-12 {
            theta[0] = (c[0] * c[1] - c[1] * c[2]) / det
            theta[1] = (c[0] * c[2] - c[1] * c[1]) / det
        }
    } else {
        // For q >= 3: use Levinson-Durbin on the residual ACF.
        // First build the normalised ACF array (length 20) for the residuals.
        var resid_acf: [f64; 20] = [0.0; 20]
        resid_acf[0] = 1.0
        var lag: i64 = 1
        while lag <= q && lag < 20 {
            resid_acf[lag as usize] = c[lag as usize] / c[0]
            lag = lag + 1
        }
        // Levinson-Durbin gives AR coefficients for the ACF structure;
        // the resulting coefficients serve as moment-based MA estimates.
        theta = levinson_durbin(resid_acf, q)
    }

    theta
}

// =============================================================================
// AR(p) Estimation via Yule-Walker
// =============================================================================

fn fit_ar(
    series: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    p: i64
) -> ARIMAResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Yule-Walker equations: Rφ = r
    // For p=1: φ₁ = r(1) (first autocorrelation)
    // For p=2: solve 2x2 system

    let autocorr = acf(series, n, p + 1)

    // Mean
    var mean = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n { mean = mean + series[i as usize]; i = i + 1 }
    mean = mean / (n as f64)

    // Levinson-Durbin recursion solves the full Yule-Walker system for any p.
    // For p == 0 it returns a zero array (pure MA / white-noise case).
    var ar_coeffs: [f64; 5] = levinson_durbin(autocorr, p)

    // Compute residuals
    var residuals: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var rss = 0.0
    i = p
    while i < n {
        var pred = mean * (1.0 - ar_coeffs[0])  // Simplified
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < p {
            pred = pred + ar_coeffs[j as usize] * series[(i - j - 1) as usize]
            j = j + 1
        }
        residuals[i as usize] = series[i as usize] - pred
        rss = rss + residuals[i as usize] * residuals[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let effective_n = n - p
    let sigma2 = rss / (effective_n as f64)
    let nf = effective_n as f64

    // Log-likelihood
    let ll = -0.5 * nf * (1.0 + ar_ln(2.0 * 3.14159265) + ar_ln(sigma2))

    // AIC, BIC
    let k = (p + 1) as f64  // p AR coeffs + variance
    let aic = -2.0 * ll + 2.0 * k
    let bic = -2.0 * ll + k * ar_ln(nf)

    ARIMAResult {
        ar_coeffs: ar_coeffs,
        ma_coeffs: [0.0; 5],
        intercept: mean,
        p: p,
        d: 0,
        q: 0,
        sigma_squared: sigma2,
        aic: aic,
        bic: bic,
        log_likelihood: ll,
        residuals: residuals,
        n_obs: n
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// ARIMA(p,d,q) Fitting
// =============================================================================

fn fit_arima(
    series: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    d: i64,
    q: i64
) -> ARIMAResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Step 1: Difference d times
    let (diff_series, diff_n) = difference(series, n, d)

    // Step 2: Fit AR(p) on differenced series via Levinson-Durbin / Yule-Walker
    var result = fit_ar(diff_series, diff_n, p)
    result.d = d
    result.q = q

    // Step 3: If q > 0, estimate MA(q) coefficients from the AR residuals.
    // The AR residuals stored in result.residuals approximate the innovations;
    // estimate_ma_coefficients regresses e[t] on e[t-1]..e[t-q] via OLS /
    // moment matching to produce initial MA parameter estimates.
    if q > 0 {
        let ma_est = estimate_ma_coefficients(result.residuals, result.n_obs, q)
        result.ma_coeffs = ma_est

        // Refine residuals with MA correction:
        //   e_arma[t] = e_ar[t] - sum_{j=1}^{q} theta_j * e_ar[t-j]
        var refined: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
        var rss2 = 0.0
        var i: i64 = q
        while i < result.n_obs {
            var corr = result.residuals[i as usize]
            var j: i64 = 0
            while j < q {
                corr = corr - ma_est[j as usize] * result.residuals[(i - j - 1) as usize]
                j = j + 1
            }
            refined[i as usize] = corr
            rss2 = rss2 + corr * corr
            i = i + 1
        }

        let eff_n2 = (result.n_obs - p - q) as f64
        let sigma2_arma = if eff_n2 > 0.0 { rss2 / eff_n2 } else { result.sigma_squared }
        result.residuals    = refined
        result.sigma_squared = sigma2_arma

        // Update log-likelihood, AIC, BIC with new sigma and parameter count
        let ll2 = -0.5 * eff_n2 * (1.0 + ar_ln(2.0 * 3.14159265) + ar_ln(sigma2_arma))
        let k2  = (p + q + 1) as f64
        result.log_likelihood = ll2
        result.aic            = -2.0 * ll2 + 2.0 * k2
        result.bic            = -2.0 * ll2 + k2 * ar_ln(eff_n2)
    }

    result
}

// =============================================================================
// Auto-ARIMA (Model Selection)
// =============================================================================

fn auto_arima(
    series: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    max_p: i64,
    max_d: i64,
    max_q: i64
) -> ARIMAResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var best_aic = 1.0e30
    var best_p: i64 = 0
    var best_d: i64 = 0
    var best_q: i64 = 0

    // Grid search over (p, d, q)
    var d: i64 = 0
    while d <= max_d {
        var p: i64 = 0
        while p <= max_p {
            // Fit ARIMA(p, d, 0) — AR models only for simplicity
            let model = fit_arima(series, n, p, d, 0)
            if model.aic < best_aic {
                best_aic = model.aic
                best_p = p
                best_d = d
                best_q = 0
            }
            p = p + 1
        }
        d = d + 1
    }

    fit_arima(series, n, best_p, best_d, best_q)
}

// =============================================================================
// Forecasting
// =============================================================================

fn forecast_arima(
    model: &ARIMAResult,
    series: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    n_ahead: i64
) -> ForecastResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var point: [f64; 50] = [0.0; 50]
    var lower: [f64; 50] = [0.0; 50]
    var upper: [f64; 50] = [0.0; 50]

    // Extend series with forecasts
    var extended: [f64; 550] = [0.0; 550]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        extended[i as usize] = series[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }

    var h: i64 = 0
    while h < n_ahead && h < 50 {
        var pred = model.intercept * (1.0 - model.ar_coeffs[0])

        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < model.p {
            let idx = n + h - j - 1
            if idx >= 0 {
                pred = pred + model.ar_coeffs[j as usize] * extended[idx as usize]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }

        point[h as usize] = pred
        extended[(n + h) as usize] = pred

        // Prediction interval widens with horizon
        let se = ar_sqrt(model.sigma_squared * ((h + 1) as f64))
        lower[h as usize] = pred - 1.96 * se
        upper[h as usize] = pred + 1.96 * se

        h = h + 1
    }

    ForecastResult {
        point: point,
        lower_95: lower,
        upper_95: upper,
        n_ahead: n_ahead
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Ljung-Box Test
// =============================================================================

fn ljung_box(residuals: [f64; 500], n: i64, max_lag: i64) -> (f64, f64) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let autocorr = acf(residuals, n, max_lag)

    // Q = n(n+2) Σ ρ²(k) / (n-k)
    var q = 0.0
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k <= max_lag && k < 20 {
        let rk = autocorr[k as usize]
        q = q + (rk * rk) / ((n - k) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    q = q * (n as f64) * ((n + 2) as f64)

    // Approximate p-value (chi-squared with max_lag df)
    let p = if q > 20.0 { 0.001 }
            else if q > 12.0 { 0.01 }
            else if q > 7.0 { 0.05 }
            else { 0.50 }

    (q, p)
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC ARIMA
// =============================================================================

fn fit_arima_epistemic(
    series: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    p: i64,
    d: i64,
    q: i64
) -> KnowledgeARIMA with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let model = fit_arima(series, n, p, d, q)

    // Ljung-Box test on residuals
    let (lb_stat, lb_p) = ljung_box(model.residuals, n, 10)

    // Residual normality (simplified)
    let resid_conf = if lb_p > 0.10 { 0.90 }
                     else if lb_p > 0.05 { 0.70 }
                     else { 0.50 }
    let norm_beta = beta_new(resid_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - resid_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    // Stationarity check (AR coefficients < 1)
    var stationary = true
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < p {
        if ar_abs(model.ar_coeffs[j as usize]) >= 1.0 { stationary = false }
        j = j + 1
    }
    let stat_conf = if stationary { 0.90 } else { 0.40 }
    let stat_beta = beta_new(stat_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - stat_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let diag = ARIMADiagnostics {
        ljung_box_stat: lb_stat,
        ljung_box_p: lb_p,
        residual_normality: norm_beta,
        stationarity: stat_beta
    }

    let overall = beta_combine(&norm_beta, &stat_beta)

    let prov = ARIMAProvenance {
        method: "YuleWalker_AR",
        order: "ARIMA",
        n_obs: n,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeARIMA {
        value: model,
        variance: model.sigma_squared,
        confidence: overall,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_ar1_fit() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // AR(1) process: y_t = 0.8 * y_{t-1} + ε
    var series: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    series[0] = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 100 {
        series[i as usize] = 0.8 * series[(i - 1) as usize] + 0.1 * ((i % 7) as f64 - 3.0)
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fit_arima_epistemic(series, 100, 1, 0, 0)

    // AR(1) coefficient should be approximately 0.8
    let phi_ok = ar_abs(result.value.ar_coeffs[0] - 0.8) < 0.3

    phi_ok
}

fn test_auto_arima() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var series: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    series[0] = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 1
    while i < 50 {
        series[i as usize] = 0.5 * series[(i - 1) as usize] + 0.1
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = auto_arima(series, 50, 3, 1, 0)

    // Should select a low-order model
    result.p <= 3 && result.d <= 1
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/timeseries/kalman.sio ===
// stats::timeseries::kalman — Epistemic Kalman Filter
//
// Linear Gaussian state space models with:
// - Kalman filter (forward pass)
// - Kalman smoother (backward pass)
// - Log-likelihood computation
// - Missing data handling
// - Knowledge<KalmanResult> with epistemic metadata
//
// State space model:
//   x_{t+1} = F·x_t + B·u_t + w_t,  w_t ~ N(0, Q)
//   y_t     = H·x_t + v_t,           v_t ~ N(0, R)
//
// References:
// - Kalman (1960): "A new approach to linear filtering and prediction"
// - Rauch, Tung & Striebel (1965): "Maximum likelihood estimates" (smoother)
// - Harvey (1990): "Forecasting, Structural Time Series Models"
// - Durbin & Koopman (2012): "Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods"

// =============================================================================
// Math Helpers
// =============================================================================

struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,
    beta: f64
}

fn beta_new(a: f64, b: f64) -> BetaConfidence { BetaConfidence { alpha: a, beta: b } }
fn beta_mean(b: &BetaConfidence) -> f64 { b.alpha / (b.alpha + b.beta) }
fn beta_combine(b1: &BetaConfidence, b2: &BetaConfidence) -> BetaConfidence {
    BetaConfidence { alpha: b1.alpha + b2.alpha - 1.0, beta: b1.beta + b2.beta - 1.0 }
}

fn kf_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

fn kf_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn kf_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / (2 * k + 1) as f64; k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

// =============================================================================
// Types (Scalar State Space Model for simplicity)
// =============================================================================

// Scalar state space: x_{t+1} = F·x_t + w_t, y_t = H·x_t + v_t
// Generalizes to: local level model (F=1, H=1)
// and local linear trend (2D state)

struct KalmanParams {
    f: f64,         // State transition (F)
    h: f64,         // Observation matrix (H)
    q: f64,         // Process noise variance (Q)
    r: f64,         // Observation noise variance (R)
    x0: f64,        // Initial state estimate
    p0: f64         // Initial state variance
}

struct KalmanFilterOutput {
    filtered_state: [f64; 500],     // x_{t|t}
    filtered_var: [f64; 500],       // P_{t|t}
    predicted_state: [f64; 500],    // x_{t|t-1}
    predicted_var: [f64; 500],      // P_{t|t-1}
    innovation: [f64; 500],         // v_t = y_t - H·x_{t|t-1}
    innovation_var: [f64; 500],     // S_t = H·P_{t|t-1}·H' + R
    log_likelihood: f64,
    n_obs: i64
}

struct KalmanSmootherOutput {
    smoothed_state: [f64; 500],     // x_{t|T}
    smoothed_var: [f64; 500]        // P_{t|T}
}



struct KalmanDiagnostics {
    innovation_normality: BetaConfidence,
    innovation_independence: BetaConfidence,
    filter_stability: BetaConfidence
}

struct KalmanProvenance {
    method: String,
    n_obs: i64,
    params: KalmanParams,
    diagnostics: KalmanDiagnostics
}

struct KnowledgeKalman {
    filter: KalmanFilterOutput,
    smoother: KalmanSmootherOutput,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: KalmanProvenance
}

// =============================================================================
// KALMAN FILTER (Forward Pass)
// =============================================================================

fn kalman_filter(
    observations: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    params: KalmanParams
) -> KalmanFilterOutput with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x_filt: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var p_filt: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var x_pred: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var p_pred: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var innov: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var innov_var: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]

    var log_lik = 0.0
    let pi2 = 6.28318530718

    // Initialize
    var x = params.x0
    var p = params.p0

    var t: i64 = 0
    while t < n {
        // Predict: x_{t|t-1} = F·x_{t-1|t-1}
        let x_p = params.f * x
        let p_p = params.f * p * params.f + params.q

        x_pred[t as usize] = x_p
        p_pred[t as usize] = p_p

        // Innovation: v_t = y_t - H·x_{t|t-1}
        let y = observations[t as usize]
        let v = y - params.h * x_p
        let s = params.h * p_p * params.h + params.r

        innov[t as usize] = v
        innov_var[t as usize] = s

        // Log-likelihood contribution
        if s > 1.0e-10 {
            log_lik = log_lik - 0.5 * (kf_ln(pi2 * s) + v * v / s)
        }

        // Update (Kalman gain): K_t = P_{t|t-1}·H' / S_t
        let k_gain = if s > 1.0e-10 { p_p * params.h / s } else { 0.0 }

        // x_{t|t} = x_{t|t-1} + K_t·v_t
        x = x_p + k_gain * v
        // P_{t|t} = (1 - K_t·H)·P_{t|t-1}
        p = (1.0 - k_gain * params.h) * p_p

        x_filt[t as usize] = x
        p_filt[t as usize] = p

        t = t + 1
    }

    KalmanFilterOutput {
        filtered_state: x_filt,
        filtered_var: p_filt,
        predicted_state: x_pred,
        predicted_var: p_pred,
        innovation: innov,
        innovation_var: innov_var,
        log_likelihood: log_lik,
        n_obs: n
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// KALMAN SMOOTHER (Backward Pass — Rauch-Tung-Striebel)
// =============================================================================

fn kalman_smoother(
    filter: &KalmanFilterOutput,
    params: KalmanParams,
    n: i64
) -> KalmanSmootherOutput with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x_smooth: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    var p_smooth: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]

    // Initialize with last filtered state
    x_smooth[(n - 1) as usize] = filter.filtered_state[(n - 1) as usize]
    p_smooth[(n - 1) as usize] = filter.filtered_var[(n - 1) as usize]

    // Backward pass
    var t: i64 = n - 2
    while t >= 0 {
        let p_filt = filter.filtered_var[t as usize]
        let p_pred_next = filter.predicted_var[(t + 1) as usize]

        // Smoother gain: L_t = P_{t|t}·F' / P_{t+1|t}
        let l = if p_pred_next > 1.0e-10 {
            p_filt * params.f / p_pred_next
        } else { 0.0 }

        // x_{t|T} = x_{t|t} + L_t·(x_{t+1|T} - x_{t+1|t})
        x_smooth[t as usize] = filter.filtered_state[t as usize] +
            l * (x_smooth[(t + 1) as usize] - filter.predicted_state[(t + 1) as usize])

        // P_{t|T} = P_{t|t} + L_t·(P_{t+1|T} - P_{t+1|t})·L_t'
        p_smooth[t as usize] = p_filt +
            l * (p_smooth[(t + 1) as usize] - p_pred_next) * l

        t = t - 1
    }

    KalmanSmootherOutput {
        smoothed_state: x_smooth,
        smoothed_var: p_smooth
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC KALMAN
// =============================================================================

fn kalman_epistemic(
    observations: [f64; 500],
    n: i64,
    params: KalmanParams
) -> KnowledgeKalman with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let filter = kalman_filter(observations, n, params)
    let smoother = kalman_smoother(&filter, params, n)

    // Innovation diagnostics
    // Check if innovations are white noise (mean 0, no autocorrelation)
    var innov_mean = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        innov_mean = innov_mean + filter.innovation[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    innov_mean = innov_mean / (n as f64)

    let mean_ok = kf_abs(innov_mean) < 0.5
    let norm_conf = if mean_ok { 0.85 } else { 0.50 }
    let norm_beta = beta_new(norm_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - norm_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    // Check filter stability (P converges, doesn't diverge)
    let p_last = filter.filtered_var[(n - 1) as usize]
    let p_first = filter.filtered_var[0]
    let stable = p_last <= p_first * 2.0  // Variance shouldn't grow
    let stab_conf = if stable { 0.90 } else { 0.50 }
    let stab_beta = beta_new(stab_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - stab_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    // Independence (simplified: check lag-1 autocorrelation of innovations)
    var lag1_sum = 0.0
    var var_sum = 0.0
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        lag1_sum = lag1_sum + filter.innovation[i as usize] * filter.innovation[(i - 1) as usize]
        var_sum = var_sum + filter.innovation[i as usize] * filter.innovation[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    let lag1_corr = if var_sum > 1.0e-10 { kf_abs(lag1_sum / var_sum) } else { 0.0 }
    let indep_conf = if lag1_corr < 0.1 { 0.90 }
                     else if lag1_corr < 0.3 { 0.70 }
                     else { 0.50 }
    let indep_beta = beta_new(indep_conf * (n as f64) * 0.3, (1.0 - indep_conf) * (n as f64) * 0.3)

    let diag = KalmanDiagnostics {
        innovation_normality: norm_beta,
        innovation_independence: indep_beta,
        filter_stability: stab_beta
    }

    let c1 = beta_combine(&norm_beta, &stab_beta)
    let overall = beta_combine(&c1, &indep_beta)

    let prov = KalmanProvenance {
        method: "Kalman_RTS",
        n_obs: n,
        params: params,
        diagnostics: diag
    }

    KnowledgeKalman {
        filter: filter,
        smoother: smoother,
        confidence: overall,
        provenance: prov
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Tests
// =============================================================================

fn test_local_level() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Local level model: x_{t+1} = x_t + w_t, y_t = x_t + v_t
    // True state = 5.0 (constant), noisy observations
    var obs: [f64; 500] = [0.0; 500]
    obs[0] = 5.1; obs[1] = 4.9; obs[2] = 5.2; obs[3] = 4.8
    obs[4] = 5.0; obs[5] = 5.3; obs[6] = 4.7; obs[7] = 5.1
    obs[8] = 4.9; obs[9] = 5.0

    let params = KalmanParams {
        f: 1.0,     // Random walk
        h: 1.0,     // Direct observation
        q: 0.01,    // Small process noise
        r: 0.1,     // Moderate observation noise
        x0: 5.0,    // Prior state
        p0: 1.0     // Prior uncertainty
    }

    let result = kalman_epistemic(obs, 10, params)

    // Filtered state should converge to ~5.0
    let state_ok = kf_abs(result.filter.filtered_state[9] - 5.0) < 0.5

    // Filtered variance should decrease (learning)
    let var_decreasing = result.filter.filtered_var[9] < result.filter.filtered_var[0]

    state_ok && var_decreasing
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stats/validation.sio ===
// stdlib/stats/validation.d
// Statistical Validation Primitives
//
// Provides functions for statistical validation:
// - Descriptive statistics (mean, variance, std dev)
// - Correlation and R-squared
// - Basic hypothesis testing
// - Confidence intervals

// =============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// =============================================================================

fn val_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0; }
    var y = x;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < 15 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    y
}

fn val_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// =============================================================================
// Descriptive Statistics
// =============================================================================

// Calculate mean of an array
pub fn mean(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }

    var sum: f64 = 0.0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        sum = sum + data[i];
        i = i + 1;
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

// Calculate sample variance (using n-1 denominator)
pub fn variance(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n < 2 { return 0.0; }

    let m = mean(data);
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let diff = data[i] - m;
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    sum_sq / ((n - 1) as f64)
}

// Calculate sample standard deviation
pub fn std_dev(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    val_sqrt_f64(variance(data))
}

// Calculate population variance (using n denominator)
pub fn variance_population(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }

    let m = mean(data);
    var sum_sq: f64 = 0.0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let diff = data[i] - m;
        sum_sq = sum_sq + diff * diff;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    sum_sq / (n as f64)
}

// Calculate standard error of the mean
pub fn standard_error(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }
    std_dev(data) / val_sqrt_f64(n as f64)
}

// Find minimum value
pub fn min(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }

    var m = data[0];
    var i: usize = 1;
    while i < n {
        if data[i] < m {
            m = data[i];
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    m
}

// Find maximum value
pub fn max(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }

    var m = data[0];
    var i: usize = 1;
    while i < n {
        if data[i] > m {
            m = data[i];
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }
    m
}

// Calculate range
pub fn range(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    max(data) - min(data)
}

// =============================================================================
// Correlation and Regression
// =============================================================================

// Pearson correlation coefficient
pub fn correlation(x: &[f64], y: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = x.len();
    if n != y.len() || n < 2 { return 0.0; }

    let mean_x = mean(x);
    let mean_y = mean(y);

    var sum_xy: f64 = 0.0;
    var sum_x2: f64 = 0.0;
    var sum_y2: f64 = 0.0;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let dx = x[i] - mean_x;
        let dy = y[i] - mean_y;
        sum_xy = sum_xy + dx * dy;
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + dx * dx;
        sum_y2 = sum_y2 + dy * dy;
        i = i + 1;
    }

    let denom = val_sqrt_f64(sum_x2 * sum_y2);
    if denom < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0; }

    sum_xy / denom
}

// R-squared (coefficient of determination)
pub fn r_squared(x: &[f64], y: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let r = correlation(x, y);
    r * r
}

// Simple linear regression: y = a + b*x
// Returns (intercept, slope)
pub struct LinearFit {
    pub intercept: f64,
    pub slope: f64,
    pub r_squared: f64,
}

pub fn linear_regression(x: &[f64], y: &[f64]) -> LinearFit {
    let n = x.len();
    if n != y.len() || n < 2 {
        return LinearFit { intercept: 0.0, slope: 0.0, r_squared: 0.0 };
    }

    let mean_x = mean(x);
    let mean_y = mean(y);

    var sum_xy: f64 = 0.0;
    var sum_x2: f64 = 0.0;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n {
        let dx = x[i] - mean_x;
        sum_xy = sum_xy + dx * (y[i] - mean_y);
        sum_x2 = sum_x2 + dx * dx;
        i = i + 1;
    }

    if sum_x2 < 1.0e-15 {
        return LinearFit { intercept: mean_y, slope: 0.0, r_squared: 0.0 };
    }

    let slope = sum_xy / sum_x2;
    let intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_x;
    let rsq = r_squared(x, y);

    LinearFit { intercept: intercept, slope: slope, r_squared: rsq }
}

// =============================================================================
// Residual Analysis
// =============================================================================

// Calculate residuals from predicted values
pub fn residuals(actual: &[f64], predicted: &[f64]) -> [f64] {
    let n = actual.len();
    var result: [f64] = [];

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n && i < predicted.len() {
        result.push(actual[i] - predicted[i]);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    result
}

// Sum of squared residuals (SSR)
pub fn sum_squared_residuals(actual: &[f64], predicted: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = actual.len();
    var sum: f64 = 0.0;

    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n && i < predicted.len() {
        let diff = actual[i] - predicted[i];
        sum = sum + diff * diff;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    sum
}

// Mean squared error (MSE)
pub fn mse(actual: &[f64], predicted: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = actual.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }
    sum_squared_residuals(actual, predicted) / (n as f64)
}

// Root mean squared error (RMSE)
pub fn rmse(actual: &[f64], predicted: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    val_sqrt_f64(mse(actual, predicted))
}

// Mean absolute error (MAE)
pub fn mae(actual: &[f64], predicted: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = actual.len();
    if n == 0 { return 0.0; }

    var sum: f64 = 0.0;
    var i: usize = 0;
    while i < n && i < predicted.len() {
        sum = sum + val_abs_f64(actual[i] - predicted[i]);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    sum / (n as f64)
}

// =============================================================================
// Hypothesis Testing (simplified)
// =============================================================================

// One-sample t-statistic
pub fn t_statistic(data: &[f64], hypothesized_mean: f64) -> f64 {
    let n = data.len();
    if n < 2 { return 0.0; }

    let sample_mean = mean(data);
    let se = standard_error(data);

    if se < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0; }

    (sample_mean - hypothesized_mean) / se
}

// Two-sample t-statistic (independent samples, equal variance assumed)
pub fn t_statistic_two_sample(x: &[f64], y: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n1 = x.len();
    let n2 = y.len();
    if n1 < 2 || n2 < 2 { return 0.0; }

    let mean1 = mean(x);
    let mean2 = mean(y);
    let var1 = variance(x);
    let var2 = variance(y);

    // Pooled variance
    let sp2 = (((n1 - 1) as f64) * var1 + ((n2 - 1) as f64) * var2) /
              ((n1 + n2 - 2) as f64);

    let se = val_sqrt_f64(sp2 * (1.0 / (n1 as f64) + 1.0 / (n2 as f64)));

    if se < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0; }

    (mean1 - mean2) / se
}

// =============================================================================
// Confidence Intervals
// =============================================================================

// Result of confidence interval calculation
pub struct ConfidenceInterval {
    pub lower: f64,
    pub upper: f64,
    pub center: f64,
    pub margin: f64,
}

// Calculate 95% confidence interval for the mean
// Uses z=1.96 (large sample approximation)
pub fn confidence_interval_95(data: &[f64]) -> ConfidenceInterval {
    let m = mean(data);
    let se = standard_error(data);
    let margin = 1.96 * se;

    ConfidenceInterval {
        lower: m - margin,
        upper: m + margin,
        center: m,
        margin: margin,
    }
}

// Calculate confidence interval with custom z-value
pub fn confidence_interval(data: &[f64], z: f64) -> ConfidenceInterval {
    let m = mean(data);
    let se = standard_error(data);
    let margin = z * se;

    ConfidenceInterval {
        lower: m - margin,
        upper: m + margin,
        center: m,
        margin: margin,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Validation Summary
// =============================================================================

// Complete validation result
pub struct ValidationResult {
    pub n: usize,
    pub mean: f64,
    pub std_dev: f64,
    pub min: f64,
    pub max: f64,
    pub ci_lower: f64,
    pub ci_upper: f64,
}

// Generate comprehensive validation summary
pub fn validate(data: &[f64]) -> ValidationResult {
    let ci = confidence_interval_95(data);

    ValidationResult {
        n: data.len(),
        mean: mean(data),
        std_dev: std_dev(data),
        min: min(data),
        max: max(data),
        ci_lower: ci.lower,
        ci_upper: ci.upper,
    }
}
