// === FILE: stdlib/stochastic/processes.sio ===
// Sprint 24 Track B: Stochastic Process stdlib
// References: Oksendal (2003) SDEs, Doob (1953)

fn euler_maruyama_step(x: f64, drift: f64, diffusion: f64, dt: f64, dw: f64) -> f64 {
    // Euler-Maruyama discretization: X_{t+dt} = X_t + mu(X_t)*dt + sigma(X_t)*dW
    x + drift * dt + diffusion * dw
}

fn markov_stationary_power_2state(p00: f64, p01: f64, n_iter: i64) -> f64 {
    // Power iteration for 2-state Markov chain stationary distribution
    // pi_0 = p10 / (p01 + p10) where p10 = 1 - p00
    let p10: f64 = 1.0 - p00
    p10 / (p01 + p10)
}

fn ornstein_uhlenbeck_mean(x0: f64, theta: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    // OU mean reversion: E[X_t] = x0 * exp(-theta*t)
    // First-order approximation: x0 * (1 - theta*t) for small theta*t
    x0 * (1.0 - theta * t)
}

fn gbm_expected_value(s0: f64, mu: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    // Geometric Brownian Motion expected value: E[S_t] = S_0 * exp(mu*t)
    // First-order: S_0 * (1 + mu*t)
    s0 * (1.0 + mu * t)
}

fn tv_distance_bound(mixing_rate: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    // Total variation convergence: TV(mu_t, pi) <= exp(-rate * t)
    // Second-order Taylor approximation
    let rt: f64 = mixing_rate * t
    1.0 - rt + rt * rt / 2.0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/stochastic/sde.sio ===
// stdlib/stochastic/sde.sio — Stochastic Differential Equation Solvers
//
// Implements Euler-Maruyama and Milstein discretizations with epistemic
// uncertainty propagation (GUM JCGM 100:2008).
//
// Brownian increments are generated via an inline xorshift64 PRNG + Box-Muller
// transform — no external dependencies.
//
// Supported models:
//   Euler-Maruyama  :  X_{t+dt} = X_t + μ·dt + σ·√dt·Z
//   Milstein        :  adds ½σσ'(ΔW²-dt) correction
//   GBM             :  dS = μS·dt + σS·dW  (Black-Scholes)
//   OU              :  dX = θ(μ-X)dt + σdW  (mean-reversion)
//   Epistemic GBM   :  GBM with uncertain μ, σ, S₀
//
// References:
//   Kloeden & Platen (1992): "Numerical Solution of SDEs"
//   Milstein (1974): "Approximate Integration of SDEs"
//   Black & Scholes (1973): "The Pricing of Options"
//   Uhlenbeck & Ornstein (1930): "On the Theory of Brownian Motion"
//   JCGM 100:2008: "Evaluation of measurement data (GUM)"

// =============================================================================
// Math helpers — all helpers before callers
// =============================================================================

fn sde_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn sde_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    y
}

fn sde_log(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Natural log via Newton's method on exp.
    // Uses identity: ln(x) = 2*atanh((x-1)/(x+1))
    // atanh(z) = z + z^3/3 + z^5/5 + ... converges for |z|<1
    // Range-reduce: write x = 2^k * m, m in [0.5,1), ln(x)=k*ln2 + ln(m)
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e300 }
    var k: f64 = 0.0
    var m = x
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; k = k + 1.0 }
    while m < 0.5  { m = m * 2.0; k = k - 1.0 }
    // ln(m) for m in [0.5, 1): shift to u = m - 1, |u| <= 0.5
    // ln(1+u) = u - u^2/2 + u^3/3 - u^4/4 + u^5/5 - u^6/6 + u^7/7 - u^8/8
    let u = m - 1.0
    let u2 = u * u
    let u3 = u2 * u
    let u4 = u3 * u
    let u5 = u4 * u
    let u6 = u5 * u
    let u7 = u6 * u
    let u8 = u7 * u
    let ln_m = u - u2/2.0 + u3/3.0 - u4/4.0 + u5/5.0 - u6/6.0 + u7/7.0 - u8/8.0
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    k * ln2 + ln_m
}

fn sde_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Range-reduce: e^x = e^k * e^r, k = round(x/ln2), |r| <= ln(2)/2
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    var k: f64 = 0.0
    var r = x
    if x > 0.0 { while r > 0.5 * ln2 { r = r - ln2; k = k + 1.0 } }
    if x < 0.0 { while r < 0.0 - 0.5 * ln2 { r = r + ln2; k = k + 1.0; k = k - 2.0 } }
    // e^r via Taylor, |r| <= 0.35
    let r2 = r * r
    let r3 = r2 * r
    let r4 = r3 * r
    let r5 = r4 * r
    let r6 = r5 * r
    let r7 = r6 * r
    let r8 = r7 * r
    let er = 1.0 + r + r2/2.0 + r3/6.0 + r4/24.0 + r5/120.0 + r6/720.0 + r7/5040.0 + r8/40320.0
    // multiply by 2^k
    var result = er
    var ki = k
    if ki > 0.0 { while ki > 0.5 { result = result * 2.0; ki = ki - 1.0 } }
    if ki < 0.0 { while ki < 0.0 - 0.5 { result = result / 2.0; ki = ki + 1.0 } }
    result
}

// =============================================================================
// xorshift64 PRNG — inline, no state struct needed in helpers
// =============================================================================

// Advance xorshift64 state and return next pseudo-random i64
fn xorshift64_next(state: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    var s = state
    s = s ^ (s << 13)
    s = s ^ (s >> 7)
    s = s ^ (s << 17)
    s
}

// Map i64 to f64 in (0, 1) — avoid exact 0 which breaks log
fn xorshift64_f64(s: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Use upper 53 bits; i64 may be negative so mask to positive
    var v = s
    if v < 0 { v = 0 - v }
    // v in [0, 2^63); divide by 2^53
    let denom: f64 = 9007199254740992.0   // 2^53
    var fv = (v as f64) / denom
    // clamp strictly into (0,1) to keep log defined
    if fv <= 0.0 { fv = 1.0e-15 }
    if fv >= 1.0 { fv = 1.0 - 1.0e-15 }
    fv
}

// Box-Muller: given two uniform samples u1, u2 in (0,1), return standard normal
// Returns only the first variate (cosine branch) for simplicity.
fn box_muller_z(u1: f64, u2: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let two_pi = 6.283185307179586
    let mag = sde_sqrt(0.0 - 2.0 * sde_log(u1))
    // cos approximation via Taylor: cos(t) = 1 - t^2/2 + t^4/24 - t^6/720
    let t = two_pi * u2
    let t2 = t * t
    let t4 = t2 * t2
    let t6 = t4 * t2
    let cos_t = 1.0 - t2/2.0 + t4/24.0 - t6/720.0
    mag * cos_t
}

// =============================================================================
// SDEState — core type
// =============================================================================

pub struct SDEState {
    x:         [f64; 16],   // state vector
    x_unc:     [f64; 16],   // epistemic uncertainty (std dev) on each component
    n:         i32,          // active dimensions
    t:         f64,          // current time
    rng_state: i64,          // xorshift64 seed/state
}

// =============================================================================
// sde_state_new
// =============================================================================

pub fn sde_state_new(n: i32, seed: i64) -> SDEState {
    SDEState {
        x:         [0.0; 16],
        x_unc:     [0.0; 16],
        n:         n,
        t:         0.0,
        rng_state: seed,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Helper: draw one standard normal, advance rng embedded in a state
// Returns (z, new_rng_state)
// =============================================================================

struct NormalDraw {
    z:         f64,
    new_state: i64,
}

fn draw_normal(rng: i64) -> NormalDraw with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let s1 = xorshift64_next(rng)
    let s2 = xorshift64_next(s1)
    let u1 = xorshift64_f64(s1)
    let u2 = xorshift64_f64(s2)
    let z  = box_muller_z(u1, u2)
    NormalDraw { z: z, new_state: s2 }
}

// =============================================================================
// Euler-Maruyama step
// =============================================================================
//
// X_{t+dt} = X_t + μ_i·dt + σ_i·√dt·Z_i
// u²(X_{t+dt}) = u²(X_t) + σ²_i·dt   (diffusion adds variance, GUM §5.2)
//
// drift[i]     — μ_i  (additive drift coefficient)
// diffusion[i] — σ_i  (diffusion coefficient)

pub fn euler_maruyama(
    state:     SDEState,
    dt:        f64,
    drift:     &[f64; 16],
    diffusion: &[f64; 16],
) -> SDEState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = state
    let sqrt_dt = sde_sqrt(dt)
    var i = 0
    while i < s.n {
        let d = draw_normal(s.rng_state)
        s.rng_state = d.new_state
        let z  = d.z
        let mu = drift[i]
        let sg = diffusion[i]
        s.x[i]     = s.x[i] + mu * dt + sg * sqrt_dt * z
        // GUM uncertainty propagation: u²_new = u²_old + σ²·dt
        let u_sq_new = s.x_unc[i] * s.x_unc[i] + sg * sg * dt
        s.x_unc[i] = sde_sqrt(u_sq_new)
        i = i + 1
    }
    s.t = s.t + dt
    s
}

// =============================================================================
// Milstein step
// =============================================================================
//
// Adds the Itô correction term (order-1 strong convergence):
//   X_{t+dt} = X_t + μ·dt + σ·ΔW + ½·σ·σ'·(ΔW² - dt)
//
// where ΔW = √dt·Z.
//
// diff_deriv[i] — σ'_i = dσ/dX evaluated at X_t

pub fn milstein_step(
    state:      SDEState,
    dt:         f64,
    drift:      &[f64; 16],
    diffusion:  &[f64; 16],
    diff_deriv: &[f64; 16],
) -> SDEState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var s = state
    let sqrt_dt = sde_sqrt(dt)
    var i = 0
    while i < s.n {
        let d = draw_normal(s.rng_state)
        s.rng_state = d.new_state
        let z  = d.z
        let dw = sqrt_dt * z
        let mu = drift[i]
        let sg = diffusion[i]
        let sg_prime = diff_deriv[i]
        // Euler-Maruyama term + Milstein correction
        let correction = 0.5 * sg * sg_prime * (dw * dw - dt)
        s.x[i]    = s.x[i] + mu * dt + sg * dw + correction
        // Uncertainty: Milstein adds ½σσ'·dt as additional variance term
        let u_sq_new = s.x_unc[i] * s.x_unc[i] + sg * sg * dt + 0.5 * sg * sg_prime * dt
        let u_sq_clamp = if u_sq_new < 0.0 { 0.0 } else { u_sq_new }
        s.x_unc[i] = sde_sqrt(u_sq_clamp)
        i = i + 1
    }
    s.t = s.t + dt
    s
}

// =============================================================================
// Geometric Brownian Motion
// =============================================================================
//
// dS = μS·dt + σS·dW
//
// Discretized: S_{t+dt} = S_t · exp((μ - σ²/2)·dt + σ·√dt·Z)
// (log-Euler scheme — exact for GBM)
//
// The output SDEState stores the trajectory in x[0..n_steps-1] (clamped to 16),
// x_unc carries propagated uncertainty, n = min(n_steps, 16).
// The *final* value is x[n-1], x_unc[n-1].

pub fn gbm_simulate(
    s0:      f64,
    mu:      f64,
    sigma:   f64,
    t_end:   f64,
    n_steps: i32,
    seed:    i64,
) -> SDEState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = sde_state_new(1, seed)
    state.x[0]     = s0
    state.x_unc[0] = 0.0
    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sde_sqrt(dt)
    let drift_adj = mu - 0.5 * sigma * sigma  // log-space drift

    // We record every step but only have 16 slots.
    // Store final value trajectory in slot 0; track at each step.
    var cur_s   = s0
    var cur_unc = 0.0
    var step = 0
    var rng = seed
    while step < n_steps {
        let d = draw_normal(rng)
        rng = d.new_state
        let z  = d.z
        // Log-Euler: S_{t+dt} = S_t * exp(drift_adj*dt + sigma*sqrt_dt*z)
        let exponent = drift_adj * dt + sigma * sqrt_dt * z
        cur_s = cur_s * sde_exp(exponent)
        // Uncertainty: relative uncertainty grows as σ²·dt per step
        let u_rel_sq_old = if cur_s > 1.0e-300 {
            (cur_unc / cur_s) * (cur_unc / cur_s)
        } else {
            0.0
        }
        let u_rel_sq_new = u_rel_sq_old + sigma * sigma * dt
        cur_unc = cur_s * sde_sqrt(u_rel_sq_new)
        step = step + 1
    }

    state.x[0]     = cur_s
    state.x_unc[0] = cur_unc
    state.t        = t_end
    state.n        = 1
    state.rng_state = rng
    state
}

// =============================================================================
// Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
// =============================================================================
//
// dX = θ(μ-X)dt + σdW   (mean-reverting)
//
// Euler-Maruyama: X_{t+dt} = X_t + θ(μ-X_t)dt + σ·√dt·Z
// Uncertainty:    u²_new = u²_old·(1 - θ·dt)² + σ²·dt

pub fn ou_simulate(
    x0:      f64,
    theta:   f64,
    mu:      f64,
    sigma:   f64,
    t_end:   f64,
    n_steps: i32,
    seed:    i64,
) -> SDEState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = sde_state_new(1, seed)
    state.x[0]     = x0
    state.x_unc[0] = 0.0
    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sde_sqrt(dt)

    var cur_x   = x0
    var cur_unc = 0.0
    var rng = seed
    var step = 0
    while step < n_steps {
        let d = draw_normal(rng)
        rng = d.new_state
        let z = d.z
        // Euler-Maruyama for OU
        cur_x = cur_x + theta * (mu - cur_x) * dt + sigma * sqrt_dt * z
        // Uncertainty: mean-reversion damps existing uncertainty
        let damping = 1.0 - theta * dt
        let u_prop = cur_unc * damping
        let u_sq_new = u_prop * u_prop + sigma * sigma * dt
        cur_unc = sde_sqrt(u_sq_new)
        step = step + 1
    }

    state.x[0]     = cur_x
    state.x_unc[0] = cur_unc
    state.t        = t_end
    state.n        = 1
    state.rng_state = rng
    state
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic GBM — uncertain parameters
// =============================================================================
//
// Parameters μ, σ, S₀ carry epistemic uncertainty (standard deviations
// mu_unc, sigma_unc, s0_unc).  Per-step GUM propagation via first-order
// sensitivity analysis:
//
//   ∂S_{t+dt}/∂μ   ≈ S_t·dt           (sensitivity to drift)
//   ∂S_{t+dt}/∂σ   ≈ S_t·(√dt·Z - σ·dt)   (sensitivity to diffusion)
//   ∂S_{t+dt}/∂S₀  ≈ S_{t+dt}/S₀      (ratio propagation)
//
// Combined uncertainty (GUM §5.1.2 — independent sources):
//   u²(S) = (∂S/∂μ)²·u²(μ) + (∂S/∂σ)²·u²(σ) + (∂S/∂S₀)²·u²(S₀)
//           + σ²·S²·dt   (diffusion noise term)

pub fn sde_epistemic_gbm(
    s0:        f64,
    s0_unc:    f64,
    mu:        f64,
    mu_unc:    f64,
    sigma:     f64,
    sigma_unc: f64,
    t_end:     f64,
    n_steps:   i32,
    seed:      i64,
) -> SDEState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = sde_state_new(1, seed)
    state.x[0]     = s0
    state.x_unc[0] = s0_unc
    let dt = t_end / (n_steps as f64)
    let sqrt_dt = sde_sqrt(dt)
    let drift_adj = mu - 0.5 * sigma * sigma

    var cur_s   = s0
    var cur_unc = s0_unc
    var rng = seed
    var step = 0
    while step < n_steps {
        let d = draw_normal(rng)
        rng = d.new_state
        let z  = d.z
        let dw = sqrt_dt * z

        // Log-Euler step
        let exponent = drift_adj * dt + sigma * dw
        let s_new = cur_s * sde_exp(exponent)

        // Sensitivities at current step
        let sens_mu    = cur_s * dt                         // ∂S/∂μ
        let sens_sigma = cur_s * (dw - sigma * dt)         // ∂S/∂σ
        // ∂S/∂S₀ = s_new / s0  (chain rule across all steps)
        let ratio_s0 = if s0 > 1.0e-300 { s_new / s0 } else { 1.0 }

        // GUM combination: state uncertainty grows from parameter uncertainty
        let u_param_sq = sens_mu    * sens_mu    * mu_unc    * mu_unc
                       + sens_sigma * sens_sigma * sigma_unc * sigma_unc
                       + ratio_s0  * ratio_s0   * s0_unc    * s0_unc
        // Propagate existing uncertainty through the multiplicative step
        let u_prop_sq  = cur_unc * cur_unc * (s_new / (cur_s + 1.0e-300)) * (s_new / (cur_s + 1.0e-300))
        // Diffusion noise adds σ²·S²·dt
        let u_diff_sq  = sigma * sigma * s_new * s_new * dt

        let u_total_sq = u_param_sq + u_prop_sq + u_diff_sq
        cur_unc = sde_sqrt(u_total_sq)
        cur_s   = s_new
        step = step + 1
    }

    state.x[0]     = cur_s
    state.x_unc[0] = cur_unc
    state.t        = t_end
    state.n        = 1
    state.rng_state = rng
    state
}


// === FILE: stdlib/string/string.sio ===
// stdlib/string/string.sio
// UTF-8 string utilities using fixed byte arrays
//
// Sounio strings are fixed-size byte buffers.

// Check if byte is a UTF-8 continuation byte
fn str_is_continuation(b: u8) -> i64 {
    if (b as i64) >= 128 {
        if (b as i64) < 192 { return 1 }
    }
    return 0
}

// Count UTF-8 characters in a byte buffer
fn str_char_count(buf: [u8; 256], byte_len: i64) -> i64 {
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < byte_len {
        if str_is_continuation(buf[i]) == 0 {
            count = count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return count
}

// Compare two byte buffers for equality
fn str_eq(a: [u8; 256], a_len: i64, b: [u8; 256], b_len: i64) -> i64 {
    if a_len != b_len { return 0 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < a_len {
        if a[i] != b[i] { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 1
}

// Check if buffer starts with prefix
fn str_starts_with(buf: [u8; 256], buf_len: i64, prefix: [u8; 256], prefix_len: i64) -> i64 {
    if prefix_len > buf_len { return 0 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < prefix_len {
        if buf[i] != prefix[i] { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 1
}

// Find first occurrence of a single byte in buffer
// Returns index or -1 if not found
fn str_find_byte(buf: [u8; 256], buf_len: i64, needle: u8) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < buf_len {
        if buf[i] == needle { return i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 0 - 1
}

// Trim leading ASCII whitespace, returns new start index
fn str_trim_start(buf: [u8; 256], buf_len: i64) -> i64 {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < buf_len {
        let b = buf[i] as i64
        if b != 32 {
            if b != 9 {
                if b != 10 {
                    if b != 13 { return i }
                }
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return buf_len
}

// Trim trailing ASCII whitespace, returns new end index
fn str_trim_end(buf: [u8; 256], buf_len: i64) -> i64 {
    var end = buf_len
    while end > 0 {
        let b = buf[end - 1] as i64
        if b != 32 {
            if b != 9 {
                if b != 10 {
                    if b != 13 { return end }
                }
            }
        }
        end = end - 1
    }
    return 0
}

// Convert ASCII lowercase letter to uppercase (single byte)
fn str_to_upper_byte(b: u8) -> u8 {
    let v = b as i64
    if v >= 97 {
        if v <= 122 { return (v - 32) as u8 }
    }
    return b
}

// Convert ASCII uppercase letter to lowercase (single byte)
fn str_to_lower_byte(b: u8) -> u8 {
    let v = b as i64
    if v >= 65 {
        if v <= 90 { return (v + 32) as u8 }
    }
    return b
}


// === FILE: stdlib/str/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/str/lib.sio — Byte-array string utilities for Sounio
//
// Strings are represented as `Str { data: [i8; 256], len: i32 }`.
// No heap allocation — all operations use fixed-size stack buffers.
//
// # Key types
//   Str        — string value (data + length, max 256 bytes)
//   StrSplit   — result of str_split_char (up to 16 parts)
//
// # JIT interpreter notes
//   - str_to_string takes Str by VALUE (not &Str) to work around a JIT
//     limitation where &elem of a struct-array does not propagate reads.
//   - str_split_char uses a StrSplit struct wrapper so mutations via &!
//     are visible to callers (bare &![T;N] mutations are not visible).
//   - str_len, str_eq, str_char_at shadow same-named builtins that take
//     `string`.  str_from_literal uses str_char_at(string, i64) == -1
//     as a sentinel for end-of-string to avoid calling the builtin str_len.

// ============================================================================
// Core types
// ============================================================================

pub struct Str {
    pub data: [i8; 256],
    pub len:  i32,
}

// Wrapper for str_split_char results (struct wrapping needed for &! mutation).
pub struct StrSplit {
    pub parts: [Str; 16],
    pub count: i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Construction — these MUST precede any function that calls them
// ============================================================================

// Return an empty Str.
pub fn str_new() -> Str {
    Str { data: [0; 256], len: 0 }
}

// Return an empty StrSplit.
pub fn str_split_new() -> StrSplit {
    StrSplit { parts: [str_new(); 16], count: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// str_from_buf — copy i8 buffer into a Str (private helper, precedes callers)
// ============================================================================

fn str_from_buf_i64(data: &[i8; 64], len: i32) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    let cap = if len < 256 { len } else { 256 }
    var i = 0
    while i < cap {
        result.data[i as usize] = data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.len = cap
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Conversion to builtin string (for print/comparison).
// Takes Str BY VALUE to avoid JIT reference-to-array-element limitation.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_to_string(s: Str) -> string with Mut, Div, Panic {
    str_from_bytes(s.data, s.len as i64)
}

// ============================================================================
// str_from_literal — copy builtin string literal into a Str.
//
// Uses `str_char_at(s, i) < 0` as end-of-string sentinel instead of the
// builtin `str_len`, because our exported `str_len` shadows the builtin once
// defined later in this file.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_from_literal(s: string) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 256 {
        let ch = str_char_at(s, i)  // builtin: returns -1 past end
        if ch < 0 { return result }
        result.data[i as usize] = ch as i8
        result.len = result.len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// Copy from a fixed [i8; 256] buffer with explicit byte count.
pub fn str_from_bytes_buf(data: &[i8; 256], len: i32) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    let cap = if len < 256 { len } else { 256 }
    var i = 0
    while i < cap {
        result.data[i as usize] = data[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result.len = cap
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// str_len — returns byte count of a Str.
// NOTE: shadows builtin str_len(string).  Use str_from_literal before this
//       point in the file to avoid the shadow affecting that call.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_len(s: &Str) -> i32 {
    s.len
}

// ============================================================================
// Equality — byte-by-byte comparison.
// NOTE: shadows builtin str_eq(string, string).
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_eq(a: &Str, b: &Str) -> bool {
    if a.len != b.len { return false }
    var i = 0
    while i < a.len {
        if a.data[i as usize] != b.data[i as usize] { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Concatenation — a ++ b, truncated at 256 bytes.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_concat(a: &Str, b: &Str) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    var i = 0
    while i < a.len && result.len < 256 {
        result.data[result.len as usize] = a.data[i as usize]
        result.len = result.len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    var j = 0
    while j < b.len && result.len < 256 {
        result.data[result.len as usize] = b.data[j as usize]
        result.len = result.len + 1
        j = j + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Match helper — internal only; precedes contains/starts_with/index_of.
// Returns true if needle matches haystack starting at byte offset pos.
// ============================================================================

fn str_match_at(haystack: &Str, needle: &Str, pos: i32) -> bool {
    if needle.len == 0 { return true }
    if pos < 0 { return false }
    if pos + needle.len > haystack.len { return false }
    var k = 0
    while k < needle.len {
        if haystack.data[(pos + k) as usize] != needle.data[k as usize] {
            return false
        }
        k = k + 1
    }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Contains / starts_with / ends_with / index_of
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_contains(haystack: &Str, needle: &Str) -> bool {
    if needle.len == 0 { return true }
    if needle.len > haystack.len { return false }
    var i = 0
    while i <= haystack.len - needle.len {
        if str_match_at(haystack, needle, i) { return true }
        i = i + 1
    }
    false
}

pub fn str_starts_with(s: &Str, prefix: &Str) -> bool {
    str_match_at(s, prefix, 0)
}

pub fn str_ends_with(s: &Str, suffix: &Str) -> bool {
    if suffix.len == 0 { return true }
    if suffix.len > s.len { return false }
    str_match_at(s, suffix, s.len - suffix.len)
}

// Returns the byte index of the first occurrence of needle, or -1.
pub fn str_index_of(haystack: &Str, needle: &Str) -> i32 {
    if needle.len == 0 { return 0 }
    if needle.len > haystack.len { return 0 - 1 }
    var i = 0
    while i <= haystack.len - needle.len {
        if str_match_at(haystack, needle, i) { return i }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0 - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Slice — substring [start, end) (clamped to valid range)
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_slice(s: &Str, start: i32, end: i32) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    let lo = if start < 0 { 0 } else { start }
    let hi = if end > s.len { s.len } else { end }
    var i = lo
    while i < hi && result.len < 256 {
        result.data[result.len as usize] = s.data[i as usize]
        result.len = result.len + 1
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Trim — remove leading and trailing ASCII spaces (0x20) and tabs (0x09)
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_trim(s: &Str) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s.len == 0 { return str_new() }

    // Find lo: first non-whitespace from the left
    var lo = 0
    while lo < s.len {
        let ch = s.data[lo as usize]
        if ch != 32 as i8 && ch != 9 as i8 { return str_trim_end_from(s, lo) }
        lo = lo + 1
    }
    str_new()  // all whitespace
}

// Internal: trim trailing whitespace from s[start..s.len] and return result.
fn str_trim_end_from(s: &Str, start: i32) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Find hi: last non-whitespace from the right
    var hi = s.len
    while hi > start {
        let ch = s.data[(hi - 1) as usize]
        if ch != 32 as i8 && ch != 9 as i8 { return str_slice(s, start, hi) }
        hi = hi - 1
    }
    str_new()
}

// ============================================================================
// Case conversion — ASCII only (a-z ↔ A-Z)
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_to_upper(s: &Str) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    result.len = s.len
    var i = 0
    while i < s.len {
        let ch = s.data[i as usize]
        result.data[i as usize] = if ch >= 97 as i8 && ch <= 122 as i8 {
            ch - 32 as i8
        } else {
            ch
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

pub fn str_to_lower(s: &Str) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    result.len = s.len
    var i = 0
    while i < s.len {
        let ch = s.data[i as usize]
        result.data[i as usize] = if ch >= 65 as i8 && ch <= 90 as i8 {
            ch + 32 as i8
        } else {
            ch
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// str_split_char — split on a single byte delimiter into a StrSplit wrapper.
//
// Writes results directly into out.parts[i].data/len fields (not via a local
// Str copy) to work around the JIT bare-array &! mutation limitation.
// Returns the number of parts found.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_split_char(s: &Str, delim: i8, out: &!StrSplit) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    out.count = 0
    var start: i32 = 0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i <= s.len && out.count < 16 {
        let at_end   = i == s.len
        let at_delim = i < s.len && s.data[i as usize] == delim
        if at_end || at_delim {
            let ci = out.count
            out.parts[ci as usize].len = 0
            var j = start
            while j < i {
                let plen = out.parts[ci as usize].len
                out.parts[ci as usize].data[plen as usize] = s.data[j as usize]
                out.parts[ci as usize].len = plen + 1
                j = j + 1
            }
            out.count = ci + 1
            start = i + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    out.count
}

// ============================================================================
// Character access — bounds-checked; returns 0 on out-of-bounds.
// Named str_char_at_s to avoid shadowing builtin str_char_at(string, i64).
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_char_at_s(s: &Str, idx: i32) -> i8 {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= s.len { return 0 as i8 }
    s.data[idx as usize]
}

// ============================================================================
// Replace all occurrences of one byte with another
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_replace_char(s: &Str, old: i8, new: i8) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    result.len = s.len
    var i = 0
    while i < s.len {
        let ch = s.data[i as usize]
        result.data[i as usize] = if ch == old { new } else { ch }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Reverse
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_reverse(s: &Str) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    result.len = s.len
    var i = 0
    while i < s.len {
        result.data[i as usize] = s.data[(s.len - 1 - i) as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Repeat n times (truncated at 256 bytes)
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_repeat(s: &Str, n: i32) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var result = str_new()
    if s.len == 0 || n <= 0 { return result }
    var rep = 0
    while rep < n && result.len < 256 {
        var i = 0
        while i < s.len && result.len < 256 {
            result.data[result.len as usize] = s.data[i as usize]
            result.len = result.len + 1
            i = i + 1
        }
        rep = rep + 1
    }
    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Number formatting helpers (private; must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

// Write decimal digits of |n| (n >= 0) into buf[pos..] in reverse order.
fn str_i64_to_buf(n: i64, buf: [i8; 64], pos: i32) -> ([i8; 64], i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var b = buf
    var p = pos
    var m = n
    while m > 0 {
        b[p as usize] = (48 + m % 10) as i8
        p = p + 1
        m = m / 10
    }
    (b, p)
}

// Reverse buf[lo..hi) in place.
fn str_buf64_rev(buf: [i8; 64], lo: i32, hi: i32) -> [i8; 64] with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var b = buf
    var l = lo
    var h = hi - 1
    while l < h {
        let tmp = b[l as usize]
        b[l as usize] = b[h as usize]
        b[h as usize] = tmp
        l = l + 1
        h = h - 1
    }
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// str_from_i64 — integer to decimal Str
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_from_i64(val: i64) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var buf: [i8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var pos: i32 = 0

    if val == 0 {
        buf[0] = 48 as i8
        return str_from_buf_i64(&buf, 1)
    }

    let neg = val < 0
    let m   = if neg { 0 - val } else { val }

    let (buf2, digit_end) = str_i64_to_buf(m, buf, 0)
    var b  = buf2
    var de = digit_end

    if neg {
        b[de as usize] = 45 as i8  // '-'
        de = de + 1
    }

    let b2 = str_buf64_rev(b, 0, de)
    str_from_buf_i64(&b2, de)
}

// ============================================================================
// str_from_f64 — float to decimal Str with `decimals` fractional digits.
//                Uses round-half-up to avoid floating-point drift.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_from_f64(val: f64, decimals: i32) -> Str with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var buf: [i8; 64] = [0; 64]
    var pos: i32 = 0

    let neg = val < 0.0
    let ax  = if neg { 0.0 - val } else { val }

    if neg {
        buf[0] = 45 as i8  // '-'
        pos = 1
    }

    // Integer part
    let int_part  = ax as i64
    let int_start = pos

    if int_part == 0 {
        buf[pos as usize] = 48 as i8
        pos = pos + 1
    } else {
        let (buf2, digit_end) = str_i64_to_buf(int_part, buf, pos)
        buf = buf2
        pos = digit_end
        buf = str_buf64_rev(buf, int_start, pos)
    }

    // Fractional part
    if decimals > 0 {
        buf[pos as usize] = 46 as i8  // '.'
        pos = pos + 1

        // Scale and round
        var scale = 1.0
        var d = 0
        while d < decimals {
            scale = scale * 10.0
            d = d + 1
        }
        let frac_i = ((ax - int_part as f64) * scale + 0.5) as i64

        // Write digits right-to-left into temp buffer, then forward into buf
        var frac_tmp: [i8; 32] = [0; 32]
        var ft: i32 = 0
        var f  = frac_i
        var dc = 0
        while dc < decimals {
            frac_tmp[ft as usize] = (48 + f % 10) as i8
            f  = f / 10
            ft = ft + 1
            dc = dc + 1
        }
        var fi = ft - 1
        while fi >= 0 {
            buf[pos as usize] = frac_tmp[fi as usize]
            pos = pos + 1
            fi  = fi - 1
        }
    }

    str_from_buf_i64(&buf, pos)
}

// ============================================================================
// str_to_i64 — parse decimal integer.  Returns 0 on error.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_to_i64(s: &Str) -> i64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s.len == 0 { return 0 }
    var result: i64 = 0
    var i = 0
    let neg = s.data[0] == 45 as i8  // '-'
    if neg { i = 1 }
    while i < s.len {
        let ch = s.data[i as usize]
        if ch < 48 as i8 || ch > 57 as i8 { return 0 }
        result = result * 10 + (ch as i64 - 48)
        i = i + 1
    }
    if neg { 0 - result } else { result }
}

// ============================================================================
// str_to_f64 — parse decimal float.  Returns 0.0 on error.
// ============================================================================

pub fn str_to_f64(s: &Str) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if s.len == 0 { return 0.0 }
    var i = 0
    let neg = s.data[0] == 45 as i8  // '-'
    if neg { i = 1 }

    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    while i < s.len && s.data[i as usize] != 46 as i8 {  // stop at '.'
        let ch = s.data[i as usize]
        if ch < 48 as i8 || ch > 57 as i8 { return 0.0 }
        int_part = int_part * 10.0 + (ch as i64 - 48) as f64
        i = i + 1
    }

    var frac_part: f64 = 0.0
    if i < s.len && s.data[i as usize] == 46 as i8 {
        i = i + 1  // skip '.'
        var scale = 0.1
        while i < s.len {
            let ch = s.data[i as usize]
            if ch < 48 as i8 || ch > 57 as i8 { return 0.0 }
            frac_part = frac_part + (ch as i64 - 48) as f64 * scale
            scale = scale * 0.1
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    let result = int_part + frac_part
    if neg { 0.0 - result } else { result }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/sync/atomic.sio ===
// stdlib/sync/atomic — Atomic integer operations
//
// AtomicI64: lock-free atomic i64 for concurrent programming.
// Uses a simple spinlock pattern since we don't have hardware atomics yet.

struct AtomicI64 {
    val: i64,
}

fn atomic_new(v: i64) -> AtomicI64 {
    AtomicI64 { val: v }
}

fn atomic_load(a: &AtomicI64) -> i64 {
    a.val
}

fn atomic_store(a: &! AtomicI64, v: i64) {
    a.val = v
}

fn atomic_add(a: &! AtomicI64, delta: i64) -> i64 {
    let old = a.val
    a.val = a.val + delta
    old
}

fn atomic_sub(a: &! AtomicI64, delta: i64) -> i64 {
    let old = a.val
    a.val = a.val - delta
    old
}

fn atomic_cas(a: &! AtomicI64, expected: i64, desired: i64) -> bool {
    if a.val == expected {
        a.val = desired
        return true
    }
    return false
}


// === FILE: stdlib/sync/channel.sio ===
// stdlib/sync/channel — Single-producer single-consumer i64 channel
//
// IntChannel: bounded ring buffer for sending i64 between contexts.
// Capacity: 1024 elements.

let CHANNEL_CAP: i64 = 1024

struct IntChannel {
    buf: [i64; 1024],
    head: i64,
    tail: i64,
    count: i64,
    closed: i64,
}

impl IntChannel {
    fn new() -> IntChannel {
        IntChannel { buf: [0; 1024], head: 0, tail: 0, count: 0, closed: 0 }
    }

    fn send(self: &! IntChannel, val: i64) -> bool {
        if self.closed == 1 { return false }
        if self.count >= CHANNEL_CAP { return false }
        self.buf[self.tail] = val
        self.tail = (self.tail + 1) % CHANNEL_CAP
        self.count = self.count + 1
        true
    }

    fn recv(self: &! IntChannel) -> i64 {
        if self.count == 0 { return 0 }
        let val = self.buf[self.head]
        self.head = (self.head + 1) % CHANNEL_CAP
        self.count = self.count - 1
        val
    }

    fn is_empty(self: &IntChannel) -> bool {
        self.count == 0
    }

    fn len(self: &IntChannel) -> i64 {
        self.count
    }

    fn close(self: &! IntChannel) {
        self.closed = 1
    }

    fn is_closed(self: &IntChannel) -> bool {
        self.closed == 1
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/sync/mutex.sio ===
// stdlib/sync/mutex — Mutex via pthread FFI
//
// Provides mutual exclusion using POSIX threads.
// pthread_mutex_t is heap-allocated (stable address required by pthreads).
// Functions: mutex_new, mutex_lock, mutex_try_lock, mutex_unlock,
//            mutex_destroy, mutex_is_locked

extern "C" {
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
    fn pthread_mutex_init(mutex: *mut u8, attr: *mut u8) -> i32;
    fn pthread_mutex_lock(mutex: *mut u8) -> i32;
    fn pthread_mutex_trylock(mutex: *mut u8) -> i32;
    fn pthread_mutex_unlock(mutex: *mut u8) -> i32;
    fn pthread_mutex_destroy(mutex: *mut u8) -> i32;
}

// pthread_mutex_t is ~48 bytes on Linux x86-64. We allocate 64 bytes
// to give headroom across platforms and alignment variants.
struct Mutex {
    ptr: *mut u8,
}

// Allocate and initialize a new mutex with default attributes.
fn mutex_new() -> Mutex {
    let ptr = malloc(64 as usize)
    let null_attr = (0 as usize) as *mut u8
    let _rc = pthread_mutex_init(ptr, null_attr)
    Mutex { ptr: ptr }
}

// Block until the mutex is acquired.
fn mutex_lock(m: &! Mutex) {
    let _rc = pthread_mutex_lock(m.ptr)
}

// Try to acquire the mutex without blocking.
// Returns true if the lock was acquired, false if already held.
fn mutex_try_lock(m: &! Mutex) -> bool {
    let rc = pthread_mutex_trylock(m.ptr)
    rc == 0
}

// Release the mutex. Caller must hold the lock.
fn mutex_unlock(m: &! Mutex) {
    let _rc = pthread_mutex_unlock(m.ptr)
}

// Destroy the mutex and free its heap storage.
// After this call the Mutex must not be used.
fn mutex_destroy(m: &! Mutex) {
    let _rc = pthread_mutex_destroy(m.ptr)
    free(m.ptr)
    m.ptr = (0 as usize) as *mut u8
}

// Returns true if the mutex handle is valid (initialized and not yet destroyed).
fn mutex_is_valid(m: &Mutex) -> bool {
    (m.ptr as usize) != 0
}


// === FILE: stdlib/sync/rwlock.sio ===
// stdlib/sync/rwlock — Reader-writer lock
//
// RwLock: allows multiple concurrent readers or one exclusive writer.
// Single-threaded simulation using counters.

struct RwLock {
    readers: i64,
    writer: i64,
}

impl RwLock {
    fn new() -> RwLock {
        RwLock { readers: 0, writer: 0 }
    }

    fn read_lock(self: &! RwLock) -> bool {
        if self.writer != 0 { return false }
        self.readers = self.readers + 1
        true
    }

    fn read_unlock(self: &! RwLock) {
        if self.readers > 0 {
            self.readers = self.readers - 1
        }
    }

    fn write_lock(self: &! RwLock) -> bool {
        if self.writer != 0 { return false }
        if self.readers != 0 { return false }
        self.writer = 1
        true
    }

    fn write_unlock(self: &! RwLock) {
        self.writer = 0
    }

    fn reader_count(self: &RwLock) -> i64 {
        self.readers
    }

    fn is_write_locked(self: &RwLock) -> bool {
        self.writer != 0
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/systems/gpu.sio ===
// stdlib/systems/gpu.d
//
// GPU Computing — Sounio v0.79
//
// Every kernel launch tracks occupancy and error.
// Every memory transfer knows its bandwidth.
// Every computation has epistemic performance bounds.
//
// # Philosophy
//
// GPU computing is not just about raw speed.
// Real deployments face:
// - Memory bandwidth limits
// - Occupancy constraints
// - Numerical precision variance
// - Hardware-specific quirks
//
// Sounio makes GPU uncertainty EXPLICIT.
//
// # Features
//
// - Type-safe kernel definitions
// - Automatic occupancy optimization
// - Memory pool management
// - Cooperative group patterns
// - Multi-GPU orchestration

// ============================================================================
// DEVICE MANAGEMENT
// ============================================================================

// GPU device properties
struct DeviceProperties {
    id: i64,
    name: [u8],
    compute_capability_major: i64,
    compute_capability_minor: i64,
    total_memory: i64,
    multiprocessors: i64,
    max_threads_per_block: i64,
    max_threads_per_mp: i64,
    warp_size: i64,
    max_shared_memory_per_block: i64,
    max_registers_per_block: i64,
    memory_clock_mhz: i64,
    memory_bus_width: i64,
    l2_cache_size: i64,
}

// Theoretical peak memory bandwidth (GB/s)
fn device_peak_bandwidth_gbps(props: DeviceProperties) -> f64 {
    let effective_rate = (props.memory_clock_mhz as f64) * 2.0  // DDR
    let bytes_per_transfer = (props.memory_bus_width as f64) / 8.0
    return effective_rate * bytes_per_transfer / 1000.0  // GB/s
}

// Theoretical peak FLOPS (single precision)
fn device_peak_flops_sp(props: DeviceProperties) -> f64 {
    // Rough estimate: 128 CUDA cores per SM for modern GPUs
    let cores_per_sm = 128.0
    let clock_ghz = 1.5  // Approximate boost clock
    return (props.multiprocessors as f64) * cores_per_sm * clock_ghz * 2.0 * 1000000000.0  // FMA = 2 ops
}

// GPU device handle
struct Device {
    id: i64,
    properties: DeviceProperties,
    current_memory_used: i64,
}

// Create a simulated device
fn device_get(id: i64) -> Device {
    let props = DeviceProperties {
        id: id,
        name: "NVIDIA GPU",
        compute_capability_major: 8,
        compute_capability_minor: 6,
        total_memory: 25769803776,  // 24 GB
        multiprocessors: 84,
        max_threads_per_block: 1024,
        max_threads_per_mp: 1536,
        warp_size: 32,
        max_shared_memory_per_block: 49152,
        max_registers_per_block: 65536,
        memory_clock_mhz: 9501,
        memory_bus_width: 384,
        l2_cache_size: 6291456,
    }

    return Device { id: id, properties: props, current_memory_used: 0 }
}

fn device_available_memory(dev: Device) -> i64 {
    return dev.properties.total_memory - dev.current_memory_used
}

fn device_memory_utilization(dev: Device) -> f64 {
    return (dev.current_memory_used as f64) / (dev.properties.total_memory as f64)
}

// Thread block dimensions
struct Dim3 {
    x: i64,
    y: i64,
    z: i64,
}

fn dim3_new(x: i64, y: i64, z: i64) -> Dim3 {
    return Dim3 { x: x, y: y, z: z }
}

fn dim3_linear(n: i64) -> Dim3 {
    return Dim3 { x: n, y: 1, z: 1 }
}

fn dim3_square(n: i64) -> Dim3 {
    return Dim3 { x: n, y: n, z: 1 }
}

fn dim3_total(d: Dim3) -> i64 {
    return d.x * d.y * d.z
}

// Kernel launch configuration
struct LaunchConfig {
    grid: Dim3,
    block: Dim3,
    shared_mem: i64,
    stream_id: i64,
}

fn launch_config_new(grid: Dim3, block: Dim3) -> LaunchConfig {
    return LaunchConfig { grid: grid, block: block, shared_mem: 0, stream_id: 0 }
}

fn launch_config_with_shared_mem(config: LaunchConfig, bytes: i64) -> LaunchConfig {
    return LaunchConfig {
        grid: config.grid,
        block: config.block,
        shared_mem: bytes,
        stream_id: config.stream_id
    }

    return LaunchConfig {
        grid: config.grid,
        block: config.block,
        shared_mem: config.shared_mem,
        stream_id: stream_id
    }
}

fn launch_config_total_threads(config: LaunchConfig) -> i64 {
    return dim3_total(config.grid) * dim3_total(config.block)
}

fn launch_config_total_blocks(config: LaunchConfig) -> i64 {
    return dim3_total(config.grid)
}

// ============================================================================
// OCCUPANCY CALCULATOR
// ============================================================================

// Occupancy calculation result
struct OccupancyResult {
    active_blocks_per_sm: i64,
    active_threads_per_sm: i64,
    occupancy: f64,
    limiting_factor: i64,  // 0=threads, 1=registers, 2=shared_memory
}

// Calculate theoretical occupancy
fn calculate_occupancy(
    props: DeviceProperties,
    block_size: i64,
    registers_per_thread: i64,
    shared_mem: i64
) -> OccupancyResult {

    // Threads per SM limited by block size
    let blocks_by_threads = props.max_threads_per_mp / block_size

    // Blocks limited by registers
    let registers_per_block = registers_per_thread * block_size
    var blocks_by_registers = blocks_by_threads
    if registers_per_block > 0 {
        blocks_by_registers = props.max_registers_per_block / registers_per_block
    }

    // Blocks limited by shared memory
    var blocks_by_shared = blocks_by_threads
    if shared_mem > 0 {
        blocks_by_shared = props.max_shared_memory_per_block / shared_mem
    }

    // Find minimum
    var active_blocks = blocks_by_threads
    var limiting_factor: i64 = 0

    if blocks_by_registers < active_blocks {
        active_blocks = blocks_by_registers
        limiting_factor = 1
    }
    if blocks_by_shared < active_blocks {
        active_blocks = blocks_by_shared
        limiting_factor = 2
    }

    let active_threads = active_blocks * block_size
    let occupancy = (active_threads as f64) / (props.max_threads_per_mp as f64)

    return OccupancyResult {
        active_blocks_per_sm: active_blocks,
        active_threads_per_sm: active_threads,
        occupancy: occupancy,
        limiting_factor: limiting_factor,
    }
}

// Find optimal block size for maximum occupancy
fn find_optimal_block_size(
    props: DeviceProperties,
    registers_per_thread: i64,
    shared_mem: i64
) -> i64 {
    var best_occupancy = 0.0
    var best_block_size: i64 = 32

    var block_size: i64 = 32
    while block_size <= 1024 {
        let result = calculate_occupancy(props, block_size, registers_per_thread, shared_mem)
        if result.occupancy > best_occupancy {
            best_occupancy = result.occupancy
            best_block_size = block_size
        }
        block_size = block_size + 32
    }

    return best_block_size
}

// ============================================================================
// COOPERATIVE GROUPS
// ============================================================================

// Cooperative group scope
// 0 = Thread, 1 = Warp, 2 = Block, 3 = Grid, 4 = MultiGrid
struct CooperativeGroup {
    scope: i64,
    size: i64,
    rank: i64,
}

fn cg_this_thread() -> CooperativeGroup {
    return CooperativeGroup { scope: 0, size: 1, rank: 0 }
}

fn cg_this_warp(lane_id: i64) -> CooperativeGroup {
    return CooperativeGroup { scope: 1, size: 32, rank: lane_id }
}

fn cg_this_block(thread_id: i64, block_size: i64) -> CooperativeGroup {
    return CooperativeGroup { scope: 2, size: block_size, rank: thread_id }
}

fn cg_this_grid(global_id: i64, grid_size: i64) -> CooperativeGroup {
    return CooperativeGroup { scope: 3, size: grid_size, rank: global_id }
}

// Warp-level ballot (simulated)
fn cg_ballot(group: CooperativeGroup, predicate: i64) -> i64 {
    if group.scope != 1 {  // Not a warp
        return 0
    }
    if predicate != 0 {
        return 1 << group.rank
    }
    return 0
}

// Warp-level shuffle (simulated)
fn cg_shfl(group: CooperativeGroup, value: f64, src_lane: i64) -> f64 {
    if group.scope != 1 {
        return value
    }
    // Simulated: would return src_lane's value
    return value
}

// Warp-level reduction sum (simulated)
fn cg_reduce_sum(group: CooperativeGroup, value: f64) -> f64 {
    if group.scope != 1 {
        return value
    }
    // Simulated: returns value * warp_size as placeholder
    return value * 32.0
}

// ============================================================================
// KERNEL RESULT WITH EPISTEMIC TRACKING
// ============================================================================

// Kernel execution result with performance metrics
struct KernelResult {
    kernel_type: i64,  // 0=reduce, 1=scan_inclusive, 2=scan_exclusive
    execution_time_ms: f64,
    gflops: f64,
    bandwidth_gbps: f64,
    occupancy: f64,
    success: i64,  // 1 = success, 0 = failure
}

fn kernel_result_efficiency(result: KernelResult, peak_bandwidth: f64) -> f64 {
    return result.bandwidth_gbps / peak_bandwidth
}

// ============================================================================
// REDUCTION PATTERN
// ============================================================================

// Reduction configuration
struct ReductionConfig {
    block_size: i64,
    items_per_thread: i64,
    use_warp_reduce: i64,  // 1 = true, 0 = false
}

fn reduction_config_default() -> ReductionConfig {
    return ReductionConfig { block_size: 256, items_per_thread: 8, use_warp_reduce: 1 }
}

// Simulate parallel reduction kernel
fn parallel_reduce(n: i64, config: ReductionConfig) -> KernelResult {
    let items_per_block = config.block_size * config.items_per_thread
    let grid_size = (n + items_per_block - 1) / items_per_block

    // Estimate performance
    let ops = (n as f64) * 2.0
    let bytes = (n as f64) * 4.0 + (grid_size as f64) * 4.0
    let bandwidth_estimate = 500.0 * 1000000000.0  // 500 GB/s typical
    let time_s = bytes / bandwidth_estimate
    let time_ms = time_s * 1000.0

    return KernelResult {
        kernel_type: 0,  // reduce
        execution_time_ms: time_ms,
        gflops: ops / time_s / 1000000000.0,
        bandwidth_gbps: bytes / time_s / 1000000000.0,
        occupancy: 0.75,
        success: 1,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// SCAN PATTERN
// ============================================================================

// Scan configuration
struct ScanConfig {
    block_size: i64,
    items_per_thread: i64,
    inclusive: i64,  // 1 = inclusive, 0 = exclusive
}

fn scan_config_default() -> ScanConfig {
    return ScanConfig { block_size: 256, items_per_thread: 4, inclusive: 1 }
}

fn scan_config_exclusive(config: ScanConfig) -> ScanConfig {
    return ScanConfig {
        block_size: config.block_size,
        items_per_thread: config.items_per_thread,
        inclusive: 0,
    }
}

// Simulate parallel scan kernel
fn parallel_scan(n: i64, config: ScanConfig) -> KernelResult {
    let time_ms = 0.5
    let ops = (n as f64) * 2.0
    let bytes = (n as f64) * 4.0 * 2.0

    var kernel_type: i64 = 1  // inclusive_scan
    if config.inclusive == 0 {
        kernel_type = 2  // exclusive_scan
    }

    return KernelResult {
        kernel_type: kernel_type,
        execution_time_ms: time_ms,
        gflops: ops / (time_ms / 1000.0) / 1000000000.0,
        bandwidth_gbps: bytes / (time_ms / 1000.0) / 1000000000.0,
        occupancy: 0.7,
        success: 1,
    }
}

// CUDA event abstraction
struct GpuEvent {
    id: i64,
    device_id: i64,
    recorded: i64,  // 1 = recorded, 0 = not recorded
}

fn event_create(device_id: i64) -> GpuEvent {
    return GpuEvent { id: device_id * 10000 + 1, device_id: device_id, recorded: 0 }
}

fn event_record(evt: GpuEvent, stream: GpuStream) -> GpuEvent {
    return GpuEvent { id: evt.id, device_id: evt.device_id, recorded: 1 }
}

fn event_elapsed_time(start: GpuEvent, end: GpuEvent) -> f64 {
    // Simulated elapsed time
    return 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// MEMORY POOL
// ============================================================================

// Memory pool entry
struct PoolEntry {
    ptr: i64,
    size: i64,
}

// Memory pool for efficient GPU allocations
struct MemoryPool {
    device_id: i64,
    block_size: i64,
    next_ptr: i64,
    total_allocated: i64,
}

fn memory_pool_new(device_id: i64, block_size: i64) -> MemoryPool {
    return MemoryPool {
        device_id: device_id,
        block_size: block_size,
        next_ptr: 8192,  // Starting address
        total_allocated: 0,
    }
}

fn memory_pool_allocate(pool: MemoryPool, size: i64) -> (MemoryPool, i64) {
    // Round up to block size
    let aligned_size = ((size + pool.block_size - 1) / pool.block_size) * pool.block_size

    let ptr = pool.next_ptr
    let new_pool = MemoryPool {
        device_id: pool.device_id,
        block_size: pool.block_size,
        next_ptr: pool.next_ptr + aligned_size,
        total_allocated: pool.total_allocated + aligned_size,
    }

    return (new_pool, ptr)
}

    id: i64,

}

    // In real implementation, would use atomic counter
    return CudaGraph { id: 1, node_count: 0 }
}

fn cuda_graph_add_kernel(graph: CudaGraph, threads: i64) -> CudaGraph {
    return CudaGraph { id: graph.id, node_count: graph.node_count + 1 }
}

fn cuda_graph_add_memcpy_h2d(graph: CudaGraph, size: i64) -> CudaGraph {
    return CudaGraph { id: graph.id, node_count: graph.node_count + 1 }
}

fn cuda_graph_add_memcpy_d2h(graph: CudaGraph, size: i64) -> CudaGraph {
    return CudaGraph { id: graph.id, node_count: graph.node_count + 1 }
}

    graph_id: i64,
    instantiated: i64,
}

fn cuda_graph_instantiate(graph: CudaGraph) -> GraphExec {
    return GraphExec { graph_id: graph.id, instantiated: 1 }
}

fn graph_exec_launch(exec: GraphExec, stream: GpuStream) -> i64 {
    if exec.instantiated == 0 {
        return 0  // Error
    }
    return 1  // Success
}

// ============================================================================
// UTILITY FUNCTIONS

// Calculate grid dimensions for 1D problem
fn calc_grid_1d(n: i64, block_size: i64) -> Dim3 {
    let grid_x = (n + block_size - 1) / block_size
    return dim3_linear(grid_x)
}

// Calculate grid dimensions for 2D problem
fn calc_grid_2d(width: i64, height: i64, block_x: i64, block_y: i64) -> Dim3 {
    let grid_x = (width + block_x - 1) / block_x
    let grid_y = (height + block_y - 1) / block_y
    return dim3_new(grid_x, grid_y, 1)
}

// Estimate memory bandwidth utilization
fn estimate_bandwidth_utilization(
    bytes_transferred: i64,
    time_ms: f64,
    peak_bandwidth_gbps: f64
) -> f64 {
    let actual_gbps = (bytes_transferred as f64) / (time_ms / 1000.0) / 1000000000.0
    return actual_gbps / peak_bandwidth_gbps
}

// Check if problem size fits in GPU memory
fn can_fit_in_memory(problem_bytes: i64, available_bytes: i64) -> i64 {
    if problem_bytes <= available_bytes {
        return 1
    }
    return 0
}

// ============================================================================
// MULTI-GPU HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Distribute work across multiple GPUs
fn distribute_work(total_items: i64, n_gpus: i64) -> i64 {
    // Items per GPU (ceiling division)
    return (total_items + n_gpus - 1) / n_gpus
}

// Calculate work range for a specific GPU
fn work_range_for_gpu(
    total_items: i64,
    gpu_id: i64,
    n_gpus: i64
) -> (i64, i64) {
    let items_per_gpu = distribute_work(total_items, n_gpus)
    let start = gpu_id * items_per_gpu
    var end = start + items_per_gpu
    if end > total_items {
        end = total_items
    }
    return (start, end)
}

// ============================================================================
// PERFORMANCE HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Calculate arithmetic intensity (FLOP/byte)
fn arithmetic_intensity(flops: f64, bytes: f64) -> f64 {
    if bytes < 0.0001 {
        return 0.0
    }
    return flops / bytes
}

// Determine if kernel is compute or memory bound
// Returns 1 if compute bound, 0 if memory bound
fn is_compute_bound(
    ai: f64,           // Arithmetic intensity
    peak_flops: f64,   // Peak compute (GFLOPS)
    peak_bw: f64       // Peak bandwidth (GB/s)
) -> i64 {
    let ridge_point = peak_flops / peak_bw
    if ai > ridge_point {
        return 1
    }
    return 0
}

// Roofline model: predict maximum achievable performance
fn roofline_performance(
    ai: f64,
    peak_flops: f64,
    peak_bw: f64
) -> f64 {
    let memory_roof = ai * peak_bw
    if memory_roof < peak_flops {
        return memory_roof
    }
    return peak_flops
}


// === FILE: stdlib/systems/lib.sio ===
//! stdlib/systems/lib.sio - Dynamical systems
//!
//! Provides numerical integration of classical continuous dynamical systems:
//! Lorenz attractor, Rössler attractor, van der Pol oscillator, pendulum.
//!
//! All integrators use explicit forward Euler with configurable step size.
//! For production use, prefer stdlib/ode for adaptive RK4/RK45.
//!
//! Effects:
//!   Mut   — functions use mutable local state
//!   Div   — functions contain loops (may diverge)
//!   Panic — functions perform division or array indexing
//!
//! References:
//!   - Lorenz (1963): "Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow", J. Atmos. Sci.
//!   - Rössler (1976): "An equation for continuous chaos", Phys. Lett. A
//!   - Van der Pol (1926): "On relaxation-oscillations", Phil. Mag.
//!   - Strogatz (1994): "Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos"

use math::pure::*

// =============================================================================
// SystemState — generic n-dimensional state vector (n ≤ 16)
// =============================================================================

pub struct SystemState {
    pub x: [f64; 16],
    pub n: i32,
    pub t: f64,
}

// Create a zeroed SystemState with dimension n
pub fn system_state_new(n: i32) -> SystemState with Mut, Panic {
    var s: SystemState
    s.n = n
    s.t = 0.0
    s.x[0] = 0.0
    s.x[1] = 0.0
    s.x[2] = 0.0
    s.x[3] = 0.0
    s.x[4] = 0.0
    s.x[5] = 0.0
    s.x[6] = 0.0
    s.x[7] = 0.0
    s.x[8] = 0.0
    s.x[9] = 0.0
    s.x[10] = 0.0
    s.x[11] = 0.0
    s.x[12] = 0.0
    s.x[13] = 0.0
    s.x[14] = 0.0
    s.x[15] = 0.0
    return s
}

// =============================================================================
// Lorenz attractor
// dx/dt = σ(y - x)
// dy/dt = x(ρ - z) - y
// dz/dt = xy - βz
//
// State layout: x[0]=x, x[1]=y, x[2]=z
// Standard chaotic parameters: σ=10, ρ=28, β=8/3
// =============================================================================

pub fn lorenz_step(state: SystemState, dt: f64, sigma: f64, rho: f64, beta: f64) -> SystemState with Mut, Panic {
    let cx = state.x[0]
    let cy = state.x[1]
    let cz = state.x[2]

    let dx = sigma * (cy - cx)
    let dy = cx * (rho - cz) - cy
    let dz = cx * cy - beta * cz

    var ns: SystemState
    ns.n = state.n
    ns.t = state.t + dt
    ns.x[0] = cx + dt * dx
    ns.x[1] = cy + dt * dy
    ns.x[2] = cz + dt * dz
    ns.x[3] = 0.0
    ns.x[4] = 0.0
    ns.x[5] = 0.0
    ns.x[6] = 0.0
    ns.x[7] = 0.0
    ns.x[8] = 0.0
    ns.x[9] = 0.0
    ns.x[10] = 0.0
    ns.x[11] = 0.0
    ns.x[12] = 0.0
    ns.x[13] = 0.0
    ns.x[14] = 0.0
    ns.x[15] = 0.0
    return ns
}

// Simulate Lorenz attractor from (x0,y0,z0) with default parameters σ=10, ρ=28, β=8/3
// Returns final state after n_steps steps
pub fn lorenz_simulate(x0: f64, y0: f64, z0: f64, dt: f64, n_steps: i32) -> SystemState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var state = system_state_new(3)
    state.x[0] = x0
    state.x[1] = y0
    state.x[2] = z0

    let sigma = 10.0
    let rho = 28.0
    let beta = 2.6666666666666665

    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        state = lorenz_step(state, dt, sigma, rho, beta)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return state
}

// =============================================================================
// Rössler attractor
// dx/dt = -y - z
// dy/dt = x + ay
// dz/dt = b + z(x - c)
//
// State layout: x[0]=x, x[1]=y, x[2]=z
// Standard chaotic parameters: a=0.2, b=0.2, c=5.7
// =============================================================================

pub fn rossler_step(state: SystemState, dt: f64, a: f64, b: f64, c: f64) -> SystemState with Mut, Panic {
    let cx = state.x[0]
    let cy = state.x[1]
    let cz = state.x[2]

    let dx = (0.0 - cy) - cz
    let dy = cx + a * cy
    let dz = b + cz * (cx - c)

    var ns: SystemState
    ns.n = state.n
    ns.t = state.t + dt
    ns.x[0] = cx + dt * dx
    ns.x[1] = cy + dt * dy
    ns.x[2] = cz + dt * dz
    ns.x[3] = 0.0
    ns.x[4] = 0.0
    ns.x[5] = 0.0
    ns.x[6] = 0.0
    ns.x[7] = 0.0
    ns.x[8] = 0.0
    ns.x[9] = 0.0
    ns.x[10] = 0.0
    ns.x[11] = 0.0
    ns.x[12] = 0.0
    ns.x[13] = 0.0
    ns.x[14] = 0.0
    ns.x[15] = 0.0
    return ns
}

// =============================================================================
// Van der Pol oscillator
// dx/dt = y
// dy/dt = μ(1 - x²)y - x
//
// State layout: x[0]=x (position), x[1]=y (velocity)
// μ>0 gives self-sustained limit cycle oscillations
// =============================================================================

pub fn van_der_pol_step(state: SystemState, dt: f64, mu: f64) -> SystemState with Mut, Panic {
    let cx = state.x[0]
    let cy = state.x[1]

    let dx = cy
    let dy = mu * (1.0 - cx * cx) * cy - cx

    var ns: SystemState
    ns.n = state.n
    ns.t = state.t + dt
    ns.x[0] = cx + dt * dx
    ns.x[1] = cy + dt * dy
    ns.x[2] = 0.0
    ns.x[3] = 0.0
    ns.x[4] = 0.0
    ns.x[5] = 0.0
    ns.x[6] = 0.0
    ns.x[7] = 0.0
    ns.x[8] = 0.0
    ns.x[9] = 0.0
    ns.x[10] = 0.0
    ns.x[11] = 0.0
    ns.x[12] = 0.0
    ns.x[13] = 0.0
    ns.x[14] = 0.0
    ns.x[15] = 0.0
    return ns
}

// =============================================================================
// Simple pendulum
// dθ/dt = ω
// dω/dt = -(g/l) sin(θ)
//
// State layout: x[0]=θ (angle, rad), x[1]=ω (angular velocity, rad/s)
// =============================================================================

pub fn pendulum_step(state: SystemState, dt: f64, g: f64, l: f64) -> SystemState with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let theta = state.x[0]
    let omega = state.x[1]

    let dtheta = omega
    let domega = (0.0 - g) / l * sin(theta)

    var ns: SystemState
    ns.n = state.n
    ns.t = state.t + dt
    ns.x[0] = theta + dt * dtheta
    ns.x[1] = omega + dt * domega
    ns.x[2] = 0.0
    ns.x[3] = 0.0
    ns.x[4] = 0.0
    ns.x[5] = 0.0
    ns.x[6] = 0.0
    ns.x[7] = 0.0
    ns.x[8] = 0.0
    ns.x[9] = 0.0
    ns.x[10] = 0.0
    ns.x[11] = 0.0
    ns.x[12] = 0.0
    ns.x[13] = 0.0
    ns.x[14] = 0.0
    ns.x[15] = 0.0
    return ns
}

// =============================================================================
// Lyapunov exponent estimate
//
// Crude finite-difference estimate of the largest Lyapunov exponent from
// a scalar trajectory stored in states[0..n-1].
// Uses log of mean separation between successive pairs of adjacent points.
//
// Method: approximate λ ≈ (1/T) * Σ log(|x_{i+1} - x_i| / δ₀)
// where δ₀ is the initial separation (first difference).
// Returns a crude estimate suitable for sign-based chaos detection.
//
// Reference: Sprott (2003) "Chaos and Time-Series Analysis" §5.2
// =============================================================================

pub fn lyapunov_estimate(states: &[f64; 256], n: i32, dt: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if n < 4 { return 0.0 }

    // Use the first difference as reference separation
    let d0 = states[1] - states[0]
    let abs_d0 = if d0 < 0.0 { 0.0 - d0 } else { d0 }
    if abs_d0 < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }

    var sum = 0.0
    var count = 0
    var i = 1
    while i < n - 1 {
        let d = states[i + 1] - states[i]
        let abs_d = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
        if abs_d > 1.0e-15 {
            let ratio = abs_d / abs_d0
            if ratio > 0.0 {
                sum = sum + ln(ratio)
                count = count + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if count == 0 { return 0.0 }

    let total_time = dt * count
    if total_time < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }

    return sum / total_time
}


// === FILE: stdlib/test/assert_advanced.sio ===
// stdlib/test/assert_advanced.sio — Advanced Assertion Utilities
//
// Provides:
//   - SoftAssertions: collect deferred failures, report at end
//   - AsserterF64: fluent assertions for f64 values
//   - AsserterI64: fluent assertions for i64 values
//   - AsserterBool: fluent assertions for bool values
//
// Design: no panics — all functions return bool (true=pass) or i64 (0=pass).
// Callers inspect return values or use soft_assert_all to bulk-check.

// ============================================================================
// Math helpers
// ============================================================================

fn assert_abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// SoftAssertions — collect up to 64 deferred failures
// ============================================================================

struct SoftAssertions {
    messages: [string; 64],
    count: i64,
    label: string
}

/// Create a new empty SoftAssertions collector.
pub fn soft_assertions_new() -> SoftAssertions {
    SoftAssertions {
        messages: [""; 64],
        count: 0,
        label: ""
    }
}

/// Create a labeled SoftAssertions collector.
pub fn soft_assertions_labeled(label: string) -> SoftAssertions {
    SoftAssertions {
        messages: [""; 64],
        count: 0,
        label: label
    }
}

/// Assert that |got - expected| <= tol. Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_near_f64(sa: &!SoftAssertions, got: f64, expected: f64, tol: f64, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    let diff = assert_abs_f64(got - expected)
    if diff <= tol { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Assert that got == expected (i64). Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_eq_i64(sa: &!SoftAssertions, got: i64, expected: i64, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    if got == expected { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Assert that cond is true. Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_true(sa: &!SoftAssertions, cond: bool, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    if cond { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Assert that cond is false. Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_false(sa: &!SoftAssertions, cond: bool, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    if !cond { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Assert that lo <= x <= hi. Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_in_range_f64(sa: &!SoftAssertions, x: f64, lo: f64, hi: f64, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= lo && x <= hi { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Assert that x > 0.0. Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_positive(sa: &!SoftAssertions, x: f64, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    if x > 0.0 { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Assert that x >= 0.0. Records failure if not.
pub fn soft_assert_non_negative(sa: &!SoftAssertions, x: f64, msg: string) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0.0 { return }
    if sa.count < 64 {
        sa.messages[sa.count as usize] = msg
        sa.count = sa.count + 1
    }
}

/// Returns the number of recorded failures.
pub fn soft_assert_count(sa: SoftAssertions) -> i64 {
    sa.count
}

/// Print all failures and return 0 if all passed, failure count otherwise.
pub fn soft_assert_all(sa: SoftAssertions) -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    if sa.count == 0 { return 0 }
    if sa.label != "" {
        println("SoftAssertions [", sa.label, "]: ", sa.count, " failure(s)")
    } else {
        println("SoftAssertions: ", sa.count, " failure(s)")
    }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < sa.count && i < 64 {
        println("  FAIL[", i, "]: ", sa.messages[i as usize])
        i = i + 1
    }
    sa.count
}

// ============================================================================
// AsserterF64 — fluent asserter for f64
// ============================================================================

struct AsserterF64 { value: f64, description: string }

/// Create an f64 asserter for the given value.
pub fn asserter_f64(x: f64) -> AsserterF64 {
    AsserterF64 { value: x, description: "" }
}

/// Set a description for this asserter (returned in failure messages).
pub fn asserter_f64_described_as(a: AsserterF64, desc: string) -> AsserterF64 {
    AsserterF64 { value: a.value, description: desc }
}

/// Assert that value == expected (exact equality). Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_f64_is_equal_to(a: AsserterF64, expected: f64) -> bool with IO {
    if a.value == expected { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected ", expected, " but got ", a.value)
    false
}

/// Assert that |value - expected| <= tol. Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_f64_is_near(a: AsserterF64, expected: f64, tol: f64) -> bool with IO {
    let diff = assert_abs_f64(a.value - expected)
    if diff <= tol { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected near ", expected, " (tol=", tol, ") but got ", a.value, " (diff=", diff, ")")
    false
}

/// Assert that value > bound. Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_f64_is_greater_than(a: AsserterF64, bound: f64) -> bool with IO {
    if a.value > bound { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected > ", bound, " but got ", a.value)
    false
}

    if a.value < bound { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected < ", bound, " but got ", a.value)
    false
}

    if a.value >= lo && a.value <= hi { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected in [", lo, ", ", hi, "] but got ", a.value)
    false
}

/// Assert that value > 0.0. Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_f64_is_positive(a: AsserterF64) -> bool with IO {
    if a.value > 0.0 { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected positive but got ", a.value)
    false
}

/// Assert that value >= 0.0. Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_f64_is_non_negative(a: AsserterF64) -> bool with IO {
    if a.value >= 0.0 { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected non-negative but got ", a.value)
    false
}

struct AsserterBool { value: bool, description: string }

/// Create a bool asserter for the given value.
pub fn asserter_bool(x: bool) -> AsserterBool {
    AsserterBool { value: x, description: "" }
}

/// Set a description for this asserter.
pub fn asserter_bool_described_as(a: AsserterBool, desc: string) -> AsserterBool {
    AsserterBool { value: a.value, description: desc }
}

/// Assert that value is true. Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_bool_is_true(a: AsserterBool) -> bool with IO {
    if a.value { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected true but got false")
    false
}

/// Assert that value is false. Returns true if passed.
pub fn asserter_bool_is_false(a: AsserterBool) -> bool with IO {
    if !a.value { return true }
    println("FAIL: [", a.description, "] expected false but got true")
    false
}

// === FILE: stdlib/test/helpers.sio ===
//! stdlib/test/helpers.sio - Simple test helpers for numerical comparisons
//!
//! This module provides simple helper functions for test files that work
//! with the current Sounio compiler without requiring advanced features.
//!
//! # Usage
//!
//! ```sio
//! use test::helpers::*
//!
//! fn run_tests() -> i32 {
//!     var pass = 0
//!     var fail = 0
//!
//!     if check_near(compute(), expected, 1e-6) {
//!         pass = pass + 1
//!     } else {
//!         fail = fail + 1
//!     }
//!
//!     if fail > 0 { return 1 }
//!     return 0
//! }
//! ```

// ============================================================================
// Floating-point comparison helpers (f64)
// ============================================================================

/// Check if two f64 values are within tolerance (absolute difference)
pub fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

/// Check if two f64 values are within relative tolerance
pub fn check_near_relative(a: f64, b: f64, rtol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    let max_abs = if a > b { a } else { b }
    if max_abs < 1e-300 {
        ad < rtol
    } else {
        ad < rtol * max_abs
    }
}

/// Check if two f64 values are approximately equal (default tolerance 1e-9)
pub fn check_approx(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    check_near(a, b, 1e-9)
}

/// Check if an f64 value is close to zero
pub fn check_near_zero(x: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let ax = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
    ax < tol
}

/// Check if an f64 value is NaN-like (NaN or very large)
pub fn check_nan_like(x: f64) -> bool {
    x != x
}

// ============================================================================
// Floating-point comparison helpers (f32)
// ============================================================================

/// Check if two f32 values are within tolerance (absolute difference)
pub fn check_near_f32(a: f32, b: f32, tol: f32) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

/// Check if two f32 values are approximately equal (default tolerance 1e-5)
pub fn check_approx_f32(a: f32, b: f32) -> bool {
    check_near_f32(a, b, 1e-5)
}

// ============================================================================
// Integer comparison helpers
// ============================================================================

/// Check if two i64 values are equal
pub fn check_eq_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> bool {
    a == b
}

/// Check if two i32 values are equal
pub fn check_eq_i32(a: i32, b: i32) -> bool {
    a == b
}

/// Check if an i64 value is within a range (inclusive)
pub fn check_in_range_i64(x: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> bool {
    x >= lo && x <= hi
}

// ============================================================================
// Test runner helpers
// ============================================================================

/// Simple test result accumulator
struct TestResult {
    pass: i32,
    fail: i32
}

/// Create a new test result
pub fn test_result_new() -> TestResult {
    TestResult { pass: 0, fail: 0 }
}

/// Record a passing test
pub fn test_pass(r: &!TestResult) with Mut {
    r.pass = r.pass + 1
}

/// Record a failing test
pub fn test_fail(r: &!TestResult) with Mut {
    r.fail = r.fail + 1
}

/// Check if all tests passed
pub fn test_all_passed(r: &TestResult) -> bool {
    r.fail == 0
}

/// Get exit code (0 for pass, 1 for fail)
pub fn test_exit_code(r: &TestResult) -> i32 {
    if r.fail > 0 { 1 } else { 0 }
}

/// Print test summary
pub fn test_print_summary(r: &TestResult) with IO {
    print("Passed: ")
    print(r.pass)
    print(" Failed: ")
    print(r.fail)
    print("\n")
}

// ============================================================================
// Assertion helpers (return bool instead of panicking)
// ============================================================================

/// Assert-like helper that returns bool for use in test accumulator pattern
pub fn assert_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64, name: string) -> bool with IO {
    if check_near(a, b, tol) {
        print("PASS: ")
        print(name)
        print("\n")
        true
    } else {
        print("FAIL: ")
        print(name)
        print(" (expected ~")
        print(b)
        print(", got ")
        print(a)
        print(")\n")
        false
    }
}

/// Assert-like helper for exact equality
pub fn assert_eq_i64(a: i64, b: i64, name: string) -> bool with IO {
    if a == b {
        print("PASS: ")
        print(name)
        print("\n")
        true
    } else {
        print("FAIL: ")
        print(name)
        print(" (expected ")
        print(b)
        print(", got ")
        print(a)
        print(")\n")
        false
    }
}
