// Prove decay bound: epsilon_0 * exp(-lambda * t) >= min_epsilon
// Maps to ProofKind::DecayBound
fn tac_decay_bound(ts: &! TacticStore, lambda: f64, t: f64) -> i32 {
    let tac = Tactic { tag: TAC_DECAY_BOUND, sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, payload_i: 0, payload_f: lambda * t, max_iters: 0 }
    return tac_store_alloc(ts, tac)
}

// Prove confidence monotonicity: Maps to ProofKind::MonoMul
fn tac_monotone(ts: &! TacticStore) -> i32 {
    let t = Tactic { tag: TAC_MONOTONE, sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, payload_i: 0, payload_f: 0.0, max_iters: 0 }
    return tac_store_alloc(ts, t)
}

// ============================================================================
// TACTIC APPLICATION ENGINE
// ============================================================================

// Apply a single tactic to a goal, return TacticResult
fn apply_tactic(ctx: &! ProofContext, ts: &TacticStore, tac_id: i32, goal: Goal) -> TacticResult {
    let tac = tac_store_get(ts, tac_id)
    let target = goal.target_prop_id
    let target_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, target)

    // TAC_REFL: prove a = a
    if tac.tag == TAC_REFL {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            if target_prop.eq_lhs == target_prop.eq_rhs {
                let prf_id = refl(ctx, target_prop.eq_lhs)
                return tac_success(prf_id)
            }
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_TRIVIAL: prove True
    if tac.tag == TAC_TRIVIAL {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_TRUE {
            let prf_id = true_intro(ctx)
            return tac_success(prf_id)
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_EXACT: use provided proof
    if tac.tag == TAC_EXACT {
        let prf_id = tac.payload_i
        let prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, prf_id)
        if prf.tag >= 0 {
            return tac_success(prf_id)
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_ASSUMPTION: search assumption context
    if tac.tag == TAC_ASSUMPTION {
        var i: i32 = 0
        while i < goal.num_assumptions {
            let idx = i as i64
            let prf_id = goal.assumptions[idx * 2 + 1]
            let prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, prf_id)
            if prf.prop_id == target {
                return tac_success(prf_id)
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_SPLIT: for P /\ Q goals, create two subgoals
    if tac.tag == TAC_SPLIT {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_AND {
            var result = tac_fail()
            result.success = true
            result.remaining = 2
            result.subgoals[0] = target_prop.left_id
            result.subgoals[1] = target_prop.right_id
            return result
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_LEFT: choose left of P \/ Q
    if tac.tag == TAC_LEFT {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_OR {
            var result = tac_fail()
            result.success = true
            result.remaining = 1
            result.subgoals[0] = target_prop.left_id
            return result
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_RIGHT: choose right of P \/ Q
    if tac.tag == TAC_RIGHT {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_OR {
            var result = tac_fail()
            result.success = true
            result.remaining = 1
            result.subgoals[0] = target_prop.right_id
            return result
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_INTRO: introduce hypothesis for P -> Q
    if tac.tag == TAC_INTRO {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_IMPLIES {
            var result = tac_fail()
            result.success = true
            result.remaining = 1
            result.subgoals[0] = target_prop.right_id
            return result
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_RING: prove ring identity by normalization
    if tac.tag == TAC_RING {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            // Ring normalization: compute both sides, check equality
            let lhs = target_prop.eq_lhs
            let rhs = target_prop.eq_rhs
            if lhs == rhs {
                let prf_id = refl(ctx, lhs)
                return tac_success(prf_id)
            }
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_OMEGA: decide linear arithmetic
    if tac.tag == TAC_OMEGA {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            let lhs = target_prop.eq_lhs
            let rhs = target_prop.eq_rhs
            if lhs == rhs {
                let prf_id = refl(ctx, lhs)
                return tac_success(prf_id)
            }
        }
        // Custom linear arithmetic: any PROP_CUSTOM where tag encodes leq/lt
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_CUSTOM {
            // Assume valid if encoded as leq (tags 20000+)
            let prf_id = trusted(ctx, 5001, target, 1.0)
            return tac_success(prf_id)
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_SIMP: normalization + trivial simplifications
    if tac.tag == TAC_SIMP {
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_TRUE {
            let prf_id = true_intro(ctx)
            return tac_success(prf_id)
        }
        if target_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            if target_prop.eq_lhs == target_prop.eq_rhs {
                let prf_id = refl(ctx, target_prop.eq_lhs)
                return tac_success(prf_id)
            }
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // TAC_CONFIDENCE_CMP: prove epsilon_1 >= epsilon_2 by literal comparison
    if tac.tag == TAC_CONFIDENCE_CMP {
        let prf_id = trusted(ctx, 5010, target, 1.0)
        return tac_success(prf_id)
    }

    // TAC_DS_COMBINE: Dempster-Shafer combination
    if tac.tag == TAC_DS_COMBINE {
        let prf_id = trusted(ctx, 5011, target, 1.0)
        return tac_success(prf_id)
    }

    // TAC_DECAY_BOUND: epsilon_0 * exp(-lambda*t) >= threshold
    if tac.tag == TAC_DECAY_BOUND {
        let prf_id = trusted(ctx, 5012, target, 1.0)
        return tac_success(prf_id)
    }

    // TAC_MONOTONE: confidence monotonicity
    if tac.tag == TAC_MONOTONE {
        let prf_id = trusted(ctx, 5013, target, 1.0)
        return tac_success(prf_id)
    }

    // TAC_TRY: apply inner, succeed even if inner fails (returns trivial proof)
    if tac.tag == TAC_TRY {
        let inner_result = apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac.sub1_id, goal)
        if inner_result.success {
            return inner_result
        }
        // Return success with a trusted fallback
        let prf_id = trusted(ctx, 5020, target, 0.9)
        return tac_success(prf_id)
    }

    // TAC_ALT: try first, if fail try second
    if tac.tag == TAC_ALT {
        let r1 = apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac.sub1_id, goal)
        if r1.success {
            return r1
        }
        return apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac.sub2_id, goal)
    }

    // TAC_THEN: apply first tactic, apply second to each subgoal
    if tac.tag == TAC_THEN {
        let r1 = apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac.sub1_id, goal)
        if r1.success == false {
            return r1
        }
        if r1.remaining == 0 {
            return r1
        }
        // Apply second tactic to first subgoal
        let sub_goal = goal_new(r1.subgoals[0])
        let r2 = apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac.sub2_id, sub_goal)
        return r2
    }

    // TAC_REPEAT: apply inner tactic repeatedly until failure
    if tac.tag == TAC_REPEAT {
        var current_goal = goal
        var last_result = tac_fail()
        var iter: i32 = 0
        let max = tac.max_iters
        var found = false
        while iter < max {
            let r = apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac.sub1_id, current_goal)
            if r.success == false {
                iter = max  // exit
            } else {
                last_result = r
                found = true
                if r.remaining > 0 {
                    current_goal = goal_new(r.subgoals[0])
                } else {
                    iter = max  // done
                }
                iter = iter + 1
            }
        }
        if found {
            return last_result
        }
        return tac_fail()
    }

    // EXFALSO: change goal to False, then apply inner
    if tac.tag == TAC_EXFALSO {
        let false_id = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_false())
        let false_goal = goal_new(false_id)
        var result = tac_fail()
        result.success = true
        result.remaining = 1
        result.subgoals[0] = false_id
        return result
    }

    return tac_fail()
}

// Solve a goal completely with a tactic. Returns proof ID or panics.
fn solve_goal(ctx: &! ProofContext, ts: &TacticStore, tac_id: i32, goal: Goal) -> i64 {
    let result = apply_tactic(ctx, ts, tac_id, goal)
    if result.success {
        return result.prf_id
    }
    // Fallback: runtime-checked proof
    return runtime_check(ctx, goal.target_prop_id)
}

// ============================================================================
// HIGH-LEVEL TACTIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Prove P /\ Q by proving P and Q separately
fn by_and_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext, p_prf_id: i64, q_prf_id: i64, pq_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    return and_intro(ctx, p_prf_id, q_prf_id, pq_prop_id)
}

// Prove P -> Q by assuming P and providing proof of Q
fn by_impl(ctx: &! ProofContext, p_prop_id: i64, q_prf_id: i64, impl_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let p_assume = assume(ctx, 9001, p_prop_id)
    return impl_intro(ctx, p_assume, q_prf_id, impl_prop_id)
}

// Prove forall x. P(x) by providing proof of P(x) for arbitrary x
fn by_forall(ctx: &! ProofContext, body_prf_id: i64, forall_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    return forall_intro(ctx, body_prf_id, forall_prop_id)
}

// Prove exists x. P(x) by providing witness and proof
fn by_exists(ctx: &! ProofContext, witness: i64, body_prf_id: i64, exists_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    return exists_intro(ctx, witness, body_prf_id, exists_prop_id)
}


// === FILE: stdlib/theorem/units.sio ===
// == kernel preamble inlined ==
// Sounio Proof Kernel — Core Proof Infrastructure
//
// Propositions-as-types, proof witnesses, natural deduction.
// Every Proof carries confidence — the fundamental departure from Lean/Coq.
//
// Mirrors the compiler's dependent/proofs.rs ProofKind (18 constructors)
// at the user level as a composable .sio API.
//
// Reference:
//   Curry-Howard correspondence (propositions = types, proofs = programs)
//   Sounio formal/lean4/SounioEpistemic.lean (confidence lattice)

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { a } else { b }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROPOSITION ARENA
// ============================================================================

// Maximum propositions in a single proof context
let PROP_ARENA_CAP: i64 = 4096

// Proposition tags
let PROP_TRUE: i32 = 0
let PROP_FALSE: i32 = 1
let PROP_AND: i32 = 2
let PROP_OR: i32 = 3
let PROP_IMPLIES: i32 = 4
let PROP_NOT: i32 = 5
let PROP_FORALL: i32 = 6
let PROP_EXISTS: i32 = 7
let PROP_EQ: i32 = 8
let PROP_CUSTOM: i32 = 9

// Proposition: tag-encoded logical claim
// Uses integer IDs to reference sub-propositions (arena-style, no recursion)
struct Prop {
    tag: i32,
    left_id: i64,       // sub-proposition (for And, Or, Implies, Not)
    right_id: i64,       // sub-proposition (for And, Or, Implies)
    var_name: i64,       // quantifier variable (for Forall, Exists)
    predicate_id: i64,   // custom predicate (for Eq, Custom)
    eq_lhs: i64,         // equality left (for Eq)
    eq_rhs: i64,         // equality right (for Eq)
}

// Arena: flat storage for propositions
struct PropArena {
    tags: [i32; 4096],
    left_ids: [i64; 4096],
    right_ids: [i64; 4096],
    var_names: [i64; 4096],
    predicate_ids: [i64; 4096],
    eq_lhs_vals: [i64; 4096],
    eq_rhs_vals: [i64; 4096],
    count: i64,
}

fn arena_new() -> PropArena {
    return PropArena {
        tags: [0; 4096],
        left_ids: [0; 4096],
        right_ids: [0; 4096],
        var_names: [0; 4096],
        predicate_ids: [0; 4096],
        eq_lhs_vals: [0; 4096],
        eq_rhs_vals: [0; 4096],
        count: 0,
    }
}

fn arena_alloc(arena: &! PropArena, p: Prop) -> i64 {
    let idx = arena.count
    if idx >= PROP_ARENA_CAP {
        return 0 - 1  // overflow sentinel
    }
    arena.tags[idx] = p.tag
    arena.left_ids[idx] = p.left_id
    arena.right_ids[idx] = p.right_id
    arena.var_names[idx] = p.var_name
    arena.predicate_ids[idx] = p.predicate_id
    arena.eq_lhs_vals[idx] = p.eq_lhs
    arena.eq_rhs_vals[idx] = p.eq_rhs
    arena.count = idx + 1
    return idx
}

fn arena_get(arena: &PropArena, idx: i64) -> Prop {
    if idx < 0 {
        return Prop { tag: PROP_FALSE, left_id: 0, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
    }
    if idx >= arena.count {
        return Prop { tag: PROP_FALSE, left_id: 0, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
    }
    return Prop {
        tag: arena.tags[idx],
        left_id: arena.left_ids[idx],
        right_id: arena.right_ids[idx],
        var_name: arena.var_names[idx],
        predicate_id: arena.predicate_ids[idx],
        eq_lhs: arena.eq_lhs_vals[idx],
        eq_rhs: arena.eq_rhs_vals[idx],
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROPOSITION CONSTRUCTORS
// ============================================================================

fn prop_true() -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_TRUE, left_id: 0, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_false() -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_FALSE, left_id: 0, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_and(left_id: i64, right_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_AND, left_id: left_id, right_id: right_id, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_or(left_id: i64, right_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_OR, left_id: left_id, right_id: right_id, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_implies(antecedent_id: i64, consequent_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_IMPLIES, left_id: antecedent_id, right_id: consequent_id, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_not(inner_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_NOT, left_id: inner_id, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_forall(var: i64, body_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_FORALL, left_id: body_id, right_id: 0, var_name: var, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_exists(var: i64, body_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_EXISTS, left_id: body_id, right_id: 0, var_name: var, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_eq(lhs: i64, rhs: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_EQ, left_id: 0, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 0, eq_lhs: lhs, eq_rhs: rhs }
}

// P <-> Q  is  (P -> Q) /\ (Q -> P)
fn prop_iff(p_id: i64, q_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_AND, left_id: p_id, right_id: q_id, var_name: 0, predicate_id: 1, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

fn prop_custom(pred_id: i64) -> Prop {
    return Prop { tag: PROP_CUSTOM, left_id: 0, right_id: 0, var_name: 0, predicate_id: pred_id, eq_lhs: 0, eq_rhs: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROOF TAGS
// ============================================================================

let PROOF_REFL: i32 = 0
let PROOF_AND_INTRO: i32 = 1
let PROOF_AND_ELIM_L: i32 = 2
let PROOF_AND_ELIM_R: i32 = 3
let PROOF_OR_INTRO_L: i32 = 4
let PROOF_OR_INTRO_R: i32 = 5
let PROOF_OR_ELIM: i32 = 6
let PROOF_IMPL_INTRO: i32 = 7
let PROOF_IMPL_ELIM: i32 = 8
let PROOF_NOT_INTRO: i32 = 9
let PROOF_NOT_ELIM: i32 = 10
let PROOF_FALSE_ELIM: i32 = 11
let PROOF_FORALL_INTRO: i32 = 12
let PROOF_FORALL_ELIM: i32 = 13
let PROOF_EXISTS_INTRO: i32 = 14
let PROOF_EXISTS_ELIM: i32 = 15
let PROOF_SYM: i32 = 16
let PROOF_TRANS: i32 = 17
let PROOF_CONG: i32 = 18
let PROOF_SUBST: i32 = 19
let PROOF_COMPOSE: i32 = 20
let PROOF_WEAKEN: i32 = 21
let PROOF_TRUSTED: i32 = 22
let PROOF_ASSUME: i32 = 23
let PROOF_RUNTIME: i32 = 24
let PROOF_TRUE_INTRO: i32 = 25

// ============================================================================
// PROOF WITNESS
// ============================================================================

// A proof of a proposition. Carries confidence — the Sounio novelty.
// confidence = 1.0 means fully verified (like Lean/Coq).
// confidence < 1.0 means epistemic evidence (unique to Sounio).
struct Proof {
    tag: i32,
    // The proposition this witnesses (arena index)
    prop_id: i64,
    // Sub-proofs (indices into proof store)
    sub1_id: i64,
    sub2_id: i64,
    sub3_id: i64,
    // Metadata
    label: i64,
    // THE KEY FIELD: confidence in this proof
    // 1.0 = verified, < 1.0 = epistemic evidence
    confidence: f64,
    // Witness value (for exists_intro, forall_elim, etc.)
    witness: i64,
}

// Proof store (flat arena, mirrors proposition arena)
struct ProofStore {
    tags: [i32; 4096],
    prop_ids: [i64; 4096],
    sub1_ids: [i64; 4096],
    sub2_ids: [i64; 4096],
    sub3_ids: [i64; 4096],
    labels: [i64; 4096],
    confidences: [f64; 4096],
    witnesses: [i64; 4096],
    count: i64,
}

fn proof_store_new() -> ProofStore {
    return ProofStore {
        tags: [0; 4096],
        prop_ids: [0; 4096],
        sub1_ids: [0; 4096],
        sub2_ids: [0; 4096],
        sub3_ids: [0; 4096],
        labels: [0; 4096],
        confidences: [0.0; 4096],
        witnesses: [0; 4096],
        count: 0,
    }
}

fn proof_store_alloc(store: &! ProofStore, p: Proof) -> i64 {
    let idx = store.count
    if idx >= 4096 {
        return 0 - 1
    }
    store.tags[idx] = p.tag
    store.prop_ids[idx] = p.prop_id
    store.sub1_ids[idx] = p.sub1_id
    store.sub2_ids[idx] = p.sub2_id
    store.sub3_ids[idx] = p.sub3_id
    store.labels[idx] = p.label
    store.confidences[idx] = p.confidence
    store.witnesses[idx] = p.witness
    store.count = idx + 1
    return idx
}

fn proof_store_get(store: &ProofStore, idx: i64) -> Proof {
    if idx < 0 {
        return Proof { tag: 0 - 1, prop_id: 0, sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0, label: 0, confidence: 0.0, witness: 0 }
    }
    if idx >= store.count {
        return Proof { tag: 0 - 1, prop_id: 0, sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0, label: 0, confidence: 0.0, witness: 0 }
    }
    return Proof {
        tag: store.tags[idx],
        prop_id: store.prop_ids[idx],
        sub1_id: store.sub1_ids[idx],
        sub2_id: store.sub2_ids[idx],
        sub3_id: store.sub3_ids[idx],
        label: store.labels[idx],
        confidence: store.confidences[idx],
        witness: store.witnesses[idx],
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// VERIFICATION RESULT
// ============================================================================

struct VerifyResult {
    is_valid: bool,
    confidence: f64,
    reason: i32,     // 0=ok, 1=tag_mismatch, 2=prop_mismatch, 3=confidence_invalid
}

fn verify_ok(conf: f64) -> VerifyResult {
    return VerifyResult { is_valid: true, confidence: conf, reason: 0 }
}

fn verify_fail(reason: i32) -> VerifyResult {
    return VerifyResult { is_valid: false, confidence: 0.0, reason: reason }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROOF CONTEXT — binds arena + proof store together
// ============================================================================

struct ProofContext {
    arena: PropArena,
    store: ProofStore,
}

fn proof_context_new() -> ProofContext {
    return ProofContext {
        arena: arena_new(),
        store: proof_store_new(),
    }
}

// Allocate a proposition in the context, return its ID
fn ctx_prop(ctx: &! ProofContext, p: Prop) -> i64 {
    return arena_alloc(&! ctx.arena, p)
}

// Allocate a proof in the context, return its ID
fn ctx_proof(ctx: &! ProofContext, p: Proof) -> i64 {
    return proof_store_alloc(&! ctx.store, p)
}

// Retrieve a proposition
fn ctx_get_prop(ctx: &ProofContext, id: i64) -> Prop {
    return arena_get(&ctx.arena, id)
}

// Retrieve a proof
fn ctx_get_proof(ctx: &ProofContext, id: i64) -> Proof {
    return proof_store_get(&ctx.store, id)
}

// ============================================================================
// NATURAL DEDUCTION: INTRODUCTION RULES
// ============================================================================

// True introduction: trivially provable
fn true_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext) -> i64 {
    let p_id = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_true())
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_TRUE_INTRO,
        prop_id: p_id,
        sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: 1.0, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// And introduction: from P, Q derive P /\ Q
fn and_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext, p_proof_id: i64, q_proof_id: i64, pq_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let p_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p_proof_id)
    let q_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, q_proof_id)
    let conf = min_f64(p_prf.confidence, q_prf.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_AND_INTRO,
        prop_id: pq_prop_id,
        sub1_id: p_proof_id,
        sub2_id: q_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Or introduction left: from P derive P \/ Q
fn or_intro_left(ctx: &! ProofContext, p_proof_id: i64, pq_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let p_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_OR_INTRO_L,
        prop_id: pq_prop_id,
        sub1_id: p_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: p_prf.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Or introduction right: from Q derive P \/ Q
fn or_intro_right(ctx: &! ProofContext, q_proof_id: i64, pq_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let q_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, q_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_OR_INTRO_R,
        prop_id: pq_prop_id,
        sub1_id: q_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: q_prf.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Implication introduction: assuming P (sub1), we proved Q (sub2) => P -> Q
fn impl_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext, assume_id: i64, q_proof_id: i64, impl_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let q_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, q_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_IMPL_INTRO,
        prop_id: impl_prop_id,
        sub1_id: assume_id,
        sub2_id: q_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: q_prf.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Negation introduction: assuming P, derive False => ~P
fn not_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext, assume_id: i64, false_proof_id: i64, not_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let f_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, false_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_NOT_INTRO,
        prop_id: not_prop_id,
        sub1_id: assume_id,
        sub2_id: false_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: f_prf.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Universal introduction: for arbitrary x, prove P(x) => forall x. P(x)
fn forall_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext, body_proof_id: i64, forall_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let body = ctx_get_proof(ctx, body_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_FORALL_INTRO,
        prop_id: forall_prop_id,
        sub1_id: body_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: body.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Existential introduction: from P(t), derive exists x. P(x)
fn exists_intro(ctx: &! ProofContext, witness_val: i64, body_proof_id: i64, exists_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let body = ctx_get_proof(ctx, body_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_EXISTS_INTRO,
        prop_id: exists_prop_id,
        sub1_id: body_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: body.confidence, witness: witness_val,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// ============================================================================
// NATURAL DEDUCTION: ELIMINATION RULES

// And elimination left: from P /\ Q derive P
fn and_elim_left(ctx: &! ProofContext, pq_proof_id: i64, p_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let pq = ctx_get_proof(ctx, pq_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_AND_ELIM_L,
        prop_id: p_prop_id,
        sub1_id: pq_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: pq.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// And elimination right: from P /\ Q derive Q
fn and_elim_right(ctx: &! ProofContext, pq_proof_id: i64, q_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let pq = ctx_get_proof(ctx, pq_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_AND_ELIM_R,
        prop_id: q_prop_id,
        sub1_id: pq_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: pq.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Or elimination: from P \/ Q, P-case proof, Q-case proof => R
fn or_elim(ctx: &! ProofContext, pq_proof_id: i64, p_case_id: i64, q_case_id: i64, r_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let pq = ctx_get_proof(ctx, pq_proof_id)
    let p_case = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p_case_id)
    let q_case = ctx_get_proof(ctx, q_case_id)
    let conf = min_f64(pq.confidence, min_f64(p_case.confidence, q_case.confidence))
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_OR_ELIM,
        prop_id: r_prop_id,
        sub1_id: pq_proof_id,
        sub2_id: p_case_id,
        sub3_id: q_case_id,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Modus ponens: from P -> Q, P => Q
fn impl_elim(ctx: &! ProofContext, impl_proof_id: i64, p_proof_id: i64, q_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let impl_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, impl_proof_id)
    let p_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p_proof_id)
    let conf = min_f64(impl_prf.confidence, p_prf.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_IMPL_ELIM,
        prop_id: q_prop_id,
        sub1_id: impl_proof_id,
        sub2_id: p_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Negation elimination: from ~P, P => False
fn not_elim(ctx: &! ProofContext, not_p_id: i64, p_proof_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let np = ctx_get_proof(ctx, not_p_id)
    let pp = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p_proof_id)
    let false_prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_false())
    let conf = min_f64(np.confidence, pp.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_NOT_ELIM,
        prop_id: false_prop,
        sub1_id: not_p_id,
        sub2_id: p_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Ex falso quodlibet: from False, derive anything
fn false_elim(ctx: &! ProofContext, false_proof_id: i64, target_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let fp = ctx_get_proof(ctx, false_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_FALSE_ELIM,
        prop_id: target_prop_id,
        sub1_id: false_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: fp.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Universal elimination: from forall x. P(x), instantiate at term t => P(t)
fn forall_elim(ctx: &! ProofContext, forall_proof_id: i64, term: i64, result_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let fp = ctx_get_proof(ctx, forall_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_FORALL_ELIM,
        prop_id: result_prop_id,
        sub1_id: forall_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: fp.confidence, witness: term,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Existential elimination: from (exists x. P(x)), use the witness
fn exists_elim(ctx: &! ProofContext, exists_proof_id: i64, body_proof_id: i64, result_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let ep = ctx_get_proof(ctx, exists_proof_id)
    let bp = ctx_get_proof(ctx, body_proof_id)
    let conf = min_f64(ep.confidence, bp.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_EXISTS_ELIM,
        prop_id: result_prop_id,
        sub1_id: exists_proof_id,
        sub2_id: body_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Reflexivity: a = a
fn refl(ctx: &! ProofContext, a: i64) -> i64 {
    let eq_prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_eq(a, a))
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_REFL,
        prop_id: eq_prop,
        sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: 1.0, witness: a,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Symmetry: a = b => b = a
fn sym(ctx: &! ProofContext, eq_proof_id: i64, ba_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let ep = ctx_get_proof(ctx, eq_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_SYM,
        prop_id: ba_prop_id,
        sub1_id: eq_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: ep.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Transitivity: a = b, b = c => a = c
fn trans(ctx: &! ProofContext, ab_proof_id: i64, bc_proof_id: i64, ac_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let ab = ctx_get_proof(ctx, ab_proof_id)
    let bc = ctx_get_proof(ctx, bc_proof_id)
    let conf = min_f64(ab.confidence, bc.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_TRANS,
        prop_id: ac_prop_id,
        sub1_id: ab_proof_id,
        sub2_id: bc_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Congruence: a = b => f(a) = f(b)
fn cong(ctx: &! ProofContext, f_id: i64, eq_proof_id: i64, result_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let ep = ctx_get_proof(ctx, eq_proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_CONG,
        prop_id: result_prop_id,
        sub1_id: eq_proof_id,
        sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: f_id, confidence: ep.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Substitution: a = b, P(a) => P(b)
fn subst(ctx: &! ProofContext, eq_proof_id: i64, pa_proof_id: i64, pb_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let ep = ctx_get_proof(ctx, eq_proof_id)
    let pa = ctx_get_proof(ctx, pa_proof_id)
    let conf = min_f64(ep.confidence, pa.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_SUBST,
        prop_id: pb_prop_id,
        sub1_id: eq_proof_id,
        sub2_id: pa_proof_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Chain two proofs together
fn compose(ctx: &! ProofContext, p1_id: i64, p2_id: i64, result_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let p1 = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p1_id)
    let p2 = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p2_id)
    let conf = min_f64(p1.confidence, p2.confidence)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_COMPOSE,
        prop_id: result_prop_id,
        sub1_id: p1_id,
        sub2_id: p2_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Weaken: add unused hypothesis (proof still holds, confidence unchanged)
fn weaken(ctx: &! ProofContext, proof_id: i64, extra_prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let p = ctx_get_proof(ctx, proof_id)
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_WEAKEN,
        prop_id: p.prop_id,
        sub1_id: proof_id,
        sub2_id: extra_prop_id,
        sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: p.confidence, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// ============================================================================
// TRUST BOUNDARIES
// ============================================================================

// Trusted: escape hatch. Creates a proof by fiat.
// confidence = 1.0 by default but caller can override.
// Maps to ProofKind::Trusted in the compiler.
fn trusted(ctx: &! ProofContext, reason: i64, prop_id: i64, confidence: f64) -> i64 {
    var conf = confidence
    if conf < 0.0 { conf = 0.0 }
    if conf > 1.0 { conf = 1.0 }
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_TRUSTED,
        prop_id: prop_id,
        sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: reason, confidence: conf, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Assume: introduce a hypothesis from context.
// Maps to ProofKind::Assume in the compiler.
fn assume(ctx: &! ProofContext, name: i64, prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_ASSUME,
        prop_id: prop_id,
        sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: name, confidence: 1.0, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// Runtime check: defers verification to runtime (gradual typing).
// Confidence is 0.9 — not fully static but likely correct.
// Maps to ProofKind::RuntimeCheck in the compiler.
fn runtime_check(ctx: &! ProofContext, prop_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let prf = Proof {
        tag: PROOF_RUNTIME,
        prop_id: prop_id,
        sub1_id: 0, sub2_id: 0, sub3_id: 0,
        label: 0, confidence: 0.9, witness: 0,
    }
    return ctx_proof(ctx, prf)
}

// ============================================================================
// PROOF INSPECTION
// ============================================================================

// Get the confidence of a proof
fn proof_confidence(ctx: &ProofContext, proof_id: i64) -> f64 {
    let p = ctx_get_proof(ctx, proof_id)
    return p.confidence
}

// Get the proposition a proof witnesses
fn proof_prop_id(ctx: &ProofContext, proof_id: i64) -> i64 {
    let p = ctx_get_proof(ctx, proof_id)
    return p.prop_id
}

// Is this proof fully static (no runtime checks, no trusted, confidence = 1.0)?
fn proof_is_static(ctx: &ProofContext, proof_id: i64) -> bool {
    let p = ctx_get_proof(ctx, proof_id)
    if p.tag == PROOF_TRUSTED { return false }
    if p.tag == PROOF_RUNTIME { return false }
    if p.confidence < 1.0 { return false }
    return true
}

// Get the proof tag (rule used)
fn proof_tag(ctx: &ProofContext, proof_id: i64) -> i32 {
    let p = ctx_get_proof(ctx, proof_id)
    return p.tag
}

// ============================================================================
// VERIFICATION
// ============================================================================

// Verify a proof: check that the proof tag is consistent with its proposition.
// Returns VerifyResult with validity and confidence.
fn verify(ctx: &ProofContext, proof_id: i64) -> VerifyResult {
    let p = ctx_get_proof(ctx, proof_id)

    // Invalid proof ID
    if p.tag < 0 {
        return verify_fail(1)
    }

    // Confidence bounds check
    if p.confidence < 0.0 {
        return verify_fail(3)
    }
    if p.confidence > 1.0 {
        return verify_fail(3)
    }

    let prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, p.prop_id)

    // Tag-specific validation
    if p.tag == PROOF_TRUE_INTRO {
        if prop.tag == PROP_TRUE {
            return verify_ok(p.confidence)
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_REFL {
        if prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            if prop.eq_lhs == prop.eq_rhs {
                return verify_ok(1.0)
            }
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_AND_INTRO {
        if prop.tag == PROP_AND {
            let s1 = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub1_id)
            let s2 = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub2_id)
            if s1.tag >= 0 {
                if s2.tag >= 0 {
                    return verify_ok(min_f64(s1.confidence, s2.confidence))
                }
            }
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_AND_ELIM_L {
        let parent = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub1_id)
        let parent_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, parent.prop_id)
        if parent_prop.tag == PROP_AND {
            return verify_ok(parent.confidence)
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_AND_ELIM_R {
        let parent = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub1_id)
        let parent_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, parent.prop_id)
        if parent_prop.tag == PROP_AND {
            return verify_ok(parent.confidence)
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_IMPL_ELIM {
        let impl_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub1_id)
        let impl_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, impl_prf.prop_id)
        if impl_prop.tag == PROP_IMPLIES {
            let ante_prf = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub2_id)
            return verify_ok(min_f64(impl_prf.confidence, ante_prf.confidence))
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_SYM {
        let parent = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub1_id)
        let parent_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, parent.prop_id)
        if parent_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            if prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
                return verify_ok(parent.confidence)
            }
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_TRANS {
        let ab = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub1_id)
        let bc = ctx_get_proof(ctx, p.sub2_id)
        let ab_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, ab.prop_id)
        let bc_prop = ctx_get_prop(ctx, bc.prop_id)
        if ab_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
            if bc_prop.tag == PROP_EQ {
                return verify_ok(min_f64(ab.confidence, bc.confidence))
            }
        }
        return verify_fail(2)
    }

    // Trust boundaries: always valid by construction
    if p.tag == PROOF_TRUSTED {
        return verify_ok(p.confidence)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_ASSUME {
        return verify_ok(p.confidence)
    }

    if p.tag == PROOF_RUNTIME {
        return verify_ok(p.confidence)
    }

    // For other proof tags, validate structurally
    if p.tag == PROOF_OR_INTRO_L { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_OR_INTRO_R { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_OR_ELIM { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_IMPL_INTRO { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_NOT_INTRO { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_NOT_ELIM { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_FALSE_ELIM { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_FORALL_INTRO { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_FORALL_ELIM { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_EXISTS_INTRO { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_EXISTS_ELIM { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_CONG { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_SUBST { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_COMPOSE { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }
    if p.tag == PROOF_WEAKEN { return verify_ok(p.confidence) }

    return verify_fail(1)
}

// ============================================================================
// PROPOSITION HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Check if two propositions are structurally equal
fn prop_eq_check(a: Prop, b: Prop) -> bool {
    if a.tag != b.tag { return false }
    if a.left_id != b.left_id { return false }
    if a.right_id != b.right_id { return false }
    if a.var_name != b.var_name { return false }
    if a.predicate_id != b.predicate_id { return false }
    if a.eq_lhs != b.eq_lhs { return false }
    if a.eq_rhs != b.eq_rhs { return false }
    return true
}

// Get the tag name as integer code (for debugging)
fn prop_tag_name(tag: i32) -> i32 {
    return tag
}

// == original file begins ==
// Sounio Theorem Units — Dimensional Analysis as Theorem Proving
//
// Proofs that unit expressions are equivalent, conversions are correct,
// and physical constants satisfy known dimensional relationships.
//
// Connects to stdlib/units/ and stdlib/epistemic/core.sio.
// Unique: convert_epistemic proves conversions preserve uncertainty.
//
// References:
//   SI brochure (2019) — International System of Units
//   CODATA 2018 — NIST values for physical constants

// kernel definitions loaded as sibling — no explicit import needed

// ============================================================================
// DIMENSION TYPE (SI 7-tuple of exponents)
// ============================================================================

// Dimension vector: exponents of the 7 SI base units
// [length(m), mass(kg), time(s), current(A), temperature(K), amount(mol), luminosity(cd)]
struct Dimension {
    length: i32,
    mass: i32,
    time: i32,
    current: i32,
    temperature: i32,
    amount: i32,
    luminosity: i32,
}

fn dim_dimensionless() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_length() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 1, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_mass() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 0, mass: 1, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_time_unit() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_current() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 1, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_temperature() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 1, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
}

fn dim_amount() -> Dimension {
    return Dimension { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 0, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 1, luminosity: 0 }
}

// ============================================================================
// DIMENSION ALGEBRA
// ============================================================================

// Product of dimensions: exponents add
fn dim_mul(a: Dimension, b: Dimension) -> Dimension {
    return Dimension {
        length: a.length + b.length,
        mass: a.mass + b.mass,
        time: a.time + b.time,
        current: a.current + b.current,
        temperature: a.temperature + b.temperature,
        amount: a.amount + b.amount,
        luminosity: a.luminosity + b.luminosity,
    }
}

// Division of dimensions: exponents subtract
fn dim_div(a: Dimension, b: Dimension) -> Dimension {
    return Dimension {
        length: a.length - b.length,
        mass: a.mass - b.mass,
        time: a.time - b.time,
        current: a.current - b.current,
        temperature: a.temperature - b.temperature,
        amount: a.amount - b.amount,
        luminosity: a.luminosity - b.luminosity,
    }
}

// Power of dimension: exponents multiply
fn dim_pow(d: Dimension, n: i32) -> Dimension {
    return Dimension {
        length: d.length * n,
        mass: d.mass * n,
        time: d.time * n,
        current: d.current * n,
        temperature: d.temperature * n,
        amount: d.amount * n,
        luminosity: d.luminosity * n,
    }
}

// Check dimensional equality
fn dim_eq(a: Dimension, b: Dimension) -> bool {
    if a.length != b.length { return false }
    if a.mass != b.mass { return false }
    if a.time != b.time { return false }
    if a.current != b.current { return false }
    if a.temperature != b.temperature { return false }
    if a.amount != b.amount { return false }
    if a.luminosity != b.luminosity { return false }
    return true
}

// ============================================================================
// DIMENSION PROOFS
// ============================================================================

// Encode a dimension as a proposition ID (compact hash)
fn dim_encode(d: Dimension) -> i64 {
    // Encode 7 small integers into a single i64
    // Each exponent occupies 8 bits, range -128 to 127
    let l = (d.length + 128) as i64
    let m = (d.mass + 128) as i64
    let t = (d.time + 128) as i64
    let c = (d.current + 128) as i64
    let k = (d.temperature + 128) as i64
    let n = (d.amount + 128) as i64
    let j = (d.luminosity + 128) as i64
    return l + m * 256 + t * 65536 + c * 16777216 + k * 4294967296 + n * 1099511627776 + j * 281474976710656
}

// Prove two dimensions are equal
fn dim_eq_proof(ctx: &! ProofContext, a: Dimension, b: Dimension) -> i64 {
    let enc_a = dim_encode(a)
    let enc_b = dim_encode(b)
    if dim_eq(a, b) {
        return refl(ctx, enc_a)
    }
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(70000 + enc_a as i32))
    return trusted(ctx, 7001, prop, 0.0)  // zero confidence: not proven
}

// Prove dimensional consistency (a matches expected)
fn dim_check(ctx: &! ProofContext, actual: Dimension, expected: Dimension) -> i64 {
    return dim_eq_proof(ctx, actual, expected)
}

// ============================================================================
// PROVED UNIT TYPE
// ============================================================================

struct ProvedUnit {
    name_hash: i64,
    dim: Dimension,
    si_factor: f64,        // value in SI base units
    dim_prf_id: i64,       // proof of dimensional correctness
}

fn unit_new(ctx: &! ProofContext, name: i64, dim: Dimension, si: f64) -> ProvedUnit {
    let prf = dim_check(ctx, dim, dim)  // trivially self-consistent
    return ProvedUnit { name_hash: name, dim: dim, si_factor: si, dim_prf_id: prf }
}

// Newton: N = kg * m / s^2
fn newton_is_kgms2(ctx: &! ProofContext) -> i64 {
    // N: force unit, dim = [1, 1, -2, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    let newton = Dimension { length: 1, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let kgms2 = dim_div(dim_mul(dim_mass(), dim_length()), dim_pow(dim_time_unit(), 2))
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(71001))
    if dim_eq(newton, kgms2) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7010, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7010, prop, 0.0)
}

// Joule: J = kg * m^2 / s^2

struct PhysicalConstant {
    name_hash: i64,
    value: f64,
    uncertainty: f64,    // standard uncertainty
    dim: Dimension,
    consistency_id: i64, // proof of dimensional consistency
}

fn speed_of_light(ctx: &! ProofContext) -> PhysicalConstant {
    // c = 299792458 m/s (exact — defined value in SI 2019)
    let dim = Dimension { length: 1, mass: 0, time: 0 - 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let prf = dim_check(ctx, dim, dim)
    return PhysicalConstant { name_hash: 100001, value: 299792458.0, uncertainty: 0.0, dim: dim, consistency_id: prf }
}

// E = mc^2: energy = mass * speed^2 => dimension check
fn energy_mass_equiv(ctx: &! ProofContext) -> i64 {
    // E: [2,1,-2,0,0,0,0]  m: [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]  c^2: [2,0,-2,0,0,0,0]
    let e_dim = Dimension { length: 2, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let m_dim = dim_mass()
    let c_dim = Dimension { length: 1, mass: 0, time: 0 - 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let mc2_dim = dim_mul(m_dim, dim_pow(c_dim, 2))
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(72001))
    if dim_eq(e_dim, mc2_dim) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7020, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7020, prop, 0.0)
}

// PV = nRT: ideal gas law dimensional consistency
fn ideal_gas_law_consistent(ctx: &! ProofContext) -> i64 {
    // P: [−1,1,−2,0,0,0,0]  V: [3,0,0,0,0,0,0]
    // n: mol = [0,0,0,0,0,1,0]  R: J/(mol*K) = [2,1,-2,0,-1,-1,0]  T: K = [0,0,0,0,1,0,0]
    let pv_dim = Dimension { length: 2, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let r_dim = Dimension { length: 2, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0 - 1, amount: 0 - 1, luminosity: 0 }
    let nrt_dim = dim_mul(dim_mul(dim_amount(), r_dim), dim_temperature())
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(72002))
    if dim_eq(pv_dim, nrt_dim) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7021, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7021, prop, 0.0)
}

// E = hf: Planck-Einstein dimensional check
fn planck_einstein_relation(ctx: &! ProofContext) -> i64 {
    // E: [2,1,-2,0,0,0,0]  h: [2,1,-1,0,0,0,0]  f: [0,0,-1,0,0,0,0]
    let e_dim = Dimension { length: 2, mass: 1, time: 0 - 2, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let h_dim = Dimension { length: 2, mass: 1, time: 0 - 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let f_dim = Dimension { length: 0, mass: 0, time: 0 - 1, current: 0, temperature: 0, amount: 0, luminosity: 0 }
    let hf_dim = dim_mul(h_dim, f_dim)
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(72003))
    if dim_eq(e_dim, hf_dim) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7022, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7022, prop, 0.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// CONVERSION PROOFS
// ============================================================================

// Prove conversion between two units is valid (dimensions match)
fn conversion_proof(ctx: &! ProofContext, from: ProvedUnit, to: ProvedUnit) -> i64 {
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(73001))
    if dim_eq(from.dim, to.dim) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7030, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7030, prop, 0.0)
}

// Compute SI conversion factor
fn conversion_factor(from: ProvedUnit, to: ProvedUnit) -> f64 {
    if to.si_factor == 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    return from.si_factor / to.si_factor
}

fn convert_value(value: f64, from: ProvedUnit, to: ProvedUnit) -> f64 {
    return value * conversion_factor(from, to)
}

// Convert with uncertainty propagation + proof
// Proves that conversion preserves epistemic uncertainty bounds
fn convert_epistemic(ctx: &! ProofContext, value: f64, uncertainty: f64, confidence: f64,
                     from: ProvedUnit, to: ProvedUnit) -> i64 {
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(73002))
    if dim_eq(from.dim, to.dim) {
        // Conversion factor scales both value and uncertainty by same factor
        // => relative uncertainty preserved => confidence preserved
        return trusted(ctx, 7031, prop, confidence)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7031, prop, 0.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// UNIT ALGEBRA PROOFS
// ============================================================================

// a * b = b * a dimensionally
fn unit_mul_comm(ctx: &! ProofContext, a: ProvedUnit, b: ProvedUnit) -> i64 {
    let ab = dim_mul(a.dim, b.dim)
    let ba = dim_mul(b.dim, a.dim)
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(74001))
    if dim_eq(ab, ba) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7040, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7040, prop, 0.0)
}

// a / a = dimensionless
fn unit_div_self(ctx: &! ProofContext, a: ProvedUnit) -> i64 {
    let result = dim_div(a.dim, a.dim)
    let dl = dim_dimensionless()
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(74002))
    if dim_eq(result, dl) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7041, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7041, prop, 0.0)
}

// a^m * a^n = a^(m+n)
fn unit_pow_add(ctx: &! ProofContext, a: ProvedUnit, m: i32, n: i32) -> i64 {
    let am = dim_pow(a.dim, m)
    let an = dim_pow(a.dim, n)
    let amn = dim_mul(am, an)
    let amn2 = dim_pow(a.dim, m + n)
    let prop = ctx_prop(ctx, prop_custom(74003))
    if dim_eq(amn, amn2) {
        return trusted(ctx, 7042, prop, 1.0)
    }
    return trusted(ctx, 7042, prop, 0.0)
}

// === FILE: stdlib/thread/pool.sio ===
// stdlib/thread/pool — Thread pool abstraction
//
// ThreadPool: fixed-size pool of worker slots with task assignment.

let POOL_MAX_WORKERS: i64 = 64

struct ThreadPool {
    worker_status: [i64; 64],
    worker_task: [i64; 64],
    num_workers: i64,
    tasks_submitted: i64,
    tasks_completed: i64,
}

impl ThreadPool {
    fn new(num_workers: i64) -> ThreadPool {
        var n = num_workers
        if n > POOL_MAX_WORKERS { n = POOL_MAX_WORKERS }
        if n < 1 { n = 1 }
        ThreadPool {
            worker_status: [0; 64],
            worker_task: [0; 64],
            num_workers: n,
            tasks_submitted: 0,
            tasks_completed: 0,
        }
    }

    fn submit(self: &! ThreadPool, task_id: i64) -> bool {
        // Find idle worker
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < self.num_workers {
            if self.worker_status[i] == 0 {
                self.worker_status[i] = 1
                self.worker_task[i] = task_id
                self.tasks_submitted = self.tasks_submitted + 1
                return true
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
        return false
    }

    fn complete(self: &! ThreadPool, worker_idx: i64) {
        if worker_idx >= 0 && worker_idx < self.num_workers {
            self.worker_status[worker_idx] = 0
            self.tasks_completed = self.tasks_completed + 1
        }
    }

    fn active_count(self: &ThreadPool) -> i64 {
        var count: i64 = 0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < self.num_workers {
            if self.worker_status[i] != 0 { count = count + 1 }
            i = i + 1
        }
        count
    }

    fn total_workers(self: &ThreadPool) -> i64 {
        self.num_workers
    }
}


// === FILE: stdlib/thread/spawn.sio ===
// stdlib/thread/spawn — Thread handle
//
// ThreadHandle: represents a spawned thread with status tracking.

struct ThreadHandle {
    id: i64,
    status: i64,
    result: i64,
}

let THREAD_CREATED: i64 = 0
let THREAD_RUNNING: i64 = 1
let THREAD_JOINED: i64 = 2

fn thread_new(id: i64) -> ThreadHandle {
    ThreadHandle { id: id, status: THREAD_CREATED, result: 0 }
}

impl ThreadHandle {
    fn is_running(self: &ThreadHandle) -> bool { self.status == THREAD_RUNNING }
    fn is_joined(self: &ThreadHandle) -> bool { self.status == THREAD_JOINED }

    fn join(self: &! ThreadHandle) -> i64 {
        self.status = THREAD_JOINED
        self.result
    }

    fn set_result(self: &! ThreadHandle, result: i64) {
        self.result = result
        self.status = THREAD_JOINED
    }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/time/lib.sio ===
// stdlib/time/lib.sio — Epoch-based time arithmetic
//
// Provides Duration and DateTime types with full calendar arithmetic.
// No OS clock access — pure epoch-based computation.
//
// References:
//   RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 calendar conventions
//   POSIX epoch: 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC

// =============================================================================
// Duration
// =============================================================================

struct Duration {
    seconds: i64,
    nanos: i64,    // 0..999_999_999
}

// Normalise: ensure 0 <= nanos < 1_000_000_000 and carry into seconds.
fn duration_normalise(secs: i64, ns: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var s = secs
    var n = ns
    if n < 0 {
        let borrow = (0 - n - 1) / 1000000000 + 1
        s = s - borrow
        n = n + borrow * 1000000000
    }
    if n >= 1000000000 {
        let carry = n / 1000000000
        s = s + carry
        n = n - carry * 1000000000
    }
    Duration { seconds: s, nanos: n }
}

fn duration_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(secs, nanos)
}

fn duration_from_secs(secs: i64) -> Duration {
    Duration { seconds: secs, nanos: 0 }
}

fn duration_from_millis(ms: i64) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let secs = ms / 1000
    let nanos = (ms - secs * 1000) * 1000000
    duration_normalise(secs, nanos)
}

fn duration_add(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(a.seconds + b.seconds, a.nanos + b.nanos)
}

fn duration_sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) -> Duration with Div, Panic, Mut {
    duration_normalise(a.seconds - b.seconds, a.nanos - b.nanos)
}

fn duration_to_secs_f64(d: &Duration) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let sf: f64 = d.seconds as f64
    let nf: f64 = d.nanos as f64
    sf + nf / 1000000000.0
}

// =============================================================================
// DateTime
// =============================================================================

struct DateTime {
    year:          i32,
    month:         i32,   // 1-12
    day:           i32,   // 1-31
    hour:          i32,   // 0-23
    minute:        i32,   // 0-59
    second:        i32,   // 0-59
    epoch_seconds: i64,   // seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
}

// =============================================================================
// Calendar helpers — must precede callers
// =============================================================================

fn is_leap_year(y: i32) -> bool with Div, Panic {
    if y % 400 == 0 { return true }
    if y % 100 == 0 { return false }
    if y % 4 == 0   { return true }
    false
}

fn days_in_month(y: i32, m: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if m == 1  { return 31 }
    if m == 2  {
        if is_leap_year(y) { return 29 }
        return 28
    }
    if m == 3  { return 31 }
    if m == 4  { return 30 }
    if m == 5  { return 31 }
    if m == 6  { return 30 }
    if m == 7  { return 31 }
    if m == 8  { return 31 }
    if m == 9  { return 30 }
    if m == 10 { return 31 }
    if m == 11 { return 30 }
    31
}

fn day_of_year(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32) -> i32 with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var doy = 0
    var mo = 1
    while mo < m {
        doy = doy + days_in_month(y, mo)
        mo = mo + 1
    }
    doy + d
}

// Days from the POSIX epoch (1970-01-01) to the start of year y.
// Uses the Gregorian formula: every 4 years +1 leap, every 100 -1, every 400 +1.
fn days_from_epoch_to_year(y: i32) -> i64 with Div, Panic {
    let y0: i64 = y as i64 - 1
    let base: i64 = (y as i64 - 1970) * 365
    let leaps: i64 = y0 / 4 - y0 / 100 + y0 / 400
    let epoch_base: i64 = 1969 / 4 - 1969 / 100 + 1969 / 400
    base + leaps - epoch_base
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_new — compute epoch_seconds from calendar components
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_new(y: i32, m: i32, d: i32, h: i32, min: i32, s: i32) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    let year_days: i64 = days_from_epoch_to_year(y)
    let month_days: i64 = day_of_year(y, m, d) as i64 - 1
    let total_days: i64 = year_days + month_days
    let epoch: i64 = total_days * 86400 + h as i64 * 3600 + min as i64 * 60 + s as i64
    DateTime {
        year: y, month: m, day: d,
        hour: h, minute: min, second: s,
        epoch_seconds: epoch,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_from_epoch — reverse: epoch → calendar fields
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_from_epoch(epoch: i64) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    var remaining: i64 = epoch

    // Extract time-of-day
    var day_secs: i64 = remaining % 86400
    var day_count: i64 = remaining / 86400
    if day_secs < 0 {
        day_secs = day_secs + 86400
        day_count = day_count - 1
    }
    let h: i32   = (day_secs / 3600) as i32
    let mn: i32  = ((day_secs % 3600) / 60) as i32
    let sec: i32 = (day_secs % 60) as i32

    // Walk forward/backward from 1970 to find the year
    var y: i32 = 1970
    if day_count >= 0 {
        while true {
            let dy: i64 = if is_leap_year(y) { 366 } else { 365 }
            if day_count < dy { break }
            day_count = day_count - dy
            y = y + 1
        }
    } else {
        while day_count < 0 {
            y = y - 1
            let dy: i64 = if is_leap_year(y) { 366 } else { 365 }
            day_count = day_count + dy
        }
    }

    // Walk months within the year
    var mo: i32 = 1
    while mo <= 12 {
        let dm: i64 = days_in_month(y, mo) as i64
        if day_count < dm { break }
        day_count = day_count - dm
        mo = mo + 1
    }
    let d: i32 = day_count as i32 + 1

    DateTime {
        year: y, month: mo, day: d,
        hour: h, minute: mn, second: sec,
        epoch_seconds: epoch,
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_add_duration
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_add_duration(dt: DateTime, d: Duration) -> DateTime with Div, Panic, Mut {
    datetime_from_epoch(dt.epoch_seconds + d.seconds)
}

// =============================================================================
// datetime_diff — returns Duration representing a - b (may be negative seconds)
// =============================================================================

fn datetime_diff(a: &DateTime, b: &DateTime) -> Duration with Div, Panic {
    let diff_secs: i64 = a.epoch_seconds - b.epoch_seconds
    Duration { seconds: diff_secs, nanos: 0 }
}

// === FILE: stdlib/toml/parser.sio ===
// stdlib/toml/parser.sio — Minimal TOML parser
//
// Represents TOML as a flat key-value document (up to 32 entries).
// No heap allocation — all storage is fixed-size arrays.
// Supports flat key=value only (no tables, no arrays-of-tables).
// Value types: string, integer, float, bool.
// Handles: # comments, blank lines, whitespace around '='.
//
// JIT note: only &!Struct field mutations propagate to callers.
// Standalone &!array and &!scalar do NOT propagate in JIT mode.
// All helpers use struct-wrapping or by-value returns for correctness.
//
// # Limits
//   - Up to 32 key-value pairs per document
//   - Keys up to 63 bytes (null-terminated in 64-byte slot)
//   - String values up to 127 bytes (null-terminated in 128-byte slot)
//   - Parse input up to 4095 bytes

// ============================================================================
// TOML VALUE TYPES
// ============================================================================

pub fn TOML_STRING()  -> i32 { 0 }
pub fn TOML_INTEGER() -> i32 { 1 }
pub fn TOML_FLOAT()   -> i32 { 2 }
pub fn TOML_BOOL()    -> i32 { 3 }

// ============================================================================
// TomlDoc — flat key→value store, up to 32 entries
// ============================================================================

pub struct TomlDoc {
    pub keys:      [[u8; 64]; 32],
    pub key_lens:  [i32; 32],
    pub str_vals:  [[u8; 128]; 32],
    pub str_lens:  [i32; 32],
    pub num_vals:  [f64; 32],
    pub bool_vals: [i32; 32],
    pub types:     [i32; 32],
    pub count:     i32,
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal result types
// ============================================================================

// Result from parsing a quoted string body (after opening '"').
struct TStrResult {
    data:    [u8; 128],
    str_len: i32,
    new_pos: i32,   // -1 on error
}

// Result from parsing a number token.
struct TNumResult {
    value:   f64,
    new_pos: i32,
    is_int:  i32,   // 1 if no decimal point seen
}

// ============================================================================
// TomlDoc constructor
// ============================================================================

pub fn toml_doc_new() -> TomlDoc {
    TomlDoc {
        keys:      [[0; 64]; 32],
        key_lens:  [0; 32],
        str_vals:  [[0; 128]; 32],
        str_lens:  [0; 32],
        num_vals:  [0.0; 32],
        bool_vals: [0; 32],
        types:     [0; 32],
        count:     0,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Internal helpers (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

// Skip spaces and tabs (but not newlines). Returns new position.
fn toml_skip_ws(input: &[u8; 4096], pos: i32, len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = pos
    while p < len {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c == 32u8 || c == 9u8 {
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            return p
        }
    }
    p
}

// Skip to end of current line (past '\n'). Returns new position.
fn toml_skip_line(input: &[u8; 4096], pos: i32, len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = pos
    while p < len {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        p = p + 1
        if c == 10u8 {
            return p
        }
    }
    p
}

// Parse a quoted TOML basic string body (after opening '"').
// Returns TStrResult; new_pos=-1 on error.
fn toml_parse_string(input: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, len: i32) -> TStrResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var r = TStrResult {
        data:    [0; 128],
        str_len: 0,
        new_pos: 0 - 1,
    }
    var p = start
    var wpos: i32 = 0
    var done: i32 = 0
    while p < len && done == 0 {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c == 34u8 {
            // closing '"'
            p = p + 1
            done = 1
        } else if c == 92u8 {
            // escape sequence
            p = p + 1
            if p >= len { return r }
            let esc = input[p as usize]
            if esc == 34u8 {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 34u8; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == 92u8 {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 92u8; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == 110u8 {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 10u8; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == 116u8 {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 9u8; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else if esc == 114u8 {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = 13u8; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            } else {
                if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = esc; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            }
            p = p + 1
        } else if c == 10u8 || c == 13u8 {
            // unterminated string
            return r
        } else {
            if wpos < 127 { r.data[wpos as usize] = c; wpos = wpos + 1 }
            p = p + 1
        }
    }
    if done == 0 { return r }
    r.str_len = wpos
    r.new_pos = p
    r
}

// Parse a number starting at pos. Handles optional sign, digits, optional '.'.
// Returns TNumResult; is_int=1 when no decimal point seen.
fn toml_parse_number(input: &[u8; 4096], start: i32, len: i32) -> TNumResult with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p = start
    var negative: i32 = 0
    if p < len && input[p as usize] == 45u8 {
        negative = 1
        p = p + 1
    }
    var int_part: f64 = 0.0
    var int_done: i32 = 0
    while p < len && int_done == 0 {
        let c = input[p as usize]
        if c >= 48u8 && c <= 57u8 {
            int_part = int_part * 10.0 + (c - 48u8) as f64
            p = p + 1
        } else {
            int_done = 1
        }
    }
    var frac: f64 = 0.0
    var frac_div: f64 = 1.0
    var is_int: i32 = 1
    if p < len && input[p as usize] == 46u8 {
        is_int = 0
        p = p + 1
        var frac_done: i32 = 0
        while p < len && frac_done == 0 {
            let c = input[p as usize]
            if c >= 48u8 && c <= 57u8 {
                frac = frac * 10.0 + (c - 48u8) as f64
                frac_div = frac_div * 10.0
                p = p + 1
            } else {
                frac_done = 1
            }
        }
    }
    var result = int_part + frac / frac_div
    if negative == 1 {
        result = 0.0 - result
    }
    TNumResult { value: result, new_pos: p, is_int: is_int }
}

// Compare a key slot in doc against a provided key. Returns 1 if equal.
fn toml_keys_equal(doc: &TomlDoc, slot: i32, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if doc.key_lens[slot as usize] != key_len { return 0 }
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < key_len {
        if doc.keys[slot as usize][i as usize] != key[i as usize] { return 0 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    1
}

// Find slot index for a key. Returns index or -1.
fn toml_find_key(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < doc.count {
        if toml_keys_equal(doc, i, key, key_len) == 1 {
            return i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    0 - 1
}

// ============================================================================
// toml_parse — main parse entry point
// ============================================================================

// Parse a flat TOML document from input bytes.
// Handles: key = "string", key = 123, key = 3.14, key = true/false,
//          # comments, blank lines.
// Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
pub fn toml_parse(input: &[u8; 4096], len: i32, doc: &!TomlDoc) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var p: i32 = 0
    while p < len {
        // Skip leading whitespace on the line.
        p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
        if p >= len { return 0 }

        let c0 = input[p as usize]

        // Blank line or comment — skip to next line.
        if c0 == 10u8 || c0 == 13u8 {
            p = p + 1
            // skip \r\n pair
            if c0 == 13u8 && p < len && input[p as usize] == 10u8 {
                p = p + 1
            }
            // Advance p (loop will handle)
        } else if c0 == 35u8 {
            // '#' comment
            p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
        } else if c0 == 91u8 {
            // '[' table header — skip entire line (no table support)
            p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
        } else {
            // Parse key (bare key: alphanumeric, '-', '_')
            var key64: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
            var klen: i32 = 0
            var key_done: i32 = 0
            while p < len && key_done == 0 {
                let kc = input[p as usize]
                // valid bare key chars
                if (kc >= 65u8 && kc <= 90u8) ||   // A-Z
                   (kc >= 97u8 && kc <= 122u8) ||  // a-z
                   (kc >= 48u8 && kc <= 57u8) ||   // 0-9
                   kc == 45u8 || kc == 95u8 {       // '-', '_'
                    if klen < 63 {
                        key64[klen as usize] = kc
                        klen = klen + 1
                    }
                    p = p + 1
                } else {
                    key_done = 1
                }
            }
            if klen == 0 {
                // Not a valid key start — skip line
                p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
            } else {
                // Skip whitespace before '='
                p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
                if p >= len { return 0 - 1 }
                if input[p as usize] != 61u8 {
                    // '=' expected
                    return 0 - 1
                }
                p = p + 1
                // Skip whitespace after '='
                p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
                if p >= len { return 0 - 1 }

                let vc = input[p as usize]

                if doc.count < 32 {
                    let slot = doc.count
                    // Copy key into slot.
                    var ki: i32 = 0
                    while ki < klen {
                        doc.keys[slot as usize][ki as usize] = key64[ki as usize]
                        ki = ki + 1
                    }
                    doc.key_lens[slot as usize] = klen

                    if vc == 34u8 {
                        // Quoted string value.
                        p = p + 1
                        let sr = toml_parse_string(input, p, len)
                        if sr.new_pos < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
                        p = sr.new_pos
                        doc.types[slot as usize] = 0
                        doc.str_lens[slot as usize] = sr.str_len
                        var si: i32 = 0
                        while si < sr.str_len {
                            doc.str_vals[slot as usize][si as usize] = sr.data[si as usize]
                            si = si + 1
                        }
                        doc.count = doc.count + 1

                    } else if vc == 116u8 {
                        // 'true'
                        if p + 3 < len &&
                           input[(p+1) as usize] == 114u8 &&
                           input[(p+2) as usize] == 117u8 &&
                           input[(p+3) as usize] == 101u8 {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 3
                            doc.bool_vals[slot as usize] = 1
                            p = p + 4
                            doc.count = doc.count + 1
                        } else {
                            return 0 - 1
                        }

                    } else if vc == 102u8 {
                        // 'false'
                        if p + 4 < len &&
                           input[(p+1) as usize] == 97u8  &&
                           input[(p+2) as usize] == 108u8 &&
                           input[(p+3) as usize] == 115u8 &&
                           input[(p+4) as usize] == 101u8 {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 3
                            doc.bool_vals[slot as usize] = 0
                            p = p + 5
                            doc.count = doc.count + 1
                        } else {
                            return 0 - 1
                        }

                    } else if (vc >= 48u8 && vc <= 57u8) || vc == 45u8 {
                        // Number (integer or float).
                        let nr = toml_parse_number(input, p, len)
                        if nr.new_pos <= p { return 0 - 1 }
                        p = nr.new_pos
                        if nr.is_int == 1 {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 1
                        } else {
                            doc.types[slot as usize] = 2
                        }
                        doc.num_vals[slot as usize] = nr.value
                        doc.count = doc.count + 1

                    } else {
                        // Unrecognised value — skip line, don't add entry.
                        p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
                    }
                }

                // Skip trailing whitespace and comment on line.
                p = toml_skip_ws(input, p, len)
                if p < len {
                    let trail = input[p as usize]
                    if trail == 35u8 {
                        // inline comment
                        p = toml_skip_line(input, p, len)
                    } else if trail == 10u8 || trail == 13u8 {
                        p = p + 1
                        if trail == 13u8 && p < len && input[p as usize] == 10u8 {
                            p = p + 1
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    0
}

// ============================================================================
// Accessor functions
// ============================================================================

// Returns string length into out buffer, or -1 if key not found / not a string.
pub fn toml_get_string(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32, out: &![u8; 128]) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = toml_find_key(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    if doc.types[idx as usize] != 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    let slen = doc.str_lens[idx as usize]
    // NOTE: &![u8;128] mutations do NOT propagate in JIT — caller must use
    // doc.str_vals[slot] directly after finding the slot via toml_find_key.
    // This function copies to out for API completeness; JIT callers see stale value.
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < slen {
        out[i as usize] = doc.str_vals[idx as usize][i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
    slen
}

// Returns number value, or 0.0 if not found / not numeric.
pub fn toml_get_number(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = toml_find_key(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx < 0 { return 0.0 }
    let t = doc.types[idx as usize]
    if t == 1 || t == 2 {
        return doc.num_vals[idx as usize]
    }
    0.0
}

// Returns 0 or 1 for bool, -1 if not found / not a bool.
pub fn toml_get_bool(doc: &TomlDoc, key: &[u8; 64], key_len: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let idx = toml_find_key(doc, key, key_len)
    if idx < 0 { return 0 - 1 }
    if doc.types[idx as usize] != 3 { return 0 - 1 }
    doc.bool_vals[idx as usize]
}

// Returns total number of key-value pairs in document.
pub fn toml_doc_count(doc: &TomlDoc) -> i32 {
    doc.count
}

// ============================================================================
// Self-tests
// ============================================================================

pub fn toml_self_test() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0

    // T1: empty doc
    var doc = toml_doc_new()
    if doc.count != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T2: parse integer
    var raw: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    // "version = 3\n"
    raw[0]  = 118u8  // v
    raw[1]  = 101u8  // e
    raw[2]  = 114u8  // r
    raw[3]  = 115u8  // s
    raw[4]  = 105u8  // i
    raw[5]  = 111u8  // o
    raw[6]  = 110u8  // n
    raw[7]  = 32u8   // space
    raw[8]  = 61u8   // =
    raw[9]  = 32u8   // space
    raw[10] = 51u8   // 3
    raw[11] = 10u8   // \n
    let r1 = toml_parse(&raw, 12, &!doc)
    if r1 != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.types[0] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    let vdiff = doc.num_vals[0] - 3.0
    let avdiff = if vdiff < 0.0 { 0.0 - vdiff } else { vdiff }
    if avdiff > 0.0001 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T3: parse bool
    var doc2 = toml_doc_new()
    var raw2: [u8; 4096] = [0; 4096]
    // "debug = true\n"
    raw2[0]  = 100u8  // d
    raw2[1]  = 101u8  // e
    raw2[2]  = 98u8   // b
    raw2[3]  = 117u8  // u
    raw2[4]  = 103u8  // g
    raw2[5]  = 32u8   // space
    raw2[6]  = 61u8   // =
    raw2[7]  = 32u8   // space
    raw2[8]  = 116u8  // t
    raw2[9]  = 114u8  // r
    raw2[10] = 117u8  // u
    raw2[11] = 101u8  // e
    raw2[12] = 10u8   // \n
    let r2 = toml_parse(&raw2, 13, &!doc2)
    if r2 != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc2.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc2.types[0] != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc2.bool_vals[0] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // T4: doc.count (direct field access — avoids borrow conflict after &!doc)
    if doc.count != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    fail
}
