//@ run-pass
// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC PBPK NATIVE DEMO — Sounio Epistemic Computing Showcase
// ============================================================================
// Rapamycin 3-compartment PBPK with GUM uncertainty propagation.
// Compiles to native ELF via lean driver — NO runtime, NO libc, NO JIT.
//
// What this proves: Sounio propagates measurement uncertainty through every
// arithmetic operation in a pharmacokinetic simulation, producing not just
// predicted drug concentrations but confidence-weighted uncertainty bounds.
//
// JCGM 100:2008 (GUM) linearization via finite differences.
// SOTA: Ferron 1997 (CYP3A4), Lampen 1998 (P-gp BBB), Schreiber 1991 (binding)
// ============================================================================

// ---- Math helpers ----

fn ep_abs(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn ep_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        y = (y + x / y) * 0.5
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

fn ep_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

// Print f64 as "integer.fraction" using multiply-truncate (6 digits)
fn print_f64_6(v: f64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0.0 {
        print("-")
        let neg_v = 0.0 - v
        let int_part = neg_v as i64
        let frac = ((neg_v - (int_part as f64)) * 1000000.0) as i64
        print_int(int_part)
        print(".")
        // Pad with leading zeros
        if frac < 100000 { print("0") }
        if frac < 10000 { print("0") }
        if frac < 1000 { print("0") }
        if frac < 100 { print("0") }
        if frac < 10 { print("0") }
        print_int(frac)
        return 0
    }
    let int_part = v as i64
    let frac = ((v - (int_part as f64)) * 1000000.0) as i64
    print_int(int_part)
    print(".")
    if frac < 100000 { print("0") }
    if frac < 10000 { print("0") }
    if frac < 1000 { print("0") }
    if frac < 100 { print("0") }
    if frac < 10 { print("0") }
    print_int(frac)
    return 0
}

// Print f64 with 3 decimal places
fn print_f64_3(v: f64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0.0 {
        print("-")
        let neg_v = 0.0 - v
        let int_part = neg_v as i64
        let frac = ((neg_v - (int_part as f64)) * 1000.0) as i64
        print_int(int_part)
        print(".")
        if frac < 100 { print("0") }
        if frac < 10 { print("0") }
        print_int(frac)
        return 0
    }
    let int_part = v as i64
    let frac = ((v - (int_part as f64)) * 1000.0) as i64
    print_int(int_part)
    print(".")
    if frac < 100 { print("0") }
    if frac < 10 { print("0") }
    print_int(frac)
    return 0
}

// ---- 3-Compartment State ----

struct Rp3St {
    blood: f64,
    brain: f64,
    periph: f64,
}

// ---- Parameters (9-field) ----

struct Rp3Prm {
    v_blood: f64,
    v_brain: f64,
    v_periph: f64,
    q_brain: f64,
    q_periph: f64,
    kp_brain: f64,
    kp_periph: f64,
    cl_hepatic: f64,
    fu_plasma: f64,
}

// ---- Epistemic priors ----

struct EpPriors {
    cl_mean: f64,
    cl_var: f64,
    cl_conf: f64,
    kp_mean: f64,
    kp_var: f64,
    kp_conf: f64,
    fu_mean: f64,
    fu_var: f64,
    fu_conf: f64,
}

// ---- Simulation metrics ----

struct Metrics {
    cmax: f64,
    auc: f64,
    brain_final: f64,
    blood_final: f64,
}

// ---- Epistemic result ----

struct EpResult {
    auc_mean: f64,
    auc_var: f64,
    auc_conf: f64,
    bpr_mean: f64,
    bpr_var: f64,
    s_cl: f64,
    s_kp: f64,
    s_fu: f64,
}

// ---- Vector operations ----

fn rp3_zero() -> Rp3St {
    return Rp3St { blood: 0.0, brain: 0.0, periph: 0.0 }
}

fn rp3_add(a: Rp3St, b: Rp3St) -> Rp3St {
    return Rp3St {
        blood: a.blood + b.blood,
        brain: a.brain + b.brain,
        periph: a.periph + b.periph,
    }
}

fn rp3_scale(s: Rp3St, f: f64) -> Rp3St {
    return Rp3St {
        blood: s.blood * f,
        brain: s.brain * f,
        periph: s.periph * f,
    }
}

// ---- ODE right-hand side ----

fn rp3_ode(st: Rp3St, p: Rp3Prm) -> Rp3St {
    let cl_eff = p.cl_hepatic * p.fu_plasma

    let inflow_brain = p.q_brain / p.v_blood * st.brain / p.kp_brain
    let inflow_periph = p.q_periph / p.v_blood * st.periph / p.kp_periph
    let outflow = (p.q_brain + p.q_periph) / p.v_blood * st.blood
    let clearance = cl_eff / p.v_blood * st.blood

    let d_blood = inflow_brain + inflow_periph - outflow - clearance
    let d_brain = (p.q_brain / p.v_brain) * (st.blood - st.brain / p.kp_brain)
    let d_periph = (p.q_periph / p.v_periph) * (st.blood - st.periph / p.kp_periph)

    return Rp3St { blood: d_blood, brain: d_brain, periph: d_periph }
}

// ---- RK4 integrator ----

fn rk4_advance(st: Rp3St, p: Rp3Prm, dt: f64) -> Rp3St {
    let k1 = rp3_ode(st, p)
    let s2 = rp3_add(st, rp3_scale(k1, dt * 0.5))
    let k2 = rp3_ode(s2, p)
    let s3 = rp3_add(st, rp3_scale(k2, dt * 0.5))
    let k3 = rp3_ode(s3, p)
    let s4 = rp3_add(st, rp3_scale(k3, dt))
    let k4 = rp3_ode(s4, p)

    let w = rp3_add(k1, rp3_add(rp3_scale(k2, 2.0), rp3_add(rp3_scale(k3, 2.0), k4)))
    return rp3_add(st, rp3_scale(w, dt / 6.0))
}

// ---- Run simulation ----

fn run_sim(prm: Rp3Prm, dose_mg: f64, t_end: f64) -> Metrics {
    let c0 = dose_mg / prm.v_blood
    var st = Rp3St { blood: c0, brain: 0.0, periph: 0.0 }
    var t = 0.0
    let dt = 0.1
    var cmax = c0
    var auc = 0.0
    var c_prev = c0

    while t < t_end {
        var dt_use = dt
        if t + dt > t_end { dt_use = t_end - t }
        st = rk4_advance(st, prm, dt_use)
        if st.blood > cmax { cmax = st.blood }
        auc = auc + (c_prev + st.blood) * 0.5 * dt_use
        c_prev = st.blood
        t = t + dt_use
    }

    return Metrics { cmax: cmax, auc: auc, brain_final: st.brain, blood_final: st.blood }
}

// ---- Reference parameters ----

fn mean_params() -> Rp3Prm {
    return Rp3Prm {
        v_blood: 5.0,
        v_brain: 1.4,
        v_periph: 50.0,
        q_brain: 0.05,
        q_periph: 87.0,
        kp_brain: 0.08,
        kp_periph: 0.5,
        cl_hepatic: 12.4,
        fu_plasma: 0.08,
    }
}

fn get_priors() -> EpPriors {
    return EpPriors {
        cl_mean: 12.4,    cl_var: 54.76,     cl_conf: 0.65,
        kp_mean: 0.08,    kp_var: 0.000625,  kp_conf: 0.55,
        fu_mean: 0.08,    fu_var: 0.0004,    fu_conf: 0.72,
    }
}

// ---- GUM finite-difference step size ----

fn fdiff_h(mean: f64, variance: f64) -> f64 {
    let h_rel = 0.000001 * ep_abs(mean)
    let h_abs = 0.01 * ep_sqrt(variance)
    return ep_max(h_rel, h_abs)
}

// ---- Epistemic propagation ----

fn run_epistemic(priors: EpPriors, dose: f64, t_end: f64) -> EpResult {
    let prm_ref = mean_params()
    let ref_m = run_sim(prm_ref, dose, t_end)
    let auc_ref = ref_m.auc
    var bpr_ref = 0.0
    if ref_m.blood_final > 0.000000000001 {
        bpr_ref = ref_m.brain_final / ref_m.blood_final
    }

    // Perturbation 1: CL
    let h_cl = fdiff_h(priors.cl_mean, priors.cl_var)
    var prm_cl = mean_params()
    prm_cl.cl_hepatic = prm_ref.cl_hepatic + h_cl
    let m_cl = run_sim(prm_cl, dose, t_end)
    let dauc_dcl = (m_cl.auc - auc_ref) / h_cl

    // Perturbation 2: kp_brain
    let h_kp = fdiff_h(priors.kp_mean, priors.kp_var)
    var prm_kp = mean_params()
    prm_kp.kp_brain = prm_ref.kp_brain + h_kp
    let m_kp = run_sim(prm_kp, dose, t_end)
    let dauc_dkp = (m_kp.auc - auc_ref) / h_kp

    // Perturbation 3: fu_plasma
    let h_fu = fdiff_h(priors.fu_mean, priors.fu_var)
    var prm_fu = mean_params()
    prm_fu.fu_plasma = prm_ref.fu_plasma + h_fu
    let m_fu = run_sim(prm_fu, dose, t_end)
    let dauc_dfu = (m_fu.auc - auc_ref) / h_fu

    // GUM variance propagation
    let var_auc = dauc_dcl * dauc_dcl * priors.cl_var
               + dauc_dkp * dauc_dkp * priors.kp_var
               + dauc_dfu * dauc_dfu * priors.fu_var

    // BPR variance (finite diff)
    var bpr_cl = 0.0
    if m_cl.blood_final > 0.000000000001 { bpr_cl = m_cl.brain_final / m_cl.blood_final }
    var bpr_kp = 0.0
    if m_kp.blood_final > 0.000000000001 { bpr_kp = m_kp.brain_final / m_kp.blood_final }
    let dbpr_dcl = (bpr_cl - bpr_ref) / h_cl
    let dbpr_dkp = (bpr_kp - bpr_ref) / h_kp

    let var_bpr = dbpr_dcl * dbpr_dcl * priors.cl_var
               + dbpr_dkp * dbpr_dkp * priors.kp_var

    // Sensitivity fractions
    var s_cl = 0.0
    var s_kp = 0.0
    var s_fu = 0.0
    if var_auc > 0.0000000000000000000000000000001 {
        s_cl = dauc_dcl * dauc_dcl * priors.cl_var / var_auc
        s_kp = dauc_dkp * dauc_dkp * priors.kp_var / var_auc
        s_fu = dauc_dfu * dauc_dfu * priors.fu_var / var_auc
    }

    // Evidence-weighted confidence
    let conf_auc = priors.cl_conf * s_cl + priors.kp_conf * s_kp + priors.fu_conf * s_fu

    return EpResult {
        auc_mean: auc_ref,
        auc_var: var_auc,
        auc_conf: conf_auc,
        bpr_mean: bpr_ref,
        bpr_var: var_bpr,
        s_cl: s_cl,
        s_kp: s_kp,
        s_fu: s_fu,
    }
}

// ---- Main ----

fn main() -> i64 {
    print("======================================================================\n")
    print("  SOUNIO EPISTEMIC PBPK — Native ELF Demo\n")
    print("  Rapamycin 3-Compartment: Blood / Brain (BBB, P-gp) / Peripheral\n")
    print("  GUM Uncertainty Propagation (JCGM 100:2008)\n")
    print("======================================================================\n\n")

    let priors = get_priors()
    let dose = 5.0
    let t_end = 48.0
    let ep = run_epistemic(priors, dose, t_end)

    // ---- Display results ----

    print("  Drug: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) 5mg IV bolus\n")
    print("  Simulation: 48h, RK4 dt=0.1h (480 steps x 4 perturbations)\n\n")

    print("  AUC(0-48h):  ")
    print_f64_3(ep.auc_mean)
    print(" +/- ")
    print_f64_3(ep_sqrt(ep.auc_var))
    print(" mg*h/L\n")

    print("  Confidence:  ")
    print_f64_3(ep.auc_conf)
    print("\n")

    let cv_auc = ep_sqrt(ep.auc_var) / ep.auc_mean
    print("  CV(AUC):     ")
    print_f64_3(cv_auc * 100.0)
    print("%\n\n")

    print("  Brain/Plasma ratio: ")
    print_f64_6(ep.bpr_mean)
    print(" +/- ")
    print_f64_6(ep_sqrt(ep.bpr_var))
    print("\n\n")

    print("  Sensitivity Analysis (AUC variance contributions):\n")
    print("    CL_hepatic (CYP3A4): ")
    print_f64_3(ep.s_cl * 100.0)
    print("%\n")
    print("    kp_brain   (P-gp):   ")
    print_f64_3(ep.s_kp * 100.0)
    print("%\n")
    print("    fu_plasma  (binding): ")
    print_f64_3(ep.s_fu * 100.0)
    print("%\n\n")

    // ---- Validation tests ----

    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    // T1: Brain/plasma < 0.15 (P-gp efflux)
    if ep.bpr_mean > 0.0 {
        if ep.bpr_mean < 0.15 {
            print("  PASS: T1 brain/plasma < 0.15 (P-gp verified)\n")
            passed = passed + 1
        } else {
            print("  FAIL: T1 brain/plasma >= 0.15\n")
            failed = failed + 1
        }
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: T1 brain/plasma <= 0\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T2: CV(AUC) > 30% (CYP3A4 variability)
    if cv_auc > 0.30 {
        print("  PASS: T2 CV(AUC) > 30% (CYP3A4 variability propagated)\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: T2 CV(AUC) <= 30%\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T3: All variances > 0
    if ep.auc_var > 0.0 {
        if ep.bpr_var > 0.0 {
            print("  PASS: T3 all epistemic variances > 0\n")
            passed = passed + 1
        } else {
            print("  FAIL: T3 bpr_var <= 0\n")
            failed = failed + 1
        }
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: T3 auc_var <= 0\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T4: Causal monotonicity — AUC(CL/2) > AUC(CL)
    var prm_low = mean_params()
    prm_low.cl_hepatic = 6.2
    let m_low = run_sim(prm_low, dose, t_end)
    if m_low.auc > ep.auc_mean {
        print("  PASS: T4 AUC(CL/2) > AUC(CL) (causal monotonicity)\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: T4 causal monotonicity violated\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T5: CL dominates AUC uncertainty (s_cl > 0.5)
    if ep.s_cl > 0.5 {
        print("  PASS: T5 CL dominates AUC uncertainty (s_cl > 0.5)\n")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: T5 s_cl <= 0.5\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    // T6: Confidence in valid range
    if ep.auc_conf > 0.0 {
        if ep.auc_conf < 1.0 {
            print("  PASS: T6 confidence in (0,1)\n")
            passed = passed + 1
        } else {
            print("  FAIL: T6 confidence >= 1.0\n")
            failed = failed + 1
        }
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: T6 confidence <= 0\n")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("\n======================================================================\n")
    print("  RESULT: ")
    print_int(passed)
    print("/6 PASS, ")
    print_int(failed)
    print(" FAIL\n")

    if failed == 0 {
        print("\n  No other language compiles uncertainty propagation to native code.\n")
        print("  This ELF binary carries epistemic guarantees through every operation.\n")
    }
    print("======================================================================\n")

    return failed
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/epistemic_reaction_glycolysis.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 10 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// Epistemic Reaction — Glycolysis Step 1 Test Suite
//
// First provenance-conserving chemical reaction in any self-hosted language.
// Glucose + ATP → Glucose-6-Phosphate + ADP (hexokinase)
//
// Verifies the invariant: product provenance is a deterministic function
// of reactant provenance, and delta_32 < 96 is preserved across the
// transformation (hardware accumulator bound).
//
// All functions inlined (tests cannot import stdlib).

// ============================================================================
// MERKLE INFRASTRUCTURE (inlined)
// ============================================================================

let RXN_MERKLE_SALT_A: i64 = 0x4F4D4547
let RXN_MERKLE_SALT_B: i64 = 0x4147454E
let RXN_MERKLE_SALT_C: i64 = 0x45534953
let RXN_MERKLE_SALT_D: i64 = 0x76312E30
let RXN_MAX_SPECIES: i64 = 8

fn rxn_merkle_mix(a: i64, b: i64, c: i64, salt: i64) -> i64 {
    ((a ^ b) + c + salt) ^ (a << 5) ^ (b >> 7)
}

fn rxn_merkle_root_lane_l64(
    p0: i64, p1: i64, p2: i64, p3: i64, p4: i64
) -> i64 {
    let h0 = rxn_merkle_mix(p0, p1, p2, RXN_MERKLE_SALT_A)
    let h1 = rxn_merkle_mix(p3, p4, h0, RXN_MERKLE_SALT_B)
    let h2 = rxn_merkle_mix(h0, h1, p0 ^ p3, RXN_MERKLE_SALT_C)
    rxn_merkle_mix(h1, h2, p1 ^ p2, RXN_MERKLE_SALT_D)
}

fn rxn_metabolite_hash(symbol: i64) -> i64 {
    var hash: i64 = 5381
    hash = hash * 33 + symbol
    hash & 9223372036854775807
}

fn rxn_provenance_seed(item_hash: i64) -> i64 {
    rxn_merkle_root_lane_l64(0, item_hash, 0, 0, 1)
}

fn rxn_provenance_merge(
    existing_root_l64: i64,
    item_hash: i64,
    variance_q32_32: i64,
    confidence_beta: i64
) -> i64 {
    rxn_merkle_root_lane_l64(
        existing_root_l64,
        item_hash,
        variance_q32_32,
        confidence_beta,
        existing_root_l64 ^ item_hash
    )
}

fn rxn_delta_32(fidelity: i64, provenance: i64, quantum: i64) -> i64 {
    let frac_f = fidelity - (fidelity / 8) * 8
    let frac_p = provenance - (provenance / 16) * 16
    let frac_q = quantum - (quantum / 32) * 32
    frac_f * 4 + frac_p * 2 + frac_q
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC REACTION STRUCT (inlined)
// ============================================================================

struct EpistemicReaction {
    reactant_prov_l64: [i64; 8],
    reactant_variance_q32_32: [i64; 8],
    reactant_confidence_beta: [i64; 8],
    reactant_count: i64,

    product_prov_l64: [i64; 8],
    product_variance_q32_32: [i64; 8],
    product_confidence_beta: [i64; 8],
    product_count: i64,

    rxn_provenance_l64: i64,
    rxn_variance_q32_32: i64,
    rxn_confidence_beta: i64,

    enzyme_prov_l64: i64,
    applied: i64,
}

fn rxn_new() -> EpistemicReaction {
    EpistemicReaction {
        reactant_prov_l64: [0; 8],
        reactant_variance_q32_32: [0; 8],
        reactant_confidence_beta: [0; 8],
        reactant_count: 0,

        product_prov_l64: [0; 8],
        product_variance_q32_32: [0; 8],
        product_confidence_beta: [0; 8],
        product_count: 0,

        rxn_provenance_l64: 0,
        rxn_variance_q32_32: 0,
        rxn_confidence_beta: 1,

        enzyme_prov_l64: 0 - 1,
        applied: 0,
    }
}

fn rxn_add_reactant(
    r: EpistemicReaction, prov_l64: i64, variance: i64, confidence: i64
) -> EpistemicReaction with Mut, Panic {
    var rxn = r
    if rxn.reactant_count >= RXN_MAX_SPECIES {
        return rxn
    }
    let id = rxn.reactant_count
    rxn.reactant_prov_l64[id] = prov_l64
    rxn.reactant_variance_q32_32[id] = variance
    rxn.reactant_confidence_beta[id] = confidence
    rxn.reactant_count = rxn.reactant_count + 1
    rxn
}

fn rxn_add_product(
    r: EpistemicReaction, product_hash: i64, variance: i64, confidence: i64
) -> EpistemicReaction with Mut, Panic {
    var rxn = r
    if rxn.product_count >= RXN_MAX_SPECIES {
        return rxn
    }
    let id = rxn.product_count
    rxn.product_prov_l64[id] = rxn_provenance_seed(product_hash)
    rxn.product_variance_q32_32[id] = variance
    rxn.product_confidence_beta[id] = confidence
    rxn.product_count = rxn.product_count + 1
    rxn
}

fn rxn_set_enzyme(r: EpistemicReaction, enzyme_prov: i64) -> EpistemicReaction {
    var rxn = r
    rxn.enzyme_prov_l64 = enzyme_prov
    rxn
}

fn rxn_reactant_count(r: EpistemicReaction) -> i64 { r.reactant_count }
fn rxn_product_count(r: EpistemicReaction) -> i64 { r.product_count }
fn rxn_provenance(r: EpistemicReaction) -> i64 { r.rxn_provenance_l64 }
fn rxn_is_applied(r: EpistemicReaction) -> bool { r.applied == 1 }

fn rxn_product_provenance(r: EpistemicReaction, idx: i64) -> i64 with Panic, Div {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= r.product_count { return 0 }
    r.product_prov_l64[idx]
}

fn rxn_product_variance(r: EpistemicReaction, idx: i64) -> i64 with Panic, Div {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= r.product_count { return 0 }
    r.product_variance_q32_32[idx]
}

fn rxn_product_confidence(r: EpistemicReaction, idx: i64) -> i64 with Panic, Div {
    if idx < 0 || idx >= r.product_count { return 0 }
    r.product_confidence_beta[idx]
}

fn rxn_apply(r: EpistemicReaction) -> EpistemicReaction with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn = r

    // Phase 1: fold reactant provenance into reaction root
    var root: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < rxn.reactant_count {
        root = rxn_merkle_mix(
            root,
            rxn.reactant_prov_l64[i],
            rxn.reactant_variance_q32_32[i],
            RXN_MERKLE_SALT_A
        )
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Include enzyme if present
    if rxn.enzyme_prov_l64 >= 0 {
        root = rxn_merkle_mix(root, rxn.enzyme_prov_l64, 0, RXN_MERKLE_SALT_B)
    }

    rxn.rxn_provenance_l64 = root
    rxn.rxn_variance_q32_32 = rxn.rxn_variance_q32_32 + 1
    rxn.rxn_confidence_beta = rxn.rxn_confidence_beta + 1

    // Phase 2: merge reaction root into each product's provenance
    var j: i64 = 0
    while j < rxn.product_count {
        let merged = rxn_provenance_merge(
            rxn.product_prov_l64[j],
            root,
            rxn.product_variance_q32_32[j] + 1,
            rxn.product_confidence_beta[j] + 1
        )
        rxn.product_prov_l64[j] = merged
        rxn.product_variance_q32_32[j] = rxn.product_variance_q32_32[j] + 1
        rxn.product_confidence_beta[j] = rxn.product_confidence_beta[j] + 1
        j = j + 1
    }

    rxn.applied = 1
    rxn
}

fn rxn_verify_conservation(r: EpistemicReaction) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if r.applied != 1 { return false }
    if r.rxn_provenance_l64 == 0 { return false }

    let rxn_delta = rxn_delta_32(r.rxn_variance_q32_32, 0, r.rxn_confidence_beta)
    if rxn_delta < 0 || rxn_delta >= 96 { return false }

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < r.product_count {
        if r.product_prov_l64[i] == 0 { return false }
        let pdelta = rxn_delta_32(r.product_variance_q32_32[i], 0, r.product_confidence_beta[i])
        if pdelta < 0 || pdelta >= 96 { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn test_empty_reaction() -> bool {
    let rxn = rxn_new()
    rxn_reactant_count(rxn) == 0 && rxn_product_count(rxn) == 0
        && !rxn_is_applied(rxn) && rxn_provenance(rxn) == 0
}

fn test_add_reactant() -> bool with Mut, Panic {
    var rxn = rxn_new()
    let prov = rxn_provenance_seed(42)
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, prov, 0, 1)
    rxn_reactant_count(rxn) == 1
}

fn test_add_product() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn = rxn_new()
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, 99, 0, 1)
    rxn_product_count(rxn) == 1 && rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 0) != 0
}

fn test_apply_sets_provenance() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn = rxn_new()
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, rxn_provenance_seed(42), 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, 99, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_apply(rxn)
    rxn_is_applied(rxn) && rxn_provenance(rxn) != 0
}

fn test_apply_changes_product_provenance() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn = rxn_new()
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, rxn_provenance_seed(42), 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, 99, 0, 1)
    let before = rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 0)
    rxn = rxn_apply(rxn)
    let after = rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 0)
    before != 0 && after != 0 && before != after
}

fn test_different_reactants_different_root() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn1 = rxn_new()
    rxn1 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn1, rxn_provenance_seed(10), 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_add_product(rxn1, 99, 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_apply(rxn1)

    var rxn2 = rxn_new()
    rxn2 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn2, rxn_provenance_seed(20), 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_add_product(rxn2, 99, 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_apply(rxn2)

    rxn_provenance(rxn1) != rxn_provenance(rxn2)
}

fn test_enzyme_changes_root() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn1 = rxn_new()
    rxn1 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn1, rxn_provenance_seed(42), 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_add_product(rxn1, 99, 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_apply(rxn1)

    var rxn2 = rxn_new()
    rxn2 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn2, rxn_provenance_seed(42), 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_add_product(rxn2, 99, 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_set_enzyme(rxn2, rxn_provenance_seed(777))
    rxn2 = rxn_apply(rxn2)

    rxn_provenance(rxn1) != rxn_provenance(rxn2)
}

fn test_delta_32_bound() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var rxn = rxn_new()
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, rxn_provenance_seed(1), 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, rxn_provenance_seed(2), 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, 3, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, 4, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_apply(rxn)
    rxn_verify_conservation(rxn)
}

fn test_glycolysis_step1() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let glucose_hash = rxn_metabolite_hash(0x474C55)
    let atp_hash = rxn_metabolite_hash(0x415450)
    let g6p_hash = rxn_metabolite_hash(0x473650)
    let adp_hash = rxn_metabolite_hash(0x414450)
    let hexokinase_hash = rxn_metabolite_hash(0x48454B)

    let glucose_prov = rxn_provenance_seed(glucose_hash)
    let atp_prov = rxn_provenance_seed(atp_hash)
    let hexokinase_prov = rxn_provenance_seed(hexokinase_hash)

    var rxn = rxn_new()
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, glucose_prov, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_reactant(rxn, atp_prov, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, g6p_hash, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_add_product(rxn, adp_hash, 0, 1)
    rxn = rxn_set_enzyme(rxn, hexokinase_prov)

    let g6p_before = rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 0)
    let adp_before = rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 1)

    rxn = rxn_apply(rxn)

    let g6p_after = rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 0)
    let adp_after = rxn_product_provenance(rxn, 1)

    let applied_ok = rxn_is_applied(rxn)
    let counts_ok = rxn_reactant_count(rxn) == 2 && rxn_product_count(rxn) == 2
    let rxn_prov_ok = rxn_provenance(rxn) != 0
    let changed = g6p_after != g6p_before && adp_after != adp_before
    let nonzero = g6p_after != 0 && adp_after != 0
    let differ = g6p_after != adp_after
    let conserved = rxn_verify_conservation(rxn)

    applied_ok && counts_ok && rxn_prov_ok && changed
        && nonzero && differ && conserved
}

fn test_deterministic_replay() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Same inputs → same outputs (provenance is deterministic)
    let glucose_prov = rxn_provenance_seed(rxn_metabolite_hash(0x474C55))
    let atp_prov = rxn_provenance_seed(rxn_metabolite_hash(0x415450))

    var rxn1 = rxn_new()
    rxn1 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn1, glucose_prov, 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn1, atp_prov, 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_add_product(rxn1, 0x473650, 0, 1)
    rxn1 = rxn_apply(rxn1)

    var rxn2 = rxn_new()
    rxn2 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn2, glucose_prov, 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_add_reactant(rxn2, atp_prov, 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_add_product(rxn2, 0x473650, 0, 1)
    rxn2 = rxn_apply(rxn2)

    rxn_provenance(rxn1) == rxn_provenance(rxn2)
        && rxn_product_provenance(rxn1, 0) == rxn_product_provenance(rxn2, 0)
}

        failed = failed + 1

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/epistemic_refined.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// EpistemicValue<RefinementType> integration tests
// Issue #8: Uncertainty propagation through refined values

// This file demonstrates the intended syntax for epistemic refined values
// in Sounio once the full type system integration is complete.

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 1: Basic positive dose with confidence
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// A dose measurement that is both:
// - Refined: guaranteed to be positive (> 0)
// - Epistemic: has 95% confidence from the measurement

fn test_positive_dose() -> bool {
    // In full Sounio, this would be:
    // let dose: Knowledge[{ x: f64 | x > 0 }] = measure_dose(sample)

    // For now, we simulate with plain values
    let dose: f64 = 500.0
    let confidence: f64 = 0.95

    // Check: value is positive (refinement holds)
    let refinement_ok = dose > 0.0

    // Check: confidence is high enough for extraction
    let confidence_ok = confidence >= 0.80

    refinement_ok && confidence_ok
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 2: Bounded interval with epistemic uncertainty
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// A probability value that is:
// - Refined: bounded to [0, 1]
// - Epistemic: uncertainty widens the effective interval

fn test_probability_bounds() -> bool {
    let prob: f64 = 0.75
    let confidence: f64 = 0.90

    // Base uncertainty factor (10% at confidence 0)
    let base_uncertainty: f64 = 0.1

    // Effective half-width based on confidence
    // At confidence 1.0, half_width = 0 (point)
    // At confidence 0.0, half_width = base_uncertainty * |value|
    let uncertainty_factor = 1.0 - confidence
    let half_width = prob * base_uncertainty * uncertainty_factor

    // Epistemic interval
    let lower = prob - half_width
    let upper = prob + half_width

    // Check: epistemic interval is within refinement bounds [0, 1]
    lower >= 0.0 && upper <= 1.0
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 3: Interval arithmetic for addition
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// When adding two epistemic refined values:
// - Refinement bounds add
// - Epistemic intervals add (using interval arithmetic)
// - Confidence is minimum of operands

fn test_interval_add() -> bool {
    // First value: 10.0 +/- 0.5, bounds [5, 15]
    let a_value: f64 = 10.0
    let a_half_width: f64 = 0.5
    let a_lower_bound: f64 = 5.0
    let a_upper_bound: f64 = 15.0
    let a_confidence: f64 = 0.90

    // Second value: 20.0 +/- 1.0, bounds [15, 25]
    let b_value: f64 = 20.0
    let b_half_width: f64 = 1.0
    let b_lower_bound: f64 = 15.0
    let b_upper_bound: f64 = 25.0
    let b_confidence: f64 = 0.85

    // Result: 30.0 +/- 1.5, bounds [20, 40]
    let sum_value = a_value + b_value
    let sum_half_width = a_half_width + b_half_width
    let sum_lower_bound = a_lower_bound + b_lower_bound
    let sum_upper_bound = a_upper_bound + b_upper_bound

    // Confidence is minimum
    var min_conf = a_confidence
    if b_confidence < min_conf {
        min_conf = b_confidence
    }

    // Verify interval arithmetic
    let value_ok = sum_value == 30.0
    let width_ok = sum_half_width == 1.5
    let bounds_ok = sum_lower_bound == 20.0 && sum_upper_bound == 40.0
    let conf_ok = min_conf == 0.85

    value_ok && width_ok && bounds_ok && conf_ok
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 4: Refinement clamping of epistemic interval
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// When epistemic uncertainty would exceed refinement bounds,
// the effective interval is clamped

fn test_interval_clamping() -> bool {
    // Value with high uncertainty near bound
    let value: f64 = 0.1     // Close to lower bound of [0, 1]
    let half_width: f64 = 0.2  // Would give interval [-0.1, 0.3]

    // Refinement bounds: [0, 1]
    let ref_lower: f64 = 0.0
    let ref_upper: f64 = 1.0

    // Raw epistemic interval
    let raw_lower = value - half_width
    let raw_upper = value + half_width

    // Clamped interval
    var clamped_lower = raw_lower
    if clamped_lower < ref_lower {
        clamped_lower = ref_lower
    }

    var clamped_upper = raw_upper
    if clamped_upper > ref_upper {
        clamped_upper = ref_upper
    }

    // Expected: [0.0, 0.3] (clamped at 0)
    let lower_ok = clamped_lower == 0.0
    let upper_ok = clamped_upper == 0.3

    lower_ok && upper_ok
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 5: Extraction with confidence threshold
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_extraction() -> bool {
    let value: f64 = 42.0
    let confidence: f64 = 0.85

    // Should extract at threshold 0.80
    let extract_low = confidence >= 0.80

    // Should NOT extract at threshold 0.90
    let extract_high = confidence >= 0.90

    extract_low && !extract_high
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Test 6: Dose calculation with propagated uncertainty
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Simulates a pharmacokinetic calculation where:
// - Weight has measurement uncertainty
// - Dose calculation propagates uncertainty
// - Result must satisfy safety bounds

fn test_dose_calculation() -> bool {
    // Patient weight: 70 kg with 95% confidence
    let weight: f64 = 70.0
    let weight_conf: f64 = 0.95

    // Dose per kg: 10 mg/kg with 99% confidence (well-established)
    let dose_per_kg: f64 = 10.0
    let dose_conf: f64 = 0.99

    // Calculated dose
    let dose = weight * dose_per_kg

    // Propagated confidence is minimum
    var result_conf = weight_conf
    if dose_conf < result_conf {
        result_conf = dose_conf
    }

    // Safety bounds: 100 < dose < 1500 mg
    let safe_lower: f64 = 100.0
    let safe_upper: f64 = 1500.0

    // Check safety
    let in_bounds = dose > safe_lower && dose < safe_upper

    // Check confidence sufficient for clinical use (>90%)
    let conf_ok = result_conf >= 0.90

    in_bounds && conf_ok
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Main test runner
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn main() with IO, Mut {
    var pass_count: i32 = 0
    var fail_count: i32 = 0

    // Test 1
    if test_positive_dose() {
        print("test_positive_dose: PASS\n")
        pass_count = pass_count + 1
    } else {
        print("test_positive_dose: FAIL\n")
        fail_count = fail_count + 1
    }

    // Test 2
    if test_probability_bounds() {
        print("test_probability_bounds: PASS\n")
        pass_count = pass_count + 1
    } else {
        print("test_probability_bounds: FAIL\n")
        fail_count = fail_count + 1
    }

    // Test 3
    if test_interval_add() {
        print("test_interval_add: PASS\n")
        pass_count = pass_count + 1
    } else {
        print("test_interval_add: FAIL\n")
        fail_count = fail_count + 1
    }

    // Test 4
    if test_interval_clamping() {
        print("test_interval_clamping: PASS\n")
        pass_count = pass_count + 1
    } else {
        print("test_interval_clamping: FAIL\n")
        fail_count = fail_count + 1
    }

    // Test 5
    if test_extraction() {
        print("test_extraction: PASS\n")
        pass_count = pass_count + 1
    } else {
        print("test_extraction: FAIL\n")
        fail_count = fail_count + 1
    }

    // Test 6
    if test_dose_calculation() {
        print("test_dose_calculation: PASS\n")
        pass_count = pass_count + 1
    } else {
        print("test_dose_calculation: FAIL\n")
        fail_count = fail_count + 1
    }

    // Summary
    print("\n--- EpistemicRefined Tests Complete ---\n")
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/epistemic_subsumption.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ ignore BLOCKED: pinned binary does not support Knowledge<T, epsilon < V> syntax
//@ expect-stdout: epistemic subsumption: PASS

// Knowledge<f64, eps=0.01> IS assignable to Knowledge<f64, eps=0.1>
// because 0.01 <= 0.1 (tighter bound satisfies looser requirement)

fn needs_loose(k: Knowledge<f64, epsilon < 0.1>) -> f64 {
    k.value
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Epistemic {
    let precise: Knowledge<f64, epsilon < 0.01> = measure(500.0, uncertainty: 5.0)
    let result = needs_loose(precise)
    print("epistemic subsumption: PASS\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/epistemic_unspecified_epsilon.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ ignore BLOCKED: pinned binary does not support Knowledge<T, epsilon < V> syntax
//@ expect-stdout: unspecified epsilon: PASS

// Knowledge<f64> (no epsilon) should be compatible with any epsilon bound
fn needs_epsilon(k: Knowledge<f64, epsilon < 0.05>) -> f64 {
    k.value
}

fn accepts_any(k: Knowledge<f64>) -> f64 {
    k.value
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Epistemic {
    let k: Knowledge<f64> = measure(500.0, uncertainty: 2.5)
    let result = accepts_any(k)
    print("unspecified epsilon: PASS\n")
    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/epsilon_comparison_valid.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Test: where result.ε >= model.ε — SMT-verifiable ε monotonicity refinement.
// A perception function that can only equal or increase uncertainty
// (active inference: observations reduce free energy, never add it).

fn perceive(model: Knowledge[f64]) -> Knowledge[f64] {
    // Observation fuses with prior — confidence can only stay or improve
    // SMT backend verifies: result.ε >= model.ε is satisfied by the implementation
    let obs: Knowledge[f64] = Knowledge { value: 0.95, epsilon: 0.05 }
    model * obs
}

fn main() with IO {
    let prior: Knowledge[f64] = Knowledge { value: 0.5, epsilon: 0.3 }
    let posterior = perceive(prior)
    println(posterior)
    // Expected: confidence >= 0.3 (monotonicity holds)
}

//@ run-pass
// FFI ctypes test - pointer arithmetic and memory operations
//
// Self-contained test suite validating basic FFI type operations:
//   pointer offset calculation, c_int size assumptions,
//   null pointer detection, manual memset/memcmp

// ============================================================================
// C TYPE DEFINITIONS (mirrors ffi::ctypes)
// ============================================================================

// Standard C integer sizes (assuming LP64 / x86-64)
fn size_of_c_int() -> i32 {
    return 4
}

fn size_of_c_long() -> i32 {
    return 8
}

fn size_of_c_char() -> i32 {
    return 1
}

fn size_of_ptr() -> i32 {
    return 8
}

// ============================================================================
// POINTER ARITHMETIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

// Compute byte offset for an array element: base + index * element_size
fn ptr_offset(base: i64, index: i32, element_size: i32) -> i64 {
    return base + (index as i64) * (element_size as i64)
}

// Compute the number of elements between two pointers
fn ptr_diff(p1: i64, p2: i64, element_size: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    let byte_diff = p1 - p2
    return (byte_diff / (element_size as i64)) as i32
}

// Check if a pointer value is null (zero)
fn is_null_ptr(p: i64) -> bool {
    return p == 0
}

// Align a pointer up to a given alignment
fn align_up(addr: i64, alignment: i32) -> i64 {
    let a = alignment as i64
    let mask = a - 1
    return (addr + mask) & (0 - a)
}

// ============================================================================
// MANUAL MEMORY OPERATIONS (byte-level simulation)
// ============================================================================

// Simulated memory buffer: fixed-size array of bytes represented as i32
// (since Sounio uses i32 for small values)

struct MemBuffer {
    data: [i32; 256],
    size: i32,
}

fn membuf_new() -> MemBuffer with Mut {
    var data: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    MemBuffer { data: data, size: 256 }
}

// Set all bytes in buffer to a given value (simulated memset)
fn membuf_set(buf: &! MemBuffer, value: i32, count: i32) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < count && i < buf.size {
        buf.data[i] = value
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Compare two buffers byte-by-byte (simulated memcmp)
// Returns: 0 if equal, negative if a < b, positive if a > b
fn membuf_cmp(a: MemBuffer, b: MemBuffer, count: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < count {
        if a.data[i] < b.data[i] {
            return 0 - 1
        }
        if a.data[i] > b.data[i] {
            return 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 0
}

// Copy bytes from source to destination (simulated memcpy)
fn membuf_copy(dst: &! MemBuffer, src: MemBuffer, count: i32) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < count && i < dst.size && i < src.size {
        dst.data[i] = src.data[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Find first occurrence of a byte value (simulated memchr)
// Returns index or -1 if not found
fn membuf_chr(buf: MemBuffer, value: i32, count: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < count && i < buf.size {
        if buf.data[i] == value {
            return i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return 0 - 1
}

// Test 1: Pointer offset calculation for i32 array
fn test_ptr_offset_i32() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let base = 0x1000 as i64
    let elem_size = size_of_c_int()
    // Element 0 should be at base
    let p0 = ptr_offset(base, 0, elem_size)
    let ok1 = p0 == base
    // Element 5 should be at base + 5*4 = base + 20
    let p5 = ptr_offset(base, 5, elem_size)
    let ok2 = p5 == base + 20
    // Element 10 should be at base + 40
    let p10 = ptr_offset(base, 10, elem_size)
    let ok3 = p10 == base + 40
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}

// Test 2: Pointer offset for byte array (c_char)
fn test_ptr_offset_char() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let base = 0x2000 as i64
    let elem_size = size_of_c_char()
    // For char arrays, offset == index
    let p3 = ptr_offset(base, 3, elem_size)
    let ok1 = p3 == base + 3
    let p100 = ptr_offset(base, 100, elem_size)
    let ok2 = p100 == base + 100
    return ok1 && ok2
}

// Test 3: Pointer difference (inverse of offset)
fn test_ptr_diff() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let base = 0x3000 as i64
    let elem_size = size_of_c_int()
    let p0 = base
    let p7 = ptr_offset(base, 7, elem_size)
    let diff = ptr_diff(p7, p0, elem_size)
    let ok1 = diff == 7
    // Diff of same pointer should be 0
    let diff0 = ptr_diff(p0, p0, elem_size)
    let ok2 = diff0 == 0
    return ok1 && ok2
}

    let ok2 = is_null_ptr(1) == false
    let ok3 = is_null_ptr(0 - 1) == false

// Test 8: Pointer alignment
fn test_align_up() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Align to 4 bytes
    let ok1 = align_up(1, 4) == 4
    let ok2 = align_up(4, 4) == 4
    let ok3 = align_up(5, 4) == 8
    let ok4 = align_up(0, 4) == 0

    // Align to 16 bytes

    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5 && ok6 && ok7 && ok8

// Test 9: Simulated memset - fill buffer with a value
fn test_memset() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var buf = membuf_new()

    // First 10 bytes should be 42
    let ok1 = buf.data[0] == 42
    let ok2 = buf.data[9] == 42
    // Byte 10 should still be 0
    let ok3 = buf.data[10] == 0
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}

// Test 10: Simulated memcmp - compare equal buffers
fn test_memcmp_equal() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var a = membuf_new()
    var b = membuf_new()
    membuf_set(&! a, 7, 16)
    membuf_set(&! b, 7, 16)
    let result = membuf_cmp(a, b, 16)
    return result == 0
}

// Test 11: Simulated memcmp - compare different buffers
fn test_memcmp_diff() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var a = membuf_new()
    var b = membuf_new()
    membuf_set(&! a, 5, 16)
    membuf_set(&! b, 5, 16)
    // Make byte 8 different
    b.data[8] = 10
    let result = membuf_cmp(a, b, 16)
    // a[8]=5 < b[8]=10, so result should be negative
    let ok1 = result < 0
    // Reverse comparison
    let result2 = membuf_cmp(b, a, 16)
    let ok2 = result2 > 0
    return ok1 && ok2
}

// Test 12: Simulated memcpy
fn test_memcpy() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var src = membuf_new()
    var dst = membuf_new()
    // Fill source with pattern
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 {
        src.data[i] = i * 3
        i = i + 1
    }
    membuf_copy(&! dst, src, 20)
    // Verify copy
    let ok1 = dst.data[0] == 0
    let ok2 = dst.data[1] == 3
    let ok3 = dst.data[5] == 15
    let ok4 = dst.data[19] == 57
    // Byte 20 should be unchanged (0)
    let ok5 = dst.data[20] == 0
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5
}

// Test 13: Simulated memchr - find byte in buffer
fn test_memchr() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var buf = membuf_new()
    buf.data[0] = 1
    buf.data[1] = 2
    buf.data[2] = 3
    buf.data[3] = 4
    buf.data[4] = 5
    // Find value 3

    let ok1 = idx == 2
    // Find value not present

    let ok2 = idx2 == (0 - 1)
    // Find first occurrence

    let idx3 = membuf_chr(buf, 3, 10)

    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}

// Test 14: Memset then memcmp roundtrip
fn test_memset_cmp_roundtrip() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    var a = membuf_new()
    var b = membuf_new()

    membuf_set(&! a, 0xFF, 64)
    membuf_set(&! b, 0xFF, 64)
    let ok1 = membuf_cmp(a, b, 64) == 0
    // Change one byte in a
    a.data[32] = 0
    let ok2 = membuf_cmp(a, b, 64) != 0
    return ok1 && ok2
}

//@ run-pass
// FFI test: call libm functions via extern "C" bindings
// Validates: extern symbol PLT resolution, -lm linking, f64 calling convention

extern "C" {
    fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn tgamma(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64;
    fn floor(x: f64) -> f64;
    fn ceil(x: f64) -> f64;
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, eps: f64) -> bool {
    let diff = a - b
    if diff < 0.0 {
        return (0.0 - diff) < eps
    }
    diff < eps
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO {
    // Verify sqrt(25.0) = 5.0 via integer truncation
    // This exercises: PLT call, xmm0 arg passing, xmm0 return
    let s = sqrt(25.0)
    let s_int = s as i64
    // s_int should be 5 if FFI call worked, 0 or garbage otherwise
    if s_int == 5 { 0 } else { s_int }
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/fft_spectral.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 15 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// FFT and Spectral Analysis Test Suite
//
// Self-contained test suite validating a radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FFT
// implementation and core spectral properties for powers of 2 up to N=64.
//
// All functions are inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Cooley & Tukey, "An algorithm for the machine calculation of complex
//       Fourier series", Math. Comp. 19 (1965), 297-301
//   Oppenheim & Schafer, "Discrete-Time Signal Processing" (3rd ed.)

// ============================================================================
// PURE MATH HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var scaled = x
    var scale_back = 1.0
    while scaled < 1.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 4.0
        scale_back = scale_back * 2.0
    }
    while scaled > 4.0 {
        scaled = scaled * 0.25
        scale_back = scale_back * 0.5
    }
    var y = 1.5
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    y = 0.5 * (y + scaled / y)
    return y / scale_back
}

fn floor_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x >= 0.0 {
        let i = x as i32
        return i as f64
    }
    let i = x as i32
    let f = i as f64
    if f > x { return f - 1.0 }
    return f
}

fn sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 6.283185307179586
    var t = x - floor_f64(x / two_pi) * two_pi
    if t > pi { t = t - two_pi }
    if t < 0.0 - pi { t = t + two_pi }
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = 0.0 - term * t * t / (((2 * n) as f64) * ((2 * n + 1) as f64))
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return sin_f64(x + 1.5707963267948966)
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

fn magnitude(re: f64, im: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    sqrt_f64(re * re + im * im)
}

// ============================================================================
// FFT DATA STRUCTURE
// ============================================================================

struct FFTResult {
    re: [f64; 64],
    im: [f64; 64],
}

// ============================================================================
// BIT-REVERSAL
// ============================================================================

fn bit_reverse(val: i32, bits: i32) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result = 0
    var v = val
    var i = 0
    while i < bits {
        result = (result * 2) + (v - 2 * (v / 2))
        v = v / 2
        i = i + 1
    }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// FORWARD FFT  (radix-2 decimation-in-time Cooley-Tukey)
// ============================================================================

fn fft(input_re: [f64; 64], input_im: [f64; 64], n: i32) -> FFTResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var re = input_re
    var im = input_im

    // Count bits: n must be a power of 2
    var bits = 0
    var temp = n
    while temp > 1 {
        bits = bits + 1
        temp = temp / 2
    }

    // Bit-reversal permutation
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let j = bit_reverse(i, bits)
        if i < j {
            let tr = re[i]
            re[i] = re[j]
            re[j] = tr
            let ti = im[i]
            im[i] = im[j]
            im[j] = ti
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Cooley-Tukey butterfly stages
    var size = 2
    while size <= n {
        let half = size / 2
        let angle = 0.0 - 6.283185307179586 / (size as f64)

        var group = 0
        while group < n {
            var k = 0
            while k < half {
                let w_angle = angle * (k as f64)
                let wr = cos_f64(w_angle)
                let wi = sin_f64(w_angle)

                let idx1 = group + k
                let idx2 = group + k + half

                let tr = re[idx2] * wr - im[idx2] * wi
                let ti = re[idx2] * wi + im[idx2] * wr

                re[idx2] = re[idx1] - tr
                im[idx2] = im[idx1] - ti
                re[idx1] = re[idx1] + tr
                im[idx1] = im[idx1] + ti

                k = k + 1
            }
            group = group + size
        }
        size = size * 2
    }

    return FFTResult { re: re, im: im }
}

// ============================================================================
// INVERSE FFT
// ============================================================================

fn ifft(input_re: [f64; 64], input_im: [f64; 64], n: i32) -> FFTResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Conjugate input imaginary part
    var conj_im = input_im
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        conj_im[i] = 0.0 - conj_im[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Forward FFT on conjugated input
    let result = fft(input_re, conj_im, n)

    // Conjugate and scale output
    var re = result.re
    var im = result.im
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = re[i] / (n as f64)
        im[i] = 0.0 - im[i] / (n as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }

    return FFTResult { re: re, im: im }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

// Test 1: FFT of constant signal [1,1,...,1] of length N=8
//   DC bin (k=0) should equal N, all other bins should be 0.
fn test_dc_signal() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    // DC bin should be N
    if approx_eq(result.re[0], 8.0, tol) == false { return false }
    if approx_eq(result.im[0], 0.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // All other bins should be zero
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        if magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 2: FFT of single impulse [1,0,0,...,0]
//   All bins should have magnitude 1.
fn test_single_impulse() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    re[0] = 1.0

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        let mag = magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i])
        if approx_eq(mag, 1.0, tol) == false { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 3: Nyquist -- FFT of alternating [1,-1,1,-1,...] (N=8)
//   All energy should be at bin N/2 = 4.
fn test_nyquist() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        // Alternating: (-1)^i
        if (i - 2 * (i / 2)) == 0 {
            re[i] = 1.0
        } else {
            re[i] = 0.0 - 1.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    // Bin N/2 = 4 should have magnitude N = 8
    let mag4 = magnitude(result.re[4], result.im[4])
    if approx_eq(mag4, 8.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // All other bins should be ~0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i != 4 {
            if magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 4: FFT of pure cosine cos(2*pi*1/N * n) for N=8
//   Peaks at bins k=1 and k=N-1 with magnitude N/2, others ~0.
fn test_single_cosine() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = cos_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-6

    // Bin 0 should be ~0
    if magnitude(result.re[0], result.im[0]) > tol { return false }

    // Bin 1 should have magnitude N/2 = 4
    let mag1 = magnitude(result.re[1], result.im[1])
    if approx_eq(mag1, 4.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Bin N-1 = 7 should have magnitude N/2 = 4
    let mag7 = magnitude(result.re[7], result.im[7])
    if approx_eq(mag7, 4.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Bins 2..6 should be ~0
    i = 2
    while i < 7 {
        if magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 5: FFT of pure sine sin(2*pi*1/N * n) for N=8
//   Peaks at bins k=1 and k=N-1 with magnitude N/2.
fn test_single_sine() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = sin_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-6

    // Bin 1 magnitude should be N/2 = 4
    let mag1 = magnitude(result.re[1], result.im[1])
    if approx_eq(mag1, 4.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Bin N-1 = 7 magnitude should be N/2 = 4
    let mag7 = magnitude(result.re[7], result.im[7])
    if approx_eq(mag7, 4.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Middle bins 2..6 should be ~0
    i = 2
    while i < 7 {
        if magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 6: IFFT roundtrip -- ifft(fft(x)) ~ x
fn test_ifft_roundtrip() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Arbitrary signal
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = sin_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + 0.5 * cos_f64(2.0 * pi * 3.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        i = i + 1
    }

    let forward = fft(re, im, n)
    let back = ifft(forward.re, forward.im, n)

    let tol = 1.0e-8
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if approx_eq(back.re[i], re[i], tol) == false { return false }
        if approx_eq(back.im[i], 0.0, tol) == false { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 7: Linearity -- FFT(a*x + b*y) = a*FFT(x) + b*FFT(y)
fn test_linearity() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let a = 2.5
    let b = 1.3

    var x_re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var y_re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var z_re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var zero_im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        x_re[i] = cos_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        y_re[i] = sin_f64(2.0 * pi * 2.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        z_re[i] = a * x_re[i] + b * y_re[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let fx = fft(x_re, zero_im, n)
    // Need fresh zero arrays for each call
    var zero_im2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    let fy = fft(y_re, zero_im2, n)
    var zero_im3: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    let fz = fft(z_re, zero_im3, n)

    let tol = 1.0e-6
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let exp_re = a * fx.re[i] + b * fy.re[i]
        let exp_im = a * fx.im[i] + b * fy.im[i]
        if approx_eq(fz.re[i], exp_re, tol) == false { return false }
        if approx_eq(fz.im[i], exp_im, tol) == false { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 8: Parseval's theorem -- sum|x[n]|^2 = (1/N)*sum|X[k]|^2
fn test_parseval() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = cos_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + 0.3 * sin_f64(2.0 * pi * 2.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Time-domain energy
    var time_energy = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        time_energy = time_energy + re[i] * re[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)

    // Frequency-domain energy
    var freq_energy = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        freq_energy = freq_energy + result.re[i] * result.re[i] + result.im[i] * result.im[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    freq_energy = freq_energy / (n as f64)

    let tol = 1.0e-6
    return approx_eq(time_energy, freq_energy, tol)
}

// Test 9: Conjugate symmetry -- for real input, X[k] = conj(X[N-k])
//   i.e. Re[k] = Re[N-k] and Im[k] = -Im[N-k]
fn test_conjugate_symmetry() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Arbitrary real signal
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = sin_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + 0.7 * cos_f64(2.0 * pi * 3.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + 1.2
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-8

    // Check X[k] = conj(X[N-k]) for k = 1..N/2-1
    i = 1
    while i < 4 {
        let mirror = n - i
        // Re[k] should equal Re[N-k]
        if approx_eq(result.re[i], result.re[mirror], tol) == false { return false }
        // Im[k] should equal -Im[N-k]
        if approx_eq(result.im[i], 0.0 - result.im[mirror], tol) == false { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 10: FFT of all zeros gives all zeros
fn test_zero_signal() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-12

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 11: Two-frequency signal -- sum of two cosines at bins 1 and 3
fn test_two_cosines() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 16
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        // cos at bin 1 + cos at bin 3
        re[i] = cos_f64(2.0 * pi * 1.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + cos_f64(2.0 * pi * 3.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = fft(re, im, n)
    let tol = 1.0e-5

    // Bins 1, N-1=15 should have magnitude N/2 = 8
    let mag1 = magnitude(result.re[1], result.im[1])
    let mag15 = magnitude(result.re[15], result.im[15])
    if approx_eq(mag1, 8.0, tol) == false { return false }
    if approx_eq(mag15, 8.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Bins 3, N-3=13 should have magnitude N/2 = 8
    let mag3 = magnitude(result.re[3], result.im[3])
    let mag13 = magnitude(result.re[13], result.im[13])
    if approx_eq(mag3, 8.0, tol) == false { return false }
    if approx_eq(mag13, 8.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Remaining bins should be ~0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if i != 1 && i != 3 && i != 13 && i != 15 {
            if magnitude(result.re[i], result.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 12: Magnitude spectrum verification
fn test_magnitude_spectrum() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    re[0] = 3.0
    im[0] = 4.0

    // |3 + 4i| = 5
    let mag = magnitude(re[0], im[0])
    let tol = 1.0e-8
    if approx_eq(mag, 5.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Test magnitude of FFT output at DC for signal [8,0,0,...]
    var re2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    re2[0] = 8.0
    let result = fft(re2, im2, n)
    let dc_mag = magnitude(result.re[0], result.im[0])
    if approx_eq(dc_mag, 8.0, tol) == false { return false }

    return true
}

// Test 13: Time-shift theorem -- a circular shift by m samples in time
//   corresponds to multiplying X[k] by exp(-j*2*pi*k*m/N).
//   We check: |FFT(shifted)[k]| = |FFT(original)[k]| for all k
//   (magnitude is invariant under phase rotation).
fn test_phase_shift() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 8
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re_orig: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im_orig: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var re_shift: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im_shift: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Original signal
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re_orig[i] = cos_f64(2.0 * pi * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + 0.5
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Circular shift by 1 sample
    let shift = 1
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        // Shifted index: (i - shift + n) mod n
        var src = i - shift + n
        // Manual mod: src - n * (src / n)
        src = src - n * (src / n)
        re_shift[i] = re_orig[src]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let f_orig = fft(re_orig, im_orig, n)
    let f_shift = fft(re_shift, im_shift, n)

    let tol = 1.0e-6
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let mag_orig = magnitude(f_orig.re[i], f_orig.im[i])
        let mag_shift = magnitude(f_shift.re[i], f_shift.im[i])
        if approx_eq(mag_orig, mag_shift, tol) == false { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return true
}

// Test 14: FFT works for both N=8 and N=16 (power-of-two sizes)
fn test_power_of_two_sizes() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test N=8: DC signal
    let n8 = 8
    var re8: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im8: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i < n8 {
        re8[i] = 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    let result8 = fft(re8, im8, n8)
    let tol = 1.0e-8
    if approx_eq(result8.re[0], 8.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // Test N=16: DC signal
    let n16 = 16
    var re16: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im16: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    i = 0
    while i < n16 {
        re16[i] = 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    let result16 = fft(re16, im16, n16)
    if approx_eq(result16.re[0], 16.0, tol) == false { return false }

    // All other bins should be zero for both sizes
    i = 1
    while i < n8 {
        if magnitude(result8.re[i], result8.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    i = 1
    while i < n16 {
        if magnitude(result16.re[i], result16.im[i]) > tol { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return true
}

// Test 15: Energy conservation -- time domain energy = frequency domain energy
//   This is essentially Parseval again but with a different signal and
//   verifies energy in both domains via IFFT as well.
fn test_energy_conservation() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n = 16
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    var re: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var im: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Complex input signal
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        re[i] = cos_f64(2.0 * pi * 2.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64)) + 0.5 * sin_f64(2.0 * pi * 5.0 * (i as f64) / (n as f64))
        im[i] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Time-domain energy
    var time_energy = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        time_energy = time_energy + re[i] * re[i] + im[i] * im[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    let forward = fft(re, im, n)

    // Frequency-domain energy (divide by N for Parseval)
    var freq_energy = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        freq_energy = freq_energy + forward.re[i] * forward.re[i] + forward.im[i] * forward.im[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    freq_energy = freq_energy / (n as f64)

    let tol = 1.0e-6
    if approx_eq(time_energy, freq_energy, tol) == false { return false }

    // Also verify IFFT roundtrip preserves energy
    let back = ifft(forward.re, forward.im, n)
    var back_energy = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        back_energy = back_energy + back.re[i] * back.re[i] + back.im[i] * back.im[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    if approx_eq(time_energy, back_energy, tol) == false { return false }

    return true
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/for_in_loops.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Test for-in loop syntax variations
// Issue #6: Document for-in loop support

fn main() with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // 1. Range iteration (exclusive): for i in start..end
    var sum = 0
    for i in 0..5 {
        sum = sum + i
    }
    // sum = 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10

    // 2. Range iteration (inclusive): for i in start..=end
    var sum_inclusive = 0
    for i in 0..=5 {
        sum_inclusive = sum_inclusive + i
    }
    // sum_inclusive = 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15

    // 3. Array iteration: for item in array
    let arr = [10, 20, 30]
    var arr_sum = 0
    for x in arr {
        arr_sum = arr_sum + x
    }
    // arr_sum = 60

    // 4. Vec iteration: for item in vec
    let vec: Vec<i32> = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    var vec_sum = 0
    for x in vec {
        vec_sum = vec_sum + x
    }
    // vec_sum = 10

    // 5. Nested for loops
    var matrix_sum = 0
    for i in 0..3 {
        for j in 0..3 {
            matrix_sum = matrix_sum + i * 3 + j
        }
    }
    // matrix_sum = sum of 0..9 = 36

    // 6. Range with variables
    let n = 5
    var var_range_sum = 0
    for i in 0..n {
        var_range_sum = var_range_sum + i
    }
    // var_range_sum = 10

    // 7. For loop with break
    var break_count = 0
    for i in 0..100 {
        if i >= 5 {
            break
        }
        break_count = break_count + 1
    }
    // break_count = 5

    // 8. For loop with continue
    var skip_sum = 0
    for i in 0..10 {
        if i % 2 == 0 {
            continue
        }
        skip_sum = skip_sum + i
    }
    // skip_sum = 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25

    println("All for-in loop tests passed!")
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/gpu_kernel_basic.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// gpu_kernel_basic.sio - GPU kernel logic test with CPU fallback
//
// This test exercises the gpu_parallel pattern and verifies results
// match expected values. It runs through the CPU fallback path when
// no GPU hardware is available, ensuring correctness of the dispatch
// logic regardless of runtime environment.

// ============================================================================
// Math helpers
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn abs_i64(x: i64) -> i64 {
    if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
}

// ============================================================================
// GPU availability check (CPU fallback path)
// ============================================================================

// Simulates the runtime check: in test harness, GPU is not available
fn gpu_available() -> bool {
    // In test environment without GPU hardware, always false
    // This exercises the CPU fallback path
    false
}

// ============================================================================
// Element-wise operations with GPU dispatch pattern
// ============================================================================

// Element-wise addition: result[i] = a[i] + b[i]
fn parallel_add(a: [i64; 64], b: [i64; 64], n: i64) -> [i64; 64] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    if gpu_available() {
        // GPU path: would launch kernel with block_size=256
        // gpu_parallel for i in 0..n { result[i] = a[i] + b[i] }
        // gpu.sync()
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = a[i as usize] + b[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        // CPU fallback: serial execution of same logic
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = a[i as usize] + b[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    result
}

// Element-wise multiply: result[i] = a[i] * b[i]
fn parallel_mul(a: [i64; 64], b: [i64; 64], n: i64) -> [i64; 64] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    if gpu_available() {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = a[i as usize] * b[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        // CPU fallback
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = a[i as usize] * b[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    result
}

// Element-wise scale: result[i] = a[i] * scalar
fn parallel_scale(a: [f64; 64], scalar: f64, n: i64) -> [f64; 64] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    if gpu_available() {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = a[i as usize] * scalar
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        // CPU fallback
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            result[i as usize] = a[i as usize] * scalar
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    result
}

// Parallel reduction: sum all elements
fn parallel_reduce_sum(a: [i64; 64], n: i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // In GPU mode, this would use a tree-based parallel reduction:
    //   1. Each thread block sums a partition into shared memory
    //   2. Warp-level primitives (shuffle) reduce within warps
    //   3. Block results are combined with a final reduction kernel

    if gpu_available() {
        // GPU tree reduction would go here
        var sum: i64 = 0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            sum = sum + a[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        sum
    } else {
        // CPU fallback: serial sum
        var sum: i64 = 0
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            sum = sum + a[i as usize]
            i = i + 1
        }
        sum
    }
}

// Parallel map with predicate: result[i] = 1 if a[i] > threshold, else 0
fn parallel_threshold(a: [f64; 64], threshold: f64, n: i64) -> [i64; 64] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var result: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    if gpu_available() {
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            if a[i as usize] > threshold {
                result[i as usize] = 1
            } else {
                result[i as usize] = 0
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
    } else {
        // CPU fallback
        var i: i64 = 0
        while i < n {
            if a[i as usize] > threshold {
                result[i as usize] = 1
            } else {
                result[i as usize] = 0
            }
            i = i + 1
        }
    }

    result
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: element-wise addition
// ============================================================================

fn test_parallel_add() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n: i64 = 16
    var a: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]
    var b: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i as usize] = i + 1
        b[i as usize] = (i + 1) * 10
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = parallel_add(a, b, n)

    // Verify: result[i] = (i+1) + (i+1)*10 = (i+1)*11
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let expected = (i + 1) * 11
        if result[i as usize] != expected {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: element-wise multiplication
// ============================================================================

fn test_parallel_mul() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n: i64 = 8
    var a: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]
    var b: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i as usize] = i + 1
        b[i as usize] = i + 2
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = parallel_mul(a, b, n)

    // Verify: result[0] = 1*2 = 2, result[1] = 2*3 = 6, ...
    if result[0] != 2 { return false }
    if result[1] != 6 { return false }
    if result[2] != 12 { return false }
    if result[3] != 20 { return false }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: floating-point scale
// ============================================================================

fn test_parallel_scale() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n: i64 = 10
    var a: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i as usize] = (i as f64) + 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = parallel_scale(a, 2.5, n)

    // Verify: result[i] = (i+1) * 2.5
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let expected = ((i as f64) + 1.0) * 2.5
        if abs_f64(result[i as usize] - expected) > 0.001 {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: parallel reduction
// ============================================================================

fn test_parallel_reduce() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n: i64 = 20
    var a: [i64; 64] = [0; 64]

    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i as usize] = i + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    let sum = parallel_reduce_sum(a, n)

    // Sum of 1..20 = 20*21/2 = 210
    sum == 210
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: threshold operation
// ============================================================================

fn test_parallel_threshold() -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n: i64 = 10
    var a: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]

    // Values: 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, ... 9.5
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        a[i as usize] = (i as f64) + 0.5
        i = i + 1
    }

    let result = parallel_threshold(a, 5.0, n)

    // Values > 5.0 are at indices 5,6,7,8,9 (values 5.5, 6.5, ...)
    if result[0] != 0 { return false }  // 0.5 <= 5.0
    if result[4] != 0 { return false }  // 4.5 <= 5.0
    if result[5] != 1 { return false }  // 5.5 > 5.0
    if result[9] != 1 { return false }  // 9.5 > 5.0

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: GPU fallback verification
// ============================================================================

fn test_gpu_fallback() -> bool {
    // Verify that gpu_available() returns false in test environment
    if gpu_available() {
        // If GPU is available, all tests still work through GPU path
        return true
    }

    // CPU fallback path is being used -- verify operations still produce
    // correct results (which we have already verified above)
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// Entry point
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    if !test_parallel_add() {
        print_int(1)
        return 1
    }

    if !test_parallel_mul() {
        print_int(2)
        return 2
    }

    if !test_parallel_scale() {
        print_int(3)
        return 3
    }

    if !test_parallel_reduce() {
        print_int(4)
        return 4
    }

    if !test_parallel_threshold() {
        print_int(5)
        return 5
    }

    if !test_gpu_fallback() {
        print_int(6)
        return 6
    }

    // All tests passed
    print_int(0)
    0
}

//
// It intentionally avoids `gpu.thread_id` and `gpu.alloc`, which are still

kernel fn vec_add(n: i64) with GPU {
}

}
