        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 2: Euler decay coarse |y(1) - exp(-1)| < 0.1 . ")
    if test_euler_decay_coarse() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 3: RK4 growth |y(0.5) - exp(0.5)| < 0.001 ... ")
    if test_rk4_growth_at_half() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 4: RK4 decay y0=2 non-unit initial value ...... ")
    if test_rk4_decay_nonunit_y0() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 5: Midpoint more accurate than Euler n=50 ..... ")
    if test_midpoint_beats_euler() {
        println("PASS")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        failed = failed + 1
    }

    print("Test 6: RK4 convergence ratio ~16 (4th order) ...... ")
    if test_rk4_order4_convergence_ratio() {
        println("PASS")

//@ run-pass
// Basic ONN (Octonion Neural Network) functionality test

// Test octonion creation and basic operations
fn main() {
    // Create test octonions
    let o1 = Octonion { w: 1.0, x: 2.0, y: 3.0, z: 4.0, t: 5.0, u: 6.0, v: 7.0, s: 8.0 }
    let o2 = Octonion { w: 0.5, x: 0.5, y: 0.5, z: 0.5, t: 0.5, u: 0.5, v: 0.5, s: 0.5 }

    // Test norm computation
    // |o1|^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36 + 49 + 64 = 204
    let norm_sq = o1.w * o1.w + o1.x * o1.x + o1.y * o1.y + o1.z * o1.z
                + o1.t * o1.t + o1.u * o1.u + o1.v * o1.v + o1.s * o1.s
    assert(abs(norm_sq - 204.0) < 0.001)

    // Test unit octonion
    let unit = Octonion { w: 1.0, x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0, t: 0.0, u: 0.0, v: 0.0, s: 0.0 }
    let unit_norm = sqrt(unit.w * unit.w + unit.x * unit.x + unit.y * unit.y + unit.z * unit.z
                       + unit.t * unit.t + unit.u * unit.u + unit.v * unit.v + unit.s * unit.s)
    assert(abs(unit_norm - 1.0) < 0.001)

    print("ONN basic test passed!")
}

// Octonion struct (should match stdlib/onn/mod.sio)
struct Octonion {
    w: f32,
    x: f32,
    y: f32,
    z: f32,
    t: f32,
    u: f32,
    v: f32,
    s: f32,
}

fn abs(x: f32) -> f32 {
    if x < 0.0 { -x } else { x }
}

fn sqrt(x: f32) -> f32 {
    // Newton-Raphson approximation
    var guess = x / 2.0
    for i in 0..10 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
    }
    guess
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/optimization_nelder_mead.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 15 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// optimization_nelder_mead.sio - Integration tests for Nelder-Mead simplex optimization
//
// Self-contained test suite validating a 2D-specialized Nelder-Mead optimizer
// on four classical test functions: Sphere, Rosenbrock, Beale, and Booth.
// All structs and algorithms are inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Nelder & Mead, "A Simplex Method for Function Minimization" (1965)
//   Lagarias et al., "Convergence Properties of the Nelder-Mead Simplex Method" (1998)

// ============================================================================
// PURE MATH HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x
    if g < 1.0 { g = 1.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 50 {
        g = (g + x / g) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return g
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct Point2D {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

struct Vertex {
    p: Point2D,
    value: f64,
}

struct NMResult {
    best: Point2D,
    value: f64,
    iterations: i32,
    converged: bool,
}

// ============================================================================
// OBJECTIVE FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Sphere: f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2, minimum at (0,0) = 0
fn obj_sphere(p: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    p.x * p.x + p.y * p.y
}

// Rosenbrock: f(x,y) = (1-x)^2 + 100*(y - x^2)^2, minimum at (1,1) = 0
fn obj_rosenbrock(p: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let a = 1.0 - p.x
    let b = p.y - p.x * p.x
    a * a + 100.0 * b * b
}

// Beale: f(x,y) = (1.5-x+xy)^2 + (2.25-x+xy^2)^2 + (2.625-x+xy^3)^2
// minimum at (3, 0.5) = 0
fn obj_beale(p: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let t1 = 1.5 - p.x + p.x * p.y
    let t2 = 2.25 - p.x + p.x * p.y * p.y
    let t3 = 2.625 - p.x + p.x * p.y * p.y * p.y
    t1 * t1 + t2 * t2 + t3 * t3
}

// Booth: f(x,y) = (x + 2y - 7)^2 + (2x + y - 5)^2, minimum at (1,3) = 0
fn obj_booth(p: Point2D) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let t1 = p.x + 2.0 * p.y - 7.0
    let t2 = 2.0 * p.x + p.y - 5.0
    t1 * t1 + t2 * t2
}

// Dispatch: evaluate the chosen objective by integer selector
fn eval_obj(p: Point2D, func_id: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if func_id == 1 { return obj_sphere(p) }
    if func_id == 2 { return obj_rosenbrock(p) }
    if func_id == 3 { return obj_beale(p) }
    return obj_booth(p)
}

// ============================================================================
// NELDER-MEAD OPTIMIZER (2D specialized, 3 vertices)
// ============================================================================

fn nm_minimize(x0: f64, y0: f64, step: f64, tol: f64, max_iter: i32, func_id: i32) -> NMResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Standard Nelder-Mead coefficients
    let alpha = 1.0   // reflection
    let gamma = 2.0   // expansion
    let rho = 0.5     // contraction
    let sigma = 0.5   // shrink

    // Initialize simplex: 3 vertices for 2D
    let p0 = Point2D { x: x0, y: y0 }
    let p1 = Point2D { x: x0 + step, y: y0 }
    let p2 = Point2D { x: x0, y: y0 + step }

    var v0 = Vertex { p: p0, value: eval_obj(p0, func_id) }
    var v1 = Vertex { p: p1, value: eval_obj(p1, func_id) }
    var v2 = Vertex { p: p2, value: eval_obj(p2, func_id) }

    var iter = 0
    while iter < max_iter {
        // Sort: v0 = best (lowest), v1 = second worst, v2 = worst (highest)
        if v0.value > v1.value {
            let tmp = v0
            v0 = v1
            v1 = tmp
        }
        if v1.value > v2.value {
            let tmp = v1
            v1 = v2
            v2 = tmp
        }
        if v0.value > v1.value {
            let tmp = v0
            v0 = v1
            v1 = tmp
        }

        // Check convergence: value spread
        let val_spread = abs_f64(v2.value - v0.value)
        if val_spread < tol {
            return NMResult { best: v0.p, value: v0.value, iterations: iter, converged: true }
        }

        // Check convergence: simplex diameter
        let d01 = sqrt_f64((v0.p.x - v1.p.x) * (v0.p.x - v1.p.x) + (v0.p.y - v1.p.y) * (v0.p.y - v1.p.y))
        let d02 = sqrt_f64((v0.p.x - v2.p.x) * (v0.p.x - v2.p.x) + (v0.p.y - v2.p.y) * (v0.p.y - v2.p.y))
        let d12 = sqrt_f64((v1.p.x - v2.p.x) * (v1.p.x - v2.p.x) + (v1.p.y - v2.p.y) * (v1.p.y - v2.p.y))
        let diam = max_f64(d01, max_f64(d02, d12))
        if diam < tol {
            return NMResult { best: v0.p, value: v0.value, iterations: iter, converged: true }
        }

        // Centroid of the two best vertices (excluding worst v2)
        let cx = (v0.p.x + v1.p.x) / 2.0
        let cy = (v0.p.y + v1.p.y) / 2.0

        // Reflection: r = centroid + alpha * (centroid - worst)
        let rx = cx + alpha * (cx - v2.p.x)
        let ry = cy + alpha * (cy - v2.p.y)
        let pr = Point2D { x: rx, y: ry }
        let fr = eval_obj(pr, func_id)

        if fr < v1.value && fr >= v0.value {
            // Reflected point is better than second-worst but not best: accept reflection
            v2 = Vertex { p: pr, value: fr }
        } else if fr < v0.value {
            // Reflected point is new best: try expansion
            let ex = cx + gamma * (rx - cx)
            let ey = cy + gamma * (ry - cy)
            let pe = Point2D { x: ex, y: ey }
            let fe = eval_obj(pe, func_id)

            if fe < fr {
                v2 = Vertex { p: pe, value: fe }
            } else {
                v2 = Vertex { p: pr, value: fr }
            }
        } else {
            // Reflected point is worse than second-worst: contract
            if fr < v2.value {
                // Outside contraction
                let ocx = cx + rho * (rx - cx)
                let ocy = cy + rho * (ry - cy)
                let poc = Point2D { x: ocx, y: ocy }
                let foc = eval_obj(poc, func_id)

                if foc <= fr {
                    v2 = Vertex { p: poc, value: foc }
                } else {
                    // Shrink
                    let s1 = Point2D { x: v0.p.x + sigma * (v1.p.x - v0.p.x), y: v0.p.y + sigma * (v1.p.y - v0.p.y) }
                    let s2 = Point2D { x: v0.p.x + sigma * (v2.p.x - v0.p.x), y: v0.p.y + sigma * (v2.p.y - v0.p.y) }
                    v1 = Vertex { p: s1, value: eval_obj(s1, func_id) }
                    v2 = Vertex { p: s2, value: eval_obj(s2, func_id) }
                }
            } else {
                // Inside contraction
                let icx = cx + rho * (v2.p.x - cx)
                let icy = cy + rho * (v2.p.y - cy)
                let pic = Point2D { x: icx, y: icy }
                let fic = eval_obj(pic, func_id)

                if fic < v2.value {
                    v2 = Vertex { p: pic, value: fic }
                } else {
                    // Shrink
                    let s1 = Point2D { x: v0.p.x + sigma * (v1.p.x - v0.p.x), y: v0.p.y + sigma * (v1.p.y - v0.p.y) }
                    let s2 = Point2D { x: v0.p.x + sigma * (v2.p.x - v0.p.x), y: v0.p.y + sigma * (v2.p.y - v0.p.y) }
                    v1 = Vertex { p: s1, value: eval_obj(s1, func_id) }
                    v2 = Vertex { p: s2, value: eval_obj(s2, func_id) }
                }
            }
        }

        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Did not converge within max_iter
    // Final sort to return the best
    if v0.value > v1.value {
        let tmp = v0
        v0 = v1
        v1 = tmp
    }
    if v0.value > v2.value {
        let tmp = v0
        v0 = v2
        v2 = tmp
    }

    return NMResult { best: v0.p, value: v0.value, iterations: max_iter, converged: false }
}

// Test 1: sphere_origin - starting at (5,5), finds (0,0)
fn test_sphere_origin() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let r = nm_minimize(5.0, 5.0, 1.0, 1.0e-10, 1000, 1)
    let ok = approx_eq(r.best.x, 0.0, 1.0e-4) && approx_eq(r.best.y, 0.0, 1.0e-4)
    print("  best=(")
    print(r.best.x)
    print(", ")
    print(r.best.y)
    println(")")
    return ok
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/pbpk_analytical_crossvalidation.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Cross-validation: Sounio Euler vs analytical Bateman equation
//
// Validates numerical accuracy of the 2-compartment PBPK solver against
// the closed-form Bateman solution at multiple time points.
//
// Analytical solution (Bateman equation):
//   Gut(t)     = Dose * exp(-ka * t)
//   Central(t) = Dose * ka / (ka - ke) * (exp(-ke * t) - exp(-ka * t))
//
// Reference: Gibaldi & Perrier, "Pharmacokinetics", 2nd Ed., Ch. 2

// Approximate exp(x) using Taylor series with range reduction
// For negative x, compute exp(|x|) and invert to avoid catastrophic cancellation
fn exp_pos(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Taylor series for positive x converges well
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 40 {
        let nf = n as f64
        term = term * x / nf
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn exp_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < -30.0 {
        return 0.0
    }
    if x < 0.0 {
        // exp(-a) = 1/exp(a) — avoids alternating-sign cancellation
        return 1.0 / exp_pos(-x)
    }
    exp_pos(x)
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return -x }
    x
}

struct PBPKState {
    t: f64,
    gut: f64,
    central: f64
}

fn euler_step(s: PBPKState, dt: f64) -> PBPKState {
    let ka = 1.0
    let ke = 0.1
    PBPKState {
        t: s.t + dt,
        gut: s.gut + (-ka * s.gut) * dt,
        central: s.central + (ka * s.gut - ke * s.central) * dt
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Div, Mut, Panic {
    let dose = 500.0
    let ka = 1.0
    let ke = 0.1
    let dt = 0.01   // Small dt for accuracy
    let total_steps = 2400   // 24 hours

    // Run simulation
    var s = PBPKState { t: 0.0, gut: dose, central: 0.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < total_steps {
        s = euler_step(s, dt)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Analytical solution at t=24h
    let t = 24.0
    let gut_analytical = dose * exp_approx(-ka * t)
    let coeff = dose * ka / (ka - ke)
    let central_analytical = coeff * (exp_approx(-ke * t) - exp_approx(-ka * t))

    // Print comparison
    println(s.gut)
    println(gut_analytical)
    println(s.central)
    println(central_analytical)

    // Validate relative errors
    // Euler is O(dt) global error; with dt=0.01 expect ~1-5% error
    let gut_error = abs_f64(s.gut - gut_analytical)
    let central_error = abs_f64(s.central - central_analytical)

    // Gut: both should be ~0, absolute check
    if gut_error > 0.01 { return 1 }

    // Central: relative error < 5% (Euler first-order accumulation)
    if central_analytical > 1.0 {
        let rel_error = central_error / central_analytical
        if rel_error > 0.05 { return 2 }
    }

    // Check at intermediate time points via checkpoints
    // Re-run and verify at t=2h (near Tmax), t=6h, t=12h
    var s2 = PBPKState { t: 0.0, gut: dose, central: 0.0 }
    var j = 0
    while j < 200 {
        s2 = euler_step(s2, dt)
        j = j + 1
    }
    // t=2h: near Cmax, analytical Central ≈ 379.7
    let c2_analytical = coeff * (exp_approx(-ke * 2.0) - exp_approx(-ka * 2.0))
    if c2_analytical > 1.0 {
        let c2_rel = abs_f64(s2.central - c2_analytical) / c2_analytical
        if c2_rel > 0.05 { return 3 }
    }

    // Continue to t=6h
    while j < 600 {
        s2 = euler_step(s2, dt)
        j = j + 1
    }
    let c6_analytical = coeff * (exp_approx(-ke * 6.0) - exp_approx(-ka * 6.0))
    if c6_analytical > 1.0 {
        let c6_rel = abs_f64(s2.central - c6_analytical) / c6_analytical
        if c6_rel > 0.05 { return 4 }
    }

    // Continue to t=12h
    while j < 1200 {
        s2 = euler_step(s2, dt)
        j = j + 1
    }
    let c12_analytical = coeff * (exp_approx(-ke * 12.0) - exp_approx(-ka * 12.0))
    if c12_analytical > 1.0 {
        let c12_rel = abs_f64(s2.central - c12_analytical) / c12_analytical
        if c12_rel > 0.05 { return 5 }
    }

    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/pbpk_caffeine.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// One-compartment oral caffeine pharmacokinetic model
// Validates ODE bridge with user-defined RHS and physiological parameters
//
// Model: dA_gut/dt = -ka * A_gut, dA_central/dt = ka * A_gut - ke * A_central
// Parameters: 200 mg oral dose, healthy adult (70 kg)
//   ka = 4.4 /h, CL = 5.46 L/h, V = 42.0 L, ke = CL/V = 0.13 /h, F = 0.99

fn pk_rhs(t: f64, y: [f64]) -> [f64] {
    let ka = 4.4
    let ke = 0.13
    let dA_gut = 0.0 - ka * y[0]
    let dA_central = ka * y[0] - ke * y[1]
    return [dA_gut, dA_central]
}

fn main() {
    let dose = 200.0
    let F = 0.99
    let V = 42.0
    let y0 = [F * dose, 0.0]

    let sol = solve_ode(pk_rhs, y0, 0.0, 24.0, 0.01)

    // Validate against analytical Bateman function
    let idx_1h = 100
    let y_1h = sol.y[idx_1h]
    let Cp_1h = y_1h[1] / V

    let idx_6h = 600
    let y_6h = sol.y[idx_6h]
    let Cp_6h = y_6h[1] / V

    let idx_12h = 1200
    let y_12h = sol.y[idx_12h]
    let Cp_12h = y_12h[1] / V

    let err_1h = Cp_1h - 4.206
    if err_1h < 0.0 { err_1h = 0.0 - err_1h }
    assert(err_1h < 0.1)

    let err_6h = Cp_6h - 2.227
    if err_6h < 0.0 { err_6h = 0.0 - err_6h }
    assert(err_6h < 0.1)

    let err_12h = Cp_12h - 1.021
    if err_12h < 0.0 { err_12h = 0.0 - err_12h }
    assert(err_12h < 0.1)

    let y_final = sol.y[sol.y.len() - 1]
    let total_final = y_final[0] + y_final[1]
    assert(total_final < F * dose)

    println("PBPK caffeine test passed")
    println("  Cp(1h)  = ", Cp_1h, " mg/L (expected ~4.2)")
    println("  Cp(6h)  = ", Cp_6h, " mg/L (expected ~2.2)")
    println("  Cp(12h) = ", Cp_12h, " mg/L (expected ~1.0)")
    println("  Total remaining at 24h: ", total_final, " mg")
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/pbpk_reproduction.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Reproduction of PBPK while-loop bug from PBPK_STABILITY_REPORT.md
// Pattern: struct mutation in while loop via intermediate Result struct

struct State {
    x: f64
}

struct StepResult {
    state_new: State
}

fn step(s: State) -> StepResult {
    return StepResult {
        state_new: State { x: s.x + 1.0 }
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Div, Mut {
    var st = State { x: 0.0 }
    var i = 0

    while i < 20 {
        let result = step(st)
        st = result.state_new  // BUG: Should update but report says freezes after ~2 iterations
        i = i + 1
    }

    // If bug exists: st.x will be ~2.0 instead of 20.0
    // If fixed: st.x will be 20.0
    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/pbpk_validation_euler.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// PBPK Validation: 2-compartment Euler model vs analytical Bateman equation
//
// Model: Dose → Gut (absorption) → Central (elimination)
//   dGut/dt     = -ka * Gut
//   dCentral/dt = ka * Gut - ke * Central
//
// Analytical (Bateman equation):
//   Gut(t)     = Dose * exp(-ka * t)
//   Central(t) = Dose * ka / (ka - ke) * (exp(-ke * t) - exp(-ka * t))
//   AUC(0→∞)   = Dose / ke  (for complete absorption)
//
// Parameters: Dose=500mg, ka=1.0/h, ke=0.1/h, dt=0.1h, 240 steps (24h)

struct PBPKState {
    t: f64,
    gut: f64,
    central: f64,
    auc: f64,
    cmax: f64,
    tmax: f64
}

fn euler_step(s: PBPKState, dt: f64) -> PBPKState {
    let ka = 1.0
    let ke = 0.1
    let d_gut = -ka * s.gut
    let d_central = ka * s.gut - ke * s.central
    let new_central = s.central + d_central * dt

    // Track Cmax/Tmax
    let new_t = s.t + dt
    var cmax = s.cmax
    var tmax = s.tmax
    if new_central > s.cmax {
        cmax = new_central
        tmax = new_t
    }

    PBPKState {
        t: new_t,
        gut: s.gut + d_gut * dt,
        central: new_central,
        auc: s.auc + s.central * dt,
        cmax: cmax,
        tmax: tmax
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Div, Mut {
    var s = PBPKState {
        t: 0.0, gut: 500.0, central: 0.0,
        auc: 0.0, cmax: 0.0, tmax: 0.0
    }
    let dt = 0.1
    var i = 0

    while i < 240 {
        s = euler_step(s, dt)
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print results for validation
    println(s.t)
    println(s.gut)
    println(s.central)
    println(s.auc)
    println(s.cmax)
    println(s.tmax)

    // Validate against analytical expectations:
    //
    // 1. Time should be 24.0h
    if s.t < 23.9 { return 1 }
    if s.t > 24.1 { return 2 }

    // 2. Gut should be ~0 (exp(-24) ≈ 1.9e-11)
    if s.gut > 0.01 { return 3 }

    // 3. Central: Bateman at t=24h
    //    C(24) = 500 * 1.0/(1.0-0.1) * (exp(-0.1*24) - exp(-1.0*24))
    //          = 555.56 * (exp(-2.4) - exp(-24))
    //          = 555.56 * (0.0907 - ~0)
    //          = ~50.4 mg
    //    Euler with dt=0.1 will be close but not exact
    if s.central < 30.0 { return 4 }
    if s.central > 70.0 { return 5 }

    // 4. AUC should be substantial (analytical AUC_0-inf = Dose/ke = 5000)
    //    But we only integrate to 24h, so expect ~4000-5000
    if s.auc < 3000.0 { return 6 }
    if s.auc > 6000.0 { return 7 }

    // 5. Cmax should be ~200-300 mg (depends on ka/ke ratio)
    //    Analytical Cmax at tmax = ln(ka/ke)/(ka-ke) = ln(10)/0.9 ≈ 2.56h
    //    Cmax = 500*(1.0/0.9)*(0.1^(0.1/0.9) - 0.1^(1.0/0.9))
    //    Euler approximation: should be in ballpark
    if s.cmax < 100.0 { return 8 }
    if s.cmax > 400.0 { return 9 }

    // 6. Tmax should be near 2.56h (analytical)
    if s.tmax < 1.5 { return 10 }
    if s.tmax > 4.0 { return 11 }

    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/pbpk_validation_rk4.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// PBPK Validation: 3-compartment RK2 model with higher-order accuracy
//
// Model: Gut → Liver (first-pass) → Central (elimination)
//   dGut/dt     = -ka * Gut
//   dLiver/dt   = ka * Gut * fa - (Q_h/V_h) * Liver - CL_h * Liver
//   dCentral/dt = (Q_h/V_h) * Liver - ke * Central
//
// Uses RK2 (midpoint method) for 2nd-order accuracy
// Parameters: Dose=500mg, ka=1.0/h, ke=0.1/h, dt=0.05h, 480 steps (24h)

struct Conc {
    gut: f64,
    liver: f64,
    central: f64
}

struct SimState {
    state: Conc,
    t: f64,
    auc: f64,
    cmax: f64,
    tmax: f64
}

fn derivatives(s: Conc) -> Conc {
    let ka = 1.0
    let fa = 0.8
    let q_h = 0.5
    let cl_h = 0.3
    let ke = 0.1
    Conc {
        gut: -ka * s.gut,
        liver: ka * s.gut * fa - q_h * s.liver - cl_h * s.liver,
        central: q_h * s.liver - ke * s.central
    }
}

fn rk2_step(s: Conc, dt: f64) -> Conc {
    // k1 = f(y_n)
    let k1 = derivatives(s)

    // midpoint: y_mid = y_n + 0.5*dt*k1
    let mid = Conc {
        gut: s.gut + 0.5 * dt * k1.gut,
        liver: s.liver + 0.5 * dt * k1.liver,
        central: s.central + 0.5 * dt * k1.central
    }

    // k2 = f(y_mid)
    let k2 = derivatives(mid)

    // y_{n+1} = y_n + dt * k2
    Conc {
        gut: s.gut + dt * k2.gut,
        liver: s.liver + dt * k2.liver,
        central: s.central + dt * k2.central
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Div, Mut {
    var sim = SimState {
        state: Conc { gut: 500.0, liver: 0.0, central: 0.0 },
        t: 0.0, auc: 0.0, cmax: 0.0, tmax: 0.0
    }
    let dt = 0.05
    var i = 0

    while i < 480 {
        let new_state = rk2_step(sim.state, dt)
        let new_t = sim.t + dt

        // Trapezoidal AUC
        let auc_increment = 0.5 * (sim.state.central + new_state.central) * dt

        var cmax = sim.cmax
        var tmax = sim.tmax
        if new_state.central > sim.cmax {
            cmax = new_state.central
            tmax = new_t
        }

        sim = SimState {
            state: new_state,
            t: new_t,
            auc: sim.auc + auc_increment,
            cmax: cmax,
            tmax: tmax
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print results
    println(sim.t)
    println(sim.state.gut)
    println(sim.state.liver)
    println(sim.state.central)
    println(sim.auc)
    println(sim.cmax)
    println(sim.tmax)

    // Validate:
    // 1. Time = 24.0h
    if sim.t < 23.9 { return 1 }

    // 2. Gut fully absorbed (exp(-24) ≈ 0)
    if sim.state.gut > 0.01 { return 2 }

    // 3. AUC should be positive and substantial
    if sim.auc < 100.0 { return 3 }

    // 4. Cmax > 0 (drug reached central compartment)
    if sim.cmax < 10.0 { return 4 }

    // 5. Tmax in physiological range (1-8h for oral absorption)
    if sim.tmax < 0.5 { return 5 }
    if sim.tmax > 12.0 { return 6 }

    // 6. All concentrations non-negative (conservation of mass)
    if sim.state.gut < 0.0 { return 7 }
    if sim.state.liver < 0.0 { return 8 }
    if sim.state.central < 0.0 { return 9 }

    // 7. 480 iterations completed
    if i != 480 { return 10 }

    return 0
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/pk_uncertainty.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// PK Domain Uncertainty Plugin Test Suite
//
// Validates WS2 Track 5 — PK-specific uncertainty analysis:
//   1.  Clearance dominance detection (CL contributes >70%)
//   2.  Volume dominance detection (V contributes most)
//   3.  Balanced contributions (no single dominant)
//   4.  SCr as proxy for clearance (Cockcroft-Gault scenario)
//   5.  Sensitivity index S_Ti > 0.7 triggers clearance dominance flag
//   6.  PK recommendations: clearance dominant -> TDM
//   7.  PK recommendations: absorption dominant -> bioequivalence
//   8.  Clinical significance: uncertainty > therapeutic window
//   9.  Clinical significance: uncertainty < therapeutic window
//  10.  Edge case: single parameter is 100% dominant
//  11.  Recommendation for SCr dominant -> cystatin C
//  12.  Sensitivity indices sum to 1.0
//
// Reference: Saltelli et al. (2008), FDA PopPK Guidance (2022)

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (self-contained, no imports)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_val(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x / 2.0
    if guess < 0.001 { guess = 0.001 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return guess
}

fn max_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_val(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// PK PARAMETER STRUCTURES (inlined from pk_plugin.sio)
// ============================================================================

struct PKParameter {
    code: i32,
    value: f64,
    std_uncert: f64,
    sensitivity: f64,
    contribution: f64,
    source_type: i32
}

fn empty_pk_param() -> PKParameter {
    return PKParameter {
        code: 0,
        value: 0.0,
        std_uncert: 0.0,
        sensitivity: 0.0,
        contribution: 0.0,
        source_type: 0
    }
}

fn make_pk_param(code: i32, value: f64, std_uncert: f64, sensitivity: f64, source_type: i32) -> PKParameter {
    let contrib = sensitivity * sensitivity * std_uncert * std_uncert
    return PKParameter {
        code: code,
        value: value,
        std_uncert: std_uncert,
        sensitivity: sensitivity,
        contribution: contrib,
        source_type: source_type
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK UNCERTAINTY PROFILE (inlined)

struct PKUncertaintyProfile {
    n_params: i32,
    p0: PKParameter,
    p1: PKParameter,
    p2: PKParameter,
    p3: PKParameter,
    p4: PKParameter,
    p5: PKParameter,
    p6: PKParameter,
    p7: PKParameter,
    combined_variance: f64,
    combined_std_uncert: f64,
    clearance_contribution: f64,
    volume_contribution: f64,
    absorption_contribution: f64,
    is_clearance_dominant: bool,
    dominant_param_idx: i32,
    dominant_param_contribution: f64,
    r0: i32,
    r1: i32,
    r2: i32,
    r3: i32,
    n_recommendations: i32
}

fn empty_pk_profile() -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    return PKUncertaintyProfile {
        n_params: 0,
        p0: empty_pk_param(),
        p1: empty_pk_param(),
        p2: empty_pk_param(),
        p3: empty_pk_param(),
        p4: empty_pk_param(),
        p5: empty_pk_param(),
        p6: empty_pk_param(),
        p7: empty_pk_param(),
        combined_variance: 0.0,
        combined_std_uncert: 0.0,
        clearance_contribution: 0.0,
        volume_contribution: 0.0,
        absorption_contribution: 0.0,
        is_clearance_dominant: false,
        dominant_param_idx: 0,
        dominant_param_contribution: 0.0,
        r0: 0,
        r1: 0,
        r2: 0,
        r3: 0,
        n_recommendations: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK SENSITIVITY RESULT (inlined)
// ============================================================================

struct PKSensitivityResult {
    s_ti_0: f64,
    s_ti_1: f64,
    s_ti_2: f64,
    s_ti_3: f64,
    s_ti_4: f64,
    s_ti_5: f64,
    s_ti_6: f64,
    s_ti_7: f64,
    s_i_0: f64,
    s_i_1: f64,
    s_i_2: f64,
    s_i_3: f64,
    s_i_4: f64,
    s_i_5: f64,
    s_i_6: f64,
    s_i_7: f64,
    n_params: i32,
    dominant_idx: i32,
    dominant_s_ti: f64,
    clearance_dominant: bool
}

fn empty_pk_sensitivity() -> PKSensitivityResult {
    return PKSensitivityResult {
        s_ti_0: 0.0, s_ti_1: 0.0, s_ti_2: 0.0, s_ti_3: 0.0,
        s_ti_4: 0.0, s_ti_5: 0.0, s_ti_6: 0.0, s_ti_7: 0.0,
        s_i_0: 0.0, s_i_1: 0.0, s_i_2: 0.0, s_i_3: 0.0,
        s_i_4: 0.0, s_i_5: 0.0, s_i_6: 0.0, s_i_7: 0.0,
        n_params: 0,
        dominant_idx: 0,
        dominant_s_ti: 0.0,
        clearance_dominant: false
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PK PARAMETER CLASSIFICATION (inlined)
// ============================================================================

fn pk_param_is_clearance_related(code: i32) -> bool {
    if code == 0 { return true }
    if code == 3 { return true }
    if code == 7 { return true }
    if code == 6 { return true }
    return false
}

fn pk_param_is_volume_related(code: i32) -> bool {
    if code == 1 { return true }
    if code == 6 { return true }
    return false
}

fn pk_param_is_absorption_related(code: i32) -> bool {
    if code == 2 { return true }
    if code == 4 { return true }
    return false
}

// ============================================================================
// PARAMETER ACCESS HELPERS (inlined)
// ============================================================================

fn get_pk_param(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, idx: i32) -> PKParameter {
    if idx == 0 { return profile.p0 }
    if idx == 1 { return profile.p1 }
    if idx == 2 { return profile.p2 }
    if idx == 3 { return profile.p3 }
    if idx == 4 { return profile.p4 }
    if idx == 5 { return profile.p5 }
    if idx == 6 { return profile.p6 }
    if idx == 7 { return profile.p7 }
    return empty_pk_param()
}

fn set_pk_param(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, idx: i32, param: PKParameter) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = profile
    if idx == 0 { result.p0 = param }
    else if idx == 1 { result.p1 = param }
    else if idx == 2 { result.p2 = param }
    else if idx == 3 { result.p3 = param }
    else if idx == 4 { result.p4 = param }
    else if idx == 5 { result.p5 = param }
    else if idx == 6 { result.p6 = param }
    else if idx == 7 { result.p7 = param }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// CORE ANALYSIS FUNCTIONS (inlined)
// ============================================================================

fn compute_pk_contributions(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, n: i32) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = profile
    result.n_params = n

    var total_var: f64 = 0.0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        total_var = total_var + p.contribution
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    result.combined_variance = total_var
    result.combined_std_uncert = sqrt_val(total_var)

    if total_var < 1.0e-15 {
        return result
    }

    var cl_contrib: f64 = 0.0
    var v_contrib: f64 = 0.0
    var abs_contrib: f64 = 0.0
    var best_idx = 0
    var best_pct: f64 = 0.0

    idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        let pct = 100.0 * p.contribution / total_var

        if pct > best_pct {
            best_pct = pct
            best_idx = idx
        }

        if pk_param_is_clearance_related(p.code) {
            cl_contrib = cl_contrib + pct
        }
        if pk_param_is_volume_related(p.code) {
            v_contrib = v_contrib + pct
        }
        if pk_param_is_absorption_related(p.code) {
            abs_contrib = abs_contrib + pct
        }

        idx = idx + 1
    }

    result.clearance_contribution = cl_contrib
    result.volume_contribution = v_contrib
    result.absorption_contribution = abs_contrib
    result.dominant_param_idx = best_idx
    result.dominant_param_contribution = best_pct

    if cl_contrib > 70.0 {
        result.is_clearance_dominant = true
    } else {
        result.is_clearance_dominant = false
    }

    return result
}

fn compute_pk_sensitivity(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, n: i32) -> PKSensitivityResult {
    var result = empty_pk_sensitivity()
    result.n_params = n

    var total_var: f64 = 0.0
    var idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        total_var = total_var + p.contribution
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    if total_var < 1.0e-15 {
        return result
    }

    var best_idx = 0
    var best_s_ti: f64 = 0.0

    idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        let s_ti = p.contribution / total_var
        let s_i = s_ti

        if idx == 0 { result.s_ti_0 = s_ti; result.s_i_0 = s_i }
        else if idx == 1 { result.s_ti_1 = s_ti; result.s_i_1 = s_i }
        else if idx == 2 { result.s_ti_2 = s_ti; result.s_i_2 = s_i }
        else if idx == 3 { result.s_ti_3 = s_ti; result.s_i_3 = s_i }
        else if idx == 4 { result.s_ti_4 = s_ti; result.s_i_4 = s_i }
        else if idx == 5 { result.s_ti_5 = s_ti; result.s_i_5 = s_i }
        else if idx == 6 { result.s_ti_6 = s_ti; result.s_i_6 = s_i }
        else if idx == 7 { result.s_ti_7 = s_ti; result.s_i_7 = s_i }

        if s_ti > best_s_ti {
            best_s_ti = s_ti
            best_idx = idx
        }

        idx = idx + 1
    }

    result.dominant_idx = best_idx
    result.dominant_s_ti = best_s_ti

    var cl_total_s_ti: f64 = 0.0
    idx = 0
    while idx < n {
        let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
        if pk_param_is_clearance_related(p.code) {
            let s_ti = p.contribution / total_var
            cl_total_s_ti = cl_total_s_ti + s_ti
        }
        idx = idx + 1
    }

    if cl_total_s_ti > 0.7 {
        result.clearance_dominant = true
    } else {
        result.clearance_dominant = false
    }

    return result
}

fn generate_pk_recommendations(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = profile
    var n_rec = 0

    if profile.is_clearance_dominant {
        if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 10 }
        else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 10 }
        else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 10 }
        else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 10 }
        n_rec = n_rec + 1
    }

    if profile.volume_contribution > 50.0 {
        if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 11 }
        else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 11 }
        else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 11 }
        else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 11 }
        n_rec = n_rec + 1
    }

    if profile.absorption_contribution > 50.0 {
        if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 12 }
        else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 12 }
        else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 12 }
        else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 12 }
        n_rec = n_rec + 1
    }

    if profile.is_clearance_dominant {
        var scr_pct: f64 = 0.0
        var idx = 0
        while idx < profile.n_params {
            let p = get_pk_param(profile, idx)
            if p.code == 7 {
                if profile.combined_variance > 1.0e-15 {
                    scr_pct = 100.0 * p.contribution / profile.combined_variance
                }
            }
            idx = idx + 1
        }
        if scr_pct > 20.0 {
            if n_rec < 4 {
                if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 13 }
                else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 13 }
                else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 13 }
                else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 13 }
                n_rec = n_rec + 1
            }
        }
    }

    if profile.combined_std_uncert > 0.0 {
        let dom_p = get_pk_param(profile, profile.dominant_param_idx)
        if abs_val(dom_p.value) > 1.0e-15 {
            let rel_uncert = 100.0 * profile.combined_std_uncert / abs_val(dom_p.value)
            if rel_uncert > 30.0 {
                if n_rec < 4 {
                    if n_rec == 0 { result.r0 = 14 }
                    else if n_rec == 1 { result.r1 = 14 }
                    else if n_rec == 2 { result.r2 = 14 }
                    else if n_rec == 3 { result.r3 = 14 }
                    n_rec = n_rec + 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if n_rec > 4 { result.n_recommendations = 4 }
    else { result.n_recommendations = n_rec }

    return result
}

fn pk_analyze(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, n: i32) -> PKUncertaintyProfile {
    var result = compute_pk_contributions(profile, n)
    result = generate_pk_recommendations(result)
    return result
}

fn pk_is_clinically_significant(profile: PKUncertaintyProfile, therapeutic_window: f64) -> bool {
    if therapeutic_window <= 1.0 { return true }
    let half_width = 2.0 * profile.combined_std_uncert
    let dom_p = get_pk_param(profile, profile.dominant_param_idx)
    if abs_val(dom_p.value) < 1.0e-15 { return true }
    let rel_half = half_width / abs_val(dom_p.value)
    let margin = 1.0 - 1.0 / therapeutic_window
    if rel_half > margin {
        return true
    }
    return false
}

fn get_s_ti(sens: PKSensitivityResult, idx: i32) -> f64 {
    if idx == 0 { return sens.s_ti_0 }
    if idx == 1 { return sens.s_ti_1 }
    if idx == 2 { return sens.s_ti_2 }
    if idx == 3 { return sens.s_ti_3 }
    if idx == 4 { return sens.s_ti_4 }
    if idx == 5 { return sens.s_ti_5 }
    if idx == 6 { return sens.s_ti_6 }
    if idx == 7 { return sens.s_ti_7 }
    return 0.0
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN TEST SUITE
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic {
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  PK Domain Uncertainty Plugin Test Suite")
    println("  WS2 Track 5 — Pharmacokinetic Sensitivity Analysis")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("")

    var passed = 0
    var failed = 0

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 1: Clearance dominance detection
    //
    // CL(code=0): value=5.0, u=1.5, sensitivity=0.8 -> contrib=(0.8*1.5)^2=1.44
    // V (code=1): value=50,  u=5.0, sensitivity=0.2 -> contrib=(0.2*5.0)^2=1.00
    // ka(code=2): value=1.0, u=0.1, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=(0.1*0.1)^2=0.0001
    //
    // Total = 1.44 + 1.00 + 0.0001 = 2.4401
    // CL is code 0 (clearance-related): 1.44/2.4401 = 59%
    // V is code 1 (volume-related): 1.00/2.4401 = 41%
    // Weight (code 6) is both CL and V related, but not present here.
    //
    // For CL dominance, need CL-related > 70%. Let us use a stronger CL.
    // CL(code=0): value=5.0, u=2.0, sensitivity=0.9 -> contrib=(0.9*2.0)^2=3.24
    // V (code=1): value=50,  u=2.0, sensitivity=0.2 -> contrib=(0.2*2.0)^2=0.16
    // ka(code=2): value=1.0, u=0.1, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=(0.1*0.1)^2=0.0001
    //
    // Total = 3.24 + 0.16 + 0.0001 = 3.4001
    // CL%: 3.24/3.4001*100 = 95.3%  -> clearance dominant
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 1: Clearance dominance detection (CL > 70%)")

    var profile1 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile1.p0 = make_pk_param(0, 5.0, 2.0, 0.9, 0)
    profile1.p1 = make_pk_param(1, 50.0, 2.0, 0.2, 1)
    profile1.p2 = make_pk_param(2, 1.0, 0.1, 0.1, 0)
    profile1 = pk_analyze(profile1, 3)

    println("  CL contribution %:")
    println(profile1.clearance_contribution)
    println("  Is clearance dominant:")
    if profile1.is_clearance_dominant { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if profile1.is_clearance_dominant == false {
        println("FAIL: Should detect clearance dominance (CL > 70%)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if profile1.clearance_contribution < 70.0 {
        println("FAIL: CL contribution should be > 70%")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Clearance dominance correctly detected")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 2: Volume dominance (V contributes most)
    //
    // CL(code=0): value=5.0, u=0.1, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=0.0001
    // V (code=1): value=50,  u=15.0, sensitivity=0.9 -> contrib=(0.9*15)^2=182.25
    // ka(code=2): value=1.0, u=0.1, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=0.0001
    //
    // Total = 182.2502
    // V%: 182.25/182.2502*100 = ~100%
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 2: Volume dominance (V contributes most)")

    var profile2 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile2.p0 = make_pk_param(0, 5.0, 0.1, 0.1, 0)
    profile2.p1 = make_pk_param(1, 50.0, 15.0, 0.9, 1)
    profile2.p2 = make_pk_param(2, 1.0, 0.1, 0.1, 0)
    profile2 = pk_analyze(profile2, 3)

    println("  Volume contribution %:")
    println(profile2.volume_contribution)
    println("  Is clearance dominant:")
    if profile2.is_clearance_dominant { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if profile2.is_clearance_dominant {
        println("FAIL: Should NOT be clearance dominant when V dominates")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if profile2.volume_contribution < 50.0 {
        println("FAIL: Volume contribution should be > 50%")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Volume dominance correctly detected")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 3: Balanced contributions (no single dominant)
    //
    // CL(code=0): u=1.0, sensitivity=1.0 -> contrib=1.0
    // V (code=1): u=1.0, sensitivity=1.0 -> contrib=1.0
    // ka(code=2): u=1.0, sensitivity=1.0 -> contrib=1.0
    //
    // Each is 33.3%. CL-related = 33.3%, not > 70%.
    // Dominant param contribution = 33.3%.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 3: Balanced contributions (no dominance)")

    var profile3 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile3.p0 = make_pk_param(0, 5.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0)
    profile3.p1 = make_pk_param(1, 50.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1)
    profile3.p2 = make_pk_param(2, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0)
    profile3 = pk_analyze(profile3, 3)

    println("  CL contribution %:")
    println(profile3.clearance_contribution)
    println("  Dominant param contribution %:")
    println(profile3.dominant_param_contribution)

    if profile3.is_clearance_dominant {
        println("FAIL: Should NOT be clearance dominant with balanced inputs")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if profile3.dominant_param_contribution > 50.0 {
        println("FAIL: No single param should dominate (>50%)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Balanced contributions correctly identified")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 4: SCr as proxy for clearance (Cockcroft-Gault scenario)
    //
    // SCr(code=7): high sensitivity, high uncertainty
    // Weight(code=6): moderate
    //
    // CrCl = (140-Age)*Weight/(72*SCr)
    //
    // SCr(code=7): value=1.2, u=0.3, sensitivity=54.4 -> contrib=(54.4*0.3)^2=266.5
    // Weight(code=6): value=70, u=2.0, sensitivity=0.926 -> contrib=(0.926*2)^2=3.43
    // V(code=1): value=50, u=1.0, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=0.01
    //
    // Total ~ 269.94
    // CL-related = SCr(7) + Weight(6) = (266.5+3.43)/269.94*100 = 99.9%
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 4: SCr dominance (Cockcroft-Gault clearance)")

    let age_val = 60.0
    let wt_val = 70.0
    let scr_val = 1.2
    // dCrCl/dSCr = -(140-Age)*Weight/(72*SCr^2)
    let s_scr = abs_val((140.0 - age_val) * wt_val / (72.0 * scr_val * scr_val))
    // dCrCl/dWeight = (140-Age)/(72*SCr)
    let s_wt = (140.0 - age_val) / (72.0 * scr_val)

    var profile4 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile4.p0 = make_pk_param(7, scr_val, 0.3, s_scr, 0)
    profile4.p1 = make_pk_param(6, wt_val, 2.0, s_wt, 0)
    profile4.p2 = make_pk_param(1, 50.0, 1.0, 0.1, 1)
    profile4 = pk_analyze(profile4, 3)

    println("  SCr sensitivity coefficient:")
    println(s_scr)
    println("  CL contribution % (SCr+Weight):")
    println(profile4.clearance_contribution)
    println("  Is clearance dominant:")
    if profile4.is_clearance_dominant { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if profile4.is_clearance_dominant == false {
        println("FAIL: SCr+Weight should trigger clearance dominance")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] SCr correctly identified as clearance proxy")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 5: Sensitivity index S_Ti > 0.7 triggers flag
    //
    // Use profile1 (CL-dominant). Compute sensitivity indices.
    // CL S_Ti should be > 0.7.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 5: Sensitivity index S_Ti > 0.7 for CL dominance")

    // Re-use profile1 data (already analyzed)
    var sens_profile = empty_pk_profile()
    sens_profile.p0 = make_pk_param(0, 5.0, 2.0, 0.9, 0)
    sens_profile.p1 = make_pk_param(1, 50.0, 2.0, 0.2, 1)
    sens_profile.p2 = make_pk_param(2, 1.0, 0.1, 0.1, 0)
    let sens5 = compute_pk_sensitivity(sens_profile, 3)

    println("  S_Ti(CL):")
    println(sens5.s_ti_0)
    println("  Dominant S_Ti:")
    println(sens5.dominant_s_ti)
    println("  Clearance dominant by Sobol:")
    if sens5.clearance_dominant { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if sens5.clearance_dominant == false {
        println("FAIL: CL S_Ti should trigger clearance dominance flag")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if sens5.dominant_s_ti < 0.7 {
        println("FAIL: Dominant S_Ti should be > 0.7")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] S_Ti > 0.7 correctly triggers clearance dominance")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 6: PK recommendations — clearance dominant -> TDM (code 10)
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 6: Clearance dominant -> TDM recommendation")

    println("  Recommendation r0:")
    println(profile1.r0)
    println("  n_recommendations:")
    println(profile1.n_recommendations)

    if profile1.r0 != 10 {
        println("FAIL: CL dominant should recommend TDM (code 10)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] TDM correctly recommended for CL dominance")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 7: PK recommendations — absorption dominant -> bioequivalence (code 12)
    //
    // ka(code=2): u=2.0, sensitivity=0.9 -> contrib=3.24
    // F (code=4): u=0.1, sensitivity=0.5 -> contrib=0.0025
    // CL(code=0): u=0.05, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=0.000025
    //
    // Absorption = ka+F = (3.24+0.0025)/3.242525*100 = 99.9%
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 7: Absorption dominant -> bioequivalence recommendation")

    var profile7 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile7.p0 = make_pk_param(2, 1.0, 2.0, 0.9, 0)
    profile7.p1 = make_pk_param(4, 0.8, 0.1, 0.5, 2)
    profile7.p2 = make_pk_param(0, 5.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0)
    profile7 = pk_analyze(profile7, 3)

    println("  Absorption contribution %:")
    println(profile7.absorption_contribution)
    println("  Recommendation r0:")
    println(profile7.r0)

    if profile7.r0 != 12 {
        println("FAIL: Absorption dominant should recommend bioequivalence (code 12)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Bioequivalence correctly recommended for absorption dominance")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 8: Clinical significance — uncertainty > therapeutic window
    //
    // Narrow therapeutic window drug (e.g., digoxin, TW ~ 2.0)
    // CL value=5.0, combined_std_uncert ~ large relative to CL.
    //
    // Use profile1: combined_std_uncert = sqrt(3.4001) = 1.844
    // dom param = CL (value=5.0)
    // half_width = 2*1.844 = 3.688
    // rel_half = 3.688/5.0 = 0.7376
    // margin for TW=2.0 = 1 - 1/2 = 0.5
    // 0.7376 > 0.5 -> clinically significant
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 8: Clinical significance (uncertainty > therapeutic window)")

    let sig8 = pk_is_clinically_significant(profile1, 2.0)
    println("  Clinically significant (TW=2.0):")
    if sig8 { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if sig8 == false {
        println("FAIL: Should be clinically significant for narrow TW")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Correctly identifies clinically significant uncertainty")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 9: Clinical significance — uncertainty < therapeutic window
    //
    // Wide therapeutic window drug (e.g., amoxicillin, TW ~ 10.0)
    // Use a profile with small uncertainty relative to value.
    //
    // CL(code=0): value=100.0, u=1.0, sensitivity=0.1 -> contrib=0.01
    // combined_std_uncert = sqrt(0.01) = 0.1
    // half_width = 2*0.1 = 0.2
    // rel_half = 0.2/100.0 = 0.002
    // margin for TW=10.0 = 1 - 1/10 = 0.9
    // 0.002 < 0.9 -> NOT clinically significant
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 9: Clinical significance (uncertainty < therapeutic window)")

    var profile9 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile9.p0 = make_pk_param(0, 100.0, 1.0, 0.1, 0)
    profile9 = compute_pk_contributions(profile9, 1)

    let sig9 = pk_is_clinically_significant(profile9, 10.0)
    println("  Combined std uncert:")
    println(profile9.combined_std_uncert)
    println("  Clinically significant (TW=10.0):")
    if sig9 { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if sig9 {
        println("FAIL: Should NOT be clinically significant for wide TW")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Correctly identifies non-significant uncertainty")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 10: Edge case — single parameter is 100% dominant
    //
    // Only CL present. It should be 100% dominant.
    // CL(code=0): value=5.0, u=1.0, sensitivity=1.0 -> contrib=1.0
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 10: Single parameter (100% dominant)")

    var profile10 = empty_pk_profile()
    profile10.p0 = make_pk_param(0, 5.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0)
    profile10 = pk_analyze(profile10, 1)

    println("  Dominant param idx:")
    println(profile10.dominant_param_idx)
    println("  Dominant contribution %:")
    println(profile10.dominant_param_contribution)
    println("  CL contribution %:")
    println(profile10.clearance_contribution)

    if profile10.dominant_param_idx != 0 {
        println("FAIL: Single param should be at idx 0")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else if abs_val(profile10.dominant_param_contribution - 100.0) > 0.1 {
        println("FAIL: Single param should be 100% dominant")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Single parameter correctly shows 100% dominance")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 11: SCr dominant -> cystatin C recommendation (code 13)
    //
    // SCr(code=7): high contribution, CL-dominant scenario
    // Use profile4 (SCr+Weight in CrCl context).
    // SCr contributes >20% AND CL is dominant -> recommend cystatin C.
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 11: SCr dominant -> cystatin C recommendation")

    // Check that cystatin C (13) is among recommendations
    var has_cystatin_c = false
    if profile4.r0 == 13 { has_cystatin_c = true }
    if profile4.r1 == 13 { has_cystatin_c = true }
    if profile4.r2 == 13 { has_cystatin_c = true }
    if profile4.r3 == 13 { has_cystatin_c = true }

    println("  Recommendations: r0=")
    println(profile4.r0)
    println("  r1=")
    println(profile4.r1)
    println("  Has cystatin C rec:")
    if has_cystatin_c { println("  true") } else { println("  false") }

    if has_cystatin_c == false {
        println("FAIL: SCr dominance should recommend cystatin C (code 13)")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Cystatin C correctly recommended for SCr dominance")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // TEST 12: Sensitivity indices sum to 1.0
    //
    // For 3 parameters, S_Ti_0 + S_Ti_1 + S_Ti_2 should equal 1.0
    // (since linear model: total Sobol = sum of first-order = 1.0)
    // ================================================================

    println("TEST 12: Sensitivity indices sum to 1.0")

    let sum_sti = sens5.s_ti_0 + sens5.s_ti_1 + sens5.s_ti_2
    println("  S_Ti_0 + S_Ti_1 + S_Ti_2:")
    println(sum_sti)

    if abs_val(sum_sti - 1.0) > 0.01 {
        println("FAIL: Sensitivity indices should sum to 1.0")
        failed = failed + 1
    } else {
        println("[PASS] Sensitivity indices correctly sum to 1.0")
        passed = passed + 1
    }
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // SUMMARY
    // ================================================================
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  PK DOMAIN UNCERTAINTY PLUGIN — TEST SUMMARY")
    println("======================================================================")
    println("  Passed:")
    println(passed)
    println("  Failed:")
    println(failed)

    if failed == 0 {
        println("  ALL 12 TESTS PASSED")
        println("  PK uncertainty plugin validated for clinical pharmacology")
    } else {
        println("  SOME TESTS FAILED")
    }
    println("======================================================================")

    return failed
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/polynomial_ops.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 18 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// polynomial_ops.sio - Integration tests for polynomial library
//
// Validates polynomial construction, arithmetic, evaluation, calculus,
// and root-finding operations. All structs and functions inlined since
// tests cannot import from stdlib.
//
// Polynomials stored in ascending order: p(x) = c[0] + c[1]*x + ... + c[n]*x^n

// ============================================================================
// HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x / 2.0
    if g < 1.0 { g = 1.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 60 {
        g = (g + x / g) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return g
}

// ============================================================================
// POLYNOMIAL DATA STRUCTURES
// ============================================================================

struct Polynomial {
    coeffs: [f64; 64],
    degree: i32,
}

struct QuadraticRoots {
    r1: f64,
    r2: f64,
    discriminant: f64,
    has_real_roots: bool,
}

// ============================================================================
// POLYNOMIAL CONSTRUCTION
// ============================================================================

// Create the zero polynomial (degree -1 by convention)
fn poly_zero() -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: -1 }
}

// Create a constant polynomial: p(x) = c
fn poly_constant(c: f64) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c
    let deg = if c == 0.0 { -1 } else { 0 }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Create a linear polynomial: p(x) = a*x + b
fn poly_linear(a: f64, b: f64) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = b
    coeffs[1] = a
    let deg = if a != 0.0 { 1 } else { if b != 0.0 { 0 } else { -1 } }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Create a quadratic polynomial: p(x) = a*x^2 + b*x + c
fn poly_quadratic(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c
    coeffs[1] = b
    coeffs[2] = a
    let deg = if a != 0.0 { 2 } else { if b != 0.0 { 1 } else { if c != 0.0 { 0 } else { -1 } } }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Create a monomial: p(x) = c * x^n
fn poly_monomial(c: f64, n: i32) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic {
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    if n >= 0 && n < 64 {
        coeffs[n] = c
    }
    let deg = if c == 0.0 { -1 } else { n }
    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// ============================================================================
// POLYNOMIAL EVALUATION
// ============================================================================

// Evaluate polynomial at x using Horner's method
fn poly_eval(p: Polynomial, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if p.degree < 0 {
        return 0.0
    }
    var result = p.coeffs[p.degree]
    var i = p.degree - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        result = result * x + p.coeffs[i]
        i = i - 1
    }
    return result
}

// Get coefficient at index i (returns 0.0 if out of range)
fn poly_coeff(p: Polynomial, i: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    if i < 0 || i > p.degree {
        return 0.0
    }
    return p.coeffs[i]
}

// Get the degree of the polynomial (-1 for zero polynomial)
fn poly_degree(p: Polynomial) -> i32 {
    return p.degree
}

// Check if polynomial is zero
fn poly_is_zero(p: Polynomial) -> bool {
    return p.degree < 0
}

// ============================================================================
// POLYNOMIAL ARITHMETIC
// ============================================================================

// Add two polynomials
fn poly_add(a: Polynomial, b: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let max_deg = if a.degree > b.degree { a.degree } else { b.degree }
    if max_deg < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= max_deg {
        let ca = if i <= a.degree { a.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        let cb = if i <= b.degree { b.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        coeffs[i] = ca + cb
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = max_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Subtract two polynomials: a - b
fn poly_sub(a: Polynomial, b: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let max_deg = if a.degree > b.degree { a.degree } else { b.degree }
    if max_deg < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= max_deg {
        let ca = if i <= a.degree { a.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        let cb = if i <= b.degree { b.coeffs[i] } else { 0.0 }
        coeffs[i] = ca - cb
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = max_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Multiply two polynomials (convolution of coefficients)
fn poly_mul(a: Polynomial, b: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if a.degree < 0 || b.degree < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    let result_deg = a.degree + b.degree
    let max_deg = if result_deg > 63 { 63 } else { result_deg }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= a.degree {
        var j = 0
        while j <= b.degree {
            let k = i + j
            if k <= max_deg {
                coeffs[k] = coeffs[k] + a.coeffs[i] * b.coeffs[j]
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = max_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Scale polynomial by a constant: c * p(x)
fn poly_scale(p: Polynomial, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if c == 0.0 || p.degree < 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= p.degree {
        coeffs[i] = p.coeffs[i] * c
        i = i + 1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: p.degree }
}

// Negate polynomial: -p(x)
fn poly_neg(p: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return poly_scale(p, 0.0 - 1.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// CALCULUS
// ============================================================================

// Compute the derivative: d/dx[c[i]*x^i] = i*c[i]*x^(i-1)
fn poly_derivative(p: Polynomial) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if p.degree <= 0 {
        return poly_zero()
    }

    let new_deg = p.degree - 1
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    var i = 0
    while i <= new_deg {
        coeffs[i] = (i + 1) as f64 * p.coeffs[i + 1]
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Trim leading zeros
    var deg = new_deg
    while deg > 0 && coeffs[deg] == 0.0 {
        deg = deg - 1
    }
    if deg == 0 && coeffs[0] == 0.0 {
        deg = -1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: deg }
}

// Compute the indefinite integral with constant c: integral p(x) dx + c
fn poly_integral(p: Polynomial, c: f64) -> Polynomial with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if p.degree < 0 {
        return poly_constant(c)
    }

    let new_deg = if p.degree < 63 { p.degree + 1 } else { 63 }
    var coeffs: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    coeffs[0] = c

    var i = 0
    while i <= p.degree && i < 63 {
        coeffs[i + 1] = p.coeffs[i] / ((i + 1) as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }

    Polynomial { coeffs: coeffs, degree: new_deg }
}

// ============================================================================
// ROOT FINDING
// ============================================================================

// Solve quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0
fn poly_roots_quadratic(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64) -> QuadraticRoots with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if a == 0.0 {
        if b == 0.0 {
            return QuadraticRoots { r1: 0.0, r2: 0.0, discriminant: 0.0, has_real_roots: false }
        }
        let r = 0.0 - c / b
        return QuadraticRoots { r1: r, r2: r, discriminant: 0.0, has_real_roots: true }
    }
    let disc = b * b - 4.0 * a * c
    if disc < 0.0 {
        return QuadraticRoots { r1: 0.0, r2: 0.0, discriminant: disc, has_real_roots: false }
    }
    let sqrt_disc = sqrt_f64(disc)
    let r1 = (0.0 - b + sqrt_disc) / (2.0 * a)
    let r2 = (0.0 - b - sqrt_disc) / (2.0 * a)
    QuadraticRoots { r1: r1, r2: r2, discriminant: disc, has_real_roots: true }
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

// Test 1: Zero polynomial has degree -1 and is_zero returns true
fn test_zero() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let z = poly_zero()
    let deg_ok = poly_degree(z) == -1
    let is_zero_ok = poly_is_zero(z)
    let eval_ok = approx_eq(poly_eval(z, 42.0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    return deg_ok && is_zero_ok && eval_ok
}

// Test 2: Constant polynomial evaluates to the constant everywhere
fn test_constant() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let c = poly_constant(5.0)
    let ok1 = approx_eq(poly_eval(c, 0.0), 5.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_eval(c, 100.0), 5.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_eval(c, 0.0 - 7.0), 5.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = poly_degree(c) == 0
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 3: Linear polynomial p(x) = 2x + 3 at x=4 gives 11
fn test_linear_eval() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_linear(2.0, 3.0)
    let val = poly_eval(p, 4.0)
    let ok1 = approx_eq(val, 11.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok2 = poly_degree(p) == 1
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(p, 0), 3.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(p, 1), 2.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 4: Quadratic p(x) = x^2 - 2x + 1 at x=3 gives 4
fn test_quadratic_eval() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_quadratic(1.0, 0.0 - 2.0, 1.0)
    let val = poly_eval(p, 3.0)
    let ok1 = approx_eq(val, 4.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok2 = poly_degree(p) == 2
    // Also check at x=1 where (1-1)^2 = 0
    let val_at_1 = poly_eval(p, 1.0)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(val_at_1, 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}

// Test 5: Addition: (x+1) + (x-1) = 2x
fn test_add() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p1 = poly_linear(1.0, 1.0)
    let p2 = poly_linear(1.0, 0.0 - 1.0)
    let sum = poly_add(p1, p2)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(sum) == 1
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(sum, 0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(sum, 1), 2.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate: 2*5 = 10
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_eval(sum, 5.0), 10.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 6: Subtraction: (x^2 + x) - (x) = x^2
fn test_sub() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p1 = poly_quadratic(1.0, 1.0, 0.0)
    let p2 = poly_linear(1.0, 0.0)
    let diff = poly_sub(p1, p2)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(diff) == 2
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(diff, 0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(diff, 1), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(diff, 2), 1.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate: 3^2 = 9
    let ok5 = approx_eq(poly_eval(diff, 3.0), 9.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5
}

// Test 7: Multiplication: (x+1)*(x-1) = x^2 - 1
fn test_mul() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p1 = poly_linear(1.0, 1.0)
    let p2 = poly_linear(1.0, 0.0 - 1.0)
    let prod = poly_mul(p1, p2)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(prod) == 2
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(prod, 0), 0.0 - 1.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(prod, 1), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(prod, 2), 1.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate at x=3: 9-1=8
    let ok5 = approx_eq(poly_eval(prod, 3.0), 8.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5
}

// Test 8: Multiply by zero gives zero
fn test_mul_by_zero() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_quadratic(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)
    let z = poly_zero()
    let prod = poly_mul(p, z)
    let ok1 = poly_is_zero(prod)
    let ok2 = poly_degree(prod) == -1
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_eval(prod, 99.0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}

// Test 9: Scaling: 3*(2x+1) = 6x+3
fn test_scale() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_linear(2.0, 1.0)
    let scaled = poly_scale(p, 3.0)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(scaled) == 1
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(scaled, 0), 3.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(scaled, 1), 6.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate at x=2: 6*2+3 = 15
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_eval(scaled, 2.0), 15.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 10: Derivative of x^2 + 2x + 1 = 2x + 2
fn test_derivative_quadratic() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_quadratic(1.0, 2.0, 1.0)
    let dp = poly_derivative(p)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(dp) == 1
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dp, 0), 2.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dp, 1), 2.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate at x=5: 2*5+2 = 12
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_eval(dp, 5.0), 12.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 11: Derivative of x^3 = 3x^2
fn test_derivative_cubic() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_monomial(1.0, 3)
    let dp = poly_derivative(p)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(dp) == 2
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dp, 0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dp, 1), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dp, 2), 3.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate at x=2: 3*4 = 12
    let ok5 = approx_eq(poly_eval(dp, 2.0), 12.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5
}

// Test 12: Integral of 2x (with c=0) = x^2
fn test_integral_linear() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_linear(2.0, 0.0)
    let ip = poly_integral(p, 0.0)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(ip) == 2
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(ip, 0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(ip, 1), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(ip, 2), 1.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate at x=3: 9
    let ok5 = approx_eq(poly_eval(ip, 3.0), 9.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5
}

// Test 13: Derivative of integral of p = p (roundtrip)
fn test_derivative_integral_roundtrip() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_quadratic(3.0, 0.0 - 2.0, 5.0)
    let ip = poly_integral(p, 0.0)
    let dip = poly_derivative(ip)
    // dip should equal p: coefficients should match
    let ok1 = poly_degree(dip) == poly_degree(p)
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dip, 0), poly_coeff(p, 0), 1.0e-10)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dip, 1), poly_coeff(p, 1), 1.0e-10)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(dip, 2), poly_coeff(p, 2), 1.0e-10)
    // Also verify by evaluation at several points
    let ok5 = approx_eq(poly_eval(dip, 1.0), poly_eval(p, 1.0), 1.0e-10)
    let ok6 = approx_eq(poly_eval(dip, 0.0 - 2.0), poly_eval(p, 0.0 - 2.0), 1.0e-10)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5 && ok6
}

// Test 14: Roots of x^2 - 4 = 0 are +2 and -2
fn test_roots_distinct() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let roots = poly_roots_quadratic(1.0, 0.0, 0.0 - 4.0)
    let ok1 = roots.has_real_roots
    let ok2 = approx_eq(roots.discriminant, 16.0, 1.0e-10)
    // r1 and r2 should be 2 and -2 (order may vary)
    let r_sum = roots.r1 + roots.r2
    let r_prod = roots.r1 * roots.r2
    let ok3 = approx_eq(r_sum, 0.0, 1.0e-10)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(r_prod, 0.0 - 4.0, 1.0e-10)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 15: Roots of x^2 - 2x + 1 = 0 is repeated root at 1
fn test_roots_repeated() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let roots = poly_roots_quadratic(1.0, 0.0 - 2.0, 1.0)
    let ok1 = roots.has_real_roots
    let ok2 = approx_eq(roots.discriminant, 0.0, 1.0e-10)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(roots.r1, 1.0, 1.0e-10)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(roots.r2, 1.0, 1.0e-10)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 16: x^2 + 1 = 0 has no real roots
fn test_roots_no_real() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let roots = poly_roots_quadratic(1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    let ok1 = roots.has_real_roots == false
    let ok2 = roots.discriminant < 0.0
    return ok1 && ok2
}

// Test 17: Negation: -(2x+3) = -2x - 3
fn test_neg() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_linear(2.0, 3.0)
    let neg = poly_neg(p)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(neg) == 1
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(neg, 0), 0.0 - 3.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(neg, 1), 0.0 - 2.0, 1.0e-12)
    // Evaluate at x=4: -(2*4+3) = -11
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_eval(neg, 4.0), 0.0 - 11.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4
}

// Test 18: Monomial 5x^3 evaluates correctly
fn test_monomial() -> bool with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let p = poly_monomial(5.0, 3)
    let ok1 = poly_degree(p) == 3
    let ok2 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(p, 3), 5.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok3 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(p, 0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok4 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(p, 1), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    let ok5 = approx_eq(poly_coeff(p, 2), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    // 5 * 2^3 = 40
    let ok6 = approx_eq(poly_eval(p, 2.0), 40.0, 1.0e-12)
    // 5 * 0^3 = 0
    let ok7 = approx_eq(poly_eval(p, 0.0), 0.0, 1.0e-12)
    return ok1 && ok2 && ok3 && ok4 && ok5 && ok6 && ok7
}

// === FILE: tests/run-pass/probability_distributions.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 18 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// Probability Distribution Function Tests
//
// Self-contained test suite validating probability distribution functions:
//   Uniform, Normal, Exponential, Poisson, Binomial
//
// All functions are inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Feller, "An Introduction to Probability Theory" (3rd ed.)
//   Abramowitz & Stegun (1964), Table 7.1 (erf approximation)
//   NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions

// ============================================================================
// PURE MATH HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x
    if g < 1.0 { g = 1.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 50 {
        g = (g + x / g) / 2.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    return g
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x > 20.0 { return exp_f64(x / 2.0) * exp_f64(x / 2.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 20.0 { return 1.0 / exp_f64(0.0 - x) }
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 25 {
        term = term * x / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    return 2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn pow_f64(base: f64, exp_val: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if base <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return exp_f64(exp_val * ln_f64(base))
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// UNIFORM DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Uniform {
    a: f64,
    b: f64,
}

fn uniform_pdf(d: Uniform, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x < d.a || x > d.b { return 0.0 }
    return 1.0 / (d.b - d.a)
}

fn uniform_cdf(d: Uniform, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= d.a { return 0.0 }
    if x >= d.b { return 1.0 }
    return (x - d.a) / (d.b - d.a)
}

fn uniform_mean(d: Uniform) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return (d.a + d.b) / 2.0
}

fn uniform_variance(d: Uniform) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let range = d.b - d.a
    return range * range / 12.0
}

// ============================================================================
// NORMAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Normal {
    mu: f64,
    sigma: f64,
}

// Error function approximation (Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.26)
fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let sign = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let a = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.3275911 * a)
    let poly = t * (0.254829592 + t * (0.0 - 0.284496736 + t * (1.421413741 + t * (0.0 - 1.453152027 + t * 1.061405429))))
    let result = 1.0 - poly * exp_f64(0.0 - a * a)
    return sign * result
}

fn normal_pdf(d: Normal, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let z = (x - d.mu) / d.sigma
    return exp_f64(0.0 - 0.5 * z * z) / (d.sigma * sqrt_f64(2.0 * pi))
}

fn normal_cdf(d: Normal, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let z = (x - d.mu) / d.sigma
    return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf_approx(z / sqrt_f64(2.0)))
}

// ============================================================================
// EXPONENTIAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Exponential {
    lambda: f64,
}

fn exponential_pdf(d: Exponential, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return d.lambda * exp_f64(0.0 - d.lambda * x)
}

fn exponential_cdf(d: Exponential, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return 1.0 - exp_f64(0.0 - d.lambda * x)
}

// ============================================================================
// POISSON DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Poisson {
    lambda: f64,
}

fn poisson_pmf(d: Poisson, k: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // P(X=k) = lambda^k * e^(-lambda) / k!
    // Use log-space to avoid overflow
    var log_pmf = (k as f64) * ln_f64(d.lambda) - d.lambda
    var i = 1
    while i <= k {
        log_pmf = log_pmf - ln_f64(i as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return exp_f64(log_pmf)
}

// ============================================================================
// BINOMIAL DISTRIBUTION
// ============================================================================

struct Binomial {
    n: i32,
    p: f64,
}

fn binomial_pmf(d: Binomial, k: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k)
    // Use log-space: log C(n,k) = sum log(n-i+1) - sum log(i) for i=1..k
    var log_pmf = 0.0
    var i = 1
    while i <= k {
        log_pmf = log_pmf + ln_f64((d.n - i + 1) as f64) - ln_f64(i as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    log_pmf = log_pmf + (k as f64) * ln_f64(d.p) + ((d.n - k) as f64) * ln_f64(1.0 - d.p)
    return exp_f64(log_pmf)
}
