    print("Failed: "); println(fail as string)
    println("")
    if fail == 0 {
        println("ALL 12 TESTS PASSED")
        return 0
    } else {
        println("SOME TESTS FAILED")
        return 1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_functional.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 12 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// test_functional.sio — Tests for computational functional analysis module
//
// Self-contained test suite for operator norms, spectral radius, condition
// number, L2 inner products, RKHS interpolation, compact operator spectrum,
// and Fredholm alternative detection. All structs, helpers, and algorithms
// are inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Kreyszig (1978): "Introductory Functional Analysis with Applications"
//   Conway (1990): "A Course in Functional Analysis"
//   Fasshauer (2007): "Meshfree Approximation Methods with MATLAB"

// ============================================================================
// PURE MATH HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn fa_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn fa_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn fa_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn fa_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 20 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn fa_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x > 500.0 { return 1.0e200 }
    if x < -500.0 { return 0.0 }
    var kf = x / 0.6931471805599453
    var k: i32 = 0
    if kf >= 0.0 { k = kf as i32 } else { k = (kf as i32) - 1 }
    let r = x - (k as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 25 { term = term * r / (n as f64); sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    var result = sum
    if k >= 0 { var i = 0; while i < k { result = result * 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    else { var i = 0; while i < (0 - k) { result = result / 2.0; i = i + 1 } }
    result
}

fn fa_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64); k = k + 1 }
    2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn fa_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 { term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64; sum = sum + term; n = n + 1 }
    sum
}

fn fa_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    fa_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn fa_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    fa_abs(a - b) < tol
}

fn approx_rel(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let denom = fa_max(fa_abs(a), fa_abs(b))
    if denom < 1.0e-30 { return fa_abs(a - b) < tol }
    fa_abs(a - b) / denom < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// VECTOR / MATRIX HELPERS (row-major flat arrays)
// ============================================================================

fn fa_dot(a: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + a[i] * b[i]; i = i + 1 }
    sum
}

fn fa_norm2(v: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { sum = sum + v[i] * v[i]; i = i + 1 }
    fa_sqrt(sum)
}

fn fa_matvec(A: &[f64; 4096], x: &[f64; 4096], n: i32, out: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + A[i * n + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        out[i] = sum
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn fa_gauss_solve(A: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 4096], n: i32, x: &![f64; 4096]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var work: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let nc = n + 1
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            work[i * nc + j] = A[i * n + j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        work[i * nc + n] = b[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    var col = 0
    while col < n {
        var max_val = fa_abs(work[col * nc + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < n {
            let v = fa_abs(work[row * nc + col])
            if v > max_val { max_val = v; max_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < nc {
                let tmp = work[col * nc + j]
                work[col * nc + j] = work[max_row * nc + j]
                work[max_row * nc + j] = tmp
                j = j + 1
            }
        }
        let pivot = work[col * nc + col]
        if fa_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            x[col] = 0.0
        } else {
            row = col + 1
            while row < n {
                let factor = work[row * nc + col] / pivot
                var j = col
                while j < nc {
                    work[row * nc + j] = work[row * nc + j] - factor * work[col * nc + j]
                    j = j + 1
                }
                row = row + 1
            }
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = work[i * nc + n]
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum - work[i * nc + j] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        let diag = work[i * nc + i]
        if fa_abs(diag) < 1.0e-30 { x[i] = 0.0 }
        else { x[i] = sum / diag }
        i = i - 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// STRUCTS
// ============================================================================

struct OpNormResult {
    norm_1: f64,
    norm_inf: f64,
    norm_fro: f64,
    norm_2: f64,
    spectral_radius: f64,
    condition: f64
}

struct RKHSModel {
    x_train: [f64; 128],
    alpha: [f64; 128],
    n_train: i32,
    length_scale: f64,
    kernel_type: i32
}

// ============================================================================
// OPERATOR NORMS
// ============================================================================

fn op_norm_1(A: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var best = 0.0
    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        var col_sum = 0.0
        var i = 0
        while i < n {
            col_sum = col_sum + fa_abs(A[i * n + j])
            i = i + 1
        }
        if col_sum > best { best = col_sum }
        j = j + 1
    }
    best
}

fn op_norm_inf(A: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var best = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var row_sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            row_sum = row_sum + fa_abs(A[i * n + j])
            j = j + 1
        }
        if row_sum > best { best = row_sum }
        i = i + 1
    }
    best
}

fn op_norm_frobenius(A: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let v = A[i * n + j]
            sum = sum + v * v
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    fa_sqrt(sum)
}

fn op_norm_2(A: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var B: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < n {
                sum = sum + A[k * n + i] * A[k * n + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            B[i * n + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var v: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let inv_sqrtn = 1.0 / fa_sqrt(n as f64)
    i = 0
    while i < n { v[i] = inv_sqrtn; i = i + 1 }

    var w: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var eigenvalue = 0.0

    var iter = 0
    while iter < 500 {
        fa_matvec(&B, &v, n, &!w)
        eigenvalue = fa_dot(&v, &w, n)
        let nrm = fa_norm2(&w, n)
        if nrm < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = w[i] / nrm; i = i + 1 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    if eigenvalue < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    fa_sqrt(eigenvalue)
}

// ============================================================================
// SPECTRAL PROPERTIES
// ============================================================================

fn spectral_radius(A: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var v: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        v[i] = 1.0 / ((i + 1) as f64)
        i = i + 1
    }
    let init_norm = fa_norm2(&v, n)
    if init_norm > 0.0 {
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = v[i] / init_norm; i = i + 1 }
    }

    var w: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var lambda = 0.0

    var iter = 0
    while iter < 500 {
        fa_matvec(A, &v, n, &!w)
        lambda = fa_dot(&v, &w, n)
        let nrm = fa_norm2(&w, n)
        if nrm < 1.0e-30 { return 0.0 }
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = w[i] / nrm; i = i + 1 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    fa_abs(lambda)
}

fn condition_number(A: &[f64; 4096], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var B: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            var sum = 0.0
            var k = 0
            while k < n {
                sum = sum + A[k * n + i] * A[k * n + j]
                k = k + 1
            }
            B[i * n + j] = sum
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Largest eigenvalue via power iteration
    var v: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n { v[i] = 1.0 / ((i + 1) as f64); i = i + 1 }
    let init_n = fa_norm2(&v, n)
    if init_n > 0.0 {
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = v[i] / init_n; i = i + 1 }
    }

    var w: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var lambda_max = 0.0
    var iter = 0
    while iter < 300 {
        fa_matvec(&B, &v, n, &!w)
        lambda_max = fa_dot(&v, &w, n)
        let nrm = fa_norm2(&w, n)
        if nrm < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0e30 }
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = w[i] / nrm; i = i + 1 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Smallest eigenvalue via inverse iteration
    i = 0
    while i < n { v[i] = 1.0 / ((i + 1) as f64); i = i + 1 }
    let init_n2 = fa_norm2(&v, n)
    if init_n2 > 0.0 {
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = v[i] / init_n2; i = i + 1 }
    }

    var lambda_min = lambda_max
    iter = 0
    while iter < 300 {
        fa_gauss_solve(&B, &v, n, &!w)
        let nrm = fa_norm2(&w, n)
        if nrm < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0e30 }
        var bw: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        fa_matvec(&B, &w, n, &!bw)
        let rq = fa_dot(&w, &bw, n) / (nrm * nrm)
        lambda_min = rq
        i = 0
        while i < n { v[i] = w[i] / nrm; i = i + 1 }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    if lambda_min < 1.0e-30 { return 1.0e30 }
    if lambda_max < 0.0 { return 1.0e30 }
    if lambda_min < 0.0 { return 1.0e30 }
    fa_sqrt(lambda_max / lambda_min)
}

// ============================================================================
// FUNCTION SPACE INNER PRODUCTS (via quadrature)
// ============================================================================

fn fa_simpson(vals: &[f64; 4096], a: f64, b: f64, n_quad: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let h = (b - a) / (n_quad as f64)
    var sum = vals[0] + vals[n_quad]
    var i = 1
    while i < n_quad {
        let rem = i - (i / 2) * 2
        if rem == 1 {
            sum = sum + 4.0 * vals[i]
        } else {
            sum = sum + 2.0 * vals[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum * h / 3.0
}

fn l2_inner_product(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    g: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                    a: f64, b: f64, n_quad: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nq = n_quad
    let rem = nq - (nq / 2) * 2
    if rem != 0 { nq = nq + 1 }

    let h = (b - a) / (nq as f64)
    var vals: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]

    var i = 0
    while i <= nq {
        let x = a + (i as f64) * h
        vals[i] = f(x) * g(x)
        i = i + 1
    }

    fa_simpson(&vals, a, b, nq)
}

fn l2_norm(f: fn(f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
           a: f64, b: f64, n_quad: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ip = l2_inner_product(f, f, a, b, n_quad)
    if ip < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    fa_sqrt(ip)
}

// ============================================================================
// RKHS KERNEL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn fa_kernel_rbf(x: f64, y: f64, length_scale: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let d = x - y
    let l2 = length_scale * length_scale
    fa_exp(0.0 - (d * d) / (2.0 * l2))
}

fn fa_kernel_eval(x: f64, y: f64, length_scale: f64, kernel_type: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Only RBF (type 0) used in tests
    fa_kernel_rbf(x, y, length_scale)
}

// ============================================================================
// RKHS KERNEL INTERPOLATION
// ============================================================================

fn rkhs_train(x_train: &[f64; 128], y_train: &[f64; 128], n: i32,
              length_scale: f64, kernel_type: i32, reg: f64,
              model: &!RKHSModel) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        model.x_train[i] = x_train[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    model.n_train = n
    model.length_scale = length_scale
    model.kernel_type = kernel_type

    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            K[i * n + j] = fa_kernel_eval(x_train[i], x_train[j], length_scale, kernel_type)
            j = j + 1
        }
        K[i * n + i] = K[i * n + i] + reg
        i = i + 1
    }

    var rhs: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n { rhs[i] = y_train[i]; i = i + 1 }

    var alpha_buf: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    fa_gauss_solve(&K, &rhs, n, &!alpha_buf)

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        model.alpha[i] = alpha_buf[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn rkhs_eval(model: &RKHSModel, x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < model.n_train {
        let kval = fa_kernel_eval(x, model.x_train[i], model.length_scale, model.kernel_type)
        sum = sum + model.alpha[i] * kval
        i = i + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn rkhs_norm(model: &RKHSModel) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < model.n_train {
        var j = 0
        while j < model.n_train {
            let kval = fa_kernel_eval(model.x_train[i], model.x_train[j],
                                      model.length_scale, model.kernel_type)
            sum = sum + model.alpha[i] * kval * model.alpha[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    if sum < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    fa_sqrt(sum)
}

// ============================================================================
// COMPACT OPERATOR SPECTRUM
// ============================================================================

fn compact_op_spectrum(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                       a: f64, b: f64, n_quad: i32, n_eig: i32,
                       eigenvalues: &![f64; 64]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nq = n_quad
    let rem = nq - (nq / 2) * 2
    if rem != 0 { nq = nq + 1 }

    let h = (b - a) / (nq as f64)

    var nodes: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i <= nq {
        nodes[i] = a + (i as f64) * h
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nn = nq + 1

    var weights: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    weights[0] = h / 3.0
    weights[nq] = h / 3.0
    i = 1
    while i < nq {
        let r2 = i - (i / 2) * 2
        if r2 == 1 {
            weights[i] = 4.0 * h / 3.0
        } else {
            weights[i] = 2.0 * h / 3.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var mat_n = nn
    if mat_n > 64 { mat_n = 64 }

    var M: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < mat_n {
        var j = 0
        while j < mat_n {
            M[i * mat_n + j] = weights[j] * K(nodes[i], nodes[j])
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var ne = n_eig
    if ne > mat_n { ne = mat_n }
    if ne > 64 { ne = 64 }

    var eig_idx = 0
    while eig_idx < ne {
        var v: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        i = 0
        while i < mat_n { v[i] = 1.0 / ((i + 1) as f64); i = i + 1 }
        let v_norm_init = fa_norm2(&v, mat_n)
        if v_norm_init > 0.0 {
            i = 0
            while i < mat_n { v[i] = v[i] / v_norm_init; i = i + 1 }
        }

        var w: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
        var eigenvalue = 0.0
        var prev_eigenvalue = 0.0

        var iter = 0
        while iter < 500 {
            fa_matvec(&M, &v, mat_n, &!w)
            eigenvalue = fa_dot(&v, &w, mat_n)
            let nrm = fa_norm2(&w, mat_n)
            if nrm < 1.0e-30 {
                eigenvalue = 0.0
                i = 0
                while i < mat_n { v[i] = 0.0; i = i + 1 }
                iter = 500
            } else {
                i = 0
                while i < mat_n { v[i] = w[i] / nrm; i = i + 1 }
                if iter > 0 {
                    if fa_abs(eigenvalue - prev_eigenvalue) < 1.0e-12 * fa_abs(eigenvalue) + 1.0e-30 {
                        iter = 500
                    }
                }
                prev_eigenvalue = eigenvalue
            }
            iter = iter + 1
        }

        eigenvalues[eig_idx] = eigenvalue

        i = 0
        while i < mat_n {
            var j = 0
            while j < mat_n {
                M[i * mat_n + j] = M[i * mat_n + j] - eigenvalue * v[i] * v[j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        eig_idx = eig_idx + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// FREDHOLM ALTERNATIVE
// ============================================================================

fn fredholm_alternative(K: fn(f64, f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic,
                        a: f64, b: f64, lambda: f64,
                        n_quad: i32) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var nq = n_quad
    let rem = nq - (nq / 2) * 2
    if rem != 0 { nq = nq + 1 }

    let h = (b - a) / (nq as f64)

    var nodes: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    var i = 0
    while i <= nq {
        nodes[i] = a + (i as f64) * h
        i = i + 1
    }
    let nn = nq + 1

    var weights: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    weights[0] = h / 3.0
    weights[nq] = h / 3.0
    i = 1
    while i < nq {
        let r2 = i - (i / 2) * 2
        if r2 == 1 {
            weights[i] = 4.0 * h / 3.0
        } else {
            weights[i] = 2.0 * h / 3.0
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var mat_n = nn
    if mat_n > 64 { mat_n = 64 }

    var A: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < mat_n {
        var j = 0
        while j < mat_n {
            let m_ij = weights[j] * K(nodes[i], nodes[j])
            A[i * mat_n + j] = 0.0 - lambda * m_ij
            j = j + 1
        }
        A[i * mat_n + i] = A[i * mat_n + i] + 1.0
        i = i + 1
    }

    var det_sign = 1.0
    var log_det = 0.0

    var col = 0
    while col < mat_n {
        var max_val = fa_abs(A[col * mat_n + col])
        var max_row = col
        var row = col + 1
        while row < mat_n {
            let v = fa_abs(A[row * mat_n + col])
            if v > max_val { max_val = v; max_row = row }
            row = row + 1
        }
        if max_row != col {
            var j = 0
            while j < mat_n {
                let tmp = A[col * mat_n + j]
                A[col * mat_n + j] = A[max_row * mat_n + j]
                A[max_row * mat_n + j] = tmp
                j = j + 1
            }
            det_sign = 0.0 - det_sign
        }
        let pivot = A[col * mat_n + col]
        if fa_abs(pivot) < 1.0e-30 {
            return false
        }
        if pivot < 0.0 { det_sign = 0.0 - det_sign }
        log_det = log_det + fa_ln(fa_abs(pivot))
        row = col + 1
        while row < mat_n {
            let factor = A[row * mat_n + col] / pivot
            var j = col + 1
            while j < mat_n {
                A[row * mat_n + j] = A[row * mat_n + j] - factor * A[col * mat_n + j]
                j = j + 1
            }
            A[row * mat_n + col] = 0.0
            row = row + 1
        }
        col = col + 1
    }

    let det_threshold = (mat_n as f64) * fa_ln(10.0) * (0.0 - 10.0)
    if log_det < det_threshold {
        return false
    }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST HELPER FUNCTIONS (used as function pointers)
// ============================================================================

fn fn_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    fa_sin(x)
}

fn fn_const_one(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    1.0
}

fn kernel_xt(x: f64, t: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    x * t
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 1: Identity matrix norms
// ||I||_1 = 1, ||I||_inf = 1, ||I||_F = sqrt(n), ||I||_2 = 1
// ============================================================================

fn test_identity_norms() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 3
    var I: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    I[0] = 1.0    // (0,0)
    I[4] = 1.0    // (1,1)
    I[8] = 1.0    // (2,2)

    let n1 = op_norm_1(&I, n)
    let ni = op_norm_inf(&I, n)
    let nf = op_norm_frobenius(&I, n)
    let n2 = op_norm_2(&I, n)

    let expected_fro = fa_sqrt(3.0)

    let ok_1 = approx_eq(n1, 1.0, 1.0e-6)
    let ok_inf = approx_eq(ni, 1.0, 1.0e-6)
    let ok_fro = approx_eq(nf, expected_fro, 1.0e-6)
    let ok_2 = approx_eq(n2, 1.0, 1.0e-6)
    ok_1 && ok_inf && ok_fro && ok_2
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 2: Norm inequality ||A||_F >= ||A||_2
// ============================================================================

fn test_norm_inequality() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 3
    // A = [[2, 1, 0], [1, 3, 1], [0, 1, 2]]
    var A: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    A[0] = 2.0; A[1] = 1.0; A[2] = 0.0
    A[3] = 1.0; A[4] = 3.0; A[5] = 1.0
    A[6] = 0.0; A[7] = 1.0; A[8] = 2.0

    let nf = op_norm_frobenius(&A, n)
    let n2 = op_norm_2(&A, n)

    // Frobenius norm must be >= spectral norm
    nf >= n2 - 1.0e-10
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 3: Frobenius norm of known matrix
// A = [[1,2],[3,4]] -> ||A||_F = sqrt(1+4+9+16) = sqrt(30)
// ============================================================================

fn test_frobenius_known() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 2
    var A: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    A[0] = 1.0; A[1] = 2.0
    A[2] = 3.0; A[3] = 4.0

    let nf = op_norm_frobenius(&A, n)
    let expected = fa_sqrt(30.0)
    approx_eq(nf, expected, 1.0e-6)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 4: Spectral radius of diagonal matrix
// diag(1, 3, 2) -> spectral_radius = 3
// ============================================================================

fn test_spectral_radius_diag() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 3
    var D: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    D[0] = 1.0    // (0,0)
    D[4] = 3.0    // (1,1)
    D[8] = 2.0    // (2,2)

    let rho = spectral_radius(&D, n)
    approx_eq(rho, 3.0, 1.0e-4)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 5: Condition number of identity = 1
// ============================================================================

fn test_condition_identity() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 3
    var I: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    I[0] = 1.0
    I[4] = 1.0
    I[8] = 1.0

    let kappa = condition_number(&I, n)
    approx_eq(kappa, 1.0, 1.0e-4)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 6: Condition number of ill-conditioned matrix >> 1
// diag(1, 1000) -> kappa = 1000
// ============================================================================

fn test_condition_ill() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = 2
    var A: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    A[0] = 1.0      // (0,0)
    A[3] = 1000.0    // (1,1)

    let kappa = condition_number(&A, n)
    // Should be close to 1000
    approx_rel(kappa, 1000.0, 1.0e-2)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 7: L2 inner product <sin, sin> on [0, pi] = pi/2
// ============================================================================

fn test_l2_inner_product_sin() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let pi = fa_pi()
    let ip = l2_inner_product(fn_sin, fn_sin, 0.0, pi, 200)
    let expected = pi / 2.0
    approx_eq(ip, expected, 1.0e-4)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 8: L2 norm of constant function ||1||_2 on [0,1] = 1
// integral_0^1 1^2 dx = 1, so ||1||_2 = sqrt(1) = 1
// ============================================================================

fn test_l2_norm_constant() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let nm = l2_norm(fn_const_one, 0.0, 1.0, 200)
    approx_eq(nm, 1.0, 1.0e-4)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 9: RKHS interpolation exact at training points
// f(x_i) should equal y_i for each training point
// ============================================================================

fn test_rkhs_interp_exact() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x_train: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var y_train: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    x_train[0] = 0.0; y_train[0] = 1.0
    x_train[1] = 0.5; y_train[1] = 2.0
    x_train[2] = 1.0; y_train[2] = 0.5
    x_train[3] = 1.5; y_train[3] = 3.0
    let n_pts = 4

    var model: RKHSModel = RKHSModel {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        alpha: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        length_scale: 0.0,
        kernel_type: 0
    }
    rkhs_train(&x_train, &y_train, n_pts, 1.0, 0, 1.0e-10, &!model)

    // Evaluate at each training point
    let e0 = fa_abs(rkhs_eval(&model, 0.0) - 1.0)
    let e1 = fa_abs(rkhs_eval(&model, 0.5) - 2.0)
    let e2 = fa_abs(rkhs_eval(&model, 1.0) - 0.5)
    let e3 = fa_abs(rkhs_eval(&model, 1.5) - 3.0)

    let ok0 = e0 < 1.0e-4
    let ok1 = e1 < 1.0e-4
    let ok2 = e2 < 1.0e-4
    let ok3 = e3 < 1.0e-4
    ok0 && ok1 && ok2 && ok3
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 10: RKHS norm non-negative
// ||f||_H >= 0 for any interpolant
// ============================================================================

fn test_rkhs_norm_nonneg() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var x_train: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var y_train: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    x_train[0] = 0.0; y_train[0] = 1.0
    x_train[1] = 1.0; y_train[1] = 0.0 - 1.0
    x_train[2] = 2.0; y_train[2] = 0.5
    let n_pts = 3

    var model: RKHSModel = RKHSModel {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        alpha: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        length_scale: 0.0,
        kernel_type: 0
    }
    rkhs_train(&x_train, &y_train, n_pts, 1.0, 0, 1.0e-10, &!model)

    let nm = rkhs_norm(&model)
    nm >= 0.0 - 1.0e-10
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 11: Compact operator dominant eigenvalue
// K(x,t) = x*t on [0,1] -> lambda_1 = 1/3
// (since integral_0^1 x*t*f(t)dt with f(t)=t gives x*1/3, eigenvalue = 1/3)
// ============================================================================

fn test_compact_dominant_eigenvalue() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var eigenvalues: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    compact_op_spectrum(kernel_xt, 0.0, 1.0, 60, 2, &!eigenvalues)

    let lambda1 = eigenvalues[0]
    let expected = 1.0 / 3.0
    approx_eq(lambda1, expected, 1.0e-4)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 12: Fredholm alternative
// For K(x,t) = x*t on [0,1], eigenvalue is 1/3 so lambda=3 is the
// reciprocal eigenvalue. lambda=2 is NOT an eigenvalue, so the
// Fredholm alternative guarantees a unique solution.
// ============================================================================

fn test_fredholm_alternative() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // lambda=2 is not an eigenvalue of K(x,t)=x*t -> should return true
    let not_eig = fredholm_alternative(kernel_xt, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 60)

    // lambda=3 IS the reciprocal of eigenvalue 1/3 -> should return false
    let is_eig = fredholm_alternative(kernel_xt, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0, 60)

    not_eig && !is_eig
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN TEST RUNNER
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Functional Analysis Test Suite ===")
    println("")

    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0

    // Test 1
    print("Test  1: Identity matrix norms ... ")
    if test_identity_norms() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 2
    print("Test  2: Norm inequality ||A||_F >= ||A||_2 ... ")
    if test_norm_inequality() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 3
    print("Test  3: Frobenius norm of [[1,2],[3,4]] ... ")
    if test_frobenius_known() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 4
    print("Test  4: Spectral radius of diag(1,3,2) ... ")
    if test_spectral_radius_diag() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 5
    print("Test  5: Condition number of identity ... ")
    if test_condition_identity() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 6
    print("Test  6: Condition number ill-conditioned ... ")
    if test_condition_ill() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 7
    print("Test  7: L2 inner product <sin,sin> = pi/2 ... ")
    if test_l2_inner_product_sin() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 8
    print("Test  8: L2 norm of constant ||1|| = 1 ... ")
    if test_l2_norm_constant() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 9
    print("Test  9: RKHS interpolation exact at points ... ")
    if test_rkhs_interp_exact() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 10
    print("Test 10: RKHS norm non-negative ... ")
    if test_rkhs_norm_nonneg() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 11
    print("Test 11: Compact op eigenvalue K=x*t, l1=1/3 ... ")
    if test_compact_dominant_eigenvalue() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 12
    print("Test 12: Fredholm alternative detection ... ")
    if test_fredholm_alternative() {
        println("PASS")
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        println("FAIL")
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    println("")
    print("Passed: "); println(pass as string)
    print("Failed: "); println(fail as string)
    println("")
    if fail == 0 {
        println("ALL 12 TESTS PASSED")
        return 0
    } else {
        println("SOME TESTS FAILED")
        return 1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/run-pass/test_gp.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ ignore BLOCKED: pinned binary borrow checker false positive
//@ expect-stdout: ALL 12 TESTS PASSED
//@ expect-stdout: Failed: 0
// test_gp.sio — Tests for Gaussian process regression module
//
// Self-contained test suite for kernels (RBF, Matern 3/2, periodic),
// Cholesky factorization/solve, GP train/predict, log marginal likelihood,
// and posterior variance behaviour. All helpers inlined since tests cannot import.
//
// References:
//   Rasmussen & Williams (2006): "Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning"
//   Bishop (2006): "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning" Ch. 6

// ============================================================================
// PURE MATH HELPERS (must precede callers)
// ============================================================================

fn gp_h_abs(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }
fn gp_h_max(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn gp_h_min(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }

fn gp_h_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 25 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    y
}

fn gp_h_exp(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    let inv_ln2 = 1.4426950408889634

    if x > 709.0 { return 1.0e308 }
    if x < -709.0 { return 0.0 }

    var k_f = x * inv_ln2
    var k: i64 = 0
    if k_f >= 0.0 { k = (k_f + 0.5) as i64 } else { k = (k_f - 0.5) as i64 }

    let r = x - (k as f64) * ln2

    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n <= 20 {
        term = term * r / (n as f64)
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }

    var result = sum
    var kabs = k
    if kabs < 0 { kabs = 0 - kabs }
    var pow2 = 2.0
    var ka = kabs
    var acc = 1.0
    while ka > 0 {
        if ka - (ka / 2) * 2 != 0 { acc = acc * pow2 }
        pow2 = pow2 * pow2
        ka = ka / 2
    }
    if k >= 0 { result = result * acc } else { result = result / acc }
    result
}

fn gp_h_ln(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return -1.0e30 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }

    var y = 0.0
    var a = x
    let ln2 = 0.6931471805599453
    while a > 2.0 { a = a * 0.5; y = y + ln2 }
    while a < 0.5 { a = a * 2.0; y = y - ln2 }

    let t = (a - 1.0) / (a + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var power = t
    var n = 1
    while n <= 30 {
        power = power * t2
        sum = sum + power / (2.0 * (n as f64) + 1.0)
        n = n + 1
    }
    y + 2.0 * sum
}

fn gp_h_sin(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var a = x
    let tp = 6.28318530717958647692
    while a >= tp { a = a - tp }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + tp }
    if a > 3.14159265358979323846 { a = a - tp }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = a
    var term = a
    var n = 1
    while n < 18 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n) * (2 * n + 1)) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    sum
}

fn gp_h_cos(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    gp_h_sin(x + 1.57079632679489661923)
}

fn gp_h_pi() -> f64 { 3.14159265358979323846 }

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    gp_h_abs(a - b) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// STRUCTS
// ============================================================================

struct GPData {
    x_train: [f64; 128],
    y_train: [f64; 128],
    n_train: i32,
    noise_var: f64
}

struct GPHyper {
    signal_var: f64,
    length_scale: f64,
    noise_var: f64,
    kernel_type: i32,
    extra_param: f64
}

struct GPModel {
    L: [f64; 4096],
    alpha: [f64; 128],
    x_train: [f64; 128],
    y_train: [f64; 128],
    n_train: i32,
    hyper: GPHyper,
    log_ml: f64
}

struct GPPrediction {
    mean: f64,
    variance: f64,
    std_dev: f64
}

// ============================================================================
// KERNEL FUNCTIONS
// ============================================================================

fn kernel_rbf(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let d = x - y
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    hyper.signal_var * gp_h_exp(0.0 - 0.5 * d * d / (l * l))
}

fn kernel_matern32(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = gp_h_abs(x - y)
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let sqrt3 = 1.7320508075688772
    let z = sqrt3 * r / l
    hyper.signal_var * (1.0 + z) * gp_h_exp(0.0 - z)
}

fn kernel_matern52(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = gp_h_abs(x - y)
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let sqrt5 = 2.2360679774997896
    let z = sqrt5 * r / l
    let z2 = 5.0 * r * r / (3.0 * l * l)
    hyper.signal_var * (1.0 + z + z2) * gp_h_exp(0.0 - z)
}

fn kernel_periodic(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let r = gp_h_abs(x - y)
    let l = hyper.length_scale
    let p = hyper.extra_param
    let s = gp_h_sin(gp_h_pi() * r / p)
    hyper.signal_var * gp_h_exp(0.0 - 2.0 * s * s / (l * l))
}

fn kernel_eval(x: f64, y: f64, hyper: &GPHyper) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if hyper.kernel_type == 0 { return kernel_rbf(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 1 { return kernel_matern32(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 2 { return kernel_matern52(x, y, hyper) }
    if hyper.kernel_type == 3 { return kernel_periodic(x, y, hyper) }
    kernel_rbf(x, y, hyper)
}

// ============================================================================
// CHOLESKY FACTORIZATION AND SOLVE
// ============================================================================

fn gp_cholesky(K: &[f64; 4096], n: i32, L: &![f64; 4096]) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var idx = 0
    while idx < n * n { L[idx] = 0.0; idx = idx + 1 }

    var j = 0
    while j < n {
        var sum_diag = 0.0
        var k = 0
        while k < j {
            let ljk = L[j * n + k]
            sum_diag = sum_diag + ljk * ljk
            k = k + 1
        }
        let diag_val = K[j * n + j] - sum_diag
        if diag_val <= 0.0 { return false }
        L[j * n + j] = gp_h_sqrt(diag_val)

        var i = j + 1
        while i < n {
            var sum_off = 0.0
            k = 0
            while k < j {
                sum_off = sum_off + L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k]
                k = k + 1
            }
            L[i * n + j] = (K[i * n + j] - sum_off) / L[j * n + j]
            i = i + 1
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    true
}

fn gp_cholesky_solve(L: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 128], n: i32, x: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var z: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + L[i * n + j] * z[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        z[i] = (b[i] - sum) / L[i * n + i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    i = n - 1
    while i >= 0 {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = i + 1
        while j < n {
            sum = sum + L[j * n + i] * x[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        x[i] = (z[i] - sum) / L[i * n + i]
        i = i - 1
    }
}

fn gp_forward_solve(L: &[f64; 4096], b: &[f64; 128], n: i32, v: &![f64; 128]) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        var sum = 0.0
        var j = 0
        while j < i {
            sum = sum + L[i * n + j] * v[j]
            j = j + 1
        }
        v[i] = (b[i] - sum) / L[i * n + i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// GP TRAINING
// ============================================================================

fn gp_train(data: &GPData, hyper: &GPHyper, model: &!GPModel) -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = data.n_train

    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        model.x_train[i] = data.x_train[i]
        model.y_train[i] = data.y_train[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    model.n_train = n
    model.hyper.signal_var = hyper.signal_var
    model.hyper.length_scale = hyper.length_scale
    model.hyper.noise_var = hyper.noise_var
    model.hyper.kernel_type = hyper.kernel_type
    model.hyper.extra_param = hyper.extra_param

    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        var j = 0
        while j < n {
            let kval = kernel_eval(data.x_train[i], data.x_train[j], hyper)
            if i == j {
                K[i * n + j] = kval + hyper.noise_var
            } else {
                K[i * n + j] = kval
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    let ok = gp_cholesky(&K, n, &!model.L)
    if !ok { return false }

    gp_cholesky_solve(&model.L, &data.y_train, n, &!model.alpha)

    var data_fit = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        data_fit = data_fit + data.y_train[i] * model.alpha[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    data_fit = 0.0 - 0.5 * data_fit

    var complexity = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        complexity = complexity + gp_h_ln(model.L[i * n + i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    complexity = 0.0 - complexity

    let norm_const = 0.0 - 0.5 * (n as f64) * gp_h_ln(2.0 * gp_h_pi())

    model.log_ml = data_fit + complexity + norm_const
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// GP PREDICTION
// ============================================================================

fn gp_predict(model: &GPModel, x_star: f64, pred: &!GPPrediction) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let n = model.n_train

    var k_star: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        k_star[i] = kernel_eval(x_star, model.x_train[i], &model.hyper)
        i = i + 1
    }

    var mean = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        mean = mean + k_star[i] * model.alpha[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    pred.mean = mean

    var v: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    gp_forward_solve(&model.L, &k_star, n, &!v)

    let k_ss = kernel_eval(x_star, x_star, &model.hyper)
    var v_dot_v = 0.0
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        v_dot_v = v_dot_v + v[i] * v[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    var variance = k_ss - v_dot_v
    if variance < 0.0 { variance = 0.0 }
    pred.variance = variance
    pred.std_dev = gp_h_sqrt(variance)
}

fn gp_log_marginal(model: &GPModel) -> f64 {
    model.log_ml
}

// ============================================================================
// HELPER: build training data from x^2 (5 points)
// ============================================================================

fn build_quad_data(data: &!GPData) with Mut, Panic {
    // 5 training points: x in {0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}, y = x^2
    data.n_train = 5
    data.noise_var = 0.01

    data.x_train[0] = 0.0
    data.x_train[1] = 1.0
    data.x_train[2] = 2.0
    data.x_train[3] = 3.0
    data.x_train[4] = 4.0

    data.y_train[0] = 0.0
    data.y_train[1] = 1.0
    data.y_train[2] = 4.0
    data.y_train[3] = 9.0
    data.y_train[4] = 16.0
}

fn make_rbf_hyper() -> GPHyper {
    GPHyper {
        signal_var: 1.0,
        length_scale: 1.0,
        noise_var: 0.01,
        kernel_type: 0,
        extra_param: 0.0
    }
}

fn make_zero_model() -> GPModel {
    GPModel {
        L: [0.0; 4096],
        alpha: [0.0; 128],
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        y_train: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        hyper: GPHyper {
            signal_var: 0.0,
            length_scale: 0.0,
            noise_var: 0.0,
            kernel_type: 0,
            extra_param: 0.0
        },
        log_ml: 0.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 1: RBF kernel at same point = signal_var
// ============================================================================

fn test_rbf_same_point() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    let val = kernel_rbf(2.5, 2.5, &hyper)
    // k(x,x) = signal_var * exp(0) = signal_var = 1.0
    approx_eq(val, 1.0, 1.0e-6)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 2: RBF kernel symmetry k(x,y) = k(y,x)
// ============================================================================

fn test_rbf_symmetry() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    let k_xy = kernel_rbf(1.0, 3.0, &hyper)
    let k_yx = kernel_rbf(3.0, 1.0, &hyper)
    approx_eq(k_xy, k_yx, 1.0e-12)
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 3: RBF kernel decays with distance
// ============================================================================

fn test_rbf_decay() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    let k_self = kernel_rbf(2.0, 2.0, &hyper)
    let k_near = kernel_rbf(2.0, 2.5, &hyper)
    let k_far = kernel_rbf(2.0, 5.0, &hyper)
    // k(x,x) > k(x,x+0.5) > k(x,x+3)
    if k_self <= k_near { return false }
    if k_near <= k_far { return false }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 4: Cholesky of known SPD matrix [[4,2],[2,3]]
// ============================================================================

fn test_cholesky_known() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // K = [[4,2],[2,3]]
    // Expected L = [[2,0],[1,sqrt(2)]]
    // L * L^T should reconstruct K
    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    K[0] = 4.0
    K[1] = 2.0
    K[2] = 2.0
    K[3] = 3.0

    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let ok = gp_cholesky(&K, 2, &!L)
    if !ok { return false }

    // Verify L[0,0] = 2.0
    if !approx_eq(L[0], 2.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }
    // Verify L[1,0] = 1.0
    if !approx_eq(L[2], 1.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }
    // Verify L[1,1] = sqrt(2) ~ 1.41421
    if !approx_eq(L[3], 1.41421356237, 1.0e-4) { return false }
    // Verify L[0,1] = 0.0 (upper triangle is zero)
    if !approx_eq(L[1], 0.0, 1.0e-12) { return false }

    // Roundtrip: L * L^T should give back K
    // (L*L^T)[0,0] = L[0,0]^2 = 4.0
    let r00 = L[0] * L[0]
    if !approx_eq(r00, 4.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }
    // (L*L^T)[1,0] = L[1,0]*L[0,0] = 1*2 = 2
    let r10 = L[2] * L[0]
    if !approx_eq(r10, 2.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }
    // (L*L^T)[1,1] = L[1,0]^2 + L[1,1]^2 = 1 + 2 = 3
    let r11 = L[2] * L[2] + L[3] * L[3]
    if !approx_eq(r11, 3.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }

    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 5: Cholesky solve accuracy: K*x = b, verify residual is small
// ============================================================================

fn test_cholesky_solve() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // 3x3 SPD matrix: K = [[10,2,1],[2,8,3],[1,3,6]]
    var K: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    K[0] = 10.0; K[1] = 2.0; K[2] = 1.0
    K[3] = 2.0;  K[4] = 8.0; K[5] = 3.0
    K[6] = 1.0;  K[7] = 3.0; K[8] = 6.0

    var L: [f64; 4096] = [0.0; 4096]
    let ok = gp_cholesky(&K, 3, &!L)
    if !ok { return false }

    // b = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
    var b: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    b[0] = 1.0; b[1] = 2.0; b[2] = 3.0

    var x_sol: [f64; 128] = [0.0; 128]
    gp_cholesky_solve(&L, &b, 3, &!x_sol)

    // Compute residual: r = K*x - b
    // r[0] = 10*x[0] + 2*x[1] + 1*x[2] - 1
    let r0 = 10.0 * x_sol[0] + 2.0 * x_sol[1] + 1.0 * x_sol[2] - b[0]
    let r1 = 2.0 * x_sol[0] + 8.0 * x_sol[1] + 3.0 * x_sol[2] - b[1]
    let r2 = 1.0 * x_sol[0] + 3.0 * x_sol[1] + 6.0 * x_sol[2] - b[2]

    let residual = gp_h_sqrt(r0 * r0 + r1 * r1 + r2 * r2)
    residual < 1.0e-6
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 6: GP predict at training points: mean ~ y_train
// ============================================================================

fn test_gp_predict_at_train() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: GPData = GPData {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        y_train: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        noise_var: 0.01
    }
    build_quad_data(&!data)

    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    var model = make_zero_model()

    let ok = gp_train(&data, &hyper, &!model)
    if !ok { return false }

    // Predict at each training point: mean should be close to y_train
    var max_err = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 5 {
        var pred: GPPrediction = GPPrediction { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 }
        gp_predict(&model, data.x_train[i], &!pred)
        let err = gp_h_abs(pred.mean - data.y_train[i])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // With noise_var=0.01, predictions should be within ~0.5 of training values
    max_err < 1.0e-1
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 7: GP variance at training points is small
// ============================================================================

fn test_gp_variance_at_train() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: GPData = GPData {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        y_train: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        noise_var: 0.01
    }
    build_quad_data(&!data)

    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    var model = make_zero_model()

    let ok = gp_train(&data, &hyper, &!model)
    if !ok { return false }

    // Variance at training points should be near noise_var (0.01)
    var all_small = true
    var i = 0
    while i < 5 {
        var pred: GPPrediction = GPPrediction { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 }
        gp_predict(&model, data.x_train[i], &!pred)
        // Posterior variance at training point should be <= noise_var
        if pred.variance > 0.1 { all_small = false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    all_small
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 8: GP variance increases away from training data
// ============================================================================

fn test_gp_variance_away() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: GPData = GPData {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        y_train: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        noise_var: 0.01
    }
    build_quad_data(&!data)

    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    var model = make_zero_model()

    let ok = gp_train(&data, &hyper, &!model)
    if !ok { return false }

    // Variance at training point x=2.0
    var pred_near: GPPrediction = GPPrediction { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 }
    gp_predict(&model, 2.0, &!pred_near)

    // Variance far from training data at x=10.0
    var pred_far: GPPrediction = GPPrediction { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 }
    gp_predict(&model, 10.0, &!pred_far)

    // Variance far away should be larger than at training point
    pred_far.variance > pred_near.variance
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 9: GP log marginal likelihood is finite (not NaN or inf)
// ============================================================================

fn test_gp_log_ml_finite() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var data: GPData = GPData {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        y_train: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        noise_var: 0.01
    }
    build_quad_data(&!data)

    let hyper = make_rbf_hyper()
    var model = make_zero_model()

    let ok = gp_train(&data, &hyper, &!model)
    if !ok { return false }

    let lml = gp_log_marginal(&model)
    // Should be a finite, reasonable number (not extremely large magnitude)
    // A valid log ML for 5 points is typically in range [-100, 100]
    if lml > 1.0e30 { return false }
    if lml < -1.0e30 { return false }
    // Check it is not zero (which would be suspicious for non-trivial data)
    if gp_h_abs(lml) < 1.0e-20 { return false }
    true
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 10: GP posterior mean interpolates when noise -> 0
// ============================================================================

fn test_gp_interpolation() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Use very small noise so predictions should closely match training values
    var data: GPData = GPData {
        x_train: [0.0; 128],
        y_train: [0.0; 128],
        n_train: 0,
        noise_var: 1.0e-6
    }
    // 4 training points: simple linear function y = 2*x + 1
    data.n_train = 4
    data.x_train[0] = 0.0; data.y_train[0] = 1.0
    data.x_train[1] = 1.0; data.y_train[1] = 3.0
    data.x_train[2] = 2.0; data.y_train[2] = 5.0
    data.x_train[3] = 3.0; data.y_train[3] = 7.0

    var hyper: GPHyper = GPHyper {
        signal_var: 10.0,
        length_scale: 2.0,
        noise_var: 1.0e-6,
        kernel_type: 0,
        extra_param: 0.0
    }

    var model = make_zero_model()
    let ok = gp_train(&data, &hyper, &!model)
    if !ok { return false }

    // Predictions at training points should almost exactly match
    var max_err = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < 4 {
        var pred: GPPrediction = GPPrediction { mean: 0.0, variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 }
        gp_predict(&model, data.x_train[i], &!pred)
        let err = gp_h_abs(pred.mean - data.y_train[i])
        if err > max_err { max_err = err }
        i = i + 1
    }
    // With noise_var = 1e-6, interpolation error should be tiny
    max_err < 1.0e-3
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 11: Matern 3/2 kernel is positive for all inputs
// ============================================================================

fn test_matern32_positive() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var hyper: GPHyper = GPHyper {
        signal_var: 2.0,
        length_scale: 1.5,
        noise_var: 0.01,
        kernel_type: 1,
        extra_param: 0.0
    }

    // Test a range of point pairs
    var all_pos = true
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        let x = (i as f64) * 0.7
        var j = 0
        while j < 10 {
            let y = (j as f64) * 0.7
            let kval = kernel_matern32(x, y, &hyper)
            if kval <= 0.0 { all_pos = false }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    all_pos
}

// ============================================================================
// TEST 12: Periodic kernel: k(x, x+period) ~ k(x, x)
// ============================================================================

fn test_periodic_kernel() -> bool with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let period = 2.0
    var hyper: GPHyper = GPHyper {
        signal_var: 1.0,
        length_scale: 1.0,
        noise_var: 0.01,
        kernel_type: 3,
        extra_param: period
    }

    // k(x, x) = signal_var (distance 0)
    let k_self = kernel_periodic(1.0, 1.0, &hyper)

    // k(x, x + period) should be approximately k(x, x)
    // since the periodic kernel has period p, sin(pi * p / p) = sin(pi) = 0
    let k_period = kernel_periodic(1.0, 1.0 + period, &hyper)

    // Both should be approximately signal_var = 1.0
    if !approx_eq(k_self, 1.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }
    if !approx_eq(k_period, 1.0, 1.0e-6) { return false }

    // Also verify that at half-period it is NOT equal to k(x,x) (it should be smaller)
    let k_half = kernel_periodic(1.0, 1.0 + period * 0.5, &hyper)
    if k_half >= k_self { return false }

    true
}
