//@ run-pass
//@ description: epistemic causal inference tests
use epistemic::stats::*
use epistemic::causal::*
/// Test suite for epistemic::causal module
///
/// Demonstrates causal inference with epistemic uncertainty

fn test_simple_confounding() -> i64 {
    println("Test 1: Simple Confounding Adjustment")
    println("======================================")

    // Create DAG: Z -> X -> Y, Z -> Y
    // Z is a confounder of X and Y
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Z", NodeType::Confounder)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)

    // Z -> X: confounder affects treatment
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "Z", "X", beta_new(8.0, 2.0), 0.5, 0.1)

    // Z -> Y: confounder affects outcome
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "Z", "Y", beta_new(7.0, 3.0), 0.4, 0.08)

    // X -> Y: causal effect of interest
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_new(6.0, 4.0), 0.3, 0.12)

    // Find backdoor adjustment set
    let adjustment = backdoor_adjustment(dag, "X", "Y")
    print("  Adjustment set size: ")
    println(len(adjustment))

    if len(adjustment) == 1 {
        print("  ✓ Correctly identified confounder Z")
    } else {
        print("  ✗ Expected 1 confounder, found ")
        println(len(adjustment))
    }
    println("")

    // Estimate ATE
    let ate = average_treatment_effect(dag, "X", "Y")
    print("  ATE mean: ")
    println(ate.mean)
    print("  ATE variance: ")
    println(ate.variance)
    println("")

    return 0
}

fn test_frontdoor_criterion() -> i64 {
    println("Test 2: Frontdoor Criterion (Mediation)")
    println("========================================")

    // Create DAG: X -> M -> Y with U -> X, U -> Y (unmeasured)
    // M is a mediator on the path from X to Y
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "M", NodeType::Mediator)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)

    // X -> M: treatment affects mediator
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "M", beta_new(9.0, 1.0), 0.6, 0.04)

    // M -> Y: mediator affects outcome
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "M", "Y", beta_new(8.0, 2.0), 0.5, 0.06)

    // X -> Y: direct effect (optional)
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_new(5.0, 5.0), 0.2, 0.15)

    // Mediation analysis
    let nde = natural_direct_effect(dag, "X", "M", "Y")
    let nie = natural_indirect_effect(dag, "X", "M", "Y")
    let prop_med = proportion_mediated(dag, "X", "M", "Y")

    print("  Natural Direct Effect (NDE): ")
    println(nde.mean)
    print("  Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): ")
    println(nie.mean)
    print("  Proportion Mediated: ")
    println(prop_med)

    if prop_med > 0.5 {
        println("  ✓ Most effect goes through mediator")
    } else {
        println("  ✓ Direct effect dominates")
    }
    println("")

    return 0
}

fn test_instrumental_variable() -> i64 {
    println("Test 3: Instrumental Variable Estimation")
    println("==========================================")

    // Create DAG: Z -> X -> Y with U -> X, U -> Y (unmeasured)
    // Z is an instrumental variable
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Z", NodeType::Instrument)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)

    // Z -> X: instrument affects treatment (relevance)
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "Z", "X", beta_new(9.0, 1.0), 0.7, 0.03)

    // X -> Y: causal effect
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_new(7.0, 3.0), 0.4, 0.08)

    // No Z -> Y edge (exclusion restriction holds)

    // IV estimation
    let iv_est = iv_estimate(dag, "Z", "X", "Y")

    print("  IV Estimate mean: ")
    println(iv_est.mean)
    print("  IV Estimate variance: ")
    println(iv_est.variance)

    if iv_est.variance < 0.05 {
        println("  ✓ Strong instrument (low variance)")
    } else {
        println("  ✓ Weak instrument (high variance)")
    }
    println("")

    return 0
}

fn test_effect_heterogeneity() -> i64 {
    println("Test 4: Effect Heterogeneity (CATE)")
    println("====================================")

    // Create DAG: X -> Y with W as effect modifier
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "W", NodeType::Confounder)  // Actually a moderator

    // X -> Y: base causal effect
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_new(6.0, 4.0), 0.3, 0.1)

    // W -> Y: effect modification
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "W", "Y", beta_new(7.0, 3.0), 0.2, 0.08)

    // Conditional ATE for different subgroups
    let cate_low = conditional_ate(dag, "X", "Y", "W", 0.0)
    let cate_high = conditional_ate(dag, "X", "Y", "W", 1.0)

    print("  CATE (W=0): ")
    println(cate_low.mean)
    print("  CATE (W=1): ")
    println(cate_high.mean)

    let diff = cate_high.mean - cate_low.mean
    print("  Heterogeneity: ")
    println(diff)

    if abs_f64(diff) > 0.1 {
        println("  ✓ Significant effect heterogeneity detected")
    } else {
        println("  ✓ Effect is relatively homogeneous")
    }
    println("")

    return 0
}

fn test_counterfactual_reasoning() -> i64 {
    println("Test 5: Counterfactual Reasoning")
    println("==================================")

    // Create simple DAG: X -> Y
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)

    // X -> Y with strong effect
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_new(8.0, 2.0), 0.6, 0.05)

    // Counterfactual: "What if X had been 1 instead of 0?"
    let cf = counterfactual(dag, "X", 0.0, 1.0, "Y")

    print("  Counterfactual outcome: ")
    println(cf.mean)
    print("  Counterfactual uncertainty: ")
    println(cf.variance)

    // Probability of necessity and sufficiency
    let pns = probability_of_necessity(dag, "X", "Y", 1.0, 0.0)
    let ps = probability_of_sufficiency(dag, "X", "Y", 0.0, 1.0)

    print("  P(Necessity): ")
    println(pns)
    print("  P(Sufficiency): ")
    println(ps)

    println("  ✓ Counterfactual reasoning complete")
    println("")

    return 0
}

fn test_structure_learning() -> i64 {
    println("Test 6: Causal Structure Learning")
    println("===================================")

    // Start with uncertain edges
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)

    // Add edge with uncertain existence
    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_uniform(), 0.0, 0.0)

    print("  Initial edge confidence: ")
    let initial_conf = beta_mean(dag.edges[0].exists)
    println(initial_conf)

    // Simulate observing correlation
    let updated_edge = update_edge_existence(dag.edges[0], 0.8, 100.0)

    print("  After observing r=0.8, n=100: ")
    let updated_conf = beta_mean(updated_edge.exists)
    println(updated_conf)

    if updated_conf > initial_conf {
        println("  ✓ Evidence increased confidence in edge")
    }

    // Prune weak edges
    let pruned = dag_prune_edges(dag, 0.5)
    print("  Edges after pruning (threshold=0.5): ")
    println(len(pruned.edges))

    println("")
    return 0
}

fn test_active_learning() -> i64 {
    println("Test 7: Active Learning for Interventions")

    // Create DAG with multiple uncertain edges
    var dag = dag_new()

    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X2", NodeType::Treatment)

    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X2", "Y", beta_new(9.0, 1.0), 0.6, 0.04)  // Low uncertainty

    // Find optimal intervention target

    println("")

    return 0
}

fn test_sensitivity_analysis() -> i64 {
    println("Test 8: Sensitivity to Unmeasured Confounding")
    println("==============================================")

    // Create DAG with observed effect
    var dag = dag_new()
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "X", NodeType::Treatment)
    dag = dag_add_node(dag, "Y", NodeType::Outcome)

    dag = dag_add_edge(dag, "X", "Y", beta_new(7.0, 3.0), 0.5, 0.08)

    // Sensitivity analysis
    let observed_effect = 0.5
    let e_value = confounder_sensitivity(dag, "X", "Y", observed_effect)

    print("  Observed effect: ")
    println(observed_effect)
    print("  E-value (confounder strength needed): ")
    println(e_value)

    let robustness = robustness_value(dag, "X", "Y")
    print("  Robustness value: ")
    println(robustness)

    if robustness > 0.5 {
        println("  ✓ Effect is robust to unmeasured confounding")
    } else {
        println("  ✓ Effect may be sensitive to unmeasured confounding")
    }
    println("")

    return 0
}

// === FILE: tests/stdlib/epistemic/test_core_e2e.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E test for stdlib/epistemic/core
// Tests: uncertainty_exact, epistemic_std, epistemic_exact, add_epistemic,
//        get_value, get_confidence, check_invariants

use epistemic::lib::*

fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    return ad < tol
}

fn run_tests() -> i32 {
    var pass = 0
    var fail = 0

    // Test 1: uncertainty_exact() has tag 0
    let ue = uncertainty_exact()
    if ue.tag == 0 {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 2: epistemic_exact creates value with conf=1.0
    let e1 = epistemic_exact(42.0, 1.0)
    let v1 = get_value(e1)
    if check_near(v1, 42.0, 0.0001) {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 3: confidence is preserved
    let c1 = get_confidence(e1)
    if check_near(c1, 1.0, 0.0001) {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 4: epistemic_std with uncertainty
    let e2 = epistemic_std(100.0, 5.0, 0.9)
    let v2 = get_value(e2)
    if check_near(v2, 100.0, 0.0001) {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 5: std uncertainty is stored correctly
    let u2 = get_std_uncertainty(e2)
    if check_near(u2, 5.0, 0.0001) {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 6: add_epistemic sums values
    let e3 = epistemic_exact(10.0, 0.8)
    let e4 = epistemic_exact(20.0, 0.9)
    let sum = add_epistemic(e3, e4)
    let sum_val = get_value(sum)
    if check_near(sum_val, 30.0, 0.0001) {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 7: confidence monotonicity: result.conf <= min(a.conf, b.conf)
    let sum_conf = get_confidence(sum)
    if sum_conf <= 0.8001 {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 8: invariants hold
    let inv = check_invariants(e2)
    if inv {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    // Test 9: confidence clamped to [0, 1]
    let e_over = epistemic_exact(1.0, 5.0)
    let c_over = get_confidence(e_over)
    if check_near(c_over, 1.0, 0.0001) {
        pass = pass + 1
    } else {
        fail = fail + 1
    }

    if fail > 0 { return 1 }
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    return run_tests()
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/epistemic/test_eg_epistemic_rewrite.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Sprint 225 Phase 3: Round-trip GUM epistemic e-graph rewrite tests (T009-T018)
//
// Verifies the core mathematical properties of the GUM-guided epistemic e-graph
// rewriting infrastructure (egraph.sio Section 14c-extra + ocp_egraph_epistemic_pass).
//
// Scientific basis: JCGM GUM 100:2008 §5.1.2 — for additive combination:
//   u(z)^2 = u(x)^2 + u(y)^2   (independence assumption)
//
// These tests implement the same math as eg_quantize_unc, eg_isqrt,
// eg_small_add_binop_with_unc, and eg_small_extract_epistemic without
// depending on internal IR module imports (self-hosted module boundaries).
//
// References:
//   JCGM 100:2008 §5.1.2; Willsey et al. "egg" (2021); Herbie PLDI 2015

// ============================================================================
// Mathematical helpers — mirror the logic in egraph.sio Section 14c-extra
// ============================================================================

// Quantize f64 uncertainty to i64 (1e9 scale, nanosecond resolution)
// Mirrors eg_quantize_unc: u_f64 * 1_000_000_000 as i64, clamped at 0
fn quantize_unc(u_f64: f64) -> i64 {
    let scaled = u_f64 * 1000000000.0
    if scaled < 0.0 { return 0 }
    scaled as i64
}

// Integer square root via Newton's method, 7 iterations
// Mirrors eg_isqrt — initial guess from leading bit position
fn isqrt(x: i64) -> i64 {
    if x <= 0 { return 0 }
    if x == 1 { return 1 }
    var y: i64 = 2
    if x > 4                     { y = 4 }
    if x > 16                    { y = 8 }
    if x > 64                    { y = 16 }
    if x > 256                   { y = 32 }
    if x > 1024                  { y = 64 }
    if x > 4096                  { y = 128 }
    if x > 16384                 { y = 256 }
    if x > 65536                 { y = 512 }
    if x > 262144                { y = 1024 }
    if x > 1048576               { y = 2048 }
    if x > 4194304               { y = 4096 }
    if x > 16777216              { y = 8192 }
    if x > 67108864              { y = 16384 }
    if x > 268435456             { y = 32768 }
    if x > 1073741824            { y = 65536 }
    if x > 4294967296            { y = 131072 }
    if x > 17179869184           { y = 262144 }
    if x > 68719476736           { y = 524288 }
    if x > 274877906944          { y = 1048576 }
    if x > 1099511627776         { y = 2097152 }
    if x > 4398046511104         { y = 4194304 }
    if x > 17592186044416        { y = 8388608 }
    if x > 70368744177664        { y = 16777216 }
    if x > 281474976710656       { y = 33554432 }
    if x > 1125899906842624      { y = 67108864 }
    if x > 4503599627370496      { y = 134217728 }
    if x > 18014398509481984     { y = 268435456 }
    if x > 72057594037927936     { y = 536870912 }
    if x > 288230376151711744    { y = 1073741824 }
    if x > 1152921504606846976   { y = 2147483648 }
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    y = (y + x / y) / 2
    if y * y > x { y - 1 } else { y }
}

// GUM additive propagation: u(z)^2 = u(x)^2 + u(y)^2
// Mirrors eg_small_add_binop_with_unc (add path)
// Inputs are quantized uncertainties (i64, 1e9 scale)
fn gum_add_unc(unc_x: i64, unc_y: i64) -> i64 {
    let max_safe: i64 = 3000000000
    let x = if unc_x > max_safe { max_safe } else { unc_x }
    let y = if unc_y > max_safe { max_safe } else { unc_y }
    isqrt(x * x + y * y)
}

// Minimum of two i64 values
fn min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    if a <= b { a } else { b }
}

// Absolute difference of two i64 values
fn abs_diff_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    if a >= b { a - b } else { b - a }
}

// ============================================================================
// T009: quantize_unc round-trips correctly (3.0 → 3_000_000_000)
// ============================================================================
fn test_t009_quantize_round_trip() -> bool {
    let result = quantize_unc(3.0)
    // 3.0 * 1e9 = 3_000_000_000
    result == 3000000000
}

// ============================================================================
// T010: isqrt(9_000_000_000_000_000_000) gives correct result
// i.e., floor(sqrt(9e18)) = 3_000_000_000
// ============================================================================
fn test_t010_isqrt_large() -> bool {
    let x: i64 = 9000000000000000000
    let result = isqrt(x)
    // floor(sqrt(9e18)) = 3_000_000_000 exactly
    result == 3000000000
}

// ============================================================================
// T011: GUM addition: u(z)^2 = u(x)^2 + u(y)^2
// u(x) = 0.003, u(y) = 0.004 → u(z) = sqrt(9+16) * 1e-3 = 0.005
// In 1e9 scale: u(x)=3_000_000, u(y)=4_000_000 → expected 5_000_000
// Using sub-3e9 values avoids i64 overflow (3e6^2 + 4e6^2 = 25e12, well within i64)
// ============================================================================
fn test_t011_gum_pythagorean() -> bool {
    let ux: i64 = 3000000    // 0.003 in 1e9 scale
    let uy: i64 = 4000000    // 0.004 in 1e9 scale
    let uz = gum_add_unc(ux, uy)
    let expected: i64 = 5000000   // 0.005 in 1e9 scale = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) * 1e6
    // Allow ±1 for integer rounding
    abs_diff_i64(uz, expected) <= 1
}

// ============================================================================
// T012: Two-var e-graph with uncertainty — min-unc extraction picks correct node
// Node A: VAR with unc 2e9; Node B: CONST with unc 0.
// Epistemic extraction should prefer node B (lower uncertainty).
// ============================================================================
fn test_t012_min_unc_extraction() -> bool {
    let unc_var: i64 = 2000000000    // 2.0 quantized
    let unc_const: i64 = 0           // exact
    // Extractor picks the node with minimum uncertainty
    let chosen_unc = min_i64(unc_var, unc_const)
    chosen_unc == 0
}

// ============================================================================
// T013: Float saturation: (a+b)+c vs a+(b+c) — same combined uncertainty
// GUM additive law is commutative/associative for independent inputs.
// ============================================================================
fn test_t013_float_saturation_assoc() -> bool {
    let ua = quantize_unc(1.0)
    let ub = quantize_unc(2.0)
    let uc = quantize_unc(2.0)
    // Left: u((a+b)+c) = sqrt(sqrt(u(a)^2+u(b)^2)^2 + u(c)^2)
    //                   = sqrt(u(a)^2 + u(b)^2 + u(c)^2)
    let u_ab = gum_add_unc(ua, ub)
    let u_left = gum_add_unc(u_ab, uc)
    // Right: u(a+(b+c)) = sqrt(u(a)^2 + sqrt(u(b)^2+u(c)^2)^2)
    //                   = sqrt(u(a)^2 + u(b)^2 + u(c)^2)
    let u_bc = gum_add_unc(ub, uc)
    let u_right = gum_add_unc(ua, u_bc)
    // Should be equal (± rounding)
    abs_diff_i64(u_left, u_right) <= 2
}

// ============================================================================
// T014: Nested binops — 3-operand case
// u(a) = 1, u(b) = 1, u(c) = 1 → u(a+b+c) = sqrt(3) ≈ 1.732
// In 1e9 scale: isqrt(3) * 1e9 ≈ 1_732_050_808
// ============================================================================
fn test_t014_nested_three_operand() -> bool {
    let u1 = quantize_unc(1.0)    // 1_000_000_000
    let u2 = quantize_unc(1.0)
    let u3 = quantize_unc(1.0)
    let u12 = gum_add_unc(u1, u2)
    let u123 = gum_add_unc(u12, u3)
    // sqrt(3) * 1e9 ≈ 1_732_050_808 — allow ±1000 for multi-step rounding
    u123 > 1731000000 && u123 < 1733000000
}

// ============================================================================
// T015: Zero uncertainty edge case — pass-through
// If u(x) = 0 and u(y) = 0, then u(x+y) = 0
// ============================================================================
fn test_t015_zero_uncertainty() -> bool {
    let uz = gum_add_unc(0, 0)
    uz == 0
}

// ============================================================================
// T016: High uncertainty operand — combined uncertainty dominated by large term
// When one operand has much larger uncertainty, it dominates the combination.
// u(x) = 2_000_000_000, u(y) = 100_000 → uz ≈ u(x) (small term negligible)
// Both well within i64 range: 2e9^2 + 1e5^2 = 4e18 + 1e10 ≈ 4e18 (fits i64)
// ============================================================================
fn test_t016_high_uncertainty_clamp() -> bool {
    let ux: i64 = 2000000000   // large but < max_safe=3e9; safe to square (4e18 < 9.2e18)
    let uy: i64 = 100000       // small operand
    let uz = gum_add_unc(ux, uy)
    // uz ≈ sqrt(4e18 + 1e10) ≈ sqrt(4e18) = 2e9 (small term negligible)
    // Property: uz is close to ux (within 0.01%)
    let diff = abs_diff_i64(uz, ux)
    diff < 100000
}

// ============================================================================
// T017: Commutative rewrite check — gum_add_unc(a,b) == gum_add_unc(b,a)
// GUM §5.1.2: combination is symmetric (both inputs treated equally)
// ============================================================================
fn test_t017_commutativity() -> bool {
    let ua = quantize_unc(2.5)
    let ub = quantize_unc(3.7)
    let forward = gum_add_unc(ua, ub)
    let reverse = gum_add_unc(ub, ua)
    // Should be identical (x*x + y*y == y*y + x*x)
    forward == reverse
}

// ============================================================================
// T018: Integration — PRECISION_PRESERVING strategy guard concept
// Epistemic pass only fires for strategy == IR_STRATEGY_PRECISION_PRESERVING.
// Represent as: standard strategy ID = 0, precision-preserving = 3.
// The guard predicate should return true only for ID 3.
// ============================================================================

// Strategy guard helper (mirrors the guard in ocp_egraph_epistemic_pass)
fn strategy_guard_fires(strategy: i64) -> bool {
    let IR_STRATEGY_PRECISION_PRESERVING: i64 = 3
    strategy == IR_STRATEGY_PRECISION_PRESERVING
}

fn test_t018_strategy_guard() -> bool {
    let IR_STRATEGY_STANDARD: i64 = 0
    let IR_STRATEGY_PRECISION_PRESERVING: i64 = 3

    let standard_fires = strategy_guard_fires(IR_STRATEGY_STANDARD)
    let epi_fires = strategy_guard_fires(IR_STRATEGY_PRECISION_PRESERVING)

    // Standard must NOT fire; epistemic MUST fire
    standard_fires == false && epi_fires == true
}

// tests/stdlib/epistemic/test_gum_builder.sio — Tests for GUM Builder Pattern

// Tests for the new builder pattern and method chaining API in epistemic/gum.sio.

use epistemic::gum::{
    GUMUncertainty, GUMResult,
    type_a_uncertainty, type_b_uncertainty, type_b_uniform, type_b_triangular, type_b_from_expanded,
    gum_simple, gum_type_a,
    gum_add, gum_sub, gum_mul, gum_div,
    coverage_factor_95, k_normal_95,
}

// =============================================================================
// Test: GUMUncertainty Builder Pattern
// =============================================================================

fn test_gum_uncertainty_type_a() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // New builder pattern
    let u = type_a_uncertainty(0.1, 10)
    
    // Standard uncertainty of mean = s / sqrt(n) = 0.1 / sqrt(10) ≈ 0.0316
    let expected_u = 0.1 / 3.16227766  // sqrt(10)
    
    assert(u.std_uncertainty > expected_u - 0.001 && u.std_uncertainty < expected_u + 0.001)
    
    // Degrees of freedom = n - 1 = 9
    assert(u.degrees_of_freedom == 9.0)
    
    // Default sensitivity = 1.0
    assert(u.sensitivity == 1.0)
}

fn test_gum_uncertainty_type_b() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // New builder pattern
    let u = type_b_uncertainty(0.05)
    
    assert(u.std_uncertainty == 0.05)
    
    // Type B has infinite DoF (represented as 1e9)
    assert(u.degrees_of_freedom == 1.0e9)
    
    assert(u.sensitivity == 1.0)
}

fn test_gum_uncertainty_type_b_uniform() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Uniform distribution: u = a / sqrt(3)
    let u = type_b_uniform(1.0)
    
    // u = 1.0 / sqrt(3) ≈ 0.577
    let expected = 1.0 / 1.732050808
    assert(u.std_uncertainty > expected - 0.001 && u.std_uncertainty < expected + 0.001)
}

fn test_gum_uncertainty_type_b_triangular() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Triangular distribution: u = a / sqrt(6)
    let u = type_b_triangular(1.0)
    
    // u = 1.0 / sqrt(6) ≈ 0.408
    let expected = 1.0 / 2.449489743
    assert(u.std_uncertainty > expected - 0.001 && u.std_uncertainty < expected + 0.001)
}

fn test_gum_uncertainty_with_sensitivity() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Method chaining for sensitivity
    let u = type_a_uncertainty(0.1, 10)
        .with_sensitivity(2.0)
    
    assert(u.sensitivity == 2.0)
}

fn test_gum_uncertainty_combine() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let u1 = type_b_uncertainty(0.1).with_sensitivity(1.0)
    let u2 = type_b_uncertainty(0.2).with_sensitivity(1.0)
    
    let combined = u1.combine(&u2)
    
    // Combined: u_c = sqrt(0.1^2 + 0.2^2) = sqrt(0.05) ≈ 0.224
    let expected = 0.223606797  // sqrt(0.05)
    assert(combined.std_uncertainty > expected - 0.001 && combined.std_uncertainty < expected + 0.001)
}

fn test_gum_result_add() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let a = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    let b = gum_simple(5.0, 0.2)
    
    let c = a.add(&b)
    
    // Value: 10 + 5 = 15
    assert(c.value == 15.0)
    
    // Uncertainty: sqrt(0.1^2 + 0.2^2) = sqrt(0.05) ≈ 0.224
    let expected_u = 0.223606797
    assert(c.std_uncertainty > expected_u - 0.01 && c.std_uncertainty < expected_u + 0.01)
}

fn test_gum_result_sub() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    let a = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    let b = gum_simple(3.0, 0.2)
    
    let c = a.sub(&b)
    
    // Value: 10 - 3 = 7
    assert(c.value == 7.0)
    
    // Uncertainty: sqrt(0.1^2 + 0.2^2) ≈ 0.224
    let expected_u = 0.223606797
    assert(c.std_uncertainty > expected_u - 0.01 && c.std_uncertainty < expected_u + 0.01)
}

fn test_gum_result_mul() with Mut, Div, Panic {

    let b = gum_simple(2.0, 0.1)
    
    let c = a.mul(&b)
    
    // Value: 10 * 2 = 20
    assert(c.value == 20.0)
    
    // Uncertainty: sqrt((2*0.1)^2 + (10*0.1)^2) = sqrt(0.04 + 1.0) ≈ 1.02
    assert(c.std_uncertainty > 1.0 && c.std_uncertainty < 1.1)
}

fn test_gum_result_scale() with Mut, Div, Panic {

    let c = a.scale(3.0)
    
    // Value: 10 * 3 = 30
    assert(c.value == 30.0)
    
    // Uncertainty: |3| * 0.1 = 0.3

fn test_gum_result_relative_uncertainty() with Mut, Div, Panic {

    let rel = result.relative_uncertainty()
    assert(rel == 0.05)
}

// =============================================================================
// Test: Complex Chain Operations
// =============================================================================

fn test_gum_result_complex_chain() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Chain: (a + b).scale(0.5).add(&c)
    let a = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    let b = gum_simple(5.0, 0.2)
    let c = gum_simple(2.0, 0.05)
    
    let result = a.add(&b).scale(0.5).add(&c)
    
    // Value: ((10 + 5) * 0.5) + 2 = 7.5 + 2 = 9.5
    assert(result.value == 9.5)
    
    // Uncertainty should propagate through chain
    assert(result.std_uncertainty > 0.0)
}

fn test_gum_backward_compatibility_type_b() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Old API should still work
    let u = type_b_uncertainty(0.05)
    assert(u.std_uncertainty == 0.05)
    
    let u_uniform = type_b_uniform(1.0)
    let expected = 1.0 / 1.732050808
    assert(u_uniform.std_uncertainty > expected - 0.001 && u_uniform.std_uncertainty < expected + 0.001)
    
    let u_tri = type_b_triangular(1.0)
    let expected_tri = 1.0 / 2.449489743
    assert(u_tri.std_uncertainty > expected_tri - 0.001 && u_tri.std_uncertainty < expected_tri + 0.001)
    
    let u_exp = type_b_from_expanded(0.196, 1.96)
    assert(u_exp.std_uncertainty == 0.1)
}

fn test_gum_backward_compatibility_gum_simple() with Mut, Div, Panic {
    // Old API should still work
    let result = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    
    assert(result.value == 10.0)
    assert(result.std_uncertainty == 0.1)
}

    // Old API for operations should still work
    let a = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    let b = gum_simple(5.0, 0.2)
    
    let c_add = gum_add(a, b)
    assert(c_add.value == 15.0)
    
    let c_sub = gum_sub(a, b)

    let a2 = gum_simple(10.0, 0.1)
    let b2 = gum_simple(2.0, 0.1)
    let c_mul = gum_mul(a2, b2)
    assert(c_mul.value == 20.0)
}

// === FILE: tests/stdlib/epistemic/test_knowledge_jit.sio ===
//@ run-pass
/// JIT-Compatible Test: Knowledge and Variance Propagation
///
/// Tests the core epistemic computing concepts in a format
/// that works with the current Sounio JIT.

// ============================================================================
// NUMERIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 10.0 { return 22026.465794806718 * exp_f64(x - 10.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 10.0 { return 0.00004539992976248485 * exp_f64(x + 10.0) }
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var nf = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 20 {
        term = term * x / nf
        result = result + term
        n = n + 1
        nf = nf + 1.0
    }
    return result
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 999999.0 }
    if x == 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    let y = (x - 1.0) / (x + 1.0)
    var result = 0.0
    var term = y
    var i = 1
    while i < 30 {
        result = result + term / (i * 1.0)
        term = term * y * y
        i = i + 2
    }
    return 2.0 * result
}

fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = 0.0 - 0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = 0.0 - 1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911
    let sign = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x_abs = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * x_abs)
    let y = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t + a4) * t) + a3) * t + a2) * t + a1) * t * exp_f64(0.0 - x_abs * x_abs)
    return sign * y
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC VALUE STRUCT (Simplified for JIT)
// ============================================================================

struct EpistemicValue {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64,
    conf_alpha: f64,
    conf_beta: f64
}

fn epistemic_new(value: f64, variance: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: value,
        variance: variance,
        conf_alpha: 1.0,
        conf_beta: 1.0
    }
}

fn epistemic_std(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(k.variance)
}

fn epistemic_conf_mean(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return k.conf_alpha / (k.conf_alpha + k.conf_beta)
}

// ============================================================================
// VARIANCE PROPAGATION
// ============================================================================

/// X + Y: Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y)
fn epistemic_add(x: EpistemicValue, y: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: x.value + y.value,
        variance: x.variance + y.variance,
        conf_alpha: x.conf_alpha + y.conf_alpha - 1.0,
        conf_beta: x.conf_beta + y.conf_beta - 1.0
    }
}

/// X - Y: Var(X - Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y)
fn epistemic_sub(x: EpistemicValue, y: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: x.value - y.value,
        variance: x.variance + y.variance,
        conf_alpha: x.conf_alpha + y.conf_alpha - 1.0,
        conf_beta: x.conf_beta + y.conf_beta - 1.0
    }
}

/// X * Y: Var(XY) ≈ Y²Var(X) + X²Var(Y) (delta method)
fn epistemic_mul(x: EpistemicValue, y: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let new_variance = y.value * y.value * x.variance + x.value * x.value * y.variance
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: x.value * y.value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: x.conf_alpha + y.conf_alpha - 1.0,
        conf_beta: x.conf_beta + y.conf_beta - 1.0
    }
}

/// X / Y: Var(X/Y) ≈ (1/Y²)Var(X) + (X²/Y⁴)Var(Y) (delta method)
fn epistemic_div(x: EpistemicValue, y: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let y2 = y.value * y.value
    let y4 = y2 * y2
    let new_variance = x.variance / y2 + x.value * x.value * y.variance / y4
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: x.value / y.value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: x.conf_alpha + y.conf_alpha - 1.0,
        conf_beta: x.conf_beta + y.conf_beta - 1.0
    }
}

/// Scale by constant: Var(cX) = c²Var(X)
fn epistemic_scale(k: EpistemicValue, c: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: k.value * c,
        variance: k.variance * c * c,
        conf_alpha: k.conf_alpha,
        conf_beta: k.conf_beta
    }
}

/// e^X: Var(e^X) ≈ e^(2X) · Var(X)
fn epistemic_exp(k: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let new_value = exp_f64(k.value)
    let new_variance = exp_f64(2.0 * k.value) * k.variance
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: new_value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: k.conf_alpha,
        conf_beta: k.conf_beta
    }
}

/// ln(X): Var(ln X) ≈ Var(X)/X²
fn epistemic_ln(k: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let new_value = ln_f64(k.value)
    let new_variance = k.variance / (k.value * k.value)
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: new_value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: k.conf_alpha,
        conf_beta: k.conf_beta
    }
}

/// √X: Var(√X) ≈ Var(X)/(4X)
fn epistemic_sqrt(k: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let new_value = sqrt_f64(k.value)
    let new_variance = k.variance / (4.0 * k.value)
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: new_value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: k.conf_alpha,
        conf_beta: k.conf_beta
    }
}

/// X²: Var(X²) ≈ 4X²Var(X)
fn epistemic_square(k: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let new_value = k.value * k.value
    let new_variance = 4.0 * new_value * k.variance
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: new_value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: k.conf_alpha,
        conf_beta: k.conf_beta
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// PROBABILITY QUERIES
// ============================================================================

/// P(X > thresh) using normal approximation
fn epistemic_prob_gt(k: EpistemicValue, thresh: f64) -> f64 {
    if k.variance <= 0.0000001 {
        if k.value > thresh { return 1.0 }
        return 0.0
    }
    let z = (k.value - thresh) / sqrt_f64(k.variance)
    return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf_approx(z / 1.4142135623730951))
}

/// 95% CI lower bound
fn epistemic_ci95_lo(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return k.value - 1.96 * sqrt_f64(k.variance)
}

/// 95% CI upper bound
fn epistemic_ci95_hi(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return k.value + 1.96 * sqrt_f64(k.variance)
}

// ============================================================================
// BELIEF UPDATE (Active Inference)
// ============================================================================

fn precision_of(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return 1.0 / max_f64(k.variance, 0.0000001)
}

fn update_belief(prior: EpistemicValue, observation: f64, obs_variance: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    let prior_prec = precision_of(prior)
    let obs_prec = 1.0 / max_f64(obs_variance, 0.0000001)
    let total_prec = prior_prec + obs_prec
    let posterior_mean = (prior_prec * prior.value + obs_prec * observation) / total_prec
    let posterior_var = 1.0 / total_prec
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: posterior_mean,
        variance: posterior_var,
        conf_alpha: prior.conf_alpha + 1.0,
        conf_beta: prior.conf_beta
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> f64 {
    var passed = 0.0
    var failed = 0.0
    let tol = 0.001

    // Test 1: Addition variance propagation
    let k1 = epistemic_new(100.0, 4.0)
    let k2 = epistemic_new(50.0, 1.0)
    let sum = epistemic_add(k1, k2)
    // Var(X + Y) = 4 + 1 = 5
    if abs_f64(sum.variance - 5.0) < tol {
        if abs_f64(sum.value - 150.0) < tol {
            passed = passed + 1.0
        } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 2: Multiplication variance propagation
    let k3 = epistemic_new(10.0, 0.25)
    let k4 = epistemic_new(5.0, 0.04)
    let prod = epistemic_mul(k3, k4)
    // Var(XY) ≈ Y²Var(X) + X²Var(Y) = 25*0.25 + 100*0.04 = 10.25
    let expected_prod_var = 25.0 * 0.25 + 100.0 * 0.04
    if abs_f64(prod.variance - expected_prod_var) < 0.1 {
        if abs_f64(prod.value - 50.0) < tol {
            passed = passed + 1.0
        } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 3: Division variance propagation
    let dose = epistemic_new(500.0, 25.0)
    let volume = epistemic_new(10.0, 0.01)
    let conc = epistemic_div(dose, volume)
    // Var(X/Y) ≈ Var(X)/Y² + X²Var(Y)/Y⁴
    // = 25/100 + 250000*0.01/10000 = 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5
    let expected_div_var = 25.0 / 100.0 + 250000.0 * 0.01 / 10000.0
    if abs_f64(conc.variance - expected_div_var) < 0.1 {
        if abs_f64(conc.value - 50.0) < tol {
            passed = passed + 1.0
        } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 4: P(X > 0) for N(0,1) should be 0.5
    let k5 = epistemic_new(0.0, 1.0)
    let p = epistemic_prob_gt(k5, 0.0)
    if abs_f64(p - 0.5) < 0.01 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 5: 95% CI for N(100, 4)
    let k6 = epistemic_new(100.0, 4.0)
    let ci_lo = epistemic_ci95_lo(k6)
    let ci_hi = epistemic_ci95_hi(k6)
    // Should be [96.08, 103.92]
    if abs_f64(ci_lo - 96.08) < 0.1 {
        if abs_f64(ci_hi - 103.92) < 0.1 {
            passed = passed + 1.0
        } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 6: Scale by constant
    let k7 = epistemic_new(10.0, 1.0)
    let scaled = epistemic_scale(k7, 3.0)
    // Value = 30, Var = 9
    if abs_f64(scaled.value - 30.0) < tol {
        if abs_f64(scaled.variance - 9.0) < tol {
            passed = passed + 1.0
        } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 7: Belief update reduces variance
    let prior = epistemic_new(10.0, 4.0)
    let posterior = update_belief(prior, 11.0, 1.0)
    if posterior.variance < prior.variance {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Test 8: Posterior mean is weighted average
    // Prior: N(10, 4), Obs: 11 with var=1
    // Posterior mean = (0.25*10 + 1*11)/(0.25+1) = 13.5/1.25 = 10.8
    let expected_mean = (0.25 * 10.0 + 1.0 * 11.0) / (0.25 + 1.0)
    if abs_f64(posterior.value - expected_mean) < 0.1 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else { failed = failed + 1.0 }

    // Return score: passed - failed (positive = success)
    return passed - failed
}

/// test_stats.d — Comprehensive tests for epistemic::stats
///

// Import the epistemic stats module
use epistemic::stats::*

// Test tolerance
fn tol() -> f64 { return 0.0001 }

// ============================================================================
// TEST HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn assert_near(actual: f64, expected: f64, name: string) -> i64 {
    let diff = abs_f64(actual - expected)
    if diff < tol() {
        print("  PASS: ")
        println(name)
        return 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: ")
        print(name)
        print(" — expected ")
        print(expected)
        print(", got ")
        println(actual)
        return 0
    }
}

fn assert_true(condition: i64, name: string) -> i64 {
    if condition > 0 {
        print("  PASS: ")
        println(name)
        return 1
    } else {
        print("  FAIL: ")
        println(name)
        return 0
    }
}

fn test_beta_construction() -> i64 {
    println("=== Beta Construction Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // Test uniform prior
    let uniform = beta_uniform()
    passed = passed + assert_near(uniform.alpha, 1.0, "uniform alpha")
    passed = passed + assert_near(uniform.beta, 1.0, "uniform beta")

    // Test Jeffreys prior
    let jeffreys = beta_jeffreys()
    passed = passed + assert_near(jeffreys.alpha, 0.5, "jeffreys alpha")
    passed = passed + assert_near(jeffreys.beta, 0.5, "jeffreys beta")

    // Test informative prior
    let info = beta_informative(0.7, 10.0)
    passed = passed + assert_near(info.alpha, 7.0, "informative alpha")
    passed = passed + assert_near(info.beta, 3.0, "informative beta")

    println("")
    return passed
}

fn test_beta_moments() -> i64 {
    println("=== Beta Moments Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // Beta(8, 4) from uniform + 7 successes, 3 failures
    let b = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 7.0, 3.0)

    // Mean = 8/12 ≈ 0.6667
    let expected_mean = 8.0 / 12.0
    passed = passed + assert_near(beta_mean(b), expected_mean, "mean")

    // Variance = (8*4) / (12^2 * 13) = 32/1872 ≈ 0.0171
    let expected_var = 32.0 / 1872.0
    passed = passed + assert_near(beta_variance(b), expected_var, "variance")

    // Mode = (8-1)/(12-2) = 7/10 = 0.7
    let expected_mode = 7.0 / 10.0
    passed = passed + assert_near(beta_mode(b), expected_mode, "mode")

    // Sample size = 12
    passed = passed + assert_near(beta_sample_size(b), 12.0, "sample size")

    println("")
    return passed
}

fn test_beta_update() -> i64 {
    println("=== Bayesian Update Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    let prior = beta_uniform()

    // Single update
    let post1 = beta_update(prior, 1.0, 0.0)
    passed = passed + assert_near(post1.alpha, 2.0, "single success alpha")
    passed = passed + assert_near(post1.beta, 1.0, "single success beta")

    // Multiple updates should be equivalent to batch
    let post_seq = beta_update(beta_update(prior, 3.0, 0.0), 2.0, 1.0)
    let post_batch = beta_update(prior, 5.0, 1.0)
    passed = passed + assert_near(post_seq.alpha, post_batch.alpha, "sequential=batch alpha")
    passed = passed + assert_near(post_seq.beta, post_batch.beta, "sequential=batch beta")

    println("")
    return passed
}

    let e2 = epistemic_point(0.4, 0.01)

    // Scale
    let scaled = epistemic_scale(e1, 2.0)
    passed = passed + assert_near(scaled.value, 1.2, "scaled value")
    passed = passed + assert_near(scaled.variance, 0.08, "scaled variance")

    // Multiply

    passed = passed + assert_near(prod.value, 0.24, "product value")
    // Var(XY) ≈ 0.6²*0.01 + 0.4²*0.02 + 0.02*0.01
    let expected_prod_var = 0.36 * 0.01 + 0.16 * 0.02 + 0.02 * 0.01
    passed = passed + assert_near(prod.variance, expected_prod_var, "product variance")

    println("")
    return passed

fn test_info_gain() -> i64 {
    println("=== Information Gain Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // Uniform prior: maximum ignorance, high info gain
    let uniform = beta_uniform()
    let ig_uniform = expected_info_gain(uniform)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if ig_uniform > 0.2 { 1 } else { 0 }, "uniform has high info gain")

    // Strong prior: low ignorance, low info gain
    let strong = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 49.0, 1.0)
    let ig_strong = expected_info_gain(strong)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if ig_strong < 0.02 { 1 } else { 0 }, "strong has low info gain")

    // Info gain decreases with evidence
    passed = passed + assert_true(if ig_uniform > ig_strong { 1 } else { 0 }, "info gain decreases with evidence")

    println("")
    return passed
}

fn test_variance_reduction() -> i64 {
    println("=== Variance Reduction Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    let b = beta_uniform()
    let vr = expected_variance_reduction(b)

    // Variance reduction should be positive
    passed = passed + assert_true(if vr > 0.0 { 1 } else { 0 }, "variance reduction positive")

    // More observations = more reduction
    let vr1 = expected_variance_reduction_k(b, 1.0)
    let vr10 = expected_variance_reduction_k(b, 10.0)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if vr10 > vr1 { 1 } else { 0 }, "more obs = more reduction")

    println("")
    return passed
}

fn test_exploration_exploitation() -> i64 {
    println("=== Exploration-Exploitation Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // High variance = explore
    let uncertain = beta_uniform()
    let ee_uncertain = exploration_exploitation_score(uncertain, 0.7)
    passed = passed + assert_near(ee_uncertain, 0.0, "uncertain -> explore")

    // Low variance = exploit
    let certain = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 99.0, 1.0)
    let ee_certain = exploration_exploitation_score(certain, 0.7)
    passed = passed + assert_near(ee_certain, 1.0, "certain -> exploit")

    println("")
    return passed
}

// ============================================================================
// SECTION 5: HIERARCHICAL COMBINATION TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_hierarchical_combine() -> i64 {
    println("=== Hierarchical Combination Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // Three similar distributions
    let d1 = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 7.0, 3.0)  // mean 0.67
    let d2 = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 6.0, 4.0)  // mean 0.60
    let d3 = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 8.0, 2.0)  // mean 0.73

    let combined = beta_hierarchical_combine([d1, d2, d3])

    // Combined mean should be between individual means
    let cm = beta_mean(combined)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if cm > 0.5 { 1 } else { 0 }, "combined mean > 0.5")
    passed = passed + assert_true(if cm < 0.8 { 1 } else { 0 }, "combined mean < 0.8")

    // Combined variance should be lower than average
    let cv = beta_variance(combined)
    let avg_var = (beta_variance(d1) + beta_variance(d2) + beta_variance(d3)) / 3.0
    passed = passed + assert_true(if cv < avg_var { 1 } else { 0 }, "combined variance < average")

    println("")
    return passed
}

fn test_precision_weighted() -> i64 {
    println("=== Precision-Weighted Combination Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // One precise, one imprecise
    let precise = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 99.0, 1.0)   // Low variance
    let imprecise = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 1.0, 1.0)  // High variance

    let combined = beta_precision_weighted([precise, imprecise])

    // Combined should be closer to precise estimate
    let cm = beta_mean(combined)
    let pm = beta_mean(precise)
    let im = beta_mean(imprecise)

    let diff_to_precise = abs_f64(cm - pm)
    let diff_to_imprecise = abs_f64(cm - im)

    passed = passed + assert_true(if diff_to_precise < diff_to_imprecise { 1 } else { 0 },
                                   "combined closer to precise")

    println("")
    return passed
}

// ============================================================================
// SECTION 6: INFORMATION THEORY TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_kl_divergence() -> i64 {
    println("=== KL Divergence Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    let p = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 7.0, 3.0)
    let q = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 6.0, 4.0)

    // KL(p||p) = 0
    let kl_self = beta_kl_divergence(p, p)
    passed = passed + assert_near(kl_self, 0.0, "KL(p||p) = 0")

    // KL(p||q) >= 0
    let kl_pq = beta_kl_divergence(p, q)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if kl_pq >= 0.0 { 1 } else { 0 }, "KL(p||q) >= 0")

    // KL(p||q) != KL(q||p) in general
    let kl_qp = beta_kl_divergence(q, p)
    // They should be close but not necessarily equal
    passed = passed + assert_true(if abs_f64(kl_pq - kl_qp) < 0.1 { 1 } else { 0 },
                                   "KL is approximately symmetric for similar distributions")

    println("")
    return passed
}

// ============================================================================
// SECTION 7: NOVELTY TESTS
// ============================================================================

fn test_observations_for_variance() -> i64 {
    println("=== Observations for Target Variance Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    let current = beta_uniform()  // Variance ≈ 0.083
    let current_var = beta_variance(current)

    // Target = current (need 0 more observations)
    let n0 = observations_for_target_variance(current, current_var)
    passed = passed + assert_near(n0, 0.0, "0 obs needed for current variance")

    // Target < current (need more observations)
    let n_low = observations_for_target_variance(current, 0.01)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if n_low > 0.0 { 1 } else { 0 }, "need obs for lower variance")

    println("")
    return passed
}

fn test_data_collection_priority() -> i64 {
    println("=== Data Collection Priority Tests ===")
    var passed: i64 = 0

    // High variance = high priority
    let uncertain = beta_uniform()
    let p_uncertain = data_collection_priority(uncertain, 1.0)

    // Low variance = low priority
    let certain = beta_update(beta_uniform(), 99.0, 1.0)
    let p_certain = data_collection_priority(certain, 1.0)

    passed = passed + assert_true(if p_uncertain > p_certain { 1 } else { 0 },
                                   "uncertain has higher priority")

    // Importance scales priority
    let p_important = data_collection_priority(uncertain, 2.0)
    passed = passed + assert_true(if p_important > p_uncertain { 1 } else { 0 },
                                   "importance scales priority")

    println("")
    return passed
}

    println("╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║  epistemic::stats Test Suite                               ║")
    println("╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    println("")

    var total_passed: i64 = 0

    // Section 1: Core Beta
    total_passed = total_passed + test_beta_construction()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_beta_moments()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_beta_update()

    // Section 2: Variance Propagation
    total_passed = total_passed + test_epistemic_value()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_epistemic_arithmetic()

    // Section 3: Active Inference
    total_passed = total_passed + test_info_gain()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_variance_reduction()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_exploration_exploitation()

    // Section 4: ML Integration
    total_passed = total_passed + test_variance_penalty()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_curriculum_weight()

    // Section 5: Hierarchical
    total_passed = total_passed + test_hierarchical_combine()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_precision_weighted()

    // Section 6: Information Theory
    total_passed = total_passed + test_kl_divergence()

    // Section 7: Novelty
    total_passed = total_passed + test_observations_for_variance()
    total_passed = total_passed + test_data_collection_priority()

    println("═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════")

        println("TEST SUITE PASSED")

    } else {
        println("TEST SUITE FAILED — check individual tests above")
        return 1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/fairness/test_fairness.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Tests for stdlib/fairness/metrics.sio
// Covers: demographic parity, equalized odds, disparate impact, Chouldechova theorem.
// Self-contained — all helpers inlined; no `use` imports required by JIT.

// ============================================================
// Math helpers
// ============================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    x
}

fn safe_div_t(num: f64, denom: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if denom == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    num / denom
}

fn ep_sqrt_t(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x / 2.0
    var k = 0
    while k < 8 {
        y = (y + x / y) / 2.0
        k = k + 1
    }
    y
}

// ============================================================
// Inline implementations of fairness metrics
// ============================================================

// demographic_parity_t: |P(Ŷ=1|A=0) - P(Ŷ=1|A=1)|
fn demographic_parity_t(predictions: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos0: f64 = 0.0
    var count1: f64 = 0.0
    var pos1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let p = predictions[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            count0 = count0 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos0 = pos0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            count1 = count1 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos1 = pos1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rate0 = safe_div_t(pos0, count0)
    let rate1 = safe_div_t(pos1, count1)
    abs_f64(rate0 - rate1)
}

// equalized_odds_t: max(|ΔTPR|, |ΔFPR|)
fn equalized_odds_t(predictions: [i32; 256], true_labels: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var tp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fp0: f64 = 0.0
    var fn0: f64 = 0.0
    var tn0: f64 = 0.0
    var tp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fp1: f64 = 0.0
    var fn1: f64 = 0.0
    var tn1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let y_hat = predictions[idx]
        let y = true_labels[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp0 = tp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp0 = fp0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 0 { fn0 = fn0 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 0 { tn0 = tn0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 1 { tp1 = tp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 1 { fp1 = fp1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 1 && y_hat == 0 { fn1 = fn1 + 1.0 }
            if y == 0 && y_hat == 0 { tn1 = tn1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let tpr0 = safe_div_t(tp0, tp0 + fn0)
    let tpr1 = safe_div_t(tp1, tp1 + fn1)
    let fpr0 = safe_div_t(fp0, fp0 + tn0)
    let fpr1 = safe_div_t(fp1, fp1 + tn1)
    let d_tpr = abs_f64(tpr0 - tpr1)
    let d_fpr = abs_f64(fpr0 - fpr1)
    if d_tpr > d_fpr { d_tpr } else { d_fpr }
}

// disparate_impact_t: min(P₀/P₁, P₁/P₀)
fn disparate_impact_t(predictions: [i32; 256], protected: [i32; 256], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var count0: f64 = 0.0
    var pos0: f64 = 0.0
    var count1: f64 = 0.0
    var pos1: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i32 = 0
    while i < n {
        let idx = i as usize
        let p = predictions[idx]
        let g = protected[idx]
        if g == 0 {
            count0 = count0 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos0 = pos0 + 1.0 }
        } else {
            count1 = count1 + 1.0
            if p == 1 { pos1 = pos1 + 1.0 }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    let rate0 = safe_div_t(pos0, count0)
    let rate1 = safe_div_t(pos1, count1)
    if rate0 == 0.0 && rate1 == 0.0 { return 1.0 }
    if rate0 == 0.0 || rate1 == 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    let r01 = safe_div_t(rate0, rate1)
    let r10 = safe_div_t(rate1, rate0)
    if r01 < r10 { r01 } else { r10 }
}

// chouldechova_check_t: returns 1 if impossibility theorem is triggered
fn chouldechova_check_t(tp0: f64, fp0: f64, tp1: f64, fp1: f64, base0: f64, base1: f64) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    let rate_diff = abs_f64(base0 - base1)
    if rate_diff < 0.001 {
        return 0
    }
    // Sufficient condition: base rates differ significantly
    if rate_diff > 0.1 {
        return 1
    }
    let ppv0 = safe_div_t(tp0 * base0, tp0 * base0 + fp0 * (1.0 - base0))
    let ppv1 = safe_div_t(tp1 * base1, tp1 * base1 + fp1 * (1.0 - base1))
    let fpr_diff = abs_f64(fp0 - fp1)
    let tpr_diff = abs_f64(tp0 - tp1)
    let ppv_diff = abs_f64(ppv0 - ppv1)
    if fpr_diff < 0.05 && tpr_diff < 0.05 && ppv_diff > 0.05 {
        return 1
    }
    0
}

// ============================================================
// Tests
// ============================================================

fn main() -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var passed = 0.0
    var failed = 0.0

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 1: Perfect fairness — equal predictions across groups → parity_diff = 0
    // Setup: 4 group-0 and 4 group-1 samples, all predicted positive
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_fair: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var true_fair: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_fair: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    preds_fair[0] = 1
    preds_fair[1] = 1
    preds_fair[2] = 1
    preds_fair[3] = 1
    preds_fair[4] = 1
    preds_fair[5] = 1
    preds_fair[6] = 1
    preds_fair[7] = 1
    true_fair[0] = 1
    true_fair[1] = 1
    true_fair[2] = 1
    true_fair[3] = 1
    true_fair[4] = 1
    true_fair[5] = 1
    true_fair[6] = 1
    true_fair[7] = 1
    // group 0: indices 0–3, group 1: indices 4–7
    prot_fair[0] = 0
    prot_fair[1] = 0
    prot_fair[2] = 0
    prot_fair[3] = 0
    prot_fair[4] = 1
    prot_fair[5] = 1
    prot_fair[6] = 1
    prot_fair[7] = 1
    let dp_fair = demographic_parity_t(preds_fair, prot_fair, 8)
    if abs_f64(dp_fair) < 0.001 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 2: Biased classifier — all positive for group 0, all negative for group 1
    // P(Ŷ=1|A=0) = 1.0, P(Ŷ=1|A=1) = 0.0 → parity_diff = 1.0
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_biased: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_biased: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    // Group 0 (indices 0–3): all predicted positive
    preds_biased[0] = 1
    preds_biased[1] = 1
    preds_biased[2] = 1
    preds_biased[3] = 1
    // Group 1 (indices 4–7): all predicted negative (default 0)
    prot_biased[0] = 0
    prot_biased[1] = 0
    prot_biased[2] = 0
    prot_biased[3] = 0
    prot_biased[4] = 1
    prot_biased[5] = 1
    prot_biased[6] = 1
    prot_biased[7] = 1
    let dp_biased = demographic_parity_t(preds_biased, prot_biased, 8)
    if abs_f64(dp_biased - 1.0) < 0.001 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 3: Perfect equalized odds — same TPR and FPR across groups
    // Both groups: 2 TP, 0 FP, 0 FN, 2 TN → TPR=1, FPR=0 for both
    // eo_diff should be 0
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_eo: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var true_eo: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_eo: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    // Group 0: indices 0–3 (2 positives predicted correctly, 2 negatives correctly)
    preds_eo[0] = 1
    preds_eo[1] = 1
    preds_eo[2] = 0
    preds_eo[3] = 0
    true_eo[0] = 1
    true_eo[1] = 1
    true_eo[2] = 0
    true_eo[3] = 0
    prot_eo[0] = 0
    prot_eo[1] = 0
    prot_eo[2] = 0
    prot_eo[3] = 0
    // Group 1: indices 4–7 (same pattern)
    preds_eo[4] = 1
    preds_eo[5] = 1
    preds_eo[6] = 0
    preds_eo[7] = 0
    true_eo[4] = 1
    true_eo[5] = 1
    true_eo[6] = 0
    true_eo[7] = 0
    prot_eo[4] = 1
    prot_eo[5] = 1
    prot_eo[6] = 1
    prot_eo[7] = 1
    let eo_equal = equalized_odds_t(preds_eo, true_eo, prot_eo, 8)
    if abs_f64(eo_equal) < 0.001 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 4: Unequal equalized odds
    // Group 0: TPR=1.0 (2TP, 0FN), FPR=0.0 (0FP, 2TN)
    // Group 1: TPR=0.5 (1TP, 1FN), FPR=0.0 (0FP, 2TN)
    // eo_diff = |1.0 - 0.5| = 0.5
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_eo2: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var true_eo2: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_eo2: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    // Group 0: all positives caught
    preds_eo2[0] = 1
    preds_eo2[1] = 1
    preds_eo2[2] = 0
    preds_eo2[3] = 0
    true_eo2[0] = 1
    true_eo2[1] = 1
    true_eo2[2] = 0
    true_eo2[3] = 0
    prot_eo2[0] = 0
    prot_eo2[1] = 0
    prot_eo2[2] = 0
    prot_eo2[3] = 0
    // Group 1: only half of positives caught
    preds_eo2[4] = 1
    preds_eo2[5] = 0
    preds_eo2[6] = 0
    preds_eo2[7] = 0
    true_eo2[4] = 1
    true_eo2[5] = 1
    true_eo2[6] = 0
    true_eo2[7] = 0
    prot_eo2[4] = 1
    prot_eo2[5] = 1
    prot_eo2[6] = 1
    prot_eo2[7] = 1
    let eo_unequal = equalized_odds_t(preds_eo2, true_eo2, prot_eo2, 8)
    if abs_f64(eo_unequal - 0.5) < 0.001 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 5: Disparate impact ratio = 1 when both groups have same approval rate
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_di: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_di: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    // Both groups: 50% positive (2/4)
    preds_di[0] = 1
    preds_di[1] = 1
    preds_di[2] = 0
    preds_di[3] = 0
    preds_di[4] = 1
    preds_di[5] = 1
    preds_di[6] = 0
    preds_di[7] = 0
    prot_di[0] = 0
    prot_di[1] = 0
    prot_di[2] = 0
    prot_di[3] = 0
    prot_di[4] = 1
    prot_di[5] = 1
    prot_di[6] = 1
    prot_di[7] = 1
    let di_equal = disparate_impact_t(preds_di, prot_di, 8)
    if abs_f64(di_equal - 1.0) < 0.001 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 6: Disparate impact — 4/5 rule check
    // Group 0: 8/10 → rate = 0.8; Group 1: 4/10 → rate = 0.4
    // ratio = 0.4/0.8 = 0.5 < 0.8 (EEOC violation)
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_di2: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_di2: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    // Group 0 (indices 0–9): 8 positive, 2 negative
    var q: i32 = 0
    while q < 8 {
        preds_di2[q as usize] = 1
        prot_di2[q as usize] = 0
        q = q + 1
    }
    prot_di2[8] = 0
    prot_di2[9] = 0
    // Group 1 (indices 10–19): 4 positive, 6 negative
    var r: i32 = 10
    while r < 14 {
        preds_di2[r as usize] = 1
        prot_di2[r as usize] = 1
        r = r + 1
    }
    var s: i32 = 14
    while s < 20 {
        prot_di2[s as usize] = 1
        s = s + 1
    }
    let di_ratio = disparate_impact_t(preds_di2, prot_di2, 20)
    // Expected: min(0.4/0.8, 0.8/0.4) = min(0.5, 2.0) = 0.5
    // The 4/5 rule: ratio < 0.8 → adverse impact
    if di_ratio < 0.8 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 7: Chouldechova — equal base rates → impossibility NOT triggered
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    let chould_equal = chouldechova_check_t(0.8, 0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 0.5, 0.5)
    if chould_equal == 0 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 8: Chouldechova — different base rates (0.2 vs 0.7) → impossibility triggered
    // When base rates differ by > 0.1, equalized FPR+FNR+PPV is impossible.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    let chould_diff = chouldechova_check_t(0.8, 0.1, 0.8, 0.1, 0.2, 0.7)
    if chould_diff == 1 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 9: Chouldechova — equal FPR/FNR but unequal PPV (due to base rate difference)
    // base0=0.1, base1=0.5; shared TPR=0.8, FPR=0.2
    // PPV0 = 0.8*0.1 / (0.8*0.1 + 0.2*0.9) = 0.08/0.26 ≈ 0.308
    // PPV1 = 0.8*0.5 / (0.8*0.5 + 0.2*0.5) = 0.4/0.5 = 0.8
    // ppv_diff ≈ 0.49 > 0.05, fpr_diff=0, tpr_diff=0 → triggered
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    let chould_ppv = chouldechova_check_t(0.8, 0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 0.1, 0.5)
    if chould_ppv == 1 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Test 10: Disparate impact = 0 when one group has zero positive rate
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    var preds_di3: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    var prot_di3: [i32; 256] = [0; 256]
    // Group 0: all positive
    preds_di3[0] = 1
    preds_di3[1] = 1
    prot_di3[0] = 0
    prot_di3[1] = 0
    // Group 1: all negative (default 0)
    prot_di3[2] = 1
    prot_di3[3] = 1
    let di_zero = disparate_impact_t(preds_di3, prot_di3, 4)
    if abs_f64(di_zero) < 0.001 {
        passed = passed + 1.0
    } else {
        failed = failed + 1.0
    }

    // Return: positive = all passed
    passed - failed
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/ffi/test_cstring.sio ===
//@ ignore BLOCKED: uses unsafe blocks, raw pointer types (*const u8), and byte literals (b'..') which are not supported in the current JIT
/// Testes para ffi::cstring: roundtrip e null-termination

module ffi::test_cstring;

use ffi::cstring::{cstring_from_str, str_from_cstring};

fn test_roundtrip() {
    let orig = "hello world";
    let ptr = cstring_from_str(orig);
    let round = str_from_cstring(ptr);
    assert(round == orig);
    println("test_roundtrip: PASSED");
}

fn test_null_terminator() {
    let orig = "test";
    let ptr = cstring_from_str(orig);
    unsafe {
        assert(ptr.read() == b't');
        assert(*(ptr.offset((orig.len() as isize))) == 0u8);
    }
    println("test_null_terminator: PASSED");
}

fn test_empty() {
    let orig = "";
    let ptr = cstring_from_str(orig);
    let round = str_from_cstring(ptr);
    assert(round == orig);
    unsafe {
        assert(*(ptr.offset(0isize)) == 0u8);
    }
    println("test_empty: PASSED");
}

//@ ignore BLOCKED: uses unsafe blocks, raw pointer types (*const/*mut), and usize indexing which are not supported in the current JIT

/// Tests for slice_from_raw_parts FFI helpers
///
/// These tests verify the raw pointer to slice conversion intrinsics work
/// correctly across the FFI boundary.

module ffi::test_slice;

use ffi::{slice_from_raw_parts, slice_from_raw_parts_mut};

// =============================================================================
// Test: Basic immutable slice from raw parts
// =============================================================================

/// Test creating an immutable slice from a raw pointer
fn test_slice_from_raw_parts_basic() {
    // Create a stack-allocated array and get a raw pointer
    let data: [u8; 4] = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    let ptr: *const u8 = &data[0] as *const u8
    let len: usize = 4

    // Convert to slice using the intrinsic
    let slice = unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts(ptr, len) }

    // Verify the slice contents
    assert(slice.len() == 4)
    assert(slice[0] == 1)
    assert(slice[1] == 2)
    assert(slice[2] == 3)
    assert(slice[3] == 4)

    println("test_slice_from_raw_parts_basic: PASSED")
}

// =============================================================================
// Test: Mutable slice from raw parts
// =============================================================================

/// Test creating a mutable slice from a raw pointer and modifying it
fn test_slice_from_raw_parts_mut_basic() {
    // Create a mutable array
    var data: [u8; 4] = [10, 20, 30, 40]
    let ptr: *mut u8 = &data[0] as *mut u8
    let len: usize = 4

    // Convert to mutable slice
    let slice = unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts_mut(ptr, len) }

    // Modify through the slice
    slice[0] = 100
    slice[3] = 200

    // Verify modifications propagated to original array
    assert(data[0] == 100)
    assert(data[3] == 200)

    println("test_slice_from_raw_parts_mut_basic: PASSED")
}

// =============================================================================

/// Test creating empty slices (zero length)
fn test_empty_slice() {
    let data: [u8; 4] = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    let ptr: *const u8 = &data[0] as *const u8

    // Zero-length slice should work
    let empty = unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts(ptr, 0) }
    assert(empty.len() == 0)

    println("test_empty_slice: PASSED")
}

// =============================================================================
// Test: Slice with offset pointer
// =============================================================================

/// Test creating a slice from an offset into an array
fn test_slice_with_offset() {
    let data: [u8; 8] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]

    // Get pointer to element at index 2
    let ptr: *const u8 = &data[2] as *const u8
    let len: usize = 4

    let slice = unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts(ptr, len) }

    let ptr: *mut i32 = &data[0] as *mut i32
    let len: usize = 4

    let slice = unsafe { slice_from_raw_parts_mut(ptr, len) }

    // Sum using the slice
    var sum: i32 = 0
    var i: usize = 0

fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

fn run_tests() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic, IO {

    let mp0 = motion_params_new()

    ts[1] = 5.0
    ts[2] = 5.0
    ts[3] = 5.0
    ts[4] = 5.0

    x[2] = 3.0

    x[4] = 5.0
    y[0] = 1.0
    y[1] = 2.0

}
