fn abs_f(x: f64) -> f64 { if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x } }

// ============================================================================
// Probability [0, 1]
// ============================================================================

fn test_probability_valid() {
    assert(probability_is_valid(0.0))
    assert(probability_is_valid(0.5))
    assert(probability_is_valid(1.0))
    assert(!probability_is_valid(1.001))
    assert(!probability_is_valid(0.0 - 0.001))
}

fn test_probability_try_new() {
    let r1 = probability_try_new(0.5)
    assert(r1.ok)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(r1.value) - 0.5) < 1.0e-15)

    let r2 = probability_try_new(2.0)
    assert(!r2.ok)

    let r3 = probability_try_new(0.0 - 0.1)
    assert(!r3.ok)
}

fn test_probability_clamp() {
    let p1 = probability_clamp(1.5)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(p1) - 1.0) < 1.0e-15)

    let p2 = probability_clamp(0.0 - 0.5)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(p2)) < 1.0e-15)

    let p3 = probability_clamp(0.3)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(p3) - 0.3) < 1.0e-15)
}

// ============================================================================
// Conversions
// ============================================================================

fn test_conversions() with Div, Panic {
    let p = probability_try_new(0.5)
    assert(p.ok)

    // probability → percentage: 0.5 → 50.0
    let pct = probability_to_percentage(p.value)
    assert(abs_f(percentage_value(pct) - 50.0) < 1.0e-10)

    // percentage → probability: 50.0 → 0.5
    let p2 = percentage_to_probability(pct)
    assert(abs_f(probability_value(p2) - 0.5) < 1.0e-10)

    // probability → unit interval: identity
    let ui = probability_to_unit_interval(p.value)
    assert(abs_f(unit_interval_value(ui) - 0.5) < 1.0e-15)

    // celsius → kelvin: 0 C = 273.15 K
    let k = temperature_celsius_to_kelvin(0.0)
    assert(abs_f(k - 273.15) < 1.0e-10)

    // kelvin → celsius: 300 K = 26.85 C
    let t = temperature_try_new(300.0)
    assert(t.ok)
    let c = temperature_kelvin_to_celsius(t.value)
    assert(abs_f(c - 26.85) < 1.0e-10)

    // positive → concentration: identity
    let pos = positive_try_new(1.5)
    assert(pos.ok)
    let conc = positive_to_concentration(pos.value)
    assert(abs_f(concentration_value(conc) - 1.5) < 1.0e-15)
}

// Main
// ============================================================================

pub fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    test_probability_valid()
    test_probability_try_new()
    test_probability_clamp()
    test_positive_valid()
    test_positive_try_new()
    test_positive_clamp()
    test_non_negative_valid()
    test_non_negative_try_new()
    test_non_negative_clamp()
    test_percentage_valid()
    test_percentage_try_new()
    test_percentage_clamp()
    test_non_zero_valid()
    test_non_zero_try_new()
    test_concentration_valid()
    test_concentration_try_new()
    test_concentration_clamp()
    test_temperature_valid()
    test_temperature_try_new()
    test_temperature_clamp()
    test_unit_interval_valid()
    test_unit_interval_try_new()
    test_unit_interval_clamp()
    test_conversions()
    println("PASS: types/refinement — all tests passed")
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/util/test_log_path_cmp.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// E2E: stdlib/log, stdlib/path, stdlib/cmp
//
// Log:  append 5 entries at different levels, filter by WARN, count
// Path: join "src" + "main.sio" → "src/main.sio", extension → "sio", parent → "src"
// Cmp:  ordering, clamp, approx_eq

use log::lib::*;
use path::lib::*;
use cmp::lib::*;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers for building paths from byte slices
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn make_path_3(a: u8, b: u8, c: u8) -> Path {
    var p = path_new()
    p.data[0] = a
    p.data[1] = b
    p.data[2] = c
    p.len = 3
    p
}

fn make_path_8(a: u8, b: u8, c: u8, d: u8, e: u8, f: u8, g: u8, h: u8) -> Path {
    var p = path_new()
    p.data[0] = a
    p.data[1] = b
    p.data[2] = c
    p.data[3] = d
    p.data[4] = e
    p.data[5] = f
    p.data[6] = g
    p.data[7] = h
    p.len = 8
    p
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Log tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_log() -> i32 {
    // Level constants
    if LOG_TRACE() != 0 { return 101 }
    if LOG_DEBUG() != 1 { return 102 }
    if LOG_INFO()  != 2 { return 103 }
    if LOG_WARN()  != 3 { return 104 }
    if LOG_ERROR() != 4 { return 105 }
    if LOG_FATAL() != 5 { return 106 }

    // Create buffer with min_level = INFO (2)
    var buf = log_buffer_new(LOG_INFO())

    // Append 5 entries at levels: TRACE(filtered), DEBUG(filtered), INFO, WARN, ERROR
    let buf1 = log_append(buf, LOG_TRACE(), 10, 1.0, 1000)  // filtered
    let buf2 = log_append(buf1, LOG_DEBUG(), 20, 2.0, 1001) // filtered
    let buf3 = log_append(buf2, LOG_INFO(),  30, 3.0, 1002)
    let buf4 = log_append(buf3, LOG_WARN(),  40, 4.0, 1003)
    let buf5 = log_append(buf4, LOG_ERROR(), 50, 5.0, 1004)

    // 3 entries should be stored (INFO, WARN, ERROR)
    if log_count(&buf5) != 3 { return 107 }

    // Count by level
    if log_count_level(&buf5, LOG_INFO())  != 1 { return 108 }
    if log_count_level(&buf5, LOG_WARN())  != 1 { return 109 }
    if log_count_level(&buf5, LOG_ERROR()) != 1 { return 110 }
    if log_count_level(&buf5, LOG_TRACE()) != 0 { return 111 }

    // Last value should be 5.0 (the ERROR entry)
    let lv = log_last_value(&buf5)
    if lv != 5.0 { return 112 }

    // Filter by WARN
    var warn_buf = log_buffer_new(LOG_WARN())
    log_filter_level(&buf5, LOG_WARN(), &! warn_buf)
    if log_count(&warn_buf) != 1 { return 113 }
    if log_count_level(&warn_buf, LOG_WARN()) != 1 { return 114 }

    // Clear
    let cleared = log_clear(buf5)
    if log_count(&cleared) != 0 { return 115 }

    0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Path tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_path() -> i32 {
    // Build "src" (115, 114, 99) and "main.sio" (109,97,105,110,46,115,105,111)
    // ASCII: s=115 r=114 c=99 m=109 a=97 i=105 n=110 .=46 s=115 i=105 o=111
    let src_path  = make_path_3(115, 114, 99)                           // "src"
    let main_path = make_path_8(109, 97, 105, 110, 46, 115, 105, 111)  // "main.sio"

    // path_join: "src" + "main.sio" → "src/main.sio"
    let joined = path_join(&src_path, &main_path)
    // Expected length: 3 + 1 + 8 = 12
    if joined.len != 12 { return 201 }
    // Check separator at index 3
    if joined.data[3] != 47 { return 202 }  // '/'

    // path_extension: "main.sio" → "sio"
    let ext = path_extension(&joined)
    // "sio" = 3 bytes
    if ext.len != 3 { return 203 }
    if ext.data[0] != 115 { return 204 }  // 's'
    if ext.data[1] != 105 { return 205 }  // 'i'
    if ext.data[2] != 111 { return 206 }  // 'o'

    // path_parent: "src/main.sio" → "src"
    let parent = path_parent(&joined)
    if parent.len != 3 { return 207 }
    if !path_eq(&parent, &src_path) { return 208 }

    // path_filename: "src/main.sio" → "main.sio"
    let fname = path_filename(&joined)
    if fname.len != 8 { return 209 }
    if !path_eq(&fname, &main_path) { return 210 }

    // path_stem: "src/main.sio" → "main"
    let stem = path_stem(&joined)
    // "main" = 4 bytes (109,97,105,110)
    if stem.len != 4 { return 211 }
    if stem.data[0] != 109 { return 212 }  // 'm'
    if stem.data[3] != 110 { return 213 }  // 'n'

    // path_is_absolute: "src" is not absolute, "/src" would be
    if path_is_absolute(&src_path) { return 214 }

    // Build "/src" = (47, 115, 114, 99)
    var abs_path = path_new()
    abs_path.data[0] = 47   // '/'
    abs_path.data[1] = 115  // 's'
    abs_path.data[2] = 114  // 'r'
    abs_path.data[3] = 99   // 'c'
    abs_path.len = 4
    if !path_is_absolute(&abs_path) { return 215 }

    // path_eq
    let src2 = make_path_3(115, 114, 99)
    if !path_eq(&src_path, &src2) { return 216 }
    if path_eq(&src_path, &main_path) { return 217 }

    0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cmp tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn test_cmp() -> i32 {
    // cmp_i64
    if cmp_i64(1, 2) != -1 { return 301 }
    if cmp_i64(2, 2) !=  0 { return 302 }
    if cmp_i64(3, 2) !=  1 { return 303 }

    // cmp_f64
    if cmp_f64(1.0, 2.0) != -1 { return 304 }
    if cmp_f64(2.0, 2.0) !=  0 { return 305 }
    if cmp_f64(3.0, 2.0) !=  1 { return 306 }

    // min/max i64
    if min_i64(3, 7) != 3 { return 307 }
    if max_i64(3, 7) != 7 { return 308 }
    if min_i64(-5, 0) != -5 { return 309 }
    if max_i64(-5, 0) != 0 { return 310 }

    // min/max f64
    if min_f64(1.5, 2.5) != 1.5 { return 311 }
    if max_f64(1.5, 2.5) != 2.5 { return 312 }

    // clamp_f64
    if clamp_f64(5.0, 0.0, 3.0) != 3.0 { return 313 }
    if clamp_f64(-1.0, 0.0, 3.0) != 0.0 { return 314 }
    if clamp_f64(1.5, 0.0, 3.0) != 1.5 { return 315 }

    // clamp_i64
    if clamp_i64(10, 0, 5) != 5 { return 316 }
    if clamp_i64(-3, 0, 5) != 0 { return 317 }
    if clamp_i64(3, 0, 5)  != 3 { return 318 }

    // approx_eq
    if !approx_eq(1.0, 1.0, 1e-10) { return 319 }
    if !approx_eq(1.0, 1.0 + 1e-11, 1e-10) { return 320 }
    if approx_eq(1.0, 2.0, 1e-10) { return 321 }

    // sign_f64
    if sign_f64(-3.0) != -1.0 { return 322 }
    if sign_f64(0.0)  !=  0.0 { return 323 }
    if sign_f64(7.0)  !=  1.0 { return 324 }

    0
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Entry point
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn main() -> i32 {
    let r1 = test_log()
    if r1 != 0 { return r1 }

    let r2 = test_path()
    if r2 != 0 { return r2 }

    let r3 = test_cmp()
    if r3 != 0 { return r3 }

    0
}


// === FILE: tests/stdlib/yaml/test_yaml.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! tests/stdlib/yaml/test_yaml.sio
//!
//! Tests for yaml::parser — minimal flat YAML parser.
//!
//! Design notes:
//! - Sounio JIT: &!Struct field mutations propagate; &!array does NOT.
//! - After any &!doc call, use direct field access (doc.types[i], doc.num_vals[i], etc.).
//! - String retrieval: use doc.str_vals[idx] directly; yaml_get_string out-copy is JIT-best-effort.

use yaml::parser::{
    YAML_STRING, YAML_NUMBER, YAML_BOOL, YAML_NULL,
    YamlDoc,
    yaml_doc_new,
    yaml_parse,
    yaml_get_string, yaml_get_number, yaml_get_bool,
    yaml_doc_count,
    yaml_self_test,
}

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn near(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < 0.0001
}

struct RawBuf {
    data: [u8; 4096],
    len:  i32,
}

// Build test YAML:
//   name: sounio\ncount: 42\npi: 3.14\nactive: true\nnone: null\n
fn mk_basic_yaml() -> RawBuf {
    var b = RawBuf { data: [0; 4096], len: 0 }
    // "name: sounio\n"
    b.data[0]  = 110u8  // n
    b.data[1]  = 97u8   // a
    b.data[2]  = 109u8  // m
    b.data[3]  = 101u8  // e
    b.data[4]  = 58u8   // :
    b.data[5]  = 32u8   // space
    b.data[6]  = 115u8  // s
    b.data[7]  = 111u8  // o
    b.data[8]  = 117u8  // u
    b.data[9]  = 110u8  // n
    b.data[10] = 105u8  // i
    b.data[11] = 111u8  // o
    b.data[12] = 10u8   // \n
    // "count: 42\n"
    b.data[13] = 99u8   // c
    b.data[14] = 111u8  // o
    b.data[15] = 117u8  // u
    b.data[16] = 110u8  // n
    b.data[17] = 116u8  // t
    b.data[18] = 58u8   // :
    b.data[19] = 32u8   // space
    b.data[20] = 52u8   // 4
    b.data[21] = 50u8   // 2
    b.data[22] = 10u8   // \n
    // "pi: 3.14\n"
    b.data[23] = 112u8  // p
    b.data[24] = 105u8  // i
    b.data[25] = 58u8   // :
    b.data[26] = 32u8   // space
    b.data[27] = 51u8   // 3
    b.data[28] = 46u8   // .
    b.data[29] = 49u8   // 1
    b.data[30] = 52u8   // 4
    b.data[31] = 10u8   // \n
    // "active: true\n"
    b.data[32] = 97u8   // a
    b.data[33] = 99u8   // c
    b.data[34] = 116u8  // t
    b.data[35] = 105u8  // i
    b.data[36] = 118u8  // v
    b.data[37] = 101u8  // e
    b.data[38] = 58u8   // :
    b.data[39] = 32u8   // space
    b.data[40] = 116u8  // t
    b.data[41] = 114u8  // r
    b.data[42] = 117u8  // u
    b.data[43] = 101u8  // e
    b.data[44] = 10u8   // \n
    // "none: null\n"
    b.data[45] = 110u8  // n
    b.data[46] = 111u8  // o
    b.data[47] = 110u8  // n
    b.data[48] = 101u8  // e
    b.data[49] = 58u8   // :
    b.data[50] = 32u8   // space
    b.data[51] = 110u8  // n
    b.data[52] = 117u8  // u
    b.data[53] = 108u8  // l
    b.data[54] = 108u8  // l
    b.data[55] = 10u8   // \n
    b.len = 56
    b
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: type constants
// ============================================================================

fn test_type_constants() -> i32 {
    var fail: i32 = 0
    if YAML_STRING() != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if YAML_NUMBER() != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if YAML_BOOL()   != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if YAML_NULL()   != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }
    fail
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: parse name/count/pi/active/none
// ============================================================================

fn test_basic_parse() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0
    let buf = mk_basic_yaml()
    var doc = yaml_doc_new()
    let res = yaml_parse(&buf.data, buf.len, &!doc)
    if res != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.count != 5 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 0: name = "sounio"  (bare string)
    if doc.types[0] != 0 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_STRING
    if doc.str_lens[0] != 6 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if doc.str_vals[0][0] != 115u8 { fail = fail + 1 }  // 's'

    // Slot 1: count = 42  (number)
    if doc.types[1] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_NUMBER
    if !near(doc.num_vals[1], 42.0) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 2: pi = 3.14  (number)
    if doc.types[2] != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_NUMBER
    if !near(doc.num_vals[2], 3.14) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 3: active = true  (bool)
    if doc.types[3] != 2 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_BOOL
    if doc.num_vals[3] < 0.5 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Slot 4: none = null  (null)
    if doc.types[4] != 3 { fail = fail + 1 }  // YAML_NULL

    fail
}

// ============================================================================
// Test: accessor functions
// ============================================================================

fn test_get_accessors() -> i32 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var fail: i32 = 0
    let buf = mk_basic_yaml()
    var doc = yaml_doc_new()
    yaml_parse(&buf.data, buf.len, &!doc)

    // yaml_get_number for "count"
    var k_count: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    k_count[0] = 99u8   // c
    k_count[1] = 111u8  // o
    k_count[2] = 117u8  // u
    k_count[3] = 110u8  // n
    k_count[4] = 116u8  // t
    let cnt = yaml_get_number(&doc, &k_count, 5)
    if !near(cnt, 42.0) { fail = fail + 1 }

    // yaml_get_bool for "active"
    var k_active: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    k_active[0] = 97u8   // a
    k_active[1] = 99u8   // c
    k_active[2] = 116u8  // t
    k_active[3] = 105u8  // i
    k_active[4] = 118u8  // v
    k_active[5] = 101u8  // e
    let ab = yaml_get_bool(&doc, &k_active, 6)
    if ab != 1 { fail = fail + 1 }

    // Missing key → -1 for bool, 0.0 for number
    var k_miss: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
    k_miss[0] = 122u8  // z
    if yaml_get_bool(&doc, &k_miss, 1) != 0 - 1 { fail = fail + 1 }
    if !near(yaml_get_number(&doc, &k_miss, 1), 0.0) { fail = fail + 1 }

    fail
}

// === FILE: tests/sync/mutex_basic.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Basic smoke test for stdlib/sync/mutex — verifies real pthread lock/unlock cycle.

use sync::mutex::*;

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    var m = mutex_new()

    // Lock and unlock — must not crash or deadlock
    mutex_lock(&! m)
    mutex_unlock(&! m)

    // try_lock should succeed when unheld, then unlock
    let got = mutex_try_lock(&! m)
    if got {
        mutex_unlock(&! m)
    }

    // Clean up
    mutex_destroy(&! m)

    println("mutex ok")
    return 0
}

// === FILE: tests/ui/ownership/branch_linear.sio ===

// === FILE: tests/ui/ownership/call_boundary_failed_explicit_release_guard_mirror.sio ===
//@ compile-fail
//@ error-pattern: more than once
//@ error-pattern: already borrowed
//@ description: Failed explicit exclusive call-boundary borrow must not release an existing exclusive borrow

fn take_exclusive(r: &!i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    *r
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut {
    var x: i64 = 1
    let held = &!x

    // Explicit exclusive borrow in call arg fails under the active exclusive borrow.
    let a = take_exclusive(&!x)

    // Must still fail: failed call-site borrow should not clear `held`.
    let s = &x

    if a >= 0 && *s >= 0 {
        return 0
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: tests/ui/ownership/call_boundary_failed_explicit_release_guard.sio ===
//@ compile-fail
//@ error-pattern: already borrowed
//@ error-pattern: more than once
//@ description: Failed explicit call-boundary borrow must not release an existing exclusive borrow

fn take_shared(r: &i64) -> i64 {
    *r
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut {
    var x: i64 = 1
    let held = &!x

    // Explicit shared borrow in call arg fails under the active exclusive borrow.
    let a = take_shared(&x)

    // Must still fail: failed call-site borrow should not clear `held`.
    let again = &!x

    if a >= 0 && *again >= 0 {
        return 0
    }
    0
}


// === FILE: tests/ui/ownership/call_boundary_failed_implicit_release_guard.sio ===
//@ compile-fail
//@ ignore
//@ error-pattern: cannot borrow sharedly while exclusive borrow is active
//@ error-pattern: cannot borrow exclusively while other borrows are active
//@ description: BLOCKED: pinned binary does not support implicit call-boundary borrow syntax (f(&T) <- x)

fn take_shared(r: &i64) -> i64 {
    *r
}

fn main() -> i32 with Mut {
    var x: i64 = 1
    let held = &!x

    // This implicit borrow fails because `held` keeps x exclusively borrowed.
    let a = take_shared(x)

    // Must still fail: the failed call above must not drop `held`.
    let again = &!x

    if a >= 0 && *again >= 0 {
        return 0
    }
    0
}

// === FILE: tests/verify-ir/call_a.sio ===
// Test equivalent function calls: direct order
fn helper(x: i64) -> i64 {
    x * 2
}

fn compute(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    helper(a) + helper(b)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    let result = compute(3, 4)
    if result == 14 {
        0
    } else {
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: tests/verify-ir/call_b.sio ===
// Test equivalent function calls: reversed order with commutative addition
fn helper(x: i64) -> i64 {
    x * 2
}

fn compute(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
    helper(b) + helper(a)
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    let result = compute(3, 4)
    if result == 14 {
        0
    } else {
        1
    }
}

fn fib(n: i64) -> i64 {
    var a: i64 = 0
    var b: i64 = 1
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        var t: i64 = a + b
        a = b
        b = t
        i = i + 1
    }
    a
}
fn main() -> i64 { fib(10) }

// === FILE: examples/advanced_glm_optimization.sio ===
// Advanced GLM-4.7 Optimization Demo
// 
// Este exemplo demonstra as novas otimizações avançadas integradas ao GLM-4.7:
// - Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO)
// - Auto-vectorization com ML
// - Interprocedural optimizations
// - Memory hierarchy optimization
// - Advanced epistemic optimizations

import stdlib.math.*

// Função com oportunidades de Profile-Guided Optimization
fn hot_path_computation(n: i32) -> Knowledge<i32> {
    // Este é um hot path - executado frequentemente
    if n < 10 {
        return Knowledge::new(n, 0, 1, "hot_path_base")
    }
    
    // Loop com oportunidades de auto-vectorization
    let mut result = Knowledge::new(0, 0, 1, "accumulator")
    for i in 0..n {
        // Padrão ideal para SIMD
        let step = i * 2 + 1
        let term = step * step + 1
        
        result = result + Knowledge::new(term, 0.1, 0.95, "iteration")
    }
    
    result
}

// Função cold path - raramente executada
fn cold_path_rare_calculation(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.001 {
        // Código rarely executed - candidato para PGO cold path
        return 0.0
    }
    
    // Algoritmo complexo mas raramente usado
    let mut sum = 0.0
    for i in 0..1000 {
        sum = sum + (x * x).sin() + (x * x).cos()
    }
    
    sum / 1000.0
}

// Função com oportunidades de interprocedural optimization
fn small_helper(x: i32) -> Knowledge<i32> {
    // Função pequena - boa candidate para inlining
    Knowledge::new(x * 2, 0.1, 0.9, "helper")
}

fn large_computation(data: i32[]) -> Knowledge<i32> {
    let mut total = Knowledge::new(0, 0, 1, "accumulator")
    
    // Calls small_helper many times - good for IPO
    for i in 0..data.len() {
        let processed = small_helper(data[i])
        total = total + processed
        
        // Complex logic that benefits from ML guidance
        if processed.uncertainty > 0.5 {
            total = total * Knowledge::new(1.1, 0.01, 0.95, "uncertainty_adjustment")
        }
    }
    
    total
}

// Função com memory hierarchy optimization opportunities
fn memory_intensive_computation(size: i32) -> Knowledge<f64> {
    // Arrays grandes - boas oportunidades de cache optimization
    let mut array_a = zero_array<f64>(size)
    let mut array_b = zero_array<f64>(size)
    
    // Inicialização com padrões de acesso previsíveis
    for i in 0..size {
        array_a[i] = Knowledge::new(
            (i as f64) * 0.1,
            0.01,
            0.95,
            format!("array_a_{}", i)
        )
        array_b[i] = Knowledge::new(
            ((size - i) as f64) * 0.05,
            0.02,
            0.92,
            format!("array_b_{}", i)
        )
    }
    
    // Computação com access patterns favoráveis ao cache
    let mut result = Knowledge::new(0.0, 0, 1, "final_result")
    
    // Loop com access patterns que podem ser otimizados pelo GLM
    for i in 0..size {
        // Sequential access - good para cache
        let product = array_a[i] * array_b[i]
        
        // Nested loops com opportunities para vectorization
        for j in 0..10 {
            let offset = (i * 10 + j) % size
            let term = array_a[offset] + product * Knowledge::new(j as f64, 0.01, 0.9, "loop_term")
            result = result + term
        }
    }
    
    result
}

// Função com advanced epistemic optimizations
fn epistemic_scientific_simulation(num_measurements: i32, num_simulations: i32) -> Knowledge<f64> {
    let mut total_uncertainty = Knowledge::new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, "total_accumulator")
    
    for sim in 0..num_simulations {
        let mut simulation_result = Knowledge::new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, "simulation_accumulator")
        
        for meas in 0..num_measurements {
            // Simulação com propagação de incerteza complexa
            let measurement = Knowledge::new(
                (sim * num_measurements + meas) as f64,
                0.5 + (meas as f64) * 0.1,
                0.85 + (sim as f64) * 0.01,
                format!("measurement_{}_{}", sim, meas)
            )
            
            // Operations que benefit de epistemic-aware optimization
            let processed = measurement * measurement + Knowledge::new(1.0, 0.1, 0.9, "transformation")
            
            // Uncertainty-aware parallelization opportunity
            if processed.confidence > 0.8 {
                simulation_result = simulation_result + processed
            } else {
                // Lower confidence operations might need special handling
                simulation_result = simulation_result + processed * Knowledge::new(0.9, 0.05, 0.95, "confidence_adjustment")
            }
        }
        
        // Provenance chain tracking
        let adjusted_result = simulation_result * Knowledge::new(1.0 / num_measurements as f64, 0.02, 0.9, "normalization")
        total_uncertainty = total_uncertainty + adjusted_result
    }
    
    // Final confidence-guided decision
    if total_uncertainty.confidence > 0.9 {
        total_uncertainty
    } else {
        // Apply additional epistemic optimization
        total_uncertainty * Knowledge::new(1.1, 0.05, 0.95, "final_adjustment")
    }
}

// Função com loop nest optimization opportunities
fn nested_loop_computation(matrix_size: i32) -> Knowledge<f64> {
    let mut matrix = zero_matrix<f64>(matrix_size, matrix_size)
    
    // Initialize matrix com patterns que benefit de polyhedral optimization
    for i in 0..matrix_size {
        for j in 0..matrix_size {
            matrix[i][j] = Knowledge::new(
                ((i + j) as f64) * 0.1,
                0.05,
                0.92,
                format!("matrix_init_{}_{}", i, j)
            )
        }
    }
    
    let mut result = Knowledge::new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, "matrix_result")
    
    // Nested loops com multiple optimization opportunities
    for i in 0..matrix_size {
        for j in 0..matrix_size {
            let mut element_sum = Knowledge::new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, "element_accumulator")
            
            // Inner loop com SIMD opportunities
            for k in 0..matrix_size {
                let term = matrix[i][k] * matrix[k][j]
                
                // Epistemic-aware loop optimization
                if term.confidence > 0.85 {
                    element_sum = element_sum + term
                } else {
                    // Apply uncertainty-aware optimization
                    element_sum = element_sum + term * Knowledge::new(0.95, 0.02, 0.9, "uncertainty_handling")
                }
            }
            
            result = result + element_sum
        }
    }
    
    result
}

// GPU kernel optimization demonstration
fn gpu_kernel_like_computation(data_size: i32) -> Knowledge<f64> {
    let mut result = Knowledge::new(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, "gpu_result")
    
    // Parallelizable computation com GPU optimization opportunities
    for i in 0..data_size {
        // Operations que benefit de GPU optimization
        let computation = Knowledge::new(
            (i as f64).sin() + (i as f64).cos(),
            0.1,
            0.88,
            format!("gpu_computation_{}", i)
        )
        
        // Memory coalescing opportunity
        result = result + computation
    }
    
    // Apply epistemic-aware GPU optimization
    result / Knowledge::new(data_size as f64, 0.01, 0.9, "gpu_normalization")
}

    println("🧠 Advanced GLM-4.7 Optimization Demo")
    println("========================================")
    
    // Test Profile-Guided Optimization
    println("\n🔥 Testing Profile-Guided Optimization...")

    // Test Epistemic Scientific Computing

// ===== 1. GERAÇÃO DE CÓDIGO BIOMÉDICO =====
fn demonstrate_biomedical_generation() {
    println("\n🧬 Geração de Código Biomédico");
    println("-------------------------------");
    
    // Simular carregamento do modelo BioMedLM
    println("Carregando BioMedLM/Galactica...");
    
    // Gerar modelo PK/PD
    let pk_model = generate_pk_model();
    println("✅ Modelo PK gerado:");
    println!("   Clearance: {}", pk_model.clearance);
    println!("   Volume: {}", pk_model.volume);
    
    // Simular simulação farmacológica
    let simulation_result = simulate_drug_concentration(&pk_model, 500.0, 24.0);
    println("✅ Simulação farmacológica:");
    println!("   Concentração em 24h: {} mg/L", simulation_result.concentration);
    println!("   Incerteza: ±{} mg/L", simulation_result.uncertainty);
    println!("   Confiança: {}%", simulation_result.confidence * 100.0);
}

struct PKModel {
    clearance: f64,
    volume: f64,
    dose: f64,
}

fn generate_pk_model() -> PKModel {
    // Código gerado pelo modelo BioMedLM
    PKModel {
        clearance: 15.0,
        volume: 45.0,
        dose: 500.0,
    }
}

struct SimulationResult {
    concentration: f64,
    uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn simulate_drug_concentration(model: &PKModel, dose: f64, time_hours: f64) -> SimulationResult {
    // Propagação de incerteza automática
    let cl = model.clearance;
    let v = model.volume;
    let kel = cl / v;  // constante de eliminação
    
    // Solução analítica: C(t) = (Dose/V) * exp(-kel*t)
    let concentration = (dose / v) * exp(-kel * time_hours);
    
    // Incerteza propagada automaticamente
    let uncertainty = concentration * 0.15;  // ~15% incerteza
    let confidence = 0.89;  // confiança baseada nos parâmetros
    
    SimulationResult {
        concentration,
        uncertainty,
        confidence,
    }
}

struct ProofResult {
    conclusion: String,
    confidence: f64,
    steps: Vec<String>,
}

fn prove_pythagorean_theorem() -> ProofResult {
    // Raciocínio gerado pelo Polymath
    let steps = vec![
        "Construir quadrados em cada lado".to_string(),
        "Área do quadrado grande = (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²".to_string(),
        "Decomposição alternativa: c² + 4 triângulos".to_string(),
        "Igualando e simplificando: a² + b² = c²".to_string(),
    ];
    
    ProofResult {
        conclusion: "Teorema de Pitágoras: a² + b² = c² ✅".to_string(),
        confidence: 0.97,
        steps,
    }
}

struct DerivativeResult {
    formula: String,
    numerical_uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn compute_derivative_uncertainty() -> DerivativeResult {
    // Cálculo com propagação de incerteza
    let base_uncertainty = 1e-10;
    let confidence = 0.995;  // Alta confiança em derivada numérica
    
    DerivativeResult {
        formula: "f'(x) = 2x + 3".to_string(),
        numerical_uncertainty: base_uncertainty,
        confidence,
    }
}

struct EpistemicNeuralNetwork {
    layers: usize,
    activation: String,
    weights: Vec<Vec<f64>>,
}

impl EpistemicNeuralNetwork {
    fn predict(&self, inputs: &[f64]) -> PredictionResult {
        // Forward pass com propagação de incerteza
        var output = 0.0
        var i = 0
        for input in inputs {
            if i < self.weights.len() {
                let weight = self.weights[i][0]
                output += input * weight
            }
            i += 1
        }
        
        // Aplicar ativação
        output = activation_relu(output);
        
        // Calcular incerteza epistêmica
        let epistemic_uncertainty = output * 0.1;
        let confidence = 0.87;
        
        PredictionResult {
            value: output,
            epistemic_uncertainty,
            confidence,
        }
    }
}

struct PredictionResult {
    value: f64,
    epistemic_uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn create_epistemic_neural_network() -> EpistemicNeuralNetwork {
    EpistemicNeuralNetwork {
        layers: 3,
        activation: "ReLU".to_string(),
        weights: vec![
            vec![0.5, 0.3, 0.2],
            vec![0.7, 0.1, 0.1],
            vec![0.4, 0.4, 0.2],
        ],
    }
}

struct OptimizationResult {
    optimal_params: Vec<f64>,
    performance_gain: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn optimize_scientific_algorithm() -> OptimizationResult {
    // Otimização com awareness epistêmica
    let optimal_params = vec![1.414, 2.718, 3.141];
    let performance_gain = 0.23;  // 23% de melhoria
    let confidence = 0.91;
    
    OptimizationResult {
        optimal_params,
        performance_gain,
        confidence,
    }
}

// ===== 4. COMPUTAÇÃO EPISTÊMICA =====
fn demonstrate_epistemic_computing() {
    println("\n🌐 Computação Epistêmica");
    println("--------------------------");
    
    // Conhecimento com incerteza
    let measurement = EpistemicValue::new(42.0, 2.1, 0.94, "experimental");
    println("✅ Medição epistêmica:");
    println!("   Valor: {}", measurement.value);
    println!("   Incerteza: ±{}", measurement.uncertainty);
    println!("   Confiança: {}%", measurement.confidence * 100.0);
    println!("   Fonte: {}", measurement.provenance);
    
    // Propagação automática
    let propagated = propagate_uncertainty(&measurement);
    println("✅ Propagação automática:");
    println!("   Resultado: {}", propagated.value);
    println!("   Incerteza propagada: ±{}", propagated.uncertainty);
    println!("   Confiança mantida: {}%", propagated.confidence * 100.0);
}

struct EpistemicValue<T> {
    value: T,
    uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
    provenance: String,
}

impl<T> EpistemicValue<T> {
    fn new(value: T, uncertainty: f64, confidence: f64, source: &str) -> Self {
        EpistemicValue {
            value,
            uncertainty,
            confidence,
            provenance: source.to_string(),
        }
    }
}

fn propagate_uncertainty(input: &EpistemicValue<f64>) -> EpistemicValue<f64> {
    // Simular operação matemática
    let result_value = input.value * 2.0;
    let result_uncertainty = input.uncertainty * 2.0;  // Propagação linear
    let result_confidence = input.confidence * 0.98;  // Leve redução na confiança
    
    EpistemicValue::new(result_value, result_uncertainty, result_confidence, &input.provenance)
}

// ===== 5. OTIMIZAÇÃO COM INCERTEZA =====
fn demonstrate_optimization_with_uncertainty() {
    println("\n⚡ Otimização com Incerteza");
    println("------------------------------");
    
    // Função objetivo com incerteza
    let objective_function = create_epistemic_objective();
    println("✅ Função objetivo epistêmica criada");
    
    // Gradient descent epistêmico
    let optimization_result = epistemic_gradient_descent(&objective_function, vec![1.0, 1.0], 0.01, 100);
    println("✅ Otimização epistêmica:");
    println!("   Parâmetros finais: {:?}", optimization_result.final_params);
    println!("   Valor ótimo: {}", optimization_result.optimal_value);
    println!("   Incerteza no ótimo: ±{}", optimization_result.optimal_uncertainty);
    println!("   Confiança: {}%", optimization_result.confidence * 100.0);
    
    // Decisão baseada em confiança
    let decision = make_epistemic_decision(&optimization_result);
    println("✅ Decisão epistêmica:");
    println!("   Ação recomendada: {}", decision.recommended_action);
    println!("   Risco calculado: {}", decision.risk_assessment);
    println!("   Confiança na decisão: {}%", decision.decision_confidence * 100.0);
}

struct EpistemicObjective {
    function: String,
    domain: String,
}

fn create_epistemic_objective() -> EpistemicObjective {
    EpistemicObjective {
        function: "f(x) = (x-2)² + sin(x)".to_string(),
        domain: "x ∈ [0, 10]".to_string(),
    }
}

struct OptimizationResultEpistemic {
    final_params: Vec<f64>,
    optimal_value: f64,
    optimal_uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn epistemic_gradient_descent(
    objective: &EpistemicObjective,
    initial_params: Vec<f64>,
    learning_rate: f64,
    iterations: usize,
) -> OptimizationResultEpistemic {
    // Simular gradient descent epistêmico
    let mut params = initial_params;
    
    for _ in 0..iterations {
        // Gradiente com incerteza
        let gradient = compute_epistemic_gradient(&params);
        let step_size = learning_rate * gradient.confidence;
        let epistemic_step = step_size * gradient.uncertainty;
        
        // Atualizar parâmetros
        var idx = 0
        for param in params {
            if idx < gradient.values.len() {
                let grad = gradient.values[idx]
                param -= grad * epistemic_step
            }
            idx += 1
        }
    }
    
    // Resultado final
    let optimal_value = 0.123;  // Valor ótimo simulado
    let optimal_uncertainty = 0.045;  // Incerteza no ótimo
    let confidence = 0.89;
    
    OptimizationResultEpistemic {
        final_params: params,
        optimal_value,
        optimal_uncertainty,
        confidence,
    }
}

struct EpistemicGradient {
    values: Vec<f64>,
    uncertainty: f64,
    confidence: f64,
}

fn compute_epistemic_gradient(params: &[f64]) -> EpistemicGradient {
    // Calcular gradiente com incerteza
    EpistemicGradient {
        values: vec![-0.5, 0.3],  // Gradiente simulado
        uncertainty: 0.02,
        confidence: 0.92,
    }
}

struct EpistemicDecision {
    recommended_action: String,
    risk_assessment: String,
    decision_confidence: f64,
}

fn make_epistemic_decision(result: &OptimizationResultEpistemic) -> EpistemicDecision {
    // Tomar decisão baseada em confiança epistêmica
    if result.confidence > 0.85 {
        EpistemicDecision {
            recommended_action: "Implementar solução otimizada".to_string(),
            risk_assessment: "Baixo risco - alta confiança".to_string(),
            decision_confidence: 0.91,
        }
    } else {
        EpistemicDecision {
            recommended_action: "Mais testes necessários".to_string(),
            risk_assessment: "Risco moderado - confiança insuficiente".to_string(),
            decision_confidence: 0.67,
        }
    }
}

// Função auxiliar para ativação ReLU
fn activation_relu(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 0.0 {
        x
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// Função auxiliar para exponencial
fn exp(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Aproximação simples de exp(x)
    1.0 + x + (x * x) / 2.0 + (x * x * x) / 6.0
}

// === FILE: examples/algo/graph_demo.sio ===
//! Graph Algorithms Demonstration
//!
//! Demonstrates Dijkstra's shortest path, DFS, and BFS algorithms
//! on a sample weighted directed graph.

extern "C" {
    fn printf(fmt: *const u8, ...) -> i32;
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

struct Edge {
    to: usize,
    weight: f64,
}

const INFINITY: f64 = 1.0e308

// Dijkstra's algorithm for shortest paths
fn dijkstra(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], n: usize, source: usize) -> *mut f64 with Alloc, Panic {
    // Allocate distance and visited arrays
    let dist = malloc(n * 8) as *mut f64
    let visited = malloc(n) as *mut bool

    // Initialize distances
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        dist[i] = INFINITY
        visited[i] = false
        i = i + 1
    }

    dist[source] = 0.0

    var remaining = n

    while remaining > 0 {
        // Find unvisited node with minimum distance
        var min_dist = INFINITY
        var min_node: i64 = -1

        i = 0
        while i < n {
            if !visited[i] && dist[i] < min_dist {
                min_dist = dist[i]
                min_node = i as i64
            }
            i = i + 1
        }

        if min_node == -1 {
            break
        }

        let u = min_node as usize
        visited[u] = true
        remaining = remaining - 1

        // Relax edges from u
        let edges = adj[u]
        let count = edge_counts[u]
        var j: usize = 0
        while j < count {
            let edge = &edges[j]
            let v = edge.to
            let new_dist = dist[u] + edge.weight

            if new_dist < dist[v] {
                dist[v] = new_dist
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }

    free(visited as *mut u8)
    return dist
}

// Breadth-first search
fn bfs(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], n: usize, source: usize) -> *mut i64 with Alloc, Panic {
    let distances = malloc(n * 8) as *mut i64

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        distances[i] = -1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Simple queue using array
    let queue = malloc(n * 8) as *mut usize
    var head: usize = 0
    var tail: usize = 0

    distances[source] = 0
    queue[tail] = source
    tail = tail + 1

    while head < tail {
        let u = queue[head]
        head = head + 1

        let edges = adj[u]
        let count = edge_counts[u]
        var j: usize = 0
        while j < count {
            let v = edges[j].to
            if distances[v] == -1 {
                distances[v] = distances[u] + 1
                queue[tail] = v
                tail = tail + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
    }

    free(queue as *mut u8)
    return distances
}

// Depth-first search
fn dfs_visit(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], u: usize, visited: &!*mut bool) with Panic {
    visited[u] = true

    let edges = adj[u]
    let count = edge_counts[u]
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < count {
        let v = edges[i].to
        if !visited[v] {
            dfs_visit(adj, edge_counts, v, visited)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn dfs(adj: &[*const Edge], edge_counts: &[usize], n: usize, source: usize) -> *mut bool with Alloc, Panic {
    let visited = malloc(n) as *mut bool

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        visited[i] = false
        i = i + 1
    }

    dfs_visit(adj, edge_counts, source, &!visited)

    return visited
}

fn main() -> i32 with Alloc, Panic {
    printf("Graph Algorithms Demonstration\n".as_ptr())
    printf("===============================\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Build sample graph: 6 nodes (0-5)
    // Graph structure:
    //   0 -> 1 (2.0), 0 -> 2 (4.0)
    //   1 -> 2 (1.0), 1 -> 3 (7.0)
    //   2 -> 4 (3.0)
    //   3 -> 5 (1.0)
    //   4 -> 3 (2.0), 4 -> 5 (5.0)

    let n: usize = 6

    // Allocate edge arrays for each node
    let edges0 = malloc(2 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges0[0] = Edge { to: 1, weight: 2.0 }
    edges0[1] = Edge { to: 2, weight: 4.0 }

    let edges1 = malloc(2 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges1[0] = Edge { to: 2, weight: 1.0 }
    edges1[1] = Edge { to: 3, weight: 7.0 }

    let edges2 = malloc(1 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges2[0] = Edge { to: 4, weight: 3.0 }

    let edges3 = malloc(1 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges3[0] = Edge { to: 5, weight: 1.0 }

    let edges4 = malloc(2 * 16) as *mut Edge
    edges4[0] = Edge { to: 3, weight: 2.0 }
    edges4[1] = Edge { to: 5, weight: 5.0 }

    let edges5 = malloc(0) as *mut Edge

    // Build adjacency list
    let adj = [edges0 as *const Edge, edges1 as *const Edge, edges2 as *const Edge,
               edges3 as *const Edge, edges4 as *const Edge, edges5 as *const Edge]
    let edge_counts: [usize; 6] = [2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 0]

    printf("Graph structure (6 nodes, weighted edges):\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  0 -> 1 (2.0), 2 (4.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  1 -> 2 (1.0), 3 (7.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  2 -> 4 (3.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  3 -> 5 (1.0)\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  4 -> 3 (2.0), 5 (5.0)\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Run Dijkstra from node 0
    printf("1. Dijkstra's Shortest Paths (from node 0):\n".as_ptr())
    let dist = dijkstra(&adj, &edge_counts, n, 0)

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n {
        if dist[i] < INFINITY {
            printf("   Distance to node %zu: %.1f\n".as_ptr(), i, dist[i])
        } else {
            printf("   Distance to node %zu: ∞ (unreachable)\n".as_ptr(), i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("\n".as_ptr())

    // Run BFS from node 0
    printf("2. Breadth-First Search (from node 0):\n".as_ptr())
    let bfs_dist = bfs(&adj, &edge_counts, n, 0)

    i = 0
    while i < n {
        if bfs_dist[i] >= 0 {
            printf("   BFS distance to node %zu: %lld hops\n".as_ptr(), i, bfs_dist[i])
        } else {
            printf("   Node %zu: unreachable\n".as_ptr(), i)
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("\n".as_ptr())

    // Run DFS from node 0
    printf("3. Depth-First Search (from node 0):\n".as_ptr())
    let visited = dfs(&adj, &edge_counts, n, 0)

    printf("   Visited nodes: ".as_ptr())
    i = 0
    var first = true
    while i < n {
        if visited[i] {
            if !first {
                printf(", ".as_ptr())
            }
            printf("%zu".as_ptr(), i)
            first = false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Verify shortest path to node 5
    printf("Shortest path from 0 to 5:\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  Dijkstra distance: %.1f\n".as_ptr(), dist[5])
    printf("  Path: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5\n".as_ptr())
    printf("  (2.0 + 1.0 + 3.0 + 2.0 + 1.0 = 9.0)\n".as_ptr())

    // Clean up
    free(dist as *mut u8)
    free(bfs_dist as *mut u8)
    free(visited as *mut u8)
    free(edges0 as *mut u8)
    free(edges1 as *mut u8)
    free(edges2 as *mut u8)
    free(edges3 as *mut u8)
    free(edges4 as *mut u8)

    printf("\nGraph algorithms completed successfully!\n".as_ptr())
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/mandelbrot.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Mandelbrot Set: ASCII render at 80×40 resolution
//!
//! Demonstrates: f64 arithmetic, nested loops, complex iteration,
//! character output — zero external dependencies.
//!
//! Outputs a text-art rendering of the Mandelbrot set.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/mandelbrot.sio

const WIDTH: i64 = 78
const HEIGHT: i64 = 36
const MAX_ITER: i64 = 64

// Compute Mandelbrot escape count for point (cx, cy)
fn mandelbrot(cx: f64, cy: f64) -> i64 {
    var zx: f64 = 0.0
    var zy: f64 = 0.0
    var iter: i64 = 0
    while iter < MAX_ITER {
        let zx2 = zx * zx
        let zy2 = zy * zy
        if zx2 + zy2 > 4.0 {
            return iter
        }
        let new_zx = zx2 - zy2 + cx
        zy = 2.0 * zx * zy + cy
        zx = new_zx
        iter = iter + 1
    }
    MAX_ITER
}

// Map escape count to ASCII character
fn iter_to_char(n: i64) -> i64 {
    if n == MAX_ITER { return 64 }   // '@' = 64
    if n > 48 { return 35 }          // '#' = 35
    if n > 32 { return 43 }          // '+' = 43
    if n > 16 { return 46 }          // '.' = 46
    if n > 8  { return 58 }          // ':' = 58
    32                                // ' ' = 32
}

fn print_char(c: i64) with IO {
    if c == 64 { print("@") }
    else if c == 35 { print("#") }
    else if c == 43 { print("+") }
    else if c == 46 { print(".") }
    else if c == 58 { print(":") }
    else { print(" ") }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    print("Mandelbrot Set (")
    print_int(WIDTH)
    print("x")
    print_int(HEIGHT)
    print(", max_iter=")
    print_int(MAX_ITER)
    print(")\n")
    print("Region: x in [-2.5, 1.0], y in [-1.2, 1.2]\n\n")

    let x_min: f64 = -2.5
    let x_max: f64 =  1.0
    let y_min: f64 = -1.2
    let y_max: f64 =  1.2

    var row: i64 = 0
    while row < HEIGHT {
        let cy = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * (row as f64) / (HEIGHT as f64)
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < WIDTH {
            let cx = x_min + (x_max - x_min) * (col as f64) / (WIDTH as f64)
            let n = mandelbrot(cx, cy)
            print_char(iter_to_char(n))
            col = col + 1
        }
        print("\n")
        row = row + 1
    }

    // Count pixels in the set (escape == MAX_ITER)
    var in_set: i64 = 0
    row = 0
    while row < HEIGHT {
        let cy = y_max - (y_max - y_min) * (row as f64) / (HEIGHT as f64)
        var col: i64 = 0
        while col < WIDTH {
            let cx = x_min + (x_max - x_min) * (col as f64) / (WIDTH as f64)
            if mandelbrot(cx, cy) == MAX_ITER { in_set = in_set + 1 }
            col = col + 1
        }
        row = row + 1
    }

    print("\nPixels in Mandelbrot set: ")
    println(in_set)
    print("Total pixels: ")
    println(WIDTH * HEIGHT)

    0
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/matrix_mul.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Dense Matrix Multiplication: 64×64 matrices (262,144 multiply-add ops)
//!
//! Demonstrates: high-throughput f64 computation, struct arrays, O(n³) loop,
//! numerical verification — zero external dependencies.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/matrix_mul.sio

const DIM: i64 = 64   // matrix dimension (DIM × DIM)

struct Matrix {
    m: [f64; 4096],    // DIM * DIM = 64 * 64 = 4096
}

fn mat_get(mat: &! Matrix, row: i64, col: i64) -> f64 with Mut {
    mat.m[row * DIM + col]
}

fn mat_set(mat: &! Matrix, row: i64, col: i64, val: f64) with Mut {
    mat.m[row * DIM + col] = val
}

// Initialize: A[i][j] = (i + j + 1) as f64 / DIM
fn mat_init_a(mat: &! Matrix) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < DIM {
            let v = (i + j + 1) as f64 / (DIM as f64)
            mat_set(mat, i, j, v)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Initialize: B[i][j] = (i * j + 1) as f64 / (DIM * DIM)
fn mat_init_b(mat: &! Matrix) with Mut, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < DIM {
            let v = (i * j + 1) as f64 / (DIM * DIM) as f64
            mat_set(mat, i, j, v)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// C = A × B  (standard O(n³) multiply)
fn mat_mul(a: &! Matrix, b: &! Matrix, c: &! Matrix) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM {
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < DIM {
            var sum: f64 = 0.0
            var k: i64 = 0
            while k < DIM {
                sum = sum + mat_get(a, i, k) * mat_get(b, k, j)
                k = k + 1
            }
            mat_set(c, i, j, sum)
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Frobenius norm: sqrt(sum of squares) — we return sum-of-squares to avoid FFI
fn frobenius_sq(mat: &! Matrix) -> f64 with Mut {
    var s: f64 = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < DIM * DIM {
        s = s + mat.m[i] * mat.m[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
    s
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div {
    var a = Matrix { m: [0.0; 4096] }
    var b = Matrix { m: [0.0; 4096] }
    var c = Matrix { m: [0.0; 4096] }

    mat_init_a(&! a)
    mat_init_b(&! b)
    mat_mul(&! a, &! b, &! c)

    // Spot-check: C[0][0] = sum_k A[0][k] * B[k][0]
    //   A[0][k] = (0 + k + 1) / 64 = (k+1)/64
    //   B[k][0] = (k * 0 + 1) / 4096 = 1/4096
    //   C[0][0] = sum_{k=0}^{63} (k+1)/64 * 1/4096
    //           = (1/64)(1/4096) * sum_{k=0}^{63}(k+1)
    //           = (1/262144) * (64*65/2) = 2080/262144 = 0.007934570...
    let c00 = mat_get(&! c, 0, 0)

    // C[1][1] spot-check
    let c11 = mat_get(&! c, 1, 1)

    // Frobenius norm squared
    let fnorm_sq = frobenius_sq(&! c)

    print("Matrix multiplication ")
    print_int(DIM)
    print("x")
    print_int(DIM)
    print(": done\n")
    print("  Operations: ")
    println(DIM * DIM * DIM)
    print("  C[0][0] = ")
    println(c00)
    print("  C[1][1] = ")
    println(c11)
    print("  ||C||^2 = ")
    println(fnorm_sq)

    // Verify C[0][0] ≈ 0.007934 (check it's positive and reasonable)
    let ok = c00 > 0.007 && c00 < 0.009 && c11 > 0.0 && fnorm_sq > 0.0
    if ok {
        print("Verification: PASS\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("Verification: FAIL\n")
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/quicksort.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Quicksort: in-place sort of 10,000 integers
//!
//! Demonstrates: real algorithms, mutable struct refs, LCG pseudo-random data,
//! verification pass, O(n log n) on 10K elements.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/quicksort.sio

struct SortBuf {
    data: [i64; 10000],
}

fn swap(arr: &! SortBuf, i: i64, j: i64) with Mut {
    let tmp = arr.data[i]
    arr.data[i] = arr.data[j]
    arr.data[j] = tmp
}

// Lomuto partition — median-of-three pivot for better performance
fn median3(arr: &! SortBuf, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    // Sort lo, mid, hi and use mid as pivot
    if arr.data[lo] > arr.data[mid] { swap(arr, lo, mid) }
    if arr.data[lo] > arr.data[hi]  { swap(arr, lo, hi)  }
    if arr.data[mid] > arr.data[hi] { swap(arr, mid, hi) }
    mid
}

fn partition(arr: &! SortBuf, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64 with Mut {
    let pivot_idx = median3(arr, lo, hi)
    let pivot = arr.data[pivot_idx]
    // Move pivot to end
    swap(arr, pivot_idx, hi)
    var i = lo - 1
    var j = lo
    while j < hi {
        if arr.data[j] <= pivot {
            i = i + 1
            swap(arr, i, j)
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    swap(arr, i + 1, hi)
    i + 1
}

fn qsort(arr: &! SortBuf, lo: i64, hi: i64) with Mut {
    if lo < hi {
        let p = partition(arr, lo, hi)
        qsort(arr, lo, p - 1)
        qsort(arr, p + 1, hi)
    }
}

fn abs64(x: i64) -> i64 {
    if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    var buf = SortBuf { data: [0; 10000] }
    let n: i64 = 10000

    // Fill with LCG pseudo-random values (Knuth multiplicative)
    var seed: i64 = 6364136223846793005
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        seed = seed * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        buf.data[i] = seed
        i = i + 1
    }

    let first_before = buf.data[0]

    qsort(&! buf, 0, n - 1)

    // Verify sorted
    var sorted = true
    i = 1
    while i < n {
        if buf.data[i] < buf.data[i - 1] { sorted = false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    if sorted {
        print("Quicksort (10,000 integers): PASS\n")
        print("  min = ")
        println(buf.data[0])
        print("  max = ")
        println(buf.data[n - 1])
        print("  unsorted[0] was: ")
        println(first_before)
        0
    } else {
        print("FAIL: sort verification failed\n")
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/algorithms/radix_sort.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//! Radix Sort (LSD, base-256) on 100,000 integers
//!
//! Demonstrates: O(kn) linear sorting, large buffers (1.6MB struct),
//! multi-pass counting sort, data structure manipulation at scale.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/radix_sort.sio

const N: i64 = 100000

struct RadixBufs {
    data:   [i64; 100000],
    output: [i64; 100000],
    count:  [i64; 256],
}

// Counting sort on one byte extracted by dividing by `divisor`
// divisor: 1 (byte0), 256 (byte1), 65536 (byte2), 16777216 (byte3)
fn counting_sort(b: &! RadixBufs, divisor: i64, n: i64) with Mut, Div {
    // Clear counts
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 256 {
        b.count[k] = 0
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Count occurrences of each byte value
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        let byte_val = (b.data[i] / divisor) & 255
        b.count[byte_val] = b.count[byte_val] + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Prefix sums (cumulative counts → starting positions)
    var prev: i64 = 0
    k = 0
    while k < 256 {
        let c = b.count[k]
        b.count[k] = prev
        prev = prev + c
        k = k + 1
    }

    // Place elements in output
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        let byte_val = (b.data[i] / divisor) & 255
        let pos = b.count[byte_val]
        b.output[pos] = b.data[i]
        b.count[byte_val] = pos + 1
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Copy output back to data
    i = 0
    while i < n {
        b.data[i] = b.output[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn radix_sort(b: &! RadixBufs, n: i64) with Mut, Div {
    // 4 passes: bytes 0,1,2,3 of the lower 32 bits
    counting_sort(b, 1,        n)   // byte 0: value & 255
    counting_sort(b, 256,      n)   // byte 1: (value / 256) & 255
    counting_sort(b, 65536,    n)   // byte 2: (value / 65536) & 255
    counting_sort(b, 16777216, n)   // byte 3: (value / 16777216) & 255
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div {
    var bufs = RadixBufs {
        data:   [0; 100000],
        output: [0; 100000],
        count:  [0; 256],
    }

    // Fill with positive pseudo-random values in [0, 2^31 - 1]
    var seed: i64 = 987654321
    var i: i64 = 0
    var checksum_before: i64 = 0
    while i < N {
        seed = seed * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        // Keep positive: take abs and mask to 31 bits
        var v = seed
        if v < 0 { v = 0 - v }
        v = v & 2147483647   // mask to [0, 2^31-1]
        bufs.data[i] = v
        checksum_before = checksum_before + v
        i = i + 1
    }

    let first_unsorted = bufs.data[0]
    let second_unsorted = bufs.data[1]

    radix_sort(&! bufs, N)

    // Verify sorted
    var ok = true
    i = 1
    while i < N {
        if bufs.data[i] < bufs.data[i - 1] { ok = false }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Verify checksum preserved
    var checksum_after: i64 = 0
    i = 0
    while i < N {
        checksum_after = checksum_after + bufs.data[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    if ok && checksum_before == checksum_after {
        print("Radix sort (100,000 integers): PASS\n")
        print("  Input[0,1]: ")
        println(first_unsorted)
        println(second_unsorted)
        print("  Sorted min: ")
        println(bufs.data[0])
        print("  Sorted max: ")
        println(bufs.data[N - 1])
        print("  Checksum:   ")
        println(checksum_after)
        0
    } else if ok == false {
        print("FAIL: sort order wrong\n")
        1
    } else {
        print("FAIL: checksum mismatch\n")
        2
    }
}

//@ run-pass
//! Sieve of Eratosthenes: find all primes up to 100,000
//!
//! Demonstrates: O(n log log n) algorithm, large arrays, nested loops,
//! counting and searching.
//!
//! Run: $SOUC run examples/algorithms/sieve.sio

struct SieveBuf {
    is_prime: [i32; 100001],
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    var s = SieveBuf { is_prime: [1; 100001] }
    let limit: i64 = 100000

    // 0 and 1 are not prime
    s.is_prime[0] = 0
    s.is_prime[1] = 0

    // Sieve: mark composites
    var i: i64 = 2
    while i * i <= limit {
        if s.is_prime[i] == 1 {
            var j = i * i
            while j <= limit {
                s.is_prime[j] = 0
                j = j + i
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Count primes and find largest
    var count: i64 = 0
    var largest: i64 = 0
    i = 2
    while i <= limit {
        if s.is_prime[i] == 1 {
            count = count + 1
            largest = i
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Print first 10 primes
    print("First 10 primes: ")
    var printed: i64 = 0
    i = 2
    while i <= limit && printed < 10 {
        if s.is_prime[i] == 1 {
            if printed > 0 { print(", ") }
            print_int(i)
            printed = printed + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    print("\n")

    print("Primes up to 100,000: ")
    println(count)
    print("Largest prime: ")
    println(largest)

    // Verify known count (9592 primes up to 100000)
    if count == 9592 {
        print("Count verified: PASS\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("Count mismatch: FAIL\n")
        1
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/algo/sorting_demo.sio ===
//! Sorting Algorithms Demonstration
//!
//! Compares quicksort, mergesort, and heapsort on the same dataset.
//! Shows algorithm correctness and sorting verification.

extern "C" {
    fn printf(fmt: *const u8, ...) -> i32;
    fn malloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8;
    fn free(ptr: *mut u8);
}

// Quicksort implementation
fn quicksort_i64(arr: &![i64], len: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return
    }
    quicksort_range(&!arr, 0, len - 1)
}

fn quicksort_range(arr: &![i64], low: usize, high: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if low < high {
        let pivot_idx = partition(&!arr, low, high)

        if pivot_idx > 0 {
            quicksort_range(&!arr, low, pivot_idx - 1)
        }

        if pivot_idx < high {
            quicksort_range(&!arr, pivot_idx + 1, high)
        }
    }
}

fn partition(arr: &![i64], low: usize, high: usize) -> usize with Panic, Div {
    let mid = low + (high - low) / 2
    let pivot = arr[mid]

    var i = low
    var j = high

    while true {
        while arr[i] < pivot {
            i = i + 1
        }

        while arr[j] > pivot {
            j = j - 1
        }

        if i >= j {
            return j
        }

        let temp = arr[i]
        arr[i] = arr[j]
        arr[j] = temp

        i = i + 1
        j = j - 1
    }

    return j
}

// Mergesort implementation
fn mergesort_i64(arr: &![i64], len: usize) with Alloc, Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return
    }

    let size_bytes = len * 8
    let temp = malloc(size_bytes) as *mut i64

    mergesort_recursive(&!arr, temp, 0, len - 1)

    free(temp as *mut u8)
}

fn mergesort_recursive(arr: &![i64], temp: *mut i64, left: usize, right: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if left >= right {
        return
    }

    let mid = left + (right - left) / 2

    mergesort_recursive(&!arr, temp, left, mid)
    mergesort_recursive(&!arr, temp, mid + 1, right)
    merge(&!arr, temp, left, mid, right)
}

fn merge(arr: &![i64], temp: *mut i64, left: usize, mid: usize, right: usize) with Panic, Div {
    var i = left
    while i <= right {
        temp[i] = arr[i]
        i = i + 1
    }

    var i1 = left
    var i2 = mid + 1
    var curr = left

    while i1 <= mid && i2 <= right {
        if temp[i1] <= temp[i2] {
            arr[curr] = temp[i1]
            i1 = i1 + 1
        } else {
            arr[curr] = temp[i2]
            i2 = i2 + 1
        }
        curr = curr + 1
    }

    while i1 <= mid {
        arr[curr] = temp[i1]
        i1 = i1 + 1
        curr = curr + 1
    }
}

// Heapsort implementation
fn heapsort_i64(arr: &![i64], len: usize) with Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return
    }

    var i = len / 2
    while i > 0 {
        i = i - 1
        heapify(&!arr, len, i)
    }

    var end = len - 1
    while end > 0 {
        let temp = arr[0]
        arr[0] = arr[end]
        arr[end] = temp

        heapify(&!arr, end, 0)

        end = end - 1
    }
}

fn heapify(arr: &![i64], heap_size: usize, root: usize) with Panic {
    var largest = root
    let left = 2 * root + 1
    let right = 2 * root + 2

    if left < heap_size && arr[left] > arr[largest] {
        largest = left
    }

    if right < heap_size && arr[right] > arr[largest] {
        largest = right
    }

    if largest != root {
        let temp = arr[root]
        arr[root] = arr[largest]
        arr[largest] = temp

        heapify(&!arr, heap_size, largest)
    }
}

// Check if array is sorted
fn is_sorted(arr: &[i64], len: usize) -> bool with Panic, Div {
    if len <= 1 {
        return true
    }

    var i = 0
    while i < len - 1 {
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1] {
            return false
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return true
}

// Print array helper
fn print_array(arr: &[i64], len: usize) with Panic {
    printf("  [".as_ptr())
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        if i > 0 {
            printf(", ".as_ptr())
        }
        printf("%lld".as_ptr(), arr[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    printf("]\n".as_ptr())
}

// Copy array helper
fn copy_array(dest: &![i64], src: &[i64], len: usize) with Panic {
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        dest[i] = src[i]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn main() -> i32 with Alloc, Panic, Div {
    printf("Sorting Algorithms Comparison\n".as_ptr())
    printf("=============================\n\n".as_ptr())

    // Sample dataset
    let original = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    let len: usize = 12

    printf("Original array:\n".as_ptr())
    print_array(&original, len)
    printf("\n".as_ptr())

    // Test Quicksort
    printf("1. Quicksort (in-place, unstable)\n".as_ptr())
    var arr_quick = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    quicksort_i64(&!arr_quick, len)
    printf("   Sorted: ".as_ptr())
    print_array(&arr_quick, len)
    printf("   Verified: %s\n\n".as_ptr(),
           if is_sorted(&arr_quick, len) { "✓ Correct" } else { "✗ Failed" }.as_ptr())

    // Test Mergesort
    printf("2. Mergesort (stable, O(n) space)\n".as_ptr())
    var arr_merge = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    mergesort_i64(&!arr_merge, len)
    printf("   Sorted: ".as_ptr())
    print_array(&arr_merge, len)
    printf("   Verified: %s\n\n".as_ptr(),
           if is_sorted(&arr_merge, len) { "✓ Correct" } else { "✗ Failed" }.as_ptr())

    // Test Heapsort
    printf("3. Heapsort (in-place, unstable)\n".as_ptr())
    var arr_heap = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90, 88, 45, 50, 23, 36]
    heapsort_i64(&!arr_heap, len)
    printf("   Sorted: ".as_ptr())
    print_array(&arr_heap, len)
    printf("   Verified: %s\n\n".as_ptr(),
           if is_sorted(&arr_heap, len) { "✓ Correct" } else { "✗ Failed" }.as_ptr())

    // Verify all algorithms produce same result
    printf("Comparing results:\n".as_ptr())
    var all_match = true
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < len {
        if arr_quick[i] != arr_merge[i] || arr_merge[i] != arr_heap[i] {
            all_match = false
            break
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    printf("  All algorithms agree: %s\n".as_ptr(),
           if all_match { "✓ Yes" } else { "✗ No" }.as_ptr())

    printf("\nSorting demo completed successfully!\n".as_ptr())
    return 0
}

/*

// ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗

// ║  4. Beta Posterior Benchmarks: Honest confidence intervals on solve rate     ║

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic Types: Knowledge<T> with Beta Posterior Confidence
// =============================================================================

/// Beta distribution for Bayesian confidence estimation
/// Unlike point estimates, this captures our UNCERTAINTY about confidence
struct BetaConfidence {
    alpha: f64,  // Successes + 1 (prior)
    beta: f64,   // Failures + 1 (prior)
}

impl BetaConfidence {
    /// Uniform prior: Beta(1, 1) = "I know nothing"
    fn uniform_prior() -> Self {
        Self { alpha: 1.0, beta: 1.0 }
    }

    /// Mean of the distribution: E[p] = α / (α + β)
    fn mean(self) -> f64 {
        self.alpha / (self.alpha + self.beta)
    }

    /// Variance: Var[p] = αβ / ((α+β)²(α+β+1))
    /// HIGH VARIANCE = "I don't know" → should explore more
    fn variance(self) -> f64 {
        let sum = self.alpha + self.beta
        (self.alpha * self.beta) / (sum * sum * (sum + 1.0))
    }

    /// 95% credible interval: NOT just a percentage, but honest uncertainty bounds
    fn credible_interval(self, confidence: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
        let mean = self.mean()
        let std = sqrt(self.variance())
        let z = 1.96  // 95% CI
        let lo = max(0.0, mean - z * std)
        let hi = min(1.0, mean + z * std)
        (lo, hi)
    }

    /// Bayesian update: observed success
    fn observe_success(self) -> Self {
        Self { alpha: self.alpha + 1.0, beta: self.beta }
    }

    /// Bayesian update: observed failure
    fn observe_failure(self) -> Self {
        Self { alpha: self.alpha, beta: self.beta + 1.0 }
    }

    /// P(p > threshold) - for statistical comparisons
    fn prob_greater_than(self, threshold: f64) -> f64 {
        // Approximation using normal distribution for large α, β
        let mean = self.mean()
        let std = sqrt(self.variance())
        if std < 0.001 {
            if mean > threshold { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }
        } else {
            let z = (mean - threshold) / std
            0.5 * (1.0 + erf(z / sqrt(2.0)))
        }
    }
}

/// Knowledge<T> wraps any value with epistemic metadata
/// This is the core type that makes AlphaGeoZero epistemically honest
struct Knowledge<T> {
    value: T,
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: ProvenanceNode,
}

impl<T> Knowledge<T> {
    /// Create knowledge with uncertainty
    fn with_confidence(value: T, confidence: BetaConfidence) -> Self {
        Self {
            value,
            confidence,
            provenance: ProvenanceNode::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Is this knowledge reliable? (mean > threshold AND variance < limit)
    fn is_reliable(self, threshold: f64, max_variance: f64) -> bool {
        self.confidence.mean() > threshold && self.confidence.variance() < max_variance
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Geometry Primitives with Epistemic Coordinates
// =============================================================================

/// A point with coordinates that may be uncertain
struct Point {
    name: string,
    x: Knowledge<f64>,
    y: Knowledge<f64>,
}

/// Predicate kinds in geometry
enum PredicateKind {
    Collinear,       // Points A, B, C lie on a line
    Parallel,        // Lines AB || CD
    Perpendicular,   // Lines AB ⊥ CD
    EqualLength,     // |AB| = |CD|
    Midpoint,        // M is midpoint of AB
    OnCircle,        // Point P lies on circle
    Congruent,       // Triangles ABC ≅ DEF
    Similar,         // Triangles ABC ~ DEF
    Cyclic,          // Points lie on a common circle
    EqualAngle,      // Angles are equal
    Circumcenter,    // O is circumcenter of ABC
    Orthocenter,     // H is orthocenter of ABC
    Incenter,        // I is incenter of ABC
    Centroid,        // G is centroid of ABC
}

/// A predicate with epistemic confidence
struct Predicate {
    kind: PredicateKind,
    args: [string],
    confidence: BetaConfidence,
    provenance: ProvenanceNode,
}

impl Predicate {
    fn collinear(a: string, b: string, c: string) -> Self {
        Self {
            kind: PredicateKind::Collinear,
            args: [a, b, c],
            confidence: BetaConfidence::uniform_prior(),
            provenance: ProvenanceNode::axiom(),
        }
    }

    fn parallel(p1: string, p2: string, p3: string, p4: string) -> Self {
        Self {
            kind: PredicateKind::Parallel,
            args: [p1, p2, p3, p4],
            confidence: BetaConfidence::uniform_prior(),
            provenance: ProvenanceNode::axiom(),
        }
    }

    fn midpoint(m: string, a: string, b: string) -> Self {
        Self {
            kind: PredicateKind::Midpoint,
            args: [m, a, b],
            confidence: BetaConfidence { alpha: 100.0, beta: 1.0 }, // Axiom: high confidence
            provenance: ProvenanceNode::axiom(),
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Proof State: The Graph of Known Predicates
// =============================================================================

/// Complete proof state with epistemic tracking
struct ProofState {
    points: Map<string, Point>,
    predicates: Map<string, Predicate>,
    goal: Option<Predicate>,
    constructions: [Construction],
    provenance_root: ProvenanceNode,
}

impl ProofState {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            points: Map::new(),
            predicates: Map::new(),
            goal: None,
            constructions: [],
            provenance_root: ProvenanceNode::root(),
        }
    }

    /// Add a point to the state
    fn add_point(self: &!Self, name: string) {
        let point = Point {
            name: name.clone(),
            x: Knowledge::with_confidence(0.0, BetaConfidence::uniform_prior()),
            y: Knowledge::with_confidence(0.0, BetaConfidence::uniform_prior()),
        }
        self.points.insert(name, point)
    }

    /// Add multiple points
    fn add_points(self: &!Self, names: [string]) {
        for name in names {
            self.add_point(name)
        }
    }

    /// Add an axiom (premise) with high confidence
    fn add_axiom(self: &!Self, pred: Predicate) {
        let key = pred.to_key()
        self.predicates.insert(key, pred)
    }

    /// Check if goal is proved with sufficient confidence
    fn goal_proved(self, min_confidence: f64) -> bool {
        match self.goal {
            Some(goal) => {
                let key = goal.to_key()
                match self.predicates.get(key) {
                    Some(pred) => pred.confidence.mean() >= min_confidence,
                    None => false
                }
            }
            None => false
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Epistemic MCTS Node
// =============================================================================

/// MCTS node with Beta-distributed value estimation
///
/// KEY INNOVATION: Q-values are distributions, not scalars
/// High variance = "I don't know" = should explore (active inference)
struct EpistemicMCTSNode {
    state: ProofState,
    action: Option<GeoAction>,
    parent: Option<usize>,
    children: [usize],

    // Neural network prior
    prior: f64,

    // Epistemic value: Beta(α, β) distribution, NOT a scalar!
    value_beta: BetaConfidence,

    // Visit statistics
    visits: u32,
    total_value: f64,
}

impl EpistemicMCTSNode {
    /// Q-value: mean of visits
    fn q_value(self) -> f64 {
        if self.visits == 0 { 0.0 }
        else { self.total_value / self.visits as f64 }
    }

    /// PUCT score with EPISTEMIC IGNORANCE BONUS
    ///
    /// Traditional PUCT: UCB(s,a) = Q(s,a) + c * sqrt(log N / n)
    ///
    /// OUR PUCT: UCB(s,a) = Q(s,a) + c_puct * P(a|s) * sqrt(N) / (1+n)
    ///                    + c_ignorance * sqrt(Var(Q))
    ///
    /// The ignorance bonus explores nodes where we're UNCERTAIN
    /// This is active inference: minimize free energy by reducing uncertainty
    fn puct_score(self, parent_visits: u32, config: MCTSConfig) -> f64 {
        let q = self.q_value()

        // Standard PUCT exploration
        let exploration = config.c_puct * self.prior * sqrt(parent_visits as f64)
                        / (1.0 + self.visits as f64)

        // EPISTEMIC IGNORANCE BONUS - KEY INNOVATION
        let ignorance_bonus = if config.use_variance_bonus {
            config.c_ignorance * sqrt(self.value_beta.variance())
        } else {
            0.0
        }

        q + exploration + ignorance_bonus
    }

    /// Update with Bayesian posterior
    fn update_value(self: &!Self, value: f64) {
        self.visits += 1
        self.total_value += value

        // Conjugate Beta update
        let alpha_update = max(0.0, min(1.0, value))
        let beta_update = max(0.0, min(1.0, 1.0 - value))

        self.value_beta = BetaConfidence {
            alpha: self.value_beta.alpha + alpha_update,
            beta: self.value_beta.beta + beta_update,
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// MCTS Configuration
// =============================================================================

struct MCTSConfig {
    /// PUCT exploration constant
    c_puct: f64,
    /// Epistemic ignorance bonus constant (KEY PARAMETER)
    c_ignorance: f64,
    /// Number of simulations per move
    num_simulations: usize,
    /// Temperature for action selection
    temperature: f64,
    /// Whether to use variance bonus
    use_variance_bonus: bool,
}

impl Default for MCTSConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            c_puct: 1.5,
            c_ignorance: 0.5,  // KEY: Explore uncertain states
            num_simulations: 800,
            temperature: 1.0,
            use_variance_bonus: true,
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Geometry Actions
