// Mouse event types
fn MOUSE_PRESS() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn MOUSE_RELEASE() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn MOUSE_MOVE() -> i32 { return 2 }
fn MOUSE_DRAG() -> i32 { return 3 }
fn MOUSE_SCROLL_UP() -> i32 { return 4 }
fn MOUSE_SCROLL_DOWN() -> i32 { return 5 }

// Mouse buttons
fn BUTTON_LEFT() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn BUTTON_RIGHT() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn BUTTON_MIDDLE() -> i32 { return 2 }

// Keyboard modifiers
fn MOD_NONE() -> i32 { return 0 }
fn MOD_SHIFT() -> i32 { return 1 }
fn MOD_CTRL() -> i32 { return 2 }
fn MOD_ALT() -> i32 { return 4 }
fn MOD_META() -> i32 { return 8 }

// Special keys
fn KEY_ESCAPE() -> i32 { return 27 }
fn KEY_ENTER() -> i32 { return 13 }
fn KEY_TAB() -> i32 { return 9 }
fn KEY_BACKSPACE() -> i32 { return 8 }
fn KEY_SPACE() -> i32 { return 32 }
fn KEY_UP() -> i32 { return 1000 }
fn KEY_DOWN() -> i32 { return 1001 }
fn KEY_LEFT() -> i32 { return 1002 }
fn KEY_RIGHT() -> i32 { return 1003 }

// ============================================================================
// Event Structures
// ============================================================================

struct MouseEvent {
    event_type: i32,  // MOUSE_PRESS, MOUSE_RELEASE, etc.
    button: i32,      // BUTTON_LEFT, BUTTON_RIGHT, BUTTON_MIDDLE
    x: i32,           // Column (0-based)
    y: i32,           // Row (0-based)
    modifiers: i32    // MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | etc.
}

fn mouse_event_new(event_type: i32, button: i32, x: i32, y: i32, modifiers: i32) -> MouseEvent {
    return MouseEvent {
        event_type: event_type,
        button: button,
        x: x,
        y: y,
        modifiers: modifiers
    }
}

fn mouse_event_none() -> MouseEvent {
    return mouse_event_new(0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
}

struct KeyEvent {
    key_code: i32,    // ASCII code or KEY_* constant
    modifiers: i32,   // MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | etc.
    is_char: i32      // 1 if printable character, 0 if special key
}

fn key_event_new(key_code: i32, modifiers: i32, is_char: i32) -> KeyEvent {
    return KeyEvent {
        key_code: key_code,
        modifiers: modifiers,
        is_char: is_char
    }
}

fn key_event_none() -> KeyEvent {
    return key_event_new(0, 0, 0)
}

// ============================================================================
// Mouse Tracking Control
// ============================================================================

// Enable mouse tracking in terminal
// Sends ANSI escape sequences to enable mouse reporting
fn enable_mouse_tracking() with IO {
    // Enable mouse button press/release tracking (X10 mode)
    print("\x1b[?1000h")

    // Enable mouse motion tracking
    print("\x1b[?1002h")

    // Enable SGR extended mouse mode (better coordinate reporting)
    print("\x1b[?1006h")

    // Enable alternate scroll mode
    print("\x1b[?1015h")
}

// Disable mouse tracking
fn disable_mouse_tracking() with IO {
    print("\x1b[?1000l")
    print("\x1b[?1002l")
    print("\x1b[?1006l")
    print("\x1b[?1015l")
}

// Enable raw mode (no line buffering, no echo)
// NOTE: This is a simplified version using ANSI codes
// Full implementation would require FFI to termios
fn enable_raw_mode() with IO {
    // Disable line buffering and echo
    print("\x1b[?25l")  // Hide cursor
    print("\x1b[?7l")   // Disable line wrapping
}

// Disable raw mode
fn disable_raw_mode() with IO {
    print("\x1b[?25h")  // Show cursor
    print("\x1b[?7h")   // Enable line wrapping
}

// ============================================================================
// Input State Management
// ============================================================================

struct InputState {
    mouse_enabled: i32,
    raw_mode: i32,
    last_mouse_x: i32,
    last_mouse_y: i32,
    last_button: i32,
    button_pressed: i32  // 1 if button currently pressed, 0 otherwise
}

fn input_state_new() -> InputState {
    return InputState {
        mouse_enabled: 0,
        raw_mode: 0,
        last_mouse_x: 0,
        last_mouse_y: 0,
        last_button: 0,
        button_pressed: 0
    }
}

fn input_init(state: &!InputState) with IO, Mut {
    enable_mouse_tracking()
    enable_raw_mode()
    state.mouse_enabled = 1
    state.raw_mode = 1
}

fn input_cleanup(state: &!InputState) with IO, Mut {
    if state.mouse_enabled == 1 {
        disable_mouse_tracking()
        state.mouse_enabled = 0
    }
    if state.raw_mode == 1 {
        disable_raw_mode()
        state.raw_mode = 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Simulated Input Events (for testing/demos)
// ============================================================================

// Generate a simulated mouse click event
fn simulate_mouse_click(x: i32, y: i32, button: i32) -> MouseEvent {
    return mouse_event_new(MOUSE_PRESS(), button, x, y, MOD_NONE())
}

// Generate a simulated mouse drag event
fn simulate_mouse_drag(x1: i32, y1: i32, x2: i32, y2: i32) -> [MouseEvent; 3] with Mut {
    var events: [MouseEvent; 3] = [mouse_event_none(); 3]

    // Press at start
    events[0] = mouse_event_new(MOUSE_PRESS(), BUTTON_LEFT(), x1, y1, MOD_NONE())

    // Drag to end
    events[1] = mouse_event_new(MOUSE_DRAG(), BUTTON_LEFT(), x2, y2, MOD_NONE())

    // Release at end
    events[2] = mouse_event_new(MOUSE_RELEASE(), BUTTON_LEFT(), x2, y2, MOD_NONE())

    return events
}

// Generate simulated scroll event
fn simulate_scroll(x: i32, y: i32, direction: i32) -> MouseEvent {
    let event_type = if direction > 0 {
        MOUSE_SCROLL_UP()
    } else {
        MOUSE_SCROLL_DOWN()
    }

    return mouse_event_new(event_type, BUTTON_MIDDLE(), x, y, MOD_NONE())
}

// ============================================================================
// Event Handlers (Callback Pattern)
// ============================================================================

// Event handler function type
// Note: Function pointers in Sounio use this syntax
// type MouseHandler = fn(&!InputState, &MouseEvent) -> i32
// type KeyHandler = fn(&KeyEvent) -> i32

// Simple event loop with handlers
// Returns 0 to continue, 1 to exit
fn event_loop_step(
    state: &!InputState,
    on_mouse: fn(&!InputState, &MouseEvent) -> i32,
    on_key: fn(&KeyEvent) -> i32
) -> i32 with Mut {
    // Poll for mouse event
    let mouse_evt = poll_mouse_event(state)
    if mouse_evt.event_type != 0 {
        let result = on_mouse(state, &mouse_evt)
        if result == 1 {
            return 1  // Exit requested
        }
    }

    // Poll for keyboard event
    let key_evt = poll_key_event()
    if key_evt.key_code != 0 {
        let result = on_key(&key_evt)
        if result == 1 {
            return 1  // Exit requested
        }
    }

    return 0  // Continue
}

// ============================================================================
// Utility Functions
// ============================================================================

// Check if mouse event is at given position (with tolerance)
fn mouse_event_at(evt: &MouseEvent, x: i32, y: i32, tolerance: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    let dx = if evt.x > x { evt.x - x } else { x - evt.x }
    let dy = if evt.y > y { evt.y - y } else { y - evt.y }

    if dx <= tolerance {
        if dy <= tolerance {
            return 1
        }
    }

    return 0
}

// Check if mouse event is within rectangle
fn mouse_event_in_rect(evt: &MouseEvent, x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32) -> i32 {
    if evt.x >= x {
        if evt.x < x + width {
            if evt.y >= y {
                if evt.y < y + height {
                    return 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return 0
}

// Check if modifier is active
fn has_modifier(modifiers: i32, mod_flag: i32) -> i32 {
    return if (modifiers & mod_flag) != 0 { 1 } else { 0 }
}

// Combine modifiers
fn combine_modifiers(mod1: i32, mod2: i32) -> i32 {
    return mod1 | mod2
}

// Helper function for printing integers
fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    // Print digit
    let ch = 48 + digit  // '0' is ASCII 48
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/31_interactive_plot.sio ===
// 31_interactive_plot.sio - Interactive plotting with zoom and pan
//
// Provides interactive visualization capabilities:
// - Zoom in/out (mouse wheel or keyboard)
// - Pan (mouse drag or arrow keys)
// - Reset view
// - Dynamic data updates
//
// NOTE: Full interactivity requires raw terminal mode and event loop.
// This implementation provides the core zoom/pan logic that can be
// integrated with input events when available.

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "02_drawing.sio"
import "03_text.sio"
import "10_axes.sio"
import "11_scatter.sio"
import "12_line_plot.sio"
import "30_input.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Interactive Plot State
// ============================================================================

struct InteractivePlot {
    // Viewport (current view bounds)
    viewport: Viewport,

    // Original viewport (for reset)
    original_viewport: Viewport,

    // Zoom state
    zoom_level: f64,     // 1.0 = original, 2.0 = 2x zoom, 0.5 = zoom out
    min_zoom: f64,       // Minimum zoom (e.g., 0.1)
    max_zoom: f64,       // Maximum zoom (e.g., 10.0)

    // Pan state
    pan_x: f64,          // Pan offset in world coordinates
    pan_y: f64,

    // Mouse interaction
    mouse_down: i32,     // 1 if mouse button is down
    drag_start_x: i32,   // Drag start position (canvas coords)
    drag_start_y: i32,
    last_mouse_x: i32,
    last_mouse_y: i32,

    // Keyboard interaction
    pan_speed: f64,      // Pan speed for keyboard arrows

    // Visual feedback
    show_controls: i32,  // 1 to show control help, 0 to hide
    dirty: i32           // 1 if needs redraw, 0 if clean
}

fn interactive_plot_new(viewport: Viewport) -> InteractivePlot {
    return InteractivePlot {
        viewport: viewport,
        original_viewport: viewport,
        zoom_level: 1.0,
        min_zoom: 0.1,
        max_zoom: 10.0,
        pan_x: 0.0,
        pan_y: 0.0,
        mouse_down: 0,
        drag_start_x: 0,
        drag_start_y: 0,
        last_mouse_x: 0,
        last_mouse_y: 0,
        pan_speed: 0.1,
        show_controls: 1,
        dirty: 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Zoom Operations
// ============================================================================

// Zoom in by a factor (e.g., 1.2 for 20% zoom in)
fn plot_zoom_in(plot: &!InteractivePlot, factor: f64) with Mut, Div {
    let new_zoom = plot.zoom_level * factor

    // Clamp to limits
    if new_zoom > plot.max_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.max_zoom
    } else {
        plot.zoom_level = new_zoom
    }

    // Update viewport based on zoom
    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Zoom out by a factor
fn plot_zoom_out(plot: &!InteractivePlot, factor: f64) with Mut, Div {
    let new_zoom = plot.zoom_level / factor

    // Clamp to limits
    if new_zoom < plot.min_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.min_zoom
    } else {
        plot.zoom_level = new_zoom
    }

    // Update viewport
    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Zoom to specific level
fn plot_set_zoom(plot: &!InteractivePlot, zoom: f64) with Mut {
    // Clamp
    if zoom < plot.min_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.min_zoom
    } else { if zoom > plot.max_zoom {
        plot.zoom_level = plot.max_zoom
    } else {
        plot.zoom_level = zoom
    }}

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Zoom centered on a specific point (world coordinates)
fn plot_zoom_at_point(
    plot: &!InteractivePlot,
    world_x: f64,
    world_y: f64,
    factor: f64
) with Mut, Div {
    // Calculate offset from center before zoom
    let vp = &plot.viewport
    let center_x = (vp.x_min + vp.x_max) / 2.0
    let center_y = (vp.y_min + vp.y_max) / 2.0
    let offset_x = world_x - center_x
    let offset_y = world_y - center_y

    // Apply zoom
    let old_zoom = plot.zoom_level
    plot_zoom_in(plot, factor)
    let zoom_ratio = plot.zoom_level / old_zoom

    // Adjust pan to keep point centered
    plot.pan_x = plot.pan_x + offset_x * (1.0 - zoom_ratio)
    plot.pan_y = plot.pan_y + offset_y * (1.0 - zoom_ratio)

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Pan Operations
// ============================================================================

// Pan by offset in world coordinates
fn plot_pan(plot: &!InteractivePlot, dx: f64, dy: f64) with Mut {
    plot.pan_x = plot.pan_x + dx
    plot.pan_y = plot.pan_y + dy

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Pan to center on a specific point
fn plot_center_on(plot: &!InteractivePlot, world_x: f64, world_y: f64) with Mut, Div {
    let vp = &plot.viewport
    let center_x = (vp.x_min + vp.x_max) / 2.0
    let center_y = (vp.y_min + vp.y_max) / 2.0

    plot.pan_x = plot.pan_x + (world_x - center_x)
    plot.pan_y = plot.pan_y + (world_y - center_y)

    plot_update_viewport(plot)
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// Reset view to original
fn plot_reset_view(plot: &!InteractivePlot) with Mut {
    plot.zoom_level = 1.0
    plot.pan_x = 0.0
    plot.pan_y = 0.0

    plot.viewport = plot.original_viewport
    plot.dirty = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Viewport Update
// ============================================================================

// Update viewport based on zoom and pan
fn plot_update_viewport(plot: &!InteractivePlot) with Mut, Div {
    let orig = &plot.original_viewport

    // Calculate width and height based on zoom
    let orig_width = orig.x_max - orig.x_min
    let orig_height = orig.y_max - orig.y_min

    let new_width = orig_width / plot.zoom_level
    let new_height = orig_height / plot.zoom_level

    // Calculate center with pan offset
    let orig_center_x = (orig.x_min + orig.x_max) / 2.0
    let orig_center_y = (orig.y_min + orig.y_max) / 2.0

    let new_center_x = orig_center_x + plot.pan_x
    let new_center_y = orig_center_y + plot.pan_y

    // Update viewport bounds
    plot.viewport.x_min = new_center_x - new_width / 2.0
    plot.viewport.x_max = new_center_x + new_width / 2.0
    plot.viewport.y_min = new_center_y - new_height / 2.0
    plot.viewport.y_max = new_center_y + new_height / 2.0
}

// ============================================================================
// Mouse Event Handling
// ============================================================================

// Handle mouse press
fn plot_on_mouse_press(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut {
    if evt.button == BUTTON_LEFT() {
        plot.mouse_down = 1
        plot.drag_start_x = evt.x
        plot.drag_start_y = evt.y
        plot.last_mouse_x = evt.x
        plot.last_mouse_y = evt.y
    }
}

// Handle mouse release
fn plot_on_mouse_release(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut {
    if evt.button == BUTTON_LEFT() {
        plot.mouse_down = 0
    }
}

// Handle mouse move (pan if dragging)
fn plot_on_mouse_move(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut, Div {
    if plot.mouse_down == 1 {
        // Calculate delta in canvas pixels
        let dx_pixels = evt.x - plot.last_mouse_x
        let dy_pixels = evt.y - plot.last_mouse_y

        // Convert to world coordinates
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let world_width = vp.x_max - vp.x_min
        let world_height = vp.y_max - vp.y_min

        let dx_world = ((dx_pixels as f64) / (vp.canvas_width as f64)) * world_width
        let dy_world = ((dy_pixels as f64) / (vp.canvas_height as f64)) * world_height

        // Pan (note: invert y since canvas y increases downward)
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0 - dx_world, dy_world)

        plot.last_mouse_x = evt.x
        plot.last_mouse_y = evt.y
    }
}

// Handle mouse scroll (zoom)
fn plot_on_mouse_scroll(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &MouseEvent) with Mut, Div {
    // Convert mouse position to world coordinates
    let world_pos = canvas_to_world(&plot.viewport, evt.x, evt.y)

    // Zoom factor
    let factor = if evt.event_type == MOUSE_SCROLL_UP() {
        1.2  // Zoom in
    } else {
        1.2  // Zoom out (will be inverted)
    }

    // Zoom at mouse position
    if evt.event_type == MOUSE_SCROLL_UP() {
        plot_zoom_at_point(plot, world_pos.0, world_pos.1, factor)
    } else {
        plot_zoom_out(plot, factor)
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Keyboard Event Handling
// ============================================================================

// Handle key press
fn plot_on_key_press(plot: &!InteractivePlot, evt: &KeyEvent) with Mut, Div {
    // Arrow keys for panning
    if evt.key_code == KEY_LEFT() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.x_max - vp.x_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0 - pan_amount, 0.0)
    }

    if evt.key_code == KEY_RIGHT() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.x_max - vp.x_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, pan_amount, 0.0)
    }

    if evt.key_code == KEY_UP() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.y_max - vp.y_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0, pan_amount)
    }

    if evt.key_code == KEY_DOWN() {
        let vp = &plot.viewport
        let pan_amount = (vp.y_max - vp.y_min) * plot.pan_speed
        plot_pan(plot, 0.0, 0.0 - pan_amount)
    }

    // '+' or '=' for zoom in
    if evt.key_code == 43 {  // '+'
        plot_zoom_in(plot, 1.2)
    }
    if evt.key_code == 61 {  // '='
        plot_zoom_in(plot, 1.2)
    }

    // '-' for zoom out
    if evt.key_code == 45 {  // '-'
        plot_zoom_out(plot, 1.2)
    }

    // 'r' for reset
    if evt.key_code == 114 {  // 'r'
        plot_reset_view(plot)
    }

    // 'h' for toggle help
    if evt.key_code == 104 {  // 'h'
        plot.show_controls = if plot.show_controls == 1 { 0 } else { 1 }
        plot.dirty = 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Rendering with Controls
// ============================================================================

// Draw control hints
fn plot_draw_controls(canvas: Canvas, plot: &InteractivePlot) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic {
    if plot.show_controls == 0 {
        return canvas
    }

    var c = canvas

    // Control panel in bottom-right corner
    let x = 50
    let y = 25

    let style = text_style_colored(COLOR_YELLOW())

    c = draw_text(c, x, y, "Controls:", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 1, "  Arrows: Pan", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 2, "  +/-: Zoom", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 3, "  r: Reset", style)
    c = draw_text(c, x, y + 4, "  h: Hide", style)

    return c
}

// Draw zoom/pan indicator
fn plot_draw_indicator(canvas: Canvas, plot: &InteractivePlot) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    let style = text_style_colored(COLOR_CYAN())

    // Zoom level
    c = draw_text(c, 2, 28, "Zoom:", style)

    // Convert zoom to string (simplified)
    let zoom_int = (plot.zoom_level * 10.0) as i32
    c = draw_text(c, 8, 28, "x.x", style)

    return c
}

    if x < 0.0 {
        print("-")
        print_f64_unsigned(0.0 - x)
    } else {
        print_f64_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_f64_unsigned(x: f64) with IO, Div, Panic {
    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)
    print(".")

    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    let scaled = (frac * 100.0) as i32
    if scaled < 10 {
        print("0")
    }
    print_i32(scaled)
}

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    let ch = 48 + digit
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/40_animation.sio ===
// 40_animation.sio - Animation framework with double buffering
//
// Provides terminal animation capabilities:
// - Frame management and timing
// - Double buffering (in-place updates)
// - FPS control (limited by terminal I/O speed)
// - Animation state tracking
//
// NOTE: Sleep/delay functionality requires FFI to platform timing.
// Current implementation relies on terminal I/O as the bottleneck.

// No imports needed - standalone module

// ============================================================================
// Animation State
// ============================================================================

struct AnimationState {
    frame: i32,           // Current frame number
    max_frames: i32,      // Total frames (0 = infinite loop)
    frame_delay_ms: i32,  // Target delay between frames
    running: i32,         // 1 if running, 0 if stopped
    loop_mode: i32,       // 0=once, 1=loop, 2=bounce
    fps_target: i32,      // Target frames per second
    elapsed_frames: i32   // Total frames elapsed (for statistics)
}

fn animation_state_new(max_frames: i32, fps: i32) -> AnimationState with Panic, Div {
    let frame_delay = if fps > 0 {
        1000 / fps
    } else {
        33  // Default ~30 FPS
    }

    return AnimationState {
        frame: 0,
        max_frames: max_frames,
        frame_delay_ms: frame_delay,
        running: 1,
        loop_mode: 0,
        fps_target: fps,
        elapsed_frames: 0
    }
}

fn animation_state_infinite(fps: i32) -> AnimationState with Panic, Div {
    return animation_state_new(0, fps)
}

fn animation_state_looping(max_frames: i32, fps: i32) -> AnimationState with Panic, Div, Mut {
    var state = animation_state_new(max_frames, fps)
    state.loop_mode = 1
    return state
}

// ============================================================================
// Animation Control
// ============================================================================

// Initialize animation (clear screen, hide cursor)
fn animation_init() with IO {
    print("\x1b[2J")      // Clear screen
    print("\x1b[H")       // Home cursor
    print("\x1b[?25l")    // Hide cursor
}

// Cleanup animation (show cursor, reset colors)
fn animation_cleanup() with IO {
    print("\x1b[?25h")    // Show cursor
    print("\x1b[0m")      // Reset colors
    print("\n")
}

// Begin a new frame (clear and home cursor)
fn animation_begin_frame() with IO {
    print("\x1b[H")       // Home cursor (don't clear to avoid flicker)
}

// End frame and update state
fn animation_end_frame(state: &!AnimationState) with Mut {
    state.frame = state.frame + 1
    state.elapsed_frames = state.elapsed_frames + 1

    // Check if animation should stop
    if state.max_frames > 0 {
        if state.frame >= state.max_frames {
            if state.loop_mode == 0 {
                // Stop after max frames
                state.running = 0
            } else { if state.loop_mode == 1 {
                // Loop mode: restart
                state.frame = 0
            } else {
                // Bounce mode: reverse (not implemented yet)
                state.running = 0
            }}
        }
    }

    // TODO: Sleep for frame_delay_ms
    // This requires FFI to platform sleep function
    // For now, terminal I/O provides natural throttling
}

// Check if animation should continue
fn animation_should_continue(state: &AnimationState) -> i32 {
    return state.running
}

// Stop animation
fn animation_stop(state: &!AnimationState) with Mut {
    state.running = 0
}

// Restart animation
fn animation_restart(state: &!AnimationState) with Mut {
    state.frame = 0
    state.running = 1
}

// ============================================================================
// Frame Utilities
// ============================================================================

// Get normalized time (0.0 to 1.0) within animation
fn animation_get_t(state: &AnimationState) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    if state.max_frames <= 0 {
        return 0.0
    }

    return (state.frame as f64) / (state.max_frames as f64)
}

// Get frame progress percentage (0-100)
fn animation_get_progress(state: &AnimationState) -> i32 with Div, Panic {
    if state.max_frames <= 0 {
        return 0
    }

    return (state.frame * 100) / state.max_frames
}

// Oscillate between 0.0 and 1.0 (smooth back-and-forth)
fn animation_oscillate(state: &AnimationState) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let t = animation_get_t(state)
    // sin((t * 2π)) maps to [-1, 1], we want [0, 1]
    // So use: (1 + sin(2π * t - π/2)) / 2
    // Simplified: (1 - cos(2π * t)) / 2

    // For now, use triangle wave approximation
    if t < 0.5 {
        return t * 2.0
    } else {
        return 2.0 - t * 2.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Animation Loop Pattern
// ============================================================================
//
// NOTE: Animation loops that use Canvas are implemented in demo files
// where Canvas is available. This module provides only the core state
// management, timing, and easing functions.

// ============================================================================
// Easing Functions (for smooth animations)
// ============================================================================

// Linear interpolation: out = a + t * (b - a)
// Note: A lerp function may exist in math stdlib, but we define our own for standalone use
fn anim_lerp(a: f64, b: f64, t: f64) -> f64 {
    return a + t * (b - a)
}

// Ease in (quadratic): starts slow, accelerates
fn ease_in(t: f64) -> f64 {
    return t * t
}

// Ease out (quadratic): starts fast, decelerates
fn ease_out(t: f64) -> f64 {
    return t * (2.0 - t)
}

// Ease in-out (quadratic): slow start and end, fast middle
fn ease_in_out(t: f64) -> f64 {
    if t < 0.5 {
        return 2.0 * t * t
    } else {
        let s = t - 0.5
        return 0.5 + 2.0 * s * (1.0 - s)
    }
}

// Bounce easing (simulates elastic bounce)
fn ease_bounce(t: f64) -> f64 {
    if t < 0.5 {
        return 8.0 * t * t * t * t
    } else {
        let s = t - 1.0
        return 1.0 - 8.0 * s * s * s * s
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Helper Functions
// ============================================================================

fn print_i32(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        print("0")
        return
    }

    if x < 0 {
        print("-")
        print_i32_unsigned(0 - x)
    } else {
        print_i32_unsigned(x)
    }
}

fn print_i32_unsigned(x: i32) with IO, Div, Panic {
    if x == 0 {
        return
    }

    let digit = x % 10
    let rest = x / 10

    if rest > 0 {
        print_i32_unsigned(rest)
    }

    let ch = 48 + digit
    print_char(ch)
}

fn print_char(code: i32) with IO {
    if code == 48 { print("0") }
    else { if code == 49 { print("1") }
    else { if code == 50 { print("2") }
    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }
    else { if code == 52 { print("4") }
    else { if code == 53 { print("5") }
    else { if code == 54 { print("6") }
    else { if code == 55 { print("7") }
    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}
}

// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen
    print("=== Animation Framework Test ===\n\n")

    // Create animation state
    var state = animation_state_new(10, 30)

    print("Animation state created:\n")
    print("  Max frames: ")
    print_i32(state.max_frames)
    print("\n")
    print("  FPS target: ")
    print_i32(state.fps_target)
    print("\n")
    print("  Frame delay: ")
    print_i32(state.frame_delay_ms)
    print("ms\n\n")

    print("Frame progression test:\n")

    var i = 0
    while i < 12 {
        print("  Frame ")
        print_i32(state.frame)
        print(": t=")

        let t = animation_get_t(&state)
        let t_int = (t * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(t_int / 100)
        print(".")
        let frac = t_int % 100
        if frac < 10 {
            print("0")
        }
        print_i32(frac)

        print(", progress=")
        print_i32(animation_get_progress(&state))
        print("%, running=")
        print_i32(state.running)
        print("\n")

        animation_end_frame(&!state)
        i = i + 1
    }

    print("\nEasing functions test (t=0.0 to 1.0):\n")

    var j = 0
    while j <= 10 {
        let t = (j as f64) / 10.0

        print("  t=")
        let t_int = (t * 10.0) as i32
        print_i32(t_int / 10)
        print(".")
        print_i32(t_int % 10)

        print(": ease_in=")
        let ei = (ease_in(t) * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(ei)

        print(", ease_out=")
        let eo = (ease_out(t) * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(eo)

        print(", ease_in_out=")
        let eio = (ease_in_out(t) * 100.0) as i32
        print_i32(eio)
        print("\n")

        j = j + 1
    }

    print("\n=== Animation Framework Ready ===\n")
    print("Use animation_loop() or animation_loop_time() for canvas animation\n")

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/41_particle_system.sio ===
// 41_particle_system.sio - Particle physics simulation
//
// Provides particle system for visual effects:
// - 2D/3D particle simulation with physics
// - Forces: gravity, drag, wind
// - Particle lifecycle management (birth, death)
// - Emitters with various patterns
// - Visual rendering with markers and trails

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "02_drawing.sio"
import "10_axes.sio"
import "20_projection.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Particle Structure
// ============================================================================

struct Particle {
    pos: Vec3D,        // Position (x, y, z)
    vel: Vec3D,        // Velocity (dx/dt, dy/dt, dz/dt)
    acc: Vec3D,        // Acceleration (forces applied)
    color: i32,        // Particle color (0-15)
    marker: i32,       // Character marker
    size: i32,         // Particle size (1-3)
    life: f64,         // Remaining lifetime (seconds)
    max_life: f64,     // Initial lifetime
    mass: f64,         // Particle mass (affects forces)
    alive: i32         // 1 if active, 0 if dead
}

fn particle_new(
    pos: Vec3D,
    vel: Vec3D,
    color: i32,
    marker: i32,
    life: f64,
    mass: f64
) -> Particle {
    return Particle {
        pos: pos,
        vel: vel,
        acc: vec3d_zero(),
        color: color,
        marker: marker,
        size: 1,
        life: life,
        max_life: life,
        mass: mass,
        alive: 1
    }
}

fn particle_dead() -> Particle {
    return Particle {
        pos: vec3d_zero(),
        vel: vec3d_zero(),
        acc: vec3d_zero(),
        color: 0,
        marker: 32,  // Space
        size: 1,
        life: 0.0,
        max_life: 1.0,
        mass: 1.0,
        alive: 0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle System
// ============================================================================

struct ParticleSystem {
    particles: [Particle; 500],
    n_particles: i32,
    max_particles: i32,

    // Global forces
    gravity: Vec3D,
    wind: Vec3D,
    drag: f64,          // Air resistance coefficient

    // Emitter settings
    emit_pos: Vec3D,
    emit_rate: i32,     // Particles per frame
    emit_velocity: f64, // Initial speed
    emit_spread: f64,   // Angle spread (radians)

    // Particle lifecycle
    particle_lifetime: f64,
    particle_mass: f64,

    // Rendering
    trail_length: i32,  // 0 = no trails
    fade_with_age: i32  // 1 = fade color as particle ages
}

fn particle_system_new(max_particles: i32) -> ParticleSystem {
    return ParticleSystem {
        particles: [particle_dead(); 500],
        n_particles: 0,
        max_particles: max_particles,
        gravity: vec3d_new(0.0, -9.8, 0.0),
        wind: vec3d_zero(),
        drag: 0.01,
        emit_pos: vec3d_zero(),
        emit_rate: 5,
        emit_velocity: 10.0,
        emit_spread: 0.5,
        particle_lifetime: 3.0,
        particle_mass: 1.0,
        trail_length: 0,
        fade_with_age: 1
    }
}

fn particle_system_fountain(max_particles: i32) -> ParticleSystem {
    var sys = particle_system_new(max_particles)
    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_new(0.0, -5.0, 0.0)
    sys.emit_velocity = 15.0
    sys.emit_spread = 0.8
    sys.emit_rate = 10
    sys.particle_lifetime = 2.5
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -15.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.02
    return sys
}

fn particle_system_explosion(max_particles: i32) -> ParticleSystem {
    var sys = particle_system_new(max_particles)
    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_zero()
    sys.emit_velocity = 20.0
    sys.emit_spread = 3.14159265359  // Full sphere
    sys.emit_rate = 50
    sys.particle_lifetime = 1.5
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -5.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.05
    return sys
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle Emission
// ============================================================================

// Emit a single particle
fn emit_particle(
    sys: &!ParticleSystem,
    direction: Vec3D,
    velocity: f64,
    color: i32,
    marker: i32
) with Mut, Panic {
    // Find dead particle slot
    var i = 0
    while i < sys.max_particles {
        if sys.particles[i].alive == 0 {
            let dir_norm = vec3d_normalize(&direction)
            let vel = vec3d_scale(&dir_norm, velocity)

            sys.particles[i] = particle_new(
                sys.emit_pos,
                vel,
                color,
                marker,
                sys.particle_lifetime,
                sys.particle_mass
            )

            sys.n_particles = sys.n_particles + 1
            return
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// Emit particles from emitter (called each frame)
fn emit_particles(sys: &!ParticleSystem, rng_seed: &!i32) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i = 0
    while i < sys.emit_rate {
        // Generate random direction within spread cone
        // Simple pseudo-random using LCG
        rng_seed.val = (rng_seed.val * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let theta = ((rng_seed.val % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * sys.emit_spread

        rng_seed.val = (rng_seed.val * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let phi = ((rng_seed.val % 1000) as f64 / 1000.0) * 6.28318530718

        // Spherical to Cartesian
        let x = sin(theta) * cos(phi)
        let y = cos(theta)
        let z = sin(theta) * sin(phi)

        let direction = vec3d_new(x, y, z)

        // Random color
        rng_seed.val = (rng_seed.val * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        let color = (rng_seed.val % 6) + 2  // Colors 2-7 (avoid black/white)

        emit_particle(sys, direction, sys.emit_velocity, color as i32, 9679)  // ●
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle Physics Update
// ============================================================================

// Apply forces to particle
fn apply_forces(particle: &!Particle, gravity: Vec3D, wind: Vec3D, drag: f64) with Mut {
    // Reset acceleration
    particle.acc = vec3d_zero()

    // Gravity (F = m * g)
    let gravity_force = vec3d_scale(&gravity, particle.mass)
    particle.acc = vec3d_add(&particle.acc, &gravity_force)

    // Wind (constant force)
    particle.acc = vec3d_add(&particle.acc, &wind)

    // Drag (F = -drag * v)
    let drag_force = vec3d_scale(&particle.vel, 0.0 - drag)
    particle.acc = vec3d_add(&particle.acc, &drag_force)
}

// Update single particle (Euler integration)
fn update_particle(
    particle: &!Particle,
    dt: f64,
    gravity: Vec3D,
    wind: Vec3D,
    drag: f64
) with Mut {
    if particle.alive == 0 {
        return
    }

    // Apply forces
    apply_forces(particle, gravity, wind, drag)

    // Update velocity: v = v + a * dt
    let dv = vec3d_scale(&particle.acc, dt)
    particle.vel = vec3d_add(&particle.vel, &dv)

    // Update position: p = p + v * dt
    let dp = vec3d_scale(&particle.vel, dt)
    particle.pos = vec3d_add(&particle.pos, &dp)

    // Update lifetime
    particle.life = particle.life - dt
    if particle.life <= 0.0 {
        particle.alive = 0
    }
}

// Update entire particle system
fn particle_system_update(sys: &!ParticleSystem, dt: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    var alive_count = 0

    while i < sys.max_particles {
        if sys.particles[i].alive == 1 {
            update_particle(
                &!sys.particles[i],
                dt,
                sys.gravity,
                sys.wind,
                sys.drag
            )

            if sys.particles[i].alive == 1 {
                alive_count = alive_count + 1
            }
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    sys.n_particles = alive_count
}

// ============================================================================
// Particle Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Render particle system (2D projection)
fn particle_system_render_2d(
    canvas: Canvas,
    sys: &ParticleSystem,
    vp: &Viewport
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    var i = 0
    while i < sys.max_particles {
        let p = &sys.particles[i]

        if p.alive == 1 {
            // Project 3D position to 2D (use x, y, ignore z for now)
            let px = world_to_canvas_x(vp, p.pos.x)
            let py = world_to_canvas_y(vp, p.pos.y)

            // Fade color with age if enabled
            let color = if sys.fade_with_age == 1 {
                let age_ratio = p.life / p.max_life
                if age_ratio < 0.33 {
                    8  // Dark gray (fading out)
                } else {
                    p.color
                }
            } else {
                p.color
            }

            // Draw particle
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, p.marker, color)
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Render particle system (3D with isometric projection)
fn particle_system_render_3d(
    canvas: Canvas,
    sys: &ParticleSystem,
    vp: &Viewport,
    scale: f64
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var c = canvas

    var i = 0
    while i < sys.max_particles {
        let p = &sys.particles[i]

        if p.alive == 1 {
            // Isometric projection
            let projected = isometric_project_scaled(&p.pos, scale)

            let px = world_to_canvas_x(vp, projected.x)
            let py = world_to_canvas_y(vp, projected.y)

            // Fade color with age
            let color = if sys.fade_with_age == 1 {
                let age_ratio = p.life / p.max_life
                if age_ratio < 0.25 {
                    8  // Dark gray
                } else { if age_ratio < 0.5 {
                    p.color + 8  // Bright version
                } else {
                    p.color
                }}
            } else {
                p.color
            }

            // Draw particle
            c = canvas_set_char(c, px, py, p.marker, color)
        }

        i = i + 1
    }

    return c
}

// Particle Effects Presets

// Create fountain effect
fn create_fountain(sys: &!ParticleSystem) with Mut {
    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_new(0.0, -5.0, 0.0)
    sys.emit_velocity = 15.0
    sys.emit_spread = 0.5
    sys.emit_rate = 8
    sys.particle_lifetime = 2.5
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -12.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.02
}

    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_zero()
    sys.emit_velocity = 18.0
    sys.emit_spread = 3.14159265359
    sys.emit_rate = 40
    sys.particle_lifetime = 1.8
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -8.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.03
}

    sys.emit_velocity = 3.0
    sys.emit_spread = 0.3
    sys.emit_rate = 12
    sys.particle_lifetime = 4.0

}

    sys.emit_pos = vec3d_new(0.0, 10.0, 0.0)
    sys.emit_velocity = 15.0
    sys.emit_spread = 0.1
    sys.emit_rate = 15
    sys.particle_lifetime = 2.0
    sys.gravity = vec3d_new(0.0, -20.0, 0.0)
    sys.drag = 0.0

}

    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen

    print(", ")
    print_f64(sys.gravity.y)
    print(", ")
    print_f64(sys.gravity.z)
    print(")\n\n")

    // Simulate a few steps
    var rng = 12345

    print("Simulation:\n")

    while frame < 5 {
        emit_particles(&!sys, &!rng)
        particle_system_update(&!sys, 0.016)  // ~60 FPS

        print("  Frame ")

        print_i32(sys.n_particles)

    }

    print("  • create_fountain() - Upward spray\n")
    print("  • create_explosion() - Radial burst\n")
    print("  • create_smoke() - Rising particles\n")
    print("  • create_rain() - Downward fall\n")

    return 0
}

    } else {

    let int_part = x as i32
    print_i32(int_part)
    print(".")

    let frac = x - (int_part as f64)
    let scaled = (frac * 100.0) as i32
    if scaled < 10 {
        print("0")
    }
    print_i32(scaled)
}

    if x == 0 {

    if x < 0 {

    } else {

    }
}

    let rest = x / 10

}

    else { if code == 51 { print("3") }

    else { if code == 56 { print("8") }
    else { if code == 57 { print("9") }
    else { print("?") }
    }}}}}}}}}}

// === FILE: examples/graphics/lib/42_fluid_sim.sio ===
// 42_fluid_sim.sio - Fluid dynamics simulation
//
// Provides 2D fluid simulation using Navier-Stokes equations:
// - Incompressible fluid flow
// - Velocity field (u, v)
// - Density/dye visualization
// - Vorticity confinement (optional)
// - Semi-Lagrangian advection
//
// Based on Jos Stam's "Stable Fluids" (SIGGRAPH 1999)
// Simplified for terminal visualization

import "stdlib/math/core.sio"
import "00_canvas.sio"
import "01_colors.sio"
import "15_heatmap.sio"

// ============================================================================
// Fluid Grid Structure
// ============================================================================

struct FluidGrid {
    width: i32,
    height: i32,

    // Velocity field
    u: [f64; 2500],      // X-velocity at each cell
    v: [f64; 2500],      // Y-velocity at each cell
    u_prev: [f64; 2500], // Previous X-velocity
    v_prev: [f64; 2500], // Previous Y-velocity

    // Density/dye field
    density: [f64; 2500],
    density_prev: [f64; 2500],

    // Simulation parameters
    diffusion: f64,      // Viscosity coefficient
    viscosity: f64,      // Kinematic viscosity
    dt: f64              // Time step
}

fn fluid_grid_new(width: i32, height: i32, diffusion: f64, viscosity: f64) -> FluidGrid {
    return FluidGrid {
        width: width,
        height: height,
        u: [0.0; 2500],
        v: [0.0; 2500],
        u_prev: [0.0; 2500],
        v_prev: [0.0; 2500],
        density: [0.0; 2500],
        density_prev: [0.0; 2500],
        diffusion: diffusion,
        viscosity: viscosity,
        dt: 0.016  // ~60 FPS
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Grid Access Helpers
// ============================================================================

fn ix(x: i32, y: i32, width: i32) -> i32 with Panic {
    return y * width + x
}

fn get_cell(grid: &[f64], x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32) -> f64 with Panic {
    if x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height {
        return 0.0
    }
    return grid[ix(x, y, width)]
}

fn set_cell(grid: &![f64], x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32, value: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < width && y >= 0 && y < height {
        grid[ix(x, y, width)] = value
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Boundary Conditions
// ============================================================================

// Apply boundary conditions to scalar field
fn set_bounds_scalar(field: &![f64], width: i32, height: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    // Left and right edges
    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        field[ix(0, y, width)] = field[ix(1, y, width)]
        field[ix(width - 1, y, width)] = field[ix(width - 2, y, width)]
        y = y + 1
    }

    // Top and bottom edges
    var x = 1
    while x < width - 1 {
        field[ix(x, 0, width)] = field[ix(x, 1, width)]
        field[ix(x, height - 1, width)] = field[ix(x, height - 2, width)]
        x = x + 1
    }

    // Corners
    field[ix(0, 0, width)] = (field[ix(1, 0, width)] + field[ix(0, 1, width)]) / 2.0
    field[ix(width - 1, 0, width)] = (field[ix(width - 2, 0, width)] + field[ix(width - 1, 1, width)]) / 2.0
    field[ix(0, height - 1, width)] = (field[ix(1, height - 1, width)] + field[ix(0, height - 2, width)]) / 2.0
    field[ix(width - 1, height - 1, width)] = (field[ix(width - 2, height - 1, width)] + field[ix(width - 1, height - 2, width)]) / 2.0
}

// Apply boundary conditions to velocity field
fn set_bounds_velocity(u: &![f64], v: &![f64], width: i32, height: i32) with Mut, Panic {
    // U velocity (horizontal): reverse at left/right walls
    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        u[ix(0, y, width)] = 0.0 - u[ix(1, y, width)]
        u[ix(width - 1, y, width)] = 0.0 - u[ix(width - 2, y, width)]
        y = y + 1
    }

    // V velocity (vertical): reverse at top/bottom walls
    var x = 1
    while x < width - 1 {
        v[ix(x, 0, width)] = 0.0 - v[ix(x, 1, width)]
        v[ix(x, height - 1, width)] = 0.0 - v[ix(x, height - 2, width)]
        x = x + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Diffusion (Implicit Method)
// ============================================================================

// Gauss-Seidel relaxation for diffusion
fn diffuse(
    current: &![f64],
    prev: &[f64],
    diff_coeff: f64,
    dt: f64,
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    iterations: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let a = dt * diff_coeff * ((width - 2) * (height - 2)) as f64

    var iter = 0
    while iter < iterations {
        var y = 1
        while y < height - 1 {
            var x = 1
            while x < width - 1 {
                let idx = ix(x, y, width)

                let neighbors =
                    current[ix(x - 1, y, width)] +
                    current[ix(x + 1, y, width)] +
                    current[ix(x, y - 1, width)] +
                    current[ix(x, y + 1, width)]

                current[idx] = (prev[idx] + a * neighbors) / (1.0 + 4.0 * a)

                x = x + 1
            }
            y = y + 1
        }

        set_bounds_scalar(current, width, height)
        iter = iter + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Advection (Semi-Lagrangian)
// ============================================================================

// Advect scalar field by velocity field
fn advect(
    current: &![f64],
    prev: &[f64],
    u: &[f64],
    v: &[f64],
    dt: f64,
    width: i32,
    height: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let dt_x = dt * (width - 2) as f64
    let dt_y = dt * (height - 2) as f64

    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        var x = 1
        while x < width - 1 {
            let idx = ix(x, y, width)

            // Backtrack position
            let x_back = (x as f64) - dt_x * u[idx]
            let y_back = (y as f64) - dt_y * v[idx]

            // Clamp to grid bounds
            let x_clamp = if x_back < 0.5 {
                0.5
            } else { if x_back > (width as f64) - 1.5 {
                (width as f64) - 1.5
            } else {
                x_back
            }}

            let y_clamp = if y_back < 0.5 {
                0.5
            } else { if y_back > (height as f64) - 1.5 {
                (height as f64) - 1.5
            } else {
                y_back
            }}

            // Bilinear interpolation
            let i0 = x_clamp as i32
            let i1 = i0 + 1
            let j0 = y_clamp as i32
            let j1 = j0 + 1

            let s1 = x_clamp - (i0 as f64)
            let s0 = 1.0 - s1
            let t1 = y_clamp - (j0 as f64)
            let t0 = 1.0 - t1

            current[idx] =
                s0 * (t0 * prev[ix(i0, j0, width)] + t1 * prev[ix(i0, j1, width)]) +
                s1 * (t0 * prev[ix(i1, j0, width)] + t1 * prev[ix(i1, j1, width)])

            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    set_bounds_scalar(current, width, height)
}

// ============================================================================
// Projection (Incompressibility)
// ============================================================================

// Project velocity field to be divergence-free
fn project(
    u: &![f64],
    v: &![f64],
    p: &![f64],    // Pressure
    div: &![f64],  // Divergence
    width: i32,
    height: i32,
    iterations: i32
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Compute divergence
    var y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        var x = 1
        while x < width - 1 {
            let idx = ix(x, y, width)

            div[idx] = -0.5 * (
                u[ix(x + 1, y, width)] - u[ix(x - 1, y, width)] +
                v[ix(x, y + 1, width)] - v[ix(x, y - 1, width)]
            ) / (width as f64)

            p[idx] = 0.0

            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    set_bounds_scalar(div, width, height)
    set_bounds_scalar(p, width, height)

    // Solve for pressure (Gauss-Seidel)
    var iter = 0
    while iter < iterations {
        y = 1
        while y < height - 1 {
            x = 1
            while x < width - 1 {
                let idx = ix(x, y, width)

                p[idx] = (
                    div[idx] +
                    p[ix(x - 1, y, width)] +
                    p[ix(x + 1, y, width)] +
                    p[ix(x, y - 1, width)] +
                    p[ix(x, y + 1, width)]
                ) / 4.0

                x = x + 1
            }
            y = y + 1
        }

        set_bounds_scalar(p, width, height)
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    // Subtract pressure gradient from velocity
    y = 1
    while y < height - 1 {
        x = 1
        while x < width - 1 {
            let idx = ix(x, y, width)

            u[idx] = u[idx] - 0.5 * (width as f64) * (p[ix(x + 1, y, width)] - p[ix(x - 1, y, width)])
            v[idx] = v[idx] - 0.5 * (height as f64) * (p[ix(x, y + 1, width)] - p[ix(x, y - 1, width)])

            x = x + 1
        }
        y = y + 1
    }

    set_bounds_velocity(u, v, width, height)
}

// ============================================================================
// Fluid Simulation Step
// ============================================================================

fn fluid_step(fluid: &!FluidGrid) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let width = fluid.width
    let height = fluid.height
    let dt = fluid.dt
    let visc = fluid.viscosity
    let diff = fluid.diffusion

    // Temporary arrays for projection
    var p: [f64; 2500] = [0.0; 2500]
    var div: [f64; 2500] = [0.0; 2500]

    // ========================================================================
    // Velocity Step
    // ========================================================================

    // Diffusion (viscosity)
    if visc > 0.0001 {
        diffuse(&!fluid.u, &fluid.u_prev, visc, dt, width, height, 4)
        diffuse(&!fluid.v, &fluid.v_prev, visc, dt, width, height, 4)
    }

    // Projection (incompressibility)
    project(&!fluid.u, &!fluid.v, &!p, &!div, width, height, 4)

    // Save for advection
    fluid.u_prev = fluid.u
    fluid.v_prev = fluid.v

    // Advection (self-advection of velocity)
    advect(&!fluid.u, &fluid.u_prev, &fluid.u_prev, &fluid.v_prev, dt, width, height)
    advect(&!fluid.v, &fluid.v_prev, &fluid.u_prev, &fluid.v_prev, dt, width, height)

    // Final projection
    project(&!fluid.u, &!fluid.v, &!p, &!div, width, height, 4)

    // ========================================================================
    // Density Step
    // ========================================================================

    // Diffusion
    if diff > 0.0001 {
        diffuse(&!fluid.density, &fluid.density_prev, diff, dt, width, height, 4)
        fluid.density_prev = fluid.density
    }

    // Advection
    advect(&!fluid.density, &fluid.density_prev, &fluid.u, &fluid.v, dt, width, height)
}

// ============================================================================
// User Interaction Helpers
// ============================================================================

// Add density at position
fn add_density(fluid: &!FluidGrid, x: i32, y: i32, amount: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < fluid.width && y >= 0 && y < fluid.height {
        let idx = ix(x, y, fluid.width)
        fluid.density[idx] = fluid.density[idx] + amount
    }
}

// Add velocity at position
fn add_velocity(fluid: &!FluidGrid, x: i32, y: i32, vx: f64, vy: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    if x >= 0 && x < fluid.width && y >= 0 && y < fluid.height {
        let idx = ix(x, y, fluid.width)
        fluid.u[idx] = fluid.u[idx] + vx
        fluid.v[idx] = fluid.v[idx] + vy
    }
}

// Clear density field
fn clear_density(fluid: &!FluidGrid) with Mut {
    fluid.density = [0.0; 2500]
}

// Fade density over time
fn fade_density(fluid: &!FluidGrid, fade_rate: f64) with Mut, Panic {
    var i = 0
    while i < fluid.width * fluid.height {
        fluid.density[i] = fluid.density[i] * fade_rate
        i = i + 1
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// Rendering
// ============================================================================

// Render fluid density as heatmap
fn fluid_render(
    canvas: Canvas,
    fluid: &FluidGrid,
    vp: &Viewport,
    colormap: i32
) -> Canvas with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Find max density for normalization
    var max_density = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < fluid.width * fluid.height {
        if fluid.density[i] > max_density {
            max_density = fluid.density[i]
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    // Render using heatmap
    return heatmap(
        canvas,
        vp,
        &fluid.density,
        fluid.width,
        fluid.height,
        0.0,
        max_density,
        colormap
    )
}

// ============================================================================
// Example/Test Function
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("\x1b[2J\x1b[H")  // Clear screen
    print("=== Fluid Simulation Test ===\n\n")

    // Create fluid grid
    var fluid = fluid_grid_new(30, 30, 0.0, 0.0001)

    print("Fluid grid created:\n")
    print("  Size: ")
    print_i32(fluid.width)
    print(" x ")
    print_i32(fluid.height)
    print("\n")
    print("  Viscosity: ")
    print_f64(fluid.viscosity)
    print("\n")
    print("  Diffusion: ")
    print_f64(fluid.diffusion)
    print("\n\n")

    // Add some initial density and velocity
    add_density(&!fluid, 15, 15, 100.0)
    add_velocity(&!fluid, 15, 15, 5.0, 3.0)

    print("Initial conditions:\n")
    print("  Density at (15, 15): ")
    print_f64(fluid.density[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
    print("\n")
    print("  Velocity at (15, 15): (")
    print_f64(fluid.u[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
    print(", ")
    print_f64(fluid.v[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
    print(")\n\n")

    // Simulate a few steps
    print("Simulation steps:\n")

    var step = 0
    while step < 5 {
        fluid_step(&!fluid)

        print("  Step ")
        print_i32(step)
        print(": density at (15, 15) = ")
        print_f64(fluid.density[ix(15, 15, fluid.width)])
        print("\n")

        step = step + 1
    }

    print("\n=== Fluid Simulation Ready ===\n")
    print("Methods:\n")
    print("  • add_density(x, y, amount) - Add dye\n")
    print("  • add_velocity(x, y, vx, vy) - Add force\n")
    print("  • fluid_step() - Advance simulation\n")
    print("  • fluid_render() - Visualize density field\n")

    return 0
}
