    (cx - ax) * (by - ay) - (cy - ay) * (bx - ax)
}

fn project_vertex(v: Vertex, width: i64, height: i64) -> Vertex2D {
    let px = ((v.pos.x + 1.0) * 0.5) * ((width - 1) as f64)
    let py = (1.0 - ((v.pos.y + 1.0) * 0.5)) * ((height - 1) as f64)
    Vertex2D {
        x: px,
        y: py,
        z: v.pos.z,
        r: v.col.r,
        g: v.col.g,
        b: v.col.b,
    }
}

fn emit_ppm(
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    fb_r: &[i64; 65536],
    fb_g: &[i64; 65536],
    fb_b: &[i64; 65536]
) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("P3\n")
    print_int(width)
    print(" ")
    print_int(height)
    print("\n255\n")

    var i: i64 = 0
    let total = width * height
    while i < total {
        print_int(clamp_byte((*fb_r)[i]))
        print(" ")
        print_int(clamp_byte((*fb_g)[i]))
        print(" ")
        print_int(clamp_byte((*fb_b)[i]))
        print("\n")
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn fill_background(
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_g: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_b: &![i64; 65536]
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var py: i64 = 0
    while py < height {
        var px: i64 = 0
        while px < width {
            let idx = py * width + px
            (*fb_r)[idx] = 12 + py / 10 + px / 32
            (*fb_g)[idx] = 16 + py / 8
            (*fb_b)[idx] = 28 + py / 5
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

fn rasterize_triangle(
    width: i64,
    height: i64,
    v0: Vertex2D,
    v1: Vertex2D,
    v2: Vertex2D,
    area: f64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_g: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_b: &![i64; 65536]
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var py: i64 = 0
    while py < height {
        var px: i64 = 0
        while px < width {
            let cx = (px as f64) + 0.5
            let cy = (py as f64) + 0.5

            let w0 = edge_fn(v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y, cx, cy)
            let w1 = edge_fn(v2.x, v2.y, v0.x, v0.y, cx, cy)
            let w2 = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, cx, cy)

            let inside = if area > 0.0 {
                w0 >= 0.0 && w1 >= 0.0 && w2 >= 0.0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0.0 && w1 <= 0.0 && w2 <= 0.0
            }

            if inside {
                let b0 = w0 / area
                let b1 = w1 / area
                let b2 = w2 / area

                let r = b0 * v0.r + b1 * v1.r + b2 * v2.r
                let g = b0 * v0.g + b1 * v1.g + b2 * v2.g
                let b_col = b0 * v0.b + b1 * v1.b + b2 * v2.b
                let shade = 0.82 + (1.0 - (b0 * v0.z + b1 * v1.z + b2 * v2.z)) * 0.2

                let idx = py * width + px
                (*fb_r)[idx] = clamp_byte((r * shade * 255.0) as i64)
                (*fb_g)[idx] = clamp_byte((g * shade * 255.0) as i64)
                (*fb_b)[idx] = clamp_byte((b_col * shade * 255.0) as i64)
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let width: i64 = 128
    let height: i64 = 128

    var fb_r: [i64; 65536] = [0; 65536]
    var fb_g: [i64; 65536] = [0; 65536]
    var fb_b: [i64; 65536] = [0; 65536]

    fill_background(width, height, &! fb_r, &! fb_g, &! fb_b)

    let tri = make_triangle()
    let v0 = project_vertex(tri.v0, width, height)
    let v1 = project_vertex(tri.v1, width, height)
    let v2 = project_vertex(tri.v2, width, height)
    let area = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y)

    rasterize_triangle(width, height, v0, v1, v2, area, &! fb_r, &! fb_g, &! fb_b)

    emit_ppm(width, height, &fb_r, &fb_g, &fb_b)
}


// === FILE: examples/render/triangle_ppm.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Software-rasterized triangle output as PPM P3
//
// Run: souc run examples/render/triangle_ppm.sio > triangle.ppm
// View: display triangle.ppm  (or open in any image viewer)
//
// Barycentric coordinate interpolation with per-vertex colors:
//   v0 (top, red), v1 (bottom-left, green), v2 (bottom-right, blue)

struct Vertex2D { x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, r: f64, g: f64, b: f64 }

fn edge_fn(ax: f64, ay: f64, bx: f64, by: f64, cx: f64, cy: f64) -> f64 {
    (cx - ax) * (by - ay) - (cy - ay) * (bx - ax)
}

fn min_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn max_i64(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }
fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a < b { a } else { b } }
fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { if a > b { a } else { b } }

fn clamp_byte(v: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0 { return 0 }
    if v > 255 { return 255 }
    v
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let w: i64 = 128
    let h: i64 = 128

    // Framebuffer (128x128 = 16384 pixels)
    var fb_r: [i64; 16384] = [20; 16384]
    var fb_g: [i64; 16384] = [20; 16384]
    var fb_b: [i64; 16384] = [30; 16384]

    // Triangle vertices in pixel coordinates
    let v0 = Vertex2D { x: 64.0, y: 10.0, z: 0.0, r: 1.0, g: 0.0, b: 0.0 }
    let v1 = Vertex2D { x: 20.0, y: 110.0, z: 0.0, r: 0.0, g: 1.0, b: 0.0 }
    let v2 = Vertex2D { x: 108.0, y: 110.0, z: 0.0, r: 0.0, g: 0.0, b: 1.0 }

    let area = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y)

    // Rasterize
    var py: i64 = 0
    while py < h {
        var px: i64 = 0
        while px < w {
            let cx = (px as f64) + 0.5
            let cy = (py as f64) + 0.5

            let w0 = edge_fn(v1.x, v1.y, v2.x, v2.y, cx, cy)
            let w1 = edge_fn(v2.x, v2.y, v0.x, v0.y, cx, cy)
            let w2 = edge_fn(v0.x, v0.y, v1.x, v1.y, cx, cy)

            let inside = if area > 0.0 {
                w0 >= 0.0 && w1 >= 0.0 && w2 >= 0.0
            } else {
                w0 <= 0.0 && w1 <= 0.0 && w2 <= 0.0
            }

            if inside {
                let b0 = w0 / area
                let b1 = w1 / area
                let b2 = w2 / area

                let r = b0 * v0.r + b1 * v1.r + b2 * v2.r
                let g = b0 * v0.g + b1 * v1.g + b2 * v2.g
                let b_col = b0 * v0.b + b1 * v1.b + b2 * v2.b

                let idx = py * w + px
                fb_r[idx] = clamp_byte((r * 255.0) as i64)
                fb_g[idx] = clamp_byte((g * 255.0) as i64)
                fb_b[idx] = clamp_byte((b_col * 255.0) as i64)
            }
            px = px + 1
        }
        py = py + 1
    }

    // Emit PPM P3
    print("P3\n")
    print_int(w)
    print(" ")
    print_int(h)
    print("\n255\n")
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < w * h {
        print_int(fb_r[i])
        print(" ")
        print_int(fb_g[i])
        print(" ")
        print_int(fb_b[i])
        print("\n")
        i = i + 1
    }

}


// === FILE: examples/render/uncertainty_field.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Uncertainty field visualization — epistemic rendering showcase
//
// Renders a 2D grid of Knowledge values as a color-mapped heatmap
// where color intensity = value and blur/alpha = uncertainty.
// This is Sounio's novel contribution: type-directed uncertainty rendering.
// Integer arithmetic version (scaled by 1000 to avoid f64).

struct Color { r: i64, g: i64, b: i64, a: i64 }

fn clamp_byte(v: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0 { return 0 }
    if v > 255 { return 255 }
    v
}

// uncertainty_to_alpha: higher uncertainty → more transparent (scaled *1000)
fn uncertainty_to_alpha_1000(eps_1000: i64) -> i64 with Div {
    let clamped = if eps_1000 > 1000 { 1000 } else { eps_1000 }
    1000 - clamped * 700 / 1000
}

// value_to_color: temperature colormap blue→red, alpha modulated by uncertainty
// v_1000 and eps_1000 are scaled *1000
fn value_to_color(v_1000: i64, eps_1000: i64) -> Color with Div {
    let t_1000 = if v_1000 > 1000 { 1000 } else { if v_1000 < 0 { 0 } else { v_1000 } }
    Color {
        r: t_1000,
        g: 200,
        b: 1000 - t_1000,
        a: uncertainty_to_alpha_1000(eps_1000),
    }
}

fn fill_channel(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, rw: i64, rh: i64,
    v: i64,
    fb: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dy: i64 = 0
    while dy < rh {
        var dx: i64 = 0
        while dx < rw {
            let px = x0 + dx
            let py = y0 + dy
            if px >= 0 && px < fb_w && py >= 0 && py < fb_h {
                let idx = py * fb_w + px;
                (*fb)[idx] = v;
            }
            dx = dx + 1
        }
        dy = dy + 1
    }
}

fn get_channel(fb: &[i64; 65536], i: i64) -> i64 with Panic {
    (*fb)[i]
}

fn rasterize_rect(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, rw: i64, rh: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    fill_channel(x0, y0, rw, rh, r, fb_r, fb_w, fb_h)
    fill_channel(x0, y0, rw, rh, g, fb_g, fb_w, fb_h)
    fill_channel(x0, y0, rw, rh, b, fb_b, fb_w, fb_h)
}

fn emit_ppm(
    w: i64, h: i64,
    fb_r: &[i64; 65536], fb_g: &[i64; 65536], fb_b: &[i64; 65536]
) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("P3\n")
    print_int(w)
    print(" ")
    print_int(h)
    print("\n255\n")
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < w * h {
        print_int(clamp_byte(get_channel(fb_r, i)))
        print(" ")
        print_int(clamp_byte(get_channel(fb_g, i)))
        print(" ")
        print_int(clamp_byte(get_channel(fb_b, i)))
        print("\n")
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let w: i64 = 128
    let h: i64 = 128
    let cell_w: i64 = 8
    let cell_h: i64 = 8

    var fb_r: [i64; 65536] = [10; 65536]
    var fb_g: [i64; 65536] = [10; 65536]
    var fb_b: [i64; 65536] = [14; 65536]

    var gy: i64 = 0
    while gy < 16 {
        var gx: i64 = 0
        while gx < 16 {
            // value = gx / 15 (scaled *1000)
            let value_1000 = gx * 1000 / 15
            // eps = gy / 15 (scaled *1000)
            let eps_1000 = gy * 1000 / 15
            let c = value_to_color(value_1000, eps_1000)
            // brightness = 1.0 - eps * 0.7 = c.a (scaled *1000)
            let brightness_1000 = c.a
            // r, g, b: channel * brightness * 255 / 1000000
            let r = clamp_byte(c.r * brightness_1000 * 255 / 1000000)
            let g = clamp_byte(c.g * brightness_1000 * 255 / 1000000)
            let b = clamp_byte(c.b * brightness_1000 * 255 / 1000000)
            rasterize_rect(
                gx * cell_w, gy * cell_h, cell_w, cell_h,
                r, g, b,
                &!fb_r, &!fb_g, &!fb_b, w, h
            )
            gx = gx + 1
        }
        gy = gy + 1
    }

    emit_ppm(w, h, &fb_r, &fb_g, &fb_b)
}


// === FILE: examples/render/uncertainty_ppm.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Uncertainty field rendered as PPM — epistemic heatmap
//
// Run: souc run examples/render/uncertainty_ppm.sio > uncertainty.ppm
//
// 16x16 grid of "measurements" with varying uncertainty.
// Color: temperature map (blue→red). Alpha/brightness modulated by uncertainty.
// Integer arithmetic version (scaled by 1000 to avoid f64).

fn clamp_byte(v: i64) -> i64 {
    if v < 0 { return 0 }
    if v > 255 { return 255 }
    v
}

fn fill_channel(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, rw: i64, rh: i64,
    v: i64,
    fb: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var dy: i64 = 0
    while dy < rh {
        var dx: i64 = 0
        while dx < rw {
            let px = x0 + dx
            let py = y0 + dy
            if px >= 0 && px < fb_w && py >= 0 && py < fb_h {
                let idx = py * fb_w + px;
                (*fb)[idx] = v;
            }
            dx = dx + 1
        }
        dy = dy + 1
    }
}

fn get_channel(fb: &[i64; 65536], i: i64) -> i64 with Panic {
    (*fb)[i]
}

fn rasterize_rect(
    x0: i64, y0: i64, rw: i64, rh: i64,
    r: i64, g: i64, b: i64,
    fb_r: &![i64; 65536], fb_g: &![i64; 65536], fb_b: &![i64; 65536],
    fb_w: i64, fb_h: i64
) with Mut, Panic, Div {
    fill_channel(x0, y0, rw, rh, r, fb_r, fb_w, fb_h)
    fill_channel(x0, y0, rw, rh, g, fb_g, fb_w, fb_h)
    fill_channel(x0, y0, rw, rh, b, fb_b, fb_w, fb_h)
}

fn emit_ppm(
    w: i64, h: i64,
    fb_r: &[i64; 65536], fb_g: &[i64; 65536], fb_b: &[i64; 65536]
) with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    print("P3\n")
    print_int(w)
    print(" ")
    print_int(h)
    print("\n255\n")
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < w * h {
        print_int(get_channel(fb_r, i))
        print(" ")
        print_int(get_channel(fb_g, i))
        print(" ")
        print_int(get_channel(fb_b, i))
        print("\n")
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    let w: i64 = 128
    let h: i64 = 128

    var fb_r: [i64; 65536] = [10; 65536]
    var fb_g: [i64; 65536] = [10; 65536]
    var fb_b: [i64; 65536] = [15; 65536]

    // Render 16x16 grid of uncertainty cells
    let cell_w: i64 = 8
    let cell_h: i64 = 8

    var gy: i64 = 0
    while gy < 16 {
        var gx: i64 = 0
        while gx < 16 {
            // value = gx / 15 (scaled *1000)
            let value_1000 = gx * 1000 / 15
            // eps = gy / 15 (scaled *1000)
            let eps_1000 = gy * 1000 / 15
            // confidence = 1.0 - eps * 0.7 (scaled *1000)
            let conf_1000 = 1000 - eps_1000 * 700 / 1000

            // Temperature colormap modulated by confidence
            let r_byte = clamp_byte(value_1000 * conf_1000 * 255 / 1000000)
            let g_byte = clamp_byte(38 * conf_1000 / 1000)
            let b_byte = clamp_byte((1000 - value_1000) * conf_1000 * 255 / 1000000)

            rasterize_rect(
                gx * cell_w, gy * cell_h, cell_w, cell_h,
                r_byte, g_byte, b_byte,
                &!fb_r, &!fb_g, &!fb_b, w, h
            )
            gx = gx + 1
        }
        gy = gy + 1
    }

    emit_ppm(w, h, &fb_r, &fb_g, &fb_b)
}


// === FILE: examples/run_sedenion_benchmark.sio ===
// Sounio Example: Run Sedenion Benchmark with PAC Learning
//
// Simple runner for the sedenion neural network benchmark
// that demonstrates parameter efficiency and PAC learning bounds

use snn::benchmark

fn main() with IO, Prob, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("Running sedenion benchmark with PAC learning...")

    let config = benchmark::default_hsi_config()
    let result = benchmark::run_kill_switch_benchmark(config)

    let output = benchmark::format_result(result)
    print(output)

    if result.kill_switch_passed {
        print("✓ BENCHMARK PASSED")
    } else {
        print("✗ BENCHMARK FAILED")
    }
}


// === FILE: examples/science/active_inference.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Minimal Friston Active Inference Agent
//
// Karl Friston's Free Energy Principle (2006-present):
//   Every biological system — from cells to brains — acts to minimize
//   variational free energy: an upper bound on the negative log-evidence
//   of sensory observations under the organism's internal model.
//
// Equivalently:
//   Perception = Bayesian inference about the world
//   Action     = selecting actions that maximize expected epistemic confidence
//
// The falsifiable claim:
//   fn act(model: WorldModel) -> (Action, WorldModel)
//       where result.1.epsilon >= model.epsilon
//
//   Actions that REDUCE confidence are rejected by the policy.
//   This refinement type constraint IS free energy minimization.
//
// Implementation:
//   World: 3-position grid {0, 1, 2}
//   State: Bayesian belief (probability distribution over positions)
//   Epsilon: posterior mean of Beta(α,β) — measured as peak belief probability
//   Perceive: Bayesian update from noisy sensor (likelihood * prior, normalize)
//   Act: choose action that maximizes expected epsilon in next step
//
// Semantics note (per external review):
//   epsilon comparison uses POSTERIOR MEANS of Beta distributions.
//   max(p0, p1, p2) = peak probability = alpha/(alpha+beta) for peaked distributions.
//   This is the measurable, comparable quantity (not full distribution comparison).
//
// The Friston connection is real if:
//   (1) perception always increases epsilon (Bayes' theorem guarantees this)
//   (2) the act policy selects epsilon-increasing actions
//   (3) the combined loop shows monotone or bounded-below epsilon trajectory
//
// If the invariant breaks, we document why.

// ── Math helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ── World belief over 3 positions ────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Represents Bayesian belief: P(position = i) for i in {0, 1, 2}
// Invariant: p0 + p1 + p2 = 1.0
//
// Epsilon (epistemic confidence) = max(p0, p1, p2)
// Interpretation: how concentrated is the agent's belief?
//   epsilon = 1/3: uniform (maximum uncertainty)
//   epsilon = 1.0: certain (agent knows exactly where it is)

struct Belief {
    p0: f64,  // P(position = 0)
    p1: f64,  // P(position = 1)
    p2: f64   // P(position = 2)
}

// Epistemic confidence = peak probability (posterior mean proxy)
// For Beta(alpha, beta): mean = alpha/(alpha+beta).
// For a probability vector, the peak IS the dominant "alpha" component.
fn epsilon(b: Belief) -> f64 {
    var m = b.p0
    if b.p1 > m { m = b.p1 }
    if b.p2 > m { m = b.p2 }
    return m
}

// Normalize belief to sum to 1
fn normalize(b: Belief) -> Belief {
    let total = b.p0 + b.p1 + b.p2
    if total < 0.00001 {
        // Degenerate: uniform fallback
        return Belief { p0: 0.3333, p1: 0.3333, p2: 0.3334 }
    }
    return Belief {
        p0: b.p0 / total,
        p1: b.p1 / total,
        p2: b.p2 / total
    }
}

// Uniform prior (maximum uncertainty, minimum epsilon)
fn uniform_belief() -> Belief {
    return Belief { p0: 0.3333, p1: 0.3333, p2: 0.3334 }
}

// ── Sensor model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Noisy observation: P(obs = i | position = j)
// Correct observation with probability 0.7, wrong with 0.3 split between others
//
// likelihood(obs, candidate_pos):
//   0.70 if obs == candidate_pos (correct reading)
//   0.15 otherwise (noise to other positions)

fn likelihood(obs: i32, position: i32) -> f64 {
    if obs == position { return 0.70 }
    return 0.15
}

// ── Perception: Bayesian belief update ────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Bayesian update: P(pos | obs) ∝ P(obs | pos) * P(pos)
// Perception ALWAYS increases epsilon (Bayes' theorem guarantee):
//   posterior is more concentrated than prior when observation is informative
//
// The refinement type claim:
//   fn perceive(b: Belief, obs: i32) -> Belief
//       where epsilon(result) >= epsilon(b)   [when observation is informative]

fn perceive(b: Belief, obs: i32) -> Belief {
    // Likelihood * prior (unnormalized posterior)
    let l0 = likelihood(obs, 0)
    let l1 = likelihood(obs, 1)
    let l2 = likelihood(obs, 2)

    let post = Belief {
        p0: l0 * b.p0,
        p1: l1 * b.p1,
        p2: l2 * b.p2
    }
    return normalize(post)
}

// ── Sensor simulation: LCG pseudo-random ─────────────────────────────────────

struct RngState { seed: i64 }

fn lcg_next(rng: &!RngState) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let modulus: i64 = 4294967296
    rng.seed = (a * rng.seed + c) % modulus
    if rng.seed < 0 { rng.seed = rng.seed + modulus }
    return (rng.seed as f64) / 4294967296.0
}

// Noisy sensor: returns true position with prob 0.7, random otherwise
fn sense(true_pos: i32, rng: &!RngState) -> i32 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let r = lcg_next(rng)
    if r < 0.70 { return true_pos }
    // Noise: pick one of the other two positions
    if r < 0.85 {
        if true_pos == 0 { return 1 }
        if true_pos == 1 { return 0 }
        return 0
    }
    if true_pos == 2 { return 1 }
    return 2
}

// ── Action selection: Free Energy Minimization Policy ─────────────────────────
//
// The agent can take 3 actions:
//   Action 0: Move left  (world position decreases, observation changes)
//   Action 1: Stay       (world position unchanged)
//   Action 2: Move right (world position increases, observation changes)
//
// Policy: choose action that maximizes EXPECTED epsilon after next observation
// Expected epsilon = sum over possible obs: P(obs | belief) * epsilon(perceive(belief, obs))
//
// This is the FREE ENERGY MINIMIZATION policy in discrete form:
//   Expected free energy = -Expected epsilon (minimizing free energy = maximizing epsilon)
//
// The refinement type invariant:
//   act() returns action a* such that: E[epsilon(perceive(move(b, a*), obs))] >= E[...]
//   — in expectation, this action does NOT reduce confidence

fn expected_epsilon_if_obs(b: Belief, obs: i32) -> f64 {
    let b_updated = perceive(b, obs)
    return epsilon(b_updated)
}

// Compute expected epsilon for a given (belief, true_pos_prediction) pair
// E[epsilon] = sum_obs P(obs | belief) * epsilon(perceive(belief, obs))
// P(obs=i | belief) = sum_j P(obs=i | pos=j) * P(pos=j)
fn expected_epsilon_for_belief(b: Belief) -> f64 {
    // P(obs = 0 | current belief)
    let p_obs0 = likelihood(0, 0) * b.p0 + likelihood(0, 1) * b.p1 + likelihood(0, 2) * b.p2
    // P(obs = 1 | current belief)
    let p_obs1 = likelihood(1, 0) * b.p0 + likelihood(1, 1) * b.p1 + likelihood(1, 2) * b.p2
    // P(obs = 2 | current belief)
    let p_obs2 = likelihood(2, 0) * b.p0 + likelihood(2, 1) * b.p1 + likelihood(2, 2) * b.p2

    let e0 = expected_epsilon_if_obs(b, 0)
    let e1 = expected_epsilon_if_obs(b, 1)
    let e2 = expected_epsilon_if_obs(b, 2)

    return p_obs0 * e0 + p_obs1 * e1 + p_obs2 * e2
}

// Shift belief left (predict: position decreases, obs distribution shifts)
fn belief_shift_left(b: Belief) -> Belief {
    // If agent moves left, it now maps position 0→out_of_bounds, 1→0, 2→1
    // Belief about what it will observe shifts accordingly
    return Belief { p0: b.p1, p1: b.p2, p2: 0.05 }
}

// Shift belief right
fn belief_shift_right(b: Belief) -> Belief {
    return Belief { p0: 0.05, p1: b.p0, p2: b.p1 }
}

// Act: policy = pick action that maximizes expected epsilon
// Action 0 = move left, Action 1 = stay, Action 2 = move right
fn act(b: Belief) -> i32 {
    let b_left  = normalize(belief_shift_left(b))
    let b_stay  = b
    let b_right = normalize(belief_shift_right(b))

    let e_left  = expected_epsilon_for_belief(b_left)
    let e_stay  = expected_epsilon_for_belief(b_stay)
    let e_right = expected_epsilon_for_belief(b_right)

    // argmax: pick action with highest expected epsilon
    var best_action = 1  // default: stay
    var best_e = e_stay

    if e_left > best_e {
        best_action = 0
        best_e = e_left
    }
    if e_right > best_e {
        best_action = 2
        best_e = e_right
    }

    return best_action
}

// Apply chosen action to true world position
fn apply_action(true_pos: i32, action: i32) -> i32 {
    if action == 0 {
        if true_pos > 0 { return true_pos - 1 }
        return 0
    }
    if action == 2 {
        if true_pos < 2 { return true_pos + 1 }
        return 2
    }
    return true_pos
}

// Apply chosen action to belief state
fn apply_action_to_belief(b: Belief, action: i32) -> Belief {
    if action == 0 { return normalize(belief_shift_left(b)) }
    if action == 2 { return normalize(belief_shift_right(b)) }
    return b
}

// ── Main: Agent Loop ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("================================================================")
    println("  Minimal Friston Active Inference Agent")
    println("  Free Energy as Type Invariant")
    println("================================================================")
    println("")
    println("  World: 3-position grid {0, 1, 2}")
    println("  Sensor: noisy (70% accurate)")
    println("  Epsilon: max(p0, p1, p2) = peak belief probability")
    println("  Policy: argmax_action E[epsilon(perceive(act(model), obs))]")
    println("  Invariant: epsilon must not systematically decrease")
    println("")
    println("  The Friston claim:")
    println("  free energy minimization = maximizing expected epistemic confidence")
    println("")

    var rng = RngState { seed: 42 }

    // Initial state: agent has no idea where it is
    var belief = uniform_belief()
    var true_pos = 1  // Agent starts at center, doesn't know this

    let eps_init = epsilon(belief)
    println("Initial belief: uniform")
    println("Initial epsilon:")
    println(eps_init)
    println("")

    // ── Agent loop: 12 steps ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    println("Step | TruePos | Action | Obs | Epsilon(after perceive)")
    println("-----+---------+--------+-----+------------------------")

    var step = 0
    var min_eps_seen = eps_init
    var max_eps_seen = eps_init
    var eps_violations = 0  // Steps where epsilon decreased significantly

    // Track epsilon trajectory for invariant check
    var prev_eps = eps_init

    while step < 12 {
        // 1. PERCEIVE: sense the world, update belief
        let obs = sense(true_pos, &!rng)
        let belief_after_perceive = perceive(belief, obs)
        let eps_after_perceive = epsilon(belief_after_perceive)

        // 2. ACT: choose action that maximizes expected future epsilon
        let action = act(belief_after_perceive)

        // 3. Execute action: update true world position and belief
        true_pos = apply_action(true_pos, action)
        belief = apply_action_to_belief(belief_after_perceive, action)

        // ── Invariant check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // The Friston invariant: epsilon should NOT systematically decrease
        // Small decreases from noisy observations are expected (Bayesian)
        // Large sustained decreases indicate policy failure
        let eps_drop = prev_eps - eps_after_perceive
        if eps_drop > 0.10 {
            eps_violations = eps_violations + 1
        }

        if eps_after_perceive < min_eps_seen { min_eps_seen = eps_after_perceive }
        if eps_after_perceive > max_eps_seen { max_eps_seen = eps_after_perceive }
        prev_eps = eps_after_perceive

        // ── Print step ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        if action == 0 {
            println("  <- LEFT")
        }
        if action == 1 {
            println("  == STAY")
        }
        if action == 2 {
            println("  -> RIGHT")
        }
        println("  true_pos:")
        println(true_pos)
        println("  observation:")
        println(obs)
        println("  epsilon after perceive:")
        println(eps_after_perceive)
        println("")

        step = step + 1
    }

    // ── Final invariant assessment ─────────────────────────────────────────
    println("================================================================")
    println("  INVARIANT ASSESSMENT")
    println("================================================================")
    println("")

    let eps_final = epsilon(belief)
    println("  Initial epsilon:")
    println(eps_init)
    println("  Final epsilon:")
    println(eps_final)
    println("  Min epsilon seen (noisy observations cause transient drops):")
    println(min_eps_seen)
    println("  Max epsilon seen:")
    println(max_eps_seen)
    println("  Steps with epsilon drop > 0.10 (significant decreases):")
    println(eps_violations)
    println("")

    // The Friston invariant: final epsilon should be >= initial
    // (agent has learned something about its position over 12 steps)
    if eps_final >= eps_init {
        println("  [PASS] Final epsilon >= initial epsilon.")
        println("         The agent's belief CONVERGED over 12 steps.")
        println("         Free energy was minimized: uncertainty decreased.")
    } else {
        println("  [NOTE] Final epsilon < initial epsilon.")
        println("         With only 3 positions and noisy sensor,")
        println("         12 steps should suffice for convergence.")
        println("         If this fails with seed=42: document sensor model.")
    }

    println("")
    println("  [REFINEMENT TYPE]")
    println("  The invariant 'result.epsilon >= model.epsilon' holds")
    println("  in expectation across the perception loop.")
    println("  Semantics: epsilon = max(p0,p1,p2) = posterior mean proxy.")
    println("  Comparison: f64 comparison on posterior means (not full Beta).")
    println("")
    println("  The Friston connection: this agent minimizes free energy")
    println("  by construction. The policy (argmax expected epsilon) IS")
    println("  the active inference policy for discrete state spaces.")
    println("  Perception = Bayesian update. Action = expected free energy min.")
    println("")
    println("  [PASS] Friston active inference agent complete.")

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/bayesian_clinical_trial.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: BAYESIAN CLINICAL TRIAL PASSED
// Bayesian Sequential Clinical Trial -- Beta-Binomial Model
// Demonstrates Bayesian updating for adaptive clinical trial design,
// the methodology that accelerated COVID-19 vaccine approval.
// Prior: Beta(1,1) = uniform (epistemic ignorance)
// Reference: Berry et al. "Bayesian Adaptive Methods for Clinical Trials" (2011)

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x / 2.0
    if g < 0.001 { g = 0.001 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 50 { g = (g + x / g) / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    return g
}

struct LCG { state: f64 }

fn lcg_next(rng: &!LCG) -> f64 with Mut {
    let a = 1664525.0
    let c = 1013904223.0
    let m = 4294967296.0
    var next = a * rng.state + c
    while next >= m { next = next - m }
    while next < 0.0 { next = next + m }
    rng.state = next
    return next / m
}

struct BetaPosterior { alpha: f64, beta_param: f64, n_success: i32, n_failure: i32 }

fn beta_mean(p: BetaPosterior) -> f64 { return p.alpha / (p.alpha + p.beta_param) }

fn beta_std(p: BetaPosterior) -> f64 with Mut {
    let a = p.alpha
    let b = p.beta_param
    let ab = a + b
    return sqrt_f64((a * b) / (ab * ab * (ab + 1.0)))
}

fn beta_ci_lower(p: BetaPosterior) -> f64 with Mut {
    let lo = beta_mean(p) - 1.96 * beta_std(p)
    if lo < 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    return lo
}

fn beta_ci_upper(p: BetaPosterior) -> f64 with Mut {
    let hi = beta_mean(p) + 1.96 * beta_std(p)
    if hi > 1.0 { return 1.0 }
    return hi
}

fn update_posterior(prior: BetaPosterior, succ: i32, fail: i32) -> BetaPosterior {
    return BetaPosterior {
        alpha: prior.alpha + (succ as f64), beta_param: prior.beta_param + (fail as f64),
        n_success: prior.n_success + succ, n_failure: prior.n_failure + fail
    }
}

fn run_batch(rng: &!LCG, n: i32, eff: f64) -> i32 with Mut {
    var succ = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < n {
        if lcg_next(rng) < eff { succ = succ + 1 }
        i = i + 1
    }
    return succ
}

fn print_round(r: i32, p: BetaPosterior) -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    print("  Round ")
    print(r)
    print(": n=")
    print(p.n_success + p.n_failure)
    print("  successes=")
    print(p.n_success)
    print("  mean=")
    println(beta_mean(p))
    print("    95% CI: [")
    print(beta_ci_lower(p))
    print(", ")
    print(beta_ci_upper(p))
    print("]  sd=")
    println(beta_std(p))
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    println("=== Bayesian Sequential Clinical Trial ===")
    println("Prior: Beta(1,1) = uniform | True efficacy: 0.72")
    println("")
    let true_eff = 0.72
    var post = BetaPosterior { alpha: 1.0, beta_param: 1.0, n_success: 0, n_failure: 0 }
    var rng = LCG { state: 42.0 }

    // 5 rounds of 20 patients each
    let s1 = run_batch(&!rng, 20, true_eff)
    post = update_posterior(post, s1, 20 - s1)
    let d1 = print_round(1, post)
    let s2 = run_batch(&!rng, 20, true_eff)
    post = update_posterior(post, s2, 20 - s2)
    let d2 = print_round(2, post)
    let s3 = run_batch(&!rng, 20, true_eff)
    post = update_posterior(post, s3, 20 - s3)
    let d3 = print_round(3, post)
    let s4 = run_batch(&!rng, 20, true_eff)
    post = update_posterior(post, s4, 20 - s4)
    let d4 = print_round(4, post)
    let s5 = run_batch(&!rng, 20, true_eff)
    post = update_posterior(post, s5, 20 - s5)
    let d5 = print_round(5, post)
    println("")

    // Validation
    var all_ok = true
    let m = beta_mean(post)
    let sd = beta_std(post)
    let ci_lo = beta_ci_lower(post)
    let ci_hi = beta_ci_upper(post)

    let err = abs_f64(m - true_eff)
    print("Check 1: |mean - 0.72| < 0.1 ... err=")
    print(err)
    if err < 0.1 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 2: 95% CI contains 0.72 ... ")
    if ci_lo < true_eff && ci_hi > true_eff { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 3: sd < 0.1 ... sd=")
    print(sd)
    if sd < 0.1 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 4: mean > 0.5 (drug effective) ... ")
    if m > 0.5 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    let ci_w = ci_hi - ci_lo
    print("Check 5: CI width < 0.3 ... w=")
    print(ci_w)
    if ci_w < 0.3 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    println("")
    if all_ok { println("BAYESIAN CLINICAL TRIAL PASSED") } else { println("BAYESIAN CLINICAL TRIAL FAILED") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/entropy_information.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: INFORMATION THEORY PASSED
// Shannon Information Theory -- The Mathematics of Knowledge
// Entropy, mutual information, KL divergence, channel capacity.
// Reference: Shannon (1948), Cover & Thomas (2006)

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}
fn log2_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 { term = term * t2; sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64); k = k + 1 }
    return (2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453) / 0.6931471805599453
}
fn entropy(p: &[f64; 16], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut {
    var h = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { if p[i] > 1.0e-15 { h = h - p[i] * log2_f64(p[i]) }; i = i + 1 }
    return h
}
fn joint_entropy(j: &[f64; 16], nx: i32, ny: i32) -> f64 with Mut {
    var h = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < nx { var jj = 0; while jj < ny { let p = j[i * ny + jj]; if p > 1.0e-15 { h = h - p * log2_f64(p) }; jj = jj + 1 }; i = i + 1 }
    return h
}
fn marginal_x(j: &[f64; 16], nx: i32, ny: i32, o: &![f64; 16]) with Mut {
    var i = 0
    while i < nx { var s = 0.0; var jj = 0; while jj < ny { s = s + j[i * ny + jj]; jj = jj + 1 }; o[i] = s; i = i + 1 }
}
fn marginal_y(j: &[f64; 16], nx: i32, ny: i32, o: &![f64; 16]) with Mut {
    var jj = 0
    while jj < ny { var s = 0.0; var i = 0; while i < nx { s = s + j[i * ny + jj]; i = i + 1 }; o[jj] = s; jj = jj + 1 }
}
fn mutual_info(j: &[f64; 16], nx: i32, ny: i32) -> f64 with Mut {
    var mx: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    var my: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    marginal_x(j, nx, ny, &!mx)
    marginal_y(j, nx, ny, &!my)
    return entropy(&mx, nx) + entropy(&my, ny) - joint_entropy(j, nx, ny)
}
fn kl_div(p: &[f64; 16], q: &[f64; 16], n: i32) -> f64 with Mut {
    var d = 0.0
    var i = 0
    while i < n { if p[i] > 1.0e-15 { if q[i] > 1.0e-15 { d = d + p[i] * log2_f64(p[i] / q[i]) } else { d = d + 1.0e10 } }; i = i + 1 }
    return d
}
fn binary_entropy(p: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if p <= 0.0 || p >= 1.0 { return 0.0 }
    return 0.0 - p * log2_f64(p) - (1.0 - p) * log2_f64(1.0 - p)
}
fn bsc_cap(p: f64) -> f64 with Mut { return 1.0 - binary_entropy(p) }

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    println("=== Shannon Information Theory ===")
    var ok = true
    // 1: Fair coin = 1.0 bit
    var fair: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    fair[0] = 0.5
    fair[1] = 0.5
    let h1 = entropy(&fair, 2)
    print("1: H(fair)=")
    print(h1)
    if abs_f64(h1 - 1.0) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 2: Biased coin H ~ 0.469
    var b2: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    b2[0] = 0.9
    b2[1] = 0.1
    print("2: H(.9,.1)=")
    print(entropy(&b2, 2))
    if abs_f64(entropy(&b2, 2) - 0.469) < 0.01 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 3: Uniform 4 = 2 bits; also used as independent joint for test 4
    var u4: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    u4[0] = 0.25
    u4[1] = 0.25
    u4[2] = 0.25
    u4[3] = 0.25
    print("3: H(u4)=")
    print(entropy(&u4, 4))
    if abs_f64(entropy(&u4, 4) - 2.0) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 4: Independent -> I(X;Y)=0
    let mi4 = mutual_info(&u4, 2, 2)
    print("4: I(indep)=")
    print(mi4)
    if abs_f64(mi4) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 5: Correlated -> I(X;Y) > 0
    var co: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    co[0] = 0.4
    co[1] = 0.1
    co[2] = 0.1
    co[3] = 0.4
    let mi5 = mutual_info(&co, 2, 2)
    print("5: I(corr)=")
    print(mi5)
    if mi5 > 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 6: Perfect correlation I(X;X) = H(X) = 1
    var pf: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    pf[0] = 0.5
    pf[3] = 0.5
    let mi6 = mutual_info(&pf, 2, 2)
    print("6: I(X;X)=")
    print(mi6)
    if abs_f64(mi6 - 1.0) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 7: KL >= 0 (Gibbs inequality)
    var p7: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    p7[0] = 0.7
    p7[1] = 0.2
    p7[2] = 0.1
    var q7: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    q7[0] = 0.33333
    q7[1] = 0.33333
    q7[2] = 0.33334
    let kl7 = kl_div(&p7, &q7, 3)
    print("7: KL>=0: ")
    print(kl7)
    if kl7 >= 0.0 - 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    print("   KL(P||P)=")
    print(kl_div(&p7, &p7, 3))
    if abs_f64(kl_div(&p7, &p7, 3)) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 8: KL asymmetry
    let kl_qp = kl_div(&q7, &p7, 3)
    print("8: asym=")
    print(abs_f64(kl7 - kl_qp))
    if abs_f64(kl7 - kl_qp) > 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 9: BSC capacity: C(0.1)~0.531, C(0)=1, C(0.5)=0
    print("9: C(.1)=")
    print(bsc_cap(0.1))
    if abs_f64(bsc_cap(0.1) - 0.531) < 0.01 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    print("   C(0)=")
    print(bsc_cap(0.0))
    if abs_f64(bsc_cap(0.0) - 1.0) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    print("   C(.5)=")
    print(bsc_cap(0.5))
    if abs_f64(bsc_cap(0.5)) < 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 10: Data processing inequality: I(X;Z) <= I(X;Y) when X->Y->Z
    var nz: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    nz[0] = 0.35
    nz[1] = 0.15
    nz[2] = 0.15
    nz[3] = 0.35
    let mi_xz = mutual_info(&nz, 2, 2)
    print("10: I(X;Z)=")
    print(mi_xz)
    print("<=")
    print(mi5)
    if mi_xz <= mi5 + 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }
    // 11: H(X|Y) = H(X,Y) - H(Y) <= H(X) and >= 0
    let hxy = joint_entropy(&co, 2, 2)
    var my_c: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    marginal_y(&co, 2, 2, &!my_c)
    let hx_y = hxy - entropy(&my_c, 2)
    var mx_c: [f64; 16] = [0.0; 16]
    marginal_x(&co, 2, 2, &!mx_c)
    let hx = entropy(&mx_c, 2)
    print("11: H(X|Y)=")
    print(hx_y)
    if hx_y <= hx + 0.001 && hx_y >= 0.0 - 0.001 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }

    println("")
    if ok { println("INFORMATION THEORY PASSED") } else { println("INFORMATION THEORY FAILED") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/epistemic_cascade.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: EPISTEMIC CASCADE PASSED
// Epistemic Uncertainty Cascade Through a Measurement Chain
// How measurement uncertainty propagates and AMPLIFIES through clinical
// calculations -- the core problem Sounio's Knowledge<T> solves.
// Scenario: Drug dosage from weight -> CrCl -> drug clearance -> dose
// Reference: Cockcroft & Gault (1976), GUM JCGM 100:2008

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x / 2.0
    if g < 0.001 { g = 0.001 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 50 { g = (g + x / g) / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    return g
}

struct Meas { value: f64, uncert: f64, source: i32 }
struct Prov { vw: f64, va: f64, vs: f64, vm: f64, total: f64 }

fn empty_prov() -> Prov { return Prov { vw: 0.0, va: 0.0, vs: 0.0, vm: 0.0, total: 0.0 } }

fn frac(p: Prov, src: i32) -> f64 {
    if p.total < 1.0e-15 { return 0.0 }
    if src == 0 { return p.vw / p.total }
    if src == 1 { return p.va / p.total }
    if src == 2 { return p.vs / p.total }
    if src == 3 { return p.vm / p.total }
    return 0.0
}

struct CrClResult { value: f64, uncert: f64, prov: Prov }
struct CLResult { value: f64, uncert: f64, prov: Prov }
struct DoseResult { value: f64, uncert: f64, rel_pct: f64, prov: Prov }

// CrCl = (140 - age) * weight / (72 * SCr)
fn compute_crcl(w: Meas, a: Meas, s: Meas) -> CrClResult with Mut {
    let crcl = (140.0 - a.value) * w.value / (72.0 * s.value)
    let dw = (140.0 - a.value) / (72.0 * s.value)
    let da = 0.0 - w.value / (72.0 * s.value)
    let ds = 0.0 - (140.0 - a.value) * w.value / (72.0 * s.value * s.value)
    let vw = dw * dw * w.uncert * w.uncert
    let va = da * da * a.uncert * a.uncert
    let vs = ds * ds * s.uncert * s.uncert
    let tot = vw + va + vs
    return CrClResult { value: crcl, uncert: sqrt_f64(tot), prov: Prov { vw: vw, va: va, vs: vs, vm: 0.0, total: tot } }
}

// CL_drug = 0.8 * CrCl + 2.1, with model uncertainty
fn compute_cl(cr: CrClResult, mu: f64) -> CLResult with Mut {
    let cl = 0.8 * cr.value + 2.1
    let s2 = 0.64  // 0.8^2
    let vw = s2 * cr.prov.vw
    let va = s2 * cr.prov.va
    let vs = s2 * cr.prov.vs
    let vm = mu * mu
    let tot = vw + va + vs + vm
    return CLResult { value: cl, uncert: sqrt_f64(tot), prov: Prov { vw: vw, va: va, vs: vs, vm: vm, total: tot } }
}

// dose = Ctarget * CL * tau
fn compute_dose(cl: CLResult, ctarg: f64, tau: f64) -> DoseResult with Mut {
    let dose = ctarg * cl.value * tau
    let s2 = ctarg * tau * ctarg * tau
    let vw = s2 * cl.prov.vw
    let va = s2 * cl.prov.va
    let vs = s2 * cl.prov.vs
    let vm = s2 * cl.prov.vm
    let tot = vw + va + vs + vm
    let u = sqrt_f64(tot)
    var rp = 0.0
    if dose > 0.001 { rp = 100.0 * u / dose }
    return DoseResult { value: dose, uncert: u, rel_pct: rp, prov: Prov { vw: vw, va: va, vs: vs, vm: vm, total: tot } }
}

fn print_prov(p: Prov) -> i32 with IO {
    print("    Weight=")
    print(100.0 * frac(p, 0))
    print("% Age=")
    print(100.0 * frac(p, 1))
    print("% SCr=")
    print(100.0 * frac(p, 2))
    print("% Model=")
    print(100.0 * frac(p, 3))
    println("%")
    return 0
}

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut {
    println("=== Epistemic Uncertainty Cascade ===")
    println("Drug dosage from uncertain measurement chain")
    println("")
    let weight = Meas { value: 75.0, uncert: 3.5, source: 0 }
    let age = Meas { value: 65.0, uncert: 1.0, source: 1 }
    let scr = Meas { value: 1.1, uncert: 0.06, source: 2 }

    println("--- Stage 1: Measurements ---")
    print("  Weight: ")
    print(weight.value)
    print(" +/- ")
    print(weight.uncert)
    println(" kg")
    print("  Age: ")
    print(age.value)
    print(" +/- ")
    print(age.uncert)
    println(" yr")
    print("  SCr: ")
    print(scr.value)
    print(" +/- ")
    print(scr.uncert)
    println(" mg/dL")

    println("--- Stage 2: CrCl (Cockcroft-Gault) ---")
    let cr = compute_crcl(weight, age, scr)
    print("  CrCl = ")
    print(cr.value)
    print(" +/- ")
    print(cr.uncert)
    println(" mL/min")
    let d2 = print_prov(cr.prov)

    println("--- Stage 3: Drug Clearance ---")
    let cl = compute_cl(cr, 1.5)
    print("  CL = ")
    print(cl.value)
    print(" +/- ")
    print(cl.uncert)
    println(" L/hr")
    let d3 = print_prov(cl.prov)

    println("--- Stage 4: Final Dose ---")
    let dose = compute_dose(cl, 0.5, 12.0)
    print("  Dose = ")
    print(dose.value)
    print(" +/- ")
    print(dose.uncert)
    println(" mg")
    print("  Relative uncertainty: ")
    print(dose.rel_pct)
    println("%")
    let d4 = print_prov(dose.prov)

    // Cascade analysis
    let init_rel = 100.0 * weight.uncert / weight.value
    let amp = dose.rel_pct / init_rel
    print("  Amplification: ")
    print(amp)
    println("x")

    let fw = frac(dose.prov, 0)
    let fa = frac(dose.prov, 1)
    let fs = frac(dose.prov, 2)
    let fm = frac(dose.prov, 3)
    if fs > fw && fs > fa && fs > fm {
        println("  DOMINANT: Serum creatinine -> recommend cystatin C eGFR")
    } else if fw > fs { println("  DOMINANT: Weight -> recommend calibrated scale") }
    println("")

    // Validation
    var ok = true
    print("Check 1: Dose uncertainty > 5% ... ")
    print(dose.rel_pct)
    if dose.rel_pct > 5.0 { println("% OK") } else { println("% FAIL"); ok = false }

    print("Check 2: Weight > 10% of variance ... ")
    print(100.0 * fw)
    if 100.0 * fw > 10.0 { println("% OK") } else { println("% FAIL"); ok = false }

    print("Check 3: SCr > 40% of variance ... ")
    print(100.0 * fs)
    if 100.0 * fs > 40.0 { println("% OK") } else { println("% FAIL"); ok = false }

    print("Check 4: Amplification > 1x ... ")
    print(amp)
    if amp > 1.0 { println("x OK") } else { println("x FAIL"); ok = false }

    let psum = fw + fa + fs + fm
    print("Check 5: Provenance sums to 1.0 ... err=")
    print(abs_f64(psum - 1.0))
    if abs_f64(psum - 1.0) < 0.01 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }

    print("Check 6: CrCl in [30,120] ... ")
    print(cr.value)
    if cr.value > 30.0 && cr.value < 120.0 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); ok = false }

    println("")
    if ok { println("EPISTEMIC CASCADE PASSED") } else { println("EPISTEMIC CASCADE FAILED") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/kalman_filter_tracking.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: PASSED
// 1D Kalman Filter for State Estimation
//
// Tracks a moving object with constant-velocity model.
// State vector: [position, velocity] (2D state, 1D measurement).
// True trajectory: constant velocity v=3.0, position = v*t, with small
// random accelerations (process noise). The filter observes only noisy
// position measurements and must recover both position and velocity.
//
// This is the canonical Kalman filter test: measurement noise is large
// (std=5.0) but the filter fuses predictions with observations to
// produce estimates far superior to raw measurements alone.
//
// Implements predict/update cycle with 2x2 inline matrix operations.
// Demonstrates filtering improvement, velocity inference from position-only
// observations, and gain convergence.
//
// References:
//   Kalman (1960) "A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction"
//   Maybeck (1979) "Stochastic Models, Estimation and Control"
//   Bar-Shalom, Li, Kirubarajan (2001) "Estimation with Applications"

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    return y
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    return 2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 6.283185307179586
    var a = x
    while a >= two_pi { a = a - two_pi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + two_pi }
    if a > pi { a = a - two_pi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// LCG PRNG + Box-Muller
// ============================================================================

struct RngState {
    seed: i64,
}

fn lcg_next(rng: &!RngState) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let modulus: i64 = 4294967296
    rng.seed = (a * rng.seed + c) % modulus
    if rng.seed < 0 { rng.seed = rng.seed + modulus }
    return (rng.seed as f64) / 4294967296.0
}

fn randn(rng: &!RngState) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var u1 = lcg_next(rng)
    if u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let u2 = lcg_next(rng)
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    return sqrt_f64(0.0 - 2.0 * ln_f64(u1)) * cos_approx(2.0 * pi * u2)
}

// ============================================================================
// 2x2 MATRIX OPERATIONS (inline)
// ============================================================================

struct Mat2 {
    a00: f64, a01: f64,
    a10: f64, a11: f64,
}

struct Vec2 {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

fn mat2_mul(m: Mat2, n: Mat2) -> Mat2 {
    Mat2 {
        a00: m.a00 * n.a00 + m.a01 * n.a10,
        a01: m.a00 * n.a01 + m.a01 * n.a11,
        a10: m.a10 * n.a00 + m.a11 * n.a10,
        a11: m.a10 * n.a01 + m.a11 * n.a11,
    }
}

fn mat2_transpose(m: Mat2) -> Mat2 {
    Mat2 { a00: m.a00, a01: m.a10, a10: m.a01, a11: m.a11 }
}

fn mat2_add(m: Mat2, n: Mat2) -> Mat2 {
    Mat2 {
        a00: m.a00 + n.a00, a01: m.a01 + n.a01,
        a10: m.a10 + n.a10, a11: m.a11 + n.a11,
    }
}

fn mat2_vec(m: Mat2, v: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
    Vec2 {
        x: m.a00 * v.x + m.a01 * v.y,
        y: m.a10 * v.x + m.a11 * v.y,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// KALMAN FILTER STATE
// ============================================================================

struct KalmanState {
    x: Vec2,
    p: Mat2,
}

fn kalman_predict(ks: KalmanState, f_mat: Mat2, q: Mat2) -> KalmanState {
    let x_pred = mat2_vec(f_mat, ks.x)
    let ft = mat2_transpose(f_mat)
    let fp = mat2_mul(f_mat, ks.p)
    let p_pred = mat2_add(mat2_mul(fp, ft), q)
    return KalmanState { x: x_pred, p: p_pred }
}

fn kalman_update(ks: KalmanState, z: f64, r: f64) -> KalmanState with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // H = [1, 0] so H*x = x[0], H*P*H' = P[0,0]
    let y_innov = z - ks.x.x
    let s = ks.p.a00 + r
    if abs_f64(s) < 1.0e-30 {
        return ks
    }
    // Kalman gain K = P * H' / S = [P[0,0]/S, P[1,0]/S]
    let k0 = ks.p.a00 / s
    let k1 = ks.p.a10 / s

    let x_new = Vec2 {
        x: ks.x.x + k0 * y_innov,
        y: ks.x.y + k1 * y_innov,
    }

    // P_new = (I - K*H) * P
    // K*H = [[k0, 0], [k1, 0]]
    let p_new = Mat2 {
        a00: (1.0 - k0) * ks.p.a00,
        a01: (1.0 - k0) * ks.p.a01,
        a10: ks.p.a10 - k1 * ks.p.a00,
        a11: ks.p.a11 - k1 * ks.p.a01,
    }

    return KalmanState { x: x_new, p: p_new }
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Kalman Filter: 1D Position+Velocity Tracking ===")
    println("True trajectory: constant velocity v=3.0 with process noise")
    println("Measurements: position only, noise_std = 5.0")
    println("")

    let dt = 1.0
    let true_vel = 3.0
    let process_noise_std = 0.5
    let meas_noise_std = 5.0
    let n_steps = 30
    let r = meas_noise_std * meas_noise_std

    // State transition: x_k = x_{k-1} + v_{k-1}*dt, v_k = v_{k-1}
    let f_mat = Mat2 { a00: 1.0, a01: dt, a10: 0.0, a11: 1.0 }

    // Process noise covariance Q (piecewise constant white noise jerk model)
    let q_var = process_noise_std * process_noise_std
    let q = Mat2 {
        a00: q_var * dt * dt * dt * dt / 4.0,
        a01: q_var * dt * dt * dt / 2.0,
        a10: q_var * dt * dt * dt / 2.0,
        a11: q_var * dt * dt,
    }

    // Initial state estimate: uncertain about position and velocity
    var ks = KalmanState {
        x: Vec2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 },
        p: Mat2 { a00: 100.0, a01: 0.0, a10: 0.0, a11: 100.0 },
    }

    // Generate true trajectory and noisy measurements
    var rng = RngState { seed: 42 }

    var true_pos = 0.0
    var actual_vel = true_vel
    var sum_meas_err_sq = 0.0
    var sum_filt_err_sq = 0.0
    var initial_gain = 0.0

    println("Step | TruePos  | Meas     | FiltPos  | FiltVel  | Gain")

    var step = 1
    while step <= n_steps {
        // Evolve true state with small process noise
        let proc_noise = process_noise_std * randn(&!rng)
        actual_vel = true_vel + proc_noise * 0.1
        true_pos = true_pos + actual_vel * dt

        // Noisy measurement of position
        let noise = meas_noise_std * randn(&!rng)
        let z = true_pos + noise

        // Predict
        ks = kalman_predict(ks, f_mat, q)

        // Update
        ks = kalman_update(ks, z, r)

        // Track errors
        let meas_err = z - true_pos
        let filt_err = ks.x.x - true_pos
        sum_meas_err_sq = sum_meas_err_sq + meas_err * meas_err
        sum_filt_err_sq = sum_filt_err_sq + filt_err * filt_err

        // Kalman gain for position (post-update)
        let current_gain = ks.p.a00 / (ks.p.a00 + r)
        if step == 1 { initial_gain = current_gain }

        // Print every 5th step and first/last
        let mod5 = step - 5 * (step / 5)
        if mod5 == 0 || step == 1 || step == n_steps {
            print("  t=")
            print(step)
            print("  true=")
            print(true_pos)
            print("  meas=")
            print(z)
            print("  filt_pos=")
            print(ks.x.x)
            print("  filt_vel=")
            print(ks.x.y)
            print("  gain=")
            println(current_gain)
        }

        step = step + 1
    }

    println("")

    let rms_meas = sqrt_f64(sum_meas_err_sq / (n_steps as f64))
    let rms_filt = sqrt_f64(sum_filt_err_sq / (n_steps as f64))
    let improvement = rms_meas / rms_filt
    print("RMS measurement error: ")
    println(rms_meas)
    print("RMS filter error:      ")
    println(rms_filt)
    print("Improvement ratio:     ")
    println(improvement)

    let vel_est = ks.x.y
    let vel_err_frac = abs_f64(vel_est - true_vel) / true_vel
    print("Velocity estimate: ")
    print(vel_est)
    print("  true: ")
    println(true_vel)
    print("Velocity error fraction: ")
    println(vel_err_frac)

    let final_gain = ks.p.a00 / (ks.p.a00 + r)
    print("Initial gain: ")
    println(initial_gain)
    print("Final gain:   ")
    println(final_gain)
    print("Gain reduction: ")
    println(initial_gain / final_gain)
    println("")

    // === VALIDATION ===
    var all_ok = true

    print("Check 1: RMS filter < RMS measurement ... ")
    if rms_filt < rms_meas { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 2: Velocity within 50% of true at t=30 ... ")
    if vel_err_frac < 0.50 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 3: Gain stabilizes (final < 0.5) ... ")
    if final_gain < 0.5 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 4: Filter improvement > 1.0x ... ")
    if improvement > 1.0 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 5: Gain converges (final < initial) ... ")
    if final_gain < initial_gain { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    println("")
    if all_ok { println("KALMAN FILTER PASSED") } else { println("KALMAN FILTER FAILED") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/lotka_volterra_ecosystem.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: PASSED
// Lotka-Volterra Predator-Prey Ecosystem Dynamics
//
// Classical ecological model with RK4 integration, oscillation detection,
// conservation invariant verification, phase portrait analysis, and
// sensitivity analysis via parameter perturbation.
//
// Equations:
//   dx/dt = alpha*x - beta*x*y    (prey: growth minus predation)
//   dy/dt = delta*x*y - gamma*y   (predator: growth minus death)
//
// Conservation quantity (Volterra integral):
//   V = delta*x - gamma*ln(x) + beta*y - alpha*ln(y)
//
// References:
//   Lotka (1925) "Elements of Physical Biology"
//   Volterra (1926) "Variazioni e fluttuazioni del numero d'individui"
//   Murray (2002) "Mathematical Biology" Ch.3

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    return 2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// STATE AND DERIVATIVES
// ============================================================================

struct EcoState {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    t: f64,
}

struct EcoDerivs {
    dx: f64,
    dy: f64,
}

fn lv_derivs(x: f64, y: f64, alpha: f64, beta: f64, delta: f64, gamma: f64) -> EcoDerivs {
    EcoDerivs {
        dx: alpha * x - beta * x * y,
        dy: delta * x * y - gamma * y,
    }
}

fn rk4_step(s: EcoState, dt: f64, alpha: f64, beta: f64, delta: f64, gamma: f64) -> EcoState {
    let k1 = lv_derivs(s.x, s.y, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
    let k2 = lv_derivs(s.x + 0.5 * dt * k1.dx, s.y + 0.5 * dt * k1.dy, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
    let k3 = lv_derivs(s.x + 0.5 * dt * k2.dx, s.y + 0.5 * dt * k2.dy, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
    let k4 = lv_derivs(s.x + dt * k3.dx, s.y + dt * k3.dy, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
    EcoState {
        x: s.x + dt / 6.0 * (k1.dx + 2.0 * k2.dx + 2.0 * k3.dx + k4.dx),
        y: s.y + dt / 6.0 * (k1.dy + 2.0 * k2.dy + 2.0 * k3.dy + k4.dy),
        t: s.t + dt,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// CONSERVATION INVARIANT
// ============================================================================

fn volterra_invariant(x: f64, y: f64, alpha: f64, beta: f64, delta: f64, gamma: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return delta * x - gamma * ln_f64(x) + beta * y - alpha * ln_f64(y)
}

// ============================================================================
// SIMULATION DRIVER
// ============================================================================

fn simulate(alpha: f64, beta: f64, delta: f64, gamma: f64, x0: f64, y0: f64, t_end: f64, dt: f64) -> EcoState with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var s = EcoState { x: x0, y: y0, t: 0.0 }
    let n_steps = (t_end / dt) as i32
    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        s = rk4_step(s, dt, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return s
}

// ============================================================================
// PEAK DETECTION: find period from prey peaks
// ============================================================================

struct PeakResult {
    period: f64,
    n_peaks: i32,
}

fn detect_oscillation(alpha: f64, beta: f64, delta: f64, gamma: f64, x0: f64, y0: f64, dt: f64) -> PeakResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Run for T=50 and collect prey peaks
    let n_steps = (50.0 / dt) as i32
    var s = EcoState { x: x0, y: y0, t: 0.0 }
    var prev_x = x0
    var prev_prev_x = x0
    var first_peak_t = 0.0
    var last_peak_t = 0.0
    var n_peaks = 0
    var i = 0
    while i < n_steps {
        s = rk4_step(s, dt, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
        // A peak occurs when prev_x > prev_prev_x and prev_x > s.x (local max)
        if i > 1 {
            if prev_x > prev_prev_x && prev_x > s.x {
                n_peaks = n_peaks + 1
                if n_peaks == 1 { first_peak_t = s.t - dt }
                last_peak_t = s.t - dt
            }
        }
        prev_prev_x = prev_x
        prev_x = s.x
        i = i + 1
    }
    var period = 0.0
    if n_peaks > 1 {
        period = (last_peak_t - first_peak_t) / ((n_peaks - 1) as f64)
    }
    return PeakResult { period: period, n_peaks: n_peaks }
}

// ============================================================================
// PHASE PORTRAIT AREA (Shoelace formula on orbit points)
// ============================================================================

fn phase_area(alpha: f64, beta: f64, delta: f64, gamma: f64, x0: f64, y0: f64, dt: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Sample one full period's worth of points
    let peak = detect_oscillation(alpha, beta, delta, gamma, x0, y0, dt)
    var period_steps = (peak.period / dt) as i32
    if period_steps < 100 { period_steps = 5000 }
    // Skip transient (first 1000 steps), then collect one period
    var s = EcoState { x: x0, y: y0, t: 0.0 }
    var skip = 0
    while skip < 1000 {
        s = rk4_step(s, dt, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
        skip = skip + 1
    }
    // Shoelace: sum (x_i * y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} * y_i)
    var area_sum = 0.0
    var prev_state = s
    var j = 0
    while j < period_steps {
        s = rk4_step(s, dt, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
        area_sum = area_sum + (prev_state.x * s.y - s.x * prev_state.y)
        prev_state = s
        j = j + 1
    }
    return abs_f64(area_sum) / 2.0
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Lotka-Volterra Predator-Prey Ecosystem ===")
    println("alpha=1.1 beta=0.4 delta=0.1 gamma=0.4")
    println("")

    let alpha = 1.1
    let beta = 0.4
    let delta = 0.1
    let gamma = 0.4
    let x0 = 10.0
    let y0 = 10.0
    let dt = 0.01

    // --- Print populations at t=0,10,20,30,40,50 ---
    println("Population dynamics:")
    var s = EcoState { x: x0, y: y0, t: 0.0 }
    let v0 = volterra_invariant(s.x, s.y, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
    print("  t=0   prey=")
    print(s.x)
    print("  pred=")
    println(s.y)

    let n_total = 5000
    var step = 0
    var target = 1
    while step < n_total {
        s = rk4_step(s, dt, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
        step = step + 1
        let t_now = s.t
        if target == 1 && t_now >= 9.995 && t_now < 10.005 {
            print("  t=10  prey=")
            print(s.x)
            print("  pred=")
            println(s.y)
            target = 2
        }
        if target == 2 && t_now >= 19.995 && t_now < 20.005 {
            print("  t=20  prey=")
            print(s.x)
            print("  pred=")
            println(s.y)
            target = 3
        }
        if target == 3 && t_now >= 29.995 && t_now < 30.005 {
            print("  t=30  prey=")
            print(s.x)
            print("  pred=")
            println(s.y)
            target = 4
        }
        if target == 4 && t_now >= 39.995 && t_now < 40.005 {
            print("  t=40  prey=")
            print(s.x)
            print("  pred=")
            println(s.y)
            target = 5
        }
        if target == 5 && t_now >= 49.995 && t_now < 50.005 {
            print("  t=50  prey=")
            print(s.x)
            print("  pred=")
            println(s.y)
            target = 6
        }
    }
    println("")

    // --- Conservation invariant ---
    let v_final = volterra_invariant(s.x, s.y, alpha, beta, delta, gamma)
    let v_drift = abs_f64(v_final - v0) / abs_f64(v0)
    print("Conservation V(0)=")
    print(v0)
    print("  V(50)=")
    print(v_final)
    print("  drift=")
    println(v_drift)

    // --- Oscillation detection ---
    let peaks = detect_oscillation(alpha, beta, delta, gamma, x0, y0, dt)
    print("Oscillation: period=")
    print(peaks.period)
    print("  peaks_found=")
    println(peaks.n_peaks)

    // --- Phase portrait area ---
    let area = phase_area(alpha, beta, delta, gamma, x0, y0, dt)
    print("Phase orbit area=")
    println(area)

    // --- Sensitivity analysis: perturb alpha by 1% ---
    let alpha_pert = alpha * 1.01
    let peaks_pert = detect_oscillation(alpha_pert, beta, delta, gamma, x0, y0, dt)
    let period_change = abs_f64(peaks_pert.period - peaks.period) / peaks.period
    print("Sensitivity: alpha+1% period=")
    print(peaks_pert.period)
    print("  change=")
    println(period_change)

    println("")

    // === VALIDATION ===
    var all_ok = true

    print("Check 1: Oscillation detected (>=2 peaks) ... ")
    if peaks.n_peaks >= 2 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 2: Period > 0 ... ")
    if peaks.period > 0.0 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 3: Conservation drift < 1% ... ")
    if v_drift < 0.01 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 4: Populations stay positive ... ")
    if s.x > 0.0 && s.y > 0.0 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 5: Phase area > 0 ... ")
    if area > 0.0 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 6: Sensitivity detectable ... ")
    if period_change > 0.0 && period_change < 0.5 { println("OK") } else { println("FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    println("")
    if all_ok { println("LOTKA-VOLTERRA PASSED") } else { println("LOTKA-VOLTERRA FAILED") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/markov_chain_monte_carlo.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: PASSED
// Metropolis-Hastings MCMC for Bayesian Posterior Inference
//
// Samples the joint posterior of (mu, sigma) for a Normal likelihood
// given 20 hardcoded observations. Uses LCG PRNG with Box-Muller
// transform for proposals, log-space density evaluation, and
// convergence diagnostics.
//
// Prior: mu ~ Normal(0, 10), sigma ~ HalfNormal(0, 5)
// Likelihood: data_i ~ Normal(mu, sigma^2)
// True generating params: mu=5.0, sigma=2.0
//
// References:
//   Metropolis et al. (1953) "Equation of state calculations"
//   Hastings (1970) "Monte Carlo sampling methods using Markov chains"
//   Gelman et al. (2013) "Bayesian Data Analysis" 3rd ed.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn ln_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    var m = x
    var e = 0
    while m >= 2.0 { m = m / 2.0; e = e + 1 }
    while m < 0.5 { m = m * 2.0; e = e - 1 }
    let t = (m - 1.0) / (m + 1.0)
    let t2 = t * t
    var sum = t
    var term = t
    var k = 1
    while k < 30 {
        term = term * t2
        sum = sum + term / ((2 * k + 1) as f64)
        k = k + 1
    }
    return 2.0 * sum + (e as f64) * 0.6931471805599453
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 30 { y = 0.5 * (y + x / y); i = i + 1 }
    return y
}

fn cos_approx(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    let two_pi = 6.283185307179586
    var a = x
    while a >= two_pi { a = a - two_pi }
    while a < 0.0 { a = a + two_pi }
    if a > pi { a = a - two_pi }
    let a2 = a * a
    var sum = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 15 {
        term = 0.0 - term * a2 / ((2 * n - 1) * 2 * n) as f64
        sum = sum + term
        n = n + 1
    }
    return sum
}

// ============================================================================
// LCG PSEUDO-RANDOM NUMBER GENERATOR
// ============================================================================

struct RngState {
    seed: i64,
}

fn lcg_next(rng: &!RngState) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // next = (1664525 * prev + 1013904223) % 2^32
    let a: i64 = 1664525
    let c: i64 = 1013904223
    let modulus: i64 = 4294967296
    rng.seed = (a * rng.seed + c) % modulus
    if rng.seed < 0 { rng.seed = rng.seed + modulus }
    return (rng.seed as f64) / 4294967296.0
}

fn box_muller_normal(rng: &!RngState) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var u1 = lcg_next(rng)
    if u1 < 1.0e-10 { u1 = 1.0e-10 }
    let u2 = lcg_next(rng)
    let pi = 3.141592653589793
    return sqrt_f64(0.0 - 2.0 * ln_f64(u1)) * cos_approx(2.0 * pi * u2)
}

// ============================================================================
// LOG-DENSITIES
// ============================================================================

fn log_normal_density(x: f64, mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if sigma <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    let z = (x - mu) / sigma
    let log_2pi = 1.8378770664093453
    return 0.0 - 0.5 * log_2pi - ln_f64(sigma) - 0.5 * z * z
}

fn log_prior_mu(mu: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // mu ~ Normal(0, 10)
    return log_normal_density(mu, 0.0, 10.0)
}

fn log_prior_sigma(sigma: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // sigma ~ HalfNormal(0, 5): proportional to Normal(0,5) for sigma > 0
    if sigma <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    return log_normal_density(sigma, 0.0, 5.0)
}

// ============================================================================
// LOG-LIKELIHOOD AND POSTERIOR
// ============================================================================

fn log_likelihood(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if sigma <= 0.0 { return 0.0 - 1.0e30 }
    // 20 observations from Normal(5.0, 2.0)
    // Hardcoded values (generated from that distribution):
    var ll = 0.0
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(4.12, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(6.34, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(3.87, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(5.91, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(7.23, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(4.56, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(3.21, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(5.67, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(6.78, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(4.89, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(5.43, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(2.98, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(6.12, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(4.76, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(7.54, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(3.65, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(5.28, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(4.91, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(6.45, mu, sigma)
    ll = ll + log_normal_density(5.02, mu, sigma)
    return ll
}

fn log_posterior(mu: f64, sigma: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    return log_likelihood(mu, sigma) + log_prior_mu(mu) + log_prior_sigma(sigma)
}

// ============================================================================
// MCMC CHAIN STORAGE
// ============================================================================

struct MCMCResult {
    mu_mean: f64,
    sigma_mean: f64,
    accept_rate: f64,
    mu_first_half: f64,
    mu_second_half: f64,
}

fn run_mcmc(rng: &!RngState) -> MCMCResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let n_iter = 5000
    let n_burnin = 1000
    let step_mu = 0.5
    let step_sigma = 0.3

    var cur_mu = 0.0
    var cur_sigma = 1.0
    var cur_lp = log_posterior(cur_mu, cur_sigma)

    var n_accepted = 0
    var n_total = 0
    var sum_mu = 0.0
    var sum_sigma = 0.0
    var n_samples = 0

    // For convergence check: first half and second half means
    var sum_mu_h1 = 0.0
    var count_h1 = 0
    var sum_mu_h2 = 0.0
    var count_h2 = 0
    let half_post_burnin = (n_iter - n_burnin) / 2

    var iter = 0
    while iter < n_iter {
        // Propose new (mu, sigma)
        let prop_mu = cur_mu + step_mu * box_muller_normal(rng)
        let prop_sigma = cur_sigma + step_sigma * box_muller_normal(rng)

        if prop_sigma > 0.0 {
            let prop_lp = log_posterior(prop_mu, prop_sigma)
            let log_alpha = prop_lp - cur_lp
            let u = lcg_next(rng)
            let ln_u = ln_f64(u)

            if ln_u < log_alpha {
                cur_mu = prop_mu
                cur_sigma = prop_sigma
                cur_lp = prop_lp
                n_accepted = n_accepted + 1
            }
        }
        n_total = n_total + 1

        // Collect post-burnin samples
        if iter >= n_burnin {
            sum_mu = sum_mu + cur_mu
            sum_sigma = sum_sigma + cur_sigma
            n_samples = n_samples + 1

            let post_idx = iter - n_burnin
            if post_idx < half_post_burnin {
                sum_mu_h1 = sum_mu_h1 + cur_mu
                count_h1 = count_h1 + 1
            } else {
                sum_mu_h2 = sum_mu_h2 + cur_mu
                count_h2 = count_h2 + 1
            }
        }
        iter = iter + 1
    }

    let mu_mean = sum_mu / (n_samples as f64)
    let sigma_mean = sum_sigma / (n_samples as f64)
    let accept_rate = (n_accepted as f64) / (n_total as f64)
    let mu_h1 = sum_mu_h1 / (count_h1 as f64)
    let mu_h2 = sum_mu_h2 / (count_h2 as f64)

    return MCMCResult {
        mu_mean: mu_mean,
        sigma_mean: sigma_mean,
        accept_rate: accept_rate,
        mu_first_half: mu_h1,
        mu_second_half: mu_h2,
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    println("=== Metropolis-Hastings MCMC Posterior Inference ===")
    println("Data: 20 obs from Normal(5.0, 2.0)")
    println("Prior: mu~N(0,10), sigma~HalfN(0,5)")
    println("Iterations: 5000, Burn-in: 1000")
    println("")

    // Data statistics for reference
    let data_mean = (4.12 + 6.34 + 3.87 + 5.91 + 7.23 + 4.56 + 3.21 + 5.67 + 6.78 + 4.89 + 5.43 + 2.98 + 6.12 + 4.76 + 7.54 + 3.65 + 5.28 + 4.91 + 6.45 + 5.02) / 20.0
    print("Data sample mean: ")
    println(data_mean)

    // Compute sample std
    var ss = 0.0
    ss = ss + (4.12 - data_mean) * (4.12 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (6.34 - data_mean) * (6.34 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (3.87 - data_mean) * (3.87 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (5.91 - data_mean) * (5.91 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (7.23 - data_mean) * (7.23 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (4.56 - data_mean) * (4.56 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (3.21 - data_mean) * (3.21 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (5.67 - data_mean) * (5.67 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (6.78 - data_mean) * (6.78 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (4.89 - data_mean) * (4.89 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (5.43 - data_mean) * (5.43 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (2.98 - data_mean) * (2.98 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (6.12 - data_mean) * (6.12 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (4.76 - data_mean) * (4.76 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (7.54 - data_mean) * (7.54 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (3.65 - data_mean) * (3.65 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (5.28 - data_mean) * (5.28 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (4.91 - data_mean) * (4.91 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (6.45 - data_mean) * (6.45 - data_mean)
    ss = ss + (5.02 - data_mean) * (5.02 - data_mean)
    let data_std = sqrt_f64(ss / 19.0)
    print("Data sample std:  ")
    println(data_std)
    println("")

    // Run MCMC
    var rng = RngState { seed: 123456789 }
    let result = run_mcmc(&!rng)

    println("MCMC Results:")
    print("  Posterior mean of mu:    ")
    println(result.mu_mean)
    print("  Posterior mean of sigma: ")
    println(result.sigma_mean)
    print("  Acceptance rate:         ")
    println(result.accept_rate)
    print("  mu first-half mean:      ")
    println(result.mu_first_half)
    print("  mu second-half mean:     ")
    println(result.mu_second_half)
    println("")

    // === VALIDATION ===
    var all_ok = true

    print("Check 1: |posterior_mu - 5.0| < 1.0 ... ")
    let mu_err = abs_f64(result.mu_mean - 5.0)
    print("err=")
    print(mu_err)
    if mu_err < 1.0 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 2: |posterior_sigma - 2.0| < 1.0 ... ")
    let sigma_err = abs_f64(result.sigma_mean - 2.0)
    print("err=")
    print(sigma_err)
    if sigma_err < 1.0 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    print("Check 3: Acceptance rate in [0.15, 0.60] ... ")
    if result.accept_rate >= 0.15 && result.accept_rate <= 0.60 {
        println("OK")
    } else {
        println("FAIL"); all_ok = false
    }

    print("Check 4: Convergence (half-means close) ... ")
    let convergence_gap = abs_f64(result.mu_first_half - result.mu_second_half)
    print("gap=")
    print(convergence_gap)
    if convergence_gap < 1.0 { println(" OK") } else { println(" FAIL"); all_ok = false }

    println("")
    if all_ok { println("MCMC PASSED") } else { println("MCMC FAILED") }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/science/maxwell_cl13.sio ===
//@ run-pass
//@ expect-stdout: MAXWELL CL13 PASSED
// Spacetime Algebra Cl(1,3) — Maxwell's Equations in Geometric Algebra
//
// The electromagnetic field is a single bivector F in Cl(1,3).
// Maxwell's four equations collapse to one: nabla * F = J / epsilon_0
//
// Cl(1,3) signature: e0^2 = +1 (time), e1^2 = e2^2 = e3^2 = -1 (space)
// Multivector dimension: 2^4 = 16 components indexed by bitset.
//
// Future syntax:  let F: Clifford(1, 3) = ...
// Today:          [f64] with 16 components + explicit geometric product
//
// References:
//   Hestenes & Sobczyk, "Clifford Algebra to Geometric Calculus" (1984)
//   Doran & Lasenby, "Geometric Algebra for Physicists" (2003)
//   Hurwitz, "Uber die Composition der quadratischen Formen" (1898)

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS (must precede callers — no forward refs in Sounio)
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var g = x / 2.0
    if g < 1.0 { g = 1.0 }
    var i = 0
    while i < 50 { g = (g + x / g) / 2.0; i = i + 1 }
    return g
}

fn approx_eq(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    abs_f64(a - b) < tol
}

// ============================================================================
// Cl(1,3) GEOMETRIC PRODUCT — SIGN COMPUTATION
// ============================================================================
//
// Basis element index = bitset of basis vectors:
//   bit 0 = e0 (time),  bit 1 = e1 (x),  bit 2 = e2 (y),  bit 3 = e3 (z)
//
//   0:1  1:e0  2:e1  3:e01  4:e2  5:e02  6:e12  7:e012
//   8:e3  9:e03  10:e13  11:e013  12:e23  13:e023  14:e123  15:e0123
//
// Metric: e0^2=+1, e1^2=e2^2=e3^2=-1
// Sign of e_A * e_B = (-1)^swaps * product of metric for common bits
//   where swaps = |{ (a,b) : a in A, b in B, a > b }|

fn geo_sign(a: i64, b: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Count transpositions: for each bit j in b, count bits in a above j
    var swaps = 0
    var j = 0
    while j < 4 {
