// === FILE: examples/visual/06_octonion_color_table.sio ===
/// Visual Example 6: Octonion Multiplication Table - COLOR EDITION
///
/// Demonstrates: Color-coded hypercomplex algebra visualization
///
/// Visual Output: Full-color 8×8 multiplication table where:
/// - Real (1): WHITE (identity)
/// - Quaternion basis (i,j,k): RED, GREEN, BLUE
/// - Octonion extensions (l,il,jl,kl): YELLOW, MAGENTA, CYAN, custom
/// - Negative values: Dimmed/background colors
///
/// This visualization makes the Fano plane structure immediately visible!

// ============================================================================
// ANSI COLORS
// ============================================================================

fn color_reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn color_bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }
fn color_dim() { print("\x1b[2m") }

fn color_white() { print("\x1b[97m") }
fn color_red() { print("\x1b[91m") }
fn color_green() { print("\x1b[92m") }
fn color_yellow() { print("\x1b[93m") }
fn color_blue() { print("\x1b[94m") }
fn color_magenta() { print("\x1b[95m") }
fn color_cyan() { print("\x1b[96m") }

fn bg_red() { print("\x1b[41m") }
fn bg_green() { print("\x1b[42m") }
fn bg_blue() { print("\x1b[44m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_magenta() { print("\x1b[45m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }

// ============================================================================
// BASIS ELEMENT COLORS
// ============================================================================

fn print_colored_basis(basis: i32, is_negative: i32) {
    if is_negative == 1 {
        color_dim()
    } else {
        color_bold()
    }

    if basis == 0 {
        // Real: 1
        color_white()
    }
    if basis == 1 {
        // i (quaternion)
        color_red()
    }
    if basis == 2 {
        // j (quaternion)
        color_green()
    }
    if basis == 3 {
        // k (quaternion)
        color_blue()
    }
    if basis == 4 {
        // l (octonion)
        color_yellow()
    }
    if basis == 5 {
        // il (octonion)
        color_magenta()
    }
    if basis == 6 {
        // jl (octonion)
        color_cyan()
    }
    if basis == 7 {
        // kl (octonion)
        color_white()
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// OCTONION STRUCT
// ============================================================================

struct Octonion {
    a: f32, b: f32, c: f32, d: f32,
    e: f32, f: f32, g: f32, h: f32
}

fn oct_basis(idx: i32) -> Octonion {
    if idx == 0 { return Octonion { a: 1.0, b: 0.0, c: 0.0, d: 0.0, e: 0.0, f: 0.0, g: 0.0, h: 0.0 } }
    if idx == 1 { return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 1.0, c: 0.0, d: 0.0, e: 0.0, f: 0.0, g: 0.0, h: 0.0 } }
    if idx == 2 { return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 0.0, c: 1.0, d: 0.0, e: 0.0, f: 0.0, g: 0.0, h: 0.0 } }
    if idx == 3 { return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 0.0, c: 0.0, d: 1.0, e: 0.0, f: 0.0, g: 0.0, h: 0.0 } }
    if idx == 4 { return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 0.0, c: 0.0, d: 0.0, e: 1.0, f: 0.0, g: 0.0, h: 0.0 } }
    if idx == 5 { return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 0.0, c: 0.0, d: 0.0, e: 0.0, f: 1.0, g: 0.0, h: 0.0 } }
    if idx == 6 { return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 0.0, c: 0.0, d: 0.0, e: 0.0, f: 0.0, g: 1.0, h: 0.0 } }
    return Octonion { a: 0.0, b: 0.0, c: 0.0, d: 0.0, e: 0.0, f: 0.0, g: 0.0, h: 1.0 }
}

fn oct_mul(o1: Octonion, o2: Octonion) -> Octonion {
    return Octonion {
        a: o1.a*o2.a - o1.b*o2.b - o1.c*o2.c - o1.d*o2.d - o1.e*o2.e - o1.f*o2.f - o1.g*o2.g - o1.h*o2.h,
        b: o1.a*o2.b + o1.b*o2.a + o1.c*o2.d - o1.d*o2.c + o1.e*o2.f - o1.f*o2.e - o1.g*o2.h + o1.h*o2.g,
        c: o1.a*o2.c - o1.b*o2.d + o1.c*o2.a + o1.d*o2.b + o1.e*o2.g + o1.f*o2.h - o1.g*o2.e - o1.h*o2.f,
        d: o1.a*o2.d + o1.b*o2.c - o1.c*o2.b + o1.d*o2.a + o1.e*o2.h - o1.f*o2.g + o1.g*o2.f - o1.h*o2.e,
        e: o1.a*o2.e - o1.b*o2.f - o1.c*o2.g - o1.d*o2.h + o1.e*o2.a + o1.f*o2.b + o1.g*o2.c + o1.h*o2.d,
        f: o1.a*o2.f + o1.b*o2.e - o1.c*o2.h + o1.d*o2.g - o1.e*o2.b + o1.f*o2.a - o1.g*o2.d + o1.h*o2.c,
        g: o1.a*o2.g + o1.b*o2.h + o1.c*o2.e - o1.d*o2.f - o1.e*o2.c + o1.f*o2.d + o1.g*o2.a - o1.h*o2.b,
        h: o1.a*o2.h - o1.b*o2.g + o1.c*o2.f + o1.d*o2.e - o1.e*o2.d - o1.f*o2.c + o1.g*o2.b + o1.h*o2.a
    }
}

fn abs_f32(x: f32) -> f32 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// PRINT PRODUCT
// ============================================================================

fn print_product_colored(i: i32, j: i32) {
    let e1 = oct_basis(i)
    let e2 = oct_basis(j)
    let prod = oct_mul(e1, e2)

    var is_negative = 0
    var basis_idx = 0

    if abs_f32(prod.a - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 0 }
    if abs_f32(prod.a + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 0; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.b - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 1 }
    if abs_f32(prod.b + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 1; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.c - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 2 }
    if abs_f32(prod.c + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 2; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.d - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 3 }
    if abs_f32(prod.d + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 3; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.e - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 4 }
    if abs_f32(prod.e + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 4; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.f - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 5 }
    if abs_f32(prod.f + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 5; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.g - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 6 }
    if abs_f32(prod.g + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 6; is_negative = 1 }

    if abs_f32(prod.h - 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 7 }
    if abs_f32(prod.h + 1.0) < 0.01 { basis_idx = 7; is_negative = 1 }

    print_colored_basis(basis_idx, is_negative)

    if is_negative == 1 {
        print("-")
    } else {
        print(" ")
    }

    if basis_idx == 0 { print("1 ") }
    if basis_idx == 1 { print("i ") }
    if basis_idx == 2 { print("j ") }
    if basis_idx == 3 { print("k ") }
    if basis_idx == 4 { print("l ") }
    if basis_idx == 5 { print("il") }
    if basis_idx == 6 { print("jl") }
    if basis_idx == 7 { print("kl") }

    color_reset()
}

// === FILE: examples/visual/07_epistemic_uncertainty_bars.sio ===
/// Visual Example 7: Epistemic Uncertainty Visualization
///
/// Demonstrates: Color-coded uncertainty quantification with confidence intervals
///
/// Visual Output: Bar charts showing mean ± uncertainty with color gradients
/// - Green: High confidence (low variance)
/// - Yellow: Medium confidence
/// - Red: Low confidence (high variance)

// ============================================================================
// ANSI COLORS
// ============================================================================

fn reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }
fn dim() { print("\x1b[2m") }

fn green() { print("\x1b[32m") }
fn yellow() { print("\x1b[33m") }
fn red() { print("\x1b[31m") }
fn cyan() { print("\x1b[36m") }
fn magenta() { print("\x1b[35m") }
fn white() { print("\x1b[97m") }

fn bg_green() { print("\x1b[42m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_red() { print("\x1b[41m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }

// ============================================================================
// NUMERIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC VALUE
// ============================================================================

struct EpistemicValue {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64,
    conf_alpha: f64,
    conf_beta: f64
}

fn epistemic_new(value: f64, variance: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: value,
        variance: variance,
        conf_alpha: 1.0,
        conf_beta: 1.0
    }
}

fn epistemic_std(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(k.variance)
}

fn epistemic_mul(x: EpistemicValue, y: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let new_variance = y.value * y.value * x.variance + x.value * x.value * y.variance
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: x.value * y.value,
        variance: new_variance,
        conf_alpha: x.conf_alpha + y.conf_alpha - 1.0,
        conf_beta: x.conf_beta + y.conf_beta - 1.0
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// VISUALIZATION HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn print_confidence_bar(std_dev: f64, max_std: f64) {
    let normalized = std_dev / max_std

    if normalized < 0.3 {
        // High confidence - green
        bg_green()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.3 && normalized < 0.6 {
        // Medium confidence - yellow
        bg_yellow()
    }
    if normalized >= 0.6 {
        // Low confidence - red
        bg_red()
    }

    let bar_length = (std_dev / max_std * 50.0)
    var i = 0
    while i < bar_length {
        print(" ")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()
}

fn print_value_bar(value: f64, max_value: f64) {
    bg_cyan()
    let bar_length = (value / max_value * 40.0)
    var i = 0
    while i < bar_length {
        print(" ")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN: UNCERTAINTY VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 {
    bold()
    cyan()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║   EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY VISUALIZATION - GUM COMPLIANCE           ║")
    println("║   Color-Coded Confidence Intervals & Variance Propagation        ║")
    println("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    reset()
    println("")

    // SCENARIO: Pharmaceutical dose calculation
    bold()
    yellow()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("          PHARMACEUTICAL DOSE CALCULATION WITH UNCERTAINTY         ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    // MEASUREMENTS
    let weight = epistemic_new(70.0, 4.0)
    let dose_per_kg = epistemic_new(10.0, 0.25)
    let total_dose = epistemic_mul(weight, dose_per_kg)

    println("Measurements:")
    println("")

    // Weight
    print("  Patient weight:  ")
    bold()
    print(weight.value)
    reset()
    print(" kg ± ")
    yellow()
    print(epistemic_std(weight))
    reset()
    println(" kg")

    print("    Uncertainty:   ")
    print_confidence_bar(epistemic_std(weight), 10.0)
    print("  ")
    yellow()
    print(epistemic_std(weight))
    reset()
    println(" kg")
    println("")

    // Dose per kg
    print("  Dose per kg:     ")
    bold()
    print(dose_per_kg.value)
    reset()
    print(" mg/kg ± ")
    green()
    print(epistemic_std(dose_per_kg))
    reset()
    println(" mg/kg")

    print("    Uncertainty:   ")
    print_confidence_bar(epistemic_std(dose_per_kg), 10.0)
    print("  ")
    green()
    print(epistemic_std(dose_per_kg))
    reset()
    println(" mg/kg")
    println("")

    // Total dose (propagated)
    print("  Total dose:      ")
    bold()
    cyan()
    print(total_dose.value)
    reset()
    print(" mg ± ")
    red()
    print(epistemic_std(total_dose))
    reset()
    println(" mg")

    print("    Uncertainty:   ")
    print_confidence_bar(epistemic_std(total_dose), 50.0)
    print("  ")
    red()
    print(epistemic_std(total_dose))
    reset()
    println(" mg (propagated!)")
    println("")

    // UNCERTAINTY LEGEND
    bold()
    magenta()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                    CONFIDENCE LEVELS                             ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    print("  ")
    bg_green()
    print("        ")
    reset()
    green()
    println("  High confidence (σ < 30% of max)")
    reset()

    print("  ")
    bg_yellow()
    print("        ")
    reset()
    yellow()
    println("  Medium confidence (30% ≤ σ < 60%)")
    reset()

    print("  ")
    bg_red()
    print("        ")
    reset()
    red()
    println("  Low confidence (σ ≥ 60%)")
    reset()
    println("")

    // COMPARISON: Multiple scenarios
    bold()
    cyan()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("              SCENARIO COMPARISON (Same Mean, Different σ)        ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    let scenario1 = epistemic_new(100.0, 1.0)
    let scenario2 = epistemic_new(100.0, 25.0)
    let scenario3 = epistemic_new(100.0, 100.0)

    print("  Scenario 1: 100 ± ")
    green()
    print(epistemic_std(scenario1))
    reset()
    print("   ")
    print_confidence_bar(epistemic_std(scenario1), 10.0)

    reset()
    println("")

    print("  Scenario 2: 100 ± ")

    print(epistemic_std(scenario2))
    reset()

    print_confidence_bar(epistemic_std(scenario2), 10.0)
    print("  ")
    yellow()
    print("MEDIUM confidence")
    reset()
    println("")

    print("  Scenario 3: 100 ± ")
    red()
    print(epistemic_std(scenario3))
    reset()
    print("  ")
    print_confidence_bar(epistemic_std(scenario3), 10.0)
    print("  ")
    red()
    print("LOW confidence")
    reset()
    println("")
    println("")

    // VALUE BARS
    bold()
    green()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                 DOSAGE COMPARISON (Multiple Patients)           ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    let patient1 = epistemic_mul(epistemic_new(50.0, 4.0), dose_per_kg)
    let patient2 = epistemic_mul(epistemic_new(70.0, 4.0), dose_per_kg)
    let patient3 = epistemic_mul(epistemic_new(90.0, 4.0), dose_per_kg)

    print("  Patient 1 (50kg): ")
    print_value_bar(patient1.value, 1000.0)
    print(" ")
    bold()
    print(patient1.value)
    reset()
    print(" mg ± ")
    yellow()
    print(epistemic_std(patient1))
    reset()
    println(" mg")

    print("  Patient 2 (70kg): ")
    print_value_bar(patient2.value, 1000.0)
    print(" ")
    bold()
    print(patient2.value)
    reset()
    print(" mg ± ")
    yellow()
    print(epistemic_std(patient2))
    reset()
    println(" mg")

    print("  Patient 3 (90kg): ")
    print_value_bar(patient3.value, 1000.0)
    print(" ")
    bold()
    print(patient3.value)
    reset()
    print(" mg ± ")
    yellow()
    print(epistemic_std(patient3))
    reset()
    println(" mg")

    println("")

    // FINAL MESSAGE
    bold()
    cyan()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║  ✓ Automatic GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation               ║")

    println("║  ✓ No external plotting library needed!                          ║")

fn reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }

fn green() { print("\x1b[32m") }

fn cyan() { print("\x1b[36m") }
fn white() { print("\x1b[97m") }

fn bg_green() { print("\x1b[42m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_blue() { print("\x1b[44m") }
fn bg_magenta() { print("\x1b[45m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }

// ============================================================================
// NUMERIC HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

fn erf_approx(x: f64) -> f64 {
    let a1 = 0.254829592
    let a2 = 0.0 - 0.284496736
    let a3 = 1.421413741
    let a4 = 0.0 - 1.453152027
    let a5 = 1.061405429
    let p = 0.3275911
    let sign = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - 1.0 } else { 1.0 }
    let x_abs = if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
    let t = 1.0 / (1.0 + p * x_abs)
    let y = 1.0 - (((((a5 * t + a4) * t) + a3) * t + a2) * t + a1) * t * exp_f64(0.0 - x_abs * x_abs)
    return sign * y
}

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 10.0 { return 22026.465794806718 * exp_f64(x - 10.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 10.0 { return 0.00004539992976248485 * exp_f64(x + 10.0) }
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var nf = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 20 {
        term = term * x / nf
        result = result + term
        n = n + 1
        nf = nf + 1.0
    }
    return result
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC VALUE
// ============================================================================

struct EpistemicValue {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64,
    conf_alpha: f64,
    conf_beta: f64
}

fn epistemic_new(value: f64, variance: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: value,
        variance: variance,
        conf_alpha: 1.0,
        conf_beta: 1.0
    }
}

fn epistemic_std(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(k.variance)
}

fn epistemic_prob_gt(k: EpistemicValue, thresh: f64) -> f64 {
    if k.variance <= 0.0000001 {
        if k.value > thresh { return 1.0 }
        return 0.0
    }
    let z = (k.value - thresh) / sqrt_f64(k.variance)
    return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf_approx(z / 1.4142135623730951))
}

fn ensemble_mean_5(m1: EpistemicValue, m2: EpistemicValue, m3: EpistemicValue, m4: EpistemicValue, m5: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let n = 5.0
    let mean_value = (m1.value + m2.value + m3.value + m4.value + m5.value) / n
    let within_var = (m1.variance + m2.variance + m3.variance + m4.variance + m5.variance) / n

    let d1 = m1.value - mean_value
    let d2 = m2.value - mean_value
    let d3 = m3.value - mean_value
    let d4 = m4.value - mean_value
    let d5 = m5.value - mean_value
    let between_var = (d1*d1 + d2*d2 + d3*d3 + d4*d4 + d5*d5) / (n - 1.0)

    let total_var = within_var + between_var
    return epistemic_new(mean_value, total_var)
}

fn print_temp_bar_colored(temp: f64, std_dev: f64, model_color: i32) {
    // Model color
    if model_color == 1 { red() }
    if model_color == 2 { green() }
    if model_color == 3 { yellow() }
    if model_color == 4 { magenta() }
    if model_color == 5 { cyan() }

    // Main value bar
    let bar_len = (temp * 20.0)
    var i = 0
    while i < bar_len {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()

    // Uncertainty extension
    dim()
    if model_color == 1 { red() }
    if model_color == 2 { green() }
    if model_color == 3 { yellow() }
    if model_color == 4 { magenta() }
    if model_color == 5 { cyan() }

    let unc_len = (std_dev * 20.0)
    i = 0
    while i < unc_len {
        print("▒")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()
}

// === FILE: examples/visual/09_pkpd_color_curves.sio ===
/// Visual Example 9: PK/PD Concentration-Time Curves - Color Edition
///
/// Demonstrates: Drug pharmacokinetics with color-coded phases
///
/// Visual Output: ASCII time-series curves showing:
/// - Absorption phase (GREEN - increasing concentration)
/// - Distribution phase (YELLOW - equilibration)
/// - Elimination phase (RED - declining concentration)
/// - Therapeutic window (CYAN background bars)

// ============================================================================
// ANSI COLORS
// ============================================================================

fn reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }
fn dim() { print("\x1b[2m") }

fn red() { print("\x1b[31m") }
fn green() { print("\x1b[32m") }
fn yellow() { print("\x1b[33m") }
fn blue() { print("\x1b[34m") }
fn magenta() { print("\x1b[35m") }
fn cyan() { print("\x1b[36m") }
fn white() { print("\x1b[97m") }

fn bg_red() { print("\x1b[41m") }
fn bg_green() { print("\x1b[42m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_blue() { print("\x1b[44m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }
fn bg_white() { print("\x1b[47m") }

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x > 10.0 { return 22026.465794806718 * exp_f64(x - 10.0) }
    if x < 0.0 - 10.0 { return 0.00004539992976248485 * exp_f64(x + 10.0) }
    var result = 1.0
    var term = 1.0
    var nf = 1.0
    var n = 1
    while n < 20 {
        term = term * x / nf
        result = result + term
        n = n + 1
        nf = nf + 1.0
    }
    return result
}

fn max_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

fn min_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    if a < b { return a }
    return b
}

// ============================================================================
// PHARMACOKINETIC MODEL
// ============================================================================

/// One-compartment oral absorption model
/// C(t) = (ka*D/Vd) * (exp(-ke*t) - exp(-ka*t)) / (ka - ke)
fn pk_concentration(t: f64, dose: f64, vd: f64, ka: f64, ke: f64) -> f64 {
    let factor = (ka * dose / vd) / (ka - ke)
    let c_elim = exp_f64(0.0 - ke * t)
    let c_absorb = exp_f64(0.0 - ka * t)
    return factor * (c_elim - c_absorb)
}

/// Determine PK phase based on concentration and time
/// Returns: 0 = absorption, 1 = distribution, 2 = elimination
fn determine_phase(c: f64, c_max: f64, t: f64, t_max: f64) -> i32 {
    if t < t_max {
        return 0  // Absorption (rising)
    }
    if t < t_max * 2.0 && c > c_max * 0.7 {
        return 1  // Distribution (plateau)
    }
    return 2  // Elimination (falling)
}

// ============================================================================
// VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn print_concentration_bar(conc: f64, max_conc: f64, phase: i32, in_window: i32) {
    // Background for therapeutic window
    if in_window == 1 {
        bg_cyan()
        print(" ")
        reset()
    }

    // Phase color
    if phase == 0 { green() }      // Absorption
    if phase == 1 { yellow() }     // Distribution
    if phase == 2 { red() }        // Elimination

    let bar_len = (conc / max_conc * 60.0)
    var i = 0
    while i < bar_len {
        print("█")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()
}

fn print_phase_label(phase: i32) {
    if phase == 0 {
        green()
        print(" [ABSORPTION]")
    }
    if phase == 1 {
        yellow()
        print(" [DISTRIBUTION]")
    }
    if phase == 2 {
        red()
        print(" [ELIMINATION]")
    }
    reset()
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN: PK/PD VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 {
    bold()
    magenta()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║    PHARMACOKINETIC CONCENTRATION-TIME CURVE VISUALIZATION        ║")
    println("║    Midazolam 7.5mg Oral - One-Compartment Model                 ║")
    println("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    reset()
    println("")

    // Midazolam PK parameters
    let dose = 7.5      // mg
    let vd = 77.0       // L (volume of distribution)
    let cl = 27.0       // L/h (clearance)
    let ka = 1.5        // /h (absorption rate constant)
    let ke = cl / vd    // /h (elimination rate constant = 0.35)

    // Therapeutic window
    let c_min = 20.0    // ng/mL (minimum effective)
    let c_max_safe = 80.0  // ng/mL (maximum safe)

    // Time to peak concentration: t_max = ln(ka/ke) / (ka - ke)
    let t_max = 1.6  // hours (approximately for these parameters)

    bold()
    cyan()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                    PHARMACOKINETIC PARAMETERS                    ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    print("  Dose:                  ")
    bold()
    print(dose)
    reset()
    println(" mg")

    print("  Volume of distribution:")

    print("  Absorption rate (ka):  ")

    reset()

    print("  Elimination rate (ke): ")
    red()
    bold()
    print(ke)
    reset()
    println(" /h")

    print("  Half-life (t½):        ")
    yellow()
    bold()
    print(0.693 / ke)
    reset()
    println(" h")

    println("")
    print("  Therapeutic window:    ")
    cyan()
    print(c_min)
    reset()
    print(" - ")
    cyan()
    print(c_max_safe)
    reset()
    println(" ng/mL")

    println("")

    // Find peak concentration
    let c_peak = pk_concentration(t_max, dose, vd, ka, ke)

    bold()
    yellow()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                CONCENTRATION-TIME PROFILE (0-12h)                ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    // Legend
    print("  ")
    green()
    print("██")
    reset()
    print(" Absorption   ")

    yellow()
    print("██")
    reset()
    print(" Distribution   ")

    red()
    print("██")

    print(" Elimination   ")

    bg_cyan()
    print(" ")
    reset()
    println(" Therapeutic window")
    println("")

    // Plot concentration curve at 30-minute intervals
    var t = 0.0
    while t <= 12.0 {
        let c = pk_concentration(t, dose, vd, ka, ke)

        let in_window = if c >= c_min && c <= c_max_safe { 1 } else { 0 }

        // Time label

        if phase == 1 { yellow() }

    }

    println("")

    blue()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                    CLINICAL INTERPRETATION                      ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")

    green()

    reset()
    yellow()

    reset()

// === FILE: examples/visual/10_kalman_filter_color.sio ===
/// Visual Example 10: Bayesian Sensor Fusion with Kalman Filter - Color Edition
///
/// Demonstrates: Sequential belief updates with color-coded uncertainty
///
/// Visual Output: Uncertainty reduction visualization
/// - RED: High uncertainty (low precision)
/// - YELLOW: Medium uncertainty
/// - GREEN: Low uncertainty (high precision)
/// - CYAN: Precision bars showing 1/σ²

// ============================================================================
// ANSI COLORS
// ============================================================================

fn reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }
fn dim() { print("\x1b[2m") }

fn red() { print("\x1b[31m") }
fn green() { print("\x1b[32m") }
fn yellow() { print("\x1b[33m") }
fn blue() { print("\x1b[34m") }
fn magenta() { print("\x1b[35m") }
fn cyan() { print("\x1b[36m") }
fn white() { print("\x1b[97m") }

fn bg_red() { print("\x1b[41m") }
fn bg_green() { print("\x1b[42m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_blue() { print("\x1b[44m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var y = x
    var i = 0
    while i < 10 {
        y = 0.5 * (y + x / y)
        i = i + 1
    }
    return y
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// EPISTEMIC VALUE (BELIEF STATE)
// ============================================================================

struct EpistemicValue {
    value: f64,
    variance: f64
}

fn epistemic_new(value: f64, variance: f64) -> EpistemicValue {
    return EpistemicValue {
        value: value,
        variance: variance
    }
}

fn epistemic_std(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    return sqrt_f64(k.variance)
}

fn epistemic_precision(k: EpistemicValue) -> f64 {
    if k.variance <= 0.0000001 { return 10000.0 }
    return 1.0 / k.variance
}

// ============================================================================
// KALMAN UPDATE (PRECISION-WEIGHTED BAYESIAN FUSION)
// ============================================================================

/// Kalman filter update: combines prior belief with new measurement
///
/// Precision-weighted mean:
///   μ_post = (τ_prior * μ_prior + τ_meas * z) / (τ_prior + τ_meas)
///   where τ = 1/σ² (precision)
///
/// Posterior precision (information addition):
///   τ_post = τ_prior + τ_meas
///   σ²_post = 1 / (1/σ²_prior + 1/σ²_meas)
///
fn kalman_update(prior: EpistemicValue, measurement: EpistemicValue) -> EpistemicValue {
    let tau_prior = epistemic_precision(prior)
    let tau_meas = epistemic_precision(measurement)
    let tau_post = tau_prior + tau_meas

    let mu_post = (tau_prior * prior.value + tau_meas * measurement.value) / tau_post
    let var_post = 1.0 / tau_post

    return epistemic_new(mu_post, var_post)
}

// ============================================================================
// VISUALIZATION HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn uncertainty_color(std_dev: f64) {
    if std_dev < 2.0 {
        green()
    }
    if std_dev >= 2.0 && std_dev < 5.0 {
        yellow()
    }
    if std_dev >= 5.0 {
        red()
    }
}

fn print_uncertainty_bar(std_dev: f64, max_std: f64) {
    let normalized = std_dev / max_std

    if normalized < 0.2 { bg_green() }
    if normalized >= 0.2 && normalized < 0.5 { bg_yellow() }
    if normalized >= 0.5 { bg_red() }

    let bar_len = (std_dev / max_std * 40.0)
    var i = 0
    while i < bar_len {
        print(" ")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()
}

fn print_precision_bar(precision: f64, max_precision: f64) {
    bg_cyan()
    let bar_len = (precision / max_precision * 40.0)
    var i = 0
    while i < bar_len {
        print(" ")
        i = i + 1
    }
    reset()
}

fn print_confidence_level(std_dev: f64) {
    if std_dev < 2.0 {
        green()
        bold()
        print("HIGH")
    }
    if std_dev >= 2.0 && std_dev < 5.0 {
        yellow()
        bold()
        print("MEDIUM")
    }
    if std_dev >= 5.0 {
        red()
        bold()
        print("LOW")
    }
    reset()
}

    println("                    SENSOR FUSION SCENARIO                        ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    println("  Task: Estimate robot position from multiple noisy sensors")
    println("")
    println("  Sensors:")

    bold()
    yellow()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                SEQUENTIAL BELIEF UPDATES                         ")

    reset()
    yellow()
    print(" Medium (2-5m)  ")
    reset()

    bg_red()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    red()
    println(" High (σ > 5m)")
    reset()

    println("")

    // STEP 0: Prior
    print("  [PRIOR]         μ = ")
    bold()
    print(prior.value)
    reset()

    uncertainty_color(epistemic_std(prior))
    bold()

    reset()
    print(" m  ")
    print_uncertainty_bar(epistemic_std(prior), max_std)
    print("  ")
    print_confidence_level(epistemic_std(prior))
    println("")

    print("                  Precision: ")
    cyan()
    print(epistemic_precision(prior))
    reset()
    print("  ")

    bold()
    print(epistemic_std(state1))
    reset()
    print(" m  ")
    print_uncertainty_bar(epistemic_std(state1), max_std)
    print("  ")
    print_confidence_level(epistemic_std(state1))
    println("")

    print("                  Precision: ")

    reset()
    print("  ")
    print_precision_bar(epistemic_precision(state1), max_precision)
    println("")

    let reduction1 = (epistemic_std(prior) - epistemic_std(state1)) / epistemic_std(prior) * 100.0

    // STEP 2: IMU fusion

    print(" m, σ = ")
    uncertainty_color(epistemic_std(state2))
    bold()
    print(epistemic_std(state2))
    reset()
    print(" m  ")
    print_uncertainty_bar(epistemic_std(state2), max_std)
    print("  ")
    print_confidence_level(epistemic_std(state2))
    println("")

    print("                  Precision: ")
    cyan()
    print(epistemic_precision(state2))
    reset()
    print("  ")
    print_precision_bar(epistemic_precision(state2), max_precision)
    println("")

    let reduction2 = (epistemic_std(state1) - epistemic_std(state2)) / epistemic_std(state1) * 100.0
    print("                  Uncertainty reduction: ")
    green()
    bold()
    print(reduction2)
    reset()
    println("%")
    println("")

    // STEP 3: Lidar fusion
    let state3 = kalman_update(state2, lidar)

    print("  [+ LIDAR]       μ = ")
    bold()
    print(state3.value)
    reset()
    print(" m, σ = ")
    uncertainty_color(epistemic_std(state3))

// === FILE: examples/visual/11_sir_epidemic_color.sio ===
/// Visual Example 11: SIR Epidemic Model - Color Edition
///
/// Demonstrates: Disease dynamics with color-coded populations
///
/// Visual Output: SIR compartmental model over time
/// - BLUE: Susceptible population (not yet infected)
/// - RED: Infectious population (actively spreading)
/// - GREEN: Recovered population (immune)
/// - Stacked bars showing population composition

// ============================================================================
// ANSI COLORS
// ============================================================================

fn reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }
fn dim() { print("\x1b[2m") }

fn red() { print("\x1b[31m") }
fn green() { print("\x1b[32m") }
fn yellow() { print("\x1b[33m") }
fn blue() { print("\x1b[34m") }
fn magenta() { print("\x1b[35m") }
fn cyan() { print("\x1b[36m") }
fn white() { print("\x1b[97m") }

fn bg_red() { print("\x1b[41m") }
fn bg_green() { print("\x1b[42m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_blue() { print("\x1b[44m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }

// ============================================================================
// SIR MODEL
// ============================================================================

struct SIRState {
    s: f64,  // Susceptible
    i: f64,  // Infectious
    r: f64   // Recovered
}

struct SIRParams {
    beta: f64,   // Transmission rate
    gamma: f64   // Recovery rate
}

/// SIR differential equations:
/// dS/dt = -β·S·I/N
/// dI/dt = β·S·I/N - γ·I
/// dR/dt = γ·I
fn sir_derivative(state: SIRState, params: SIRParams, n: f64) -> SIRState {
    let infection_rate = params.beta * state.s * state.i / n
    let recovery_rate = params.gamma * state.i

    return SIRState {
        s: 0.0 - infection_rate,
        i: infection_rate - recovery_rate,
        r: recovery_rate
    }
}

/// Euler method integration step
fn sir_step(state: SIRState, params: SIRParams, n: f64, dt: f64) -> SIRState {
    let deriv = sir_derivative(state, params, n)
    return SIRState {
        s: state.s + deriv.s * dt,
        i: state.i + deriv.i * dt,
        r: state.r + deriv.r * dt
    }
}

/// Calculate R0 (basic reproduction number)
fn calculate_r0(params: SIRParams) -> f64 {
    return params.beta / params.gamma
}

// ============================================================================
// VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn print_population_bar(s: f64, i: f64, r: f64, total: f64) {
    let bar_width = 60.0

    // Susceptible (blue)
    bg_blue()
    let s_len = (s / total * bar_width)
    var j = 0
    while j < s_len {
        print(" ")
        j = j + 1
    }
    reset()

    // Infectious (red)
    bg_red()
    let i_len = (i / total * bar_width)
    j = 0
    while j < i_len {
        print(" ")
        j = j + 1
    }
    reset()

    // Recovered (green)
    bg_green()
    let r_len = (r / total * bar_width)
    j = 0
    while j < r_len {
        print(" ")
        j = j + 1
    }
    reset()
}

fn print_phase_indicator(i: f64, peak: f64) {
    if i < peak * 0.1 {
        cyan()
        print(" [EARLY GROWTH]")
    }
    if i >= peak * 0.1 && i < peak * 0.7 {
        yellow()
        print(" [ACCELERATION]")
    }
    if i >= peak * 0.7 && i <= peak {
        red()
        bold()
        print(" [PEAK APPROACH]")
    }
    if i < peak && i >= peak * 0.7 {
        yellow()
        print(" [DECELERATION]")
    }
    reset()
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN: SIR EPIDEMIC VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 {
    bold()
    magenta()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║       SIR EPIDEMIC MODEL - Disease Dynamics Visualization        ║")
    println("║       COVID-19-like Parameters (R₀ = 2.5)                        ║")
    println("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    reset()
    println("")

    // Parameters (COVID-19-like)
    let params = SIRParams {
        beta: 0.5,    // Transmission rate (/day)
        gamma: 0.2    // Recovery rate (/day, ~5 day infectious period)
    }

    let r0 = calculate_r0(params)
    let n = 1000.0    // Total population
    let dt = 0.5      // Time step (days)

    // Initial conditions
    var state = SIRState {
        s: 990.0,     // 99% susceptible
        i: 10.0,      // 1% initially infected
        r: 0.0        // No recovered yet
    }

    bold()
    cyan()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                     EPIDEMIC PARAMETERS                          ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    print("  Population (N):          ")
    bold()
    print(n)
    reset()
    println(" people")

    print("  Transmission rate (β):   ")
    red()
    bold()
    print(params.beta)
    reset()
    println(" /day")

    print("  Recovery rate (γ):       ")
    green()
    bold()
    print(params.gamma)
    reset()
    println(" /day")

    print("  Infectious period:       ")
    yellow()
    bold()
    print(1.0 / params.gamma)
    reset()
    println(" days")

    print("  Basic reproduction (R₀): ")
    if r0 > 2.0 {
        red()
    }
    if r0 > 1.0 && r0 <= 2.0 {
        yellow()
    }
    if r0 <= 1.0 {
        green()
    }
    bold()
    print(r0)
    reset()
    if r0 > 1.0 {
        red()
        print(" (EPIDEMIC)")
    }
    if r0 <= 1.0 {
        green()
        print(" (CONTROLLED)")
    }
    reset()
    println("")

    println("")

    // Find peak by simulating ahead
    var temp_state = state
    var t_sim = 0.0
    var peak_i = state.i
    while t_sim <= 100.0 {
        temp_state = sir_step(temp_state, params, n, dt)
        if temp_state.i > peak_i {
            peak_i = temp_state.i
        }
        t_sim = t_sim + dt
    }

    bold()
    yellow()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                EPIDEMIC TIME COURSE (0-50 days)                 ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    // Legend
    print("  ")
    bg_blue()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    blue()
    print(" Susceptible  ")
    reset()

    bg_red()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    red()
    print(" Infectious  ")
    reset()

    bg_green()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    green()
    println(" Recovered")
    reset()
    println("")

    // Simulate and visualize
    var t = 0.0
    var peak_reached = 0

    while t <= 50.0 {
        // Print time
        print("  Day ")
        if t < 10.0 { print(" ") }
        bold()
        white()
        print(t)
        reset()
        print(" │ ")

        // Population bar
        print_population_bar(state.s, state.i, state.r, n)

        // Numbers
        print("  ")
        blue()
        print("S:")
        print(state.s)
        reset()
        print(" ")
        red()
        print("I:")
        print(state.i)
        reset()
        print(" ")
        green()
        print("R:")
        print(state.r)
        reset()

        // Peak detection
        if state.i >= peak_i * 0.95 && peak_reached == 0 {
            red()
            bold()
            print(" ← PEAK")
            reset()
            peak_reached = 1
        }

        println("")

        // Update state
        state = sir_step(state, params, n, dt)
        t = t + 2.0  // Print every 2 days
    }

    println("")

    // Final statistics
    bold()
    green()
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    println("                     EPIDEMIC SUMMARY                             ")
    println("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━")
    reset()
    println("")

    print("  Peak infections:         ")
    red()
    bold()
    print(peak_i)
    reset()
    print(" people (")
    red()
    print(peak_i / n * 100.0)
    reset()
    println("% of population)")

    print("  Final recovered:         ")
    green()
    bold()
    print(state.r)
    reset()
    print(" people (")
    green()
    print(state.r / n * 100.0)
    reset()
    println("% attack rate)")

    print("  Final susceptible:       ")
    blue()
    print(state.s)
    reset()
    println(" people (escaped infection)")

    println("")

    bold()
    white()
    println("  Key insights:")
    reset()
    cyan()
    println("    • R₀ = 2.5 means each infected person infects 2-3 others")
    reset()
    cyan()
    println("    • Peak infections occur when S ≈ N/R₀ (herd immunity threshold)")
    reset()
    cyan()
    println("    • Final size depends on R₀: higher R₀ → more total infections")
    reset()
    cyan()
    println("    • Recovery (green) grows as infectious (red) declines")
    reset()

    println("")

    bold()
    magenta()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║  ✓ Compartmental model dynamics visualized with stacked bars     ║")
    println("║  ✓ Epidemic phases color-coded (growth → peak → decline)         ║")
    println("║  ✓ Classic SIR model - foundation of epidemiology!               ║")
    println("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    reset()

    return 0
}


// === FILE: examples/visual/12_animated_diffusion.sio ===
/// Visual Example 12: Animated Heat Diffusion - Frame-Based Animation
///
/// Demonstrates: Terminal animation using frame updates
///
/// Visual Output: 2D heat diffusion simulation
/// - RED: Hot (high temperature)
/// - YELLOW: Warm
/// - CYAN: Cool
/// - BLUE: Cold (low temperature)
/// - Updates in place using ANSI cursor control

// ============================================================================
// ANSI CONTROL CODES
// ============================================================================

fn reset() { print("\x1b[0m") }
fn bold() { print("\x1b[1m") }
fn clear_screen() { print("\x1b[2J") }
fn home_cursor() { print("\x1b[H") }
fn hide_cursor() { print("\x1b[?25l") }
fn show_cursor() { print("\x1b[?25h") }

fn red() { print("\x1b[31m") }
fn green() { print("\x1b[32m") }
fn yellow() { print("\x1b[33m") }
fn blue() { print("\x1b[34m") }
fn magenta() { print("\x1b[35m") }
fn cyan() { print("\x1b[36m") }
fn white() { print("\x1b[97m") }

fn bg_red() { print("\x1b[41m") }
fn bg_yellow() { print("\x1b[43m") }
fn bg_cyan() { print("\x1b[46m") }
fn bg_blue() { print("\x1b[44m") }

// ============================================================================
// HEAT DIFFUSION SIMULATION
// ============================================================================

/// Simple 2D heat diffusion using finite differences
/// ∂T/∂t = α·∇²T
/// Discrete: T_new[i,j] = T[i,j] + α·dt·(T[i-1,j] + T[i+1,j] + T[i,j-1] + T[i,j+1] - 4·T[i,j])/dx²

fn get_temp(grid: [f64; 256], i: i32, j: i32, size: i32) -> f64 {
    if i < 0 || i >= size || j < 0 || j >= size {
        return 0.0  // Boundary condition: cold edges
    }
    let idx = i * size + j
    return grid[idx]
}

fn set_temp(grid: [f64; 256], i: i32, j: i32, size: i32, value: f64) -> [f64; 256] {
    var new_grid = grid
    let idx = i * size + j
    new_grid[idx] = value
    return new_grid
}

fn diffusion_step(grid: [f64; 256], size: i32, alpha: f64, dt: f64, dx: f64) -> [f64; 256] {
    var new_grid = grid
    let coeff = alpha * dt / (dx * dx)

    var i = 1
    while i < size - 1 {
        var j = 1
        while j < size - 1 {
            let idx = i * size + j
            let t_center = grid[idx]
            let t_left = get_temp(grid, i - 1, j, size)
            let t_right = get_temp(grid, i + 1, j, size)
            let t_up = get_temp(grid, i, j - 1, size)
            let t_down = get_temp(grid, i, j + 1, size)

            let laplacian = t_left + t_right + t_up + t_down - 4.0 * t_center
            let t_new = t_center + coeff * laplacian

            new_grid[idx] = t_new
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return new_grid
}

// ============================================================================
// VISUALIZATION
// ============================================================================

fn temp_to_color(temp: f64) {
    if temp < 25.0 {
        bg_blue()
    }
    if temp >= 25.0 && temp < 50.0 {
        bg_cyan()
    }
    if temp >= 50.0 && temp < 75.0 {
        bg_yellow()
    }
    if temp >= 75.0 {
        bg_red()
    }
}

fn render_frame(grid: [f64; 256], size: i32, frame: i32) {
    home_cursor()

    bold()
    cyan()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    print("║   HEAT DIFFUSION ANIMATION - Frame ")
    print(frame)
    println("                            ║")
    println("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    reset()
    println("")

    // Render grid
    var i = 0
    while i < size {
        print("  ")
        var j = 0
        while j < size {
            let idx = i * size + j
            let temp = grid[idx]
            temp_to_color(temp)
            print("  ")
            reset()
            j = j + 1
        }
        println("")
        i = i + 1
    }

    println("")
    print("  ")
    bg_blue()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    blue()
    print(" Cold (&lt;25°C)  ")
    reset()

    bg_cyan()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    cyan()
    print(" Cool (25-50°C)  ")
    reset()

    bg_yellow()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    yellow()
    print(" Warm (50-75°C)  ")
    reset()

    bg_red()
    print("  ")
    reset()
    red()
    println(" Hot (&gt;75°C)")
    reset()
}

// Note: Array initialization workaround - Sounio doesn't support array literals yet
fn init_grid(size: i32) -> [f64; 256] {
    var grid = [0.0; 256]

    // Hot spot in center
    let center = size / 2
    var i = center - 2
    while i <= center + 2 {
        var j = center - 2
        while j <= center + 2 {
            let idx = i * size + j
            grid[idx] = 100.0
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    return grid
}

// ============================================================================
// MAIN: ANIMATED DIFFUSION
// ============================================================================

fn main() -> i32 {
    clear_screen()
    hide_cursor()

    let size = 16
    let alpha = 0.1    // Thermal diffusivity
    let dt = 0.1       // Time step
    let dx = 1.0       // Spatial step

    var grid = init_grid(size)
    var frame = 0

    // Animate for 20 frames
    while frame < 20 {
        render_frame(grid, size, frame)
        grid = diffusion_step(grid, size, alpha, dt, dx)
        frame = frame + 1

        // Delay (platform-dependent - would need sleep function)
        // For now, just show frames in sequence
    }

    show_cursor()
    println("")
    bold()
    magenta()
    println("╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗")
    println("║  ✓ Frame-based animation with ANSI cursor control                ║")
    println("║  ✓ Heat diffusion from center hot spot                           ║")
    println("║  ✓ Color gradient shows temperature distribution                 ║")
    println("╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝")
    reset()

    return 0
}

/// Wave 1 Example: Bayesian Coin Flip Inference

/// Demonstrates probabilistic inference with distributions.
/// We observe coin flips and update our belief about fairness.

/// This example shows:
/// - Working with probability distributions
/// - Sampling from distributions

fn main() {
    println("=== Bayesian Coin Flip Inference ===");

    // Prior belief: the coin is fair-ish (mean 0.5, std 0.1)
    let prior = Distribution::Normal(0.5, 0.1);

    println!("Prior belief about coin bias:");
    println!("  Mean: 0.5");
    println!("  Std Dev: 0.1");

    // Simulate some coin flips
    let num_flips = 100;
    let true_bias = 0.6;  // The coin is actually biased towards heads
    let heads_count = count_heads(true_bias, num_flips);

    println!("\nObserved {} heads in {} flips ({:.1}%)",
             heads_count, num_flips, 100.0 * heads_count as f64 / num_flips as f64);

    // Posterior distribution would be Beta distributed
    // For now, simulate with samples from the prior
    let posterior = Distribution::Beta(
        0.5 + heads_count as f64,      // alpha
        0.5 + (num_flips - heads_count) as f64  // beta

    println!("\nPosterior distribution (Beta):");
    println!("  alpha: {}", 0.5 + heads_count as f64);
    println!("  beta: {}", 0.5 + (num_flips - heads_count) as f64);

    // Sample from posterior
    let posterior_mean = sample(posterior);
    println!("\nEstimated coin bias: {:.3}", posterior_mean);
    println!("True bias was: {:.1}", true_bias);
}

fn count_heads(bias: f64, n: i64) -> i64 {
    // Simple simulation: count how many times a random number < bias
    let mut count = 0;
    for i in 0..n {
        // Pseudo-random: use sin(i) to generate values
        let random = (sin(i as f64 * 3.7) + 1.0) / 2.0;  // Normalize to [0, 1]
        if random < bias {
            count = count + 1;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

fn sin(x: f64) -> f64 {

    // For now, use a simple approximation
    return x - (x * x * x) / 6.0;  // Taylor series approximation
}

// === FILE: examples/wave1_projectile_motion.sio ===
/*
Aspirational example preserved below.
To restore, remove this stub and uncomment the original content.

/// Wave 1 Example: Projectile Motion with Units
///
/// Demonstrates physical simulation with dimensional analysis.
/// Computes trajectory of a projectile under gravity.
///
/// This example shows:
/// - Type-safe physics calculations
/// - Unit annotations
/// - Scientific functions

fn main() {
    println("=== Projectile Motion ===");

    // Initial conditions
    let initial_velocity = 20.0;  // m/s
    let angle_degrees = 45.0;     // degrees
    let g = 9.81;                 // m/s² (acceleration due to gravity)

    // Convert angle to radians
    let angle_rad = angle_degrees * 3.14159 / 180.0;

    // Initial velocity components
    let vx = initial_velocity * cos(angle_rad);
    let vy = initial_velocity * sin(angle_rad);

    println("Initial velocity: {:.2} m/s", initial_velocity);
    println("Launch angle: {:.1}°", angle_degrees);
    println("Vx = {:.2} m/s, Vy = {:.2} m/s", vx, vy);

    // Maximum height
    let max_height = (vy * vy) / (2.0 * g);

    // Time to reach maximum height
    let time_to_max = vy / g;

    // Total flight time (when y returns to 0)
    let total_time = 2.0 * time_to_max;

    // Range (horizontal distance)
    let range = vx * total_time;

    println("\n=== Results ===");
    println("Max height: {:.2} m", max_height);
    println("Time to max height: {:.2} s", time_to_max);
    println("Total flight time: {:.2} s", total_time);
    println("Range: {:.2} m", range);

    // Compute trajectory at several time points
    println("\n=== Trajectory ===");
    println("Time (s) | Height (m) | Distance (m)");
    println("---------|------------|-------------");

    let num_points = 11;
    for i in 0..num_points {
        let t = total_time * i as f64 / (num_points - 1) as f64;

fn dot(a: [f64], b: [f64]) -> f64 {
    let mut sum = 0.0;
    for i in 0..len(a) {
        if i < len(b) {
            sum = sum + a[i] * b[i];

    }
    return sum;

fn magnitude(v: [f64]) -> f64 {
    let mut sum_sq = 0.0;
    for i in 0..len(v) {
        sum_sq = sum_sq + v[i] * v[i];

    return sqrt(sum_sq);
}

fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    // Newton's method for square root
    if x == 0.0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let mut guess = x;
    for _ in 0..10 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0;
    }
    return guess;
}

/// Wave 1 Example: Uncertainty Propagation
///
/// Demonstrates working with measurements that have uncertainty bounds.
/// Shows how uncertainty propagates through calculations.
///
/// This example shows:
/// - Creating uncertain values
/// - Arithmetic with uncertainty
/// - Analyzing measurement error

fn main() {
    println("=== Uncertainty Propagation ===");

    // Measure a resistor
    let resistance = Uncertain { mean: 100.0, std: 2.5 };  // 100 ± 2.5 Ω
    let voltage = Uncertain { mean: 5.0, std: 0.1 };       // 5 ± 0.1 V

    println!("Resistance: {} ± {} Ω", resistance.mean, resistance.std);
    println!("Voltage: {} ± {} V", voltage.mean, voltage.std);

    // Ohm's law: I = V / R
    let current = divide_uncertain(voltage, resistance);

    println!("\nOhm's Law: I = V / R");
    println!("Current: {:.4} ± {:.4} A", current.mean, current.std);

    // Power dissipation: P = V * I = V² / R
    let power = multiply_uncertain(voltage, current);

    println!("\nPower dissipation: P = V × I");
    println!("Power: {:.3} ± {:.3} W", power.mean, power.std);

    // Relative uncertainty
    let voltage_rel_unc = voltage.std / voltage.mean;
    let resistance_rel_unc = resistance.std / resistance.mean;
    let current_rel_unc = current.std / current.mean;

    println!("\n=== Relative Uncertainty ===");
    println!("Voltage uncertainty: {:.2}%", voltage_rel_unc * 100.0);
    println!("Resistance uncertainty: {:.2}%", resistance_rel_unc * 100.0);
    println!("Current uncertainty: {:.2}%", current_rel_unc * 100.0);

    // Temperature measurement
    println!("\n=== Temperature Measurement ===");
    let temp_celsius = Uncertain { mean: 25.0, std: 0.5 };
    println!("Temperature: {} ± {} °C", temp_celsius.mean, temp_celsius.std);

    // Convert to Fahrenheit: F = 9/5 * C + 32
    let temp_fahrenheit = scale_and_shift_uncertain(temp_celsius, 9.0/5.0, 32.0);
    println!("Temperature: {:.1} ± {:.2} °F", temp_fahrenheit.mean, temp_fahrenheit.std);

    // Measurement reproducibility
    println!("\n=== Multiple Measurements ===");
    let measurements = [24.8, 25.1, 25.0, 24.9, 25.2];
    let mean_val = compute_mean(measurements);
    let std_val = compute_std(measurements, mean_val);

    println!("Measurements: {} values", len(measurements));
    println!("Mean: {:.2} °C", mean_val);
    println!("Std Dev: {:.4} °C", std_val);
    println!("95% CI: [{:.2}, {:.2}] °C",
             mean_val - 1.96*std_val,
             mean_val + 1.96*std_val);
}

struct Uncertain {
    mean: f64,
    std: f64,
}

fn multiply_uncertain(a: Uncertain, b: Uncertain) -> Uncertain {
    // P(A×B) ≈ (A×B) ± sqrt((B×σ_A)² + (A×σ_B)²)
    let mean_product = a.mean * b.mean;
    let std_product = sqrt(
        (b.mean * a.std)*(b.mean * a.std) +
        (a.mean * b.std)*(a.mean * b.std)
    );

    return Uncertain { mean: mean_product, std: std_product };
}

fn divide_uncertain(a: Uncertain, b: Uncertain) -> Uncertain {
    // P(A/B) ≈ (A/B) ± (A/B) × sqrt((σ_A/A)² + (σ_B/B)²)
    let mean_quotient = a.mean / b.mean;
    let rel_std = sqrt(
        (a.std/a.mean)*(a.std/a.mean) +
        (b.std/b.mean)*(b.std/b.mean)
    );
    let std_quotient = mean_quotient * rel_std;

    return Uncertain { mean: mean_quotient, std: std_quotient };
}

fn scale_and_shift_uncertain(u: Uncertain, scale: f64, shift: f64) -> Uncertain {
    // For linear transformation: Y = scale*X + shift
    // Mean transforms: E[Y] = scale*E[X] + shift
    // Std dev scales: σ_Y = |scale| * σ_X
    return Uncertain {
        mean: scale * u.mean + shift,
        std: scale * u.std  // Assuming scale > 0
    };
}

fn compute_mean(values: [f64]) -> f64 {
    let mut sum = 0.0;
    for i in 0..len(values) {
        sum = sum + values[i];
    }
    return sum / (len(values) as f64);
}

fn compute_std(values: [f64], mean: f64) -> f64 {
    let mut sum_sq_dev = 0.0;
    for i in 0..len(values) {
        let dev = values[i] - mean;
        sum_sq_dev = sum_sq_dev + dev * dev;
    }
    let variance = sum_sq_dev / (len(values) as f64);
    return sqrt(variance);
}

fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x == 0.0 { return 0.0; }
    let mut guess = x;
    for _ in 0..20 {
        guess = (guess + x / guess) / 2.0;
    }
    return guess;
}

*/

// === FILE: examples/wave2_causal_intervention.sio ===
/// Wave 2 Example: Causal Intervention with do-calculus
///
/// Demonstrates causal effect estimation using the do-operator.
/// Distinguishes between observation and intervention.
///
/// This example shows:
/// - Causal DAG specification
/// - do-operator for interventions
/// - Average treatment effect (ATE)
/// - Difference between P(Y|X) and P(Y|do(X))

fn main() with IO {
    print("=== Causal Intervention: do-calculus ===\n")
    print("Example: Effect of Education on Income\n")

    print("\n=== Causal Model ===\n")
    print("Nodes: Ability, Education, Income\n")
    print("Edges:\n")
    print("  Ability -> Education\n")
    print("  Ability -> Income\n")
    print("  Education -> Income\n")
    print("  (Ability is a confounder)\n")

    print("\n=== Observational Data P(Income | Education) ===\n")
    // Observed correlation: Higher education -> higher income
    // BUT this includes effect of ability (confounder)

    let income_no_education: i64 = 30000   // Average income if Education=0
    let income_with_education: i64 = 50000 // Observed income if Education=1

    let obs_difference = income_with_education - income_no_education
    print("Average income without education: $")
    print_int(income_no_education)
    print("\n")
    print("Average income with education: $")
    print_int(income_with_education)
    print("\n")
    print("Observed difference: $")
    print_int(obs_difference)
    print("\n")

    print("\n=== Causal Effect P(Income | do(Education)) ===\n")
    // Using do-operator removes confounding
    // We set Education=1 AND remove the Ability -> Education path
    // This reveals the CAUSAL effect, not the confounded effect

    let causal_effect_education: i64 = 15000 // Actual causal effect
    print("Setting Education = 1 via intervention\n")
    print("This breaks the Ability -> Education pathway\n")
    print("Causal effect of education: $")
    print_int(causal_effect_education)
    print("\n")
    print("Difference from observation: $")
    print_int(obs_difference - causal_effect_education)
    print("\n")

    print("\n=== Interpretation ===\n")
    print("Observed effect ($")
    print_int(obs_difference)
    print(") includes:\n")
    print("  1. Direct causal effect of education: $")
    print_int(causal_effect_education)
    print("\n")
    print("  2. Confounding effect via ability: $")
    print_int(obs_difference - causal_effect_education)
    print("\n")

    print("\nThis shows why observational studies need causal reasoning!\n")
    print("We must identify confounders and account for them properly.\n")

    // Counterfactual reasoning
    print("\n=== Counterfactual: What if Alice had more education? ===\n")
    print("Observed: Alice without education earns $30k\n")
    print("Counterfactual prediction: If Alice had education, she would earn:\n")
    print("  $30k + $")
    print_int(causal_effect_education)
    print(" = $")
    print_int(30000 + causal_effect_education)
    print("\n")
}


// === FILE: examples/wave2_causal_simpson.sio ===
/// Wave 2 Example: Simpson's Paradox in Causal Inference
///
/// Demonstrates how causal reasoning resolves Simpson's paradox.
/// Classic example: UC Berkeley admissions data
///
/// This example shows:
/// - Causal reasoning with confounders
/// - Simpson's paradox detection
/// - Proper causal adjustment

fn main() {
    println("=== Simpson's Paradox ===");
    println("UC Berkeley Admissions Case Study");

    // Simulate data
    // Male applicants: 60% admitted (overall)
    // Female applicants: 50% admitted (overall)
    // Appears males have higher admission rate

    println("\n=== Marginal (Unadjusted) Statistics ===");
    let male_admitted = 1198;
    let male_total = 1993;
    let male_rate = male_admitted as f64 / male_total as f64;

    let female_admitted = 557;
    let female_total = 1831;
    let female_rate = female_admitted as f64 / female_total as f64;

    println("Males admitted: {}/{} = {:.1}%", male_admitted, male_total, male_rate * 100.0);
    println("Females admitted: {}/{} = {:.1}%", female_admitted, female_total, female_rate * 100.0);
    println!("Difference: {:.1}%", (male_rate - female_rate) * 100.0);

    // But when stratified by department, the pattern reverses!
    println("\n=== Conditional (Stratified by Department) ===");

    // Engineering (high admission rate)
    println("\nEngineering Department:");
    let eng_male_adm = 512;
    let eng_male_total = 825;
    let eng_male_rate = eng_male_adm as f64 / eng_male_total as f64;

    let eng_female_adm = 89;
    let eng_female_total = 108;
    let eng_female_rate = eng_female_adm as f64 / eng_female_total as f64;

    println("  Males: {:.1}%", eng_male_rate * 100.0);
    println("  Females: {:.1}%", eng_female_rate * 100.0);

    // Liberal Arts (lower admission rate)
    println("\nLiberal Arts Department:");
    let la_male_adm = 353;
    let la_male_total = 1022;
    let la_male_rate = la_male_adm as f64 / la_male_total as f64;

    let la_female_adm = 207;
    let la_female_total = 1075;
    let la_female_rate = la_female_adm as f64 / la_female_total as f64;

    println("  Males: {:.1}%", la_male_rate * 100.0);
    println("  Females: {:.1}%", la_female_rate * 100.0);

    println!("\n=== Causal Analysis ===");
    println("The confounder: DEPARTMENT");
    println("- Females apply more to Liberal Arts (lower admission rate)");
    println("- Males apply more to Engineering (higher admission rate)");
    println("- When we stratify by department, females have higher rates!");

    println!("\n=== Conclusion ===");
    println("This is Simpson's Paradox: the direction of association reverses");
    println("when we properly account for the confounder (department).");
    println!("\nCausal principle: Always adjust for confounders identified");
    println("in your causal DAG, not just observed association.");
}

/// Wave 2 Example: Gradient Descent Optimization
///
/// Demonstrates using automatic differentiation for optimization.
/// Minimizes the Rosenbrock function using gradient descent.
///
/// This example shows:
/// - Computing gradients of multivariate functions
/// - Iterative optimization
/// - Convergence to minimum

fn main() {
    println("=== Gradient Descent Optimization ===");
    println("Minimizing f(x, y) = (1-x)² + 100(y-x²)²");
    println("(Rosenbrock function)");

    // Starting point
    let x = 0.0;
    let y = 0.0;

    println!("\nInitial point: ({}, {})", x, y);
    println("f(x, y) = {}", rosenbrock(x, y));

    // Simulate gradient descent steps
    let learning_rate = 0.001;
    let mut curr_x = x;
    let mut curr_y = y;

    println("\n=== Optimization Progress ===");
    println("Iteration | f(x, y)        | x          | y");
    println("----------|----------------|------------|----------");

    for iter in 0..10 {
        let f = rosenbrock(curr_x, curr_y);

        // Numerical gradient approximation (since grad() is being implemented)
        let h = 0.0001;
        let grad_x = (rosenbrock(curr_x + h, curr_y) - f) / h;
        let grad_y = (rosenbrock(curr_x, curr_y + h) - f) / h;

        // Gradient descent step
        curr_x = curr_x - learning_rate * grad_x;
        curr_y = curr_y - learning_rate * grad_y;

        println("{:9} | {:14.6} | {:10.6} | {:10.6}", iter, f, curr_x, curr_y);
    }

    println!("\nFinal point: ({:.6}, {:.6})", curr_x, curr_y);
    println("f(x, y) = {:.6}", rosenbrock(curr_x, curr_y));
    println!("Target: (1.0, 1.0) where f = 0");
}

// === FILE: examples/wave2_neural_ode.sio ===
/*
Aspirational example preserved below.
To restore, remove this stub and uncomment the original content.

/// Wave 2 Example: Neural ODE (Advanced)
///
/// Demonstrates combining ODEs with automatic differentiation.
/// A neural network transforms an ODE solution in continuous time.
///
/// This example shows:
/// - Solving ODEs
/// - Computing gradients through ODE solutions
/// - Combining neural networks with differential equations

fn main() {
    println("=== Neural ODE ===");
    println("Combining differential equations with neural networks");

    // Define a simple neural ODE layer
    // dy/dt = f_neural(y, t; θ)
    // where f_neural is a learned neural network

    println!("\n=== Defining the Neural ODE ===");
    println("dy/dt = tanh(W₁y + b₁) × W₂ + b₂");
    println("where W₁, b₁, W₂, b₂ are learnable parameters");

    // Initialize parameters
    let w1 = [0.1, 0.2];  // 2×2 weight matrix (flattened)
    let b1 = [0.01, 0.02];
    let w2 = [0.15, 0.25];
    let b2 = [0.03];

    println!("\nInitial parameters:");
    println("W₁ = [{}, {}]", w1[0], w1[1]);
    println("b₁ = [{}, {}]", b1[0], b1[1]);

    // Initial condition
    let y0 = [1.0, 0.5];
    println!("\nInitial state: y₀ = [{}, {}]", y0[0], y0[1]);

    // Solve the neural ODE
    println!("\n=== Solving Neural ODE from t=0 to t=1 ===");

    let solution_t_points = [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0];
    let solution_values = [
        [1.0, 0.5],
        [0.98, 0.48],
        [0.92, 0.43],
        [0.84, 0.35],
        [0.71, 0.22],
    ];

    println("t     | y₁(t) | y₂(t)");
    println("------|-------|-------");
    for i in 0..5 {
        println!("{:.2} | {:.3} | {:.3}", solution_t_points[i],
                 solution_values[i][0], solution_values[i][1]);
    }

    // Loss computation: MSE to target
    let target = [0.5, 0.2];
    let y_final = solution_values[4];

    let error_1 = y_final[0] - target[0];
    let error_2 = y_final[1] - target[1];
    let loss = (error_1 * error_1 + error_2 * error_2) / 2.0;

    println!("\n=== Loss Computation ===");
    println("Target final state: [{:.1}, {:.1}]", target[0], target[1]);

/// Wave 3 Example: Hybrid Neural-Symbolic Regression
///
/// Learns a quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c using a hybrid model:
/// - Symbolic part: ax² + bx + c (structural form is symbolic)
/// - Neural part: learns parameters a, b, c via gradient descent
/// - Fusion: direct evaluation (combine parameters with structure)
///
/// This demonstrates how symbolic structure can guide neural learning.

fn main() {
    println!("=== Hybrid Neural-Symbolic Regression ===");
    println!("Learning f(x) = ax² + bx + c from data\n");

    // Simulated training data from f(x) = 2x² - 3x + 1

    println!("=== Data Points ===");
    let data = [
        (-2.0, 15.0),   // 2(4) - 3(-2) + 1 = 8 + 6 + 1 = 15
        (-1.0, 6.0),    // 2(1) - 3(-1) + 1 = 2 + 3 + 1 = 6
        (0.0, 1.0),     // 2(0) - 3(0) + 1 = 1
        (1.0, 0.0),     // 2(1) - 3(1) + 1 = 2 - 3 + 1 = 0
        (2.0, 3.0),     // 2(4) - 3(2) + 1 = 8 - 6 + 1 = 3
        (3.0, 10.0),    // 2(9) - 3(3) + 1 = 18 - 9 + 1 = 10

    println!("-----+----------");

        println!("{:.1}\t| {:.1}", x, y);
    }
    println!();

    println!("=== Model Structure (Symbolic) ===");
    println!("f(x) = a*x^2 + b*x + c");
    println!("where a, b, c are learnable parameters\n");

    println!("=== Initial Parameters (Random) ===");
    let mut a = 0.1;
    let mut b = 0.2;
    let mut c = 0.5;
    println!("a = {}, b = {}, c = {}\n", a, b, c);

    println!("=== Training Phase ===");
    println!("Using gradient descent to minimize MSE loss:\n");

    let learning_rate = 0.01;
    let epochs = 5;

    for epoch in 0..epochs {
        let mut total_loss = 0.0;

        println!("Epoch {} / {}:", epoch + 1, epochs);
        println!("  a={:.4}, b={:.4}, c={:.4}", a, b, c);

            // Forward pass: evaluate model
            let y_pred = a * x * x + b * x + c;
            let error = y_pred - y_true;
            let loss = error * error;
            total_loss += loss;

            // Symbolic gradients (exact, not numeric)
            // ∂(y-ŷ)²/∂a = 2(y-ŷ) * ∂ŷ/∂a = 2(y-ŷ) * x²
            // ∂(y-ŷ)²/∂b = 2(y-ŷ) * x
            // ∂(y-ŷ)²/∂c = 2(y-ŷ)
            let grad_a = 2.0 * error * x * x;
            let grad_b = 2.0 * error * x;
            let grad_c = 2.0 * error;

            // Update parameters
            a -= learning_rate * grad_a;
            b -= learning_rate * grad_b;
            c -= learning_rate * grad_c;
        }

        let avg_loss = total_loss / data.len() as f64;
        println!("  Loss: {:.6}", avg_loss);
    }

    println!("\n=== Final Parameters (Learned) ===");

    println!("✓ Symbolic structure ax² + bx + c is interpretable");
    println!("✓ Neural learning optimizes parameters precisely");
    println!("✓ Exact gradients from symbolic form");
    println!("✓ No black-box: we know the learned formula");
}

/*
Aspirational example preserved below.
To restore, remove this stub and uncomment the original content.

/// Wave 3 Example: Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN)
///
/// Uses a hybrid model to solve the 1D heat equation:
/// ∂u/∂t - ∂²u/∂x² = 0
///
/// The symbolic component encodes the PDE constraint,
/// and the neural component approximates the solution.

fn main() {
    println!("=== Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) ===");
    println!("Solving heat equation: ∂u/∂t = ∂²u/∂x² \n");

    println!("=== Problem Setup ===");
    println!("Domain: x ∈ [0, 1], t ∈ [0, 1]");
    println!("Initial condition: u(x, 0) = sin(π*x)");
    println!("Boundary conditions: u(0, t) = 0, u(1, t) = 0\n");

    println!("Analytical solution:");
    println!("u(x, t) = sin(π*x) * exp(-π²*t)\n");

    println!("=== PINN Strategy ===");
    println!("1. Use neural network to approximate u(x, t)");
    println!("2. Compute ∂u/∂t and ∂²u/∂x² symbolically (autodiff)");
    println!("3. Enforce PDE residual: r = ∂u/∂t - ∂²u/∂x²");
    println!("4. Loss = data_loss + physics_loss\n");

    println!("Data points (observations):");
    let observations = vec![
        // (x, t, u_observed)
        (0.5, 0.0, 1.0),           // Initial: u(0.5, 0) = sin(π*0.5) = 1.0
        (0.5, 0.1, 0.070),         // u(0.5, 0.1) ≈ exp(-π²*0.1) ≈ 0.070
        (0.25, 0.0, 0.707),        // u(0.25, 0) = sin(π*0.25) ≈ 0.707
        (0.75, 0.0, 0.707),        // u(0.75, 0) = sin(π*0.75) ≈ 0.707
    ];

    println!("x\t| t\t| u_observed");
    for (x, t, u) in &observations {
        println!("{:.2}\t| {:.2}\t| {:.3}", x, t, u);
    }
    println!();

    println!("Physics-informed collocation points:");
    let collocation = vec![
        (0.3, 0.05),
        (0.5, 0.05),
        (0.7, 0.05),
        (0.3, 0.1),
        (0.5, 0.1),
        (0.7, 0.1),
    ];
    println!("({} interior points for PDE constraint)\n", collocation.len());

    println!("=== Training Loop ===");
    let epochs = 10;
    for epoch in 0..epochs {
        println!("Epoch {}/{}:", epoch + 1, epochs);

        println!("  Data loss:");
        let mut data_loss = 0.0;
        for (x, t, u_true) in &observations {
            // u_pred would come from neural network
            // For illustration: use exact solution
            let u_pred = (std::f64::consts::PI * x).sin() * (-std::f64::consts::PI * std::f64::consts::PI * t).exp();
            let error = u_pred - u_true;
            data_loss += error * error;
            println!("    ({:.2}, {:.2}): error = {:.6}", x, t, error.abs());
        }
        data_loss /= observations.len() as f64;

        println!("  Physics loss (PDE residual):");
        let mut physics_loss = 0.0;
        for (x, t) in &collocation {
            // For exact solution: residual should be ~0
            // r = ∂u/∂t - ∂²u/∂x²
            // u = sin(πx) * exp(-π²t)
            // ∂u/∂t = -π² * sin(πx) * exp(-π²t)
            // ∂²u/∂x² = -π² * sin(πx) * exp(-π²t)
            // r = -π² * sin(πx) * exp(-π²t) - (-π² * sin(πx) * exp(-π²t)) = 0
            let residual = 0.0;  // Would be computed from neural network output
            physics_loss += residual * residual;
        }
        physics_loss /= collocation.len() as f64;

        println!("    Physics residual norm: {:.6}", physics_loss);

        let total_loss = data_loss + physics_loss;
        println!("  Total loss: {:.6}\n", total_loss);
    }

    println!("=== Solution Visualization ===");
    println!("t=0.0:");
    for x in (0..=10).map(|i| i as f64 / 10.0) {
        let u = (std::f64::consts::PI * x).sin();
        let bar_len = (u * 40.0) as usize;
        println!("{:.1} | {}  {:.3}", x, "█".repeat(bar_len), u);
    }

    println!("\nt=0.1:");
    for x in (0..=10).map(|i| i as f64 / 10.0) {
        let u = (std::f64::consts::PI * x).sin() * (-std::f64::consts::PI * std::f64::consts::PI * 0.1).exp();
        let bar_len = (u * 40.0) as usize;
        println!("{:.1} | {}  {:.3}", x, "█".repeat(bar_len), u);
    }

    println!("\n=== Key Insights ===");
    println!("✓ PINNs encode physics as soft constraints (loss term)");
    println!("✓ No need for mesh generation or numerical discretization");
    println!("✓ Handles complex boundary conditions naturally");
    println!("✓ Can work with sparse data + strong physics");
    println!("✓ Symbolic derivatives ensure conservation laws");
}

// === FILE: examples/wave3_symbolic_calculus.sio ===
/// Wave 3 Example: Symbolic Calculus
///
/// Demonstrates symbolic mathematical operations:
/// - Parsing mathematical expressions
/// - Symbolic differentiation
/// - Algebraic simplification
/// - Symbolic evaluation
///
/// This is the foundation for hybrid neural-symbolic models.

fn main() {
    println!("=== Symbolic Calculus ===" );
    println!("Using symbolic math for exact computation\n");

    // Example 1: Basic polynomial differentiation
    println!("Example 1: Differentiate f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x");
    println!("Expected: df/dx = 3x^2 - 4x + 1\n");

    // Example 2: Trigonometric derivatives
    println!("Example 2: Differentiate f(x) = sin(x) * cos(x)");
    println!("Using product rule: f'(x) = cos(x) * cos(x) + sin(x) * (-sin(x))");
    println!("Simplified: f'(x) = cos^2(x) - sin^2(x) = cos(2x)\n");

    // Example 3: Chain rule
    println!("Example 3: Differentiate f(x) = exp(x^2)");
    println!("Chain rule: f'(x) = exp(x^2) * 2x\n");

    // Example 4: Simplification
    println!("Example 4: Algebraic Simplification");
    println!("x + 0 simplifies to x");
    println!("x * 1 simplifies to x");
    println!("x * 0 simplifies to 0");
    println!("x / x simplifies to 1 (when x ≠ 0)\n");

    // Example 5: Symbolic evaluation
    println!("Example 5: Evaluate expression with variable bindings");
    println!("Expression: f(x, y) = x^2 + 2xy + y^2");
    println!("Evaluate at x=3, y=4:");
    println!("Result: 3^2 + 2(3)(4) + 4^2 = 9 + 24 + 16 = 49");
    println!("Also equals: (x + y)^2 = (3 + 4)^2 = 49\n");

    // Example 6: Second derivative (higher-order derivatives)
    println!("Example 6: Second Derivative");
    println!("f(x) = x^4");
    println!("f'(x) = 4x^3");
    println!("f''(x) = 12x^2\n");

    // Example 7: Practical application - curvature analysis
    println!("Example 7: Curvature Analysis");
    println!("f(x) = sin(x)");
    println!("f'(x) = cos(x)   (slope)");
    println!("f''(x) = -sin(x) (curvature)");
    println!("At x=0: f(0)=0, f'(0)=1 (steep), f''(0)=0 (inflection)\n");

    // Example 8: Integration (antiderivative)
    println!("Example 8: Integration (Antiderivatives)");
    println!("∫ x^2 dx = x^3/3 + C");
    println!("∫ sin(x) dx = -cos(x) + C");
    println!("∫ exp(x) dx = exp(x) + C\n");

    // Example 9: Taylor series
    println!("Example 9: Taylor Series (via repeated differentiation)");
    println!("f(x) = exp(x) at x=0:");
    println!("f(0) = 1");
    println!("f'(0) = 1");
    println!("f''(0) = 1");
    println!("f'''(0) = 1");
    println!("Taylor series: exp(x) = 1 + x + x^2/2! + x^3/3! + ...\n");

    println!("=== Key Insight ===");
    println!("Symbolic math enables:");
    println!("✓ Exact computation (no floating-point errors)");
    println!("✓ Symbolic simplification (human-readable formulas)");
    println!("✓ Automatic differentiation (with chain rule, product rule)");
    println!("✓ Pattern matching (recognizing mathematical structure)");
    println!("✓ Hybrid models (combining symbolic + learned parameters)");
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/cl44_vs_octonion.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Benchmark: Cl(4,4) Geometric Product vs Octonion Multiplication
//
// Cl(4,4): 256-component multivector, geometric product = O(256^2) = 65536 muls
// Octonion: 8-component, Graves-Adcock formula = 64 muls + 56 adds = 120 FLOPs
//
// This benchmark measures the raw computation cost of each product in a tight
// loop. With AVX-512, the Cl(4,4) product can be vectorized (8 f64 per ZMM),
// reducing the effective operation count by ~8x vs scalar.
//
// Signature Cl(4,4): e0^2=e1^2=e2^2=e3^2=+1, e4^2=e5^2=e6^2=e7^2=-1
// Dimension: 2^8 = 256 components
//
// Note: wall-clock timing requires `use stdlib::time::instant`.
// This benchmark uses iteration counting and accumulated checksums.

// ============================================================================
// MATH HELPERS
// ============================================================================

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { return 0.0 - x }
    return x
}

// ============================================================================
// Cl(4,4) GEOMETRIC PRODUCT — 256-COMPONENT
// ============================================================================

// Precomputed sign table for Cl(4,4): 256x256 = 65536 entries.
// Each entry is +/-1.0. Filled once, then every geo_sign_44 call in the
// hot loop becomes a single indexed load instead of a bit-scanning loop.
var cl44_table: [f64; 65536] = [0.0; 65536]
var cl44_ready: bool = false

// Sign computation for Cl(4,4) metric: bits 0-3 square to +1, bits 4-7 to -1
fn geo_sign_44(a: i64, b: i64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var swaps = 0
    var j = 0
    while j < 8 {
        if (b >> j) & 1 != 0 {
            var k = j + 1
            while k < 8 {
                if (a >> k) & 1 != 0 { swaps = swaps + 1 }
                k = k + 1
            }
        }
        j = j + 1
    }
    let common = a & b
    var msign = 1.0
    // Bits 4-7 square to -1 (negative-definite part of signature)
    if (common >> 4) & 1 != 0 { msign = 0.0 - msign }
    if (common >> 5) & 1 != 0 { msign = 0.0 - msign }
    if (common >> 6) & 1 != 0 { msign = 0.0 - msign }
