    let n_correct = s0a.correct + s0b.correct + s1a.correct + s1b.correct + s2a.correct + s2b.correct
    let n_total = 6

    println("  Correct classifications:")
    println(n_correct)
    println("  of 6 total")

    // Mean confidence and uncertainty across test set
    let mean_conf = (s0a.conf + s0b.conf + s1a.conf + s1b.conf + s2a.conf + s2b.conf) / 6.0
    let mean_unc = (s0a.unc + s0b.unc + s1a.unc + s1b.unc + s2a.unc + s2b.unc) / 6.0
    let accuracy = n_correct as f64 / 6.0

    println("  Accuracy:")
    println(accuracy)
    println("  Mean confidence:")
    println(mean_conf)
    println("  Mean prediction uncertainty:")
    println(mean_unc)
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // ECE — Expected Calibration Error
    // With 6 samples, use 1 bin (simple ECE = |accuracy - mean_conf|)
    // ================================================================
    let ece = abs_f64(accuracy - mean_conf)
    println("Expected Calibration Error (ECE):")
    println(ece)

    // ================================================================
    // SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
    // ================================================================
    println("")
    println("Sensitivity Analysis (∂output/∂weight_uncertainty):")

    let sens = sensitivity_at(&w, in0_c0a, in1_c0a, 0.001)
    println("  ∂(confidence)/∂(weight_unc):")
    println(sens.d_conf_d_wu)
    println("  ∂(entropy)/∂(weight_unc):")
    println(sens.d_ent_d_wu)
    println("")

    // ================================================================
    // UNCERTAINTY MONOTONICITY CHECK
    // Theorem 4.2 from paper: for IID data, Bayesian concentration
    // ensures weight uncertainty decreases monotonically
    // ================================================================
    let final_unc = mean_weight_unc(&w)

    // ================================================================
    // EXTENDED VALIDATION (10 checks)
    // ================================================================
    println("====================================================================")
    println("  VALIDATION RESULTS")
    println("====================================================================")
    var passed = 0

    // Check 1: Uncertainty decreased with training
    if final_unc < init_unc {
        println("[PASS] Weight uncertainty decreased with training")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Weight uncertainty did not decrease")
    }

    // Check 2: Monotonic uncertainty decay (Bayesian concentration)
    if monotonic_decrease == 1 {
        println("[PASS] Uncertainty decreased monotonically across epochs")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Non-monotonic uncertainty decay")
    }

    // Check 3: GUM propagation produces non-zero prediction uncertainty
    if s0a.unc > 0.0 {
        println("[PASS] GUM propagation active through Hamilton products")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] No uncertainty propagated")
    }

    // Check 4: Entropy is computed and positive
    let p0 = predict(&w, in0_c0a, in1_c0a)
    if p0.entropy > 0.0 {
        println("[PASS] Predictive entropy computed")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Entropy zero or negative")
    }

    // Check 5: Softmax probabilities sum to 1.0
    let logits = qnn_forward(&w, in0_c0a, in1_c0a)
    let probs = softmax3(logits)
    let prob_sum = probs.p0.v + probs.p1.v + probs.p2.v
    if prob_sum > 0.99 && prob_sum < 1.01 {
        println("[PASS] Softmax probabilities sum to 1.0")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Softmax probabilities do not sum to 1.0")
    }

    // Check 6: ECE is bounded (calibration quality)
    if ece < 0.5 {
        println("[PASS] ECE bounded (< 0.5)")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] ECE too large (poor calibration)")
    }

    // Check 7: Sensitivity is non-zero (GUM chain rule working)
    if abs_f64(sens.d_conf_d_wu) > 1e-10 {
        println("[PASS] Confidence sensitive to weight uncertainty")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Confidence insensitive to weight uncertainty")
    }

    // Check 8: Entropy increases with uncertainty (sensitivity sign)
    if sens.d_ent_d_wu > 0.0 - 1e-10 {
        println("[PASS] Entropy non-decreasing with uncertainty")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Entropy decreased with uncertainty (anomalous)")
    }

    // Check 9: All predictions have bounded uncertainty
    let all_bounded = s0a.unc < 1.0 && s0b.unc < 1.0
                      && s1a.unc < 1.0 && s1b.unc < 1.0
                      && s2a.unc < 1.0 && s2b.unc < 1.0
    if all_bounded {
        println("[PASS] All prediction uncertainties bounded (< 1.0)")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Unbounded prediction uncertainty")
    }

    // Check 10: Final weight uncertainty significantly reduced (> 50%)
    let reduction = (init_unc - final_unc) / init_unc
    if reduction > 0.3 {
        println("[PASS] Weight uncertainty reduced by > 30%")
        passed = passed + 1
    } else {
        println("[FAIL] Insufficient uncertainty reduction")
    }

    println("")
    println("====================================================================")
    println("  BENCHMARK SUMMARY")
    println("====================================================================")
    println("  Architecture: 2 EQ -> 2 hidden -> 3 classes")
    println("  Training: 10 epochs x 9 samples = 90 steps")
    println("  Test set: 6 samples (2 per class)")
    println("  Accuracy:")
    println(accuracy)
    println("  ECE:")
    println(ece)
    println("  Final weight eps:")
    println(final_unc)
    println("  Uncertainty reduction:")
    println(reduction)
    println("  Checks passed:")
    println(passed)
    println("  of 10")
    println("====================================================================")

    if passed < 8 {
        return 1
    }
    return 0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/sounio_bench/sb_001_uncertainty_propagation.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// sb_001: GUM uncertainty propagation through arithmetic
//
// Given measured values with uncertainties, compute a derived quantity
// with propagated uncertainty using the Guide to Uncertainty in Measurement.
//
// Formula: z = (a * b) / c
// u(z) = z * sqrt((u(a)/a)^2 + (u(b)/b)^2 + (u(c)/c)^2)

struct Measurement {
    value: f64,
    uncertainty: f64
}

fn my_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x
    if x > 1.0 { guess = x * 0.5 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 60 {
        guess = 0.5 * (guess + x / guess)
        i = i + 1
    }
    guess
}

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

// Multiply two measurements: z = a * b
// u(z)/z = sqrt((u(a)/a)^2 + (u(b)/b)^2)
fn mul_measurement(a: Measurement, b: Measurement) -> Measurement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let z = a.value * b.value
    let ra = a.uncertainty / a.value
    let rb = b.uncertainty / b.value
    let rz = my_sqrt(ra * ra + rb * rb)
    Measurement { value: z, uncertainty: abs_f64(z) * rz }
}

// Divide two measurements: z = a / b
// u(z)/z = sqrt((u(a)/a)^2 + (u(b)/b)^2)
fn div_measurement(a: Measurement, b: Measurement) -> Measurement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let z = a.value / b.value
    let ra = a.uncertainty / a.value
    let rb = b.uncertainty / b.value
    let rz = my_sqrt(ra * ra + rb * rb)
    Measurement { value: z, uncertainty: abs_f64(z) * rz }
}

// Add two measurements: z = a + b
// u(z) = sqrt(u(a)^2 + u(b)^2)
fn add_measurement(a: Measurement, b: Measurement) -> Measurement with Mut, Panic, Div {
    let z = a.value + b.value
    let uz = my_sqrt(a.uncertainty * a.uncertainty + b.uncertainty * b.uncertainty)
    Measurement { value: z, uncertainty: uz }
}

fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: Multiplication uncertainty propagation
    // a = 10.0 +/- 0.5  (5% relative)
    // b = 20.0 +/- 1.0  (5% relative)
    // z = a * b = 200.0
    // u(z) = 200 * sqrt(0.05^2 + 0.05^2) = 200 * sqrt(0.005) ~ 14.14
    let a = Measurement { value: 10.0, uncertainty: 0.5 }
    let b = Measurement { value: 20.0, uncertainty: 1.0 }
    let z = mul_measurement(a, b)
    assert(check_near(z.value, 200.0, 0.01))
    assert(check_near(z.uncertainty, 14.142135, 0.01))

    // Test 2: Division uncertainty propagation
    // a = 100.0 +/- 2.0
    // b = 50.0 +/- 1.0
    // z = a / b = 2.0
    // u(z) = 2 * sqrt((2/100)^2 + (1/50)^2) = 2 * sqrt(0.0004 + 0.0004) = 2 * sqrt(0.0008) ~ 0.0566
    let c = Measurement { value: 100.0, uncertainty: 2.0 }
    let d = Measurement { value: 50.0, uncertainty: 1.0 }
    let w = div_measurement(c, d)
    assert(check_near(w.value, 2.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(w.uncertainty, 0.05657, 0.001))

    // Test 3: Addition uncertainty propagation
    // a = 5.0 +/- 0.3
    // b = 3.0 +/- 0.4
    // z = 8.0, u(z) = sqrt(0.09 + 0.16) = sqrt(0.25) = 0.5
    let e = Measurement { value: 5.0, uncertainty: 0.3 }
    let f = Measurement { value: 3.0, uncertainty: 0.4 }
    let v = add_measurement(e, f)
    assert(check_near(v.value, 8.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(v.uncertainty, 0.5, 0.001))

    // Test 4: Chained operation  z = (a * b) / c
    let m1 = Measurement { value: 10.0, uncertainty: 0.1 }
    let m2 = Measurement { value: 5.0, uncertainty: 0.05 }
    let m3 = Measurement { value: 2.0, uncertainty: 0.02 }
    let prod = mul_measurement(m1, m2)
    let result = div_measurement(prod, m3)
    assert(check_near(result.value, 25.0, 0.001))
    // Relative uncertainties: 1%, 1%, 1% => combined ~1.73%
    // u(result) ~ 25 * 0.01732 ~ 0.433
    assert(check_near(result.uncertainty, 0.433, 0.01))

    println("sb_001: All uncertainty propagation tests passed")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/sounio_bench/sb_002_effect_safe_division.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// sb_002: Effect-tracked safe division
//
// Demonstrates Sounio's effect system for tracking division safety.
// Functions that divide must declare `with Div, Panic`.
// Pure functions have no effect annotations.

fn abs_f64(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if x < 0.0 { 0.0 - x } else { x }
}

fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

// Pure function: no effects needed
fn add(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    a + b
}

// Requires Div + Panic effects
fn divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    a / b
}

// Safe division returns a tuple (result, error_code)
// error_code: 0 = success, 1 = division by zero
fn safe_divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> (f64, i32) with Div, Panic {
    if abs_f64(b) < 0.0000000001 {
        return (0.0, 1)
    }
    (a / b, 0)
}

// Compute harmonic mean: n / (1/x1 + 1/x2 + ... + 1/xn)
// Must declare Div, Panic because it calls divide
fn harmonic_mean(data: &[f64; 64], len: i64) -> (f64, i32) with Mut, Div, Panic {
    var sum_reciprocals = 0.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        let (recip, err) = safe_divide(1.0, data[i])
        if err != 0 { return (0.0, 1) }
        sum_reciprocals = sum_reciprocals + recip
        i = i + 1
    }
    let (result, err2) = safe_divide(len as f64, sum_reciprocals)
    (result, err2)
}

// Compute percentage: (part / whole) * 100
fn percentage(part: f64, whole: f64) -> (f64, i32) with Div, Panic {
    let (ratio, err) = safe_divide(part, whole)
    if err != 0 { return (0.0, 1) }
    (ratio * 100.0, 0)
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: Normal division
    let r1 = divide(10.0, 3.0)
    assert(check_near(r1, 3.33333, 0.001))

    // Test 2: Safe division success
    let (r2, e2) = safe_divide(22.0, 7.0)
    assert(e2 == 0)
    assert(check_near(r2, 3.14285, 0.001))

    // Test 3: Safe division by zero
    let (r3, e3) = safe_divide(1.0, 0.0)
    assert(e3 == 1)
    assert(r3 == 0.0)

    // Test 4: Harmonic mean
    var data: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    data[0] = 1.0
    data[1] = 2.0
    data[2] = 4.0
    let (hm, hm_err) = harmonic_mean(&data, 3)
    assert(hm_err == 0)
    // Harmonic mean of 1,2,4 = 3 / (1 + 0.5 + 0.25) = 3 / 1.75 ~ 1.714
    assert(check_near(hm, 1.71428, 0.001))

    // Test 5: Harmonic mean with zero element (should error)
    var data2: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    data2[0] = 1.0
    data2[1] = 0.0
    data2[2] = 4.0
    let (hm2, hm2_err) = harmonic_mean(&data2, 3)
    assert(hm2_err == 1)

    // Test 6: Percentage
    let (p, pe) = percentage(3.0, 4.0)
    assert(pe == 0)
    assert(check_near(p, 75.0, 0.001))

    // Test 7: Pure function needs no effects
    let sum = add(2.5, 3.5)
    assert(sum == 6.0)

    println("sb_002: All effect-safe division tests passed")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/sounio_bench/sb_003_higher_order_pipeline.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// sb_003: Higher-order pipeline using named fn refs
//
// Chain map -> filter -> fold operations using function references.
// Sounio does not have closures; all higher-order patterns use named functions.

fn double(x: i64) -> i64 { x * 2 }
fn square(x: i64) -> i64 { x * x }
fn add(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a + b }
fn mul(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a * b }
fn is_even(x: i64) -> bool with Div, Panic { x % 2 == 0 }
fn is_positive(x: i64) -> bool { x > 0 }
fn negate(x: i64) -> i64 { 0 - x }
fn add_one(x: i64) -> i64 { x + 1 }

// map: apply f to each element
fn map8(arr: [i64; 8], f: fn(i64) -> i64) -> [i64; 8] with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i] = f(arr[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

// filter: keep elements where pred is true, pack to front, return (arr, count)
struct FilterResult { data: [i64; 8], count: i64 }

fn filter8(arr: [i64; 8], pred: fn(i64) -> bool with Div, Panic) -> FilterResult with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var out: [i64; 8] = [0; 8]
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        if pred(arr[i]) {
            out[count] = arr[i]
            count = count + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    FilterResult { data: out, count: count }
}

// fold: reduce array to single value
fn fold8(arr: [i64; 8], len: i64, init: i64, f: fn(i64, i64) -> i64) -> i64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var acc = init
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        acc = f(acc, arr[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    acc
}

// any: return true if predicate holds for any element
fn any8(arr: [i64; 8], len: i64, pred: fn(i64) -> bool with Div, Panic) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        if pred(arr[i]) { return true }
        i = i + 1
    }
    false
}

// all: return true if predicate holds for all elements
fn all8(arr: [i64; 8], len: i64, pred: fn(i64) -> bool with Div, Panic) -> bool with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        if !pred(arr[i]) { return false }
        i = i + 1
    }
    true
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let data: [i64; 8] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]

    // Test 1: map(double) => [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16]
    let doubled = map8(data, double)
    assert(doubled[0] == 2)
    assert(doubled[7] == 16)

    // Test 2: map(square) => [1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64]
    let squared = map8(data, square)
    assert(squared[0] == 1)
    assert(squared[3] == 16)
    assert(squared[7] == 64)

    // Test 3: fold(add, 0) => sum = 36
    let sum = fold8(data, 8, 0, add)
    assert(sum == 36)

    // Test 4: fold(mul, 1) => product = 40320
    let product = fold8(data, 8, 1, mul)
    assert(product == 40320)

    // Test 5: filter(is_even) => [2, 4, 6, 8], count=4
    let evens = filter8(data, is_even)
    assert(evens.count == 4)
    assert(evens.data[0] == 2)
    assert(evens.data[1] == 4)
    assert(evens.data[2] == 6)
    assert(evens.data[3] == 8)

    // Test 6: Pipeline: map(double) -> filter(is_even) -> fold(add)
    // double: [2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16] (all even)
    // filter: all 8 pass
    // sum: 2+4+6+8+10+12+14+16 = 72
    let step1 = map8(data, double)
    let step2 = filter8(step1, is_even)
    let pipeline_sum = fold8(step2.data, step2.count, 0, add)
    assert(pipeline_sum == 72)

    // Test 7: Pipeline: map(square) -> fold(add) => sum of squares
    // 1+4+9+16+25+36+49+64 = 204
    let sum_sq = fold8(map8(data, square), 8, 0, add)
    assert(sum_sq == 204)

    // Test 8: any and all
    assert(any8(data, 8, is_even) == true)
    assert(all8(data, 8, is_positive) == true)

    // Test 9: Chained map
    // map(add_one) then map(double): [(1+1)*2, (2+1)*2, ...] = [4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18]
    let chained = map8(map8(data, add_one), double)
    assert(chained[0] == 4)
    assert(chained[7] == 18)

    println("sb_003: All higher-order pipeline tests passed")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/sounio_bench/sb_004_struct_accumulator.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// sb_004: Running statistics accumulator using by-value struct update
//
// Tracks count, sum, sum of squares, min, and max.
// Uses Welford's online algorithm variant for numerical stability.
// Returns updated struct by value (no &! needed).

struct RunningStats {
    count: i64,
    sum: f64,
    sum_sq: f64,
    min_val: f64,
    max_val: f64
}

fn stats_new() -> RunningStats {
    RunningStats {
        count: 0,
        sum: 0.0,
        sum_sq: 0.0,
        min_val: 999999999.0,
        max_val: 0.0 - 999999999.0
    }
}

// Add a value and return updated stats (by-value update pattern)
fn stats_push(s: RunningStats, x: f64) -> RunningStats {
    let new_count = s.count + 1
    let new_sum = s.sum + x
    let new_sum_sq = s.sum_sq + x * x
    let new_min = if x < s.min_val { x } else { s.min_val }
    let new_max = if x > s.max_val { x } else { s.max_val }
    RunningStats {
        count: new_count,
        sum: new_sum,
        sum_sq: new_sum_sq,
        min_val: new_min,
        max_val: new_max
    }
}

fn stats_mean(s: RunningStats) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    s.sum / (s.count as f64)
}

fn stats_variance(s: RunningStats) -> f64 with Div, Panic {
    let n = s.count as f64
    let mean = s.sum / n
    s.sum_sq / n - mean * mean
}

fn my_sqrt(x: f64) -> f64 with Mut, Panic, Div {
    if x <= 0.0 { return 0.0 }
    var guess = x
    if x > 1.0 { guess = x * 0.5 }
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 60 {
        guess = 0.5 * (guess + x / guess)
        i = i + 1
    }
    guess
}

fn stats_stddev(s: RunningStats) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic {
    my_sqrt(stats_variance(s))
}

fn check_near(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
    let d = a - b
    let ad = if d < 0.0 { 0.0 - d } else { d }
    ad < tol
}

// Merge two RunningStats into one
fn stats_merge(a: RunningStats, b: RunningStats) -> RunningStats {
    let min_v = if a.min_val < b.min_val { a.min_val } else { b.min_val }
    let max_v = if a.max_val > b.max_val { a.max_val } else { b.max_val }
    RunningStats {
        count: a.count + b.count,
        sum: a.sum + b.sum,
        sum_sq: a.sum_sq + b.sum_sq,
        min_val: min_v,
        max_val: max_v
    }
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: Build stats from individual values
    var s = stats_new()
    s = stats_push(s, 2.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 4.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 4.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 4.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 5.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 5.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 7.0)
    s = stats_push(s, 9.0)

    assert(s.count == 8)
    assert(check_near(stats_mean(s), 5.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(s.min_val, 2.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(s.max_val, 9.0, 0.001))

    // Variance = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 = (4+16+16+16+25+25+49+81)/8 - 25 = 29 - 25 = 4
    assert(check_near(stats_variance(s), 4.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(stats_stddev(s), 2.0, 0.001))

    // Test 2: Build stats from array
    var data: [f64; 64] = [0.0; 64]
    data[0] = 10.0
    data[1] = 20.0
    data[2] = 30.0
    data[3] = 40.0
    data[4] = 50.0
    let len: i64 = 5

    var s2 = stats_new()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len {
        s2 = stats_push(s2, data[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    assert(s2.count == 5)
    assert(check_near(stats_mean(s2), 30.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(s2.min_val, 10.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(s2.max_val, 50.0, 0.001))

    // Test 3: Merge two stats
    var sa = stats_new()
    sa = stats_push(sa, 1.0)
    sa = stats_push(sa, 2.0)
    sa = stats_push(sa, 3.0)

    var sb = stats_new()
    sb = stats_push(sb, 4.0)
    sb = stats_push(sb, 5.0)

    let merged = stats_merge(sa, sb)
    assert(merged.count == 5)
    assert(check_near(merged.sum, 15.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(merged.min_val, 1.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(merged.max_val, 5.0, 0.001))

    // Test 4: Single element stats
    var s3 = stats_new()
    s3 = stats_push(s3, 42.0)
    assert(s3.count == 1)
    assert(check_near(stats_mean(s3), 42.0, 0.001))
    assert(check_near(stats_variance(s3), 0.0, 0.001))

    println("sb_004: All struct accumulator tests passed")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/sounio_bench/sb_005_enum_state_machine.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// sb_005: State machine using enum + match
//
// Models a simple traffic light controller:
//   Red -> Green -> Yellow -> Red
// Each state has a duration. The machine steps through states
// and tracks total elapsed time.

enum Light { Red, Green, Yellow }

struct TrafficState {
    light: i64,
    ticks_in_state: i64,
    total_ticks: i64,
    transitions: i64
}

fn traffic_new() -> TrafficState {
    TrafficState {
        light: 0,
        ticks_in_state: 0,
        total_ticks: 0,
        transitions: 0
    }
}

// Duration for each light state
fn light_duration(light: i64) -> i64 {
    match light {
        Light::Red => 30
        Light::Green => 25
        Light::Yellow => 5
        _ => 0
    }
}

// Next state transition
fn next_light(light: i64) -> i64 {
    match light {
        Light::Red => 1
        Light::Green => 2
        Light::Yellow => 0
        _ => 0
    }
}

// Name as integer code for verification (0=Red, 1=Green, 2=Yellow)
fn light_code(light: i64) -> i64 {
    match light {
        Light::Red => 0
        Light::Green => 1
        Light::Yellow => 2
        _ => 3
    }
}

// Step the state machine by one tick, return updated state
fn traffic_tick(state: TrafficState) -> TrafficState {
    let new_ticks = state.ticks_in_state + 1
    let duration = light_duration(state.light)

    if new_ticks >= duration {
        // Transition to next state
        let nl = next_light(state.light)
        TrafficState {
            light: nl,
            ticks_in_state: 0,
            total_ticks: state.total_ticks + 1,
            transitions: state.transitions + 1
        }
    } else {
        TrafficState {
            light: state.light,
            ticks_in_state: new_ticks,
            total_ticks: state.total_ticks + 1,
            transitions: state.transitions
        }
    }
}

// Run for N ticks
fn traffic_run(n: i64) -> TrafficState with Mut, Panic {
    var state = traffic_new()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < n {
        state = traffic_tick(state)
        i = i + 1
    }
    state
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    // Test 1: Initial state is Red
    let s0 = traffic_new()
    assert(light_code(s0.light) == 0)
    assert(s0.ticks_in_state == 0)
    assert(s0.total_ticks == 0)

    // Test 2: After 1 tick, still Red (duration=30)
    let s1 = traffic_tick(s0)
    assert(light_code(s1.light) == 0)
    assert(s1.ticks_in_state == 1)
    assert(s1.total_ticks == 1)

    // Test 3: After 30 ticks, transition to Green
    let s30 = traffic_run(30)
    assert(light_code(s30.light) == 1)
    assert(s30.transitions == 1)

    // Test 4: After 55 ticks (30 Red + 25 Green), transition to Yellow
    let s55 = traffic_run(55)
    assert(light_code(s55.light) == 2)
    assert(s55.transitions == 2)

    // Test 5: After 60 ticks (30 + 25 + 5), back to Red
    let s60 = traffic_run(60)
    assert(light_code(s60.light) == 0)
    assert(s60.transitions == 3)

    // Test 6: Full cycle is 60 ticks. After 120 ticks, 6 transitions, back to Red
    let s120 = traffic_run(120)
    assert(light_code(s120.light) == 0)
    assert(s120.transitions == 6)
    assert(s120.total_ticks == 120)

    // Test 7: Durations are correct
    assert(light_duration(0) == 30)
    assert(light_duration(1) == 25)
    assert(light_duration(2) == 5)

    // Test 8: After 180 ticks = 3 full cycles
    let s180 = traffic_run(180)
    assert(s180.transitions == 9)

    println("sb_005: All enum state machine tests passed")
    0
}


// === FILE: benchmarks/stdlib_validation/epistemic_gum/sounio_bench.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Benchmark: gum.sio NIST Supp1 Ex4-like R = V/I propagation
pub use epistemic::gum::*;

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    // V = 10.00 +/- 0.02 rectangular (half=0.02)
    let u_v = type_b_uniform(0.02);
    let v_res = gum_simple(10.0, u_v.std_uncertainty);
    // I = 1.005 +/- 0.003 rectangular
    let u_i = type_b_uniform(0.003);
    let i_res = gum_simple(1.005, u_i.std_uncertainty);
    // R = V / I
    let r_res = gum_div(v_res, i_res);
    print("{{\\"r_value\\": ");
    print(r_res.value);
    print(", \\"r_std_unc\\": ");
    print(r_res.std_uncertainty);
    print(", \\"r_exp_unc95\\": ");
    print(r_res.expanded_uncertainty_95);
    print("}}");
    0
}

// Benchmark: epistemic_matrix matmul GUM propagation
pub use linalg::epistemic_matrix::*;

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    // 2x2 matrices with unc = 1e-6, conf=0.95
    var a = ematrix_zeros(2, 2);
    ematrix_set(&a, 0, 0, 1.0, 1e-6, 0.95);
    ematrix_set(&a, 0, 1, 0.5, 1e-6, 0.95);
    ematrix_set(&a, 1, 0, 0.5, 1e-6, 0.95);
    ematrix_set(&a, 1, 1, 2.0, 1e-6, 0.95);
    var b = ematrix_zeros(2, 2);
    ematrix_set(&b, 0, 0, 3.0, 1e-6, 0.95);
    ematrix_set(&b, 0, 1, 1.0, 1e-6, 0.95);
    ematrix_set(&b, 1, 0, 1.0, 1e-6, 0.95);
    ematrix_set(&b, 1, 1, 4.0, 1e-6, 0.95);
    let c = ematrix_mul(&a, &b);
    print("{{\\"c00_val\\": ");
    print(ematrix_get_val(&c, 0, 0));
    print(", \\"c00_unc\\": ");
    print(ematrix_get_unc(&c, 0, 0));
    print(", \\"c00_conf\\": ");
    print(ematrix_get_conf(&c, 0, 0));
    print("}}"); // exemplo c00
    0
}

// === FILE: benchmarks/stdlib_validation/stats_regression_linear/sounio_bench.sio ===
//@ run-pass
// Benchmark: stats::regression::linear OLS epistemic vs SciPy linregress
// Dados fixos n=20, y ≈ 2 + 3x + noise pequena
// Output JSON: {"intercept", "slope", "r_squared"}
pub use stats::regression::linear::*;
pub use stats::shared::*; // assumido

fn main() -> i32 with IO {
    let n: i64 = 20;
    var x: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100];
    var y: [f64; 100] = [0.0; 100];
    var i: i64 = 0;
    while i < n {
        x[i as usize] = i as f64;
        y[i as usize] = 2.0 + 3.0 * (i as f64) + 0.05 * ((i % 2) as f64 - 0.5);
        i = i + 1;
    }
    let model = fit_linear_regression_epistemic(x, y, n);
    print("{\\"intercept\\": ");
    print(model.value.coefficients[0]);
    print(", \\"slope\\": ");
    print(model.value.coefficients[1]);
    print(", \\"r_squared\\": ");
    print(model.value.r_squared);
    print("}");
    0
}
